《大秦国师》作者：故筝
文案：
一朝穿越到神棍忽悠秦始皇现场。
作为辣个神棍，徐福为了保住小命，
被迫走上成为大秦第一国师（神棍），忽悠整个大秦子民的光明（黑暗）大道。
职业生涯第一步，
先从忽悠面前的秦始皇开始……
始皇攻X神棍技能颜值技能点满的徐福受，主角苏爽
…
内容标签：强强 穿越时空 励志人生 历史剧
搜索关键字：主角：徐福，嬴政 ┃ 配角：赵高，扶苏，胡亥…… ┃ 其它：秦始皇，神棍，爽文，金手指，作者故筝
晋江银牌编辑：
美貌值与神棍技能均已点满的徐福一朝穿越，来到了第一神棍忽悠秦始皇求长生的现场，为了保住小命，他被迫走上成为大秦第一国师（神棍），忽悠整个大秦子民的光明（黑暗）大道。职业生涯第一步，先从忽悠住面前的秦始皇开始……
本文开篇趣味十足，主角一穿越，就遭遇人生最大危机，主角如何凭着强大忽悠功底，登上国师之位，秦始皇又是如何在与主角的配合下，走上千古一帝的道路，成为全文最大的亮点。

烈日高照。
北京天桥底下，徐福扯下脸上罩着的三块钱大草帽，整了整身上的八卦衣，竖起了旁边的招牌杆子，上书两个大字：算命。
徐福面前还摆着一张小方桌，桌上签筒、龟甲、八卦盘……一应俱全。再配上他俊逸出尘的打扮，端的是仙风道骨，正如同喧嚣都市中的一股清流。
……可是特么的没人来理他这股清流啊！
要是一桩生意都揽不到，他这个月就只能以天桥为家了啊摔！
几个断腿断脚瞎眼的“乞丐”蹲在离徐福不远的地方。
“嘻嘻，你看那个人，是不是有病？竟然在这里摆摊算命？还不如我们乞讨来钱快呢……”
“长得挺好看，怎么做了这个营生……”
“我看个傻逼吧……”
……
你特么才傻逼！
徐福憋着一股气，一定要揽到一桩生意。
就在这时，一个戴着墨镜、穿着西装、脖子上两根粗金条，一脸“我很有钱快来宰”的男人从那头过来了，他身后还跟着几个看上去比他还要威武霸气的保镖。
徐福只看了一眼那个男人，双眼就亮了。
此时不下手，何时下手！
那男人还没走近，徐福就端足了架子，悠悠道：“这位先生可是做娱乐生意的？相逢即是有缘，不如坐下来，我为先生算一卦。”
周围的人看向徐福的目光都透着“你是个傻逼吗”的味道。
他们越是轻视他，徐福就越是要好好算这一卦。
徐福的声音实在好听，清泠泠的，带着股空灵的味道。
男人摘下墨镜，将徐福从上打量到下，暗自嘀咕，这么好看的人倒是少见，他将墨镜扔给身后的小弟，拉过凳子坐下来了。
徐福双眼更亮，顿时摩拳擦掌。终于轮到自己大显身手了！
他看着男人那张粗犷的脸，都不带磨蹭的，迅速地下了批语，“我观先生面相，绿云罩顶，又印堂发黑，恐有血光之灾，并且还是女祸……这可不大好啊，但也不是没有破解的办法，相逢即是……啊！你打我干嘛？”
徐福的话还没说完，男人脸色一变，一拳就将徐福揍倒在地，“妈的，说老子绿云罩顶？去你娘的狗屁！给老子揍他！长得挺好一张脸，却他妈是个神经病！”
男人身后的小弟一拥而上，三两脚将徐福的摊子踢翻，随即强硬地将徐福按在了下面拳脚相交。
徐福懵了。
卧槽！你们才特么神经病啊！我说的都是真的啊！
男人在旁边摸出一串佛珠，冷冷道：“像我这样坚守我党宗旨，坚信马克思唯物主义哲学，坚信科学发展观，坚持要走具有社会主义特色的新时代黑社会发展建设道路的共产主义者，你还想赚我的钱？给老子继续打。”
徐福一口老血哽在喉咙口。
你特么一开赌场的黑社会大佬，你坚持个屁的科学发展观啊！
“你别不信我！真的有血光……啊啊啊！”
“噗通”一声，徐福脚一滑，翻过栏杆沉下了水。
我特么不会游泳啊！
徐福挣扎两下，直接沉了下去。
“落落、落水了啊！”有人惊叫。
大佬浑不在意地一挥手，赶紧让人将他捞上来送医院。
刚刚离开师门摆了摊，没来得及算到自己有血光之灾的徐福，被送往了医院抢救。
大佬拍拍屁股回家，他正要跟他那小情人说起这个算命的傻逼，却一开门就被小情人和她的奸夫砍了个照面。那一刀正好砍在大佬锁骨上，鲜血咕咚咕咚地往外冒。
大佬脑子里突然涌现那算命的批语。
我操操操！大师我错了啊！你是神算啊！
“去……去医院……给我找那个大师，去……”
小弟打了个电话回来，苦着脸，“大大大师……进太平间了。”
躺在太平间的徐福，如果灵魂还有感知，一定是日了狗的。
我！死！不！瞑！目！啊！
*
徐福以为自己睁开双眼第一眼看见的会是牛头马面，谁知道睁眼以后，依旧是烈日高照，一转头，旁边的杆子上还是上书两个大字：算命。面前的桌子上依旧摆着签筒、龟甲、八卦盘……
唯一不同的是，面前坐着的男人，头戴高冠，大襟窄袖，腰间系有革带，通体贵气，气势凌然，不知道甩了那个黑社会大佬多少条街。
出于职业惯性，徐福迅速端详起了男人的脸。
观仪表。神气生威！
观头额。额高头方，贵为天子！
徐福心下一惊，继续看。
观双眸。眼眸深邃，却是眸光清铄，不怒自威！
观五岳三亭、五官六府……竟都是贵气之相！
都说看人先看脸是不无道理的，一个人的品德心性都可从脸上得出。眼前的男人，难以挑出不足来，怪不得长得如此英俊，当得起凤表龙姿四字。
这个男人一定是惯为上位者，加之他身形高大，往面前一坐，饶是粗神经的徐福也感觉到了一丝压迫感。
“先生可得出了什么？”男人突然开口了，声音低沉有力，暗含锋芒。
坐在算命摊前的男人正是嬴政，他原本是不相信这些五行八卦算命之法的。但是面前的少年着一身白衣，唇红齿白，五官生得无比清丽，笑起来的时候，双眸波光潋滟令人忍不住心神一荡，连宫中生得极美的郑妃与胡姬，竟都难敌少年的颜色。
嬴政没由来得生出了些好感，这才怀着猎奇和欣赏的心情，坐了下来。
只可惜了，生得这样好的少年公子，偏偏要摆摊算命。——嬴政和他身后一干狗腿子都这么想。
徐福又细细将嬴政端详一番，嘴上依旧没把门，就跟给那个黑社会大佬下批语一样，张嘴就来，“我观先生面相，绿云罩顶，又印堂发黑，恐有血光之灾，并且还是女祸。”等说完之后，徐福马上住嘴。他要等男人不会有揍他的意思，再说下去。
嬴政的面色沉了沉，气势微显。
徐福还在心里嘀咕，这个男人明显要大度多了，他嘴角竟然还噙着一丝笑意。
徐福却没能品味出那抹笑意，叫冷笑啊！
嬴政身后跟着个面孔白净的人，那人站直身体，对徐福横眉竖目，声音尖厉，“大胆！”
我胆子是一向很大，徐福在内心认同，下一秒却听见那个“大度”的男人，转过头对身后的人说：“将他抓起来，关进大牢。”
等等……抓起来？关大牢？
徐福觉得自己还可以抢救一下，“先生，我说的都是真的啊！我还知道你是谁，你是……”徐福的嘴被随即涌上来的高大侍从堵住了嘴。
他的算命摊子又一次被掀翻了。
徐福顿觉不好，连忙抬手抱头，“就算说得不合你心意，你也别揍人啊……”
“王上如此英明神武，霸气英俊，怎么会绿云罩顶呢？这些江湖术士，果然尽是满嘴胡言！”尖厉的声音再度响起。
“赵高。”嬴政不悦。
身后一干侍从齐齐倒抽一口气。
绿云罩顶……
那四个字，他竟然说出来了！
赵高也随即惶恐不已，捂脸跪地。
嬴政站起身来，身高八尺有余，他居高临下地瞥了一眼尽管抱着头，也依旧一派仙风道骨的徐福，“带走。”
而徐福脑子里盘旋着一个词，王上？果然是贵为天子！他没算错！
chapters.title: 第1章
chapters.translated_text:
The scorching sun hung high in the sky.

Beneath the Tianqiao overpass in Beijing, Xu Fu pulled off the three-yuan straw hat he had been wearing over his face, straightened his Daoist robe patterned with the Eight Trigrams, and erected his signpost. Two large characters were written upon it: Fortune Telling.

In front of Xu Fu was also a small square table, complete with divination sticks, tortoise shells, and a Bagua compass. Paired with his refined and otherworldly attire, he truly had the air of an immortal, standing out like a breath of fresh air in the bustling metropolis.

...Yet damn it, nobody was paying any attention to this breath of fresh air!

If he couldn't even bag a single customer, he would be living under the overpass for the rest of the month, damn it!

Several "beggars" with broken legs and missing eyes squatted not far from Xu Fu.

"Hehe, look at that guy. Is he sick in the head? Setting up a stall to tell fortunes here? It's way slower than us begging for money..."

"He's quite good-looking, why did he take up this trade..."

"I think he's a fucking idiot..."

...

You're the fucking idiot!

Xu Fu held back his breath, determined to land a customer.

Just then, a man wearing sunglasses and a suit, with two thick gold chains around his neck and an expression that screamed "I'm super rich, come fleece me," walked over from that direction. Behind him followed a few bodyguards who looked even more intimidating and domineering than he was.

Xu Fu took one look at the man, and his eyes lit up.

If not now, when!

Before the man even walked close, Xu Fu struck a practiced pose and said leisurely, "Is this gentleman in the entertainment business? Meeting is fate; why not sit down, and I'll read a fortune for you."

The surrounding people looked at Xu Fu with expressions that clearly conveyed, "Are you a fucking idiot?"

The more they looked down on him, the more determined Xu Fu was to do a good reading of this fortune.

Xu Fu's voice was genuinely pleasant, crisp and clear, carrying an ethereal quality.

The man took off his sunglasses, looked Xu Fu up and down, and muttered to himself that it was rare to see someone so good-looking. He tossed his sunglasses to the lackey behind him, pulled over a stool, and sat down.

Xu Fu's eyes brightened even more, and he immediately rubbed his hands together. It was finally his turn to show off his skills!

Looking at the man's rugged face, he didn't hesitate at all and quickly delivered his verdict: "Based on your physiognomy, sir, your head is shrouded in green clouds, and your space between the eyebrows is darkened. I'm afraid you have the disaster of bloodshed, and it stems from a woman... This isn't great, but it's not without a solution. Meeting is fate—ah! Why are you hitting me?"

Before Xu Fu could finish his sentence, the man's expression changed, and with a single punch, he knocked Xu Fu to the ground. "Damn it, you say my head is shrouded in green clouds? Fuck your mother's nonsense! Beat him up for me! Such a good-looking face, but the fucking guy's a psycho!"

The lackeys behind the man swarmed forward, kicking Xu Fu's stall over in two or three steps, and then forcefully pinned Xu Fu down, punching and kicking him.

Xu Fu was dumbfounded.

What the fuck! You guys are the fucking psychos! Everything I said is true!

The man pulled out a string of Buddhist prayer beads nearby and said coldly, "A communist like me who upholds the principles of our Party, firmly believes in Marxist materialistic philosophy, firmly believes in the scientific outlook on development, and insists on walking the path of socialist-style construction of the new era's underworld—you still want to make money off me? Keep beating him."

A mouthful of old blood choked in Xu Fu's throat.

You're a damn mafia boss running a casino, what the hell are you insisting on the scientific outlook on development for!

"Don't you disbelieve me! There really is bloodshed... Ah, ah, ah!"

With a "thud," Xu Fu's foot slipped, and he tumbled over the railing and sank into the water.

I can't fucking swim!

Xu Fu struggled twice and sank straight down.

"He's, he's fallen into the water!" someone screamed.

The boss waved his hand indifferently and hurriedly told people to fish him up and send him to the hospital.

Having just left his sect to set up a stall, before he had time to foresee his own disaster of bloodshed, Xu Fu was rushed to the hospital for emergency treatment.

The boss patted his backside and went home. Just as he was about to tell his little lover about that fortune-telling idiot, he opened the door only to run face-to-face with his little lover and her adulterer. That knife landed right on the boss's collarbone, and blood spurted out in gushing streams.

The fortune-teller's verdict suddenly flashed in the boss's mind.

Holy shit, shit, shit! Master, I was wrong! You are a divine fortune-teller!

"Go... go to the hospital... find that master for me, go..."

The lackey made a phone call and came back with a bitter face, "Ma-ma-master... went to the morgue."

Xu Fu, lying in the morgue, if his soul could still perceive anything, must have felt like he was being fucked by a dog.

I! Die! With! Eyes! Unclosed!

*

Xu Fu thought the first thing he would see when he opened his eyes would be Ox-head and Horse-face. Who would have thought that after opening his eyes, the scorching sun was still hanging high, and when he turned his head, the signpost beside him still had two large characters written on it: Fortune Telling. The table in front of him still displayed divination sticks, tortoise shells, a Bagua compass...

The only difference was that the man sitting in front of him wore a towering crown, large lapels and narrow sleeves, and a leather belt around his waist. He radiated noble status and an imposing, awe-inspiring aura, leaving that mafia boss in the dust by countless streets.

Out of professional habit, Xu Fu quickly scrutinized the man's face.

Observing his demeanor: His spirit and Qi generated might!

Observing his forehead: High forehead and square head—he is noble enough to be the Son of Heaven!

A jolt went through Xu Fu's heart, and he continued to look.

Observing his eyes: Deep-set eyes, yet the gaze was bright and piercing, commanding respect without anger!

Observing the Five Peaks and Three Regions, the Five Organs and Six Chambers... they were all physiognomies of nobility!

They say it's not without reason that judging a person starts with their face; a person's character and disposition can be read from their visage. The man before him was hard to find fault with, no wonder he was so handsome and worthy of the four words "phoenix appearance and dragon bearing."

This man must be accustomed to being in a position of authority. Coupled with his tall stature, sitting right in front of him, even the thick-skinned Xu Fu felt a trace of pressure.

"Has the gentleman deduced anything?" The man spoke suddenly, his voice low and powerful, concealing a sharp edge.

The man sitting before the fortune-telling stall was none of other than Ying Zheng. Originally, he did not believe in these methods of the Five Elements, Bagua, and fortune-telling. But the young man before him was dressed in white, with red lips and white teeth, and facial features of peerless and delicate beauty. When he smiled, his eyes rippled with light, making one's heart involuntarily flutter. Even Lady Zheng and Lady Hu, who possessed extreme beauty in the palace, could hardly match the young man's coloring.

Ying Zheng inexplicably felt a surge of favorable impression, which was why he sat down with a sense of novelty and appreciation.

It was just a pity that a young gentleman born with such good looks insisted on setting up a stall to tell fortunes. — This was what Ying Zheng and his retinue of lackeys all thought.

Xu Fu scrutinized Ying Zheng carefully once more, his mouth still completely unchecked. Just like when he delivered the verdict to that mafia boss, the words spilled right out of his mouth: "Based on your physiognomy, sir, your head is shrouded in green clouds, and your space between the eyebrows is darkened. I'm afraid you have the disaster of bloodshed, and it stems from a woman." After he finished speaking, Xu Fu immediately clamped his mouth shut. He would wait until the man showed no intention of beating him before continuing.

Ying Zheng's expression darkened slightly, his aura faintly manifesting.

Xu Fu was still muttering inwardly that this man was obviously much more magnanimous; there was even a hint of a smile lingering at the corners of his lips.

Xu Fu failed to recognize that that trace of a smile was actually a sneer!

Following behind Ying Zheng was a pale-faced person. That person straightened his body, glared at Xu Fu with hostile eyes, and spoke in a shrill voice, "Audacious!"

My audacity has always been very great, Xu Fu acknowledged inwardly, but the next second he heard that "magnanimous" man turn his head and say to the person behind him, "Seize him and lock him in the dungeon."

Wait... Seize him? Lock him in the dungeon?

Xu Fu felt he could still be saved. "Sir, everything I said is true! I even know who you are, you are—" Xu Fu's mouth was promptly blocked by a tall attendant who rushed up.

His fortune-telling stall was overturned once again.

Xu Fu felt a sense of impending doom and hurriedly raised his hands to protect his head. "Even if what I said isn't to your liking, you don't have to hit people..."

"His Majesty is so brilliant and martial, domineering and handsome, how could his head be shrouded in green clouds? These wandering charlatans are truly nothing but full of empty talk!" The shrill voice sounded once more.

"Zhao Gao." Ying Zheng said with displeasure.

The retinue of attendants behind him simultaneously sucked in a cold breath.

Head shrouded in green clouds...

Those four words, he actually said them!

Zhao Gao was likewise struck with sudden panic, covering his face and dropping to his knees.

Ying Zheng stood up, standing well over eight feet tall. He glanced down condescendingly at Xu Fu, who, despite covering his head, still maintained the air of an immortal. "Take him away."

Meanwhile, a single phrase swirled in Xu Fu's mind: His Majesty? He truly was noble enough to be the Son of Heaven! His calculation hadn't been wrong!

chapters.title: 第10章
chapters.translated_text:
The side hall of Xianyang Palace.

A wisp of smoke slowly rose from the censer.

Ying Zheng put down the bamboo slips, rubbed the corners of his eyes, and picked up the teacup at hand to take a sip. However, the refreshing tea could not ease his irritation. His coming-of-age ceremony was approaching, yet countless people were unwilling to let him smoothly reach adulthood. As the dignified King of Qin, he was far less powerful than the influential ministers in his court.

A palace maid walked in and knelt down, "Your Majesty, Mr. Xu has arrived."

"Let him in."

The palace maid retreated. Not long after, Xu Fu followed behind Zhao Gao into the hall.

Zhao Gao bowed to Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, the person has been brought here." With that, he stepped aside.

Xu Fu had spent a long time trying to figure out how the ancients performed bows and greetings, but after much thought, he still couldn't remember, so he simply stood there rigidly. Noticing his absent-mindedness, Ying Zheng couldn't help but look him over a few times.

Just as others in the Bureau of Fengchang had gossiped, very few people actually looked good in red official robes.

Most of the low-ranking officials were awkward-looking or elderly and frail; once they put on the red official robes, it was as if they were wearing a padded floral jacket—an absolute eyesore.

Yet this detested official robe, when worn by Xu Fu, made his lips even redder and his teeth even whiter. Far from looking like a commoner, he instead resembled a noble youth from a distinguished family.

"You are skilled at observing the weather and divining fortune and misfortune. Then calculate for Us: when would be the most appropriate time for Us to hold our coming-of-age ceremony?"

As soon as Ying Zheng opened his mouth, he dropped a bombshell on Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was stunned for a second.

The date of King Ying Zheng of Qin's coming-of-age ceremony—he was being asked to calculate it?

He was being asked to calculate the date of the capping ceremony!

Don't blame Xu Fu for lacking worldly experience. Even someone poorly versed in history like him knew about Qin始皇 (Qin Shi Huang), the First Emperor through the ages. In the eyes of many people, this emperor was lofty and sacred. Countless individuals had dreamed of returning to the Great Qin to witness the majesty of the First Emperor. And as for him, having blundered into this era, the very first person he saw was Qin Shi Huang. It was already enough that he had managed to fool Qin Shi Huang and smoothly land an official post.

Now, Qin Shi Huang actually wanted him to divine the coming-of-age ceremony.

In history, the First Emperor's coming-of-age ceremony was a turning point! It was during this ceremony that the First Emperor executed a batch of people, imprisoned his mother, and subsequently brought down Lü Buwei, gathering all the supreme power of Qin into his own hands. Following that, the centralized system of government began with him.

"What? Is it difficult?" Seeing that Xu Fu remained silent for a long time, Ying Zheng shifted his sitting posture. Ying Zheng was already tall by nature, and coupled with his straight back, his imposing aura was even more intense. Standing before him, Xu Fu felt almost entirely engulfed by his shadow.

Xu Fu shook his head, suppressing the excitement in his heart, "No, it's not difficult. It is my honor."

To be able to witness such a piece of history was indeed thrilling and honorable.

Xu Fu felt like his career was about to reach its peak, didn't he?

"I need to calculate it carefully. When should this date be reported to Your Majesty?" Xu Fu quickly regained his composure and asked. In Ying Zheng's eyes, his demeanor was consistently calm and unruffled.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but praise Xu Fu's attitude of neither being servile nor overbearing; even upon receiving such a fine task, he did not show excessive joy because of it. It was just like the demeanor of "distinguished scholars and pure currents" currently advocated.

"We hope the sooner, the better."

Xu Fu raised his head and locked eyes with Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu's eyes weren't actually pure black, but rather a bit light grey, yet they looked exceptionally pure. Ying Zheng stared for a moment and was slightly dazed. Xu Fu's gaze was clear and resolute.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but let his imagination run wild again.

Someone like Xu Fu probably came from a prominent family, possessed consummate skills, yet had a pure mind and a proud disposition. Having such a person handle divination and observation matters, untainted by the filth of the mortal world, was simply fitting.

The "untainted" Xu Fu had no idea what kind of persona Ying Zheng had concocted for him in his head. Having received the assignment, he gave a bow with cupped hands and requested to take his leave so he could return, consult ancient texts, and perform the calculations.

A palace maid suddenly entered. Lowering her gaze and submissively kneeling beside Xu Fu, she said in a low voice, "Your Majesty, Lady Hu requests an audience."

In this period, society wasn't too strict about women not meeting external men, so even with Xu Fu standing by, it was of no great consequence.

Ying Zheng nodded, allowing Lady Hu to enter.

As soon as Xu Fu heard the palace maid's title, he guessed she must be one of Ying Zheng's harem consorts. He wondered just how breathtakingly beautiful Qin Shi Huang's wife would be. Just as he was guessing, he saw a slender, graceful young woman walking over from that direction. Her attire was magnificent and luxurious, her waist bound with a silk ribbon that accentuated a slender willow waist. The woman also wore her long black hair loose, without a single hair ornament, which only made her appear all the more enchanting. As she walked, the ends of her hair swayed along with her steps.

Such a beauty, it's a pity her makeup was a bit too garish.

Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng's expression. Shouldn't he be tactful and take his leave while the going was good?

Yet Ying Zheng never said the words to let him leave.

Lady Hu served pastries and broth, her voice seductive as she spoke, "Your Majesty has rarely entered the harem recently, and this concubine misses you dearly."

Then, this gorgeously appearance consort cast a flirtatious wink at the King of Qin right in front of everyone.

Xu Fu suddenly felt even more redundant.

Ying Zheng didn't spare even a fraction of a glance for Lady Hu; instead, he ordered Zhao Gao to escort Xu Fu back.

Lady Hu knew that Zhao Gao was a close attendant by the King of Qin's side. Now, hearing the King of Qin give such an order, her interest in Xu Fu was instantly piqued, and she turned her head to look at him.

Xu Fu had never been one to shy away from people's scrutinizing gazes. If he were afraid, he probably wouldn't have had the thick skin to set up a fortune-telling stall under the Tianqiao Bridge.

The more Lady Hu looked, the more astonished she became.

Ever since she entered the palace, she hadn't even placed Consort Zheng, who had entered earlier, in her eyes—simply because she had absolute confidence in her own looks. She was softly alluring, with a captivating voice and a fine figure. Although palace attendants secretly compared her to a dancing girl behind her back, so what? She was born beautiful and could always win a measure of favor from the Great King. This was something others could never hope to catch up with, no matter how hard they whipped their horses.

Yet Lady Hu had never imagined that there would be someone even more outstanding in appearance than her.

And this person turned out to be a man.

Looking at those exquisitely beautiful brows and eyes, and that ethereal temperament, Lady Hu couldn't help feeling a bit jealous. She didn't recognize the official robe Xu Fu was wearing, only feeling that that red gown made the person before her outshine every single color in the harem.

Jealousy at work in secret, Lady Hu asked with a charming smile, "This concubine was wondering why Your Majesty hasn't liked visiting the harem lately, but now I know. So Your Majesty has acquired such a beauty; no wonder you can lavish him with such favor."

Xu Fu was somewhat dumbfounded.

Young lady, what kind of nonsense are you babbling?

Author's note: Lady Hu is Huhai's mother, and Consort Zheng is Fusu's mother. Fusu and Huhai will be born soon, and then tormented by Xu Fu's various deceptions.
chapters.source_text:
咸阳宫偏殿。
一缕烟缓缓从香炉中升起。
嬴政放下竹简，揉了揉眼角，端起手边的茶杯抿了一口。但清爽的茶水并不能缓解他的烦躁。他成年加冠在即，偏偏却有无数人不愿意让他顺利加冠。他堂堂秦国的大王，却不如权臣手中掌握的权势之盛。
宫女走进来跪下，“王上，徐先生到了。”
“让他进来。”
宫女退出去，不多时，徐福就跟在赵高身后进来了。
赵高冲嬴政躬了躬身，“王上，人已带到。”随后便退到一边去了。
徐福思考了半天古人是怎么行礼的，但是想半天也没能想出来，于是就这样直愣愣地站在那里了。嬴政发觉的走神，不由得多打量了他几眼。
正如奉常寺中其他人闲聊时所说的那样，红色官袍其实很少有人能穿得好看。
那些底层的官员们，大都是歪瓜裂枣的，还有些年老体衰的，红色官服一套上身，简直就跟套个了花棉袄似的，要有多戳眼就能有多戳眼。
偏偏就这样一套被嫌弃的官服套在徐福身上，将徐福衬得越发的唇红齿白，只不过这个模样可不像是什么平民，反倒像是长于世家的贵气少年。
“你会观天气、测祸福，那你便为寡人算一算，寡人应当何时加冠，更为合适呢？”
嬴政一开口就扔了个重磅炸弹到徐福的头上。
徐福愣了一秒。
秦王嬴政加冠的时间，要他来测算？
要他来测算加冠时间！
不要怪徐福没见过世面。像他这样历史不通的人，都知道千古一帝秦始皇。这位皇帝在很多人看来都是崇高又神圣的。无数人都曾希望能梦回大秦，目睹始皇风采。而他，误打误撞来到这个时代，第一眼看到的人就是秦始皇，他将秦始皇忽悠住了，顺利做个官儿也就罢了。
现在秦始皇竟然要他去测算加冠礼。
秦始皇的加冠礼在历史上可是一个转折点啊，就是在这场加冠礼中，秦始皇斩杀了一批人，囚禁了他的母后，并且在此之后他还撂倒了吕不韦，将秦国大权尽揽于手，之后，中央集权制度便从他这里开始。
“怎么？很为难？”见徐福半天没有言语，嬴政换了个坐着的姿势。嬴政身材本就高大，加上他背脊笔直，气势更盛。徐福站在他的面前，简直就要被他的阴影完全笼罩在内。
徐福摇摇头，压下心中的激动，“不，不为难，这是我的荣幸。”
能够见证这样一段历史，那的确是令人激奋又荣幸的。
徐福感觉自己的职业生涯简直要走向巅峰了好吗？
“我需要仔细测算，这个时间要几时禀报给王上呢？”徐福迅速恢复了平静，问道。在嬴政眼中，他的模样就是始终无波无浪的。
嬴政都不得不称赞一句，徐福的态度相当不卑不亢，哪怕是接到这样好的差事，他也没有因此而过分喜悦。正如现在所推崇的“名仕清流”之风姿。
“寡人希望越快越好。”
徐福抬头与嬴政对视了一眼。
徐福的眼眸其实不算纯黑色，有些偏浅灰，但看上去格外的纯粹，嬴政望了一眼竟然些微失神。徐福的眼神清澈又坚毅。
嬴政忍不住又展开了一番心理活动。
徐福这样的人，大概就是出身名门，一身技艺，但却心思纯粹，性情孤傲的吧，这样的人做做卜筮观测事宜，不沾世间污浊，正好。
“不沾污浊”的徐福全然不知道嬴政将自己脑补成了什么模样，领了差事的他一拱手，就要请求告退回去翻阅典籍进行测算。
宫女突然进来了，她低眉顺目地跪在徐福旁边，低声道:“王上，胡姬求见。”
这个时期还不太讲究女子不见外男，所以就算徐福在侧也没有什么大碍。
嬴政点头放那位胡姬进来了。
徐福一听宫女的称呼，就猜应该是嬴政的后宫，也不知道秦始皇的老婆应该是长得如何貌美。他正猜想着呢，就见那头走来一体态袅娜的年轻女子，衣饰华美，腰间以丝带系扎，勒出细细的柳腰来，女子还披散着黑色长发，不添一点头饰，但却更显得风情万种，走起路来，发尾都跟着摇曳起来。
这般美人，可惜脸上妆容丑了点儿。
徐福瞥了一眼嬴政的脸色。他是不是应该识相一点，先走为妙呢？
偏偏嬴政始终不说让他离开的话。
胡姬送上点心汤水，开口声线妩媚，“王上近来少入后宫，妾心甚为思念。”
然后这位姿容艳丽的胡姬就当着一干人的面，朝秦王抛了个媚眼。
徐福顿时更觉得自己多余了。
嬴政连半分目光都没分给胡姬，他吩咐赵高将徐福送回去。
胡姬知道赵高是秦王身边近侍，如今听到秦王竟然这样吩咐，她顿时对徐福起了兴趣，于是转头来看。
徐福向来不畏惧别人打量的目光，若是畏惧的话，他恐怕根本没那个脸皮在天桥下摆算卦摊。
胡姬越瞧越惊讶。
她从入宫以来，连那位早先入宫的郑妃都未曾放在眼中。只因为她对自己的容貌有着绝对的自信。她长得柔媚，声音惑人，身段儿生得也好，尽管私底下有宫人偷偷将她比做舞姬，可那又如何？她生得貌美，总能得大王几分青睐。这是其他人拍马也赶不上的。
可胡姬从未想过，会有人比她生得还要出色。
而这个人竟然还是男子。
瞧着这眉目昳丽、气质出尘的模样，胡姬不免有些嫉妒，她没认出徐福身上的官服，只觉得那一身红袍将眼前这人衬得竟是将后宫中所有颜色都比下去了。
嫉妒心暗自作祟，胡姬笑吟吟地问：“妾正好奇王上近来为何不爱入后宫，现下便得知了。原来王上竟得了如此颜色，怪不得能拥有王上这般宠爱。”
徐福有点目瞪口呆？
姑娘你瞎说什么玩意儿呢？
作者有话要说：　　胡姬就是胡亥他娘，郑妃就是扶苏他娘。扶苏胡亥很快就会出生，然后被徐福各种忽悠祸害。

chapters.title: 第100章
chapters.source_text:
“刺杀是谁的主意？”
郑有安却吭哧了半天，才道：“也……是我。”
徐福只看他一眼就猜出事情大致的过程了。龙阳君也淡淡笑了，语气轻巧地说：“哦，看来是你不服气，没能杀死王翦将军和都尉，就提了这个建议。但是你却没想到，最后被派出的人，是你。”
龙阳君实在是猜人心思一把好手，郑有安的脸色顿时就变了。
见他如此模样，哪还有不明白的呢？
原来只是一个急于出头，却反把自己给坑了的人……当真是好愚蠢的一个穿越者！真不知他方才那一身藐视他人的优越感，从何而来。
“将阏与之中，诸将领的名单写下来。口述也可以。”李信对他出了什么主意，怎么出的主意，一点也不关心，“不……不行……”郑有安就是再蠢也知道，一旦供出名单，他就什么都完了。
“城中布防，也要交代出来。”李信却直接忽视了他的抗拒之言。
如今利刃握在他的手中，哪里容得郑有安来拒绝？
接下来的审问，徐福就觉得没意思了，便没再掺合，只是同桑中等人，坐在一旁休息去了。徐福这番闲适的模样，与那郑有安的处境相对比，更教那郑有安眼珠子都瞪红了。
李信又问了郑有安，可还派了其它刺客，郑有安答了声“没了”，李信这才将匕首从他身体里拔了出来，郑有安疼得直打哆嗦。
徐福站起身来，问李信：“可是问完了？”
李信点头。
“那我便与他说几句话。”
李信自然不会反驳，当即便带着人出去了。
桑中等人犹豫一阵，还是在徐福的目光驱使下，只守在了帐外，顿时帐内就只剩下了徐福和郑有安二人。
“你是穿越过来的？”徐福出声问。
郑有安疼得嘶气，他咬牙切齿地看着徐福，按捺不下胸中的熊熊怒火，怒骂道：“是！我是穿越过来的，但你凭什么能做了秦军都尉？而我却只能做个小卒子！我不服气！都是穿越者，难道你还得了什么老天的馈赠吗？”
徐福漫不经心地道：“为什么啊……大概是，若这个世界为一本书，那不过恰好我是主角，你是配角罢了。”
“我是配角？不！不可能！我到了这个世界以后，潜心学习，诗书骑射无一不精！”
徐福暗道，骑射是挺厉害，诗书就算了吧……就你那张口闭口骂人的姿势，诗书都难以驯化你，可见你学习时也不过敷衍了事。
“凭什么你恰好就能落在秦国，而我却在他国……”
“你不服气，你自可以到秦国去便是。”
郑有安也不知是不是受了太大的刺激，双眼猩红地瞪着徐福，笑道：“我疯了才会去秦国！既然不在秦国，那便是我的机会，我身为穿越者，掌军事政治之能，有什么是我不会的？我要帮着赵国打秦国，我要让统一六国的那个人变成我！变成我！”
徐福顿了顿，“……你小说看多了吧？”
郑有安恨恨地咬着牙，怒瞪着他，根本没注意徐福说了什么。
在未与王翦大军对上之前，他顺风顺水，日日脑子里都是对未来的美好畅想，哪怕后来听闻秦军攻打阏与，他也并无惊慌，他知道，他扬名立万的时候来了。听闻带兵的是王翦。哈……王翦……
秦王十一年，王翦已经老了吧，一个老头子，哪有史书上传得那样神奇！而他正值壮年，又身负大才，只需稍想几个计策，就能拿下王翦了！难道现代人还斗不过古代人吗？想一想终点的那些历史小说，个个主角都能成为霸主，他自然也能！那些小说里的手段，他可是记得很清楚呢……
郑有安却不想一想，王翦老虽老了，但经验摆在那里，旁人如何能与他相比？他的智慧都是从战场上拼杀得来的，比郑有安从小说之中汲取而来的知识不知道高了多少。郑有安太拿自己当一回事了。真当穿越者便高人一等了，却也不瞧瞧他那坐井观天、目中无人的姿态，谁也不会高看他一分！
“你是怎么穿越来的？”徐福又问。
能遇见一个穿越者可是难得的机会，徐福难免要问一问这穿越的契机，弄清楚这究竟是怎么一回事，而且这里会出现一个郑有安，其它地方会不会又出现另外的穿越者呢？他成为了煽动翅膀影响战国历史的那只蝴蝶，那他会不会带来更多的蝴蝶呢？历史的进程会不会遭到破坏？最重要的是，嬴政的大业会被阻挡破坏吗？
郑有安虽然狂妄自大，在王翦、李信、龙阳君面前便显得拙劣了太多。但是虱子多了也会痒，若是多几个郑有安这样梦想建功立业推翻嬴政的穿越者，那也终归是麻烦，而且难保其中不会有比郑有安更聪明的。
郑有安冷笑道：“自然是死了再过来的。”
“你以前是做什么的？”
郑有安却咬紧了牙没有要答话的意思。
见他半天都不说话，徐福顿时悟了，“不便开口？白领上班族？”
郑有安反问徐福：“你又是做什么的？”
“算命的。”徐福淡淡道。
郑有安毫不客气地讥笑道：“算命的？一个搞歪门邪道，四处被城管驱逐的人？”
徐福却不急不怒，只甩了一句话回去，“是啊，一个算命的，成了秦国的护军都尉，而你……”徐福的目光将他上下打量一番，“却是个阶下囚。是个令人鄙夷的刺客。”
不过短短一段话，就让郑有安再度跳脚，他剧烈地挣扎起来，刑架被他带得抖动不已，他破口大骂，骂的全是上辈子那些粗鄙不看的话语。
什么“操你妈”“死全家”“狗杂种”……
徐福微微皱眉。
郑有安的粗鄙简直超乎了他的想象，不用再问，徐福也已经能猜出他上辈子是做什么的了。受教育水平不高，家境绝对算不得富裕。多少人家都是家贫人却不贫，而这个郑有安，放在上辈子估计也就是过得不好怨社会那一类。
徐福从不觉得自己算命有何不对，他靠手艺吃饭，不偷不抢，还真轮不到郑有安来瞧不起他。
就在郑有安破口大骂这段时间里，桑中已经忍不住掀起帷帐，大步走了进来，李信握着匕首紧随其后。
“好大的胆子！竟敢辱骂都尉！”桑中怒喝一声，面上冰寒。
李信慢腾腾地走上前，看着郑有安的目光就如同看一个死人。
“都尉可问完了？”李信出声问道。
“问完了。”徐福不着痕迹地皱了皱眉，跟这样没有素质的人说话，实在太过恶心，左右也问不出什么有效的东西来了，那就算了吧。
李信朝徐福点了点头，“都尉那日伤的何处？”
徐福一怔，“脖颈。”
“只有脖颈吗？”
“只有脖颈。”
李信二话不说，走得近了，将郑有安那哆哆嗦嗦的模样收入眼中，心生厌恶，当即抽出匕首来，手上动作迅疾，等郑有安回过神来时，匕首已经擦过了他的脖颈。
郑有安疼得又惨叫了一声，身子抖得更加剧烈，“你干什么？你放开我！别杀我！你还有什么想问的？我都说！我都说！”
龙阳君慢条斯理道：“之前看着，我还当是个多么聪明的人物，如今看来，不仅蠢笨，还连半点骨气也无。”
郑有安听见这话气得脸色涨红，但他却不敢乱动，更不敢再骂，他感受着脖颈被开了一道口子，鲜血往外流的感觉，冷……疼……还有死亡的恐惧。
徐福听罢，倒是暗道一声，龙阳君果真不是好惹的，在军中虽然轮不到他来对刺客动手，但是将郑有安气个半死倒是没问题的。
“昨晚哪只手握的匕首，来谋害都尉？”
徐福扫了一眼郑有安，道：“昨日天黑，也没瞧个清楚。”
“那便当右手吧。”李信的话音刚落，他手中的匕首就已经在郑有安的手腕上划拉出一条口子来了，郑有安吓得惨叫连连。这人是要割了他的腕吗？
鲜血涌出来，刺激着郑有安的要求，他大喊大叫：“放了我！放了我！我和你们都尉是一个地方的人，看在这个份儿上，放了我吧……”
桑中倒是气笑了，对郑有安的厚脸皮和没骨气厌恶不已，骂道：“你算什么东西？我们都尉出自鬼谷！你竟敢大言不惭说与都尉是一个地方的人！”
“鬼……鬼谷……”那人呆了呆，突然间眼底的目光变得疯狂起来，“凭什么，凭什么他却能是鬼谷弟子……凭什么！浑身上下不过皮相比我好了些……”
“实在聒噪了些。”李信冷冷地出声，随之将匕首贴在了郑有安的脸上，“再大喊大叫，我就剁了你的嘴。”
李信身上的气势太过凶煞，郑有安僵在了那里，再不敢动。
“都尉请吧，此处脏污不堪，恐玷污了都尉的衣袍。”李信收起匕首，回转身来道。
徐福也不愿再留下去，原本遇见穿越者的心情顿时就淡了，一个这样的穿越者，也不值得被他称为同类。徐福当先走了出去，桑中紧随其后。倒是蒹葭忍不住问李信：“那这人怎么办？”
“挂在这里，放血。”李信将最后二字说得极为平淡，就好像是说炖肉一样平常简单。
他身后的郑有安却听了个一清二楚，忍不住疯狂大叫起来。放血？是要把他的血一点点放干吗？太可怕了！魔鬼！古时的人就是蛮人！那个穿越者更可恶，竟然不救他……冷血！不配为人！对，那个人实在可恶，他怎么配做鬼谷弟子呢？为什么不是自己呢？郑有安的目光越发疯狂起来，但他就算再嘶叫，却也只能被那帷帐隔绝在其后。
而帐子外把守着士兵，他逃不出去，赵军也不会派人来救他的性命。
一时逞英雄，还就真当自己是英雄了，太高看自己，郑有安合该落得这个下场。
蒹葭出了帐子后，快步跟上了徐福，他好奇地问：“先生，之前那人口中骂的同性恋，小白脸是什么意思？”
徐福扫了一圈身后的人，见他们都盯着自己，虽然面上不显，但眼底却都透着几分好奇。
“同性恋啊……”徐福的目光落在了龙阳君的身上，“假如蒹葭倾慕龙阳君那就是同性恋了。”
蒹葭打了个哆嗦，“先生，我……我怎么会倾慕于他……”蒹葭抬头去看龙阳君，却见龙阳君似笑非笑地看着他，蒹葭更觉可怕，忙收回了目光，默默离他两步远。
一旁的桑中脸色也有些怪异。
徐福见状，心道，可不要怪我为你们打开了新世界的大门啊。
“小白脸么，就是指，靠着女人吃软饭的英俊男人。”
“夸我英俊，倒也不错。”龙阳君缓缓道。
蒹葭：“……桑中啊，我有点恶心。”
龙阳君淡淡一笑，也不说话。
蒹葭心中微微有些得意，看来在外也是很好的，若是在府中他这样说，龙阳君必定会马上道，“有喜的不该是我么？怎么夫君也害喜恶心了？”蒹葭还能想象得出当时龙阳君脸上会是什么表情。
审问完郑有安，时辰也不早了，军中分发食物，李信几人便为徐福取去了，徐福倒是能得个闲暇，就这样坐在帐子里等着便行了。
等到傍晚时，秦军又与赵军交战一次，赵军已初具疲态，王翦知道，最佳的时机已经到来。
那边秦军回营，这边有人前来徐福的帐中，道：“都尉，那刺客死了。”
死了？
徐福愣了愣，一时间心中还稍微有些复杂，同为穿越者，他当初遭遇的危险更大，却是硬生生在秦始皇的眼皮子底下活了下来，还越发混得风生水起，而这人却偏偏能把自己一手好棋玩成死棋，还真是愚蠢至极，落得这个下场，也不冤。
“都尉可要过去瞧一瞧？”那人问道。那人想着这刺客胆敢刺杀都尉，都尉应当是想去瞧一瞧他的惨状的。
“去吧。”徐福也不犹豫，当即就起了身。
桑中等人自然也是随他过去。
等徐福进了帐子时，才发现归营的李信也在里头站着了。
徐福站得远远的，只瞥了一眼郑有安，随后便转过了头，看着尸体，可一点也不美妙。
而李信身旁的士兵，手中托着一物，李信见徐福进来，便带着士兵走到徐福跟前来，道：“都尉，刺客身上掉下一物。现呈给都尉。”
什么东西？
徐福朝那士兵手上看去。
他的呼吸一顿。
小巧，精致，巴掌可托，青铜铸就，花纹古朴。
那是个鼎！
但这只鼎怎么这样小？徐福从士兵手中抓起那只鼎，来回打量，没错，模样与宫中那两只鼎都是一样的，但是大小实在差了些啊……这里人多，徐福也不便太过打量，于是便将那鼎收了起来，道：“我对此物颇有兴趣，收回帐中把玩一番，可行？”
士兵们哪敢说不行？他们都看向了李信。
而徐福的目光也紧紧盯着李信。
李信沉声道：“自然是行的。”
徐福“嗯”了一声，也不再回头，吩咐人将尸首处置了，然后就出了帐子。其实就算他不吩咐，这些事李信也一定会安排妥帖的，只是他一句话也不说的话，未免显得他就是冲这鼎来的。
出了帐子，徐福自己走着走着又觉得有些好笑。死了身上掉个鼎下来，难道还和打怪一样，打死就爆装备吗？
回到自己的帐中，徐福也不再遮掩，直接拿出了那小鼎，放置在桌案上，桑中等人只是安静守在一旁。过了会儿，帷帐动了动，李信站在帐子口，问道：“都尉，李信可否能进来？”
徐福头也不抬地冲他招了招手。
李信进来后，见徐福在瞧那只鼎，倒也不打扰他，也跟着桑中他们一起守在一旁。
此时外面天色渐黑，帐子里点着蜡烛，烛光难免有些昏暗，徐福抬手摩挲着鼎身上的花纹，又借着烛光看了看。他心中原本已有猜测，如今只需印证猜测，自然省事不少，不像从前那样，摸着花纹，还要天马行空地去想，可能会是什么玩意儿。
蒹葭毕竟年纪小一些，忍耐不了这样的静寂，忍不住问道：“先生，你在摸什么？”
“摸上面的花纹。”说着徐福转动手中的小鼎，将它有花纹的地方面对蒹葭，“你看，这是不是火焰的纹路？”
龙阳君显然更为识货，他眯眼瞧了一眼，道：“这是火纹？”
徐福点头。
龙阳君倒不觉得稀奇，“十二章纹，乃周天子令用于祭祀礼服之上的花纹。十二章纹，也是分辨周朝大臣官职高低的凭据。刻在鼎身上，倒是稀奇。”最后一句话他说得一点也不诚心。
周王室衰微，诸侯国虎视眈眈，都想称霸，甚至隐隐要展示一番，自己势大到盖过了周王室，于是周朝上下才用的十二章纹，在诸侯国想来也是屡见不鲜的。诸侯国不见得有多么喜欢这十二章纹，但却一定要用一用，好表示，你周天子用得起，我们也是用得起的！
龙阳君跟在魏王身边，怎么会没见过呢？
徐福差不多已经断定了，日月星辰、锦雉华虫、火焰之纹，都是十二章纹中的纹路。
十二章纹始于周，年代相隔不久，说明这鼎铸来也不久，连个古董都算不上，能是什么了不得的物事？说不定真的就只能被自己拿来炼炼丹药罢了。
徐福随手搁下那鼎，帐中烛光昏暗，鼎中似乎隐隐有光华流转，徐福瞥了一眼，却又什么都没看见。或许只是视觉上的差错罢了……徐福收起目光。
龙阳君道：“看来先生对鼎相当喜爱啊。”
之前那只鼎也是龙阳君为他寻来的，龙阳君会注意到他的不同寻常，并不奇怪。
“我喜好炼丹药，不爱用寻常的鼎，偏爱用这样奇特精巧的鼎。”
龙阳君指着桌案上的鼎道：“不过这个可是小了些……”
“不小了。”拿来捣药也好，反正找了这么个玩意儿回去，总得让它体现一下价值，不然显得自己去找他，多傻帽啊。
众人对鼎的好奇心消退，不多时便到了用晚饭的时候，他们便正好一起简单用了饭。
蒹葭与龙阳君出帐子去了，或许是要四处逛一逛。
唯有桑中和李信还留在帐中，桑中是不敢轻易离了徐福的身，担心再来一次刺杀，如今徐福位高，难保赵军不会再次盯上没有功夫的他。
但是李信还留在这里做什么？
桑中不由得道：“将军不走吗？”
李信看向徐福，镇静道：“我有话同都尉讲。”
桑中皱了皱眉，不知这二人如何会关系这样深，但他实在没有置噱的资格，便自动退了出去。帷帐动了动，帐子里便只剩下了他们二人。
徐福还能听见外面刮风的声音，和士兵粗犷的声音。
“都尉看我如今的面相，是如何模样？”李信开门见山地问道。
徐福心道，你面相如何，还真不关我的事啊，该叫侯生来为你算才是，而且徐福也不喜欢多次为谁瞧面相，瞧一次便够了，瞧那么多你想做什么？真当知晓了自己的命格，就一定能把握住未来吗？
于是徐福冷酷地拒绝了他，“将军何必再求面相的结果？如今将军在军中畅通，未来大有可待，何必再问我？”
李信稍微有些失望，不过他倒也没再追问。
这令徐福欣赏地瞧了他一眼。
及时收住，能进能退，那才是有本事的人。
李信似乎还有话要对徐福说，但是一对上徐福的目光，他又咬着牙，憋住了，最后什么话都没再说，就急急地出去了。
男人心，海底针。
徐福不知道李信在想什么，他也没兴趣去知道他在想什么。
之后王翦亲来见徐福，问他明日可还随军，徐福这才知道，原来王翦已经制定好明日的攻城计划了。阏与，秦国势在必得。郑有安反叛得太快，要摘下阏与，无疑是又多了分保障。
徐福也想瞧一瞧，打胜仗是如何模样的，他叫来桑中询问，上战场可否会给他们造成负累。
桑中、蒹葭皆是斩钉截铁道，会护住徐福的，徐福思忖一番，这才答应了王翦。王翦转头看了一眼龙阳君，心道这是个沉得住气的，与徐都尉的其他随从大不一样。随后王翦便笑眯眯地出去了。
等走出了老远，王翦才突然顿住了脚步，脸上的笑容霎地消失了个一干二净。
他身旁的小兵见他脸色变化如此之快，还当是哪里惹怒了王翦，忙低声道：“将军？”
王翦却根本没应他的声音，或者说王翦已经顾不上应他了，他满脑子都是方才帐中那人的脸……若他没有记错……那张脸，他曾经是见过的，魏王带在身边，跟宝贝一般护着，使有一手好剑法，掌握魏国一半权势，令数人痛骂其奸佞的……龙阳君！
“将军？”小兵讷讷地又叫了一声。
“走吧。”王翦脸色恢复如常，大步离去。
龙阳君在都尉身边，王上可知晓？昔日魏国的龙阳君，如何会抛下那些权势，来秦国甘愿做个隐姓埋名的小卒子？王翦自是不知，那全都是徐福拐回来的啊！
若是那信陵君长得也似龙阳君这样年轻貌美，说不定徐福也把人给一块儿拐了呢。
第二日清晨，天色还是漆黑的，徐福便被桑中从睡梦中唤醒了，他草草地洗漱一番，用了早饭，然后便等着同王翦一块儿出发了。今日秦军精神抖擞，尤其是见了徐福后，精神面貌更好了。徐福有些不解，暗自嘀咕，难道他还是精神良药吗？他却不知，秦国将士，只是不愿在他面前吧表现差了，被都尉记上一笔罢了。
若是能得都尉的青睐，他们说不得便要高升了呢。
想一想秦王下的命令，依战功封赏，谁人能不激动？
他们很快来到了阏与城下，分兵先行突袭，随后叫阵。徐福安安稳稳地待在自己的战车上，看着将士们拼杀在一起。
这一日依旧是顶着烈日的，还有夏日的热风吹拂在身上，赵军依旧派出了那些脱去盔甲，身形轻巧的士兵，但秦军也不是毫无准备，挡在前面的皆是秦军精锐，那些人再轻巧，却也抵不过秦军同样的动作敏捷以及手中的利刃。赵军的生命很快被收割走，秃鹫在空中盘旋，掠夺走这些人的尸体血肉。
阏与城破……
那是两个时辰后的事了，秦军大股地涌入城中，城中剩余的赵军和百姓，只得投降。
徐福却是心念一动，将桑中叫过来，“去替我请李信过来。”
桑中指着一方道：“李信将军还在善后。”
善后便是指将城外剩下的将士宰个干净。
这种血腥残忍的做法，徐福不加评判。战争本就如此，没有残忍不残忍的道理。
李信提着刀戟，一身血色，仿佛地狱而归的修罗，披着一身日光，先进了城，城中百姓见了他，瑟瑟不已。
徐福顿了顿，“我们也一同进去吧。”
“好。”桑中护着徐福往里去，很快便与王翦等人会和。
徐福叫住了李信，“可否劳烦李将军一件事？”
李信翻身下马，走在徐福身侧，道：“何事？”军中旁的人忍不住打量李信与徐福，心道，李信这动作真够快的，不知何时便与都尉攀上了。可惜了，那日都尉遇刺，他们都慢了一步。
“李将军跑一趟那郑有安的府邸，为我留下郑有安从小到大的物事可好？”他不知秦军入城可否会烧了阏与城中的一些府邸，以前瞧一些电视剧里就会如此，为了以防意外，他还是拜托李信一番比较好。至于为什么要将那些东西拿到手，穿越者的东西，流露出去，可不一定是好事。还是握在手中，他更为放心。
李信也不多问，连对徐福为何要如此做，丝毫的好奇也无。他应了声，带着人便转头走了，显然是朝着郑有安的住处去了。
占领阏与之后，秦军并未庆功，连半分松弛也无，不仅如此，王翦还让军中年俸禄不满百石的小官回家，十人中挑选二人留下，可谓皆是精锐。被赶回家的小官，自然心中有些不满，但王翦积威已久，他们如何敢说什么？
徐福听桑中说起此事，也未放在心上，王翦身为秦国老将，更通军事，旁人不能领会他的意思，但并不代表王翦的决定就是错的。
秦军未做停顿，很快便又启程朝橑杨而去。
消息传回秦国，王翦之举，有人推崇，自然也有人斥责。嬴政一律不管，他用人便不会疑心，王翦的本事他是知晓的，他没什么好怀疑的。相比之下，秦国的征途顺利，他反倒更担心徐福的安危。那军队之中也实在是些蠢笨人，送来的快报之中，什么都讲到了，偏偏不提及徐福半句，这如何让嬴政不抓心挠肺地难受？
吃得可好，睡得可好，可有受伤……无数的担忧都挤在嬴政的脑子里，不过嬴政将这些情绪都压了下去，照常处理政务，照常将扶苏叫到跟前来提点，只是如今，因为徐福的缘故，他对胡亥倒也不如过去那样恶劣了，隐隐有些一视同仁的味道。宫人们知道嬴政并非不重视胡亥公子，自然就上心不少。
只是胡亥久不见徐福，难免趴在地上，天天嘴里喊着“啊糊”。
嬴政越听越觉得心头不安。
他倒是也希望自己能像徐福那样，做个梦便能预测未来的祸福，只可惜没有什么入梦来，倒是连从前的春梦也不做了。
此时朝堂上下都知晓，徐福去了战场以后，便救了王翦一次，众臣也只得叹息，这位果真是个有本事的啊！能救王翦，以后还不知道会获利多少呢……
远在赵国国境内，徐福又收拾包袱，跟着王翦大军往橑杨去了。
若是嬴政知晓，肯定气得掀了桌案。
行军途中，众人骑马，唯徐福乘马车，不过军中对他多有敬畏，自然也不会说什么。马车之内，蒹葭摩拳擦掌。阏与之战，激起了他的兴奋，他一腔热腾腾的血，正期待着好好挥洒一番呢。阏与打得不过瘾，正好又去橑杨。
桑中见蒹葭那样雀跃，只能暗自叹气，看来保护先生，还是自己更为靠谱啊。
秦军行军极快，徐福为了不拖后腿，中途也不叫苦叫累，就算难受他也憋着，他分得清轻重，他不会让秦军来迁就自己。王翦见他虽为都尉，但并不仗着自身身份而有蛮横的要求，心中印象登时又好了许多。时经十来天，他们抵达了橑杨。
抵达之后，先是寻地驻扎，勘察地形，休整一番，吃个饱饭睡个好觉。不然一身疲惫，如何能打胜仗。
徐福不知那赵国已然撕破了面皮，当日驻扎下来以后，橑杨城中收到消息，当夜便有几波刺客前来，幸而帐中有桑中守候，到了后半夜，连李信都过来守着了，前来的刺客，皆被抓住了，有的则是当场格杀了。
只不过这些刺客的嘴就比郑有安硬多了，什么也没能撬出来便死了。王翦也不在意，要攻下橑杨，并非靠着从刺客嘴里打探消息，他自有一番本事。
刺客三天两头地前来，徐福渐渐地倒也习惯了，而此时王翦已经制定好战术，准备好先带秦军出去遛一遛，探一探橑杨城中的底。
此时消息传来，桓齮攻下邺城，无疑更助长了秦军的气势。
桓齮接令立刻转去攻打栎阳，此时能不能打下橑杨，便成了关键所在。
军营之中气氛陡然紧张起来，只有徐福还维持着那副悠闲的姿态，在帐中鲜少出来，只是入了夜，偶尔观个星，若有路过士兵见了，必然小心翼翼，不敢打扰徐福半分，似乎只要妨碍了徐福，这一场仗也会出点岔子一般。
其实徐福哪里是在看这场仗能不能赢，他是盯着天空在走神。
……好像日子久了些，就忍不住去想，嬴政在宫中如何了。
徐福微微皱起了眉，这可不是个好兆头啊。
就在此时，徐福发觉身后传来了细微的声音，像是踩过枯树枝和枯草面一样，桑中比他更为敏锐，当即就回头去看，还叫来士兵搜寻了一番。
不过什么也没能搜到，连个脚印也没有。
出于谨慎，李信还亲自带人巡视了一番，最后并无所得。
桑中不好意思地道：“或许是我听错了。”
徐福本想说，不是你听错了，因为我也听见了，但是现在确实什么踪迹也未发现，再劳动李信等人实在不太好。他身边守有桑中、蒹葭，应当是不会有事的，这几日的刺客还少了吗？
李信亲自将徐福送回了帐中，天空之中，星宿光芒大放，明日是个晴天。
当夜徐福依旧睡得很安稳，连半点惊扰也无，或许他睡熟以后，军营中又来了刺客，不过他是半点响动也没听到的，左右自有人为他解决。他洗漱过后，慢吞吞地出了帐子。此时晨光熹微，正好呼吸一番新鲜空气，望一望远方。这样的日子虽然枯燥了些，不过比起在王宫中，倒是更为规律了，早睡早起，没有半点耽搁，他的肤色也越发的莹白如玉了。
王翦带着众将领还在调整战术，士兵们一刻也不懈怠地在操练。
徐福站在帐外，却见蒹葭疾步走过来，眉头紧皱，“先生……”他的语气有些嗫喏，似乎在犹豫该不该告诉徐福。
“出了何事？”
蒹葭咬咬唇，道：“……龙阳君不见了。”
“不见了？”徐福一怔，“谁能掳走他？”
是啊，龙阳君使得一手好剑法，智商奇高，何况与他一同的蒹葭功夫也不低，龙阳君怎么样都不可能会被掳走啊！
自己这个手无缚鸡之力的都没被掳走呢。
“先生？”蒹葭的声音微微焦灼。
“此时不便前去打扰李信，你先与桑中去四处搜寻一番……”说到这里，徐福顿住，忙挥手将一旁巡视的士兵叫来，“你们同蒹葭一起，寻找我身边另外一名随从。”
士兵们心中稍有不满。
一个随从，哪里值得大动干戈去寻找他？若这随从失踪了，那这随从也实在该死！竟然抛下主人离去。
徐福哪能不知晓他们心中所想，只淡淡道：“橑杨城中紧紧盯着我们，若是我这随从失踪了，还不知是不是赵军的手笔，若是让赵军得逞，我们实在面上无光。”
军中士兵心中的不满，来得快去得也快，听徐福如此说，心中愤怒顿时被激起，道：“都尉说得不错，确实不能让那赵军得意！你们随我过来！”这些士兵二话不说，便同蒹葭一起去寻人了。
桑中却固执地不肯离去，他口中道：“若是连龙阳君都真的失踪了，那难保先生不会出事，我还是守在先生身边更为稳妥。”
徐福拗不过他，桑中本也是为了他好，何况转念一想，那么些人跟着蒹葭应当也足够了，遂便放弃了。
待到那厢王翦与众将领商量完毕之后，也听说了徐福身边有一随从失踪的消息，王翦对于徐福的事还是很放在心上的，正好此时也有空暇，便亲自过去了。
“都尉身边何人失踪了？”王翦话音刚落，那头蒹葭便又带着人回来了，虽然他一脸冷色，但徐福还是能从他的眼中窥见几分失望之色。
没找到人？
王翦扫了一眼蒹葭，又扫了一眼徐福身边的桑中，哪能还不知是谁失踪了？他心中陡然一沉。
竟然是龙阳君失踪了吗？
这可是个麻烦啊！王翦眉头紧皱，但是碍于人前，又不好直接询问徐福，只能出声道：“不如到帐中，我与都尉详谈一二？”
见王翦的神色有些怪异，徐福心中疑惑，也就顺水应下。
桑中掀起帷帐，徐福与王翦并肩进去，其余人则是被留在了外面，倒是蒹葭因为知晓龙阳君失踪的过程，也被叫了进去。
如今帐中再无他人，王翦也不再隐藏了，便直截了当地问道：“敢问都尉，身边那随从，可是龙阳君？”说完，他不待徐福说话，又补充道：“我曾见过龙阳君一面，容貌出色，实难忘记，近日再见，我心中惊讶无比。”
王翦这眼睛真利！
他还是第一个在见过后便确认龙阳君身份的，要知道多少人哪怕看出来了，也不一定敢确认，毕竟谁会想到，魏王身边的龙阳君，真的会出现在秦国呢？
既然王翦都认出来了，再遮遮掩掩也没有意思，徐福便点了下头。
“真是龙阳君？”王翦的脸色变得严肃起来，甚至连眉头也皱了起来，像是手中握了个烫手山芋般。
“将军可是担忧龙阳君通敌？”徐福语气淡淡，好像他口中说出的话，并非什么惊人之语。
而蒹葭在一旁闻言，已经忍不住道：“龙阳君不会如此做的！”
王翦也不与蒹葭争论，只是定定地看着徐福，如今人是他带来的，有何后果，得徐福来承担。任谁都不会想平白趟这滩浑水。何况王翦以秦国大业为重，若龙阳君当真有异，他定然不会手软。
个中种种，徐福都能理解。
不过现在不见龙阳君，谁也不能就此下定论，“先寻人再说吧，少不得要麻烦军中将士了。”
“这倒无事。”王翦顿了顿，还是问出了最关键的问题，“若是龙阳君有通敌之意。”
蒹葭不自觉地绷紧了脸上的肌肉。
徐福低下头，漫不经心地道：“那便拿下龙阳君。”
王翦笑了笑，站起身来，“那我这便再派些人手去寻人，还请都尉的随从随我过去。”
徐福抬头看向蒹葭，“去吧。”
蒹葭有些紧张，但他面上极沉得住气，一声不吭地就跟着王翦出去了。
王翦派了人继续寻龙阳君的下落。
如此折腾了两天，却是毫无消息，王翦再来见徐福时，脸色已经微微阴沉了。帐中只有他们二人，王翦开口便道：“我不得不怀疑龙阳君有异，若是发现，恐怕手底下人不仔细，伤了他，甚至……杀了他。”
徐福还是漫不经心的样子，点了点头。
王翦见徐福如此合作，这才松了口气，又与徐福闲话几句，笑问他对明日之仗，可有何批语箴言，徐福还是漫不经心地道：“并无。”
王翦也不失望，脸色温和地出去了。
帐外蒹葭脸色也已经十分阴沉了。龙阳君突然不知去向，他要负最大的责任，若真是龙阳君心中有异，存了心地要破坏秦国攻打他国，那他自然不会为龙阳君多说一句话。但就是想着想着，便觉得心里难受。
蒹葭也不知道自己在外头站了有多久。
天色渐渐地晚了，一阵热风吹来，蒹葭动了动腿，呼出一口气，有些酸麻了。他转身却不见桑中的人影，想必是为先生取饭菜了吧。蒹葭撩起帷帐，走进去，声音沙哑地叫了一声，“先生。”
帐子里寂寥无语。
蒹葭不自觉地打了个寒颤，他定下神来，仔细打量帐子里的模样，没有半个人影，只有影影绰绰的烛光，将帐子照亮，他的影子被拉得长长的，随着烛光晃动，平白让人觉得心慌。
蒹葭疾步走出去，拉住一旁的士兵问：“方才可见都尉出来了？”
士兵茫然摇头，“没……见呀……”
蒹葭心一紧，推了那士兵一把，“快！快去找桑中！”“你去请李信将军前来！”
桑中正巧手里端着食物过来了，见蒹葭一副火急火燎的模样，不由得问道：“怎么了？”
蒹葭见了桑中，顿时脸色垮了下来，暴露出了内心的恍然无措，“桑中……”他的声音微微发着抖，“我找不见先生了。”
桑中脸色一变，“你胡说什么？我方才走时，先生不是在帐中休息吗？”说着他便将手中的食物交托给蒹葭，快步走过去一掀帷帐，但见里头空无一人，只余烛光。
桑中心下一凉，好像心脏瞬间被人掏空了一样。
他的嘴唇动了动，最后转过身来，一咬牙，恨声道：“都尉失踪！”这一声惊了不少人，还包括被士兵请来的李信，李信脸色骤变，上前来揪住桑中的衣领，“你说什么？都尉失踪？”
桑中也顾不上与李信计较他粗鲁的举动，沉着脸应了声“是”。
李信当即派人四处搜寻，同时命人去告知王翦。
先是身边随从，紧接着却轮到了徐福本人失踪，那随从失踪他们可以不放在心上，但是堂堂护军都尉失了踪，那可就是要命的大事了！
王翦接到消息后，脸色也是瞬间就变了，他沉声道：“这种手段并不少见，如今赵军是打不赢了，就使这些法子了，前几日那些个刺客恐怕都是只是做个掩护，要绑走徐都尉才是真的。”
蒹葭忙问：“那如何是好？”
“一面派人去寻。”
“可若是寻不到呢？”
“寻不到就只有等了。”
“等什么？”
王翦目光一冷，“等着赵军将徐都尉带出来，威胁秦军不得进攻。”
蒹葭气得脸色涨红，脖颈上青筋迸出，俊秀的一张脸，顿时变得杀气腾腾。王翦将话说到这一步，哪里还有不明白的？到时候他们见到的说不定就是被赵军挟持在手的徐福了。那个时候两军对峙，若是救不下来怎么办？
而此时王翦又说了一句话，“若是到了那时，我们无力救下徐都尉……”
桑中和蒹葭几乎是同时屏住了呼吸，牢牢地盯着王翦。
王翦低声说出了后半句，“那便只有放弃了。”
蒹葭心头的火气登时就蹿了上来，他上前一步，桑中见势不好，马上拉住了他。
“将军怎么能如此？！难道那时就不管徐都尉了吗？”蒹葭气得吼道。
王翦岂会惧了这样一个毛头小子？王翦知晓对方是护主心切，倒也不与他计较，只是冷声反问：“若不能救，还能如何？难道这仗就不打了吗？秦军就因为一个人，收拾收拾包袱回家了吗？到时候我们如何向王上交代？”
蒹葭被堵得说不出话来。
桑中沉默不语，面色漠然。
李信站在旁边也是动也不动。
气氛凝滞。
王翦也不再与他们闲话，转身便又商讨战术去了，那一块地方很快就空了，夏日的热风吹拂而来，直叫人越发心烦意乱。
chapters.translated_text:
"Whose idea was the assassination?"

Zheng You'an stammered for a long time before saying, "It... it was also me."

Xu Fu only had to look at him once to guess the general course of events. Lord Longyang also smiled faintly, his tone light as he said, "Oh, it seems you were unconvinced, and since you couldn't kill General Wang Jian and the Commandant, you proposed this suggestion. But you didn't expect that the person sent out in the end would be you."

Lord Longyang was truly an expert at guessing people's thoughts; Zheng You'an's expression changed instantly.

Seeing him like this, how could one not understand?

He was just someone eager to stand out, only to end up digging his own grave... truly a foolish transmigrator! I really don't know where that sense of superiority he had just now, looking down on others, came from.

"Write down the list of generals in Eyu. Or you can dictate it." Li Xin didn't care at all about what ideas he had come up with or how he had come up with them. "No... no way..." No matter how stupid Zheng You'an was, he knew that once he gave up the list, he would be finished.

"The city's defense layout must also be confessed." Li Xin ignored his resistance entirely.

Now that the sharp blade was in his hand, how could he allow Zheng You'an to refuse?

As for the subsequent interrogation, Xu Fu felt it was boring, so he didn't get involved anymore and just went to sit aside and rest with Sang Zhong and the others. Xu Fu's leisurely appearance, in contrast to Zheng You'an's predicament, made Zheng You'an's eyes turn red with rage.

Li Xin asked Zheng You'an again if he had sent any other assassins. Zheng You'an replied, "No more." Only then did Li Xin pull the dagger out of his body, and Zheng You'an shivered in pain.

Xu Fu stood up and asked Li Xin, "Are you finished asking?"

Li Xin nodded.

"Then I will have a few words with him."

Li Xin naturally wouldn't object and immediately took his men outside.

Sang Zhong and the others hesitated for a moment, but under Xu Fu's gaze, they stayed outside the tent. Suddenly, only Xu Fu and Zheng You'an were left inside.

"Are you a transmigrator?" Xu Fu asked.

Zheng You'an gasped in pain. He looked at Xu Fu through gritted teeth, unable to suppress the raging fire in his chest, and cursed, "Yes! I am a transmigrator, but why are you able to be a Qin Commandant while I can only be a small pawn! I'm not convinced! We are both transmigrators; did you get some gift from heaven?"

Xu Fu said nonchalantly, "Why... perhaps it's just that if this world were a book, I happen to be the protagonist, and you are just a supporting character."

"I'm a supporting character? No! Impossible! After I arrived in this world, I devoted myself to learning; I am proficient in poetry, books, archery, and horsemanship!"

Xu Fu thought to himself, the archery and horsemanship might be impressive, but let's forget about the poetry and books... with your habit of cursing every other word, even poetry couldn't tame you, which shows you were just going through the motions when you studied.

"Why is it that you happen to land in the Qin State, while I am in another country..."

"If you're not convinced, you can go to the Qin State yourself."

Whether Zheng You'an was too stimulated or not, he stared at Xu Fu with bloodshot eyes and laughed, "I'd have to be crazy to go to Qin! Since I'm not in Qin, that's my opportunity. As a transmigrator with military and political talent, what is there that I can't do? I want to help Zhao fight Qin; I want to be the one who unifies the six states! It will be me!"

Xu Fu paused, "...You've read too many novels, haven't you?"

Zheng You'an gritted his teeth bitterly and glared at him, not paying any attention to what Xu Fu said.

Before he faced Wang Jian's army, everything had gone smoothly for him. Every day his mind was filled with beautiful fantasies about the future. Even when he heard that the Qin army was attacking Eyu, he wasn't panicked; he knew his time to make a name for himself had come. He heard the one leading the troops was Wang Jian. Ha... Wang Jian...

In the eleventh year of the King of Qin, Wang Jian must be old by now. An old man, how could he be as miraculous as the history books say! And he himself was in his prime, possessing great talent; he only needed to think of a few strategies to take down Wang Jian! Could a modern person really not beat an ancient person? Think of all those historical novels at the end; every protagonist could become a hegemon, and naturally, he could too! He remembered the methods in those novels very clearly...

Zheng You'an didn't stop to think that although Wang Jian was old, his experience was there; how could others compare to him? His wisdom was earned from fighting on the battlefield, far surpassing the knowledge Zheng You'an had gleaned from novels. Zheng You'an thought too highly of himself. He really thought transmigrators were superior, but he didn't look at his own narrow-minded, arrogant posture; no one would think highly of him!

"How did you transmigrate?" Xu Fu asked again.

Meeting a transmigrator was a rare opportunity. Xu Fu couldn't help but ask about the catalyst for this transmigration to understand what was going on. Moreover, if a Zheng You'an could appear here, could other transmigrators appear elsewhere? He had become the butterfly that flapped its wings and affected the history of the Warring States period; would he bring more butterflies? Would the course of history be destroyed? Most importantly, would Ying Zheng's great cause be blocked or destroyed?

Although Zheng You'an was arrogant and appeared clumsy in front of Wang Jian, Li Xin, and Lord Longyang, even lice become itchy if there are too many. If there were more transmigrators like Zheng You'an who dreamed of building a career and overthrowing Ying Zheng, it would eventually be a nuisance, and there was no guarantee that some wouldn't be smarter than Zheng You'an.

Zheng You'an sneered, "Naturally, I died and then came here."

"What did you do before?"

Zheng You'an bit his lip and had no intention of answering.

Seeing him silent for a long time, Xu Fu suddenly realized, "Inconvenient to say? A white-collar office worker?"

Zheng You'an countered, "And what did you do?"

"A fortune teller," Xu Fu said faintly.

Zheng You'an mocked him unceremoniously, "A fortune teller? Someone who dabbles in crooked ways and is chased away by city inspectors everywhere?"

Xu Fu was neither anxious nor angry, simply throwing one sentence back, "Yes, a fortune teller who became a Qin Commandant, while you..." Xu Fu looked him up and down, "...are a prisoner. A despicable assassin."

With just these few words, Zheng You'an jumped again. He struggled violently, causing the rack to shake, and cursed with the most vulgar language from his past life.

Things like "f*ck your mother," "die, your whole family," "bastard"...

Xu Fu frowned slightly.

Zheng You'an's vulgarity was beyond his imagination. Without needing to ask further, Xu Fu could already guess what he did in his past life. His education level was low, and his family background was definitely not wealthy. Many families were poor but not lacking in character, but this Zheng You'an was likely the type who lived poorly and blamed society in his past life.

Xu Fu never felt there was anything wrong with fortune-telling; he made a living by his craft, not stealing or robbing, so it really wasn't Zheng You'an's place to look down on him.

During the time Zheng You'an was cursing, Sang Zhong had already couldn't help but lift the curtain and stride in, with Li Xin following closely behind, holding the dagger.

"How bold! How dare you insult the Commandant!" Sang Zhong shouted angrily, his face icy.

Li Xin walked up slowly, looking at Zheng You'an as if he were looking at a dead man.

"Is the Commandant finished asking?" Li Xin asked.

"Finished." Xu Fu frowned imperceptibly. Talking to such an unrefined person was truly disgusting, and since nothing useful could be asked anyway, let it be.

Li Xin nodded at Xu Fu, "Where did the Commandant get injured that day?"

Xu Fu was startled, "My neck."

"Only the neck?"

"Only the neck."

Li Xin didn't say another word. He walked closer, took in Zheng You'an's shivering appearance, felt disgust, and immediately drew his dagger. His movements were swift, and by the time Zheng You'an realized what was happening, the dagger had already grazed his neck.

Zheng You'an screamed in pain again, his body shaking even more violently, "What are you doing? Let me go! Don't kill me! What else do you want to ask? I'll tell! I'll tell everything!"

Lord Longyang said slowly, "Watching from before, I thought he was quite a clever person. Now it seems he is not only stupid but lacks even the slightest bit of backbone."

Zheng You'an's face flushed red with anger at these words, but he dared not move, let alone curse. He felt the cut on his neck and the blood flowing out—the cold... the pain... and the fear of death.

After hearing this, Xu Fu thought to himself that Lord Longyang was truly not someone to be trifled with. Although it wasn't his place to deal with the assassin in the army, scaring Zheng You'an half to death was no problem at all.

"Which hand held the dagger to harm the Commandant last night?"

Xu Fu glanced at Zheng You'an and said, "It was dark yesterday, I didn't see clearly."

"Then let's assume it was the right hand." As soon as Li Xin finished speaking, the dagger in his hand cut a gash into Zheng You'an's wrist. Zheng You'an screamed repeatedly in terror. Was this man going to cut off his wrist?

Blood gushed out, stimulating Zheng You'an's nerves. He shouted, "Let me go! Let me go! I am from the same place as your Commandant; for that sake, let me go..."

Sang Zhong was so angry he laughed. Disgusted by Zheng You'an's thick skin and lack of backbone, he scolded, "What are you? Our Commandant comes from Guigu! How dare you speak such nonsense about being from the same place as the Commandant!"

"Gui... Guigu..." The man was stunned, and suddenly the look in his eyes became crazy, "Why, why is he a disciple of Guigu... Why! He's just better-looking than me..."

"Too noisy." Li Xin said coldly, then placed the dagger against Zheng You'an's face, "If you scream again, I'll cut off your mouth."

The aura on Li Xin was too fierce; Zheng You'an froze there, not daring to move again.

"Commandant, please. This place is filthy and may stain your robes." Li Xin put away the dagger and turned back to say.

Xu Fu didn't want to stay any longer either. The mood of meeting a transmigrator had suddenly faded; such a transmigrator wasn't even worth being called his peer. Xu Fu walked out first, with Sang Zhong following closely. Jianjia couldn't help but ask Li Xin, "What about this person?"

"Hang him here and bleed him out." Li Xin said the last two words very plainly, as if he were talking about stewing meat.

Zheng You'an, who was behind him, heard it clearly and couldn't help but scream wildly. Bleed him out? Was he going to drain his blood drop by drop? Too terrifying! Devils! People in ancient times were savages! That transmigrator was even more hateful for not saving him... Cold-blooded! Not worthy of being human! Yes, that person was truly hateful; how was he worthy of being a Guigu disciple? Why wasn't it him? Zheng You'an's gaze became increasingly insane, but no matter how much he screamed, he could only be isolated behind the curtain.

And there were soldiers guarding outside the tent; he couldn't escape, and the Zhao army wouldn't send anyone to save his life.

Acting like a hero for a moment, he really thought he was a hero. He overestimated himself; Zheng You'an deserved this end.

After Jianjia left the tent, he quickly caught up with Xu Fu and asked curiously, "Sir, what did that person mean by 'homosexual' and 'pretty boy'?"

Xu Fu scanned the people behind him and saw that they were all staring at him. Although they didn't show it on their faces, their eyes were full of curiosity.

"Homosexual..." Xu Fu's gaze fell on Lord Longyang, "If Jianjia admired Lord Longyang, that would be homosexual."

Jianjia shivered, "Sir, I... how could I admire him..." Jianjia looked up at Lord Longyang, only to see Lord Longyang looking at him with a half-smile. Jianjia felt even more terrified and quickly withdrew his gaze, silently moving two steps away.

Sang Zhong's expression on the side was also a bit strange.

Seeing this, Xu Fu thought to himself, don't blame me for opening the door to a new world for you all.

"As for a 'pretty boy,' it refers to a handsome man who relies on women for a living."

"Being called handsome is not bad," Lord Longyang said slowly.

Jianjia: "...Sang Zhong, I feel a bit sick."

Lord Longyang smiled faintly and didn't speak.

Jianjia felt a little proud in his heart. It seems it's also good to be outside. If he said this in the mansion, Lord Longyang would definitely say immediately, "Shouldn't I be the one who is pregnant? Why is my husband having morning sickness?" Jianjia could imagine the expression on Lord Longyang's face at that time.

After interrogating Zheng You'an, it was getting late. The army was distributing food, so Li Xin and the others went to get some for Xu Fu. Xu Fu was able to get some leisure time and just sat in the tent waiting.

By evening, the Qin army fought the Zhao army again. The Zhao army was already showing signs of fatigue. Wang Jian knew that the best opportunity had arrived.

On the side where the Qin army returned to camp, someone came to Xu Fu's tent and said, "Commandant, the assassin is dead."

Dead?

Xu Fu was stunned. For a moment, his heart felt a bit complicated. As fellow transmigrators, he had faced greater dangers, yet he had survived under the nose of the First Emperor of Qin and was even thriving, while this person had managed to play a good hand into a losing game. It was truly foolish to the extreme; he didn't deserve any sympathy for this end.

"Does the Commandant want to go and take a look?" the man asked. He thought that since the assassin dared to assassinate the Commandant, the Commandant would want to see his miserable state.

"Let's go." Xu Fu didn't hesitate and stood up immediately.

Sang Zhong and the others naturally followed him.

When Xu Fu entered the tent, he found that Li Xin, who had returned to camp, was also standing inside.

Xu Fu stood far away, glanced at Zheng You'an, and then turned his head away. Looking at a corpse was not pleasant at all.

The soldier beside Li Xin was holding something in his hand. Seeing Xu Fu enter, Li Xin brought the soldier to Xu Fu and said, "Commandant, something fell off the assassin. Presenting it to the Commandant."

What is it?

Xu Fu looked at the soldier's hands.

His breath hitched.

Small, exquisite, palm-sized, cast in bronze, with ancient patterns.

It was a tripod!

But why was this tripod so small? Xu Fu grabbed the tripod from the soldier's hand and examined it back and forth. That's right, the appearance was the same as the two tripods in the palace, but the size was really quite different... There were many people here, so it wasn't convenient for Xu Fu to examine it too much, so he put the tripod away and said, "I am quite interested in this object. I will take it back to my tent to play with it. Is that okay?"

How would the soldiers dare to say no? They all looked at Li Xin.

And Xu Fu's gaze was also fixed on Li Xin.

Li Xin said in a deep voice, "Naturally, it is fine."

Xu Fu said "Hmm," and without looking back, he ordered people to dispose of the corpse, then left the tent. In fact, even if he didn't order it, Li Xin would definitely have arranged these things properly, but if he didn't say a word, it would seem like he came just for this tripod.

After leaving the tent, Xu Fu felt a bit funny as he walked. A tripod falling off a dead body—is it like fighting a monster where it drops equipment after you kill it?

Returning to his tent, Xu Fu no longer hid it and took out the small tripod, placing it on the desk. Sang Zhong and the others just stood quietly to the side. After a while, the curtain moved, and Li Xin stood at the entrance of the tent, asking, "Commandant, may Li Xin come in?"

Xu Fu waved at him without raising his head.

After Li Xin entered, seeing Xu Fu looking at the tripod, he didn't disturb him and followed Sang Zhong and the others to stand aside.

It was getting dark outside, and candles were lit in the tent. The candlelight was inevitably a bit dim. Xu Fu raised his hand to stroke the patterns on the tripod and looked at it by the candlelight. He already had a guess in his heart, and now he just needed to verify it, which saved a lot of trouble, unlike before when he had to let his imagination run wild while touching the patterns, wondering what it could be.

Jianjia was younger after all and couldn't endure the silence, so he couldn't help but ask, "Sir, what are you touching?"

"The patterns on it." As he spoke, Xu Fu turned the small tripod in his hand, facing the patterned side toward Jianjia, "Look, is this a flame pattern?"

Lord Longyang was clearly more knowledgeable. He squinted at it and said, "This is a fire pattern?"

Xu Fu nodded.

Lord Longyang didn't find it strange, "The Twelve Ornaments are patterns that the Zhou Emperor ordered to be used on sacrificial robes. The Twelve Ornaments are also the basis for distinguishing the rank of officials in the Zhou Dynasty. It's rare to see them carved on a tripod." He didn't say the last sentence sincerely.

The Zhou royal family was declining, and the vassal states were eyeing them covetously, all wanting to become hegemons, even vaguely wanting to show that their power had surpassed that of the Zhou royal family. Therefore, the Twelve Ornaments used by the Zhou Dynasty were also common in the vassal states. The vassal states didn't necessarily like the Twelve Ornaments, but they had to use them to show that if the Zhou Emperor could afford to use them, they could too!

Lord Longyang was by the side of the King of Wei, so how could he not have seen them?

Xu Fu had almost concluded that the sun, moon, stars, pheasant, and flame patterns were all among the Twelve Ornaments.

The Twelve Ornaments originated in the Zhou Dynasty, and the time interval was not long, which meant that this tripod was not cast long ago, and it couldn't even be considered an antique. What kind of amazing thing could it be? Maybe it could really only be used by himself to refine alchemy pills.

Xu Fu set the tripod aside. The candlelight in the tent was dim, and there seemed to be a faint luster flowing inside the tripod. Xu Fu glanced at it, but saw nothing. Perhaps it was just a visual error... Xu Fu withdrew his gaze.

Lord Longyang said, "It seems the Sir is quite fond of tripods."

The previous tripod was also found for him by Lord Longyang; it was not strange that Lord Longyang would notice his unusual behavior.

"I like to refine alchemy pills and don't like to use ordinary tripods; I prefer such unique and exquisite ones."

Lord Longyang pointed to the tripod on the desk, "But this one is a bit small..."

"It's not small." It's fine for grinding medicine anyway. Since he found such a thing, he had to make it show its value, otherwise, it would seem very stupid that he went to look for it.

The curiosity of the crowd about the tripod faded, and soon it was time for dinner, so they just had a simple meal together.

Jianjia and Lord Longyang went out of the tent, perhaps to walk around.

Only Sang Zhong and Li Xin remained in the tent. Sang Zhong didn't dare to leave Xu Fu's side easily, worried about another assassination. Now that Xu Fu was in a high position, there was no guarantee that the Zhao army wouldn't target him again, as he had no martial arts skills.

But what was Li Xin still doing here?

Sang Zhong couldn't help but say, "General, aren't you leaving?"

Li Xin looked at Xu Fu and said calmly, "I have something to say to the Commandant."

Sang Zhong frowned, not knowing how the two of them had become so close, but he really didn't have the qualifications to comment, so he automatically retreated. The curtain moved, and only the two of them were left in the tent.

Xu Fu could still hear the sound of the wind outside and the rough voices of the soldiers.

"How does the Commandant see my physiognomy now?" Li Xin asked straightforwardly.

Xu Fu thought to himself, how your physiognomy is really isn't my business. You should ask Hou Sheng to calculate it for you. Besides, Xu Fu didn't like to read someone's physiognomy multiple times; once was enough. What do you want to do by reading so many? Do you really think that knowing your fate means you can grasp the future?

So Xu Fu coldly refused him, "Why does the General need to seek the result of physiognomy again? Now that the General is smooth in the army and the future is promising, why ask me?"

Li Xin was slightly disappointed, but he didn't ask further.

This made Xu Fu look at him with appreciation.

Knowing when to stop and being able to advance or retreat—that is a capable person.

Li Xin seemed to have more to say to Xu Fu, but as soon as he met Xu Fu's gaze, he gritted his teeth and held it back. In the end, he didn't say anything else and hurried out.

A man's heart is like a needle at the bottom of the sea.

Xu Fu didn't know what Li Xin was thinking, and he had no interest in knowing what he was thinking.

Later, Wang Jian came to see Xu Fu himself and asked him if he would follow the army tomorrow. Only then did Xu Fu know that Wang Jian had already formulated the plan to attack the city tomorrow. Eyu, the Qin State was determined to win. Zheng You'an's rebellion was too fast, and taking Eyu would undoubtedly add another layer of security.

Xu Fu also wanted to see what winning a battle looked like. He called Sang Zhong to ask if going to the battlefield would cause them to become a burden.

Sang Zhong and Jian Jia both stated firmly that they would protect Xu Fu, and after some deliberation, Xu Fu agreed to Wang Jian's request. Wang Jian turned to glance at Lord Longyang, thinking to himself that this one was composed and very different from the other attendants of the Commandant. Then, Wang Jian walked out with a smile on his face.

After walking a long distance, Wang Jian suddenly stopped in his tracks, and the smile on his face vanished in an instant.

The soldier beside him saw the rapid change in his expression and, fearing he had offended Wang Jian, whispered, "General?"

Wang Jian did not respond to his voice at all, or rather, he was too preoccupied to respond. His mind was filled with the face of the man in the tent just now... If he remembered correctly... he had seen that face before. The King of Wei kept him by his side, protecting him like a treasure; he possessed excellent swordsmanship, held half the power of the State of Wei, and was cursed by many as a sycophant... it was Lord Longyang!

"General?" the soldier called out again, stammering.

"Let's go." Wang Jian's expression returned to normal, and he strode away.

Does the King know that Lord Longyang is by the Commandant's side? How could the former Lord Longyang of Wei abandon all that power to come to Qin and willingly act as a small, nameless soldier? Wang Jian naturally didn't know; that was all Xu Fu's doing!

If Lord Xinling had been as young and beautiful as Lord Longyang, perhaps Xu Fu would have abducted him as well.

The next morning, while it was still pitch black, Xu Fu was awakened from his sleep by Sang Zhong. He washed up briefly, ate breakfast, and waited to set off with Wang Jian. The Qin army was in high spirits today, and their morale was even better after seeing Xu Fu. Xu Fu was somewhat puzzled and muttered to himself, wondering if he was some kind of morale-boosting medicine. He did not know that the Qin soldiers simply did not want to perform poorly in front of him and be noted down by the Commandant.

If they could gain the Commandant's favor, they might just be promoted.

Thinking of the order from the King of Qin—to reward based on military merit—who could not be excited?

They soon arrived at the foot of Eyu City, divided their forces to launch a surprise attack, and then challenged the enemy to battle. Xu Fu stayed safely in his chariot, watching the soldiers clash.

This day was still under the scorching sun, with hot summer winds blowing against them. The Zhao army again sent out those soldiers who had shed their armor and were light on their feet, but the Qin army was not unprepared. Those blocking the front were all elite Qin troops; no matter how agile the others were, they were no match for the equally nimble Qin soldiers and their sharp blades. The lives of the Zhao soldiers were quickly harvested, and vultures circled in the sky, scavenging the flesh and blood of the fallen.

Eyu City fell...

That was two hours later. The main force of the Qin army poured into the city, and the remaining Zhao soldiers and civilians had no choice but to surrender.

Xu Fu had a sudden thought and called Sang Zhong over, "Go and invite Li Xin for me."

Sang Zhong pointed in one direction, "General Li Xin is still handling the aftermath."

Handling the aftermath meant slaughtering the remaining soldiers outside the city.

Xu Fu did not judge this bloody and cruel practice. War was simply like this; there was no logic of cruelty or lack thereof.

Li Xin carried his halberd, covered in blood, appearing like an Asura returned from hell. Bathed in sunlight, he entered the city first, and the city's residents trembled at the sight of him.

Xu Fu paused, "Let us go in together."

"Alright." Sang Zhong protected Xu Fu as they headed inside, soon reuniting with Wang Jian and the others.

Xu Fu stopped Li Xin, "Could I trouble General Li with one thing?"

Li Xin dismounted and walked beside Xu Fu, saying, "What is it?" Others in the army couldn't help but observe Li Xin and Xu Fu, thinking, Li Xin is really fast; who knows when he got close to the Commandant. It's a pity; when the Commandant was assassinated that day, they were all a step too slow.

"Could General Li make a trip to Zheng You'an's residence and retrieve his belongings from childhood to the present for me?" He didn't know if the Qin army would burn down some of the residences in Eyu upon entering; he had seen such things in TV dramas before. To prevent any accidents, it was better to entrust this to Li Xin. As for why he wanted those things, it might not be a good thing for a transmigrator's belongings to leak out. He felt more at ease keeping them in his own hands.

Li Xin did not ask further, nor did he show any curiosity as to why Xu Fu wanted to do this. He agreed, turned around with his men, and clearly headed toward Zheng You'an's residence.

After occupying Eyu, the Qin army did not celebrate, nor did they relax in the slightest. Furthermore, Wang Jian ordered the minor officials in the army with annual salaries of less than a hundred shi to return home, selecting only two out of every ten to stay—all of whom were elites. Those sent home were naturally dissatisfied, but Wang Jian's prestige had been long-established; how could they dare to say anything?

When Xu Fu heard about this from Sang Zhong, he didn't take it to heart. Wang Jian was a veteran general of Qin and understood military affairs better; just because others couldn't grasp his intentions didn't mean Wang Jian's decision was wrong.

The Qin army did not pause and soon set off again toward Liaoyang.

When news reached the State of Qin, some praised Wang Jian's actions, while others criticized them. Ying Zheng ignored it all; he did not doubt those he employed, and he knew Wang Jian's capabilities, so he had nothing to doubt. By contrast, while Qin's campaign went smoothly, he was more worried about Xu Fu's safety. There were truly some foolish people in that army; the reports sent back mentioned everything, yet failed to mention a single word about Xu Fu. How could this not make Ying Zheng feel anxious and tormented?

Was he eating well, sleeping well, was he injured... Countless worries crowded into Ying Zheng's mind. However, Ying Zheng suppressed these emotions, handled government affairs as usual, and continued to call Fusu to his side for guidance. Only now, because of Xu Fu, he was not as harsh toward Huhai as he had been in the past, showing a faint hint of treating them equally. The palace staff, realizing that Ying Zheng did not undervalue Prince Huhai, naturally became more attentive.

It was just that Huhai hadn't seen Xu Fu for a long time and would inevitably lie on the ground, calling out "A-Fu" every day.

The more Ying Zheng heard it, the more uneasy he felt.

He wished he could be like Xu Fu, dreaming and predicting the future's fortunes, but unfortunately, no dreams came to him, and he didn't even have the erotic dreams he used to have.

By this time, the entire court knew that after Xu Fu went to the battlefield, he had saved Wang Jian once, and the ministers could only sigh. This man truly had ability! Saving Wang Jian—who knows how much he will benefit from this in the future...

Far within the borders of the State of Zhao, Xu Fu packed his bags again and followed Wang Jian's army toward Liaoyang.

If Ying Zheng knew, he would surely be angry enough to flip his desk.

During the march, everyone rode horses, except for Xu Fu who rode in a carriage. However, the army held him in great awe, so naturally, no one said anything. Inside the carriage, Jian Jia was eager to get into the action. The Battle of Eyu had stirred his excitement, and his hot blood was waiting to be spilled. The fight at Eyu hadn't been enough to satisfy him, so heading to Liaoyang was just right.

Seeing Jian Jia so exuberant, Sang Zhong could only sigh to himself; it seemed that protecting the Master was more reliably left to him.

The Qin army marched extremely fast. To avoid holding them back, Xu Fu did not complain of bitterness or fatigue along the way, suppressing any discomfort. He knew the priorities and would not let the Qin army accommodate him. Seeing that although Xu Fu was a Commandant, he did not make unreasonable demands based on his status, Wang Jian's impression of him improved even more. After ten days, they arrived at Liaoyang.

Upon arrival, they first found a place to camp, surveyed the terrain, rested, and ate their fill and slept well. Otherwise, how could they win battles while exhausted?

Xu Fu did not know that the State of Zhao had already torn off its mask. The day they set up camp, Liaoyang City received the news, and that very night, several waves of assassins arrived. Fortunately, Sang Zhong was guarding the tent, and by the second half of the night, even Li Xin had come to keep watch. The incoming assassins were all captured, and some were killed on the spot.

It was just that the mouths of these assassins were much tougher than Zheng You'an's; they died without revealing anything. Wang Jian didn't care; conquering Liaoyang didn't depend on extracting information from assassins; he had his own methods.

Assassins came every few days, and Xu Fu gradually got used to it. By now, Wang Jian had already formulated his tactics and was prepared to take the Qin army out for a stroll to test the strength of Liaoyang City.

At this time, news arrived that Huan Yi had captured Ye City, which undoubtedly boosted the morale of the Qin army even further.

Huan Yi received orders to immediately turn and attack Liyang; whether they could take Liaoyang now became the key.

The atmosphere in the military camp suddenly became tense. Only Xu Fu maintained his leisurely demeanor, rarely coming out of his tent. Only at night would he occasionally observe the stars. If passing soldiers saw him, they would inevitably be cautious, not daring to disturb Xu Fu in the slightest, as if hindering him might cause this battle to go awry.

In fact, Xu Fu wasn't watching to see if the battle would be won; he was staring at the sky, lost in thought.

...It seemed that as time went on, he couldn't help but wonder how Ying Zheng was doing in the palace.

Xu Fu frowned slightly; this was not a good sign.

Just then, Xu Fu noticed a faint sound behind him, like someone stepping on dry branches and withered grass. Sang Zhong was even more sensitive than him and immediately turned to look, even calling soldiers to search the area.

However, they found nothing, not even a footprint.

Out of caution, Li Xin personally led men to patrol the area, but ultimately found nothing.

Sang Zhong said apologetically, "Perhaps I heard wrong."

Xu Fu wanted to say, it wasn't that you heard wrong, because I heard it too, but since no traces were found, it was really not good to trouble Li Xin and the others further. He had Sang Zhong and Jian Jia guarding him, so nothing should happen; hadn't there been enough assassins these past few days?

Li Xin personally escorted Xu Fu back to his tent. In the sky, the stars shone brightly; tomorrow would be a clear day.

That night, Xu Fu slept soundly again, without the slightest disturbance. Perhaps after he fell into a deep sleep, assassins came to the camp again, but he didn't hear a sound; there were people to handle it for him anyway. After washing up, he slowly walked out of the tent. At this time, the morning light was faint; it was just right to breathe some fresh air and look into the distance. Although such days were a bit monotonous, they were more regular than in the palace—sleeping early and rising early without any delay, and his complexion was becoming increasingly white and jade-like.

Wang Jian was still adjusting tactics with the generals, and the soldiers were training without a moment's slack.

Xu Fu stood outside the tent and saw Jian Jia walking over quickly, his brows furrowed, "Master..." His tone was hesitant, as if debating whether he should tell Xu Fu.

"What happened?"

Jian Jia bit his lip and said, "...Lord Longyang is gone."

"Gone?" Xu Fu was startled, "Who could abduct him?"

Indeed, Lord Longyang possessed excellent swordsmanship and high intelligence; furthermore, Jian Jia, who was with him, was no slouch in martial arts. There was no way Lord Longyang could be abducted!

Even he, who had no strength to truss a chicken, hadn't been abducted.

"Master?" Jian Jia's voice was slightly anxious.

"It's not convenient to disturb Li Xin right now. You and Sang Zhong go and search around..." Having said this, Xu Fu paused and hurriedly waved to call over some patrolling soldiers, "You go with Jian Jia and search for my other attendant."

The soldiers felt a bit of dissatisfaction in their hearts.

An attendant—was he worth such a big fuss to find? If this attendant went missing, he deserved to die! To actually abandon his master and leave.

How could Xu Fu not know what they were thinking? He just said calmly, "Liaoyang City is watching us closely. If my attendant has gone missing, I don't know if it's the work of the Zhao army. If we let the Zhao army succeed, we will truly lose face."

The dissatisfaction in the soldiers' hearts came and went quickly. Hearing Xu Fu say this, their anger was immediately ignited, "The Commandant is right; we truly cannot let the Zhao army be smug! Follow me!" These soldiers didn't say another word and went with Jian Jia to search for the person.

Sang Zhong, however, stubbornly refused to leave. He said, "If even Lord Longyang has truly gone missing, there's no guarantee that the Master won't be in danger. It's safer for me to stay by the Master's side."

Xu Fu couldn't sway him, and Sang Zhong was doing it for his own good. Besides, upon second thought, having so many people follow Jian Jia should be enough, so he gave up.

When Wang Jian finished discussing with the generals, he heard the news that one of Xu Fu's attendants was missing. Wang Jian took Xu Fu's affairs very seriously, and since he had some free time, he went over personally.

"Who is missing from the Commandant's side?" As soon as Wang Jian finished speaking, Jian Jia returned with his men. Although his face was cold, Xu Fu could still glimpse a hint of disappointment in his eyes.

Didn't find him?

Wang Jian glanced at Jian Jia and then at Sang Zhong beside Xu Fu; how could he not know who was missing? His heart sank suddenly.

Was it actually Lord Longyang who had gone missing?

This was trouble! Wang Jian frowned, but in front of others, it wasn't convenient to ask Xu Fu directly, so he could only say, "Why don't we go into the tent, and I can discuss it in detail with the Commandant?"

Seeing Wang Jian's strange expression, Xu Fu was puzzled and agreed.

Sang Zhong lifted the tent flap, and Xu Fu and Wang Jian went in side by side, while the others were left outside. Jian Jia, however, was called in because he knew the process of Lord Longyang's disappearance.

Now that there was no one else in the tent, Wang Jian stopped hiding and asked directly, "May I ask the Commandant, is the attendant by your side Lord Longyang?" After speaking, he didn't wait for Xu Fu to reply and added, "I once saw Lord Longyang; his appearance is outstanding, and it's hard to forget. Seeing him again recently, I was extremely surprised."

Wang Jian's eyes were truly sharp!

He was the first to confirm Lord Longyang's identity after seeing him. One must know that many people, even if they suspected it, wouldn't dare to confirm it. After all, who would have thought that the Lord Longyang from the King of Wei's side would really appear in Qin?

Since Wang Jian had already recognized him, there was no point in being evasive, so Xu Fu nodded.

"It really is Lord Longyang?" Wang Jian's expression became serious, and his brows furrowed as if he were holding a hot potato.

"Is the General worried that Lord Longyang is colluding with the enemy?" Xu Fu's tone was calm, as if what he said wasn't something shocking.

Jian Jia, hearing this from the side, couldn't help but say, "Lord Longyang would not do such a thing!"

Wang Jian didn't argue with Jian Jia, but stared fixedly at Xu Fu. Now that he was the one who brought the person, Xu Fu would have to bear the consequences. No one would want to wade into this muddy water for no reason. Moreover, Wang Jian prioritized the great cause of Qin; if Lord Longyang truly had ulterior motives, he would certainly not be soft-hearted.

Xu Fu could understand all of this.

But now that Lord Longyang was missing, no one could draw a conclusion just yet, "Let's find the person first. I'm afraid I'll have to trouble the soldiers in the army."

"That's no problem." Wang Jian paused, then asked the most critical question, "What if Lord Longyang has the intention of colluding with the enemy?"

Jian Jia unconsciously tightened the muscles on his face.

Xu Fu lowered his head and said nonchalantly, "Then we shall apprehend Lord Longyang."

Wang Jian smiled, stood up, and said, "Then I will send more men to search for him. Please have the Commandant's attendant come with me."

Xu Fu looked up at Jian Jia, "Go."

Jian Jia was a bit nervous, but he remained very composed on the surface and followed Wang Jian out without a word.

Wang Jian sent men to continue searching for Lord Longyang's whereabouts.

After two days of such turmoil, there was still no news. When Wang Jian came to see Xu Fu again, his face was slightly gloomy. With only the two of them in the tent, Wang Jian said, "I have to suspect that Lord Longyang has ulterior motives. If he is found, I fear my men might not be careful and hurt him, or even... kill him."

Xu Fu remained nonchalant and nodded.

Seeing Xu Fu so cooperative, Wang Jian breathed a sigh of relief. He chatted with Xu Fu for a few more moments and asked with a smile if he had any words of wisdom for tomorrow's battle. Xu Fu still replied nonchalantly, "None."

Wang Jian was not disappointed and walked out with a gentle expression.

Outside the tent, Jian Jia's expression was already very gloomy. Lord Longyang had suddenly gone missing, and he bore the greatest responsibility. If Lord Longyang truly had ulterior motives and intended to sabotage Qin's attack on other countries, he certainly wouldn't say a word for him. But just thinking about it made him feel miserable.

Jian Jia didn't know how long he had been standing outside.

The sky gradually darkened, and a hot wind blew. Jian Jia moved his legs and let out a breath; they were a bit sore and numb. He turned around but didn't see Sang Zhong; he must have gone to get food for the Master. Jian Jia lifted the tent flap, walked in, and called out in a hoarse voice, "Master."

The tent was silent.

Jian Jia shivered involuntarily. He steadied himself and carefully examined the tent; there was no one there, only the flickering candlelight illuminating the tent. His shadow was stretched long, swaying with the candlelight, making him feel inexplicably panicked.

Jian Jia walked out quickly and grabbed a soldier nearby, asking, "Did you see the Commandant come out just now?"

The soldier shook his head blankly, "No... I didn't..."

Jian Jia's heart tightened, and he pushed the soldier, "Quick! Go find Sang Zhong!" "You go and invite General Li Xin!"

Sang Zhong happened to be coming over with food. Seeing Jian Jia's frantic appearance, he couldn't help but ask, "What's wrong?"

Seeing Sang Zhong, Jian Jia's expression collapsed, revealing his inner bewilderment, "Sang Zhong..." his voice trembled slightly, "I can't find the Master."

Sang Zhong's expression changed, "What nonsense are you talking about? When I left just now, wasn't the Master resting in the tent?" As he spoke, he handed the food to Jian Jia and walked quickly to lift the tent flap, but saw that it was empty, with only the candlelight remaining.

Sang Zhong's heart turned cold, as if his heart had been hollowed out in an instant.

His lips moved, and finally, he turned around, gritted his teeth, and said hatefully, "The Commandant is missing!" This exclamation startled many people, including Li Xin, who had been invited by the soldiers. Li Xin's expression changed drastically; he stepped forward and grabbed Sang Zhong by the collar, "What did you say? The Commandant is missing?"

Sang Zhong didn't care to argue with Li Xin about his rude behavior and replied with a dark face, "Yes."

Li Xin immediately sent men to search everywhere and ordered someone to inform Wang Jian.

First an attendant, and then Xu Fu himself went missing. They could ignore the attendant's disappearance, but the disappearance of the dignified Protector Commandant was a life-threatening matter!

After receiving the news, Wang Jian's expression changed instantly. He said in a deep voice, "This kind of tactic is not uncommon. Now that the Zhao army cannot win, they resort to these methods. Those assassins from the past few days were probably just a cover; kidnapping Commandant Xu was the real goal."

Jian Jia asked hurriedly, "Then what should we do?"

"Send men to search, for one."

"But what if we can't find him?"

"If we can't find him, we can only wait."

"Wait for what?"

Wang Jian's gaze turned cold, "Wait for the Zhao army to bring Commandant Xu out and threaten the Qin army not to attack."
