Inside the grand hall, a man lay prostrate on the ground.

As soon as Xu Fu and Ying Zheng stepped inside, they could see the man’s body trembling slightly.

"Raise your head and speak," Ying Zheng said coldly.

The man turned his head, and upon seeing Ying Zheng, he finally let out a sigh of relief, "Your Majesty, it has not rained in the Nanyang administrative district for half a month."

Ying Zheng frowned, "Why was this not reported sooner?"

"Nanyang has always had little rain, so at first, the governor did not pay much attention to it, not daring to rashly disturb Your Majesty with such matters. But it has been half a month without rain in Nanyang, the weather is hot, the fields are parched, and if this continues, I fear this year's harvest will be greatly reduced..."

Before the man could finish speaking, an attendant stepped into the hall and bowed, "Your Majesty, an urgent report from Sanchuan."

"Send him in."

In the blink of an eye, a middle-aged man rushed in, "Greetings, Your Majesty." Whether it was because his limbs were too weak or he was exhausted from the journey, he collapsed onto the floor and could not get back up.

"Has something happened in Sanchuan?"

"Your Majesty, it has not rained in Sanchuan for a month. The people's land has cracked open, and in many villages, there is no water to drink. If this continues, I fear people will die of thirst..." The middle-aged man said, tears and snot streaming down his face.

The two men knelt together, both looking extremely disheveled.

Ying Zheng did not ask again why they hadn't reported it sooner; it took time for them to travel from Nanyang and Sanchuan, and before the situation was clear, who would dare to rashly come and disturb the King of Qin?

Ying Zheng’s expression was icy. Without further delay, he stood up and called Zhao Gao to his side, "Who are the governors of these two districts?"

Zhao Gao answered readily, "Yang Huai and Shu Hua."

"Order men to investigate the situation in both places, and summon Li Si and Wei Liao to the palace to see me."

"Yes." Zhao Gao quickly gave the orders.

Not long after, Li Si and Wei Liao were invited to the palace. Droughts caused by long periods without rain were common; Wei Liao had seen many during his travels through various states. However, neither he nor Li Si were experts in this area and could not offer much insight, so after hearing the report, they could only look troubled.

"Your Majesty, why not invite my senior fellow apprentice? He should have some research into this matter." Although he couldn't think of a solution, Li Si could recommend someone.

Ying Zheng had talked with Han Fei for a long time before and knew that Han Fei’s expertise lay in Legalism; he likely had no solution for this either.

Thinking of this, Ying Zheng could not help but feel a sense of irritation.

A severe drought often lasts a long time, easily forcing the people to have no harvest. Without food or water, they would soon become refugees; starvation and death from thirst were not uncommon. The most terrifying thing was that the drought could bring about a plague, and in a single epidemic, tens of thousands could die. And now, the Qin army was out on a campaign; if there was a lack of food at home, where would the Qin army find a solid backing? By then, let alone the people, the pace of attacking the six states would have to be delayed again and again.

A sudden drought—who knew how much trouble it would bring to the Qin State!

Xu Fu had been listening to others the whole time, his expression cold and his brows locked in a frown, as if he were immersed in his own thoughts.

Xu Fu was thinking of a solution. But he knew very well that this time was different from the incident at the Han border. That time, he used the rain-seeking ritual, which aligned with the timing and the geographical advantages, to achieve the final result. But this time, both Nanyang and Sanchuan districts were suffering, and no one knew if another place would fall into the same state. Thinking of the divination, Xu Fu felt a splitting headache; who knew how long this drought would last?

Fortunately, the Qin State grew millet and sorghum, which were relatively drought-resistant crops; otherwise, they might not have lasted even a month. Currently, the people still had small amounts of stored grain, so filling their stomachs was not a problem, but what about water? What if they got thirsty? When the wells and rivers dried up, what then?

Ying Zheng waved everyone away, "Very well, we shall discuss this at the morning court tomorrow."

After they retreated, Ying Zheng finally revealed his hidden displeasure and anger.

"If only I could have divined it sooner..."

Ying Zheng interrupted Xu Fu without a second thought, "This is not your fault. No one could have foreseen such a great disaster." Disasters are sudden; who can foresee everything like a god?

Xu Fu was somewhat distracted and did not respond to Ying Zheng.

That night, after the two went to sleep, Xu Fu did not dream of heavy rain again. It must be so; dreams are sometimes the opposite. The heavy rain in the dream, so illusory and intangible, was precisely a premonition of the reality of the drought, where there was not a drop of rain.

At the morning court the next day, the Qin officials were somewhat alarmed to hear about the drought.

Although the Qin State had become increasingly wealthy, they dared not forget the past. The old Qin was poor; the whole country could not collect much grain, and the King of Qin had to lead the army to fight personally, supporting the war with war. Let alone the people, even the ministers of Qin often went hungry without receiving their salaries.

Thinking of it now, how could it not make them feel alarmed? They were terrified that the past would repeat itself.

Ying Zheng had calmed down by now. He quickly set a disaster relief policy, arranged for people to go to both places to investigate, and at the same time ordered Zheng Guo to be summoned, along with anyone skilled in drought management.

The morning court ended quickly.

Within a day, the news of the drought in Nanyang and Sanchuan had spread throughout Xianyang. The people did not know how the drought came about; they only knew that it wasn't raining, that they were going to suffer, that the fields couldn't produce grain, and that the wells couldn't provide water. Without food or drink, how were they to live? Although Xianyang had not reached that point yet, the people could not help but feel a bit panicked.

They even wondered if, during the Wax Sacrifice at the end of last year, they had not been sincere enough, causing the gods to be angry and unwilling to protect them, thus bringing about this drought.

When the news reached the palace, Xu Fu’s expression was indifferent.

Having been at ease for so long, he had even forgotten what the old Grand Diviner had once said.

After the Wax Sacrifice, if the following year had a good harvest, the people might not necessarily be grateful to the person who presided over the sacrifice. But if, after the sacrifice, the weather was not favorable and the people did not live well, then the person who presided over the sacrifice would inevitably be subjected to public criticism.

At this time, no matter how miraculous his character reading, physiognomy, or divination was, the people would not care. They only cared about whether they were living well. If they were not living well, then the person who caused them to live poorly was naturally their enemy.

With this matter right in front of him, there was no way to avoid it; no matter what, Xu Fu would have to take the blame.

Let them blame him; having been smooth sailing for so long, this little difficulty could be considered a tempering. Xu Fu rubbed his temples and signaled the palace attendants to pack his things.

Ying Zheng walked into the hall with a dark face and saw the attendants busy packing Xu Fu’s things. A bad premonition suddenly arose in Ying Zheng’s heart. He frowned and asked, "What is this for?"

"Packing things, um, going to Sanchuan first," Xu Fu said softly, not feeling that his words were particularly shocking.

"You are going to Sanchuan?" An icy chill immediately covered Ying Zheng’s face.

"There are many rumors in Xianyang; Your Majesty must have heard them, right?"

"Why bother with such absurd talk?" Ying Zheng frowned.

"Why fuel public anger? If I go, I can at least temporarily appease the dissatisfaction in the hearts of the people. Besides, if this matter can be resolved smoothly, the status of the Wax Sacrifice in the eyes of the people will not decline, and divination and sacrifice will not lose the trust of the people." Of course, these were not the most important reasons. Xu Fu paused and said, "How can there be a stain on me?"

Moreover, he had received premonitions repeatedly before this happened. If he really abandoned it and did nothing, he would not be able to get past it in his own heart.

Ying Zheng’s expression darkened further as he stared fixedly at Xu Fu.

If the drought really couldn't be controlled, it was possible for the locals to start a riot. If Xu Fu went there, he would be surrounded by danger everywhere; how could he protect himself?

Xu Fu, however, could not sense what was in Ying Zheng’s heart. He met Ying Zheng’s gaze, his own eyes steady and completely unafraid.

Xu Fu was truly not afraid of difficulties and obstacles. If he hadn't been able to divine any great disaster before, with his heart hanging high, that would have been worrying and uncomfortable. But now that he knew where the problem was, the pressure on his heart was suddenly relieved.

Since he couldn't change his decision.

Ying Zheng withdrew his gaze and said coldly, "Pack my clothes as well."

The attendants froze in unison, "...Y-Your Majesty?"

Ying Zheng looked at Xu Fu, his voice still cold, making no effort to hide his dissatisfaction with Xu Fu’s actions, "I am going with you."

Xu Fu was slightly stunned and looked away, "Your Majesty is busy with official duties; why is there a need to go with me?"

"This is a matter of the state; I should naturally go personally."

Who was the only stubborn one? There was also Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng was holding back anger in his heart, and it was a time when no one could persuade him otherwise.

Their things were packed quickly. Ying Zheng did not pause and immediately called Wei Liao and Li Si in, ordering them to manage the affairs of the court together and insisting that they must often send people to report to him.

Wei Liao did not care and only said he would definitely look after the state affairs for Ying Zheng. Li Si, however, could not help but be a little excited. He had squeezed from a minor official into the power center of Qin, gained the appreciation of the King of Qin, and now had the opportunity to manage the affairs of the court—what a high honor! What great power! His choice back then was indeed correct! Li Si was stirred with emotion and bowed heavily to Ying Zheng, saying, "I will definitely not fail Your Majesty."

Ying Zheng glanced at them and then left Zhao Gao in the palace.

Although Wei Liao did not submit to him in his heart, he was upright in character. Since he served the Qin State, he would not develop any other rebellious thoughts. Moreover, there was the connection with Xu Fu. Li Si was clever enough, had methods, and was skilled in government affairs, but he was a man from another state; with power in hand, he would inevitably develop selfish motives, so he would perfectly complement Wei Liao. Zhao Gao was his confidant, and his wisdom and methods were not inferior to Li Si’s; having him stay in the palace would also be much more stable.

Not to mention that there were other trusted men of Ying Zheng left in the court, so no matter what, if he left Xianyang, Xianyang would not fall into chaos.

It was just that before leaving, Ying Zheng summoned Wang Jian back.

If there was a shortage of military rations, what would the Qin army do abroad? Should they go back to the old path of supporting war with war? Ying Zheng had heard that there had been many droughts in the Zhao State recently; I fear that even if they took over the entire Zhao State, it might not be enough to feed the Qin army. Since that was the case, it was better to delay for a while, return to the country to recuperate, and after the drought, store up enough grain before fighting again.

After everything was prepared, Ying Zheng went with Xu Fu to Sanchuan District.

Sang Zhong and the others were already familiar with Xu Fu, so they were not left behind when heading to Sanchuan District.

As they traveled forward, Xu Fu began to feel the pain.

The scorching sun was in the sky, making it easy to feel parched. The further they went toward Sanchuan, the more they could see that many trees along the road were withered. Dust flew on the paths they walked, and it was hard to find a river or stream.

Fortunately, they had some water reserves, so they wouldn't die of thirst before reaching Sanchuan.

Along the way, Ying Zheng’s expression was icy, making people not even dare to breathe loudly. Xu Fu didn't know if he was unhappy because of the drought in the two districts or because he was unhappy that he was going to Sanchuan. If it was the latter... it was rare for Ying Zheng to hold a grudge for so long.

Because Ying Zheng’s aura was majestic, no one dared to speak along the way. It was so quiet it could almost drive people crazy. Jianjia had visibly lost weight, and Xu Fu’s mood was inevitably affected, his appearance unconsciously looking a bit withered.

Could it be that he is waiting for me to apologize and coax him? Xu Fu was conflicted in his heart.

Xu Fu found it hard to adapt to this kind of Ying Zheng.

When he first arrived in the Qin State, even if Ying Zheng treated him coldly, he felt nothing. But since the change in their relationship, Ying Zheng had become increasingly gentle toward him, even caring for him in every possible way. Thinking about it carefully now, it could be considered as indulging him to the extreme. Since then, when had Ying Zheng ever given him such a cold face?

Xu Fu suddenly felt an indescribable sense of grievance in his heart.

He cooled his expression, holding back his unhappiness. If Ying Zheng changed his face so quickly, wouldn't he change his face just as quickly in the future?

Xu Fu unconsciously clenched his palms, his fingernails almost digging into his flesh.

After a while, Xu Fu slowly calmed down and regained his reason. Well, it was normal for Ying Zheng to worry about his safety. He had wanted to go to Shu, to Wei and Han, and later to the Zhao battlefield; Ying Zheng had disagreed, but in the end, he had compromised. This time, he had indulged him just the same. Well, since that was the case, he should give Ying Zheng the right to be unhappy.

As Xu Fu thought, his gaze swept over to Ying Zheng, and who knew that Ying Zheng was also looking at him? Their gazes happened to collide.

Ying Zheng’s gaze was indifferent, while Xu Fu’s was feigning calmness. As their gazes met, Xu Fu unconsciously wanted to withdraw his, but Ying Zheng suddenly reached out and pulled him to his side, his voice low and fierce, "If I hadn't taken the initiative, would you have just let me stay angry?"

Xu Fu’s skin was quite thick, and he said righteously, "No, I was just puzzled as to why A-Zheng was unhappy. I thought for a long time before I came to a conclusion, and I was just thinking about how to make A-Zheng happy."

Xu Fu sold his cuteness quickly and without leaving a trace.

Ying Zheng really loved and hated this appearance of his. If they were in the palace, he would have already thrown him onto the bed and punished him in a different way, but now they were in a carriage... a carriage... Ying Zheng suddenly felt a stir in his heart.

It was not entirely impossible in the carriage. The carriage was very spacious, and the attendants were all guarding outside. Even if they heard some movement, they would definitely not dare to peek or ask.

Ying Zheng lowered his head and leaned toward Xu Fu’s neck.

A thin layer of sweat slowly seeped out on Xu Fu’s back. In the space that was clearly spacious enough, it suddenly became stifling.

"Then I will tell you a way to make me happy."

Xu Fu had slept with Ying Zheng more than once or twice. Hearing his tone and seeing his actions, he knew what Ying Zheng was thinking. Xu Fu, who had just been sincere to win Ying Zheng’s forgiveness, raised his arm and ruthlessly rejected Ying Zheng, "No, there is no water."

"What does this have to do with having no water?"

"How can we bathe without water?" Xu Fu turned his head to look at him, "Does Your Majesty not need to bathe afterward?" His eyes revealed, "So Your Majesty is such a person who doesn't like to be clean."

Ying Zheng could only sigh and let go of Xu Fu, "Looking at it now, I really shouldn't have let you come to Sanchuan."

Who knew what the situation would be like when they reached Sanchuan District? Would they not even have water to wash up? Staying here for ten days or half a month, they would really become savages. Thinking about it, Ying Zheng felt sorry for Xu Fu.

If that clean appearance changed, could Xu Fu still maintain that ethereal temperament?

At this moment, Xu Fu hadn't even thought of this point.

On this journey, perhaps it was heaven’s favor, or perhaps Xu Fu brought his own good luck, they found a small stream. The group first boiled the water, drank their fill, and then used the water to wash up properly.

And Ying Zheng stood by the stream, looking at the stream and then at Xu Fu, his eyes smiling, but that smile carried a bit of ambiguity and heat.

After nightfall, everyone rested there for a while. Ying Zheng hugged Xu Fu alone and stood by the stream. Ying Zheng lowered his voice and asked him, "Now is there a chance to please me?"

Xu Fu pointed to the stream, "If we bathe here, how can this water still be drunk?"

Ying Zheng thought about the water being polluted... well, it was indeed impossible to drink.

When the next day dawned bright, Bo Zhou walked up and said, "Your Majesty, I don't know where else there will be a stream. Sanchuan lacks water, so why don't Your Majesty and Master Xu bathe here first?"

"If this water is dirtied, how can it be drunk later?" Xu Fu used yesterday’s words to refute Bo Zhou.

Sang Zhong walked over at this time and laughed, "Master does not know, but in this stream, there are swimming fish, insects, perhaps birds passing by and leaving droppings, and even the saliva of other animals; it was never really clean to begin with. When we drink water, we always boil it before drinking. Besides, we have already reserved water in advance, so it doesn't matter if we use it now; after the stream water flows away, it will purify itself."

After hearing this, Xu Fu’s face turned a bit pale.

Ying Zheng’s face also turned a bit green.

Sang Zhong’s string of words, if one thought about it carefully, was truly disgusting...

In fact, Sang Zhong had even more disgusting things he hadn't said; he was worried that if he really disgusted the King, the King would be furious and kill him right there.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng looked at each other, dismissed the crowd, and without further hesitation, used the stream water to take a simple bath.

It was Ying Zheng who felt it was a pity.

Since it was already this dirty anyway... then they should have dirtied it some more.

But at this moment, Ying Zheng just thought about it.

After the whole group had washed simply, they packed up and headed to Sanchuan again.

Fortunately, after getting back on the road, the sun was not as poisonous; otherwise, sweating every day without being able to bathe, that feeling... I don't know how sour and refreshing it would be. After traveling for about five days like this, the group arrived at Sanchuan District.

chapters.source_text:
嬴政闻言也愣了愣，其他人更是安静得诡异。
胡姬左右瞧了一眼，笑道：“妾可是说错了什么？”胡姬暗自咬牙，难道这个新人如此得大王爱重，她连提也提不得吗？
嬴政扫了一眼徐福的神色，见他双目微瞪，模样倒是比沉着冷静的时候更要讨人喜欢了。徐福长成这样，是容易被误会成是他的男宠。
嬴政没见过那位名满诸国的龙阳君，但他觉得徐福兴许比龙阳君还要出色些。
半天没人发话，徐福就只能自己站出来为自己证清白了。
“想必夫人误会了什么，我只是个太史令。”徐福将“只是”两字咬得重了一点。
胡姬面上闪过尴尬之色，顿时也不敢看嬴政了。她本意是想借此嘲讽徐福两句，谁知道她平时好使的眼光，今天不好使了，竟然闹出这样的笑话来。
嬴政终于开口了，“回去。”
嗯？
徐福和胡姬同时看向嬴政，最后徐福发现这两个字不是对自己说的，再转头看胡姬的脸色，就见对方涂了胭脂香粉的脸颊一阵红一阵白。
胡姬福了福身，模样有些委屈，但她却不敢忤逆嬴政的意思，只能一步三回头地走了。
徐福心道，嘴贱果然是要招霉运的。
等胡姬走了之后，气氛又回归沉寂。大约嬴政也觉得有些尴尬，沉默一会儿后，他便开口，“胡乱之言，无需放在心上。”
徐福点点头，“臣告退。”
赵高随即跟上徐福的脚步，面带笑容地将他送了出去。
嬴政看了一眼徐福的背影，不知道怎的，鬼使神差地冒出个想法来。不知道他若做男宠，又会是什么模样？
宫女进来换香。嬴政的思绪也随着烟飘散远去了。
他抓起竹简翻阅，不一会儿便满面寒霜。加冠礼上，他该狠狠动个手了。
赵高将徐福送走后很快便回来了，他其实是不解的，毕竟加冠礼的日期已经由奉常寺的太史、太祝、太卜共同定下呈上了，为何王上还会让徐福也去测算个日期出来呢？
*
不知是被谁无意中瞥见了赵高在奉常寺出现的身影，奉常寺里顿时又传开了一些流言。有人说，这奉常寺有人得了王上的青睐，指不准将来很快就要升职；还有人说，奉常寺里那位新上任的刘奉常，办事不牢靠，引得王上不喜，说不准这个官帽就要被撸掉；还有人说，赵高说不定是冲着那位那位空降的新人少年来的……
不过最后一个说法刚刚冒出头，就很快被其他人在嗤笑中打消了。
徐福回到奉常寺的时候，恰好也听闻了这些流言，他突然有种我有个大秘密你们谁也不知道的爽快感。走进大厅的时候，徐福的嘴角是微弯的。看着他们猜了半天也没能猜对，他就觉得十分好玩儿。
徐福利用自己的职务之便，翻找起了典籍，他要先看一看史上的记载，避免犯一些秦国的忌讳，然后再根据自己的观测推算得出从中选取最好的日子。
其余同僚见他做出个忙得不亦乐乎的模样来，个个都对他十分不屑，每当从他身边走过，都要轻哼一两声，以示对他的敌意。
徐福完全没放在心上。不是他性格多么善良宽和，而是他的脑子里塞满了事情，怎么可能去关注这种小鱼小虾的表现？如果这些人真有本事，怎么可能还在这里做小官儿，天天与他为难？不过一群跳梁小丑。
那些人也多是欺软怕硬的，见徐福不理会，他们也只能变本加厉地当着面拿话刺徐福。
只是却没人敢再提茅厕的事儿了。
“若是要越快的话，那最好的日子便是……九月三日。”徐福嫌弃拿小刀刻着麻烦，便用手指沾了水在桌面上写写画画，权当打个草稿。
其他人可不知道他在做什么，无意中瞥见他动作的时候，都是取笑道：“神神叨叨的也不知在做什么，这般没有才学之人，实在丢了奉常寺的脸……”
徐福没空去跟他们唇枪舌战，他又低头细细核对了一番。
九月三日，应当是近期内最适宜的日子了。
这时候刚刚入秋，天气也正适宜，不会过分闷热，也不会过分寒冷。
宜祭祀，宜出行，宜冠笄。
徐福又抬手将那些水迹全部抹掉，微皱的眉头慢慢松开来。
因为对这个时代了解还不够深，徐福总觉得还有些什么地方自己没有注意到，但结合典籍翻查一番，他又想不出哪里不对劲。算到这个地步，徐福认为自己也已经尽力了，便不再纠结。
就算不是最好的日期，从他嘴巴里说出来，那也变成最好了。
徐福还是相当相信自己忽悠八级的功底的。
既然已经算出日期了，徐福便也不再耽搁，他起身就往外走了，但是等走出去之后，徐福就傻眼了。不对啊，之前都是赵高来接的他，现在他一介芝麻小官，怎么能主动见到秦王呢？而且出了奉常寺，他连路都不认得。
徐福吐出一口气，激情顿消，只能慢吞吞地又回去了。
而这时候，为秦王加冠礼要做的准备变得更紧要了，奉常寺里忙得团团转，徐福正坐在那儿扮忧郁呢，结果来了个陌生男子将他使唤走了。
“这几日正是最忙的时候，你怎么还在这里坐着？还不快去少府与尚冠丞核对祭祀礼服事宜。”男子力道极大，不由分说地将徐福推出了奉常寺的门。
徐福一脸茫然地看着外面的环境。
少府？
什么鬼地方？
就在他一脸路痴相的时候，那头走来一名中年男子，身后还跟着一名随从。
中年男子穿着一身华贵的衣袍，头戴高冠，五官还算俊朗。
徐福职业病又犯了，盯着人家好好瞧了一会儿，最后忍不住皱了皱眉。
那随从注意到徐福打量的目光，当即上前两步，不客气地斥责道：“哪里来的没眼色的小人？我们家大人，岂是你能打量的？”
如果说本来他还有心提示对方几句，现在见对方一个随从就这么气势嚣张，而那中年男子也极为不屑地瞥了徐福一眼。
不好意思，得罪你大爷我，我就不开这个口了。
徐福不卑不亢地道了声，“恭送。”然后就转身要回奉常寺。
中年男子似乎有什么急事，也没对徐福不依不饶，他加快脚步往前走，那随从却还在低声唾弃徐福，“这等小人，哪里来的狗胆，冒犯丞相，合该好好惩治。”
徐福脚步顿了顿，忍不住回头去看了一眼中年男子离去的背影。
丞相？
官儿这么大？
chapters.title: 第11章
chapters.translated_text:
Ying Zheng was also stunned upon hearing this, and everyone else grew eerie in their silence.

Lady Hu glanced left and right, then smiled: "Did this concubine say something wrong?" Lady Hu secretly gnashed her teeth. Could it be that this newcomer was so deeply favored by the Great King that she couldn't even mention him?

Ying Zheng glanced at Xu Fu's expression and saw his eyes slightly widened, a look that actually made him more endearing than when he was calm and collected. With Xu Fu looking like this, it was easy for people to mistake him for a male favorite.

Ying Zheng had never met Lord Longyang, who was famous throughout the various states, but he felt that Xu Fu might even be more outstanding than Lord Longyang.

When no one spoke for a long time, Xu Fu had no choice but to step forward and clear his name.

"Madame must have misunderstood something; I am merely the Taishi Ling." Xu Fu emphasized the word "merely" slightly.

A look of embarrassment flashed across Lady Hu's face, and she immediately dared not look at Ying Zheng. Her original intention was to mock Xu Fu a little with this, but who would have thought that her usually reliable judgment failed her today, resulting in such a joke.

Ying Zheng finally spoke: "Go back."

Huh?

Xu Fu and Lady Hu looked at Ying Zheng at the same time. Eventually, Xu Fu realized these words were not spoken to him. Turning back to look at Lady Hu's expression, he saw her rouged and powdered cheeks flush red and pale by turns.

Lady Hu curtsied with a somewhat aggrieved look, but she dared not defy Ying Zheng's will and could only leave, looking back three times with every step.

Xu Fu thought to himself, having a sharp tongue really does bring bad luck.

After Lady Hu left, the atmosphere returned to silence. Ying Zheng probably also felt a bit awkward. After a moment of silence, he spoke: "Wild words, no need to take them to heart."

Xu Fu nodded: "This official takes his leave."

Zhao Gao immediately followed in Xu Fu's footsteps, smiling as he escorted him out.

Ying Zheng glanced at Xu Fu's retreating back, and for some inexplicable reason, a whimsical thought popped into his mind. I wonder what he would look like if he were a male favorite?

Palace maids came in to change the incense. Ying Zheng's thoughts drifted far away with the smoke.

He picked up the bamboo slips to read them, and before long, his face was frost-covered. At the capping ceremony, he must make a ruthless move.

Zhao Gao returned very soon after seeing Xu Fu off. In truth, he was puzzled; after all, the date for the capping ceremony had already been jointly determined and submitted by the Grand Astrologer, Grand Invoker, and Grand Diviner of the Fengchang Temple. Why would the King still ask Xu Fu to calculate a date as well?

*

Whether it was accidentally glimpsed by someone who happened to see Zhao Gao appearing in the Fengchang Temple, various rumors immediately began to spread within the temple. Some said that someone in the Fengchang Temple had won the King's favor and might soon receive a promotion; others said that the newly appointed Fengchang official, Liu, was unreliable in his duties and had incurred the King's displeasure, and that his official cap might soon be stripped away; and still others said that Zhao Gao might have come for that parachuted-in newcomer...

However, this last rumor had just surfaced before it was quickly dismissed by others with sneers.

When Xu Fu returned to the Fengchang Temple, he happened to overhear these rumors, and he suddenly felt the exhilaration of "I have a big secret that none of you know about." Walking into the main hall, the corners of Xu Fu's mouth curved slightly. Watching them guess for a long time without ever hitting the mark, he found it immensely amusing.

Using his official position as convenience, Xu Fu flipped through historical records. He wanted to check historical accounts first to avoid violating any Qin taboos, and then make calculations based on his own observations to select the best date.

The rest of his colleagues saw him acting all busy and engrossed, and every single one of them looked at him with utmost disdain. Whenever they walked past him, they would let out a light scoff or two to show their hostility.

Xu Fu didn't pay it any mind at all. It wasn't that his personality was particularly kind and forgiving, but rather that his mind was packed with matters—how could he possibly care about the antics of these small fry? If these people were truly capable, how could they still be minor officials here, making things difficult for him every day? They were merely a bunch of clowns.

Those people were mostly bullies who feared the strong. Seeing that Xu Fu ignored them, they simply escalated and began poking at Xu Fu with pointed words right to his face.

Yet no one dared to bring up the outhouse incident ever again.

"If we want it to be as soon as possible, then the best date would be... September the third." Xu Fu found carving with a small knife troublesome, so he dipped his finger in water and scribbled on the tabletop to use as a rough draft.

The others had no idea what he was doing. When they accidentally caught a glimpse of his movements, they mocked him: "Muttering and mumbling, who knows what he's even doing. Such an unlearned person is truly a disgrace to the Fengchang Temple..."

Xu Fu had no time to engage in a war of words with them; he lowered his head again to carefully cross-check everything.

September the third should be the most suitable date in the near future.

At this time, autumn had just begun, and the weather was just right—neither excessively sultry nor bitterly cold.

Auspicious for ancestral sacrifices, auspicious for travel, and auspicious for the capping ceremony.

Xu Fu raised his hand and wiped away all the water traces, his slightly furrowed brow slowly relaxing.

Because his understanding of this era was still not deep enough, Xu Fu always felt there were places he hadn't noticed, but after reviewing the historical texts, he couldn't think of what was wrong. Having calculated to this extent, Xu Fu felt he had done his utmost and stopped dwelling on it.

Even if it wasn't the best date, coming from his mouth, it would become the best.

Xu Fu still had considerable faith in his level-eight skill at bluffing.

Since the date had already been calculated, Xu Fu didn't delay any further. He got up and walked outside, but once he stepped out, Xu Fu was dumbfounded. That wasn't right. Previously, Zhao Gao always came to pick him up. Now, as a mere sesame-seed minor official, how could he possibly get to see the King of Qin on his own initiative? Furthermore, once outside the Fengchang Temple, he didn't even recognize the roads.

Xu Fu let out a breath, his enthusiasm instantly dashed, and he could only slowly trudge back inside.

At this time, the preparations for the King of Qin's capping ceremony became even more urgent. The Fengchang Temple was spinning in chaos. Just as Xu Fu was sitting there playing the melancholic, a strange man came and ordered him about.

"This is the busiest time of these past few days; why are you still sitting here? Hurry up and go to the Shaofu to cross-check the sacrificial ceremonial attire with the Minister of Crown Adornment." The man used a great deal of force, pushing Xu Fu out of the gates of the Fengchang Temple without any room for argument.

Xu Fu looked dazedly at his surroundings outside.

Shaofu?

What kind of ghost place is that?

Just as he was wearing his lost-lamb expression, a middle-aged man walked over from that direction, followed by an attendant.

The middle-aged man was dressed in lavish robes, wore a tall crown, and had rather handsome facial features.

Xu Fu's occupational hazard flared up again. He stared closely at the man for a while, and finally couldn't help frowning.

That attendant noticed Xu Fu's scrutinizing gaze, immediately stepped forward two paces, and unceremoniously rebuked him: "Where did this unobservant wretch come from? Is our Lord someone you are fit to stare at?"

If Xu Fu had originally intended to give the other party a few hints, now, seeing that even an attendant was so arrogant and overbearing, and that the middle-aged man had glanced at Xu Fu with extreme disdain—

Sorry, but since you've offended your grandpa here, I'm not opening my mouth.

Xu Fu said unctuously yet firmly, "Farewell." Then he turned around to head back into the Fengchang Temple.

The middle-aged man seemed to have some urgent business and didn't hound Xu Fu relentlessly. He quickened his pace and walked forward, while his attendant was still softly spitting venom at Xu Fu: "Such a lowlife, where did he get the dog's courage to offend the Prime Minister? He deserves a sound punishment."

Xu Fu's footsteps paused, and he couldn't help turning back to look at the retreating back of the middle-aged man.

Prime Minister?

An official that big?

Along the way to Sanchuan, Xu Fu and his party felt that the landscape was excessively desolate. Not a single soul was to be seen on the road, giving everything a sense of decay. It was only after entering Sanchuan Commandery that they finally saw people. However, as far as the eye could see, everyone looked miserable and frail. Due to severe water shortages, their cheeks were sunken and their lips were cracked and peeling, as if they had been left out in the sun for days on end.

The expressions on the faces of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were far from pleasant. They had found the lack of water during their few days on the road difficult to bear; how much more miserable must these commoners, who had been suffering from water shortages for nearly a month, be?

Fortunately, the State of Qin had always encouraged its people to store grain, and since Ying Zheng ascended the throne, he had exempted them from many taxes, so they had not yet reached the point of having nothing to eat after a month. As long as they could still fill their stomachs for the time being, these people would not be overly grief-stricken or indignant.

Xu Fu breathed a slight sigh of relief.

The administrative center of Sanchuan Commandery was located in Luoyang. Before they even reached the city, the Commandery Governor had already led his officials to meet them from afar.

But Ying Zheng did not even lift the carriage curtain, his majestic voice echoing from within, "Continue forward."

Shu Hua, the Governor of Sanchuan, trembled slightly, feeling a sense of dread in his heart. Although he had not seen the King of Qin for a long time, he had not missed a single piece of news from Xianyang. The former Chancellor Lu and the former Marquis of Changxin, both figures of immense power, had met tragic ends; who would dare to underestimate the King of Qin? How could Shu Hua not be afraid?

Seeing this, the officials of Sanchuan Commandery hurriedly followed behind Ying Zheng, not daring to make a sound, as they escorted the carriage into Luoyang city.

Two groups of people had arrived in Luoyang one after another. The first was sent by Ying Zheng to scout the situation, but before they had been there long, Ying Zheng himself arrived.

Hearing that the King of Qin had arrived in person, the people of Luoyang had long been gathering on both sides of the streets under the scorching sun. Seeing the carriage enter, followed by the Governor and his officials, the people immediately knew that the King of Qin was inside. Overcome with emotion, they knelt down, shouting "King of Qin" in unison, many of them choking with sobs.

How many people would go their whole lives without ever seeing the King of Qin? Now that they had the chance, how could they not be moved?

With no rain falling in Sanchuan, they had been anxious and panicked, fearing they had offended the gods and lost their protection. But now that the King of Qin had come in person, their worship and blind trust in the monarch made them rejoice, as if the god who could save them had arrived.

They perhaps could not think of much else; they only knew that with the King among them, what was there to fear?

With such simple thoughts, the people shed tears as they watched Ying Zheng’s carriage pass.

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain slightly to look outside. The haggard-looking people were still kowtowing in the direction of the carriage. A lump formed in Xu Fu’s throat, making it difficult to swallow.

Now, he could only hope that a solution would be found soon.

However... although Xu Fu was not well-versed in history, he knew that in ancient times, natural disasters were the hardest to manage. Thinking back to the divination, Xu Fu felt an even greater sense of unease in his heart. Who knew how long this predicament would last...

He could observe the celestial phenomena, but sometimes the heavens were the most unpredictable of all. Xu Fu suddenly felt a sense of self-doubt. Could he really contribute to solving the drought by coming to Sanchuan?

Ying Zheng turned his head, his gaze falling on Xu Fu’s face. Seeing that although his expression remained unchanged, there was a hint of agitation in his eyes, he couldn't help but reach out and cover the back of Xu Fu’s hand. "Not just the State of Qin, but all the states in the past were prone to droughts, and in the end, they were always resolved."

"Droughts lead to famine, refugees, plagues, and riots... will many people die?"

"That is unavoidable."

Xu Fu sighed involuntarily. Only at such moments did he feel how precious his previous life had been. Who had ever worried about water or food? Unlike in ancient times, where natural and man-made disasters could kill thousands or tens of thousands at any moment.

After exchanging a few words with Ying Zheng, the discomfort in Xu Fu’s heart quickly dissipated.

The drought was now unavoidable, but couldn't the famine, refugees, plagues, and riots be controlled? The pessimistic thoughts were quickly driven from Xu Fu’s mind. He shook his head secretly; having traveled all the way here under the scorching sun and seen so much of the people’s suffering, he had almost let his own state of mind be affected.

That wouldn't do!

Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng’s face; it was firm and composed.

It was no wonder he was the emperor of the ages; this level of mental fortitude was unmatched. Even he, who was usually so calm, couldn't help but have a thousand thoughts racing through his mind, yet Ying Zheng remained completely unaffected.

As the two spoke, the carriage arrived outside the Governor’s mansion. Shu Hua dismounted and stepped forward, bowing, "Shu Hua, Governor of Sanchuan, pays respects to the King."

Only then did Bai Zhou approach the carriage and say, "Your Majesty, we have arrived at the Governor’s mansion."

Receiving a signal from Ying Zheng, Xu Fu reached out to lift the curtain and stepped out first.

The officials of Sanchuan Commandery had been bowing their heads, waiting cautiously for the King of Qin to emerge. But when they heard the movement and looked up, they saw a handsome youth in a simple white robe, his hair not yet bound in a crown. The youth carried himself with an air of grace. But... this didn't look like the King of Qin. The King had been on the throne for several years; how could he still look like a youth?

But if this wasn't the King of Qin... then how did he dare to sit in the carriage?

Just as the group was bewildered, the curtain was lifted again, and Ying Zheng stepped out.

Now, no one had any doubts.

Ying Zheng was tall and imposing, dressed in simple robes. The officials didn't even dare to look directly at him, feeling their legs go weak. This aura was not something just anyone could possess. They hurriedly bowed, "Your Majesty."

"Lead the way." Ying Zheng glanced at Shu Hua.

Shu Hua was curious about the identity of the person who had stepped out first, but it was clearly not the time to be distracted. To salvage his image as Governor, he immediately acted like a sycophant, walking in front to lead Ying Zheng’s party inside.

The attendants brought by Ying Zheng were all cold-faced, swords at their waists, as if radiating a murderous aura. Seeing this, the others could only click their tongues in secret and instinctively gave them a wide berth.

"Your Majesty must be exhausted from the journey. I shall arrange for water so Your Majesty can wash up and have some food..." As soon as they entered the hall, Shu Hua bowed low and said.

Ying Zheng glanced at him, his voice laced with sarcasm, "The Governor is quite thoughtful. Have you already made all the decisions for me?"

Shu Hua had only wanted to curry favor with Ying Zheng to show his attentiveness, never expecting this. He was terrified, hurriedly kneeling before Ying Zheng to defend himself, "I had no such intention, please forgive me, Your Majesty! I only... I only..."

Perhaps it was Ying Zheng’s overwhelming presence, but as he looked down at Shu Hua, the dignified Governor couldn't even finish a sentence.

Xu Fu glanced at him, thinking to himself that it was no wonder the Governor had only sent word after a month of no rain. He clearly wasn't a very bright person; he wondered how he had even attained the position of Governor.

Ying Zheng strode to the upper seat and knelt down. Seeing this, the others hurriedly sat down below.

Since the King had sat down, how could they dare to remain standing?

For a moment, in the hall, besides the original servants of the Governor’s mansion, only the attendants brought by Ying Zheng remained standing, along with Xu Fu, who stood by Ying Zheng’s side.

Everyone was suddenly even more curious.

Could this person be a eunuch serving by the King’s side?

But... how could a eunuch look like that?

With such good looks, why would he choose to be a eunuch?

Xu Fu didn't know how their imaginations were running wild; he simply maintained an indifferent posture, observing their appearances, clothing, and expressions.

"Governor, tell me about the disaster situation in Sanchuan."

Hearing Ying Zheng’s voice, Xu Fu knew that the Governor’s attempt at flattery had backfired. Ying Zheng was concerned about the disaster; upon arriving in Luoyang, he naturally asked about it first. As Governor, if he were truly worried about the King’s wrath, he should have explained the situation clearly first before pleading for mercy, rather than pretending to be attentive and arranging food and lodging. This was simply not what a Governor should be doing.

Shu Hua’s face turned pale, clearly realizing this as well. He smiled awkwardly, ordering someone to fetch the records while reporting the situation to Ying Zheng.

Guanzhong had always lacked water. Before Sanchuan belonged to the State of Qin, there had been several major droughts, to the point where one could travel through the commandery and find no signs of human life.

In this era, when a drought occurred, the monarch would send people to organize the migration of the people; this was a common way to provide relief. But so many people had lived here for generations; forcing them to migrate was cruel. Moving from a place where they had land and homes to a completely unfamiliar place, they would be outsiders, and without houses or fields, many troubles would arise.

Currently, in Sanchuan, the well water had not completely dried up, and there were still some rivers or streams nearby; it had not yet reached the point where not a blade of grass could grow.

But Shu Hua had been under immense pressure for the past month, and especially now, under Ying Zheng’s icy gaze, he felt like he was sitting on pins and needles. He couldn't help but suggest to Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, why not move all the people in the commandery away, and when the drought passes, move them back?"

The look Ying Zheng gave him was as if he were looking at an idiot.

Xu Fu also thought this Governor was quite ridiculous.

Was migration that easy? Many people wouldn't want to leave; how would you handle that? Moving people back and forth sounds easy, but they are a group, not a single person. If it were one person, it would be easy to manipulate, like moving a chess piece from one side to the other. But what about a pile of chess pieces? And how would you handle the riots that might ensue?

Before Ying Zheng could mock the Governor’s stupidity, a man suddenly stood up and knelt before Ying Zheng, saying, "Your Majesty, the Governor’s proposal is highly inappropriate."

Hearing this, Shu Hua’s face changed instantly. With the King of Qin right there, he didn't even dare to stop the man from speaking. Being slapped in the face by a subordinate like this was incredibly embarrassing.

"Then what do you suggest?"

"Mobilize people to find water sources. Every household in Sanchuan must conserve water, especially the Governor’s mansion..."

Xu Fu thought to himself, isn't this just "increasing revenue and reducing expenditure"?

Shu Hua could no longer hold back, immediately shouting angrily, "What do you mean by this? Are the dozens of people in my mansion not allowed to use water?"

The man faced Shu Hua without fear, saying coldly, "Using water like the Governor, who, knowing the commandery is short of water, still seeks pleasure with concubines and bathes daily?"

"You... you are malicious, slandering me before the King!" Shu Hua’s face shifted colors like an overturned paint pot; he looked incredibly embarrassed.

"Whether it is slander or not, the King is wise and will naturally have his judgment. Why does the Governor need to argue with me?" The man remained steady, not getting angry at all, as if he didn't care about his superior’s embarrassment. Observing the two, the difference in their character was clear.

Ying Zheng watched this farce coldly. When Shu Hua was left speechless, he finally spoke, "Who are you?"

"Your Majesty, your humble servant is Liu Zixun, the Magistrate of Luoyang."

"Good. I order you to find water sources. Are you willing?"

"Your humble servant is willing," Liu Zixun said excitedly, his face full of admiration for Ying Zheng.

Seeing this, Xu Fu couldn't help but glance at Shu Hua again. This was how a smart person flattered the King. Perhaps in a few days, the positions of these two would be swapped.

Liu Zixun stood up, about to prepare to find manpower, when Xu Fu suddenly spoke, "Magistrate Liu, may I accompany you?"

Ying Zheng’s expression darkened, "What are you going to do with him?"

"Is Magistrate Liu skilled in geography and water conservancy?" Xu Fu looked at Liu Zixun.

Liu Zixun looked embarrassed, "Not skilled, but I can ask the elders in the city and mobilize people to search everywhere."

"Searching aimlessly is a waste of energy and not a good choice. Magistrate Liu is not skilled, but I am," Xu Fu said calmly.

Hearing this, Ying Zheng frowned even more tightly. He looked up at Xu Fu; how did he not know that Xu Fu was skilled in geography and water conservancy?

"This... this..." Liu Zixun looked at Xu Fu, then at Ying Zheng. He didn't know Xu Fu’s identity and didn't dare to refuse easily for fear of offending a noble, but since the King hadn't spoken, how could he agree rashly?

Ying Zheng looked at Xu Fu deeply and said in a low voice, "Go. Take some attendants with you."

Xu Fu nodded and took two steps forward, then suddenly turned back. His eyes met Ying Zheng’s, and Xu Fu curled the corners of his mouth, revealing a faint smile, but it was enough to soothe Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng was still feeling angry, but he was susceptible to Xu Fu’s ways. He withdrew his gaze, pressed down the corners of his mouth that were involuntarily curling up, and with a cold face, continued to assign tasks to the officials.

Liu Zixun was also a person who could read the room. Seeing Ying Zheng’s indulgent attitude toward Xu Fu, he became alert and asked Xu Fu to walk ahead of him. Xu Fu didn't care about walking in front or behind; he wasn't familiar with Luoyang, so it was better for Liu Zixun to lead the way.

"Magistrate Liu, please."

Hearing Xu Fu’s cold, clear voice, Liu Zixun shivered involuntarily. Not daring to continue with pleasantries, he hurriedly turned and walked in front to lead the way.

Xu Fu followed slowly, with Sang Zhong and Jian Jia close behind.

Seeing this, everyone in the hall had a rough idea of Xu Fu’s status.

...He must be someone of very high status by the King’s side. Must not offend! Absolutely must not offend!

As soon as Liu Zixun left the Governor’s mansion, he regained his professional demeanor as the Magistrate of Luoyang. He quickly ordered people to organize manpower, leading the able-bodied men in Luoyang who volunteered to help, along with a few bailiffs, to Xu Fu. Liu Zixun didn't know what official position Xu Fu held, but since he was by the King’s side, he had to treat him as a superior to avoid any accidental offense.

The people of Luoyang had never seen anyone with Xu Fu’s appearance; as soon as they saw him, they all became stiff and awkward.

Xu Fu’s gaze swept over them, making them even more nervous, wishing they could shrink away.

Liu Zixun rubbed his hands together involuntarily and asked with a smile, "What does the Master think of these men as helpers?"

"Just call me 'Sir'," Xu Fu said. "First, send some people to ask the elders in the city where there might be water sources or streams outside Luoyang. You and I will take a few others to search for other water sources."

Liu Zixun nodded repeatedly and sent some people off.

Xu Fu didn't know much about geography, but he knew a thing or two about Feng Shui. Any auspicious Feng Shui location required water; flowing water had good connotations, and water could bring wealth. Therefore, many auspicious locations required winding streams. For Xu Fu, could finding water be difficult for him?

"Are there any 'winnowing basket' terrains surrounded by mountains on three sides, either inside or outside the city?"

Xu Fu was looking for groundwater.

Surface water sources might dry up due to drought, but groundwater would not dry up as quickly. As long as they found a few places with abundant water and dug wells to draw it, it wouldn't be difficult to hold out for a while. It was just that without water for the fields, there would likely be little harvest this year.

Liu Zixun rolled his eyes, thinking carefully. After a while, he clapped his hands, "Yes, yes, there is a 'winnowing basket' terrain surrounded by mountains on three sides to the west of the city."

"Let’s go, lead the way there first to take a look." Xu Fu didn't expect to succeed on the first try. If it didn't work, he would try again; he would eventually succeed. The divination from that day still echoed in his mind. This matter could not be rushed. Haste makes waste.

Liu Zixun led the way, Xu Fu followed slowly, and the helpers trailed behind. The group attracted the attention of many people in the city.

The people looked at Xu Fu’s figure and muttered, "...Is this an immortal descending to earth?"

"The King must have invited an immortal..."

Where Xu Fu could not see, some people secretly knelt and kowtowed in his direction. The fear of the drought made them revere any straw they could grasp for survival.
chapters.title: 第110章
chapters.source_text:
往三川行去的一路上，徐福等人只觉得过分荒凉了些，路上竟是不见半点人烟，顿时让人觉得处处都透着衰败感。等进了三川郡，他们才看见了人影。但是目之所及，皆是面容凄苦衰弱，因为过度缺水，面颊都凹陷进去了，嘴唇也是干裂起皮，就好似放在太阳底下，接连晒了好几天。
徐福和嬴政的脸色都好看不到哪里去。他们在路上几日缺水缺得厉害，便觉难以忍受，那这些缺水将近一月的百姓，岂不是更加悲苦？
幸好秦国上下素来提倡百姓存粮，这几年嬴政即位也免了不少的赋税，倒不至于一个月过去，便连吃食也没了。只要眼时还能果腹，这些百姓就不会过于悲痛或激愤。
徐福微微松了口气。
三川郡治所位于雒阳，还不等行到雒阳，便已经有郡守率领手下大小官，远远地迎上前来了。
但嬴政连车帘都没掀，威严的声音从马车里传了出去，“继续往前走。”
三川郡守叔华身体微微一颤，心中有些畏惧。他虽许久没有见过秦王，但是对咸阳城中的消息却是一点也没漏过的。曾经的吕相，曾经的长信侯，都是位极人臣的人物，他们都落了个悲惨下场，谁还敢小瞧秦王半分？叔华心中如何能不惧？
三川郡的大小官员见状，忙小心翼翼地跟在嬴政之后，谁也不敢发出声来，只拥簇着他们的马车进了雒阳城中。
雒阳城中前后接连来了两拨人，第一拨是嬴政先派来查探情况的，没想到那拨人刚到不久，嬴政便亲至了。
雒阳城中百姓听闻秦王亲至，早早地便顶着日头，汇集在街道两旁了，见马车进来，身后还跟着郡守等人，百姓们立时便知晓，那马车之中便是秦王了。百姓们心情激荡不已，忙跪下来，口中高呼“秦王”，还多有语带哽咽之人。
多少人一辈子也未必能见到秦王一面，如今有缘得见，岂会不激动？
三川干旱不降雨，他们焦急惊慌，担忧着是不是触怒了神灵，才得不到庇佑，但如今秦王亲至，对君王的崇拜和盲目信任，令百姓们欢天喜地了起来，仿佛迎来的便是可以拯救他们的神灵。
他们或许想不到太多，他们只想得到，有王上与他们同在，那还有何畏惧的？
怀着这等单纯心思的百姓们，望着嬴政的车驾，流出了眼泪。
徐福小幅度地掀起了车帘，往外面瞧了瞧，那些模样憔悴的百姓，还在朝着马车的方向磕头。徐福顿时觉得喉咙里像是哽了些什么，实在噎得慌。
如今只能希望，早些找出解决的办法了。
但是……徐福虽然历史不精，但他也知道在古代，天灾是最难治理的。再一想到那卦象的指示，徐福便更觉得心里梗得难受。谁知道这个困境会持续多久……
他能观天象，但有时候天却又是最难测的。徐福突然间对自己升起了几分不信任的感觉，他来到三川，真的能为解决旱灾出一份力？
嬴政转过头来，目光落在徐福的脸上，见他虽然表情没有变化，但眼底却隐隐透着焦躁之色，他不由得伸出手盖住了徐福的手背，“不止秦国，从前各国都极易出现旱灾，到最后，都能解决的。”
“旱灾，会引发饥荒，流民，瘟疫，暴乱……会死很多人吗？”
“这是无可避免的。”
徐福不自觉地轻叹了一口气，这种时刻，他才觉得上辈子的生活实在难得。谁曾为水、粮忧心过？哪像古代，天灾人祸，动不动便死个上千上万的人。
跟嬴政交谈两句，徐福心中的那点不快倒是很快就打消了。
旱灾如今已是避无可避了，但是饥荒、流民、瘟疫、暴乱，却还是可以避免控制的不是吗？悲观的情绪迅速从徐福脑中驱走。徐福暗暗摇头，一路行来，顶着烈日，见多了百姓们凄苦的模样，他倒是险些连心境都被影响了。
这样可不好！
徐福打量了一眼嬴政的面容，坚毅沉稳。
怪不得人家是千古一帝，这份心性，无人能及。自己平日里那样镇定，这时都忍不住心中心思千万，也就嬴政还全然不受影响。
两人说话间，马车已经行到了郡守府外，叔华下马上前，躬身道：“三川郡守叔华见过王上。”
此时柏舟才凑近到马车旁，道：“王上，郡守府到了。”
徐福得到嬴政目光示意，伸手掀起车帘，先一步走了下去。
原本三川郡的大小官员们，都是低着头，小心翼翼恭候着秦王出来，但是他们听见下马车的动静，再一抬头，见着的却是个着普通白袍，连头发也未冠上的俊美少年，那少年举手投足，端的好气度。但……但这也不像是秦王啊……秦王即位数年，如今哪里还会是个少年模样？
可这若不是秦王……那、那他怎么敢坐在马车之上呢？
这群人正懵逼着呢，突然间车帘又是一掀，紧接着才是嬴政走了下来。
这下倒是没谁再怀疑了。
嬴政身材高大，穿着一身普通的衣袍，大小官员们连看也不敢多看一眼，就觉得自个儿有些腿软了。这气势，倒不是谁都能有的。他们忙躬身，“王上。”
“带路。”嬴政看了一眼叔华。
叔华倒是也有些好奇先下来的人是个什么身份，不过显然这个时候是不适合走神的，为了挽回自己这个郡守的形象，叔华马上狗腿地走在了前面，将嬴政一行人引了进去。
嬴政所带的侍从，个个面色冷凝，腰间佩剑，好似带着一身杀气，众人见状，只能暗自咋舌，不自觉地便绕着他们走了。
“王上一路行来，想来已是劳累不已，臣这便安排人去准备水，王上先洗漱一番，用些食物……”一踏进厅中，叔华便立即躬着腰道。
嬴政瞥了他一眼，语带嘲讽，“郡守好生体贴，这是为寡人一并做好决定了？”
叔华本来也只是想讨好嬴政一番，好展露出自己细心的一面来，哪里想到这一茬？闻言顿时大惊失色，忙跪在嬴政的跟前，为自己辩白道：“臣并无此意，还请王上恕罪！臣只是……只是……”
或许是嬴政的气势太强，当他垂着目光看向叔华时，堂堂郡守竟是连句话都说不顺了。
徐福扫了他一眼，心道，难怪三川郡不降雨都有一月了，那郡守才命人来报。看来不是个多么聪明的人物，也不知是如何坐上这郡守之位的。
嬴政大步走到上座跽坐下来，众人见状，忙在下首也坐了下来。
王上都坐下了，他们哪敢站着？
一时间厅中，除了郡守府原本的下人外，便只有嬴政带来的侍从们还站着，以及独独一个徐福，站在了嬴政的身侧。
众人顿时更是好奇不已。
难道这人还是王上身边伺候的内侍？
可这……这哪有内侍长得这般模样啊……
如此好的相貌，做什么不好？怎么会去做内侍呢？
徐福不知这些人如何脑洞大开，他只是摆出了漫不经心的姿态，然后打量着这些人的外貌、衣着、神色。
“郡守将三川郡的受灾情况，讲与寡人听一听。”
听见嬴政的声音，徐福就知道刚才郡守拍马屁的方式，是拍在马腿上了。嬴政心系灾情，一到雒阳，自然是先过问灾情，他身为郡守，若是当真担心嬴政降罪，那也应该先讲清楚灾情，随后再请罪，而不是装作体贴细心，一上来便为嬴政安排衣食住行。这实在不是他一个郡守应该去做的事。
叔华脸色白了白，显然也想到了这一点，他勉强地笑了笑，一边令人取来卷宗，一边与嬴政汇报情况。
关中历来缺水，在三川还不属于秦国的时候，也曾经有过几次大旱，几乎到了入三川境内，遍寻不到人烟的地步。
在这个时代，什么地方发生旱灾，君主便派出人来组织百姓迁移，是比较常见的救灾方式。可是多少人世代居于此地，要令他们迁移，对于他们来说，是太残忍不过的事。从一个原本有地有宅的地方，迁到另外一个全然陌生的地方，他们对于那个地方便是外来人士，没了屋宅和田地，迁移过去之后，也会生出许多麻烦事来。
如今三川郡内，井水尚未完全干涸，周边还有些河流或小溪，还全然未到寸草不生的地步。
但一个月内叔华遭受的压力极大，尤其是现在顶着嬴政冰冷的目光，他便更觉得如坐针毡，于是忍不住向嬴政提出，“王上，不如，将郡内百姓都迁走，待到旱灾过去，再将百姓都迁回来？”
嬴政看向他的目光，都快跟看蠢货一样了。
徐福也觉得这郡守实在好笑得很。
迁移之事哪有那样容易？很多百姓不愿意走的，你要如何处理？迁来迁去，说得容易，但他们是一群人，而不是一个人。若是一个人，拿捏方便，就像是你要从这一边移动一个棋子到另一边，十分容易，但若是一堆棋子呢？引起暴乱又要如何处理？
不待嬴政开口讥讽那郡守的愚蠢，有一男子突然起身跪到嬴政跟前来，道：“王上，郡守此举多有不妥。”
叔华闻言，脸色刹那就变了，偏生秦王在跟前，他连阻拦那男子的话都不敢说，这般被下属打脸，好不尴尬。
“那你认为应当如何？”
“发动人寻找水流，三川郡内，每户人家都要省着用水，尤其是郡守府中……”
徐福暗道，这不正是开源节流么？
叔华再也忍不住了，当即怒道：“你这是何意？我郡守府上下几十号人，难道都不许用水了吗？”
男子丝毫不惧地直面叔华，冷声道：“用水，便是像郡守那样，明知郡内缺水，还要与姬妾寻欢作乐，日日用水沐浴吗？”
“你……你心思歹毒，竟在王上跟前污蔑于我！”叔华脸色变幻，就跟打翻了染缸似的，瞧上去可不是尴尬极了么？
“是不是污蔑，王上英明，自然会有决断，郡守何必在我跟前争辩。”男子倒是稳得住，竟是半点都不与叔华急脸，好似压根不将上级的恼羞成怒放在眼中一般。观这二人处事行为，高下立判。
嬴政冷眼看着这一出闹剧，待叔华被堵得无话可说了，他这才出声道：“你是何人？”
“王上，下臣乃雒阳县令刘子训。”
“好，寡人命你去寻水源，你可愿意？”
“下臣愿意。”刘子训激动道，面上全是对嬴政的仰慕之色。
徐福见状，忍不住又瞥了一眼旁边的叔华。刘子训这般才叫聪明人的拍马屁方法啊。说不定过不了几日，这二人的位置便会对调个个儿了。
刘子训站起身来，正要准备去寻人手，徐福这时才突然出声道：“刘县令可否带上我？”
嬴政面色一沉，“你跟他去做什么？”
“刘县令可擅地理水利？”徐福看向刘子训。
刘子训面带尴尬之色，“不擅，但我能从百姓口中询问，再发动人手，四处搜寻。”
“漫无目的，耗费体力，实在不是个好选择，刘县令不擅，我却是擅长的。”徐福淡淡道。
嬴政闻言，眉头拧得更紧，他抬头看了一眼徐福，他怎么不知，徐福何时擅长什么地理水利了？
“那……这……”刘子训看了看徐福，又看了看嬴政，他不知徐福身份，不敢轻易拒绝以免得罪了贵人，但如今王上又未开口，他如何能贸然答应？
嬴政深深地看了徐福一眼，沉声道：“去吧，带上侍从。”
徐福点头，往前走了两步，然后突然回了个头，目光与嬴政的目光相对接，徐福翘了翘嘴角，露出了个寡淡的笑容来，但是用来安抚嬴政已经足以了。
嬴政心中还浮动着怒气呢，但是偏生他就吃徐福这一套。嬴政收回目光，将不自觉跟着翘起来的唇角往下压了压，冷着脸，继续指派那群大小官员。
刘子训也是个会看眼色的人，见嬴政待徐福态度纵容，心中立刻警觉了几分，请徐福走在自己前头。徐福却根本不在乎走前面还是走后面，他不熟悉雒阳城中，自然还是刘子训走在前带路更好。
“刘县令请。”
刘子训耳中乍然灌进徐福那清冷的嗓音，他不自觉地打了个激灵，也不敢与徐福继续客套下去，忙转过头去走在前面带路。
徐福慢慢跟上去，随后桑中、蒹葭二人紧跟其后。
厅中众人瞧见这一幕，心中对徐福的地位有了个大致的认知。
……应当是王上跟前地位很高的人吧。不能得罪！决不能得罪！
刘子训一出了郡守府，便恢复了他作为雒阳县令应有的职业素质，他很快命人去组织人手，带领雒阳城中自愿帮忙的青壮，以及几名差役，到了徐福的跟前。刘子训不知徐福是个什么官职，偏偏他是王上身边的人，既跟随他而来，那他总要将对方先奉作上级，请示一番，那才能避免不慎得罪对方。
雒阳城中的人哪里见过徐福这等相貌的人，一见了他，立马个个都变得束手束脚起来。
徐福的目光从他们身上扫过，这些人便更紧张了，恨不得将手脚都缩起来才好。
刘子训不自觉地搓了搓手，笑着问道：“他们几人来做个帮手，大人以为如何？”
“称我为先生即可。”徐福道，“你先分些人出去，请教城中老人，瞧一瞧雒阳城外，哪里可有水源溪流。你与我，再带上几人去寻另外的水源。”
刘子训连连点头，先分了几人出去。
徐福是不通什么地理，但他却是对风水略通一二的。凡风水宝地，则是要有水才好，活水有好的寓意，水能带财，所以许多风水宝地，都要求有曲折水流。对于徐福来说，要想寻个水，还能难得倒他吗？
“城中和城外可有三面环山的撮箕地？”
徐福要寻的正是地下水。
地上水源或许会因为干旱而枯竭，但地下水却不至于枯竭得那样快，只要寻到几处水源丰足的地方，再挖井引水，要撑过一段时日并非难事，只是农田没水浇灌，今年恐怕是难有产出了。
刘子训转了转眼珠子，似乎仔细思考，过了会儿，他一拍手掌，“有的有的，城西有三面环山的撮箕地。”
“走吧，先带路往那边去瞧一瞧。”徐福也没打算一次就能成功，一次不成，那便多试几次，总能有成功的时候。他脑中还回荡着那日的卦象。这事，急不得。忙中便容易出错。
刘子训带路，徐福慢慢走在身后，其后还跟着那些帮手，一行人可算是吸引了不少城中百姓的目光。
百姓们望着徐福的身影，讷讷道：“……这可是仙人下凡了？”
“定是王上请了仙人来吧……”
在徐福目光不及的地方，有些百姓还偷偷朝着他的方向跪地磕头。对旱灾的恐惧，让他们对一切可以抓住的救命稻草都变得敬畏了起来。

chapters.translated_text:
The mountain path was difficult to traverse. The group followed behind, watching Xu Fu walk with a brisk, airy grace alongside Liu Zixun. His white robes fluttered, giving him an ethereal, immortal-like appearance. Little did they know, beneath those white robes, Xu Fu’s calves were actually trembling. He was only walking faster to reach their destination sooner and escape the discomfort.

In the blink of an eye, they descended the mountain, arriving exactly at the exit of the winnowing-basket-shaped terrain.

Xu Fu stepped on the ground to test it.

Because it was surrounded by mountains on three sides, this depression was inevitably cool and shaded, and the soil beneath his feet remained slightly damp.

Liu Zixun crouched down to touch the earth, ecstatic. "Is there really a water source here?"

Xu Fu knew that the dampness was merely due to the lack of sunlight, which slowed the evaporation of moisture. Whether there was an actual water source would only be known after digging.

Due to the topography, groundwater easily collected and flowed toward lower areas, and the mouth of the "winnowing basket" was precisely such a low point. Digging a well nearby made it more likely to strike water. If they couldn't find water here, the entire area could be abandoned.

"Dig the well here." Xu Fu pointed at the ground with his toe.

"Dig here?" Liu Zixun’s mouth hung open. "Shouldn't we look around a bit more?"

"No need. If there is no water here, we will have to look elsewhere," Xu Fu said with absolute certainty, leaving no room for doubt.

How could anyone be so definitive? Everyone couldn't help but stare at him, silently trying to shake his resolve with their gazes, hoping he would retract his words. If he were wrong, wouldn't it be embarrassing? Yet, Xu Fu remained completely oblivious to their stares.

"If there are no objections, go find the laborers and prepare to start work," Xu Fu cut them off.

Liu Zixun gave a forced smile. Ultimately, wary of the King of Qin standing behind Xu Fu, he didn't dare argue. "I shall go find the men at once."

After saying this, Liu Zixun felt his legs go weak and his heart flutter with uncertainty. Was deciding so quickly not just child's play? He couldn't help but glance at Xu Fu again. Seeing Xu Fu’s indifferent expression, which somehow carried an air of undeniable authority, Liu Zixun gritted his teeth—decided it was! He didn't know where else to find water anyway. If it failed, it wouldn't be his fault, and if it succeeded, he could take some credit. That was still better than the current Governor.

Seeing that Liu Zixun had agreed, the others didn't say much, though one man glanced at Xu Fu and couldn't help but curl his lip. His expression showed that, while he didn't say it aloud, he looked down on this "noble."

Xu Fu didn't care at all how they looked at him, as long as they could find enough water to survive the drought.

The group immediately returned the way they came.

Xu Fu stood for a moment, his legs already aching, but he had to maintain his composure. He had to fully demonstrate his unwavering authority. How could he show weakness?

On the return trip, Xu Fu didn't walk as quickly, and Sang Zhong keenly noticed that Xu Fu’s gait was slightly unsteady.

It was to be expected. Xu Fu was usually pampered; even when he went out, he was served by a carriage. Apart from his trip to Shu, when had he ever walked such rugged, uneven roads?

Sang Zhong clenched his fists, forcing himself to suppress the urge to step forward and support Xu Fu.

By the time they returned to the Governor’s residence, Xu Fu’s legs felt nothing but numb and sore. Although the others were dissatisfied with Xu Fu’s arbitrariness, they were secretly impressed that such a delicate person had walked the whole way without a single complaint.

Xu Fu left the task of finding laborers to Liu Zixun and stepped into the Governor’s residence.

The attendant guarding the residence spotted Xu Fu immediately, stepped forward, and bowed. "Master Xu, the King is resting inside. Please, follow me."

Xu Fu nodded and followed the attendant.

Sang Zhong sighed softly, feeling a sense of regret. It was precisely because he was so hesitant and cautious that he only dared to watch Xu Fu’s back, never daring to harbor any further thoughts. Jianjia patted his shoulder. "Let's find a place to rest, too. Today has been truly exhausting."

Sang Zhong nodded, his gaze suddenly catching Jianjia’s thinned cheeks. He couldn't help but ask, "Did you lose weight from exhaustion?"

Jianjia shook his head but didn't elaborate.

Originally, when he left Xianyang, he had been quite happy, finally free from the old steward nagging him: "Where is the Madam? Master, go find the Madam you heartlessly abandoned! Master, how could you be so cruel?"

Jianjia had thought the trip to Sanchuan would be free and beautiful. But after leaving Xianyang, under the scorching sun, whenever he felt irritable and wanted to vent to those around him, he would turn his head only to find Bozhou driving the carriage, Gantang being his usual cold self, and Sang Zhong’s mind wandering off to who knows where... and... and the former Lord Longyang was no longer there either. Unknowingly, Jianjia had become melancholy.

After such a toll, how could he not lose weight?

Previously, Xu Fu only knew he was suffering from a bit of homesickness, not realizing that Jianjia’s sorrow had a specific name: "lovesickness."

·

With a creak, Xu Fu pushed the door open, but Ying Zheng was not resting on the bed.

Sunlight spilled into the room, casting long shadows.

Ying Zheng sat at the desk, flipping through bamboo slips, his face taut and his expression cold. If it were anyone else, seeing Ying Zheng like this, they would have fled in fear, terrified that a single cold glance from him would scare the soul out of their body.

Xu Fu’s footsteps were not light, but Ying Zheng didn't turn around even after hearing the noise.

Xu Fu knew he was surely still displeased.

"A-Zheng." Xu Fu called out. His voice was always cool; apart from when they were intimate in bed, Ying Zheng had never heard him use any other tone. Yet, at this moment, his voice was slightly hoarse, easily giving the illusion of provocation.

Ying Zheng’s heart stirred, but he suppressed the urge to look up. He could indulge every decision Xu Fu made, but he also had to express his dissatisfaction and anger so that Xu Fu would learn to consider his feelings. Otherwise, who knew how many years it would take for him to win Xu Fu’s sincere heart.

"A-Zheng."

A gust of wind blew outside, causing Xu Fu’s robes to flutter and his shadow on the floor to sway.

Ying Zheng remained unmoved.

Xu Fu suddenly felt a bit uncomfortable, as if a hand had gripped his heart, squeezed it slightly, and then given it a twist, leaving him feeling indescribably uneasy.

"A-Zheng..." Xu Fu was getting annoyed. Ying Zheng wouldn't even turn to look at him.

He shifted his feet, and the aching numbness spread through his legs—it was unbearable. The combination of physical and mental discomfort made Xu Fu’s mood even worse. He immediately thought of the cold war they had in the carriage earlier. That was a cold war, right? In his past life, it seemed that when young girls were in relationships, that’s what a cold war looked like.

Why was Ying Zheng angry? Because he had ignored his concern?

But... but I am an individual, not an appendage of the King of Qin. If I want to go somewhere, isn't it enough to just inform him? Is there a need to be this angry?

Xu Fu pursed his lips, his racing thoughts suddenly scattering. Fine, he should show weakness to Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu moved again, walking to Ying Zheng’s side. Without a word, his legs gave way, and he collapsed against him.

Xu Fu’s move was so sudden that Ying Zheng was startled and hurriedly reached out to catch him. But because he was unprepared, he was pushed backward by Xu Fu’s weight, and the desk was knocked out of place.

The door was still open, but no one dared to look inside.

Ying Zheng’s expression changed, and he said angrily, "What are you doing? If I hadn't caught you, would you have just fallen like that?" When did Xu Fu learn this trick? Should he praise Xu Fu for being cleverer?

Xu Fu glared at him. "I walked too much, my legs are weak and sore. I can barely walk anymore."

Xu Fu never showed his vulnerability; he always wrapped himself in a cold, aloof exterior, appearing as if his mental world were so strong that no one could pierce it.

But Ying Zheng felt he could still hear a hint of grievance.

Was this Xu Fu’s alternative way of acting spoiled?

Ying Zheng could only pack away his anger and suppress it deep in his heart. He helped Xu Fu sit up. "Do you know why I am unhappy?"

"If you don't say it, how would I know?" Xu Fu said quite frankly.

Ying Zheng was choked by this, but upon reflection, it was true. Xu Fu appeared strong but was actually less attuned to matters of the heart than he was. Other things didn't need to be said, and Xu Fu could be in sync with him, but there were some things that if he didn't say them, Xu Fu would never know.

"Close the door," Ying Zheng said in a measured tone.

The attendants outside immediately closed the door, keeping their heads down, faithfully carrying out the principle of "do not look at what is improper."

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu into his arms, not minding the heat, and said slowly, "I told you long ago that whatever you want to do, I will permit it. But have you thought about what our relationship is now? If you were in danger, how worried would I be?"

"So, it seems your indifference when you agreed to me was all an act?"

"Naturally, it was all an act," Ying Zheng thought to himself. Otherwise, if I showed the anger in my heart, wouldn't it scare you to death?

Every time Xu Fu wanted to run off, Ying Zheng had already imagined various scenarios of binding and forcing him in his mind countless times. However, Ying Zheng had extreme self-control, so he only thought about it and never revealed a shred of it in front of Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was silent for a while. "I know."

He had originally thought he couldn't understand that feeling, as he had never truly worried about anyone. But he suddenly remembered the first time Wei Liao told him the King of Qin was deep and calculating and not to be associated with; the anger and dissatisfaction that had flared up in his heart were almost identical. That was probably the same feeling.

After Xu Fu realized this, he felt a bit guilty when he met Ying Zheng’s gaze.

Although he didn't trust the ways of love, he could clearly feel how good Ying Zheng was to him. Calculating it this way... his own contribution to Ying Zheng was not much. Hmm, and seeing that it would be hard for him to divine for Ying Zheng in the future... he would have even less to offer.

He had to compensate him somehow.

So, unexpectedly, Xu Fu suddenly raised his hand to peel off his robe, revealing a shoulder and a fair neck, and said generously, "Will this appease the unhappiness in your heart, A-Zheng?"

Ying Zheng was stunned, then couldn't help but laugh and cry at the same time.

Xu Fu was always exceptionally clever in some aspects, beyond the reach of others, but in other aspects, he was exceptionally naive, leaving one helpless.

At this moment, Ying Zheng didn't know if Xu Fu was clever or naive, but the scenery before his eyes was truly hard to let go of. Since it was offered voluntarily, he wouldn't be polite. Ying Zheng untied his leather belt and pushed aside his deep robe.

Xu Fu shifted his position, straddling Ying Zheng, and narrowed his eyes slightly. Sunlight filtered through the window paper, landing on Xu Fu’s back, making his expression look alluring in the play of light and shadow.

Xu Fu took the initiative to reach out and undress Ying Zheng’s outer robe.

Their body temperatures rose sharply, and a thin layer of sweat broke out on their backs. The heat, which should have been annoying, instead made the air in the room feel ambiguous.

"Bang, bang," the door was knocked.

"Your Majesty, the water sources, disaster-stricken fields, affected households, existing wells, and the grain reserves in the commandery have all been tallied. Please, have a look." It was Shuhua’s voice, sycophantic and completely ill-timed.

Ying Zheng’s face turned cold.

Xu Fu climbed off him. "Go attend to your business, Your Majesty. I suddenly remembered we haven't bathed yet."

Covered in the dust of travel, they really couldn't do the deed.

Ying Zheng rose with a dark face, straightened his robes, and after Xu Fu had done the same, he walked to the door and opened it.

Shuhua stood outside, hurriedly offering a fawning smile to Ying Zheng. "Your Majesty." He thought to himself, surely the King wouldn't say I was incompetent this time.

Ying Zheng snatched the bamboo slips from his hand and said coldly, "Go prepare some water."

"Does Your Majesty wish to bathe?"

"Yes, a simple wash will suffice." Although the sticky feeling on his body was truly uncomfortable, water was a life-saving resource now. Even as the King of Qin, he couldn't be wasteful.

Shuhua bowed repeatedly and turned to order the servants. Looking at him, one wouldn't see a shred of the demeanor a Governor should have. Xu Fu sat in the room, watching Shuhua’s retreating back, and shook his head secretly.

By the time the water arrived, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had calmed down.

This place was really not a good venue; he would just have to endure it. Once they returned to Xianyang, he would extract his reward from Xu Fu to his heart's content.

Xu Fu didn't know Ying Zheng was already planning their future intimate life. He washed first, then changed into clean robes, feeling much more relaxed. If he hadn't washed, his white robes might have turned gray-yellow before long. He could forget about maintaining any ethereal, otherworldly posture.

If he became disheveled, the mere thought made him shudder.

Afterward, Ying Zheng also washed, changed into clean robes, and sat down to open the bamboo slips.

There were over a hundred wells that hadn't dried up yet. It seemed like a lot, but the Sanchuan Commandery was densely populated, so it probably wouldn't be enough. As for the dried-up fields, there was no need to count them; it was hard to find any crops still alive in Sanchuan.

Ying Zheng closed the bamboo slips, his expression not relaxing in the slightest.

...The situation was truly dire.

The bamboo slips mentioned several households where, due to the extreme heat, fires had broken out. Without water, they couldn't even put them out and had risked their lives to save some belongings. Two families had even lost people because they were too busy grabbing their possessions.

If the drought continued, fires would only increase, and they wouldn't even have the means to fight them.

...

Over the next few days, because of Ying Zheng’s arrival, the disaster relief in Sanchuan Commandery proceeded rapidly, without the slightest delay.

The commoners were quickly gathered to dig wells and draw water, which they could trade for grain.

The hot weather and lack of water easily triggered plagues, so soon after, medical attendants arrived in Sanchuan Commandery to make preparations and prevent an outbreak.

But these were only measures to quench immediate thirst.

Ten days later, a haggard-looking Zheng Guo was brought to Sanchuan Commandery.
chapters.title: 第111章
chapters.source_text:
山路难走，一干人就在后头瞧着徐福脚下生风，同刘子训一起走得极快，身上白袍飘动，让人不由得生出飘渺欲仙之感。他们哪里知道，那白袍之下，徐福的腿肚子其实有些打颤，只是为了减少这种难受的感觉，他才走得更快，好早些走到目的地去。
转眼间，他们就从山上走下来了，落脚处正是撮箕地形的出口处。
徐福踩了踩那处地。
因为三面环山的缘故，这个凹地难免有些阴凉，脚下的泥土还微微有些湿润。
刘子训蹲下身去摸了摸，欣喜若狂，“这里真有水源？”
徐福倒是知道，地上泥土湿润，只是因为光照不及，湿气散的慢而已，究竟有没有水源，还要挖下去才知道。
因为地形原因，地下水很容易在汇集之后，流向低处，而撮箕口恰好就是低处，在那附近打井，更容易引出水来。若是这里都打不出水来，那么这个地方便可以直接放弃了。
“在此处打井。”徐福用脚尖点了点地面。
“在这里打井？”刘子训张大了嘴，“不用再瞧一瞧吗？”
“不用，若是此处无法出水，那便要换个地方再寻了。”徐福说得十分笃定，半点都不含糊。
哪有人能将话一口断得这样死的？众人都忍不住看向他，想默默地用目光来撼动他的想法，让他收回刚才的话。话说得这么死，要是丢脸了，那岂不尴尬？偏偏徐福压根就接收不到他们的目光。
“若是没有异议，便去寻了人手来，准备一番就开工。”徐福一口截断。
刘子训勉强笑了笑，终究还是顾忌着徐福身后站了个秦王，不敢说什么，道：“那我这便去寻找人手。”
刘子训说完这话，都觉得脚下有点飘，心里还发虚。这么快就定下来，真的不是儿戏吗？刘子训忍不住又看了一眼徐福，见徐福神色淡漠，偏偏又是一副让人不得不信服的姿态，刘子训咬咬牙，定就定吧！反正自己也不清楚哪儿一定能找到水源，就算出了错，那总归也不是自己的错，若是找到了水源，自己还能沾点光，总比那郡守强。
其他人见刘子训都应承下来了，自然也不会多说什么，只是有个男子，瞧了徐福一眼，忍不住撇了撇嘴。瞧那模样，嘴上虽然不说，但心底是有些瞧不上这个“贵人”的。
徐福压根不在乎他们拿什么目光看自己，反正只要最后能找到足够撑过旱灾的水源就好。
一行人马上又原路返回。
徐福站了会儿，脚已经有些酸麻了，但是还得维持他那气度啊，得充分向人展现自己说一不二的威严啊。那他怎么能怂？
原路返回的时候，徐福走得就没那样快了，桑中敏锐地注意到徐福步履有些乱。
想来也是，徐福平日里可以说是养尊处优的了，哪怕是出个门都是马车伺候，除了之前去了一次蜀地，之后他还哪里走过什么坎坷崎岖的路？
桑中掐了掐手掌，强忍住想要上前去扶徐福的冲动。
等他们走回郡守府的时候，徐福的双腿已经只感觉得到酸麻了。那些人虽然不服气徐福太过独断，不过他们见徐福这样娇贵的人，一路走下来连吭都不吭一声，心中还有暗自有些佩服的。
去寻人手的事，徐福就直接交给了刘子训，他抬脚进了郡守府。
守在郡守府内的侍从一眼就看见了徐福，马上上前来，躬身道：“徐奉常，王上已经在屋中休息了，请徐奉常随我来。”
徐福点了点头，跟着那侍从走了过去。
桑中轻叹了口气，心中难免升起了些遗憾，也就是他这样瞻前顾后，所以才只敢瞧着徐福的背影，半点多的心思都不敢有。蒹葭拍了拍他的肩，“咱们也寻个地方去歇会儿吧，这一天可真够累的。”
桑中点了点头，目光突然触及到蒹葭瘦了许多的脸颊，不由得问道：“你这是累瘦了？”
蒹葭摇摇头，却没多说。
本来他从咸阳城中离开的时候，还是很高兴的，终于不用再看着老管家在他跟前念叨，夫人呢？主子，快去将你无情抛弃的夫人找回来啊！主子，你怎么能如此负心？
蒹葭想一想便觉得三川之行是自由美好的，但是从咸阳城中走后，顶着烈日，心中烦躁之时，忍不住想向身边人吐槽，结果一转头，柏舟在驾车，甘棠素来冷漠，桑中心神游荡，不知道游到哪儿去了……还有……还有昔日龙阳君，也不在。蒹葭不知不觉间就惆怅了起来。
如此一番折腾，哪里还会不瘦呢？
之前徐福都只知他是有些水土不服，却不知蒹葭心中愁绪，有个别名叫“思春”。
