chapters.source_text:
女子刚一嘶吼出声，村民们都有些尴尬地移开了目光，低声嘟哝道：“哎哟，谁知道那是谁的女儿……”
“可不是嘛……”
徐福实在懒得听下去，再往下听，他都觉得污了自己的耳朵。
他指了指那男子，“叔华，此人也要带走。”
村民们顿时被这道声音吸引走了目光，他们怔怔地看着徐福，听着徐福直呼郡守的名字，敬畏和恐惧瞬间就从心底冒了出来。他们哪里见过徐福这样夺目的人物？方才见徐福骑在那高头大马之上，这些村民就已经心生畏惧了，此刻见人走近了，村民们就不自觉地想要往后退缩。
那男子倒是毫不畏惧，转过头来嗤笑一声，一身流里流气的味道，“带走我？疯了吗你，应该带走的是这个女人！难道你还要给这个女人出头？”男子全然没注意刚才徐福开口叫的是郡守的名字。
连郡守的名字都敢直呼，徐福能是什么小人物吗？能是他惹得起的吗？
嬴政就站在一旁，叔华身上压力倍增，他抬手重重地甩了那男子一巴掌，“刁民！我看你才疯了！”
反正徐福开口了，叔华立刻让差役上前，“把这个男人也带走。”
这个时候嬴政才缓慢道，“还有此人，一并带走。”
另一男子也被点到了。
那名男子反应更为激烈，“凭什么抓我？是郡守就能随意抓人了吗？”
嬴政连看都没看他一眼，冷声道：“这二人身上也染了疫病。”
“啊！”村民们吓得大惊失色，连忙避开那二人。
刚才那对母女凄苦无助的时候，他们二人还在肆意嘻笑，却不曾想现在他们也被村中人视作污秽肮脏，恨不得远远避开。
方才还叫嚣着的要将这对母女扔进火堆去的男子，这时脸色都白了，只梗着脖子高声叫道：“不可能，我不可能染病……我……”
蒹葭冷着脸上前一脚将他踹翻在地，落脚时刚好落在他的脸上，堵得他一句话也喊不出来了，男子正要挣扎，蒹葭脚下一使力，他就不敢再乱动了。
差役都被他吓了一跳，顿时频频看向蒹葭，眼中又是佩服又是敬畏。
差役将男子拎了起来，堵上他的嘴。另外一名男子见状浑身哆嗦，哪里还敢反抗？只能顺从地被差役带走了。
而那女子将女儿紧紧拥在怀中，目光呆滞，神色漠然，哪怕那欺侮她的丈夫先被带走，她也丝毫反应都没有。
叔华心头恼恨，真恨不得命人将她推入火堆里去。
徐福慢慢走到那女子跟前。
嬴政脸色微变，想要拉住徐福，但最后还是压住了这股冲动。
徐福并未跟那女子搭话，而是微微俯身，与那小姑娘保持平行，问她：“你叫什么？”
小姑娘还有些害怕，抽泣了两声，不自觉地对上徐福的目光，“丫头。”她的声音又低又细，带着几分怯怯的味道。
见惯了扶苏、胡亥这样的小孩儿，乍一见这么乖巧怯弱的小姑娘，徐福倒是多了些耐心。
“丫头，你怕死吗？”
小姑娘不一定知晓死是什么，但是她本能地流下了眼泪，泪汪汪地看着徐福。
“我给你一口仙气，你把它攥在手里，紧紧的，不要放。若你觉得自己很难受的时候，就张开手掌，仙气就会救你了。知道吗？”
小姑娘点点头，怯怯地问：“……可以、可以给两口吗？还、还有阿娘的。”
“你伸手给我。”
小姑娘伸出了手，徐福像模像样地随手虚空一抓，然后放在了小姑娘的掌心，小姑娘绷紧了身体，紧张地合紧了手掌，“……好了吗？”
“好了。”徐福没再说多余的话，他直起身子走开了。
周围的人目瞪口呆地看着这一幕。
虽然众人都是崇拜神灵的，但他们也没见过这等敷衍了事的举动啊，随手一抓，我说是仙气，便是仙气了吗？长了一副好模样，怎么脑子不太行呢？
那小姑娘紧紧握着手掌，一脸小心翼翼，生怕那两口仙气就这样飞走了。
徐福这番话当然不是用来诓骗小姑娘，他是说给那女子听的。
世间许多女子为母则强，那女子方才神色漠然，像是已经对活下来失去了盼头和坚持。一旦没了希望，她还如何带着她的女儿从病痛中挣扎着活下来？徐福所为，不过是给小姑娘一根活下来的稻草，精神上的支柱，而给那女子的，却是要用小姑娘求生渴望的模样来敲醒她，让那女子知道，她不能带着女儿去死。
活下来比死要艰难，但是一旦心头还有着牵挂，就舍不得死了。
徐福走回到嬴政的身边，叔华尴尬道：“王上，这……”
“寻地安置，派以大夫。”嬴政冷淡地交代了四个字，便紧紧箍着徐福的手腕，将人带着转身就走了。
见多了徐福诓人的桑中等人，一脸淡定地跟随着也转身离开。
村民们小心地看着他们上马走远，这才松了口气，低低地议论起来，说那人长得可真好看，又说那人怎么好端端的装神仙骗人……
女子似乎将这些声音都无视，她紧紧抱着女儿从地上缓慢地站起来，开口对那差役道：“走吧……”刚才的嘶吼让她耗尽了力气，如今的嗓音沙哑难听。
村民和差役们依旧对她避而远之，连碰也不敢碰。
但她眼中的绝望和悲痛却陡然消失了，转而迸发出黑亮的光芒来。
小姑娘还紧紧地攥着那只手，一刻也不敢放松，她们相互依靠着走开，走出了这片被烧得一片焦黑的土地。
……一定，一定能活下去的！
·
回城路上，徐福依旧和嬴政同骑一马，他靠在嬴政的胸膛前，扯了扯嬴政的衣袍，“王上可是又生气了？”
嬴政并没回答他的话，转而道：“寡人与你说的话，如今看来，是一句也未曾放在心上。”
徐福觉得有点心虚。
“我只是觉得这是个很好的机会。”
“什么机会？”
“我看出了那小姑娘能熬过这一劫，她若不死，自然会有人将我奉若神明，那时，蜡祭之后大灾带来的影响，自会消散，且若我在三川郡有了两分薄名，日后做了国师，才更叫人信服不是吗？”
“……”
“王上？”
“……”
“阿政？”
“……你还是先好好思考一番，这次又如何取得寡人原谅吧。”
徐福垂下眼眸。
三十六计……光美人计就可以百战百胜了啊。
chapters.translated_text:
As soon as the woman let out a hoarse cry, the villagers shifted their gazes in embarrassment, muttering under their breath, "Oh my, who knows whose daughter that is..."

"Indeed..."

Xu Fu really couldn't bear to listen any longer; he felt his ears would be sullied if he heard another word.

He pointed at the man, "Shuhua, take this person away as well."

The villagers were instantly drawn by this voice. They stared blankly at Xu Fu, hearing him address the Governor by his given name, and awe and fear welled up from the depths of their hearts. Where had they ever seen someone as striking as Xu Fu? Just seeing him atop that tall, majestic horse had already filled them with dread; now that he was close, the villagers instinctively wanted to shrink back.

The man, however, was completely unafraid. He turned his head and sneered, reeking of a hooligan's air, "Take me away? Are you crazy? It's this woman who should be taken away! Are you trying to stand up for her?" The man had completely failed to notice that Xu Fu had addressed the Governor by his name.

Daring to address the Governor by his name—could Xu Fu be just some nobody? Could he be someone he could afford to provoke?

Ying Zheng was standing right beside them. The pressure on Shuhua increased tenfold. He raised his hand and slapped the man hard across the face, "You insolent peasant! I think you're the one who's crazy!"

Since Xu Fu had spoken, Shuhua immediately ordered the bailiffs forward, "Take this man away too."

It was then that Ying Zheng said slowly, "And this one as well, take him along."

The other man was pointed out too.

That man reacted even more violently, "On what grounds are you arresting me? Just because you're the Governor, can you arrest people at will?"

Ying Zheng didn't even glance at him, saying coldly, "These two have also contracted the plague."

"Ah!" The villagers were terrified and scrambled to stay away from the two men.

Just moments ago, when the mother and daughter were miserable and helpless, these two had been laughing wantonly. Now, they were viewed by the villagers as filthy and unclean, and everyone wished to stay as far away as possible.

The man who had been clamoring to throw the mother and daughter into the fire turned pale. He stiffened his neck and shouted, "Impossible, I couldn't have caught the disease... I..."

Jianjia stepped forward with a cold face and kicked him to the ground, her foot landing squarely on his face, stifling his words. As the man struggled, Jianjia applied pressure, and he dared not move again.

The bailiffs were startled by her, casting frequent looks of admiration and awe toward Jianjia.

The bailiffs hauled the man up and gagged him. Seeing this, the other man trembled all over; how could he dare to resist? He could only submit and be led away by the bailiffs.

As for the woman, she held her daughter tightly in her arms, her gaze dull and her expression indifferent. Even when her abusive husband was taken away first, she showed no reaction at all.

Shuhua felt a surge of resentment; he truly wished he could order someone to push her into the fire.

Xu Fu walked slowly up to the woman.

Ying Zheng’s expression shifted slightly, and he wanted to pull Xu Fu back, but he ultimately suppressed the urge.

Xu Fu didn't speak to the woman; instead, he leaned down slightly to be at eye level with the little girl and asked, "What is your name?"

The little girl was still frightened. She sobbed twice and instinctively met Xu Fu’s gaze, "Ya Tou." Her voice was low and thin, filled with a sense of timidity.

Having grown accustomed to children like Fusu and Huhai, Xu Fu found himself with more patience upon seeing such a well-behaved and timid little girl.

"Ya Tou, are you afraid of dying?"

The little girl didn't necessarily know what death was, but she instinctively shed tears, looking at Xu Fu with watery eyes.

"I will give you a breath of immortal energy. Hold it in your hand, tightly, and don't let go. If you ever feel very unwell, open your palm, and the immortal energy will save you. Do you understand?"

The little girl nodded and asked timidly, "...Can, can you give me two breaths? One... one for Mother too."

"Give me your hand."

The little girl extended her hand. Xu Fu made a show of grabbing something from the air and placed it in her palm. The little girl tensed her body and nervously closed her hand, "...Is it done?"

"It is done." Xu Fu said nothing more and stood up to walk away.

The surrounding people stared at this scene, dumbfounded.

Although everyone worshipped the gods, they had never seen such a perfunctory act. A casual grab, and just because he said it was immortal energy, it was? He had such a handsome face, so why wasn't his brain working right?

The little girl held her palm tightly, looking cautious, terrified that the two breaths of immortal energy might fly away.

Of course, Xu Fu’s words weren't meant to deceive the little girl; he was saying them for the woman to hear.

Many women in this world become strong for their children. The woman had been indifferent just now, as if she had lost all hope and persistence to live. Without hope, how could she struggle to survive the illness with her daughter? What Xu Fu did was merely to give the little girl a straw to cling to—a spiritual pillar. And for the woman, he used the little girl’s desire to live to wake her up, letting her know that she could not take her daughter to the grave.

Living is harder than dying, but once there is something to hold onto in one's heart, one cannot bear to die.

Xu Fu walked back to Ying Zheng’s side. Shuhua asked awkwardly, "Your Majesty, this..."

"Find a place to settle them, and send a physician." Ying Zheng gave these four cold instructions, then gripped Xu Fu’s wrist tightly and turned to leave.

Sang Zhong and the others, who had seen Xu Fu deceive people many times before, followed calmly as they turned to leave as well.

The villagers watched them mount their horses and ride away before they finally relaxed and began to whisper, saying how good-looking that man was, and how strange it was for someone like him to pretend to be an immortal to trick people...

The woman seemed to ignore these voices. She held her daughter tightly and slowly stood up from the ground, saying to the bailiff, "Let's go..." Her previous screaming had exhausted her strength, and her voice was now hoarse and harsh.

The villagers and bailiffs still kept their distance, not even daring to touch her.

But the despair and grief in her eyes suddenly vanished, replaced by a bright, dark glow.

The little girl still held her hand tightly, not daring to relax for a moment. They leaned on each other and walked away, exiting that patch of land scorched black by the fire.

...They must, they must be able to survive!

·

On the way back to the city, Xu Fu was still riding the same horse as Ying Zheng. He leaned against Ying Zheng’s chest and tugged at his robe, "Is Your Majesty angry again?"

Ying Zheng did not answer his question, instead saying, "It seems that not a single word I said to you has been taken to heart."

Xu Fu felt a bit guilty.

"I just thought it was a very good opportunity."

"What opportunity?"

"I could see that the little girl would survive this ordeal. If she doesn't die, others will naturally hold me in high regard as a god. By then, the impact of the great disaster following the Wax Festival will naturally dissipate. Besides, if I gain a bit of a reputation in Sanchuan Commandery, won't it be more convincing when I become the State Preceptor later?"

"..."

"Your Majesty?"

"..."

"A-Zheng?"

"...You had better spend some time thinking about how to earn my forgiveness this time."

Xu Fu lowered his eyes.

The Thirty-Six Stratagems... the beauty trap alone is enough to win every battle.
chapters.title: 第113章

chapters.translated_text:
With a plan in mind, Xu Fu felt a bit more emboldened.

Seeing that they were about to reach the commandery governor's residence, Ying Zheng looked down and was so angry he almost wanted to flip Xu Fu over and give him a beating. He had been counting on Xu Fu to show some guilt, anxiety, or internal conflict, but he couldn't find a trace of such emotions. The expression on Xu Fu's face was as open and guileless as could be.

Ying Zheng pulled a long face and dismounted, and Xu Fu habitually reached out to lean on Ying Zheng’s shoulder.

The horse was too tall; if he jumped down directly, Xu Fu was genuinely worried he might sprain his waist or legs.

Ying Zheng walked forward a few steps, and Xu Fu’s hand grasped at empty air. Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng’s back—did he seem... even angrier?

By this time, Sang Zhong had already dismounted and walked over, asking in a low voice, "Does Master need any help?"

They had traveled together many times, and Sang Zhong knew that Xu Fu was not skilled at horse riding.

How could Ying Zheng not hear Sang Zhong’s voice? He immediately changed his mind, stopped in his tracks, turned back, and reached out to scoop Xu Fu off the horse’s back. The movement was smooth and fluid, without a single pause.

Sang Zhong hurriedly lowered his head and stepped aside, a look of dejection on his face.

To avoid being left behind by Ying Zheng, Xu Fu quietly reached out from under his sleeves and grabbed onto Ying Zheng’s robe. He lagged half a step behind, and as they walked, no one noticed the small movement of Xu Fu’s hand. Only Ying Zheng felt his clothes tugging downward with every step; if the fabric hadn't been of such high quality, it probably would have let out a "rip" and torn open.

Ying Zheng felt an indescribable mix of anger and amusement.

Once they entered the main hall, someone knelt before Ying Zheng and said, "I implore the King to return to Xianyang."

Xu Fu glanced at the man; he was covered in dust, looking as if he had just rushed over from Xianyang.

Ying Zheng was somewhat surprised. "Has something happened in Xianyang?"

Xu Fu was also surprised. They hadn't been gone for long, and besides, the people left in the court were the pillars of the Qin State—Wei Liao, Li Si, Zhao Gao—who among them was easy to deal with?

The man looked solemn and said in a low voice, "Since the King and Master Xu left, there has been no rain in Xianyang."

Ying Zheng’s expression turned stern in an instant.

Ying Zheng might not personally intervene in how other places suffered from drought or water shortages, but Xianyang was absolutely different. How could the capital of the Qin State have problems? If something went wrong in Xianyang, the royal family, the nobility, and the talented scholars of Qin would all suffer; it would be equivalent to destroying the foundation of the state.

Long before this, rulers had linked drought and floods to the governance of the country. If one could not manage a drought, how could one manage a country?

"It’s been over half a month..." Xu Fu remarked.

"Pack up. We depart for Xianyang tomorrow," Ying Zheng decided decisively.

Xu Fu hesitated. Should he follow immediately as well? He still felt concerned about those who had fallen ill; how could he set his mind at ease without waiting for the epidemic to fully subside?

But what if the same thing was happening in Xianyang?

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng, but Ying Zheng didn't even spare him a glance. He stood up and walked away quickly, calling for attendants to summon the officials of Sanchuan Commandery. It seemed Ying Zheng had many things to do and was too busy to pay him any mind.

Xu Fu felt a bit bitter in his heart.

The First Emperor of Qin was a petty person.

He was even willing to offer himself up to seek forgiveness, yet Ying Zheng was still angry?

Xu Fu had completely forgotten that he had once argued with Wei Liao for a long time about whether Ying Zheng was broad-minded or narrow-minded, almost rolling up his sleeves to fight.

Xu Fu stood silently to the side, his face cold, putting on airs as well.

As soon as the officials of Sanchuan Commandery entered the hall, they felt a cold wind blowing.

But it was clearly the height of summer... Could it be that they were so guilty that they felt a chill throughout their bodies?

The officials knelt before Ying Zheng and took a cautious look, and their souls nearly left their bodies.

It was finally coming... The little people in the officials' hearts were shivering and curling up, silently weeping. The day had come; the King was finally going to punish them for their incompetence.

"Where is Shu Hua?"

"This subordinate is here." Shu Hua knelt tremblingly before Ying Zheng, his back slightly hunched, showing none of his former high spirits.

...

As Xu Fu watched, he found he couldn't take in a single word. Clearly, when they first arrived at Sanchuan Commandery, he had also stood by Ying Zheng’s side, silent, watching Ying Zheng issue orders, but why didn't it feel as strange then as it did now? It was as if he couldn't fit in.

Feeling stifled, Xu Fu turned and walked out.

Although everyone kept their heads down, they noticed Xu Fu leaving. They immediately felt a chill down their spines. Had the King ordered him to go get something? What was it? Evidence of their crimes? Or a headsman's sword? Or a dagger for cutting off noses?

The more they thought about it, the colder they felt...

Meanwhile, Xu Fu walked to the door and called for Sang Zhong and Jian Jia. "Go and ask where that mother and daughter have been settled."

Jian Jia didn't think much of it and turned to find an officer to ask, but Sang Zhong’s expression was a bit strange. He couldn't help but ask, "Master, being concerned about those two for no reason might not be very good..." The hidden meaning in Sang Zhong’s words was to remind Xu Fu not to provoke the King for nothing and cause a misunderstanding. Seeing that the woman was plain-looking, Sang Zhong didn't think Xu Fu had any romantic intentions.

"If it were anyone else who had contracted the plague, I would be just as concerned. The plague is a major issue. If the Qin State were to suffer a widespread epidemic because of this, how could I tolerate it?" Xu Fu worried that the wings of this butterfly he had flapped would change the future of the entire Great Qin. If it caused extra trouble for Ying Zheng’s journey, how could that be allowed?

Sang Zhong moved his lips, but in the end, he said nothing.

By this time, Jian Jia had returned with the information and had even brought a carriage. Xu Fu got into the carriage. "Go find those two."

He was going to leave with Ying Zheng, so he had to tidy up loose ends before departing.

The carriage soon left the city again.

The mother and daughter had been settled in a mountain cave. In this weather, staying in a cave was a decent shelter. Now that the village had been destroyed and they had nowhere to go, building a thatched hut would likely be more prone to catching fire.

It was just that the location of the cave was a bit remote.

Xu Fu’s legs felt weak as he walked. Just as the cave came into view, he suddenly heard a scream, followed by a woman’s angry curse: "If you have the guts, touch me! I'll make sure you end up with rotting limbs just like me!"

Xu Fu’s expression turned colder, and he forgot about his weak legs, quickening his pace.

Jian Jia bypassed Xu Fu and walked in front, so that if there were any danger in the cave, he could protect Xu Fu.
chapters.title: 第114章
chapters.source_text:
心中有计，徐福多少有了点儿有恃无恐的心理。
眼看着他们便要到郡守府跟前了，嬴政低头瞧了一眼，差点气得没将徐福倒拎起来揍一顿。他还指望徐福能表露点愧疚、忐忑、纠结的情绪来，结果半点情绪也找不到。徐福脸上的表情，坦荡得不能再坦荡。
嬴政拉着脸翻身下马，徐福习惯性地伸手要去搭嬴政的肩。
这马太高，他直接跳下来，徐福实在有些担忧自己会不会闪了腰，或是闪了腿。
嬴政往前走了几步，徐福的手顿时就摸了个空，徐福瞅了一眼嬴政的背影，好像……更生气了？
此时桑中已经下了马，走上前来，低声问道：“先生可要帮一把？”
他们同行的次数也不少了，桑中知晓徐福不擅骑马。
嬴政怎么会听不见桑中说话的声音，当即主意一变，顿住脚步又转身回来，伸手将徐福从马背上捞了下来，动作一气呵成，行云流水，不带半点停顿。
桑中忙低下头退到一边去，脸上的神色有几分黯然。
为了避免被嬴政甩在后面，徐福的手悄然从袖袍下伸了出来，而后抓住了嬴政的衣袍，他稍稍落后嬴政半步，二人走动间，无一人发现徐福手上的小动作，只有嬴政每走一步都感觉自己衣服往下坠了坠，若非质量过硬，恐怕就要“嘶啦”一声，扯出条口子来了。
嬴政心中说不出的又好气又好笑。
待走进了大厅之中，有人往嬴政面前一跪，道：“请王上回咸阳。”
徐福抬眼瞥了那人一眼，一身仆仆风尘，看上去像是刚从咸阳城赶过来的。
嬴政有些惊讶，“可是咸阳城中出了何事？”
徐福也有些惊讶。他们离开的时日并不算久，何况朝中留下的人，都是秦国栋梁，尉缭、李斯、赵高，谁是好对付的人？
那人面色沉重，低声道：“自王上同徐奉常离去后，咸阳城中便也未再降雨了。”
嬴政的脸色瞬间就肃穆了起来。
旁的地方如何干涸，如何缺水，嬴政或许可以不亲自插手去管，但是咸阳却是绝对不行的。秦国都城，怎能出事？若是咸阳城中出了事，那秦国的王室贵族和有才之士都要遭殃，相当于会毁坏一国根基。
早在更早之前，便有君王将旱灾、水祸同治国联系起来，若是旱灾不能治，焉能治国？
“有大半个月了……”徐福出声道。
“收拾一番，明日启程回咸阳。”嬴政当机立断。
徐福有些犹豫，他也应该立即跟着离去吗？他心中还有些牵挂染了病的人，不等到疫病完全消退，他怎么能放下心呢？
但是咸阳城中万一也出了同样的事呢？
徐福看向了嬴政，而嬴政却连一个眼神也没给他，起身便快步走了，他叫来侍从吩咐那人去叫三川郡的官员前来，瞧上去嬴政还有许多事要做，忙得没空搭理他。
徐福心底有点酸。
秦始皇是个小气鬼。
他都要献出自己去取得原谅了，嬴政竟然还生气？
徐福全然忘记了，从前他还和为嬴政心胸宽大还是狭隘一点，和尉缭争辩了许久，就差没撸袖子揍人了。
徐福默默地站在一旁，冷着脸，也端上了架子。
那些三川郡大小官员一进厅来，就觉得冷风飕飕。
这可明明是大热天啊……难道是他们太过心虚，才觉得浑身发冷？
官员们跪在嬴政的面前，小心翼翼地瞧了一眼，这三魂七魄就差点去了一半。
终于要来了……官员们心底的小人儿瑟瑟发抖，蜷缩起来默默流泪。待到今日，王上终于要处置他们这些办事不利的人了。
“叔华何在？”
“下官在。”叔华颤巍巍地跪在嬴政面前，背微微躬着，瞧不出半点意气风发来。
……
徐福看着看着，就觉得什么话也听不进耳中去了。明明刚到三川郡的时候，也是他站在嬴政身旁，默默不语，看着嬴政发号施令，但那时怎么就没有现在的怪异感呢？就好似他插不进去似的。
徐福觉得有些气闷，便转身出去了。
众人虽然都低着头，但也注意到徐福走出去了，他们顿时觉得背脊发凉，难道王上令他出去取什么东西了？是取什么？罪状证据吗？还是砍头的大刀？还是割鼻子的匕首？
越想越觉得浑身发冷……
而这厢徐福走到门口，叫上桑中和蒹葭二人，“去问一问，那对母女被安置在何处了？”
蒹葭倒是并未多想，转身就去找差役来问了，倒是桑中神色有些怪异，不由得问道：“先生无端对那二人上心，怕是有些不大好……”桑中话里暗藏的意思，其实就是提醒徐福一下，不要因此白白触怒王上，让王上起了误会。桑中瞧那女子容貌普通，倒是没觉得徐福会有什么怜香惜玉的心。
“若是换做别人染了疫病，我也会上心一分。疫病乃是大事，若是秦国因此瘟疫蔓延，那我如何能容忍？”徐福担心自己这只蝴蝶扇动的翅膀，改变了整个大秦的未来。若是害得嬴政征途之中平添麻烦，那怎么行？
桑中动了动唇，最后倒是什么也没说出来。
此时蒹葭已经打听出结果回来了，还顺便牵了马车过来，徐福坐上马车，“去寻那二人。”
他要随着嬴政走的，走之前总要料理个干净。
马车很快又出了城。
那对母女被安置在了一处山洞之中，在这样的天气里，呆在山洞里也算是不错的栖身之所了。如今村庄被毁，无处可去，若是搭个草庐，恐怕更容易起火。
只是那山洞的位置，稍微偏了一些。
徐福走得有些脚软，眼看着那山洞就在不远的前方了，他突然听见一声尖叫，随后便是女子的怒骂声，“你有胆子便来碰我！好叫你也同我一样，烂了手脚！”
徐福面色更冷，倒是忘记了脚软，加快了脚步。
蒹葭绕过徐福走在了前方，若是那山洞中有什么意外，他也好护着徐福。

chapters.title: 第115章
chapters.translated_text:
The people in the cave must have heard the footsteps as well. Xu Fu followed closely behind Jianjia to the cave entrance, where he immediately saw the man squatting on the ground turn his head viciously, his bloodshot eyes glaring at the entrance.

It was the very man the woman had previously referred to as "Wang Laosan."

On one side of the cave entrance, the woman was huddled. She looked at Wang Laosan coldly, a malicious smile appearing on her face.

Wang Laosan recognized Xu Fu, and a sudden surge of resentment rose in his heart.

It was him! It was he who ordered the bailiffs to arrest him too, and it was he who caused him to be stuck with this stinking woman!

How could Xu Fu not sense the savage gaze in Wang Laosan's eyes? Before he could even speak, Jianjia sneered, drew the long sword from behind his waist, and walked up to Wang Laosan.

Wang Laosan, who had originally rolled up his sleeves preparing to teach Xu Fu a lesson, stared blankly, his legs suddenly turning to jelly. He stammered, "W-what are you doing?"

Jianjia held such men in deep contempt. He let out a disdainful snort and, without saying a word, continued walking toward Wang Laosan without stopping. His handsome face looked terrifyingly ferocious in Wang Laosan's eyes, causing the man to retreat repeatedly.

Xu Fu didn't watch what Jianjia was about to do; he walked over to the woman. Only then did he notice her daughter lying beside her, eyes closed, cheeks flushed, looking as if she were suffering from a high fever. The little girl’s hands were tightly clenched, not loosening in the slightest even in her delirium.

The woman slowly raised her head, her vision taking a long moment to clear. When she saw Xu Fu, she hurriedly straightened her back, wanting to stand up, but she was so weak that she lacked the strength; as soon as she put force into her legs, she sat back down.

"I beg you, sir, please summon a physician for me..." the woman said, her voice gentle and piteous, showing none of the sharp coldness she had displayed earlier.

"There are physicians assigned to look after you all," Xu Fu frowned. "What happened? Did they not come?"

The woman shook her head repeatedly, tears sliding down her cheeks.

"Ahhh! Don't kill me!" A howl suddenly erupted in the cave. Xu Fu turned to look and saw that the long sword in Jianjia's hand was now stuck in the ground right next to Wang Laosan's face. Wang Laosan was clutching his face, screaming in a breakdown, his legs trembling uncontrollably as if he were about to lose control of his bladder.

Jianjia pulled back his sword and said disdainfully, "Coward!" He then turned and walked back.

Wang Laosan curled up there, shivering. Even when he heard the footsteps moving away from him, he dared not lower his hands from his face.

Xu Fu frowned slightly; he truly was a bully who feared the strong.

Such a man was truly unworthy of this woman.

Sang Zhong slowly stepped forward and said, "When we left the city, I had already ordered the bailiffs to bring a physician."

The woman let out a sigh of relief, though her expression remained somewhat dazed. It was fortunate; Luoyang City had not left them to fend for themselves. If that man died, so be it, but she could not bear to let her daughter die.

The woman slowly regained her composure and said to Xu Fu, "Thank you, sir."

"No need," Xu Fu looked at her and said very earnestly, "The two breaths of immortal energy I gave you can truly save your lives; you must hold onto them." Xu Fu's voice was very soft, yet it carried a miraculous, soothing power.

The woman was stunned. She didn't believe in such things...

But how could this person be so certain that they were truly two breaths of immortal energy?

At this moment, a man's voice cut in, "What immortal energy? It's all a lie! We are all going to die! No one will survive! Wang Laosan, it's all your wife's fault for infecting us too."

The woman sneered, her tone sharp, "Blame me? Wang Laosan, your heart must be pitch black! You deceived me, wanting to sell me to this beast. When I refused, you colluded with him to commit such disgusting acts against me. Now, this can be considered retribution!"

Xu Fu's expression turned icy in an instant. He turned his head and looked with disgust at Wang Laosan and the other man who had been hiding in the cave without speaking.

After the woman said this, was there anything Xu Fu still didn't understand?

Although the epidemic was contagious, it wasn't something one could catch just by walking together or talking for a few words. It required eating, living, or even more intimate contact to be easily infected.

These two...

Truly disgusting!

Jianjia had the worst temper, and he immediately drew his long sword again, "Sir, it would be better to slaughter such filthy people."

Upon hearing this, Wang Laosan scrambled up from the ground, "No, no, I didn't do anything..." He said this while running deeper into the cave.

"Go ahead," Xu Fu said indifferently.

Having received Xu Fu's order, Jianjia's eyes burned with a stunning, brilliant light. He gripped his long sword, stepped forward quickly, grabbed Wang Laosan by the collar, threw him heavily to the ground, and then stepped on his cheek.

"Jianjia, killing him like this is too easy on him," Sang Zhong remarked.

Jianjia understood. He first kicked him in the head, causing Wang Laosan to howl repeatedly, unable to even roll on the ground.

The man in the cave began to laugh loudly, as if he had gone mad.

The sounds of the two men echoing in the cave were truly like a farce.

The force in Jianjia's legs was not small; Wang Laosan was stomped into a purple-faced pig's head. This bout of pure physical suppression made Jianjia feel much better; at least the pent-up frustration and anger in his chest had been vented. With a cold face, he swung his long sword. There was no sound, but Xu Fu saw an object fly off, followed immediately by Wang Laosan letting out a shrill, miserable scream, his body instantly curling up like a shrimp.

Jianjia withdrew his foot. Wang Laosan was rolling on the ground in pain, slamming against the cave wall, screaming in agony while cursing the woman.

Only then did Xu Fu hear clearly that the woman's name was "Yingniang."

Watching this scene, a look of gratification flashed across Yingniang's face.

Xu Fu couldn't help but sigh in his heart. Even if Wang Laosan were tortured and died a miserable death, it could not erase the suffering and pain Yingniang had endured. Yingniang had borne him a daughter, yet he could be so heartless as to want her and their daughter to die upon learning she was infected. Yingniang was right; Wang Laosan was indeed facing retribution.

Thinking back to the villagers' earlier reactions, whispering about whose daughter Yingniang's child really was, Xu Fu felt even more disgusted.

It was clearly Wang Laosan who had abandoned all shame and morality to commit such evil deeds, so why did those villagers cast their blame onto Yingniang?

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more he felt as if he had swallowed a fly.

By now, Jianjia had seen enough of Wang Laosan's screaming and was about to finish him off with one strike.

"Jianjia, don't kill him," Xu Fu interrupted his movement.

Jianjia turned back, frowning in confusion.

"Throw him outside, bury him in the dirt, leaving only his head exposed. With the sun scorching him from above and the pain of his wounds from below, combined with the onset of the epidemic, he will surely wish he were dead," Xu Fu said, then turned to Yingniang, "If you survive, go find his corpse after he dies and burn it to ashes." If not burned, Wang Laosan's body would become a nuisance outside.

However, before he left, he definitely had to get Wang Laosan out; leaving him in the cave was a hidden danger for Yingniang and her daughter.

After these words were spoken, both Sang Zhong and Jianjia stared at him in astonishment, and even Yingniang showed a look of slight shock.

Seeing that no one responded to him for a long time, while Wang Laosan continued to scream, shouting, "No, I know I was wrong."

Xu Fu said displeasedly, "Why are you looking at me as if you're seeing me for the first time?"

Sang Zhong and Jianjia swallowed involuntarily.

How could... how could the master suddenly come up with such a novel method?

Yes, novel... they thought silently to themselves, it was novel, not cruel.

Jianjia turned and went to lift Wang Laosan up from the ground, "I'll go bury him down below."

Yingniang’s face looked as if she were laughing and crying at the same time, "That is very good. That way, I can listen to the sound of his screams."

Jianjia nodded and carried Wang Laosan out of the cave. Wang Laosan struggled while letting out pig-like squeals. He had truly underestimated Jianjia; Jianjia could easily carry a bucket full of water, so naturally, he could hold him with one hand, and no matter how he struggled, he couldn't escape.

Wang Laosan thought his blood was about to run dry, his whole body aching as if he were being sliced open. Jianjia let go, dropping him into the dirt pit.

Yingniang suddenly braced herself against the cave wall and stood up, stumbling to the outside of the cave. She looked down at Wang Laosan with cold eyes. Wang Laosan accidentally met her gaze and shivered violently. His fear doubled, and his previous screams were choked off in his throat, as if he were too terrified to make a sound.

The commotion was too great.

The little girl was disturbed and furrowed her brows, opening her mouth to call out, "Mother."

Just at this moment, two physicians were brought over by the bailiffs. The two physicians had heard the screams from far away and had goosebumps all over. When they got closer and saw Jianjia burying a man alive, while a woman stood at the cave entrance in thin, tattered clothes with a terrifying expression on her face,

both physicians shivered in unison, swallowed involuntarily, and were so terrified that they practically crawled into the cave.

"Sir, the people have arrived." The bailiffs also felt a chill in their hearts. Upon seeing Xu Fu, they hurriedly pushed the physicians forward, eager to leave as quickly as possible.

Even if they had caught Xu Fu's men cutting up human flesh, they wouldn't have dared to say a word. They all knew Xu Fu was a person not to be offended. Now that they had seen such ruthless methods, they were even more in awe. They thought to themselves, perhaps he really was an immortal.

The bailiffs hurriedly took their leave.

The physician said tremblingly, "Sir? D-do you have any instructions?"

"Go take a look at her."

Only then did the physicians notice the little girl in the corner. Not daring to ask more, they hurriedly surrounded her, not daring to be the least bit negligent.

Sang Zhong pointed to the raving man inside the cave and said, "Sir, how should this person be dealt with?"

Xu Fu said without looking up, "Deal with him together with Wang Laosan; give him some company."

Sang Zhong nodded, strode forward, picked up the man, and without any mercy, threw him out of the cave entrance. Although the distance wasn't high, it was enough to make the man feel as if his bones were shattered.

Jianjia then buried the two of them together.

The physicians inside the cave heard the continuous screams outside, trembling and wiping away sweat.

"From now on, take good care of these two and treat them with all your heart. Can you do that?" Xu Fu said indifferently.

His detached manner made the two physicians feel immense fear, and they hurriedly said, "This is what we should do."

"Yes, yes, it is our duty. For those who study medicine, saving lives is our primary vocation."

Xu Fu gave an "En," and said, "Then let it be so." As he spoke, he moved his feet.

The little girl opened her eyes at this moment. She looked toward Xu Fu. Perhaps because she was delirious, her gaze couldn't focus, and she could only see a blurry outline. She smiled, and blood seeped from her cracked lips. The little girl was oblivious, "Immortal, are you leaving?"

"En."

"Where are you going?"

Xu Fu casually replied, "To the Penglai Fairyland."

The little girl nodded, "Then... when I survive, I will go to worship the Immortal..."

"En," Xu Fu responded, then turned and walked out. By the time the little girl grew up, she might not remember him at all.

"Sang Zhong, Jianjia, return to Luoyang City."

"Understood." Jianjia stomped on the dirt under his feet, clapped the dust off his hands, and walked away quickly.

Seeing that begging and screaming were useless, Wang Laosan and the other man could only curse, using the foulest language they could think of.

Xu Fu's party boarded the carriage and gradually drove away.

Yingniang's legs gave way, and she knelt down, sobbing, "Thank you... thank you, Immortal!" Before she could finish, tears were already streaming down her face like rain.

At this time, a physician came out and carefully helped Yingniang into the cave, showing no signs of disgust. In the physician's eyes, Yingniang was just a patient who needed his treatment. Although he carefully avoided the festering, ulcerated parts of Yingniang's body, he treated her with respect.

Yingniang entered the cave and heard her daughter let out a painful cry, "Mother... Mother... it hurts..."

"Don't be afraid," Yingniang patted her forehead.

The little girl opened her palm, "Mother, for you..."

·

On the road back to the city, Ying Zheng had already finished handling all matters. He turned his head to look, but there was still no sign of Xu Fu. He called his attendant to his side and only then learned that Xu Fu had left the Governor's mansion. Ying Zheng's expression immediately darkened.

Could it be that he didn't want to return to Xianyang with him?

An indescribable irritability rose in Ying Zheng's heart, as if a treasure he held in his palm, fearing it would fall, and kept in his mouth, fearing it would melt, had suddenly stopped playing with him and was spreading its wings to fly far away.

Could the feeling of losing a treasure ever be good?

To make matters worse, the messenger was still kneeling before Ying Zheng, saying, "I beg the King to return to Xianyang."

Ying Zheng swept a glance at him. The messenger was trembling with fear, but he still stiffened his neck without retreating in the slightest.

Ying Zheng stood up and said, "Depart immediately." The messenger was so panicked that perhaps the situation in Xianyang was even less optimistic than described. However, he still didn't like this person demanding things of him. How could a mere nobody dare to speak to a King in such a tone?

The messenger was detained by the attendants.

Ying Zheng left the Governor's mansion, mounted his horse, and simultaneously called Liu Zixun to his side, "When the Fengchang Xu before me returns, tell him that I have returned to Xianyang first."

Liu Zixun’s eyes widened slightly, and he hurriedly agreed. Only he knew how shocked he was at this moment. Fengchang... so that Master Xu was actually the Fengchang! This official position was not small at all. Moreover, Master Xu was young and looked as if he hadn't even reached his capping ceremony. Of course, that wasn't the main point; what surprised him most was the King's tone. How many people could be treated like this by the King?

By the time Liu Zixun regained his senses, Ying Zheng's party had already left.

Liu Zixun turned around and saw a man still standing there coldly. He whispered, "Are you not following the King?"

The man glanced at him and said, "I am waiting here for Master Xu."

Liu Zixun suddenly felt a complex emotion. The King truly treated his valued subordinates with great favor! He had even left an attendant behind to wait for Master Xu.

Just then, a carriage drove over from afar, and the one driving it was Jianjia.

Jianjia jumped off the carriage and walked over, "Gantang, why are you standing at the door?"

Gantang frowned, "Where is the master?"

"The master is in the carriage..." Before Jianjia could finish, Gantang had already stepped forward and lifted the carriage curtain, "Master, the King ordered me to wait for you here."

Xu Fu was startled, "Where is the King?"

"The King has already returned to Xianyang first."

Xu Fu's expression turned cold. He didn't say a word, but he felt extremely uncomfortable inside, as if a piece had been suddenly dug out of him, leaving him empty and leaking wind.

The big tree that had sheltered him from the wind and rain and indulged him wantonly had suddenly moved to another place.

It felt like losing money; this feeling was not good at all!

Xu Fu's face darkened, and he pulled down the carriage curtain, "Chase after him."

Jianjia and Sang Zhong were still dazed, but Gantang had already reacted. He grabbed Jianjia, brought him onto the carriage, then took over the driver's seat from Jianjia. With a lash of the horse's whip, they rushed out of the city in a flurry.

Liu Zixun, who was standing at the Governor's mansion gate and had eaten a mouthful of dust: ...

The bailiff beside him said cautiously, "Hehe, Governor..."

Liu Zixun's darkened face immediately eased.

That's right, he was the Governor now; what else could make him unhappy? Liu Zixun turned and walked inside with a full face of smiles.

·

Without Xu Fu by his side, Ying Zheng naturally had fewer concerns. He led his entourage, riding horses quickly onto the small path. Where they passed, one could only see countless hoof prints and flying dust, with the rest being mere shadows, showing how fast they were moving.

How could Xu Fu, sitting in a carriage, catch up?

Xu Fu was displeased. He had intended to return to Xianyang with Ying Zheng, but instead, Ying Zheng had left him behind. Xu Fu felt a stifling tightness in his chest.

Sang Zhong keenly noticed his bad expression and couldn't help but ask, "Master, are you feeling unwell anywhere?"

Xu Fu said with a cold face, "My chest is uncomfortable."

Sang Zhong pointed, "Master, the tortoise shell is about to fall out."

Xu Fu looked down and saw the tortoise shell hanging halfway out from his chest, dangling heavily. How could his chest feel comfortable?

Xu Fu pulled the tortoise shell out, feeling even more unhappy.

Sang Zhong sighed in his heart and looked away. It seemed the master was definitely thinking of the King...

Gantang and Jianjia were sitting outside... fighting over the reins.

Gantang wanted to drive the carriage, but Jianjia wouldn't allow it, always feeling that Gantang was stealing his job. Jianjia wanted to drive, but Gantang wouldn't allow it even more, saying he was careless and might drive the carriage into a ditch. Gantang was furious, pinned Jianjia down, won with his physical advantage, and lashed the horse fiercely. The horse suddenly went wild, and once it started, it was hard to stop.

Xu Fu almost fell flat on his face inside the carriage.

Sang Zhong's head hit the carriage wall several times before he finally stabilized his body. His face turned as dark as charcoal; he knew those two were unreliable at driving. He stood up shakily, about to leave the carriage to replace them, but the carriage was speeding along, shaking him until his stomach felt like it was churning. How could Sang Zhong drive those two away? Thus, the carriage went wild, speeding forward like a runaway horse.

·

With a "thud," someone on horseback suddenly fell off.

An attendant shouted loudly, "King, that man is dead!"

Ying Zheng pulled his horse to a stop, and everyone had to follow suit. They turned back to look and saw that the messenger, who had been detained and was riding with one of the attendants, was now lying on the ground, eyes wide open, blood overflowing from his mouth and nose.

Ying Zheng felt something was wrong and scanned the surroundings. The attendants were no fools and all became alert.

"Go!" Ying Zheng didn't hesitate and spurred his horse to fly again. A volley of arrows shot out from the forest, but unfortunately, Ying Zheng's party was moving too fast, and the arrows missed. Seeing that the plan had failed, a group of people dressed as assassins jumped out from the woods on both sides, weapons in hand, flying toward them. Their target was Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng pulled his horse to a stop, his expression cold and stern. He drew his sword and shouted sharply, "Slaughter these thieves!" It was just as well; he could vent his anger.

"Understood!" Everyone responded loudly, drew their weapons, and fought fiercely with the assassins.

The horses were left aside, showing no intention of abandoning their masters to flee.

At this moment, another sound of hoofbeats approached, and Ying Zheng's expression became even uglier.

Who knew if they were friends or foes?

Several of the assassins had already been dealt with, and two of Ying Zheng's attendants had died. The remaining attendants were tense and nervous. If the approaching party were enemy reinforcements, they would have to fight to the death to protect the King.

They didn't know that the assassins on the other side were also tense, their minds filled with, "Damn, we have no one left? Why are more people coming? Are they reinforcements for the other side? I'm so anxious! What if we can't kill Ying Zheng?"

The sound of hoofbeats grew closer and closer.

The sounds of fighting on both sides subconsciously quieted down.

"King?" A cry of surprise suddenly rang out.

The hoofbeats stopped. A carriage pulled up, and a man and a youth jumped off. Both had eyes that looked like they were spewing fire. They charged forward, and the assassins felt their hearts go cold as they were slashed at the throat.

The attendants on the other side breathed a sigh of relief.

...

Xu Fu slowly lifted the carriage curtain. He looked at the scene before him, somewhat dazed. This was... an assassination? He looked closer and saw an assassin holding a dagger, charging toward Ying Zheng. That movement looked like a slow-motion effect in Xu Fu's eyes. His heart tightened, and he grabbed whatever was at hand, jumped off the carriage, and threw it. The assassin was just about to risk it all, ignoring the swords piercing his body, to kill Ying Zheng. But just as Ying Zheng turned around, a black object suddenly fell from the sky, covering his head and blocking his eyes. The assassin was startled. By the time he recovered, Ying Zheng's long sword had already pierced him through.

The assassin spat out a mouthful of blood, fell to the ground, and the black object on his head fell off.

It was a tortoise shell.

It looked charred black, as if mocking his pitiful state.

...Damn, I actually died by a tortoise shell!

Xu Fu looked at this dramatic scene, also stunned, but he soon regained his composure.

It was just an assassination, wasn't it? He had seen the scene of Lao Ai's rebellion; what was there to fear?

Sang Zhong got off the carriage and pulled Xu Fu back, "Master, stand behind me to avoid being hurt." The King was important, but Sang Zhong wanted to stay and protect Xu Fu; anyway... he had initially followed Xu Fu just to protect his safety.

The assassins were very stubborn, all aiming for Ying Zheng. Xu Fu stood by the carriage, and no one paid him any mind.

The golden sun hanging in the sky was slowly setting, and the horizon was covered with a layer of blood-colored glow.

It wouldn't be long before it turned dark.

Xu Fu felt somewhat anxious; he really wished he could point at someone and make them die.

No, when he returned to the Xianyang Palace, he would definitely study the witchcraft records carefully and learn a few tricks!

With a "squelch," the sound of a weapon piercing flesh and being pulled out echoed.

The last assassin fell.

Ying Zheng's attendants had also suffered some casualties, but unlike the assassins, they hadn't been wiped out completely.

Ying Zheng gripped his long sword tightly, his expression as dark as a cloud. He walked quickly toward Xu Fu. Xu Fu's breathing paused involuntarily, and he suddenly felt a bit nervous, his heartbeat quickening, thumping like it was about to break out of his chest.

Ying Zheng, covered in blood and filled with murderous aura, definitely didn't look very pleasant at this moment. If it were anyone else, they would probably have weak legs by now.

Xu Fu had no other feelings, just stared at him blankly. When Ying Zheng got close, he asked, "...Are you hurt?"

His voice was low, as if he had been hungover for a night, and Xu Fu was startled by his own voice.

"Nothing," Ying Zheng said, downplaying it, then reached out and pulled Xu Fu over. Xu Fu stumbled and fell directly into Ying Zheng's arms. Ying Zheng turned and ordered, "Find a place to spend the night."

"Understood." The attendants received the order and immediately split up to find a place to stay, clean up the mess, find food, and search for water... Ying Zheng held Xu Fu in his arms and walked forward.

Xu Fu felt a bit uncomfortable, as if he were being tucked under Ying Zheng's arm. He opened his mouth, but finally pursed his lips. Forget it. Just consider it that he had made a mistake earlier.

Those who make mistakes can only hold it in.
chapters.source_text:
山洞里的人大约是也听见了脚步声，徐福紧随在蒹葭身后走到洞口，一眼就看见那个蹲在地上的男子凶恶地转过了头，双目殷红地瞪着洞口。
正是之前被女子称作“王老三”的男子。
洞口的一侧，依偎着那个女子，她冷冷地看着王老三，脸上露出了恶意的笑容。
王老三认出了徐福的模样，心中愤恨顿起。
就是他，就是他下令让差役将自己也抓走了，就是他害得自己只能跟这个臭娘们儿呆在一起！
徐福怎么会感受不到王老三眼底狰狞的目光，不待他开口，蒹葭已经冷笑一声，抽出了腰后的长剑，走到了王老三的跟前去。
原本还撸起袖子，准备叫徐福吃点教训的王老三，两眼发直，腿一下子就软了，哆哆嗦嗦道：“你、你要做什么？”
蒹葭十分瞧不上这样的男子，轻蔑地哼了一声，一句话也不说，只是停也不停地朝着王老三走了过去，他那张俊秀的脸看在王老三眼中，简直狰狞得可怕，王老三连连后退。
徐福没去看蒹葭要做什么，他走到了那女子的跟前，徐福这才发现，她的女儿躺在她的身侧，双眼闭着，脸颊发红，看上去像是发着高热。小姑娘的手紧紧地握着，哪怕是神志不清，也没有松开分毫。
女子缓缓抬起头来，好一会儿视线才清明了，她看清了徐福的模样，忙挺直了背，想要起身，但是偏偏浑身虚弱得没了力气，腿刚一用力就又坐了回去。
“求先生为我请个大夫……”女子开口，声音温婉凄楚，哪里有与人相对时的尖利冷漠。
“有大夫负责照看你们。”徐福皱了皱眉，“如何？他们没有来吗？”
女子连连摇头，眼泪顺着脸颊滑落了下来。
“啊啊啊！别杀我！”嚎叫声突然在山洞里响起，徐福转头看向过去，只见蒹葭手中的长剑就插在王老三脸旁，王老三捂着脸崩溃大叫，双腿抖动不已，像是要吓得失禁了一样。
蒹葭抽回长剑，不屑地道：“怂货！”随后就转身走了回来。
王老三蜷在那里瑟瑟发抖，哪怕听见脚步声渐渐从他身边离开，他也不敢放下挡着脸的手。
徐福微微皱眉，果然是个欺软怕硬的。
这样的男人实在配不上这女子。
桑中慢慢走上前来，道：“从城中走时，我已经命差役去带大夫了。”
那女子松了一口气，神色还有些恍惚。还好，雒阳城没有让他们自生自灭。那个男人死了也就罢了，她却是舍不得女儿死的。
女子慢慢恢复了冷静，她向徐福道：“多谢先生。”
“不必。”徐福看着她，很认真地道：“我交予你们的那两口仙气，当真能救你们的命，要握住了。”徐福的声音很轻，但是带着奇迹的安抚力量。
女子愣了愣，她是不信这些的……
可这人怎么能一口确定，那真的是两口仙气呢？
此时有个男声插了进来，“什么仙气？糊弄人的！我们都要死了！谁也活不下来！王老三，都怪你家婆娘给我们也染上了。”
女子冷笑一声，语调尖利，“怪我？王老三，你的心肝怕是都黑透了！你诓骗了我，要将我卖给这禽兽，我不从，你便联合他对我做出那等恶心的事来，如今也算是报应！”
徐福的脸色几乎是顷刻间就变得冰冷了起来，他转头厌恶地看了一眼那王老三，还有那个之前一直没有说话，窝在洞里的男子。
女子这番话说出来，徐福还有什么是不明白的呢？
疫病虽会传染，但也并非走一起说两句话就能传染上的。而是要吃住，甚至更亲密的事都在一块儿，才能容易被传染上。
这二人……
实在恶心！
蒹葭脾气最为不好，当即便又将长剑抽了出来，“先生，这等腌臜之人，还是宰了更好。”
王老三闻言，迅速从地上爬了起来，“不不不，我什么都没做……”他一边说着一边洞里更深处跑去。
“去吧。”徐福淡淡道。
蒹葭得了徐福的命令，双目灼灼生辉，亮得惊人。他抓着长剑，快步上前，一手抓住那王老三的衣襟，将他往地上重重一摔，再一脚踩在他的脸颊上。
“蒹葭，这样杀了他，实在便宜了他。”桑中出声道。
蒹葭会意，先照头踹，将那王老三踹得嚎叫连连，连在地上翻滚也不得。
那洞中的男子哈哈大笑起来，倒像是疯了一般。
洞中回荡着二人的声音，实在像一出闹剧。
蒹葭腿上的力道实在不小，王老三硬生生被他踩成了一个面容紫胀的猪头。这一顿单纯的武力压制，让蒹葭舒服了不少，至少胸中堵着的郁气和愤怒都倾泻出来了，他冷着脸，握着那长剑一挥，其实连个声音也没有，徐福就瞧见一个什么物体飞了出去，紧接着王老三发出了一声凄厉的惨叫，身子顿时躬成了虾米。
蒹葭收回脚，王老三痛得在地上打滚，直往那洞壁上撞，口中一边痛得大叫，一边又大骂那女子。
徐福这才听清原来那女子名叫“英娘”。
英娘看着这一幕，脸上闪过快意之色。
徐福心中忍不住叹惋。就算那王老三得到折磨，最后惨死，但也无法消除英娘身上所受的折磨和痛苦。英娘与他育有一女，他竟都能如此狼心狗肺，得知英娘染病，便要让她和女儿一起去死。英娘说得不错，王老三的确是报应。
再思及之前村民们的反应，低声说英娘的女儿不知是谁的，徐福更觉得恶心了。
明明是王老三抛却了羞耻心和道德，做出这等恶事，那些村民怎么还将指责落到了英娘的身上？
徐福越想越觉得如同吞了苍蝇一样膈应。
此时蒹葭已经看够了王老三惨叫的模样，当即便要一剑结果了他。
“蒹葭，别杀他。”徐福出声打断了他的动作。
蒹葭回过头来，有些不解地皱着眉。
“将他扔出去，埋在土里，留出头来，上有日光暴晒，下又有伤口疼痛，身上疫病发作，他定然会生不如死。”徐福说完，又转头对英娘道：“你若活下来，便去寻到他死后的尸体，一把火将他烧个干净。”若是不烧的话，王老三死在外头还会成个麻烦。
不过在他走之前，他肯定是要将王老三弄出去的，留在这洞中，对于英娘母女来说，是个隐患。
这一番话说完，桑中和蒹葭都是目瞪口呆地看着他，就连英娘也流露出了微微错愕的神情来。
见半天没人应自己的声，倒是那王老三惨叫连连，喊着“不要，我知错了”。
徐福不悦道：“怎么像是头一次认识我一般看着我？”
桑中和蒹葭不自觉地咽了咽口水。
先生怎么……怎么突然间能提出这么新奇的法子呢？
对，是新奇……他们默默在心底道，是新奇，不是残暴。
蒹葭转身就去将王老三从地上拎了起来，“我就把他埋在下头吧。”
英娘脸上似笑似哭，道：“这样很好，这样我也可以听一听他惨叫的声音了。”
蒹葭点了点，拎着王老三出了洞口，王老三一边挣扎，一边发出杀猪般的嚎叫声，他实在小看了蒹葭，蒹葭能轻松扛起盛满水的桶来，一只手自然也能将他抓住，任他怎么挣扎也是逃不掉的。
王老三以为自己的血快流尽了，浑身疼得像是要被剖开了一样，蒹葭一松手，将他砸在那土坑上。
英娘忽然撑着山壁站了起来，跌跌撞撞地走到洞外，居高临下地看着那王老三，眼神冰冷，王老三不小心和她的目光相撞，结结实实地打了个哆嗦，心中恐惧倍增，原本的惨叫声也被他掐在了嗓子里，像是被吓得硬生生的发不出声来了。
这一番动静太大。
小姑娘被吵得拧起了眉，张嘴叫了声，“阿娘。”
恰好在此时，有两个大夫被差役带了过来，那两个大夫老远就听见惨叫声了，起了一身鸡皮疙瘩，待他们走近了，一看蒹葭正在活埋一个男子，而还有一个女子站在洞口处，身上衣衫单薄褴褛，脸上的表情有些可怖。
两个大夫齐齐打了个冷颤，不自觉地咽了咽口水，心中惊恐不已，几乎是连滚带爬地进了山洞。
“先生，人带到了。”差役也觉得一阵胆寒，见到徐福后赶紧将大夫推了出去，恨不得快快离开。
哪怕是撞见徐福手下的人切人肉，他们也是不敢说半句话的。他们都知晓徐福是个不可得罪的人物，如今见了这般狠辣手段，那更是敬畏不已。心中暗道，说不定人家真是神仙呢。
差役们忙告退离开。
大夫颤巍巍道：“先生？可、可有指令？”
“去瞧一瞧她。”
大夫这才注意到那角落里还有个小姑娘呢，也不敢多问，他们忙围了上去，不敢怠慢分毫。
桑中指了指那洞内疯疯癫癫的男子，道：“先生，这人如何处置？”
徐福头也不抬地道：“便与那王老三一并处置吧，给他做个伴。”
桑中点头，大步走上前去，将那男子拎起来，毫不留情的，直接从洞口出来便扔了下去，那距离虽然不高，但也足够叫那男子痛得如同粉身碎骨一样了。
蒹葭就顺便将两人一起埋了。
洞内的大夫听见外面惨叫连连，一边哆嗦，一边抹汗。
“日后便要好生照顾这二人，尽心医治，可能做到？”徐福淡淡出声。
他这副淡漠的模样，让那两名大夫心中畏惧不已，忙道：“这是我们应该做的。”
“是是，应该做的，学医之人，救人命，乃是本职。”
徐福“嗯”了一声，“那就如此吧。”说着他挪动了脚步。
小姑娘就在此时睁开了眼睛，她看向了徐福的方向，大约是神志未清的缘故，她的目光都难以聚焦，只能瞧个模模糊糊的轮廓，她笑了笑，干裂的唇渗出了血丝来，小姑娘恍然未觉，“仙人，你要走了吗？”
“嗯。”
“去哪里呢？”
徐福随口扯了一句，“蓬莱仙境。”
小姑娘点了点头，“那我……活下来，就去参拜仙人……”
“嗯。”徐福应了一声，这才转身走了出去。等那小姑娘长大了，未必会记得他。
“桑中，蒹葭，回雒阳城。”
“喏。”蒹葭踩了踩脚下的土，拍了拍手上的灰，快步走开了。
王老三二人见求饶惨叫都无效，便只有痛骂出声，什么话难听便骂什么。
徐福一行人上了马车，渐渐驶远。
英娘双腿一软，跪倒下来，嘶声道：“多谢……多谢仙人！”话未说完便已是泪如雨下。
此时一大夫走了出来，小心地将英娘扶进了山洞之中，倒是没有什么嫌弃之感。在那大夫眼中，英娘便只是个需要他来医治的病人而已。虽然他小心避开了英娘身上化脓溃烂的地方，但他倒是尊重英娘的。
英娘进了山洞，见女儿发出了痛苦的叫声，“阿娘……阿娘……难受……”
“别怕。”英娘拍了拍她的额头。
小姑娘张开了手掌，“阿娘，给你……”

马车走在回城的路上，那厢嬴政已经处理完了所有的事务，转头一瞧，却还是没有徐福的人影，他将侍从叫到面前来，这才知晓徐福出了郡守府，嬴政的脸色顿时就阴沉了起来。
难道这是不愿同他回咸阳的意思？
嬴政心中顿时说不出的烦躁，就好像捧在掌心怕摔了，含在嘴里怕化了的宝贝，突然间不跟他玩儿了，要插着翅膀奔远方去了。
丢了珍宝的感觉，能好吗？
偏生那报信之人，还跪在嬴政跟前道：“请王上回咸阳。”
嬴政扫了他一眼，报信之人吓得直打哆嗦，但还是梗着脖子没有丝毫后退。
嬴政起身道：“即刻启程。”报信之人如此慌张，或许咸阳城中情况比描述的还要不容乐观。不过他依旧不喜欢此人来要求他。区区小人，如何敢以这等口吻与君王说话？
报信之人被侍从扣押了起来。
嬴政出了郡守府，翻身上马，同时将刘子训叫到跟前来，“待到寡人身前的徐奉常归来，你便告知他，寡人先行回咸阳去了。”
刘子训微微瞪大眼，忙应下来了，只有他自己知道，此刻心中如何震惊。奉常……原来那徐先生，竟然是奉常！这官职可也不小了。何况那徐先生年纪轻轻，瞧上去还像是未加冠一样。当然这也不算什么，最令他惊奇的，还是王上的口吻。能被王上这般对待的，能有几人？
等刘子训回过神来时，嬴政一行人已经走了。
刘子训转过身，见一人还冷冰冰地站在那里，他小声道：“你不随王上走吗？”
那人瞥了他一眼，道：“我在此处等候徐先生。”
刘子训顿觉复杂不已，王上对待看重的下属果真是厚待不已啊！竟是还留下了侍从等待那徐先生。
就在此时，一辆马车遥遥驶来，驾车的正是蒹葭。
蒹葭跳下马车，走过来，“甘棠，你如何站在门口？”
甘棠皱眉道：“先生呢？”
“先生在车上啊……”蒹葭话音未落，甘棠已经快步走上前，将车帘一掀，“先生，王上命我在此等你。”
徐福一怔，“王上呢？”
“王上已经先行回咸阳了。”
徐福脸色冷了冷，一句话也未说，心里头极为不舒服，就跟陡然被谁挖走一块似的，空荡荡的漏着风。
原本遮风挡雨肆意纵容的大树，现在忽然换个地儿了。
仿佛丢了钱一样的感觉，这滋味一点也不好！
徐福脸色一黑，将那车帘扯下来，“去追。”
蒹葭和桑中都还有些懵呢，甘棠已经反应过来，拎着蒹葭就带着他上了车，然后代替了蒹葭车夫的位置，一抽马屁股，又风风火火地朝城外去了。
站在郡守府门口吃了一嘴灰的刘子训：……
旁边的差役小心道：“嘿嘿，郡守……”
刘子训黑着的脸顿时舒缓了开来。
对啊，如今他是郡守了，还有何事能令他不开心呢？刘子训满面微笑地转身进去了。

不带徐福在身边，嬴政自然没了诸多讲究，他带着一干人，骑着马快速奔上了小道，所行之处，只能瞧见无数马蹄印和飞扬的尘土，余下的便是一抹抹残影了，可见他们速度之快。
徐福这头坐着马车，如何能追得上？
徐福心中不悦。他本要与嬴政一同回咸阳，结果倒好，嬴政直接将他扔下了。徐福觉得胸口闷得难受。
桑中敏锐地察觉到他的脸色不好，不由问道：“先生可是何处不适？”
徐福冷着脸，“胸口不适。”
桑中抬手指了指，“先生，龟甲要掉出来了。”
徐福低头一瞧，胸前放着龟甲坠了一半在外头，沉甸甸地吊着，胸口能舒服吗？
徐福将那龟甲扯了出来，心中更为不快了。
桑中在心底叹了口气，转移了目光。想来先生心中定是挂念着王上的……
甘棠和蒹葭二人坐在外面……抢缰绳。
甘棠要驾马车，蒹葭不许，总觉得甘棠抢了自己的活计，蒹葭要驾马车，甘棠更不许，言他粗心马虎，指不准将马车驾到河沟里去了。甘棠怒极，将蒹葭压得死死的，以身形优势取胜，猛地一抽马儿，马儿突然狂奔起来，这一狂奔就难以停歇下来。
徐福在马车里差点摔个大马趴。
而桑中的头在马车壁上，连续磕了好几次，好不容易才稳住了身体，脸色顿时难看得如同黑炭一样，就知道，这二人驾马车实在不靠谱。他摇摇晃晃起身，正要出马车，将那二人换下来，但是马车一路疾驰，晃得他肚子里都要翻江倒海了，桑中怎么还能驱赶那两人？于是，这马车就如同脱了缰一般，朝着前方飞驰而去。
