三川郡。
有热风穿越过林子，灌进山洞里来。
似乎还带来了一股浊臭的气息。
英娘喘息着从地上挣扎着爬起来，她……还活着……她忙扶起身边的女儿，小姑娘慢吞吞地睁开了双眼，然后露出了惊喜的笑容，“阿娘，你瞧，我们真的靠着那两口仙气，变好了……这里、这里没有那么疼了……”
英娘拥着她，急急地喘息着，眼泪从脸上冲刷而下。
“是啊，要谢谢他啊，丫头，你要记住他……”
“嗯……”
“你在这里等我。”英娘将她放开，然后虚弱地站起身来，借着洞中还未燃尽的火堆，点了火把，然后拖着裙摆慢慢走了下去。那两个被埋在土里的人，挣扎出来了一些，他们身上散发着恶臭味儿，四肢也有溃烂的迹象。他们已经没有力气了，只能这样虚弱地靠在土里，双眼因为被太阳灼烤，也不太中用了，所以哪怕英娘走近了，他们也没有任何反应。
瞧着这两个昔日里，得意洋洋，欺侮自己的男人。
瞧着他们那丑恶的嘴脸，如今因为疫病而变得更为丑陋。
英娘的身体微微抖动着，像是有激动的电流从她身上蹿过。
她举起了手中的火把，笑了笑，“我早说过，你们总有一日，是要血债血偿的……”
她的声音透着阴冷，那两人剧烈地抖动了起来，声音嘶哑难听，“你……要做什么？你、你疯了？毒妇……”
英娘笑靥如花，“终日辱骂我为毒妇，那我今日便叫你瞧一瞧，如何才叫毒妇。”说罢，她将那火把扔在了二人身上，火苗迅速点燃了身上破烂的衣衫，然后将他们吞没在里头。二人的嗓子已经破败不堪了，但被烈火灼烧之下，他们还是发出了疼痛的嘶叫。
多么像是她当初痛苦嘶叫时的声音啊。
一报还一报。
英娘冷冷一笑，又慢慢拖着裙摆回了山洞，她温柔地捧起女儿的脸蛋，“日后啊，我们便在屋子里，供着那仙人的雕像，求他日后也要庇佑我的丫头啊……”
小姑娘咯咯一笑，与山坡下的嘶哑的惨叫声交织在一起。
不久之后，三川郡中瘟疫的威胁，消除了。
·
不断有急报被呈到嬴政的跟前来，莫说百姓们了，纵然是满朝大臣，也多有慌乱的了。
时七月，秦国全国大旱，足有一月未见半点雨水。
郑国四处奔波，修建水渠，百姓们虽觉悲苦，但倒不至于整日恐慌。三川、南阳最早没了雨水，但这两处却也是最早开始着手寻水源，开水流，挖掘深井的。土地无法救，但百姓们倒多少还有水喝。
而其他地方并无防备，之前还在嘲笑三川、南阳两处的郡守倒了大霉，谁知道很快这大霉便落到自己头上来了。
全国上下，最为恐慌之处，竟是在咸阳。
嬴政对朝中官员极为不满，到了此时，他们倒是跟着恐慌起来了。不过倒也不能怪他们恐慌，实在是别的郡都还好，偏偏咸阳真的爆发了疫病，这一传染，便是极为迅猛，范围又极为广阔的。那最先染上疫病的官大夫府中上下，都很快病倒了，继官大夫幼子之后，便很快又死了几人，之后甚至连周边两户人家都染上了。
不得已，嬴政便令蒙恬将那处隔离出来，其他人统统迁走。
但感染源并非只这一处。
不过短短几日，便又有两处宅子里死了人。
有大臣跪在嬴政跟前，道：“请王上迁都！”
迁都？迁都乃是何等重要的大事！秦国国境内，多么富庶的地方并不多，自旧都雍城迁至咸阳以后，秦国便从未有想过，未来还会迁到何处去。现下全国大旱，又能往何处迁？往没有瘟疫的地方迁吗？这么多王室贵族，官员大臣，要迁动起来，哪里是小事？恐怕还不等迁都，就在路中死了一大半了。
何况身为国君，抛下百姓便走，这样的事，嬴政自认，他再如何心狠手辣也是做不出来的。
这些都是他秦国的百姓，受他庇佑的百姓，若是连这点都做不好，嬴政的自尊如何能容忍？
“不必再言，此时，我秦国上下，应当团结一心，度过大旱难关。”嬴政沉着脸散了朝。
他回到寝宫中时，便见徐福一手撑在桌案上，正低头看着什么书简。他只能瞥见徐福的侧脸，有点儿苍白，像是精力透支了一样。
嬴政走上前去，问他：“可是今日晨起忘了吃饭？”
徐福推开竹简，摇头，“不是。”说完他指了指旁边的布条儿，“喏，按照巫术里的方法，做了个试验。”
“什么试验？”
嬴政对那布条儿没甚兴趣，当即就推开了。
徐福将竹简推到他的面前。
嬴政低头一看，上书，“用己身之精血浸之，方可大成”。己身之精血？嬴政脸色陡然沉了下来，他抓起徐福的手腕，上头虽然包扎了一番，但还往外渗着血呢。
“你是闲的吗？来做这等试验？”
徐福眉目间透着一股厌倦的味道，嬴政实在没从他脸上见过这副模样，心中不由得微微揪住了，但是怒骂的话已经说出口了，此时嬴政也只能硬生生将自己面上的表情，从震怒改为平淡。
徐福眉头微皱，低声道：“我也不是故意的，我本来只想取一滴血试一试，谁知道手一抖，那笔刀就在手腕上割了条口子。”那布条直接被染了个通红，瞧上去更难看了。要不是想到上面还有自己的血呢，徐福定然将这丑不拉几的玩意儿给丢出去了。
想一想为了做个试验，硬是将自己变成了像是要割腕自杀一样，徐福便觉得有些丢面子。
嬴政挥手让众人退下，不由得问道：“近几日，你心中烦躁？”
“你怎么知道？”徐福有些惊讶。他已经算是很能控制自我情绪了，从前没人能发现他的情绪何处不对劲。
“我与你日日同吃同睡，如何不知？”嬴政没好气地道，“寡人都还未曾心生烦躁，你倒是比寡人还先焦灼起来了。”
徐福皱着眉头半点不见有松开的意思，“阿政，我不想你如此忧心。”食君之禄，忠君之事。他从嬴政这里该得的好处都得了，嬴政也的确是个万里挑一的好情人。他怎么能容忍自己掉链子呢？
嬴政嘴角翘了起来，又被他自己硬生生压了下去。
心中是有些快意，但是嬴政不能这么快就被哄住啊。
于是他没说话。
而这头徐福已经自顾自地说起来了，“若是我失去价值了，那会如何呢？”
“什么？”嬴政没明白他的意思。怎么突然间扯到这样一句话上来了。
“我之前向你求了旨意，说要在城楼上卜筮，可后来我却又推迟了，阿政可知为何？”
“为何？”徐福都是对他说，时日未到，嬴政自然也不会催促，在这点上他还是可以放心信任徐福的。哪怕到时候祭祀和卜筮起不了作用，他自然还有别的法子来善后。
“因为，”徐福顿了下，眼眸里一瞬间空茫，“我又什么都卜不出来了。”
嬴政闻言并不惊讶，连半点着急之色都没有，他温声道：“你去年不也是这般么？那时都是你未曾休息好的缘故，说不定这次也是如此呢。前段时间你也说自己卜不出了，可你用了那什么……铜钱，不也卜出来了吗？”
“可是六爻也没用了。”徐福的声音隐隐透着急躁的味道。
嬴政微微一怔，看着徐福如今的模样。
也不知是方才失血过多，还是这段时间压力过大，才让他脸色过分苍白了起来，不过嬴政瞧着他这副模样，倒是突然想起来，徐福好像还未加冠吧，也只是个少年而已，年纪如此小，怎么比自己操心的事还多？他能做到如今的地步，已是不易了……
嬴政倒是未曾去想，他更小的时候，便要想着如何生存了。
徐福的手指绞动了一下，“我什么也卜不出，你还记得我曾经与你说，算命者不可自算吗？”
“记得。”
“我与你如今什么关系？”
嬴政张了张嘴，正想着要答个什么关系，才能令徐福感动不已，徐福却已经直接打断了他说话的机会。
“你瞧，如今我与你这样亲近，你的命格说不得还要受我的影响。算命之人，本来应当是无亲无友的，但多了个你。现在连你的事，我都一概卜不出了……”
“说不得到时候上了城楼，我还要出个大丑。”
“我什么也卜不出，还做什么国师？”
嬴政突然憋不住笑出了声。
徐福抬起头，冷冷地瞧着他，“有何可笑之处吗？”
话说完，徐福自己倒也觉得有些可笑。
他是不是脑子中邪了？从前他可不会说这样的话的。幸好殿中无宫人，不然的话，那岂不是丢了大脸！什么风度什么仪态什么气质，全丢了！
徐福可不想承认，自己像是在撒娇一样。
嬴政正要开口好好与他解释一番，突地有一宫女跪在门口，浑身哆嗦不已，“王上，禀王上……扶苏公子，扶苏公子发起了高热……”
这个时候发起高热，不会有任何人觉得这是个好现象。
chapters.title: 第117章
chapters.translated_text:
Palace attendants hurriedly draped a robe over Ying Zheng, and the eunuchs worked together to push open the palace doors, which let out a teeth-gritting creak.

The eunuch stumbled in, drenched in sweat, not even caring that he had tripped over the threshold. He hurried forward a few steps before falling heavily to his knees. "Your Majesty, in the residence of the Official Physician in the north of the city, three people suddenly developed high fevers yesterday. The Official Physician has a young son who passed away an hour ago. The Official Physician requested an imperial physician to go, and only upon examination did they discover that several people in the residence had contracted the illness..."

As the eunuch spoke, he couldn't help but shiver, large beads of sweat rolling down his forehead; panic seemed to be swallowing him whole.

Ying Zheng’s expression was already as grim as it could possibly be.

"What about the people in the Official Physician's residence now?" Xu Fu reacted to this shocking news, stood up from his seat, and asked, enduring the numbness in his legs.

The eunuch carefully glanced at Ying Zheng’s expression. Seeing that Ying Zheng did not object, he replied to Xu Fu, "The people in the residence are in a panic and have lost their wits; some are packing their things to run away, while others are shouting that they should just burn the sick people to death..."

"And what does the Official Physician say?" Ying Zheng asked in a deep voice.

"The Official Physician ordered the imperial physician to cure the people in the residence, and then ordered the other servants to drive out those who had fallen ill."

Just as Ying Zheng was about to erupt in anger, Xu Fu’s voice rang out first, "Is this Official Physician an idiot?"

It was the first time anyone had dared to insult a Qin official in such a way. The eunuch hung his head in embarrassment, not daring to echo Xu Fu’s words at all.

Xu Fu was feeling quite incensed. "Pig-brained! Everyone knows that falling ill after a drought is highly likely to be a plague! He actually had the sick servants driven out at will; is he hoping to infect the entire city?" He had been burning the midnight oil, racing against time to find ways to subdue the nobles and convince them not to underestimate this matter. Now that something had happened at an official's residence, it seemed he wouldn't even need to use those methods; those nobles would naturally value their own lives.

He only hoped this Official Physician wasn't stupid enough to let the people from his residence wander about freely and spread the virus everywhere.

"Summon Meng Tian." Ying Zheng had been on the verge of an outburst, but Xu Fu had already vented the anger he was about to unleash, and he had calmed down for the moment.

The eunuch carefully observed Ying Zheng’s expression, thinking to himself that the King was becoming increasingly unfathomable, his temperament not easily shaken.

The eunuch naturally couldn't leave yet, so other attendants hurried out of the palace gates to deliver the order to find Meng Tian.

Xu Fu frowned. "How is it that people in Xianyang City have fallen ill so quickly?"

"Luoyang City does not have as many people as Xianyang, and furthermore, the population of Luoyang is mostly commoners, making it easier to govern. Xianyang is not like that," Ying Zheng said calmly, a layer of suppressed anger on his face. The people in Xianyang were simply jumping at the chance because the King of Qin was away; they paid no heed to the orders issued by the likes of Li Si or Wei Liao. They didn't take talk of the great drought or the potential plague after the drought to heart. They only enjoyed their current comfort and were self-satisfied.

One must know that the current King of Qin did not value the nobility as he once did. Most of those who could get ahead in front of him now were even commoners, and some even came from other states; these people had become the main force under the King of Qin. Once the nobles dared to put on airs in front of the King, they were met with even greater oppression from Ying Zheng.

Seeing that Ying Zheng was gone, even Li Si and Wei Liao dared to order them around. How could these nobles and officials easily submit?

Wasn't the incident at the Official Physician's residence precisely because he had disregarded the notices posted by Wei Liao’s men?

A city like Xianyang, filled with nobles and officials, was naturally more prone to trouble.

Xu Fu’s thoughts quickly aligned with Ying Zheng’s.

However, Xianyang City did have one advantage: many famous physicians were concentrated in the city.

During the Zhou Dynasty, palace physicians were divided into disease physicians, veterinary physicians, diet physicians, and ulcer physicians.

Although the Qin State did not divide them so meticulously, the imperial physicians each had their own areas of expertise, and among them were some skilled in treating epidemics. Upon learning of the incident at the Official Physician's residence, these imperial physicians immediately realized the severity of the situation. One of the older physicians volunteered to come before Ying Zheng, requesting to go to the Official Physician's residence to take a look.

This physician was someone whom high-ranking officials usually found difficult to invite to treat their illnesses.

Ying Zheng had a eunuch bring a soft cushion and ordered the physician to sit first.

At this moment, a eunuch stepped into the hall and said, "General Meng has arrived."

As soon as the words fell, a tall man walked in with a serious expression. Xu Fu glanced at his facial expression; it seemed Meng Tian was already aware of what had happened in the city. He appeared to be a sensible man who understood the gravity of the situation.

"Your Majesty." Meng Tian bowed to Ying Zheng, then his gaze fell on Xu Fu, and he also offered a salute, saying, "Master Xu." Given his status and family background, being able to treat Xu Fu with such courtesy showed he held him in high regard.

Xu Fu nodded at him.

Meng Tian then shifted his gaze away.

"I will not waste time with pleasantries. You are to take troops to surround the Official Physician's residence in the north of the city and take Physician Qiu with you. From now on, without my orders, no one is to be allowed to leave the residence."

The Meng family were all loyal subjects of the Qin royal house, and Meng Tian’s loyalty to Ying Zheng was even more profound. Whatever Ying Zheng ordered him to do, he would strictly follow, never allowing for the slightest negligence.

Meng Tian bowed and said, "Please forgive me, Your Majesty. Half an hour ago, when I learned that something had happened at the Official Physician's residence, I immediately ordered Meng Yi to take troops there to surround it. I acted without authorization; please punish me, Your Majesty."

Xu Fu looked at Meng Tian with some surprise.

He truly had not expected this. He had originally thought that people like Meng Tian and Meng Yi were loyal generals with straightforward, unbending personalities, but he hadn't expected them to be so flexible. Come to think of it, if they were truly unbending, how could they have become famous generals of Qin, expanding the territory for Ying Zheng?

"Go." Ying Zheng neither praised nor criticized, simply ordering the eunuch to lead him out. Meng Tian walked a bit slower, waiting for Physician Qiu.

Only then did Xu Fu turn to look at Ying Zheng. "Is the Great Court session still being held?"

"Yes."

"Then I..."

"You don't need to go." Which of those nobles wasn't cunning? Once they heard that someone had contracted the plague, they would surely hide faster than anyone else.

Xu Fu suddenly relaxed, but instead felt a sense of loss.

Having made all the preparations, yet by the next day, he hadn't been able to help Ying Zheng with anything.

Meanwhile, Ying Zheng had already quickly tidied up, eaten some food, and headed toward the palace hall for the morning meeting, radiating a cold aura.

Xu Fu stood there for a while, then suddenly said, "Bring me the set of robes the King prepared for me earlier."

The palace maid was stunned, but didn't ask any questions and hurried to fetch the robes.

That set of robes was primarily black and red with intricate patterns; at first glance, it looked somewhat like a grand ceremonial garment for sacrifices. But at best, it was a cosplay version.

Ever since Xu Fu wore the sacrificial robes and held Ying Zheng’s gaze, he had specifically ordered several similar sets made for Xu Fu, though they were far less solemn and complex than the actual sacrificial ones. These robes were squeezed in with the white robes Xu Fu usually wore, and he rarely took them out to wear.

Xu Fu touched the robe, his movements coming to a sudden halt.

...The last time he wore it, it seemed to have been during some intimate play.

Xu Fu lowered his gaze, his face showing no sign of anything strange.

"Dress me."

"Yes."

Xu Fu spread his arms, and the maid helped him into the robes.

Although the clothing was light, it couldn't withstand layer upon layer; before long, Xu Fu felt himself sweating on his back.

The maid looked up and smiled, "Master Xu still looks like an immortal."

"Hmm." Xu Fu responded faintly.

The maid hadn't expected Xu Fu to respond to her, and a look of surprise flashed across her face.

"Where are Young Masters Fusu and Huhai?" Xu Fu asked while adjusting his sleeves.

"They should still be resting in the palace at this hour."

"Have they felt afraid these past few days?"

The maid was even more surprised, thinking to herself that it was rare for Master Xu to care about the two young masters. But then she thought, these were extraordinary times, so it was normal for Master Xu to show some concern.

"Young Master Huhai is young and has been quite frightened these past few days, but Young Master Fusu is older and has often been comforting him."

Xu Fu felt relieved. "Order the little eunuch to drive the carriage and take me out of the palace."

"Is Master Xu going to the Fengchang Temple at this hour?" the maid asked, surprised. With the city in such chaos, Master Xu still wanted to go to work; this... this didn't seem like Master Xu’s style.

"Yes." Xu Fu had no intention of saying more.

The maid had to swallow the words that had reached her throat. Even if Master Xu wasn't wearing his official uniform, it should be fine.

Xu Fu arrived outside the Fengchang Temple by carriage and lifted the curtain to step out. "Wait for me here."

The little eunuch nodded hurriedly, not daring to wander off.

Some people had already arrived at the Fengchang Temple to work, though there were far fewer than usual. When Xu Fu walked in, no one noticed him at first. After a while, someone rubbed their sleepy eyes, looked again, and couldn't help but exclaim, "Master Xu?"

Xu Fu turned to look at him and said coldly, "Once everyone at the Fengchang Temple has arrived, gather before me. Record the names of those who are absent; I will check them later."

The man swallowed hard, having never seen Xu Fu so sharp and efficient. He nodded involuntarily and whispered, "Understood..." After answering, he realized his response wasn't formal enough and was about to speak again, but Xu Fu had already left him behind.

Whether the plague in the city was tricky was not his concern, and whether the nobles and officials listened was also not his concern for now. But Xu Fu remembered that such a great disaster hanging over Xianyang City would inevitably cause unrest and make everyone feel panicked; such panic was not a good thing.

Regardless of how serious the plague was, at least for now, he could calm this panic and make the people trust the King of Qin and the State of Qin. Perhaps, by taking this opportunity... it wasn't impossible to make more people trust him.

Xu Fu calculated his plan in his heart.

On the other side, Wei Liao had left the Great Court early and couldn't find Xu Fu. Upon learning that he had gone to the Fengchang Temple, Wei Liao frowned, the wrinkles on his forehead deep enough to crush a mosquito.

Now that chaos was beginning to show in Xianyang, Xu Fu had actually run off to the Fengchang Temple.

In Wei Liao’s view, it was naturally safer for his junior brother to stay under his own nose.

Wei Liao didn't hesitate and immediately rushed to the Fengchang Temple. From afar, he saw the little eunuch standing honestly outside the temple, guarding the carriage.

"Greetings, State Lieutenant." The little eunuch saluted him.

Wei Liao nodded briefly and stepped into the Fengchang Temple. "Where is your Master Xu?" he asked someone.

The man was dazed, his mind blank upon seeing such a high official as the State Lieutenant, and he stammered, "I... I will lead the way for the State Lieutenant." With that, he led Wei Liao inside.

This person was Qiu Ji.

Qiu Ji had long heard from others that Master Xu actually had an extraordinary background, and not only that, he had a senior brother who was the State Lieutenant, and this senior brother often came to the Fengchang Temple to look for him.

Qiu Ji was already very afraid of Xu Fu, and now seeing Wei Liao, he was naturally even more in awe.

If he hadn't repented in time and softened his stance toward Xu Fu, he probably would have ended up no better than Master Liu and Grand Diviner Zhao. Many thoughts raced through Qiu Ji’s mind.

As they walked, they entered the inner courtyard.

What presented itself before them was a group of people standing in the courtyard, with Xu Fu standing before them, his expression cold and stern, looking down at them from above.

Seeing Xu Fu like this, a slight sense of incongruity arose in Wei Liao’s heart.

...Why did he feel that his junior brother was becoming more and more like the King of Qin?

Xu Fu had no idea that Wei Liao had found him at the temple; he gave brief instructions.

He ordered the Fengchang Temple staff to cooperate in building an altar in Xianyang City and then perform divination.

Since the people suspected that the gods were bringing disaster and were panicked, Xu Fu would play a trick: let the gods take back the disaster and feed good fortune back to the State of Qin.

By using this divination, Xu Fu actually wanted to clarify what disasters would arise from this drought and how long it would last. He wanted to know a more specific timeframe.

After giving his orders, he dismissed everyone to make preparations. When the crowd dispersed, Wei Liao entered Xu Fu’s line of sight.

"Senior Brother." Xu Fu walked up to him.

Wei Liao snapped out of his daze. "Have you reported this to the King?"

Xu Fu shook his head openly. "No."

Wei Liao was choked. "You haven't told the King, yet you take it upon yourself to decide such a major matter as divination? How will you get onto the city tower then?" Wei Liao had a headache, thinking that this was indeed his junior brother; his willfulness was simply fatal!

"I will mention it to him after the King finishes the court session."

Seeing Xu Fu so nonchalant, Wei Liao was extremely anxious. "Regardless of what relationship you have with him in private, do not forget that he is the King. If you make decisions without his consent, can he be happy?"

"He isn't that petty." Xu Fu once again selectively forgot that he had cursed Ying Zheng for being petty while in Sanchuan.

"Senior Brother, I won't go to the nobles' side anymore. Now that the plague has broken out, those nobles don't need us to warn them." Xu Fu spoke again, blocking all of Wei Liao’s words. Seeing Xu Fu’s serious expression, Wei Liao couldn't scold him anymore. After a long silence, he only said, "I know you are intelligent; just use your own judgment."

"Thank you, Senior Brother." Xu Fu said these four words with rare sincerity.

The two walked side by side toward the exit.

Someone in the Fengchang Temple couldn't help but secretly watch their backs.

Su Yi glanced over and walked into the hall, seeing Wang Liu seriously preparing the divination items.

Wang Liu heard the movement, glanced at him, and then coldly withdrew his gaze. Ever since they realized they had misunderstood each other, they had rarely interacted due to embarrassment.

Su Yi had originally wanted to praise him, but after bumping into Wang Liu’s cold demeanor, he swallowed his words.

Instead, someone outside the door said in a sour tone, "Someone used to be at odds with Master Xu, but this person is smart; knowing Master Xu has real ability, he immediately followed him to curry favor. Look, now that Master Xu gives an order, he immediately goes to do it. What a good act of a bootlicker..."

Wang Liu had been too prominent these days.

Who would have thought that after Xu Fu became the Fengchang, he would really let bygones be bygones and dare to entrust Wang Liu with important tasks? As a result, Wang Liu had stolen quite a bit of the spotlight. How could this not make people jealous? Some shallow-minded people who couldn't hide their thoughts couldn't help but jump out to mock Wang Liu.

To be honest, those with slightly better information knew that a plague might break out in Xianyang. If that was the case, who would want to go up to the city tower to publicly demonstrate divination for those lowly people? But those who were dissatisfied didn't dare to resist Xu Fu. They all knew how capable Xu Fu was. Angering Xu Fu was one thing, but offending the State Lieutenant was fatal. Moreover, Xu Fu was becoming increasingly authoritative; facing his cold, clear face, no one dared to say "no."

Someone was unhappy but didn't dare to vent in front of Xu Fu, so they wanted to prick Wang Liu.

Anyway, I didn't name you, so you can't argue with me, right?

It was also because Wang Liu had been performing too well lately, almost changing his past playboy attitude, and he no longer had his usual lackeys following him, making people forget what his temper used to be like.

Could Wang Liu take this? Of course not. He immediately threw down the bamboo slip in his hand, stood up with a dark face, and stepped outside. "What? No ability to do things, yet you have the temper to talk behind my back? Like a dog, hiding outside the door and barking, yet you think you're someone? If you don't want to do the things Master Xu ordered, go tell him yourself that you don't want to come to the Fengchang Temple anymore. I don't deign to be a colleague with a petty person like you."

Wang Liu went on a rant, mercilessly, and even grasped the essence of Xu Fu’s style of scolding, hitting people where it hurt.

Su Yi suddenly reached out and pulled him back.

Wang Liu’s anger flared even higher, thinking, what, do you think I'm bullying people again? You look down on me and want to lecture me?

"This person is lazy and likes to be jealous of others. I will definitely report to the Fengchang to have you expelled from the temple." Su Yi said coldly.

The other person was stunned.

Wang Liu was also stunned.

...Could Su Yi have caught the plague too? And happened to have it in his brain? Wang Liu, who hadn't been lectured, suddenly felt a serious sense of disorientation.

·

Xu Fu and Wei Liao entered the palace together. Xu Fu was going to catch up on sleep, while Wei Liao continued to see Ying Zheng, so they naturally parted ways after entering.

Throwing thoughts of the drought and plague to the back of his mind, Xu Fu fell into a deep sleep shortly after. A thought faintly emerged in his heart: perhaps he was actually cold-hearted, otherwise, how could he calmly fall asleep when the city was in such a critical state...

"A-Fu, A-Fu, it's time to eat." Ying Zheng reached out and pushed Xu Fu, who woke up from his dream with a start.

There was no trace of fatigue on Ying Zheng’s face; he looked steady and reliable. Xu Fu grabbed his arm, used the strength to sit up, suppressed the urge to yawn, and sat slowly at the table, unwilling to move. Ying Zheng immediately ordered the attendants to bring the food.

Xu Fu didn't hide it and told Ying Zheng what he had done at the Fengchang Temple.

"You want to use this to calm the panic in the city?"

Xu Fu nodded, his movements while eating slow, not as crisp as before. He looked as if he had no appetite.

"Then in a few days. In a few days, I will order everyone to come and watch the ceremony."

"Good." Xu Fu smiled involuntarily.

That smile was like a flash in the pan; if Ying Zheng’s attention hadn't been on him the whole time, he might not have noticed it at all.

With Ying Zheng’s affirmation, Xu Fu didn't need to worry anymore. The feeling of having no worries behind him suddenly made him want to gently stroke his chest; a warmth seemed to be lingering there.

Afterward, the Fengchang Temple prepared even more meticulously.

Xu Fu also took out his own divination tools to practice in the palace.

·

Sanchuan Commandery.

A hot wind blew through the forest and into the cave.

It seemed to bring with it a foul, putrid smell.

Ying Niang gasped and struggled to climb up from the ground. She... was still alive... She hurriedly helped her daughter up. The little girl slowly opened her eyes and then revealed a surprised smile. "Mother, look, we really relied on those two breaths of immortal energy and got better... Here, here it doesn't hurt as much..."

Ying Niang hugged her, gasping hurriedly, tears washing down her face.

"Yes, we must thank him. Girl, you must remember him..."

"Hmm..."

"Wait for me here." Ying Niang let her go, stood up weakly, and using the fire that hadn't yet gone out in the cave, lit a torch and dragged her skirt as she slowly walked down. The two men buried in the dirt had struggled out a bit; their bodies emitted a foul stench, and their limbs showed signs of festering. They had no strength left and could only lean weakly in the dirt. Their eyes were not working well from being scorched by the sun, so even as Ying Niang approached, they had no reaction.

Looking at these two men who used to be smug and bully her.

Looking at their ugly faces, which had become even uglier due to the plague.

Ying Niang’s body trembled slightly, as if an excited electric current had passed through her.

She raised the torch in her hand and smiled. "I told you long ago that one day, you would pay for your blood debts..."

Her voice was cold. The two men shook violently, their voices hoarse and unpleasant. "You... what are you doing? Are you... are you crazy? You poisonous woman..."

Ying Niang smiled like a flower. "You called me a poisonous woman every day, so today I will let you see what a real poisonous woman is." With that, she threw the torch onto them. The flames quickly ignited their tattered clothes and swallowed them whole. Their throats were already ruined, but under the scorching fire, they still let out painful screams.

How much they sounded like her own painful screams back then.

An eye for an eye.

Ying Niang smiled coldly and slowly dragged her skirt back to the cave. She gently cradled her daughter’s face. "In the future, we will keep the immortal’s statue in our house and pray that he will protect my girl in the future too..."

The little girl giggled, her laughter intertwining with the hoarse screams from the hillside.

Not long after, the threat of the plague in Sanchuan Commandery was eliminated.

·

Urgent reports were constantly presented to Ying Zheng. Not to mention the commoners, even the court officials were in a panic.

It was the seventh month, and the entire Qin State was suffering from a great drought, with not a drop of rain seen for a full month.

Zheng Guo traveled everywhere, building irrigation canals. Although the people felt miserable, they weren't in a constant state of panic. Sanchuan and Nanyang were the first to lose rain, but they were also the first to start looking for water sources, opening water flows, and digging deep wells. The land couldn't be saved, but the people at least had water to drink.

Other places had no precautions, and those who had laughed at the governors of Sanchuan and Nanyang were in for bad luck; who knew that this bad luck would soon fall on their own heads?

The place in the entire country that was most panicked was, surprisingly, Xianyang.

Ying Zheng was extremely dissatisfied with the officials in the court; at this point, they were following the panic. But one couldn't blame them for panicking; it was just that while other commanderies were okay, Xianyang had actually seen an outbreak of the plague. This contagion was extremely rapid and widespread. The entire residence of the Official Physician, who had been the first to contract it, soon fell ill. After the Official Physician’s young son, several more people died, and later, even the two neighboring households were infected.

Having no other choice, Ying Zheng ordered Meng Tian to isolate that area and move everyone else away.

But the source of infection was not just in that one place.

In just a few days, people had died in two other residences.

An official knelt before Ying Zheng and said, "Please move the capital, Your Majesty!"

Move the capital? Moving the capital was such a major event! Within the territory of the Qin State, there weren't many prosperous places. Since moving from the old capital of Yongcheng to Xianyang, the Qin State had never thought about where else to move. Now that there was a great drought, where could they move? To a place without a plague? With so many royal nobles and officials, moving them was no small matter. They would probably die halfway before the capital was even moved.

Moreover, as a monarch, abandoning the people to leave—Ying Zheng believed that no matter how ruthless he was, he couldn't do such a thing.

These were the people of his Qin State, the people under his protection. If he couldn't even do this well, how could Ying Zheng’s self-esteem tolerate it?

"Say no more. At this time, all of us in the Qin State should unite as one to overcome the difficulties of the drought." Ying Zheng dismissed the court with a dark face.

When he returned to his sleeping quarters, he saw Xu Fu leaning on the table, looking down at some bamboo slips. He could only see Xu Fu’s side profile, which was a bit pale, as if his energy had been exhausted.

Ying Zheng walked up and asked him, "Did you forget to eat this morning?"

Xu Fu pushed the bamboo slips away and shook his head. "No." After saying that, he pointed to the cloth strip beside him. "Look, I did an experiment according to the methods in the witchcraft."

"What experiment?"

Ying Zheng had no interest in the cloth strip and pushed it away immediately.

Xu Fu pushed the bamboo slips to him.

Ying Zheng looked down and saw it written: "Soak with one's own essence and blood to achieve success." His own essence and blood? Ying Zheng’s expression suddenly darkened. He grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist; although it had been bandaged, blood was still seeping out.

"Are you bored? Doing this kind of experiment?"

Xu Fu’s brows were filled with a sense of weariness. Ying Zheng had never seen him like this, and his heart tightened slightly, but the angry scolding had already been spoken, so Ying Zheng could only force his expression from rage to calm.

Xu Fu frowned and whispered, "I didn't mean to. I just wanted to take a drop of blood to test, but my hand shook, and the pen-knife cut a gash on my wrist." The cloth strip was stained bright red, looking even worse. If it weren't for the fact that his own blood was on it, Xu Fu would have thrown this ugly thing away.

Thinking that he had made himself look like he was trying to commit suicide just to do an experiment, Xu Fu felt he had lost face.

Ying Zheng waved his hand to dismiss the others and couldn't help but ask, "Have you been irritable these past few days?"

"How did you know?" Xu Fu was surprised. He was already very good at controlling his emotions; no one had ever been able to notice anything wrong with his mood before.

"I eat and sleep with you every day, how could I not know?" Ying Zheng said irritably. "I haven't even felt irritable yet, and you’ve become anxious before me."

Xu Fu frowned, showing no sign of relaxing. "A-Zheng, I don't want you to be so worried." He had received all the benefits he should have from Ying Zheng, and Ying Zheng was indeed a one-in-a-million lover. How could he allow himself to fail?

Ying Zheng’s mouth curled up, but he forced it back down.

He felt a bit of pleasure, but Ying Zheng couldn't be coaxed so easily.

So he didn't speak.

Xu Fu continued to speak for himself, "If I lose my value, what will happen?"

"What?" Ying Zheng didn't understand what he meant. Why did he suddenly bring up such a sentence?

"I asked for your decree before, saying I wanted to perform divination on the city tower, but later I postponed it. Do you know why, A-Zheng?"

"Why?" Xu Fu had told him the time hadn't come, so Ying Zheng naturally wouldn't urge him. On this point, he could still trust Xu Fu. Even if the sacrifice and divination didn't work, he naturally had other ways to handle the aftermath.

"Because," Xu Fu paused, his eyes blank for a moment, "I can't divine anything anymore."

Ying Zheng was not surprised upon hearing this, not showing even a hint of anxiety. He said gently, "Weren't you like this last year too? That was because you hadn't rested well. Maybe this time it's the same. You said you couldn't divine before, but when you used that... copper coin, didn't you divine it?"

"But the Six Lines are useless too." Xu Fu’s voice was faintly tinged with impatience.

Ying Zheng was slightly startled, looking at Xu Fu’s current appearance.

He didn't know if it was because of the blood loss or the excessive pressure during this period that made his face so pale. But seeing him like this, Ying Zheng suddenly remembered that Xu Fu hadn't even reached his capping ceremony; he was just a teenager. Being so young, how could he have more things to worry about than himself? It was already not easy for him to reach this point...

Ying Zheng didn't think about how he had to think about how to survive when he was even younger.

Xu Fu’s fingers twisted together. "I can't divine anything. Do you remember I once told you that a fortune-teller cannot divine for themselves?"

"I remember."

"What is our relationship now?"

Ying Zheng opened his mouth, thinking about what relationship he could answer to make Xu Fu moved, but Xu Fu interrupted him.

"Look, we are so close now, your fate might even be affected by mine. A fortune-teller should have no family or friends, but I have you. Now, even your affairs, I can't divine at all..."

"I might even make a fool of myself when I go up to the city tower."

"If I can't divine anything, what kind of National Master am I?"

Ying Zheng suddenly couldn't help but laugh out loud.

Xu Fu looked up and stared at him coldly. "Is there anything funny about that?"

After saying this, Xu Fu himself felt it was a bit ridiculous.

Was his brain possessed? He wouldn't have said such things before. Fortunately, there were no palace maids in the hall, otherwise, he would have lost all face! All his poise, manners, and temperament, all gone!

Xu Fu didn't want to admit that he was acting like he was acting spoiled.

Ying Zheng was about to explain it to him properly when a palace maid suddenly knelt at the door, trembling uncontrollably. "Your Majesty, report to Your Majesty... Young Master Fusu, Young Master Fusu has developed a high fever..."

Developing a high fever at this time—no one would think it was a good sign.

chapters.title: 第118章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu and Ying Zheng stood up almost simultaneously, "Summon the imperial physician!"

The palace maid barely managed to regain some composure, whispering, "Replying to Your Majesty, the physician has already been summoned."

Xu Fu took a step forward, "How did the young master develop such a high fever?"

The palace maid was long accustomed to Xu Fu's status in the palace; even though he had questioned her before Ying Zheng, she was not surprised and immediately replied, "Because of the many incidents in the city lately, we have been extremely careful in caring for the young master. These past few days, the young master has shown no symptoms of catching a cold..." As she spoke, the maid’s face turned paler, and her voice even choked with emotion.

Neither Xu Fu’s nor Ying Zheng’s expression looked good.

If it wasn't a cold, then it could only be the more terrifying alternative.

...Fusu might have contracted the plague.

High fever, vomiting, and diarrhea were common early symptoms.

The conversation between Xu Fu and Ying Zheng was interrupted and cast to the back of their minds. Ying Zheng grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist and led him out of the hall. Xu Fu unconsciously loosened his clenched fist, only then noticing a slight stinging sensation in his palm; he must have pinched his own skin in his nervousness.

Ying Zheng’s large hand opened his palm, gently stroking it as if transferring his own steadiness and calm to Xu Fu.

When Xu Fu and Ying Zheng arrived outside the side hall and were about to enter, they saw an imperial physician walk out and kneel before Ying Zheng, his forehead pressed to the ground, "Your Majesty, please consider your health and do not enter the hall."

Xu Fu pursed his lips and remained silent.

Ying Zheng’s face was already icy, "So it seems, Young Master Fusu has indeed contracted the plague?"

Even though the summer heat had not yet dissipated, the physician felt waves of cold sweat on his back. He braced himself to keep from collapsing, meeting Ying Zheng’s cold, sharp gaze, and said, "Yes, Young Master Fusu has contracted the plague. This humble official questioned the maids attending him, and they said the young master had no contact with any source of infection. I fear we must wait for the young master to wake up and question him carefully to determine the symptoms."

Palace maids inevitably have lapses, but in Ying Zheng’s eyes, this lapse was truly fatal.

"Move aside," Ying Zheng said in a deep voice.

The physician remained kneeling, "Your Majesty, the plague is highly contagious! Please, for your own sake, take care!"

"Can Young Master Fusu merely having a high fever infect me? I am not that fragile."

Seeing Ying Zheng’s firm attitude, the physician could only climb up with weak limbs and clear the path into the side hall.

The physician knew Ying Zheng’s stubborn nature; for the sake of his own life, he had to be sensible and move. He had said his piece, and if something truly happened, he shouldn't die too miserably.

Xu Fu followed Ying Zheng into the side hall.

Suddenly, they heard a maid’s startled cry.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng exchanged a look; had something happened? They quickened their pace, but upon entering, they both froze.

Fusu lay on the bed, his face flushed with an unnatural red, his entire being delirious with fever, unable to even open his eyes. He seemed to hear footsteps and weakly opened his mouth, but no sound came out before he closed it again powerlessly.

Beside the bed sat a chubby little dumpling, wearing a red robe that looked quite festive—almost comically so.

The palace maid, with a bitter face and teary eyes, grabbed his hem, "Young Master Huhai, please don't get any closer, let us take you back."

"Your Majesty," the attendant by the bed saw the two and was startled, immediately kneeling to pay respects, "Master Xu."

Hearing the sound, Huhai turned his head and looked at Xu Fu with grievance, blinking his teary eyes. He looked back at the unconscious Fusu, seemingly making a difficult choice in those few seconds. Then, Huhai moved his short legs and slowly walked over to Xu Fu. He hugged Xu Fu’s leg and began to wail, tears streaming down his face.

"Wuu... brother..." Huhai tugged at Xu Fu’s robe. Though he looked young, he had quite a bit of strength. Xu Fu had to bend down, "Don't cry. If you cry, Fusu will be too scared to wake up."

Huhai covered his mouth with his hands, his cheeks puffed out like buns, "Mmm... five..." The broken sobs were muffled in his mouth, his obedient appearance making him look truly pitiable.

Seeing this, Ying Zheng’s gaze toward Huhai deepened.

He hadn't expected Huhai to have more affection than his parents; at such a young age, he already knew how to worry about his brother. Fusu’s kindness toward him hadn't been in vain. However, a sense of pride followed; that Huhai could be so sensible was surely due to his and Xu Fu’s teaching.

Ying Zheng withdrew his gaze and walked to the bedside.

Huhai wouldn't let go of Xu Fu’s leg, making it difficult for Xu Fu to move. The surrounding servants, seeing Huhai crying so miserably, dared not come forward to pull him away. Xu Fu had to find an excuse to make him let go.

"Go hug Fusu and talk to him to wake him up," Xu Fu whispered. After saying it, he felt he was overestimating Huhai’s intelligence; he was so young, could he understand the meaning?

Huhai let go of his leg, grabbed Xu Fu’s hem, and followed him to the bedside. Then, with great effort, he arched his bottom, crawled onto the edge of the bed, and squeezed himself right next to Fusu.

Xu Fu’s heart jumped to his throat; Huhai was young and easily infected. If something were to happen...

While Xu Fu was thinking, Huhai had already leaned against Fusu’s cheek, breathing and puffing.

Xu Fu was genuinely worried that when Fusu finally woke up, he would touch his face and find it wet.

Because Huhai let go of his hand, he opened his mouth to cry, "Brother... wuu... hiccup..." The dark cloud hanging over Xu Fu and Ying Zheng was inexplicably lightened by the comical way he cried.

One wondered if Fusu simply couldn't stand having a human space heater, an automatic fountain, and a professional mourner with a winding vocal range next to him.

He opened his eyes and pushed Huhai’s head aside.

"Father..."

"Wuu wuu... brother..." Huhai sobbed and lunged forward, his chubby body pressing directly onto Fusu’s face.

Fusu: ...

As Huhai cried, he hiccuped on Fusu’s head. His teeth hadn't fully grown yet, so the crying was a mixture of tears and saliva.

Fusu resisted the urge to flip him away, trying to ignore the tragic feeling that his hair might be getting rained on.

Xu Fu was worried Huhai would deform Fusu’s face, so he stepped forward and grabbed Huhai’s collar, but he couldn't lift him. Xu Fu had to acknowledge that he was still the weakling he was; he couldn't lift people as easily as Jianjia could.

Ying Zheng reached out from behind, almost encircling Xu Fu in his arms. He lifted Huhai up. Huhai was hiccuping from crying; he raised his hand to rub his nose, then squinted his eyes, "Ah... pfft—" and spat squarely onto Fusu’s face.

Fusu was suddenly much more awake after being sprayed.

"Father." His voice was clearer and stronger this time.

The palace maid, looking horrified, hurried forward to wipe Fusu’s face.

Huhai seemed to realize he had done something wrong; he quickly covered his mouth, obediently held in Ying Zheng’s hand, not moving, his dark eyes fixed on Fusu.

Fusu coughed lightly, "Father, perhaps you should send Huhai away."

Ying Zheng put Huhai down.

Huhai tumbled face-first onto the ground, his bottom in the air, and mumbled, "No... go..."

Fusu’s mouth twitched, and he had to temporarily put his troublesome younger brother out of his mind, saying to Ying Zheng, "Father, have I contracted the plague?" Fusu’s small face was pale, but his gaze was steady, much like Ying Zheng’s usual demeanor.

Ying Zheng was silent for a few seconds before replying without concealment, "Yes."

The palace attendants lowered their heads, feeling a heavy heart.

The eldest son, Fusu, was highly regarded by the King; if something happened to him... no one could bear the responsibility.

And at such a young age... how could he be destroyed by the plague...

Fusu, on the contrary, smiled magnanimously, "Father and Teacher need not worry about me. I was weak as a child and took much medicine, often spending time in bed to recover. Now, with a mere plague, as the King’s eldest son, how could I be so easily defeated?"

If said under normal circumstances, these words might sound cheesy, but now, they were perfectly appropriate.

The gloom on Ying Zheng’s face dissipated, and he smiled gently, patting Fusu’s head, "Good, worthy of being my son!"

Seeing that Fusu was not despondent, Xu Fu felt relieved. He turned his gaze to Huhai, who was still sprawled on the floor, looking nothing like Ying Zheng’s son. Xu Fu picked Huhai up. Huhai, with his red, swollen eyes, leaned toward Xu Fu’s chest, but Xu Fu blocked him with his hand and asked, "Young Master Fusu, have you come into contact with any filthy objects recently?"

"Filthy objects?" Fusu was confused.

"Such as sewage, carcasses of rodents, etc..."

Fusu’s face suddenly turned deathly pale, looking as if he were about to retch, "...Teacher, that day, I... I was in the garden and encountered an attendant who had taken the fish kept in the palace, skinned and gutted them, and buried them in the garden while they were still bloody. The scene was disgusting. Because I accidentally bumped into him, the attendant was so panicked he collided with me. Later, I... I ordered him to be dragged out and beaten to death."

Ying Zheng naturally didn't think his son was cruel for killing a lowly attendant; on the contrary, he thought Fusu showed the beginnings of resolve, being able to decisively deal with those who offended him.

"Chicken plague?" Xu Fu’s attention was entirely on the attendant’s strange behavior.

How strange, killing fish for no reason in the garden?

Seeing the doubt in Xu Fu’s eyes, Fusu immediately added, "Later, I ordered an investigation and learned that the attendant had seen others die miserably from the plague in his childhood. Now, hearing that people in Xianyang had contracted the plague, he was terrified. He stole several fish, killed them in the same way, and buried them in the garden."

Without Fusu needing to say more, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng understood what a foolish thing the attendant had done.

Those fish might not have been problematic initially, but being skinned and buried bloody in the soil during the hot weather, they would soon rot. The garden was full of insects, and insects carried bacteria and viruses; who knew who they might land on...

Xu Fu felt a chill run through him just thinking about it.

It was truly disgusting... the scene must have been foul and rotting.

Xu Fu had never seen such a plague. Although he had learned some medical theory and pharmacology from bamboo slips, it didn't mean he could overcome such a historical challenge. However, he quickly thought of Sanchuan Commandery and wondered if that mother and daughter had survived. If they had, it proved the plague wasn't so terrifying—at least not invincible.

Ying Zheng thought of this too and nodded slightly at Xu Fu, "I have already ordered men to Sanchuan Commandery to inquire about them."

Xu Fu responded, "Do the palace physicians have a way?"

"We must wait." Ying Zheng beckoned the physicians over.

The physicians, who had been acting like wooden stakes, finally gained a sense of presence. Despite this, they remained humble and cautious. After receiving Ying Zheng’s permission, they whispered questions to Fusu about what happened that day and where he felt discomfort. After asking everything, the physicians’ expressions remained grim. They prescribed medicine to help Fusu lower his fever and prevent the plague from worsening.

Then they requested to leave to discuss the matter further.

Ying Zheng knew that forcing them wouldn't yield results, so he waved them away.

Fusu, having been questioned for so long, was exhausted, his eyelids drooping. Seeing that Fusu was not in immediate danger, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng felt reassured. Just as they were about to take Huhai out, Huhai struggled in Xu Fu’s arms and pointed toward Fusu, "Mmm! Mmm... brother..."

Xu Fu bent down and put him down.

Ying Zheng said, "Let Young Master Huhai stay here for a while, then you can take him back to the side hall."

"Yes," the attendants replied hurriedly.

Ying Zheng took hold of Xu Fu’s wrist again; he didn't know if it was his imagination, but Xu Fu’s wrist seemed thinner, "Come back to the palace with me."

Xu Fu pointed at Huhai’s small figure clambering toward the bed, "Then he..." Was it not too heartless of them to just leave Huhai here?

"Huhai," Xu Fu couldn't help but call out.

Huhai turned his head, looked at Xu Fu, then sprawled by the bed, burying his head in front of Fusu, "With brother," he said softly. This sentence was uncharacteristically clear, albeit with a slight lisp of saliva.

Fusu, exhausted, had already closed his eyes; even as Huhai leaned against him, he did not open them again.

Huhai refused to leave, and Xu Fu couldn't force him. In the end, it was because he and Ying Zheng were not qualified parents; Huhai followed Fusu everywhere, so naturally, he couldn't be separated from his brother.

Ying Zheng whispered, "Just have the attendants take him away in a while. Children fall asleep easily and sleep soundly; they won't notice when they are carried away."

Xu Fu thought of Huhai’s red, swollen eyes and nodded, "Let's go."

However, after coming out, Ying Zheng still had the physicians prepare medicine for Huhai as well.

Meanwhile, many items were cleared from the side hall to be burned. After returning to the palace, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng took off their robes, bathed to cleanse themselves, and set the clothes aside.

After eating together, they retired to bed early.

Since the nationwide drought, it had been rare for them to get a good rest. Resting early was Xu Fu’s suggestion. Excessive fatigue lowered resistance, and those with low resistance were easily infected by the plague. Both he and Ying Zheng had to oversee the big picture; they couldn't afford to fall ill. The best approach was to balance work and rest, leaving no opportunity for the plague to take hold.

Once they lay down, their thoughts seemed to sink into the depths along with their bodies.

Ying Zheng tried hard to restore the previous atmosphere, his low voice sounding in the darkness, "Does A-Fu still worry about not being able to perform divination for me?"

Xu Fu opened his eyes and looked at the top of the bed, his gaze vacant for a moment.

Perhaps he should thank Hu Hai for that bit of clowning around; the thoughts that had been filling his head were suddenly gone.

"...I don't worry about it anymore," Xu Fu said softly.

Ying Zheng felt it was a pity. He never denied Xu Fu's formidable abilities or the wondrous nature he possessed. However, Xu Fu was always formidable and aloof in front of others, and he was the same in front of him, so what difference did it make? He felt his role as a lover was a bit stifling. Only when day after day passed and Xu Fu dared to open up his vulnerable side to him would the heart hanging high in his chest finally settle.

"Let's hold the divination tomorrow," Xu Fu said.

Ying Zheng felt a bit helpless, "You can't just decide things on a whim like this. I need to notify people in advance for the divination day so that more people can gather at the foot of the city tower; otherwise, wouldn't it fail to achieve your original intention?"

Xu Fu also felt a bit ashamed. Before, when Ying Zheng had taken the initiative to ask him, he had kept putting it off, but now he was suddenly acting like he was having a fit, saying he wanted to hold it tomorrow. It was only because Ying Zheng had a good temper that he hadn't lost it.

Xu Fu nodded, "Then... then when do you say?"

Ying Zheng keenly sensed the weakness in Xu Fu's tone. It was rare for him to be so compliant; Ying Zheng almost wondered if it was the moon or the sun hanging outside.

"The day after tomorrow, then." Ying Zheng didn't know why Xu Fu had suddenly let go of his inner misgivings and was able to hold the divination so openly and naturally, but he knew Xu Fu was anxious, so he moved the date up as much as he could.

The next day, Xu Fu did not go to the Fengchang Temple, but went to the side hall to check on Fusu.

Fusu was sleeping soundly, his face not as deathly pale as the day before, nor was he running such a high fever. The air in the side hall was not very good, so after Xu Fu instructed the palace maids to ventilate the room, he left.

He didn't notice that the moment he stepped out, a lump arched up under Fusu's quilt, and after a while, that lump struggled to crawl out.

The palace attendants had just seen Xu Fu off and turned around to see a cute, dazed head resting outside the quilt. The attendants were so frightened they almost screamed, and it took them a long time to suppress their startled souls, "...Young Master Hu Hai, why are you here?"

Hu Hai yawned lazily, ignoring the attendants entirely, and fell asleep hugging Fusu's arm.

Seeing Hu Hai's relaxed manner, the attendants paced back and forth in anxiety, but they didn't dare to forcefully pull him off. They were even more afraid to report to Xu Fu that Young Master Hu Hai had appeared on Young Master Fusu's bed again for some unknown reason. After a night had passed, who knew if he would catch the illness?

The attendants looked at each other with bloodshot eyes and kept the matter a secret from each other.

In the blink of an eye, it was the day of the divination.

The city had long known that the Fengchang Xu would personally preside over the divination ceremony and allow the commoners to observe, which was incredibly novel for them. With feelings of reverence, admiration, or fear, they gathered under the city tower.

The location Xu Fu chose was not high; it was within the walls of Xianyang City, and after he walked up, the commoners could surround him on all sides.

At this moment, not only the commoners but also the city's nobles and even court officials had found their places to stand, looking forward to the upcoming divination ceremony.

From afar, they saw a group of people coming from the other end.

This group was dressed in sacrificial robes, serious and unsmiling, each with a solemn look on their faces. They held divination tools in their hands, such as tortoise shells... these were things the commoners usually only heard about but could never truly see. The commoners temporarily cast aside the panic brought by the drought, unable to help but show expressions of wonder and joy, looking at the items in these people's hands with immense reverence.

It was these very items that, in the eyes of the crowd, became symbols of ancient, mysterious power.

At this time, some commoners noticed a carriage in front of this group. The carriage had no side panels, only a layer of cloth draped over it. The cloth was very thin and would lift with a breeze, vaguely revealing the figure inside. The commoners stretched their necks. They had roughly guessed the identity of this person. They remembered the Grand Diviner who had presided over the Wax Festival with the King in the fields last year.

They could still vaguely recall that person's demeanor.

Even though he was wearing heavy, stiff sacrificial robes, and even though he was just standing in the field, he was different from everyone else. Every gesture, every glance back, was something one could never forget...

The crowd held their breath involuntarily.

They thought they would see a Grand Diviner in full regalia again.

But the carriage stopped, and Xu Fu stepped out. He was still wearing that simple, modified sacrificial robe. The robe was not cinched at the waist, making it look somewhat loose. It was neither heavy nor complex, and wearing it gave it a different kind of appeal.

If the Xu Fu in the fields before was like a spokesperson for the gods, with an ancient aura as if he had come from the distant past and had already spoken with the ancestral spirits...

...then the Xu Fu at this moment appeared elegant and free-spirited, yet possessed an indescribable, haughty temperament. That pride was something that commanded submission; no one would feel dissatisfaction or doubt toward his arrogance.

Ying Zheng, surrounded by attendants, was mixed in the crowd. He was tall enough that, no matter how many people were around, he could clearly see Xu Fu stepping off the carriage.

Every gesture carried a natural, noble air.

A sense of pride surged in Ying Zheng's heart.

This bit of nobility in Xu Fu was truly cultivated from him. Seeing him like this now, Xu Fu looked even more like someone from the heavens. Where was he like a spokesperson for the gods? He looked more like a god himself! Compared to the images of immortals on ancient murals, Ying Zheng felt no one could surpass this appearance of Xu Fu.

Xu Fu remained completely composed. He beckoned Wang Liu and Su Yi to come forward, and the two took their places, one on the left and one on the right, two steps behind him.

They ascended the city tower together. Xu Fu's hem dragged across the ground, but no one thought about whether it was clean or not. They were all so excited their faces flushed red, staring tightly at Xu Fu's figure. They watched as Xu Fu stood on the tower and turned around, as if looking down on all living beings, forcing everyone who accidentally met his gaze to bow at his feet.

The crowd couldn't help but kneel and kowtow.

Only Ying Zheng stood out from the crowd, standing among the people and gazing at Xu Fu from afar.

In that instant, Ying Zheng really felt the thrill of secretly exchanging affections with Xu Fu.

"Set the tortoise shell, place the six lines," Xu Fu said in a clear, cold voice. The volume wasn't high, but it reached everyone's ears perfectly.

The commoners knew of tortoise shells, but they truly didn't know what those "six lines" were. Thinking of the rumors about this Fengchang Xu in Xianyang, the commoners didn't think too much about it. They had long heard that he was a man of great ability; perhaps he was using methods that many people didn't know about. Thinking this, the commoners became even more excited. They wanted to know, besides tortoise shell divination, what other methods could there be? Was this Fengchang Xu really that accurate?

Facing Xu Fu's face, the dissatisfaction some commoners had felt when the drought first arrived vanished in an instant.

Such a dashing figure must surely have great skills... the Wax Festival couldn't have gone wrong in his hands, they thought to themselves.

Su Yi set the tortoise shell, and Wang Liu placed the six lines and the Bagua.

The two retreated consciously, and then torches were lit on the city tower. The flickering firelight illuminated Xu Fu's eyes.

Later, countless people mentioned this day.

They all said that on that day, Fengchang Xu's eyes seemed to be filled with the light of the world. With every move, his whole body radiated an immortal aura. The divination he performed was something others dared not even look at, fearing they would be blinded. That day, they looked up at Fengchang Xu's figure—handsome, resilient, cold, and powerful.

Only such a person seemed like someone sent by the gods to save them.

Commoners are sometimes like grass in the wind; they don't care what you are, they only seek a good life. At this moment, they pinned their hopes on Fengchang Xu and naturally did not stint on their faith as believers.

The commoners knelt on the ground, muttering vernacular that Xu Fu couldn't understand. It sounded a bit eerie, but Xu Fu automatically translated all of it into praise for himself.

Xu Fu's fingers swept over the tortoise shell and the Bagua in front of him. He went through the motions of burning wooden sticks, inserting them into the tortoise shell, and then patting the Bagua disc.

"Silence," Xu Fu said.

The commoners looked at him with anxiety and unease.

By now, the day was gradually turning to evening. A round sun was sliding down toward the horizon, and red clouds hung in the sky. Some said red clouds were a good omen, others said they were a bad one, but who could say for sure? At this moment, they only hoped it was a good sign.

Xu Fu simply replaced the words in the divination he had interpreted with Ying Zheng before going to Sanchuan Commandery, so that the commoners could roughly understand what the divination meant. Upon hearing this, the commoners were stunned.

So Fengchang Xu had long ago calculated that there would be a disaster, and that this disaster was caused by water. There were many difficulties on the water, and it required everyone to unite and give enough trust to achieve final victory.

The commoners were dizzy from listening, feeling that not many of Xu Fu's words were applicable.

And just at this moment, Xu Fu suddenly spoke, saying, "Do you think the gods have already abandoned you?"

A buzzing sound rose from the crowd. When the drought first hit Xianyang, they did indeed believe it was a disaster sent by the gods. What was Fengchang Xu going to say now? Was he going to deny their words? The commoners looked at each other, not daring to openly question Xu Fu. In their bones, they still instinctively held fear for him.

Just as people in ancient tribes had to respect the shaman and dared not offend them lightly.

Xu Fu's volume rose slightly as he said, "Do you know that the gods have already granted you several sources of water?"

"What?!" The commoners were shocked. Watching the water run out day by day and the wells drying up, could a blessing really descend at this time?

"Water sources!"

"Heavens, Fengchang Xu really has great ability..."

"Who knows if it's true..." Just as a discordant voice emerged, it was immediately shouted down.

Xu Fu raised his finger and pointed into the distance, "Ten miles to the northwest."

His expression was indifferent and aloof, truly like a god who could easily control life and death with a wave of his hand. The commoners watched him, dazed. Not to mention them, even Ying Zheng was slightly stunned.

Xu Fu was indeed suited to stand on high ground.

He was still suited to stand on high ground with me.

For some reason, Ying Zheng felt his heartbeat quicken.

At this moment, Xu Fu raised his hand again and pointed casually into the distance, yet it stirred the hearts of countless people below the city tower, "Five miles to the southeast."

"Three miles from the east of the city toward the back mountain."

"The hollow in the north of the city."

"Lian Family Village outside Xianyang City."

"..."

Xu Fu pointed out several places in one breath. The commoners' hearts beat like drums, and they held their breath, not daring to let go, fearing they would disturb the god. Oh, where was the god? Wasn't it the person in the sacrificial robes on the city tower?

Xu Fu finally stopped, "People will be sent to these places to search for the life-saving springs left to us by the gods."

Xu Fu looked up at the sky and spoke again, "The gods have indicated that if this disaster is to be resolved, it can be aided by external forces. Then the disaster will end early, and you will no longer have to suffer." Xu Fu pointed casually, "Water." Then he pointed to the red clouds in the sky, "Fire."

"Water to save lives, fire to burn away the sick body, isolating death from the outside."

"Finally, divine medicine must be used; only then can those infected with the plague recover."

In fact, many ministers in the court were already unable to contain themselves, wanting to know what the divine medicine was. Did the god even write down the prescription for him? The ministers, full of curiosity, were hindered by face and the fact that Ying Zheng was standing not far away, so they had to suppress their curiosity.

Actually, Xu Fu wanted to say, I want to know what the divine medicine is too.

However, Xu Fu couldn't just gloss over it, so he made up some nonsense, pointing to the road outside Xianyang City, "The gods told me that someone will carry the divine medicine, coming from this road, bringing the protection the gods have given to Qin."

The commoners were trembling with excitement. Could it really be true? Although they couldn't see with their own eyes how Fengchang Xu performed the divination, they were already deeply convinced in their hearts.

The commoners knelt down again.

Xu Fu also shouted out a line fitting the occasion, "Great Qin conforms to the will of heaven and deserves the protection of the gods. Do not be panicked or anxious. We must wait for the blessings of the gods..."

The commoners did not doubt him and hurriedly bowed again, shouting, "Thank you, Immortal Xu."

Xu Fu was startled.

These people didn't call him by his official title or "Sir," but instead called him "Immortal Xu," which sounded like a name for a half-baked swindler.

But regardless of whether the title was good or not, at least these commoners had truly kept him in their hearts. They might still wonder how water could be found just by pointing, and that this trick of Xu Fu's was really fooling people. But soon they would know their own horizons were narrow!

The torches on the city tower were blown out, and Xu Fu lowered his eyes, coldly ordering, "The divination is over. Everyone disperse."

The commoners were still immersed in Xu Fu's demeanor, swaying as they dispersed with light steps.

As for the court ministers, their gazes toward Xu Fu held awe, but also sneers and disdain.

Xu Fu walked down the city tower and searched for that gaze, but because there were so many people, he couldn't find the owner. Xu Fu frowned secretly, but even if the other party had bad intentions, they couldn't act on them at this moment.

Because Xu Fu had already seen Ying Zheng walking slowly toward him.

Seeing this, the ministers hurriedly bowed, "Greetings, Your Majesty."

Ying Zheng walked up to Xu Fu, the light in his eyes burning so hot it could almost scald someone. He grabbed Xu Fu's wrist and led him toward the carriage, leaving the ministers behind. The ministers looked at each other, even greater doubts rising in their hearts, but they could only grit their teeth and hold it in.

Lest they be slaughtered by the King.

Ying Zheng brought Xu Fu into the carriage, and Xu Fu reached out and tugged at his sleeve, "Come closer."

Ying Zheng thought to himself, could it be that Xu Fu was so stirred that he wanted to vent his emotions with a kiss? Ying Zheng prepared himself, even thinking about how to take the initiative and kiss Xu Fu until he was dizzy. Who knew, just as he moved closer, Xu Fu leaned directly against him, as if the spine he had been holding straight all day had finally collapsed.

"A-Fu?"

徐福和嬴政几乎是同时站了起来，“请侍医！”
宫女勉强找回了几分镇静，低声道：“回王上，已经去请侍医了。”
徐福往前挪了挪步子，“公子怎么会发起高热？”
宫女早已习惯徐福在宫中的地位，哪怕他越过嬴政当先发了问，宫女也并不惊奇，立即便回了徐福的话，“因着近来城中事端不少，奴婢们已经十分小心照顾公子了，这几日公子也并未有受凉的症状……”那宫女越说脸色越白，声音甚至还有些哽咽。
徐福和嬴政的脸色，谁都好不起来。
若不是受凉，那就只能是更可怖的那个结果。
……扶苏或许，染上疫病了。
高热，呕吐，腹泻，会是初期容易出现的反应。
徐福和嬴政的对话被打断，此时也抛到脑后去了。嬴政抓住徐福的手腕便将他往殿外带，徐福握紧的手掌不自觉地松开，然后才发觉掌心有些微微的刺痛，大约是刚才太过紧张，竟然不小心将掌心掐出印子来了。
嬴政的大手撑开他的手掌，动作轻柔地抚弄了一下他的掌心，像是将他的沉稳冷静传递给了徐福一样。
徐福和嬴政到了偏殿外，正要往里走去，却见一侍医走出来，跪在了嬴政的跟前，侍医额头磕地，“王上，请王上为身体着想，勿要进殿。”
徐福抿了抿唇，没有开口说话。
嬴政此时脸色已经一片冰寒了，“如此看来，扶苏公子的确是染上疫病了？”
明明暑气未散，但侍医愣是感觉到了后背阵阵冷汗。他强撑着不让自己背脊软倒下去，生顶着嬴政冷厉的目光，道：“是，扶苏公子，染了疫病。下臣询问了公子身旁随侍的宫女，宫女说公子并未接触到什么病源，恐怕还要等公子清醒之后，仔细询问一番，才好对准症状。”
宫女难免有疏漏的时候，不过这个疏漏在嬴政眼中，实在可致死了。
“让开。”嬴政沉声道。
侍医跪地不起，“王上，疫病恐会传染啊，王上请保重自己！”
“公子扶苏不过发个高热，便能给寡人染上病了吗？寡人还没有这样虚弱。”
见嬴政态度坚决，侍医也只能四肢酸软地从地上爬了起来，让出了踏进偏殿的路来。
侍医知道嬴政说一不二的性子，为了自己的小命着想，他应当识时务地让出路来，反正他劝的话是说了，若是当真出了什么事，自己应当也不至于死得太惨。
这头徐福跟着嬴政进了偏殿。
突然听见宫女一声惊叫。
徐福不自觉地和嬴政对视了一眼，难道出什么事了？他们不由得加快了脚步，朝里走去，等走进去之后，两人却是齐齐呆住了。
扶苏躺在床榻之上，面上浮动着不正常的红晕，整个人都烧得迷迷糊糊的，连双眼也睁不开，他似乎听见了脚步声，虚弱地张了张嘴，但是什么声音也未能发出来，便又无力地合上了。
而那床榻边上，却有个矮墩墩的团子，穿着一身红袍子，看上去还挺喜庆，喜庆得有点憨。
宫女苦着脸，眼泪婆娑地抓住他的衣摆，“胡亥公子，可不要凑上前了，快快与我们回去吧。”
“王上。”床边的内侍见了徐福二人，面上一惊，马上跪地行礼，“徐奉常。”
胡亥听见了声音，转过头来，委屈地看着徐福，眨了眨双眼，有点儿泪眼朦胧的意思。他回头又看了一眼昏迷不醒的扶苏，似乎正在这短短的时间里做着什么艰难的抉择。随后，胡亥还是迈动了小短腿，慢慢走到了徐福的跟前来，他伸手抱着徐福的腿，呜呜咽咽地就开始哭，眼泪哗啦啦地往下掉。
“呜……哥哥……”胡亥拽着徐福的袍子，他年纪瞧上去小，但力道还真不小，徐福不得不往下弯了弯腰，“别哭，你一哭，扶苏就会被你吓得醒不来了。”
胡亥抬起手捂住嘴，两颊鼓成了包子，“唔……五……”破碎的哭声挤在他口中，乖巧的模样，看上去好不引人怜惜。
嬴政见状，看着胡亥的目光倒是变得深了一些。
他不曾想到，这胡亥倒是当真比他那父母更有情意些，小小年纪，倒也知道心疼担忧兄长了，平日里扶苏对他的好倒是没白给。不过紧接着，嬴政便心中自豪了几分。胡亥能如此明理懂事，想来那也是他和徐福教得好。
嬴政收回目光，走到了床榻边去。
胡亥抱着徐福的大腿不撒手，弄得徐福要挪动个步子都变得艰难起来了。周围的宫人见胡亥哭得正惨，谁也不敢上前来将胡亥抱走。徐福只能找个借口，让胡亥先撒手了。
“去抱一抱扶苏，与他说话，将他叫醒。”徐福低声道。等说完，徐福又觉得自己实在太高看胡亥的心智了，他年纪这样小，能完整理解自己话里的意思么？
胡亥却松开腿转而抓住徐福的衣摆，跟着徐福一起走到了床榻边，然后胡亥费力地拱起屁股，趴在床榻边上往前拱了两下，硬生生凑到了扶苏跟前去。
徐福的心顿时提到了嗓子眼儿，胡亥年幼，恐怕是很容易被传染上的，若是不小心……
徐福正思考着呢，胡亥就已经凑到扶苏脸颊边上，吐气，喷气。
徐福真有点担心，等扶苏好不容易醒来之后，一摸脸，一手湿。
因为胡亥松开了手，于是张嘴一叫，“哥哥……呜……嗝……”原本徐福和嬴政心头都罩着一层阴云，却被他这样曲折的哭的方式给弄得莫名生出了些喜感来。
也不知道扶苏是不是实在受不了，旁边搁着一个人肉制热机加自动喷泉，以及音调山路十八弯的专业哭丧小崽子了。
他睁开了双眼，将胡亥的脑袋往旁边推了推。
“父王……”
“呜呜……哥哥……”胡亥泪眼朦胧地扑了上去，矮墩的身子直接压在了扶苏的脸上。
扶苏：……
胡亥哭着哭着，还在扶苏的头上打了个嗝，胡亥牙还没长好呢，那一哭，就是泪水混合着口水。
扶苏强忍着把人给掀飞的冲动，努力忽视掉自己头发可能会被降个雨的悲催感。
徐福真担心胡亥把扶苏的脸给挤变形了，马上快步上前，拎住了胡亥的领口，但是提了一下，没能提起来。徐福不得不认识到，自己还是那个手无缚鸡之力的自己，根本不能像蒹葭那样，轻轻松松拎人。
嬴政从背后伸出手来，几乎将徐福圈在了自己的怀里，他伸手将胡亥提了起来，胡亥哭的打嗝，他抬起手揉了揉鼻子，然后眯了眯眼经，“啊……噗嗤——”这才是结结实实地呸了扶苏一脸。
扶苏被这么一喷，还陡然清醒了不少。
“父王。”他的声音这次倒是清晰有力了些了。
宫女一脸惨不忍赌地忙上前，为扶苏擦了擦脸。
胡亥大约也知道自己干了坏事，忙捂住了嘴，乖乖地被嬴政拎在手里，动也不动，一双眼乌溜溜地盯着扶苏。
扶苏轻咳一声，“父王，还是将胡亥送走吧。”
嬴政把胡亥放下来。
胡亥咕咚就摔了个大马趴下去，脸着地，屁股拱起，口齿不清地说：“不……肘……”
扶苏嘴角抽了抽，只能暂时将这个特别熊的幼弟抛到脑后去，对嬴政道：“父王，我是不是染上疫病了？”扶苏小脸煞白，但是目光却十分的沉稳，倒是很像嬴政平日里的风采。
嬴政沉默几秒，毫不隐瞒地应道：“是。”
宫人们都低下了头，顿觉揪心不已。
长公子扶苏，颇受王上看重，若是出了事……谁也担不起这个责任。
而且那么小的年纪……怎么能被疫病给毁了呢……
扶苏反倒是豁达地笑了笑，道：“父王和老师无须担心我，幼时扶苏体弱，便也吃过不少药，有好多时候都是睡在床榻上养病的。如今区区疫病，扶苏身为父王的长子，又岂能这样轻易便被打倒呢？”
这番话若是平常说出来，肯定显得有些肉麻，但此时说出来，再合适不过。
嬴政脸上阴沉之色散去，他温和地笑着拍了拍扶苏的头，“好，不愧是寡人的儿子！”
见扶苏并没有露出意志消沉的一面，徐福就放心了，他将目光落到了胡亥的身上，胡亥还死死地扒在地面上，看上去还真不像是嬴政的儿子。徐福将胡亥从地面上抱了起来，胡亥睁着一双哭得微微红肿的眼，往徐福的胸前凑，徐福伸手将他的头挡住了，一边出声问道：“扶苏公子近日可是接触了什么污秽之物？”
“污秽之物？”扶苏不解。
“比如污水，鼠类尸体等等……”
扶苏突然间面色惨白，甚至看上去像是要作呕了一样，“……老师，那日，我、我在花园中，遇见了一内侍，将宫中养着的鱼，扒骨去鳞，还一身血污的埋进了花园里。场面实在恶心，因被我无意撞见，那内侍仓皇不已，竟然撞到我的身上。后来我、我便命人将他拖出去打死了。”
打死一个小小内侍，嬴政自然不会觉得自己儿子多么残酷，相反的，他还认为扶苏已经初具魄力了，能在意外发生之时，果决处置冒犯自己的人。
“鸡瘟？”徐福的注意力也全在那内侍的奇怪举动上。
真奇怪，好好的，在花园里杀鱼？
见徐福眼中流露出疑惑之色，扶苏马上道：“后来扶苏命人去查了一番，得知那个内侍幼年时，曾见他人因瘟疫惨死的情景，现在他听闻咸阳城中有人染了疫病，就害怕不已，连偷数鱼，都以同样手法杀死后，埋入花园。”
不消扶苏再说下去，徐福和嬴政就已经明白那个内侍做了何等愚蠢的事了。
那些鱼说不定本来是没有问题的，但是却因为被扒骨去鳞后，血淋淋地埋入土中，天气炎热，时间一久就发臭了，花园中本来多昆虫，虫类携带着细菌病毒，不知道会落到谁身上去……
徐福想一想便觉得心中寒颤连连。
实在太恶心了……那场面定然是腥臭腐烂不堪的。
徐福实在没见过这样的疫病，他虽从书简中另外学了些医理和药学，但并不代表，他就能克服历史上的大难题了。不过他倒是很快想到了三川郡，也不知三川郡中，那对母女是否活下来了，若是她们活下来了，那就证明这疫病并没有那样恐怖，至少不是强大到让人无法战胜。
嬴政也想到了这一点，他朝徐福微微点头，“寡人已经命人前往三川郡，探听那二人消息了。”
徐福应了一声，“宫中侍医可有法子？”
“还要等。”嬴政招手将侍医叫到跟前来。
刚才一直充当木桩子的一干侍医，这时才有了存在感，尽管如此，他们也姿态谦逊恭谨的，在得到嬴政的同意之后，他们低声地询问着扶苏那日发生的事，还有他身上都有何处不适，待一一问清楚之后。侍医们的脸色却半点不见放松，他们为扶苏暂时开了些药，可以保他退烧，防止疫病变得更加严重。
随后他们便请求先行离开，要仔细商讨一番。
嬴政知道这些人逼也逼不出个什么结果来，便大手一挥让他们下去了。
而扶苏被盘问了许久，精神已经十分差了，眼皮都快磕到一起了。徐福和嬴政见他眼下没有什么危急情况出现，便放下了心，正要将胡亥抱着一块儿带出去，胡亥却是从徐福怀中挣扎两下，指着扶苏的方向，“嗯！嗯……哥哥……”
徐福弯腰将他放下来。
嬴政道：“胡亥公子在此处陪上一会儿，你们便带他回偏殿。”
“喏。”宫人们赶紧应了。
嬴政重新握住徐福的手腕，也不知是不是他的错觉，徐福的手腕倒像是细了一些，“你随寡人回寝宫。”
徐福指了指胡亥咯噔咯噔跑到床边去的小身子，“那他……”他们这样是不是太不厚道了些？就这样将胡亥丢在这里？
“胡亥。”徐福忍不住出声叫道。
胡亥转过头来，看了徐福一眼，然后就趴在床榻边上，将头埋在扶苏的面前了，“和哥哥一起。”他软声道。这句话倒是难得的格外口齿清晰，就是带了点儿轻微的口水音。
扶苏因为疲累过度，已经闭上双眼了，哪怕胡亥凑到他旁边去，他也没有再睁开双眼。
胡亥不肯走，徐福也不能将他强硬抱走，说来说去，还是他和嬴政这两个大人实在不合格，整日里都是胡亥跟着扶苏同进同出，自然便离不开哥哥了。
嬴政低声道：“过一会儿让宫人将他抱开就是，小孩子很容易便睡着了，觉又沉，抱走时没有自觉的。”
徐福想到胡亥那双微微红肿的眼，点了点头，“走吧。”
不过出来之后，嬴政还是让侍医给胡亥也备了药。
同时偏殿之中还收拾了不少东西出来，都要被拿去焚烧。而徐福和嬴政回到寝宫后，也脱去了身上的衣袍，洗澡净污，再将衣袍也收拾起来。
两人一起用了饭食后，便早早一同歇在了床榻上。
从全国大旱后，两人实在难得好好休息上一回。提前在床榻上休息是徐福提出的。过度劳累会导致抵抗力下降，而抵抗力下降的人自然也容易染上疫病，他和嬴政都是要主持大局的，他们可不适合病倒，最好的便是劳逸结合，让那疫病无可趁之机。
躺下来之后，思绪仿佛都跟着倒下去的姿势，一起沉到深处去了。
嬴政很努力地找回之前的气氛，低低的声音在黑夜中响起，“如今阿福还惦记着，不能为寡人卜筮之事吗？”
徐福睁开眼，看着床顶，目光有一瞬的空茫。
或许他应该感谢胡亥那一番插科打诨，他脑子里塞满的思绪就这样没了。
“……不惦记了。”徐福轻声道。
嬴政觉得有些可惜。他从来不否认徐福的能力强悍，和他一身的奇妙。但是徐福在人前总是强悍高冷的，在他跟前也是强悍高冷的，那又有何区别？自己这情人倒是做得憋屈了些。要一日日过去，令徐福敢对他敞开脆弱一面来，那才能让他心中高悬着的那颗心落地。
“明日便举行卜筮吧。”徐福出声道。
嬴政有些无奈，“你也不能如此想一出便是一出，卜筮日寡人要提前令人通知下去，这样才有更多人能被聚到城楼脚下，不然的话，便是未能达到你的初衷吧？”
徐福也觉得有些羞赧，之前嬴政主动问他，他倒是一推再推，现在突然间又跟抽风似的，说要明日举行，嬴政没发作，那都是好脾气了。
徐福点点头，“那……那你说几时？”
嬴政敏锐地听出徐福语气里的示弱，难得语气乖顺一分啊，嬴政都要怀疑如今挂在外头的是月亮呢，还是太阳呢。
“后日吧。”嬴政不知为何徐福突然间又放下心中芥蒂，能够坦荡自然地举行卜筮了，但他知道徐福焦急，所以还是能提前，便将时日提前一些。
到了第二日徐福并未前往奉常寺，而是前往偏殿去瞧了瞧扶苏。
扶苏睡得正熟，脸色没有昨日那样煞白了，也不似昨日那样发起高热极为厉害了。偏殿中空气并不大好，徐福嘱咐宫女将门窗多多通风后，便从偏殿中出来了。
他倒是没瞧见，他前脚刚走出来，后脚扶苏的被子下面，就拱起了一团，过了会儿，那一团才费力地钻了出来。
宫人们刚送走了徐福，回转身来，就见一只呆萌可爱的脑袋搁在被子外头，宫人们被吓得差点惊叫出声，好半天才勉强压住了惊飞的魂魄，“……胡、胡亥公子，怎么会在此处？”
胡亥懒懒地打了个呵欠，根本没有理会宫人，抱着扶苏的胳膊便睡过去了。
宫人们见着胡亥一副闲适模样，急得团团转，但是又不敢强硬地将胡亥抱下来，他们更此时去禀报徐福，说昨日胡亥公子不知为何，又出现在了扶苏公子的床榻之上。这一夜过去，谁知道会不会染病啊？
宫人们满眼血丝地对视一眼，彼此瞒下了这件事。
转眼便是卜筮之日。
城中早就知晓那位徐奉常要亲自主持卜筮仪式，并且允许百姓们旁观，这对于百姓们来说，是无比新奇的。他们怀着或崇敬或仰慕或害怕的心情，聚集到了城楼下。
徐福选择的这个地点，并不高，是在咸阳城的城墙之内，他走上去之后，四周便都可环绕上百姓。
此时不止是百姓们，还有城中贵族，甚至是朝廷官员们，都各自寻了地方站好，以期接下来的卜筮仪式。
远远的，他们便见一行人从另一头来了。
这一行人，身穿祭祀礼服，不苟言笑，个个脸上都带着肃穆之色，他们手中捧有卜筮的用具，如龟甲等……这些都是百姓们平日里只能听说，却不能真正瞧见的玩意儿，百姓们倒是暂时抛却了旱灾带来的恐慌，他们忍不住露出了惊奇和欣喜的表情，无比崇敬地看着这些人手中捧着的物什。
正是这些物什，在众人的眼中，便化作了上古神秘力量的标志。
此时有百姓注意到，这行人之前有着一辆马车，那马车两边没有挡板，只笼着一层布，那布十分轻薄，一吹便能扬起，隐约露出里面的人影来。百姓们伸长了脖子。他们大约猜到了这位的身份。百姓们想起了去年在田埂间，与君王一同主持蜡祭的那位太卜。
他们依稀还能想起那位的风采。
明明是穿着厚重死板的祭祀礼服，明明只是站在田埂间，但他就是与旁人不一样，那举手投足，回眸来看，都是能叫人过目难以忘却的……
众人不自觉地屏住了呼吸。
他们以为自己又会看见一个盛装的太卜。
但是马车停了，徐福从里面走了下来，他身上穿的依旧是那简单的祭祀改良服，这衣袍并未束腰，因而显得有些宽大，衣袍并不厚重，也不繁复，穿在身上顿时便又另外的一种味道。
若说之前在田埂间的徐福，像是神灵的代言人，一身古老的气息，仿佛他就是来自过去的远古，仿佛他已经和先祖神灵对过话了一般。
而此时的徐福，却显得身姿飘逸洒脱，偏偏又说不出的气质高傲，那种傲气是令人折服的，不会有一人对他的傲气生出不满和疑问来。
嬴政由侍从拥着，混杂在人群之中，他的个子够高，所以哪怕周围的人再多，他也能够清晰地瞧见走下马车来的徐福。
举手投足，还带上几分浑然天成的贵气。
嬴政心中涌动着引以为豪的情绪。
徐福这点儿贵气，还真是从他身上陶冶出来的，如今这样一看，徐福看上去更像是从天上来的人一般了。此时的他哪里像是什么神灵的代言人，他如今就更像是神灵！比那些古时壁画上加载的神仙形象，嬴政倒觉得谁也是比不过徐福这副模样的。
徐福丝毫不乱，他招手令王柳和苏邑二人前来，这二人恰好一左一右，落后两步走在他之后。
他们一同上了城楼，徐福的裙摆拖过地面，倒是不会有人想到干净与否的问题，他们全都个个激动得面色涨红，紧紧地盯着徐福的身影，他们看着徐福站在城楼上，转过身来，仿佛睥睨众生，叫所有不慎与他对上目光的人，都不得不臣服在他的脚下。
众人情不自禁地跪下叩拜。
唯有嬴政鹤立鸡群，站在人群之中，与徐福遥遥相望。
那瞬间，嬴政还真有点儿自己和徐福，偷偷摸摸传递情愫的刺激感。
“摆龟甲，置六爻。”徐福声音清冷，音量也不大，但却很好地传入了众人的耳中。
百姓们知晓龟甲，但他们当真不知那六爻是个什么东西，思及咸阳城中对于这位徐奉常的传言，百姓们倒是也不多想了，早就听闻这位是能人，说不定便是用的许多人都不知晓的法子吧。这么一想，百姓们更激动了，他们想知道，除了龟甲占卜，还能有什么法子？这位徐奉常真的有那样准么？
百姓们对上徐福那张脸，之前因为旱灾来临时而对徐福有所不满的，顷刻间便烟消云散了。
这般风流人物，想来本事也是很高的……蜡祭应当没有在他手中出错吧……众人暗暗想道。
苏邑摆龟甲，王柳置六爻八卦。
二人自觉地退后，然后城楼之上点起火把，火光闪烁，映亮了徐福的眼眸。
后来，无数人曾提起这一日。
他们都说，那一日徐奉常的眼眸像是盛满了世间的光明，他一举一动，浑身仙气四溢，他卜筮出来的卦，旁人甚至不敢看，害怕自己被灼瞎了眼睛。那一日，他们仰望着徐奉常的身影，俊美，坚韧，冷漠，强大。
这样的人，才像是被神灵派来救赎他们的人。
百姓们有时候便是如此墙头草，他们不管你如何，他们只求能够得好的生活，此时他们寄希望于徐奉常，自然毫不吝啬自己作为信徒的那点信仰。
百姓们跪地，口中讷讷念着徐福听不懂的俗语，反正听起来有几分诡异，徐福一律将这些话自动翻译成夸自己的了。
徐福的手指扫过面前的龟甲和六爻八卦，他装模作样地燃木条，入龟甲，再装模作样的拍一拍八卦盘。
“噤声。”徐福道。
百姓们惶惶不安地看着他。
此时天色渐渐晚了，一轮圆日从天边的地平线往下滑去，而红霞却是挂在天边的。有人说红霞是吉兆，也有人说是凶兆，但谁又能全然说准呢？此时，他们便只期望，那是好的寓意了。
徐福将之前去三川郡前，与嬴政解的那一卦，又简单替换一下各中词语，好让这些百姓们也能大致听明白，那卦象是个什么意思。这一听，百姓们就愣了。
原来徐奉常早就算出有劫，而这劫是由水引起的，水上困难重重，须得众人团结，给予足够的信任，才能获得最后的胜利。
百姓们听得晕头转向的，只觉得徐福讲的话，没有几句是适用的。
而就在此时，徐福突然开了口，道：“尔等是否以为，神灵已然抛弃了你？”
百姓堆中嗡嗡作响，当初咸阳旱灾，他们的确认为这便是神灵降下的祸事，此时徐奉常还要说什么？难道要否决他们的话吗？百姓们你看我我看你，倒是不敢大声质疑徐福。他们骨子里还是本能地对徐福怀着畏惧。
就像是古时候部落中人都要尊崇巫师，不敢轻易得罪一样。
徐福的音量这才稍微拔高了一些，道：“尔等可知，神灵已经赐了你们几处有水之源。”
“什么？！”百姓们这才震惊了。眼看着水一日一日用光，水井也快要干涸，难道此时真的还会有福事降临吗？
“水源啊！”
“天哪，徐奉常实在好本事……”
“谁知是不是真的啊……”刚又一个不和谐的声音冒头，便立即被骂了下去。
徐福抬起手指，遥遥一指，“西北行上十里路。”
他神色淡漠，高高在上，当真像是随手间，便能轻易主宰人生死的神明。百姓们看着他的模样，不自觉地看得呆了。莫说他们，就连嬴政也微微有些怔忡。
徐福果然是适合站在高处的。
他还是适合与寡人一同站在高处的。
不知为何，嬴政发觉到自己的心跳快了许多。
而此时徐福已经再度抬手，又看似漫不经心地遥遥一指，却是牵动着城楼之下无数人的心，“东南行五里路。”
“城东往后山走三里。”
“城北凹地。”
“咸阳城外连家村。”
“……”
徐福一口气指了好几个地方，百姓们跟着心跳如擂鼓般，他们屏着呼吸，都不敢轻易松开，生怕惊扰了神明。哦，神明在何处？不正是那城楼之上，一身祭祀礼服的人吗？
徐福终于住了口，“这几处将有人前往去寻觅神灵留于我们的救命之泉。”
徐福抬头看了看天，再度出声道：“神灵有指示，若要化解此次灾祸，可有外力辅佐之，届时灾祸将提前结束，尔等也不必再受灾祸之苦。”徐福随意一指，“水。”再指天上红霞，“火。”
“水以救人命，火以烧去病体，将死亡隔绝其外。”
“最后，便要用以神药，染了疫病的人，方可痊愈。”
其实朝中大臣已经都有许多按捺不住，想要知道，用什么神药了，那神灵难道还给他连方子都写下来了？心中满是好奇的大臣们，碍于面子，又碍于不远处还站着一个嬴政，于是只能硬生生地打消了心中的好奇。
其实徐福想说，我还想知道神药是什么呢。
不过徐福也不能就这么含糊带过去，于是他就瞎扯了一通，指着咸阳城外的道路，道：“神灵向我道，会令一人身负神药，从此路走来，带来神灵给予秦国的庇佑。”
百姓们激动得浑身发抖，真的会有吗？虽然他们并不能亲眼瞧见徐奉常是如何卜筮的，但他们心中已经万分敬服了。
百姓们再度跪地。
徐福也十分应景地喊出了一句，“大秦顺应天命，理应得到神灵庇佑。诸位勿要心中慌乱焦灼。神灵的赐福，我们要等……”
百姓们不疑有他，忙再度行礼，口中高呼，“多谢徐神仙。”
徐福一怔。
这些人不称他官职，不称他先生，却是称了个“徐神仙”，听上去倒像是个半吊子坑人的名号。
不过不管这个称呼好不好，起码这些百姓是真正将他记在心中了。他们或许还会疑惑，水源哪里是一点就能点出来的，徐福这一招实在糊弄人。但是很快他们就会知晓自己是眼界是狭隘的！
城楼上的火把被吹熄，徐福这才垂下眼眸，冷淡地下令，“卜筮已结束，众人散去。”
百姓们还沉浸在徐福的风采之中，各自摇摇晃晃，步履轻飘飘地便散去了。
而朝中大臣，看向徐福的目光，有敬畏，却也有嗤笑不屑。
徐福走下城楼，搜寻了一番那道目光，但是因为人实在有些多，他却没能搜寻到目光的主人。徐福暗暗皱眉，不过就算对方再有什么坏心思，那也不能在此时施展出来。
因为徐福已经瞧见缓缓朝他行来的嬴政了。
众大臣见状，忙俯身道：“见过王上。”
嬴政走到徐福跟前，眼底光芒灼热，几乎能将人烫伤，他抓住了徐福的手腕，带着他朝马车行去，留下了那一干大臣，大臣们你看我我看你，心中浮起了更大的疑问，但他们也只能咬紧牙关，死死憋着。
免得被王上给宰了。
嬴政带着徐福上了马车，徐福伸手拉了拉他的衣袖，“过来一些。”
嬴政心道，难道徐福心中激荡不已，要以亲吻来发泄心中的激荡之情？嬴政做好了准备，甚至想好了要如何反客为主将徐福吻得晕乎乎才好。谁知道，他刚移得近一些，徐福便直接靠在了他的身上，像是终日挺着的脊梁终于轰然倒塌。
“阿福？”

嬴政伸手将徐福的脸抬了起来，徐福闭着眼，睫毛微微颤动着，他“啪”的将嬴政的手打开，虽然动作有气无力了些，不过至少证明他不是晕过去了。
嬴政松了口气。
马车很快回到了王宫外，嬴政正思考着要不要在众目睽睽之下，将徐福抱起来带进去，徐福就突然从他怀中惊醒过来了，惊醒后的徐福，抬手拢了拢身上的衣袍，面容上不见半点倦色，他和嬴政一同下了马车。
有人看见这一幕，虽然心中觉得王上和下臣同坐马车实在违和了些，不过想一想，王上自己都不觉得有什么，又哪里需要旁人来指手画脚？
徐福下了马车就径直往王宫内走了，而且是压根没有等嬴政，直直地就朝里走了。
嬴政有些哭笑不得，他这才知道，刚才徐福脸上的清明应该都是伪装出来的，此时他的脑子指不准糊成了什么模样。
其他人咋舌不已，暗道王上实在太过爱重身边的有能之士，徐福越过王上往宫内走，竟然都没得到王上的半句斥责，这等荣宠，实在令人心中激荡向往，恨不得自己将徐福替换下来，也为王上好生奉献一番。
……
这方卜筮仪式顺利结束，徐福再度大出风头，这一日，他的一言一行都深深印进了百姓的眼眸之中，不少百姓思维单纯，认为世上哪有如此容貌出众的人，若是有，那他也一定是神灵转世，仙人下凡吧。
见效是极快的，当日过后，咸阳城中便逐渐恢复了往日的生气，他们盲目地信任着神灵的力量，认为光明就就在不远的前方。
只是街道两旁仍旧不见小贩和酒馆了，要想恢复从前的繁华喧闹，还要等到降雨后，方能彻底解放这座城。
秦国大旱的消息传到其它六国，除了韩王性子胆小，只是略略松了口气外，另外五国莫不是拍手称快，以赵、魏最为兴高采烈，纷纷咬牙切齿，散播消息，称“秦王作为，残暴不仁，触怒神灵”。不过这样的消息也就只是不痛不痒的传一下。毕竟春秋战国时期，你打我，我打你是再正常不过的事。或许昨天咱们还是姻亲呢，今天我就要打得你不能自理了。
秦王好战是不可否认的，但哪个国家没有点儿野心？只是如今六国眼瞧着秦国壮大，心头不痛快，要讽刺一下秦王，再乐得看秦国倒霉罢了。
赵、魏两国乐过头了，却没想想自己国内也好不到哪里去，这也就罢了，他们还丢了城池呢。
他们在高兴之余，倒是隐隐听说了秦国的那位太卜，据传容貌极为出色，连龙阳君都难以与其相比。这边魏王一听，陡然想到失踪的龙阳君，被气得头晕眼花，当即在朝中对大臣们道，“如今秦国大旱数日，颗粒无收，疫症四起，更有难民四处流亡。实乃我大魏攻打秦国的好时机。寡人欲点兵，趁此时秦国虚弱攻入，也拿他秦国几座城池，狠狠羞辱之，也叫秦王知晓，我魏国不是好惹的。诸位以为如何？”
魏王一厢情愿地脑补着，秦国此时肯定是哀声四起，到处都是染了疫病的人，路边都能随意捡到尸体……
这番脑洞一开，魏王那颗被伤透了的心，终于得到了慰藉，恨不得自己亲自带兵狠狠踩一踩秦王的威风才好。
魏王如何胡作非为，徐福和嬴政都是不知晓的，他们压根不关心魏国如何作妖。
徐福先请了侍医来为自己瞧一瞧身体状况。
侍医看着他的目光有些怪异。
“如何？可是我身体有异？”饶是承受能力极强的徐福，都忍不住出声问道。
话音刚一落下，侍医就感觉到王上的目光冷飕飕地落到自己身上来了。
“不、不。”侍医脸上的表情僵了僵，忙道：“只是好奇……”
“好奇什么？”
“咸阳城中都传徐奉常是仙人……”
“仙人也是需要看病的。”徐福面无表情地说。
侍医狗腿地笑笑，忙老老实实地为徐福把起了脉。
那侍医五官皱成一团，半晌才松开了徐福的手腕，“……精气亏损。”
徐福凉凉地看向了嬴政。
侍医见状，忙道：“不、不是那个精气。想来只是徐奉常连日来都未曾休息好，劳思过度，这才会觉得浑身无力。这几日好好休息便可。”侍医说完，又补了两句，“徐奉常需要多补一补身体，人在长，身体又在操劳，却不见足够的进补，自然便会出问题。”
徐福和嬴政闻言，神色都有些怪异。
徐福是觉得侍医口中的操劳二字实在太有内涵。
而嬴政却是突然间想起，徐福还未加冠，如今正是长身体的年纪，怪不得那日他看见徐福的背影时，总觉得他的身量似乎有了变化。自己已经身量长成，而徐福却还在成长，怎么想嬴政心中都觉得有几分怪异。
侍医认认真真地写下了方子，又恭恭敬敬地退了出去。
走到殿外，看一眼远方，叹一口气，“……说不定神仙也是要吃喝拉撒的呢。”
而这厢嬴政走到了徐福的身边，将他拉了起来。平时不注意，此时一瞧，才骤然发觉，徐福长高了不少，不过嬴政还是有着绝对的身高优势，他可以轻松地把自己的下巴搁在徐福的头顶。
徐福：……
打破殿内诡异气氛的是一名小内侍，那小内侍躬着腰，道：“王上，三川郡的人归来了。”
三川郡的消息被带了回来，徐福和嬴政对视一眼，当即便决定先召见那人。
那人跪在嬴政跟前，面带喜色，“那二人情况已经大有改善，修养一段时日之后，应当就可痊愈，如今三川郡内情况得到控制，再无其他人染病。此乃药方。”说着那人从袖中掏出了一块绢布呈上。
嬴政将药方接过，粗略扫了一眼，随后便将内侍叫过来，“将此药方送到侍医手中去。”
内侍捧着绢布，快步出去了。
那人任务已完成，当即便告退了。
徐福脑子里浮现了那个小姑娘的面容，幸好，那个小姑娘保住了性命，她活下来了。倒是嬴政忍不住扬了扬眉，道：“如今看来，你在三川郡中也要声名远扬了。”
徐福断定那二人能存活下来，当时周围的人都听见了这么一段话。疫病在百姓眼中都是可怕的，是没有人能染过病后还能活下来的，若是那母女安然无恙，定然能叫那些认为徐福瞎忽悠的人，再不敢生出半分不敬之心。而三川郡内恐怕更甚至会将徐福敬若神明。
徐福瞥了嬴政一眼，淡淡道：“看上去，一切都朝着好的方向在发展。”
虽然徐福面上不显，但嬴政知道，这是这么久一来，徐福心中最放松的时刻。
当日侍医便按照药方，制出了药来，先令人试药，之后再分别用到了扶苏和城里染病的人身上。三名侍医守在偏殿外，不眠不休，时时刻刻都关注着扶苏的动静。而徐福和嬴政也难以睡个好觉，所幸前几日休息得不错，这一夜熬一熬，倒也不会有太大的损害。
到了第二日，三名侍医睁着布满血丝的眼，对着嬴政叹了一口气，“王上，此药并未能改善扶苏公子的病情，此方无效。”
嬴政皱了皱眉，因为一宿没能好好休息，他的面色有些阴沉，看上去气势十足，压迫性极强。
侍医们忍不住颤抖了起来，心中有些委屈，这方子也是王上自己提供的啊……本来疫病就极难医治，说不得便会有许多人死在不断试药的过程中。可不试药又怎么样？史上也并没有完整的，关于治愈瘟疫的记载啊。
倒是徐福很快冷静下来，斟酌道：“难道是因为咸阳城中的疫病和三川郡内的疫病并不相同？所以那方子在三川郡能治好人，在咸阳的却不见效了？”
侍医双眼一亮，道：“徐奉常说得有理，或许引起疫病的源头都不一样，自然也就不能用一个方子来治。”那侍医倒像是从中得到了什么启发，忙向嬴政请求，先回去再细细研究一番。
嬴政看了看偏殿内的扶苏，扶苏已经再度陷入了昏迷，他脸色苍白，脸颊上本来就没有多少肉，这么一病，看上去就更为瘦弱了。嬴政就算再冷的心，瞧着独子这般模样，心中也觉得有些揪着难受。
就好似看见了过去那个疼痛难忍，却只能自己舔舐伤口的质子赵政。
嬴政转身出来，放那侍医回去了。
此时徐福倒是想起了一人。
“王上，鬼谷有多厉害？”徐福出声问道。
嬴政有些不解，他怎么在此时突然问起了鬼谷？而且对鬼谷最熟悉的人，应当是他吧。嬴政的思绪滞了滞，突然想起来，尉缭曾说过，徐福如今没了以前的记忆。嬴政耐心与徐福讲了讲外界对鬼谷的评价，总结起来，鬼谷就是一处聚集奇人异事的地方。
“那王上可愿请鬼谷中的一人，前来试一试治这疫病。”
“何人？若是那人有真本事，寡人自然求之不得。”
徐福面上飞速地闪过尴尬之色，“……姜游。”
嬴政的脸色瞬间就拉了下来。
尽管事情已经过去有不短的时日，但是对于给自己折腾出一片绿云来的姜游，嬴政心里实在爽快不起来。
徐福将嬴政的反应收入眼底，故作漫不经心地道：“我听说姜游师兄那里，有很多花样的……”
这个花样被打上了和谐的色彩。
嬴政蓦地想起那脂膏。
于是笑了笑，点头道：“寡人心胸宽阔，如今为了满城百姓和扶苏，放那姜游进咸阳又何妨？”
徐福立刻顺着杆子往上爬，夸道：“王上英明！”
chapters.title: 第119章
chapters.translated_text:
Ying Zheng reached out and lifted Xu Fu’s face. Xu Fu’s eyes were closed, his eyelashes trembling slightly. He slapped Ying Zheng’s hand away with a "slap." Although the movement was a bit weak, it at least proved he hadn't fainted.

Ying Zheng breathed a sigh of relief.

The carriage soon returned to the outside of the palace. Just as Ying Zheng was considering whether to pick Xu Fu up and carry him inside in full view of everyone, Xu Fu suddenly woke up from his arms. After waking, Xu Fu raised his hand to adjust his robes, his face showing no trace of fatigue, and he stepped out of the carriage with Ying Zheng.

Some people saw this scene. Although they felt it was truly inappropriate for the King and a subordinate to share a carriage, they thought about it—if the King himself didn't think there was anything wrong with it, who were they to point fingers?

As soon as Xu Fu got off the carriage, he walked straight into the palace, not waiting for Ying Zheng at all, heading directly inside.

Ying Zheng was left between laughter and tears. Only then did he realize that the clarity on Xu Fu’s face just now must have been a facade; his mind was likely a complete mess at this moment.
