Others were left speechless, secretly thinking that the King truly cherished the talented people around him. Xu Fu had walked past the King into the palace without receiving a single word of reprimand. Such favor was truly stirring and enviable, making them wish they could replace Xu Fu and serve the King with equal devotion.

...

The divination ceremony concluded successfully, and Xu Fu was once again the center of attention. On this day, his every word and action were deeply etched into the eyes of the common people. Many simple-minded folk believed that there was no one in the world with such outstanding appearance; if there were, he must be a reincarnated deity or an immortal descended to earth.

The effect was immediate. After that day, Xianyang gradually regained its former vitality. They blindly trusted in the power of the gods, believing that light was not far ahead.

It was just that there were still no peddlers or taverns along the streets; to restore the former prosperity and bustle, they would have to wait until the rain fell to truly liberate the city.

News of the great drought in Qin reached the other six states. Except for the King of Han, who was timid and merely felt a slight sense of relief, the other five states were all clapping and cheering. Zhao and Wei were the most jubilant, gnashing their teeth and spreading rumors that "the King of Qin is cruel and inhumane, angering the gods." However, such news was just a painless jab. After all, during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, it was perfectly normal to attack one another. Perhaps we were in-laws yesterday, and today I’m going to beat you until you can’t take care of yourself.

It was undeniable that the King of Qin was bellicose, but which state didn't have some ambition? It was just that now the six states saw Qin growing stronger, felt unhappy, wanted to mock the King of Qin, and enjoyed seeing Qin suffer.

Zhao and Wei were too happy, not realizing that their own countries were no better off. That aside, they had even lost territory.

While rejoicing, they vaguely heard about that Grand Diviner of Qin, who was rumored to be so exceptionally handsome that even Lord Longyang could not compare. Upon hearing this, the King of Wei suddenly thought of the missing Lord Longyang and was so angry he felt dizzy. He immediately said to his ministers in court, "Now that Qin has suffered a drought for days, with no harvest, epidemics spreading, and refugees fleeing everywhere, it is truly a good time for our Great Wei to attack Qin. I intend to raise an army to invade while Qin is weak, seize a few of their cities, and humiliate them severely, so that the King of Qin knows that our Wei is not to be trifled with. What do you all think?"

The King of Wei was indulging in wishful thinking, imagining that Qin must be filled with wails, people infected with the plague everywhere, and corpses lying by the roadside...

Once his imagination took flight, the King of Wei’s broken heart finally found some solace, and he wished he could lead the troops himself to trample on the King of Qin’s prestige.

How the King of Wei acted foolishly was unknown to both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng; they didn't care at all about how Wei was stirring up trouble.

Xu Fu first asked the palace physician to check his physical condition.

The physician looked at him with a strange expression.

"How is it? Is there something wrong with my body?" Even Xu Fu, who had a high tolerance, couldn't help but ask.

As soon as the words fell, the physician felt the King’s cold gaze land on him.

"No, no." The expression on the physician’s face stiffened, and he hurriedly said, "I was just curious..."

"Curious about what?"

"It is rumored throughout Xianyang that Master Xu is an immortal..."

"Immortals also need to see a doctor," Xu Fu said expressionlessly.

The physician gave a sycophantic smile and hurriedly and honestly began to take Xu Fu’s pulse.

The physician’s features were scrunched together, and it was a long while before he let go of Xu Fu’s wrist. "...Depletion of vital energy."

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng coldly.

Seeing this, the physician hurriedly said, "No, not that kind of vital energy. It is likely just that Master Xu has not rested well for days and has been overthinking, which is why he feels weak. He just needs to rest well for a few days." After finishing, the physician added two more sentences, "Master Xu needs to nourish his body more. He is still growing, and his body is being overworked, yet he isn't getting enough nourishment, so naturally, problems will arise."

Upon hearing this, the expressions of both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were somewhat strange.

Xu Fu felt that the word "overworked" used by the physician was far too suggestive.

As for Ying Zheng, he suddenly remembered that Xu Fu had not yet reached his capping ceremony and was at the age where he was still growing. No wonder when he saw Xu Fu’s back the other day, he always felt his stature had changed. He himself had already finished growing, while Xu Fu was still developing; no matter how he thought about it, Ying Zheng felt a bit strange in his heart.

The physician wrote down the prescription earnestly and then retreated respectfully.

Walking outside the hall, he took a look at the distance and sighed, "...Perhaps immortals also need to eat, drink, and relieve themselves."

Meanwhile, Ying Zheng walked to Xu Fu’s side and pulled him up. He hadn't noticed it before, but now, looking closely, he suddenly realized that Xu Fu had grown quite a bit taller. However, Ying Zheng still held an absolute height advantage, and he could easily rest his chin on top of Xu Fu’s head.

Xu Fu: ...

The one who broke the strange atmosphere in the hall was a young attendant, who bowed and said, "Your Majesty, the people from Sanchuan Commandery have returned."

The news from Sanchuan Commandery had been brought back. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng exchanged a look and immediately decided to summon the man first.

The man knelt before Ying Zheng, his face filled with joy. "The conditions of those two have greatly improved. After a period of recuperation, they should be fully recovered. Now the situation in Sanchuan Commandery is under control, and no one else is infected. This is the prescription." As he spoke, the man took a piece of silk from his sleeve and presented it.

Ying Zheng took the prescription, scanned it roughly, and then called an attendant over. "Take this prescription to the palace physician."

The attendant held the silk and walked out quickly.

Having completed his mission, the man immediately took his leave.

The face of that little girl appeared in Xu Fu’s mind. Fortunately, that little girl had been saved; she had survived. Ying Zheng couldn't help but raise his eyebrows and said, "It seems you will soon be famous in Sanchuan Commandery as well."

Xu Fu had asserted that those two would survive, and everyone around had heard those words at the time. In the eyes of the common people, the plague was terrifying, and no one could survive after being infected. If that mother and daughter were safe and sound, it would surely make those who thought Xu Fu was spouting nonsense never dare to show the slightest disrespect again. And in Sanchuan Commandery, they would likely revere Xu Fu as a god.

Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng and said indifferently, "It looks like everything is moving in a good direction."

Although Xu Fu did not show it on his face, Ying Zheng knew that this was the most relaxed moment Xu Fu had felt in a long time.

That same day, the physician prepared the medicine according to the prescription, had someone test it first, and then used it on Fusu and the infected people in the city. Three physicians stayed outside the side hall, sleepless, constantly monitoring Fusu’s condition. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng also found it hard to get a good night’s sleep, but fortunately, they had rested well in the previous days, so staying up this night wouldn't cause too much damage.

By the next day, the three physicians, with bloodshot eyes, sighed at Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, this medicine has not improved Prince Fusu’s condition. This prescription is ineffective."

Ying Zheng frowned. Because he hadn't rested well all night, his complexion was somewhat gloomy, and he looked imposing with strong pressure.

The physicians couldn't help but tremble, feeling a bit aggrieved in their hearts. This prescription was provided by the King himself... The plague was already extremely difficult to treat, and it was inevitable that many would die in the process of continuous testing. But what else could they do if they didn't test the medicine? There were no complete records in history about curing a plague.

Xu Fu, however, quickly calmed down and deliberated, "Could it be that the plague in Xianyang is different from the one in Sanchuan Commandery? That’s why the prescription that could cure people in Sanchuan Commandery is ineffective here in Xianyang?"

The physician’s eyes lit up. "Master Xu’s words make sense. Perhaps the sources of the plague are different, so naturally, one prescription cannot treat both." The physician seemed to have gained some inspiration and hurriedly asked Ying Zheng for permission to go back and study it carefully.

Ying Zheng looked at Fusu in the side hall. Fusu had fallen into a coma again. His face was pale, and there hadn't been much flesh on his cheeks to begin with; being sick like this made him look even thinner. Even with a cold heart, seeing his only son in this state made Ying Zheng feel a tug of pain.

It was as if he were seeing the past hostage Zhao Zheng, who was in unbearable pain but could only lick his own wounds.

Ying Zheng turned and walked out, letting the physician return.

At this moment, Xu Fu remembered someone.

"Your Majesty, how capable is Guigu?" Xu Fu asked.

Ying Zheng was a bit puzzled. Why was he suddenly asking about Guigu at this time? And he should be the one most familiar with Guigu. Ying Zheng’s thoughts paused, and he suddenly remembered that Wei Liao had once said that Xu Fu had lost his previous memories. Ying Zheng patiently explained to Xu Fu the outside world’s evaluation of Guigu, summarizing it as a place that gathered strange people and unusual events.

"Then would Your Majesty be willing to invite someone from Guigu to come and try to treat this plague?"

"Who? If that person has real ability, I would naturally be more than happy to ask for them."

A look of embarrassment flashed across Xu Fu’s face. "...Jiang You."

Ying Zheng’s expression sank instantly.

Although quite some time had passed, Ying Zheng still couldn't feel good about Jiang You, who had given him a "green hat."

Xu Fu took in Ying Zheng’s reaction and said nonchalantly, "I heard that Senior Brother Jiang You has many tricks up his sleeve..."

These "tricks" were tinged with a harmonious color.

Ying Zheng suddenly remembered that ointment.

So he smiled and nodded, saying, "I am broad-minded. Now, for the sake of the people in the city and Fusu, what does it matter if I let Jiang You into Xianyang?"

Xu Fu immediately climbed up the pole, praising, "Your Majesty is wise!"

chapters.title: 第12章
chapters.source_text:
凉风拂过厅前的门槛儿，徐福慢悠悠地转动着手里的杯盏，里头装的是热腾腾的水，恰好在这个时候抿上一口，能暖了不少。
那王柳和邱机已经是几日未见了。
邱机倒是说得过去，倒是王柳，难道堂堂男儿脸皮也这样薄？出了丑，还要躲在家里哭鼻子哭个够才行？
徐福不想掺合进去被奉常寺的人使唤来使唤去，就特地挑了个角落自己玩儿。
兴趣来了，他还推算了一番，邱机什么时候能有转运的机会。不过算来算去的，徐福倒是想到前几天在奉常寺外大道上见到的那个中年男子。
那个中年男子的命格非常奇怪。
观面相，眼角下垂，眉不及眼长。应当是劳碌命的面相，而且过分劳碌还不一定能换来丰厚的回报。但是再仔细打量，就会发现这人生得英俊，面孔上还罩着一层贵气。那必然是他人生道路途中，突然经了一个拐弯儿，导致他的命格硬生生地改变了。
但这并不是令徐福惊奇的一点。
他惊奇的是，对方眉眼周围多细纹，应该是近来常思虑的过。这是因为什么大事而寝食难安吗？再联想到那天他匆匆离去的背影，和他身上那股逐渐消逝的贵气。
徐福总觉得对方就要倒霉了。
本来他还惦记着职业道德打算出声提醒一番，可惜可惜……只是不知道秦朝的丞相是谁？那么大派头，连个侍从也能在王城中气焰嚣张，难道就不怕触怒了秦王？
不对……
徐福猛然反应过来。
这个时候，秦始皇还未加冠，未能正式掌权，他手中的权利似乎是分别握在吕不韦和太后赵姬的手中，而后来赵姬将权利全交给了情人嫪毐。等等，他仔细想想，吕不韦当时似乎就是……官拜丞相？！
徐福又暗道一声好险。
他该多谢那位侍从狗眼看人低，不然的话，他提醒了吕不韦，之后坏了秦始皇的计划怎么办？那还不得把他扒皮抽骨？
徐福记得历史上对于秦始皇这位千古一帝，可是功过参半的。其中他的过错，有一点便是说他残暴不仁，为人狠辣，不容异己。
不管真残暴还是假狠辣，他都不想做那个“异己”。
思及至此，徐福顿时又微微激动了两分。他正好可以将吕不韦的倒霉状告诉秦始皇嘛，再动用口舌之力，忽悠一番，秦始皇自然对他更为看重，升官加爵，走上人生巅峰，指日可待嘛！
有了事儿要思量，徐福便不再躲着自个儿清闲了，他起身回去，还没等踏进门呢。
就见一身褐色官服的王柳正与里头的人交谈呢。
“柳可知几日前，王上身旁的内侍亲来奉常寺了，也不知道是为了找什么人。”
“还用思量么？柳出身比我们都要高一分，那内侍过来，除了是来寻柳的，还能是寻什么人嗯？”
……
寻柳？
我还寻花问柳呢。
他们也是真够有文化水平的。
徐福看向王柳的目光都变得怪异了起来，以这位油头粉面的模样，如果不是深情猥琐了些，也还能算得上是“花柳”的。
众人一番恭维，倒是让王柳沉着的脸色慢慢好转了，他方才露出些微得意的笑容来，“胡说什么？应当不是来找我的吧。”
徐福在背后听了个一清二楚，王柳说出口的话虽然是推脱之意，但他的语气，只要长了耳朵的人，都能听出来，王柳正得意着呢。显然是默认了赵高过来，就是来找他这位出身高门的太卜的。
个个智商低下还非要出来现眼，真是让人不忍直视。
别说徐福了，就是王柳自己也没想到打脸会来得如此之快。
赵高这次没再避讳旁人，他身后还带着几名小侍监，从那奉常寺的大门跨进来以后，王柳和身后一干人等就都有些蠢蠢欲动了。
他们虽然瞧不上赵高这个做了宦官的异国人，但他们都知道，能够得到赵高来邀，那必然能好好显示一番自己在王上心中的地位。
王柳抬高了下巴，瞧那模样，眼里都快看不见其他人了。
简直就是“目中无人”的标准教科书般的姿势啊。
赵高看也没看他一眼。
赵高虽然是异国人，但也是出身贵族，现在他又是王上身边的近侍，哪里会将一个高门子弟看在眼中呢？除非他也能像徐福那样“铁口直断”，那倒还能换得他三分钦佩。
“徐太史，王上有请，请跟奴婢前往。”
因为碍着这么多人在旁，赵高自然不可能再称徐福为“先生”，不然那便是在侮辱徐福了。毕竟“先生”是白身之称。
赵高这段话一脱口，王柳就呆了呆，他身后的一干人更是目瞪口呆，连咽口水的动作都忘记做了，好半天才回过神来，都惶惶地对视了一眼，生怕王柳出了这样的大丑，之后会责怪他们之前那样殷勤恭维，却是错拍到了马腿上。
其实这些人也很委屈啊。
本来他们这个小圈子里，身份较高的就是王柳了，那赵高来奉常寺，除了是找这些高门子弟，还能是找谁呢？
谁会想到，赵高偏偏就冲着这个来历不明不白的人呢！
王柳为人自负，但他并不蠢，丢了一次脸面，肯定不可能再丢第二次，尽管脸色一阵青一阵白，却也随即带着人就要告辞，偏偏他身后有个猪队友，站了出来，且相当义愤填膺地道：“赵公公，此等小子，怎能面见王上？他实在不配！”
赵高听见这句话，白净的面孔上顿时就染了一丝怒气，“哦？徐太史为何不配了？他可是王上指名要见的。”
这样一句话原本是为了提点对方不要不识相，偏偏却被对方当做一番炫耀。
这个人自从进了奉常寺便风波不断，先是邱机，又是王柳，指不准以后还要闹出什么事儿来，就这样的货色？还能得王上青睐？
那人也是一时被激了，心中嫉愤不已，还要上前反驳，却被王柳一把抓住，推给旁人，“他都忙晕了头了，还不快将人扶进去。”
赵高似笑非笑地看了一眼王柳，这才带着徐福走了。
作者有话要说：
**小剧场**
NN年后，成仙不死的徐福对那些考古学家的话嗜之以鼻。
徐福：不是我吹当年吕不韦是被我忽悠死的。
chapters.translated_text:
A cool breeze swept across the threshold in front of the hall. Xu Fu slowly twirled the cup in his hand, which was filled with piping-hot water. Taking a sip right at this moment could warm one up quite a bit.

Wang Liu and Qiu Ji hadn't been seen for several days.

Qiu Ji's absence was somewhat understandable, but Wang Liu? Could it be that a grown man's skin was also this thin? After making a fool of himself, he had to hide at home and have a good cry?

Xu Fu didn't want to get mixed up and be ordered around by the people of the Fengchang Temple, so he deliberately picked a corner to amuse himself.

When the mood struck, he even made a divination about when Qiu Ji might get a chance to turn his luck around. But as he calculated back and forth, Xu Fu thought of the middle-aged man he had seen outside the Fengchang Temple a few days prior.

That middle-aged man's physiognomy was extremely strange.

Judging by his facial features, the corners of his eyes drooped, and his eyebrows fell short of his eyes. It should have been the face of a toil-worn fate, and excessive toil might not necessarily bring in generous rewards. But upon closer inspection, one would find that this person was handsome, and his face was shrouded in an aura of nobility. That must mean he had suddenly encountered a sharp turn in the path of his life, which drastically altered his fate.

But this wasn't what astonished Xu Fu.

What astonished him was that there were many fine lines around the man's brows and eyes, which should be the result of recent constant worry. Was he losing sleep over some major matter? Connected with his hurried departure that day and the gradually fading aura of nobility on his body—

Xu Fu had a lingering feeling that the other man was about to suffer a disaster.

Originally, he had even considered professional ethics and intended to step forward and give a warning, but what a pity, what a pity... Just who was the Prime Minister of the Qin State? He was so putting on airs that even an attendant could act arrogant and domineering within the royal city. Weren't they afraid of angering the King of Qin?

No...

Xu Fu suddenly realized.

At this time, the King of Qin had not yet undergone the capping ceremony and could not formally wield power. The power in his hands seemed to be held separately by Lü Buwei and the Queen Dowager Zhao Ji, and later Zhao Ji handed all power over to her lover, Lao Ai. Wait, he thought carefully, Lü Buwei at that time seemed to be... serving as the Prime Minister?!

Xu Fu secretly muttered that it was a close call.

He should thank that dog of an attendant for looking down on people; otherwise, if he had warned Lü Buwei and subsequently ruined the King of Qin's plan, what would happen? Wouldn't he be skinned and deboned?

Xu Fu remembered that historically, the First Emperor of Qin, this emperor through the ages, had merits and demerits in equal measure. Among his faults, one point was that he was said to be cruel and inhumane, ruthless in nature, and intolerant of dissent.

Regardless of whether the cruelty was real or fake, he didn't want to be that "dissent."

Thinking of this, Xu Fu suddenly became a bit excited again. He could just tell the King of Qin about Lü Buwei's impending misfortune, and then use his silver tongue to bluff and bluster. The King of Qin would naturally value him all the more—getting a promotion, raising his noble rank, and reaching the peak of his life was just around the corner!

Having something to ponder, Xu Fu stopped hiding to enjoy his leisure. He stood up to head back, but before he even stepped through the door—

He saw Wang Liu, dressed in brown official robes, chatting with the people inside.

"Could Liu know that a few days ago, an inner attendant by the King's side came personally to the Fengchang Temple? I wonder who he was looking for."

"Is there even any need to ponder? Liu's background is a notch higher than all of ours. When that attendant came, besides looking for Liu, who else could he be looking for, hmm?"

......

Looking for Liu?

Why not look for flowers and willow trees instead.

They really had quite a high level of cultural literacy.

Xu Fu's gaze toward Wang Liu became strange. With this slick and greasy appearance, if he weren't a bit affectionate and lewd, he could still barely be considered a "flower and willow" kind of fellow.

A round of flattery from the crowd slowly improved Wang Liu's gloomy expression. He then revealed a slightly smug smile, "What nonsense are you uttering? It surely shouldn't be me he was looking for."

Xu Fu heard everything clearly from behind. Although the words Wang Liu spoke were meant to deflect, anyone with ears could tell from his tone that Wang Liu was feeling quite pleased with himself. Clearly, he had taken it for granted that Zhao Gao had come specifically to look for him, a grand master of divination from a prominent family.

Everyone had such low IQs yet still insisted on showing off; it was truly too painful to look at.

Let alone Xu Fu, even Wang Liu himself hadn't expected the slap in the face to arrive so quickly.

This time Zhao Gao didn't avoid outsiders, bringing several junior eunuchs behind him. After stepping through the main gate of the Fengchang Temple, Wang Liu and the crowd behind him all grew restless.

Although they looked down upon Zhao Gao, a foreigner who had become a eunuch, they all knew that being invited by Zhao Gao would surely be a great way to display one's status in the King's heart.

Wang Liu lifted his chin higher. By the look of it, he could barely see anyone else in his eyes.

It was simply a textbook posture of "looking down on everyone."

Zhao Gao didn't even spare him a glance.

Although Zhao Gao was a foreigner, he also came from a noble family, and now he was a close attendant by the King's side; how could he possibly hold a scion of a prominent family in his eyes? Unless that person could also "make infallible divinations with a single word" like Xu Fu, then he might still win three parts of his admiration.

"Grand Historian Xu, the King invites you. Please follow this servant."

Because there were so many people around, Zhao Gao naturally couldn't call Xu Fu "sir" anymore, or else that would be insulting Xu Fu. After all, "sir" was a title for a commoner without official status.

The moment Zhao Gao let out these words, Wang Liu froze, and the crowd behind him was even more dumbfounded, forgetting even to swallow. It took them a long time to recover, and they exchanged timid glances, terrified that Wang Liu would make such a huge fool of himself and later blame them for buttering up the wrong person with such obsequious flattery.

Actually, these people felt quite wronged as well.

Originally, within this small circle of theirs, the one with the highest status was Wang Liu. When Zhao Gao came to the Fengchang Temple, besides looking for these prominent scions, who else could he be looking for?

Who would have thought that Zhao Gao would head straight for this person of unknown and murky background!

Wang Liu was arrogant by nature, but he wasn't stupid. Having lost face once, it was certainly impossible to lose it a second time. Although his face turned a patchy blue and white, he immediately prepared to take his leave with his people. Yet someone behind him, acting as a pig-teammate, stepped forward and said with righteous indignation, "Eunuch Zhao, how can such a brat have an audience with the King? He is truly unworthy!"

Hearing these words, Zhao Gao's fair face instantly flushed with a trace of anger, "Oh? Why is Grand Historian Xu unworthy? He is someone the King specifically asked to see."

Such a remark was originally meant to hint to the other party not to be ungracious, but it was instead taken by the other party as a show of boasting.

This person had been stirring up trouble ever since he entered the Fengchang Temple—first Qiu Ji, then Wang Liu, and who knows what kind of chaos he might stir up in the future. Just such a piece of trash, and he could still win the King's favor?

That person had been provoked for a moment, and feeling intensely jealous and resentful, he was about to step forward to retort, but Wang Liu grabbed him by the arm and shoved him toward someone else, saying, "He's lost his mind from overwork. Hurry up and help him inside."

Zhao Gao gave Wang Liu a look that was a smile yet not a smile, and then left with Xu Fu.

Author's note:

**Mini-theater**

N years later, Xu Fu, who had become an immortal and never died, scoffed at the words of those archaeologists.

Xu Fu: I'm not bragging, but back in the day, Lü Buwei was bluffed to death by me.

chapters.title: 第120章
chapters.source_text:
姜游在外云游，有心留意秦国的消息，听闻秦国大旱，疫病四起的版本后，大惊失色，慌得打翻了桌案。他拉着郑姬便要起身，却被那店家拉住为难了好一阵子才放他离开。
郑姬看出了姜游心中的忧虑，低声道：“我们再寻个人问一问吧。”
其实何止是姜游忧虑，她也是忧虑的。扶苏孤身一人在宫中，尽管有个做秦王的父亲，但那又如何？疫病染上你的时候，可不会问你父母是谁，斟酌一番惹不惹得起再落在你身上。
两个因为忧心咸阳而恍恍惚惚的人，在连续问过几个人之后，他们对视了一眼，“……我们回咸阳吧。”
几乎是异口同声。
姜游和郑姬同时松了一口气，轻松一笑，马上去买了马车，往咸阳进发。
所幸他们本来也离秦国不远，所以等到了咸阳城外时，正好听人说奉常寺的徐奉常，将在城楼之上举行卜筮仪式。
二人早早地守在了城外，因为距离实在太远，所以那一日，他们就只能瞧见徐福站在城楼上大致的轮廓，姜游捂着胸口，颇有些吾家有儿初长成的自豪感。师弟长大了！师弟长大了啊啊啊啊！
待到卜筮结束之后，姜游走路都是用飘的。
很快他就和郑姬惆怅以对了，“走时曾说永不再回咸阳……”如今他们却又走回来了，也不知秦王会如何对待他们？
二人坐在破败的小屋子里，相对着叹了口气。
“不如，不如我们去试一试，能不能偷摸进城里去？”姜游低声道。
郑姬本想骂他天真，但心中却也有些蠢蠢欲动，二人还真就偷偷摸摸地又来了城门口，然后就被正要出城门满天下找姜游的侍从给撞上了。
“……姜、游？”那人呆了呆，本还有些不确定，但是目光一落在郑姬的脸上，轰然变色，“将他们带走！”那人冷声道。
话音一落，背后便登时蹿出了两名男子，将姜游和郑姬抓住了，郑姬弱，姜游更弱，二人被抓住之后，只能懵懵地看着那侍从，心脏狂跳着被拖走了。
他们……会被砍死？
还是剁手剁脚？
想到嬴政那张冷硬的脸，两个人都不自觉地打了个哆嗦。
但是被拖进城中之后，那人就干脆利落地直接将他们塞进了马车里，马车四周被封死，他们只能听见马车在地上滚动过的声音。
在他们快要脸色煞白、抖成筛子之前，他们下了马车，被带到了嬴政的跟前。
嬴政本在处理事务，闻言当即放下了手中的笔刀，看向殿门口。
没错，被带进来的是姜游和郑姬。
嬴政不由得皱了皱眉，他方才下了命令，这二人就被带过来了？若不是嬴政确认自己的双眼没有问题，他都以为侍从随便带了两人过来了。
而姜游和郑姬见嬴政皱眉，腿就已经有些软了。
此时徐福从围屏后走了出来，朝姜游微微点头，“师兄。”姜游的心这才落了回去，有徐福在，他和郑姬应当不会死得太惨了。
“师兄怎么会出现在咸阳？”徐福问道。
嬴政的目光紧跟着也落到了姜游的身上，那目光带着冷意，姜游不自觉地咽了咽口水。
“我、我和郑姬听闻秦国大旱，心中放心不下，便过来了。”姜游选择了说实话。
徐福点了点头，“师兄来得正巧，或许可以帮我一个大忙。”
嗯？姜游猛地抬起头，帮忙？没有说要弄死他们？姜游和郑姬齐齐松了一口气，因为身体绷紧了太久，两个人陡然放松以后，差点趴倒在地上。
“师兄随我来……”徐福说着就已经先朝门外去了。
姜游自然是马上爬起来，跟上了徐福。
而郑姬此时留在殿中就显得有些尴尬了。
嬴政看也不看跪在地上的她，挥手招来宫人，“送她出去。”
郑姬猛地抬起头，难道秦王要将姜游留在此处，而却将她驱逐出去？不过很快郑姬就发现自己是想岔了，宫人只是将她领到了殿外，却并未说要将她驱走的话。郑姬此时有些尴尬，她也明白过来嬴政是什么意思了，就是单纯的不乐意见到她。
郑姬在那里站了会儿，忍不住问道：“敢问扶苏公子现在何处？”既然已经来了王宫，要她憋着不去瞧一眼，郑姬实在做不到。就像是之前她能信誓旦旦，答应自己绝不会出现在咸阳，但现在不还是出于心中的忧虑，而出现在此处了吗？
宫人惊讶地看了她一眼，道：“扶苏公子尚在病中。”这里的宫人有些并不识郑姬是谁，他们不知郑姬身份，当然不敢说更多。
郑姬却是陡然变了脸色，“……病中？扶苏公子可是染上疫病了？”
宫人微微皱眉，有些不喜郑姬这样激烈的反应。
见宫人闭口不言，郑姬心中的冲动慢慢退了下去，整个人冷静了不少。只是她死死地掐住了手掌，疼痛才能提醒她，不要做出乱了规矩的事。当年她是如何能忍的一个人，离开王宫之后，倒是变得越发乖张了。
“能否请你进去替我问一问王上，我想求见公子扶苏。”郑姬立刻改变了态度，声音温软道。
郑姬本也是个美人，语气这样温和，自然就挽回了不少形象。宫人瞧了她一眼，本来想骂她太拿自己当回事，但是见郑姬面容柔美，模样又极为诚恳，犹豫一下还是转身进了大殿。
嬴政知道郑姬想要见扶苏。
宫人出来又将郑姬带进了殿中，郑姬有些不安地跪了下来，叩首道：“求王上允我见扶苏公子一面。”
“你不必去见了。”嬴政淡淡道，“扶苏染上了疫病，你去见了，也只是增加你染病的风险。”
郑姬重重地喘了口气，“……我、我不怕。”
早年的时候，她就并未给过扶苏多少疼爱，慈母这个词从来不能用在她的身上，而后来，她更是丢下了扶苏，独自与人离开咸阳。如今扶苏染病，她又怎么能够若无其事？
就在郑姬想着如何求嬴政时，徐福刚好回来了。
郑姬回头看了一眼，只有徐福，却并无姜游的身影，郑姬紧紧地握了握手掌，“徐奉常，姜游呢？”
“我有事要拜托姜游师兄，便将姜游师兄留着同宫中侍医一起商讨治疫病的方子了。”
郑姬微微松了口气。
徐福见她这副模样，心中隐隐有些不悦。郑姬这般做派，难道是担心嬴政对她和姜游做什么吗？嬴政若是真想做什么，当初就不会放他们离开了，当初就不会纵容郑姬这样给他戴绿帽子了。郑姬这样不信任嬴政，实在令人膈应了些。徐福收起面上的表情，道：“若是郑姬无事，便先自行回去吧了。”
郑姬也敏锐地听出了徐福话里的冷意，她顿时更觉尴尬了。
郑姬咬了咬牙，见嬴政根本没有看自己，也只能憋着先出去了。不去见……也好……反正她也是要离开扶苏的，又何必在此时去伪装一个关心的母亲呢？郑姬装作若无其事地走了出去。
那宫人见着她出来后，便站在那里动也不动，倒也不觉得惊奇。
“敢问扶苏公子住在何处？”她不能见，但听一听他的事，也是一种慰藉了。
宫人回头看了一眼殿内，正好和徐福的目光对上，见徐福冲他点了点头，宫人这才道：“奴婢可以带你到偏殿外瞧一瞧。”
郑姬面带喜色，跟着宫人走开了。
郑姬站在宫殿前，喃喃道：“原来还是住在此处啊……”
此时她忽然见一个子极矮，但模样生得十分可爱的小娃娃，从殿前跑过，身后跟着一干宫人。
“那是谁？”郑姬有些惊奇，难道王上又添了子嗣？可王上与徐奉常的关系……徐奉常会允许？
“胡亥公子。”
郑姬这才突然反应过来。是了，是胡亥。宫中如今也有扶苏和胡亥两个孩子了，时间久了她倒是不记得胡亥的模样了。果然日子久了，便会令人变得健忘起来。
她看着胡亥迈着短腿，艰难地跨过门槛，口中咋咋呼呼地喊着，“哥哥！”
郑姬忽地觉得有些眼酸。
她转过身去，“多谢，不看了吧……”
郑姬又被宫人带回了那大殿外，她朝殿中看了一眼，却不见了嬴政和徐福的身影，郑姬茫然地看了看四周，一个人坐在了大殿前。
而此时徐福和嬴政已经出宫去了，与他们随行的有邱侍医，以及一个姜游。
柏舟在外驾马车，抿着唇，冷着脸，看上去气势逼人。
他们的马车行过，无人敢挡，慢慢的，那马车停在了栅栏前。
姜游当先跳下了马车，指着眼前的地方，道：“此处便是隔离区？”
嬴政已经十分厚道了，若是换做其它君王，莫说是在城中留出隔离区来，恐怕早已经将那些染了病的人，统统驱逐出去，并且要驱得远远的，令他们自生自灭了，更甚者则是将所有染病的人都杀死，再将尸体丢进大坑中焚烧埋葬。
换作历史上的嬴政，说不定还真会做出这样的举动来。但此时的嬴政倒是想也未曾想过这样的做法。
姜游推开木栅栏，在柏舟的带领下，接受了重重检查，这才顺利进入了隔离区。而徐福和嬴政二人远远地坠在后面，邱侍医紧跟着他们，时时盯着他们的面色，生怕他们在此处也染上病。
嬴政走了没几步便停住了。
他自己不想进去，也并不希望带着徐福进去。
嬴政并非圣人，除了自己儿子他还能接触外，其他人染了病，他自然都不会去接触，他不会拿自己这条命来开玩笑，更舍不得带着徐福的命一起去开玩笑。
“流言是从这里传出的？”嬴政冷声问道。
若非有人前来禀报，说城中又有流言肆虐，将徐福气得变了脸色，嬴政也不会带徐福前来此处。
身后侍从上前来，道：“正是此处。”
“去将那人揪出来，此处还不配让寡人踏入，亲自去揪那人。”嬴政沉下脸来。
“喏。”侍从根本不在乎这里是什么地方，他大大方方地进去，寻了几个人来打听。
哪怕他们并未往里走去，但徐福也能听见里面传出的哀嚎和痛呼声，还有隐隐的哭声。这些人被病痛折磨得太久了。
徐福忍不住道：“他们若是求我主持祭祀，倒也并非不可……”
只是多给百姓一个希望而已，并不会耗费他什么心力。
嬴政却脸色难看道：“寡人是忧心恐有人故意针对你。你已经替咸阳城寻到了水源，哪里不能证明你的神通？偏偏还有人要质疑你口中所言，故意散播谣言，令患病的人认为自己没命可活了，更令满城上下都以为咸阳要成为一个死都了。这等心思险恶的人，你又怎能如他的愿？”
徐福想一想，倒也是这么个的道理。若是背后真的有人故意谋划，那称了那人的心，就实在太蠢了。
不多时，姜游先和柏舟一起出来了。
姜游面色有些难看，对徐福道：“比我想象中还要严重一些。”
“有解吗？”
“我心中有些法子已经成形，但却还要试一试才能知晓，究竟能否在他们身上起作用。”
“可有需要我帮忙的地方？”徐福问道。
姜游笑了笑，“师弟幼时只爱学炼药，却不爱学行医看病，可不要给师兄弟添乱才好……”
“师兄觉得我会添乱？”其实徐福就是帮忙，再顺便偷个师。若是能学到两手，那也是好的。居家旅行必备啊！
姜游识趣地马上改口，特别的没骨气，“不不，师弟自然是能帮上忙的。”
此时有侍从拎着一人出来了，侍从并不敢将那人带得太近，担心那人身上的秽气冲撞了徐福和嬴政。
嬴政冷冷地看了一眼，那是个中年男子，身形瘦弱，已经被疫病折磨得就剩下一把骨头了，就这样的人，也能散播谣言？
“他可交代了？”
侍从无奈道：“硬骨头。”
徐福倒是料到了这个结果，染了疫病的人，本身就很难存活下来，这人或许就是想着，左右他也没什么活的机会，那也就不必因为三两句威胁，便交代出自己的作为了。
嬴政觉得有些恶心，将徐福往自己身前拉了拉，然后抬手遮住了他的眼，低声道：“杀了吧。”
侍从也不犹豫，当即抽出随身武器来，结果了那人的性命，之后便有人用木板车将人拉走，拉去焚烧。
见着这么一幕，姜游双腿都打颤了，心里凉透了，连看都不敢看嬴政了。若是那次他抢夺扶苏，嬴政真的要发落他，说不定他也就血溅三尺了……然后连个全尸都留不下来了。幸好幸好，幸好师弟变成秦王媳妇了。
当初如何不满嬴政配不上徐福的人，此时正打着自己的脸，在心底特别怂地夸着，秦王真是个好人啊……
实在太配得起师弟了！
嬴政低声在徐福耳边道：“我们在城中随处走走，你不是想去瞧一瞧挖出来的水井吗？”
徐福知道嬴政这是在给自己找散心好方法，想也不想就答应下来了，旱灾和瘟疫带来的压力太大，天天顶在头上，心理再强悍也总会有心神俱疲的时候。徐福倒是想拥有一具不知疲累的身体，但那不可能，而且失去了感官之后，那也没用了。只有当体会到劳累、疲倦和抑郁的时候，才会知道幸福、开心是多么难得的滋味。
徐福和嬴政有另外的活动，姜游自然不敢去当插在中间的第三人，当即便道：“那我同邱侍医再瞧一瞧生病的人，随后便回王宫中去研究药方，师弟有空时再给我帮忙好了。”
嬴政很满意他的识趣，带着徐福上了马车。
姜游却不知突然想起了什么，他快步走过来，扒住了马车，激动地道：“王上是个好人，师弟你可以嫁！”
徐福和嬴政都是同时一懵，旁边侍从和邱侍医更是懵了。
姜游不知道自己这番有感而发实在不合时宜了些，夸奖了秦王之后的姜游，感觉到了满足，他认为自己还是很有远见的，当初没和尉缭一样傻逼，去阻拦师弟和秦王在一起。他心满意足地转身退回去了。
嬴政放下车帘，脸上的冷色褪去，倒是露出了个浅淡的笑容来，“你师兄难得聪明了一次……”
徐福毫不客气地道：“我这师兄十天里总有就九天是不带脑子的。”
嬴政早被那话说得通体舒畅，此时只笑了笑，道：“有时候蠢笨一些，也是福气。”姜游说出这番话，起码让他心中对这个徐福的师兄高看了一眼。
是谁都能得嬴政高看的吗？当然不是。
所以姜游蠢一次，换嬴政一次人情，实在划算。
不过他们的好心情实在没能维持多久，马车一路行过，等到了城外，便能见到许多不归家的百姓了，这些百姓都低声议论着什么，徐福隐隐能听见，他们在说，那位太卜……
那位太卜？能指谁？
无非便是指他了。
“如此下去，我们还有命活吗？”
“谁知道呢？那位太卜在卜筮时说得那样好听，可这么久过去了，我只听说城中谁又死了，城外谁又死了……”
“不是找到水了吗？”
“找到水又如何？唉，若是疫病治不好，大家都被染上，到时候，我们就谁也回不去家中了，大家都死了……”
“你们知道吗？我听了个消息。那位太卜啊，长得是跟个神仙似的，但他实在没什么本事啊，他抢了老太卜的位置，勾上了王上……”
“什么意思啊？”
“嘿，就是拿那张好看的脸，去王上跟前邀宠的意思呗……”
那些人根本想不到，就在不远处，那普普通通极不起眼的马车里，就坐着他们议论的人。
这群人里或许有两三个市井混混，口中的话甚至还渐渐变得荤了起来。徐福转头去看嬴政的时候，就见嬴政的脸色已经极为冷厉了，他差点当场拔出自己的随身佩剑来，不过最终嬴政也只是道：“杀了。”
徐福按住了嬴政的手背，出声道：“不必了。”
“这些话哪里算得难听？”徐福今日心情不错，因为姜游的到来，身上的压力缓解了不少，自然也就从另一个角度去看问题了，而不会将自己陷在死胡同里。
徐福不动声色地够了勾唇角，道：“这些人，不过是嫉妒我能同秦王同榻罢了。”
嬴政心头的火降下去了些，目光落在徐福脸上，见徐福眼中露出得色，嬴政这才觉得那口气舒畅了。
徐福能说出这般话，岂不是说明，他也觉得能同寡人在一起，是能令他得意欢喜的事？
嬴政脸上挤出了个阴沉的笑来，“这等泼皮无赖，还是杀了好。”“待明日，自然有人沉不住气。”
徐福接口道：“要跳出来逼我祭祀了是吗？”
那得跟他多大仇啊！逼他祭祀，再捣个乱，煽动一下，说他祭祀也没用，甚至就说灾祸其实因他所起，反正百姓能被他忽悠，自然也能被对方忽悠。
到时候最好给他泼一身的墨水，让他洗也不洗不掉，那对方自然就达到目的了。
嬴政实在不愿意徐福被外面的脏话污了耳朵，于是也只能提前结束这场散心了，虽然不满有些人故意说徐福的坏话，不过想一想今日徐福的表现，嬴政倒觉得自己心中没那么苦涩涩的了。
嬴政此时并不知道，自己又高兴得太早了。
二人刚进寝宫，坐下来没一会儿，便听有人报，姜游求见。
姜游来找徐福帮忙了。
徐福二话不说，抛下嬴政就出去了。
嬴政脸色一黑，不得不承认徐福的话，他这师兄果然是十天里有九天都是不带脑子的。
他眼睁睁地看着徐福走了出去，黑色的袍子后面，隐隐缀了根什么在晃动，就像是条尾巴一样。嬴政定睛再看，却又什么也没瞧见了。
嬴政忽然有些心累。
寡人这是禁欲禁出老花眼了吗？
chapters.translated_text:
Jiang You was wandering outside, keeping an eye on news from the Qin State. Upon hearing the version of the story where the Qin State was suffering from a severe drought and rampant epidemics, he was so shocked that he knocked over his table. He grabbed Zheng Ji and prepared to leave, but was held back by the shopkeeper, who gave him a hard time for quite a while before finally letting him go.

Zheng Ji sensed the anxiety in Jiang You’s heart and whispered, "Let’s find someone else to ask."

In truth, it wasn't just Jiang You who was worried; she was, too. Fusu was all alone in the palace. Even though he had a father who was the King of Qin, what did that matter? When an epidemic infects you, it doesn't ask who your parents are or weigh whether it can afford to offend you before striking.

The two of them, dazed and distracted by their worry for Xianyang, exchanged a look after questioning several people: "...Let’s go back to Xianyang."

It was almost as if they had spoken in unison.

Jiang You and Zheng Ji both let out a sigh of relief, shared a lighthearted smile, and immediately bought a carriage to head toward Xianyang.

Fortunately, they hadn't been far from the Qin State to begin with, so by the time they reached the outskirts of Xianyang, they happened to hear people saying that Grand Master Xu of the Fengchang Temple would be holding a divination ceremony atop the city wall.

The two waited outside the city early. Because the distance was so great, they could only see the general silhouette of Xu Fu standing on the city wall that day. Jiang You clutched his chest, filled with the pride of a parent seeing their child grow up. *My junior brother has grown up! My junior brother has grown up, ahhhhh!*

After the divination ended, Jiang You felt like he was floating as he walked.

Soon, he and Zheng Ji were left feeling melancholy as they faced each other. "When we left, we said we would never return to Xianyang..." Now they had walked right back, and they had no idea how the King of Qin would treat them.

The two sat in a dilapidated little hut and sighed at each other.

"How about... how about we try to see if we can sneak into the city?" Jiang You whispered.

Zheng Ji initially wanted to scold him for being naive, but her own heart was also stirring. The two of them really did sneak back to the city gate, only to bump straight into the attendants who were out searching the world for Jiang You.

"...Jiang You?" The man froze. He was initially uncertain, but as his gaze fell upon Zheng Ji’s face, his expression shifted violently. "Take them away!" he ordered coldly.

As soon as the words fell, two men sprang out from behind, grabbing Jiang You and Zheng Ji. Zheng Ji was weak, and Jiang You was even weaker. Once captured, they could only stare blankly at the attendant, their hearts pounding as they were dragged away.

Would they... be beheaded?

Or would their hands and feet be chopped off?

Thinking of Ying Zheng’s cold, hard face, both of them shivered involuntarily.

But after being dragged into the city, the man simply shoved them into a carriage. The carriage was sealed shut, and they could only hear the sound of the wheels rolling along the ground.

Before they could turn deathly pale and shake like leaves, they were taken out of the carriage and brought before Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng had been handling official business; upon hearing the news, he immediately put down his brush and looked toward the palace entrance.

Indeed, it was Jiang You and Zheng Ji who had been brought in.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but frown. He had just given the order, and these two were brought in already? If Ying Zheng hadn't confirmed his own eyes were working fine, he would have thought the attendant had just grabbed two random people.

Seeing Ying Zheng frown, Jiang You and Zheng Ji’s legs went soft.

At this moment, Xu Fu walked out from behind a screen and nodded slightly at Jiang You. "Senior brother." Jiang You’s heart finally settled back into place. With Xu Fu there, he and Zheng Ji probably wouldn't die too miserably.

"Why has senior brother appeared in Xianyang?" Xu Fu asked.

Ying Zheng’s gaze followed, landing on Jiang You. The look carried a chill, and Jiang You swallowed involuntarily.

"Zheng Ji and I heard that the Qin State was suffering from a great drought, and we couldn't set our minds at ease, so we came," Jiang You chose to tell the truth.

Xu Fu nodded. "Senior brother has come at just the right time; perhaps you can do me a great favor."

*Huh?* Jiang You jerked his head up. A favor? He didn't say he was going to kill them? Jiang You and Zheng Ji both let out a collective sigh of relief. Because their bodies had been tense for so long, they nearly collapsed to the floor the moment they relaxed.

"Senior brother, follow me..." Xu Fu said, already heading toward the door.

Jiang You naturally scrambled up immediately to follow Xu Fu.

Zheng Ji, left behind in the hall, felt somewhat awkward.

Ying Zheng didn't even look at her as she knelt on the ground; he waved for a palace servant. "Take her out."

Zheng Ji looked up sharply. Was the King of Qin going to keep Jiang You here while banishing her? However, Zheng Ji soon realized she had misunderstood. The servant only led her out of the hall and didn't say anything about driving her away. Zheng Ji felt awkward; she realized what Ying Zheng meant—he simply didn't want to see her.

Zheng Ji stood there for a while and couldn't help but ask, "May I ask where Prince Fusu is now?" Since she had already come to the palace, she couldn't bear to leave without taking a look. Just as she had been able to swear she would never appear in Xianyang, yet here she was, driven by the worry in her heart.

The servant looked at her with surprise and said, "Prince Fusu is still ill." Some of the servants here didn't know who Zheng Ji was; not knowing her identity, they naturally dared not say more.

Zheng Ji’s expression changed abruptly. "...Ill? Has Prince Fusu contracted the epidemic?"

The servant frowned slightly, displeased by Zheng Ji’s intense reaction.

Seeing the servant remain silent, the impulse in Zheng Ji’s heart slowly receded, and she calmed down significantly. She gripped her palms tightly; only the pain could remind her not to do anything that broke the rules. How patient she had been in the past—since leaving the palace, she had become increasingly erratic.

"Could you please go in and ask the King for me? I wish to request an audience with Prince Fusu," Zheng Ji changed her attitude, her voice soft and gentle.

Zheng Ji was a beauty, and with such a gentle tone, she naturally regained some of her image. The servant glanced at her; he had wanted to scold her for being too full of herself, but seeing her delicate features and sincere expression, he hesitated before turning to enter the hall.

Ying Zheng knew Zheng Ji wanted to see Fusu.

The servant came out and brought Zheng Ji back into the hall. Zheng Ji knelt down uneasily and kowtowed. "I beg the King to allow me to see Prince Fusu."

"You do not need to see him," Ying Zheng said flatly. "Fusu has contracted the epidemic; if you go to see him, you only increase your own risk of infection."

Zheng Ji took a heavy breath. "...I... I am not afraid."

In her early years, she hadn't given Fusu much affection; the word "loving mother" could never be applied to her. Later, she even abandoned Fusu to leave Xianyang with someone else. Now that Fusu was ill, how could she act as if nothing had happened?

Just as Zheng Ji was thinking about how to plead with Ying Zheng, Xu Fu happened to return.

Zheng Ji looked back; there was only Xu Fu, with no sign of Jiang You. Zheng Ji gripped her palms tightly. "Grand Master Xu, where is Jiang You?"

"I have something to ask of Senior Brother Jiang You, so I kept him behind to discuss prescriptions for treating the epidemic with the palace physicians."

Zheng Ji breathed a slight sigh of relief.

Seeing her like this, Xu Fu felt a faint displeasure. With Zheng Ji acting this way, was she worried that Ying Zheng would do something to her and Jiang You? If Ying Zheng really wanted to do something, he wouldn't have let them leave back then, and he wouldn't have indulged Zheng Ji in cuckolding him. Zheng Ji’s lack of trust in Ying Zheng was truly grating. Xu Fu smoothed his expression and said, "If Zheng Ji has nothing else, you may return on your own."

Zheng Ji keenly caught the chill in Xu Fu’s words, and she felt even more awkward.

Zheng Ji gritted her teeth. Seeing that Ying Zheng wasn't even looking at her, she had no choice but to hold it in and leave first. *Not seeing him... is fine too...* After all, she was going to leave Fusu anyway, so why pretend to be a concerned mother at a time like this? Zheng Ji walked out, pretending that nothing was wrong.

Seeing her come out and just stand there without moving, the servant didn't find it strange.

"May I ask where Prince Fusu is staying?" She couldn't see him, but hearing news of him would be a comfort.

The servant looked back into the hall and happened to meet Xu Fu’s gaze. Seeing Xu Fu nod at him, the servant said, "This servant can take you outside the side hall to take a look."

Zheng Ji’s face lit up with joy as she followed the servant away.

Standing before the palace, Zheng Ji murmured, "So he still lives here..."

Just then, she saw a very short but adorable-looking little child running past the front of the hall, followed by a group of servants.

"Who is that?" Zheng Ji was surprised. Had the King added another heir? But given the King’s relationship with Grand Master Xu... would Grand Master Xu allow it?

"Prince Huhai."

Zheng Ji suddenly realized. *Right, it’s Huhai.* There were now two children in the palace, Fusu and Huhai. As time passed, she had forgotten what Huhai looked like. Indeed, as time goes by, people become forgetful.

She watched Huhai use his short legs to struggle over the threshold, shouting noisily, "Brother!"

Zheng Ji suddenly felt her eyes sting.

She turned around. "Thank you, I won't look anymore..."

Zheng Ji was led back outside the hall by the servant. She glanced into the hall, but Ying Zheng and Xu Fu were gone. Zheng Ji looked around blankly and sat down alone in front of the hall.

At this time, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had already left the palace, accompanied by Physician Qiu and one Jiang You.

Bo Zhou was driving the carriage outside, lips pursed and face cold, looking quite imposing.

As their carriage passed, no one dared to block them. Slowly, the carriage stopped in front of a fence.

Jiang You jumped off the carriage first and pointed to the area in front of them. "Is this the quarantine zone?"

Ying Zheng had been very generous. If it were any other monarch, let alone setting aside a quarantine zone in the city, they would have likely driven all the infected people out, driven them far away, and left them to fend for themselves. Even worse, they might have killed all the infected and thrown the bodies into a mass grave to be burned and buried.

If it were the Ying Zheng of history, he might have actually done such a thing. But the current Ying Zheng hadn't even considered such an approach.

Jiang You pushed open the wooden fence and, led by Bo Zhou, underwent rigorous checks before successfully entering the quarantine zone. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng followed far behind, with Physician Qiu trailing them, constantly watching their complexions, terrified that they might catch the disease here.

Ying Zheng stopped after only a few steps.

He didn't want to go in himself, and he didn't want to bring Xu Fu inside either.

Ying Zheng was no saint. Aside from his son, whom he could still interact with, he wouldn't touch anyone else who had contracted the disease. He wouldn't gamble with his own life, and he certainly wouldn't gamble with Xu Fu’s life.

"Is this where the rumors originated?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.

If not for someone reporting that rumors were rampant in the city again, and that they had angered Xu Fu, Ying Zheng wouldn't have brought him here.

An attendant stepped forward from behind. "It is indeed here."

"Go and drag that person out. This place is not fit for Us to step into; go and drag him out yourself," Ying Zheng said, his face darkening.

"Yes." The attendant didn't care what kind of place this was; he walked in openly and found a few people to inquire.

Even though they hadn't walked far inside, Xu Fu could hear the wailing and cries of pain from within, along with faint sobs. These people had been tortured by illness for too long.

Xu Fu couldn't help but say, "If they ask me to preside over a ritual, it is not impossible..."

It would just be giving the people a bit more hope; it wouldn't cost him much effort.

Ying Zheng’s expression turned ugly. "I am worried that someone is deliberately targeting you. You have already found a water source for Xianyang; how is that not proof of your divine powers? Yet there are still people who question your words, deliberately spreading rumors to make the sick believe they have no hope of survival, and making the whole city think Xianyang is destined to become a city of the dead. How can you let someone with such malicious intentions get their way?"

Xu Fu thought about it, and that made sense. If there was someone behind this, then playing into their hands would be truly foolish.

Before long, Jiang You came out first with Bo Zhou.

Jiang You’s expression was somewhat grim. He said to Xu Fu, "It is even more serious than I imagined."

"Is there a solution?"

"I have some ideas forming in my mind, but I need to test them to see if they will work on them."

"Is there anything I can help with?" Xu Fu asked.

Jiang You smiled. "Junior brother only loved learning alchemy when we were young, not medicine or healing. Don't go making trouble for your senior brother..."

"Does senior brother think I would make trouble?" In reality, Xu Fu just wanted to help and steal a few techniques while he was at it. If he could learn a thing or two, that would be great. Essential for home and travel!

Jiang You tactfully changed his tune, showing absolutely no backbone. "No, no, junior brother can naturally be of help."

Just then, an attendant brought a man out. The attendant didn't dare bring him too close, fearing the miasma on the man would offend Xu Fu and Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng looked coldly. It was a middle-aged man, thin and gaunt, reduced to nothing but skin and bones by the epidemic. Could a person like this really spread rumors?

"Has he confessed?"

The attendant said helplessly, "He’s a tough nut to crack."

Xu Fu had expected this result. People who had contracted the epidemic were unlikely to survive anyway. Perhaps this man thought that since he had no chance of living, there was no need to confess his actions just because of a few threats.

Ying Zheng felt a bit disgusted. He pulled Xu Fu in front of him, raised a hand to cover his eyes, and whispered, "Kill him."

The attendant didn't hesitate, immediately drawing his weapon to end the man’s life. Afterward, someone used a wooden cart to haul the body away to be burned.

Seeing this scene, Jiang You’s legs trembled. His heart turned cold, and he didn't even dare to look at Ying Zheng. If Ying Zheng had really decided to punish him back when he tried to snatch Fusu, he might have been bleeding on the ground... and wouldn't even have a whole corpse left. *Thank goodness, thank goodness. Thank goodness junior brother became the King of Qin’s wife.*

The person who had once been so dissatisfied that Ying Zheng wasn't good enough for Xu Fu was now slapping his own face, cowardly praising in his heart: *The King of Qin is truly a good man...*

*He is truly a perfect match for junior brother!*

Ying Zheng whispered in Xu Fu’s ear, "Let’s walk around the city. Didn't you want to see the wells that were dug?"

Xu Fu knew Ying Zheng was finding a way for him to relax, so he agreed without a second thought. The pressure brought by the drought and the epidemic was too great, hanging over his head every day; no matter how strong one’s mind was, there would always be times of exhaustion. Xu Fu wished he had a body that didn't know fatigue, but that was impossible. Besides, without senses, that would be useless. Only when one experiences exhaustion, fatigue, and depression does one know how rare happiness and joy are.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had other activities, so Jiang You naturally didn't dare to be the third wheel. He immediately said, "Then I will take another look at the sick with Physician Qiu, and then return to the palace to study the prescriptions. Junior brother can help me when you have time."

Ying Zheng was satisfied with his tact and took Xu Fu into the carriage.

Jiang You, however, suddenly remembered something. He hurried over, grabbed the carriage, and said excitedly, "The King is a good man, junior brother, you can marry him!"

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were both stunned simultaneously. The nearby attendants and Physician Qiu were even more bewildered.

Jiang You didn't realize that his heartfelt remark was highly inappropriate. Having praised the King of Qin, Jiang You felt satisfied. He believed he was quite far-sighted; he hadn't been an idiot like Wei Liao, trying to stop his junior brother from being with the King of Qin. He turned around and retreated, feeling content.

Ying Zheng lowered the carriage curtain, the coldness on his face fading to reveal a faint smile. "Your senior brother is rarely clever..."

Xu Fu said bluntly, "My senior brother is brainless nine out of ten days."

Ying Zheng had already been left feeling thoroughly pleased by those words; he just laughed and said, "Sometimes being a bit foolish is a blessing." Jiang You saying that at least made him think more highly of Xu Fu’s senior brother.

Is it easy for just anyone to be thought highly of by Ying Zheng? Of course not.

So, Jiang You being foolish once in exchange for a favor from Ying Zheng was a good deal.

However, their good mood didn't last long. As the carriage drove along, once they reached the outskirts, they could see many people who hadn't returned home. These people were whispering about something. Xu Fu could faintly hear them talking about that Grand Master...

That Grand Master? Who else could it refer to?

It could only be him.

"If this continues, will we even survive?"

"Who knows? That Grand Master spoke so nicely during the divination, but so much time has passed, and I only hear about who died in the city and who died outside..."

"Didn't they find water?"

"What does finding water matter? Sigh, if the epidemic can't be cured and everyone gets infected, then none of us will be able to return home. We’ll all be dead..."

"Do you know? I heard some news. That Grand Master, he looks like a god, but he really has no ability. He stole the old Grand Master’s position and hooked up with the King..."

"What does that mean?"

"Heh, it just means he uses that pretty face to curry favor with the King..."

Those people had no idea that just a short distance away, in that ordinary, inconspicuous carriage, sat the very person they were discussing.

Among this group were perhaps two or three street thugs, and their words were even becoming vulgar. When Xu Fu turned to look at Ying Zheng, he saw that his expression had become extremely cold and stern. He almost drew his sword on the spot, but in the end, Ying Zheng only said, "Kill them."

Xu Fu pressed down on Ying Zheng’s hand. "No need."

"How can these words be considered harsh?" Xu Fu was in a good mood today. Because of Jiang You’s arrival, the pressure on him had eased significantly, so he naturally viewed the problem from a different perspective instead of trapping himself in a dead end.

Xu Fu curled his lips slightly and said, "These people are just jealous that I can share a bed with the King of Qin."

The fire in Ying Zheng’s heart subsided a little. His gaze fell on Xu Fu’s face, and seeing the look of triumph in Xu Fu’s eyes, Ying Zheng finally felt that breath of relief.

If Xu Fu could say such things, didn't that mean he also felt that being with Us was something to be proud and happy about?

Ying Zheng forced a gloomy smile. "These rascals should still be killed." "Tomorrow, someone will naturally lose their patience."

Xu Fu added, "They’re going to jump out and force me to perform a ritual, right?"

That would be a huge grudge! Forcing him to perform a ritual, then causing trouble, inciting people, saying his ritual was useless, or even saying the disaster was caused by him—after all, if the people could be fooled by him, they could be fooled by the other side.

At that point, it would be best to splash him with enough ink that he couldn't wash it off, and the other side would have achieved their goal.

Ying Zheng really didn't want Xu Fu’s ears to be dirtied by the filth outside, so he had to end this outing early. Although he was displeased that some people were deliberately bad-mouthing Xu Fu, thinking about Xu Fu’s performance today, Ying Zheng felt less bitter inside.

Ying Zheng didn't know at this moment that he was happy too soon again.

As soon as the two entered the sleeping quarters and sat down, they heard someone report that Jiang You requested an audience.

Jiang You had come to ask Xu Fu for help.

Xu Fu didn't say a word, abandoned Ying Zheng, and went out.

Ying Zheng’s face turned black. He had to admit Xu Fu was right; his senior brother really was brainless nine out of ten days.

He watched as Xu Fu walked out, and behind his black robes, something seemed to be swaying, like a tail. Ying Zheng looked closer, but then saw nothing.

Ying Zheng suddenly felt a bit weary.

*Have I practiced abstinence so long that I’ve developed presbyopia?*

chapters.title: 第121章
chapters.translated_text:
Jiang You’s so-called "help" involved digging out ancient texts, looking up information, and sorting through medicinal herbs himself. If Xu Fu accidentally handed him the wrong one, Jiang You would grind his teeth and glare at him with a chilling intensity.

Only at these moments would Jiang You’s aura suddenly and invisibly become overwhelming.

Feeling guilty, Xu Fu worked all the harder. He knew that making a mistake at a time like this was absolutely forbidden; if he accidentally caused someone’s death, how would he ever face himself? Xu Fu focused all his attention. Even though he didn't recognize many of the herbs, he gritted his teeth, flipped through the ancient texts rapidly, and identified them one by one. In this back-and-forth process, he was forced to memorize the contents of the ancient texts by sheer willpower. In the blink of an eye, he looked outside and realized it was already nightfall.

He didn't even know what time it was.

Xu Fu beckoned to the attendant waiting outside the door. The attendant’s face lit up with joy as he hurried in, "Is Master Xu finished?"

Only then did Xu Fu snap back to reality and realize he was nearly starving to death. Fortunately, his stomach hadn't thrown a tantrum and started growling in front of so many people.

"Why didn't you come in and call me?"

The attendant replied aggrievedly, "People from the King’s side have come to urge us several times, but since you were busy, we didn't dare to disturb you."

Xu Fu was stunned. Was he really that engrossed?

"Then I will tell my Senior Brother and head back now." While it was important to create a cure for the epidemic as soon as possible, he couldn't sacrifice his rest for it. Xu Fu really didn't want to experience another time where a court physician smiled at him and said, "You are suffering from a deficiency of vital energy."

The attendant smiled happily and agreed, secretly wiping the sweat from his brow.

If they didn't get him back now, they would surely be kicked flying by the King.

"Senior Brother, I’m leaving now." Xu Fu walked over to tell Jiang You, but Jiang You didn't even look up. Xu Fu called out a few more times, only then realizing why the attendant couldn't get a response from him earlier. Xu Fu had no choice but to turn and walk toward the door. Just as he reached the threshold, Jiang You suddenly seemed to wake up, pointed at his backside, and roared, "Junior Brother, have you become a spirit?"

You’re the one who’s a spirit!

Xu Fu turned back with a dark face, followed his gaze, and reached back to rip off something stuck to his robe.

A long... strip of cloth?

Xu Fu realized with confusion that the strip looked familiar, but it had changed significantly from before. It had grown longer.

It was as if it were a living thing with a soul, growing on its own... Xu Fu couldn't help but shiver, and countless horror stories flooded his mind. He pretended nothing was wrong and stuffed the strip into his sleeve, "Senior Brother, you’ve been busy for too long and your eyes are playing tricks on you. You should rest more."

Jiang You looked closely and saw that it was indeed empty. He sighed and smiled, "Perhaps I am tired. Thank you for your concern, Junior Brother." After saying this, Jiang You even showed a moved expression.

The others in the palace, however, were astonished.

They had originally thought Jiang You was just a talented individual invited by the King, but hearing him openly address Xu Fu as "Junior Brother"... didn't that mean he also came from the same school as the State Lieutenant? That he was also from Guigu? Immediately, their gazes toward him changed, and they secretly warned themselves never to offend him.

Xu Fu walked out of the room, crossed an archway, and followed a small path until he reached the wide main road.

The moon in the sky cast a cold light, and the night felt chilly. Xu Fu tucked his hands into his sleeves, but he felt the strip of cloth moving. He pinched it, but it felt soft and limp, with nothing unusual about it.

How strange.

After returning to his sleeping quarters, the attendant who had led him there retreated on his own. Ying Zheng sat under the candlelight, still flipping through bamboo slips. Hearing footsteps, he didn't even look up and said, "A-Fu, do you know which part of the Qin State has remained unscathed this time?"

"There is a place that hasn't suffered?" Xu Fu was surprised. He had assumed the entire Qin State was trapped in the drought. Hearing Ying Zheng say this, he was naturally astonished. If there was such a place, would it become a target for everyone’s greed? Would everyone be desperate to flee there? Xu Fu knew very well that one place couldn't support too many people; if it did, this sanctuary would quickly perish as well.

"You have been there before," Ying Zheng said in a low voice.

Xu Fu keenly noticed the corners of his mouth lift slightly, carrying a hint of a smile.

In a flash of lightning, two words popped into Xu Fu’s mind: "Shu Commandery?"

Ying Zheng nodded, "Exactly."

The expression on Xu Fu’s face relaxed unconsciously. Perhaps he hadn't even realized it himself, but in front of Ying Zheng, his demeanor was no longer always so tense.

"In that case, the construction of the Dujiangyan was not only correct, but it has also made a great contribution."

"Yes." Ying Zheng no longer hid the joy on his face. "I never expected Li Bing to contribute so much to the Dujiangyan. While the rest of Qin is in such dire straits, only the Dujiangyan can still live a normal life." The joy on Ying Zheng’s face slowly faded. He paused and said, "However, this is not a long-term solution. If it doesn't rain for much longer, no one knows how long Qin can hold out."

The relaxed look on Xu Fu’s face faded as well.

Since arriving in Qin, his divination had almost never failed. The shocked and reverent gazes of others had almost made him believe there was nothing in this era he couldn't predict. But now, he felt a deep sense of powerlessness. Even if the I Ching had warned him of disaster, what of it? It was too late; there were no measures to save the situation. He couldn't even calculate an accurate time for the disaster to end.

"If someone forces me to perform a sacrifice tomorrow..."

"You don't have to agree." Ying Zheng’s expression darkened. He absolutely detested people plotting against Xu Fu behind his back. If he caught them, he would surely subject them to the harshest punishment so they would know that not everyone could be threatened at will.

Xu Fu shook his head at this moment, "No, I must agree to this."

"You know that person has ill intentions, yet you still want to agree?" Ying Zheng frowned slightly. In truth, there might not be any real danger, but it was highly likely the opponent would use it to smear Xu Fu’s name. Even if it was just mud-slinging, Ying Zheng didn't want to see it. His person was to be protected by him; he wouldn't allow anyone to lay a finger on him.

However, Xu Fu clearly didn't have the awareness of having a "big boss" backing him, so he made a decision based on his usual habits, "If he wants a sacrifice, then I shall perform one. The rumors are already out there anyway. If I don't step forward, people will likely say I’m feeling guilty." Every time someone knelt before him calling him an immortal, although Xu Fu found it a bit cringey and "Mary Sue," being called an immortal was better than being called a "star of disaster" or having the drought blamed on him.

If a tiger doesn't show its claws, do they really think I’m a kitten that can be pushed around?

"I will not only perform the sacrifice, but I will also lead the disaster toward that person," Xu Fu said coldly.

Seeing his confident demeanor, Ying Zheng swallowed back all the advice he had intended to give. How could he have forgotten? Xu Fu was not only his person, but also an independent individual. Xu Fu had never relied on others to avoid plots and hidden arrows.

Xu Fu’s eyes were shining, and the depression of the past few days had been swept away.

Having an opponent hiding in the shadows was more effective than taking medicine; it instantly made him feel refreshed.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but sigh inwardly. Does this mean I have to thank him?

"If there is anything you need me to do, just let me know," Ying Zheng couldn't help but say. Xu Fu being too independent wasn't a good thing. Ying Zheng felt he didn't even have a place to be useful, which was truly frustrating.

When Ying Zheng first fell for him, he had thought about keeping Xu Fu like other kings kept their favorites—spreading his wings to fully protect him. He never would have imagined that his relationship with Xu Fu would eventually turn into this. How could he find any of a king’s dignity or authority in front of Xu Fu? Thinking back, his first threat to Xu Fu—that if he lied, he would hang him from the mast to dry—felt like something from a past life.

The mounting pressure of this period had made Xu Fu’s emotions unstable, and he would occasionally become sentimental, though this had made him more delicate in certain aspects.

For instance, at this moment, Xu Fu noticed that Ying Zheng’s mood didn't seem very high.

"A-Zheng, are you worried about me?" Xu Fu naturally wouldn't guess Ying Zheng’s thoughts; he only assumed Ying Zheng was worried about his safety.

After all, every time Ying Zheng showed displeasure toward him, it was because he was worried about his well-being.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu’s thoughts stalled for a moment... It seemed that Ying Zheng’s concern and worry for him were always greater.

"Naturally, I am worried about you." Seeing that Xu Fu was finally not so thick-skinned, the emotions in Ying Zheng’s heart were soothed. A little progress now, and in the future, Xu Fu would make leaps and bounds and realize his burning love.

However, after Ying Zheng finished speaking, he realized Xu Fu had drifted off again.

"A-Fu?"

"..."

Ying Zheng had to raise his voice, "Junfang."

Xu Fu was truly unfamiliar with this name, but it was precisely because it was unfamiliar that it pulled him out of his thoughts.

"Are you thinking about the sacrifice?"

Xu Fu shook his head and blurted out, "I was thinking, have I ever worried about you?"

Ying Zheng was stunned, secretly finding it amusing. For Xu Fu to think this way was truly progress... Ying Zheng suddenly felt a bit sad. It was so hard to wait for Xu Fu to care about him.

Once the words were out, Xu Fu felt a bit ashamed, but he was a broad-minded person, and saying it out loud actually tore away that layer of shame. Xu Fu said, "I have worried about you."

"Oh? Is that so?" Ying Zheng truly hadn't felt it. When had Xu Fu ever worried about him? Xu Fu was someone who sometimes just disguised his coldness on the outside, but the more he got to know him, the more he felt that Xu Fu was cold on the inside—someone who looked easy to deal with but was actually indifferent to the world. He didn't know if it had to do with his upbringing and past experiences.

Xu Fu quickly recalled in his mind, feeling more confident now, and said in a low voice, "Of course. Look, when you were coming of age, if I hadn't been worried about you, I wouldn't have cast so many divinations for you and helped you find the Imperial Seal. I was anxious for you, but you didn't even take it to heart; I worried for nothing that time. And later, I went to see Lü Buwei for you and scared him to death. And I went to Shu for you to solve the floods. And I went to Wei and Han for you..."

"..." Ying Zheng felt a bit suffocated. He really wanted to say that it was clearly Xu Fu who wanted to go out and play, and who wanted to find those strange tripods.

But Xu Fu seemed to have opened a floodgate and suddenly became talkative, "And when you were arguing with Zhao Ji, I was very worried about you. And when Hu Ji betrayed you, look, I didn't even dare to get close to Hu Hai..."

It was clearly because you didn't like children yourself.

"And also, I brought Lord Longyang to Qin because I was worried that he had great talent and staying with the King of Wei would hinder your unification cause. And when Wei Liao came to Qin, he told me you were a bad person—malicious, narrow-minded, and tyrannical—and told me not to play with you, but I scolded him severely..." At this point, a hint of smugness flashed quickly in Xu Fu’s eyes.

Ying Zheng suddenly grasped the key sentence in this, "When Wei Liao came to Qin, he said these things to you? And that’s why you gave him the cold shoulder later?"

Xu Fu paused.

Eh? He seemed to have let something slip...

He had originally intended to never mention what Wei Liao said about Ying Zheng, so as not to upset him.

Seeing that Xu Fu, who had been talkative just a moment ago, had suddenly stopped, Ying Zheng’s heart stirred, and a small flame seemed to be dancing in his chest. He had thought his doting on Xu Fu was a one-way street, with no sign of Xu Fu being moved, but Xu Fu’s devotion to him was much more subtle.

So there was such a story, and he hadn't even known...

No wonder Wei Liao always had a cold attitude toward him later. It was just because his Junior Brother, Xu Fu, had scolded him for the sake of another man.

Ying Zheng felt he could almost sketch out the image of Xu Fu protecting him back then—cold, sharp, aloof, and suppressing his anger. Ying Zheng felt like he had eaten honey; it was too sweet, but not cloying at all. The pleasure in Ying Zheng’s heart was built entirely on Wei Liao’s pain. Hahaha... So Xu Xiaofu had actually scolded his Senior Brother for my sake...

Ying Zheng selectively forgot that at that time, Xu Fu had no idea who Ying Zheng was.

One was a stranger, the other was someone he had slept with; even if it was just a "friends with benefits" situation, Xu Fu would definitely defend the one he knew.

Thinking about this, it was quite something. The more Ying Zheng thought about it, the more he felt that perhaps Xu Fu’s trips to Shu, Wei, and Han were indeed partly for his sake.

Even this divination—Xu Fu was clearly exhausted, yet he still wanted to hold the ceremony to calm the people’s panic. He said it was for Xianyang and for Qin, but wasn't it also for him? Ying Zheng thought further and almost believed that Xu Fu had loved him from the very beginning, but was just too stubborn to say it...

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng with a strange expression.

Why did his expression change so quickly? He looked a bit... like a fanboy?

Xu Fu coughed lightly and resumed his cold demeanor, "Count it up, there were many times I worried about you."

It was the same in Sanchuan Commandery; he worried about what would happen if Ying Zheng got sick, how could Ying Zheng leave him and return to Xianyang first, and he was furious when he saw Ying Zheng encounter assassins.

The scales in Xu Fu’s heart balanced out in a flash.

See, I’m actually very good to him. Xu Fu breathed a slight sigh of relief. That’s good; it shows I’m not a "scum top."

To prevent Ying Zheng from asking too closely about what Wei Liao had said that day, Xu Fu timely changed the subject, "Since Shu is safe and sound, will there be people in Qin who want to go to Shu?"

"No."

"Why not? If they all knew that Shu could escape the drought, wouldn't they all swarm to Shu for refuge?"

Ying Zheng looked indifferent, suppressing the myriad emotions in his heart, and played along with Xu Fu, "No one will believe it. In the eyes of the people, the journey to Shu is difficult, and Shu is backward and poor. How could such a place escape the drought? No one will believe it." Ying Zheng paused and said, "However, I firmly believe that if Zheng Guo can finish the canal, then in the future, Guanzhong will surely become another Shu and be spared the disaster of drought."

When Ying Zheng said this, he was still carefully observing the expression on Xu Fu’s face. In Ying Zheng’s heart, he had unconsciously begun to see Xu Fu as someone who was cold on the outside but shy on the inside (?).

If Ying Zheng were in the modern era, he would surely know a term for Xu Fu—"gap moe."

Xu Fu didn't know Ying Zheng’s imagination was running wild; he only felt Ying Zheng’s gaze was a bit creepy. Uh, was he moved by me? Xu Fu moved back a step silently, then said, "I wonder if the State of Han will regret sending such a talented Zheng Guo to you with both hands."

"The King of Han won't regret it, but Han Fei already regrets it," Ying Zheng sneered.

Xu Fu had almost forgotten about Han Fei. Suddenly hearing the name, he realized, Han Fei was... supposed to be dead, right? He wouldn't die in this disaster, would he?

"Is Han Fei still in the city?"

"Yes, he stays behind closed doors. Occasionally someone goes to deliver some things," Ying Zheng said. Although Han Fei’s temper was unpleasant, his talent was undeniable. Ying Zheng simply let him be. If he could survive, perhaps there would be a chance to use him in the future; if he couldn't, then it was heaven’s will, and he couldn't keep someone who was so devoted to Han.

Xu Fu silently noted this, thinking he would go check on him in a few days.

This Han Fei could be considered one of his "experimental subjects," just like Concubine Zheng and Lord Longyang.

"King... A-Zheng, have you eaten today?"

Ying Zheng lifted his eyes and swept them across his abdomen, and without a word, ordered the attendants to bring food, "Are you tired? If you are, don't go help anymore. There are so many attendants in the palace, why do you need to help personally?"

Xu Fu shook his head, "I just happened to be learning some things from my Senior Brother."

The corners of Ying Zheng’s mouth curled up, and he smiled maliciously, "Learning how to do more interesting tricks?"

Xu Fu ignored him. When the food was brought up, he immediately lowered his head and ate quietly. When he raised his hand to pick up food, the strip of cloth in his sleeve slipped out somehow.

Seeing this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but laugh, "My Master of Ceremonies actually has such a childish side, hiding a strip of cloth in his sleeve." As he said this, he reached out and grabbed the strip.

After Ying Zheng grabbed the strip, he felt it looked truly strange, as if it were soaked in blood, and when he looked closely, he felt the blood seemed to be flowing. In a moment of distraction, Ying Zheng let out a muffled grunt.

Xu Fu almost overturned his tableware, "What’s wrong?" He turned back quickly.

Ying Zheng pinched the strip, "What is this thing?"

Xu Fu looked closely and his eyes almost popped out.

Blood beads were actually spurting from Ying Zheng’s fingertips.

Xu Fu felt unhappy, thinking this strip was truly playing tricks. If it really had the power of witchcraft, why couldn't it take shape? Instead, it was like sticky taffy, clinging to him every day, and even the new strips he made would inexplicably disappear.

Xu Fu grabbed the strip with a dark face and ordered someone to bring a tripod.

The attendant carefully brought the tripod Xu Fu treasured. Xu Fu threw the strip in, lit it with a candle, and then set it aside, ignoring it.

Ying Zheng curled his fingers, "Is that the thing you soaked in blood before? Are you testing witchcraft?"

Xu Fu was full, so he put down his chopsticks, "Yes. It’s a bit evil." But as a fangshi who always relied on divination to fool people, calling someone else "evil" felt a bit like the pot calling the kettle black.

Ying Zheng wasn't worried about the experiments Xu Fu did in private; he knew Xu Fu could handle the degree. Besides, even if Ying Zheng claimed to be knowledgeable, he was truly shallow in these areas.

After the meal, Xu Fu washed up briefly, then changed his robes and lay on the bed with Ying Zheng to rest.

Xu Fu closed his eyes, then suddenly opened them again.

He fidgeted under the covers, then turned over and pressed down on Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng was caught off guard by his sudden weight and couldn't help but smile bitterly. What was he doing?

He saw Xu Fu very boldly pull his deep robe down, revealing his small shoulder, "Let’s do something... fun."

Ying Zheng’s throat moved, "Something fun?"

"Yes." Xu Fu very generously revealed a look of "at your service."

Ying Zheng, who had been abstinent for over half a month because Xu Fu was basically uncooperative, naturally wouldn't refuse such beauty delivered to his door, so he generously "ate" Xu Fu.

And Xu Fu silently kept a tally in his heart.

Look, I’m actually very considerate of you. See how you were憋坏了 (suffocating), I just thoughtfully lay flat automatically.

Thinking this, Xu Fu immediately felt he was a "bottom" rarely found in heaven or earth.

The candlelight and the curtains swayed together.

The small tripod was placed on the table. Who knows how much time had passed—perhaps when the moon was in the middle of the sky—a thin, long black shadow struggled and crawled out of the tripod, and even like a person, it let out a long breath, "Hoo..."

Sometimes, appropriate indulgence is a good way to relieve stress and make one feel refreshed.

Xu Fu, who had been suffering from a deficiency of vital energy, woke up the next morning feeling full of energy. If Ying Zheng hadn't also been full of vigor after waking up, Xu Fu would have suspected he had learned some incredible skill and sucked Ying Zheng’s vital energy away.

After the two changed their robes, they went to court together.

Yes, together.

Xu Fu wanted to see the person behind the mischief, and the fully satisfied Ying Zheng was also very willing to let Xu Fu stand by his side, letting him feel that lingering taste.

At the grand court today, Ying Zheng wore black court robes, with the crown tassels hanging in front of his forehead, making his face look even colder and more handsome.

Actually, Ying Zheng wanted to make such a hat for Xu Fu too, so he could hide Xu Fu’s incomparably handsome face.

If Xu Fu became the State Preceptor in the future, he would openly grant him one.

The two entered the hall together, and Xu Fu’s appearance in white robes entered the public eye.

Wearing white robes was Xu Fu’s own request, and Ying Zheng only hesitated slightly before agreeing to Xu Fu’s choice.

White robes were common attire for commoners, but Ying Zheng had to say that there was absolutely no second person in the world who could wear white robes better than Xu Fu. And Xu Fu also quite unceremoniously thought that indeed, no one could wear them better than him. Most importantly, he was used to this attire, which made him look more like an immortal with an arrogant and otherworldly air, making ordinary people afraid to provoke him easily. Since he was going to face the person behind the scenes today, he naturally had to show his most imposing side.

It would be best to have a good contrast with that person’s ugly face!

Xu Fu suppressed his thoughts and stood by Ying Zheng’s side with complete naturalness.

The ministers bowed to Ying Zheng one after another. These ministers were the ones who hadn't fallen ill yet, but the torment of this period had already made their faces pale or sallow. They all looked like they had been abused by the King of Qin.

And among this group, a hidden gaze fell on Xu Fu, only to be withdrawn quickly.

Xu Fu knew someone was observing him; he could even guess what the other person was thinking. That hidden gaze, carrying a hint of glee...

He must be thinking, "Haha, this idiot actually dares to come here. Perfect, I will ridicule and humiliate him here until he loses all face, and then force him to agree, finally showing an expression of annoyance."

Xu Fu wasn't in a hurry to search for this gaze, because he knew that person would stand out soon.

After the daily monarch-subject dialogue ended, an old man took the initiative to step forward and said, "King, the situation in the city is dire, and there has been no improvement in any part of the Qin State. Your servant dares to ask: was what Master Xu said on the city wall that day all a deception?"

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng glanced at the man almost simultaneously, and both confirmed in their hearts: it wasn't him.

If that person stood out, he would definitely be aggressive. After all, having plotted in the shadows for so long, he must be unable to hold back, eager to trample Xu Fu underfoot. His words would surely be intense, and every sentence would be aimed at splashing mud on Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng swept a cold glance at the man, "When did Master Xu deceive you?"

The man frowned, "Master Xu said that water, fire, and the divine medicine would solve the epidemic and drought. Is that not so?"

Ying Zheng blocked him back without haste, "Now there is only groundwater, but no water from heaven. There are many kinds of medicine, but the divine medicine has yet to be found. Only fire can be started anywhere. How can it be considered complete? Since it is not complete, naturally the drought and epidemic in the city have not been alleviated. Disaster is not that easy to solve. If it were as easy as you say, why don't I leave this matter to you to be responsible for?"

The man’s face turned pale, and he hurriedly said, "I dare not, I dare not." Saying this, he quickly retreated.

At this moment, someone else laughed with a sarcastic, mocking tone, "In my opinion, Master Xu’s words are mostly excuses. It’s just to clear himself of the suspicion of not presiding over the wax sacrifice well, so he pretended to hold a divination ceremony to confuse the people and make them believe what Master Xu said. But now? Now the people are full of complaints, and desperate people can be seen everywhere in the city. Master Xu told us to wait. Wait?" The man burst into a loud laugh, "What can we wait for? Wait until everyone is dead?" He said these words with extreme coldness, showing no mercy.

Right, it’s you.

Xu Fu slowly raised his head, his indifferent gaze falling on the man.

Ying Zheng looked over at the same time as him.

The person who was usually somewhat afraid of Ying Zheng was now putting on a righteous posture, as if he were doing it for the greater good.

What a great performance!

Throughout the court, not to mention those who didn't want to make an enemy of Wei Liao, there were others who didn't want to make an enemy of Xu Fu himself. None of them stood up to accuse Xu Fu of being wrong. They might have had doubts and anxiety in their hearts, but since the King didn't blame Xu Fu, why should they go out of their way to blame him? Had there been few disasters recorded in history? Which time didn't involve tens of thousands of deaths? This time could already be considered the mercy of the gods and the protection of the King.

Only one person had a hatred for Xu Fu that could be described as irreconcilable.

This person hated Xu Fu, and he also hated Ying Zheng.

"Then, according to Lord Changping, what should be done?" Xu Fu looked at the other party and said in a measured tone, without any loss of composure after being provoked. If one were to say Xu Fu was a very patient person, that wouldn't be entirely true. When he heard it, he felt a bit annoyed in his heart; this Lord Changping was clearly trying to label him as a sinner. Being labeled like this naturally made him unhappy. It was the displeasure of having his dignity violated.

Lord Changping didn't hide his purpose. He lifted his head, showing a bit of the arrogance of a descendant of the Chu royal family, and then said loudly, "Please perform a sacrifice!"

The ministers were stunned. They had previously seen Lord Changping’s targeting of Xu Fu, and now hearing him say this, they couldn't help but think of the sacrifice.

Sacrifice reached its peak during the Shang and Zhou dynasties. They were superstitious about ghosts and gods, divining everything and often performing sacrifices—sacrificing to heaven, ghosts, gods, and ancestors. By the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, this custom had not been erased. Not only that... according to the meager historical knowledge Xu Fu possessed, he knew that sacrifice would continue to be carried forward in later dynasties.

Because the way of sacrifice had little to do with physiognomy, Xu Fu only knew a little bit about it.

Even if Xu Fu knew nothing, he had the confidence to accept it. He could definitely fool everyone so that no one could find a fault. Of course, except for Lord Changping; even if there were no faults, Lord Changping would rack his brains to create one.

"What do you all think?" Ying Zheng leaned forward slightly and asked.

Lord Changping was slightly startled, then regained his composure.

Lord Changping hadn't expected Ying Zheng’s first sentence not to be a reprimand. He sneered in his heart. Didn't Ying Zheng treasure him? Didn't these two have a private affair? Why, at this moment, was he abandoning his male favorite?

Lord Changping felt very happy, as if he had already seen Xu Fu’s miserable end.

At this moment, Wei Liao’s face was extremely ugly. He knew Xu Fu didn't know how to perform a sacrifice at all. Lord Changping’s suggestion was clearly meant to make things difficult, and what made Wei Liao even more dissatisfied was that the King of Qin didn't stop it at all. If the King of Qin didn't allow it, who would dare to let Xu Fu perform a sacrifice?

The ministers didn't dare to answer casually at this moment.

Sacrifice was a custom passed down from ancient times, and many people held it in awe. Now that they were in a time of crisis, did they dare to say sacrifice was useless?
