In the blink of an eye, they were almost at Sanchuan Commandery.

Since then, Xu Fu had never seen that woman again, and he had no interest in asking. Along the way, there were no more traces of those assassins.

At this time, the cost of preparing countless assassins and killing across regions was quite high. If the first strike failed, it would be difficult to find another opportunity later. Furthermore, General Huan Yi was pressing the State of Zhao step by step, and Zhao was currently too preoccupied to play such underhanded tricks. As for the monarchs of other states, they didn't even know where Ying Zheng was at this moment, so how could they send people to assassinate him?

Once they entered Sanchuan Commandery, those people naturally had no more chances.

Ever since Ying Zheng encountered an assassination on the road from Sanchuan back to Xianyang last time, his control over the territory within Qin had become much stricter.

The carriage stopped outside the seat of Sanchuan Commandery. Gan Tang lifted the curtain and jumped down. After being inspected by the soldiers, they soon entered the city.

The city inevitably still held a sense of desolation; after all, it had only been half a year since the drought ended. It would take some time for Sanchuan to fully recover to its former appearance.

However, Xu Fu noticed that there was no longer a look of gloom on the faces of the people.

It seemed that since Liu Zixun became the governor of Sanchuan, there had been some improvement.

No one in Sanchuan Commandery knew of Ying Zheng's visit. However, because their group was slightly large, they still attracted quite a few gazes after entering the city.

Gan Tang and An Niang went to find an inn to stay at.

The only reason An Niang hadn't left them was because Hu Hai craved her cooking. Bringing one more person wasn't a bother, so Ying Zheng agreed without hesitation.

Xu Fu sat in the carriage with Ying Zheng, moving along slowly.

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain to look outside.

He felt quite satisfied in his heart; after all, he and Ying Zheng had contributed to saving this place.

Before they knew it, they arrived outside an inn. They stepped out of the carriage. The people at the inn rarely saw such figures. Upon seeing Xu Fu, they only felt he was handsome and stunning, as if they had seen him somewhere before, but they simply couldn't remember where.

Xu Fu nodded at them, then walked into the building with Ying Zheng with an indifferent expression.

In the lobby of the inn, someone scratched their head, "Hey, why do I feel like those two look very much like the King and that... that Fengchang who came to Sanchuan before?"

Someone next to him heard this and immediately sneered, "What nonsense are you spouting? How could the King be seen here? The King should be in Xianyang right now! Our Great Qin is currently attacking Zhao, why would the King come to Sanchuan for no reason? Even if the King did come, he would stay at the Governor's Mansion, not this humble place of ours!"

"What you say makes sense..."

The two lowered their heads and chatted for a while, and before long, the topic shifted elsewhere.

Thinking about it, it was true. Sometimes, when the truth is placed right in front of you, you don't dare to believe it. This is what is called "the darkest place is under the lamp."

Even though Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were so ostentatious, no one believed they were the figures who should be sitting in the Xianyang Palace.

After entering the room, Xu Fu immediately sat down at the table. If he weren't waiting for the attendant to return and report, he would have collapsed onto the bed regardless of his image.

Just as he was thinking this, an attendant came to knock on the door.

"The mother and daughter that the Master ordered me to ask about..."

"How are they?"

"Both survived. Governor Liu Zixun found them a place to live in the city. Now, the woman is making a living by helping people sell things in the city. Life is actually quite good."

Upon hearing this, Xu Fu felt much more cheerful.

Without the scumbag, and with the epidemic cured, the mother and daughter could leave that small village, so their life was naturally good!

"What about the two men I ordered to be buried when I left?" Xu Fu asked again. He believed in seeing things through to the end; since he had ordered those two scumbags to be buried, he naturally had to ask if they were dead for sure.

The attendant frowned and said, "I haven't heard any news about them, but someone did go to that village to ask."

Xu Fu nodded.

Ying Zheng waved the attendant away and was about to wash up and rest with Xu Fu when Hu Hai burst in barefoot, followed by a Fusu who looked like he had lost all hope.

Seeing Hu Hai use all his strength to push the door open, Ying Zheng felt a mix of amusement and anger.

Hu Hai's face was flushed red. While rubbing his little belly, he looked at Xu Fu with watery eyes, "Hungry, Father, so hungry..."

Xu Fu's concept of family was relatively shallow. Compared to Hu Hai and Fusu, he had to say that Ying Zheng was more important. If Ying Zheng didn't want to be disturbed, Xu Fu wouldn't necessarily tolerate Hu Hai interrupting their rest time either.

Xu Fu directed Fusu without any guilt, "Take him to find An Niang."

Upon hearing the name "An Niang," even if Hu Hai couldn't remember her face, he at least remembered the smell of the food in her hands.

Fusu helplessly apologized to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, then led Hu Hai out.

After Xu Fu and Ying Zheng lay down on the bed, he thought to himself with a clear conscience.

The cultivation of brotherly love starts with small things.

Seeing how good Fusu is to Hu Hai now, would Hu Hai still think about killing his brother when he grows up? Although Xu Fu felt that Hu Hai might still think about killing his father. But what kind of person was Ying Zheng? Xu Fu wasn't worried about that at all.

Sleeping until dawn, Xu Fu finally felt refreshed.

After getting up and washing, a waiter soon brought food. Hu Hai followed the aroma of the food and snuck in, swallowing his saliva while whispering, "Last night, Brother Gan Tang, like this... like this... and An Niang like this..."

Xu Fu: "...What like this and like this?"

So the Second Emperor of Qin loved gossip when he was a child?

"It's like Father to Father, like this, like this..." Hu Hai held up his chubby, soft fingers and pointed them forward, the rounded tips touching each other.

Hu Hai's words made Ying Zheng find it quite amusing.

Ying Zheng rested his forehead on one hand and smiled at Hu Hai, "Is it kissing?"

Hu Hai frowned and thought for a while, "Like, like the way Brother kisses me."

As soon as he finished speaking, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng looked at Fusu in surprise at the same time.

Fusu was completely bewildered.

"I, I, I haven't done anything..." Fusu was on the verge of tears, "When Hu Hai was young, he loved to rub against my face after drinking milk. During the time I was sick, I drank medicine, and Hu Hai saw it and thought it was delicious, so he insisted on licking the medicine from my mouth..."

Xu Fu's gaze became even more bizarre.

Fusu felt that the more he explained, the worse it got, so he simply shut his mouth. He wanted to glare at Hu Hai, but seeing his innocent and naive expression, Fusu felt like vomiting blood. He could only curse in his heart that he and Hu Hai were truly born enemies!

So it was the young Hu Hai who had forced himself on Fusu.

Xu Fu cast a subtle, apologetic look at Fusu. It was indeed hard on him...

Hu Hai's shocking words were set aside for now, but after they finished their meal and just stepped out of the room, Xu Fu noticed something wrong with the atmosphere.

Gan Tang's expression was usually cold, looking like a piece of wood, albeit a good-looking piece of wood.

Today, he was pulling a long face, and there was a sense of listlessness between his brows.

Xu Fu soon heard the gossip about Gan Tang from Yao Jia.

He had fallen in love with An Niang.

So what Hu Hai said wasn't really a lie...

An Niang was more than ten years older than Gan Tang. In ancient times, this wasn't a pairing everyone could accept. Gan Tang's personality was unrestrained; in less than half a month, he could develop feelings for someone. But one only had to think a little about the life An Niang had lived before to know that she certainly didn't have much trust in Gan Tang.

For a woman like An Niang, love and men were probably dispensable things.

Therefore, the reason Gan Tang was in this state now was likely because his pursuit of love had been thwarted.

When Yao Jia was telling this gossip, Ying Zheng was also on the side.

It was clearly such gossip, but coming from Yao Jia's mouth, it didn't seem vulgar at all; instead, it was very natural, as if he were narrating ordinary events.

He didn't even have a shred of shame on his face for reporting gossip.

After hearing these words, a strange sense of pride rose in Ying Zheng's heart.

Gan Tang was completely incomparable to him. He had easily (after experiencing many hardships) lured Xu Fu into bed.

As expected, he couldn't compare to me...

Xu Fu told Yao Jia to step down, just pondering whether to show some concern for Gan Tang's love life, when not long after, he heard someone say that An Niang had returned to the inn and was preparing to bid everyone farewell.

Gan Tang ran over without stopping.

And Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, with a tiny bit of mischief, followed.

An Niang stepped into the lobby. At this time, apart from their group, there was no one else in the lobby. Therefore, the person following An Niang was very conspicuous.

When Xu Fu looked, he discovered that he actually recognized the person.

Wasn't that the woman from the mother-daughter pair? Why would she come with An Niang?

Because Sang Zhong and Jian Jia were not brought this time, the woman looked around and saw only strangers, so she didn't know that her benefactors had already arrived in Sanchuan and were watching them from upstairs.

Gan Tang and An Niang went to talk alone on the other side. Because he couldn't hear or see anything clearly, Xu Fu felt it was meaningless.

However, some attendants noticed the clues and whispered, "An Niang wouldn't be willing to marry. Maybe she's going to stay in the city with this woman..."

"Yeah, yeah, Gan Tang falling for a woman so much older than him, I really don't understand..."

"Perhaps An Niang feels their statuses aren't equal. If I were to fall in love with a woman in the future, and that woman was much more outstanding than me, I probably wouldn't dare to be with her either..."

As Xu Fu listened, he couldn't help but whisper, "Ah Zheng and I are quite equal."

The attendants behind him who had accidentally overheard this were all shocked at the same time.

Huh?

Equal to the King?

This...

Did Fengchang Xu exaggerate a little too much...

The attendants didn't expect their King to nod slightly, his voice low and powerful, "Ah Fu is right."

Attendants: ???

What was right about it?

Just as the attendants were exchanging glances, Gantang and Anniang seemed to have fallen into an argument. Their voices rose sharply, and some words drifted into Xu Fu’s ears.

Anniang’s attitude was firm, but Gantang’s voice was even more resolute. Neither could convince the other, and Anniang, frustrated, scolded: "How can one force matters of the heart? I have no intentions toward you; if I were to easily submit, wouldn't that be harming you instead?"

Ying Zheng also heard this, and his expression suddenly darkened.

Xu Fu’s gaze shifted slightly, catching the strange look on Ying Zheng’s face. Xu Fu was completely baffled—could one really gain such profound insights just from watching gossip? He had completely forgotten that, in the beginning, he and Ying Zheng hadn't exactly shared mutual affection either, yet they had just ended up together anyway.

After a while, the voices of Anniang and Gantang gradually faded.

When Gantang walked out again, his wooden face held a mix of frustration and stubbornness. These two emotions intertwined, giving him an appearance that was both pitiful and amusing. However, Xu Fu felt that his expression revealed the most intuitive truth: he was simply too young, and even in moments like this, his reactions were naive.

For Anniang, she likely didn't care for a man like him. She had suffered so much in the past; looking at her now, she probably just wanted a simple, ordinary life. Moreover, Gantang hadn't thought things through. Anniang was a citizen of Zhao, and although she had followed him to the Qin state without complaint, Gantang was a servant in the Xianyang Palace. Could Anniang really live with him in Xianyang? Such problems couldn't be solved by a single word like "like."

Anniang followed closely behind and bowed to the other attendants, saying, "Anniang requests to see Master Xu."

The attendants exchanged glances and hurried upstairs to report.

Xu Fu guessed that she might want to settle down in Sanchuan, and that her request to see him was likely to bid farewell.

Xu Fu tugged on Ying Zheng’s sleeve to bring him back to his senses so they could go downstairs together.

Ying Zheng put away his previous expression and walked downstairs with Xu Fu. Hearing footsteps, the woman standing behind Anniang looked up in the direction of Xu Fu. A flash of shock, gratitude, and joy crossed her face. Perhaps the impact was too great, for she stepped forward in excitement and nearly tripped right in front of Xu Fu.

Anniang caught her just in time, looking back and forth between her and Xu Fu with surprise.

Xu Fu looked at the woman’s face; a sense of familiarity was still etched in his mind, but embarrassingly, he couldn't quite recall her name.

Anniang spoke up: "Master, thank you for saving me, and thank you for setting aside all else to allow me to follow everyone to Sanchuan. Your great kindness is something I may never be able to repay in this lifetime..."

Hearing Anniang’s words, the woman beside her also trembled slightly with excitement.

Back then, hadn't she been just like Anniang? It was a pity, though; her own strength was meager, and the Master seemed to lack nothing. How could she repay such kindness? She could only keep it locked in her heart and pray for him every day.

Xu Fu nodded slightly upon hearing this.

Anniang calmed her excitement a little, took a deep breath, and said, "Anniang had intended to serve you in the future to repay your kindness." Before she could finish, Ying Zheng’s icy gaze was already fixed upon her.

Anniang shivered involuntarily and immediately skipped over that part, stating her purpose for today: "But after careful consideration, I realized that you surely do not lack people to serve you. And from the bottom of my heart, I also wish to live a free and simple life. After getting to know Yingniang of Sanchuan Commandery, I want to open a small shop with her to sell some trinkets. To spend the rest of my life this way would be the greatest blessing. When you leave this place, Anniang will no longer follow you."

Oh, right, this woman’s name was Yingniang... Xu Fu finally remembered her name from Anniang’s words.

Because Xu Fu had long anticipated Anniang’s thoughts, he wasn't surprised to hear this and nodded immediately: "You are a free person; if you think it is good, then stay."

Anniang nodded heavily. Xu Fu’s short sentence made her finally feel that she was truly free, no longer bound by anything, and she couldn't help but tear up. Fusu seemed to have heard the commotion downstairs and came pattering down, looking left and right before asking cautiously: "Anniang, are you leaving?"

Anniang nodded.

Fuhai looked as if he had suffered a devastating blow, stuttering as he looked at Xu Fu: "Fa-father... are you... leaving? The delicious food..."

It turned out that in his mind, Anniang was practically synonymous with food.

The attendants couldn't help but stifle their laughter.

Yingniang, however, looked at Fuhai with some surprise. Perhaps it was because Xu Fu looked so young that he didn't seem like someone who would have a son so early.

Ying Zheng thought Fuhai’s behavior was truly pathetic; did he look like a member of the Qin royal family at all? But then, considering that the boy wasn't his own flesh and blood, Ying Zheng didn't know whether to laugh or be annoyed. Fuhai was currently in the Qin palace, and he was indeed losing face for the royal family, but if he remained this foolish his whole life, he could at least be a safe little brother for Fusu, which was somewhat reassuring.

Xu Fu’s gaze lowered, sweeping over Fuhai’s small face, and then he raised his hand and expressionlessly wiped from the top of his head all the way to his chin.

Fuhai’s hair immediately flopped down over his face.

Xu Fu’s comforting gesture was a bit rough, but Fuhai was a simpleton; feeling comforted, he immediately hugged Xu Fu’s arm, rubbed against it, and then pretended not to care: "Then... you go..."

Anniang smiled, and just as she was about to pull Yingniang away to take her leave, Yingniang stepped forward and bowed gracefully: "I never thought I would see you again, Master."

Anniang shivered, finding the look between the two of them rather strange.

Ying Zheng’s expression also darkened. It wasn't that he disliked Yingniang, but he was annoyed by Anniang’s wild imagination. Besides himself, who else could Xu Fu have a relationship with?

"Your daughter..."

"She survived as well, and she still remembers the two breaths of 'immortal energy' you gave us."

Immortal energy? What immortal energy? Anniang was even more confused. The words were simple enough to understand, but when put together, why couldn't she grasp the meaning?

The attendants, however, were long accustomed to this and instead looked at Xu Fu with worship. Ah, as expected of Master Xu, he could even find immortal energy... It was truly a great blessing for the Qin state to have such a living immortal! The attendants’ minds were already filled with images of other nations burning with jealousy. Thinking of this, they felt a small sense of pride.

Seeing that Yingniang was living well, Xu Fu had nothing left to worry about, though he still asked a few questions about the current Governor of Sanchuan.

Anniang, listening from the side, became increasingly alarmed.

Who could inquire about the Governor of Sanchuan in such a casual tone? Could it be... could he be the King of Qin! No, that wasn't right; the King of Qin should be older than this man’s appearance. Anniang never imagined that Ying Zheng was standing behind Xu Fu, because Ying Zheng had been so indulgent toward Xu Fu throughout the journey. That overly doting posture was obvious to anyone with eyes. How could Anniang have guessed that such a person, even as the King of Qin, could bow his head and bend his knees in front of his beloved?

It wasn't just Anniang who found it unbelievable; even if this were told to others, no one would dare to believe it.

Even for Lord Longyang, who had ever seen the King of Wei act in such a manner before him?

Only those who were often by Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s side, like these attendants, didn't feel that anything was amiss.

"...Then this Liu Zixun is not bad." Xu Fu calmly brought the conversation to a close.

Yingniang hesitated: "Then Master, will you not see the Governor?" As she spoke, she couldn't help but look at Ying Zheng. She had only heard later how extraordinary the backgrounds of these two were. One was the King of Qin, the other was the Fengchang of Xianyang. People like them were usually ones she would never have a chance to meet in a lifetime.

"No need." Ying Zheng cut her off directly. He paused, then added: "Back then, you and your daughter only had a chance to be treated because of Xu Fu. Now, Xu Fu has merely come to take a look, to see if the good deed he performed on a whim has yielded a satisfactory result."

Even though Ying Zheng used the words "on a whim," the more he said so, the more excited Yingniang became.

Only someone like the Master could treat such great kindness as a casual act, and only such a person could be considered a true saint!

Yingniang smiled: "Master, you probably don't know, but in Sanchuan Commandery, the Governor is currently having a statue of you sculpted."

Why were the ancients so fond of sculpting statues?

Xu Fu felt a bit embarrassed. If the statues in all the places he had visited looked different, that would be quite funny.

Ying Zheng’s expression softened significantly. If it were before, he would never have imagined that someone within his borders would build a statue not for him, yet he would feel immensely happy and honored by it.

It was precisely because Ying Zheng had guessed that Sanchuan Commandery would do this that he had brought Xu Fu to see it. Xu Fu sowed seeds of kindness everywhere; in a few years, his name would likely be known throughout the world. Even if he still revealed little of his own name, people weren't stupid. With a "Master Xu" everywhere, and once the reputation of the Qin Fengchang Xu Fu spread, combined with his background of coming from Guigu and possessing divine arts, how could people not know that this "mysterious" Master Xu was the Qin state’s Xu Fu?

Although Ying Zheng had always looked down on fame, he had to admit that if one had a good reputation—or rather, a reputation that reached a terrifying level—it would only benefit Xu Fu, not harm him. Even if Xu Fu were to pursue the path of longevity in the future and his life continued while he himself passed away, without his protection, Xu Fu would still be able to stand gracefully in the world.

Ying Zheng hadn't even realized how far into the future he had thought...

Xu Fu seemed to sense something and turned back to look at him.

Xu Fu couldn't guess what Ying Zheng was thinking. Just now, Ying Zheng’s gaze had been too intense; perhaps... was his profile too charming?

"If you want to see that statue, we can go together..." Ying Zheng suggested.

"No, no need." Xu Fu emphasized his tone.

If the statue turned out to be too ugly, should he laugh or cry?

It was better to let it maintain a sense of mystery in his mind. He hoped that thousands of years later, when future generations unearthed his statue, they wouldn't print it in textbooks. At the thought of the portrait of Qin Shi Huang in history books, Xu Fu’s heart trembled.

As long as it was Xu Fu’s wish, Ying Zheng would not oppose it. Since he refused, they wouldn't go.

Yingniang felt a bit disappointed, but at the same time, her worship of Xu Fu deepened. To be so indifferent to fame and wealth—what a detached state of mind! In this world, who else could possess it?

"In that case, Anniang, you may go with her." Ying Zheng spoke, signaling that it was time for them to leave.

The others immediately realized they had been intruding for quite a while and quickly exited.

Xu Fu looked back in the direction of Gantang, seeing his face tightly set, even more wooden than his usual wooden face. Some colleagues stepped forward to pull Gantang aside to comfort him.

Ying Zheng noticed his gaze and couldn't help but whisper: "If one is together without affection, is it unbearable for people?"

"It depends on the person." Xu Fu answered instinctively, but then his mind suddenly cleared. He couldn't help but turn to look at Ying Zheng: "Is it unbearable for you to be with me?" After saying this, Xu Fu couldn't help but frown. It had been so long, and he hadn't seen him suffering! And weren't they just long-term bed partners? Why elevate it to the level of being unbearable? Truly strange!

Ying Zheng was stunned upon hearing this.

Shouldn't this sentence be what he said to Xu Fu? Was this reversed?

"Naturally not." Although Ying Zheng didn't know why Xu Fu had reversed the words, he keenly knew that if he didn't deny it quickly, there would definitely be trouble.

The coldness on Xu Fu’s face weakened instantly, and he nodded with satisfaction, unconsciously lifting his chin. Seeing Xu Fu like this, Ying Zheng’s heart nearly melted into a puddle. What affection, what suffering—all of it was crumpled up and shoved to the bottom of his heart, not to be pulled out easily. With Xu Fu looking like this, even if there were no affection, even if it were unbearable, could he bear to let go? Ying Zheng felt he had been thinking too much.

If Xu Fu knew what Ying Zheng was thinking, he might even let out a long sigh of relief.

Ah, this was the normal style of Qin Shi Huang.

Whatever he wanted, he had to hold in his hand; who cared about anything else?

Seeing Ying Zheng remain silent for a long time, Xu Fu examined his expression and, after a moment of hesitation, added: "You and I are different from Anniang and Gantang."

Xu Fu originally meant that their relationship was different.

However, Ying Zheng nodded inwardly. Not bad; at least he held Xu Fu in his arms, while Gantang was too useless, unable to chase after Anniang no matter what.

Ying Zheng met Xu Fu’s gaze, which lacked the indifference he showed others. Perhaps even Xu Fu himself hadn't realized that his gaze was gentle and relaxed. Ying Zheng’s heart was immediately soothed. Xu Fu must have sensed his displeasure and was comforting him...

Ying Zheng, having overthought it, happily took Xu Fu back to their room to engage in "adult" activities.

Gantang, on the other side, felt pained and sad for the romance he hadn't even had a chance to start. When he finally recovered his state, only to discover his masters were "tossing and turning," the stimulated Gantang felt even more pained and sad...

Neither Xu Fu nor Ying Zheng wished to stay long in Sanchuan Commandery. They spent two days experiencing what the commandery was like under the new governor, then set off to leave. Gantang, with his broken young heart, was naturally overjoyed; at least he could leave this place of heartbreak...

As the group left the city, Gantang suddenly pointed in one direction and frowned: "What is that?"

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain and followed his gaze. Ying Zheng also leaned against Xu Fu’s shoulder to look out.

Xu Fu only took one look, and his expression turned even colder.

He never expected that the statue he was determined to avoid would be forced upon his view.

The statues were erected in a highly conspicuous position outside the city. Anyone entering the city could see them at a glance, showing that Sanchuan Commandery regarded these statues as the pride of the region. But Xu Fu felt they weren't worth being proud of at all...

The statues outside the city were positioned left and right.

The one on the left was tall and sturdy, with facial features blurred and unrecognizable; the one on the right was tall and slender, with facial features equally blurred and unrecognizable.

But looking at their attire, Xu Fu felt it was extremely discordant. The one on the left was majestic, while the one on the right had a temperament that was... gentle? If one didn't know better, they might think the statue on the right was a woman.

Xu Fu guessed almost immediately that these two statues were likely Ying Zheng on the left and himself on the right. Why was Ying Zheng’s statue so heroic, while his own was so cowardly?

The attendants’ mouths twitched repeatedly at the sight, thinking to themselves that it was no wonder Master Xu didn't want to see the statues. These statues didn't even capture one ten-thousandth of Master Xu’s presence. If they hadn't heard Yingniang mention it, they probably wouldn't have recognized them even if they saw them.

These two statues were likely not yet fully completed, as craftsmen soon came out of the city to continue carving around them. Xu Fu watched as several hands touched and poked at his statue, his expression growing colder and colder. Finally, unable to watch any longer, he let go of the curtain and said coldly: "Let's go."

Ying Zheng’s face was also dark as water, signaling the group to continue forward.

Gantang, who had caused Xu Fu to feel so displeased by pointing out the statues, suddenly realized he was receiving several looks of disdain.

Gantang felt a sense of bewilderment: What did I do???

·

Although Fuhai and Fusu were young, they were better at enduring hardship than Xu Fu. By the time Xu Fu realized he had become accustomed to a comfortable life and was unwilling to endure even the slightest hardship, it was already too late.

Ying Zheng had spoiled him into this state; surely there wasn't some hidden agenda, right?

Xu Fu leaned in Ying Zheng’s arms, suppressing the urge to yawn and the fatigue on his face, and asked in a low voice: "Are we not there yet?"

Ying Zheng also felt a pang of heartache: "We should be close; we have already entered the Shu region." This journey was exhausting and truly too much for Xu Fu.

Xu Fu said "Hmm," his head lowered, his expression unclear.

But in reality, he was feeling melancholy.

In his past life, he was someone who could easily enter the deep mountains; he could handle these hardships with ease. But in this life, he couldn't endure them at all! Was it because he had suffered enough in his past life, so he should enjoy himself to the fullest in this one?

As Xu Fu’s thoughts drifted, he heard someone outside call out: "Master, it is time to get off the carriage." Because Ying Zheng was outside, it was inconvenient to use formal titles, so the attendants mostly just called out to Xu Fu directly, and Ying Zheng usually didn't get angry. The attendants gradually got used to it.

Xu Fu was helped off the carriage by Ying Zheng. They abandoned the carriage and horses, found a place to store them, and then began to climb over the mountains.

Gantang led the way with his head down, while Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walked behind, chatting from time to time, which invisibly dissipated some of the fatigue.

But as they walked, Xu Fu always felt something was wrong. Although it had rained when he came to Shu last time and his vision had been blurred, he always felt that this didn't seem to be the same road...

"Gantang, did you take the wrong road?" Xu Fu stopped and asked.

Gantang looked around: "It’s correct."

The other attendants had never been here, so they naturally didn't know the way. Ying Zheng frowned: "It seems... this is indeed not the road." He had been talking with Xu Fu the whole time and hadn't noticed where Gantang was leading them.

Hearing Ying Zheng say this, Gantang could no longer maintain his composure: "This... please forgive me, Master." Gantang turned around and knelt down in front of Ying Zheng with a thud.

Ying Zheng didn't look at him, but looked up at the sky: "It is getting late, let us find a place to rest first."

Yao Jia stepped forward consciously to invite Xu Fu: "I know of a village nearby." During these days, Yao Jia had confirmed Ying Zheng’s identity, and now, serving as a servant for Xu Fu, he was naturally even more convinced and submissive.

"A village?" The image of a mountain stronghold immediately popped into Xu Fu’s mind.

Ying Zheng’s focus wasn't on this; he looked at Yao Jia with surprise and asked: "How do you know there is a village here?"

"The Shu region has many Di and Qiang people; it is very common to have villages on the mountainsides," Yao Jia replied respectfully, bowing his body.

"Then do you know the way?" Ying Zheng asked.

Xu Fu looked around: "Yao Jia, do you see it over there?" Xu Fu suddenly pointed in one direction.

Everyone immediately looked in the direction he pointed.

But they saw nothing.

"Look carefully, what is that?" Xu Fu said with great patience.

The attendants felt a strange chill in their hearts. Could it be that Master Xu could see things they couldn't? Thinking of this, everyone shivered.

Ying Zheng’s thinking was at least on the same wavelength as Xu Fu’s. He looked carefully for a while and finally saw it: on a path they had passed, extending out, it looked like a cliff, but in reality, there was a rope bridge made of bamboo and wooden planks, which didn't look very sturdy. However, Ying Zheng was puzzled: why did this prove that it was a village of the Di and Qiang people?

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng exchanged glances, secretly pleased that Ying Zheng could "communicate" with him. He knew Ying Zheng had seen it too, so he immediately explained: "I have heard that the places where the Qiang people live are often high mountains and dangerous waters, so they are accustomed to making rope bridges to barely pass through." After a pause, he pointed in that direction again: "Look, hidden in the mountain forest, there are high towers."

To be able to build such high houses at this time was truly remarkable.

Xu Fu vaguely remembered that these should be the watchtowers of the Di and Qiang tribes, usually built next to houses in the village. If there were no people here, why would they build watchtowers?

By comparison, Xu Fu was more worried about another point. Would this place be xenophobic? After all, thousands of years ago, because such places were in the deep mountains, they rarely interacted with the outside world. Sometimes, not only was language a problem, but they might not accept strangers coming into the village.

Yao Jia seemed to sense Xu Fu’s thoughts and looked at him: "I have seen relevant records in bamboo slips; the Di and Qiang people worship white stones."

Xu Fu’s memory was also triggered: "That’s right. White stones are sparkling and symbolize gods among the Qiang people."

Yao Jia smiled slightly, delivering a compliment seamlessly: "With a figure like you, Master, if you enter the village, you will probably be treated as an immortal immediately."

In summary, his meaning was probably that Xu Fu’s temperament was quite like a white stone.

Xu Fu’s mouth twitched slightly. He didn't dare to be so arrogant. However, in this wilderness, no matter what, they would only know the result after trying. He looked at Ying Zheng, who received his gaze and immediately ordered everyone to return along the path and cross the rope bridge to explore.

There was indeed a small cliff under the rope bridge, but it didn't look very deep, as they were only at the mountainside. However, for someone with a fear of heights, just one look down might be enough to scare them to death.

At this time, the mountains were cool, and mist was gradually drifting across the mountainside. To Xu Fu, walking on the rope bridge felt like being in a fairyland among the clouds.

Xu Fu was about to walk up fearlessly, but Ying Zheng’s heart jumped with terror at the sight, and he quickly reached out to grab him back.

Yao Jia consciously stepped forward to be the pioneer. Having been with them for a long time, Yao Jia wasn't stupid; he naturally saw the relationship between Ying Zheng and Xu Fu. Since Ying Zheng couldn't bear for Xu Fu to go first, he would go instead. Yao Jia didn't consider himself unlucky enough to lose his life just by walking across a rope bridge.

Yao Jia walked across easily.

Xu Fu was about to go up again, but Ying Zheng’s brows were tightly locked, and he reached out and grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist with some roughness.

His palm was scorching hot, and Xu Fu couldn't help but rub against it, then grabbed the back of Ying Zheng’s hand and walked forward with him. The narrow rope bridge was crowded by the two of them, but there was a strange sense of balance that reduced the vibration of the bridge.

Xu Fu held the back of Ying Zheng’s hand, rubbing it from time to time, earnestly expressing his intention to comfort him. Ah, so Qin Shi Huang was also afraid of walking on rope bridges...

Ying Zheng, who was entirely focused on Xu Fu’s safety and full of assumptions about what would happen if the rope bridge broke, had no idea that his image in Xu Fu’s mind had been distorted.

It didn't take long for them all to reach the other side. The road ahead was not easy to walk; it was right against the edge of the cliff, and perhaps a moment of carelessness could lead to a fall. However, for the seasoned attendants, this was nothing. Only Ying Zheng was somewhat dissatisfied.

The road was so narrow that he naturally couldn't walk side-by-side with Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was broad-minded and didn't care about this, walking in front first. Ying Zheng’s face darkened, looking displeased. In his eyes, Xu Fu’s actions were a bit reckless, but... but there was no other way. Was Xu Fu supposed to stay there and not move? Naturally, that was impossible!

Xu Fu keenly sensed the emotion on Ying Zheng and, without looking back, touched the cliff wall and said: "A-Zheng always walks in front for me; occasionally, you should let me walk in front."

Ying Zheng was suddenly moved.

Xu Fu meant that he always shielded him from the wind and rain, so this time he would also walk in front to shield him from the wind and rain.

Ying Zheng didn't even think about the fact that it was just walking on a mountain road; what kind of wind and rain could one shield?

Anyway, he was very moved.

Because the mountain road was indeed dangerous, they didn't take the time to show affection, just holding hands and walking forward.

After rounding a cliff, the view in front suddenly opened up.

This path was much wider...

After walking up, Xu Fu felt his heart slowly settle back down. The fatigue from the carriage had vanished because he had concentrated for so long. Xu Fu was very satisfied; it seemed his ability to climb mountains hadn't disappeared completely.

Ying Zheng followed closely and grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist again.

Yao Jia walked quickly in front, leading the group into the forest. Soon after, they saw the watchtowers. There were no guards under the towers, suggesting that almost no one came this way, so the people here had no defensive mindset.

However, as they got closer, the people in the village immediately noticed them.

Someone walked out and said something in a gibberish language.

Xu Fu examined the people in front of him carefully. Their clothing was far from the exquisite beauty of later generations, but they already had a very distinct ethnic style, embroidered with patterns and lines that looked somewhat like animals.

Xu Fu vaguely remembered that the ancient Qiang people seemed to worship animal totems, so it wasn't strange for their clothing to have such patterns. As for the Di tribe, Xu Fu didn't know much, and he rarely heard of them in later generations. He didn't know if the people in this village were Di or Qiang, or both.

The man’s gaze swept over them, full of caution and surprise.

However, when the man’s gaze fell on Xu Fu, his expression changed drastically, and he ran back inside, babbling. The other party was probably speaking a local dialect, which was troublesome. Xu Fu guessed he might not understand a single word. Writing things down wasn't reliable either; it was said that the ancient Qiang people had no written language, and everything was passed down orally. Who knew if they recognized seal script?

Just as Xu Fu was pondering, a large group of people suddenly surged out of the village.

The people behind Xu Fu and Ying Zheng couldn't help but swallow hard.

Only the three of them and Yao Jia remained exceptionally calm. Oh, perhaps one should add Gantang, who was so heartbroken over leading them the wrong way that his perception of external danger had become dull.

The attendants suddenly heightened their vigilance, ready for battle.

But the other party pointed at Xu Fu and started whispering as if no one else was there.

Immediately after, a little girl ran out of the crowd, pointed at Xu Fu, then pointed inside the village, and said in a very awkward Shu dialect: "Come in."

Xu Fu was full of confusion. Why did these people have such a strange reaction when they saw him?

Xu Fu lifted his foot to follow, but Ying Zheng grabbed him: "These people are difficult to communicate with, and they look fierce..."

Xu Fu "Hmm"ed and whispered: "I don't think they look fierce; perhaps it’s just an expression the locals are accustomed to? Look at that little girl; she isn't like that, she smiles very sweetly."

Hearing the second half of the sentence, Ying Zheng became even angrier.

Still smiling sweetly???

Xu Fu started walking inside again, not forgetting to reach out and grab Ying Zheng’s palm: "Trust me, it’s fine."

With Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walking inside, the others naturally had no objections and followed immediately.

The group walked in majestically, and the further they went, the more Xu Fu couldn't help but marvel.

This place was truly beautiful!

They used natural materials to build houses, including watchtowers and flat houses. Some were made of bamboo and wood, but more were built of stone. In this era of backward construction, the fact that they could build small three-story houses was truly amazing.

There were some stones placed on these buildings. Xu Fu scanned them roughly and found that there were five stones on top of each, which probably had some fixed symbolic meaning. Xu Fu guessed that these must be the white stones Yao Jia mentioned.

Along the way, they could see many totems in the village. At first glance, it made people feel that their beliefs were a bit chaotic.

However, Xu Fu remembered that this seemed to be a local characteristic.

After walking for a while, Xu Fu vaguely heard someone call the little girl "A-Yi," which sounded like a modal particle. Xu Fu heard it many times before he dared to confirm it.

A-Yi suddenly turned back, looked at Xu Fu, and gave him a sweet smile, saying in a strained voice: "Here, you, want, it..."

Xu Fu looked over and saw a small field where some plants were being cultivated, and those plants had small brown fruits hanging from them. However, Xu Fu knew very well that those weren't fruits. Smelling the fragrant, numbing scent, Xu Fu quickly guessed what they were.

...It was Sichuan peppercorn.

Xu Fu reined in his excited thoughts.

That’s not right...

Why did this little girl say to him, "Here, you, want, it"?

就在侍从们互相对视的那一瞬间，甘棠似乎和安娘发生了争吵，他们的声音陡然拔高，有些字词顺着飘进了徐福的耳朵里。
安娘态度坚决，甘棠的声音却比她更坚决，二人谁也说服不了谁，气得安娘骂道：“感情一事如何强求？我本无意于你，若是轻易顺从，岂非反倒害了你？”
嬴政也听见了这么一句话，突然间面色沉了沉。
徐福的目光微微一偏，便能瞥见嬴政脸上怪异的神色。徐福一头雾水，看个八卦，还能看出什么感触来么？徐福倒是全然忘记了，当初他同嬴政也谈不上互通情意，随后便凑合着在一起了。
过了会儿，安娘和甘棠的声音渐渐小了。
等甘棠再走出来的时候，木头脸上多了点沮丧和执拗，两种情绪交错在一起，给人一种又可怜又好笑的感觉。不过徐福觉得，他这模样容易带给人最直观的感受，那就是他太年轻了，就连这样的时候，反应都是稚嫩的。
对于安娘来说，应当并不喜欢他这模样的男子。她从前吃了那么多苦，瞧她如今的模样，应当也只想要过过平凡的生活便足以。何况甘棠也的确考虑不周，安娘为赵国人，尽管她跟着来到秦国，并无二话，但甘棠是在咸阳宫中当差的人，安娘能跟着他一起住在咸阳吗？种种问题，倒不是一句“喜欢”能便能解决的。
安娘紧跟着走出来，朝其余侍从躬身道：“安娘求见徐先生。”
侍从们对视一眼，忙上楼来禀报。
徐福猜测她说不定是想要就此定居在三川，她要见自己，应当就是为了辞别。
徐福拉了拉嬴政的袖子，让嬴政回过神来，好同自己一起下楼去。
嬴政收起面上的神色，和徐福一起往楼下走。因为听见了脚步声的缘故，立在安娘身后的女子迎着徐福下来的方向，抬起了头，女子脸上很快闪过了震惊、感激、欣喜等不同的情绪，许是一时间带来的冲击太大，她激动地往前走了走，结果差点扑倒在徐福的跟前。
还是安娘一把抓住了她，惊讶地在她和徐福身上来回打量。
徐福看着女子的面孔，熟悉感还印在脑子里，不过窘迫的是，徐福不大记得起对方的名字了。
安娘出声道：“先生，多谢先生救助了我，也多谢先生不计其它，同意了我跟着大家来到三川。先生的大恩，安娘这辈子或许都无法回报了……”
旁边的女子听见安娘的话，身子也因为激动而微微颤抖了起来。
当初，她何尝不是与安娘一样的呢？只是可惜了，她毕竟力量微薄，而对方似乎又什么也不缺，自己又能如何报恩呢？她便只能将此事牢记心中，日日为对方祈福了。
徐福闻言，只微微点头。
安娘稍微平复了些激动的情绪，随后深吸一口气，道：“安娘本欲想着日后伺候先生来报恩。”还不等她说完，嬴政冰冷的目光已经投到她身上去了。
安娘不自觉地打了个哆嗦，马上将这句话给揭过，道出自己今日的目的，“但安娘细细思考过后，想到先生身边应当也并不缺伺候的人。而从心底来讲，安娘也希望自己能过上自由平淡的生活。我与三川郡的英娘认识后，便想跟她一同，开个小铺子，卖些小玩意儿，余生如此度过，已经是最大的幸事。到先生离开此地时，安娘便不会再跟随先生而去了。”
哦，对，这个女子叫英娘……徐福终于从安娘的话中，记起了女子的名字。
因为徐福早就料到安娘的心思，听见她这样说也并不惊异，当即便点了点头，“你本是自由身，你觉得好那便留下。”
安娘重重点了点头，徐福短短一句话，却让她终于感觉到，自己的的确确是自由了，不用再受任何束缚了，顿时还免不了有些热泪盈眶。胡亥似乎也听见了楼下的响动，迈着腿哒哒哒冲了下来，左瞧瞧右看看，小心地问：“安娘，要走吗？”
安娘点了点头。
胡亥一脸打击太过重大，有些承受不来的表情，结结巴巴地看着徐福，“父、父亲……要、要走了？好吃的……”
原来在他心中，安娘几乎可以和食物划上等号。
侍从们闻言都忍不住憋笑。
倒是英娘有些惊诧地看了看胡亥。大约是徐福的外表瞧上去实在太嫩了，实在不像是早早便会生出儿子来的人。
嬴政觉得胡亥这模样实在太不争气了些，哪里像是秦王室的人？不过随即思考到对方本也并非自己的血脉，会有这般模样，嬴政反倒不知是该笑，还是该不满了。胡亥如今身在秦王室，丢的确是秦王室的脸，但他若一辈子就这样愚钝，那倒是可以一辈子做扶苏的好弟弟，这样也令人放心不少。
徐福目光低垂从胡亥那张小脸上扫过，然后抬手面无表情地从他的头顶，一口气撸到了下巴。
胡亥的头发顿时就耷拉在了脸上。
徐福这个安抚的动作实在有些粗暴，但胡亥傻白甜啊，得到安抚的胡亥立时就抱住徐福的手臂，再蹭了蹭，然后才装作不在乎地说：“那你走吧……”
安娘抿唇笑了笑，正要拉着英娘告退，英娘却在此时也迎了上来，盈盈一拜，“未曾想到，还能再见先生。”
安娘打了个哆嗦，看着他们二人的目光未免奇怪了起来。
嬴政面色也沉了沉，他倒并非不喜英娘，而是恼怒安娘在一旁瞎脑补。除却寡人之外，徐福还能同谁有关系？
“你的女儿……”
“她也活下来了，还始终记着先生给予我们的那两口仙气。”
仙气？什么仙气？安娘更是听得一头雾水。明明挺好理解的话语，但是凑在一起，自己怎么就不能理解了呢？
而侍从们早已经见怪不怪了，反而还对着徐福露出了崇拜的神色。啊，不愧是徐奉常，还能找到仙气呢……秦国有这样的活神仙，实在乃秦国大幸啊！侍从们脑子里已经涌现了他国嫉妒不已的神色。想到此处，心中还有点小小的骄傲呢。
见英娘如今生活得不错，其实徐福就已经没甚可关心的，不过他还是随口问了几句，关于如今三川郡守的事。
那安娘在旁边听得愈发心惊。
谁才能过问三川郡守？还用这样浑然不在意的口吻！难道……难道他……难道他便是秦王！不、不对啊，秦王的年纪应当比他这副模样要大才是啊。安娘全然没想到徐福身后还站了一个嬴政，盖因嬴政对待徐福一路上实在太过纵容，那过分宠溺的姿态，只要眼没瞎的人都能瞧出来。安娘怎么会想到，就是这样的人，纵然身为秦王，但在面对自己的心上人时，也是能低头弯腰屈膝的。
莫说是安娘觉得难以置信了，这样的事就算说出去，恐怕也没人敢相信。
纵然是龙阳君，谁可曾见到魏王在他跟前，做出这般姿态？
只有常常跟在徐福和嬴政身边的人，如这些侍从，便并不觉得何处不对。
“……那这刘子训倒是不错的。”徐福淡淡地给这段聊天画上了句号。
英娘迟疑道：“那先生，不见郡守吗？”说着英娘忍不住也看向了嬴政。她也是后头才听人说起，这二人的来头多么了不得的。一个是秦王，一个是咸阳城中的奉常。像他们这样的人，原本是一辈子也没机会见到的。
“不必。”嬴政直接出声截断了，他顿了顿，随后才道：“当初你们母女因为徐福才能得机会医治，如今徐福不过前来瞧一瞧，当初随手行的善事，如今是否得了个圆满的结果。”
嬴政口中纵然说着“随手”二字，但越是如此，英娘便越忍不住激动。
只有先生这样的人，才能将这等大恩惠当做随手所为，也正是这样的人，才算得上是真正的善人！
英娘笑了笑，“先生恐怕不知吧，三川郡中，郡守主持正在塑先生的像呢。”
怎么古人都好塑像？
徐福倒是觉得有些窘。若是他行过的这些地方，塑的像都长得不一样，那可就好玩儿了。
嬴政面上的神色柔和了不少。若是换做以前，他绝对不会想到，国境之内有人塑像，却不是为自己，而自己偏生还能万分喜悦，与有荣焉一般。
嬴政正是猜到三川郡会如此做，他才会将徐福带过来瞧一瞧。徐福广结善缘，恐怕要不了几年，天下便遍是他的名号了，哪怕那时他仍旧少透露自己的名字，但这么多人又不蠢，处处都有一个徐先生，再等秦国徐奉常的名声传出去，再结合他出自鬼谷，身有神术的背景，众人哪里还会不知道，这位“神秘”的徐先生便是秦国徐福呢？
虽然嬴政一向对名声这玩意儿不太看得上眼，但他不得不承认，若是有个好的名声，甚至说，名望到了极为可怕的地步，那对于徐福来说，是只有益处没有害处的。哪怕日后徐福得修长生之道，生命延续，而自己却寿终离去，没有了自己的庇护，徐福也足以在世间潇洒立足了。
嬴政全然没发觉到自己都想到多久以后去了……
徐福似有所觉地回头看了他一眼。
徐福猜不到嬴政在想什么。刚才嬴政的目光太过热烈，大概是……自己侧脸太迷人？
“你若想要去看那塑像，我们便一起过去……”嬴政出声道。
“不，不必了。”徐福加重了一下语气。
如果那塑像做得实在太丑，他是该笑呢还是该哭呢？
还是就让它在自己心目中保持一种神秘感吧，希望数千年后，后世的人挖掘出自己塑像时，不会顺便印上教科书。一想到秦始皇在历史书上的画像，徐福的心肝儿就颤了颤。
只要是徐福的意思，嬴政都不会反对，既然他拒绝，那不去便是了。
英娘心中有些失落，不过同时对徐福的崇拜却更深了。对名利等身外物丝毫不在意，何等淡泊的心性！问世间，谁人能有？
“既如此，那安娘你随她去吧。”嬴政出声，有了点逐客的意思。
对方顿时意识到自己打扰好一会儿了，便迅速出去了。
徐福回头扫了眼甘棠的方向，见他紧紧绷着脸，比从前的木头脸还要木头脸，有的同僚上前拉着甘棠到一旁安慰去了。
嬴政注意到他的目光，忍不住低声道：“若无感情便在一起，会教人难以忍受吗？”
“因人而异。”徐福脱口而出地回答完，脑子里骤然清明起来，他不由得转头看了看嬴政，“难道与我在一起你难以忍受？”说完徐福忍不住皱了皱眉。明明这么久了，也没见你难受啊！而且不就做个长期床伴吗？何必上纲上线到难不难以忍受的地步，当真奇怪！
嬴政闻言，懵了懵。
这句话，难道不应该是他对着徐福说？这话说反了吧？
“自然不是。”嬴政虽然不知徐福为何会将话说反，但他敏锐地知道，若是此时不快速否决，那必然麻烦了。
徐福脸上的清冷之色顿时便弱了几分，他满意地点头，不自觉地抬了抬下巴。嬴政见了徐福这副模样，心底都快化作一滩水了，什么有没有感情，什么会不会难受，此时全都被揉皱了塞在心底下，轻易不会扯出来了。徐福这模样，就算没感情，就算难受，他能舍得放手？嬴政觉得自己实在是想太多了。
徐福若是知道嬴政心中所想，说不准还会长吁一口气。
啊，这才是正常画风的秦始皇啊。
要什么就必须捏在手里，哪管其它？
见嬴政半天不再说话，徐福打量了一眼他的神色，迟疑一下，补上了一句：“你我与安娘、甘棠是不同的。”
徐福本意是想说，关系是不同的。
不过嬴政却暗自点头，不错，至少他将徐福拥在怀了，而甘棠太没用了，死活追不上安娘。
嬴政对上徐福的目光，里头没有面对旁人时的漠然，或许连徐福自己都没发觉，他的目光是温和的，放松的。嬴政心头顿时被抚慰了不少。徐福是察觉到他的不快，在安慰他吧……
想多了的嬴政十分欣喜地带着徐福回屋去做小儿不宜的事了。
甘棠在另一头为自己还没来及恋的感情而感觉到痛苦难过，等他好不容易恢复了状态，却发现主子们正在翻云覆雨的时候，受到刺激的甘棠，更加痛苦难过了……
徐福和嬴政都不欲在三川郡内多作停留，他们领略了两天，换了郡守的三川郡如今是什么样的，随后便启程准备离开三川郡。被伤透了少男心的甘棠自然也是欢喜不已，至少可以离开这处伤心地了……
一行人出了城，甘棠突然指着一方，皱眉道：“那是何物？”
徐福掀起车帘顺着他的目光看了过去。嬴政也紧跟着半靠在徐福的肩上，往外看去。
徐福只看了一眼脸色顿时就更加冷了。
他万万没想到，决心要避开的塑像，还强制性要让他观看。
塑像被立在了城外极为显眼的位置，一旦有人进城，便能一眼望见，可见三川郡是完全将这塑像当做三川郡的骄傲来立的。但徐福只看了一眼，便觉得一点也不值得骄傲好吗……
城外的塑像一左一右。
左边的身材高大，五官糊得看不清楚；右边的个子挺拔清瘦，五官照样糊得看不清楚。
但看二人衣着打扮，徐福觉得极其地违和，左边威风凛凛，右边气质……温婉？若是不知道，乍一看，还觉得右边的塑像是个女子呢。
徐福几乎是第一时间就猜到了，这两座塑像，应当左边为嬴政，而右边为自己。凭什么嬴政的塑像好生英武，而自己的却是那样的怂？
侍从们见状，嘴角频频抽搐，心道怪不得徐奉常不愿来看塑像了。就这塑像，连徐奉常的万分之一也没表现出来呢，若非早就听那英娘说过，此时他们就算是见了，恐怕也认不出来。
这两个塑像大约还未彻底完工，不多时还有工匠出城来，围着两座塑像开始继续雕刻，徐福就看着几只手在自己的塑像之上摸来摸去，徐福的脸色越来越冷，最后实在看不下去了，撒手放下车帘，沉声道：“走吧。”
嬴政也面沉如水，示意众人继续向前走。
而突然出声导致徐福看了塑像备感不快的甘棠，骤然发觉自己收到了好几道鄙视的目光。
甘棠心头一阵莫名其妙：我做什么了吗？？？
