胡亥和扶苏年纪虽小，但相比起来，倒是比徐福更能吃苦，徐福发觉到自己已经习惯舒适生活，半点苦也不愿意吃的时候，已经太迟了。
嬴政把他惯成这个模样，应当不是有什么阴谋吧？
徐福靠在嬴政怀中，压住打呵欠的冲动和脸上的疲倦，低声问道：“还未到吗？”
嬴政也有些心疼，“应当快了，已经入蜀地了。”这一路劳累，实在太折腾徐福了。
徐福“嗯”了一声，低着头，神色瞧不清楚。
但其实此时他正在惆怅。
想上辈子，他也是能轻松入深山的人，这些苦都是能轻松驾驭下来的，但这辈子他却半点都忍受不了了！这是因为上辈子吃够了，所以这辈子该尽情享受了吗？
徐福的思绪乱飞间，就听见外面的人喊了一声，“先生，该下马车了。”因着嬴政在外，实在不好称呼，侍从们便大都时候就直接唤徐福了，而嬴政往往也并不生气。侍从们渐渐也都习惯了。
徐福由嬴政扶着下了马车。他们抛弃了马车、马匹等物，寻了个地方寄存，然后才开始翻山越岭。
甘棠闷着头在前面带路，徐福和嬴政走在后头，时不时聊上几句，倒是将劳累无形间消去了几分。
只是走着走着，徐福总觉得有些不对劲。虽然上次来时，蜀地有雨，视线都被模糊得有些不大清楚，不过他总觉得，他走的似乎也并非这条路啊……
“甘棠，你是不是带错路了？”徐福顿住脚步，出声问。
甘棠抬头四顾，“没错啊。”
其余侍从并未来过此地，自然也是不识路的，倒是嬴政皱了皱眉，“似乎……的确并非此路。”方才他与徐福一路说着话，也没注意甘棠带路带往何方去了。
甘棠听见连嬴政都如此说了，顿时再难维持镇定，“这……请主上恕罪。”甘棠掉转身来，噗通一声就在嬴政跟前跪下了。
嬴政并未看他，而是抬头打量了一眼天色，“天色不晚了，先寻一处地方休息。”
姚贾很自觉地上前来恭请徐福，“我知晓附近有个寨子。”这段日子里，姚贾几句已经确定了嬴政的身份，现在给徐福当起仆人来，自然更加心服口服。
“寨子？”徐福脑子里登时便蹦出了山寨的身影。
嬴政的关注点倒是并不在这上面，他诧异地看了看姚贾，问道：“你如何知晓此处有寨子？”
“蜀地多氐族、羌族人，山腰有寨子是极为常见的。”姚贾躬着身子，恭恭敬敬地道。
“那你可知晓路？”嬴政问。
徐福环视周围一圈，“姚贾，你看可在那边？”徐福突然指着一个方向说道。
众人都立刻顺着他指的方向看了过去。
他们却什么也没看见。
“你们仔细瞧，那是什么？”徐福极为耐心地道。
侍从们总觉得心底莫名有点凉意。嗯，难道是徐奉常能看见的东西，但他们看不见？想到这里，众人打了个哆嗦。
嬴政的思维好歹还和徐福在一个线上，他仔细地瞧了会儿，总算看清了，在他们之前路过一条道上，延伸出去，看上去像山崖，但实际上那里有一条绳桥，那绳桥有竹子和木板缠绕连接，看上去其实并不大牢固。不过嬴政有些疑惑，为何凭这个，便能认出那方就是氐羌族人的寨子了？
徐福与嬴政对视了一眼，心底隐隐欣喜于嬴政能和自己“心灵相通”。他知道嬴政也看见了，于是便立即解释道：“我听闻羌族人居住的地方，往往山高水险，他们便习惯做出绳桥来，勉强能通行。”说完他顿了顿，又指了指那个方向，“你再看，隐藏在山林之间，有高楼。”
这个时候，能搭出那么高的屋子，实在是厉害了。
徐福隐约记得，这应当便是氐羌族中的碉楼，一般都建在村中住宅旁，若是此处无人，那他们怎么会修起碉楼呢？
相比之下，徐福如今更担忧另一点。不知此地可否排外？毕竟千年之前，因为这样的地方都在深山之中，他们少与外界交流，有时候不仅是语言交流成问题，甚至他们可能并不接受有陌生人来到寨中。
姚贾似乎察觉到了徐福的想法，于是看向他，道：“我曾在书简中见过相关记载，氐羌族人供奉白石。”
徐福也被勾起了记忆，“不错。白石莹莹，在羌族中是象征神的。”
姚贾微微一笑，将奉承的话说得不留痕迹，“似先生这样的人物，若是进了寨子，恐怕立即便被人当做神仙了。”
总结起来，他的意思大概就是，徐福一身好气质，还挺像白石的。
徐福嘴角微微抽搐。这他可不敢托大。不过如今荒郊野岭的，不管如何，先前去是试一试才知道结果如何。他看向了嬴政，嬴政接收到他的目光，便立即下令，让众人都按路返回，从那绳桥过去探一探。
绳桥之下的确是个小山崖，不过瞧上去还算不得深，毕竟此时他们才到山腰呢。只是若有恐高的人，走上去只消往下看一眼，说不定就能被活活吓死。
此时山间清凉，山腰间便有些雾气渐渐飘散开来了，换做徐福来看，他就觉得走在那绳桥之上，恍惚间会有置身云间仙境的感觉。
徐福当先便要无畏地走上去，嬴政见状顿时心跳如雷，赶紧伸手将人抓回来了。
姚贾很自觉地走上前，当了这个先锋。跟他们一起久了，姚贾又不蠢，当然瞧出来嬴政与徐福是个什么关系了，嬴政舍不得徐福先去走，那便他来走好了。姚贾自认没那么倒霉，走个绳桥就丢命了。
姚贾轻轻松松地走了过去。
徐福便又要往上走，嬴政眉头紧紧锁着，伸手动作有些粗暴地抓住了徐福的手腕。
他的掌心滚烫，徐福忍不住蹭了蹭，然后反抓住嬴政的手背，带着他一起往前走，窄窄的绳桥被他们两个人挤满了，不过倒是有种诡异的平衡感，让绳桥减少了震感。
徐福抓着嬴政的手背，时不时地蹭一蹭，很认真地表达着自己安抚的意思。啊，原来秦始皇也会害怕走绳桥啊……
一心担忧着徐福安危，还满脑子都假设万一绳桥断了怎么办的嬴政，全然不知道自己的形象在徐福心中被歪曲了。
并未花上多久的时间，他们就全部到达了对面，面前的路并不好走，是紧贴着山崖边上的，或许稍不注意，也会掉下去。不过这对于历经考验的侍从们来说，并算不得什么。只是嬴政有些不满意。
这路如此之窄，他自然无法与徐福并行了。
徐福心宽，并不在意此事，当先便走在前了，嬴政的脸色沉了沉，不大好看。在他眼中，徐福的举动稍微鲁莽了些，但是……但是偏偏也就只能这样。徐福难道要留在那里不走吗？自然不可能！
徐福敏锐地察觉到嬴政身上的情绪，于是头也不回的，一边摸着山崖壁，一边道：“阿政总为我走在前，偶尔也让我走在前才是。”
嬴政突然间便被感动到了。
徐福的意思是，自己总是在他跟前为他遮风挡雨，于是这次他便也走在自己跟前为自己遮风挡雨吧。
嬴政压根没去想，不就走个山路吗？能遮风挡雨个什么鬼？
反正心里很感动就是了。
因为山路的确艰险，他们倒是没在这个时候抓紧时间还来秀恩爱，牵着手往前走。
等绕过一处山壁之后，面前的景色顿时豁然开朗起来。
这条道可就宽多了……
徐福走上去之后，才觉得悬起的心慢慢落了回去，之前在马车内的一身疲累，因为这个时候集中了太久的精神，反倒什么疲倦的感觉都没了。徐福极为满意，看来他的那点儿翻山越岭的本事，暂时还没丢得连个影儿都看不见。
嬴政紧跟上来，再度抓住了徐福的手腕。
姚贾快步走在前，带着一行人入了林子，不久后他们便看见了碉楼，碉楼下面并没有把守着人，想来平时往这边走的人近乎没有，所以这里的族人才会没有防备心。
不过等他们走近了，寨子里的人便立即注意到了他们。
有人走出来，叽里呱啦说了两句什么。
徐福细细打量面前的人，衣饰还远不如后世的精美漂亮，但这时他们身上的衣饰，已经有着很鲜明的民族风格了，上面绣有图案，纹路，有些像是动物。
徐福隐约记得，羌族古时候好像是崇拜动物图腾的，所以衣物上会有这样的图案也并不奇怪了。倒是那个氐族，徐福了解并不多，后世也少听闻。也不知道这个寨子里的，是氐族人还是羌族人，又或是两族皆有之。
那人的目光从他们身上扫过，有提防有诧异。
不过那人在目光落到徐福身上时，突然脸色大变，呜里哇啦地又跑进去了。对方说的大约是当地的俚语，这可就麻烦了，徐福猜测自己说不准是一句也听不明白的。写字出来也不靠谱，据说羌族古时并没有文字，他们一切都靠口述，就连传承，都是用口口相传。谁知道，他们是否认识篆体字呢？
就在徐福思虑间，突然间从寨子里涌出了一大波人。
徐福和嬴政身后的人都不自觉地咽了咽口水。
就他们和姚贾三人在内格外的镇定。哦，或许还要加上一个甘棠，他因为带错路而心痛不已，对外界危险的感知都变得迟钝了。
侍从们骤然提高了警惕，严阵以待。
而对方却指着徐福，旁若无人地嘀咕了起来。
紧接着，有个小姑娘快步从人群中跑了出来，指了指徐福，又指了指寨子里头，用极为生涩别扭的蜀地语，道：“进来。”
徐福一脸疑惑，这些人为什么见了自己，反应这么奇怪？
徐福抬脚要跟上去，嬴政却抓住了他，“这些人难以交流，瞧上去又神色凶恶……”
徐福“唔”了一声，低声道：“我觉得他们应当并非神色凶恶，大概只是，当地人习惯摆出的表情？你瞧那个小姑娘便不是如此，她笑得很甜。”
听了后半句话，嬴政顿时更生气了。
还笑得很甜？？？
徐福再度拔腿往里走，还没忘记伸手抓住嬴政的手掌，“相信我，没事的。”
徐福和嬴政都往里走了，其他人自然也不会有二话，当即就跟了上去。
一行人浩浩荡荡地走进去，越往里走，徐福便越忍不住惊叹。
这个地方实在漂亮！
他们利用天然的原料，造出了屋子来，有碉楼，有平屋。有的用竹子木头铸就，而更多的则是垒石成屋，在这个建筑水平落后的时代，他们还能做个小三楼出来，实在令人惊叹了。
这些建筑之上还放着一些石头，徐福粗略扫了一遍，便发现顶上的石头皆是五块，大约有什么固定的象征意义。徐福猜测，那应当便是姚贾口中的白石。
一路行来，他们还能发现寨子里有着不少的图腾，乍一看，会让人觉得他们的信仰有些混乱。
不过徐福记得，似乎这也是当地的一种特色。
走了没多久，徐福隐约听见有人叫那小姑娘为“阿咿”，听上去就像是个语气词一样，徐福重复听见好多次，才敢确定下来。
阿咿突然回过头来，看了看徐福，又冲他甜甜一笑，声音艰涩道：“这里，你要，的……”
徐福看过去，只见那里一块小小的田，田里培养了一些植物，那些植物上坠着褐色的小小果实。不过徐福很清楚，那可不是果实，闻着香麻的气息，徐福很快便猜出了那是什么玩意儿。
……是花椒。
徐福收住激动的思绪。
不对啊……
这小姑娘为什么对他说“这里，你要，的”？
chapters.title: 第143章
第144章
chapters.source_text:
见徐福站在那里动也不动，阿咿着急地上前去拉他的手，嬴政大步上前护卫在徐福身旁，阿咿受气势所迫，不自觉地往后退了退，她露出了沮丧的表情，又指了指那些花椒，“你的。”
徐福也不知道她能否听懂自己说的话，他很肯定地告诉对方，“不是我要的。”
阿咿苦恼地皱了皱脸，很执拗地重复道：“是！”
徐福顿觉语言不通实在是个大麻烦，他只有闭嘴沉默了。
他不上前去看花椒，而有嬴政在旁，阿咿也不敢去拽他，阿咿叹了口气，招手将周围的族人招过来。有个青年健步如飞走到她的身旁，弯下腰来听阿咿说话。
看他们这副模样，徐福猜测阿咿在寨子里或许还有一定的地位。
很快，青年直起了腰，引着他们继续往前走。他们用手比划再带猜，勉强也能让他们进行交流了。青年将住处分配给了他们，但是轮到徐福和嬴政的时候，青年却指了另外一处地方。那是一间单独分出来的屋子，虽然都是石头垒成，但徐福觉得自己还能发现，两间屋子的不同之处。
这一间看上去外形更小，但外表却更好看，或者说，明显能看出在建造的时候，花了更多的心思。
徐福走上前去，推开门进入。
发现里面并没有住人的痕迹，但奇怪的是，里面打扫得极为干净，并不见落灰。
阿咿笑着挤上前来，只是在注意到嬴政的时候，她不自觉地颤了颤，记着不往徐福的方向靠太近，阿咿对着屋子比划了一番，“这里，你的。”
这里也是我的？徐福踏入屋子，在屋子里寻找了一番，最后发现了一捆竹简。
竹简外面被人擦得很干净，很光亮，徐福走上前打开了竹简，谁知道里面却飞出了不少灰尘，糊了他一脸。徐福眯了眯眼，抬手挥开面前飞舞着的灰尘。
总算是看清了上面的字。
氐羌族没有刻字记录的习惯，所以这应当是属于外来人的。
徐福细细看下去，惊愕地发现，这竟然是一部讲述观星象的书。也不知道是谁带来的，徐福的心底升起了一股浓浓的怪异感。他简单翻阅过后，便合上了竹简。不过大拇指贴合竹简的地方，似乎触到了什么凹凸不平的地方。是刻了字？徐福将书简翻转过来，只见书简外面篆刻了两个小字。
君房。
徐福猛地怔住了，瞬间便联想到了之前尉缭将书简给自己时，上面也刻了三个字，“赠君房”，那无疑，君房就是指自己。所以，“君房”乃是自己的字？
这具身体的原主，曾经来过这个寨子？他带来了这些竹简，被寨子中人好好保存了下来？这里说不定也是他曾经住过的地方……怪不得阿咿的态度会那样奇怪了。
心头震惊过后，徐福倒是慢慢的就恢复了镇定。既然现在他已经和这具身体融为一体了，前身留下来的善缘，他也只有误打误撞、厚着脸皮去享受了。他总不能对阿咿说，我不是那个人吧。
因为徐福拿着竹简看了太久，嬴政不由得跟着走了过来，他抓起竹简看了看，一眼就看见了竹简上的名字。
“你从前来过这里？”嬴政有些惊讶，等问完后，嬴政紧跟着又沉声道：“这件事你是不是也忘了？”
徐福僵硬地点了点头。
嬴政眉头半点不见舒缓。
这段时日他都快要忘记徐福那个容易失忆的毛病了。
再骤然提起此事，嬴政可就有些不大好了，因为这无疑是提醒着他，时时刻刻徐福都有可能会失忆，而他忘掉的记忆中还将会包括自己。这种滋味实在太苦涩，嬴政一点也不打算去尝试。
徐福发觉到嬴政脸上的表情越来越难看，心中忍不住暗暗嘀咕，不过是自己忘了这件事，为何反倒是嬴政不快起来了？
阿咿站在门口，对着徐福抬手比划了一番，拉走了二人的注意力。
徐福猜测对方大约是在问自己满意不满意，于是点了点头。阿咿笑了笑，这才转身出去了。
过了没多久，还有个青年体贴地送来了食物，徐福和嬴政席地而坐，吃起了面前的食物，他们在路上折腾那么久，现在陡然放松下来，还真是又累又饿。
这些食物味道有些浓重，但却并没有放入花椒、辣椒等物，徐福不知这时的蜀地人，是不是还并不擅长将这两物用来烹饪。
不过无论如何相比之下，都比他们风餐露宿时吃的食物要好，徐福和嬴政迅速用完之后，便在屋子里休息了起来，不等他们仔细打量这个屋子里的摆设，屋外突然有胡亥小跑了进来。
胡亥哭丧着脸，“哥哥……”
“哥哥在外面，进来做什么？”嬴政扫了他一眼。
胡亥委屈地指着外面，“他和别人，和别人说话……”
胡亥话音刚落下，徐福就瞥见窗外，扶苏竟然在和阿咿说话，而且看上去，扶苏似乎还能和对方交流自如。扶苏才多大年纪，他难道能听明白阿咿说的话？还是说小孩子之间有什么特殊的交流方式？
胡亥不高兴地指了指他们的方向，“不理我。”
嬴政看了看窗外的扶苏，有些不满扶苏与阿咿亲近的模样，于是怂恿胡亥道：“他若不理你，你便再去缠着他。”
胡亥眨了眨眼，“可以吗？”
“去吧。”
徐福也忍不住眨了眨眼，看着胡亥跟个小炮弹一样射了出去，直冲着扶苏的方向。
扶苏在人小姑娘跟前还没来得及多说上两句话呢，便被胡亥残忍无情地破坏了，徐福和嬴政坐在屋内，都能听见胡亥砸进扶苏怀里，还抱着他的袖子嗷呜哭泣的声音。
徐福很不厚道地想，扶苏的袖子应该满是鼻涕眼泪了吧？
阿咿小姑娘尴尬地回头来看，脸颊边的小辫子甩啊甩，看向屋内的徐福时，水汪汪的眼睛里满含期待。徐福不知道她在期待什么，他搜刮尽了原主的记忆，但是实在什么也想不起来，大概真的是失忆失得太厉害了。
扶苏被胡亥缠住之后，就面色僵硬了，他抬头朝徐福的方向看过来，见徐福和嬴政都分外淡定地看着他们，扶苏顿时便知晓求助无门，只能耐心地将胡亥哄到一边去，起码不要让他再祸害自己身上的袍子了。
阿咿在外头踮了踮脚，将窗户给他们关上了，就这样一个小小的动作，顿时便让嬴政消退了所有的恶感。这小姑娘，眼色还是有几分的。
这寨子虽然很偏僻，但寨子里的人似乎都十分爱干净，屋子和床铺都打扫得很干净，只是这屋子里并没有床榻，被子直接就铺在了地上，因为铺得足够厚，倒是不会让人担心地上湿润的问题。徐福和嬴政在屋子里静静坐了会儿，便撑不住想要休息了。徐福起身打开屋门，走出去询问到哪里打水洗漱。
他费了极大的劲儿才比划出了水的意思，有个青年叽里咕噜地指了一个方向。
徐福抬脚便要往那边去，但嬴政考虑到他应当没有那样大的力气，便跟着过去，只是等他们走近，才顿时傻眼了。
嬴政觉得面前的这一幕有些惊奇。
这是一汪池子，但池子里竟然冒着气体，可以让人清晰地看见。
嬴政少见这样的景色，只隐约记得书简上似乎对此是有记载的。
徐福则是一眼就认了出来，这分明就是一个温泉！他也不矫情，当即便抬起手来宽衣解带。这水应当是活水，倒也不用担忧干净与否的问题。
嬴政盯着池子里的水瞧了会儿，一转头便见徐福将手指搭在胸前，革带被抽出，外袍从肩上滑落，他的手又伸向了深衣。嬴政不自觉地喉头一动，随即视线便黏在了徐福的手指上，目光跟随着他手上的动作而动作。
“……做什么？”嬴政怔然地问出声。
徐福的耳朵动了动，他发觉到自己似乎听见了嬴政的声音有些……沙哑？他转头对上嬴政的目光，很轻易地便从嬴政看似平常的目光底下，找到了点迷醉之色。徐福不自觉地勾了勾嘴角，心底涌起了些，连他自己都没发觉的喜悦。他对嬴政这样的反应感觉到喜悦。
徐福加快了速度，很快便脱了个干净。
此时嬴政反倒紧张起来了，他朝四周打量了一圈，发现并没有什么人出现，嬴政方才放下心，等他转过头来，徐福已经跳下水去了，嬴政想要抓住他都来不及，嬴政不由得皱眉，低声斥道：“你可知水中是什么？便这样莽撞地跳下水去了！”
徐福在温泉池中划了下水，认真点头，“我知道。”说完，他还冲嬴政勾了勾手指头。
嬴政怎么能抵挡住这般主动的徐福，他的唇角也不自觉地勾了勾，便立即跳了下去。
山间本有些凉意，但进入池水中后，嬴政便发觉浑身都被暖融融所包裹着了，此时他敏锐地察觉到水流动了动，嬴政担心是水蛇等物，他却不知温泉之中，哪会有这些玩意儿出现？嬴政潜入水中，低头一看，却见徐福在池水中，宛如一尾鱼，朝着自己灵活地游了过来。
这还是徐福对上辈子阴影实在太大，特地学的，乍然在嬴政跟前展露。
他纤长的四肢在水中舒展开来，莫名带了点儿勾人的意味，嬴政发觉到自己的胸口被涨得闷闷的，他伸手捞住了徐福，徐福如同水草一般展开双腿缠在了他的腰上。
嬴政的喉结动了动，顿时觉得自己的某个部位张扬挺立了起来。
原本想在水底下吓一吓嬴政的徐福顿时便郁卒了。
不过他那张脸上也瞧不出什么情绪，因为温泉水将他的脸颊烘得微微泛红，清冷的美人，突然面带红云，无疑是极为迷人的，此时在嬴政的眼中，便成了徐福破天荒的羞涩反应。往日里徐福也常有主动的时候，所以这次嬴政并未作怀疑，当即便将徐福揽在怀中，两人没羞没臊地在温泉池中留下了自己的子子孙孙。
也不知道过去了多久，徐福感觉到自己呼吸有些困难了。
温泉池子里本来就不能泡得太久，他们没死在里头也是不容易了。
徐福推了推嬴政，两人这才慢腾腾地从池子里起来了，只是等出来以后，两人就跟中了毒似的，手脚发软。
徐福有些心虚地回头看了一眼并不平静的池子，也不知道等寨子中人发现的时候，会不会觉得池水里好像有哪里不太对劲……啊，不能再想了，这样的事就让它永埋心中好了。徐福连忙打住了自己的思维。
他们四肢酸软地穿上衣袍，步履缓慢地回到了屋中，两人迅速窝在被子里入了眠。
等到第二日醒来的时候，两人都有些睁不开眼。
徐福悲伤地发现，自己和嬴政大概是温泉泡太久，出现后遗症了，现在都还是昏昏沉沉，四肢酸软的。
不久之后，有人进来了，嬴政勉强还能撑着睁开眼，他目光冰冷地看向来人，却见是胡亥迈着小短腿正往这边来，他走近了一头扎进徐福的怀中。嬴政今日也没力气斥责他，便随他去了。而徐福发现到嬴政难得的温和之后，心中顿时觉得有些好笑，嬴政会有这样虚弱的时候，可实在不多见，徐福都快要将他当做非人类来看待了。
胡亥见徐福和嬴政都不搭理自己，就抬起手想要去摸摸徐福的脸，一摸，他就惊叫了起来，随后便立即小跑着出去了，徐福隐隐能听见胡亥在外头大叫扶苏快来的声音。
徐福不由得想到了，几年前的时候，年幼却并不讨喜的胡亥因为发起高热，自己让嬴政一同前去看一看他的事。果然，留下一个胡亥，也还是有好处的。至于日后他还会不会是秦二世，谁能想那么远呢？
徐福不自觉地再度闭上了眼。
等他发觉到自己思维已经飘散得有些远的时候，外面又有人进来了。
哪怕他和嬴政躺在一起，那些人也并没有觉得哪里不对。寨子里似乎有专门的巫医，徐福模模糊糊地看见一个妇人，从外头走了进来，妇人头上戴着黑色羽毛，脸上神色严肃，她弯下腰，伸手就去扒徐福的衣服，吓得徐福赶紧往后缩了缩。
阿咿走上前来，皱眉按着他的手臂，“要治，治病。”
妇人撤去脸上严肃的神色，冲徐福笑了笑。
徐福这才犹豫着放松了下来。他不知这巫医有什么本事，不过古代有些古法，总是有一定道理的。
妇人毫不客气地脱了徐福的上衣，还顺便扒了嬴政的上衣，嬴政的脸色顿时黑如碳。
不得不说，这还是头一次，胆敢违背秦王意愿，强扒他衣服的，原本还觉得有些难堪的徐福，若不是实在浑身无力，恐怕他已经忍不住笑出声了。
其他人早就不敢再多看了，他们都很自觉地退了出去。
徐福和嬴政，这两人谁光着上半身，他们都是不敢看的。
不过尽管如此，徐福和嬴政身上的吻痕还是没羞没臊地钻进了他们的视线中。
寨子中人似乎并不觉得有何奇怪之处，就连小姑娘阿咿都很淡定地出去了。
等徐福和嬴政终于病好之后，他们已经在寨子中滞留好几日了，恰好便到了寨中举行祭山会的日子。嬴政骤然想起这个时候已经不早了，他原本为徐福计划着的加冠礼，等到回咸阳的时候，怕是已经太晚了。左思右想后，嬴政便特意决定在此处再停留两日。他从那堆书简中发现，祭山会时，头次参与祭山会的男子，代表成年了，将会受到祝福，倒是与加冠礼有些相似。
一身不适褪去之后，徐福和嬴政都感觉到舒服多了，就连走路时，都觉得脚下生风，精神抖擞了。
到祭山会这一日，徐福便早早起了。
阿咿指派了个青年前来，那青年给徐福与嬴政送了衣物前来，正是寨中的服饰。
一套花花绿绿，一套黑乎乎。
徐福想了想，一咬牙还是将黑乎乎的让给了嬴政，毕竟作为堂堂秦王，总不能穿得花花绿绿的吧……
徐福强忍着不适，将那花花绿绿的衣服穿在了身上，幸好这时的染色技术还不太好，所以颜色染得不深，倒还没有大红配大绿的惊悚感。等衣物一件一件地套上身，徐福奇迹地发现，还挺合身的，只是不知道自己此时是否像是一只孔雀。
啊，总是穿白衣，气质出尘高洁的自己啊……万万没想到，今日会毁在一套艳丽的衣服上。
徐福几乎预见到了，等自己穿着这套衣服出去时，那些人看着自己的目光，会如何地惊悚可怕了。
他全然未注意到，一旁的嬴政瞧着他的模样，眼底还闪过了惊艳之色。
徐福平日穿的衣服颜色实在太单调，气质倒是足了，不过偶见他穿上这般艳色的衣服，他的五官瞬间便减了冷意，转而被衬得精致俊美起来，帽子戴在头上，漂亮的银饰坠下来，贴在眉心，显得有些神秘不可侵犯，但同时还有点儿妩媚的感觉。
若是嬴政换在现代的话，他便会知道，他此刻脑子里想到的，就跟制服诱惑差不多。
“走吧。”徐福抬起头，正好撞进嬴政的目光中，徐福有些不解他怎么会露出这样的目光，自己打扮得跟孔雀（山鸡）一样，他还能看着自己露出迷醉之色，这……这……他该说情人眼中出西施，还是天哪，秦始皇他竟然眼瘸？
“嗯。”嬴政收起目光，和徐福一起走了出去。
在寨子里狭小的空地上，有许多白石搭起来的小塔，小塔前点燃了火堆，还放上了贡品，看上去，塔前似乎就是举行祭山会的场所。徐福和嬴政走过去的时候，空地上已经站了不少人了，只是那些人在听见脚步声后，就立即让出了路，好让徐福和嬴政往前走。
数道目光朝着徐福的身上投来，徐福本来对周围目光都能维持淡定，于是此时，哪怕他打扮得十分奇怪，他也没有露出半分窘迫和慌乱，见周围的目光并无嘲讽惊吓之色，徐福猜测一定是自己的淡定大气，稳住了这些人。不过等他越往前走，徐福无意间的一个回头，才发觉这些人的确没有嘲讽惊吓之色，但他们眼底却还有着满满的惊艳。
惊艳？
难道这些人也跟着嬴政一起眼瘸了吗？
阿咿此时从人群中出来，手中拖着酒碗，她将酒碗放到了徐福的手中。
徐福疑惑不解地看着她，这是什么意思？他转头环视一圈，也并未见到其他人手中有酒碗，身边的嬴政也没有人送酒来。难道就自己一人是特殊的？可自己酒量不大好啊……徐福不着痕迹地皱了皱眉，正想着如何将酒推拒掉。阿咿却在此时顶着嬴政锐利的目光，抬手拉住了徐福的衣角，带着他往前走，嬴政竟是被抛下了。
嬴政虽然心有不快，但到底还是没有跟上去。
而徐福跟着阿咿往前走着走着……
眼看便要走到小塔跟前了。
此时阿咿指了指他手里的酒，又指了指火堆。
徐福恍然大悟，抬手将酒都倒了出去，酒水遇火，便燃烧了起来，火苗骤然升高，吓了徐福一跳，不过在众人眼中，徐福此时格外淡定，站在那里动也不动，实在令人敬服。
阿咿见状，甜甜地笑了笑，又交了个树枝缠成的木杖到他手中。
徐福抓紧木杖，内心有些茫然，这是又要做什么？
就在他迷茫时，周围却突然响起了寨中人的声音，他们高喝一声，然后开始唱起了歌。徐福觉得，这个仪式约莫就和蜡祭差不多，蜡祭时也会进行吟唱，只不过远不如他们奔放，歌声高亢得都可以将林中的鸟儿统统惊飞了。
阿咿见徐福半天不动，便再度出声用别扭生涩的蜀地语道：“主持，仪式，君房，主持……以前一样……”
徐福差不多将她的话组织成了完整的语句。
她的意思是让自己来主持仪式，就像从前那样？原身那个时候年纪才多大啊？这便能给一个寨子主持祭山会了，可比他厉害多了。
徐福虽然并未主持过祭山会，不过刚好，他从竹简中看见了记载，那些记载似乎还是原身亲手篆刻下来的，此时倒是正好便宜了自己。徐福在心底轻叹一声，面上却是摆出了极为庄严的神色，高举起木杖，开始迎合着那些歌声，其实徐福也不知道他们在唱什么，不过要跟着发个音，当做空耳来跟着唱，倒是没有什么问题的。
其他人听见徐福清泠泠的声音加入，顿时激动不已，声音高亢得再上一个台阶，奇迹的是，他们的声音虽然高亢，但却并不会压制过徐福的声音，相反的，徐福的声音还格外的明晰。
嬴政看着他的背影，目光万分灼热。
而姚贾则是有些目瞪口呆，其余侍从也皆是无比崇拜地看着徐福的方向，哪怕已经数次见识过徐奉常的厉害之处了，如今见着了，也还是会觉得让人拜服不已呢！
歌声远远地飘荡开……
有青壮年抓了家畜前来，切断脖子，流出血来，洒在塔前。
徐福虽然觉得有些血腥，不过他也很清楚，这在古时并不少见，这已经是较为普通的祭祀方法了。
尔后徐福用手中木杖敲击起塔前的羊皮鼓，发出沉闷的声响，不知道的还以为这是在给歌声伴奏呢。
火堆慢慢地塌下来，火焰也不似之前那样旺盛了，整个仪式算是画上了句号，徐福将木杖收起，突然间反应过来，自己身上穿的衣服，应当就是主持的人才能穿的，幸好没给嬴政……
仪式结束后，阿咿赶紧跑上前来，热情地抓住了徐福的手腕，像是在冲着他道谢。
徐福随手拍了拍她的头，一转眼就看见胡亥气鼓鼓地瞪着阿咿。徐福心头觉得有些好笑，秦二世小时候还争风吃醋呢？徐福走上前去，也拍了拍胡亥的头。小孩子的气性来得快，去得也快，胡亥立即便抱着徐福的手掌蹭了起来。阿咿看着这一幕笑了笑，小姑娘大大方方地走开了。
徐福放开胡亥之后，抬头看向嬴政，他发现嬴政的目光似乎有一些复杂。
“怎了？”徐福大步走到他的跟前，观察了一番嬴政的目光。
嬴政掩下眼底狂热的色彩，笑道：“阿福如斯优秀。”
徐福随口道了句，“嗯，如斯优秀，却还是跟了你。”再优秀，也优秀不过秦始皇去啊！何况徐福并不觉得自己去跳个大神，装会儿逼，便有多么厉害了。
嬴政嘴角的笑容更加浓烈，“阿福说得是。”
侍从们低下头，一致地装作，我们听不见。
仪式结束后，寨子里便趁着天还未黑，迅速搭起桌案，放上食物，再架起火堆，俨然一副要开篝火晚会的姿态。
徐福和嬴政也未脱掉身上的衣服，他们就这样围坐了下来。
此时有人拿了面馍馍上来，赠给第一次参加祭山会的男子，也就是那些刚刚成年的男子。嬴政见状，便也伸手拿了一只馍馍，递到徐福的嘴边。
嬴政低声道：“你成年了……”他的声音在渐晚的天色下，应当是有一种令人迷醉的味道。
但徐福却忍不住在内心吐槽。
什么叫他成年了？搞了半天，嬴政嫖了这么久的未成年？
不过徐福很快又反应过来，古代的成年和后世的成年，实在不是一个范畴的，这才淡定了些，不过嬴政原本想营造的气氛，早就在徐福的无知无觉中挥发光了。
嬴政盯着他的脸庞瞧了一会儿，见半天徐福的脸上都没有其它情绪出现，嬴政心下免不了有些微的失望。
徐福往前凑了凑，身子微微前倾，一口咬在那馍馍上，味道实在不怎么样，但是吧，徐福觉得自己好像品出了别样的滋味。嬴政放在他身上的目光实在太过深沉，徐福也不知道是不是有火在一旁炙烤着的缘故，徐福感觉到自己的脸颊都发烫起来了，还有耳根似乎也有点怪异的感觉……
徐福自己心里也挺纳闷的，按理来说，他对什么目光都足够免疫了啊，怎么突然之间，便有些难以抵挡嬴政的注视了。
难不成自己被酒香给熏醉了？
他忍不住抬起头，想问嬴政看够了吗，但嬴政却突然俯身亲了一口他的嘴巴。
嬴政这个动作做得极为迅疾，他直起身来，随即便装作了若无其事的模样。其实这也不能怪他，盖因当时火光映在徐福的脸上，将他衬得太过诱人。
寡人把持不住，那都是有原因的。
徐福懵懵地抬起手摸了摸嘴角。
一嘴的馍馍渣……
他很想问嬴政舔到残渣的感觉舒服吗？但是见嬴政一脸享受的淫荡表情，徐福便顿时觉得，自己大约是不必问了。
这时他的脑子里忽然蹦出来一个念头。
别说是馍馍渣了，也许就算自己喷点口水出来，嬴政也觉得很香？想到这里，徐福自己忍不住打了个寒颤，真是太……恶寒了！
寨子里的人激动起来似乎会唱情歌，没一会儿徐福和嬴政的目光，便被歌声吸引过去了。
唱歌的有男有女。
不过徐福隐约记得，要在这样的寨子里讨个女孩儿，那可不容易。
要知道许多这样寨子，都还维持着母系氏族的习俗，男子说是娶，还不如说是嫁，在有些地方，一名女子拥有多名男子，并不是什么稀奇事。
想到这里，徐福忍不住抬起手摸了摸自己的脸，如果不是自己的颜值具有欺骗性，恐怕在这里的地位也不见得能高到哪里去。
嬴政凑在徐福的耳边，低声问：“他们在唱什么？”
温热的气息干扰了徐福的思绪，徐福别开了目光，心不在焉地答道，“情歌。”
七国中也多有唱情歌的习俗，放在这个时代，唱个情歌并算不得多么惊世骇俗。
“寡人也曾听过一首歌……”
“嗯？”徐福转头看他。
嬴政微微眯着眼，眸光似乎被火光映衬着，陡然间都变得温柔了万分。
“喓喓草虫，趯趯阜螽；
未见君子，忧心忡忡。
亦既见止，亦既觏止，我心则降。
陟彼南山，言采其蕨；
未见君子，忧心惙惙……”
嬴政刚开口的时候，徐福还懵了一下，直到他用低沉的嗓音，略微语不成调地吟唱出声，徐福才猛地反应过来，他对着我唱情歌？？？
秦始皇对着我唱情歌？？？
徐福有些凌乱。
但听了一会儿，徐福便发现，这应当是诗经中的情诗吧……当我没学过诗经吗？徐福的关注点不知不觉就歪了，他压根忘记了，过去诗词的确是能当做歌来唱的啊！
上辈子徐福听过很多歌手的情歌，有哀怨的，有如泣如诉的，有狂放热切的……但是，好像都跟这一刻的不大一样，也不知道是因为古人的诗太美，还是自己的审美太糟糕，徐福竟然莫名觉得有几分好听。
用低沉的声音演绎出来时，全然是另一种味道。
没有任何人注意到他们这一隅，或许有人注意到了，但也绝对不会有人想到，他们的秦王啊，现在跟狗腿子似的凑在旁边跟人唱情歌呢。
嬴政原本是极为瞧不起这样的行为的。
男女情爱，时时放在心上，岂能有何作为？直到这时，嬴政才发现二者并无冲突，只是有的人学不会克制罢了。
“……亦既见止，亦既觏止，我心则夷。”嬴政的声音终于落下了尾音，徐福忍不住心中一动。
“你想和我谈恋爱？”徐福恍恍惚惚地脱口而出。
“什么？”见徐福脸上连半点感动也无，反倒开口说出句奇怪的话，嬴政心下更为失落了，不过还是耐着性子和徐福继续说话。
“不，没什么。”嬴政面色平淡，哪有半分想要和他谈恋爱的样子？方才唱情歌，或许只是君王的好胜心在作祟，认为自己可以比别人唱得更好嘛。
更何况，你能想象得出，秦始皇正儿八经要谈恋爱的模样？
或许有，不过大约是对着历史上那个神秘的阿房女？
chapters.translated_text:
Seeing Xu Fu standing there motionless, A-Yi anxiously stepped forward to pull his hand. Ying Zheng strode forward to stand guard by Xu Fu’s side. Forced by his imposing aura, A-Yi retreated involuntarily. She wore a dejected expression and pointed at the Sichuan peppercorns, "Yours."

Xu Fu didn't know if she could understand him, but he told her very firmly, "It’s not what I wanted."

A-Yi wrinkled her face in distress and stubbornly repeated, "Yes!"

Xu Fu suddenly felt that the language barrier was a huge problem, so he had no choice but to remain silent.

He didn't go forward to look at the peppercorns, and with Ying Zheng by his side, A-Yi didn't dare to pull him. A-Yi sighed and beckoned for her tribespeople to come over. A young man walked over to her side with nimble steps and bent down to listen to her.

Seeing them like this, Xu Fu guessed that A-Yi might hold a certain status in the village.

Soon, the young man straightened up and led them further ahead. By gesturing and guessing, they could barely communicate. The young man assigned them a place to stay, but when it came to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, he pointed to a different location. It was a separate room, and although it was built of stone, Xu Fu felt he could spot the differences between the two dwellings.

This one looked smaller in size, but it was better looking on the outside, or rather, it was obvious that more care had been put into its construction.

Xu Fu walked up and pushed the door open to enter.

He found no signs of anyone living there, but strangely, it was extremely clean inside, with no dust to be seen.

A-Yi smiled and squeezed in, but upon noticing Ying Zheng, she trembled involuntarily and made sure not to get too close to Xu Fu. A-Yi gestured toward the room, "Here, yours."

This is also mine? Xu Fu stepped into the room, searched around, and finally found a bundle of bamboo slips.

The outside of the bamboo slips had been wiped very clean and shiny. Xu Fu walked up and opened them, but to his surprise, a cloud of dust flew out, covering his face. Xu Fu squinted and raised his hand to wave away the swirling dust.

He finally managed to see the characters clearly.

The Di-Qiang tribe did not have the habit of recording things by carving characters, so these must have belonged to an outsider.

Xu Fu read on carefully and was astonished to find that this was actually a book about observing the stars. He didn't know who had brought it, but a deep sense of strangeness rose in his heart. After a brief look, he closed the bamboo slips. However, where his thumb pressed against the slips, he seemed to touch something uneven. Were there characters carved there? Xu Fu turned the slips over and saw two small characters engraved on the outside.

Junfang.

Xu Fu was stunned, instantly associating it with the time Wei Liao gave him bamboo slips with the words "Gift for Junfang" carved on them. Without a doubt, Junfang referred to him. So, "Junfang" was his courtesy name?

Had the original owner of this body been to this village before? Did he bring these bamboo slips, which were then well-preserved by the villagers? Perhaps this was even where he used to live... No wonder A-Yi’s attitude was so strange.

After the initial shock, Xu Fu slowly regained his composure. Since he had now merged with this body, he would just have to stumble along and shamelessly enjoy the good karma left behind by his predecessor. He couldn't exactly tell A-Yi that he wasn't that person.

Because Xu Fu had been holding the bamboo slips for too long, Ying Zheng walked over. He grabbed the slips to take a look and immediately saw the name on them.

"You’ve been here before?" Ying Zheng asked, surprised. After asking, he added in a deep voice, "Did you forget about this too?"

Xu Fu nodded stiffly.

Ying Zheng’s brow did not relax at all.

During this time, he had almost forgotten about Xu Fu’s tendency to lose his memory.

Bringing it up suddenly now made Ying Zheng feel quite uneasy, as it was a constant reminder that Xu Fu could lose his memory at any time, and those forgotten memories would include him. This feeling was too bitter, and Ying Zheng had no intention of experiencing it.

Xu Fu noticed that the expression on Ying Zheng’s face was becoming increasingly ugly. He couldn't help but mutter to himself: it was just him forgetting this matter, so why was Ying Zheng the one getting upset?

A-Yi stood at the door and gestured to Xu Fu, drawing their attention away.

Xu Fu guessed she was asking if he was satisfied, so he nodded. A-Yi smiled and turned to leave.

Not long after, a young man thoughtfully brought them food. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng sat on the floor and began to eat. After all the trouble on the road, they were truly tired and hungry now that they could finally relax.

The food had a strong flavor, but it didn't contain any Sichuan peppercorns or chili. Xu Fu didn't know if the people of Shu at this time were not yet skilled at using these two things for cooking.

In any case, it was better than the food they had eaten while sleeping in the wilderness. After Xu Fu and Ying Zheng finished quickly, they rested in the room. Before they could carefully examine the room's furnishings, Hu Hai ran in from outside.

Hu Hai said with a mournful face, "Brother..."

"Your brother is outside, why are you coming in here?" Ying Zheng glanced at him.

Hu Hai pointed outside, aggrieved, "He is talking to someone... talking to someone..."

As soon as Hu Hai finished speaking, Xu Fu glanced out the window and saw Fusu actually talking to A-Yi. Moreover, it looked like Fusu could communicate with her freely. How old was Fusu? Could he understand what A-Yi was saying? Or did children have some special way of communicating?

Hu Hai pointed unhappily in their direction, "He won't pay attention to me."

Ying Zheng looked at Fusu outside the window, somewhat dissatisfied with Fusu’s closeness to A-Yi, so he instigated Hu Hai, "If he won't pay attention to you, go and pester him some more."

Hu Hai blinked, "Can I?"

"Go."

Xu Fu couldn't help but blink as he watched Hu Hai shoot out like a little cannonball, heading straight for Fusu.

Fusu hadn't even had the chance to say much to the young girl before Hu Hai cruelly and mercilessly ruined it. Sitting in the room, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng could hear the sound of Hu Hai crashing into Fusu’s arms and crying while clutching his sleeve.

Xu Fu thought uncharitably that Fusu’s sleeve must be covered in snot and tears by now.

The young girl A-Yi looked back awkwardly, her little braids swinging. When she looked at Xu Fu in the room, her watery eyes were full of expectation. Xu Fu didn't know what she was expecting. He searched his memory for the original owner’s recollections, but he really couldn't remember anything. Perhaps his memory loss was truly severe.

After being pestered by Hu Hai, Fusu’s expression stiffened. He looked up toward Xu Fu, and seeing that both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were watching them with extreme calmness, Fusu knew there was no help to be found. He could only patiently coax Hu Hai aside, at least to stop him from ruining his robe any further.

A-Yi stood on tiptoe outside and closed the window for them. This small gesture immediately made Ying Zheng’s bad feelings subside. This young girl had some sense after all.

Although the village was very remote, the people there seemed to be very clean. The room and bedding were kept tidy, but there was no bed; the quilts were spread directly on the floor. Because they were thick enough, there was no need to worry about the dampness of the ground. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng sat quietly in the room for a while before they couldn't hold out any longer and wanted to rest. Xu Fu got up, opened the door, and went out to ask where to get water to wash up.

He tried very hard to gesture the meaning of water, and a young man pointed in a direction with a babble.

Xu Fu started to walk that way, but Ying Zheng, considering that he probably didn't have much strength left, followed him. However, when they got close, they were both stunned.

Ying Zheng found the scene before him quite amazing.

It was a pool, but gas was rising from it, which could be clearly seen.

Ying Zheng rarely saw such scenery and only vaguely remembered that there seemed to be records of it in the bamboo slips.

As for Xu Fu, he recognized it at a glance—this was clearly a hot spring! He didn't act coy and immediately raised his hands to undress. The water seemed to be flowing, so there was no need to worry about its cleanliness.

Ying Zheng stared at the water in the pool for a while. When he turned his head, he saw Xu Fu resting his fingers on his chest, pulling out his leather belt, and letting his outer robe slide off his shoulders. His hands then reached for his inner garment. Ying Zheng’s throat moved involuntarily, and his gaze became glued to Xu Fu’s fingers, following his every movement.

"...What are you doing?" Ying Zheng asked in a daze.

Xu Fu’s ears twitched. He realized that Ying Zheng’s voice sounded... hoarse? He turned to meet Ying Zheng’s gaze and easily found a hint of intoxication beneath his seemingly normal look. Xu Fu curled his lips involuntarily, a joy he hadn't even noticed himself welling up in his heart. He felt happy about Ying Zheng’s reaction.

Xu Fu sped up and was soon completely undressed.

At this point, Ying Zheng became nervous. He looked around and found that no one was there, which put him at ease. When he turned back, Xu Fu had already jumped into the water. Ying Zheng couldn't even grab him in time. He couldn't help but frown and scold in a low voice, "Do you know what’s in the water? How could you be so reckless as to jump in!"

Xu Fu paddled in the hot spring pool and nodded seriously, "I know." After saying that, he crooked his finger at Ying Zheng.

How could Ying Zheng resist such an proactive Xu Fu? The corners of his lips curled up involuntarily, and he immediately jumped in.

The mountains were a bit chilly, but after entering the pool, Ying Zheng felt his whole body wrapped in warmth. At this moment, he keenly sensed the water moving. Fearing it might be a water snake or something similar—not knowing that such things wouldn't appear in a hot spring—Ying Zheng dove into the water. Looking down, he saw Xu Fu swimming toward him flexibly like a fish.

This was something Xu Fu had specifically learned because of his deep trauma from his past life, and he was showing it off in front of Ying Zheng for the first time.

His slender limbs stretched out in the water, inexplicably carrying a seductive quality. Ying Zheng felt a tightness in his chest. He reached out and caught Xu Fu, who wrapped his legs around his waist like water grass.

Ying Zheng’s Adam’s apple moved, and he suddenly felt a certain part of him standing tall and proud.

Xu Fu, who had originally wanted to scare Ying Zheng underwater, was suddenly depressed.

However, his face didn't show any emotion because the hot spring water had flushed his cheeks slightly red. A cold, beautiful person suddenly appearing with a rosy glow was undoubtedly extremely charming. In Ying Zheng’s eyes, this became a rare, shy reaction from Xu Fu. Since Xu Fu had been proactive in the past, Ying Zheng didn't suspect anything and immediately pulled Xu Fu into his arms. The two of them shamelessly left their descendants in the hot spring pool.

He didn't know how much time had passed, but Xu Fu felt that his breathing was becoming difficult.

One shouldn't soak in a hot spring for too long; it was a miracle they hadn't died in there.

Xu Fu pushed Ying Zheng, and the two of them slowly got up from the pool. But after getting out, they felt as if they had been poisoned, their limbs weak and soft.

Xu Fu looked back at the restless pool with a guilty conscience, wondering if the villagers would think something was wrong with the water when they discovered it... Ah, he couldn't think about it anymore; let such things be buried in his heart forever. Xu Fu quickly stopped his train of thought.

With weak limbs, they put on their robes and walked slowly back to the room, where they quickly huddled under the covers and fell asleep.

When they woke up the next day, neither of them could open their eyes.

Xu Fu sadly discovered that he and Ying Zheng were likely suffering from the aftereffects of soaking in the hot spring for too long; they were still groggy and their limbs were weak.

Not long after, someone entered. Ying Zheng could barely manage to open his eyes and looked coldly at the intruder, only to see Hu Hai walking over with his short legs. He walked up and dove into Xu Fu’s arms. Ying Zheng didn't have the strength to scold him today, so he let him be. Seeing Ying Zheng’s rare gentleness, Xu Fu found it somewhat funny. It was rare to see Ying Zheng so weak; Xu Fu was almost starting to view him as a non-human.

Seeing that neither Xu Fu nor Ying Zheng were paying attention to him, Hu Hai raised his hand to touch Xu Fu’s face. As soon as he did, he shrieked and then immediately ran out. Xu Fu could vaguely hear Hu Hai shouting outside for Fusu to come quickly.

Xu Fu couldn't help but think of a few years ago, when the young and unlikable Hu Hai had a high fever, and he had asked Ying Zheng to go see him together. Sure enough, keeping a Hu Hai around still had its benefits. As for whether he would be the Second Emperor of Qin in the future, who could think that far ahead?

Xu Fu closed his eyes again involuntarily.

By the time he realized his thoughts had drifted quite far, someone else entered.

Even though he and Ying Zheng were lying together, those people didn't think anything was wrong. The village seemed to have a specialized shaman doctor. Xu Fu vaguely saw a woman walk in from outside. She wore black feathers on her head and had a serious expression on her face. She bent down and reached out to pull at Xu Fu’s clothes, scaring him into shrinking back.

A-Yi walked up and frowned, pressing on his arm, "Need to treat, treat illness."

The woman’s serious expression faded, and she smiled at Xu Fu.

Only then did Xu Fu hesitantly relax. He didn't know what skills this shaman doctor had, but some ancient methods always had their reasons.

The woman unceremoniously took off Xu Fu’s top and then stripped Ying Zheng’s as well. Ying Zheng’s face turned as black as charcoal.

It had to be said that this was the first time anyone had dared to defy the Qin King’s will and forcibly strip his clothes. Xu Fu, who had initially felt embarrassed, would have laughed out loud if he weren't so weak.

Others had long since stopped daring to look and had consciously retreated.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng—no one dared to look at either of them with their upper bodies bare.

However, despite this, the hickeys on Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s bodies shamelessly entered their line of sight.

The villagers didn't seem to find anything strange about it; even the young girl A-Yi walked out very calmly.

By the time Xu Fu and Ying Zheng finally recovered, they had been stranded in the village for several days, and it just happened to be the day of the village’s Mountain Sacrifice Festival. Ying Zheng suddenly realized that it was getting late. He feared that the capping ceremony he had planned for Xu Fu would be too late by the time they returned to Xianyang. After much thought, Ying Zheng decided to stay here for two more days. He discovered from the pile of bamboo slips that at the Mountain Sacrifice Festival, men participating for the first time were considered adults and would receive blessings, which was somewhat similar to the capping ceremony.

After the discomfort faded, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng both felt much better, and even their steps felt light and spirited.

On the day of the Mountain Sacrifice Festival, Xu Fu got up early.

A-Yi assigned a young man to bring clothes to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, which were the traditional attire of the village.

One set was colorful, and the other was pitch black.

Xu Fu thought about it and gritted his teeth, letting Ying Zheng have the black one. After all, as the dignified King of Qin, he couldn't wear something colorful...

Xu Fu endured the discomfort and put on the colorful clothes. Fortunately, the dyeing technology at this time wasn't very advanced, so the colors weren't deep, and there was no horrifying clash of bright red and green. As he put the clothes on piece by piece, Xu Fu miraculously found that they fit quite well, though he didn't know if he looked like a peacock.

Ah, his usual self, who wore white and had an ethereal and noble temperament... He never expected to be ruined today by a set of gaudy clothes.

Xu Fu could almost foresee how horrifying the looks from those people would be when he went out wearing this outfit.

He didn't notice at all that Ying Zheng, watching him from the side, had a flash of amazement in his eyes.

The colors Xu Fu usually wore were too monotonous. He had the temperament, but occasionally seeing him in such vibrant colors made his features lose their coldness and instead look exquisite and handsome. With the hat on his head and beautiful silver ornaments dangling against his brow, he looked somewhat mysterious and untouchable, yet also a bit alluring.

If Ying Zheng were in the modern era, he would know that what he was thinking about was similar to "uniform temptation."

"Let’s go." Xu Fu looked up and happened to bump into Ying Zheng’s gaze. Xu Fu was a bit confused as to why he would show such a look. He was dressed like a peacock (or a pheasant), and Ying Zheng could still look at him with such intoxication. This... this... should he say love is blind, or my god, is the First Emperor of Qin actually blind?

"Mm." Ying Zheng withdrew his gaze and walked out with Xu Fu.

In the small open space of the village, there were many small towers made of white stones. Bonfires were lit in front of the towers, and offerings were placed there. It seemed that the area in front of the towers was the venue for the Mountain Sacrifice Festival. When Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walked over, there were already many people standing in the open space, but those people immediately made way after hearing their footsteps so that Xu Fu and Ying Zheng could move forward.

Several gazes were cast upon Xu Fu. Xu Fu was usually able to maintain his composure regardless of the surrounding gazes, so even though he was dressed very strangely, he didn't show any embarrassment or panic. Seeing that there was no mockery or shock in the surrounding gazes, Xu Fu guessed that his calm and dignified manner must have stabilized them. However, as he walked further, Xu Fu accidentally looked back and realized that while there was indeed no mockery or shock, there was a look of pure amazement in their eyes.

Amazement?

Could it be that these people were also as blind as Ying Zheng?

A-Yi emerged from the crowd, dragging a wine bowl in her hand, and placed it in Xu Fu’s hands.

Xu Fu looked at her in confusion. What did this mean? He turned and looked around, but didn't see anyone else with a wine bowl, and no one had brought wine to Ying Zheng. Was he the only special one? But he didn't have a high tolerance for alcohol... Xu Fu frowned imperceptibly, thinking about how to refuse the wine. At this moment, A-Yi, ignoring Ying Zheng’s sharp gaze, reached out and grabbed the hem of Xu Fu’s robe, leading him forward, leaving Ying Zheng behind.

Although Ying Zheng was unhappy, he didn't follow.

And as Xu Fu followed A-Yi forward...

They were about to reach the small tower.

A-Yi pointed at the wine in his hand and then at the bonfire.

Xu Fu suddenly realized and raised his hand to pour the wine out. When the wine hit the fire, it ignited, and the flames suddenly soared, startling Xu Fu. However, in the eyes of the crowd, Xu Fu was exceptionally calm, standing there motionless, which was truly admirable.

Seeing this, A-Yi smiled sweetly and handed him a wooden staff wrapped in branches.

Xu Fu gripped the staff, feeling somewhat lost. What was he supposed to do now?

Just as he was confused, the voices of the villagers suddenly rose around him. They shouted loudly and began to sing. Xu Fu felt that this ritual was probably similar to the La Sacrifice, where chanting was also performed, but it was far less unrestrained than this; the singing was so high-pitched that it could have scared all the birds in the forest away.

Seeing that Xu Fu hadn't moved for a long time, A-Yi spoke again in awkward, broken Shu dialect: "Preside, ritual, Junfang, preside... same as before..."

Xu Fu managed to organize her words into a complete sentence.

She meant for him to preside over the ritual, just like before? How old was the original owner back then? To be able to preside over a village’s Mountain Sacrifice Festival at that age—he was much more impressive than him.

Although Xu Fu had never presided over a Mountain Sacrifice Festival, it just so happened that he had seen records of it in the bamboo slips, and those records seemed to have been carved by the original owner himself, which was convenient for him now. Xu Fu sighed lightly in his heart, but on the surface, he put on a very solemn expression, raised the wooden staff high, and began to match the singing. In fact, Xu Fu didn't know what they were singing, but there was no problem with just making sounds to follow along.

When the others heard Xu Fu’s clear, ringing voice join in, they were instantly excited, and their voices rose to an even higher pitch. Miraculously, although their voices were high, they didn't suppress Xu Fu’s voice; on the contrary, Xu Fu’s voice remained exceptionally clear.

Ying Zheng watched his back, his gaze burning with intensity.

As for Yao Jia, he was dumbfounded, and the other attendants were all looking at Xu Fu with immense admiration. Even though they had witnessed the prowess of the Fengchang Xu many times, seeing it now, they still couldn't help but be in awe!

The singing drifted far away...

Some young men brought livestock, cut their throats, and let the blood flow, sprinkling it in front of the tower.

Although Xu Fu found it a bit bloody, he was well aware that this was not uncommon in ancient times and was already a relatively ordinary method of sacrifice.

Afterward, Xu Fu used the wooden staff in his hand to beat the sheepskin drum in front of the tower, making a dull sound. Anyone who didn't know better would have thought it was accompaniment for the singing.

The bonfire slowly collapsed, and the flames were no longer as vigorous as before. The entire ritual came to an end. Xu Fu put away the wooden staff and suddenly realized that the clothes he was wearing must be for the person presiding over the ritual. Fortunately, he hadn't given them to Ying Zheng...

After the ritual, A-Yi ran up and enthusiastically grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist, as if thanking him.

Xu Fu patted her head casually, and as he turned, he saw Hu Hai glaring at A-Yi, puffed up with anger. Xu Fu found it somewhat funny—the Second Emperor of Qin was jealous even as a child? Xu Fu walked up and patted Hu Hai’s head as well. A child’s temper comes and goes quickly; Hu Hai immediately began rubbing against Xu Fu’s palm. A-Yi watched this scene and smiled, the young girl walking away generously.

After Xu Fu let go of Hu Hai, he looked up at Ying Zheng and noticed that his gaze seemed somewhat complex.

"What’s wrong?" Xu Fu strode up to him and observed Ying Zheng’s gaze.

Ying Zheng hid the fanatical color in his eyes and smiled, "A-Fu is so excellent."

Xu Fu said casually, "Mm, so excellent, yet I still ended up with you." No matter how excellent he was, he couldn't be more excellent than the First Emperor of Qin! Besides, Xu Fu didn't feel that jumping around and pretending to be profound made him all that great.

The smile at the corners of Ying Zheng’s mouth grew more intense, "A-Fu is right."

The attendants lowered their heads, unanimously pretending, "We can't hear anything."

After the ritual, the villagers took advantage of the fact that it wasn't dark yet to quickly set up tables, place food, and build bonfires, looking like they were about to have a bonfire party.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng didn't take off their clothes and sat around like that.

At this time, someone brought over steamed buns to give to the men who were participating in the Mountain Sacrifice Festival for the first time—that is, those who had just come of age. Seeing this, Ying Zheng reached out, took a bun, and handed it to Xu Fu’s mouth.

Ying Zheng whispered, "You are an adult now..." His voice, in the darkening sky, must have had an intoxicating quality.

But Xu Fu couldn't help but complain internally.

What did he mean he was an adult now? After all this time, had Ying Zheng been "soliciting" a minor?

However, Xu Fu quickly realized that the definition of adulthood in ancient times and in later generations was not in the same category, which calmed him down. But the atmosphere Ying Zheng had originally wanted to create had long since evaporated in Xu Fu’s ignorance.

Ying Zheng stared at his face for a while, and seeing that there was no other emotion on Xu Fu’s face for a long time, Ying Zheng couldn't help but feel a slight disappointment.

Xu Fu leaned forward slightly and took a bite of the bun. The taste wasn't very good, but Xu Fu felt like he could taste something different. The gaze Ying Zheng had on him was too deep, and Xu Fu didn't know if it was because of the fire roasting nearby, but he felt his cheeks burning, and his earlobes also felt a bit strange...

Xu Fu was also puzzled himself. Logically speaking, he should be immune to any kind of gaze, so why was it suddenly so difficult to resist Ying Zheng’s stare?

Could it be that he was intoxicated by the scent of the wine?

He couldn't help but look up, wanting to ask if Ying Zheng had seen enough, but Ying Zheng suddenly leaned over and kissed his mouth.

Ying Zheng performed this action extremely quickly. He straightened up and immediately pretended as if nothing had happened. In fact, he couldn't be blamed; it was because the firelight reflecting on Xu Fu’s face made him look too alluring at that moment.

If the King couldn't hold back, there were reasons for it.

Xu Fu touched the corner of his mouth in a daze.

A mouthful of bun crumbs...

He really wanted to ask if Ying Zheng felt good licking the residue, but seeing the lewd, satisfied expression on Ying Zheng’s face, Xu Fu immediately felt that he probably didn't need to ask.

At this moment, a thought suddenly popped into his head.

Never mind bun crumbs; perhaps even if he spat out some saliva, Ying Zheng would think it was fragrant? Thinking of this, Xu Fu couldn't help but shiver—it was just too... chilling!

The people in the village seemed to sing love songs when they got excited, and before long, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s attention was drawn to the singing.

There were both men and women singing.

However, Xu Fu vaguely remembered that it wasn't easy to get a girl in a village like this.

One had to know that many such villages still maintained matrilineal customs. For men, it was less like "marrying" and more like "being married into." In some places, it wasn't a rare thing for a woman to have multiple men.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu couldn't help but raise his hand to touch his face. If his looks weren't so deceptive, his status here probably wouldn't be very high either.

Ying Zheng leaned into Xu Fu’s ear and whispered, "What are they singing?"

The warm breath disturbed Xu Fu’s thoughts. Xu Fu looked away and answered absentmindedly, "Love songs."

There were many customs of singing love songs among the Seven States. In this era, singing a love song wasn't considered shocking.

"I have also heard a song..."

"Mm?" Xu Fu turned to look at him.

Ying Zheng narrowed his eyes slightly, his gaze seemingly reflected by the firelight, suddenly becoming extremely gentle.

"The grasshoppers chirp, the locusts leap;

Before I see my lord, my heart is full of sorrow.

Once I see him, once I meet him, my heart is at peace.

Climbing that southern mountain, to gather the ferns;

Before I see my lord, my heart is full of anxiety..."

When Ying Zheng first started, Xu Fu was stunned. It wasn't until he sang out in a low, slightly off-key voice that Xu Fu suddenly realized: he is singing a love song to me???

The First Emperor of Qin is singing a love song to me???

Xu Fu was a bit disoriented.

But after listening for a while, Xu Fu realized that this must be a love poem from the Book of Songs... Do you think I haven't studied the Book of Songs? Xu Fu’s focus drifted unconsciously, and he completely forgot that in the past, poems were indeed meant to be sung!

In his past life, Xu Fu had heard many love songs from singers—some mournful, some pleading, some wild and passionate... But it seemed different from this moment. He didn't know if it was because the ancient poem was too beautiful or his own aesthetic sense was too poor, but Xu Fu inexplicably felt it sounded quite good.

When performed in a low voice, it had a completely different flavor.

No one noticed their corner, or perhaps someone did, but no one would ever imagine that their King of Qin was now acting like a sycophant, leaning over to sing a love song to someone.

Ying Zheng had originally looked down on such behavior.

How could one achieve anything if they were always preoccupied with romantic love? Only now did Ying Zheng realize that the two were not in conflict; it was just that some people didn't know how to exercise restraint.

"...Once I see him, once I meet him, my heart is at peace." Ying Zheng’s voice finally faded, and Xu Fu couldn't help but feel a stir in his heart.

"Do you want to date me?" Xu Fu blurted out in a daze.

"What?" Seeing that there wasn't even a hint of being moved on Xu Fu’s face, but rather a strange question, Ying Zheng felt even more disappointed, but he still patiently continued to talk to Xu Fu.

"No, nothing." Ying Zheng’s expression was plain; how could he look like he wanted to date him? Singing the love song just now might have been the monarch’s competitive spirit at work, thinking he could sing better than others.

Besides, could you imagine the First Emperor of Qin seriously trying to date someone?

Perhaps there was someone, but it would probably be the mysterious Afang Lady from history?

chapters.title: 第145章
chapters.translated_text:
When the moon hung high in the sky, the people in the village grew increasingly excited. Here, they knew nothing of curfews.

Xu Fu, however, could not help but feel sleepy; after all, he had long since grown accustomed to the ancient routine.

Xu Fu rose to leave, and Ying Zheng naturally followed. Their movements immediately drew many gazes. A young man hurried over to Ying Zheng’s side and gestured to him.

A-Yi whispered, "He invites you, together, to sing."

Ying Zheng could sing love songs in Xu Fu’s ear, casting aside all shame.

But to have him sing a love song in front of so many people? The singing voice of the majestic King of Qin was not something just anyone could hear.

Xu Fu guessed that Ying Zheng wouldn't sing, but he didn't expect that after Ying Zheng exchanged a few gestures with the young man and the youth muttered something to him, Ying Zheng would nod before walking out with Xu Fu.

"What were you talking about?" Xu Fu couldn't help but be a little curious. His relationship with Ying Zheng was already deep enough that asking openly at this moment shouldn't cause any trouble.

"Nothing," Ying Zheng replied, tight-lipped.

This was truly rare for Ying Zheng. Xu Fu couldn't even remember when Ying Zheng had started answering his every request and question. But today, he was suddenly playing at having a little secret he couldn't share. Xu Fu felt a bit uncomfortable deep down, though he couldn't force Ying Zheng to tell him.

He pursed his lips unconsciously and returned to the room with Ying Zheng.

Outside, the sound of singing broke the silence from time to time. Before he knew it, Xu Fu had cast aside that bit of unhappiness, and after falling asleep, he rolled into Ying Zheng’s embrace.

After waking up the next day, A-Yi brought her tribespeople to see Xu Fu off. She knew Xu Fu was leaving.

"Will it be a long, long time before Junfang comes again?" A-Yi asked, feeling somewhat reluctant.

Xu Fu replied out of habit, "We shall meet again if fate allows."

A-Yi sighed like a little adult, "You, last time, said the same..."

Xu Fu patted her head, but just as he barely touched her, Hu Hai immediately crowded forward and bumped Xu Fu aside, clearly expressing his dissatisfaction and jealousy.

By comparison, Xu Fu naturally chose to go along with Hu Hai’s wishes.

Thus, after a hurried farewell to the villagers, they left immediately. As they departed, Xu Fu brought along some Sichuan peppercorns—the item A-Yi had emphasized countless times. Since it was something he wanted, he might as well take it, and Xu Fu did indeed want to study how to use it for seasoning.

It was a pity that An Niang had remained in Sanchuan; there was no skilled cook left to use it for flavoring.

Passing once more through the difficult path outside the village, Xu Fu looked back at the settlement hidden in the mountain mist and clouds. A premonition that he would return suddenly surged in his mind. However, it lasted only a split second before Xu Fu dismissed it.

Some premonitions shouldn't be dwelled upon, especially for a charlatan like himself; if he wasn't careful, he might just make them come true.

After leaving the village, Gan Tang tried very hard to make up for his mistake, but Xu Fu, considering he didn't want to take the wrong path again, cruelly rejected him.

Gan Tang’s wooden face became even more wooden.

This time, with a different guide, they did indeed arrive at the Chengdu administrative center quickly.

Their group inevitably drew the attention of others, and Li Bing happened to be on the street, so he caught sight of them at a glance.

Li Bing nearly dropped what he was holding. His attendant hurriedly asked, "Governor Li?"

"H-how could this be?" Li Bing straightened his robes, suppressed the shock and panic on his face, and quickly walked toward the city gate. By the time he approached, he had regained his composure.

Li Bing did not dare to call out "Your Majesty" directly, so he bowed and said, "My Lord."

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain, "Governor Li."

Seeing Xu Fu, Li Bing was even more surprised, though the joy on his face grew more pronounced.

He admired Xu Fu greatly and had not expected the King to bring him along as well, so he naturally could not hide his joy.

"Lead the way," Ying Zheng did not show himself, his voice coming from behind the curtain. Upon hearing this, Li Bing nodded and immediately called for his attendants.

They walked carefully in front to lead the way. The attendants were filled with curiosity, but seeing Li Bing’s cautious expression, they dared not ask. They were not the people who had been around the former governor, Chen Hui; those people had become fools following Chen Hui, but they knew how to read the room.

After leading them to the Governor’s mansion, Li Bing immediately dismissed everyone else.

"Your Majesty, Grand Master Xu," Li Bing bowed in greeting.

"No need to be so cautious. We are just here to see to what extent the water conservancy in the Shu region has been improved. The fact that the Shu region could safely survive the previous great drought in Qin is to your credit."

Being praised by the King of Qin, and specifically for his strengths, even Li Bing could not help but reveal a smile, "Thank you, Your Majesty."

Ying Zheng went with Li Bing to inspect the water conservancy projects, while Xu Fu, exhausted from the journey and unwilling to move, stayed behind.

After a short nap, he called over an attendant from the Governor’s mansion to ask about Lady Feng, only to suddenly remember that Lady Feng was not at the Chengdu administrative center.

But the attendant, having followed Li Bing for a long time, knew Lady Feng as well and immediately smiled, "Lady Feng? She left last year, perhaps she went home."

Xu Fu was slightly startled, "Is her home not here?"

"It is not. I once heard her mention it, it seems to be in Shanfu of the Qi State..."

"A person from the Qi State?"

"Probably," the attendant didn't dare to be certain and smiled awkwardly.

Xu Fu had only asked out of casual concern. The only people he knew in the Shu region were Lady Feng and Li Bing. Since Lady Feng had already left and was from the Qi State, Xu Fu naturally wouldn't ask further.

Xu Fu’s party did not stay in the Shu region for long.

Xu Fu had no old friends to visit, so once the water conservancy was inspected, it was time to leave.

Li Bing, however, was thrilled by Ying Zheng’s personal visit. He saw them out of the city and followed them for quite a distance. Just as they were about to leave the jurisdiction of Chengdu, Xu Fu discovered two statues. This time, without waiting for Gan Tang to speak, Xu Fu jumped down to take a look.

Those two statues...

One was of Li Bing, and the other... was actually his own!

Xu Fu knew that Li Bing’s statue would likely be displayed a thousand years later, and many people might come to Dujiangyan to admire his heroic posture.

But his own? That could truly not be called heroic in the slightest.

Xu Fu examined his statue from head to toe and could only say that the master responsible for the sculpture was perhaps slightly better than the one in Sanchuan.

He suppressed the urge to smash them, put on a cold face, and got back into the carriage.

The attendants, upon seeing the statues, were overjoyed, feeling a sense of reflected glory, whispering to themselves that Grand Master Xu was truly amazing!

"The statue isn't good-looking?" Ying Zheng saw through Xu Fu’s thoughts at a glance and couldn't help but speak up once he returned to the carriage.

Xu Fu shook his head and said nothing.

The ancients loved building statues to express their reverence and love so much; what kind of pillow talk would he need to use to bewitch the First Emperor into starting a trend of banning and smashing statues, following the burning of books and burying of scholars? After thinking for a long time, Xu Fu felt it was too hard to be a femme fatale.

This kind of thing... he really couldn't do it.

Better to just let it be...

If the statue is ugly, so be it. If he overdid the pillow talk and it ended up in the history books, who knows, future generations might make an even uglier one for him.

Xu Fu’s heart stirred, and he turned to Ying Zheng, "After we return to Xianyang, let’s have two statues made."

"Hmm?" Ying Zheng looked at him in confusion.

"Find the best craftsmen in the world, sculpt two statues that look exactly like us, and place them in Xianyang. If we die in the future, they can be buried with us as funerary objects."

That way, when future archaeologists dig up the tomb, they will know that statues looking like this are the truly accurate ones! Everything else is a knock-off, inferior product!

Ying Zheng didn't know what Xu Fu was thinking; he interpreted it directly as a profession of love. The contours of his face softened significantly, and he nodded, "Good."

Utterly indulgent.

Afterward, they accelerated their pace, quietly passing through several places. Only when they left did the news spread that the King of Qin had personally come to care for the people. This avoided giving enemies an opening while also burnishing his reputation.

Having experienced the great drought, the Qin State slowly recovered quite a bit during its period of recuperation.

As Xu Fu traveled along, he felt that the reason Qin could be so tenacious and eventually unify the six states was not entirely due to Ying Zheng alone.

The Qin State now had a solid foundation; even great storms could hardly topple it. Ying Zheng was indispensable to Qin, but his own arrival in Qin was merely the icing on the cake.

After much traveling, they finally returned to Xianyang.

By this time, the news of the King of Qin touring many places with a Grand Diviner had already spread throughout the Qin State.

The King of Qin had originally been cold and aloof. Because of Qin’s strict laws, the commoners feared those in power, and as for the King of Qin... if he were to walk before them, they would surely prostrate themselves in worship. The spread of this news gave the commoners a different feeling.

It was as if they suddenly realized that the high and mighty King of Qin also cared about them.

Compared to other states, we are truly so fortunate, so fortunate.

This will not be elaborated upon further.

When they returned to Xianyang, Wei Liao was the first to greet them. If not for Ying Zheng being by his side, he would have already rushed to Xu Fu regardless of anything else. Even so, Wei Liao let everyone see how much he valued this junior brother. His burning gaze silently confronted Ying Zheng’s cold one, leaving the other ministers confused.

This Wei Liao... he held quite a bit of power while in Xianyang! Why is he still dissatisfied with the King? Talented people are truly excessively arrogant!

Some thought with displeasure.

Turning around, the ministers fully expressed their longing for Ying Zheng, wishing they could kneel at his feet.

Waiting for him was not easy...

With Zhao Gao, Li Si, and Wei Liao controlling the government, the other ministers couldn't help but be envious. If these three weren't all formidable characters, these people would have caused a scene long ago. The reason Ying Zheng made such arrangements when he left was to have these three suppress the ministers while keeping each other in check. At the same time, it was a means to push talented people even higher.

These three were not without ambition; once given the chance, they would try their best to control people and things in their own hands.

Ying Zheng surveyed the crowd, then lowered the carriage curtain, signaling for the carriage to continue forward.

The ministers quickly stepped aside. They had come forward to greet him with the intention of showing favor, and naturally, they wouldn't be so tactless as to continue following the carriage.

Only Wei Liao frowned, not very happy.

He hadn't even had a chance to say a word to his junior brother before he was taken away...

Seeing that his junior brother’s birthday was approaching, he wondered what the King of Qin intended to do this time?

Ying Zheng had always kept Xu Fu’s birthday in mind; how could he forget? Since the capping ceremony arranged earlier had been missed, he would simply make up for it on his birthday.

On the very day they returned to the palace, news spread that Grand Master Xu was to have his capping ceremony.

Although the officials in Xianyang held Xu Fu in high regard, that didn't mean they would attach much importance to his capping ceremony.

Instead, because of the talk of the capping ceremony, everyone suddenly realized that this kid hadn't even been capped yet? A person who hadn't even been capped had actually reached the position of Grand Master! Thinking of this, it was truly terrifying; his future was bound to be immeasurable.

As for whether this was in line with the rules, thinking of the King of Qin who ascended the throne at a young age, did they dare to say anything more?

Xu Fu’s capping ceremony was not something for the children Fusu and Hu Hai to worry about; they naturally ate and slept as they pleased.

After resting for two days, Xu Fu went to the Grand Master’s Temple.

Having not been to the temple for a long time, it was being well-managed by Wang Liu and Su Yi. Both had high status and backgrounds, and their positions had been adjusted to very high levels, ranking just below Xu Fu.

The entire temple was jealous of the two of them.

Having a superior like Xu Fu was truly convenient. They never had to worry about their credit being stolen because Xu Fu didn't care; they didn't have to worry about being pushed out by their superior’s relatives because Xu Fu’s relatives were all very capable; they didn't have to worry about their influence being suppressed because Xu Fu was often away, allowing the two of them to hold great power... how delightful...

Everyone finally understood. Look at how Wang Liu fared when he opposed Xu Fu before? Look at him now, following Su Yi and keeping close to Xu Fu’s footsteps; isn't he living better than all of them? These people lamented, regretting that they hadn't discovered Xu Fu’s value earlier.

And so, on this day...

As soon as Xu Fu stepped into the Grand Master’s Temple, he was met with burning gazes from all around.

Xu Fu didn't find this strange. Over the past few years, he had enjoyed the worship of the common people; what was this bit of enthusiasm? It was far from comparable to those people.

Xu Fu walked inside with a calm expression.

Those who had gathered their courage, intending to leave a good impression on the long-absent Xu Fu, were stunned and couldn't help but feel a bit discouraged.

It wasn't easy for them to set aside their pride to curry favor.

They sighed softly and slowly followed him in.

Su Yi and Wang Liu, hearing that Xu Fu had arrived, immediately set aside their work. The affairs in the temple were complex but not overly significant, and with their high status, they didn't need to worry about every little thing.

"Grand Master," the two bowed respectfully before Xu Fu.

Xu Fu looked them over.

Su Yi hadn't changed much, but Wang Liu’s temperament had become more restrained, unlike before when he gave off an arrogant and playboy vibe at first glance.

"The temple is about to conduct the end-of-month divination. Would the Grand Master like to preside over it personally?" Su Yi asked.

Xu Fu had no great interest in this, so he waved his hand and tossed a few bamboo slips he had brought back from the Di-Qiang village in Shu to them, "If you are interested, take a look." Xu Fu didn't know if the contents of these slips came from Guigu, but some things on them were extremely interesting, and even bore similarities to some things he had learned in his later life.

For the people in the temple, there should still be much to learn.

Well, this could also be considered fulfilling the old Grand Diviner’s last wish, letting the people in the temple learn more.

After dropping the bamboo slips, Xu Fu didn't stay long before preparing to leave.

Because he had been away from the temple for so long, it was indeed difficult for him to sit quietly there for a long time now. Hu Hai was at the age where he was gradually developing his own consciousness, so he might as well return to the palace and teach Hu Hai how to be a charlatan. The more he thought about it, the more Xu Fu felt he wasn't suited for the position of Grand Master.

He was indeed often derelict in his duties, running around outside, which didn't look very proper for a Grand Master.

Since Su Yi and Wang Liu were managing the temple well, he might as well ask Ying Zheng for a favor and let one of them become the Grand Master.

Thinking this, Xu Fu looked at Su Yi and Wang Liu again.

Both felt uncomfortable under his gaze, so Su Yi spoke first.

"Is the Grand Master going to have his capping ceremony?"

Some people in the temple had heard that Xu Fu hadn't had his capping ceremony yet, and their words were full of sourness! They truly couldn't compare to Xu Fu’s abilities.

After blushing, Su Yi and Wang Liu quickly accepted it calmly.

They had seen Xu Fu’s abilities many times; how could they still join these people in doubting him?

...

Xu Fu nodded, "That is correct."

Su Yi said thoughtfully, "Where will the Grand Master hold his capping ceremony? If you don't mind, please let Wang Liu and me know the location, and we will definitely rush there." Although Su Yi’s relationship with Xu Fu wasn't as intimate as before due to their lack of meetings, his feelings toward Xu Fu hadn't changed. Setting aside their superior-subordinate status, Su Yi wanted to go as a friend.

Xu Fu hesitated.

Ying Zheng said he would handle the capping ceremony personally, and he truly didn't know where it would be held.

Xu Fu told the truth, "I don't know either."

Su Yi was astonished, "The Grand Master doesn't know either?"

Xu Fu shook his head.

Wang Liu, standing to the side, felt he had discovered some truth and asked hesitantly, "Is the Grand Master’s capping ceremony not being held outside the palace?"

Su Yi was also startled upon hearing Wang Liu’s question.

Not even holding the capping ceremony outside the palace?

This...

Could it be that the King now treats Grand Master Xu as a member of the royal family? Otherwise, who could hold a capping ceremony in the royal palace? He didn't know what the ministers in the court would think then. Su Yi’s habit of worrying flared up again. He couldn't help but think that Grand Master Xu was becoming more and more important in the King’s eyes...

Would this growing favor eventually become a sharp arrow that kills Grand Master Xu?

Su Yi thought to himself for a long time, finally deciding in his heart: if that day ever came, he would protect him out of gratitude for Grand Master Xu’s kindness.

Xu Fu had no idea what kind of messy thoughts were going through Su Yi’s mind in this short time.

Wang Liu said with a complex expression, "The King’s treatment of the Grand Master must be sincere." If it were his old self, he would definitely have looked down on Xu Fu’s situation. But now, his thinking had broadened significantly.

Su Yi, standing to the side, strongly disagreed with Wang Liu’s words, but he said nothing. Wang Liu was thinking so naively, but he shouldn't expose him...

From the gazes and expressions of the past two days, Xu Fu could roughly tell that the two had different thoughts, but their concern was the same. Xu Fu found it amusing and softened his expression, "If possible, I will invite you both."

If it were truly in the royal palace, Xu Fu naturally couldn't act recklessly and would have to discuss it with Ying Zheng first.

Su Yi nodded and sent Xu Fu off with emotion.

Wang Liu looked at him coldly, "Were you dissatisfied with what I said just now?"

"Not dissatisfied, just worried about Grand Master Xu..."

"What is there to worry about? Look at how things are now; the King is clearly deeply affectionate toward Grand Master Xu..."

"What if he is deeply affectionate? Think of Lord Longyang back then..."

Wang Liu interrupted him, "How can they be compared? As expected, nothing can be explained to a fool like you. You don't understand anything about matters of the heart, yet you can spout nonsense so casually..."

Su Yi, who was still single and had just been mocked, opened his mouth but had no rebuttal, so he closed it.

Xu Fu didn't know his love life had become the fuse for others' arguments. After leaving the temple, he first went to visit Wei Liao.

Although he didn't like Wei Liao in the past, Wei Liao was just stubborn in certain aspects, just as he himself was persistent about his own divination. Wei Liao had always insisted on what he saw from Ying Zheng’s physiognomy. Now that Wei Liao was his senior brother, he treated him quite well, so even for the sake of the original body, he couldn't be too indifferent to him.

When he arrived at Wei Liao’s mansion, Wei Liao hadn't returned from court yet.

However, the people in the mansion already knew Xu Fu and immediately welcomed him in, with great respect and extra attentiveness.

After sitting down, Xu Fu noticed that Wei Liao’s mansion seemed as lonely as ever.

Xu Fu couldn't help but ask in a low voice, "In the days I was away, did Senior Brother not even have a confidante?"

The servant smiled, "The State Minister has no interest in such matters."

Xu Fu said with a cold face, "Could it be that Senior Brother prefers men?"

Wei Liao happened to step in from outside the mansion and his face darkened upon hearing this, "It’s been a long time, and this is how you talk about your Senior Brother behind his back?"

Xu Fu stood up, not feeling guilty at all, "Senior Brother." That wasn't an insult; he was genuinely curious.

Seeing his polite demeanor, Wei Liao felt a bit better inside.

Finally, he felt a bit like a senior brother...

Having a junior brother who was always losing his memory was truly frustrating...

Wei Liao’s expression shifted before he sat down opposite Xu Fu.

He smiled slightly, and although his usually stern face showed some wrinkles when he smiled, "Junior Brother, since you are having your capping ceremony and are not in Guigu, how about I preside over it for you?"

Capping ceremonies required a virtuous and respected elder to preside. Although Wei Liao was an elder, Xu Fu felt from the bottom of his heart that he couldn't be associated with the words "virtuous and respected" for the time being.

"This... I can't decide this," Xu Fu naturally shifted the blame onto Ying Zheng.

Wei Liao’s face immediately darkened, but since the other person was the King of Qin, he had to swallow his complaints.

"But Senior Brother can watch me get capped." Xu Fu paused, as if he hadn't noticed Wei Liao’s displeasure at all, and whispered, "Is Senior Brother unwilling?"

"...Naturally, I am willing!" Wei Liao replied.

Xu Fu nodded, "That’s good. I haven't been back to Xianyang for a long time, so I came to see you today. Seeing that you have become plump recently, I feel at ease."

Become plump recently???

Wei Liao was stunned, feeling a bit hit.

But after careful consideration, he felt the concern behind Xu Fu’s words.

Wasn't his junior brother always like this? Upright and not good with words. The "plump" he mentioned definitely didn't mean he was calling him fat; he was simply expressing concern.

Wei Liao raised his hand, covering his chest slightly, feeling moved.

Xu Fu glanced outside the hall; it was getting late.

"Senior Brother, I will take my leave then. I’m a bit hungry." Xu Fu clearly expressed his intention to return to the palace for a meal.

Wei Liao didn't stop him and immediately saw him out personally.

Watching Xu Fu’s figure walk away, Wei Liao, who had finally received some concern from his junior brother, couldn't recover for a long time. My junior brother treats me well... it’s just that the King of Qin loves to whisper in his ear, which makes my junior brother treat me coldly. Wei Liao sighed softly and returned to the mansion.

...

It is evident there are three types of people in the world who are easiest to coax.

One, a stupid son; two, the King of Qin; three, two senior brothers.

·

Before they knew it, the day of Xu Fu’s capping ceremony arrived. The ministers didn't take it to heart, only receiving the invitation after they had finished their duties.

The capping ceremony was to be held in the Xianyang Palace.

In that instant, the ministers thought their eyes were failing, or they were dizzy, or hard of hearing... it must be their own problem, not the King of Qin’s.

But unfortunately, after they sobered up, they found it was true—the capping ceremony was indeed in the Xianyang Palace, and of course, it wasn't for the two young princes, but for Grand Master Xu...

He is just a Grand Master, just an official of the Qin State like us; how could he be treated like this by the King of Qin?

At this moment, Li Si, who had received the news, finally realized something.

No matter how capable he was under the King, he would never reach the height Xu Fu held in the King’s heart in this lifetime.

Thinking back to the past, he had hoped for special treatment from the King... he was truly naive.

But this was enough. In the Qin State, there was only one Xu Fu, and wasn't there only one Li Si? The special treatment he received under the King was already infinitely better than before.

The ministers had different thoughts, but finally, forced by the majesty of the King of Qin, they had to come to the palace.

The palace attendants were quite enthusiastic toward them today, and they felt a complex mix of emotions.

At this time, Xu Fu, sitting up from his bed, also felt quite complex. In his previous life, not many people valued coming-of-age ceremonies. At that time, coming of age for many just meant losing shackles and being able to do things they couldn't before. For Xu Fu, the concept was even thinner. After all, as an orphan, he had no parents, only a sect, and there were many orphans in the sect; who would remember his birthday? Xu Fu didn't care about it anyway, and his eighteenth birthday had passed in a blur.

He never expected that after coming to the Qin State, he would experience the feeling of coming of age.

The palace attendants helped Xu Fu put on his robes; these robes were different from those worn after coming of age.

And the ceremonial cap was something Ying Zheng would put on Xu Fu himself later.

Although Ying Zheng was not happy about Xu Fu appearing before everyone in just a deep robe, considering this was part of the ritual, Ying Zheng could let his own capping ceremony be ruined, but Xu Fu was different; he could not tolerate a single step going wrong.

After the attendants dressed him, Ying Zheng stood to the side, watching Xu Fu intently.

This robe made him look even more slender, making him look like he hadn't come of age yet, with a youthful air that made Ying Zheng feel a bit itchy.

Afterward, Ying Zheng withdrew his gaze and left first for the garden of the Xianyang Palace.

This garden was huge, perfect for the capping ceremony.

Besides, for Xu Fu, there were no ancestors or spirits to worship.

Subsequently, Xu Fu followed the attendants slowly to the garden.

The ministers watched Xu Fu walk over with a calm expression, their feelings extremely complex. They didn't know why, but they always felt this scene was like the King of Qin crowning a Queen...

Thinking of this, the ministers shuddered, and hurriedly shook their heads to cast the thought away.

They steadied themselves and forced themselves to watch the ceremony carefully.

They looked at Xu Fu’s usual cold expression and muttered to themselves. No wonder this kid was young yet highly favored by the King; even in a place like this, he could maintain his composure—he was truly unflappable in the face of honor or disgrace.

Ying Zheng, like the ministers, stared fixedly at Xu Fu. When he noticed the ministers watching intently, he felt a bit unhappy.

He knew that Xu Fu shouldn't have been let out looking like this...

Besides himself, there were so many people who could appreciate the beauty on him at the same time.

Ying Zheng suppressed the restless emotions in his chest and revealed a smile. The ministers were all focused on Xu Fu and didn't notice the doting look on their King’s face, which was truly abnormal. If they had known, they would have been on high alert.

At this time, the ministers were still thinking that although Xu Fu could have his capping ceremony in the palace, so what? When Lord Longyang was favored, what capricious and absurd things hadn't happened? Compared to that, this was nothing.

...

Xu Fu’s expression drifted slightly.

Not to mention the ministers' wild imaginations, he himself felt it was a bit strange. He looked, no matter how he looked at it, like a bride holding her skirt, shyly walking toward the groom...

Xu Fu shuddered secretly.

Finally, he reached Ying Zheng.

Both sat on their heels, facing each other. Ying Zheng looked at him with burning eyes, and Xu Fu, who had always been thick-skinned, didn't avoid his gaze. At first glance, the two looked like they were gazing deeply at each other, but because of the angle, the ministers didn't see the illicit affair within.

Ying Zheng gently placed the prepared cap on his head, reciting the blessings for the capping ceremony.

Wei Liao, seeing this, was quite jealous.

It was a pity it wasn't him...

Not long after, Ying Zheng removed the cap from Xu Fu’s head.

Everyone watched this scene, with faint guesses in their hearts, but they dared not be sure. Because it was truly hard to believe.

But the fact was, Ying Zheng did indeed take a more magnificent cap from the attendants and placed it on Xu Fu’s head again.

Xu Fu only vaguely remembered that when Ying Zheng had his capping ceremony, it was the same, repeating the capping several times, each more valuable than the last. But he didn't know the difference. Several cappings showed how deep the blessings the person presiding had for the youth.

Only someone like Ying Zheng dared to do this several times; who else dared to surpass him?

But what was going on with Xu Fu now... making it so grand, so grand that the ministers were blocked in their hearts and couldn't speak for a long time.

Ying Zheng seemed unaware of these gazes and continued to act as he pleased.

As the cap on Xu Fu’s head was changed again, the ministers felt their hearts were about to burst.

Even the King of Wei hadn't given Lord Longyang a capping ceremony. The ministers, unable to continue making comparisons, felt a bit panicked.

Fortunately, Ying Zheng didn't go too far, and by the third cap, he stopped changing them.

Everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

Ying Zheng, with an unhappy expression, removed Xu Fu’s outer robe and replaced it with adult robes. His movements were extremely fast, almost leaving no chance for others to see Xu Fu in just his deep robe.

Xu Fu’s black hair was tied up by the cap, and with the magnificent and exquisite robes on his body, plus his temperament which was already a cut above others, if someone said he was a member of the Qin royal family, no one would dare not believe it.

Ying Zheng looked at Xu Fu’s hair with a hint of obsession.

If not for the many ministers present, he probably wouldn't have wanted to let go.

Finally, Ying Zheng said, "His courtesy name shall be Junfang."

Everyone hurriedly offered their congratulations.

After the courtesy name was given, it was finally over.

However, everyone repeating the name "Junfang" felt it was exceptionally familiar, but they couldn't recall it for a long time. It wasn't until the palace attendants sent them out of the palace that the ministers suddenly realized.

Xu Junfang.

Wasn't that the name that had spread from Guigu long ago?

The ministers looked at Wei Liao with displeasure.

Wei Liao chuckled, "What? Is my junior brother not worthy of such a capping ceremony?"

"No, no, he is worthy, he is worthy!" the ministers endured the pain and said against their will.

月上中天时，寨中的人越发激动起来。在这里，宵禁不知为何物。
不过徐福倒是难免困倦起来了，毕竟他早已习惯古代的作息了。
徐福起身要走，嬴政自然跟从，而他们的动作顿时便吸引了不少的目光，有青年快步跑到嬴政的身边，与他比划了一番。
阿咿小声说：“他请你，一起，唱歌。”
嬴政能在徐福耳边低唱情歌，抛却一切羞耻。
但让他在这么多人跟前唱情歌？堂堂秦王的歌声，倒不是谁都能听的。
徐福猜到嬴政不会唱，但他没料到，嬴政和那青年比划了一下，青年叽叽咕咕跟嬴政说了什么，嬴政点了点头，这才同徐福一起往外走。
“你们在说什么？”徐福难免有些好奇，他与嬴政的关系已经足够深厚，这个时候大大方方问出来，想来也不会有什么妨碍。
“无事。”嬴政却守口如瓶。
这放在嬴政的身上实在太少见了。徐福都不记得从何时开始，嬴政在他跟前便是有求必应、有问必答的了。但今日却突然间玩起了不能告诉你的小秘密。徐福心底有点硌得难受，不过他也不能强制嬴政告诉自己。
他不自觉地抿了抿唇，和嬴政回了屋子。
外面还有歌声时不时地打破寂静，徐福不知不觉间，倒是将那点儿不快抛开了，睡着后还滚入了嬴政的怀抱中。
第二日醒来后，阿咿便带着族人前来送徐福了。她知道徐福要走了。
“会很久、很久，君房再来吗？”阿咿有些不舍地问。
徐福还是惯性地说了一句，“有缘再会。”
阿咿像小大人似的叹了口气，“你，上次，也这样……”
徐福摸了摸她的头，才不过蜻蜓点水一下，胡亥便立即凑上前来，将徐福给撞到一边去了，很明显地表达了自己争风吃醋的不满。
相比之下，徐福当然选择更顺着胡亥的意思。
于是匆匆和寨中人打过招呼后，他们便立时离开了，走的时候，徐福还带上了一点花椒，那是阿咿强调了无数次，他要的东西，既然是他要的，那就带上好了，而徐福也的确想研究一下，怎么用这个东西来入味儿。
只可惜安娘留在了三川，倒是没有手艺好的厨子用它来入味了。
再一次从寨子外面艰难的小路上走过，徐福回头看了一眼那隐藏在山林云雾间的寨子，脑子里突然涌出了还会再回来的预感。不过也就瞬间的功夫，随即便被徐福打消了。
有些预感是不能瞎想的，尤其是自己这种神棍，说不好便想成真了。
离开寨子之后，甘棠便很努力地想要挽回自己的错误，但是徐福出于不想再走一次错路的考量，残酷地拒绝了他。
甘棠那张木头脸再次变得更木头了。
而这一次换了引路人，他们也的确很快抵达了成都治所。
他们这一行人难免引起了旁人的注目，而李冰恰巧便在街头，于是刚好一眼就看见了。
李冰差点砸了手中的东西，他身旁的随从忙道：“李郡守？”
“怎、怎么会？”李冰理了理衣袍，压下面上的震惊、慌张，抬脚迅速朝着城门的方向而去。就在他快要走近的时候，他已经恢复镇定了。
李冰并不敢直接口呼“王上”，遂只拜了拜，出声道：“主上。”
徐福掀起车帘，“李郡守。”
见着徐福，李冰更加惊讶，不过面上的喜色倒是更为浓厚了。
他极为欣赏徐福，不曾想到王上会将他也带过来，自然难掩喜色。
“带路吧。”嬴政并未露面，他的声音从车帘后传了出来。李冰听见后，点了点头，当即便叫来了随从。
他们小心地走在前面带路，随从心中好奇不已，但见李冰面色慎重，又不敢多问。他们可不是曾经的郡守陈会身边的人，那些人跟着陈会变成了蠢货，而他们却是极会看眼色的。
将人引到郡守府中后，李冰便立即屏退了左右。
“王上，徐奉常。”李冰躬身见礼。
“不用如此小心，我们只是过来瞧一瞧，如今蜀地水利被改善到何等地步了，之前秦国大旱，蜀地能安然度过，是你的本事。”
被秦王夸奖，又恰好是夸在自己的长处上，饶是李冰也忍不住露出了笑意，“多谢王上。”
嬴政与李冰前去视察水利工程，徐福路途劳累不愿再动，便留了下来。
他睡了个小觉起来，将郡守府的随从叫过来，问了问凤姑娘，等问完徐福才骤然想起，凤姑娘可不在成都治所。
但那随从毕竟是跟随李冰许久的人，他也是认识凤姑娘的，当即便笑道：“凤姑娘啊，去岁便离去了，许是回家了吧。”
徐福微微一怔，“她家不在此处吗？”
“不在的，从前曾听她说起过，像是在齐国单父……”
“齐国人？”
“大约是吧。”那随从也不敢一口咬定，尴尬地笑了笑。
徐福本也只是随口关心一下，他在蜀地认识的人，便也就凤姑娘和李冰了，既然凤姑娘已经离去，又为齐国人，徐福自然也不会再多问。
徐福一行人并未在蜀地停留多久。
徐福没什么认识的旧友要见，等水利瞧完之后，自然便该离去了。
倒是李冰对嬴政亲自前来的举动激动不已，李冰将他们送出城，还一路跟了不短的路。快要出成都治所范围的时候，徐福又发现了两座塑像。这次不消甘棠开口说，徐福已经先跳下去查看了。
那两座塑像……
一座乃是李冰的，而另一座……竟然是自己的！
徐福知道李冰的塑像还很有可能在千年后展出，可能会有不少人到都江堰来欣赏他的英姿。
而自己的呢？那可当真是半点英姿也谈不上。
徐福将自己的塑像从头打量到脚，只能说这个负责雕塑的师傅，水平约莫比三川的高一点。
他按捺住体内想要打碎他们的冲动，冷着脸又上了车。
侍从们见了塑像，却是欢喜不已，颇有种与有荣焉的感觉，嘴里默默念叨着，徐奉常就是厉害！
“那塑像不好看？”嬴政一眼就看出了徐福的心思，等他回到马车中，便不由得出声道。
徐福摇了摇头并不说话。
古人这么喜欢修塑像来表达自己的崇敬爱意，他得怎么样吹枕头风，才能蛊惑秦始皇，在继焚书坑儒之后，掀起禁塑像、砸塑像的风潮呢？想了半天，徐福觉得祸水太难当了。
这种事儿……他还真干不来。
还是歇一歇吧……
塑像丑就丑吧，万一他吹枕头风吹过头了，都吹上史书了，后世说不准还有人给他做更丑的塑像。
徐福心中一动，转头对嬴政道：“等回咸阳后，我们去修两个塑像。”
“嗯？”嬴政疑惑地看向他。
“寻天下最好的手艺匠人，塑两樽与我们极为相似的塑像，立于咸阳，假若日后我们死了，也就当做陪葬品一起埋了。”
这样等后世挖到坟墓的时候，那些考古学家们就会知道，长这个样子的塑像，才是真正无误的塑像！其它全是山寨的伪劣品！
嬴政不知徐福心中想的什么，他很直接地将这领会成了情话，脸上的轮廓顿时柔和了不少，他点头，“好。”
极尽纵容。
之后他们便加快了进程，悄然地走过数个地方，直等到他们离去时，才传出秦王亲至关怀百姓的消息，这样免得给敌人空子钻，一方面倒也全了名声。
经历过大旱之后的秦国，在休养生息的过程中，慢慢恢复了不少。
徐福一路行来，感觉就是，秦国能如此顽强，最终统一六国，也并不全是因为有嬴政一人。
如今的秦国已经有足够的基础了，大风大浪都难以摧垮它。嬴政是秦国不可缺少的，但自己来到秦国，就是来锦上添花的。
在外折腾许久后，他们终于回到了咸阳。
此时秦王带着一太卜巡走多处的消息，俨然传遍了秦国。
秦王原本是冷酷又高高在上的，因着秦国刑法严峻，平民们便更是畏惧秦国有权势的人，至于秦王……若是走到他们跟前，他们肯定都是要顶礼膜拜的。这番消息一传出去，倒是令这些平民百姓，心头多了点儿别样的滋味。
就好像突然间知道，高高在上的秦王也是会关心我们的。
与他国相比，我们真是好幸福啊好幸福。
此处不再赘述。
他们回到咸阳时，尉缭一马当先，若非有嬴政在侧，他已经不管不顾先扑到徐福跟前去了，不过尽管如此，尉缭也让所有人见识到了，他对这个师弟的看重，那灼热的目光，与嬴政冰冷的目光默默对抗着，让其余大臣看得一头雾水。
这尉缭……留在咸阳时手头的权利可不少！如今怎的还对王上不满意呢？这有才华的人，还当真倨傲得过分！
有人心头不快地想道。
转过头来，大臣们便对着嬴政充分表达出了心中的思念之情，就恨不得跪在嬴政的脚边了。
等到他，不容易啊……
朝中赵高、李斯、尉缭三人把持朝政，其他大臣看得久了，难免不眼红啊。若非这三个谁也不是善茬，这些人早便闹起来了。当初走时，嬴政之所以做这样的安排，便也是为了让这三人压住朝臣，但又互相牵制。同时，也是将有才之人往上推得更高的手段。
这三个人，都并非没有野心的人，一旦给他们机会，他们便会竭力地将人和物都掌控在自己手中。
嬴政环视一眼众人，这才放下车帘，示意马车继续向前。
大臣们迅速退开，他们上前来迎接，本意只是在嬴政面前表个殷勤罢了，之后当然不会不识相地继续跟着马车。
只有尉缭不大高兴地皱了皱眉。
还没来得及和师弟说上一句话，就把人给带走了……
眼瞧着师弟的生辰又要到了，也不知这一次，那秦王又欲如何？
嬴政一直牢记着徐福的生辰，怎会忘记？既然之前安排好的加冠礼错过了，那便在生辰日补上就是。
就在他们回宫的当日，便传出了徐奉常要行加冠礼的消息。
咸阳城中的官员虽然对徐福高看一眼，但并不代表徐福行个加冠礼，就能让他们如何重视了。
反倒是因为加冠礼之说，众人才骤然发觉，这小子竟然还未加冠？一个还未加冠的人，竟然就坐到了奉常的位置！如此一想，着实有些可怕啊，其未来，必然是不可估量的。
至于这合不合乎规矩，想一想年少即位的秦王，他们还敢多说什么吗？
徐福要行冠礼，轮不到扶苏和胡亥俩小孩儿去操心，他们自然吃吃睡睡，该如何便是如何。
徐福休息两日后，便到奉常寺中去了。
许久未到奉常寺，奉常寺中被王柳和苏邑打理得不错，王柳和苏邑的出身地位都不低，如今位置也被调动到了极高的位置，仅仅屈居徐福之下。
奉常寺上下对他二人嫉妒不已。
有徐福这样一个上司实在太省事，他们丝毫不用担忧被抢功，因为徐福根本不屑；他们不用担心被上司的亲戚给挤掉位置，因为徐福的亲戚都很厉害；他们不用担心自己势力受到压制，因为徐福常不在奉常寺中，他们二人反倒能揽得大权……好不快意……
众人终于明白过来，你且看从前王柳与徐福作对时，可讨到什么好了？再看他如今，跟着苏邑一起，紧跟徐福脚步，如今岂不是比他们都过得好？这些人扼腕不已，只恨当初没能发现徐福身上的宝贵之处。
于是这一日……
徐福一跨进奉常寺中，便享受到了四周投来的灼热目光。
徐福对此并不觉得陌生，这几年，他可是享尽了百姓的膜拜，这点热切算什么？还远不能与那些百姓相比呢。
徐福神色平淡地往里走。
这些鼓足气打算在久不见的徐福心中留个好印象的人，都呆了呆，心头难免有些沮丧。
