要他们放下矜持去讨好人，也是不容易了。
他们轻叹一口气，慢慢跟了进去。
此时苏邑和王柳听闻徐福进门来了，立即搁下了手头的事务。如今奉常寺中事务只是繁杂，但却算不得多么重大，他们地位不低，当然不需事事操心了。
“奉常。”两人恭敬地在徐福跟前见了礼。
徐福打量了他们一眼。
苏邑并无多少变化，不过王柳身上的气质逐渐内敛起来了，不似从前那样，第一眼便给人倨傲纨绔的感觉。
“奉常寺中正要进行月末卜筮，奉常可要亲自主持？”苏邑出声问。
徐福对此并无多大兴致，于是摆了摆手，顺手还将从蜀地氐羌寨中带回来的竹简扔了几个给他们，“你们若有兴致，便看一看。”徐福也不知这些竹简上的内容，是否来自鬼谷，不过上面有些东西极为有趣，甚至还与后世他曾学过的某些东西，颇有相似之处。
对于奉常寺中人，应该还有的学。
唔，这也算是应了老太卜的遗愿吧，让奉常寺中人学到更多的东西。
将竹简扔下之后，徐福待了没多久便准备离开。
因为离开奉常寺太久，他如今的确很难安静在奉常寺坐上许久了。如今胡亥正是渐渐拥有自己意识的时候，他还不如回宫中教胡亥如何成为一个神棍。越想徐福便越觉得自己不大适合奉常一职。
他确实常常失职，整个人都常在外跑来跑去，作为奉常实在有些不大像样。
左右苏邑和王柳将奉常寺管理得也不错，还不如干脆在嬴政跟前求个人情，便让他们中间一人来做奉常好了。
如此想着，徐福便再度打量起了苏邑和王柳。
二人都被打量得有些不自在，于是苏邑先开了口。
“奉常要行冠礼？”
奉常寺中有些人听闻徐福还未行冠礼，开口好不酸气！他们的确谁都比不上徐福的本事。
苏邑和王柳二人脸红过后，很快便坦然接受了。
徐福的本事如何，他们已经见过许多，怎会再同这些人一起怀疑徐福？
……
徐福点了点头，“不错。”
苏邑若有所思道：“奉常在何处行冠礼，若不嫌弃，便请奉常届时告知我与王柳地点，我们二人定会赶去。”苏邑虽然与徐福之间，因为少在奉常寺见面而不如从前姿态亲密，但他与徐福的关系倒并未变过。抛开上下级的身份，苏邑很想作为朋友前去。
徐福迟疑了一下。
嬴政说冠礼他一手负责，自己还当真不知晓届时会在何处举行。
徐福说了实话，“我也不知晓。”
苏邑惊讶不已，“奉常也不知晓吗？”
徐福摇了摇头。
王柳在一旁觉得自己似乎发现了什么真相，他迟疑着问道：“奉常的加冠礼并非在宫外举行？”
苏邑听见王柳问出口的话，也惊了一跳。
连加冠礼也不在宫外举行？
这……
难道王上如今都是将徐奉常看作王室中人对待了吗？不然谁能在王宫中举行冠礼？届时也不知朝中大臣会如何作想。苏邑操心的毛病又犯了。心中还忍不住想了起来，如今徐奉常在王上眼中越来越重要……
一日胜过一日的宠爱，到了日后是否会成为害死徐奉常的利箭呢？
苏邑暗自想了许久，最终在心中道。若真有那一日，自己也要瞧在徐奉常的恩义上，护一护他。
徐福全然不知道，在这短短的时间内，苏邑脑子里都想了些什么乱七八糟的东西。
王柳神色复杂道：“王上待奉常，想来是真心的。”若是换做以前的自己，定然是瞧不上徐福的处境。但如今，却思维开阔了许多。
一旁的苏邑十分不同意王柳的话，但苏邑什么也没说。王柳想得如此天真，但自己还是不要戳穿他了吧……
徐福从这两天的目光和表情，便能大约知道，这二人的想法是不一致的，不过关心的意思倒是一致的。徐福心中觉得好笑，便将脸上的神色放得和缓了些，“若有可能，我便邀你二人前来。”
若是当真在王宫中，徐福自然是不能乱来的，届时还得与嬴政说过才知。
苏邑点头，感慨地将徐福送了出去。
王柳冷眼看着他，“你方才对我的话有所不满？”
“并无不满，只是心中担忧徐奉常……”
“有何担忧的？瞧如今的模样，王上分明对徐奉常十分情深……”
“情深又如何？想当初那龙阳君……”
王柳打断了他，“他们怎能放在一起比较？果然与你这傻子，什么也说不通，自己于感情之事半分不通，倒也能随意开口放谬论了……”
被嘲讽了一脸的至今还单身的苏邑张了张嘴，无从反驳地闭了嘴。
徐福不知自己的感情生活已经成为别人吵架的导火索了，他出了奉常寺后，先去拜访了尉缭。
虽然以前他的确不喜欢尉缭此人，但是尉缭只是某些方面固执了点儿，正如自己对自己的卦象十分坚持一样，尉缭也始终坚持他从嬴政面相上观得的东西。如今尉缭身为他的师兄，待他的确不错，就算是为了原身，他也不能对待尉缭太过漠然。
他到尉缭府上的时候，尉缭还未散朝归来。
不过府中人早已认识徐福，当即便将他迎了进去，而且是极为恭敬的，分外殷勤的。
徐福落座以后，才发觉到尉缭的府上似乎还是那样寂寥。
徐福忍不住低声问：“我不在的日子里，师兄连个红颜也无吗？”
下人笑道：“国尉对此道并无兴致。”
徐福用清冷的面孔，吐出一句话来，“难道师兄好男风？”
尉缭恰好从府外跨进来，闻言脸色免不了黑了黑，“许久不见，你便是如此在背后言及师兄的？”
徐福站起身来，半点也不心虚，“师兄。”那话又不是骂人的，他是当真好奇罢了。
尉缭见着他彬彬有礼的模样，心底这才舒服了些。
总算有了点儿当师兄的感觉……
有个总是失忆的师弟实在太糟心了……
尉缭的脸色变幻了一番，然后才在徐福的对面落座。
他微微笑了，虽然平日里严肃的脸，突然笑起来，还带出了点儿褶子，“师弟，此次你加冠，不在鬼谷，那便由我来为你主持加冠如何？”
加冠礼都需要德高望重的长辈主持，尉缭虽为长辈，但徐福打心里觉得，他暂时跟德高望重四字是扯不上的。
“这……此事我难做主。”徐福很自然地将这个锅推到了嬴政的头上。
而尉缭的脸色立时便黑了，但人家是秦王，他满腹牢骚也只能憋着。
“不过届时师兄可以瞧着我加冠了。”徐福顿了顿，像是根本没发现尉缭的不快一样，低声道：“难道师兄不愿吗？”
“……自然是愿的！”尉缭应道。
徐福点点头，“那便好，我许久未回咸阳，因而今日特来见师兄一面，见师兄近日身材丰腴，那我便觉心安了。”
近日身材丰腴？？？
尉缭呆了呆，有点受打击。
但是细细斟酌一番，他感受到了其中徐福的关怀意味。
师弟不是一向如此吗？为人耿直，不善言辞，他所说的丰腴，定然不是嫌师兄我胖，他只是单纯的关心而已。
尉缭抬起手，微微捂住胸口，心中感动不已。
徐福往厅堂外瞧了一眼，时辰不早了。
“师兄，那我便告辞了，我有些饿了。”徐福很明确地表达出自己想回宫用饭的意思。
尉缭果然没有拦他，当即便亲自将他送了出去。
看着徐福的身影走远，好不容易得到师弟一次关怀的尉缭，久久不能回神。师弟待我还是不错的……只是秦王爱吹枕边风，才会令师弟常对我冷言冷语。尉缭轻叹一口气，回到了府中。
……
可见世间最好哄的三种人。
一，蠢儿子；二，秦王政；三，俩师兄。
·
不知觉间，便到了徐福加冠这一日，满朝大臣并未放在心上，只是等他们散值以后，才陡然接到了邀请。
咸阳宫中行加冠礼。
那一瞬间，大臣们都以为自己眼瘸了，或者头晕了，或者是耳背了……绝对是自己的问题，而不是秦王的问题。
但是很遗憾的，等他们清醒过来之后，发现没错，的确是在咸阳宫中行冠礼，而这个冠礼当然不会是两位尚且年幼的公子的。而是徐奉常的……
他不过是个奉常，不过与我等一样身为秦国官员，他如何就能被秦王如此对待？
此时接到消息的李斯，也终于意识到了一点。
不管他在王上手底下如何厉害，他这辈子也不可能达到徐福在王上心底那样的高度。
想起曾经，自己一心想着王上会如何给予自己优待……还真是有些天真。
不过这样足以。秦国之中，徐福只有一个，李斯又何尝不是只有一个，他在王上手底下得到的优待，已经比他从前好过无数倍。
朝中大臣们心思各异，最后迫于秦王的威严，还是不得不来到了宫中。
今日宫中的宫人，对待他们还挺热情的，他们心中滋味复杂。
而这个时候，从床榻上坐起来的徐福，心情也挺复杂的。上辈子已经没有多少人重视成年礼了。在那个时候，成年不过对于很多人来说，是失去了桎梏，可以做很多从前不能做的事了。而对于徐福来说，便更觉概念单薄了。毕竟他身为孤儿，没有家长，只有师门，师门之中孤儿众多，谁又会记得他的生辰？左右徐福自己也不在乎这个，十八岁那一天便稀里糊涂过去了。
他可没想到，自己来到秦国，还能体验一次成年的滋味。
宫人们伺候着徐福穿上衣袍，这样的衣袍与成年后的衣袍是不同的。
而冠服都是之后，嬴政亲手为徐福换上。
虽然嬴政不太乐意让只着深衣的徐福出现在众人跟前，但考虑到这是仪式的一个环节，嬴政可以让自己的加冠礼搞砸也不在意，但徐福不同，他不能容忍一个环节出错。
待宫人将衣袍为他穿好之后，嬴政站在一旁，目不转睛地打量着徐福。
这身衣袍将他衬得越发纤细，看上去确实像是还未成年一般，整个人都透着一股青嫩的味道，勾得嬴政有些心痒痒。
之后嬴政抽走了自己的视线，先行离开到了咸阳宫的花园之中。
这花园极大，正好可以做加冠的场所。
左右对于徐福来说，他也不没有什么祖先神灵可祭拜的。
随后徐福才跟着宫人，慢慢到了花园之中。
大臣们看着徐福一脸淡然地行来，心中滋味万分复杂，他们也不知怎的，总感觉这场景，就跟秦王加封王后似的……
想到这里，大臣们将自己雷得打了个哆嗦，于是忙摇头将念头甩出去了。
他们定下神来，强迫自己认真观礼。
他们看着徐福面上一如既往的清冷之色，心中直犯嘀咕，怪不得这小子年纪轻轻，却能颇得王上青睐，哪怕是在这样的地方，他竟然也能维持常态，当真称得上是荣辱皆不惊了。
嬴政也与那些大臣一样，定定地瞧着徐福，等他注意到那些大臣看得入神的时候，自己心中就有些不大乐意了。
他就知道，这般模样的徐福，就不应当放出来……
除却寡人之外，竟然还有这样多的人，能同时欣赏见他身上的美丽。
嬴政压下胸中躁动的情绪，面上露出了点儿笑容。大臣们一心看着徐福呢，谁都没注意到他们家王上，脸上的宠溺实在太不正常了。若是知道的话，他们肯定这时便会高高提起警惕了。
这时的大臣们，都还想着，虽然徐福能在宫中行加冠礼，但那又如何？当年龙阳君得宠时，什么任性荒唐的事没发生过。与之相比，徐福这还不算得什么。
……
徐福的神色微微有些飘忽。
别说是那些大臣脑补了，他自己都觉得有些怪异。他怎么瞧都怎么觉得，自己就跟那抓着裙摆，羞答答走向新郎的新娘……
徐福暗暗打了个哆嗦。
好不容易，他走到了嬴政的跟前。
二人都跽坐下来，只不过是面对面，嬴政目光灼灼地看着他，徐福向来脸皮厚，目光避也不避，乍一看，两人的模样就像是在深情对望一般，不过因为角度的问题，那些大臣并未看见其中奸情。
嬴政将早就备好的冠动作轻柔地戴在他的头上，口中念着加冠时的祝福语。
尉缭见状，颇有些嫉妒。
可惜不是他……
不久后，嬴政取下了徐福头上的冠。
众人看着这一幕，心中隐隐有些猜测，但却根本不敢肯定。因为这实在令人难以相信。
但事实是，嬴政的确又从宫人手中取了更华美的一顶冠，再度戴在了徐福的头上。
徐福只隐约记得当初嬴政加冠时，便也是这样，重复加了几次冠，一次比一次贵重。但他却并不知其中的分别。数次加冠，可见主持加冠礼的人，对即将加冠的少年人有着多么深厚的祝福。
像嬴政那样数次加冠的，也就只有他敢如此了，别的人，谁还敢越过他去？
但现在徐福算是怎么回事……搞得这般隆重，隆重得大臣们心里都被堵住了，半天说不出话来。
嬴政对这些视线恍若未觉一般，继续我行我素地动作下去。
随着徐福头上的冠再次被换下，大臣们觉得自己的心快要爆裂开了。
当初魏王也没给龙阳君加过冠啊，无法再继续做对比的大臣们，觉得有些慌张。
幸好，嬴政没有太过夸张，到第三个冠时，他便没再换下了。
众人松了一口气。
嬴政面色不虞地为徐福脱去外袍，再换上成人的袍服，他的动作极快，几乎没留给其他人看徐福只穿深衣的机会。
徐福一头黑发被冠挽起，身上再加以华美精致的袍服，加上他气质本身便显得比旁人高出一等来，因而，若说他是秦王室的人，恐怕也没有人不敢相信。
嬴政略带痴迷地瞧了瞧徐福的头发。
若非诸多大臣在场，恐怕他便要舍不得就此丢开了。
最后嬴政才出声道：“其字，为君房。”
众人忙出声恭贺。
加完字，这才算是结束了。
不过众人念着君房二字，总觉分外熟悉，半天却又想不起来，直到最后宫人送他们出宫，大臣们才猛地反应过来。
徐君房。
那不是早就从鬼谷里传出的名字吗？
大臣们不太高兴地看向了尉缭。
尉缭冷呵呵，“怎么？我这师弟当不起如此冠礼吗？”
“不不，当得起当得起！”大臣们忍痛违心，如是道。

chapters.title: 第146章
chapters.source_text:
加冠礼看起来加单，做起来却极为繁琐，待到折腾完毕后，紧绷了一天的徐福实在打不起精神了，回到寝宫后，便早早上了床榻休息。
本以为一场加冠礼，能换来徐福感动不已、投怀送抱的嬴政，见到近乎熟睡的徐福后，他只得无奈地放弃了心中的期待。
反正日子还长着呢……
秦王如此安慰自己。
……
这一年，是秦王政十三年。
秦王在秦国越发地受拥戴，同时徐福的名声也渐渐传开了去，甚至隐隐有向其余六国传开的趋势。有人言，这是第二个龙阳君，秦国百姓听过之后并不在意。秦王和谁在一起，他们不关心，反正日子过得舒适，那位太卜有大本事，能帮秦国风调雨顺，那他们就觉得小日子很舒服了。
反倒是魏国人，听闻之后，心中多有不忿，认为这什么徐奉常，是远不能与龙阳君相比的。曾经这些将龙阳君视为祸水的人，此时倒是一致对外起来了。
不过很快这些就都不重要了。
秦国大将桓齮连破九城，攻下了赵国平阳、武城，赵国大将扈辄带兵来救，他却连同十万大军，都被桓齮斩于马下。
赵国大败……
赵王惊慌不已，其余六国皆受惊不少。
桓齮并未就此停下自己的脚步，他将消息传回咸阳之后，嬴政大悦，当即便批了他继续进攻赵国。
而桓齮报来的消息中，还特地感激了徐福，其中言辞真诚热切，令徐福实在摸不着头脑。
自己不就是帮忙算了一卦？但也并没有什么出奇的地方啊。
徐福还未想明白其中缘由，他的名声就已经又一次传出去了。六国众人都万分好奇，徐福到底是个什么样的人物，他的卜筮之术究竟如何厉害。
这些传闻传进了魏王的耳中。
失去龙阳君的魏王，看着赵国逐渐丢失城池，看着韩国对着秦王弯下腰，再看着信陵君对危境无动于衷……魏王的性格日益暴躁。现在听说徐福有何等大的本事，甚至桓齮能攻下赵国九座城池，也沾了徐福的光云云……
这样的话定然是有夸大之处的，但在魏王耳中就觉得格外的刺耳。
“这样的人物若是在我魏国……”魏王心中万分嫉妒，面上冷笑不已，“那寡人定能给他更尊贵的地位，奉常之位算什么？”
宫人们闻言，心中暗自吐槽不已。
难道您又要将爵位随意送出去吗？再封个XX君，和龙阳君遥遥相对？那信陵君乃至魏国上下，肯定又得给气死了。
魏王从知道徐福便是那次前来魏国出使的人后，魏王心底的嫉妒便更加浓厚了。
秦王？不过一个毛头小子！却能拥有这等美人！
越想徐福的面容，魏王便越觉得心痒痒。
魏王不思进取，不思己过，反倒抱着这些可笑的想法来麻痹自己，他想得心痒难耐，嫉妒至极的时候，便命人取来酒水，痛快地醉上一场……
魏国大臣见状，顿时忧心不已，这时他们倒是怀念起龙阳君了。
这位虽然是个媚上惑主的家伙，但他那一身本事，的确是比后宫不少女子强的，最重要的是，至少这时他能劝得住魏王，不要让他在这样的危机关头，还继续放纵下去。
不说徐福在六国中已然打下了怎么样的名望基础，这时秦王政十三年都过去大半了。
见到赵国惨状的韩国惊恐万分，韩王派人前来催促韩非，务必与徐福交好，再讨得秦王欢心。
尤其是因为这次的传闻过后，诸国都以为秦王与那魏王一样，是个也好男色。韩王便大言不惭地让韩非也去勾引秦王嬴政，韩非听到使者的转述后，窘迫之下，差点气得吐出血来。
徐福可不知自己的床伴被人觊觎了。
将朗诵完的扶苏打发走之后，徐福注意到了天边现有异象。
这个时代也当真奇怪。
上辈子奇景异象哪里会跟大白菜一样，说见就见啊，除非是当地本就容易形成奇特的异象。偏生在这个时候，异象和灾祸都再常见不过的东西。
徐福马上命人搬来小榻，然后自己坐到了窗户底下。
……
彗星落于东方，加之此时正值日落时分，因而霞光大作，哪怕是个再不通天象的人，在看见这等奇景之后，第一反应也是有好的征兆！
徐福担心出现之前郑国来到秦国那样的乌龙，便不敢随意断言这是大福之兆。将天象都记在心中之后，徐福立刻便命人取来了龟甲。
还没开始用龟甲，徐福就觉得自己脑子里似乎出现了很奇异的景象。
他的双眼像是蒙上了一层雾似的，仿佛身置幻境之中，他能看见眼前大朵代表吉祥的红云环绕，但在之后，他又见一个白色的身影，出现在了跟前，但这个身影渐渐离自己远了，像是要从自己的眼前彻底消失一般。
那是谁？
徐福根本想不起，自己认识的人中，除了自己，还有谁喜欢整日穿着白衣晃来晃去的。
这景象总不会是预言我自己要死了吧？徐福心下一颤，他眼前的景象骤然消失，整个人都从那层雾里脱离了出来。由幻境突然转到现实中，徐福还略微有些不习惯，因而没能第一时间便回过神。
而他身边的宫人指着他面前惊讶地叫了起来，“徐奉常……那……那……”
什么？
徐福不明所以地低下头，见宫人取来的龟甲上，竟然出现了长长的裂缝，那裂缝很细，乍一看，与用木条灼烤出来的倒也差不多。
徐福心下惊奇，他可什么也没做啊。
宫人褪去最初的震惊之后，看向徐福的目光便充满膜拜了，像是认定那裂缝一定是徐福造出来的一样，但那宫人倒是没想过，好端端的，徐福做什么要让龟甲自己裂开啊，这样的灵异事件，做出来不是很折腾人吗？
“收起来吧。”龟甲突然出了这样的状况，他自然是无法再用了。
宫人点了点头，看着那龟甲的目光，就仿佛在看什么传家至宝一样。宫人蹲下身来，小心翼翼地将龟甲捧了起来。
“等等。”徐福的目光滞了滞，将那龟甲留了下来。
宫人当然不会对徐福的吩咐有任何异议，哪怕此时徐福多折腾上他们几回，他们也会认为徐福的做法那都是有道理的，徐福一定是不会有错的。
徐福抬手摩挲着龟甲上的裂纹。
两条不同的走向，分明是代表了两个卦象。
再想到彗星有好的象征，同时却又有坏的象征，甚至有些地方的人就将这当做扫把星。
再想到脑子里涌现的奇异画面……
徐福惊奇地发觉到……难道是自己的水平提高了？所以才会出现这样诡异的局面？竟然是还未起卦，却就能得出两个卦象了。这样的场面，可以说徐福从前都是未曾遭遇过的。
此时有宫人进来，躬身道：“徐奉常，新的衣袍制好了。”
“新的衣袍？”徐福的思绪被打断，不得不暂时放下了手中的龟甲，不过他也挥手让身边的人退下，没再让对方将龟甲收走了。这究竟是怎么回事儿，待他空闲下来，还要仔细研究一番的。
宫人将新的衣袍送到了徐福的面前。
徐福猜测应当是嬴政特地命人制的，那不是他惯穿来装逼的白袍，而是选用了更深沉的颜色，与黑色极为接近。衣袍做得极为精致，上面还有着精美的花纹。怎么瞧都像是出席正式场合才需要穿的。
试了试衣袍，很快徐福就印证了心中的猜测，因为有宫人来告知他，韩国使臣来访。
虽然秦国如今并不怎么将韩国放在眼中，而且嬴政还觉得韩王派来郑国举动分外好笑，但毕竟是国与国之间的交流，嬴政还是命人准备了晚宴。
大臣们闻言，难免面带喜色，松了一口气。
这两年也不知王上是哪里不对劲了，他竟然是少有举行宴会的时候了，说起上次看舞姬跳舞，约莫是一年前？唉，瞧瞧，次数少得他们都记忆模糊了。
身为男人，连美色都没得欣赏，还有何意趣？要知道秦国最好的舞姬，都养在王宫中呢，没有王上举办宴会，谁能见得到？
很快便到了晚宴时分，徐福顺手将那龟甲抄起来藏在了胸口，然后才由宫人引着往嬴政而去。
徐福少有参加晚宴的时候，因为他发现嬴政确实不好奢靡享受。
这样一个一心装着统一大业，不好美色，不好美食，不好享受，也并不爱以折磨百姓为己好的男人……他究竟是怎么样变成历史上赫赫有名的暴君的？
徐福心下感慨不已。
走着神，他很快便到了大殿之中。
殿中大臣们已经分坐在两侧，中央留出空地。而嬴政则是高坐在台阶之上。次一级的台阶上，安排下的桌案，便是徐福的位置。
若非赵姬将自己作死了，说不定便是她了。
若非胡姬也把自己作死了，那说不定没了赵姬，那个位置也就是她了。
徐福莫名有了一种，我乃最后赢家的怪异感。
大臣们见到徐福进门而来，有人目光温和，而有人却是眼带嫉妒。
徐福直接无视了这些目光，就连尉缭都没能得到徐福一个回眸，被伤透了心的师兄捂了捂自己的胸口，低头作冷漠状，本要与他攀话的大臣，不得不又缩了回去，心中暗暗道。
这对师兄弟，真是都好生高冷！
徐福在嬴政的左手边跽坐下来，大臣们的眼珠子差点从眼眶里蹦了出来。
我们都是秦王的臣子啊！
我们都好好坐在两侧，哪怕你师兄他也坐得很规矩啊！
凭什么你能坐王上身边啊？不公平啊！我们瞧你的时候，竟然还要抬头仰望！大家不都是王上的臣子吗？
大殿中的众人心下都有些酸酸的，不过他们顶多也就腹诽罢了。他们也知晓徐福如今是个炙手可热的人物，在王上面前颇受重视，更何况他与王上还有暧昧，谁那样想不开，在这样的事上非要与他为难？
秦国君王做过的出格的事多了去了，并不在这一桩……
心理坚韧的大臣们如此自我安慰道。
因为是韩国来使，于是许久不见的韩非也被请了过来，他穿着韩国的衣饰，坐在下首，眸光冷淡，并不与任何人视线想交。
徐福对他感官复杂，有好有坏，所以只匆匆扫了一眼便没再看了。
而大殿之中，倒是还有个人的出现，让徐福觉得有些惊奇。
姚贾竟然也在座！
徐福都差点忘记自己还捡了个拖油瓶姚贾回来了，他和嬴政入王宫后，那姚贾便被直接抛给甘棠了。
姚贾见徐福的目光扫过来，当即便厚着脸皮对徐福笑了笑，那笑容还能让人倍觉真诚，挑不出半点不对劲来。
姚贾知晓徐福和嬴政的身份之后，有惊异，但还不足以震惊，毕竟他心中早就隐隐有猜测了。嬴政身为秦王更好，姚贾已经预见到自己能在这位君王手下大展身手的模样了。
原本对未来充满迷茫的姚贾，心中深深隐藏的野心，再度被点燃了。
尽管姚贾已经在掩藏眼底的野心了，但徐福还是一眼就看了出来。秦国还真是自带吸引人才的光环啊……李斯、赵高、尉缭、龙阳君、郑国、李冰……现在再多一个姚贾，日后还会有更多的有才之士加入……
所以，秦王不能做人生赢家，谁还能做？
徐福忍不住转头瞥了一眼嬴政，难得的，嬴政并未能马上注意到他的目光，因为嬴政正在与那韩国来使说话，韩国来使初时还想故意拿捏一下态度，强装出高傲的模样，但是等见了这位秦王，他便立即无法维持姿态了。
腿发软，语不成调，这都已经是轻的了。
韩非看着这一幕，心头觉得有些讽刺。
那韩国使臣，在他跟前是何等的耀武扬威，口吻是何等严厉不容拒绝，但到了秦王跟前，也就不过如此。
原来自己国家的人，反倒不如别国的人高贵么？
韩非压下心中日渐汹涌的沉痛。
他不敢去思考韩国是如何对待他的，他害怕自己越思考，便越加动摇初衷了。秦王是待他很好，但他更要考虑自己的国家……
韩非闭了闭眼，将这段话在心底默念了无数次，才安抚下了激动的心绪。
徐福注意到了韩非的动作，忍不住往他的方向看了一眼，徐福差不多已经能想到韩非此时的心思了。徐福对韩非没抱多大的期望，既然不愿为秦国效力，他也别幻想秦国能做善事将他放回去。要知道，就算将他放走，韩国也不一定敢收呢，何况秦国又不是做慈善的。
何必时时刻刻都是一副我不同流合污，莫想蛊惑我的贞烈模样！
说他偏心也好，先入为主也好，或是与古人代沟深重也好，总之他是越发瞧不上韩非的行为了。
与嬴政一番对话之后，那韩国来使畏畏缩缩地回到了位置上。
随后便有舞姬上来，开始载歌载舞，总算将晚宴的气氛炒热了些。
如今秦国正为秦王跟前红人的也就那么几位。
舞姬也是聪明人，自然是费尽心思地抛媚眼，竭力勾搭。尉缭、李斯、蒙恬等人便接收到了无数挑逗的目光。
李斯正在打量韩非。
尉缭满心师弟。
蒙恬还不如对着酒更感兴致。
于是舞姬们很快便发现，自己的媚眼抛出去根本没人搭理，她们怎么愿意就此收手？遂转头目光灼灼地看向了徐福。
虽然这一位的容貌足以令她们身为女子都陡然失色，但是，就算你长得再好看，也不能对着自己意淫过一生吧？舞姬们如此想着，勾引得更加卖力了。
至于这位年轻的奉常与君王间那点逸闻，舞姬们并不放在心上。
若是连王上垂青的人，她们都能招到自己身边，那岂不是更有挑战吗？这要是说出去，姐姐的身价都要倍增啊！
她们舒展腰肢，摆动手臂，展露着自己妩媚的一面。
大臣们看得目瞪口呆，他们还没见过舞姬这样卖力的时候呢。
而韩国来使暗自道。
秦国哪怕经历了大旱灾和瘟疫，却依旧能过着这样舒适奢侈的生活，可见秦国国力不弱，韩王派来的郑国，也不知何时才能将秦国拖垮啊……韩国来使忧心不已。
他哪里知道，其实大臣们已经许久没见过这样的宫宴了呢。
徐福欣赏了会儿舞蹈，便忍不住去瞧嬴政了。
毕竟在晚宴之上，他一人独坐，又不能和谁交谈，这样难耐的孤寂感，让徐福一时间还有些难以适应。
习惯了嬴政常在身边，徐福的目光便朝他而去了。
嬴政原本正不满于那些大胆的舞姬，正恨不得统统拖出去砍了，此时见徐福无动于衷，还频频朝自己看来，嬴政的心窝顿时便被暖洋洋的感觉填满了。
连带着嬴政身上冷凝的气势收敛了不少。
韩国来使松了一口气。
终于不用感觉自己随时都像是要死了一样了……
没等到散了晚宴，徐福便寻了个借口起身出去了。
不久之后，嬴政便也跟了出来，自然的，晚宴也就只能散了。
晚宴散去时，姚贾从大殿中出来，正好见到徐福和嬴政离去的背影，他大着胆子，厚着脸皮，快步往他们那边接近，“王上，徐奉常！”姚贾这样的举动，可以说是有些无礼了，但那些守卫知道姚贾乃是被秦王请进宫来的人，一时拿捏不住对方的地位，倒也不敢将他怎么样。
而就是守卫迟疑的这个时间里，徐福和嬴政都听见了姚贾的声音。
徐福按了按嬴政的手背，转身过来，“让他过来。”
守卫小心地觑了一眼嬴政的脸色，见徐福敢直接越过嬴政发话，心中暗道，这徐奉常实在是好大的胆子！
嬴政小幅度地点了点头，守卫这才放了姚贾过去。
姚贾不急不缓地走到徐福的跟前，拱手道：“徐奉常，敢问徐奉常之前对我做的表现可否满意？”他顿了顿，道：“徐奉常如今可愿为我改这个命了？”
姚贾也是个性子坚韧的人，能忍到这一路，的确不易，徐福又不是故意刁难别人的人。
徐福漫不经心地指了指身旁的嬴政，“喏，去找秦王，这便是我为你改命了。”
嬴政颇为享受徐福这样随意又隐隐透着与他关系亲密的口吻，因而听见徐福这样说，便默认了。
姚贾惊了惊，有点无言以对的感觉。
徐福微微挑眉，明明个子只与他差不多，但却能给他一种高高在上的感觉，“怎么？这个改命，你觉得不满意？”徐福都觉得这是自己改命改得最贵的了！你想啊，秦始皇是随便谁都能接触的吗？认识秦始皇，那就是改命的最直接方式啊！
“不，满意。”姚贾不自觉地躬身道，“多谢徐奉常。”他的语气依旧真诚。
“但我不会为你说话，你有何本事，需自己在王上跟前展露，若是不能教王上瞧上你的本事，那我就算再有本事也无法为你改命。”其实说来说去，还是全凭自己的本事，徐福不过恰巧给他提供一个机遇。
姚贾是个聪明人，之前他能有那样的地位，又哪里会蠢呢？
他自然有自己的本事，他也不消去走后门。
姚贾笑着转向嬴政，正正经经地朝嬴政见了一个大礼，“拜见王上，姚贾愿为王上效劳。还请王上听姚贾几言。”
嬴政却想也不想便拒绝了他，“时辰不早，明日寡人再令人带你入宫。”
姚贾这才松了一口气，脸上的笑容越发的狗腿，“那便恭送王上……与徐奉常。”
“嗯。”嬴政带着徐福转身离开。
好半晌姚贾才直起腰。
这头徐福无意中摸到胸前的龟甲，便将自己遇到的奇事跟嬴政说了一遍。
“你可有觉得，自己的本事更甚从前了？”嬴政问道。
或许因为徐福手中的卜卦算命极为玄妙的缘故，所以徐福身上的变化也显得很玄妙。但嬴政与他实在太过亲密了，亲密到两人之间的距离都是为负的，嬴政的情思又只拴在徐福一个人的身上，徐福有什么变化，他又哪里会注意不到呢？
最明显的便是，徐福在多次算卦之后，不如从前那样疲累了。
徐福身上的气质也等到了更显著的提升，走到哪里，恐怕都容易将他当做神仙。
而且他对福祸的感知，似乎变得更为直接和敏锐了。现在听徐福这样一说，嬴政便更加肯定了。
“唔，你说得似乎没错。”徐福细细回忆了一番，是觉得这些日子，自己的身上有了变化。
“这是好事。”嬴政面上的神色柔和不少。
徐福点了点头，改日他要算一算嬴政的命格，看看现在他是否能插手嬴政的命格了。
“你说自己在幻觉中见到了一着白衣的人物？”嬴政又问。
“是，瞧那模样，总觉得是不好的征兆。”
“可是象征死？”
“有可能。”
“那寡人心中倒是有一个人。”
“谁？”徐福紧紧盯着他的面孔，见嬴政面色轻松，就猜他说的人定然不是自己。
而嬴政口中说出来的人，也的确并非他。
嬴政：“韩非。”
徐福猛地想起，不错，他早就从韩非的手相上，看见他未来的死路了。后头韩非不知被嬴政安排何处了，他与韩非许久不见，倒是渐渐将此事忘记了。就连韩非那奇异的手相，他也没去印证了。
“在晚宴前，李斯来见寡人，向寡人进言，韩非若是不愿效力秦国，便杀了他。”
徐福有些惊讶，他可还记得两年前，李斯亲口对自己说，并不会要韩非性命的笃定口吻。
是发生了何事，才会导致李斯陡然转变了想法。难道韩非还从何处惹怒他了？
“寡人对韩非极为欣赏。”嬴政出声道。
徐福心里微微有些别扭。你欣赏便是，为何偏要特地说出来？
“哦。”徐福的目光往旁边的小池子上扫去，语气顿时寡淡了许多。
“只可惜，李斯说得也不错，韩子大才……还是永远留在秦国，寡人更觉舒心。”嬴政的嗓音有些冷，哪里见半分欣赏的味道？
徐福霎时抽回目光，转头讶异地看了一眼嬴政。
嬴政脸上神色变幻自如，他微笑道：“为何如此看寡人？莫非阿福认为寡人手段太过狠辣？”
“不，不是。我也只是跟你一样，可惜韩非的大才吧……”徐福与韩非并无多少交情，这时当然想得更多的便是韩非著的书简了。若是他真活不了了，那书简留下来也不错了。
若是他死后，却是秦国将这些书简上的内容实现，也不知到了黄泉下的韩非是否会觉得讽刺。
“韩非身死，彗星落下，倒也算合得上……那红云的吉兆呢？”徐福问。
嬴政笑道：“这不应当是寡人来问你吗？”
徐福半点尴尬也无，他点了点头，“……或许便是这两个月内吧，定然就会有喜事。等等……”徐福脑子里陡然划过一道亮光。
“嗯？”嬴政耐心地等他说下去。
“红云伴彗星而生，难道是……韩非若身亡，才会牵连出之后的福兆？”徐福心中已然有了猜测，“韩非身亡，韩国必然万分惊恐，以为韩非触怒了秦国，韩王胆小，害怕秦国攻打，那他说不定会……向你称臣。”
嬴政面上涌现笑意，他抬手抚弄了一下徐福的发丝，入手顺滑，让嬴政眼眸中的柔色更甚，“那寡人便借阿福吉言，等那一日的到来。”
徐福没再说话，只心中暗暗琢磨了起来。
难道说，韩非必须死了？
这可真是令人不好选择啊……
选韩非好，还是选韩国称臣好……嬴政定然是会选韩国称臣的。
徐福很快便将这件事抛到脑后，转而去研究自己越发厉害的感知能力了。不是什么事他都要插手，都能插手的。嬴政若是做出决定，他可不能用自己的想法去干扰嬴政。
接下来的几日，徐福便体验到了仿佛升级一般的快感。
那种滋味很奇妙，从他陡然明悟过后，他便能感知许多东西了。就好像胡亥走着走着，他都能感知出来胡亥会不会摔一跤，沾上血光之灾。这种感觉就好比开了外挂。
“……小心。”徐福坐在殿中，突然出声。
嬴政在门槛前，踩中了地上的小滚珠，约莫是胡亥留下来的，嬴政面色一黑，幸而在徐福的提醒下稳住了身体，才没摔下来。
嬴政叫宫人去收走胡亥殿中的小玩意儿，随后才走到了徐福的跟前。
“姚贾如何？”徐福问道。
嬴政在他跟前并不计较礼仪，就这样跽坐了下来，与他极为贴近，“姚贾与李斯应当能说得上话。”
“嗯？”
“他们二人在看某些事时，倒是极为相似。姚贾是有些本事，但还远不如李斯，寡人并未给他客卿之位，只让他先为秦国使臣，带上金银，前往六国。”
徐福想起，用金银收买各国权臣的事，才进展了一部分呢，后面因为没有合适的人选便暂时搁置了，这时倒是交到姚贾手中去了。
“姚贾此人声名并不算好，寡人还不能完全相信他。”
徐福点了点头，“反正他的命运能不能改全看他自己。”说完，徐福倒是突地发现，他给不少人相面的时候，都会发现对方原本应当陷入不好的境地，但却极有可能遇贵人。
而自己……好像有时候却恰好成了那个贵人……
自己之于李斯，于郑妃，于书秋……似乎都是这般。
这种滋味，还挺奇妙的，也不知自己究竟的掺合，打乱了多少历史上的细节。
话说完，徐福便觉得有些困倦了。
嬴政对徐福疲累的姿态十分在意，毕竟从前徐福就出现过这样的症状，他立时便问：“阿福可是要上床榻休息？”
徐福摆了摆手，“不必，我发现我对祸福的感知虽然强了，但同时也变得杂了，大小事我都能有所感知，这样下来，我的精力也是经不住消耗的。”而且他开的这个外挂实在太逆天了。
别人都要掏出龟甲算对吧？有时候弄不好还要算很久对吧？但他就强横了。能够一个照面，便感知祸福。
近乎可怕的能力……
却是要许多的精神来支撑的。
其中定然还有如何使用这个金手指的诀窍，但徐福现在就跟没说明书的新手一样，一切全得自己琢磨。
他懒洋洋地顺势靠进嬴政怀里，“这样休息一会儿便是了。”
嬴政面色温和，当然不会拒绝徐福这样投怀送抱。
两人便安静坐在那里了。
宫人们不自觉地屏了屏呼吸，生怕打破了面前的画面。
另一头胡亥哭哭啼啼地找扶苏求安慰，被拒绝，被收走玩具的胡亥，感觉到了生无可恋，便躺在了宫殿外很努力地想在徐福面前刷存在感。
但很可惜两个爹都没注意到他……这一躺反而还染上风寒了，之后又折腾出不少事来，暂且不提。
两日后，嬴政收到三则上书。
一则乃李斯进言，再度恳求他杀了韩非。
二则却是韩非自请想到云阳去传学。
三则就让嬴政有点不能忍了，桓齮竟然求嬴政将徐福给派去。桓齮言辞恳切，仿佛没有了徐福，他便难以一口气拿下赵国了。其中桓齮提到了一点，听闻徐奉常爱收藏鼎，听闻赵王宫中便有一奇鼎，徐奉常定然会喜欢……
嬴政放下了第一则上书，他是想杀韩非，但不能这么急，不然会教人寒心。
第二则顺势却被他纳入了考虑的范畴，韩非若是死在云阳，倒也不会令人觉得，是他秦王心胸狭隘，见韩非不肯臣服秦国，便杀了这样一个人物。
第三则么，嬴政是很想一口气塞进柜子里，放到压箱底的位置，一辈子也不要拿出来的。但嬴政自然是没这样幼稚的，于是他也只能不情不愿地拿着绢布，带回给了徐福。
徐福愿不愿去……寡人竟然都做不了主。
想一想，真是倍觉心酸啊……
秦王管上管下，唯独管不了自己的小情人。
**
徐福这头拿到绢布还没做下决定，而另一头，韩非却已经跪在宫门外，恳请嬴政同意他前去云阳了，瞧那架势颇有不达目的不罢休的意思。
徐福对韩非的执拗脾气早有了解。
若是嬴政不同意，他恐怕还真能将膝盖给跪没。
chapters.translated_text:
The capping ceremony looked simple, but the process was incredibly tedious. By the time it was over, Xu Fu, who had been tense all day, was too exhausted to keep his spirits up. After returning to his sleeping quarters, he went to bed early to rest.

Ying Zheng, who had hoped the capping ceremony would move Xu Fu to tears and make him throw himself into his arms, had to helplessly abandon his expectations when he saw Xu Fu nearly fast asleep.

There was always plenty of time ahead, anyway...

The King of Qin consoled himself with this thought.

...

This year was the thirteenth year of King Zheng of Qin.

The King of Qin was becoming increasingly popular in the State of Qin, and at the same time, Xu Fu's reputation gradually spread, even showing signs of reaching the other six states. Some said he was a second Lord Longyang, but the people of Qin didn't care. They didn't concern themselves with who the King of Qin was with; as long as their lives were comfortable and the Grand Diviner possessed great abilities that could help bring favorable weather to Qin, they were satisfied with their simple lives.

The people of the State of Wei, however, were quite indignant upon hearing this, believing that this so-called Grand Master Xu was far from comparable to Lord Longyang. Those who had once viewed Lord Longyang as a disaster were now united against an outsider.

But soon, none of this mattered.

The Qin general Huan Yi broke through nine cities in succession, capturing Pingyang and Wucheng of the State of Zhao. The Zhao general Hu Zhe led an army to the rescue, but he and his one hundred thousand troops were all cut down by Huan Yi.

The State of Zhao suffered a crushing defeat...

The King of Zhao was panic-stricken, and the other six states were all deeply alarmed.

Huan Yi did not stop there. After he sent the news back to Xianyang, Ying Zheng was overjoyed and immediately authorized him to continue attacking Zhao.

In the report Huan Yi sent back, he specifically expressed gratitude to Xu Fu, using such sincere and fervent language that it left Xu Fu completely baffled.

Hadn't he just helped cast a divination? There hadn't been anything particularly extraordinary about it.

Before Xu Fu could figure out the reason, his reputation had spread once again. People in the six states were extremely curious about what kind of person Xu Fu was and how powerful his art of divination truly was.

These rumors reached the ears of the King of Wei.

Having lost Lord Longyang, the King of Wei watched as the State of Zhao lost city after city, watched the State of Han bow down to the King of Qin, and watched Lord Xinling remain indifferent to the crisis... The King of Wei's temper grew increasingly volatile. Now, hearing of Xu Fu's great abilities, and even that Huan Yi's capture of the nine cities of Zhao was partly due to Xu Fu's blessing...

Such talk was bound to be exaggerated, but to the King of Wei, it sounded exceptionally grating.

"If such a person were in my State of Wei..." The King of Wei was consumed with jealousy, a cold sneer on his face. "Then I would certainly grant him a much higher status. What is a mere position of Grand Master?"

The palace attendants heard this and secretly rolled their eyes.

Was he going to hand out titles again? Perhaps confer another "Lord XX" to stand in opposition to Lord Longyang? That would surely infuriate Lord Xinling and the rest of the Wei court to death.

Ever since the King of Wei learned that Xu Fu was the same person who had come to Wei as an envoy, his jealousy had only deepened.

The King of Qin? Just a green boy! Yet he possessed such a beauty!

The more the King of Wei thought of Xu Fu's face, the more his heart itched.

The King of Wei did not seek progress or reflect on his own faults; instead, he numbed himself with these ridiculous thoughts. When his jealousy reached a fever pitch, he ordered wine to be brought so he could get thoroughly drunk...

Seeing this, the ministers of Wei were deeply worried, and at this moment, they actually began to miss Lord Longyang.

Although he was someone who seduced the ruler, his abilities were indeed stronger than many women in the harem. Most importantly, at least he could persuade the King of Wei not to continue indulging himself during such a critical time.

Not to mention the reputation Xu Fu had already established among the six states, more than half of the thirteenth year of King Zheng of Qin had already passed.

The State of Han, seeing the miserable state of Zhao, was terrified. The King of Han sent people to urge Han Fei to be sure to befriend Xu Fu and win the favor of the King of Qin.

Especially after these recent rumors, all the states assumed the King of Qin, like the King of Wei, was fond of men. The King of Han shamelessly told Han Fei to seduce King Ying Zheng of Qin. When Han Fei heard the envoy's relay, he was so embarrassed he nearly coughed up blood.

Xu Fu had no idea that his bed partner was being coveted by others.

After dismissing Fusu, who had finished his recitation, Xu Fu noticed an unusual phenomenon in the sky.

This era was truly strange.

In his previous life, strange phenomena were not as common as cabbage; you didn't just see them unless the area was prone to them. Yet in this time, phenomena and disasters were common occurrences.

Xu Fu immediately ordered a small couch to be moved and sat down beneath the window.

...

A comet fell in the east, and since it was sunset, the sky was filled with a brilliant glow. Even someone completely ignorant of celestial phenomena would, upon seeing such a sight, first think it was a good omen!

Fearing a blunder like the one when Zheng Guo came to Qin, Xu Fu dared not casually declare it a sign of great fortune. After memorizing the celestial signs, he immediately ordered someone to bring a tortoise shell.

Before he even began using the shell, Xu Fu felt a strange vision appear in his mind.

His eyes felt as if they were covered in a layer of mist, as if he were in an illusion. He could see large red clouds representing good fortune surrounding him, but then, he saw a white figure appear before him. The figure gradually moved away, as if it were about to disappear from his sight entirely.

Who was that?

Xu Fu couldn't think of anyone he knew, besides himself, who liked to wander around in white clothes all day.

Surely this vision wasn't a prophecy of his own death? Xu Fu's heart trembled. The scene before him suddenly vanished, and he was pulled out of the mist. Transitioning from the illusion to reality, Xu Fu was a bit unaccustomed to it and couldn't immediately regain his composure.

The attendant beside him pointed at the shell in front of him and cried out in surprise, "Grand Master Xu... that... that..."

What?

Xu Fu looked down, confused, and saw that the tortoise shell the attendant had brought had developed long cracks. The cracks were very fine; at first glance, they looked similar to those made by scorching with wooden sticks.

Xu Fu was amazed; he hadn't done anything at all.

After the initial shock faded, the attendant looked at Xu Fu with eyes full of worship, as if he were certain that Xu Fu must have created the cracks. But the attendant never considered why Xu Fu would make the shell crack on its own—such a supernatural event would be quite a hassle to perform, wouldn't it?

"Put it away." Since the shell had suddenly ended up in such a state, he naturally couldn't use it anymore.

The attendant nodded, looking at the shell as if it were a family heirloom. He crouched down and carefully picked it up.

"Wait." Xu Fu's gaze lingered, and he kept the shell.

The attendant, of course, had no objections to Xu Fu's orders. Even if Xu Fu made them go through more trouble, they would believe there was a reason for it; Xu Fu could never be wrong.

Xu Fu reached out and traced the cracks on the shell.

Two different directions clearly represented two different divinations.

Thinking again that a comet had both good and bad symbolism—some places even considered it a "broom star" of misfortune.

And thinking of the strange vision that had flooded his mind...

Xu Fu was astonished to realize... could it be that his level had improved? Was that why such a bizarre situation had occurred? To be able to derive two divinations before even casting them—this was a scene Xu Fu had never encountered before.

At this moment, an attendant entered and bowed, "Grand Master Xu, your new robes are ready."

"New robes?" Xu Fu's train of thought was interrupted, and he had to temporarily put down the shell. However, he waved for the people around him to leave, not letting them take the shell away. He would have to study this carefully when he had some free time.

The attendant brought the new robes to Xu Fu.

Xu Fu guessed that Ying Zheng must have specifically ordered them to be made. They weren't the white robes he usually wore to look sophisticated, but rather a deeper color, very close to black. The robes were exquisitely made, with beautiful patterns. They looked like something meant for a formal occasion.

After trying on the robes, Xu Fu soon confirmed his suspicion, as an attendant came to inform him that an envoy from the State of Han had arrived.

Although the State of Qin didn't think much of Han, and Ying Zheng found the move by the King of Han to send Zheng Guo quite laughable, it was still an exchange between nations, so Ying Zheng ordered a banquet to be prepared.

The ministers were visibly pleased and relieved when they heard this.

They didn't know what had been wrong with the King for the past two years; he rarely held banquets. The last time they watched dancing girls perform was about a year ago? Sigh, look at that, the frequency was so low they could barely remember.

As men, if they couldn't even enjoy beauty, what was the point? The best dancing girls in Qin were kept in the palace; without the King holding a banquet, who could see them?

Soon it was time for the banquet. Xu Fu grabbed the tortoise shell and hid it in his chest before being led by an attendant to Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu rarely attended banquets because he had discovered that Ying Zheng truly did not care for extravagance or indulgence.

A man who was single-mindedly focused on the cause of unification, who didn't care for beauty, food, luxury, or the torture of his people... how on earth did he become the infamous tyrant of history?

Xu Fu felt a deep sense of emotion.

Lost in thought, he soon arrived at the main hall.

The ministers were already seated on both sides, leaving the center empty. Ying Zheng sat high on the dais. The table arranged on the step below was Xu Fu's seat.

If Zhao Ji hadn't brought about her own downfall, it might have been her.

If Hu Ji hadn't also brought about her own downfall, then without Zhao Ji, that seat might have been hers.

Xu Fu had a strange feeling of being the "last man standing."

When the ministers saw Xu Fu enter, some looked at him with warmth, while others had eyes full of jealousy.

Xu Fu ignored these gazes directly. Even Wei Liao didn't get a single glance back from Xu Fu. His heartbroken senior brother clutched his chest and lowered his head, acting cold. Other ministers who wanted to strike up a conversation had to shrink back, thinking to themselves:

This pair of senior and junior brothers is truly aloof!

Xu Fu knelt to the left of Ying Zheng, and the ministers' eyes nearly popped out of their sockets.

We are all subjects of the King of Qin!

We are all sitting properly on both sides, and even your senior brother is sitting very correctly!

Why do you get to sit beside the King? It's unfair! When we look at you, we have to look up! Aren't we all subjects of the King?

Everyone in the hall felt a bit sour, but they could only grumble to themselves. They knew Xu Fu was a hot figure, highly valued by the King, and there was that ambiguous relationship between them. Who would be so foolish as to make things difficult for him over such a matter?

The King of Qin had done many unconventional things; this was not the only one...

The mentally resilient ministers consoled themselves this way.

Because it was an envoy from Han, Han Fei, who hadn't been seen for a long time, was also invited. He wore Han attire and sat in the lower section, his gaze cold, not meeting anyone's eyes.

Xu Fu had complex feelings about him—both good and bad—so he only glanced at him briefly and looked away.

In the hall, there was one other person whose presence surprised Xu Fu.

Yao Jia was actually there too!

Xu Fu had almost forgotten that he had picked up the "dead weight" Yao Jia. After he and Ying Zheng entered the palace, Yao Jia had been tossed to Gan Tang.

Seeing Xu Fu's gaze sweep over, Yao Jia shamelessly smiled at him, a smile so sincere that one couldn't find a single thing wrong with it.

After Yao Jia learned of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng's identities, he was surprised, but not shocked; he had already had faint suspicions. It was even better that Ying Zheng was the King of Qin; Yao Jia already envisioned himself showing off his skills under this monarch.

The ambition that had been deeply hidden in Yao Jia, who had originally been full of confusion about the future, was ignited once again.

Although Yao Jia was hiding the ambition in his eyes, Xu Fu saw it at a glance. The State of Qin truly had an aura that attracted talent... Li Si, Zhao Gao, Wei Liao, Lord Longyang, Zheng Guo, Li Bing... and now another Yao Jia. In the future, more talented people would join...

So, if the King of Qin couldn't be the winner in life, who could?

Xu Fu couldn't help but turn to glance at Ying Zheng. Rarely, Ying Zheng didn't notice his gaze immediately because he was talking to the Han envoy. The envoy had initially wanted to put on airs and act arrogant, but upon seeing this King of Qin, he immediately couldn't maintain his posture.

His legs went soft, and his speech became incoherent—and that was the mildest of it.

Han Fei watched this scene, feeling a bit ironic.

That Han envoy had been so arrogant and unyielding in front of him, but in front of the King of Qin, he was nothing more than this.

Were the people of his own country actually less noble than those of other countries?

Han Fei suppressed the surging pain in his heart.

He didn't dare to think about how the State of Han treated him; he was afraid that the more he thought, the more his original intention would waver. The King of Qin treated him very well, but he had to consider his own country...

Han Fei closed his eyes and repeated this to himself countless times to soothe his agitated emotions.

Xu Fu noticed Han Fei's actions and couldn't help but look in his direction. Xu Fu could pretty much guess what Han Fei was thinking. Xu Fu didn't hold high hopes for Han Fei; since he wasn't willing to serve Qin, he shouldn't fantasize that Qin would do a charity act and let him go. Even if they let him go, Han wouldn't necessarily dare to take him back, and Qin wasn't a charity.

Why must he always have that "I will not be corrupted, don't try to seduce me" look of a martyr!

Call it bias, or prejudice, or a deep generation gap with the ancients—in any case, he was increasingly looking down on Han Fei's behavior.

After a conversation with Ying Zheng, the Han envoy returned to his seat, trembling.

Then, dancing girls came up and began to sing and dance, finally heating up the atmosphere of the banquet.

There were only a few people in Qin who were currently in the King's favor.

The dancing girls were smart, naturally trying their best to throw flirtatious glances and seduce. Wei Liao, Li Si, Meng Tian, and others received countless provocative looks.

Li Si was busy observing Han Fei.

Wei Liao was full of his junior brother.

Meng Tian was more interested in his wine.

So the dancing girls soon found that their flirtatious glances were being ignored. How could they be willing to stop there? They turned their burning gazes toward Xu Fu.

Although this person's beauty was enough to make them, as women, suddenly pale in comparison, even if you were good-looking, you couldn't spend your whole life fantasizing about yourself, could you? The dancing girls thought this and seduced even harder.

As for the anecdotes between this young Grand Master and the King, the dancing girls didn't take them to heart.

If they could lure someone favored by the King to their side, wouldn't that be even more of a challenge? If word got out, their status would double!

They stretched their waists and waved their arms, showing off their charming side.

The ministers were dumbfounded; they had never seen the dancing girls work so hard.

And the Han envoy thought to himself.

Even after experiencing a great drought and plague, the State of Qin could still live such a comfortable and luxurious life. It was clear that Qin's national strength was not weak. He wondered when Zheng Guo, sent by the King of Han, would be able to drag Qin down... The Han envoy was deeply worried.

Little did he know that the ministers hadn't seen such a palace banquet in a long time.

Xu Fu enjoyed the dance for a while, then couldn't help but look at Ying Zheng.

After all, at the banquet, he sat alone and couldn't talk to anyone. This unbearable sense of loneliness made it hard for Xu Fu to adapt for a moment.

Accustomed to having Ying Zheng by his side, Xu Fu's gaze turned toward him.

Ying Zheng had been dissatisfied with the bold dancing girls and wished he could have them all dragged out and executed. Seeing Xu Fu indifferent and frequently looking at him, his heart was suddenly filled with a warm feeling.

Consequently, the cold, condensed aura around Ying Zheng softened significantly.

The Han envoy breathed a sigh of relief.

Finally, he didn't feel like he was going to die at any moment...

Before the banquet ended, Xu Fu found an excuse to get up and leave.

Not long after, Ying Zheng followed, and naturally, the banquet had to end.

As the banquet dispersed, Yao Jia came out of the hall and happened to see the backs of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng leaving. He gathered his courage, acted shamelessly, and walked quickly toward them. "Your Majesty, Grand Master Xu!" This action of Yao Jia's could be considered somewhat rude, but the guards knew Yao Jia had been invited into the palace by the King of Qin, so they didn't dare do anything to him.

In the time the guards hesitated, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng both heard Yao Jia's voice.

Xu Fu pressed the back of Ying Zheng's hand and turned around. "Let him come over."

The guard carefully glanced at Ying Zheng's expression. Seeing Xu Fu dare to speak directly over Ying Zheng, he thought to himself, this Grand Master Xu is truly bold!

Ying Zheng nodded slightly, and the guard let Yao Jia pass.

Yao Jia walked to Xu Fu unhurriedly and bowed. "Grand Master Xu, may I ask if you are satisfied with my performance earlier?" He paused and said, "Is Grand Master Xu willing to change my fate now?"

Yao Jia was also a resilient person; it was truly not easy to endure until now, and Xu Fu wasn't the type to deliberately make things difficult for others.

Xu Fu pointed at Ying Zheng beside him nonchalantly. "There, go find the King of Qin. This is me changing your fate."

Ying Zheng quite enjoyed Xu Fu's casual tone, which hinted at their close relationship, so he acquiesced.

Yao Jia was startled, feeling a bit speechless.

Xu Fu raised his eyebrows slightly. Although he was about the same height as him, he gave off a sense of being high above. "What? Are you not satisfied with this change of fate?" Xu Fu thought this was the most expensive fate-change he had ever performed! Think about it: could just anyone get in touch with the First Emperor of Qin? Knowing the First Emperor was the most direct way to change one's fate!

"No, I am satisfied." Yao Jia bowed involuntarily. "Thank you, Grand Master Xu." His tone remained sincere.

"But I won't speak for you. You must show your own abilities to the King. If you can't make the King appreciate your skills, then no matter how capable I am, I can't change your fate." Actually, it all depended on his own ability; Xu Fu was just providing him with an opportunity.

Yao Jia was a smart man; how could he be stupid if he had achieved such a status before?

He naturally had his own skills and didn't need to take the back door.

Yao Jia smiled and turned to Ying Zheng, performing a formal bow. "Greetings, Your Majesty. Yao Jia is willing to serve you. I hope Your Majesty will listen to a few words from me."

Ying Zheng refused him without a second thought. "It is late. Tomorrow, I will have someone bring you into the palace."

Yao Jia breathed a sigh of relief, the smile on his face becoming even more sycophantic. "Then I will respectfully see off Your Majesty... and Grand Master Xu."

"Hmm." Ying Zheng turned and left with Xu Fu.

It took a long while for Yao Jia to straighten his back.

On their way, Xu Fu accidentally touched the tortoise shell in his chest and told Ying Zheng about the strange thing he had encountered.

"Do you feel that your abilities are greater than before?" Ying Zheng asked.

Perhaps because the divination Xu Fu performed was extremely mysterious, the changes in him also appeared mysterious. But Ying Zheng was too close to him—so close that the distance between them was negative—and Ying Zheng's feelings were tied only to Xu Fu. How could he not notice any changes in him?

The most obvious was that after many divinations, Xu Fu was not as tired as before.

Xu Fu's temperament had also significantly improved; wherever he went, people would likely mistake him for an immortal.

And his perception of fortune and misfortune seemed to have become more direct and sharp. Now, hearing Xu Fu say this, Ying Zheng was even more certain.

"Hmm, you seem to be right." Xu Fu recalled carefully; he did feel that there had been changes in him these days.

"This is a good thing." The expression on Ying Zheng's face softened.

Xu Fu nodded; another day, he would calculate Ying Zheng's destiny to see if he could interfere with it now.

"You said you saw a figure in white in your hallucination?" Ying Zheng asked again.

"Yes, looking at it, I always felt it was a bad omen."

"Does it symbolize death?"

"It's possible."

"Then I have someone in mind."

"Who?" Xu Fu stared at his face. Seeing Ying Zheng's relaxed expression, he guessed that the person he was talking about was definitely not himself.

And the person Ying Zheng mentioned was indeed not him.

Ying Zheng: "Han Fei."

Xu Fu suddenly remembered. That's right, he had long seen his future path of death from Han Fei's palmistry. Later, he didn't know where Ying Zheng had arranged for Han Fei to go. He hadn't seen Han Fei for a long time and had gradually forgotten about it. He hadn't even verified Han Fei's strange palmistry.

"Before the banquet, Li Si came to see me and advised me that if Han Fei is unwilling to serve Qin, I should kill him."

Xu Fu was a bit surprised. He remembered two years ago, Li Si had told him personally with a firm tone that he would not take Han Fei's life.

What had happened to cause Li Si to suddenly change his mind? Had Han Fei angered him somewhere?

"I admire Han Fei very much." Ying Zheng said.

Xu Fu felt a little awkward. If you admire him, why do you have to say it specifically?

"Oh." Xu Fu's gaze swept toward the small pond nearby, his tone becoming much flatter.

"It's a pity, but Li Si is right. Han Fei has great talent... It would be more comforting if he stayed in Qin forever." Ying Zheng's voice was cold; where was the sign of admiration?

Xu Fu immediately withdrew his gaze and turned to look at Ying Zheng in surprise.

Ying Zheng's expression changed freely. He smiled and said, "Why look at me like that? Does A-Fu think my methods are too ruthless?"

"No, not at all. I'm just like you, regretting Han Fei's great talent..." Xu Fu didn't have much friendship with Han Fei, so naturally, he thought more about Han Fei's books. If he really couldn't live, it would be good to leave the books behind.

If, after his death, it was Qin that realized the content of those books, he wondered if Han Fei, in the underworld, would find it ironic.

"Han Fei dies, the comet falls—that matches up... What about the good omen of the red clouds?" Xu Fu asked.

Ying Zheng laughed: "Shouldn't I be asking you that?"

Xu Fu felt no embarrassment at all. He nodded, "...Perhaps within these two months, there will definitely be good news. Wait..." A flash of light suddenly crossed Xu Fu's mind.

"Hmm?" Ying Zheng waited patiently for him to continue.

"Red clouds born with a comet—could it be... that Han Fei's death will lead to the subsequent good omen?" Xu Fu already had a guess in his heart. "If Han Fei dies, the State of Han will be terrified, thinking Han Fei angered Qin. The King of Han is cowardly and fears a Qin attack, so he might... submit to you."

A smile appeared on Ying Zheng's face. He reached out and stroked Xu Fu's hair. It was smooth, making the softness in Ying Zheng's eyes even deeper. "Then I will borrow A-Fu's auspicious words and wait for that day to come."

Xu Fu didn't speak again, just pondered in his heart.

Could it be that Han Fei must die?

This was truly a difficult choice...

Choosing Han Fei or choosing for Han to submit... Ying Zheng would definitely choose for Han to submit.

Xu Fu soon threw this matter to the back of his mind and went to study his increasingly powerful perception ability. He didn't have to interfere in everything, nor could he. If Ying Zheng made a decision, he couldn't use his own ideas to interfere with him.

Over the next few days, Xu Fu experienced the pleasure of what felt like leveling up.

That feeling was very strange. Since his sudden epiphany, he could perceive many things. It was as if, as Hu Hai walked, he could perceive whether Hu Hai would trip and suffer a bloody disaster. This feeling was like using a cheat code.

"...Careful." Xu Fu was sitting in the hall when he suddenly spoke.

Ying Zheng stepped on a small marble on the floor in front of the threshold—likely left behind by Hu Hai. Ying Zheng's face darkened, but fortunately, with Xu Fu's reminder, he steadied himself and didn't fall.

Ying Zheng told the attendants to take away the small toys in Hu Hai's palace before walking to Xu Fu.

"How is Yao Jia?" Xu Fu asked.

Ying Zheng didn't care about etiquette in front of him and just knelt down, very close to him. "Yao Jia and Li Si should be able to talk."

"Hmm?"

"They are very similar in how they view certain things. Yao Jia has some ability, but he is far inferior to Li Si. I didn't give him the position of Guest Minister; I only let him be an envoy for Qin, taking gold and silver to the six states."

Xu Fu remembered that the matter of using gold and silver to bribe the powerful ministers of various countries had only progressed a little, and it had been temporarily shelved because there was no suitable candidate. Now it had been handed over to Yao Jia.

"Yao Jia's reputation is not very good, and I cannot fully trust him yet."

Xu Fu nodded. "Anyway, whether his fate can be changed depends entirely on himself." After speaking, Xu Fu suddenly discovered that when he performed face-reading for many people, he would find that they were originally supposed to be in a bad situation, but were very likely to meet a noble person.

And himself... sometimes he happened to be that noble person...

For Li Si, for Consort Zheng, for Shu Qiu... it seemed to be the same.

This feeling was quite strange, and he didn't know how many historical details his interference had disrupted.

After finishing speaking, Xu Fu felt a bit sleepy.

Ying Zheng was very concerned about Xu Fu's tired posture, as Xu Fu had shown such symptoms before. He immediately asked, "Does A-Fu want to go to bed and rest?"

Xu Fu waved his hand. "No need. I find that although my perception of fortune and misfortune is stronger, it has also become cluttered. I can perceive both big and small things, and my energy cannot withstand such consumption." And the cheat code he had opened was truly heaven-defying.

Others had to take out a tortoise shell to calculate, right? Sometimes they had to calculate for a long time, right? But he was overbearing. He could perceive fortune and misfortune in a single glance.

An almost terrifying ability...

...but it required a lot of mental energy to support.

There must be tricks to using this "gold finger," but Xu Fu was like a novice without an instruction manual; he had to figure everything out himself.

He lazily leaned into Ying Zheng's arms. "Just resting here for a while is fine."

Ying Zheng's expression was gentle; naturally, he wouldn't refuse Xu Fu's act of throwing himself into his arms.

The two sat there quietly.

The attendants held their breath, afraid of breaking the scene before them.

On the other side, Hu Hai was crying and looking for Fusu for comfort, but was rejected. Having had his toys taken away, Hu Hai felt life was meaningless, so he lay outside the palace, trying very hard to brush his presence in front of Xu Fu.

But unfortunately, neither of his two dads noticed him... This lying down actually caused him to catch a cold, and he caused many more troubles later, which we won't mention for now.

Two days later, Ying Zheng received three memorials.

One was from Li Si, once again begging him to kill Han Fei.

The second was Han Fei's own request to go to Yunyang to teach.

The third made Ying Zheng a bit unable to endure: Huan Yi actually asked Ying Zheng to send Xu Fu over. Huan Yi's words were earnest, as if without Xu Fu, he would find it difficult to take Zhao in one go. Huan Yi mentioned one point: he heard Grand Master Xu loved collecting tripods, and there was a strange tripod in the Zhao palace that Grand Master Xu would surely like...

Ying Zheng put down the first memorial. He wanted to kill Han Fei, but he couldn't be so hasty, or it would chill people's hearts.

The second one was taken into consideration. If Han Fei died in Yunyang, it wouldn't make people think he, the King of Qin, was narrow-minded and killed such a person because he refused to submit to Qin.

As for the third one, Ying Zheng really wanted to stuff it into a cabinet and put it at the bottom, never to be taken out again. But Ying Zheng was naturally not that childish, so he could only reluctantly take the silk scroll back to Xu Fu.

Whether Xu Fu was willing to go... I actually can't make the decision.

Thinking about it, it really felt heartbreaking...

The King of Qin managed everything, but he couldn't manage his own little lover.

**

Xu Fu hadn't made a decision after receiving the silk scroll, but on the other side, Han Fei was already kneeling outside the palace gate, begging Ying Zheng to agree to let him go to Yunyang. The posture looked like he wouldn't stop until he achieved his goal.

Xu Fu had long known about Han Fei's stubborn temper.

If Ying Zheng didn't agree, he might really kneel until his knees were gone.

chapters.source_text:
韩非对李斯的举动若有所觉，于是便先一步自请发配。李斯往王宫中来时，正巧在殿外看见了跪地不起的韩非。
韩非在李斯跟前是傲气的，尽管他开口说话仍旧避免不了口吃的毛病。
听到他说自请前往云阳的李斯愣住了。
韩非什么时候还会这样变化手段了？按照他的性格，不应该是为了韩国，忍着不快和屈辱留在咸阳，哪怕不给秦国效力，也要膈应死秦王吗？
要知道韩非那点膈应人的事儿还真没少做。
何况李斯是真不喜欢这个师兄。韩非傲气，傲得看不上钻营的自己。但李斯自认不比谁差，你一个从韩国来辛苦维持生存的人，凭什么看不上我？李斯一般不记仇，但记起仇来，一般也就难以忘记了。
李斯也不自诩是多么高尚的人，所以对于推翻自己从前的话，他谈不上如何愧疚脸红。
李斯想得很好，但却没想到韩非这里出了点变故……
不过没关系，李斯不急不忙地走进殿内，准备探一探王上的口风。
徐福坐在殿内和嬴政说着桓齮的事，内侍突然进来，说李斯求见。
徐福想到还跪在外头的韩非，心里顿时有些微妙，也不知他们二人见到面时，心情是何样的。
“让他进来吧。”嬴政出声道。他也正打算借此机会，将自己的意思透露给李斯。比起韩非，自然是李斯更得他心，偶尔倾向一下手底下的人，能让对方更为尽心。
李斯面带笑容地走进来，但却在见到徐福的身影之后，略略踟蹰了。徐福和尉缭也同为师兄弟，自己若是这样对韩非下手，徐福是否会因而对自己生出什么看法来？他会不会从此后便再也不将我视作朋友了？
对啊，自己还在他的跟前说过，不会对韩非下手的，这样是不是会在他的心中，留下自己反复无常的印象？
李斯深深地忧虑了起来，忧虑得险些忘记了自己的来意。
回过神来，便见徐福和嬴政都盯着他。
“许久不见，客卿可好？”徐福回到咸阳后，也只走了尉缭一处，若非如此，怎么能安抚得住尉缭那颗受伤的师兄心。徐福回咸阳只见了他一人，已经足够让尉缭冲着李斯、蒙恬炫耀（装逼）一番了。
想想这还是徐福回咸阳后，头一次正经地问候起李斯。
李斯恭敬地答道：“除却师兄韩非总引来不快以外，斯一切都好。”这倒是半点都不加隐瞒，坦诚得就差没自己脱裤衩了。
这也算是他变相地对着徐福做个解释了。
随后李斯便转头朝向了嬴政，他并没有开口就提及韩非的事，而是先和嬴政聊起了正事。也正是因为李斯分得清轻重缓急的性子，嬴政才并不介意他对韩非的芥蒂。
李斯将正事说完，最后才提起了韩非。
这些日子，李斯将为何要除掉韩非的原因，已经阐述得差不多了，如今再提起，他也只是点到即止，免得引起王上厌烦。
“寡人欲准韩非之请，云阳并非富裕之所，韩非前去，不过吃吃苦头。”嬴政淡淡道。
李斯隐约猜到了嬴政背后的意思，立时便面带微笑道：“王上英明。”他这一脸真诚的表情，还真与姚贾有几分相似，不知道李斯与姚贾日后是否又合得来呢？
徐福心中诡异地升起了一点，日后要如何站队的苦恼。
原本许久不见，李斯是很想邀请徐福过府一聚的，想当年他还和苏邑一同与徐福坐拢闲谈呢，但如今想一想，倒好像是很多年前的事了。
李斯隐隐看了嬴政一眼。
虽然很尊敬王上，也很感激王上，但在这种时候，实在是对王上爱不起来啊……
李斯掩下眼中的情绪，规规矩矩地告别了徐福和嬴政。李斯自认还没那个本事，能在嬴政跟前约徐福。
“等等。”见李斯转身要跨出殿门，徐福忙出声叫住了他。
李斯略略惊讶，回过头来看着徐福，眼中暗含惊喜和期待，莫非徐奉常要主动邀请他？
而徐福实际上只是将李斯从头到脚打量了一遍。
李斯知晓徐福职业病，但难免还是觉得有几分发毛，他忍不住低声问道：“徐奉常，我身上可是有何处不对？”
徐福摇了摇头，“没有不对劲之处。”
李斯露出心有余悸的笑容，“方才徐奉常倒是吓住我了。”
徐福挥了挥手，“去吧。”
李斯的背影消失在了殿门口。
而徐福却是有句话没对他说。就是没有不对劲之处，那才奇怪呢。要知道李斯对韩非心怀杀意，那么李斯的面相、气质之上都应当有具体的表现才是。
而令人觉得惊奇的正是，他满怀杀意，他的面相却并无怪异之处。
就连半点血光也无……
怎么会这样呢？李斯促进了韩非的死，他脸上应当带有血光才是！
徐福暂时按捺下了心中的疑问。
李斯走后不久，便有内侍走到殿外向韩非传达嬴政的意思。
“准、准了？”韩非结巴地问道，面上还有一丝怔然。就这样轻易地同意了？韩非不由得想到了方才出来的李斯。难道……难道是他又在秦王面前说了什么？他不是对自己不喜吗？为何还要帮自己求情好让自己去云阳？
恍恍惚惚回到宅子中的韩非，因为这个难解的谜题，陷入了辗转反侧的痛苦之中。
他哪里知道，李斯不过是等着先将他放养，然后再一举宰了呢？
在韩非还未收拾东西离开咸阳之前，他听闻了姚贾的声名。
姚贾此人还是颇有些名气的，只是这个名气并不好，他的出身经历颇受争议。而韩非恰好也瞧不上他这么一个人。韩非没想到，他竟然会投奔到秦国来，而且在这样短的时间里就得到秦王的派遣。
因为韩非在咸阳蹦跶了这么久，秦王都还没弄死他，于是咸阳中不少人还是比较尊重韩非的，他们担心自己一不小心就得罪了王上想要拉拢的人。于是当韩非问起的时候，他们也并未隐瞒，提及了姚贾将前往诸国，为秦王大业出一份力。
韩非一听，如何还能忍？这些话便如同戳在他的心尖子上一样。他会忍不住想到，姚贾也将会这样去对待韩国。
姚贾，小人也！
韩非胸中的斗士之魂再度燃起，反正要前往云阳的他，也不在乎最后和秦王掐的这几架了。于是韩非又请求入宫见秦王。
嬴政听到他请求的时候，还微微一愣。
韩非从前与他交谈的时候，因为嬴政眼界心胸的开阔，所以他很能接受韩非的思想，若非身份摆在那里，二人说不定也能成为知己。那段时间，韩非态度狂热，总往王宫而来。待到这股情绪过去之后，韩非认识到自己的东西有人认可欣赏之后，他便立即不与嬴政来往了。
嬴政在召他入宫，韩非都表现得如同在接触一个强迫自己的恶霸一般。
嬴政很快知道了韩非是个什么性子。除却他的国家和他的抱负，对待其他人，他就是个地道的白眼狼啊。白眼狼突然来找你了，那得是有什么大事，他才会这样做啊……
好奇的不止嬴政，还有徐福。
他们叫了韩非进殿来。
韩非今日有备而来，并且言辞激烈，开篇直入。
“王、王上，姚贾，此、此人不……可用。”韩非开口便道。
这口吻，简直就如当初尉缭粗暴地告诉徐福，秦王残暴，不可与之交游一样。徐福都有些目瞪口呆了。韩非是怎么样才能在快走的时候，还没忘记踩姚贾一脚的？
韩非似乎真的十分难以忍受姚贾，他引经据典，条理分明，将姚贾批得一文不值，不知不觉间倒是还能让人忘记他结巴的毛病。
“……姚贾以、以重金……贿、贿以各国君王！乃以王、王之权，国之宜，外自、自交于诸、诸侯。”
意思就是姚贾此人有异心，他竟然准备带着您的珍宝，借您的权势，去私自结交他国君王。这样的人怎能为秦国大臣？王上您还不快点清醒过来，看一看那人的丑恶面孔！这等奸佞就不应该留着啊！
徐福听罢，再度目瞪口呆了。
韩子啊，你还真是误会姚贾了，毕竟携带珍宝，结交君王，是嬴政发的话，姚贾再迎上来一拍而合罢了。
……难怪韩非一身才学，少有人能与之比，最后却还要落个死的下场。他这一手拉仇恨的功夫，谁敢与之相比啊？
嬴政态度冷漠拒之，丝毫不给他面子，遂令人将韩非送走。
韩非没想到自己这番话都未能打动嬴政，不甘不愿、满目不舍地被侍从架了出去。
看了一眼韩非那执拗的目光，徐福忍不住问出了心中不解，“韩非应当不是这样的人啊，他怎会在你我跟前，诋毁起姚贾呢？”
嬴政对韩非此举也有些不喜。
嬴政不一定多么喜欢姚贾，但姚贾的确是个聪明人，还有些可以派上用场的地方。与满腹才识但却孤傲不肯屈就的韩非相比，姚贾真是可爱太多了。韩非突然跑来说道一通，难道是指责自己眼瞎选了这么人物吗？
嬴政面色微冷，回答起徐福的话，“寡人从前便与你说过，姚贾此人名声不大好。”
徐福心中好奇不已，姚贾的名声究竟糟到了何等地步。
总不至于有历史上那个，被称作“鸡鸣狗盗之徒”的家伙那样糟糕吧。
见徐福满面好奇之色，嬴政心中兴味上来，便摇头道：“你且等一等，过不了几日，韩非还会再来，那时你便可知晓。”
徐福按捺住心中的好奇，继续做回了自己的高冷姿态。
嬴政忍不住抬手轻抚着他柔顺的发丝，一边处理着手头的事务，效率倒是奇异地高。
·
因为韩国使臣听闻了韩非自请前往云阳后，就微微慌了，连忙找到韩非处，与他进行不厌烦地讲述着韩王的意思。被缠住的韩非，一时间倒是没工夫去祸害姚贾了。
韩非在王宫中说的这番话并非什么机密，嬴政也未刻意遮掩住，很快便传开了。而之前告诉韩非消息的人，顿时懊悔不已。姚贾声名虽不好，但他毕竟在王上跟前也有地位了，好端端的，自己怎么就给了韩非一个机会，让他同姚贾掐起来呢？
韩国使臣越发折磨韩非，韩非便在姚贾之事上越战越勇。
他再一次来到嬴政的跟前，仍旧是当着徐福的面，道：“姚贾此、此人，梁监门、门子，尝、尝盗于梁，臣、臣于赵而、而逐。取世……监门子，梁之大、大盗，赵之逐臣，与、与同知社、社稷之计，非、非所以厉群、群臣也！”
这番话还被他说得铿锵有力，一副若是嬴政不采纳，他便悲痛万分的表情。只是因为结巴的缘故，难免将其中的情绪大打了折扣。
韩非这回的意思大约便是，姚贾不过是一个守门人的儿子，在魏国当过盗贼，还被赵国驱逐出境。这样一个看门人的儿子、魏国的盗贼、赵国的逐臣，让他参与国家大事，可不是勉励群臣的办法！秦王你不能如此蠢！
徐福又一次惊呆了。
他确实没想到姚贾会有这样丰富的经历，之前他观姚贾面相的时候，也并未放过太过心思，所以只瞧了他近年的际遇，和以后的轨迹。
不过更令徐福想不到的，还是嬴政竟然预料到了韩非的性子，是真的毫不客气，将姚贾的身份背景都揭了出来。不知道的恐还以为二人有什么深仇大恨呢。
徐福隐约猜到了两分韩非的心思。
姚贾欲前往诸国结交君王，为秦王的统一大业出力，这在秦国人看来，姚贾真是聪明又能干啊。但是在即将被收拾韩国的韩非眼中，姚贾便是要破坏他国家的人，是敌人，仇人，令他憎恶的人。
韩非哪怕舍下孤傲清高，也要到嬴政跟前踩姚贾一脚。
君王多疑。若是按照两年前嬴政对韩非的欣赏，说不定当真问也不问，便将姚贾推出去弄死了。可这已经不是过去了，嬴政对韩非的爱才之心渐渐淡了，又有李斯想弄死他，现在韩非又这样粗暴地去得罪一个聪明人姚贾。
韩非做的这一切，恐怕注定只是白费功夫。
徐福正低头思考着，突然听内侍道：“王上，姚贾求见。”
徐福不自觉地朝嬴政看了过去。他本来想对嬴政说，你应当不会被韩非所挑拨吧？不过在对上嬴政目光的那瞬间，徐福便有了点儿奇异的心灵相通的感觉。他很快便知道，至少如今的嬴政不会。
换做那个历史上的嬴政，还真说不准。
“让他进来，寡人正好要问一问他。”嬴政面色微沉道。他这话是说给韩非听的。
韩非的面色白了白，不过他很快就收拾好了情绪，立在殿中一侧，连半点的目光都不施舍到殿门口去，像是根本不屑瞧姚贾一眼。
脚步声渐渐近了。
姚贾跨过殿门进来，他面色绯红，可见其步履匆匆，会给人一种，为了自证清白而急促前来的感觉。等他到了殿中，便迅速整了整衣袍，面色也逐渐镇静下来，给人一种急而不乱的感觉。
而且他面见秦王，整理衣袍和表情的举动，很容易便讨好了上位者。
相比之下，耿直得过了头，衣服皱巴巴，脸色菜兮兮就敢来见嬴政的韩非，这二人根本就不是一个段位的啊。只要姚贾想，他恐怕就能靠着一张嘴，和真诚的面容，甚至是说动秦王除掉韩非。
徐福觉得自己也许一不小心，发现了什么历史上的桥段。
“王上，徐奉常。”姚贾与二人见了礼，却独独没搭理韩非。
韩非不掩饰自己的鄙夷，那是他确实坚持自有的底线，坚持自己心中的清流，是有几分君子之风的。
而姚贾也没掩饰自己对韩非的不待见，将真小人三个字体现得淋漓尽致，我不待见你，我也不会迎合你。
这二人……还挺有意思的。观战的徐福很不厚道地想。
嬴政的面色依旧阴沉，他迅速切入主题，厉声问责道：“韩子言，你乃世监门子，梁之大盗，赵之逐臣。姚贾，你可有话要为自己辩驳？”
听嬴政如此厉声问责姚贾，背后说人坏话，现在又与人面对面的韩非，心中稍稍松了口气。姚贾人品有劣，但本事却不小，若能令他与秦王离心，秦王更能将之逐之杀之，那便最好不过了。
韩非子今日也是这样天真地想着。
姚贾面色沉了沉，目光阴冷地朝韩非的方向扫了一眼，但也仅仅只是一眼而已，因为他很快便收回了目光。
徐福心中暗暗叹息。
韩非，姚贾，谁好谁坏，并不是一言便可断定的。
姚贾被赵王驱逐，却还能顽强生存在赵境内，后更是不服输地寻上自己与嬴政，准确稳妥地抱住了大腿，姚贾能忍常人所不能忍，他聪明，有口才，拍马屁功夫也是一流。
而韩非将毕生心血注于《韩非子》，他不通人情事故，哪怕受韩王多年冷待嘲讽，也能保持心中清流，他虽然傻得令人叹息，敬服，但也改变不了他傻的事实啊。
这样的韩非，招惹上这样的姚贾，徐福在心底忍不住为他心疼了会儿。
徐福转头看向韩非，见韩非终于将目光落在了姚贾的身上，只是那目光是冰冷的。
姚贾恍若未觉，他微微皱眉，面带忍受屈辱却依旧不卑不亢的表情，有条不紊地道：“王上请听姚贾几言。姜太公被妻子赶出家门，在朝歌做屠户时连肉都卖不出去，他还是被子良驱逐的家臣，在棘津时卖劳力都无人雇用。但文王慧眼独具，以之为辅佐，最终建立王业。管仲为商贩时，在南阳穷困潦倒，在鲁国时更被囚禁，但齐桓公却任用他建立了霸业。百里奚曾经也不过是一介乞丐，身价不过五张羊皮，而秦穆公任用他为相后却能无敌于西戎……”
姚贾的声音并未刻意带上铿锵有力之音，但他不疾不徐地道来，姿态更令人忍不住忽视他的出身背景，不自觉地去认同他所说的话。
这是徐福头一次，直面姚贾的口才之利。
连自己都被说服了……
徐福再往韩非看去，就见韩非的脸色异常难看了，眼眸里甚至还隐隐涌动着怒火，也不知他是固执地认为姚贾在诡辩，还是因为忍不住被姚贾说服而恼羞成怒。
徐福心中对姚贾的感官顿时上升了不少，不管他是诡辩还是真心实言，徐福都佩服他。
这也正是应了，曾经历史课上老师提到过的，秦王政时，他任贤用能，只瞧能力本事，却不瞧那人出身。与后世朝代任命状元探花还要看相貌相比，且看嬴政能对韩非摆出尊敬的姿态，秦朝时便已胜出太多。
看人看出身，有时候的确是有失偏颇的。
姚贾却还未说完，他的声音陡然一转，这才激烈了些许，道：“他们出身卑贱，身负恶名，甚至为人所不齿！但明主加以重用，是因为知道他们身负大才，能为有建立国家大业的功勋。若人人都如卞随、务光、申屠狄那样，又有谁能为国效命呢？”
韩非的脸色更难看了，姚贾这番话，就如同化作了巴掌，啪啪啪抽在他的脸颊上。
“英明之君不会计较臣子的过失，不会听信他人的谗言，而只会考察他们能否为己所用。”
“能够安邦定国的明君，不听信毁谤，不封赏空有清高之名、没有尺寸之功的人。正是因为如此，所有为臣之人才不敢用虚名希求于国君……”姚贾字字恳切，说到这里的时候，话锋还陡然一转。
道：“姚贾相信王上乃英明之君。”
一边将自己捧到了姜太公、管仲之流的位置上，又一边不动声色骂了韩非是个爱毁谤的人，是个空有清高名，没有尺寸功的人，最后再来个总结语，夸一夸秦王您是英明的，您是有慧眼的，您定然不会听信小人的。
这番话说完，韩非在旁已经憋得脸色涨红，半晌硬是说不出一句话来。
就他那结结巴巴的功夫，姚贾就能口舌伶俐，还挑不出半点错处地将他抵回去了。他实在不是姚贾的对手，短短一番话下来，胜负已分，更别说嬴政心头的天平早就不往韩非那边倾斜了。
徐福忍不住看着姚贾，淡淡道：“我倒是没有看错，你确是有才能的人物，你未来的命运想来是定然能改的。”徐福语气虽淡，但心底其实是在笑的。
像韩非这样的，那是真不好改，因为他个性执拗，拒绝被搓圆捏扁。而姚贾却是为了活命，为了名利，便能迅速适应环境的人，姚贾这样的人都不能改命，谁还能改命？所谓事在人为，便是姚贾这样的！
听徐福这般夸姚贾，韩非顿时更觉喉头哽血。
原本徐福对他也是礼遇有加的，但后来却渐渐冷漠以对，韩非对秦国不喜，但他对徐福是欣赏的，如今见徐福对小人姚贾颇有好感，韩非心里有种说不出的难受。
韩非神色黯淡，“是、是韩非……败了……”但他的语气可丝毫没有退让的意思。
姚贾微微一笑，彬彬有礼，并不与韩非说话。
韩非知道自己的算盘都被打破了，他自然也不会再腆着脸留于此处。
他躬身，向嬴政道，他欲明日便离开咸阳。
嬴政欣然同意，并命人将他送了出去。
因极为欣赏今日姚贾这一番话，嬴政还送了姚贾车架、珍宝甚至一把宝剑，可见秦王欣赏谁人时，是绝对不会有半分吝啬的。
徐福都不由得想起了，初时嬴政对他，就是共食一席，共睡一榻。
徐福也不知道自己想到哪里去了，脸色忍不住黑了黑。
可见嬴政……其实是个撩人的高手啊！
送走那二人之后，权当看了一场戏的嬴政心情颇好，谁知道转过头来，却见徐福面色不虞。嬴政自是立即便问道：“可是饿了？”
这一句话也不知为何又捅中了今日徐福的马蜂窝。
秦始皇你那么会撩也就罢了，为何我在你心中就是个时刻都需要被问候“饿了吗”的人！徐福深思起来，自己那高贵冷艳的形象，究竟是何处发生了转折，才会导致在嬴政心底发生了扭曲变异。
徐福百思不得其解，神思乱飞，一时间倒是忘记了搭理嬴政。
嬴政心中一派茫然。
纵然是很会撩臣子的嬴政，他也并不能完全洞悉喜欢的人的心思。
因为喜欢，所以小心翼翼，所以当局者迷，所以愈难看清。
不过出了大殿后，徐福很快就将这一茬忘得一干二净了。
·
秦王政十四年。
韩非收拾东西准备离开咸阳，另一边，姚贾也准备收拾东西离开，前往赵国。在赵国受尽欺辱，姚贾如今自然是要还回去的。
两人不偏不倚竟是恰好选了同一日离开，等两人的马车在城门口相撞，守城的士兵让他们下马车接受检查时，二人面对面，彼此都不掩饰眼底的不快。
实在是相看两相厌。
就连守城的士兵也听闻了二人的不对付，匆匆检查一番，便放二人走了。
在离开的这段路上，他们都难免一路同行。
韩非说不过姚贾，便只能被他气得脸色一日比一日红润。那是日日面色涨红，却无法抒发的后果。
直到两人分了道，韩非才骤然松了一口气。
韩非去往云阳的消息，很快由韩国使臣带会给了韩王。韩王等了许久郑国的好消息，却半点也没等到，如今寄希望于韩非，韩非却偏生又不合作。
韩王失望之极，又担心韩非是不是得罪了秦王，韩王夜晚入梦后，赵国的覆灭画面和韩国被攻上门的画面在脑中交替反复。
韩王终日思虑，眉间的愁绪一日胜过一日，内心的惶恐是可以打败人的最大武器。秦王一日不动韩国，却反倒令韩国提心吊胆，不知道秦国的屠刀，什么时候便会竖立在自己的头上。
韩王寻来贵族大臣，与众人商量如何能在秦国之下存活。
有人提议道：“秦王野心，众人皆知，唯有满足他的胃口，他方会收手，不然我韩国再如何卑躬屈膝，秦王放过韩国一时，却未必放过韩国一世。”
另又有人沉默一会儿，道：“以你之意，便是让韩向秦臣服吗？”
……
姚贾为秦王所用的消息很快也传遍了诸国，其中赵国气得最狠。姚贾曾是赵国大臣，后被其声名狼藉，以及赵王疑心其有异，便将其逐出赵国，当时姚贾可谓是丢够了面子，狼狈至极，顿时从大臣沦落为乞丐般的人物。
而如今这个赵国的旧臣，竟然转过头就帮着秦国来对付我们，果真不是好东西！
这样的臣子，如今能效忠秦王，日后谁知道他会不会为了其它利益，便效忠其他的君主呢？赵王心中冷笑不已，甚至暗暗期盼着秦王倒霉。
不过不管他如何期盼，起码在秦国倒霉之前，姚贾先以秦国使臣的身份进入了赵国。
再回到此地，他已然与从前不同了。赵王或许也爱才，但与秦王的慷慨和信任相比起来，赵王就是个心胸狭隘的小孩儿，两者在姚贾的心中，前者是地上的烂泥，后者是天边的星辰。
姚贾又不是生来性狠，他这样的人，谁对他好他能记住，他对他坏他更能百倍地记住。秦王待他如何，他深深记在心中，自然更要怀着不辜负秦王和坚决打击旧敌人的心思，让赵国上下吃了亏还说不出来了。
话分两头，姚贾在这边如何大展神威，徐福是不知晓的。
一转眼胡亥的年纪便也不小了。
除却徐福担任他的专业课老师以外，还总得有个教常识的。因着胡亥身份特殊，嬴政也并不想寻身份多么高的人来教导他，可身份若是太低，难免又教人看出端倪。
刚刚好，此时赵高站了出来。
他自请为胡亥教授知识。
赵高见识不算短，他是嬴政身边的宠臣，但毕竟身份算不得高，这样的人，正好适合与胡亥做老师。
胡亥与赵高也见过不少面了，只是胡亥的眼中，除了吃喝玩乐，便只剩下徐福和扶苏，大约……勉勉强强还可以算上一个嬴政吧。
他对赵高要当自己的老师，相当的不情愿。
“要父亲……”胡亥闷着脸重复这么一句话，稚嫩的气音从鼻子里喷了出来。作为一个秦王室中的公子，说话带喷气儿的，胡亥也真是头一份了。
徐福和扶苏见状，都不得不认为，胡亥是该好好学学常识礼仪了，否则日后代表秦王室的脸面，又打喷嚏又吐泡泡，还鼻子喷气……这该是如何美丽得让人不敢看的画面？
赵高哄孩子似乎很有一手，哪怕徐福和扶苏在一旁盯着，他也能镇定自若地蹲下身来，拼尽全力地去哄胡亥，胡亥毕竟年纪小，倒是很快便被赵高哄住了。
处理完熊孩子的学业问题，徐福便开始处理奉常寺的职位问题了。
靠着吹枕头风的超强功力，徐福顺利从奉常寺抽身。
奉常之位空了出来，奉常寺上下在见到徐福，双眼都是冒光的。虽然从前对徐福爱恨交加，但如今他们对徐福都变得极为喜欢了。能有一个根本不在乎官位和名利的上司，他能轻松让出屁股下的位置，这简直是难以遇上的好事！尽管他们都知道，哪怕是没了徐福，也还有王柳和苏邑，但这两人的位置若是变动，相应的下面也就有位置空出来了，总归不是坏事，总有人能吃到肉的。
徐福也没粗暴地直接定下人选，他带了个小内侍到奉常寺去打转，可以算作是调查众人品行的方式。
“徐奉常……”
“徐奉常今日也依旧气质出众，令我等望尘莫及啊……”
一踏进奉常寺的门，比起往日还要热忱数倍的人们，不远不近地在徐福的周围，做出自认为最真诚的表情，奋力夸奖着他。
如今这些人也知道，自己和徐福是绝对没有可比性的了。
若对方只是比你强上一些，那你或许还会嫉妒，或是觉得心有不甘。但当对方已经甩出你一大截，成为七国膜拜对象时，奉常寺中人也很清楚，他们是拍马也赶不上的，那还不如正视徐福的厉害之处。
王柳和苏邑作为与徐福最熟悉的人，此时也并不矫情，直接出来接走了徐福。
“你们二人对奉常之位，有何想法？”徐福直接了当地问道。在他离开咸阳的日子里，都是这两人在打理原本属于他的事务。徐福还真没打算亏待他们。
苏邑脸上露出了点笑容来，虽然他的眼角立刻就挤出了一条褶子皮，但那也是清俊的褶子皮，他道：“奉常之位，还是王柳更合适。”
原本低头漫不经心听着的王柳，霎地抬起了头，脸上毫不掩饰惊讶之色。
这是他从未想过的事情……
在如此年轻的年纪里，便能被人往奉常之位上推。就连他家里人都未曾想过……
苏邑无意奉常之位，徐福自然尊重他的意思，遂点了点头，“我知道了。”
王柳平复下心情，看着徐福的面容，看着这个曾经自己最为厌恶，到了后来却又最为佩服的人。
他低声道：“徐奉常若是要离开奉常寺，这个月，徐奉常可愿主持最后一次的月末卜筮？”
原本什么感觉也无的徐福，愣了愣，心底顿时涌上了一股难言的滋味。
虽然到了后来，他便少到奉常寺中来了，但突然间说要离开，倒还并不似想象中那样随意……
徐福的目光闪了闪，淡然点头，“好。”
徐福竭力忽略掉了内心那种高高竖起flag的感觉。
作者有话要说：　　记者：国尉你看韩子要被李斯弄死了，请问你有什么感想？
尉缭：哈哈哈哈哈哈哈哈哈我师弟对我真是太好了！谁让韩非摊上了这么个师弟呢╮(╯_╰)╭记者：……请问国尉您谜の优越感从何而来？
尉缭：╮(╯_╰)╭我师弟又不会弄死我。
记者：_(:зゝ∠)_原来不想着弄死师兄的师弟，就是感动七国好师弟了吗？
**
姚贾那段话，作者君语文课貌似还背过哈哈。姚贾这人，好坏参半吧，我觉得还蛮有好感的，真小人比伪君子好。韩非呢，立场不同，他有自己的坚持，傻得可爱。其实觉得他们在一起也不错，诶我的脑洞……
chapters.translated_text:
Han Fei seemed to sense Li Si’s intentions, so he took the initiative to request exile. When Li Si arrived at the palace, he happened to see Han Fei kneeling outside the hall, refusing to rise.

Han Fei was arrogant in front of Li Si, even though he could not avoid his stuttering habit when he spoke.

Li Si, hearing that he had requested to go to Yunyang, was stunned.

Since when did Han Fei start changing his tactics? Given his personality, shouldn't he be staying in Xianyang, enduring discomfort and humiliation for the sake of Han, and even if he didn't serve Qin, wouldn't he want to annoy the King of Qin to death?

One must know that Han Fei had certainly done his fair share of annoying things.

Besides, Li Si truly disliked this senior fellow apprentice. Han Fei was arrogant, so arrogant that he looked down upon the scheming Li Si. But Li Si considered himself no worse than anyone else; you, someone from Han struggling to survive, what right do you have to look down on me? Li Si generally didn't hold grudges, but once he did, it was usually hard to forget.

Li Si didn't claim to be a noble person either, so he felt no shame or guilt about overturning his previous words.

Li Si had planned it well, but he hadn't expected a change in variables regarding Han Fei...

But it didn't matter; Li Si walked into the hall unhurriedly, prepared to sound out the King’s intentions.

Xu Fu was sitting in the hall discussing Huan Yi with Ying Zheng when an attendant suddenly entered, saying that Li Si requested an audience.

Xu Fu thought of Han Fei, who was still kneeling outside, and felt a sudden sense of subtlety; he wondered what their moods would be like when the two of them met.

"Let him in," Ying Zheng said. He was also planning to take this opportunity to reveal his intentions to Li Si. Compared to Han Fei, Li Si was naturally more to his liking, and occasionally favoring one's subordinates could make them more dedicated.

Li Si walked in with a smile, but hesitated slightly upon seeing Xu Fu. Xu Fu and Wei Liao were also fellow apprentices; if he were to take action against Han Fei like this, would Xu Fu develop a negative opinion of him? Would he never regard him as a friend from now on?

That’s right, he had even told him in front of Xu Fu that he wouldn't take action against Han Fei; would this leave an impression of fickleness in his heart?

Li Si became deeply worried, so worried that he almost forgot his original purpose.

Coming back to his senses, he saw Xu Fu and Ying Zheng both staring at him.

"Long time no see, Guest Minister, are you well?" After returning to Xianyang, Xu Fu had only visited Wei Liao; if not for that, how could he have appeased Wei Liao’s wounded senior brother heart? That Xu Fu only saw him upon returning to Xianyang was enough for Wei Liao to show off (flex) in front of Li Si and Meng Tian.

Thinking about it, this was the first time Xu Fu had properly greeted Li Si since returning to Xianyang.

Li Si replied respectfully: "Except for the fact that Senior Brother Han Fei always brings about unpleasantness, everything is well with Si." This was said without any concealment, so frank that he might as well have stripped himself bare.

This could also be considered a roundabout explanation to Xu Fu.

Subsequently, Li Si turned toward Ying Zheng. He did not mention Han Fei immediately, but instead began discussing official business with Ying Zheng. It was precisely because of Li Si's ability to distinguish priorities that Ying Zheng did not mind his grudge against Han Fei.

After Li Si finished discussing official business, he finally brought up Han Fei.

Over these days, Li Si had already explained the reasons for wanting to eliminate Han Fei quite thoroughly, so now that he brought it up again, he only touched upon it lightly to avoid annoying the King.

"I intend to grant Han Fei’s request. Yunyang is not a wealthy place; if Han Fei goes there, he will merely suffer a bit," Ying Zheng said indifferently.

Li Si vaguely guessed the meaning behind Ying Zheng’s words and immediately smiled: "The King is wise." His sincere expression was actually quite similar to Yao Jia’s; one wonders if Li Si and Yao Jia would get along in the future?

A strange sense of distress regarding which side to take in the future rose in Xu Fu’s heart.

Originally, having not seen each other for a long time, Li Si would have liked to invite Xu Fu to his residence; he remembered when he and Su Yi used to sit and chat with Xu Fu, but now, thinking about it, it seemed like something that happened many years ago.

Li Si glanced at Ying Zheng subtly.

Although he respected the King and was grateful to him, at times like this, he really couldn't bring himself to love the King...

Li Si hid the emotions in his eyes and took his leave of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng in a disciplined manner. Li Si considered himself not yet capable enough to invite Xu Fu while in front of Ying Zheng.

"Wait." Seeing Li Si turn to step out of the hall, Xu Fu hurriedly called out to him.

Li Si was slightly surprised and looked back at Xu Fu, his eyes containing hidden surprise and anticipation; could it be that Master Xu was going to invite him?

In reality, Xu Fu was simply looking Li Si up and down from head to toe.

Li Si knew about Xu Fu’s professional habit, but he still couldn't help but feel a bit creeped out. He couldn't help but ask in a low voice: "Master Xu, is there something wrong with me?"

Xu Fu shook his head, "There is nothing wrong."

Li Si revealed a lingering smile, "Master Xu startled me just now."

Xu Fu waved his hand, "Go."

Li Si’s back disappeared at the palace entrance.

But there was one thing Xu Fu didn't tell him. It was precisely because there was nothing wrong that it was strange. One must know that Li Si harbored murderous intent toward Han Fei; therefore, there should have been specific manifestations in Li Si’s physiognomy and temperament.

And what was astonishing was that even though he was full of murderous intent, his physiognomy showed nothing strange.

Not even a hint of blood-light...

How could this be? Li Si was facilitating Han Fei’s death; there should be blood-light on his face!

Xu Fu temporarily suppressed the questions in his heart.

Not long after Li Si left, an attendant walked outside the hall to convey Ying Zheng’s decision to Han Fei.

"Gr-granted?" Han Fei asked, stuttering, a trace of bewilderment on his face. It was agreed to so easily? Han Fei couldn't help but think of Li Si, who had just come out. Could it be... could it be that he said something to the King of Qin again? Didn't he dislike him? Why would he help him plead his case so he could go to Yunyang?

Returning to his residence in a daze, Han Fei fell into the agony of tossing and turning because of this unsolvable puzzle.

How could he know that Li Si was just waiting to let him graze in the pasture before slaughtering him in one go?

Before Han Fei had packed his things to leave Xianyang, he heard of Yao Jia’s reputation.

This person, Yao Jia, was quite famous, but this fame was not good; his background and experiences were highly controversial. And Han Fei happened to look down on such a person. Han Fei did not expect that he would actually defect to Qin, and in such a short time, receive an assignment from the King of Qin.

Because Han Fei had been jumping around in Xianyang for so long and the King of Qin still hadn't killed him, many people in Xianyang still respected Han Fei, fearing that they might accidentally offend someone the King wanted to win over. So when Han Fei asked, they did not hide it and mentioned that Yao Jia was going to the various states to contribute to the King of Qin’s great cause.

Once Han Fei heard this, how could he endure it? These words were like stabbing his heart. He couldn't help but think that Yao Jia would treat Han the same way.

Yao Jia, a villain indeed!

The fighter’s soul in Han Fei’s chest ignited once again; since he was going to Yunyang anyway, he didn't care about these last few clashes with the King of Qin. Thus, Han Fei requested to enter the palace to see the King of Qin again.

When Ying Zheng heard his request, he was slightly stunned.

When Han Fei spoke with him in the past, because of Ying Zheng’s broad vision and mind, he was very receptive to Han Fei’s ideas; if not for their positions, the two might have become soulmates. During that time, Han Fei’s attitude was fanatical, and he constantly came to the palace. After this emotion passed, once Han Fei realized that his ideas were recognized and appreciated by someone, he immediately stopped associating with Ying Zheng.

When Ying Zheng summoned him to the palace, Han Fei acted as if he were dealing with a bully who was forcing him.

Ying Zheng quickly learned what kind of personality Han Fei had. Aside from his country and his ambitions, he was a thorough ingrate to everyone else. If an ingrate suddenly comes to find you, it must be because of something major...

It wasn't just Ying Zheng who was curious; Xu Fu was too.

They called Han Fei into the hall.

Han Fei came prepared today, and his words were fierce, getting straight to the point.

"K-King, Yao Jia, this person is... not usable," Han Fei said as soon as he opened his mouth.

This tone was exactly like when Wei Liao crudely told Xu Fu that the King of Qin was cruel and should not be associated with. Xu Fu was dumbfounded. How could Han Fei, when he was about to leave, still not forget to step on Yao Jia?

Han Fei seemed to truly find Yao Jia unbearable; he cited classics and reasoned clearly, criticizing Yao Jia as worthless, and inadvertently, one could even forget his stuttering habit.

"...Yao Jia uses heavy bribes... to bribe the rulers of various countries! Using the King's power and the country's resources to privately associate with the feudal lords."

The meaning was that this person Yao Jia had ulterior motives; he was actually preparing to take your treasures and use your power to privately associate with the rulers of other countries. How could such a person be a minister of Qin? King, wake up quickly and see the ugly face of that person! Such a treacherous villain should not be kept!

After hearing this, Xu Fu was dumbfounded again.

Master Han, you really misunderstood Yao Jia; after all, carrying treasures and associating with rulers was what Ying Zheng had ordered, and Yao Jia just went along with it.

...No wonder Han Fei was so talented, with few who could compare, yet he ended up with a death sentence. With this skill of drawing hatred, who would dare compare to him?

Ying Zheng rejected him coldly, giving him no face at all, and ordered someone to take Han Fei away.

Han Fei did not expect that even these words of his could not move Ying Zheng, and he was dragged out by the attendants, unwilling and full of reluctance.

Looking at Han Fei’s stubborn gaze, Xu Fu couldn't help but ask about the confusion in his heart, "Han Fei shouldn't be such a person; why would he slander Yao Jia in front of you and me?"

Ying Zheng was also somewhat displeased with Han Fei’s actions.

Ying Zheng didn't necessarily like Yao Jia that much, but Yao Jia was indeed a smart person and had some uses. Compared to the talented but arrogant Han Fei who refused to compromise, Yao Jia was much more likable. Han Fei suddenly ran over to lecture him; was he accusing him of being blind for choosing such a person?

Ying Zheng’s expression cooled slightly as he answered Xu Fu, "I told you before, Yao Jia’s reputation is not very good."

Xu Fu was filled with curiosity about just how bad Yao Jia’s reputation was.

It couldn't be as bad as that guy in history who was called a "person of petty tricks," could it?

Seeing Xu Fu’s curious expression, Ying Zheng felt a spark of interest and shook his head, "Just wait; in a few days, Han Fei will come again, and then you will know."

Xu Fu suppressed his curiosity and returned to his cold, aloof posture.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but reach out and gently stroke his smooth hair while handling the matters at hand, his efficiency strangely high.

·

Because the Han envoy heard that Han Fei had requested to go to Yunyang, he panicked and hurriedly found Han Fei to tirelessly recount the King of Han’s intentions. Entangled, Han Fei had no time to wreak havoc on Yao Jia for a while.

The words Han Fei spoke in the palace were not confidential, and Ying Zheng did not deliberately hide them, so they soon spread. And the person who had told Han Fei the news earlier was now full of regret. Although Yao Jia’s reputation was not good, he had a position in front of the King; why on earth did he give Han Fei a chance to clash with Yao Jia?

The more the Han envoy tormented Han Fei, the more courageous Han Fei became in the matter of Yao Jia.

He came to Ying Zheng again, still in front of Xu Fu, and said: "Yao Jia, this person, is the son of a gatekeeper in Liang, once a thief in Liang, and was expelled from Zhao. Taking the world... a gatekeeper’s son, a great thief of Liang, an expelled minister of Zhao, to discuss the plans of the state with him is not the way to encourage the ministers!"

He said these words with vigor, looking as if he would be heartbroken if Ying Zheng did not adopt his advice. It was just that because of his stutter, the emotions within were greatly discounted.

The meaning of Han Fei’s words this time was roughly that Yao Jia was just the son of a gatekeeper, had been a thief in Wei, and had been expelled from Zhao. To let such a gatekeeper’s son, a thief from Wei, and an expelled minister from Zhao participate in state affairs was not the way to encourage the ministers! King of Qin, you cannot be so stupid!

Xu Fu was stunned once again.

He really didn't expect Yao Jia to have such a rich history; when he observed Yao Jia’s physiognomy before, he hadn't put much thought into it, so he only looked at his recent encounters and future trajectory.

But what surprised Xu Fu even more was that Ying Zheng had actually anticipated Han Fei’s personality and was truly unceremonious, exposing Yao Jia’s identity and background. Those who didn't know might think the two had some deep-seated hatred.

Xu Fu vaguely guessed two parts of Han Fei’s thoughts.

Yao Jia wanted to go to the various states to associate with rulers and contribute to the King of Qin’s great cause of unification; in the eyes of the people of Qin, Yao Jia was truly smart and capable. But in the eyes of Han Fei, who was about to be dealt with by Qin, Yao Jia was the person who was going to destroy his country; he was an enemy, a foe, someone he loathed.

Even if Han Fei had to cast aside his arrogance and aloofness, he had to come to Ying Zheng to step on Yao Jia.

Kings are suspicious. If it were two years ago, given Ying Zheng’s appreciation for Han Fei, he might have pushed Yao Jia out and killed him without even asking. But this was no longer the past; Ying Zheng’s appreciation for Han Fei’s talent had gradually faded, Li Si wanted to kill him, and now Han Fei was crudely offending a smart person like Yao Jia.

Everything Han Fei did was probably destined to be a waste of effort.

Just as Xu Fu was bowing his head in thought, he suddenly heard an attendant say: "King, Yao Jia requests an audience."

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng involuntarily. He originally wanted to say to Ying Zheng, you shouldn't be provoked by Han Fei, right? But the moment he met Ying Zheng’s gaze, Xu Fu had a strange feeling of mutual understanding. He soon knew that, at least for the current Ying Zheng, he would not.

If it were the Ying Zheng in history, it would be hard to say.

"Let him in; I happen to want to ask him," Ying Zheng said with a darkened expression. He said this for Han Fei to hear.

Han Fei’s face turned pale, but he quickly composed his emotions and stood to one side of the hall, not even sparing a glance at the palace entrance, as if he disdained to look at Yao Jia at all.

Footsteps gradually approached.

Yao Jia crossed the palace door and entered; his face was flushed, showing his hurried steps, giving the impression that he had come in a rush to prove his innocence. Once he reached the hall, he quickly straightened his robes, and his expression gradually calmed down, giving the impression of someone who was hurried but not chaotic.

Moreover, his actions of tidying his robes and expression when meeting the King of Qin easily pleased the superior.

In contrast, Han Fei, who was too upright, with wrinkled clothes and a sallow complexion, dared to come to see Ying Zheng; these two were simply not on the same level. If Yao Jia wanted to, he could probably rely on his mouth and a sincere expression to even persuade the King of Qin to eliminate Han Fei.

Xu Fu felt that he might have accidentally discovered a plot point from history.

"King, Master Xu." Yao Jia greeted the two, but ignored Han Fei entirely.

Han Fei did not hide his disdain; that was his堅持 (insistence) on his own bottom line, his insistence on the clear stream in his heart, which had a bit of a gentleman’s style.

And Yao Jia did not hide his dislike for Han Fei, embodying the three words "true villain" to the fullest: I dislike you, and I won't cater to you either.

These two... were quite interesting. Xu Fu, watching the battle, thought uncharitably.

Ying Zheng’s expression remained gloomy, and he quickly cut to the chase, sternly questioning: "Han Fei says you are the son of a gatekeeper, a great thief of Liang, and an expelled minister of Zhao. Yao Jia, do you have anything to say in your own defense?"

Hearing Ying Zheng reprimand Yao Jia so sternly, Han Fei, who had been speaking ill of others behind their backs and was now face-to-face with them, felt a slight sense of relief. Yao Jia was a man of poor character, but his abilities were not to be underestimated. If he could be made to drift apart from the King of Qin, and the King of Qin could banish or execute him, that would be for the best.

Han Feizi was thinking just as naively today.

Yao Jia’s expression darkened, and he cast a cold, sharp glance in Han Fei’s direction, but it was only for a moment, as he quickly withdrew his gaze.

Xu Fu sighed inwardly.

Between Han Fei and Yao Jia, who was good and who was bad could not be determined by a single word.

Yao Jia had been expelled by the King of Zhao, yet he had managed to survive tenaciously within Zhao’s borders. Later, he had unyieldingly sought out Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, accurately and securely latching onto a powerful backer. Yao Jia could endure what others could not; he was clever, eloquent, and his flattery was top-notch.

As for Han Fei, he poured his life’s work into "Han Feizi." He was ignorant of worldly affairs, and even after years of cold treatment and mockery from the King of Han, he maintained a pure heart. While his foolishness was enough to make one sigh and admire him, it did not change the fact that he was indeed foolish.

With such a Han Fei provoking such a Yao Jia, Xu Fu couldn't help but feel a pang of pity for him in his heart.

Xu Fu turned to look at Han Fei, seeing that Han Fei had finally fixed his gaze upon Yao Jia, though that gaze was icy cold.

Yao Jia seemed not to notice. He frowned slightly, wearing an expression of enduring humiliation while remaining neither humble nor arrogant, and said in an orderly manner: "Your Majesty, please hear a few words from Yao Jia. When Jiang Taigong was driven out of his home by his wife and worked as a butcher in Zhaoge, he couldn't even sell his meat. He was a retainer expelled by Zi Liang, and when he was in Jijing, he couldn't even find work as a laborer. Yet King Wen had the discerning eye to use him as an advisor, eventually establishing a royal legacy. When Guan Zhong was a merchant, he lived in poverty in Nanyang and was even imprisoned in the State of Lu, yet Duke Huan of Qi employed him to establish hegemony. Baili Xi was once nothing more than a beggar, worth no more than five sheepskins, yet after Duke Mu of Qin appointed him as chancellor, he became invincible against the Western Rong..."

Yao Jia’s voice did not intentionally carry a resonant, powerful tone, but he spoke at a steady pace, his demeanor making one unable to ignore his background and causing one to unconsciously agree with what he said.

This was the first time Xu Fu had faced the sharpness of Yao Jia’s eloquence directly.

Even he had been persuaded...

Xu Fu looked at Han Fei again and saw that his face was exceptionally ugly, with anger faintly surging in his eyes. It was unclear whether he stubbornly believed Yao Jia was sophistical, or if he was embarrassed and angry because he couldn't help but be persuaded by Yao Jia.

Xu Fu’s opinion of Yao Jia rose significantly. Whether it was sophistry or sincere words, Xu Fu admired him.

This was exactly what the history teacher had mentioned: during the reign of King Zheng of Qin, he employed the virtuous and capable, looking only at their talent and ability rather than their background. Compared to later dynasties that judged candidates for the imperial examinations by their appearance, the fact that Ying Zheng could show respect to Han Fei already put the Qin Dynasty far ahead.

Judging people by their background is, at times, indeed biased.

Yao Jia had not finished yet. His voice suddenly shifted, becoming a bit more intense: "They were of humble origin, bore evil reputations, and were even despised by others! But an enlightened ruler used them heavily because he knew they possessed great talent and could contribute to the grand cause of the state. If everyone were like Bian Sui, Wu Guang, or Shen Tu Di, who would be left to serve the country?"

Han Fei’s face grew even uglier. Yao Jia’s words were like slaps landing repeatedly on his cheeks.

"A wise monarch does not dwell on the faults of his subjects, nor does he listen to the slander of others; he only examines whether they can be of use to him."

"An enlightened ruler who can secure the nation does not listen to slander, nor does he reward those who only have a reputation for nobility but no real achievements. It is precisely because of this that all subjects dare not seek favor from the ruler with empty names..." Yao Jia’s words were earnest, and as he reached this point, his tone shifted again.

He said: "Yao Jia believes Your Majesty is an enlightened ruler."

While placing himself in the ranks of Jiang Taigong and Guan Zhong, he simultaneously and subtly scolded Han Fei for being a slanderer—someone with an empty reputation for nobility but no real achievements—and finally concluded by praising the King of Qin for being wise and discerning, ensuring he would not listen to petty people.

After these words were finished, Han Fei stood by, his face flushed with frustration, unable to utter a single word for a long time.

With his stuttering, he was no match for Yao Jia’s glib tongue, which left no room for error. He was simply not Yao Jia’s opponent; after this brief exchange, the outcome was decided, not to mention that the scales in Ying Zheng’s heart had long since tilted away from Han Fei.

Xu Fu couldn't help but look at Yao Jia and say faintly: "I was not mistaken; you are indeed a person of talent. I imagine your future destiny will surely be changed." Although Xu Fu’s tone was calm, he was actually smiling inside.

Someone like Han Fei was truly hard to change because he was stubborn and refused to be molded. But Yao Jia was someone who could quickly adapt to his environment for the sake of survival, fame, and fortune. If someone like Yao Jia couldn't change his destiny, who could? The saying "human effort can change things" was exactly describing someone like Yao Jia!

Hearing Xu Fu praise Yao Jia like this, Han Fei felt a lump of blood rising in his throat.

Originally, Xu Fu had treated him with great courtesy, but later he had become gradually indifferent. Han Fei did not like the Qin State, but he admired Xu Fu. Now, seeing Xu Fu show such favor to the petty man Yao Jia, Han Fei felt an indescribable discomfort.

Han Fei’s expression dimmed. "It is... it is Han Fei who... has lost..." But his tone showed no sign of yielding.

Yao Jia smiled slightly, polite and refined, and did not speak to Han Fei.

Han Fei knew his plans had been shattered, so naturally, he would not linger here any longer.

He bowed and told Ying Zheng that he intended to leave Xianyang tomorrow.

Ying Zheng readily agreed and ordered someone to see him off.

Because he greatly appreciated Yao Jia’s words today, Ying Zheng even gifted Yao Jia a carriage, treasures, and a precious sword, showing that when the King of Qin appreciated someone, he was never stingy.
