正因着一次近乎交心般的瞎聊，徐福和嬴政之间的距离无形中被拉近了一些。情到深处，自然便会忍不住用肢体相交来表达心底的激烈之情。之后几日二人都是要大干一场才会罢休。
转眼到了蒹葭成婚这一日。
徐福记得很牢，所以哪怕前一夜并未休息好，他也揉着眼睑下淡淡的黑眼圈，从床榻上爬起来，并且命宫人选了一套黑色的衣袍。黑色在这样的场合会显得更加尊重人吧。
嬴政甫一睁开眼，便看见了徐福穿着黑袍的模样，他的头发被冠起，黑袍贴着白皙的脖颈，两种截然相反的颜色给人以极大的视觉冲击，嬴政心中一动，下身不自觉地便站了起来。
他撑着床榻坐了起来，被子滑下来，露出赤裸的胸膛，黑发垂落在紧实的肌肉上，他却不知自己也成了别人眼中一道富有野性，极为张狂的美景。
每回做完，徐福都很是想不通。
为什么自己做完看上去娘炮了？而嬴政就更男人味儿了？
难道是自己差了点儿肌肉？
徐福不自觉地抬手捏了捏自己的胸膛，嬴政瞥见他手上的动作，简直恨不得将徐福的手拉过来，搁在自己的胸膛上，缓慢抚摸而过，那样才叫好。
“如今已经不需去奉常寺了，为何今日起得这样早？”嬴政出声问道。若是起得晚些，他还能将人摁在床榻上，再吃一遍。
“我要出宫。”
“出宫？”嬴政心中危机感顿生，几乎是立刻便从床榻上起来了。
内侍忙上前递衣袍，嬴政接过来匆匆往身上一罩，走到了徐福的身边，“你要去何处？”徐福在咸阳城中认识的人并不多，无端出宫他能去做什么？
“蒹葭还记得吗？他要成婚，托人与我说了一声，我总要是去一趟的。”
不过是成个婚么……这话嬴政当然没有说出来。
“寡人与你同去。”嬴政不容拒绝地说完，随即便宽衣洗漱，同时还让人先送来了食物，二人用了一番。
徐福马上要走，嬴政却按住了他的手，“急什么？昏礼在黄昏时，你一早跑过去，恐怕府中都无人招待你。”
徐福愣了愣，迅速冷静下来。
是的，他差点忘记了，这可不是在上辈子，上辈子结婚都是大清早的便起来接新娘了，这辈子却是黄昏时才举行。
徐福按捺下来，与难得有闲暇时刻的嬴政坐在一处，他继续制药，嬴政则是在翻阅书简。
很快到了下午，二人这才坐车马车，缓缓出了宫。
到达蒹葭府上时，光看府外的打扮便能感受到说不尽的喜气了。等跨进府中，却只有三三两两的宾客，其中大部分还都是不认识的。这些人看上去打扮普通，自然也是认不出徐福和嬴政的。
还是过了一会儿，徐福才看见了桑中、柏舟等人，他们在见到徐福之后，都不约而同地面带微笑，而在见到嬴政后，他们却是齐齐打了个冷颤，好半天都说不出话来，更别说往徐福跟前来凑了。
嬴政冷飕飕地扫了他们一眼，便独自带着徐福寻了个地方落座。
不久后老管家出来招待众人，老管家是认识徐福的，但那老管家对徐福还有点提防，虽然徐福可是很久都没来府上了，但老管家怎么也忘不掉当初徐福来找他们家夫人的事啊……
万一他今日前来，是来主子墙角的，那可如何是好？
徐福本想着总归是熟人了，便对那老管家道：“蒹葭在何处？我能否前去探看？”其实徐福也就是有些好奇，蒹葭的成婚对象会是谁。
但老管家实在提防徐福，于是拉长了脸，拒绝与徐福交谈。哼，别以为他人老眼花，就看不见对方那张俊美的小脸如何勾人，这要是真去了，让夫人突然间嫌弃主子，不愿成婚了怎么办？
老管家称职地将徐福阻挡在了外面，徐福无法，也只能老实地等待蒹葭出来了。
不多时，便见着喜袍的两人出来了。
这时不兴红盖头，新娘子画着美丽的妆容，大大方方地出来了。
徐福心中还在暗自想着，也不知等龙阳君来见着这窈窕的姑娘时，心中该如何气愤难过了……
想着想着，蒹葭和他的新婚妻子便走近了。
只是徐福觉得哪里有点怪异……他皱了皱眉，陡然反应过来，嗯？等等，为何这新娘比新郎还要高呢？
大约是宾客中也有人发现了这一点，于是尴尬不已地笑了笑。
徐福准备厚着脸皮去打量那新娘的面容，却瞬间目瞪口呆。
这张面容，俊美，冷傲，用妆容修饰过后，便减了几分英气，多了几分媚气，实在是个大美人！
但这个大美人……他是龙阳君啊！
徐福瞬间无言以对。
难道龙阳君当真扮女子扮上瘾了吗？
龙阳君若有所觉地迎上徐福的目光，他还勾了勾嘴角，冲着徐福笑了笑，这副模样，与当初徐福刚见他时，简直判若两人。
不远处的老管家也若有所觉地看了一眼徐福，尤其在注意到龙阳君冲徐福笑了之后，老管家危机感瞬间浓重了起来，死死地盯着徐福不放。
徐福心中觉得好笑不已。
蒹葭和龙阳君行了昏礼，满堂宾客虽然觉得新娘怪异了些，但却无一人看出，那哪里是什么新娘，那分明就是名男子！
嬴政初时注意力都放在别处了，他也是后头才认出了龙阳君。
嬴政的目光闪了闪。
他没想到龙阳君会做到这般地步……不过嬴政更没想到的是，蒹葭竟然这样便与龙阳君成婚了？诸国之中虽常见好男风的人，但却从未听说过，哪个男子与哪个男子成婚了的。
嬴政模糊间觉得，蒹葭同龙阳君的昏礼，倒是为自己提供了点儿别样的想法。
徐福也看得津津有味。
上辈子虽说风气开放，但也少有同性结婚的例子，据徐福所知，反倒是骗婚的人更多，能见到蒹葭同龙阳君成婚，一时间徐福心中的感受还有些复杂。
蒹葭和龙阳君很快便离去了，连与徐福寒暄两句的时间也无。
老管家脸上终于见了笑容，他走到了徐福的跟前，“徐先生，多谢今日来参加主子的昏礼，您请。”
您请回吧，别再顶着好看的脸来勾引我们家夫人啦！
徐福知道老管家的心思，配合地抓住嬴政的手臂，跟着他一起往外走了。
老管家可认不出秦王的面孔，他只一眼看出这二人之间的气氛不对，太亲密了……哪有男子到了这个岁数，还这般亲昵挽着手臂的？老管家恍然大悟，难道是好男风的？他脸上瞬间就笑出了一朵花儿来，“先生，请……”态度无比热情地将徐福送出去了。
等离开了蒹葭的府邸，嬴政不由问道：“那老管家怎么突地又转变了态度？”
嬴政也知道那老管家的心思，若非如此，他早就发作了，哪能容得一个老管家来对徐福冷颜冷语。
“他啊……”徐福轻飘飘地道：“不过是瞧你我二人姿态亲密，便知我不会用这张脸去勾搭他们家夫人了。”
嬴政面色缓和了些，“这老管家总算有了点眼光。”
有什么眼光？有眼光看出了我们是一对儿？徐福转头瞥了嬴政一眼，从他的脸上发现了隐藏着的喜色。
徐福不自觉地也跟着露出了点儿喜色，虽然是在眼底。
二人上了马车回宫。
虽然这一趟似乎什么也没做，不过二人都不约而同地觉得，给了极大的启发，至于启发的是什么方面，那就各自不一了。
回到寝宫后，嬴政开口说了第一句话，“……蒹葭龙阳尚且敢举以昏礼，寡人与你为何就不能有呢？”嬴政的口气竟然是酸的。
身为秦王，连这都会嫉妒？
徐福眨了眨眼，“你为秦王，自然不似蒹葭和龙阳君那般随心肆意。”
嬴政摇头，“阿福说得不对，正是因为寡人乃秦王，才应当能随心肆意的。在国事上，寡人须得处处斟酌，但家事上，寡人是能随心做主的，不然这秦王哪里还能称得上是君王呢？”
家事。
徐福心中微微一动。
从未听过这两个字被用在他的身上，感受好不新颖！
“那你欲如何？”徐福出声问。他的表情看上去冷淡镇定，但实际上，徐福也不知道为什么自己的心跳还有些快。
嬴政察觉到了徐福掩藏住的紧张，他嘴角动了动，忍不住笑道：“此事寡人会好生斟酌，寡人怎能让蒹葭、龙阳君二人越过我们去？”
徐福发觉自己有点难以控制心跳的速度了。
这也便罢了，听过之后，他心上竟然还有些痒痒，脸颊也忍不住发热，就如同莫名其妙生了什么病一样。
“……嗯。”为了掩饰自己不正常的情绪，徐福含含糊糊应了一声。
嬴政知道徐福还未全然信任自己，他只当这都是徐福从前一心修卜筮之道的后遗症，心中虽然想要叹气，也还是被嬴政生生忍住了。
蒹葭和龙阳君的昏事被扔到了脑后去。
因为嬴政思虑起了，如今没了奉常之位，徐福应当做什么好呢？
徐福如今反倒是不大在意了，这和他初到秦国时急需官位保身不同，也和他后期需要在奉常寺中好好生存，更急需升职不同。这时他背后有个嬴政不说，他本身的手段也已经让众人都见识到了，无人再敢轻视于他，更何况在他的辛苦经营下，在嬴政的有意推动之下，他的名气已经越发地大了。
正合了当初他的想法。
若是有一日与嬴政过得不快，那去别国也是行的，反正他也名扬诸国了，到时候说不定还能留给世人一个神秘的形象，只是会可惜了国师之位。
“此事不必时刻放在心上，顺其自然便可。”徐福反过来劝了嬴政一句，便没心没肺地日日到偏殿中，去瞧赵高如何给胡亥授课了。
就这样盯了几天，徐福也没看出赵高有何处不对劲。看来当真是自己以小人之心度君子之腹了？徐福没敢就这样彻底放了心，因为胡亥和赵高这二人组合到一起的危险性，还是让他在心底多留了个心眼。
转眼便要到秦王政十六年了。
就在蜡祭前，赵国和韩国强行送来了美人，同时姗姗回来还有姚贾。
嬴政并未召见赵国和韩国使臣，而是先将姚贾叫到了宫中来。
姚贾风尘仆仆，还没来得及做休息，便匆匆进宫来了，或许是连日赶路的缘故，姚贾的面容有些憔悴，就连眼底都染上了红血色。但这并不是令徐福感觉到惊奇的地方。
徐福心中重重一跳，不由得将身子坐得更直。
他紧紧盯着姚贾的面孔，发现他的面上罩着一层淡薄的血光。
血光……
这当然不是传统意义上所谓的血光之灾，而是徐福从前想要从李斯脸上寻找，却硬是半点也没寻到的血光。
韩非……死于姚贾？
徐福总觉得哪里有些怪异，但仔细一想，却又没什么不对。韩非之前可都那样得罪姚贾了，姚贾心中要是半分也不记恨，那才是怪事！何况韩非自己都说姚贾是小人，不是君子。
作为一个小人，哪里还会有什么高尚的情操来放你一马呢？
徐福不动声色地观察着姚贾，姚贾并未察觉到他的目光，姚贾勉强压下疲态，细细为嬴政禀报连日来发生的事。
短短的时日内，姚贾很难有所成，嬴政也知晓这一点。
不过徐福倒是忍不住想到，若韩非在此，恐怕又要借此来抨击姚贾了。
正说话间，有一内侍狂奔到殿外，跪地道：“王上，云阳来了消息。”
“取来。”
那内侍走进来，递上绢布。
徐福本能地觉得有点不大好。
嬴政展开绢布，扫了一眼，面上闪过惊讶之色，但惊讶又并不浓，似乎他早就料到了一般。
徐福心中隐约也猜到了两分。
果然，韩非的命还是没法子改吗？
嬴政放下绢布，低声道：“韩子在云阳，意外中毒身亡。”说这句话的时候，嬴政的目光往姚贾身上扫了扫。
姚贾仍旧无所觉一般，他站在那里动也不动，满面冰寒之色。
徐福心中就纳闷了。
姚贾身在他国，是如何将韩非弄死的呢？姚贾如今身份今非昔比，他可没有什么人手可以调动到云阳去弄死韩非。
chapters.translated_text:
Why on earth would Jianjia have something to entrust to a little eunuch to give to him? For a split second, Xu Fu even imagined a scene where Jianjia was suffering, wronged, and had nowhere to appeal, finally using all her strength to entrust a token to the little eunuch...

But Xu Fu soon realized he was overthinking it.

The little eunuch presented bamboo slips, bound together into a volume. Xu Fu vaguely remembered that such things were used to carry blessings and auspicious words.

In other words, at this time, they were mostly used as invitations.

What kind of invitation?

Weddings, funerals, moving house, or dividing the family—all required invitations to convey the message. No one in Jianjia’s family had passed away, he wouldn't move without reason, and there was no talk of dividing the family. That left only one possibility... Was Jianjia getting married?

Thinking of Jianjia’s young and beautiful face, Xu Fu found it a bit hard to accept for a moment. Then again, people in ancient times married early; many had offspring before they were even adults. If Jianjia were to marry at this time, it wouldn't be strange at all.

Xu Fu put away the bamboo slips and, seeing the little eunuch smiling brightly, couldn't help but ask, "You've worked hard. What is your name?"

The little eunuch blushed and whispered, "Zhao Cheng."

Xu Fu didn't have any impression of the name, but since the little eunuch had delivered things to him many times, Xu Fu secretly noted it down. He nodded at Zhao Cheng before leaving.

Xu Fu took the bamboo slips to have his meal first, and only after eating did he open them to carefully read what was written.

It roughly stated that a joyous occasion was approaching and requested that the Fengchang (Master of Ceremonies) Xu must attend. It didn't even list the names of the bride and groom.

Xu Fu was genuinely curious about who was marrying Jianjia, as it was quite sudden. Anyone would be curious. After returning to his sleeping quarters, Xu Fu casually placed the bamboo slips on the table; even if Ying Zheng saw them, he didn't think there would be any issue.

He didn't wait for Ying Zheng to return first; instead, he received the end-of-month divination bamboo slips sent by the Fengchang Temple.

The bamboo slips were piled on the table. He grabbed one and flipped through it. Based on the divinations from that day, they had added more detailed content. The extent of their improvement surprised Xu Fu.

These people had some aptitude, but they hadn't taken the art of divination seriously before, just muddling through, which was why they hadn't stood out. Now, having received Xu Fu’s guidance, they had experienced an epiphany, and with a little more effort, they had naturally grown quite a bit.

But the most outstanding among them was still Wang Liu.

Seeing his work, Xu Fu wasn't surprised. He had known Wang Liu was capable when he first arrived at the Fengchang Temple. If it hadn't been for the unfortunate timing of meeting him, Wang Liu would have been one of the top figures in the temple. Once Wang Liu let go of his arrogance and began to study seriously, he underwent a complete transformation—his temperament changed, and even his skill in divination improved drastically.

Wang Liu analyzed the hexagrams in detail.

He believed that the State of Qin would offend someone, thereby inviting some disaster.

But the State of Qin was currently powerful, even to the point of being invincible. Who else could be called a "tiger" in front of Qin?

Xu Fu read Wang Liu’s analysis. At first glance, it made sense, but as someone who stayed by Ying Zheng’s side, Xu Fu had seen much more and quickly spotted the irrationality from another perspective. After ruling out these analyses one by one, Xu Fu set the bamboo slips aside for the time being.

They were different from him; they didn't have his unique advantages, so naturally, they would miss certain considerations. However, this time Xu Fu didn't say they were wrong; instead, he ordered someone to bring more bamboo slips and used a stylus to carve words of praise on them.

Constantly negating others wasn't a good thing, after all...

Along with these bamboo slips, Wang Liu’s appointment order was issued; he was officially promoted to the position of Fengchang, and Xu Fu honorably resigned from the Fengchang Temple. The people in the temple had thought it would take a long time for Xu Fu to be willing to step down, but they never expected him to be so carefree.

In their eyes, the end-of-month divination had become the final assessment. Everyone regretted not working harder, thinking that if they had, they might have been promoted too.

When they got their hands on Wang Liu’s bamboo slips and passed them around, they couldn't even feel jealous anymore.

Wang Liu might have a bad temper, but his ability was beyond doubt.

Soon, the Fengchang Temple was filled with sounds of congratulations.

Wang Liu’s face finally regained his former arrogance. He clutched the appointment order and turned to ask Su Yi, "You were closer to him than I was, why did you push the position of Fengchang away?" After asking, he couldn't help but bite his lip, his eyes revealing a hint of expectation.

Su Yi frowned and pondered for a moment, "...Being Fengchang is troublesome."

Wang Liu’s eyes widened, and he was almost angered to the point of fainting.

To be yielded to by a rival like this... he couldn't feel happy at all.

·

He had been standing in the shadows for quite a while.

The window in front of him was half-open, and the light outside flickered on his cold, stern face. Xu Fu stepped into the hall, looking in his direction, his heart trembling slightly.

Was he unhappy again today?

Xu Fu called the eunuch to his side, "What happened in the hall today?"

The eunuch didn't know that Ying Zheng hadn't told Xu Fu yet, so he lowered his voice and told Xu Fu everything without missing a word.

"It is said that both the Zhao and Han states have intentions of forming a marriage alliance with Qin."

A marriage alliance? Xu Fu immediately thought of the most cliché plot—marrying a princess to the King of Qin.

"The King refused, and the ministers were extremely anxious. They repeatedly urged the King in court not to bear the reputation of being a tyrant, saying that he should stop attacking Zhao and accept the goodwill of Han."

Xu Fu found it amusing. These ministers, who didn't contribute a shred of effort, were now rushing to point fingers. According to them, did they expect Ying Zheng to marry two princesses at once?

The eunuch hadn't finished yet. He curled his lip in indignation and continued, "The King refused them one by one and strictly ordered them not to mention it again. But then someone stood up and asked if the King refused to take concubines because of you. Once that was said, the court immediately fell into chaos..."

"What are you talking about?" Ying Zheng noticed the commotion, looked over with a cold expression, and strode toward them.

The eunuch’s face turned pale instantly. He knelt on the ground in terror, trembling as he called out, "Your Majesty..."

"Who gave you the courage to discuss court matters?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.

The eunuch was almost scared out of his wits. He prostrated on the ground, not daring to lift his head, only muttering, "Your Majesty, this servant..."

Xu Fu interrupted him, "I heard a few words, should I kneel down too?"

Ying Zheng detected the emotion hidden in Xu Fu’s words, and the coldness on his face faded, becoming much softer, "I didn't intend to tell you about such trivial, troublesome matters."

"It is precisely because you didn't tell me that I had to ask him." Xu Fu didn't hide his displeasure. He frowned, his expression cold, "This feeling is very unpleasant."

Ying Zheng was stunned, but he admitted his mistake quickly, "If you don't like it, I won't hide things from you in the future."

"There is nothing to hide, and you can't hide it from me." If he wanted to know, he could easily find out, especially about such matters; he only needed to ask his senior brother, Wei Liao, to know everything clearly. Rather than hearing it from others, it was better for Ying Zheng to tell him everything himself.

If it really came to him asking Wei Liao, there was no telling how Wei Liao might embellish the story.

Ying Zheng immediately realized the potential issue. He had originally just been annoyed by the ministers and didn't want to bring that mood to Xu Fu, but he hadn't realized that he was creating a barrier between them.

Realizing this, Ying Zheng couldn't fix it fast enough!

He had finally managed to feel that Xu Fu had feelings for him; if he messed it up because of those ministers, he would be furious!

"It was nothing important, just those people being idle and worrying about things in the palace. How many concubines I have is not for them to decide," Ying Zheng snorted coldly.

Xu Fu was unhurried.

At this time, the trend of ministers stuffing their daughters or sisters into the monarch’s harem hadn't become popular yet... At this moment, the ministers were just short-sighted, thinking that letting the King "harm" another country's princess would somehow make them look good.

Xu Fu could still find the leisure to complain in his heart because he had enough trust in Ying Zheng.

Who was Ying Zheng? He didn't fear the ministers; on the contrary, the ministers feared him. If Ying Zheng were truly angry, he could even exile his own mother, let alone these ministers. If someone was truly ignorant, Ying Zheng wouldn't sacrifice his own happiness for the sake of some reputation.

"When the Son of Heaven is angry, a million corpses fall"—that was Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng was a man of strong will; as long as he didn't want to, the ministers wouldn't keep courting death. It was just a matter of this period, and it would soon pass.

Xu Fu thought clearly, but Ying Zheng felt a bit awkward. Was Xu Fu still not valuing him enough? Even after hearing such news, he remained completely unmoved.

Ying Zheng suppressed the disappointment in his heart and was about to change the subject.

Xu Fu suddenly remembered a question he had kept in his heart for a long time, and it was a perfect time to ask it directly.

"A-Zheng, why are you unwilling to accept the goodwill of Zhao and Han?" Xu Fu’s voice was as soft as he could make it, though because of his naturally cold tone, the improvement wasn't much. But if one listened carefully, they could hear the warmth in his voice.

Ying Zheng didn't even think before saying, "There is only one you in the world; how can anyone compare to you?"

Xu Fu, who had reminded himself several times that sweet talk was poison, still couldn't help but tremble in his heart, as if someone had touched a string, leaving him unable to calm down for a long time.

Xu Fu opened his mouth.

Ying Zheng watched him quietly, his heart suddenly beating faster. For some reason, Ying Zheng held his breath, feeling as if something major was about to happen.

"Then, A-Zheng, what are your feelings for me?" Xu Fu asked softly. His voice was lower and warmer.

Ying Zheng was stunned for a moment, then a wave of ecstasy surged in his heart.

Was Xu Fu finally discovering his affection? Did Xu Fu want him to confess his feelings? Ying Zheng couldn't suppress his excitement for a long time. His chest rose and fell slightly, his whole body tense, standing like a tall mountain in front of Xu Fu.

"My feelings for you..." He started, but was startled by his own hoarse voice. He paused, then continued, "My feelings for you, naturally..." Naturally what? Ying Zheng was speechless. He couldn't find the right words to describe it.

What should my feelings for you be?

Ying Zheng only knew that his heart was filled with Xu Fu alone, but he hadn't thought about the finer, deeper details.

Ying Zheng had had concubines, but he had never had someone he truly loved.

So-called love and admiration. Ying Zheng had poured all the love and admiration of his life into Xu Fu alone.

...

Xu Fu stared at Ying Zheng’s face. Seeing Ying Zheng stop after just starting, Xu Fu rarely saw him so distracted. Xu Fu’s heart beat faster involuntarily. He felt his whole body tense up, and even his breathing became soft.

This was so rare for him.

It’s okay, wait a little longer...

After Ying Zheng started, Xu Fu felt he had to know the answer. If it were before, if Ying Zheng didn't say it, he might have lost patience and gone to sleep. But today, he was surprised to find his patience had increased.

He could wait.

Because he was too fixated on the answer, Xu Fu didn't notice that in that instant, Ying Zheng looked at him and blurted out, "My feelings for you." It was "I," not "the King." Perhaps neither of them noticed, but something had changed in the unseen.

...

"My feelings for you are simply that I only wish to be with you, and apart from you, I can no longer see anyone else." Ying Zheng’s voice was still hoarse, but he said it all in one breath.

After finishing, he kicked the eunuch prostrate on the ground. The eunuch stiffened and ran out, crying and laughing at the same time.

Heavens!

He had actually witnessed such a deep moment of affection from the King... If he told anyone, no one would believe him. No, that wasn't true; everyone in the palace knew that if there was one special person in the King’s heart, it was Master Xu.

Finally seeing the King express his heart to Master Xu, the eunuch didn't know why, but he felt his spirits soar, unable to stop the joy in his heart, forgetting all about the fear of being scolded just moments ago.

...

Ying Zheng being so frank made Xu Fu feel stunned. Now that he had the answer, what should he say? What should he do? He didn't know either. He had just wanted to know the answer...

But he couldn't just say a dry "Oh" to Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu accidentally met Ying Zheng’s gaze. The tenderness and fervor that the other party no longer hid almost drowned him. Xu Fu was startled and wanted to look away, but found he couldn't.

"Hmm..." Unable to delay any longer, Xu Fu could only force out, "Hmm." Hmm what? Hmm, I like you too? Not really. Xu Fu was a bit lost. Ying Zheng could confess so generously, why couldn't he even say "I like you"?

"Although I am not like you, I also like A-Zheng very much," Xu Fu said with a blank expression.

After saying that, he felt it wasn't so difficult after all.

"..."

Silence spread between them.

What did that mean? Suddenly stopping? Xu Fu looked up at Ying Zheng, only to see the majestic King of Qin, the future First Emperor, with his mouth slightly agape, showing an expression of astonishment.

Xu Fu curled his lip in displeasure.

Was what he said so shocking? Ying Zheng actually had that expression!

"I... am very happy," Ying Zheng said, regaining his composure, his expression complex. It was like a sentence he had longed for for a long time had finally been received; the impact was so great that he couldn't recover for a moment.

Ying Zheng began to think secretly.

Since he and Xu Fu were now in mutual love, there would naturally be no one else beside them in the future, and the Queen of Qin would naturally become Xu Fu. Ying Zheng even thought that since Xu Fu was no longer the Fengchang, he might as well just become the Queen...

But in the end, Ying Zheng just thought about it. He could ignore etiquette and ministers, but he worried about making Xu Fu angry.

After setting aside this absurd idea, Ying Zheng felt much lighter.

Xu Fu felt the same way at this moment.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but speak to break the stagnant atmosphere, "I am so deeply affectionate toward you, how will you repay me?"

"Repay?" Xu Fu looked around the hall. He didn't know when everyone else had left. His gaze swept to the door, where the palace servants shivered in unison and then consciously closed the doors.

So, after a moment of silence, Xu Fu generously began to undress, "Hmm, repay like this."

It was the most practical repayment!

Ying Zheng was absolutely delighted!

...

·

Because of this heart-to-heart chat, the distance between Xu Fu and Ying Zheng was invisibly shortened. When feelings reached a certain depth, they naturally couldn't help but use physical intimacy to express their intense emotions. For the next few days, the two of them would go at it until they were exhausted.

In the blink of an eye, it was the day of Jianjia’s wedding.

Xu Fu remembered it well, so even though he hadn't rested well the night before, he rubbed the dark circles under his eyes, climbed out of bed, and ordered the servants to choose a black robe. Black would show more respect on such an occasion.

As soon as Ying Zheng opened his eyes, he saw Xu Fu in the black robe. His hair was crowned, and the black robe clung to his fair neck; the two contrasting colors gave a great visual impact. Ying Zheng’s heart stirred, and his lower body stood up involuntarily.

He sat up, the quilt sliding down to reveal his bare chest, his black hair falling onto his firm muscles. He didn't know that he had also become a wild, arrogant, and beautiful sight in someone else’s eyes.

Every time they finished, Xu Fu couldn't understand.

Why did he look feminine after they were done? And why did Ying Zheng look even more masculine?

Was it because he lacked a bit of muscle?

Xu Fu couldn't help but reach out and pinch his own chest. Ying Zheng, catching the movement, wished he could pull Xu Fu’s hand over and place it on his own chest, slowly stroking it—that would be better.

"You don't need to go to the Fengchang Temple anymore, why get up so early today?" Ying Zheng asked. If he got up later, he could have pinned him to the bed and had him again.

"I am going out of the palace."

"Out of the palace?" A sense of crisis arose in Ying Zheng’s heart, and he got out of bed almost immediately.

The eunuch hurried forward to hand him his robe. Ying Zheng put it on hastily and walked to Xu Fu’s side, "Where are you going?" Xu Fu didn't know many people in Xianyang; why would he go out of the palace for no reason?

"Remember Jianjia? He is getting married and sent someone to tell me. I have to go."

It’s just a wedding... Ying Zheng didn't say this out loud.

"I will go with you," Ying Zheng said in a tone that brooked no refusal. He then dressed and washed, and had food brought in for them to eat.

Xu Fu was about to leave, but Ying Zheng held his hand, "What’s the rush? The wedding ceremony is at dusk. If you go early, there probably won't be anyone to entertain you."

Xu Fu was stunned and quickly calmed down.

Yes, he had almost forgotten; this wasn't his past life. In his past life, weddings were held early in the morning, but in this life, they were held at dusk.

Xu Fu settled down and sat with Ying Zheng, who had rare leisure time. He continued to make medicine, while Ying Zheng flipped through bamboo slips.

Soon it was afternoon, and the two took a carriage and slowly left the palace.

When they arrived at Jianjia’s mansion, they could feel the endless joy just by looking at the decorations outside. When they stepped inside, there were only a few guests, most of whom he didn't recognize. These people looked plainly dressed and naturally couldn't recognize Xu Fu or Ying Zheng.

It was only after a while that Xu Fu saw Sang Zhong, Bo Zhou, and others. They all smiled when they saw Xu Fu, but when they saw Ying Zheng, they all shivered and couldn't speak for a long time, let alone approach Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng swept a cold glance at them and took Xu Fu to find a seat alone.

Not long after, the old steward came out to entertain the guests. The old steward recognized Xu Fu, but he was still wary of him. Although Xu Fu hadn't been to the mansion for a long time, the old steward couldn't forget the time Xu Fu came looking for their lady...

What if he came today to steal his master’s wife? What would happen then?

Xu Fu thought they were acquaintances, so he said to the old steward, "Where is Jianjia? Can I go see him?" In fact, Xu Fu was just curious about who Jianjia’s partner was.

But the old steward was very wary of Xu Fu, so he pulled a long face and refused to talk to him. Hmph, don't think that just because he was old and dim-sighted, he couldn't see how seductive that handsome face was. If he really went in and made the lady dislike the master and refuse to marry, what then?

The old steward dutifully blocked Xu Fu, and Xu Fu had no choice but to wait honestly for Jianjia to come out.

Before long, he saw two people in wedding robes come out.

At this time, there was no red veil; the bride came out openly with beautiful makeup.

Xu Fu was thinking to himself, wondering how angry and sad Lord Longyang would be when he saw this graceful girl...

As he thought, Jianjia and his new wife approached.

But Xu Fu felt something was a bit strange... He frowned and suddenly realized, "Huh? Wait, why is the bride taller than the groom?"

Perhaps some guests noticed this too, and they smiled awkwardly.

Xu Fu prepared to shamelessly examine the bride’s face, but was instantly dumbfounded.

This face, handsome and cold—with makeup, it had less heroic spirit and more charm; he was truly a great beauty!

But this great beauty... he was Lord Longyang!

Xu Fu was instantly speechless.

Was Lord Longyang really addicted to dressing as a woman?

Lord Longyang seemed to sense Xu Fu’s gaze and met it, even curling his lips and smiling at Xu Fu. This appearance was like a different person from when Xu Fu first met him.

The old steward in the distance also sensed something and glanced at Xu Fu. Especially after noticing Lord Longyang smiling at Xu Fu, the old steward’s sense of crisis intensified, and he stared at Xu Fu unblinkingly.

Xu Fu found it hilarious.

Jianjia and Lord Longyang performed the wedding ceremony. Although the guests felt the bride was a bit strange, no one noticed that it wasn't a bride at all, but a man!

Ying Zheng’s attention had been elsewhere at first, and he only recognized Lord Longyang later.

Ying Zheng’s eyes flickered.

He didn't expect Lord Longyang to go to such lengths... But what Ying Zheng didn't expect even more was that Jianjia would marry Lord Longyang just like that? Although it was common to have a fondness for men among the states, he had never heard of one man marrying another.

Ying Zheng vaguely felt that Jianjia and Lord Longyang’s wedding gave him some different ideas.

Xu Fu also watched with great interest.

Although his past life was open-minded, there were few examples of same-sex marriage. As far as Xu Fu knew, there were more cases of fraudulent marriages. Seeing Jianjia and Lord Longyang marry, Xu Fu’s feelings were a bit complex.

Jianjia and Lord Longyang soon left, without even time for a brief chat with Xu Fu.

The old steward finally smiled and walked up to Xu Fu, "Master Xu, thank you for coming to the master’s wedding today. Please."

Please leave, and don't use that handsome face to seduce our lady again!

Xu Fu knew the old steward’s thoughts and cooperated by grabbing Ying Zheng’s arm and walking out with him.

The old steward couldn't recognize the King of Qin, but he saw the atmosphere between the two was wrong—too intimate... What man at this age would still hold arms so affectionately? The old steward suddenly realized, were they fond of men? His face instantly bloomed with a smile, "Master, please..." He sent Xu Fu out with extreme enthusiasm.

After leaving Jianjia’s mansion, Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask, "Why did that old steward suddenly change his attitude?"

Ying Zheng also knew the old steward’s thoughts; otherwise, he would have acted long ago and wouldn't have tolerated an old steward being cold to Xu Fu.

"Him..." Xu Fu said lightly, "He just saw that you and I are intimate, so he knew I wouldn't use this face to seduce their lady."

Ying Zheng’s expression softened, "This old steward finally has some insight."

What insight? Insight to see we are a couple? Xu Fu turned to glance at Ying Zheng and discovered the hidden joy on his face.

Xu Fu couldn't help but show a bit of joy himself, though it was in the depths of his eyes.

The two got into the carriage and returned to the palace.

Although they seemed to have done nothing on this trip, both of them felt they had received great inspiration. As for what aspect that inspiration was in, that was a different matter for each.

After returning to the sleeping quarters, Ying Zheng said his first sentence, "...Jianjia and Longyang dared to hold a wedding, why can't we?" Ying Zheng’s tone was actually sour.

As the King of Qin, he was jealous of this?

Xu Fu blinked, "You are the King of Qin; naturally, you cannot be as carefree as Jianjia and Lord Longyang."

Ying Zheng shook his head, "A-Fu is wrong. It is precisely because I am the King of Qin that I should be able to be carefree. In state affairs, I must be cautious, but in family affairs, I can make my own decisions. Otherwise, how can the King of Qin be called a monarch?"

Family affairs.

Xu Fu’s heart stirred slightly.

He had never heard these two words used for him; it felt so novel!

"Then what do you want?" Xu Fu asked. His expression looked calm and steady, but in reality, he didn't know why his heart was still beating fast.

Ying Zheng noticed Xu Fu’s hidden tension. His mouth moved, and he couldn't help but laugh, "I will consider this carefully. How can I let Jianjia and Lord Longyang get ahead of us?"

Xu Fu found it hard to control his heart rate.

That was fine, but after hearing it, his heart felt itchy, and his cheeks couldn't help but heat up, as if he had caught some inexplicable illness.

"...Hmm." To hide his abnormal emotions, Xu Fu responded vaguely.

Ying Zheng knew Xu Fu didn't fully trust him yet. He attributed this to the aftereffects of Xu Fu’s past devotion to divination. Although he wanted to sigh, he held it back.

Jianjia and Lord Longyang’s wedding was thrown to the back of his mind.

Because Ying Zheng began to think about what Xu Fu should do now that he no longer had the position of Fengchang.

Xu Fu didn't care much now. This was different from when he first arrived in Qin and desperately needed an official position to protect himself, and different from when he needed to survive in the Fengchang Temple and desperately needed a promotion. Now, not only did he have Ying Zheng behind him, but his own methods had been seen by everyone, and no one dared to look down on him. Moreover, through his hard work and Ying Zheng’s intentional promotion, his fame had grown increasingly large.

It was exactly as he had originally thought.

If one day he wasn't happy with Ying Zheng, going to another country would be fine. He was already famous among the states, and he might even leave a mysterious image for the world, though it would be a pity to lose the position of National Master.

"Don't keep this on your mind all the time; let nature take its course," Xu Fu advised Ying Zheng in turn, then went to the side hall every day to watch how Zhao Gao taught Hu Hai.

After watching for a few days, Xu Fu didn't see anything wrong with Zhao Gao. It seemed he had truly used a small mind to measure a gentleman’s heart? Xu Fu didn't dare to be completely at ease, because the danger of the combination of Hu Hai and Zhao Gao still made him keep a wary eye on them.

In the blink of an eye, it was the 16th year of King Zheng of Qin.

Just before the Wax Sacrifice, Zhao and Han forcibly sent beauties, and Yao Jia also returned late.

Ying Zheng did not summon the envoys from Zhao and Han, but first called Yao Jia into the palace.

Yao Jia was dusty and hadn't had time to rest before rushing into the palace. Perhaps because of the long journey, Yao Jia’s face was haggard, and even his eyes were bloodshot. But this wasn't what surprised Xu Fu.

Xu Fu’s heart jumped heavily, and he couldn't help but sit up straighter.

He stared at Yao Jia’s face and found a faint layer of blood-red light covering it.

Blood-red light...

This was not the traditional "disaster of blood," but the blood-red light Xu Fu had once wanted to find on Li Si’s face but had never found at all.

Han Fei... died because of Yao Jia?

Xu Fu always felt something was strange, but upon closer inspection, there was nothing wrong. Han Fei had offended Yao Jia so much before; it would be strange if Yao Jia didn't hold a grudge! Moreover, Han Fei himself said Yao Jia was a villain, not a gentleman.

As a villain, how could he have the noble sentiment to let you off?

Xu Fu observed Yao Jia calmly. Yao Jia didn't notice his gaze. Yao Jia barely suppressed his fatigue and reported the events of the past few days to Ying Zheng in detail.

In such a short time, it was hard for Yao Jia to achieve much, and Ying Zheng knew this.

However, Xu Fu couldn't help but think that if Han Fei were here, he would probably use this to attack Yao Jia again.

Just as they were talking, a eunuch ran to the hall and knelt, "Your Majesty, news from Yunyang."

"Bring it here."

The eunuch walked in and handed over a piece of silk.

Xu Fu instinctively felt something was wrong.

Ying Zheng unfolded the silk and glanced at it. A look of surprise flashed across his face, but it wasn't strong; it seemed he had expected it.

Xu Fu vaguely guessed it too.

Sure enough, Han Fei’s fate couldn't be changed?

Ying Zheng put down the silk and whispered, "Han Zi died of accidental poisoning in Yunyang." When he said this, Ying Zheng’s gaze swept over Yao Jia.

Yao Jia still seemed unaware. He stood there motionless, his face cold.

Xu Fu was puzzled.

Yao Jia was in another country; how did he kill Han Fei? Yao Jia’s status was different now, but he had no men he could mobilize to Yunyang to kill Han Fei.
chapters.title: 第149章

chapters.source_text:
徐福吃饱了便会犯困，但嬴政向来没有午间小憩的习惯，最后还是只有徐福自己躲进了后面的围屏去休息。因为在王宫里，徐福也没资格乱跑，就只能委屈他贴身跟着嬴政了。徐福向来看得开，有吃有喝有得住，还有可以发挥职业水平的地方，他就没什么可计较的了。
于是——
嬴政处理政务的时候，徐福搭着小榻在围屏后面睡觉。
嬴政翻阅书简的时候，徐福搭着小榻在围屏后面睡觉。
嬴政该用晚膳的时候，徐福……闻到香气爬起来了。
他一睁眼，再抬头，正好对上赵高那张神色复杂的脸。大约是从没见过他这样睡姿也如此完美的人？徐福翻身坐好，理了理衣袍，站起身来，又是一派姿态超然，仿佛刚才那个睡得天昏地暗的人不是他一样。
徐福从围屏后走出，刚想要抬手捂唇打个呵欠，却在目光触及到站在对面的嬴政时，不得不生生将这个呵欠压了回去，他嘴微张，慢慢吐出一口气，眼角缀了两点生理盐水。他身上清冷的气质顿时平白软和了不少。
嬴政的目光从他脸上扫过，随后叫宫女打了水来，示意徐福擦脸清醒清醒。
有人伺候多好啊，徐福从善如流地闭上双眼，享受宫女拿着面巾轻轻拭擦过脸部的感觉。
嬴政从旁看着徐福的模样，觉得徐福实在奇妙。明明是街头白衣，却自称出身名门；会做出不合礼宜的事来，但又举手投足仿佛傲气天成。让人看不穿。
洁过面之后，徐福果然清爽了不少，眼眸都变得更加清澈了。
晚膳依旧是两人一起用。
这个时候的帝王侯爵还不算十分讲究贵贱高低之分，君臣坐于一席往往能传成美谈，而不像是后世，一介小官不配与帝王同坐。
秦王的膳食依旧丰富，徐福吃了个爽快，约莫半柱香后，宫人上前来撤掉了桌案和餐具。时辰已经不早了，按照惯例，嬴政这个时候原本是在翻阅古籍的。但是嬴政一转头就瞥见了徐福脸上略略困倦的神情。
又困了？嬴政不得不也有一丝佩服徐福的心宽。在他面前，能如此放纵自我的，又有几人？
嬴政不自觉地脱口而出，“回寝宫。”
赵高脸上闪过一丝诧异，显然没想到今日秦王怎么转了性子？但赵高从不会置噱嬴政的决定，他微微弓腰，推开门，在前面开路。宫人随后提着宫灯跟上。
这个时候，天色微暗，橘黄的灯光照亮了徐福那一圈儿的范围，他走在嬴政的身后，抬头便能望见嬴政高阔的背影，黑色宽阔的衣袖被秋风吹过，还会扑扇到徐福的脸上。
比人矮，真是高兴不起来啊。
为什么他拥有了神棍技能，拥有了超高颜值，却没有一个与之匹配的一米八呢？
徐福不太高兴地暗自撇嘴，将头转向另一边。
他们走在长长的走廊上，左手边往下看是长长的阶梯，那头是广场，还有高大巍峨的城墙。
不管是谁，每日从这里走过，肯定都会生出波澜壮阔的情绪来。吕不韦和嫪毐，肯定就很喜欢这种站在高处，一览众小的感觉。可惜了，他们都没嬴政高啊，还是嬴政个子更高，看得更远。所以注定这座王城是能匍匐在嬴政的脚下嘛。
想到这里，徐福觉得自己的忽悠能力也许可以又上一个台阶了。
不知不觉，他们就走到寝宫外了。
宫门推开，嬴政和徐福先后进入，暖融融的气息很快喷洒到了徐福的脸上，他不自觉地抽了抽鼻子，总觉得鼻间萦绕着一股香气，用作提神或许不错，但对于他这种不爱香气的人来说，就浓得有点发臭了。
徐福进门以后，目光就四处乱瞥，最后他的目光定在了床榻前的香炉上，那香炉还缓缓升腾着一缕青烟。
宫女小声道：“这是定神，熏衣的暖香。”
徐福皱了皱眉，不过好歹知道他只是个客人，这里的主人秦始皇，所以再不适也只有憋着了。
嬴政站在床榻边，宫女上前为他脱去外袍，换上另外的衣裳。
徐福站在那里突然觉得自己有点儿傻，就像是一个原本一切秩序井然的的地方，突然多了他这么一根桩子。
“徐福。”嬴政的声音突然在安静的寝殿内响起。
嗯？不叫他徐先生了？
徐福转过身去，只见宫女手中也捧着干净的白色丝织衣袍，有些像是中衣。
“我也要换吗？”徐福诧异。嬴政有这么贴心？还给他准备了睡衣？
嬴政“嗯”了一声，目光却是盯着徐福的。
徐福伸手摸了摸，还挺舒服，顿时也不排斥了，他张开双手，任由宫女靠近自己，脱下那身不太合适的官服。徐福对于在这么多人面前脱衣服，基本感觉不到什么羞耻心。他的神经早就被师父的教导和成长的环境所磨砺得十分淡定了。
上衣褪去，因为徐福背对着嬴政，嬴政一眼只能看见徐福光洁的背脊。
有句话是怎么说的？
美人不在皮而在骨。
真正的美人连骨头都是美的。
嬴政看着徐福的背影，脑子里不自觉地就蹿出了这么一个想法来，嬴政倒是并未多想。春秋战国时期都十分推崇美丽的事物，尤其是粉面朱唇的美男子。嬴政便将这当做了纯粹的欣赏。
很快徐福就换好了衣服，白色的衣裳穿在他的身上，嬴政看了一眼，恍惚像是又回到在街边初见他的时候一样，正是那一眼惊艳，才让他停住了脚步。
徐福抚了抚凌乱的头发，压抑住打呵欠的冲动，双眼眯了眯。
嬴政实在不能理解他的困倦，便出声问：“你很嗜睡吗？怎么下午休息了，现在又困了？”
徐福内心呵呵。
这特么要怪谁？还不是怪你！他之所以困，都是因为晚上挑灯熬夜刻竹简啊！耗力气耗心神也就罢了，一不小心打个盹儿，小刀就戳到手上去了。那种酸楚的滋味，徐福完全不想再回忆了好吗？
徐福冷着脸没有说话。
嬴政挑了挑眉，正诧异这难道还有什么不能说的吗？却听殿外传来了脚步声，宫人跪倒在地，怯弱道：“王上，胡姬……胡姬来了。”
嬴政蓦地想起，前段时间常是胡姬侍寝的。
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu would get sleepy once he was full, but Ying Zheng never had the habit of taking an afternoon nap, so in the end, Xu Fu had to hide behind the folding screen to rest by himself. Since he was in the royal palace, Xu Fu wasn't qualified to wander around, so he was forced to stick close to Ying Zheng. Xu Fu had always been easygoing; as long as he had food, drink, a place to stay, and a way to utilize his professional skills, he had nothing to complain about.

And so—

When Ying Zheng handled state affairs, Xu Fu would set up a small couch behind the folding screen to sleep.

When Ying Zheng flipped through bamboo slips, Xu Fu would set up a small couch behind the folding screen to sleep.

When it was time for Ying Zheng to have dinner, Xu Fu... smelled the aroma and crawled up.

As soon as he opened his eyes and looked up, he happened to meet Zhao Gao's complex expression. Perhaps he had never seen someone who could look so perfect even while sleeping? Xu Fu rolled over and sat up, straightened his robes, and stood up with an air of detachment, as if the person who had been sleeping soundly just a moment ago wasn't him.

Xu Fu walked out from behind the screen and was about to raise his hand to cover a yawn, but when his gaze landed on Ying Zheng standing opposite him, he was forced to swallow the yawn back down. His mouth opened slightly, he slowly exhaled, and two beads of moisture welled up in the corners of his eyes. The cold, aloof aura about him softened significantly.

Ying Zheng's gaze swept across his face, then he called for a palace maid to bring water, signaling for Xu Fu to wash his face and wake up.

How nice it was to have someone wait on him. Xu Fu followed the flow, closed his eyes, and enjoyed the feeling of the palace maid gently wiping his face with a towel.

Ying Zheng watched Xu Fu from the side, finding him truly fascinating. He was clearly a man in white from the streets, yet he claimed to be from a prestigious family; he would do things that defied etiquette, yet every gesture of his seemed to carry a natural, haughty pride. He was impossible to read.

After washing his face, Xu Fu was indeed much more refreshed, and his eyes became even clearer.

Dinner was still shared between the two of them.

In this era, the distinction between the high and low status of kings and nobles was not yet strictly emphasized; a ruler and his subject sitting at the same table could often be praised as a fine story, unlike in later generations where a minor official would not be worthy of sitting with the emperor.

The King of Qin's meal was still sumptuous, and Xu Fu ate to his heart's content. About half an incense stick's time later, the palace servants came forward to clear away the table and utensils. It was already late, and according to custom, Ying Zheng would usually be reading ancient texts at this hour. But as soon as Ying Zheng turned his head, he caught a glimpse of the slight drowsiness on Xu Fu's face.

Sleepy again? Ying Zheng couldn't help but feel a hint of admiration for Xu Fu's carefree nature. In his presence, how many people could be so self-indulgent?

Ying Zheng blurted out unconsciously, "Return to the bedchamber."

A flash of surprise crossed Zhao Gao's face; he clearly hadn't expected the King of Qin to change his routine today. But Zhao Gao never questioned Ying Zheng's decisions. He bowed slightly, pushed open the door, and led the way. The palace servants followed behind, carrying palace lanterns.

At this time, the sky was dim, and the orange light illuminated the area around Xu Fu. He walked behind Ying Zheng, and looking up, he could see Ying Zheng's tall, broad back. The wide black sleeves were caught by the autumn wind, occasionally flapping against Xu Fu's face.

Being shorter than someone else really made it hard to be happy.

Why did he possess divine charlatan skills and an incredibly high level of attractiveness, but not a matching height of 1.8 meters?

Xu Fu curled his lip in secret, not very happy, and turned his head to the other side.

They walked along the long corridor. Looking down on the left side, there were long stairs leading to the plaza, and beyond that, the tall, imposing city walls.

No matter who it was, walking through here every day would surely stir up grand and magnificent emotions. Lü Buwei and Lao Ai must have loved this feeling of standing on high and looking down on everyone else. It was a pity that neither of them was as tall as Ying Zheng; Ying Zheng was taller and could see further. Therefore, it was destined that this royal city would crawl at Ying Zheng's feet.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu felt that his ability to bluff might be able to reach a new level.

Before they knew it, they had reached the outside of the bedchamber.

The palace doors were pushed open, and Ying Zheng and Xu Fu entered one after another. A warm, cozy atmosphere soon washed over Xu Fu's face. He sniffed unconsciously, feeling that a lingering fragrance filled the air. It might be good for refreshing the mind, but for someone like him who didn't like fragrances, it was a bit too thick and cloying.

After entering, Xu Fu's gaze wandered around, eventually settling on the incense burner in front of the bed, from which a wisp of blue smoke was slowly rising.

A palace maid whispered, "This is a warm scent for calming the mind and perfuming the robes."

Xu Fu frowned, but at least he knew he was just a guest and the master here was the First Emperor of Qin, so no matter how uncomfortable he was, he had to endure it.

Ying Zheng stood by the bed, and a palace maid stepped forward to remove his outer robe and change him into different clothes.

Standing there, Xu Fu suddenly felt a bit foolish, like a post suddenly stuck in a place where everything was orderly.

"Xu Fu." Ying Zheng's voice suddenly rang out in the quiet bedchamber.

Hmm? He wasn't calling him "Master Xu" anymore?

Xu Fu turned around and saw that the palace maid was also holding a clean, white silk robe, looking somewhat like an undergarment.

"Do I need to change too?" Xu Fu was surprised. Was Ying Zheng this thoughtful? He even prepared pajamas for him?

Ying Zheng gave an "en," his gaze fixed on Xu Fu.

Xu Fu reached out and touched the fabric; it was quite comfortable, so he didn't resist. He opened his arms and let the palace maid approach him to remove his ill-fitting official robes. Xu Fu felt almost no shame in undressing in front of so many people. His nerves had long been tempered to be very calm by his master's teachings and the environment in which he grew up.

As the upper garment was removed, because Xu Fu was standing with his back to Ying Zheng, Ying Zheng could only see Xu Fu's smooth, clean back.

How did that saying go?

A true beauty lies not in the skin, but in the bones.

A true beauty has beauty even in their bones.

Watching Xu Fu's back, this thought popped into Ying Zheng's mind unconsciously, though he didn't dwell on it. The Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods highly valued beautiful things, especially handsome men with fair faces and red lips. Ying Zheng took this as pure appreciation.

Soon, Xu Fu had changed his clothes. Wearing the white garment, he looked to Ying Zheng as if he had returned to the moment he first saw him on the street—it was that stunning glance that had made him stop in his tracks.

Xu Fu smoothed his messy hair, suppressed the urge to yawn, and narrowed his eyes.

Ying Zheng really couldn't understand his drowsiness, so he asked, "Are you very prone to sleep? How is it that you rested in the afternoon, and now you are sleepy again?"

Xu Fu laughed inwardly.

Who the hell was to blame for this? It was all his fault! The reason he was sleepy was that he had been burning the midnight oil carving bamboo slips! It was one thing to exhaust his energy and focus, but if he accidentally dozed off, the small knife would poke his hand. Xu Fu didn't want to recall that stinging pain at all, okay?

Xu Fu kept a straight face and said nothing.

Ying Zheng raised an eyebrow, wondering if there was something he couldn't say, when he heard footsteps outside the hall. A palace servant knelt on the ground and said timidly, "Your Majesty, the Hu woman... the Hu woman has arrived."

Ying Zheng suddenly remembered that the Hu woman had often attended to him at night recently.
chapters.title: 第15章

chapters.translated_text:
Watching Ying Zheng's expression, Xu Fu immediately felt that he knew some inside information, or rather, that letting Han Fei die was Ying Zheng's intention all along, and Yao Jia only needed to fan the flames... But if that were the case, why did Ying Zheng's physiognomy not show any signs of blood or violence? Or was this a privilege belonging to a monarch—that no matter how many people I kill, it counts for nothing?

Weren't there many such tropes in old folklore and monster stories? True Dragon Emperors are protected by gods; they are immune to ghosts and evil, and enjoy immense privileges in the world... Xu Fu cut off his train of thought; he was really drifting too far away.

"Han Zi's accidental death is truly lamentable. Your Majesty, why not order someone to bring Han Zi's body back to Xianyang for burial?" Yao Jia said with extreme naturalness. It was difficult for others to discern his true thoughts about Han Fei from his expression or tone.

Ying Zheng pondered for a long while before calling someone in to go to Yunyang to retrieve Han Fei's body. At the same time, he sent an attendant to the Princess of Han to convey the news of Han Fei's death.

Xu Fu guessed that upon hearing the news, the Princess of Han would surely be frightened out of her wits, viewing the State of Qin as a man-eating place, and the King of Han might also be left restless and uneasy.

Watching Ying Zheng issue a series of orders, Yao Jia straightened his back. Seeing the fatigue on his face that he could barely conceal, Ying Zheng finally let him go to rest.

Once Yao Jia left, Xu Fu spoke three words: "What a pity."

Ying Zheng knew who he was talking about and said with a half-smile: "It is a pity, but what is more of a pity is that this person cannot be used by me." Clearly, Ying Zheng valued Han Fei's talent, but valued even more whether this person could be put to his own use.

Xu Fu fell silent. Although he also admired Han Fei, Ying Zheng was right. Moreover, now that he stood with Ying Zheng, their positions were different, and naturally, his perspective on Han Fei's life and death was different as well.

He and Ying Zheng simultaneously cast the matter to the back of their minds. Han Fei's death would not stir up much of a splash in Qin. At most, it would make everyone more wary of Yao Jia, not daring to provoke him lightly. When a person dies, it is like a lamp going out; even if it were Han Fei, how many people would think of him after death?

The Wax Festival this year was the same as in previous years, with no major differences. The only difference was probably that the people of Xianyang trusted Xu Fu more with each passing year; they were just short of kneeling down and worshipping him.

After the Wax Festival ended, Xu Fu changed out of his ceremonial robes and ate dinner with Ying Zheng as usual, with Fusu and Huhai sitting nearby. This was a family dinner after the festival. It looked no different from that of an ordinary household.

They were able to spend the Wax Festival in Xianyang, but the soldiers outside did not have this opportunity. Fortunately, Ying Zheng never mistreated the soldiers who expanded his territory; he ordered many provisions to be sent to them. However, when the person in charge returned, the news he brought was not good.

Huan Yi had fallen ill.

General Huan Yi's contributions in the campaign against Zhao were well known. He was a talented general, and the outcome of the war with Zhao depended largely on his command. But now that the commander had fallen, the fact that the soldiers had not descended into chaos was already a testament to the unity of the Qin army.

"No wonder," Xu Fu said after hearing the news.

Previously, Huan Yi had wanted to request that Xu Fu accompany the army. But it had been a while since Huan Yi last sent word, and Xu Fu had assumed he had given up on the idea. Who knew it was only because Huan Yi had suddenly fallen ill? If it were just Huan Yi falling ill, it wouldn't have taken so long for news to arrive. This was because, besides Huan Yi, another general had gone missing.

For a time, the army was leaderless, so it was normal that news hadn't been sent to Xianyang in time.

After hearing the report, Ying Zheng's face darkened instantly, the joy after the Wax Festival washed away. "Do you know why General Huan Yi fell ill?" People like them who had been campaigning for years, how could they be so fragile? Moreover, Huan Yi had been fighting Zhao for so long, how could he suddenly fall ill, and why hadn't he recovered after such a long time? And that missing young general was also very strange—how could a perfectly fine person just go missing? Ying Zheng had to consider the possibility of defection.

All of this was certainly not good news for the State of Qin, which had been sailing smoothly in its conquests.

"This... I do not know." The man was drenched in cold sweat and lowered his head even further. "I have already asked the people in the army, and they all say they don't know why the general fell ill. The military doctors examined him and said it was a strange illness."

"A strange illness?" Ying Zheng's expression grew even uglier. If they knew what the illness was, it would be easy to solve, but the most troublesome thing was a "strange illness." Who knew what symptoms it had or how to cure it? In the end, Huan Yi's life might be in jeopardy.

"And how did that general named Li Xin go missing?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.

"This... I don't know either. They said it was too strange; I suspect they might have been possessed by evil spirits," the man said with a weird expression.

Hearing this from the side, Xu Fu's heart stirred.

Li Xin was missing?! Because it was someone he knew, Xu Fu couldn't help but feel concerned, and even wanted to go see for himself just how strange things were in the Qin army.

Ying Zheng pursed his lips and ordered the man to compile a report and submit it. Seeing that Ying Zheng wasn't angry, the man breathed a sigh of relief, nodded quickly, and hurried out.

Not long after, the bamboo slips were presented to Ying Zheng, and Xu Fu stepped forward to read them with him.

In the bamboo slips, the man described the process of Li Xin's disappearance.

How did Li Xin go missing? It was indeed somewhat bizarre. He was leading men to scout the enemy when he disappeared mysteriously right in front of his subordinates. Those subordinates watched him, and after a flash of green light, everyone felt a stinging pain in their eyes and couldn't help but close them. When they opened them again, Li Xin was nowhere to be seen.

Someone listening to the story would probably subconsciously treat it as a supernatural event.

It was no wonder the man called it strange.

But it was precisely this strangeness that piqued Xu Fu's interest. Besides him, what else could be more bizarre in this world? Could there really be ghosts and spirits? Xu Fu didn't dare to deny it completely, because he still remembered the heroic appearance of the small cloth strip turning into a black shadow.

Ying Zheng looked back at him, having guessed Xu Fu's thoughts.

Ying Zheng knew this matter was tricky, and having Xu Fu solve it was undoubtedly the best way, but his reluctance was also real. Even the commanding general had met with trouble; how could he ensure Xu Fu's safety if he went? Yet, his reason reminded him to resolve it quickly and send Xu Fu.

As if he hadn't seen the conflict on Ying Zheng's face, Xu Fu said, "Send me there. I will often have people send you letters." If it were in the past, Xu Fu would never have thought of this, but now it was as if he had suddenly become self-taught; he could think of such small details.

Ying Zheng's expression softened immensely. He looked at Xu Fu deeply and replied, "Good. My trouble, yet I must trouble you to solve it."

My trouble?

These five words flashed through Xu Fu's mind, making him think of the previous divination. Could this be the so-called "small trouble" on Ying Zheng?

That was perfect; he would go solve it himself!

Xu Fu was confident and even filled with anticipation.

If Huan Yi really had a strange illness that others couldn't solve, he would ask Jiang You to try. Thinking of this, Xu Fu felt a little guilty. Was he treating his senior brother as someone to be summoned at will? Was this too much? But with trouble at hand, Xu Fu didn't have the energy to think about it. He quickly returned to his palace to pack his luggage and had someone call Fusu and Huhai.

After briefly explaining the matter to Fusu and Huhai and informing them that he would be away for a while, Xu Fu set off for outside the city, accompanied by Ying Zheng.

Before leaving, Xu Fu gave orders to find Jiang You's whereabouts first. Finding him early would be a precaution, and Xu Fu would be able to rest easier.

At this moment, Ying Zheng sighed; only when Xu Fu could help him did he realize he couldn't help Xu Fu in return.

Outside the city of Xianyang, Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou were waiting. In Ying Zheng's eyes, Gan Tang was too unreliable, so he didn't call him, and as for Jian Jia... although the person he married was a bit strange, they were newlyweds, and Ying Zheng wasn't cruel enough to call him out to work just yet.

Xu Fu stepped off the carriage and switched to Sang Zhong's carriage. Ying Zheng's expression was cold, his gaze fixed on Xu Fu as he departed.

Xu Fu left quickly, and after Ying Zheng returned to the palace, he heard that the Princess of Han requested to return to the State of Han. Not in a pleasant mood, the King of Qin ordered the Princess of Han to be brought before him. The Princess of Han was indeed a beauty; she cried uncontrollably before Ying Zheng, not even caring about her makeup, crying without any of a lady's restraint.

Ying Zheng knew she was truly terrified of Qin.

In her own country, the Princess of Han was the apple of the King of Han's eye. Who would have thought that after arriving in Qin, not only was it hard to see the King of Qin, but she had no affection for him, viewing him as extremely cruel? How could she want the King of Qin to take a fancy to her? Then, hearing of Han Fei's death, the Princess of Han felt a chill, believing the King of Qin was ruthless. She had heard how well the King of Qin treated Han Fei. At that time, she thought she was more favored in Han than Han Fei was, so she assumed life in Qin wouldn't be too bad, even if she had to marry such a man.

How could the Princess of Han have imagined that reality would be like this!

She was truly afraid; she wanted to return to Han. She didn't want to die an unnatural death like Han Fei, dying in a foreign land.

Looking at the miserable Princess of Han crying before him, a flash of disgust crossed Ying Zheng's eyes, and he ordered her to be sent back.

"Since you want to leave, then return to your country."

"Han... Han Fei's body..." The Princess of Han asked cautiously.

"Han Fei will be buried in Qin. I granted him a courtyard while he was alive; naturally, he will be buried there now that he is dead."

The Princess of Han breathed a sigh of relief. This was fine; she wouldn't need to carry a corpse back with her.

After she was sent away, Ying Zheng suddenly remembered there was another Princess of Zhao in the palace. He called an attendant and asked, "How is the Princess of Zhao? Has she said anything about wanting to return to Zhao?"

The attendant lowered his head and replied, "She hasn't mentioned it. The Princess of Zhao has no complaints in the palace; she spends her days eating, drinking, and resting, occasionally walking in the nearby courtyard."

Compared to the Princess of Han, she was much more composed.

The Qin army was still stationed in Zhao; how could the King of Zhao dare to stand up to the King of Qin? Presumably, the Princess of Zhao understood this, which was why she was more willing to sacrifice herself for her country than the Princess of Han.

It was just a pity that whether Zhao wanted to sacrifice, it depended on whether Ying Zheng agreed.

Ying Zheng waved his hand, telling them to keep an eye on the Princess of Zhao, and asked no more.

Having dealt with these matters, Ying Zheng felt the reluctance in his heart due to Xu Fu's departure fade slightly.

Although Xu Fu was gone, seeing Fusu and Huhai reminded Ying Zheng of the four of them sitting together. On a whim, Ying Zheng grabbed Huhai and Fusu to check their studies. Fusu's expression remained normal, but Huhai, who never studied properly, was completely stunned.

Father, come back quickly! As soon as you leave, Father the King comes to torture us...

Poor little Huhai cried out in his heart with teary eyes.

·

Not long after Xu Fu's party left Xianyang, horses caught up. Sang Zhong lifted the curtain to look back and saw two familiar figures, stunned in extreme surprise.

"How is it? Who is it?" Xu Fu asked, leaning in the carriage.

"Jian Jia, and Lord Longyang." Sang Zhong's lips moved, his expression still filled with disbelief.

Xu Fu was also surprised, but he kept these emotions buried deep inside.

Bo Zhou stopped the carriage to let Jian Jia and Lord Longyang approach. Bo Zhou asked in a deep voice, "Why have you come?" If they had treated Lord Longyang with the caution reserved for legendary figures in the past, now that they had seen Jian Jia and Lord Longyang marry, their attitude toward him was much more casual. Setting aside his status, he was now just Jian Jia's family.

Lord Longyang lifted his eyelids coldly and said, "Jian Jia and I originally didn't want to come, but the King ordered Jian Jia to follow. Since Jian Jia is coming, I naturally have to accompany him."

Hearing their conversation from inside the carriage, Xu Fu realized that Ying Zheng had regretted his decision and couldn't help but let Jian Jia follow. Ying Zheng must have calculated that if Jian Jia came, Lord Longyang would surely follow. Lord Longyang had his own forces, and his swordsmanship was indeed rarely matched; having him by his side was a powerful asset.

After seeing through Ying Zheng's intentions, the feeling in Xu Fu's heart suddenly became strange.

It felt a bit tingly, like a string of electric current brushing quickly across his heart.

He suppressed this emotion and signaled for them to continue.

Jian Jia and Lord Longyang entered the carriage, and soon, it moved forward again.

Lord Longyang looked at the items placed in front of Xu Fu and said with interest, "Why did you think to bring these, Sir?" The items in front of Xu Fu were tripods, and Lord Longyang remembered that one of them was given to Xu Fu by himself.

"General Huan Yi is seriously ill; I am bringing these to make medicine."

"Make medicine?" Lord Longyang's expression was a bit strange. There were so many tools for making medicine, why use these broken tripods? In any case, with Lord Longyang's picky eyes, he couldn't see anything precious about them. "How come I didn't know you were skilled in the arts of Huang and Qi, Sir?"

"I just learned a trick or two from my senior brother," Xu Fu said shamelessly. His tone didn't sound like "just learning a trick or two" at all.

Lord Longyang's mouth twitched.

Xu Fu's senior brother, Jiang You, was indeed a divine doctor rarely seen in the world; after all, they both came from the Guigu school.

The indifference on Lord Longyang's face faded, and he smiled slightly: "Then I shall wait to see your great skills, Sir."

Having grown familiar with Lord Longyang, Xu Fu knew there was no mockery in his words. He nodded and replied seriously, "Good." He also wanted to see how much he had improved after studying for so long.

Because he was concerned about the situation in the army, Xu Fu didn't dare to delay and instructed Bo Zhou to travel quickly.

Although the journey was arduous, Xu Fu's spirits were quite good, and they finally arrived at the Qin army's camp after half a month.

When they arrived, Xu Fu was still sleeping in the carriage to catch up on rest.

Sometimes, forced by circumstances, people couldn't be picky. Xu Fu was like that; in the past, he would have preferred the carriage to move as slowly as possible, but this time, the carriage raced along, stopping only briefly each night before setting off again, and the food was increasingly simple, sometimes even leaving him hungry, but Xu Fu endured it all.

Eventually, no matter how bumpy the carriage was, Xu Fu could fall asleep.

"Sir, Sir, we have arrived."

Sang Zhong lifted the curtain and entered the carriage.

Jian Jia and Lord Longyang had already left the carriage and headed to the camp first to scout.

Xu Fu was still sleeping soundly in the carriage. Helpless, Sang Zhong had to walk closer and lower his head to call him. Xu Fu's face was magnified in his eyes, his skin so clear that Sang Zhong couldn't even find a single mole.

His appearance was truly exquisite.

Sang Zhong watched his eyelashes flutter and saw Xu Fu open his mouth unconsciously before opening his eyes. His beautiful eyes were exceptionally bright, but in that brief moment, they became cold.

Sang Zhong felt his heart tremble, and it took a long time to suppress the inexplicable excitement rising within him.

"We're here?" Xu Fu's voice was still hoarse from sleep, sounding very much like the voice after intimacy. Sang Zhong's heart trembled even more violently; he didn't dare to think further, turned his face away in a hurry, and answered softly.

Xu Fu lifted the curtain and stepped down.

Just then, Jian Jia and Lord Longyang walked back, bringing soldiers with them.

Those soldiers had seen Xu Fu while following Huan Yi, and naturally recognized him. They immediately hurried forward and bowed deeply, calling out, "Chief Commandant Xu!"

Facing their enthusiastic eyes, Xu Fu was a bit puzzled.

Why were these people so enthusiastic toward him? It was as if they had finally seen their own parents...

The soldiers held Xu Fu in high esteem and respectfully welcomed him in. This time, to make it convenient for Xu Fu to take over, Ying Zheng had once again appointed him as the Chief Commandant of the Guard. The Chief Commandant of the Guard commanded all the generals. Now that the two major generals had fallen, only a group of minor generals and soldiers remained, and Xu Fu's arrival was just in time to take control of them.

They didn't need to rush to attack Zhao for the moment, so Xu Fu's position wouldn't hinder military affairs. What he needed to do now was to stabilize the morale, save Huan Yi's life, and find Li Xin.

Actually, Ying Zheng had overthought it; he had paved the way for Xu Fu, and since Huan Yi had previously shown reverence for Xu Fu, the soldiers naturally followed suit, viewing Xu Fu as an incredibly powerful figure. He would definitely save the general! The soldiers thought so.

Thus, Xu Fu, who was playing the immortal everywhere, had to continue playing the immortal in the camp.

The business of being a charlatan is truly endless...

Xu Fu sighed lightly and was led by the soldiers to his tent to put away his luggage. After organizing his belongings, he immediately went to Huan Yi's tent.

As soon as the curtain was lifted, Xu Fu stood at the entrance and smelled a heavy medicinal odor mixed with a bit of stench. Because the air inside was not circulating, the stuffy air rushed out, and Xu Fu wanted to turn around and leave immediately.

At this rate, someone could be suffocated to death.

Xu Fu felt sorry for Huan Yi for a moment and immediately ordered someone to prop up the tent curtains, then walked in quickly. The soldiers looked at each other, confused. Why prop up the curtains as soon as he arrived? Would the general's illness get better just by doing that? Out of blind trust in Xu Fu, they immediately propped up the curtains and waited quietly to see Xu Fu work his magic.

Xu Fu walked inside and soon saw Huan Yi lying on the bed.

Huan Yi was not old, but in a short time, his face had withered significantly, looking as if he had aged ten years.

His face was a pale blue-white, his lips purple, and his hair and eyebrows even showed signs of falling out. Huan Yi seemed to have some consciousness; he wanted to open his eyes to look at the person by the bed, but he didn't have the strength.

A cold breeze blew in from the propped-up curtain, and Huan Yi shivered and suddenly began to cough.

The soldiers were nervous and were about to pull the curtain down, but Xu Fu shouted, "Don't move!"

The soldiers shivered, not daring to move, and had to stop. They suppressed their confusion and kept comforting themselves: Chief Commandant Xu must have a way, he must have a way... He is a living immortal...

Huan Yi coughed violently, and suddenly, he opened his mouth and spat out blood. Xu Fu was startled, but he steadied his feet and didn't make any embarrassing movements.

Huan Yi seemed to be in great pain; he couldn't help but twitch slightly, his brows furrowed, and sweat beads quickly seeped out on his forehead.

Xu Fu looked closely and saw that the blood he had just spat out actually contained bits of flesh.

Xu Fu couldn't help but shiver. Huan Yi's illness was indeed too strange. What kind of illness could make someone cough up blood containing bits of flesh? Xu Fu didn't even dare to imagine what his abdominal cavity looked like right now.

Were his internal organs rotting?

Xu Fu steadied himself and turned to order, "Call all the military doctors to me."

"Yes." The soldiers ran off to find the doctors.

Lord Longyang and the others followed and saw the blood Huan Yi had spat out. Lord Longyang frowned, "This is not optimistic." He was telling the truth, without a shred of schadenfreude.

Looking at Huan Yi's current state, anyone could see he might die at any moment.

Xu Fu walked closer, wanting to see Huan Yi's condition more clearly, but a soldier behind him suddenly said urgently, "Commandant, don't..."

Don't what? Xu Fu turned back, looked at the soldier, and then followed his gaze to Huan Yi.

Xu Fu's heart stirred, and he reached out to lift the quilt.

After the quilt was lifted, the stench became even more obvious; it was coming from Huan Yi's body.

Xu Fu clearly noticed that the skin on Huan Yi's neck was not right. He reached out to pull at Huan Yi's robe. The soldier screamed, "Commandant!"

Xu Fu steadily pulled back the robe, and then he knew why the soldier didn't want him to look.

Because Huan Yi's body was rotting and peeling. At first glance, it was indeed a huge visual shock, but Xu Fu had been fully prepared since standing at the entrance, so even this terrifying sight didn't make his expression change.

Xu Fu squeezed his palms and quickly searched his mind for any relevant records.

While he was thinking, footsteps approached, and a soldier whispered, "Commandant, the military doctors are here."

"Come in," Xu Fu said without looking back.

There were only two military doctors; there had originally been four, but two had died. These two became precious in the army. Xu Fu called them over and asked them to describe the process from when Huan Yi first fell ill to the present.

One remained silent, head lowered, while the other, eager to show off, quickly described the process of Huan Yi's illness.

Low fever, vomiting, diarrhea.

Oral ulceration, gray-blue fingernails, pale skin, purple lips.

Weakness in the limbs, body beginning to rot.

Could only lie in bed, unable to get up, delirious, tremors, bloody stool, severe coughing even leading to vomiting blood, just as Xu Fu had seen.

This was the process of Huan Yi's illness.

Just listening to it made Xu Fu feel terrified. He didn't know how much pain Huan Yi had endured during this process. A man who was once incredibly strong was fading day by day, and now he was in critical condition. What kind of despair must Huan Yi be feeling?

Xu Fu sighed inwardly and asked what medicine the two doctors had prescribed.

They wrote it on silk and then left.

The soldier beside him couldn't help but whisper, "Commandant, I think Military Doctor Hu has a problem."

Military Doctor Hu was the one who was eager to show off.

"Why not the other one?"

"Of course not! Military Doctor Hu is cowardly but loves to show off and take credit. The symptoms on the general were clearly discovered by Military Doctor Liu first, but when speaking to you, Commandant, Military Doctor Hu spoke first."

Based on the soldier's description, Military Doctor Hu did have poor character, but that shouldn't be a reason to suspect him.

The soldier whispered, "That Military Doctor Hu seems to have hidden something in his tent, but we can't search the doctors' tent without reason. If we offend him and the brothers have no one to treat them, I'll be the sinner."

"Do Military Doctor Hu and Military Doctor Liu live in the same tent?" Lord Longyang suddenly asked.

The soldier didn't understand why but nodded. After nodding, he wanted to say more about how bad Military Doctor Hu was, but Xu Fu waved his hand, "You go out first, I know."

The soldier had to obey and left the tent.

Xu Fu now understood Lord Longyang's meaning; he thought the same.

Comparing the two, he felt Military Doctor Liu was more suspicious. Based on the soldier's description, Military Doctor Hu's character had flaws, but those flaws didn't reach the level of a major crime. If he were truly a suspicious person, he should be keeping a low profile, not being so sharp. Moreover, they were all military doctors; who didn't want to be valued? Military Doctor Hu's sycophancy was low-class, but Military Doctor Liu's silence and feigned indifference were also very discordant.

Was there really someone who was indifferent to fame and fortune and had a perfect personality?

People indifferent to fame and fortune might exist, but there were no people without flaws.

Xu Fu and Lord Longyang thought the same. The soldier suspected Military Doctor Hu most because he thought he hid something in the tent, but Military Doctor Liu lived in the same tent; if Military Doctor Hu had hidden something, how could Military Doctor Liu not know? Based on their performances, Military Doctor Liu should be much smarter than Military Doctor Hu. Thus, Xu Fu could reasonably suspect that the one who hid something in the tent might be Military Doctor Liu, not Military Doctor Hu.

Xu Fu directly called people over and ordered them to search the tent later.

Lord Longyang took Jian Jia with him; they were mainly there to watch Military Doctor Liu. Military Doctor Liu had a good reputation in the army, and the soldiers might not be wary of him.

Lord Longyang was a very smart person; if the other party were playing tricks, they couldn't fool him.

Afterwards, Xu Fu took Sang Zhong and set up a medicine station in the tent.

He placed the tripods, took out the medicinal herbs he carried, and the pills he had made earlier. These pills looked black and ugly, but Xu Fu had tested them, and their effects were quite good. Although he hadn't developed any "healing" potions, he had pills that accelerated wound recovery, stopped bleeding, relieved fatigue, treated altitude sickness, and quickly lowered fever...

All sorts of things were the results of Xu Fu's efforts over this period. Before leaving, he had left some for Ying Zheng. Although Ying Zheng didn't lack doctors or medicine, Xu Fu thought about it and left them anyway; it seemed such an act could make him feel more at ease.

Xu Fu chose pills for fever reduction, stopping bleeding, and promoting wound recovery, and told the soldiers serving Huan Yi how to administer them. The soldiers looked solemn, as if holding divine medicine, and carefully guarded Huan Yi's side.

Xu Fu wanted to make medicine to prevent infection and treat rot, but with his current level, he really couldn't make it yet. He had brought many bamboo slips with him and hoped to find something by flipping through them.

The Chief Commandant of the Guard, who had just arrived at the camp on the first day, was busy grinding herbs.

On the other side, the camp's tranquility was broken as a group of soldiers surrounded the military doctors' tent.

Military Doctor Hu was scared and angry, running out to curse the soldiers for being heartless. In fact, Military Doctor Hu was a bit scared; he worried that the Chief Commandant would settle scores with him and that the general's failure to recover was because he had prescribed the wrong medicine.

The soldiers looked cold, grabbed Military Doctor Hu like a chicken, and went straight into the tent.

Military Doctor Hu cursed loudly, wanting to stop them, but his frame was too small to stop a group of fierce Qin soldiers, so he was thrown out.

With a "thud," Military Doctor Hu was thrown to the ground and couldn't get up.

Military Doctor Liu was nowhere to be seen.

The soldiers searched the tent without obstruction and finally found a small broken tripod under Military Doctor Hu's bed. The tripod was tightly sealed. The soldiers didn't dare to open it rashly, glanced coldly at Military Doctor Hu, and brought this evil-looking thing to the main tent.

Lord Longyang felt something was wrong. After exchanging glances with Jian Jia, they split up to look for Military Doctor Liu.

He was almost certain it had nothing to do with Military Doctor Hu. The soldiers went to search the tent, and Military Doctor Hu tried to stop them, but that was the anger of being offended, not the guilt of trying to stop them at all costs.

Later, when Military Doctor Hu was thrown to the ground, he didn't even try to get up, and even when the thing was found under his bed, he didn't feel there was anything wrong with it; his expression didn't change, showing he was truly ignorant of it.

If Xu Fu hadn't arrived here with him, Military Doctor Liu's scheme might have succeeded.

...

"Commandant, the item has been found," the soldier said happily.

"Come in, put it here," Xu Fu said without looking up.

The soldier brought the small tripod in. Seeing Xu Fu brewing medicine, his expression became even more cautious, and his gaze toward the brewing tools became exceptionally intense.

Xu Fu finally spared a glance at the small broken tripod.

"Open it."

The soldier struggled to open the lid, and the smell rushed out—it was extremely foul!

Xu Fu's expression changed drastically, "Close it! Take it away! Take it out! Don't let anyone open it to look again!"

看嬴政的表情，徐福顿觉他知晓什么内情，或者说，让韩非死，本就是嬴政的意思，所以姚贾只需推波助澜就行了……但若是这样的话，为何嬴政的面相并不带血光呢？还是说这是属于君王的特权——哪怕我杀再多的人，也都不算什么？
从前许多精怪故事里，不是就有这样的桥段吗？真龙天子都是受神灵庇佑的，他们鬼邪不侵，享有世间极大的特权……徐福打住了自己的思绪，真是越扯越远了。
“韩子意外身死，叫人叹惋，王上，不若令人将韩子的尸身带回咸阳安葬吧？”姚贾无比自然地说道，别人很难从他的表情或者语气里看出，他究竟对韩非是个什么心思。
嬴政沉吟半晌，叫人进来，去云阳寻韩非的尸身，同时还派了一名内侍到韩国公主处，传达韩非身死的消息。
徐福猜测，韩国公主听到消息之后，肯定吓得魂不附体，将秦国当做吃人的地方，韩王说不定也会坐立难安。
姚贾看着嬴政将一系列的命令发下去，他这才直起了腰身，嬴政见他脸上的疲色都快掩盖不住了，这才放手让他下去休息。
姚贾一走，徐福才出声说了三个字，“可惜了。”
嬴政知道他说的是谁，似笑非笑地道：“是可惜了，但更可惜的是，这个人寡人用不得。”明显嬴政看重韩非身上的才能，但却更看重这个人能不能为自己所用。
徐福沉默了。他虽然也欣赏韩非，但是嬴政说得不错。何况如今他同嬴政站在一起，立场不同，自然对韩非的生死的看法也有所不同了。
他和嬴政同时将这件事抛到了脑后去，韩非身死，不会在秦国掀起多么大的浪花。顶多就是让众人都对姚贾多加提防，不敢随意去招惹姚贾罢了。人死如灯灭，纵然是韩非，死后又有多少人能想着他呢？
这一年的蜡祭与往年一样，并没有多大的区别，唯一不同的，大概就是咸阳的百姓们，一年比一年更信任徐福了，就差没跪下来，对着徐福顶礼膜拜了。
结束蜡祭后，徐福换下了身上的祭服，照旧同嬴政一起吃着晚膳，旁边坐着扶苏和胡亥，这便是一家人在蜡祭结束后的晚宴。看上去，倒是与普通人家也没有什么不同。
他们能够在咸阳城中过蜡祭，而在外的将士却没这个机会，幸而嬴政从不亏待为自己开疆辟土的士兵，他命人送了许多食物前去，等到负责人归来时，带来的却不是个好消息。
桓齮病倒了。
桓齮将军在攻打赵国上出的力，是众所周知的，他是个将才，与赵国之间的输赢胜负，有很大一部分都取决于桓齮的指挥。但如今指挥的人倒下了，士兵们没有乱作一团，那已经是秦军团结了。
“怪不得了。”徐福听见这个消息之后，忍不住说了这四个字。
之前桓齮一直想要向嬴政请求，让徐福随军。但是桓齮已经有一段时间没有再递消息来了，徐福还当他已经打消这个念头了，谁知道不过是因为桓齮突然病倒了。若单单只是桓齮病倒，也不至于这么久才传来消息。盖因除却桓齮之外，还有位将军也失踪了。
一时间，军中群龙无首，没能及时向咸阳递消息倒也是正常的。
嬴政听过那人的禀报之后，脸色登时就阴沉了起来，蜡祭后的喜悦被冲散了，“可知桓齮将军为何会病倒？”他们这些常年行军打仗的人，哪有那样脆弱？何况桓齮打了这么久的赵国，怎么突然间说病就病了，而且还这么长的时间都未能恢复康健，那个失踪的年纪将领也很是古怪，好好的人，怎么会失踪？嬴政不得不考虑对方通敌叛国的可能性。
这一切，对于征战路上几乎一路顺风的秦国来说，可实在不是个什么好消息。
“这……不知。”那人冷汗涔涔，将头低得更低了，“小人已经问过军中的人了，他们都说不知将军为何会病倒，军医看过后都说是怪病。”
“怪病？”嬴政的面色更难看了。若是知晓生的什么病，那倒也好解决，可最麻烦的便是“怪病”，谁知道那怪病有什么症状，又怎么样才能治好。弄到最后，恐怕桓齮的小命都堪忧。
“那个叫李信的将军，又是如何失踪的？”嬴政冷声问。
“这……也不知，他们说得太过古怪，小的以为他们恐是中邪了。”那人的面色怪异道。
徐福从旁闻言，心中不由一动。
李信失踪了？！因为是认识的人，徐福难免上了点心，甚至还有些想要亲自去看看，秦军之中究竟如何古怪了？
嬴政抿了抿唇，令那人整理成文书递交上来，那人见嬴政并未发火，顿时松了一口气，忙点点头快步出去了。
不久之后，竹简被呈到了嬴政的跟前，徐福主动凑上前去，和嬴政一同翻看。
那人在竹简之中对李信失踪的过程进行了描述。
李信是如何失踪的呢？的确有几分离奇。他是带着人前去查探敌军的时候，从他带去的手下跟前，离奇消失的。那些手下就眼睁睁地看着他，从一道绿光过后，众人只觉得眼球刺痛，忍不住闭了闭眼，等再睁开眼的时候，李信就不见了踪影。
听故事的人，恐怕会不自觉地将它当做是个灵异事件。
也难怪那人说古怪了。
但正是这样的古怪才挑起了徐福的兴趣，除了他之外，这世上还能有什么更离奇的事？难道真的有鬼怪吗？徐福也不敢完全否认，因为他现在都还记得小布条化为黑影的英姿。
嬴政回头看了他一眼，差不多猜到了徐福的心思。

徐福一行人刚出了咸阳城没多久，便有马儿追上来了，桑中撩起车帘往后一看，却见着了两个熟悉的身影，桑中愣了愣，惊讶无比。
“如何？是谁？”徐福靠在车厢里，出声问道。
“蒹葭，还有龙阳君。”桑中嘴唇动了动，脸上的表情都还有一些不敢置信。
徐福也有些惊讶，只不过他将这些情绪都收在了心底。
柏舟停下马车，好让蒹葭和龙阳君走近。柏舟沉声问他们：“你们如何会来？”若说以前他们见着龙阳君，还拿他如同传说中的人物一样来谨慎对待，那么如今都看着蒹葭和龙阳君成婚了，他们对待龙阳君的态度也就随意许多了。抛开龙阳君那层身份，他现在就是蒹葭的家眷而已。
龙阳君冷淡地掀了掀眼皮，道：“我与蒹葭本是不想来的，奈何王上还是下令让蒹葭跟来，蒹葭要来，我自然也只有随行。”
徐福在马车内听见他们的对话，这才知道嬴政之后又后悔了，还是忍不住让蒹葭跟过来了。当时嬴政应该是算到了的，蒹葭要来，龙阳君又怎么会不跟随？龙阳君有自己的势力，何况他那一手好剑法，的确少有敌手，带在身边是个强有力的助手。
徐福窥破嬴政的心思之后，心底的滋味陡然间变得怪异了起来。
好像有点儿酥酥麻麻的，像是一串电流迅疾地贴着心脏擦过。
他将这股情绪压下去，示意他们继续往前走。
蒹葭和龙阳君进了马车，不一会儿，马车便再度往前行了。
龙阳君看了徐福跟前摆着的东西，饶有兴致地道：“先生如何会想起来带这些东西？”摆在徐福的面前都是鼎，龙阳君记得，其中有一只还是自己交给徐福的。
“桓齮将军病重，我带这些前去制药。”
“制药？”龙阳君的面色有些怪异，制药的用具那么多，怎么偏偏用这么几个破鼎？反正以龙阳君那挑剔的目光，是看不出这几个鼎有何珍贵之处的。“龙阳怎么不知，先生何时还会黄岐之术了？”
“也就跟师兄瞎学了两招。”徐福厚着脸皮毫不客气地道。他的口气哪里像是“瞎学”啊。
龙阳君嘴角抽了抽。
徐福的师兄姜游，的确是天下难得一见的神医，毕竟都出自鬼谷门下啊。
龙阳君面上的淡漠之色褪去，他微微笑道：“那龙阳便等着瞧先生的好本事了。”
徐福与龙阳君熟了，便知道他这话并无半点嘲讽的意思，徐福点了点头，正儿八经地应了，“好。”他也想看一看，自己跟着学了那么长的时间，到底有多少长进。
因为心系军中境况，徐福不敢耽搁，便早早嘱咐了柏舟快速赶路。

有时候环境所迫，人也讲究不起来了，徐福便是如此，从前他巴不得马车行得越慢越好，这一次马车在路途上狂奔不已，每晚也只是匆匆休息便要快速启程，吃的东西也越发简陋，甚至偶尔还有饿肚子的时候，但徐福也硬生生扛下来了。
到了后来，马车就算是行得再颠簸，徐福都能入睡了。

徐福在马车之中还睡得正香，桑中无奈之下，只得走得更近一些，低头去唤徐福。徐福的面容在他眼底放大，对方脸上的皮肤一寸一寸，桑中清晰可见，徐福的脸上连颗痣都寻不见了。
他的模样实在足够精致。

桑中看得心中颤动不已，好半天才强行忍住心中莫名升起的激动。

徐福掀起车帘走了下去。

对上他们那热情的眼眸，徐福有些疑惑。
这些人对自己怎么这样热情？就像是好不容易见到亲爹妈了一样……

于是处处装神仙的徐福，到了营地里，还是得继续装起神仙。
神棍事业，还真是永生不止啊……

低热，呕吐，腹泻。
口腔溃烂，指甲青灰，面皮发白，嘴唇泛紫。
四肢无力，肢体开始溃烂。
