Fortunately, Zhao Cheng didn't mind the thinness of the remark. Not only did he not mind, but he also excitedly replied, "I-I am fine." His expression was one of immense gratitude, and his cheeks even flushed slightly from the excitement.

Some soldiers shared a bit of tiger meat.

Because it had been roasted in a rush and lacked any spices, the tiger meat was only about eighty percent cooked, making it look quite unappetizing. However, that was just in Xu Fu's eyes.

Zhao Cheng took the meat, thanked the soldier hurriedly, and then piled it all in front of Xu Fu. "Sir, please eat some. This servant has noticed that you haven't really eaten anything these past two days."

"No, you eat it." Xu Fu truly had no appetite. Besides, there were no vegetables to be found outdoors, and the water supply wasn't sufficient; if he ate this meat, he might end up constipated. Even though people called him an "immortal," at his core, he was still a proper mortal with a mortal body.

Zhao Cheng didn't understand Xu Fu's meaning; he simply assumed Xu Fu was intentionally giving it to him.

Xu Fu accidentally caught Zhao Cheng's gaze and saw that his eyes were slightly red, his expression agitated, and his face full of emotion.

Xu Fu was a bit bewildered.

Did he say something? Did he say something that touched Zhao Cheng's heart? Xu Fu suddenly felt that his and the other person's way of thinking were simply not on the same wavelength.

However, Xu Fu didn't show these doubts. He said calmly, "Eat slowly. I'm a bit tired, so I'm going to rest first."

Zhao Cheng nodded vigorously with red eyes. "Go ahead, Sir. I will stand guard for you."

Xu Fu glanced at Meng Tian, who was eating meat not far away, thinking to himself that having him there was more than enough. But since Zhao Cheng was so devoted, he shouldn't refuse. Once they returned to Xianyang, he would ask Ying Zheng to give him a promotion. Xu Fu felt this was the simplest and most direct way to repay him.

He lay down and, thinking about it, fell asleep.

The night passed quickly.

Because they had been through so much the night before, no one woke up early; in fact, Xu Fu was the first to rise. He sat up and saw that the fire was dim, so he grabbed some branches and wood to throw in. After throwing a few, the fire... went out even more thoroughly...

Xu Fu: ...

"Sir, you put in too much." Zhao Cheng, not sure when he had woken up, spoke from behind Xu Fu. He walked over, squatted down, poked at the fire a few times, and blew on it, causing the flames to reignite.

Although the fire couldn't provide light during the day, the others were still sleeping, and staying near the heat source would keep them warm—it was autumn, after all.

After waking up, Zhao Cheng immediately attended to Xu Fu's washing.

Calling it "attending" was really just helping fetch water for Xu Fu to wash his face and rinse his mouth, then drinking some warm water to warm his stomach.

So thoughtful! Almost on par with Sang Zhong!

This thought popped into Xu Fu's mind.

Because of Zhao Cheng's extra diligence, Xu Fu's attitude toward him became even better, and after receiving Xu Fu's gentle demeanor, Zhao Cheng worked even harder.

After the two of them fussed about for a while, the others woke up one after another.

Everyone quickly packed their things and set off to leave Mianzhu.

The commoners took one last look at the city, then, suppressing the sobs threatening to escape their throats, turned around and walked forward without looking back.

These people had perhaps lived in this city since birth; having to leave suddenly just to survive, no one's heart felt good.

But after turning around, they placed all their hope in Xu Fu, believing that he would lead them to a better future.

Xu Fu, who didn't want to be burdened with such high expectations at all, suddenly felt the weight on his shoulders increase.

He could only comfort himself: wasn't the reason he came to Mianzhu to bring hope to everyone? This was the greatest use of the reputation he had accumulated for so long. Everyone was willing to trust him; as long as it was something he said, no one would doubt it. When disaster struck, his abilities were exactly what was needed most.

Perhaps because Xu Fu was traveling with them, it was truly miraculous that no one complained of hardship or fatigue; they were all full of hope for the future.

After leaving Mianzhu, they experienced a few more aftershocks, but the tremors were not significant. At first, the people were panicked, but later, they were able to pass through them with great composure under Xu Fu's command.

As they got further and further away from Mianzhu, their gaze toward Xu Fu became increasingly reverent.

Such reverence was by no means born from the wild rumors about how powerful Xu Fu was; this reverence was more precious, born from living with him day and night and seeing his capabilities more and more.

A few days later, they arrived at the next city.

They had been traveling quickly, and the people's condition should have been terrible, but after these few days, they were in very good spirits. Not only that, they had shed their previous emaciated appearance; at first glance, one wouldn't associate them with refugees.

...

The cities around Mianzhu had also been hit by the disaster. After all, the construction standards of this era could not be compared to later generations, and in later generations, even advanced construction standards were useless when an earthquake struck, let alone now.

This city was no exception; when they arrived, they were met with a scene of devastation.

The soldiers and commoners spent a great deal of effort to find many survivors, and this group was incorporated into their traveling party.

Xu Fu was responsible for instilling hope in these people, while the coordination and arrangement of them were left entirely to Meng Tian. Fortunately, Meng Tian was used to being a general, so handling a group of commoners didn't trouble him. After the team grew, they still only stayed for one night before moving on.

Among the cities they passed next, some had even become entirely dead cities.

Xu Fu looked at the silent ruins before him, with only the city walls standing stubbornly. There was no sign of life in the city, and he could even smell the scent of decay; such a smell made one feel terrified. The commoners following behind, seeing such a city, all fell silent.

Some were even affected and couldn't help but sob softly.

To prevent such a depressed atmosphere from spreading, they didn't stay long. Before leaving, Meng Tian set a great fire in the city.

On the road ahead, after the commoners finished crying, their gaze toward Xu Fu became even more firm.

Perhaps this was the peculiar nature of faith; it could truly bring you hope and light when you were in despair. After seeing the dead city, the commoners' gratitude toward Xu Fu and the King grew even deeper. If they hadn't come, they would also be lying quietly underground.

More than half a month passed.

In the blink of an eye, it was late autumn.

There was no one left to save; the cities with light damage had already received help from nearby cities, and those with heavy damage couldn't wait for Xu Fu to arrive.

Xu Fu held on with a breath of determination, not daring to let go, and even less daring to bring any negative emotions to everyone. Before he knew it, they had arrived at Yongcheng.

By the time they reached Yongcheng, there were few commoners left behind Xu Fu. They had been distributed along the way to cities that were unaffected or lightly affected. However, a city's capacity was limited, and those who hadn't been distributed followed them to Yongcheng.

Yongcheng was the old capital of the Qin State, and its walls were built very sturdily. When they arrived, the walls had no damage at all, but after entering the city, they realized Yongcheng was not as intact as it appeared on the outside.

Almost the entire south side of Yongcheng had collapsed, while other areas were much better.

The streets were gradually returning to normal; some shops had opened one after another, and there were people selling food on the roadside. Looking into the distance, Xu Fu could still see the ruins in the south of the city. Turning his head, he could also see white mourning banners everywhere. Had many people died in Yongcheng too? Logically, the disaster in Yongcheng should have been relatively light.

Just as Xu Fu was puzzled, a rider appeared on the street. The leader was a young man with a mature, steady demeanor; when his features were tightly set, he looked even older than Meng Tian.

The man recognized Meng Tian's face first and immediately rode over, calling out loudly, "General Meng!" His voice caused the commoners on the street to look toward Meng Tian.

Meng Tian nodded and said indifferently, "General Feng."

Xu Fu understood in his heart that this must be Feng Jie, the son of Feng Quji.

Meng Tian turned to introduce Xu Fu's identity to Feng Jie.

Perhaps Feng Jie had heard when he left that he was originally supposed to be sent to Mianzhu, but in the end, this Commandant Xu had volunteered to take his place, leaving him to come to the less dangerous Yongcheng. Feng Jie's features relaxed, he gave Xu Fu a smile, and cupped his hands, saying, "Commandant Xu."

Xu Fu nodded faintly. "General Feng."

Even if Xu Fu's attitude was cold, Feng Jie didn't mind. He had heard countless rumors about this Commandant Xu: first about how powerful his skills were, then about how many people he had saved, then that he was arrogant and cold and hard to approach, and even that he was the King's lover... Feng Jie had heard so much that he had long ago sketched an image of Xu Fu in his mind.

Now, it didn't seem much different from his mental construct, so Feng Jie was naturally not surprised.

The county office hadn't collapsed, so Feng Jie led the group there first. The commoners were naturally handed over to the appropriate people.

Feng Jie said, "It is fitting for them to stay in Yongcheng. Many people died in Yongcheng during this earthquake."

"Why is that?" Xu Fu frowned.

Feng Jie said helplessly, "When the King gave instructions that there might be an earthquake, many wealthy families and nobles in Yongcheng refused to believe it. Instead, they indulged in even more pleasure. That would be one thing, but some commoners who wanted to temporarily hide outside the city were also blocked by them."

Xu Fu still remembered that when Ying Zheng held his capping ceremony in Yongcheng, many families had colluded with Lao Ai to help him rebel. If Ying Zheng hadn't made arrangements in advance, perhaps Lao Ai would have succeeded.

Were these people expressing their dissatisfaction and resistance toward Ying Zheng with their actions?

Xu Fu's expression darkened immediately. "And these people?"

Feng Jie gave a sarcastic smile. "It's quite funny; they caused their own deaths. More than half of these people died. The houses the commoners lived in were small, and they ran out desperately when the earthquake hit, so they were fine."

This could be considered heaven's will in the dark.

Such people deserved to lose their lives!

They chatted all the way to the county office. Finally having a place to shelter, Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief. Having been tense for so long, suddenly relaxing made Xu Fu's face turn pale.

Feng Jie arranged for people to prepare water and food.

Xu Fu went to bathe without a word; if he didn't bathe now, he would be truly filthy. At this point, Xu Fu couldn't help but sigh that it was fortunate it was autumn and not summer. Otherwise, a group of people would probably have stunk each other to death.

After cleaning up, Xu Fu ate some food and went to catch up on sleep.

By the time he woke up feeling refreshed, the moon was already high in the sky.

He pushed open the door and walked out, only to see Zhao Cheng still leaning against the doorframe, having actually fallen asleep like that. Xu Fu was surprised and hurriedly woke him up. "Why did you fall asleep here?"

"This servant saw that you looked weary, Sir, and was worried you might feel uncomfortable when you woke up, so I waited outside the door..." Zhao Cheng said in a low voice.

Xu Fu's expression was complex. "Thank you for your hard work. Go and rest quickly."

Zhao Cheng couldn't help but yawn. He whispered, "Sir, do you need hot water and food now?"

"No, go ahead." After saying this, Xu Fu beckoned to the soldiers guarding the courtyard. There were plenty of people he could call upon; why would he need to call on Zhao Cheng at this time?

Zhao Cheng probably couldn't hold on any longer, so after bowing, he walked away quickly.

Xu Fu couldn't help but look at Zhao Cheng's back. He didn't know if he was too cold. Clearly, Zhao Cheng was as good to him as Sang Zhong, but Xu Fu felt more gratitude toward Sang Zhong; toward Zhao Cheng, there was a more complex feeling. Perhaps it was because he hadn't yet gotten used to the devotion of servants in ancient times willing to sacrifice for their masters. Or perhaps it was because he had spent years with Sang Zhong, and the deep bond naturally couldn't be compared to Zhao Cheng.

Xu Fu shook his head, casting these thoughts to the back of his mind.

He ordered someone to bring silk and a charcoal pencil, lit a lamp, and prepared to write at the desk.

...Never would he have imagined that one day he, Xu Fu, would be writing a family letter.

Hmm, "family letter"—when he whispered these two words in his heart, Xu Fu felt a warmth in his chest. This was something he never had the chance to experience in his previous life.

If it weren't for the fact that Ying Zheng, Fusu, and Huhai had sent him letters while he was at the military camp, Xu Fu wouldn't have thought of this.

Along the way, Xu Fu had been too busy to write a letter to Ying Zheng, relying entirely on soldiers to pass messages back. But those messages were cold; how could they compare to writing it himself?

Xu Fu hesitated for a while before deciding to write.

...When Ying Zheng received it, his unhappiness and worry should... should suddenly diminish quite a bit, right?

Xu Fu gripped the charcoal pencil and carefully wrote in the barely elegant seal script he had worked hard to practice.

A-Zheng,

I have reached Yongcheng and should be able to return to Xianyang before long...

Writing this, Xu Fu felt the content was too dry.

How does one write a family letter? Xu Fu racked his brains.

Like Ying Zheng, simply narrating what happened? But Xu Fu's journey had been too dangerous, and he didn't want to write it down. If he were to narrate it, he would wait until he was safely back in Xianyang and tell Ying Zheng in person so as not to make him worry so much.

Then what to write? Like Huhai and Fusu, rambling about daily life? What he ate? He couldn't write that either. He had eaten poorly and slept badly on this trip; writing it out would only cause Ying Zheng worry.

Xu Fu was troubled, but deep down, a sentence was on the verge of coming out.

Hmm...

I miss you a little.

...

Xu Fu hesitated, then finally ended the family letter with a short sentence.

A-Zheng, I have reached Yongcheng and should be able to return to Xianyang before long. I miss you a little.

Oh, and Huhai and Fusu.

...

Xu Fu added the last sentence and then folded the silk.

After placing the silk against his chest, Xu Fu turned to continue sleeping. When he woke up, he washed quickly, found a soldier, and told him to present this item to Ying Zheng when he took the message back to Xianyang. The soldier nodded repeatedly and placed it cautiously in his bosom.

Xu Fu wanted to return to Xianyang quickly, but everyone was exhausted from the journey, relying entirely on a single breath of determination. Now that this breath had dissipated, the fatigue and hardship surged up immediately. Soldiers were human, too; they needed rest.

After discussing with Meng Tian, they decided to rest in Yongcheng for two days before returning to Xianyang.

Feng Jie had to stay in Yongcheng until new officials were sent and the city returned to its former order.

After the family letter was handed over, Xu Fu felt a rare sense of nervousness.

It wasn't an anxious nervousness, but an expectant one. He didn't know what would happen when Ying Zheng saw his letter.

Xu Fu didn't know what was wrong with him; perhaps it was seeing so many life-and-death separations, seeing people crying loudly but still having family to lean on.

Xu Fu vaguely drew an equals sign between his heart and the Xianyang Palace.

That could also be considered his home.

Once he thought this way, the feeling changed suddenly, as if a part of his heart had been tethered. Xu Fu even doubted whether he could ever walk away so freely again. It was a bit like being bound, but he didn't feel sad about it.

Xu Fu clutched his chest, sat at the desk, and stared at the tree branches outside the window in a daze.

Zhao Cheng knocked on the door carefully from the outside. "Sir."

"Come in." Xu Fu collected his thoughts and turned to look at him. "Is something the matter?"

Zhao Cheng smiled embarrassedly. "I came to attend to you, Sir."

Xu Fu was about to say he didn't need attending, but meeting Zhao Cheng's dark eyes, he couldn't say anything and just nodded. "You don't have to be so reserved. If you're tired, sit down and rest." Zhao Cheng didn't look very old, and it wasn't easy for him to be tired while taking care of him. Making him stand by his side at all times waiting for orders was too heartless.

Zhao Cheng smiled but didn't say anything about "this servant wouldn't dare."

He seemed to notice Xu Fu's boredom and said, "Sir, would you like this servant to find some books for you?"

Xu Fu was indeed a bit bored, but if he sat here reading bamboo slips, what would Zhao Cheng do? Just leave him neglected on the side?

So Xu Fu refused.

"Zhao Cheng, when did you enter the palace?" Xu Fu simply started chatting with him.

Zhao Cheng shook his head. "This servant doesn't remember; I was still small then."

"And later you were always driving carriages in the palace?"

Zhao Cheng laughed. "No, I wasn't even qualified to drive carriages before. I only raised horses. It wasn't until you entered the palace, Sir, that I had the opportunity to follow you and drive the carriage. All my opportunities were given by you, Sir."

Xu Fu smiled faintly.

Zhao Cheng said in surprise, "I've never seen you smile before, Sir! When you smile, it's really... really... this servant is at a loss for words; I can't think of any words to describe it, I just think it's beautiful..." Zhao Cheng looked honest, and his praise was incredibly sincere.

Xu Fu hadn't expected himself to smile at him either.

Zhao Cheng had shown him so much kindness, so he shouldn't be stingy either, right?

Xu Fu racked his brains for a topic to change the subject. Although everyone liked to hear nice things, when Zhao Cheng praised him, Xu Fu always felt a faint sense of incongruity. Perhaps it was just that men weren't used to being praised for being "beautiful."

Before he could think of a topic, Zhao Cheng had already spoken again.

"After you return, Sir, can I be a personal attendant by your side?" Zhao Cheng asked cautiously.

After asking, Zhao Cheng immediately added, "It... it is this servant being too greedy. If that's not possible, driving the carriage for you is fine too. It's just that you are no longer the Fengchang, Sir, so there are fewer times you need me."

"Hmm..." Xu Fu was deep in thought, considering the feasibility of Zhao Cheng becoming a personal attendant.

In fact, Xu Fu had no official status in the palace; he used the palace servants from Ying Zheng's bedroom, and those servants were very obedient to him, so Xu Fu had never thought about having his own personal attendant. But Zhao Cheng's request wasn't excessive.

Driving a carriage was never as good as being a personal attendant.

If he were a personal attendant, he could make him more relaxed, which would repay this kindness. Besides, hadn't he been planning to promote Zhao Cheng anyway?

He would mention this to Ying Zheng when he returned.

With a plan in mind, Xu Fu looked up at Zhao Cheng and said, "Okay."

Zhao Cheng was stunned. "S-Sir? What did you just say?"

Seeing his incredulous look, Xu Fu found it a bit funny and felt his heart soften. He was truly young; just this could make him so happy.

"I said okay."

"Sir..." Zhao Cheng bit his lip and swallowed. "This servant... this servant is so excited, I... I don't know what to say..."

"Then don't say anything," Xu Fu said calmly.

Zhao Cheng nodded. "Yes! Yes... Sir... this servant will definitely serve you well!" There were even tears in Zhao Cheng's eyes, and the gratitude in his gaze toward Xu Fu grew even thicker.

Author's note:

A reminder: Zhao Cheng is a historical figure who actually existed.

chapters.title: 第168章
chapters.source_text:
两日后，冯劫送着徐福一行人从雍城离开，休整过后的众人，再度恢复到了精神抖擞的时候。
休息了两日的徐福，顿时就不大能忍受艰苦的回城路了，原本之前走得更为艰苦，他也并未觉得什么，但是人一旦放松过后，就很难再回到之前的紧绷状态了。
赵成对徐福有求必应，尽全力做到事事照顾好徐福，而蒙恬也极为配合徐福，就连那些士兵们也都没说什么。他们似乎并不觉得奇怪。按照他们原先认为的，徐都尉本就该是和他们不一样的，徐都尉怎么能受苦呢？后来到了去救灾的地方，他们才发现徐都尉竟然忍下来了！心中顿时对徐都尉敬畏不已。
而如今徐福不过是回到了他们设想中的模样上去罢了，这有什么可奇怪的？这本来才是徐都尉啊！
因为所有人都捧着徐福好生照顾，几乎都了有求必应的地步，回城的路上渐渐倒也不是很难熬了，徐福都有些惊讶，他没想到这些人会发自真心地捧着自己。看来这就是古代信仰的好处啊！
想来离他将秦国上下都忽悠成功也不远了吧……
徐福仿佛看见国师之位在远处对着自己招手笑。
路上又走了十来天的功夫，眼瞧着便要入冬了，徐福总算是赶回了咸阳，只是他仍旧错过了嬴政的生辰。
他们踏入了咸阳城，眼前见到的是全然不同的景象。
在他们入城后，一直盯着城门口的人都各自回去禀报了，然后他们前行了没多久，就有人前来拦人了。蒙恬皱了皱眉，“来者何人？”
徐福也跟着掀起车帘看了过去。
离开雍城的时候徐福便将交通工具换做了马车。
那下人目光殷切地看向了徐福，道：“小的乃是国尉派来请徐都尉的。”
国尉啊……徐都尉的师兄啊……众人闻言，恍然大悟。
而蒙恬却有些为难。他应当是先将徐福带回到王宫中去见王上的，但是尉缭的性子他也很清楚，若是今日他不给这个面子，那尉缭能记恨上许久，再见他的时候，绝对是看他哪里都不顺眼。蒙恬觉得实在没必要和尉缭将关系闹得更僵，于是干脆将面见王上的事儿交给了自己的副手，随即便看向徐福，问道：“不如我陪都尉过去？”
徐福本来也是想要见嬴政的，但是尉缭还是他师兄呢，而且尉缭对他当真不错，犹豫一下，徐福便决定先去见尉缭了。反正待他回宫后，尉缭能见他的时候也就少了，而他能见嬴政的时候可是多得不能再多的。
徐福唯一觉得惊讶的是，蒙恬竟然会主动提出陪同自己前去，他不是与尉缭不合吗？
“那走吧。”徐福掩下心中的惊讶。
赵成驾着马车跟随那下人往国尉府的方向而去，后面还跟了个蒙恬。
而蒙恬的副手已经苦着脸恨不得躺平在这里了。
徐都尉能不去见王上，将军你能吗？这要是怪罪下来可怎么是好啊！
·
下人引着他们踏进了国尉府中，这还是蒙恬头一次正儿八经地踏进国尉府，毕竟从他当初强留下尉缭后，尉缭便心中记恨，延续几年都与蒙恬不合，并且尉缭还从不在朝上遮掩自己对蒙恬的抵制。在这样的情况下，蒙恬又怎么可能会踏足国尉府呢？就算他主动想来，恐怕也是踏进来，便被人打出去了吧。
尉缭并不知徐福身后跟了个尾巴，他听人来报，说是徐福过来了，当即便喜不自禁地出去了。
“师弟。”尉缭脚下生风，快步迎到了门边，他的面上竟是挂着极为明显的喜悦之色。这要在尉缭的脸上看见，就算是不容易了。毕竟尉缭常年都是一张晚娘脸。
虽然尉缭已经舍得放手让徐福去棉诸了，但是实际上他心底也深藏了不少担忧。那些大臣明里暗里的猜测，尉缭也都有耳闻，听过之后他也就是背后骂两句。尉缭不去见秦王，只是因为他知道，此时秦王心头说不准比他更为糟心，两人互相见了，说不定心中的担忧就扩大成双份儿的了。尉缭没想到，自己不过一个小小的举动，竟是让人误以为他对徐福都是虚情假意。气得尉缭把那些人的名字都挨个记下来了。
尉缭思绪乱飞间，瞥见了蒙恬的身影。
尉缭的脚步顿时就僵住了，脸上的喜悦之色也退了个一干二净，几乎是转眼间他就又恢复了他的晚娘脸。
“蒙将军怎么会在这里？”尉缭极不高兴地道。
徐福想着这段日子蒙恬照顾自己还挺多的，于是便主动出声化解二人之间的锋芒，“蒙将军是王上派来保护我的，我要来见师兄，他自然是跟着来了。”
尉缭别的都没听见，倒是就听见了一句“我要来见师兄”。顿时心中的喜悦止不住地往外冒，连带着蒙恬也那么顺眼一点了。
尉缭心中极为得意。
师弟没有先去见秦王，先来见了我……
他欲将徐福迎进去，徐福却摇了摇头，道：“我知晓师兄担忧我的安慰，因而先来与师兄报个平安，但是我还得去见王上，还有灾情要禀报。”
听到最后一句话，尉缭这才褪去了不情愿的情绪，他知晓灾情的重要性，无论如何也得徐福先去禀报了再说。
“那你去吧。”
徐福对上尉缭的目光，微微一笑，露出十分诚挚的目光来，“多谢师兄为我忧心。”从一开始的时候，他是的确厌恶尉缭此人，但到如今，那些厌恶早就飞走了，他也渐渐能体会到尉缭这个师兄独特的对人好的方式了。
徐福说完，忍不住又补上了一句，“这一路还得多谢蒙将军，若非有他跟在我的身边，我便丧命了。为此蒙将军还受了伤，被老虎咬了。”
尉缭闻言，就算心中再不以为意，但面上对着蒙恬的时候，倒是温和了不少，“多谢蒙将军照顾我这师弟了。”
蒙恬道：“不必，这本就是我该做的。”
尉缭目光怪异地看了他一眼，看蒙恬的目光，就如同是在看觊觎自己师弟的坏人一样。蒙恬并没能感受到尉缭的目光。
他们转身要走，尉缭却突然叫住了他们，“既然蒙将军是因师弟而受伤，那我便送蒙将军一些伤药，请蒙将军好生养伤。”养好可就别拿这个去指望我师弟知恩图报了！心中总觉得别的男人对自己师弟图谋不轨的傻师兄如此想道。
管家很快送来了伤药，蒙恬挑了挑眉，惊讶地收起来，然后才和徐福一起离开了。
马车进宫后，徐福犹豫了一下便让蒙恬独自去见嬴政了，然后他往寝宫的方向去了。嬴政要见的人不止他一个，所以嬴政就绝不可能带着胡亥和扶苏同到殿中去，反正殿中有其他人，自己也不大方便与嬴政说话，干脆就先去见胡亥和扶苏好了。
许久不见，徐福也有些想他们了。
在一起相处得久了，难免情谊一日深厚过一日。
宫人见到徐福的时候，惊讶不已，还有两个宫女竟是忍不住连眼泪都飚了出来，“先生可回来了！先生是要寻扶苏公子和胡亥公子吗？”宫人不用问便能知晓徐福的心思了。
徐福点了点头，转过头看了一眼跟在身后的赵成，“你便先在此处等我吧。”
赵成小心地点了点头，然后有些拘谨地站在了那里。
徐福这才命令宫人道：“带路吧。”
宫人们好奇地看了一眼赵成，然后便带着徐福到扶苏的偏殿中去了，身边的内侍低声道：“最近胡亥公子也都是呆在扶苏公子殿中的呢。”
徐福差不多的已经能想得到，胡亥又是如何缠着扶苏的了。
说话间徐福已经走进了殿中。
里面隐隐传出了扶苏的读书声，过了会儿，是扶苏气愤的声音，“你怎么这么蠢？”
胡亥不服气地道：“不蠢。”
“不蠢还背不下来？”扶苏给气笑了。
胡亥重重地“哼”了一身，“我不背了！”
“不背算了，昨日也不知道是谁来寻我说要多学写字的，哦，今日我便给父亲写信。”
徐福听着这段对话，心中觉得好笑不已，他慢慢地走近了，刚好看见气急的胡亥抱着扶苏的手就往上啃，气得扶苏大骂，“你怎么爱咬人？你当自己是犬类吗？”
胡亥哼哼两声，不说话。
“不必写了，若有什么话，现在说与我听便是。”徐福的声音在殿中响起。
殿中的宫人们立即跪了下来。
而胡亥和扶苏都愣了愣，转过身来呆愣愣地看着徐福。扶苏的模样看上去与他平日相去甚远，徐福顿时觉得心中分外的愉悦。
“父亲！”胡亥一脚踹在扶苏的腿上，松开扶苏的胳膊，撒腿就朝着徐福的方向跑了过去。
徐福也很高兴地将他接到了怀中，胡亥的体重一天天在增加，但是徐福抱着他的时候，却再也不会感觉到厌烦了，相反的，心中还涌动着的愉悦。
徐福不知道此刻自己脸上的表情多么的温和。
他的双眸绽放着迷人的光彩，原本就极为俊美的五官，此时更是裹上了一层令人着迷的气质。人喜悦时，便会光彩照人，约莫便是这样了。
扶苏这才慢吞吞地走到了徐福的跟前来，不大好意思地跟着胡亥一起叫道：“父亲。”
徐福伸手摸了摸他的头。
殿中的宫人们见着这一幕，已经彻底确认，此后这王宫中的“女主人”便是徐先生无误了。
另一头的殿中，嬴政虽然隐约猜到徐福会先回寝宫去，但见到只有蒙恬一人进来时，还是难免有些失望。
蒙恬装作没看见嬴政的不虞一般，老老实实地开始交代整个过程，徐福在其中做了什么，经历了什么危险，他都一一说了，没有任何错漏。嬴政的面色慢慢紧绷了起来，“徐都尉可有受伤？”
“并未，只是徐都尉应当会觉得疲累。”
疲累是正常的，若是换做他前去，定然也会觉得疲累。嬴政心中浮起心疼之情，不过倒是没方才那样担心了。只要徐福没受伤就好。
“此次辛苦你了。”嬴政语气亲近地道。他与蒙家兄弟年少时期便结识了，因而感情也同普通的大臣不同。这也是嬴政能放心将徐福交付给蒙恬的原因。蒙恬是个什么样的人，他再清楚不过了。蒙恬替他护着徐福，正合适不过。
蒙恬听后，笑道：“王上不必这般客气，能与徐都尉同行，于我来说，也是极好的一段经历。”
嬴政笑了笑，却想起了方才蒙恬口中频繁提起的一个名字。
“赵成是谁？你手下的兵？他救了徐都尉，寡人会赏他。”
蒙恬摇了摇头，“他不是我手下的兵，他是个内侍，徐都尉当时带过去的。”
内侍？嬴政对这个名字没甚印象。不过也无所谓了，回去后好好赏赐一番便是了。
此次地动救灾完成得极为顺利，也算得上是极为圆满了，待蒙恬禀报完之后，嬴政便让他回去休息了，随后便也立即起身，带着宫人往回寝宫的路上去了。
很快其他大臣也都知道了徐福和蒙恬平安归来的消息，这些人都忍不住咋舌。没想到啊，没想到啊都去这样的地方了，竟然还能安全归来。这还真是……怎么也死不了啊！
想一想当初人去蜀地的时候吧，就有人开始嘲笑他有病，自找死路了。结果都嘲笑好几年了……人家危险的地方去了个遍，愣是没死，还半点伤都没受。
真是人比人，气死人！
不管那些大臣暗地里如何内伤，这一边嬴政已然走到寝宫里来了。
他跨进偏殿中，正好看见徐福懒洋洋倚在榻上，指着摊开的竹简，对胡亥说着什么，待嬴政走近了，隐约能听见“巫术”“下蛊”一类的词。
这就开始教了？
嬴政惊讶地转到了他们跟前去。
徐福乍见一双鞋出现在视线之中，他差点惊掉了手中的竹简。
扶苏犹豫着要不要先拉胡亥避开，还没等他想出个结果来呢，嬴政突然上前一弯腰，将徐福打横抱了起来，然后就这样抱着徐福往外走了，徐福手里的竹简还是啪嗒掉在了地上。胡亥赶紧去捡竹简。
目瞪口呆的扶苏：……
胡亥你是不是傻？重点不在于掉地上的竹简吧？
不过很可惜胡亥没能感受到他心底的呐喊，胡亥将竹简捡起来以后，又在扶苏面前铺开了，“有字不认识。”
扶苏只得无奈地将心神转移到竹简上去。
·
寝宫的大门被合上，殿中的光顿时便暗了不少，只余下点亮的烛火在殿中摇曳。
嬴政将徐福放了下来，连走到床榻边上去都来不及了，他就这样躺在了地上，幸好地面上还铺着厚厚的毯子，不然肯定会硌得徐福肩背都疼起来。
嬴政双腿分开，跪在他的身上，目光深深地凝望着他，其中狂热的火焰几乎要将徐福灼烧得眼球发疼。
徐福的心脏紧了紧，但他却没有抗拒。
刚才嬴政直接将他抱走的时候，徐福是有些不大能适应的，但是这瞬间，什么羞耻都被抛开了。
他忍不住微微起身，蜻蜓点水地在嬴政唇上落下一吻，然后就因为没有支撑而倒了回去，嬴政心中压抑着的火被这个吻给点燃了，他抬手从徐福的肩颈处绕过去，大掌从后面扣住了徐福的脖颈，他甚至觉得隐隐间，自己能感受得到徐福脖颈之下隐藏着的血脉在跳动。这样的滋味令他着迷。
令他想起最早对徐福动情时，忍不住想要在他的身上留下许多痕迹的感觉。
嬴政不再回忆了，他俯下身热烈地吻住了徐福的唇。
这个吻太过霸道，他的动作力道之大，像是要将徐福的唇吮破一样，徐福也感觉到了自己的嘴唇被咬住吮吸的轻微刺痛感，但是这一刻的感觉实在太好，徐福竟然有些舍不得。
不多时，衣衫破裂后，随之响起的便是暧昧的声响，在殿中久久回响。
徐福不自觉地缠着嬴政的腰，将自己这一年份的热情都挥洒进去了……
此时白日天边挂着一轮红日。
秋日春光正好。
·
男人要满足是相当的容易。
徐福和嬴政彼此都餍足了，心情指数也蹭蹭往上涨了不少，就算第二日嬴政还要早起上小朝，他的面色都是温和的。那些大臣们实在摸不透嬴政这谜一样的心思，随后互相对视一眼，只能暗暗道，看来王上对那徐福还并未失去兴致呢。要等下一次，还不知道要等多久呢，一转眼都是五年啦，再等个五年，他们都要老了……
朝上嬴政大肆表扬了徐福和蒙恬，因着冯劫还未归来，表扬暂时还没有他的份儿，不过冯去疾也并不在意。
就在嬴政决心封赏徐福的时候，众人都以为那冯去疾会站出来反对，谁知道人家站出来，无比认真地道了一句，“王上英明！”
众人：……
是在他们不知道的时候，发生了什么吗？冯去疾的那个臭脾气也不像是会屈服的人啊，他会在朝中跟着夸赞徐福，应当不会是王上的授意啊。难道说徐福真有那个魅力，就连冯去疾都对他心服口服了？
众臣暗暗感叹，恐怕没等到王上对他失去兴致的那一日，他们就先等到徐福成长为又一个龙阳君了。
嬴政要给徐福封爵，也是水到渠成的事儿了，众人拦不住，想一想，也没什么可拦的。人家一身功绩，只要王上不是一来便给人封君，那就好！
大约是有了个龙阳君在前头做对比，大家的心理接受能力也就很强了。
嬴政非常满意今日这些人的识趣，高高兴兴地大笔一挥，封徐福爵位“驷车庶长”。秦国自商鞅变法后，立二十级军功爵，想要在秦国加官进爵，便是就这样一条路，拿军功！其中驷车庶长排在第十七级，等同于别国的卿。
驷车庶长有多么厉害呢？
它取自乘驷马之长而为众长之意。这时候乘马车，几匹马来拉，那都是有规格的，一般人你让几匹马来拉你，那无非是嫌自己命太长。驷车庶长能乘驷马，可见其身份地位。而在秦王政之前，驷车庶长便如同未来丞相的地位。
这时官爵不分，驷车庶长还能正儿八经地掌上军权。
众人一听就懵逼了。
王上啊，您是不封君啊，您一来就给封驷车庶长。他才多大一毛孩儿？我们这些老头子还有面子嘛？不过他们也就只能心底埋怨埋怨。聪明的人都知道如今徐福是个不能得罪的，他是个有本事也就算了，他还缕缕都能躲过祸事，这样的人，如今还年轻着呢，要是他能一直这样好运下去，以后定然是位极人臣的。
谁还想去得罪他？
算了算了，不就是个驷车庶长吗？众人再度安慰了，并且这一次改口了，心道，只要王上不是跑来说想要封他当王后就好。
与徐福相比，蒙恬的封赏就很是一般了，不过蒙恬也并不在乎这个，朝中有眼睛的人也知道，蒙恬的封赏根本不急在这一时。如今秦国老将王翦将军，还有蒙恬的祖父蒙骜，还有王贲，蒙武……实在屈指可数。蒙恬两兄弟同王上本就有幼时的交情，如今这两兄弟又极为悍勇，日后还会愁军功吗？他们二人怕是不封则以，一封就会惊人！
小朝散去后，大臣们纷纷向蒙恬和尉缭恭贺。
他们倒是想向徐福恭贺啊，但是连个人影都见不着，那就跟人家师兄寒暄几句，勉强也算是祝贺过了吧。
尉缭对于前来祝贺的人，态度都难得还不错，搞得大臣们越发看不明白了。王上怎么想的他们看不懂，这尉缭怎么想的，他们也看不懂……他们对徐福到底是爱护呢还是假意呢？
总是在疑惑的大臣们不舍地在宫门外散开了。
很快徐福封爵的消息也传开了。
嬴政寝宫中的宫人们跪了一地，齐声道：“恭贺庶长。”
徐福愣了愣，由人服侍着从床榻上起身。
“庶长？”徐福还真不知道这是个什么官位。
宫人们喜气盈盈地去准备吃食了，说是庆贺今日，而徐福还是一头雾水呢。正好此时扶苏带着胡亥来见徐福了。徐福正吃着早饭，见他们进来了，便立即问扶苏：“庶长是什么？”
扶苏愣了愣，没想到徐福竟然连这都不知道，于是忙哭笑不得地为徐福解释起来。
“父王应当是封了您的爵位为驷车庶长。驷车庶长手中可掌军政事务……”
徐福听罢也有些咋舌。
他是当真没想到嬴政会这样大方。原本他所求只是一个国师之位，但是意外的，老天好像给了他很多额外的东西。
掌军政大权，嬴政就对自己这样放心吗？他不会担心自己是另一个龙阳君？想到这里，徐福自己也忍不住心中觉得好笑。也是，嬴政可不是魏王能比的。徐福和扶苏拉开了话茬，聊起了其它的事。一边的胡亥可不管什么爵位不爵位，他偷喝起了徐福的汤，徐福有些哭笑不得但也随他去了。
嘴上虽然说着另外的事，但只有徐福知道，其实自己的心中有着什么样的滋味。
甚至徐福还觉得，嬴政这样大肆封赏他的行为，简直就是不动声色地在众臣跟前秀了一次恩爱。徐福感觉自己的嘴角都要绷不住翘起来了。
扶苏敏锐地察觉到徐福的心情愉悦，便也更卖力地说些好笑的事给徐福来听。
胡亥见状也争宠似的，在一旁逗徐福开心。
嬴政下了小朝，迫不及待想要见一面徐福的时候，谁知道一进殿门便又听见了扶苏和胡亥的笑声，虽然不高兴两人独处又要被破坏了，不过嬴政也不会像过去那样，很无情地命宫人将他们抱走了。嬴政步履轻快地走近，突然间他听见了一道笑声。
尾音还能听出些微清冷的痕迹。
清泠泠的声音一旦笑起来的时候，嬴政便倍觉无法抵抗。
那一声声仿佛搔在了他的心上，让他忍不住心中心绪翻涌。
他走近了。
他也终于看见了徐福头一次，毫不顾忌，放声笑出来的模样。
双眼微眯，眸光黑亮勾人，嘴角翘起，唇变得殷红，让人恨不得一吻才好。他标致的五官仿佛都随着这个笑容而灵动了起来。
嬴政一眼看过去，便再难挪开眼。
嬴政从未考虑过有一日会不喜欢徐福。他觉得徐福身上的每一处，哪怕是上百年，他也看不厌。
徐福听见了脚步声，便立即回过头来，正好与嬴政目光相撞。
徐福脸上的笑容还未撤去，嬴政眼底的痴迷也还尚在。对视的这一眼，那瞬间就变得甜滋滋了起来。
嬴政低声道：“阿福如此愉悦，寡人这里还有一件喜事要与你说。”
封爵的事儿吗？徐福刚想与他说，这事儿我已经知道了。
作者有话要说：　　众大臣：跟龙阳君一比好像也不算什么啦……
众大臣：好担心会不会是又一个龙阳君……
众大臣：唉，他还是比龙阳君好的，只要不是来当王后就好啦！
龙阳君：WTF？？？？关我什么事？？？坐着也躺枪了？？？？

Two days later, Feng Jie saw Xu Fu and his party off as they departed from Yongcheng. After two days of rest, the group had returned to their spirited selves.

Having rested for two days, Xu Fu suddenly found it hard to endure the arduous journey back to the capital. He hadn't thought much of the even harsher travel before, but once a person relaxes, it is difficult to return to that previous state of tension.

Zhao Cheng catered to Xu Fu’s every need, doing his utmost to take care of him, while Meng Tian was extremely cooperative, and even the soldiers didn't say a word. They didn't seem to find it strange. According to their original perception, Commandant Xu was supposed to be different from them; how could Commandant Xu suffer? It wasn't until they reached the disaster relief site that they discovered Commandant Xu had actually endured it! Their hearts were immediately filled with awe and respect for him.

And now, Xu Fu was simply returning to the image they had envisioned for him; what was there to be strange about? This was the real Commandant Xu, after all!

Because everyone pampered Xu Fu and catered to his every whim, the journey back gradually became less grueling. Xu Fu was even a bit surprised; he hadn't expected these people to genuinely pamper him. It seems this is the benefit of ancient faith!

It seemed he wasn't far from successfully fooling all of the Qin State...

Xu Fu could almost see the position of State Preceptor waving and smiling at him from afar.

After traveling for another ten days or so, with winter fast approaching, Xu Fu finally made it back to Xianyang, though he had still missed Ying Zheng’s birthday.

As they stepped into Xianyang, they were met with a completely different scene.

After they entered the city, those who had been watching the gates went back to report, and they hadn't traveled far before someone came to intercept them. Meng Tian frowned, "Who goes there?"

Xu Fu also lifted the carriage curtain to look out.

Xu Fu had switched to a horse-drawn carriage when they left Yongcheng.

The servant looked at Xu Fu with eager eyes and said, "I was sent by the State Lieutenant to invite Commandant Xu."

The State Lieutenant... Commandant Xu’s senior fellow apprentice... The group realized with a start.

Meng Tian, however, was in a bit of a dilemma. He should have taken Xu Fu to the palace to see the King first, but he knew Wei Liao’s temperament well. If he didn't give him this face today, Wei Liao would hold a grudge for a long time and would definitely look at him with disdain the next time they met. Meng Tian felt there was no need to make their relationship even more strained, so he simply handed the task of meeting the King to his deputy, then looked at Xu Fu and asked, "Shall I accompany you, Commandant?"

Xu Fu had intended to see Ying Zheng, but Wei Liao was his senior apprentice, and Wei Liao had truly been good to him. After a moment of hesitation, Xu Fu decided to see Wei Liao first. Anyway, once he returned to the palace, there would be fewer opportunities to see Wei Liao, while he could see Ying Zheng as much as he wanted.

The only thing that surprised Xu Fu was that Meng Tian would take the initiative to accompany him. Wasn't he on bad terms with Wei Liao?

"Let's go then." Xu Fu masked his surprise.

Zhao Cheng drove the carriage toward the State Lieutenant’s mansion, with Meng Tian following behind.

Meng Tian’s deputy, meanwhile, looked so bitter he wished he could just lie down and give up.

Commandant Xu can skip seeing the King, but can you, General? What if we get blamed for this!

·

The servant led them into the State Lieutenant’s mansion. This was the first time Meng Tian had stepped foot in the mansion properly. Ever since he had forcibly kept Wei Liao in the capital, Wei Liao had harbored a grudge, remaining at odds with him for years, and never hiding his resistance toward Meng Tian at court. Under such circumstances, how could Meng Tian have visited? Even if he had wanted to come, he likely would have been beaten out the door.

Wei Liao didn't know a tail was following Xu Fu. When he heard the report that Xu Fu had arrived, he was overjoyed and went out to meet him.

"Junior brother." Wei Liao moved with brisk steps, reaching the door quickly, a look of obvious joy on his face. Seeing this on Wei Liao’s face was rare indeed, as he usually wore a sour expression.

Although Wei Liao had been willing to let Xu Fu go to Mianzhu, he had actually harbored deep concerns. He had heard the rumors and speculations from the officials, and he would just curse them behind their backs. He didn't go to see the King of Qin only because he knew the King was likely feeling even worse than he was, and if they met, their worries might double. Wei Liao hadn't expected that his small action would lead people to misunderstand that he was insincere toward Xu Fu. He was so angry he had written down all their names.

As Wei Liao’s thoughts wandered, he caught sight of Meng Tian.

Wei Liao’s steps froze, the joy on his face vanished completely, and in the blink of an eye, he returned to his usual sour look.

"Why is General Meng here?" Wei Liao asked, extremely displeased.

Xu Fu, thinking of how much Meng Tian had taken care of him lately, took the initiative to defuse the tension, "General Meng was sent by the King to protect me. Since I wanted to come see my senior brother, he naturally followed."

Wei Liao didn't hear anything else, only the words "wanted to come see my senior brother." The joy in his heart bubbled up, making even Meng Tian look a bit more pleasing.

Wei Liao felt immensely proud.

My junior brother didn't go see the King of Qin first, he came to see me...

He wanted to welcome Xu Fu inside, but Xu Fu shook his head, "I know you were worried about my safety, so I came to report that I am safe, but I still need to see the King to report on the disaster."

Hearing the last sentence, Wei Liao shed his reluctance. He knew the importance of the disaster relief; Xu Fu had to report it first no matter what.

"Then go."

Xu Fu met Wei Liao’s gaze and smiled, his expression very sincere, "Thank you for worrying about me, Senior Brother." At first, he had truly disliked Wei Liao, but by now, that dislike had long since vanished, and he had gradually come to understand his senior brother’s unique way of showing kindness.

After speaking, Xu Fu couldn't help but add, "I must also thank General Meng for this journey. If not for him by my side, I would have lost my life. General Meng even got injured, bitten by a tiger."

Upon hearing this, no matter how indifferent he felt, Wei Liao’s expression softened significantly when he looked at Meng Tian, "Thank you, General Meng, for taking care of my junior brother."

Meng Tian said, "No need, this is what I should have done."

Wei Liao gave him a strange look, as if looking at a villain coveting his junior brother. Meng Tian did not sense Wei Liao’s gaze.

As they turned to leave, Wei Liao suddenly called out, "Since the General was injured because of my junior brother, I will send you some medicine. Please take good care of your wounds." And don't use this to expect my junior brother to repay you! thought the silly senior brother who always felt other men were harboring evil intentions toward his junior brother.

The butler quickly brought the medicine, and Meng Tian raised an eyebrow, accepted it in surprise, and then left with Xu Fu.

After the carriage entered the palace, Xu Fu hesitated and let Meng Tian go to see Ying Zheng alone, while he headed toward the sleeping quarters. Ying Zheng had others to see, so he wouldn't be able to bring Fusu and Huhai to the hall. Since there were others there, it wouldn't be convenient to talk to Ying Zheng, so he decided to see Fusu and Huhai first.

It had been a long time, and Xu Fu missed them.

After spending so much time together, their bond had inevitably grown deeper day by day.

When the palace servants saw Xu Fu, they were astonished, and two maids couldn't help but burst into tears, "Sir has returned! Are you looking for Young Masters Fusu and Huhai?" The servants knew Xu Fu’s thoughts without asking.

Xu Fu nodded and turned to look at Zhao Cheng, who was following behind, "You wait for me here."

Zhao Cheng nodded carefully and stood there, looking a bit reserved.

Xu Fu then ordered the servants, "Lead the way."

The servants looked at Zhao Cheng with curiosity before leading Xu Fu to Fusu’s side hall. A eunuch whispered, "Young Master Huhai has been staying in Young Master Fusu’s hall lately."

Xu Fu could already imagine how Huhai was pestering Fusu.

As they spoke, Xu Fu walked into the hall.

Fusu’s reading could be heard faintly, and after a while, Fusu’s angry voice followed, "Why are you so stupid?"

Huhai retorted, unconvinced, "Not stupid."

"If you're not stupid, why can't you memorize it?" Fusu was so angry he laughed.

Huhai let out a heavy "Hmph," "I'm not memorizing it anymore!"

"Fine, don't. I don't know who it was that came to me yesterday asking to learn more writing. Oh well, I'll write to Father today."

Listening to this, Xu Fu found it amusing. He walked closer and saw the furious Huhai biting Fusu’s arm, causing Fusu to yell, "Why do you love biting people? Do you think you're a dog?"

Huhai snorted twice and said nothing.

"No need to write. If you have anything to say, tell me now," Xu Fu’s voice rang out in the hall.

The servants in the hall immediately knelt down.

Huhai and Fusu were both stunned, turning around to stare blankly at Xu Fu. Fusu’s appearance was far from his usual self, and Xu Fu felt an extra sense of joy in his heart.

"Father!" Huhai kicked Fusu’s leg, let go of his arm, and ran toward Xu Fu.

Xu Fu happily caught him in his arms. Huhai’s weight was increasing day by day, but Xu Fu no longer felt annoyed when holding him; instead, a sense of joy welled up in his heart.

Xu Fu didn't know how gentle the expression on his face was at that moment.

His eyes sparkled with a charming glow, and his already handsome features were now wrapped in a fascinating aura. Perhaps this is what it means to be radiant when happy.

Fusu then walked slowly to Xu Fu’s side, feeling a bit shy as he followed Huhai, "Father."

Xu Fu reached out and patted his head.

Seeing this, the servants in the hall were completely convinced that from now on, the "mistress" of the palace was undoubtedly Master Xu.

In the other hall, although Ying Zheng vaguely guessed that Xu Fu would return to his sleeping quarters first, he couldn't help but feel a bit disappointed when only Meng Tian entered.

Meng Tian pretended not to see Ying Zheng’s displeasure and honestly began to recount the whole process—what Xu Fu did and what dangers he faced—without missing a single detail. Ying Zheng’s expression slowly tightened, "Was Commandant Xu injured?"

"No, but the Commandant must be feeling tired."

Fatigue was normal; if he had gone himself, he would certainly feel tired too. A sense of heartache rose in Ying Zheng’s heart, but he wasn't as worried as before. As long as Xu Fu wasn't injured, it was fine.

"You have worked hard this time," Ying Zheng said with a close tone. He had known the Meng brothers since they were young, so his feelings for them were different from those for other officials. This was why Ying Zheng could safely entrust Xu Fu to Meng Tian. He knew exactly what kind of person Meng Tian was. Having Meng Tian protect Xu Fu was just right.

Meng Tian smiled, "Your Majesty, no need to be so polite. Being able to travel with Commandant Xu was a very good experience for me."

Ying Zheng smiled, but remembered a name Meng Tian had frequently mentioned.

"Who is Zhao Cheng? A soldier under your command? He saved the Commandant; I will reward him."

Meng Tian shook his head, "He is not a soldier under my command; he is a eunuch, brought along by the Commandant."

A eunuch? Ying Zheng had no impression of the name. But it didn't matter; he would reward him well upon his return.

The disaster relief had been completed very smoothly and could be considered a great success. After Meng Tian finished reporting, Ying Zheng let him go to rest, then immediately stood up and headed toward the sleeping quarters with his attendants.

Soon, other officials also learned the news of Xu Fu and Meng Tian’s safe return, and they couldn't help but click their tongues. They hadn't expected that after going to such a place, they could still return safely. This was truly... how could he never die!

Think back to when he first went to the Shu region; some people mocked him for being sick and seeking his own death. Yet, they had been mocking him for years... he had been to all the dangerous places and hadn't died, nor had he suffered even a scratch.

Truly, comparing people is infuriating!

Regardless of how the officials felt internally, Ying Zheng had already arrived at the sleeping quarters.

As he stepped into the side hall, he happened to see Xu Fu lazily leaning on a couch, pointing at an open bamboo slip and saying something to Huhai. As Ying Zheng approached, he could vaguely hear words like "witchcraft" and "gu."

He’s already teaching him this?

Ying Zheng walked over in surprise.

Seeing a pair of shoes suddenly appear in his line of sight, Xu Fu almost dropped the bamboo slip in his hand.

Fusu hesitated whether to pull Huhai away, but before he could decide, Ying Zheng suddenly leaned over, scooped Xu Fu up horizontally, and walked out while holding him. The bamboo slip in Xu Fu’s hand fell to the floor with a clatter. Huhai hurriedly went to pick it up.

The dumbfounded Fusu: ...

Huhai, are you stupid? The point isn't the bamboo slip on the floor, is it?

Unfortunately, Huhai couldn't sense his inner cry. After picking up the bamboo slip, he spread it out in front of Fusu, "I don't recognize these characters."

Fusu had no choice but to helplessly shift his focus to the bamboo slip.

·

The doors to the sleeping quarters were closed, and the light in the hall dimmed, leaving only the flickering candlelight.

Ying Zheng put Xu Fu down; he couldn't even wait to reach the bed, so he lay down on the floor. Fortunately, it was covered with thick carpets, otherwise, it would have hurt Xu Fu’s back and shoulders.

Ying Zheng knelt over him, his gaze deep and intense, the fanatical fire in his eyes almost burning Xu Fu’s eyes.

Xu Fu’s heart tightened, but he did not resist.

When Ying Zheng had carried him away, Xu Fu was a bit unaccustomed to it, but at this moment, all shame was cast aside.

He couldn't help but rise slightly, planting a dragonfly-light kiss on Ying Zheng’s lips, then fell back due to lack of support. The fire suppressed in Ying Zheng’s heart was ignited by this kiss. He reached around Xu Fu’s neck, his large palm cupping the back of his neck. He even felt as if he could sense the pulse hidden beneath Xu Fu’s skin. This sensation fascinated him.

It reminded him of when he first fell for Xu Fu, the feeling of wanting to leave many marks on his body.

Ying Zheng stopped reminiscing and leaned down to kiss Xu Fu’s lips passionately.

The kiss was too overbearing, his movements so forceful it felt like he wanted to suck Xu Fu’s lips raw. Xu Fu felt the slight stinging sensation of his lips being bitten and sucked, but the feeling at this moment was so good that he couldn't bear to stop.

Before long, after clothes were torn, ambiguous sounds echoed in the hall for a long time.

Xu Fu unconsciously wrapped his arms around Ying Zheng’s waist, pouring out all his passion for the year...

Outside, a red sun hung in the sky.

The autumn sunshine was just right.

·

It is quite easy to satisfy a man.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were both satisfied, and their mood indices rose significantly. Even though Ying Zheng had to get up early for the morning court the next day, his expression was gentle. The officials couldn't fathom Ying Zheng’s mysterious mood, so they looked at each other and could only secretly think that it seemed the King hadn't lost interest in Xu Fu yet. Who knew how long they would have to wait for the next time? Five years had passed in the blink of an eye; wait another five years, and they would all be old...

At court, Ying Zheng lavishly praised Xu Fu and Meng Tian. Since Feng Jie hadn't returned yet, there was no praise for him for the time being, but Feng Quji didn't care.

Just as Ying Zheng decided to bestow a title upon Xu Fu, everyone thought Feng Quji would stand up to object, but to their surprise, he stood up and said with utmost seriousness, "Your Majesty is wise!"

Everyone: ...

Did something happen that they didn't know about? Feng Quji’s foul temper didn't seem like the type to yield. He wouldn't praise Xu Fu in court unless it was the King’s instruction. Could it be that Xu Fu really had that much charm, even making Feng Quji submit?

The officials sighed secretly, fearing that before the King lost interest in him, they would see Xu Fu grow into another Lord Longyang.

It was a natural progression for Ying Zheng to grant Xu Fu a title; no one could stop it, and thinking about it, there was nothing to stop. The man had merit; as long as the King didn't make him a Duke right away, it was fine!

Perhaps having Lord Longyang as a comparison made everyone’s psychological acceptance much stronger.

Ying Zheng was very satisfied with their tact today and happily took up his brush to grant Xu Fu the title of "Siche Shuzhang." Since Shang Yang’s reforms, the Qin State had twenty ranks of military merit; this was the only way to gain rank in Qin—by earning military merit! Siche Shuzhang was the seventeenth rank, equivalent to a Minister in other states.

How impressive was a Siche Shuzhang?

It meant being the leader of those who rode four-horse chariots. At that time, the number of horses pulling a carriage was strictly regulated; if an ordinary person used four horses, it was just asking for death. Being a Siche Shuzhang meant one could ride a four-horse chariot, showing his status. Before King Zheng, the position of Siche Shuzhang was equivalent to that of a future Chancellor.

At this time, official rank and nobility were not separated, and a Siche Shuzhang could properly hold military power.

Everyone was stunned upon hearing this.

Your Majesty, you didn't make him a Duke, but you immediately made him a Siche Shuzhang. He’s just a kid! Do we old men have any face left? But they could only complain in their hearts. Smart people knew that Xu Fu was someone not to be offended. He was capable, and he repeatedly avoided disaster. Such a person, still young, would surely reach the pinnacle of officialdom if his luck continued.

Who would want to offend him?

Forget it, forget it, it’s just a Siche Shuzhang. Everyone comforted themselves again, and this time they changed their tune, thinking, as long as the King doesn't come and say he wants to make him Queen, it’s fine.

Compared to Xu Fu, Meng Tian’s reward was quite ordinary, but Meng Tian didn't care. Those with eyes in the court knew that Meng Tian’s reward wasn't urgent. Now, with old generals like Wang Jian, Meng Ao, Wang Ben, and Meng Wu... there were very few left. The Meng brothers had a childhood friendship with the King, and they were extremely brave; would they worry about military merit in the future? They probably wouldn't be rewarded until they achieved something shocking!

After the court dispersed, the officials congratulated Meng Tian and Wei Liao one after another.

They wanted to congratulate Xu Fu, but they couldn't even see a shadow of him, so chatting with his senior fellow apprentice was barely enough to count as a congratulation.

Wei Liao’s attitude toward those coming to congratulate was surprisingly good, making the officials even more confused. They couldn't understand what the King was thinking, and they couldn't understand what Wei Liao was thinking either... Did they truly cherish Xu Fu, or was it just a facade?

The perpetually confused officials reluctantly dispersed outside the palace gates.

Soon, the news of Xu Fu’s title spread.

The servants in Ying Zheng’s sleeping quarters knelt on the floor and said in unison, "Congratulations, Shuzhang."

Xu Fu was stunned and was helped up from the bed.

"Shuzhang?" Xu Fu really didn't know what kind of official rank that was.

The servants happily went to prepare food, saying it was to celebrate the day, while Xu Fu remained confused. Just then, Fusu brought Huhai to see him. Xu Fu was eating breakfast and asked Fusu immediately, "What is a Shuzhang?"

Fusu was stunned, not expecting Xu Fu to not even know this, so he explained it to him with a mix of laughter and tears.

"Father must have granted you the title of Siche Shuzhang. A Siche Shuzhang can hold military and political power..."

Xu Fu was also a bit taken aback after hearing this.

He really hadn't expected Ying Zheng to be so generous. Originally, he only sought the position of State Preceptor, but unexpectedly, it seemed Heaven had given him many extra things.

Holding military and political power—was Ying Zheng that confident in him? Wouldn't he worry that he might be another Lord Longyang? Thinking of this, Xu Fu couldn't help but find it funny. Also, Ying Zheng was not someone the King of Wei could compare to. Xu Fu started a conversation with Fusu about other things. Huhai, on the side, didn't care about titles and started stealing Xu Fu’s soup; Xu Fu was amused but let him be.

Although he was talking about other things, only Xu Fu knew what he was feeling inside.

Xu Fu even felt that Ying Zheng’s act of bestowing such a lavish title was simply showing off his affection in front of the officials without a word. Xu Fu felt the corners of his mouth twitching, unable to keep from curling up.

Fusu keenly sensed Xu Fu’s good mood and tried even harder to tell funny stories to make him happy.

Seeing this, Huhai also competed for attention, trying to make Xu Fu laugh.

When Ying Zheng finished the morning court and couldn't wait to see Xu Fu, he heard the laughter of Fusu and Huhai as soon as he entered the hall. Although he was unhappy that their alone time was being interrupted again, he wouldn't heartlessly order the servants to take them away like before. Ying Zheng walked over with light steps, and suddenly he heard a laugh.

The tail end of the sound still held a trace of coldness.

When that clear, cool voice laughed, Ying Zheng felt completely unable to resist.

Each sound seemed to scratch at his heart, making his emotions surge.

He walked closer.

He finally saw Xu Fu laughing out loud for the first time, without any restraint.

His eyes were slightly narrowed, dark and bright, his mouth curled up, his lips turning a deep red, making one want to kiss them. His exquisite features seemed to come alive with this smile.

Ying Zheng looked at him and couldn't look away.

Ying Zheng had never considered that he would one day stop liking Xu Fu. He felt that every part of Xu Fu was something he wouldn't tire of even after a hundred years.

Xu Fu heard footsteps and turned around, his eyes meeting Ying Zheng’s.

The smile on Xu Fu’s face hadn't faded, and the obsession in Ying Zheng’s eyes remained. The moment their eyes met, everything became sweet.

Ying Zheng said in a low voice, "A-Fu is so happy, I have another piece of good news to tell you."

Was it about the title? Xu Fu wanted to tell him that he already knew.

Author's Note: Officials: Compared to Lord Longyang, it doesn't seem like much...

Officials: Worried that he might be another Lord Longyang...

Officials: Sigh, he is still better than Lord Longyang, as long as he doesn't come to be the Queen, it's fine!

Lord Longyang: WTF???? What does this have to do with me???? Why am I being dragged into this while sitting still????

嬴政转身对身后紧跟而来的内侍道：“堪舆图。”
那内侍双手举上，稳稳地放置在徐福的跟前，然后缓缓摊开来。徐福惊奇地发现，这似乎是一张别国的地图。毕竟他在上面并没有看见秦国郡县的标示。
嬴政指着一处道：“你可知这是何地？”
一旁的扶苏和胡亥跟着凑了上去。
徐福细细看了两眼，有些惊讶，“……这里是邺城？”上面标着一个“鄴”字，临近的地方又有邯郸的字样。这是赵国的地图。
嬴政拿着这样的地图给他看，还能是什么喜事？徐福几乎是瞬间就明白过来了。
“有新的战报传来了？”徐福淡淡挑眉。
嬴政点头，面上喜色明显，“桓齮与李信兵分两路，一路直逼邯郸，攻至邺城，一路攻入太原，取下狼孟。”他顿了顿，面上的笑容有些冷，“赵王惶恐，决意送上公子迁至秦为质子。”
徐福能从嬴政那双眼眸里，看见嘲讽和快意。
当初秦国派出不受宠的公子到赵国为质，嬴政便在赵国吃了不少的苦，这样深厚的恩怨，嬴政怎么会轻易忘记？如果赵秦两国位置颠倒，赵王忙不迭地往秦国送人来，岂能不令人觉得快哉？
所谓雪耻之快，便是如此了！
扶苏低声道：“父王，听闻公子迁乃是赵国下任储君，赵王也舍得送来？”
嬴政勾起唇角，笑了笑，带出狂妄又令人敬服的味道来，“如何不舍得呢？国都要亡了，储君算得了什么？赵王正是希望拿公子迁来平息寡人心头的怒火呢。若是换个不受宠的来，哪能凸显诚意呢？”
尽管如此说，徐福也依旧觉得那赵王实在太舍得了。儿子说送就送。或许跟这个时代，国君子女众多，因而并不心疼有关系吧。徐福在心底给那位公子迁点了根蜡。
嬴政突然收起脸上的笑容，很是认真地看着徐福问道：“阿福，这质子，寡人可能收？”
扶苏在旁边听见嬴政与徐福这般对话，顿时嘴角抽搐不已。这……这当真还是他的父王吗？
徐福对上嬴政的目光，顿时就想到了那赵国公主的身上去。
“行啊。”徐福能看得出来，嬴政是很想借此机会将赵国的面子狠狠踩在脚下的。之前赵国还摆出了一副宁死不屈，我和韩国是不一样的姿态来，谁知道赵王这么快便决定送上儿子了呢？这样能将赵王颜面踩下去的机会，莫说是嬴政了，便是徐福都觉得，是个不可多得的好机会。
嬴政能主动询问他的意见，也算态度极好了。一个质子而已，徐福没觉得自己需要放在心上。
“那如今桓齮将军可是要班师回朝？”徐福出声问道。桓齮和李信的身体毕竟都是才刚好不久，这样长期折腾下去，恐怕也不好。
嬴政皱眉，“此事倒是有些麻烦，赵王派出李牧、司马尚分别御桓齮，李信。若非赵王不信任他们二人，恐怕桓齮和李信也难以得手。如今赵王欲召回李牧和司马尚，但这二人却拒不听令，势要与秦军厮杀到底……如今就看赵王能不能压得住他们了？”
“以赵王如今的昏聩程度，怕是不远了吧……”徐福猜测。
“这便要看姚贾的本事了。”嬴政淡淡说着，合上了那堪舆图，交予了一旁的内侍。那内侍小心地捧着下去了。
“姚贾又到邯郸去了？”徐福没想到他的动作那样快，也不知他将韩非带去了没有，徐福瞥了一眼嬴政的神色，总觉得嬴政在说到姚贾时，态度有些奇怪。
“嗯，你让姚贾做的是何事？”嬴政随口问了一句。
“若是有眉目了，我自然便告诉你了。”这种奇妙的事当真不好说，所以他还真不能就这样莽撞地告诉嬴政。
嬴政心中有些不快，但是被很好地压制住了。
可以说徐福在他跟前，几乎是丝毫没有秘密隐瞒的。徐福没想过要瞒他，也没什么好瞒的，所以二人之间的信任度相对来说还是比较高的。上次因着大臣瞎捣乱，让嬴政娶公主，他就瞒了徐福那样一回，都差点倒了霉。
现在见徐福有话也不愿意说了，嬴政方才尝到了那时的滋味。
二人出于不同的心理，但同样的默契，将这件事儿给揭过了。
为了庆贺徐福封为驷车庶长，四人便像是普通家庭一般为此吃了一顿美味的食物，在用膳结束以后，也难得进行了家庭式聊天，东扯西扯一番，气氛温馨。
只是徐福有些无力吐槽。
“阿政，那你可以再封我一个爵位，以此来庆祝。”封赏的是嬴政，封赏完，他还能一脸好大惊喜地给徐福庆贺，好像封赏自己的那个人不是他一样。
嬴政闻言，答应得十分畅快，“好，你要什么，寡人便给你什么。”
扶苏默默地塞了塞耳朵。
嬴政答应得太畅快了，徐福反倒觉得没乐趣了，转眼就将这句话给抛开了。
接下来几日，徐福都是懒惰地待在寝宫中休息，然后听着宫人说起外面与他相关的传言，宫人们说得绘声绘色，仿佛徐福当真已经变身做仙人了一般。
此时一内侍踏门进来，低低地唤了一声，“先生。不……庶长。”那人慌忙改了口，声音里透着些微的紧张。
徐福转头看去。
果然是赵成。
他已经与嬴政简单提了赵成的事，然后赵成便被安排到了他的身边，只是今日才在经过培训之后，正式到他身边来上岗了。徐福也没指望让赵成做什么事，毕竟寝宫之中宫人众多，可以供他差遣的人简直不要太多。现在将赵成放到身边，更多都是为了还恩情罢了。
“你如何安置，便听他的吧。”徐福刻意将声音放得和缓了一些，这在高冷的他的身上实在是太少见了。其余宫人好奇地看了一眼赵成，在心中暗暗对这个新来的人进行了地位估算。
这是徐福刻意做出来的，这样的话，赵成就算未必会享受到什么特权，但这些宫人也一定不会去排挤他了。路子都铺好了，赵成日后想要过得不错，应当不难。若非赵成的身份还未调查清楚，嬴政已经看在他的面子上，给他升个更高的位置了。
赵成有些跃跃欲试地道：“日后奴婢便能伺候庶长的饮食起居了吗？”
旁边一人笑道：“饮食起居伺候的人都是分开的。你若要伺候，那也只能选一样。”
赵成尴尬地笑了笑，道：“那、那奴婢便在晨间伺候庶长起身吧。”
那人这才点头道：“这还差不多。”
徐福想了想还是与赵成说了句，“日后便要辛苦你了。”
“不、不辛苦。”赵成羞涩地笑了笑。
旁人看在眼中，更是记在心里，暗暗道，庶长待他果然是不同的，日后定是要小心着不能得罪了。
赵成很快便被人带下去安置了。徐福的目光从其他宫人的脸上一一扫过。待到嬴政回到寝宫后，徐福便与他说了，“赵成救过我，因而我要礼遇他，但你的寝宫毕竟不是寻常地方，我在众人面前温和待他，是为了让众人日后勿要排挤他，但我担心会有人会错意，以后纵容赵成，万一犯下什么错误便不好了。”
嬴政立即就明白了徐福的意思，徐福是让他去做这个黑脸，将宫人们再敲打一遍，告诉他们某些事上是绝不能放纵的。
嬴政突然发觉到，从徐福这样的一个小举动里，他是不是就可以看做，徐福是在担忧他，处处为他考虑呢？嬴政心情顿时愉悦了起来。
徐福见嬴政的脸上莫名其妙带着笑，只当他是因赵王要送质子来了的缘故。徐福懒洋洋地打了个呵欠，将头埋在嬴政的胸前，动作无比自然地就这样睡着了，全然没觉得自己这模样有多么依赖嬴政。
秦王政十五年入冬。
蜡祭之前，徐福正琢磨着要不要给嬴政将生辰补回来的时候，赵国的使臣再一次抵达了咸阳，只不过这一次他们的队伍之中多了一位公子迁。
当日赵国使臣却没能进到城中来。
原因是城门口的人一听赵国公主又跟来了，便不敢随意放人进来了，哪怕你是赵国使臣也不行。这边转头就先禀报王上去了。还是等王上发话再说吧。
赵国使臣虽然觉得秦国欺人太甚，但也知道如今他们就是任人宰割的，实在没资格来硬气，于是也只有憋着一腔苦楚先留在了城外。
这还是赵国使臣头一次享受这样的待遇。
此时那赵国公主和公子迁坐在马车之中，说起了秦王宫中的事情。
赵嫣咬了咬唇，低声道：“或许是我得罪了一人的缘故，秦王才不允许我进城去吧。”
“得罪了谁？这般小心眼？”公子迁不满地皱起眉。
“徐福。”
公子迁面色微变，轻叹了一口气，“若是当真不允你进城，你便寻个县城先住下来吧。”
赵嫣点了点头，笑道：“这样也好，至少我们同在秦国。”
公子迁也不知想到了什么，突然悲从中来，不由得垂下了头。
另一头的咸阳宫中，徐福惊讶地听宫人说着外面的消息。
原来那赵嫣与公子迁还是一母同胞的兄妹啊！公子迁要来秦国为质，还带买一送一打包带走的啊！徐福觉得自己的见识又增长了呢。

chapters.translated_text:
Ying Zheng turned to the attendant following closely behind him and said, "The map."

The attendant held it up with both hands, placed it steadily in front of Xu Fu, and then slowly spread it out. Xu Fu was surprised to find that this appeared to be a map of another country. After all, he did not see any markings for the commanderies and counties of the Qin State on it.

Ying Zheng pointed to a certain spot and asked, "Do you know what place this is?"

Fusu and Huhai, who were standing to the side, leaned in to take a look.

Xu Fu examined it carefully for a moment, feeling somewhat surprised. "...Is this Ye City?" It was marked with the character "鄴" (Ye), and nearby were the characters for Handan. This was a map of the Zhao State.

Ying Zheng was showing him such a map; what else could it be but good news? Xu Fu understood almost instantly.

"Has there been a new battle report?" Xu Fu raised his eyebrows faintly.

Ying Zheng nodded, a clear look of joy on his face. "Huan Yi and Li Xin split their forces into two routes. One went straight toward Handan and attacked Ye City, while the other invaded Taiyuan and captured Langmeng." He paused, his smile turning somewhat cold. "The King of Zhao is terrified and has decided to send Prince Qian to Qin as a hostage."

Xu Fu could see mockery and satisfaction in Ying Zheng's eyes.

Back then, when the Qin State sent an unfavored prince to Zhao as a hostage, Ying Zheng had suffered a great deal in Zhao. How could Ying Zheng easily forget such deep-seated grievances? If the positions of Zhao and Qin were reversed and the King of Zhao was scrambling to send people to Qin, how could it not feel gratifying?

This was the joy of washing away one's shame!

Fusu said in a low voice, "Father, I have heard that Prince Qian is the next heir to the Zhao throne. Is the King of Zhao truly willing to send him?"

Ying Zheng curled his lips into a smile that was both arrogant and awe-inspiring. "Why wouldn't he be willing? When the country is about to fall, what is a crown prince worth? The King of Zhao hopes to use Prince Qian to appease the anger in my heart. If he sent someone unfavored, how could he show his sincerity?"

Even so, Xu Fu still felt that the King of Zhao was being far too willing. He sent his son away just like that. Perhaps it had to do with the fact that in this era, rulers had many children and thus did not feel much heartache. Xu Fu lit a candle for that Prince Qian in his heart.

Ying Zheng suddenly withdrew the smile from his face and looked at Xu Fu very seriously, asking, "A-Fu, should I accept this hostage?"

Fusu, listening to this conversation between Ying Zheng and Xu Fu from the side, felt his mouth twitch uncontrollably. This... was this truly his father?

Xu Fu met Ying Zheng's gaze and immediately thought of the Princess of Zhao.

"It's fine." Xu Fu could tell that Ying Zheng very much wanted to use this opportunity to trample the face of the Zhao State into the dirt. Previously, Zhao had put on a stance of "rather die than submit" and "I am different from the Han State," yet who knew the King of Zhao would decide to send his son so quickly? An opportunity to trample the King of Zhao's dignity like this—let alone Ying Zheng, even Xu Fu felt it was a rare and excellent chance.

That Ying Zheng would take the initiative to ask for his opinion showed a very good attitude. It was just a hostage; Xu Fu didn't feel the need to take it to heart.

"Then is General Huan Yi returning to the capital now?" Xu Fu asked. After all, both Huan Yi and Li Xin had only just recovered from their illnesses; being tossed about like this for a long time probably wouldn't be good.

Ying Zheng frowned. "This matter is actually a bit troublesome. The King of Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to resist Huan Yi and Li Xin respectively. If it weren't for the King of Zhao not trusting those two, Huan Yi and Li Xin might not have succeeded. Now the King of Zhao wants to recall Li Mu and Sima Shang, but those two refuse to obey, determined to fight the Qin army to the end... Now it depends on whether the King of Zhao can suppress them."

"Given the current level of the King of Zhao's muddleheadedness, I fear it won't be long..." Xu Fu speculated.

"That will depend on Yao Jia's ability." Ying Zheng said faintly, closing the map and handing it to the attendant nearby. The attendant held it carefully and left.

"Has Yao Jia gone to Handan again?" Xu Fu hadn't expected him to act so quickly, and he didn't know if he had taken Han Fei with him. Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng's expression and always felt that Ying Zheng's attitude was a bit strange when mentioning Yao Jia.

"Hmm, what is it that you had Yao Jia do?" Ying Zheng asked casually.

"If there is any progress, I will naturally tell you." This kind of strange matter was really hard to explain, so he truly couldn't just rashly tell Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng felt a bit unhappy, but it was well suppressed.

It could be said that Xu Fu had almost no secrets hidden from him. Xu Fu had never intended to hide anything from him, nor was there anything worth hiding, so the level of trust between the two was relatively high. The last time, because the ministers were making a mess and trying to get Ying Zheng to marry a princess, he had hidden it from Xu Fu once, and it had almost led to disaster.

Now, seeing that Xu Fu was unwilling to speak, Ying Zheng finally tasted that same feeling.

Out of different psychologies but the same tacit understanding, the two let the matter pass.

To celebrate Xu Fu being enfeoffed as a Siche Shuzhang, the four of them had a delicious meal like an ordinary family. After the meal, they had a rare family-style chat, rambling about this and that, creating a warm atmosphere.

It was just that Xu Fu found it hard to complain.

"A-Zheng, then you can enfeoff me with another title to celebrate this." The one giving the reward was Ying Zheng, and after giving it, he could still act as if it were a huge surprise and celebrate with Xu Fu, as if the person who had given the reward wasn't him at all.

Upon hearing this, Ying Zheng agreed very readily, "Fine, whatever you want, I will give it to you."

Fusu silently plugged his ears.

Ying Zheng had agreed too readily, and Xu Fu instead felt it had lost its fun, so he cast the remark aside in the blink of an eye.

For the next few days, Xu Fu lazily stayed in his sleeping quarters to rest, listening to the palace servants talk about the rumors related to him outside. The servants spoke so vividly, as if Xu Fu had truly transformed into an immortal.

At this moment, an attendant stepped through the door and called out in a low voice, "Sir. No... Shuzhang." The man hurriedly corrected himself, his voice filled with slight nervousness.

Xu Fu turned his head to look.

It was indeed Zhao Cheng.

He had already briefly mentioned Zhao Cheng's situation to Ying Zheng, and Zhao Cheng had been arranged to be by his side, but it was only today, after training, that he officially came to work. Xu Fu didn't expect Zhao Cheng to do anything; after all, there were many servants in the sleeping quarters, and there were more than enough people he could order around. Putting Zhao Cheng by his side now was mostly to repay a favor.

"Whatever arrangements are made for you, just listen to him." Xu Fu deliberately softened his voice, which was very rare for someone as cold and aloof as him. The other servants curiously glanced at Zhao Cheng, secretly estimating the status of this newcomer in their hearts.

This was something Xu Fu did deliberately. In this way, even if Zhao Cheng didn't necessarily enjoy any special privileges, these servants would certainly not ostracize him. The path had been paved; it shouldn't be difficult for Zhao Cheng to live well in the future. If it weren't for the fact that Zhao Cheng's background hadn't been fully investigated, Ying Zheng would have already promoted him to a higher position for his sake.

Zhao Cheng said with a sense of eagerness, "From now on, will this servant be able to attend to the Shuzhang's meals and daily life?"

Someone nearby laughed and said, "The people who attend to meals and daily life are separate. If you want to serve, you can only choose one."

Zhao Cheng smiled awkwardly and said, "Then, then this servant will attend to the Shuzhang when he rises in the morning."

That person then nodded and said, "That's more like it."

Xu Fu thought for a moment and still said to Zhao Cheng, "It will be hard work for you from now on."

"No, it's not hard work." Zhao Cheng smiled shyly.

Others saw this and kept it in their hearts, secretly thinking that the Shuzhang truly treated him differently, and they must be careful not to offend him in the future.

Zhao Cheng was soon taken away to be settled. Xu Fu's gaze swept over the faces of the other servants one by one. After Ying Zheng returned to the sleeping quarters, Xu Fu spoke to him, "Zhao Cheng once saved me, so I must treat him with courtesy. But your sleeping quarters are not an ordinary place after all. I treated him gently in front of everyone to ensure they wouldn't ostracize him later, but I am worried that some might misunderstand and indulge Zhao Cheng in the future, and it would be bad if he committed some mistake."

Ying Zheng immediately understood what Xu Fu meant. Xu Fu wanted him to play the "bad cop," to give the palace servants another warning and tell them that there were certain things that absolutely could not be indulged.

Ying Zheng suddenly realized that from such a small action by Xu Fu, could he interpret it as Xu Fu being worried about him and considering him in everything? Ying Zheng's mood suddenly became pleasant.

Seeing the inexplicable smile on Ying Zheng's face, Xu Fu assumed it was because the King of Zhao was sending a hostage. Xu Fu lazily yawned, buried his head in Ying Zheng's chest, and fell asleep with such natural movements, completely unaware of how dependent he looked on Ying Zheng.

Winter of the 15th year of King Zheng of Qin.

Before the Wax Sacrifice, just as Xu Fu was pondering whether to make up for Ying Zheng's birthday, the envoys from the Zhao State arrived in Xianyang once again, only this time, Prince Qian was among their party.

That day, the Zhao envoys were unable to enter the city.

The reason was that when the people at the city gate heard that the Princess of Zhao had come along again, they dared not let anyone in casually, not even if they were envoys from Zhao. They turned around and reported it to the King first. They would wait for the King's word before doing anything else.

Although the Zhao envoys felt that the Qin State was bullying them too much, they also knew that they were now at the mercy of others and had no qualifications to be tough, so they had to swallow their bitterness and stay outside the city.

This was the first time the Zhao envoys had enjoyed such treatment.

At this time, the Princess of Zhao and Prince Qian were sitting in a carriage, talking about matters in the Qin palace.

Zhao Yan bit her lip and said in a low voice, "Perhaps it is because I offended someone that the King of Qin does not allow me to enter the city."

"Offended whom? Such a petty person?" Prince Qian frowned in dissatisfaction.

"Xu Fu."

Prince Qian's expression changed slightly, and he sighed softly, "If he truly does not allow you to enter the city, find a county town and stay there for now."

Zhao Yan nodded and smiled, "That is fine too, at least we are both in the Qin State."

Prince Qian didn't know what he was thinking, but suddenly a sense of sorrow welled up, and he couldn't help but lower his head.

On the other side, in the Xianyang Palace, Xu Fu was surprised to hear the news from the palace servants.

So that Zhao Yan and Prince Qian were actually siblings born of the same mother! Prince Qian was coming to Qin as a hostage, and he even brought a "buy one get one free" package deal! Xu Fu felt that his knowledge had grown once again.

chapters.source_text:
这时，突然响起了摔杯盏的声音。
徐福心中一惊，秦始皇这是要和吕不韦掐起来了？但随即徐福又觉得不对。
那时的杯盏大多是青铜酒器，摔落地面，声音沉闷无比，却足够惊醒一个熟睡中的人。
所以……这个声音其实是秦始皇在提醒他？免得他突然醒来后，轻举妄动，与吕不韦起了冲突？徐福心中稍定，顿时在小榻上躺得更安心了。他只需要偷听就行了。秦始皇又不是纸糊的，要对付吕不韦应该是绰绰有余的。
“吕相说得不错，这长信侯着实可恶！可……”嬴政先是虚张声势一番的怒吼，随即又音量一降，道：“可，可这长信侯也是吕相当初送予母后做个侍卫的，他虽然可恶，可寡人这个做儿子的，又怎么能随意处置母后身边的人呢？”
躲在围屏后的徐福都不得不感叹嬴政的演技。
这一番话，先是附和吕不韦，给吕不韦传达出一个，他还是听从吕不韦的信息；随后又话锋一转，表示他不能出手对付嫪毐，碍于太后的面子，必然又给吕不韦传达一个，他遇事退缩，并未将嫪毐势力放在眼中的信息。两个错误的信息绝对会在无形中，误导吕不韦对秦始皇的认知，麻痹吕不韦的头脑，让他完全猜不到秦始皇早已对他们起了戒心。
“王上将这话与太后提一提不就是了？”吕不韦的声音已经褪去了严厉，陡然温和了不少。
看来他是放弃了将秦始皇推出去替他出头，除掉嫪毐的打算了。
徐福猜测，吕不韦此刻的心情一定是复杂的，一面他对秦始皇的表现觉得心安不少，但一面他让秦始皇和赵太后、嫪毐先斗起来的计划也没办法用了。
秦始皇这一手，简直是让吕不韦吃了个憋屈，还暗自高兴呢。
“母后前些日子刚因身体不适去了雍城，寡人又怎能为这等事去打扰她呢？”嬴政表现得很是孝顺恭谨。
昔日幼年的公子政与母亲赵姬在赵国做人质，相依为命。于是如今嬴政表现得依赖赵太后，敬畏赵太后，并没有一丝违和的地方。
徐福暗自嘀咕，别说一直被秦始皇蒙着的吕不韦了，就是他乍一听秦始皇这样说，都会忍不住去相信他的话。搞不好秦始皇也能拿个忽悠六级证书什么的……
“此等小人企图扰乱朝纲，王上却还要忍受如此委屈。”吕不韦叹了一口气，装作很为嬴政着想的样子，“不如……王上在朝上提一提……”
要知道秦国除了吕不韦、赵太后和嫪毐这三个霍乱朝纲的以外，也是有着忠实的保皇派的。
比如蒙家。从祖父蒙骜到年轻一代的蒙恬、蒙毅。都是秦国名将，而且十分忠于秦王。
吕不韦无非就是想借这个手。
徐福听得越发来了兴趣，秦始皇要怎么回绝呢？
正想着呢，就听见嬴政的声音轻叹一声，道：“吕相想必是忘了，寡人还未加冠，尚不能亲政呢。不过……”嬴政拔高声音，郑重道：“既是吕相所求，没有几日寡人便要加冠了，待到那时吕相便可放心。”
去你的加冠！等到加冠之时，说不定你就被搞死了！
吕不韦被堵得一句话都说不出来，喉咙里就跟哽了一口血，吞也不能，吐也不能一样。
嬴政未加冠不能亲政，这个理由可是被他和赵太后联手玩起来，糊弄了嬴政好多次，现在却是被还给他了，偏偏吕不韦什么也不能说。他这出算计还在嬴政的口中变成了是吕不韦在求他。
徐福在围屏后都忍不住快笑出声来了。
可惜他看不见吕不韦此刻的表情。那肯定是相当好看的！
“……那，那便等加冠时再说吧。”吕不韦下的套子，嬴政一个也不钻，吕不韦也不能强硬要求嬴政做什么。吕不韦心气不顺，硬邦邦地说了声“告退”，便甩袖离去了。
徐福听着脚步声慢慢走远，然后又捱了一会儿才慢慢从小榻上爬起来。
秦始皇和吕不韦说的都是机密之事，如果被吕不韦刚发现躲在后面，说不定他就要丢小命了。
不过话说回来，秦始皇为什么这么放心地让他听到这些事呢？
徐福从围屏后缓步踏出去，就见嬴政坐在桌案前，面色冷凝，随手摆弄着一旁的竹简。
徐福能看出，秦始皇此刻的心情肯定好不到哪里去。后世为无数人膜拜敬服的始皇帝，在如今却还要步步为营，隐忍蓄力，以求一击必中，将吕不韦和嫪毐除去。
赵高指挥着宫人收拾殿内凌乱的地方，随后还有宫女送了新的茶水上前来。
徐福站在那里觉得有点尴尬，他此刻不能贸然开口，没有秦始皇发话，也不能坐下，于是就只能站在那里，继续伪装自己的淡定从容。许久之后，他才听见嬴政的声音突然响起，“你认为吕相如何？”
嗯？问谁？
徐福用余光将殿内扫了一圈，其他人都恭敬地低着头。
所以这句话是……问他？
这种问题竟然还问他？！答错了会被车裂吗？会被挂桅杆上烤成人干吗？会被剁成赵公公吗？
徐福暗自咽了咽口水，继续发挥自己的神棍技能，张嘴就来，“王上既然要我说，那我便说实话，王上可不要怪罪于我。”说完他也不等嬴政开口，顿了顿便继续往下说：“此前，我也曾听闻过吕相的大名。”
“继续。”嬴政淡淡地吐出两个字，偏偏就是让人莫名地感觉到压迫，仿佛下一刻要是说错了话，就很可能要去见阎王了。
徐福胆子之肥，从他敢出于职业道德，对人直言不讳便可见。当初他敢说秦始皇绿云罩顶，现在他便敢说吕不韦之过。
“吕不韦是个商人，他具有商人的头脑，很懂得为自己谋利。吕不韦最大的成就，便是曾在邯郸街头遇秦庄襄王，言‘此奇货可居也’……”
还没等徐福说完，赵高突然站直了身子，高喊了一声，“大胆！”
赵高也是被徐福这串话给吓得神魂都飞了。
因为在赵国的遭遇，哪怕嬴政回到秦国，也常有人说他并非王室血脉，而是吕不韦和赵姬偷情所生。“奇货可居”四字自然会令人联想到当年的耻辱，那岂不是如同揭开堂堂秦王的伤疤。
这如何了得？
徐福站在那里，动也不动，明明身量不及秦人，但也顿生巍然之感。
徐福在赌，在他看来，秦始皇并非残暴之人，他也并不小心眼儿，不然的话，历史上六国前来投奔的门客早被他剁碎了。
一时间，室内一片寂静，宫人们连喘气也不敢了。
嬴政推开手中的竹简，转头瞥向徐福……
赵高的心顿时提到了嗓子眼儿。
完了完了……
chapters.translated_text:
At that moment, the sound of a cup smashing suddenly rang out.

Xu Fu felt a start. Was Ying Zheng about to come to blows with Lü Buwei? But immediately, Xu Fu realized something was amiss.

Cups and vessels back then were mostly bronze wine ware. When dropped onto the ground, the sound was extremely dull, yet loud enough to wake a sleeping person.

So... was this sound actually Ying Zheng's way of reminding him? To prevent him from suddenly waking up, acting rashly, and coming into conflict with Lü Buwei? Xu Fu's heart settled slightly, and he immediately lay back down on the small couch with greater peace of mind. All he needed to do was eavesdrop. Ying Zheng wasn't made of paper; dealing with Lü Buwei should be more than enough for him.

"Lord Lü speaks correctly; this Marquis of Changxin is indeed atrocious! But..." Ying Zheng first gave a blustering, angry roar, then abruptly lowered his volume and said, "But, but this Marquis of Changxin was also originally given to the Queen Mother by Lord Lü to serve as a guard. Though he is atrocious, how can I, as a son, casually dispose of someone close to the Queen Mother?"

Hiding behind the folding screen, even Xu Fu couldn't help but marvel at Ying Zheng's acting skills.

This speech first agreed with Lü Buwei, conveying the message that he still obeyed Lü Buwei. Then, the tone suddenly shifted, expressing that he could not take action against Lao Ai due to the Queen Mother's face. This undoubtedly conveyed another message to Lü Buwei: that he shrank from trouble and did not take Lao Ai's faction seriously at all. These two pieces of false information would definitely imperceptibly mislead Lü Buwei's perception of Ying Zheng, dulling Lü Buwei's mind so that he would never guess that Ying Zheng had long been on his guard against them.

"Can Your Majesty not simply mention this matter to the Queen Mother?" Lü Buwei's voice had lost its severity and suddenly become much gentler.

It seemed he had abandoned the plan of pushing Ying Zheng out to fight his battles and eliminate Lao Ai.

Xu Fu guessed that Lü Buwei's feelings at the moment must be complicated. On one hand, he felt quite reassured by Ying Zheng's performance, but on the other hand, his plan to make Ying Zheng, Queen Mother Zhao, and Lao Ai fight each other first was no longer viable.

Ying Zheng's move had essentially made Lü Buwei swallow his frustration while secretly feeling pleased about it.

"The Queen Mother went to Yongcheng a few days ago precisely because of poor health. How could I disturb her over such a matter?" Ying Zheng appeared extremely filial and respectful.

In the past, the young Prince Zheng and his mother, Lady Zhao, had been hostages in Zhao, depending on each other for survival. Thus, Ying Zheng appearing dependent on and in awe of Queen Mother Zhao today didn't have the slightest trace of discordance.

Xu Fu muttered inwardly: never mind Lü Buwei, who was kept in the dark by Ying Zheng, even he, upon hearing Ying Zheng speak this way out of nowhere, couldn't help but be inclined to believe his words. Chances are Ying Zheng could even win some sort of level-six master-deceiver certificate...

"Such a petty villain attempts to disrupt the court, yet Your Majesty must endure such grievance." Lü Buwei sighed, pretending to be very considerate of Ying Zheng. "Why not... Your Majesty bring it up at court..."

One must know that apart from Lü Buwei, Queen Mother Zhao, and Lao Ai—the three who threw the imperial court into chaos—the State of Qin also possessed loyal pro-monarch factions.

For instance, the Meng family. From grandfather Meng Ao to the younger generation of Meng Tian and Meng Yi, they were all renowned generals of Qin and extremely loyal to the King of Qin.

Lü Buwei simply wanted to borrow their hands.

Listening, Xu Fu grew increasingly interested. How would Ying Zheng refuse?

Just as he was thinking this, he heard Ying Zheng's voice let out a light sigh and say, "Lord Lü must have forgotten; I have not yet reached adulthood and am not yet able to personally rule. However..." Ying Zheng raised his voice and said solemnly, "Since it is what Lord Lü requests, in a few days I shall cap. Once that time comes, Lord Lü may rest easy."

To hell with your capping! By the time of the capping ceremony, you might already be plotted against and killed!

Lü Buwei was choked so badly he couldn't say a single word, a mouthful of blood seemingly stuck in his throat—he could neither swallow it nor spit it out.

Ying Zheng had not reached adulthood and could not personally rule—this excuse had been played by him and Queen Mother Zhao together to fool Ying Zheng many times, but now it was being returned to him. Yet Lü Buwei couldn't say a thing. This plot of his had even been turned by Ying Zheng's words into Lü Buwei begging him.

Behind the folding screen, Xu Fu almost laughed out loud.

It was a pity he couldn't see Lü Buwei's expression at that moment. It must have been quite a sight!

"...Then, then let us speak of it when the capping ceremony arrives." Lü Buwei's traps were not walked into by Ying Zheng at all, nor could Lü Buwei make harsh demands on Ying Zheng. Feeling out of sorts, Lü Buwei stiffly uttered a "taking my leave," flicked his sleeves, and departed.

Xu Fu listened as the footsteps slowly faded into the distance, then waited a while longer before slowly climbing up from the small couch.

What Ying Zheng and Lü Buwei had discussed were confidential matters. If Lü Buwei had suddenly discovered him hiding in the back, he might have lost his little life.

But speaking of which, why was Ying Zheng so confident as to let him hear these things?

Xu Fu stepped out slowly from behind the folding screen and saw Ying Zheng sitting before the desk, his expression cold and stern as he casually fiddled with the bamboo slips beside him.

Xu Fu could tell that Ying Zheng's mood right now definitely couldn't be good. The First Emperor, adored and revered by countless people in later generations, currently still had to tread carefully every step of the way, enduring and accumulating strength in order to strike with a single, decisive blow to eliminate Lü Buwei and Lao Ai.

Zhao Gao directed the palace attendants to tidy up the messy parts of the hall, after which palace maids brought in fresh tea.

Standing there, Xu Fu felt a bit awkward. He couldn't speak rashly right now, and without Ying Zheng's permission, he couldn't sit down either, so he could only stand there and continue pretending to be calm and composed. Long afterwards, he heard Ying Zheng's voice suddenly ring out, "What do you think of Lord Lü?"

Huh? Asking whom?

Xu Fu swept the hall with his peripheral vision; everyone else was respectfully keeping their heads lowered.

So this sentence was... asking him?

Such a question was actually being asked of him?! Would he be torn apart by chariots if he answered wrong? Would he be hung from a mast and roasted into jerky? Would he be chopped up like Eunuch Zhao?

Xu Fu secretly swallowed his saliva, continuing to play his role as a charlatan as he opened his mouth and blurted out, "Since Your Majesty wants me to speak, then I will speak the truth; Your Majesty must not blame me." Without even waiting for Ying Zheng to speak, he paused and continued, "Previously, I also heard of Lord Lü's great name."

"Continue." Ying Zheng spat out two flat words, which inexplicably carried a heavy sense of oppression, as if saying the wrong thing the next moment might send one straight to the King of Hell.

How daring Xu Fu was could be seen from the fact that he dared to speak bluntly to people out of professional ethics. Back then, he dared to tell the King of Qin that his head was crowned with green; now he dared to speak of Lü Buwei's faults.

"Lü Buwei is a merchant; he possesses a merchant's mind and knows very well how to scheme for his own benefit. Lü Buwei's greatest achievement was meeting King Zhuangxiang of Qin on the streets of Handan and saying, 'This is a rare commodity worth hoarding'..."

Before Xu Fu could finish, Zhao Gao suddenly straightened his body and shouted loudly, "Audacious!"

Zhao Gao had nearly been scared out of his wits by Xu Fu's string of words.

Because of the encounters in the State of Zhao, even after returning to Qin, people often whispered that Ying Zheng was not of royal blood, but rather born from an illicit affair between Lü Buwei and Lady Zhao. The four words "rare commodity worth hoarding" naturally brought to mind that humiliation of the past, as if tearing open the scars of the majestic King of Qin.

How could this be tolerated?

Xu Fu stood there without moving an inch. Although his stature fell short of the Qin people, a towering presence spontaneously arose.

Xu Fu was gambling. In his view, the First Emperor was not a cruel person, nor was he petty; otherwise, the retainers from the six states who came to seek refuge in history would have long since been chopped to pieces.

For a moment, the room was dead silent; the palace attendants didn't even dare to breathe.

Ying Zheng pushed aside the bamboo slips in his hand, turned his head, and glanced at Xu Fu...

Zhao Gao's heart instantly leaped into his throat.

It's over, it's over...
