chapters.source_text:
好歹是赵国公子，小朝上，大臣们建议可以摆个小晚宴来招待一下公子嘉。也有人道，如今是赵国求着秦国，而非秦国求着赵国，何必再礼遇公子嘉？简单收拾一通，给人安排个住处就是了。说着话的是尉缭。哦，没错，他就是不待见赵国，不待见赵国送来的王女公子。
嬴政就看着他们在下面瞎扯一气，最后什么话也没说便散朝了。
公子嘉来秦，还不值得他嬴政如何上心。
当日公子嘉便先被安置在了驿馆中，连面见秦王的机会都还没有。
使臣心中多有不满，但是想到当初自己放下了狠话，如今不还是得乖乖来秦跪在秦王的脚边以示臣服？于是一下子便没了脾气。如今的秦国已不是过去的秦国了，这个秦王比起往任秦王更为厉害，他再多抱怨又能怎么样呢？
公子嘉倒是心性平和，或许是平日里已经被赵王的宠姬磋磨够了，于是便什么都不惧了。
内侍来驿馆接他进宫时，推门而入便见一翩翩青年，坐在桌案之前，用笔刀在竹简上刻着些什么，见内侍进来，他也并不避讳，分外坦然地起身。内侍扫了一眼他跟前的竹简，确定不会是什么紧要的东西，这才抬起了头。
很快，公子嘉跟随内侍坐着马车到了宫门口。
恰巧此时又有一辆马车过来了。
公子嘉掀起车帘往外看去，却惊讶地发现，拉着马车的有四匹马，可见其地位并不低。
此时驾马车的内侍回过头来对他道：“请公子下马车。”
公子嘉知道王宫里是不能纵马的，更不能大摇大摆坐着马车进去。他二话不说便与侍从一起走了下去。就在他走下去的时候，便眼睁睁地看着那马车在宫门口只稍作停顿，随后就进了宫门。公子嘉心中惊讶不已。
内侍注意到他惊异的目光，笑道：“那是驷车庶长的车驾，宫中唯有他的马车能来去自如。”
公子嘉更为好奇了，他在来秦国的路上，可未曾听说秦国多了一位驷车庶长，不由问道：“敢问驷车庶长是？”
那内侍却不再言，只道：“公子日后便知了。”说完，他就在前面引路，将公子嘉带了进去。
……
那坐在马车里的人的确是徐福。
蒙恬也算是为救他而受伤，如今蒙恬的伤还未完全好起来，徐福自然是有空便要上门拜访一番。只是今日他先到国尉府上去见了尉缭，然后便带着尉缭一起过去了。
因为想着今日赵国公子应当要进宫了，徐福心中好奇，在见过蒙恬后不久就先坐着马车回宫来了。
徐福不得不感叹，升了爵位之后的确不同了。
四匹马拉车，气派立时就涨了起来。
不过徐福并不大习惯这样的排场，以后出宫需要低调时，还是得坐小马车。
很快马车停在了宫殿外，徐福走了下去，赵成从后面跟了上来，低声道：“方才公子嘉跟在后面进宫来了。”
公子嘉在后面？
徐福回头看了一眼，却什么也没看见。
赵成见状，马上解释道：“公子嘉应当是步行前来的。”
徐福这才想起，能坐着马车肆无忌惮的，貌似也就自己独一份儿了。虽然嘴上不说，但徐福自己也能感觉得到心底的愉悦。好吧，这样的唯一，的确能取悦到他。
尽管尉缭在小朝上鄙视了赵国，但嬴政还是举办了这个晚宴。只是徐福很清楚，这个晚宴可根本不是为了欢迎公子嘉，若说是羞辱还差不多。当初赵国如何待嬴政，今日怕是要原样尝一遍了。
徐福哪怕知道内情，也并不会劝阻嬴政。
冤有头债有主，当初赵国那样嚣张，就总得有个被人报复回来的觉悟吧？嬴政的童年和年少时期都是不愉快的，现在他要将那些不快都宣泄出去，有何不可？
一切心上的负累都被发泄出去之后，嬴政只会越发地成熟，手段越发地厉害，离秦始皇的位置越发地近。
徐福也承认，他心底也有那些护短的心思。在他瞧来，赵国如今的境地便当真是活该了。
只可怜了公子嘉而已。
想着想着徐福便走进了殿中，此时嬴政还在处理手头的政务，见徐福进来，他才搁下了竹简。
“如何了？”嬴政头也不抬地问道。
“蒙将军的伤还没好，不过我留师兄给他上药了。”
嬴政忍不住笑出了声来，“你将尉缭留在那里了？”也不知明日蒙恬可还有性命来上朝。
徐福点了点头。在他看来，尉缭和蒙恬之间的矛盾，是完全可以调和的，因而并未往严重的方向去想。
“有什么不对吗？”徐福反问。
“不，并无不对。”尉缭给他找过那么多麻烦，嬴政哪里还会好心去提醒徐福？
“几时了？”嬴政转头问内侍。
“王上，酉时三刻了。”
嬴政将徐福招到身边来，让他在自己身旁坐下，道：“陪寡人到戌时，我们便到那边大殿去。”
“嗯。”徐福应了一声，还顺便自己调整了一下坐姿，力求舒适。
这头徐福和嬴政倒是优哉游哉，舒适极了，另一头公子嘉却是被带到殿中，坐在那里小心翼翼，等上了许久也不见秦王，顿时心中忐忑不已。而秦国官员陆续落座，并无一人有要搭理他的意思。赵国使臣扬起笑脸与秦国官员搭话，但都是说不了几句话便没音了。
那使臣越发心焦，回转身来与公子嘉道：“秦国怕是要故意冷待我们了。”
公子嘉淡然点头，“这有何妨？”公子嘉说完就陷入了自己的沉思之中，不再与那使臣说话。
使臣心中更加难受了，看着公子嘉的方向忍不住叹气。一个被抛弃了的公子，自己跟随而来，还有未来和前途可言吗？
秦王未来，大殿中的气氛便凝滞得很，不久后有一男子走了进来，公子嘉见不少人都上前与他说话，可见其地位。使臣在旁边忙解说道：“那是秦国国尉尉缭。”
从前公子嘉便听说过此人，他轻叹一口气，道：“这等人才，也被秦国揽过来了，赵国如今无人，怎会不败呢？怎会不败呢？”
使臣听他语气凄苦，心中一颤，说不出话来。
从前只一味想着赵国乃是大国，如今被公子点破才惊觉赵国竟是人才凋零了。相比之下，秦国却是揽得多方大才。不说别的，就说那这段时间传得极为热闹的徐福……就连其它六国之中，也多有百姓视他为神仙的。
有这样的人在身旁做助力，秦王的实力实在不容小觑啊。
这时又听一阵轰动声，使臣忙抬起头来，只见年轻英武的秦王，佩着象征权利的长剑进来了，他面容冷酷。
公子嘉望着他的方向，心中一动。用只有他自己能听见的声音，喃喃道，和过去不一样了……
和他记忆中不一样了。
公子嘉的瞳孔猛地一缩，他发现秦王身旁还站了一个人，穿着普普通通的平民才爱穿的白袍，但他的容貌可一点却不普通。公子嘉也想起了那个传言。说是秦国的徐福，喜穿白。想来天上神仙便是喜好纯白之色的。一段时间里，那些穿白袍的平民，甚至还因此而欣喜。
徐福从踏入殿中后，便发觉有一道目光朝自己这边扫了过来，不过等了一会儿之后，徐福就发现，那道目光看的是嬴政，而并非自己。他朝那个方向看了过去，便见一个穿着黑袍的年轻男子，容貌俊逸，气质温和，给人以青涩和沉稳相糅杂的怪异感。
他就是公子嘉？
徐福跟着嬴政一同往里走去。
秦国的官员们统统起身，口呼“王上”。
哪怕是看着徐福和嬴政一同走到台阶上，一上一下落座，秦国官员们也没有露出半点惊讶之色。实在是这样的行为他们见得太多了，也就不觉得哪里怪异了，何况徐福如今在秦国的地位本就有些超然，不就坐在王上下首吗？那就是展现一下王上的宠爱嘛，他们没事儿去纠结这个做什么？
但公子嘉就不一样了，他哪里见过这样的规矩礼仪？当即就瞪大了眼。
公子嘉脸上的惊讶之色实在太不遮掩了，使臣顿觉尴尬不已，忙与他解释起来，“公子怕是少有听闻，传闻都说这徐福是秦王的男宠呢。”说完那使臣忙做贼心虚地往两旁看了看，见秦国的宫人并未注意到自己，这才放心了。
秦王霸道狂傲，若是知晓他在秦国的地盘上，议论这样的事，怕是要让他吃个大教训。
公子嘉面上迅速闪过各色情绪，讷讷道：“……这样啊。”
徐福落座以后朝那公子嘉看了好几眼。他觉得这公子嘉的表现实在好玩儿。明明也曾是未来储君，怎么这般情绪外泄呢？
徐福的动作引得嬴政大为吃醋。
那公子嘉生得清俊，算是时下极为受欢迎的长相。嬴政见了后，心中危机感顿生。难道徐福喜欢这般模样的人？等到徐福很快没了兴趣，将头扭转回来，嬴政心中才觉得舒畅多了。
嬴政脑子里甚至又蹦出了一个想法。
早知便应该将那公子嘉也同赵国公主一起，拦在咸阳城外不让进来的。嬴政觉得自己心好累，什么人都不想让徐福看见才好。
宴会很快开始了，舞姬来到殿中，翩翩起舞。
这样的场景徐福已经见过数次了，渐渐也就失去了兴致，旁人都在欣赏舞姬，他却是摊开竹简，更深入地研究起了医理。徐福已经不大记得晚年嬴政是如何死的了，但他觉得，医术这个东西，是万分实用的，有比没用好。
不久之后，公子嘉主动举起手中的酒器，要敬嬴政。
徐福这才分了点目光给对方。
“昔日在赵国与秦王见过数面，再见秦王，秦王如今已是越发的神武了。”公子嘉微笑着说完。
满堂寂静。
那使臣都不自觉地咽了咽口水，隐隐知道公子说错了什么，但是却半晌又想不到，究竟是哪里出错了。
徐福闻言，顿觉好笑。这公子嘉是当真天真愚蠢呢，还是他故意说出这样的话来刺激嬴政呢？
昔日在赵国与秦王见过数面。
这不是明晃晃地提醒嬴政记起那段不快的回忆吗？
公子嘉怎么会如此蠢笨？他想找死也太快了些吧。
嬴政手中捏着酒器，目光森然地看着他，半点要和他说话的意思都没有。那舞姬倒是没有停下舞步，但是其他人却都不说了，这样诡异的境地似乎终于让公子嘉意识到不对了。
公子嘉慌乱地先抬头一饮而尽，他喝的动作有些急，酒水将他狠狠呛了一下，等他放下酒器后，徐福便见他白皙的脸庞泛起了一层红，想来刚才被呛得狠了。他的面上便如同点了胭脂般，原本并不显格外出色的容貌，陡然间就变得艳色了起来。
徐福总觉得心中有些怪异，他忽然想到了一个可能性。
这公子嘉应当不会是赵王派来勾搭嬴政的吧？
毕竟曾是未来储君，赵王当真会这样要求他吗？但是转念一想，如果六国都知晓嬴政独宠自己一人，后宫形同虚设。一个储君算得了什么？若是亡国了，那便什么都没有了，只要赵王狠狠心，说不定便真的能将儿子送来。而且，这公子嘉还恰巧是与幼时嬴政认识的。
徐福越想便越觉得是这么回事。
而嬴政注意到徐福的目光黏在对方身上，收也收不回来的时候，差点把手中的酒器给砸了。
嬴政心中妒火燃烧，他看了一眼那公子嘉。
是有几分姿色，那又如何？
能比寡人好吗！
这头徐福也想到了同样的问题。
公子嘉……能比他优秀吗？能比他更好吗？
公子嘉顿时感觉到投射到自己身上的两道目光都冷了冷，公子嘉忍不住打了个寒颤，心中暗道，难怪赵嫣那般聪慧，来秦以后也是毫无所获便回去了。秦王已经不是过去的赵政了，以他如今的脾气，怕是不能轻易接近的。
公子嘉尴尬地坐了回去，而嬴政那杯酒始终都没喝。
不久之后晚宴结束，嬴政很大方地送了一名舞姬给公子嘉。
哦，当初嬴异人在赵国时，赵王便是将他圈禁起来，但却令他陷在温柔乡中，生生养出那么个性子来。
如今他便也如此待公子嘉好了。
不过嬴政膝下子嗣不多，扶苏和胡亥也是常年在宫中，因而公子嘉并不会像当初嬴政在赵国时那样，任秦国王室贵族的欺负。
公子嘉收到舞姬后，慌乱不已，面上的红晕更为浓重了。
嬴政不愿徐福再去打量公子嘉，便迅速带着徐福离去了。
公子嘉原本憋了许多话，结果一句话都没能说出来，只得黯然地在宫人的引路下，先住在了王宫一个极为偏远寂静的小院子中。
公子嘉的存在感极低，晚宴过后，众人便将他抛到脑后去了，就连徐福都渐渐忘记这个人了。
秦王政十五年，虽然出了地动的大祸，但是大祸很快便过去了。这一年，经历了大喜和大悲，就这样过去了。
徐福在秦国的声望逐年提升，再主持蜡祭时，咸阳城的百姓已经对他狂热万分了。
在快要到秦王政十六年的时候，徐福单独给嬴政补上了生辰。
至于生辰贺礼，徐福便只能委屈委屈自己，将自己包扎起来送上门了。
拐个弯儿就是秦王政十六年了。
扶苏已经有些小少年的模样了，胡亥也开始跟着徐福学巫蛊卜筮了，虽然学习的时候，胡亥实在不比扶苏用心。
在胡亥又一次打着喷嚏，把小布条喷飞的时候。
赵成走了进来，面色尴尬地道：“庶长，有一侍从求见。”
“嗯？谁？”
“赵国公子嘉的侍从。”
徐福这才骤然想起，那个昙花一现就再无音讯的公子嘉。“他怎么了？”
“公子嘉病重……”
“没请侍医？”徐福惊讶了。
赵成无奈道：“公子嘉不能请，也无法请。”
怎么还不能请也无法请了？徐福实在不懂个中就里，只得先拍拍胡亥的头，让他等着，然后起身往外走，“此事应当轮不到我来管吧。”徐福并不想插手这样的事，免得令嬴政误会。
“那侍从求过来了……”赵成也极为无奈。
徐福却摇了摇头，“以后这样的事你只管拦住便是了。”赵成这件事儿做得的确不得他心。
赵成忐忑地点点头，等徐福跨出殿门的时候，他咬了咬唇，忍不住问道：“庶长可是生奴婢的气了？”
徐福无奈，“并无。”
赵成这才眸光闪亮了起来，低声道：“庶长心胸宽厚。”
说话间，徐福就已经走到那侍从跟前去了。
那侍从看上去一副面黄肌瘦的样子，模样实在落魄得很。
徐福这才想起，公子嘉这么久没被过问，就连那赵王也从未关心过自己被送到秦国去的儿子，难免公子嘉和他的侍从受到苛待。
徐福心中也有些复杂。他皱了皱眉。
按理来说，赵国确实该还这笔债。但当初欺侮过秦国的人，却并非公子嘉。
这公子嘉到底是救，还是不救呢？
chapters.translated_text:
He was, after all, a prince of Zhao. During the minor court session, the ministers suggested holding a small banquet to entertain Prince Jia. Others argued that since it was Zhao begging Qin, not the other way around, there was no need to treat Prince Jia with such courtesy; they should just tidy up a bit and assign him a place to stay. The one speaking was Wei Liao. Oh, right, he simply didn't like Zhao, nor did he like the princesses or princes sent over by Zhao.

Ying Zheng watched them chatter away below, and in the end, he dismissed the court without saying a word.

Prince Jia’s arrival in Qin was not worth Ying Zheng’s attention.

That same day, Prince Jia was settled into the guesthouse, without even having had the chance to meet the King of Qin.

The envoy was filled with dissatisfaction, but thinking back to the harsh words he had once uttered, he realized he still had to obediently come to Qin and kneel at the feet of the Qin King to show submission. His temper vanished instantly. The Qin of today was no longer the Qin of the past, and this King of Qin was far more formidable than his predecessors. What could he do even if he complained more?

Prince Jia, however, had a peaceful temperament, perhaps because he had been worn down enough by the favorite concubines of the King of Zhao, so he feared nothing anymore.

When the attendant came to the guesthouse to take him to the palace, he pushed the door open and saw a graceful young man sitting at a desk, carving something onto bamboo slips with a stylus. Seeing the attendant enter, he did not shy away and stood up with great composure. The attendant glanced at the bamboo slips before him, confirmed they were nothing important, and only then raised his head.

Soon, Prince Jia followed the attendant and arrived at the palace gate by carriage.

Just then, another carriage happened to arrive.

Prince Jia lifted the carriage curtain to look out, only to be surprised to find that the carriage was pulled by four horses, indicating that its occupant’s status was not low.

At this moment, the attendant driving the carriage turned back to him and said, "Please disembark, Prince."

Prince Jia knew that one could not ride horses within the palace, let alone enter in a carriage with such fanfare. He stepped down with his attendants without a word. Just as he stepped down, he watched with his own eyes as the carriage paused only briefly at the palace gate before entering. Prince Jia was filled with astonishment.

The attendant noticed his surprised gaze and smiled, "That is the carriage of the Siche Shuzhang; in the palace, only his carriage can come and go as it pleases."

Prince Jia became even more curious. On his way to Qin, he had never heard that Qin had an additional Siche Shuzhang, so he couldn't help but ask, "May I ask who the Siche Shuzhang is?"

The attendant, however, said no more, only replying, "The Prince will know in the future." After saying this, he led the way and brought Prince Jia inside.

...

The person sitting in that carriage was indeed Xu Fu.

Meng Tian had been injured while saving him, and now that Meng Tian’s wounds had not yet fully healed, Xu Fu naturally visited him whenever he had time. It was just that today, he had first gone to the Office of the Grand尉 (Guowei) to see Wei Liao, and then brought Wei Liao along with him.

Because he thought the Prince of Zhao would be entering the palace today, Xu Fu was curious, and shortly after seeing Meng Tian, he returned to the palace by carriage.

Xu Fu had to sigh; it was indeed different after being promoted in rank.

Being pulled by four horses, the prestige immediately increased.

However, Xu Fu was not used to such ostentation; when he needed to be low-key in the future, he would still have to take a smaller carriage.

Soon the carriage stopped outside the palace, and Xu Fu stepped down. Zhao Cheng followed from behind and whispered, "Prince Jia just followed us into the palace."

Prince Jia was behind?

Xu Fu looked back, but saw nothing.

Seeing this, Zhao Cheng immediately explained, "Prince Jia must have come on foot."

Only then did Xu Fu remember that he seemed to be the only one who could ride a carriage so brazenly. Although he didn't say it, Xu Fu could feel the pleasure in his heart. Well, such uniqueness did indeed please him.

Although Wei Liao had looked down on Zhao during the minor court session, Ying Zheng still held this banquet. But Xu Fu knew very well that this banquet was not at all meant to welcome Prince Jia; it was more like a humiliation. How Zhao had treated Ying Zheng in the past, they would likely taste the same treatment today.

Even knowing the inside story, Xu Fu would not try to dissuade Ying Zheng.

Every grievance has its source, and every debt has its debtor. Since Zhao was so arrogant back then, they should have been prepared to be retaliated against, right? Ying Zheng’s childhood and youth were unpleasant, and now that he wanted to vent those unpleasantries, why not?

After all the burdens on his heart were vented, Ying Zheng would only become more mature, his methods more formidable, and he would be closer to the position of the First Emperor of Qin.

Xu Fu also admitted that he had a protective streak in his heart. In his view, the current state of Zhao was truly deserved.

It was only a pity for Prince Jia.

Thinking this, Xu Fu walked into the hall. Ying Zheng was still dealing with official business, and seeing Xu Fu enter, he put down the bamboo slips.

"How is it?" Ying Zheng asked without looking up.

"General Meng’s wounds haven't healed yet, but I left my senior brother there to apply medicine for him."

Ying Zheng couldn't help but laugh out loud, "You left Wei Liao there?" He wondered if Meng Tian would still have the life to attend court tomorrow.

Xu Fu nodded. In his view, the conflict between Wei Liao and Meng Tian was perfectly reconcilable, so he didn't think in a serious direction.

"Is there something wrong?" Xu Fu asked in return.

"No, there is nothing wrong." Wei Liao had caused him so much trouble; how could Ying Zheng be kind enough to warn Xu Fu?

"What time is it?" Ying Zheng turned to ask the attendant.

"Your Majesty, it is the third quarter of the You hour (5:45 PM)."

Ying Zheng beckoned Xu Fu to his side, let him sit beside him, and said, "Accompany me until the Xu hour (7:00 PM), and then we will go to the main hall."

"Mm." Xu Fu responded, and even adjusted his sitting posture for comfort.

While Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were leisurely and comfortable, Prince Jia was brought into the hall, sitting there cautiously. After waiting for a long time without seeing the King of Qin, he felt uneasy. The Qin officials took their seats one after another, and none of them had any intention of paying him any mind. The Zhao envoy raised a smiling face to talk to the Qin officials, but the conversations would die out after only a few sentences.

The envoy became increasingly anxious, turned around, and said to Prince Jia, "It seems Qin intends to deliberately slight us."

Prince Jia nodded indifferently, "What does that matter?" After saying this, Prince Jia fell into his own thoughts and stopped talking to the envoy.

The envoy felt even more miserable, and looking at Prince Jia, he couldn't help but sigh. A discarded prince—following him here, was there any future or prospect to speak of?

With the King of Qin not yet arrived, the atmosphere in the hall was stagnant. Soon after, a man walked in. Prince Jia saw many people go up to speak with him, showing his status. The envoy hurriedly explained from the side, "That is the Qin Guowei, Wei Liao."

Prince Jia had heard of this man before. He sighed softly and said, "Such talent has also been recruited by Qin. With Zhao having no one left, how could it not be defeated? How could it not be defeated?"

Hearing his bitter tone, the envoy felt a tremor in his heart and couldn't speak.

He had only blindly thought that Zhao was a great power, but now, pointed out by the Prince, he suddenly realized that Zhao was indeed devoid of talent. By comparison, Qin had recruited many great talents from all over. Not to mention anything else, just that Xu Fu, who had been the talk of the town recently... even among the other six states, many commoners regarded him as an immortal.

With such a person as an assistant, the strength of the King of Qin was truly not to be underestimated.

Just then, there was another commotion. The envoy hurriedly looked up and saw the young and heroic King of Qin, wearing the long sword that symbolized power, enter. His expression was cold.

Prince Jia looked in his direction, his heart stirred. In a voice only he could hear, he murmured, "It’s different from the past..."

It was different from his memory.

Prince Jia’s pupils shrank sharply. He discovered that there was another person standing beside the King of Qin, wearing the plain white robes that only commoners loved to wear, but his appearance was not ordinary at all. Prince Jia also recalled that rumor. It was said that Xu Fu of Qin liked to wear white. It stood to reason that the immortals in heaven would favor the color of pure white. For a time, those commoners who wore white robes were even happy because of this.

From the moment Xu Fu stepped into the hall, he noticed a gaze sweeping toward him. However, after waiting for a while, Xu Fu discovered that the gaze was looking at Ying Zheng, not himself. He looked in that direction and saw a young man in black robes, with a handsome face and a gentle temperament, giving off a strange mix of greenness and steadiness.

Was he Prince Jia?

Xu Fu followed Ying Zheng as they walked inside together.

The Qin officials all stood up and called out, "Your Majesty."

Even seeing Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walk to the steps together and take their seats one after the other, the Qin officials did not show any surprise. They had seen such behavior too many times to find it strange. Besides, Xu Fu’s status in Qin was already somewhat transcendent; wasn't sitting below the King just showing the King’s favor? Why would they bother to dwell on this?

But Prince Jia was different. Where had he ever seen such etiquette? He widened his eyes immediately.

The surprise on Prince Jia’s face was undisguised, and the envoy felt extremely embarrassed, hurriedly explaining to him, "The Prince might have heard little of this; rumors all say that this Xu Fu is the male favorite of the King of Qin." After saying this, the envoy hurriedly looked around with a guilty conscience, and seeing that the Qin attendants hadn't noticed him, he felt relieved.

The King of Qin was overbearing and arrogant; if he knew that someone was discussing such matters on Qin territory, he would likely be taught a harsh lesson.

Various emotions flashed across Prince Jia’s face, and he stammered, "...Is that so."

After taking his seat, Xu Fu looked at Prince Jia several times. He found Prince Jia’s performance truly amusing. Having once been a future crown prince, how could he be so emotionally transparent?

Xu Fu’s actions made Ying Zheng extremely jealous.

Prince Jia was handsome, a look that was very popular at the time. Seeing this, a sense of crisis arose in Ying Zheng’s heart. Did Xu Fu like people who looked like that? It wasn't until Xu Fu lost interest and turned his head back that Ying Zheng felt much more comfortable.

A thought even popped into Ying Zheng’s mind.

If he had known, he should have blocked Prince Jia outside Xianyang City, just like the Princess of Zhao, and not let him in. Ying Zheng felt his heart was very tired; he didn't want Xu Fu to see anyone at all.

The banquet soon began, and the dancers came into the hall to dance gracefully.

Xu Fu had seen such scenes several times and gradually lost interest. While others were admiring the dancers, he unfolded a bamboo slip and studied medical principles more deeply. Xu Fu couldn't quite remember how Ying Zheng died in his later years, but he felt that medical knowledge was extremely practical; having it was better than not having it.

Not long after, Prince Jia took the initiative to raise his wine vessel to toast Ying Zheng.

Only then did Xu Fu spare a glance for the other party.

"I met the King of Qin several times back in Zhao. Seeing the King of Qin again, he has become increasingly heroic," Prince Jia said with a smile.

The hall was silent.

The envoy couldn't help but swallow his saliva, vaguely knowing that the Prince had said something wrong, but for a long time, he couldn't figure out where it had gone wrong.

Hearing this, Xu Fu found it funny. Was this Prince Jia truly innocent and stupid, or was he deliberately saying such things to provoke Ying Zheng?

"I met the King of Qin several times back in Zhao."

Wasn't this a blatant reminder for Ying Zheng to recall those unpleasant memories?

How could Prince Jia be so stupid? If he wanted to seek death, he was doing it too quickly.

Ying Zheng held the wine vessel in his hand, looking at him with a chilling gaze, with no intention of speaking to him at all. The dancers didn't stop their steps, but everyone else stopped talking. This eerie situation finally seemed to make Prince Jia realize something was wrong.

Prince Jia hurriedly raised his head and drank it all in one gulp. He drank a bit too quickly, and the wine choked him severely. After he put down the wine vessel, Xu Fu saw a layer of red flush on his fair face, likely from being choked hard. His face looked as if it had been dabbed with rouge, and his appearance, which was not particularly outstanding, suddenly became vivid.

Xu Fu always felt something was strange in his heart. He suddenly thought of a possibility.

Prince Jia couldn't have been sent by the King of Zhao to seduce Ying Zheng, could he?

After all, he was once a future crown prince; would the King of Zhao really ask him to do such a thing? But on second thought, if the six states all knew that Ying Zheng only favored one person and his harem was in name only, what was a crown prince worth? If the country perished, there would be nothing left. If the King of Zhao was ruthless enough, he might really send his son. Moreover, this Prince Jia happened to have known Ying Zheng in his childhood.

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more he felt this was the case.

And when Ying Zheng noticed Xu Fu’s gaze glued to the other person, unable to pull away, he almost smashed the wine vessel in his hand.

Jealousy burned in Ying Zheng’s heart, and he glanced at Prince Jia.

So he had some looks, so what?

Could he be better than me!

On this side, Xu Fu was thinking about the same question.

Prince Jia... could he be more excellent than him? Could he be better than him?

Prince Jia suddenly felt the two gazes cast upon him turn cold. Prince Jia couldn't help but shiver, thinking to himself, no wonder Zhao Yan was so intelligent, yet returned empty-handed after coming to Qin. The King of Qin was no longer the Zhao Zheng of the past; with his current temper, he was probably not someone who could be easily approached.

Prince Jia sat back down in embarrassment, and Ying Zheng never drank that cup of wine.

Shortly after the banquet ended, Ying Zheng generously gave a dancer to Prince Jia.

Oh, when Ying Yiren was in Zhao, the King of Zhao had imprisoned him but kept him in a den of gentleness, raising him into that kind of personality.

Now, he would treat Prince Jia the same way.

However, Ying Zheng did not have many descendants, and Fusu and Huhai were often in the palace, so Prince Jia would not be bullied by the Qin royal family and nobles like Ying Zheng was in Zhao.

After receiving the dancer, Prince Jia was flustered, and the flush on his face became even deeper.

Ying Zheng did not want Xu Fu to keep studying Prince Jia, so he quickly took Xu Fu away.

Prince Jia had originally held back many words, but in the end, he couldn't say a single one. He could only gloomily follow the palace attendants to stay in a very remote and quiet small courtyard in the palace.

Prince Jia’s presence was extremely low. After the banquet, everyone threw him to the back of their minds, and even Xu Fu gradually forgot about this person.

In the 15th year of King Zheng of Qin, although there was a disaster of an earthquake, the disaster passed quickly. This year, having experienced great joy and great sorrow, just passed like that.

Xu Fu’s reputation in Qin increased year by year. When he presided over the La sacrifice again, the people of Xianyang City were already fanatical about him.

As it was about to reach the 16th year of King Zheng of Qin, Xu Fu made up for Ying Zheng’s birthday separately.

As for the birthday gift, Xu Fu could only wrong himself and wrap himself up to present as a gift.

Just around the corner was the 16th year of King Zheng of Qin.

Fusu already had the look of a young boy, and Huhai had also started learning witchcraft and divination from Xu Fu, although Huhai was not as diligent as Fusu when learning.

When Huhai sneezed again and blew away a small strip of cloth.

Zhao Cheng walked in and said with an embarrassed expression, "Shuzhang, an attendant is asking to see you."

"Hmm? Who?"

"An attendant of Prince Jia of Zhao."

Xu Fu suddenly remembered Prince Jia, who had appeared briefly and then disappeared without a trace. "What happened to him?"

"Prince Jia is seriously ill..."

"Didn't you call a physician?" Xu Fu was surprised.

Zhao Cheng said helplessly, "Prince Jia cannot call one, and is unable to call one."

Why couldn't he call one and was unable to call one? Xu Fu really didn't understand the ins and outs, so he had to pat Huhai’s head, tell him to wait, and then get up and walk out. "This matter shouldn't be for me to handle, right?" Xu Fu didn't want to intervene in such matters, lest he cause Ying Zheng to misunderstand.

"That attendant begged for help..." Zhao Cheng was also extremely helpless.

Xu Fu shook his head, "In the future, just block such matters." Zhao Cheng had indeed not done this to his satisfaction.

Zhao Cheng nodded uneasily. When Xu Fu stepped out of the hall, he bit his lip and couldn't help but ask, "Is the Shuzhang angry with this servant?"

Xu Fu was helpless, "No."

Only then did Zhao Cheng’s eyes brighten, and he whispered, "The Shuzhang is broad-minded."

As they spoke, Xu Fu had already walked up to the attendant.

The attendant looked sallow and emaciated, and his appearance was truly miserable.

Only then did Xu Fu remember that Prince Jia hadn't been asked about for so long, and even the King of Zhao had never cared about the son he sent to Qin, so it was inevitable that Prince Jia and his attendants were being mistreated.

Xu Fu’s heart was also a bit complicated. He frowned.

Reasonably speaking, Zhao did indeed owe this debt. But the people who had bullied Qin back then were not Prince Jia.

Should this Prince Jia be saved, or not?

chapters.title: 第171章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu hesitated after seeing the attendant; if Ying Zheng didn't want to bother with them, why should he go out of his way to intervene?

"Find a physician to take a look at him. Tell them it's on my orders—if he can be saved, save him; if not, then so be it." Xu Fu felt that meeting this Gongzi Jia would be pointless and might even invite trouble.

The attendant's expression shifted. He suddenly sprang up from the ground, pointing at Xu Fu's nose with immense indignation, and cursed, "Is this how the Qin people treat a prince of my Zhao state?"

The palace guards and attendants, seeing this, immediately swarmed over and tackled the attendant beside Gongzi Jia to the ground.

Daring to point at Xu Fu's nose—who gave him the nerve?

Xu Fu wasn't angry; he simply stood further away, glancing at the attendant coldly. "Tell me, how have I treated your master? I ordered someone to fetch a physician for him; is there anything wrong with that?"

The attendant’s face flushed red. "You... you are humiliating the prince like this..."

"If we're talking about humiliation, didn't your Zhao state bring this upon yourselves?" Xu Fu frowned, his tone displeased. He knew he was being protective, but so what? Gongzi Jia was sent over by the King of Zhao himself; it wasn't as if the Qin state had begged for him to come, and he certainly didn't have the standing to demand how the Qin state should treat him.

The attendant stammered, unable to find words.

"Go," Xu Fu said to Zhao Cheng, turning to leave.

No matter how the attendant cursed in grief and anger behind him, Xu Fu didn't look back even once.

Gongzi Jia was sick, so wasn't it reasonable to find a physician? Looking for him was useless anyway. Even if Xu Fu had the best medical skills, he wouldn't be idle enough to treat Gongzi Jia.

This interlude was quickly forgotten by Xu Fu, and it wasn't until a month later, when he suddenly remembered, that he called Zhao Cheng to his side.

"How is Gongzi Jia?"

"He has already recovered from his illness."

Xu Fu nodded, dismissed Zhao Cheng, and called Hu Hai over to continue teaching him about witchcraft.

Zhao Cheng opened his mouth as if to say something more, but in the end, he retreated in silence, causing the palace servants nearby to look at him strangely several times.

Hu Hai leaned into Xu Fu's arms, lazily yawning several times. "It's time to go..."

Xu Fu knew that at this time, Zhao Gao should be coming to teach him, so he put down the bamboo slips in his hand.

It just so happened that today, Zhao Gao hadn't found Hu Hai, so he came over to this side.

Zhao Gao stepped into the hall, paid his respects to Xu Fu, and smiled. "I didn't expect to run into someone at your place, Sir." Even after so much time, Zhao Gao still used the initial title he had for Xu Fu.

"Who?" Xu Fu's curiosity was piqued.

"I have a younger brother..."

Hearing only the first half, Xu Fu immediately understood in his mind. "...Zhao Cheng?" Xu Fu was genuinely surprised. It was enough that he remembered there was a Zhao Gao in history; he truly didn't know that Zhao Gao had a younger brother.

"That's right."

Thoughts swirled in the back of Xu Fu's mind.

What kind of person was Zhao Gao? The man who ruined the Qin Dynasty in history! Zhao Cheng was actually his younger brother! Could there be a problem with Zhao Cheng's attitude toward him? Just as Xu Fu thought this, he quickly dismissed the idea.

If Zhao Cheng really had ulterior motives, would Zhao Gao be so open about their relationship in front of him? Wouldn't it be better to keep the relationship hidden and strike unexpectedly later?

Xu Fu's gaze swept lightly over Zhao Gao.

Perhaps he was just too biased...

Zhao Gao might not necessarily follow the path he took in history; for instance, he had even slept with the First Emperor of Qin, so what else was impossible?

Xu Fu nodded with a gentle attitude. "Zhao Cheng once protected my life, so I brought him by my side. I didn't expect him to be your brother." Xu Fu paused and asked openly, "Why haven't I seen him with you before?"

Zhao Gao smiled helplessly. "Although he is my own brother, we are not close. I grew up in the Zhao state, while he grew up in the Qin state. So, after entering the palace, I wanted to look after him, but he was unwilling."

"I see." Xu Fu felt relieved and handed Hu Hai over to him.

Zhao Gao smiled. "Today, I will teach the Prince about penal law."

Xu Fu frowned involuntarily, but thinking that Zhao Gao hadn't taught anything sensitive, he forced himself to relax.

He couldn't always be suspicious of Zhao Gao.

Teaching penal law was normal; Xu Fu had once heard Ying Zheng mention that Meng Tian had studied penal law in his youth and had even served as a clerk for legal trials.

Hu Hai looked back at Xu Fu with reluctance before following Zhao Gao out.

After they left, Xu Fu couldn't help but yawn as well.

Although he had been promoted in rank, he actually didn't have much to do. Even if he were asked to intervene in military and political affairs, Xu Fu wouldn't dare to get involved easily. He knew his own limits; forcing himself to handle things he wasn't good at would only ruin Ying Zheng's plans.

Resting in the palace like this for a while, Xu Fu felt like he was becoming a babysitter.

It was truly a bit boring...

Xu Fu called for a palace servant. "Are there any places in the palace that I am not allowed to go?"

The servant smiled. "The Shu-zhang can go anywhere, of course."

Xu Fu thought to himself, nonsense. If I went to the concubines' quarters or to the Empress Dowager Huayang... that would be a disaster, wouldn't it? Of course, Xu Fu wouldn't be idle enough to go to those places anyway.

He simply ordered someone to take him on a tour of all the accessible parts of the palace.

He had been in the Qin state for several years, yet he hadn't properly walked through the palace. Since staying in the hall was boring anyway, he might as well go for a walk.

It was spring, a rare time when the palace scenery was at its best. Xu Fu took two or three servants, along with Zhao Cheng, and wandered aimlessly through the palace.

Xu Fu’s original intention was just to wander, but his face was so well-known that wherever he went, the servants would kneel and bow repeatedly, making Xu Fu feel like a god who had descended to earth.

Just as he was thinking about finding a place to rest, someone suddenly rushed out of the courtyard ahead and collided straight into Xu Fu.

"How bold!" Zhao Cheng's expression changed in shock, and he shouted angrily, hurriedly pulling Xu Fu aside to protect him. The person who had collided with them fell to the ground due to a loss of balance.

Who would dare to run around recklessly in the palace?

"Pull him up," Xu Fu said coldly.

The attendant immediately stepped forward to pull the person up. The man kept his head down, not daring to look at anyone.

"Raise your head," Xu Fu's voice was even colder.

The man still did not look up.

The attendant restraining him didn't hesitate and forcefully tilted his head up.

Xu Fu glanced at him and found him somewhat familiar, but couldn't recall who he was for a long time. It was Zhao Cheng who said in surprise, "Shu-zhang, isn't this the attendant beside Gongzi Jia?"

The attendant beside Gongzi Jia? Xu Fu examined him closely. Indeed, it was the man who had pointed and cursed at him earlier.

"Search him," Xu Fu ordered.

"What are you doing?" The man finally couldn't hold back and spoke. Seeing the attendant about to pin him down for a search, he immediately struggled violently.

"Stole something? Feeling that guilty?" Xu Fu looked down at him from above.

The man struggled even more fiercely.

Xu Fu was almost certain now.

What had he stolen to make him flee in such a panic?

While he was thinking, another person ran out of the courtyard. The man was wearing a gray robe, had a slender build, and was panting after running only a few steps. Xu Fu heard him say with grief and indignation: "You, how could you do this?" Clearly, he was addressing the attendant.

Xu Fu looked toward him.

He examined him carefully.

Indeed, it was exactly the appearance of Gongzi Jia from his memory.

It had been a few months, and he hadn't expected Gongzi Jia to be so thin. However, his temperament hadn't changed much, and even though he wasn't dressed in finery, he looked very clean and tidy, which naturally evoked a sense of goodwill.

In contrast, the attendant seemed detestable.

Xu Fu asked indifferently, "Did this attendant of yours steal your belongings?"

Gongzi Jia was stunned and looked up at Xu Fu. "...Yes, he did." His throat moved, and a look of embarrassment flashed across his face.

Being a prince of the Zhao state and falling to such a state, he naturally felt extremely ashamed.

Xu Fu looked away to avoid making Gongzi Jia feel even more uncomfortable.

Seeing Gongzi Jia come out, the attendant felt guilty and trembled uncontrollably on the ground.

At this moment, the items on him were also searched out.

Coins, gold.

Xu Fu sneered, "Back then you accused me like that; I thought you were a loyal servant, but I didn't know you were such a piece of trash!"

The attendant kept his head down, saying nothing.

Gongzi Jia was full of sorrow and only after a long time said, "Since you have betrayed me, you are no longer a person of the Zhao state."

Xu Fu ordered the attendant nearby, "Take him away." Xu Fu knew that being taken away like this meant death. But, a Zhao person, and one who had even betrayed his master—what good character could he have? Such a person was better off dead to avoid causing trouble.

The man was dragged away, wailing.

Gongzi Jia watched him being dragged away with a complex expression. Zhao Cheng handed the items that had been searched out to Gongzi Jia.

Gongzi Jia looked embarrassed and said to Xu Fu, "Thank you."

Xu Fu didn't say much and was about to leave with his people, but Gongzi Jia hurried forward two steps and squeezed out a string of words from his throat: "May I ask, when will the King of Qin be willing to let me go?"

Xu Fu glanced at the courtyard; there were no guards outside, and hadn't he just chased him out? Xu Fu asked in confusion, "Why would you need to be let go? Gongzi Jia is already a free man."

Gongzi Jia looked bitter. "That is not so. I know that the King of Qin has sent people to watch me. If I am free, please ask the King of Qin to allow me to meet with the envoys of the Zhao state."

"You can't ask me about this; you have to go and speak to the King yourself." Xu Fu really didn't have the audacity to rashly agree to such a thing.

Gongzi Jia looked even more embarrassed, and two blushes appeared on his cheeks. "This... the King of Qin is unwilling to see me..."

Then I can't help you either, Xu Fu added in his heart.

If Ying Zheng was unwilling to see him, then he certainly couldn't help. One was a stranger, the other was his lover; Xu Fu naturally sided with Ying Zheng.

"Gongzi Jia should go back and rest well," Xu Fu said, blocking everything he had to say.

Gongzi Jia shook his head repeatedly and couldn't help but step forward and grab Xu Fu's arm. "I... once the attendant is gone, I will be all alone in the courtyard. Am I to die like this in this lifetime? I beg the King of Qin to see me once, just once, to let me say the words I've held in for so long..."

"If you have something to say, say it right here in front of me," Ying Zheng stared coldly at Gongzi Jia's hand, his gaze wishing he could turn into reality and chop it off.

Today was Fusu's birthday, and Ying Zheng had finished his official duties early. When he returned and didn't see Xu Fu, he had followed his trail here.

Who would have thought that the long-unseen Gongzi Jia would appear in front of Xu Fu again?

Heh, what a scheme!

He must be intending to seduce Xu Fu!

The jealous King of Qin thought, feeling very unhappy.

"K-King of Qin!" Gongzi Jia was ecstatic, and in his excitement, he grabbed Xu Fu even tighter.

Xu Fu: ...

"Gongzi Jia, stand back," Ying Zheng said coldly.

Gongzi Jia was stunned, hurriedly let go, and moved back very obediently. His eyes were a bit sore, and his lips trembled as he said, "King of Qin, I... I want to see the envoys of the Zhao state..."

"You may," Ying Zheng agreed generously.

Xu Fu couldn't help but look back at him.

Could it be that he saw Gongzi Jia's red eyes and felt pity, so he couldn't help but agree?

Xu Fu couldn't help but feel sour inside.

Gongzi Jia's eyes lit up, and he immediately added, "C-can I leave this courtyard?"

"Where do you want to go?" Ying Zheng's voice was even colder, and he sneered in his heart. Heh, finally revealing your purpose? Do you want to say you'll follow Xu Fu? Sorry, Xu Fu lives with me.

Gongzi Jia thought blankly for a while. "...Just, just don't be so remote." Gongzi Jia couldn't help but say, "Living alone, I really feel quite anxious."

Xu Fu couldn't help but look at Gongzi Jia a few more times.

Why did he give off such an innocent and naive feeling?

"You may." Although it was unexpected, Ying Zheng decided to wait and see when his true purpose would be revealed.

Gongzi Jia's face flashed with excitement repeatedly.

Xu Fu was already feeling very jealous.

In his heart, there were two big capital letters: "HEH."

"Can... can I handle that attendant myself?"

"You may."

Xu Fu: Heh.

"Can I ask the Shu-zhang for advice from time to time?" Gongzi Jia suddenly turned to look at Xu Fu.

"Ask for advice on what?" Ying Zheng's face was gloomy, his anger ready to burst forth.

"I have also studied the art of divination, and having heard of the Shu-zhang's abilities, I admire you greatly..."

Admire???

Admire greatly!!!

Ying Zheng was completely ignited.

Xu Fu: ???
chapters.source_text:
徐福看见那侍从后就犹豫了，若是嬴政不愿管他们，自己何苦去插这个手？
“寻个侍医给他瞧瞧，就说是我说的，救得活便救，救不活就算了。”徐福觉得他去见了那公子嘉也没意思，说不定反倒还惹来麻烦。
侍从脸色一变，突然从地上蹿了起来，无比愤慨地指着徐福的鼻子骂道：“秦人便是如此待我赵国公子的吗？”
宫中的守卫、侍从见状立刻围了上来，将公子嘉身边的那名侍从扑倒在了地上。
敢指着徐福的鼻子，谁给他的胆子啊？
徐福也不生气，只站得远了，冷漠地睨着那侍从，“你且说说，我如何待你公子了？我命人去为他请侍医，可有何处不对？”
那侍从涨红了脸，“你们……你们这般羞辱公子……”
“若说羞辱，那不是你们赵国自己送上门来的吗？”徐福皱起眉，语气不快。徐福知道自己是在护短。但护短又怎么样？公子嘉是赵王自己送上来的，这可真不是秦国求着让他来的，他还真没这个资格要求秦国必须对他如何。
侍从支支吾吾说不出话来。
“去吧。”徐福对赵成说了一句，转身便要走。
任那侍从在后面如何悲愤痛骂，徐福都没有回头多看一眼。
公子嘉病了，找侍医去不是很合理的事吗？找他也没用啊。徐福就是再好的医术，他也不会闲到去给公子嘉看病啊。
这段插曲很快便被徐福遗忘了，只是过了一个月，徐福突然想起来的时候，才将赵成叫到了身边来。
“那公子嘉如何了？”
“已然病愈了。”
徐福点点头，挥退赵成，又将胡亥叫到了身边来，继续与他讲巫术。
赵成张了张嘴，还想说些什么，最后却又沉默地退了下去。弄得一旁的宫人怪异地打量了他好几眼。
胡亥靠在徐福的怀里，懒懒地打了好几个呵欠，“该走了……”
徐福知道这个时候，该是赵高来教他了，便放下了手中的竹简。
只是今日赵高没寻到胡亥的身影，便往这边来了。
赵高踏进殿内，朝徐福见了礼，笑道：“没成想在先生这里碰见一个人。”过去这么久了，赵高都仍旧是叫徐福最初的称呼。
“谁？”徐福被他撩起了好奇心。
“我有个弟弟……”
刚听了前半句，徐福脑子里就立时明白过来了，“……赵成？”徐福心中是真的惊讶。他能记得历史上有个赵高就不错了，他实在是不知晓历史上赵高还有个弟弟啊。
“不错。”
徐福心底的思绪打了个转儿。
赵高是个什么人物？历史上把秦王朝给祸害了的人啊！赵成竟然是他的弟弟！那赵成对自己的态度，会不会有问题呢？徐福刚这样想着，很快倒是又自己打消了。
如果赵成真的有问题，赵高还会这样坦荡地在自己跟前说出关系来吗？将关系捂着，以后出其不意，那不是更好吗？
徐福的目光从赵高的身上淡淡扫过。
或许是他带有太多偏见了吧……
赵高此人也并非一定会像历史上那样来走吧，就好比自己连秦始皇都给睡了，还会有什么事不可能发生呢？
徐福态度温和地点头，“赵成护佑过我的性命，我便将他带在身边了，没成想到竟是你的弟弟。”徐福顿了顿，光明正大地问道：“怎么从前不见他同你一起？”
赵高无奈一笑，“虽是我的亲弟，但我们二人并不亲近，我幼时是长在赵国的，他是长在秦国的。因而入宫后，我要照拂他，他也不愿。”
“原来如此。”徐福放下了心，然后将胡亥交给了对方。
赵高笑道：“今日我便教公子刑狱。”
徐福不自觉地皱了皱眉，不过想到赵高也并未教什么敏感的东西，便也只得强制放下心来。
他不能总这样怀疑赵高。
教授刑狱乃是正常的，徐福曾听嬴政说起过，蒙恬少年时便习过刑狱法，更曾担任过审理狱讼的文书。
胡亥不舍地看了徐福几眼，才跟着赵高出去了。
他们离开后，徐福忍不住也打了个呵欠。
虽然他如今升了爵位，但实际上并无多少事可做，军政大事就算让他去插手，徐福也不敢轻易往上凑啊。他很清楚自己的斤两，不擅长的事非要强揽，那只会坏了嬴政的事。
如此在宫中休息一段时日，徐福都觉得自己快变成一个带孩子的了。
实在无趣了些……
徐福叫上宫人，“王宫中有哪些地方是不能去的吗？”
宫人笑道：“庶长自是哪里都能去的。”
徐福心道，鬼扯。我要是去后宫姬妾那儿，去华阳太后那儿……那还了得吗？当然徐福也不会闲着没事儿跑那些地方去的。
他只是命人带着自己将王宫能去的地方都走一遍。
来到秦国几年，他却还没能正经地将王宫走上一遍，左右在殿中待着也是无聊，还不如出来走一走。
此时正值春日，王宫中也是难得景致正好的时候，徐福带了两三名宫人，联同赵成一起便在王宫中瞎晃了起来。
徐福本意是出来瞎晃，但他那张脸知名度实在太高，走到哪儿，便惊得宫人们连连跪拜，顿时让徐福觉得自己活像下凡神仙一样。
正想着要不要寻个地方停下来休息一二，前方的院子里突然匆匆走出来一人，直直与徐福撞上了。
“大胆？”赵成脸色惊变，怒斥一声，忙将徐福拉了一把，护住了他。而那撞上来的人，因为重心不稳倒在了地面上。
什么人敢在王宫里横冲直撞？
“把人拉起来。”徐福冷声道。
侍从立即上前将人拉了起来，那人低着头不敢看人。
“抬起头来。”徐福的声音更冷了。
那人依旧没有抬头。
钳制住他的侍从却不再犹豫，直接强硬地将他的头掰正了。
徐福看了一眼只觉得有些眼熟，但是半天没能想起来对方是谁。倒是赵成惊异道：“庶长，这不是公子嘉身边的侍从吗？”
公子嘉身边的侍从？徐福细细打量了他几眼。不错，是之前指着他骂的那个男人。
“搜他身上。”徐福下了命令。
“你们干什么？”那人终于憋不住开口了，在看见侍从要按倒他搜身的时候，立刻就激烈地挣扎了起来。
“偷了东西？这么心虚？”徐福居高临下地看着他。
那人挣扎得更激烈了。
徐福几乎已经确定没错了。
是偷了什么东西？才会让他这样仓皇地逃出来？
正思考间呢，就见院子里又跑出了一个人来。那人穿着一身灰袍子，身材清瘦，跑了没几步便气喘吁吁了。徐福听他口中悲愤道：“你、你怎能如此？”显然是冲着那侍从说的。
徐福朝他看过去。
细细打量一番。
不错，正是记忆中那公子嘉的模样。
几个月不见，没曾想公子嘉竟是这般清瘦了。不过他那身气质倒是没甚变化，而且尽管穿得并不华贵，瞧上去倒是很干净整洁，令人顿生好感。
相比之下，这侍从便令人觉得可恶了。
徐福淡淡问道：“可是你这侍从偷了你的东西？”
公子嘉怔了怔，抬起头来看徐福，“……是、是。”他喉头动了动，面上闪过窘迫之色。
好歹也是赵国公子，落得这样，自然会觉得羞窘无比。
徐福移开了目光，免得公子嘉愈加无所适从。
那侍从见公子嘉出来了，顿时心虚不已，在地上抖个不停。
此时他身上的东西也被搜了出来。
钱币，金子。
徐福冷笑道：“当初你还那样指责我，我还当是个忠仆，却不知原来你是这么个东西！”
那侍从死死低着头，什么话也不说。
公子嘉满面悲戚之色，久久才道：“既已背叛了我，那你以后便也不是赵国人了。”
徐福吩咐一旁的侍从，“将人带下去。”徐福知道这一带下去多半是死的了。但是，一个赵国人，还是一个连主子都被背叛的人，能有什么好的品德？这样的人，还是死了好，免得搅出乱子来。
那人哭嚎着被拖了下去。
公子嘉神色复杂地看着他被拖走。赵成将那些搜出来的东西，递到了公子嘉的面前。
公子嘉面色尴尬，冲徐福道了声，“多谢。”
徐福也没多说什么，正要带着人离去，公子嘉却急急忙忙上前两步，从喉中挤出一串话来，“敢问秦王，何时才肯放我出来？”
徐福瞥了一眼那院子，院子外并无守卫，他刚才不是就追出来了吗？徐福疑惑道：“何须放你？公子嘉已经是自由身。”
公子嘉面露苦色，“并非如此，我知道的，秦王派了人盯着我。若是自由，便请秦王允我见一见赵国使臣吧。”
“这个你与我说不行，你得自己去与王上说。”徐福还真没那么大脸，能贸然答应这样的事。
公子嘉面色更尴尬了，面颊上还浮起了两抹绯色，“这……秦王不愿见我……”
那我也爱莫能助啊。徐福在心中接口道。
嬴政若是不愿见他，那自己就更不能帮忙了。一个陌生人，一个是情人，徐福当然是向着嬴政的。
“公子嘉还是回去好生休息吧。”徐福一句话就给全堵了回去。
公子嘉连连摇头，甚至忍不住上前抓住了徐福的胳膊，“我……侍从一走，我便一人在院中，这辈子难道我就要这样死去吗？求秦王见我一面，只求见一面，让我将憋了许久的话都说了……”
“有何话说，便当着寡人的面就在这儿说吧。”嬴政目光冰冷地盯着公子嘉那只手，目光恨不得化为实质给他剁下来。
今日该是扶苏生辰，嬴政早早处理完了政务，回来不见徐福人影，便一路寻过来了。
谁知道那个许久不见的公子嘉竟然又出现在了徐福的跟前。
呵呵，真是好心机！
一定是意图勾引徐福！
妒火狂烧的秦王政非常不高兴地想。
“秦、秦王！”公子嘉欣喜若狂，一时激动之下，反而将徐福抓得更紧了。
徐福：……
“公子嘉，你往后站一些。”嬴政冷声道。
公子嘉愣了愣，忙松开手，极为顺从地往后挪了挪步子，只是他的眼眶有些酸，嘴唇喏嗫一番，道：“秦王，我、我想见赵国的使臣……”
“可以。”嬴政很大方地答应了。
徐福都忍不住回头看了他一眼。
这不会是瞧见公子嘉眼眶红红惹人心疼，就忍不住答应了吧？
徐福心里忍不住泛着酸。
那公子嘉双眼一亮，马上又道：“我、我能否离开这个院子？”
“你想去哪里？”嬴政的声音更冷，心中冷笑。呵呵，终于要暴露你的目的了吗？你想说跟着徐福？不好意思，徐福是跟着寡人住的。
公子嘉茫然地想了会儿，“……就，就不要这样偏远就好了。”公子嘉忍不住道：“我一人住着，实在有些心慌。”
徐福忍不住多看了两眼公子嘉。
怎么给人一种天真稚嫩的感觉呢？
“可以。”虽然出乎了他的意料，但是嬴政还是决定瞧一瞧，他的目的什么时候才会说出来。
公子嘉面上连连闪过激动之色。
徐福心中已经很吃味了。
心中写着两个大写的“呵呵”。
“那个……那个侍从我能自己处理吗？”
“可以。”
徐福：呵呵。
“我能时时请教庶长吗？”公子嘉突然间转头看向了徐福。
“请教什么？”嬴政面色阴沉，身上怒气欲喷薄而出。
“我也曾习过卜筮之术，听闻庶长本事，仰慕不已……”
倾慕？？？
倾慕不已！！！
嬴政整个人都被点燃了。
徐福：？？？

chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu nodded faintly, "Very well."

The tone was identical, mimicking Ying Zheng’s manner of speaking exactly, yet Ying Zheng didn't notice this; his mind was entirely occupied by one thought.

Xu Fu had agreed!!!

He said it was okay?

Ying Zheng felt a mouthful of blood stuck in his throat, neither swallowing nor spitting it out, feeling incredibly uncomfortable.

"Young Master of Zhao, when did you learn the art of divination? Why was I not aware of this?" The expression on Ying Zheng’s face was cold, and his gaze toward Gongzi Jia carried a hint of a threat. He wanted to tell Gongzi Jia that regardless of whether he had learned it or not, he had to say he hadn't today.

But to Xu Fu’s ears, the meaning was entirely different. The sentence even carried a hint of intimacy, as if saying, "When I knew you before, you didn't learn this stuff, so why have you learned it now?" In short, to Xu Fu, it sounded very annoying.

Were these two that close before? No wonder Gongzi Jia was so intent on seeing Ying Zheng.

Gongzi Jia looked up and met Ying Zheng’s gaze.

Ying Zheng’s eyes were cold, thinking to himself, *Now he should finally understand my threat.*

Gongzi Jia, however, nodded and said in a low voice, "I did indeed learn it. I admired the Shu Zhang back in the State of Zhao, but since the Shu Zhang is not someone just anyone can approach, I dared not speak to him... In any case, I will be living in the State of Qin for the rest of my life, so please, King of Qin, grant me this request."

"That is enough. If you have any questions in the future, just come find me." Xu Fu spoke up, putting an end to the request.

The matter was thus settled.

The more Ying Zheng looked at Gongzi Jia, the more he felt that face was highly deceptive—what a schemer! He must have ulterior motives toward Xu Fu. It didn't matter; he would keep a close eye on him and see what he could come up with!

Besides, with that appearance, could Gongzi Jia be better than him?

He probably didn't even measure up to a fraction of him!

Seeing that both men had fallen silent, Gongzi Jia said in a low voice, "...I, I will go pack my things. I trouble the King of Qin to prepare a courtyard for me."

He was climbing up the pole the moment it was offered.

Xu Fu frowned inwardly. Gongzi Jia was a smart man, and a smart man who knew how to feign weakness exceptionally well. He didn't mind exposing his weak side to gain what he wanted. How could a person like this be abandoned by the King of Zhao? Was it that Gongzi Jia’s methods were slightly inferior, or was the King of Zhao’s brain kicked by a donkey?

Since Ying Zheng had already agreed, he naturally wouldn't change his mind, so he called an attendant to follow him and pack his things. Turning around, Ying Zheng immediately said to Xu Fu, "Fusu should be waiting for us by now."

Without needing Ying Zheng to say anything more, Xu Fu nodded and quickly turned to walk outside, "I didn't realize I had been wandering in the palace for so long. Fusu shouldn't have been waiting for too long, right?"

Ying Zheng thought to himself, *If we walk a little faster, he won't have to.*

He reached out to put his arm around Xu Fu’s shoulders and quickened his pace.

By the time Gongzi Jia had packed his things and come out, the figures of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were long gone.

·

"Thank you, Father, King Father." Fusu bowed respectfully to both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng at the same time.

After his birthday passed this year, Fusu would be eleven years old.

In ancient times, men would marry as early as eleven or twelve, but fortunately, things weren't that twisted yet. Fusu, who had already grown into a youthful physique, looked increasingly handsome and elegant. His temperament even faintly showed signs of developing toward Xu Fu’s style; at first glance, he appeared aloof enough to be intimidating, yet one couldn't help but admire him.

When Huhai stood next to him, he looked a bit short and stout.

Huhai was very unhappy; why did he look so short in the blink of an eye? He tugged at the leather belt around Fusu’s waist, insisting on climbing up. Fusu, helpless, had to lift him up.

Food was laid out on the table.

In the center was a simple, ugly-as-sin small cake provided by Xu Fu, with a matching ugly-as-sin small candle stuck on top.

When Fusu first saw this thing, he felt as if Xu Fu were cursing him to die.

Lighting a candle—wasn't that only for memorial services?

After Xu Fu explained it, Fusu accepted this new invention without any resistance.

Fusu held Huhai’s bottom with one hand and looked at Xu Fu with eyes full of anticipation.

Xu Fu put on airs and slowly voiced his blessings for Fusu, "I hope that in the future... you will always be happy in your heart, possess a healthy body, and grow into a gentleman of fine character."

In pre-Qin texts, "gentleman" (junzi) usually referred to the son of a king, merely denoting his noble status, but Confucius had already imbued the term with another layer of meaning, giving it moral virtue. Xu Fu knew that the Fusu in history books was a gentleman of fine character, and he certainly hoped for the same here. So, after struggling for a long time, he squeezed out this string of words.

Xu Fu would have liked to be eloquent, but idioms didn't exist yet, let alone five-character or seven-character regulated verse.

Fusu was stunned for a moment before he finally said, "Thank you, Father."

Now, calling Xu Fu this way, Fusu no longer felt awkward or embarrassed.

Then Fusu looked at Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng had high hopes for Fusu; he couldn't help but pat Fusu’s shoulder and said in a deep voice, "In the future, you will surely become my pride."

Xu Fu knew how much the First Emperor of Qin loved his eldest son, Fusu, in history. Watching this scene, Xu Fu couldn't help but curl the corners of his lips. It was starting to feel more and more like a home.

He turned his head to look at Fusu.

Fusu had been shaken by Ying Zheng’s words, as if he had never expected Ying Zheng to speak to him like that.

It was true that Ying Zheng rarely showed his affection for Fusu directly. Seeing Fusu standing there in a daze, he couldn't help but raise his hand and ruffle his hair. If this had been in the past, Ying Zheng would never have done such a thing; this was something he had learned from Xu Fu.

Xu Fu liked to pat Huhai and pat Fusu.

Fusu looked very much like an adult, but when Xu Fu patted him, he would also obediently rub against Xu Fu’s palm. After a while, Ying Zheng found it interesting and followed suit.

Fusu’s eyes turned slightly red, and he moved his lips, but couldn't say a single word.

"Huhai, it's your turn." Xu Fu casually pinched Huhai’s chubby cheek.

"Oh." Huhai responded, then rubbed his chin, "I hope Brother... grows a little slower—oh, no, wait, grow faster, otherwise you won't be able to carry me. Brother also needs to become more capable." After a pause, Huhai added with a smile, "That way I can just play!"

Fusu’s face darkened and darkened again; he really didn't know how to evaluate Huhai’s childish words.

Xu Fu, however, thought it was good.

Brothers should be like this so that they wouldn't kill each other in the future and bring disaster to Great Qin.

After the blessings were said, Fusu, under Xu Fu’s guidance, made a wish, blew out the candle, and began to eat that simple-beyond-simple cake.

No exquisite feast had been prepared today, but the atmosphere in the hall was exceptionally good.

Spring passed just like that, in a warm and cozy atmosphere.

As summer approached, Xu Fu heard that Huan Yi and Li Xin had successively withdrawn some troops from the State of Zhao. Meanwhile, the State of Zhao was in such a chaotic mess that they had no energy left to counterattack.

The conflict between Li Mu and the King of Zhao had been pushed to the extreme.

Someone had suggested to the King of Zhao that Li Mu and Sima Shang had intentions of rebellion.

At the same time, in Xianyang, the envoy from the State of Zhao had entered the palace once again.

Ying Zheng summoned the man in the hall and also had Gongzi Jia brought in. When Xu Fu heard this news, he didn't hesitate at all and got up to rush over there.

Leaving Ying Zheng and Gongzi Jia alone made Xu Fu feel uncomfortable, and since he felt uncomfortable, there was no need to hold it in; he would just go over and see for himself.

Xu Fu had forgotten that it could hardly be called "alone" in the hall; not to mention the Zhao envoy, even if he weren't there, there were still a room full of palace attendants and servants, and guards outside the hall.

...

When the Zhao envoy was speaking excitedly to Gongzi Jia, Xu Fu arrived at the entrance of the hall with his people.

An attendant hurried inside to announce him, and in the blink of an eye, the attendant came out and respectfully invited Xu Fu inside.

When the Zhao envoy saw Xu Fu, he felt particularly uneasy.

This person was rumored to be too divine, and some even said that the reason Zhao was defeated so badly had something to do with him. And this man had indeed saved the Qin generals Huan Yi and Li Xin. If it weren't for him... the Zhao envoy lowered his head and sighed inwardly. He didn't dare to show any ill will in front of Ying Zheng. If he did, he might end up bleeding on the spot.

He knew very well how much the King of Qin doted on this person.

"Gongzi Jia." Seeing the other party look toward him, Xu Fu greeted him.

Gongzi Jia smiled, "Shu Zhang."

The expression on Ying Zheng’s face softened significantly because of Xu Fu’s arrival.

Xu Fu stood in the hall without continuing to walk toward Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng had no choice but to withdraw his gaze and signal for the envoy to continue speaking. The envoy bowed and said, "The King of Zhao has words he wishes for me to convey to the King of Qin. If Gongzi Jia has offended the King of Qin in any way, I hope the King of Qin will be forgiving." In truth, the King of Zhao was just trying to probe what Ying Zheng’s attitude toward Gongzi Jia was.

Xu Fu glanced at Gongzi Jia and saw that although he was smiling, his face was clearly pale.

The King of Zhao’s words were stepping on his own son’s heart.

Sending his son to be a hostage and then speaking ill of him—could Gongzi Jia take that? A thought faintly rose in Xu Fu’s mind...

Gongzi Jia couldn't help but speak up, "I have never offended the King of Qin; my father is truly overthinking."

The envoy smiled but said nothing more. As an envoy delivering messages, being caught in the middle was very difficult. Even he felt some sympathy for Gongzi Jia.

The envoy continued to say to Ying Zheng, "This is an offering for the King of Qin."

As he spoke, the attendant behind him stepped forward.

That attendant had such a low presence that Xu Fu hadn't even noticed there was someone there just now.

Seeing him suddenly walk forward, Xu Fu couldn't help but take a few extra looks at him. At this glance, Xu Fu sensed something wrong.

In physiognomy, there was one extremely important aspect: observing the "Qi."

Sometimes, observing a person’s Qi could reveal their mental state, or even their physical condition; more importantly, you could catch a glimpse of their character.

The Qi on this person carried the scent of blood; he was not someone to be trifled with.

How could such a person be brought before Ying Zheng?

Without a second thought, Xu Fu forcefully blocked the man’s path.

"What is it?" Ying Zheng frowned immediately upon seeing his action.

The man looked up, the box he was holding flipped over, and he raised his hand to stab at Xu Fu. The gleaming blade made Xu Fu’s heart jump, and he hurriedly retreated.

Ying Zheng erupted, shouting angrily, "Seize them!"

Guards and attendants all sprang into action.

Wanting to assassinate Ying Zheng without the skills of Jing Ke—what were they dreaming of?

With a "pfft" sound, a blade sliced through clothing. The next moment, the assassin was tackled to the ground, and the guards swarmed over, pinning the assassin, the envoy, and Gongzi Jia.

The envoy was already stunned, trembling uncontrollably, unable to say a word for a long time. Gongzi Jia was also scared silly, his face deathly pale. However, he was at least calmer than the envoy and wasn't trembling incessantly.

Gongzi Jia’s gaze was panicked, finally landing on Xu Fu.

Xu Fu still felt dizzy. The assassin’s attack had been too sudden; Xu Fu had only blocked him by instinct, and then retreated by instinct, but the opponent’s movements were faster, so by the time Xu Fu felt a pain in his arm, he had already been wounded.

Fortunately, he had retreated, otherwise his entire arm might have been pierced through.

Zhao Cheng had already supported him from behind, his face looking even worse than Xu Fu’s, his eyes even red and watery, as if he were about to cry.

Palace attendants scrambled to surround Xu Fu, calling out, "Shu Zhang!" "Is the Shu Zhang injured?" "He’s bleeding!"

Xu Fu looked down and saw blood soaking through his sleeve, dripping onto the floor.

Ying Zheng had already strode down. With a gloomy expression, he pushed aside the attendants and roughly pulled Xu Fu into his arms, though his movements became much gentler once he held him.

An attendant had already run out to fetch the palace physician.

Ying Zheng glanced at Xu Fu’s blood-soaked sleeve, his expression growing colder. He gritted his teeth and said, "Are you a fool? Why did you throw yourself in the way at that moment?"

He hadn't felt it just now, but now Xu Fu felt a tearing pain in his arm. He couldn't help but frown. Now he was hearing Ying Zheng call him a fool in front of so many people?

Xu Fu’s face immediately darkened as well.

Ying Zheng’s heart was still pounding wildly, unable to calm down for a long time. Looking at Xu Fu’s injured arm, he felt as if his own heart were being tightly squeezed.

Ying Zheng led him toward the seat without even looking at the assassin.

The assassin’s mouth was gagged, and he could only struggle desperately.

Gongzi Jia looked at the assassin with loathing, feeling a chill go through his heart.

Xu Fu sat down by the table with Ying Zheng. Blood dripped onto the table, the crimson contrasting with the pure black, piercing deeply into Xu Fu’s eyes.

Xu Fu sighed softly.

So the danger had been waiting for him here.

Just then, he heard an attendant look toward Ying Zheng and cry out, "Your Majesty?"

What was wrong? Xu Fu looked up at Ying Zheng, only to see crimson blood flowing down from his philtrum...

Xu Fu: ...

He was the one who got hurt, so why was Ying Zheng bleeding?

It turned out that the dripping on the table all this time had been Ying Zheng’s!
