徐福淡淡一点头，“可以。”
那个音调，都不带变一下的，简直就是将方才嬴政的口吻学了个十成十，但是嬴政并未注意到这一点，他满脑子就剩下了一句。
徐福答应了！！！
他说可以？
嬴政憋得一口血哽在心头，不上不下难受得紧。
“赵国公子，何时学了卜筮之术？寡人怎么不知道？”嬴政脸上的表情冷漠，看着公子嘉的目光已经带上几分威胁的意思了。他就想告诉公子嘉，我不管你学没学，你今天都得说自己没学。
但是听在徐福耳中，那滋味就完全不一样了。这句话甚至透着点儿亲近的意思。就像是在说，以前我认识你的时候，你都没学这玩意儿，你现在怎么学了？总而言之，听在徐福耳中就是很烦。
这二人从前有那么熟吗？怪不得公子嘉一心想要见到嬴政。
那公子嘉抬头和嬴政对视一眼。
嬴政目光冰冷，心道，这下他总该明白寡人的威胁了吧。
公子嘉却点了点头，声音低低道：“我的确是学过的，在赵国就曾仰慕庶长了，只是庶长不是旁人能接近的，我这才不敢与庶长搭话……左右我这辈子也是活在秦国了，求秦王允我这个要求吧。”
“可以了，你日后若有疑问，来找我便是。”徐福出声为这个要求划上了终结符号。
事情就这样定下了。
嬴政越看越觉得公子嘉那张脸极富欺骗性，实在是好有心机！一定是对徐福有所企图。没关系，寡人就盯着你，瞧你能做出什么来！
就公子嘉那模样，能有寡人优秀吗？
连寡人一分也不及吧！
见二人都不出声了，公子嘉才又低声道：“……我，我收拾一下东西。劳烦秦王为我再准备院子了。”
这是马上就顺着杆子往上爬了。
徐福暗暗皱眉。公子嘉是个聪明人啊，还是个极会示弱的聪明人，他不介意暴露出自己弱的一面，以此来换取更多他想要的东西。就这样的人，还能被赵王抛弃？那是公子嘉手段稍逊一筹，还是那赵王脑子被驴踢了？
嬴政既然已经应下，自然就不会更改，叫了个内侍跟着他去收拾东西了。转过身来，嬴政就立即与徐福道：“扶苏此时应当在等我们了。”
不消嬴政再说多余的话，徐福便点了点头，迅速转身往外走，“不知不觉我在宫中逛了这么久了。扶苏应当不会等上许久吧？”
嬴政暗自道，咱们走快一点儿就不会了啊。
他伸手揽住徐福的肩，加快了脚步。
待公子嘉收拾好东西出来后，早已不见徐福和嬴政的身影了。
·
“多谢父亲，父王。”扶苏极为恭谨地朝徐福和嬴政同时行了礼。
今年生辰过去，扶苏便有十一岁了。
古时男子十一二岁甚至就早早成婚了，不过幸好此时还没那样变态。已经长出少年体态的扶苏，瞧上去越发的姿容俊逸了，身上的气质甚至还隐隐有些朝徐福发展的趋势，乍一看，那是高冷得令人望而生畏，但又暗自敬服。
胡亥往他身边一站，就显得有些矮墩墩了。
胡亥很不高兴，为什么转眼间，自己就显得那样矮了。他扒拉着扶苏腰上的革带，非要往上拱，扶苏无奈，只得将他提了起来。
桌案之上摆着食物。
中间是徐福提供的简易版丑得要死小蛋糕，上头插着同款丑的要死小蜡烛。
扶苏第一次看见这玩意儿的时候，总觉得徐福像是要咒他死一样。
点蜡烛，那不是祭奠才用的吗？
待徐福解释过后，扶苏就丝毫不抗拒地接受了这一新兴事物。
扶苏一手托着胡亥的屁股，然后目光充满期待地看着徐福。
徐福端着架子，缓慢道出了心中对扶苏的祝福，“希望你日后……都能心中愉悦，拥有健康的躯体，长成品行优良的君子。”
在先秦书籍中，君子通常指君王的儿子，仅以表述其崇高的地位，但是孔子已经赋予了这个词另外一层的含义，让它具备了德性。徐福知道历史书上的扶苏是个品行优良的君子，这里当然也希望如此。于是他憋了半天，憋出了这么一串话。
徐福倒是想要妙语连珠，但此时还没成语呢，更没什么五律七律诗呢。
扶苏怔了怔，好一会儿才出声道：“多谢父亲。”
如今再这样叫徐福，扶苏倒是不会觉得尴尬窘迫了。
然后扶苏看向了嬴政。
嬴政对扶苏寄予了厚望，他忍不住拍了拍扶苏的肩，沉声道：“将来你定会成为寡人的骄傲。”
徐福知道历史上秦始皇多么疼爱他长子扶苏。看着这一幕，徐福忍不住嘴角勾了勾。倒是越来越有家的感觉。
他转头去看扶苏。
扶苏已经被嬴政那句话震住了，像是压根没想到嬴政会如此对他说似的。
嬴政也的确少有直接表现自己对扶苏的疼爱的时候，他见扶苏呆在了那里，不由得抬起手又揉了揉他的头。若是换做以前，嬴政是绝不会做这样的事的，这还是从徐福处学来的。
徐福很喜欢摸摸胡亥，摸摸扶苏。
扶苏看上去很有大人的模样，但是徐福摸他的时候，他也会很乖顺地在徐福的掌心蹭蹭。一来二去，嬴政觉得有趣，便也跟着做了。
扶苏的眼眶微微泛红，动了动唇却一句话也没能说出来。
“胡亥，该你了。”徐福顺手掐了一把胡亥肉嘟嘟的脸颊。
“哦。”胡亥应了一声，然后摸了摸下巴，“希望哥哥……长得慢一点，哦，不对，还是长快一点吧，不然不能抱我了。哥哥还要变得更能干一点。”说完顿了顿，随后胡亥笑眯眯地道：“这样我就可以只玩儿啦。”
扶苏面色黑了又黑，实在不知道该如何评价胡亥这番孩子气的话。
徐福倒是觉得很好。
兄弟间就是要这样，日后才不会手足相残，祸害大秦呢。
祝词说完后，扶苏便在徐福的指导下许愿，吹蜡烛，然后开始吃那个简陋得不能再简陋的蛋糕。
今日并未准备什么精致的大餐，但是殿中气氛却格外的好。
春天，便是就这样在一派温馨之中过去了。
快要入夏的时候，徐福听闻桓齮和李信先后从赵国撤出了一些兵力。而赵国之中，乱得一塌糊涂，也没心力去反扑了。
李牧与赵王的矛盾被挑到了极致。
有人向赵王进言，说李牧、司马尚，有谋反之意。
同时咸阳城中，赵国的使臣再度进了宫。
嬴政在殿中召见了此人，同时还将公子嘉传到了殿中去，徐福听闻这个消息时，丝毫不犹豫地起身往那边赶去了。
让嬴政与公子嘉独处，徐福总觉得心里不太舒服，既然不舒服，那也没必要憋着，他大大方方过去看就是了。
徐福倒是忘记了，那殿中怎么样也谈不上独处啊，且不说有个赵国使臣，就算没有他，那还有满屋子的宫人侍从呢，殿外还有守卫呢。
……
赵国使臣激动地与公子嘉说话时，徐福便带着人走到了殿门口。
内侍匆忙进去通报了一声，也就一眨眼的功夫，那内侍便出来恭敬地请徐福进去了。
赵国使臣见着徐福后，心中特别不是滋味。
这人被传得太神了，甚至还总有人说，赵国会败得这样差，跟他也有关系。而此人也的确救了秦国将军桓齮和李信。若没有他……那赵国使臣低下头，暗自叹了口气。他是不敢在嬴政面前显露半点不善情绪的。若是显露出来了，他说不定便会立即血溅当场。
他可是深知秦王对这人的宠爱的。
“公子嘉。”见对方朝自己看了过来，徐福便出声与他打了个招呼。
公子嘉笑了笑，“庶长。”
嬴政脸上的表情因为徐福的到来而柔和了不少。
徐福就站在了殿中，并未朝嬴政的方向继续走去。
嬴政也只得收回视线，示意那使臣继续说话，使臣躬身道：“赵王有话令我传于秦王。若公子嘉有何处触犯秦王，还请秦王多加包容。”其实就是那赵王想试探一下，嬴政对公子嘉是个什么态度。
徐福看了一眼公子嘉，见他虽然面带微笑，可脸色分明是泛着白。
赵王这话，是往他儿子心上踩呢。
将儿子送来做质子了，还言语间说自己儿子的不好，那公子嘉能受得了吗？徐福心中隐隐升起了一个念头……
公子嘉忍不住出声道：“我并未触怒过秦王，父王实在多虑了。”
使臣笑了笑，却并不多言。作为一个传话的使臣，被夹在中间也甚觉为难啊。连他都有些同情这公子嘉了。
使臣继续冲嬴政道：“这是献于秦王的。”
说着他身后的随从便绕上前来了。
那随从存在感极低，方才徐福根本就没注意到还有个人。
见他突然往前走，徐福不由得多打量了他好几眼，这一看，徐福就察觉到了不对劲的地方。
相面之中还有一点极为重要，为望气。
有时候观人的气，可看出他的精神状态，甚至是身体状况，更重要的是，你还能窥见他的品性一二。
这个人身上的气带血腥，不是个好相与的。
这样的人，怎么会被带到嬴政跟前来呢？
徐福想也不想就直接强横地挡在了那人的跟前。
“怎么？”嬴政见他动作，立即皱起了眉。
而那个人抬起头来，手中举着的盒子翻了面，抬手就朝徐福刺来，明晃晃的刀刃晃得徐福心中一跳，连忙后退。
嬴政暴起，怒喝一声，“拿下他们！”
守卫、侍从皆是动了起来。
想要刺杀嬴政，没有荆轲的功夫还妄想什么？
“噗嗤”一声刀刃割破衣帛，下一刻刺客便被扑倒在了地上，守卫们一拥而上，将刺客、使臣连同公子嘉都押了起来。
使臣已然懵了，浑身哆嗦不已，半晌说不出一句话来，公子嘉也吓傻了，面色惨白。不过他好歹比那使臣更镇定一些，没有哆嗦连连。
公子嘉的目光慌忙，最后落到了徐福的身上。
徐福头还有些晕眩，刚才那刺客出手来得太突然，徐福只是凭本能地挡在了他的跟前，后来又本能地往后退，但是对方的动作毕竟更快一些，所以等徐福感觉到手臂一痛的时候，就已经被刺伤了。
幸好他往后退了，不然整只手臂说不定会被刺穿。
赵成已经从后面扶住了他，脸色比他的还要难看，更甚至双眼红红，像是要忍不住流泪一般。
宫人们手忙脚乱地将徐福围在中间，口中呼喊着，“庶长！”“庶长可是受伤了？”“流血了！”
徐福低头看了一眼，血渗透他的衣袖，滴滴答答落在了地上。
嬴政已然大步走了下来，他面色阴沉地推开一旁的宫人，将徐福粗暴地搂在了怀中，等搂住以后，动作便轻柔了不少。
宫人已经跑出去请侍医了。
嬴政看了一眼徐福被血浸透的袖子，面色越发地冷了，他咬牙切齿地道：“你是蠢的么？怎么偏在那个时候往上扑？”
方才不觉得，现在徐福才感觉到了手臂上传来撕裂般的疼痛，他忍不住皱起了眉，现在听嬴政当着这么多人骂自己蠢？
徐福的脸色顿时也拉了下来。
嬴政的心还在狂跳，半晌都无法平静下来，他看着徐福那只受伤的手臂，甚至感觉自己的心都被用力揪了起来。
嬴政带着他往座位边上走，看也没看那刺客一眼。
刺客被堵住了嘴，只能拼命挣扎。
公子嘉憎恶地朝那刺客看了一眼，心中凉了个透。
徐福跟着嬴政一起在桌案旁坐下，血滴滴答答落在了桌案上，殷红和纯黑交映，深深刺进徐福的眼底。
徐福轻叹一口气。
原来危险在这儿等着他呢。
此时忽听内侍望着嬴政的方向一声惊叫，“王上？”
怎么了？徐福抬头朝嬴政看去，却见嬴政的人中处顺着往下流出了殷红的血……
徐福：……
他受个伤，怎么是嬴政流血？
敢情那桌案上滴滴答答半天，全是嬴政的！
chapters.title: 第172章

chapters.source_text:
徐福懵了一下，抬手想摸一摸嬴政的鼻子，但是却忘记自己受伤了，于是一抬手，反倒把自己的伤处拉扯到了，他的手瞬间便垂了下去。
恰巧此时那侍医一路狂奔着踏进殿门来，一见徐福满手血，再见秦王脸上也带着血，那侍医脚下晃了晃，差点因为冲击过大，而直接扑倒在殿门前。
“王上！王上可有恙？”侍医快步冲上前去，一边庆幸自己来得这样快。若是救治及时，还能得个赏赐呢。
“先给徐福瞧一瞧。”嬴政阴着脸，拿起绢布缓缓拭擦着脸上的血迹，明明是可笑的动作，但是由他做来，顿时便不一样了，反倒有种令人不敢直视的气势。
侍医知道徐庶长在王上心中是个什么地位，此时也不敢辩驳，立即就上前给徐福查看了起来。
袖口被小心翼翼地卷起，因为略微狭窄的缘故，卷到一半便有些吃力了。
袖口之下，一截雪白的手臂，沾染着点点鲜血，映入了嬴政的眼眸，嬴政顿时觉得自己胸中又有一股血气在涌动，他的脸色沉了沉，低声道：“直接从伤口处将袖子割开。”一点一点挽起来，实在太折磨看过来的人了。
当然还有一点，嬴政并不希望被其他人看见。
明明是受了伤，嬴政都觉得徐福的浑身上下充满了，让人难以抵抗的诱惑力。仅仅露出一截雪白的胳膊，都能勾得他心神一动。
侍医哪敢不从，当然是嬴政说什么他便如何做。
徐福疼得额上冒出了冷汗，但是为了维持一贯的姿态，哪怕再疼，徐福也都是一脸淡漠的表情，更没喊上半句疼。引得那侍医看着徐福的时候，心中暗暗感叹，徐庶长实在厉害！若是换做旁人，恐怕早恨不得在王上面前哀声呼痛了吧。
袖口被剪开，被刺中的皮肉露了出来，那一块皮肤被血色覆盖，难以看清伤口。正是如此，才更给人以触目惊心之感。
徐福一路顺风顺水太久了，还未受过这样的伤，他面上虽然不显，但手上却忍不住狠狠掐了嬴政一把。
徐福都不记得当时自己为什么要挡在那个刺客的面前了。明明大殿中四处都是人，那么多人就算是组成人墙，也不可能让刺客伤到嬴政啊，自己这个毫无武力值的弱鸡为什么要往上冲？
徐福真是后悔不已。
嬴政满眼就剩下了心疼，见那侍医半天都处理不好伤口，他烦躁地拧起眉，直接将徐福打横抱起，往寝宫而去了。
面瘫着脸的徐福：……
侍从忙追上去，低声道：“王上，那刺客……”
“此事交予赵高处理。”嬴政沉声道。
赵高？徐福心中为那刺客默哀了会儿。赵高在审讯拷打上，应当并非什么良善之辈。不然的话，嬴政也不会将这个交给赵高了。
侍从点了点头，忙派人去请赵高过来，等他回到方才的大殿中时，见那公子嘉目光极为漠然，撤去温和的气质后，公子嘉望着使臣和刺客的方向，那眼神令人暗自心惊。
侍从低下了头，暗暗道，这又如何？赵国行刺秦王已经坐实了，这公子嘉还不如忧心一下自己的小命吧。
不久后赵高走进殿中，见赵成跟个无头苍蝇似的乱撞，不由得皱了皱眉，深深地看了他一眼，然后才走到了那公子嘉的跟前，冷声道：“带走。”
赵高对公子嘉竟是连半分寒暄都无。
公子嘉的心顿时沉了下去，这是……秦王的意思吗？不再将他视作赵国公子。
·
伤口周围的血污被清理干净之后，皮肉微微泛白的伤口终于清晰地暴露在了视线之中。徐福光是看着都觉得自己心揪着疼了。
嬴政的眉头皱得越来越紧了，但他却一直盯着徐福的伤口，半点没有要移开目光的意思。
直到侍医将伤口处理完毕，嬴政才跟着松了一口气。
徐福一直紧绷着的身体缓缓放松下来，他这才想起，自己的手还捏在嬴政的胳膊上，他抽回手，瞥了一眼嬴政的手臂，有些想要掀起他的袖子看一看，但是又有些迟疑。哦，他心中的火气还在那儿压着呢。能这么快就算了吗？
嬴政像是根本没注意到自己的手臂被掐了多久一样，他命人取来新的衣袍，给徐福披上。
痛感越发地明晰，徐福的嘴唇发白，恨不得就这样躺下去。
嬴政察觉到他的不适，立即就将人平放了下去，还顺带给他盖上了被子，但嬴政却并未急于离去，他沉声问道：“方才为何要挡在那人跟前？”
徐福有气无力地答道：“你忘记我是做什么了的吗？”
“你从他的脸上看出了什么不对劲？”嬴政惊诧地问。
“不错。”
但嬴政脸上的表情却并未转好，不仅如此，他的脸色反而更沉了，“既然知晓他是什么样的人，怎么还要上前挡住？旁边就是宫人内侍，你应当出声呼喊才是。”嬴政心中其实是忍不住觉得想笑，但又忍不住怒气磅礴。
徐福之所以会有如此动作，定是觉得那人会伤害自己，这才想也不想就将人挡住了。徐福的维护令嬴政很是受用。但若是用徐福受伤换来的，他便宁可不要了。
“赵国使臣着实该死。”嬴政阴沉沉地道。
徐福听见这句话，就知道那赵国使臣的下场基本已经被定下来了。
徐福不知道那使臣是不是无辜之人，但是用这个时代的刑法来看，他是注定要死了。毕竟是他将刺客带了进来，他一身的嫌疑已经注定洗不掉了。赵王何必如此呢？赵王就算昏聩，也不至于昏聩到这般地步吧？
徐福突然想起了另外一人，他看着嬴政，低声问道：“公子嘉呢？”
嬴政的面色顿时便阴沉得如同暴风雨前的天空，“……怎么问起他来了？”公子嘉啊，寡人一定会宰了他啊。你都受伤了还想着问他的境况，寡人能不宰了他吗？
而徐福看着嬴政的面色，顿时又脑补向了另一个方向。连问都不能问？公子嘉从前与嬴政到底有什么年少情谊？那公子嘉总不至于是嬴政心头的白月光吧？徐福皱了皱眉，不过很快就将自己安慰住了。公子嘉长得没他好看！
徐福压下心头的不快，想起了正事。
“阿政，公子嘉此人不能死。”
嬴政心头呵呵。寡人转过身去就能悄无声息把人弄死，保你以后都记不起这个人！
“阿政，我觉得公子嘉可以发挥更大的作用，而不是让他死在这里。”徐福顿了顿，面无表情的，用毫无起伏的声音说道：“当然，要看你舍不舍得了。”
嬴政被他这番话说得一头雾水，不过他还是立即道：“面对你，寡人何时舍不得满足你的时候？”
“有啊，就比如我去棉诸的时候……”
嬴政脸色一黑，“这二者不能混为一谈。”
徐福轻飘飘地点了点头。
嬴政觉得徐福面色不大好，立即将话茬又引了回去，“你想用公子嘉做什么？”
徐福点了点头，然后不动声色地打量着嬴政的表情。
奇怪，竟是半点变化也没有。难道公子嘉压根就不是他心头的什么白月光朱砂痣？徐福疑惑了。若是并无半分情谊的话，那一日嬴政怎么会在公子嘉跟前那样好说话？
徐福低声道：“不战而胜，方能为秦国节约兵力和粮食。”
“你要用公子嘉来不战而胜？公子嘉在赵国越来越不受宠了，不然也不会被送到秦国来。你欲拿他如何战胜？”嬴政不解。
徐福的思维可就比他简单多了，他淡淡一挑眉，哪怕是苍白的面容，也难掩他那瞬间不经意间表露出来的风情，“既然不受宠，那就把地位转换一下，让别人来等着他去宠爱好了。”
你既然当个公子不受宠，那你还当什么公子啊？直接去当君王啊！掀翻你爹的政权啊！
徐福甚至冥冥中觉得，自己这次受伤其实就是个很好的契机，可以让他们放心和公子嘉合作。因为公子嘉已经无路可选了。
徐福甚至觉得，如果自己没看错，公子嘉的确是聪明人的话，那么不消多说，他自己就会凑上来，他会竭力为自己寻找一条生路的。
徐福骤然仰头看着嬴政，张了张嘴，本来想说与嬴政一同去审个公子嘉，但是突然间他又改变了想法。
如果他不去的话，嬴政与公子嘉会弄出什么幺蛾子来吗？徐福觉得这正是考验嬴政的好时机啊！所以徐福闭上了眼，也闭上了嘴，什么话都不说了。
原本聚精会神等着徐福说话的嬴政蓦地一呆，徐福这是什么意思？难道是表达对自己的不满？
嬴政不由分说将这个过错也顺便推到了公子嘉的身上。反正都是他的错。
不等嬴政出去审讯人，就先有内侍恭谨地跪在嬴政的跟前，低声道：“公子嘉求见王上，说求王上饶他一命。”
徐福“唰”地睁开了眼。
果然，他就说公子嘉应当是个聪明人，并不如他表现出来的那样天真单纯好欺负。
嬴政回头看了徐福一眼，见他听见公子嘉求见之后，顿时便精神（？）了起来，心中再度燃起了妒火。公子嘉有什么地方值得徐福去关注的？
尽管嬴政心中很清楚，徐福不可能对公子嘉有男女之间的情谊，但光是这样就已经令他心中极为不爽了。
能够享受徐福这般特殊对待的，应当只有自己才是。
嬴政本要去其它的殿中召见公子嘉，但是徐福一句话就打消了他的念头，“不如我与阿政一同见公子嘉吧，我受了伤，也正需要他给出解释来。”
徐福这番话，嬴政能拒绝吗？不能。
嬴政便立即召见了公子嘉。
公子嘉是被人押着进来的，头上的冠歪歪倒着，发丝散乱，看上去狼狈得根本不像是赵国公子。公子嘉脸上的表情有些憔悴。殿中的宫人看得都忍不住心中叹气。赵国实在是太找死了，这是何必呢？
而徐福只看了一眼，就不得不佩服公子嘉的本事。
公子嘉这样狼狈，殿中的人见了他这副模样，难免不觉得同情，而同情往往就是心软的开头。那么之后，公子嘉身上遭受的怒火就会减轻无数倍了。
嬴政如今看着公子嘉极为不顺眼，他目光冰冷地盯着公子嘉，“你要面见寡人，可是还有话要说？”
公子嘉再不顾忌半点礼仪，就这样在嬴政跟前跪了下来，“王上，嘉在秦宫中素来安分，并不曾与外界传递过消息，这刺客之事与嘉实在无关啊！不过那刺客终归是赵国人……”公子嘉面带痛色，“若王上觉得不够解恨，那边将嘉当做那刺客来处置吧。”
嬴政刚想说“好啊”，徐福突然就出声了，“公子嘉人中龙凤，若是就这样处置了，岂不是可惜？”
于是嬴政只得将那两个简短有力的字给憋了回去。
公子嘉看向了徐福，苦笑道：“庶长谬赞了，嘉还不值当。”
“怎会不值当呢？”徐福撑着床榻勉强坐了起来，嬴政大步走上前，捞住徐福的腰，直接将他带到了怀中，看上去动作粗暴，但实际上，他小心翼翼地避开了徐福的伤处。实在少有人能比他更温柔了。
只是单看嬴政那张冷硬的面容，没人敢去想象他温柔起来，会是什么样子的。
“公子若是做了赵王，那可就是万分值当的。”徐福慢条斯理地说。
公子嘉身体一颤，抬起头来，看着徐福，声音微微哆嗦，“庶长这是何意？”
徐福并未看他。徐福懒洋洋地就这样倚在嬴政的怀中，继续淡淡道：“没有何意，我只是觉得公子更适合做赵王。我听闻赵王欲立公子迁为太子……”
公子嘉的脸色登时就变了。
徐福的这串话才是真正踩到了他的脉门之上。
“公子如今心中可还能舒坦起来？”徐福漫不经心地问道。
公子嘉闭唇不语。
而嬴政也始终未出声，他将所有权利都交给了徐福，不管此时徐福要说什么，他都是不会插手的。
徐福的语调依旧是不紧不慢的，往往能给人的心理上造成较大的心理压力，“我还当公子会求见王上，正是因为公子心中已经有了决断。”
公子嘉深深地看了一眼徐福，他的眼神终于起了变化，而不再是伪装成那个单纯的公子嘉了。“庶长如此说，可是有何提议？”
要知道如今宫中宠姬倡后当道，赵王对她千依百顺，如今又欲立公子迁为太子，而他却只能在秦国做个质子，还要时时忍受性命的威胁。这样大的差距，叫他心中如何不难受？
“我认为，应当是公子嘉有话要先与王上说吧。”徐福稳稳地坐在嬴政的腿上，低声道。
公子嘉的脸色变了变，“……你说得不错。”公子嘉当机立断，在嬴政跟前跪了下来，高声道：“请王上助我夺得赵王之位，待到那一日，便是赵国向秦称臣之时。”
嬴政挑了挑眉没说话。
徐福转头冲嬴政眨了眨眼，其中带了点儿连他自己都没注意到的邀功意味。
会生出这个想法，徐福本也是为了嬴政，如果可以节省成本，能不打仗就不打仗，那自然是最好的。公子嘉是个聪明人，经历种种之后，待他再回到赵王宫，背后又有秦国支持，他岂能还坐不上赵王的位置？
嬴政不喜欢公子嘉，自然也不乐意伸手帮他，于是嬴政并无半分心动，反而问起了公子嘉，“若是你背信弃义，那寡人该如何？”这样的例子并不少见，出于为自己铺路的心理，将敌人给放回去了，谁知道转眼就被对方给哄骗了，反倒成了输家。
徐福只管提议，现在他可不管中间公子嘉会不会背信弃义，因为他相信嬴政的驭下手段，定然能拿捏住公子嘉的。
就这样将公子嘉送回赵国去，多好。
公子嘉看向徐福，道：“王上最信任的人便是徐庶长了，若是徐庶长能同我前往……”
嬴政的脸立刻就拉了下来，“不行。”
公子嘉轻叹一口气，“那，那我要将何物献于王上呢？”
嬴政皱了皱眉，低声道：“赵国之中可有鼎？一只极为特殊的鼎？若是寻到，便与寡人送来，那时寡便能信你了。”
徐福靠在嬴政的怀中，听完了这串话，胸口顿时鼓鼓囊囊，酸酸涨涨的……
还有点儿小感动。
公子嘉面色尴尬，道：“赵国之中鼎有许多，不知您要的是……”
徐福立即叫来宫人，让他们将自己的鼎搬过来，公子嘉将鼎抓在手里打量了许久，将花纹和外形暗暗记在心中，“若是我见到了，自然会收起来送到秦王跟前来。”
“你的死罪，寡人便给你免了。”
公子嘉面上闪过喜色，但是嬴政没有说完话，他就不敢起身。
“你说的，寡人希望你也能做到。”嬴政不再看他，此时他与徐福的思维重叠了。送回赵国去也好。祸害赵王去呗。
“多谢王上！”公子嘉深深一拜，口中的称呼也发生了转变。
称嬴政为王上，可见公子嘉已然视自己为嬴政的臣。
“来人，带他下去。”
有宫人上来将公子嘉带走了，殿中很快便又安静了下来，碍于还有宫人在场，徐福费了很大的力气，才抑制住了打呵欠的冲动。
公子嘉走后不久，赵高便也过来求见了。徐福和嬴政都知晓，定然是刺客那里审问出了什么，于是赶紧让人进来了。
赵高面带笑容，行过礼后，一一道来。
原来那使臣还真知道刺客的来历，只是他选择了装瞎，皆因为那刺客是赵国倡后的人。
倡后是谁？赵王的宠姬，将曾经的王后都给斗倒了，以一介舞姬之身，登到了如今的位置上，而她的儿子公子迁更是备受赵王喜爱，几度欲立其为太子。原王后与原太子公子嘉也并非善茬。只是公子嘉很不幸地被派到了秦国为质子，于是赵王在国内才能顺心地准备立公子迁为太子。他们都想着，反正公子嘉这辈子也很难回去了。
倡后在赵王那里何等受宠，可见她是个极为漂亮也极有手段的女人，就是这个女人在挑拨君王与将军之间关系时，也极为厉害。但她却有一个弱点。单看她费尽心思算计李牧就知晓了，她是个眼界狭窄，只能在内宅中吃开的女人。不然的话，她也不会蠢到派刺客来刺杀嬴政。她以为嬴政一怒之下，就会立即斩了公子嘉吗？她怎么也不想一想，若是嬴政当真怒了，到时候打的可不是公子嘉，而是赵国。
赵国还能经受得起这样的重击吗？
当了太久的宠姬，倡后已经越发地愚蠢了，难及当年华阳夫人的万分之一。同是极为受宠的女人，但华阳夫人是如何做的？华阳夫人能受嬴政尊敬，成为秦国太后。而徐福看，那倡后恐怕说不得是要得个凄惨境遇的。
赵高交代了许多话，事无巨细。
嬴政也没有了再审的兴趣，当夜那二人便没了性命。
等到第二日，公子嘉便从咸阳出发，往着邯郸回去了。也不知道那倡后见不到使臣和刺客，却独独见到公子嘉时，该是何等的心情？
chapters.title: 第173章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu was stunned for a moment and raised his hand, wanting to touch Ying Zheng's nose, but he forgot that he was injured. As he lifted his arm, he pulled at his wound, and his hand instantly dropped back down.

Just then, the palace physician came sprinting into the hall. Seeing Xu Fu’s blood-covered hands and the blood on the Qin King’s face, the physician’s legs wobbled; he nearly collapsed at the entrance from the sheer shock.

"Your Majesty! Are you unharmed?" The physician rushed forward, secretly feeling lucky that he had arrived so quickly. If he provided treatment in time, he might even receive a reward.

"Check on Xu Fu first." Ying Zheng’s face was dark as he picked up a silk cloth and slowly wiped the blood from his face. It was a ridiculous action, but when he did it, it felt different—it carried an aura that made others afraid to look directly at him.

The physician knew what kind of status the Chief Shuzhang held in the King's heart, so he didn't dare to argue and immediately stepped forward to examine Xu Fu.

The sleeve was carefully rolled up, but because it was slightly tight, it was a struggle to get it halfway up.

Beneath the sleeve, a section of snow-white arm stained with specks of blood entered Ying Zheng’s vision. Ying Zheng suddenly felt a surge of blood rushing through his chest. His expression darkened, and he said in a low voice, "Cut the sleeve open directly from the wound." Rolling it up bit by bit was too torturous for those watching.

Of course, there was another reason: Ying Zheng didn't want others to see it.

Even though he was injured, Ying Zheng felt that Xu Fu was filled with an irresistible temptation from head to toe. Just the sight of that exposed, snow-white arm was enough to make his heart stir.

The physician dared not disobey; naturally, he did exactly as Ying Zheng commanded.

Xu Fu broke into a cold sweat from the pain, but to maintain his usual demeanor, he kept an indifferent expression and didn't utter a single sound of pain. This led the physician to secretly marvel at Xu Fu as he watched him; the Chief Shuzhang was truly remarkable! If it were anyone else, they would have likely been wailing in pain before the King long ago.

The sleeve was cut open, revealing the pierced flesh. That patch of skin was covered in blood, making it hard to see the wound clearly. It was precisely because of this that it looked all the more shocking.

Xu Fu had been sailing smoothly for too long and had never suffered such an injury. Although he didn't show it on his face, he couldn't help but pinch Ying Zheng hard.

Xu Fu couldn't even remember why he had jumped in front of that assassin at the time. There were people everywhere in the hall; even if they had formed a human wall, it would have been impossible for the assassin to hurt Ying Zheng. Why did a weakling like him, with zero combat ability, rush forward?

Xu Fu was filled with regret.

Ying Zheng’s eyes were full of heartache. Seeing that the physician was taking forever to treat the wound, he frowned in irritation, picked Xu Fu up horizontally, and headed toward the sleeping quarters.

The stone-faced Xu Fu: ...

An attendant hurriedly chased after them and whispered, "Your Majesty, that assassin..."

"Leave this matter to Zhao Gao," Ying Zheng said in a deep voice.

Zhao Gao? Xu Fu silently offered a prayer for the assassin. Zhao Gao was likely not a kind soul when it came to interrogation and torture. Otherwise, Ying Zheng wouldn't have handed this task to him.

The attendant nodded and hurriedly sent someone to summon Zhao Gao. When he returned to the hall, he saw that Gongzi Jia’s gaze was extremely indifferent. Once his gentle demeanor was stripped away, the way Gongzi Jia looked at the envoy and the assassin was enough to make one shudder.

The attendant lowered his head and thought to himself, so what? It was confirmed that the Zhao state had attempted to assassinate the Qin King; Gongzi Jia would be better off worrying about his own life.

Not long after, Zhao Gao walked into the hall. Seeing Zhao Cheng bumping around like a headless fly, he frowned, gave him a deep look, and then walked up to Gongzi Jia, saying coldly, "Take him away."

Zhao Gao didn't even offer a single word of pleasantry to Gongzi Jia.

Gongzi Jia’s heart sank instantly. Was this... the King of Qin’s intention? To no longer regard him as a prince of the Zhao state.

·

After the bloodstains around the wound were cleaned away, the slightly pale flesh of the wound was finally clearly exposed. Just looking at it made Xu Fu feel a tug of pain in his own heart.

Ying Zheng’s brow furrowed tighter and tighter, but he kept his eyes fixed on Xu Fu’s wound, showing no intention of looking away.

Only when the physician finished treating the wound did Ying Zheng finally let out a sigh of relief.

Xu Fu’s body, which had been tense the whole time, slowly relaxed. Only then did he remember that his hand was still pinching Ying Zheng’s arm. He pulled his hand back and glanced at Ying Zheng’s arm, wanting to lift his sleeve to take a look, but he hesitated. Oh, the anger in his heart was still simmering. Could he just let it go so quickly?

Ying Zheng seemed not to notice how long his arm had been pinched; he ordered someone to bring a new robe and draped it over Xu Fu.

The pain became more distinct, and Xu Fu’s lips turned pale; he felt like just lying down right there.

Noticing his discomfort, Ying Zheng immediately laid him flat and even covered him with a quilt. However, Ying Zheng did not leave in a hurry. He asked in a deep voice, "Why did you block that person earlier?"

Xu Fu answered weakly, "Have you forgotten what I do?"

"Did you see something wrong on his face?" Ying Zheng asked in surprise.

"Indeed."

But the expression on Ying Zheng’s face did not improve; instead, it darkened further. "Since you knew what kind of person he was, why did you still go up to block him? There were palace servants right beside you; you should have called out." Ying Zheng actually wanted to laugh, but he couldn't help the surging anger.

The reason Xu Fu acted that way must have been because he thought the man would hurt him, so he had jumped in to block it without a second thought. Xu Fu’s protection was very gratifying to Ying Zheng. But if it came at the cost of Xu Fu’s injury, he would rather not have it.

"The Zhao envoy truly deserves to die," Ying Zheng said gloomily.

Hearing this, Xu Fu knew that the fate of the Zhao envoy was basically sealed.

Xu Fu didn't know if the envoy was innocent, but by the laws of this era, he was destined to die. After all, he was the one who brought the assassin in; his suspicion could never be cleared. Why would the King of Zhao do this? Even if the King of Zhao was muddled, he shouldn't be muddled to this extent, right?

Xu Fu suddenly remembered someone else. He looked at Ying Zheng and asked in a low voice, "What about Gongzi Jia?"

Ying Zheng’s expression instantly turned as dark as the sky before a storm. "...Why are you asking about him?" Gongzi Jia, huh? I will definitely slaughter him. You’re already injured and you’re still thinking about asking about his situation—how can I not slaughter him?

Seeing Ying Zheng’s expression, Xu Fu immediately imagined a different scenario. He couldn't even ask about him? What kind of youthful bond did Gongzi Jia have with Ying Zheng in the past? Could it be that Gongzi Jia was the "white moonlight" in Ying Zheng’s heart? Xu Fu frowned, but he quickly comforted himself. Gongzi Jia wasn't as good-looking as he was!

Xu Fu suppressed the unhappiness in his heart and thought about the important business.

"A-Zheng, Gongzi Jia cannot die."

Ying Zheng scoffed internally. I could turn around and kill him silently, ensuring you never remember this person again!

"A-Zheng, I think Gongzi Jia can serve a greater purpose rather than just dying here." Xu Fu paused, his face expressionless, and said in a flat voice, "Of course, it depends on whether you are willing to let him go."

Ying Zheng was confused by these words, but he immediately said, "When have I ever been unwilling to satisfy you?"

"There was a time, like when I went to Mianzhu..."

Ying Zheng’s face turned black. "Those two things cannot be mentioned in the same breath."

Xu Fu nodded lightly.

Sensing that Xu Fu didn't look well, Ying Zheng immediately steered the conversation back. "What do you want to use Gongzi Jia for?"

Xu Fu nodded and then calmly observed Ying Zheng’s expression.

Strange, there wasn't even the slightest change. Could it be that Gongzi Jia wasn't his "white moonlight" or "cinnabar mole" at all? Xu Fu was puzzled. If there was no bond at all, why was Ying Zheng so easy to talk to in front of Gongzi Jia that day?

Xu Fu said in a low voice, "Winning without a fight is the only way to save the Qin state’s troops and provisions."

"You want to use Gongzi Jia to win without a fight? Gongzi Jia is becoming less and less favored in Zhao; otherwise, he wouldn't have been sent to Qin. How do you intend to win with him?" Ying Zheng was puzzled.

Xu Fu’s thinking was much simpler than his. He raised an eyebrow faintly, and even with his pale face, he couldn't hide the charm that inadvertently revealed itself. "Since he is not favored, then let’s change his status and let others wait for him to bestow favor upon them instead."

If you’re not favored as a prince, then why be a prince? Go straight to being the King! Overthrow your father’s regime!

Xu Fu even felt, in some mysterious way, that his injury this time was actually a good opportunity to let them cooperate with Gongzi Jia with peace of mind. Because Gongzi Jia had no other path to choose.

Xu Fu even felt that if he hadn't misjudged him, and if Gongzi Jia was indeed a smart man, then without needing to say much, he would come forward himself; he would do his utmost to find a way to survive.

Xu Fu suddenly looked up at Ying Zheng and opened his mouth, wanting to say he would go with Ying Zheng to interrogate Gongzi Jia, but he suddenly changed his mind.

If he didn't go, would Ying Zheng and Gongzi Jia cause any trouble? Xu Fu felt this was the perfect time to test Ying Zheng! So, Xu Fu closed his eyes and his mouth, saying nothing more.

Ying Zheng, who had been focused and waiting for Xu Fu to speak, was suddenly stunned. What did Xu Fu mean by this? Was he expressing his dissatisfaction?

Ying Zheng couldn't help but push this fault onto Gongzi Jia as well. It was his fault anyway.

Before Ying Zheng could go out to interrogate the man, an attendant knelt respectfully before him and whispered, "Gongzi Jia requests an audience with Your Majesty, saying he begs Your Majesty to spare his life."

Xu Fu’s eyes snapped open.

Sure enough, he had said Gongzi Jia was a smart man, not as naive, simple, and easy to bully as he appeared.

Ying Zheng looked back at Xu Fu and saw that he had become spirited (?) upon hearing that Gongzi Jia requested an audience, and jealousy flared in his heart again. What was there about Gongzi Jia worth Xu Fu’s attention?

Although Ying Zheng knew very well that Xu Fu couldn't have romantic feelings for Gongzi Jia, just the thought of it made him extremely uncomfortable.

The only one who should be able to enjoy such special treatment from Xu Fu was himself.

Ying Zheng had intended to summon Gongzi Jia to another hall, but one sentence from Xu Fu dispelled that thought: "Why don't I see Gongzi Jia with you, A-Zheng? I’m injured, and I need him to provide an explanation."

Could Ying Zheng refuse this request from Xu Fu? He could not.

Ying Zheng immediately summoned Gongzi Jia.

Gongzi Jia was brought in under guard, his crown tilted, his hair disheveled; he looked so wretched that he didn't look like a Zhao prince at all. The expression on Gongzi Jia’s face was haggard. The palace servants in the hall couldn't help but sigh inwardly. The Zhao state was truly courting death; what was the point of this?

Xu Fu only had to take one look to admire Gongzi Jia’s ability.

With Gongzi Jia looking so wretched, it was hard for those in the hall not to feel sympathy, and sympathy was often the beginning of a soft heart. Then, the anger directed at Gongzi Jia would be reduced countless times over.

Ying Zheng found Gongzi Jia extremely unpleasant to look at now. He stared at him with icy eyes. "You requested an audience with me; do you have something left to say?"

Gongzi Jia no longer cared about etiquette and knelt before Ying Zheng. "Your Majesty, I have always been well-behaved in the Qin palace and have never passed information to the outside world. This assassin matter has nothing to do with me! But the assassin is, after all, a man of Zhao..." Gongzi Jia’s face showed pain. "If Your Majesty feels that is not enough to vent your anger, then treat me as that assassin."

Ying Zheng was just about to say "Very well," when Xu Fu suddenly spoke up, "Gongzi Jia is a phoenix among men; wouldn't it be a pity if he were disposed of just like that?"

Thus, Ying Zheng had to swallow those two short, powerful words.

Gongzi Jia looked at Xu Fu and smiled bitterly. "The Chief Shuzhang is too kind; I am not worth it."

"How could you not be worth it?" Xu Fu propped himself up on the bed with difficulty. Ying Zheng strode forward, caught Xu Fu by the waist, and pulled him directly into his arms. The action looked rough, but in reality, he carefully avoided Xu Fu’s wound. Few people could be more gentle than him.

It was just that looking at Ying Zheng’s cold, hard face, no one dared to imagine what he would be like when he was gentle.

"If the Gongzi were to become the King of Zhao, then it would be worth it indeed," Xu Fu said slowly.

Gongzi Jia’s body trembled. He looked up at Xu Fu, his voice trembling slightly. "What does the Chief Shuzhang mean by this?"

Xu Fu didn't look at him. He leaned lazily in Ying Zheng’s arms and continued calmly, "Nothing in particular. I just think the Gongzi is better suited to be the King of Zhao. I heard that the King of Zhao intends to make Gongzi Qian the Crown Prince..."

Gongzi Jia’s face changed instantly.

This string of words from Xu Fu had truly hit his sore spot.

"Can you still feel at ease in your heart now, Gongzi?" Xu Fu asked nonchalantly.

Gongzi Jia kept his lips sealed and said nothing.

Ying Zheng also remained silent throughout. He had handed all authority to Xu Fu; no matter what Xu Fu wanted to say, he would not interfere.

Xu Fu’s tone remained unhurried, which often caused significant psychological pressure on others. "I assumed you requested an audience with the King precisely because you had already made a decision in your heart."

Gongzi Jia looked deeply at Xu Fu. His eyes finally changed; he was no longer pretending to be that simple Gongzi Jia. "Since the Chief Shuzhang says so, do you have any suggestions?"

One had to know that the favored concubine, Lady Chang, was currently in power in the palace, the King of Zhao was obedient to her every whim, and now he intended to make Gongzi Qian the Crown Prince, while he could only be a hostage in Qin, constantly enduring threats to his life. With such a huge disparity, how could he not feel bitter?

"I believe it is Gongzi Jia who has something to say to the King first," Xu Fu said, sitting steadily on Ying Zheng’s lap.

Gongzi Jia’s expression shifted. "...You are right." Gongzi Jia made a prompt decision, knelt before Ying Zheng, and said loudly, "Please, Your Majesty, help me seize the throne of Zhao. When that day comes, it will be the day the Zhao state submits to Qin."

Ying Zheng raised an eyebrow but didn't speak.

Xu Fu turned his head and winked at Ying Zheng, with a hint of seeking credit that even he himself hadn't noticed.

Coming up with this idea, Xu Fu was ultimately doing it for Ying Zheng. If costs could be saved and war avoided, that would naturally be best. Gongzi Jia was a smart man; after experiencing all this, when he returned to the Zhao palace with the support of Qin behind him, how could he not secure the position of King of Zhao?

Ying Zheng didn't like Gongzi Jia, so naturally, he wasn't happy to help him, so he wasn't moved in the slightest. Instead, he asked Gongzi Jia, "What if you break your promise? What should I do then?" Such examples were not rare. Out of a desire to pave their own way, they would release an enemy, only to be deceived by the other party in the blink of an eye, becoming the loser instead.

Xu Fu only made the suggestion; he didn't care if Gongzi Jia would break his promise in the middle, because he believed in Ying Zheng’s ability to control his subordinates; he would definitely be able to handle Gongzi Jia.

Just like that, sending Gongzi Jia back to Zhao was a good idea.

Gongzi Jia looked at Xu Fu and said, "The person the King trusts most is the Chief Shuzhang. If the Chief Shuzhang could accompany me..."

Ying Zheng’s face immediately darkened. "No."

Gongzi Jia sighed lightly. "Then, what should I offer to the King?"

Ying Zheng frowned and said in a low voice, "Is there a cauldron in the Zhao state? A very special cauldron? If you find it, send it to me, and then I will be able to trust you."

Xu Fu leaned in Ying Zheng’s arms, listening to this, his chest feeling full and achy...

And a little touched.

Gongzi Jia looked embarrassed. "There are many cauldrons in Zhao; I don't know which one you want..."

Xu Fu immediately called for a palace servant to bring his own cauldron over. Gongzi Jia took the cauldron and examined it for a long time, secretly memorizing the patterns and shape. "If I see it, I will naturally collect it and send it to the King of Qin."

"I will spare you from your death sentence."

A look of joy flashed across Gongzi Jia’s face, but since Ying Zheng hadn't finished speaking, he didn't dare to stand up.

"What you said, I hope you can also achieve." Ying Zheng stopped looking at him. At this moment, his thinking overlapped with Xu Fu’s. Sending him back to Zhao was fine. Let him go and be a scourge to the King of Zhao.

"Thank you, Your Majesty!" Gongzi Jia bowed deeply, and the way he addressed him had changed.

Calling Ying Zheng "Your Majesty" showed that Gongzi Jia already regarded himself as Ying Zheng’s subject.

"Someone, take him away."

Palace servants came up and took Gongzi Jia away. The hall soon became quiet again. With palace servants still present, Xu Fu used great effort to suppress the urge to yawn.

Not long after Gongzi Jia left, Zhao Gao also came to request an audience. Both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng knew that they must have interrogated something from the assassin, so they quickly let him in.

Zhao Gao wore a smile, performed the salute, and recounted everything one by one.

It turned out that the envoy really did know the assassin’s background, but he chose to play dumb because the assassin was a person of Lady Chang of Zhao.

Who was Lady Chang? The King of Zhao’s favored concubine who had defeated the former Queen and risen from the status of a mere dancing girl to her current position. Her son, Gongzi Qian, was deeply loved by the King of Zhao and had several times been considered for the position of Crown Prince. The former Queen and the former Crown Prince, Gongzi Jia, were no soft targets either. It was just that Gongzi Jia had been unluckily sent to Qin as a hostage, so the King of Zhao could comfortably prepare to make Gongzi Qian the Crown Prince back home. They all thought that, anyway, it would be difficult for Gongzi Jia to return in this lifetime.

How favored Lady Chang was by the King of Zhao showed that she was a very beautiful and capable woman; she was also very skilled at sowing discord between the King and his generals. But she had a weakness. Just looking at how she painstakingly plotted against Li Mu, one could tell she was a woman with a narrow vision who could only thrive in the inner chambers. Otherwise, she wouldn't have been stupid enough to send an assassin to kill Ying Zheng. Did she think that Ying Zheng would immediately execute Gongzi Jia in a fit of rage? Why didn't she think about the fact that if Ying Zheng were truly angry, the one who would be hit wouldn't be Gongzi Jia, but the Zhao state?

Could the Zhao state withstand such a heavy blow?

Having been a favored concubine for too long, Lady Chang had become increasingly stupid, not even a ten-thousandth as capable as Lady Huayang had been. Both were highly favored women, but what had Lady Huayang done? Lady Huayang was respected by Ying Zheng and became the Queen Dowager of Qin. But in Xu Fu’s view, Lady Chang would likely meet a miserable end.

Zhao Gao reported many things, down to the smallest detail.

Ying Zheng had no interest in further interrogation, and that night, both of them lost their lives.

The next day, Gongzi Jia departed from Xianyang and headed back to Handan. One wondered what Lady Chang’s mood would be when she saw Gongzi Jia returning alone, without the envoy or the assassin?

chapters.title: 第174章
chapters.translated_text:
In the sixteenth year of King Zheng of Qin, an envoy from Zhao attempted to assassinate the King of Qin. The King was furious, but mindful of their past ties, he sent the hostage Prince Jia back to Zhao, and the Qin army once again marched against the state of Zhao.

The Qin generals, who had barely had time to rest, were forced to lead their troops into battle once more.

Everyone believed that this war would not actually happen; the Qin army needed time to recuperate, and this mobilization was merely for show. Furthermore, the great Zhao general Li Mu had been repeatedly reprimanded, and the Zhao army was exhausted. How could such sides possibly engage in a real war?

Yet, just when everyone was convinced that no battle would take place, the Zhao army suddenly rose up, full of vigor and determination, ready to clash with the Qin forces.

Where did the King of Zhao find the confidence and courage for this?

When the news returned, the reactions at court were mixed. Some cursed Zhao and demanded a harsh retaliation, while others worried that Qin should not have pushed Zhao to such an extreme. With such conflicting views, arguments were inevitable.

Ying Zheng was a monarch with strong convictions; he would never waver in his decisions just because of the differing opinions of his officials. No matter how heated the arguments became in court, Ying Zheng did not utter a single word. After the small court session ended, Xu Fu learned of the matter.

As a *Siche Shuzhang* (a high-ranking official), Xu Fu was supposed to be informed of such news. If it weren't for the fact that he detested attending court in the winter, he would likely have been standing among the officials in the small court session.

After Zhao Cheng spoke with Xu Fu, Xu Fu remained silent for a long time.

Xu Fu fell into deep thought. He could not understand why Zhao had suddenly changed its attitude. However, a man like the King of Zhao would dare to challenge Qin again as long as he had the slightest bit of confidence or backing. The King of Zhao had never wanted to submit to Qin, and he would seize any opportunity to resist.

Xu Fu was eager to know what kind of opportunity he was holding in his hands now.

"Shuzhang, the King requests your presence," an attendant walked into the hall and said respectfully to Xu Fu.

Xu Fu had been ignoring Ying Zheng for the past few days. He originally wanted to refuse, but the thought of the situation in Zhao made him change his mind. "...Hmm, let's go." At a time like this, Ying Zheng would never summon him for personal matters. It was highly likely he wanted to discuss the situation in Zhao.

At times like this, Xu Fu felt that there were advantages to men being together.

If he were a woman in this era, he would likely lack such freedom and find it much harder to intervene in the military and political affairs of Qin.

Soon, guided by the attendant, Xu Fu arrived at the hall and immediately spotted a familiar figure.

The surprise on Xu Fu's face lasted only for a fleeting moment.

He had not expected Yao Jia to return so quickly. Could it be that he had information regarding Zhao?

Xu Fu unconsciously quickened his pace, walked up to Yao Jia, and asked, "Does Yao Jia know who is leading the Zhao army?" Xu Fu was fairly certain that the King of Zhao would not send Li Mu or Sima Shang again. In fact, those two were likely not far from death.

Yao Jia looked at Xu Fu, then at Ying Zheng. "The King might not believe me when I say the name."

Xu Fu already understood. "Is it Xiong Yi?" Because the incident of dressing in women's clothes was too embarrassing, Xu Fu had not told Ying Zheng about it after returning to Xianyang. He had only mentioned that Xiong Yi was still alive and in Zhao.

Hearing this, Ying Zheng frowned. "Him? He can lead an army?" Ying Zheng did not believe this.

Although Xiong Yi had some ability, it was nowhere near enough to support him as a general. What kind of education had he received in the first half of his life? It had nothing to do with leading troops in battle. Even if he started late, how could he have pushed out Li Mu and Sima Shang in just a few years, and made the King of Zhao rely on him?

Ying Zheng said coldly, "There must be something fishy behind this."

Xu Fu had already guessed where the trick lay.

If it were Xiong Yi, then everything was possible. After all, he still possessed the things left behind by Zheng You'an. Who knew how much future technology was among those items? If Zheng You'an was even slightly capable of producing gunpowder, in an era dominated by cold weapons, it would undoubtedly have immense destructive power and could sweep across other nations.

If Xiong Yi had shown this power to the King of Zhao...

Then it was no surprise that the King of Zhao would trust him.

"Then, what about the matter I entrusted to you?" Xu Fu asked, not avoiding Ying Zheng's presence at all.

Yao Jia had initially thought this was a highly private matter, but seeing Xu Fu speak of it in front of Ying Zheng, he gained a new understanding of the relationship between the two.

"I have verified that such a thing does exist, but it will take some effort to get our hands on it."

"What thing?" Hearing the two discuss something he knew nothing about, Ying Zheng's brow furrowed immediately.

"When I was in Zhao, I met a man named Zheng You'an. He had an object that recorded many strange things, some of which people had never even heard of. These things could be used to harm people, perhaps even to save them, and they could even be used in war. And the power is immense. I think that might be exactly why the King of Zhao feels confident enough to confront our Great Qin head-on." Xu Fu selectively shared some information with Ying Zheng.

"And what does that have to do with Xiong Yi?"

"Zheng You'an died long ago, and he left the things to Xiong Yi."

Ying Zheng leaned forward slightly. "Is this thing truly that powerful?"

"We will know once we get our hands on it." Xu Fu's gaze darkened. "Of course, we will also know by watching what Xiong Yi does now."

He hoped Prince Jia was a smart man and wouldn't immediately change his mind because of this.

What worried Xu Fu more now was that Xiong Yi might have actually learned something from it and used it all against the Qin army. If that happened, what kind of disaster would the Qin army suffer? Xu Fu worried that the course of history had been disrupted by time travel, and that things that shouldn't exist in this timeline had appeared. No one knew what kind of trouble that would cause.

Ying Zheng could tell what Xu Fu was thinking just by glancing at his expression. Even though, to others, Xu Fu's expression remained indifferent, showing no change, with neither joy nor anger readable.

"If that is truly the case, I shall have to take a good look at its power," Ying Zheng said coldly. In truth, despite what Xu Fu said, Ying Zheng was not afraid. How powerful could the things recorded on it be? If they were truly that powerful, why had no one ever heard of them? They should have had some fame. As for Zheng You'an, he had never even heard of the man.

What kind of good thing could be considered a treasure by Xiong Yi?

However, Ying Zheng ultimately chose to trust Xu Fu. Xiong Yi might lack vision, but Xu Fu certainly did not.

Having said all he needed to, Yao Jia took his leave.

"What else did Yao Jia say just now?" Xu Fu asked as he walked toward Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu hadn't spoken properly to him for several days. Since Xu Fu had taken the initiative to ask, even though it was about Yao Jia, Ying Zheng answered immediately: "Li Mu is in danger." After saying this, Ying Zheng smiled sarcastically. "Now the King of Zhao treats Xiong Yi as a treasure for his resurgence, yet he turns to deal with the capable generals Li Mu and Sima Shang. When these two also leave Zhao, the state of Zhao will truly be near its end."

Although the Qin army was fierce, Li Mu was no pushover. He was an extremely capable man, as all the states knew. Yet, the King of Zhao had such a good general and still wasn't satisfied. If the King of Zhao insisted on cutting off his own last claws, who could stop him from driving his country to its doom?

A country without loyal ministers and good generals would perish sooner or later.

Ying Zheng knew this well, and so did Xu Fu.

It seemed Yao Jia had accomplished quite a lot in Handan.

Xu Fu narrowed his eyes slightly, making no effort to hide his disgust for Zhao, and said coldly, "Then let us wait for the day he brings about his own destruction."

Ying Zheng watched him, feeling exceptionally pleased by Xu Fu's protective stance. If it weren't for him, Xu Fu might not have felt such strong animosity toward Zhao.

Since Yao Jia had nothing else to report, Xu Fu had no desire to learn more. Without a word, he turned to leave.

Leaving so soon?

The bit of pleasure that had just risen in Ying Zheng vanished completely.

"What has A-Fu been doing these past few days? Why not stay in the hall today?" Ying Zheng hurriedly called out to stop him.

Xu Fu looked back and gave him a cold glare. "Looking for my senior brother."

Looking for Wei Liao?

A sour feeling bubbled up in Ying Zheng's heart.

Even if it was his senior brother, that wouldn't do!

Ying Zheng stepped forward and forcefully kept Xu Fu by his side. "Have you been unhappy these past few days?" Ying Zheng asked, pulling Xu Fu's waist into his embrace. If he couldn't keep him with words, he would use his hands.

"Who dared to anger you? Tell me, and I will certainly not let them off lightly," Ying Zheng's deep, powerful voice resonated in Xu Fu's ear.

Xu Fu tilted his head and looked at him sideways.

Xu Fu's gaze made Ying Zheng feel somewhat uneasy.

"Who is it?" Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask again in a low voice.

The displeasure in Xu Fu's heart had already dissipated for the most part; he had teased Ying Zheng long enough. He opened his mouth and said slowly, "When you were in Zhao..."

Hearing this opening, Ying Zheng tightened his arm instinctively. He really didn't want Xu Fu to know about that inglorious past. If he could, he would prefer Xu Fu knew nothing of it. But that was clearly impossible. Because everyone knew about that past, he naturally couldn't hide it from Xu Fu.

"When you were in Zhao, did you know Prince Jia?" Xu Fu asked the question in his heart. He could have asked this long ago, but at the time, Xu Fu always felt it would be letting him off too easily.

A look of confusion flashed across Ying Zheng's face. Why had the topic suddenly shifted to Prince Jia? Was Xu Fu curious about Prince Jia's past?

"I met him a few times when I was in Zhao, but he was the Crown Prince then; how could I have had much interaction with him? If you want to ask me about him, I truly know nothing."

Xu Fu raised an eyebrow slightly. "Why would I want to ask about him?"

The jealousy in Ying Zheng's heart climbed higher and higher. "You have mentioned him to me several times; wasn't it to ask about him?"

Xu Fu was completely bewildered.

What was going on?

Ying Zheng... was jealous of Prince Jia???

Xu Fu suddenly found it incredibly funny. So they were both jealous of each other?

Seeing Xu Fu remain silent for a long time, Ying Zheng felt even more uncomfortable. "Why must you focus on Prince Jia?"

"Because of you."

"...Because of... me?" In his excitement, Ying Zheng even forgot to refer to himself as "Guaren."

"It is naturally because of you. I have no ties to Prince Jia and have never met him before. If it weren't for the fact that he knows you, why would I care about such an irrelevant person?" Xu Fu gave Ying Zheng a cold, indifferent look. But even this cold look made Ying Zheng beam with joy.

This was the most beautiful love confession Ying Zheng had ever heard from Xu Fu.

"So it was for me..." The smile on Ying Zheng's face could not be suppressed. "Then ask away; I will tell you everything."

"You only met Prince Jia a few times? Then what could you possibly tell me?"

"This... it is true that we only met a few times." Ying Zheng paused and asked cautiously, "A-Fu, do you mind that I know Prince Jia?" Ying Zheng's heart was beating fast; it was truly not easy to get Xu Fu to feel a spark of jealousy.

"Naturally I mind." Xu Fu was exceptionally frank. "When Prince Jia first arrived in Xianyang, his tone was as if he were very familiar with you. Later, you even agreed to everything he asked." Xu Fu sneered. "Why aren't you like that with me, A-Zheng?" That "A-Zheng" was wrapped in thick coldness.

It was truly not easy to see a sneer on Xu Fu's indifferent face.

Ying Zheng was not panicked or angry; instead, his joy grew with every passing moment.

He couldn't help but pull Xu Fu tighter into his arms, the corners of his mouth curling up. "It is all my fault, all my fault. It is truly too difficult to make A-Fu unhappy."

Xu Fu asked coldly, "You really want me to be unhappy?"

How would Ying Zheng dare to answer that? He immediately denied it. "How would I dare?" As the King of Qin, to say something like "How would I dare" showed he had truly let go of his status.

But Xu Fu was not someone who could be soothed in a few words. He closed his eyes, leaned against Ying Zheng's chest, and said faintly, "I am a bit tired; I will rest here for a while."

Let alone resting for a while, Ying Zheng would be willing to let him rest for a long time. When Xu Fu leaned against him, it gave him a great sense of satisfaction. Only at such times did he feel he truly had Xu Fu in his grasp. His domineering possessiveness was fully satisfied.

Xu Fu leaned there and fell asleep just like that.

Ying Zheng stared at his face, motionless, for a long time.

The hall fell into complete silence.

The palace attendants looked over with anxiety. How... how could the King remain as still as a wooden stake? Oh, pfft! How could one say that about the King? The attendants looked up and quickly lowered their heads again.

After a long time, Ying Zheng, holding Xu Fu in his arms, thought of a question.

Xu Fu hadn't said whether he had stopped being angry or not.

Ying Zheng glanced at Xu Fu's peaceful face as he slept and had no choice but to turn away, continuing to handle the official business at hand. Other questions... would have to wait until Xu Fu was well-rested.

A long time later, the attendants looked up and found Shuzhang Xu sleeping soundly in the King's arms, and they sighed repeatedly.

To be able to sleep in the King's arms, the Shuzhang was truly the only one.

Even Prince Fusu had never had that privilege. Not to mention the King's former concubines; sleeping in his arms? It was difficult enough just to see the King freely. The attendants even had a faint thought: if one day the Shuzhang became the Queen, they probably wouldn't even be surprised.

When Xu Fu woke up, it was already dark. He leaned in Ying Zheng's arms and asked lazily, "By the way, when you sent Prince Jia back, you said it was out of 'past ties.' What past ties do you and Prince Jia have? Tell me about them."

Ying Zheng never expected that the first thing Xu Fu would say upon waking was this, and for a moment, he couldn't react.

"This... this was merely a pretext... A-Fu, please don't take it to heart."

Xu Fu's expression was cold, his eyelids lowered, not looking at him at all. "Even if it was a pretext, the fact that the whole world knows you have some 'past ties' with Prince Jia makes me very unhappy."

Xu Fu was truly unhappy about that statement. Rationally, he knew it was just a pretext, but emotionally, there was a sense of discomfort that something belonging to him had been labeled by everyone as belonging to someone else. When he first heard it, Xu Fu even felt a surge of emotion in his chest, as if it were about to burst forth.

"If someone thought I had an affair with my senior brother, would you feel comfortable?" Xu Fu asked back.

Did that even need to be asked?

Ying Zheng's eyebrows shot up, and his entire aura became sharp. "I would be far more than just 'uncomfortable'." He would be satisfied only after dragging Wei Liao out to be torn apart by chariots.

"What if that was also a pretext?"

Ying Zheng's aura receded. He raised his hand to pull Xu Fu's waist tighter, then leaned down to press against him. "I understand. From now on, no one will ever say that again."

Xu Fu said very seriously, "Possessiveness is not something only you have." He had it too. Originally, he was quite a free-spirited person, and his possessiveness would probably only exist toward his professional tools, but now there was an extra Ying Zheng. Since he was already there, Xu Fu had to guard what belonged to him; he hated it when others touched his things.

Not even a little bit.

Ying Zheng suppressed the surging emotions in his heart and gently stroked Xu Fu's neck. "Okay." After a while, Ying Zheng realized what Xu Fu meant. Could it be that his feelings were the same as his own? Ying Zheng was almost certain from the bottom of his heart that Xu Fu must like him, even if it wasn't as deep as his own feelings.

Xu Fu felt he had conveyed the meaning of observing "husbandly duties" well enough, and he had slept quite well today, after all, there was a human cushion. He got up from Ying Zheng's arms and glanced outside. "I want to eat."

"Okay." Ying Zheng held his hand and sat there, giving orders to the attendants, who quickly retreated to prepare the evening meal.

Ying Zheng was rubbing the back of Xu Fu's hand, really enjoying it, when Xu Fu pulled his hand back.

Ying Zheng felt a bit regretful. He looked at Xu Fu and asked in a low voice, "A-Fu doesn't like me doing this? I will certainly not make such a mistake again in the future. But, since A-Fu doesn't like me being linked to others, then in the future, if I say that the Queen of Qin is you, will you be angry?" If he said directly who the Queen was, then no one would dare link him to others.

The expression on Xu Fu's face almost cracked.

The Queen?

Ying Zheng actually had such thoughts!

Xu Fu looked back at him; Ying Zheng's eyes were filled with anticipation. Xu Fu changed his words at the last minute. "If A-Zheng can handle all the consequences, why would I be angry?"

Xu Fu thought that perhaps by then, he would have to worry about whether it was better to be the National Master or the Queen.

Thinking about it, the image was even a bit... comical.

Xu Fu walked away. Ying Zheng closed the last bamboo slip, threw it into the attendant's arms, and immediately chased after him, his steps much larger due to his extreme joy.

In the blink of an eye, a few days passed. Xu Fu went to the Fengchang Temple several times, mostly to guide Wang Liu and other diviners. When he returned to the palace, he learned the news of the Qin army's defeat.

Throughout the campaign, there had only been talk of failed sieges, how could there be a defeat? Xu Fu was shocked and immediately thought of Xiong Yi. Could it be that he led the Zhao army to not only defend against the Qin army but also counterattack?

At this time, Ying Zheng was not at the small court session. Xu Fu called an attendant to lead the way and quickly headed toward the hall where Ying Zheng handled official business.

When Xu Fu arrived, he saw that there were already people inside—it could be said that most of Qin's elite were there: the old general Wang Jian, the young Meng Tian, his senior brother Wei Liao, and the guest minister Li Si.

Wasn't this most of Qin's elite?

Xu Fu walked in slowly.

Wang Jian was the first to show him a smile. He was likely still thinking about the time he hadn't helped Xu Fu. Now, he would show favor to Xu Fu whenever he could, just to make up for the past.

The people standing in this hall were all those close to Xu Fu, or those willing to be close to him.

Xu Fu's mood was very complex. He never expected that after coming to Qin, he would gain such a group of friends and family. It was probably... incomparable... After all, whose lover could be the First Emperor of Qin? Whose senior brother could be Wei Liao? Who could know and maintain good relationships with Li Si, Zhao Gao, Meng Tian, and Wang Jian?

"Continue, don't mind me." Xu Fu waved his hand and casually found a seat.

Because there were many people in the hall, Xu Fu didn't go to Ying Zheng's side; that would seem too frivolous and undignified.

They were indeed talking about the situation in Zhao.

"We don't even know who is leading the troops. No one knows where he popped out from, but he possesses very powerful skills. People say he can throw fireballs..." Wang Jian frowned tightly and said in a low voice. Even with his vast experience, he had never seen such a thing.

Ying Zheng said in a deep voice, "I know who it is."

Wang Jian's eyes flickered. "Oh? I truly cannot think of any other powerful general in Zhao." Wang Jian's words indeed contained disdain for Zhao, but with his current fame and status, he had the capital to be disdainful.

"It is Xiong Yi," Ying Zheng said calmly. "Xiong Yi had an accident in Shu, and I thought he was dead. I didn't expect him to become a guest of Lord Xinling and follow him to Zhao, after which he was recommended to the King of Zhao to offer strategies. Now he is even leading troops into battle himself..."

Although everyone present knew perfectly well that Xiong Yi's death was no accident, none of them were stupid enough to say it.

Wang Jian's brow furrowed deeply. "This... this doesn't make sense. Your Majesty, we all know very well who Xiong Yi is. How could he possibly win against Huan Yi?"

"Because he has a book in his hands. You can think of it as a military manual, and the things recorded on it are likely things that many people find difficult to resist." Xu Fu spoke up then.

"Is there truly such a magical ancient book?" Wang Jian had already defaulted to it being an ancient book; Xu Fu certainly wouldn't say it was something recorded by Zheng You'an. In the first place, that wisdom didn't originate from Zheng You'an either.

Meng Tian said in a deep voice, "I naturally believe what the Shuzhang says."

Wei Liao, standing to the side, glanced at him but said nothing. Even if Wei Liao didn't speak, everyone knew what he meant; if he were to speak, it would be nothing more than "I believe my junior brother."

"If there really is such an ancient book, we must get our hands on it," Li Si said with a smile.

Ying Zheng knew that the book was something Xu Fu wanted, so he didn't mention it too much. Even when they got their hands on it, it would be for Xu Fu to look at first.

Xu Fu himself was quite generous. These things weren't his to begin with, so he felt no pain in giving them away, as long as it could make Qin stronger. However, he would never hand them over to anyone other than Ying Zheng, because such things were too powerful and best kept in the hands of the monarch.

Wang Jian and the others were smart people and naturally thought of this. Although they were tempted by the magical book, they would never say anything like asking the King to hand it over to them.

They knew their own standing well.

Bringing the topic back to business, "Xiong Yi's actions are too strange. I must go and see for myself to be at ease. The great cause has reached this point; I cannot tolerate Xiong Yi causing any destruction."

"This..." Everyone hesitated, wanting to dissuade Ying Zheng, but none dared to.

Having been ministers to Ying Zheng for so long, they knew when he could not be dissuaded and when he could not be stopped.

Li Si looked at Xu Fu and smiled. "Does the Shuzhang have a way?"

Xu Fu was a bit surprised. "Why does the Guest Minister say that?"

"The Shuzhang will surely accompany the King, won't you?"

Xu Fu said nonchalantly, "Who said that?"

Li Si was stunned. Usually, at a time like this, even if the King didn't go, Xu Fu would want to go. Why was he so indifferent this time?

Not to mention Li Si, even Ying Zheng was stunned. He had prepared everything to take Xu Fu with him, even thinking of using this opportunity to dispel the unhappiness in Xu Fu's heart. But... did Xu Fu mean he didn't intend to go? He didn't intend to go with him? The expression on Ying Zheng's face stiffened.

Ying Zheng suppressed the sudden displeasure in his heart, turned his gaze back to his ministers, and continued to discuss the situation in Zhao with them.

Meng Tian said in a low voice, "General Huan Yi has just recovered from a serious illness and has been fighting for a long time. Why don't I go and replace the General?"

Wang Jian actually wanted to go and see for himself, but as an old general of Qin, he couldn't easily go to the battlefield. At a time like this, it was clearly better to give the opportunity to Meng Tian. Wang Jian understood Ying Zheng's intention to hone Meng Tian. Meng Tian would be cultivated into another great general for Qin.

Ying Zheng nodded. "Hmm, you take the troops and go first."

Wei Liao couldn't help but turn to look at Xu Fu, but in the end, he said nothing. Although he was the National Marshal, such a war didn't require him to do anything. It was better for him to stay in the palace and coordinate the court affairs for Ying Zheng. Because of Xu Fu, Wei Liao was now much more sincere in his work for Ying Zheng. It could be said that as long as he was in court, he would at least not let Qin fall into chaos.

Li Si added a few more words, and then they had the intention to disperse.

Wei Liao was the last to leave.

When he was about to leave, he walked up to Xu Fu and said in a low voice, "Are you having a falling out with the King?"

A falling out? Why did that word sound like something that would only appear between the male and female leads in a melodramatic love story?

Xu Fu shook his head immediately.

Wei Liao frowned. He originally wanted to say, "Junior brother, you are being too willful now; relying on the King's favor to give him the cold shoulder is wrong." But Wei Liao suddenly had a change of heart. That's right, isn't my junior brother meant to be pampered? If the King doesn't treat him well, who else would he treat well? The King should indulge him! My junior brother should live willfully!

So Wei Liao swallowed everything he was about to say.

"If you aren't going with the King, then come to my residence to rest." In the end, Wei Liao only said this. He assumed that if Xu Fu didn't go, he would definitely be lonely. So come and keep your senior brother company; that would be best.

"National Marshal, you may leave now," Ying Zheng interrupted him bluntly.

Wei Liao's dream of brotherly love was shattered just like that. He had no choice but to obey Ying Zheng's words and turn to walk out.

Ying Zheng suppressed the displeasure in his heart, walked slowly to Xu Fu's side, and asked softly, "I have noticed that Wei Liao is no longer like he was before. He seems much more sincere when speaking to me and is even more dedicated in his work. Did you say something to him?"

Xu Fu shook his head. He really hadn't said anything to Wei Liao recently.

How could Xu Fu have guessed that Wei Liao had "awakened" on his own?

Ying Zheng didn't believe him when he denied it. After all, he had heard from Xu Fu that Xu Fu also had possessiveness toward him, so Ying Zheng felt that Xu Fu must have been doing many things for him in silence, including persuading Wei Liao. Ying Zheng thought of many past events, even the fact that Xu Fu went to Shu, and automatically filled in the gaps, thinking everything Xu Fu did was for him. The more he thought, the sweeter his heart felt.

The bit of displeasure from just now dissipated in such beautiful memories.

"I am going to the army. Are you not worried for me this time?" Ying Zheng couldn't help but hug Xu Fu tightly, burying his head in his neck, breathing in the scent of Xu Fu—only the faint fruity smell of freshly laundered clothes. He opened his mouth and gently bit the soft flesh on Xu Fu's neck, saying in a low voice, "You truly have a cruel heart."

Xu Fu felt like he was about to be suffocated by his embrace. To use a standard Mary Sue novel sentence, it was as if Ying Zheng wanted to knead him into his own bones and blood.

It hurt!

Especially since Ying Zheng was still gnawing on his neck, it felt tingling and itchy, and Xu Fu's breathing suddenly became unnatural.

To use the standard Mary Sue novel sentence again, he felt that Ying Zheng was lighting a fire on his body.

This posture was truly upside down.

Ying Zheng quickly let go, but he only released his mouth and embrace, then immediately placed his hand on Xu Fu's waist. "If you go with me, I won't say anything the next time you want to travel."

Xu Fu was unmoved and just wanted to swat away the hand Ying Zheng had placed on his waist. "My freedom is my own; I don't need you to give it to me."

Ying Zheng was choked up and had to change his words. "Next time you travel, I will certainly pack your things happily, how about that?"

Was Ying Zheng truly willing to make such a sacrifice? Xu Fu glanced at him and then said graciously, "Okay."

In fact, Xu Fu hadn't said a word about definitely not going. But since Ying Zheng had offered a benefit, he would pretend to agree reluctantly.

Not many people knew about Ying Zheng's plan to lead the campaign personally; they mostly knew that Meng Tian had been sent out by the King of Qin.

Meng Tian was also a fierce general of Great Qin.

After other states learned of this, they couldn't help but be curious: just how badly had the state of Zhao's mysterious general pushed Qin that even Meng Tian had been sent out? Would Huan Yi be reprimanded? People in other states were excited, as if they saw hope for their own countries' survival in this Zhao general.

Even the state of Han was somewhat shaken by this.

However, Ying Zheng didn't care for the time being, because once he dealt with Xiong Yi, Han would naturally be terrified and kneel at his feet again; that was when he would make Han pay a higher price. It was truly unnecessary to argue with them now.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng's luggage was quickly packed, and the accompanying personnel were selected.

They were just waiting to set off together the next day.

Because the things to be prepared were far from simple, Ying Zheng was still handling affairs until late at night. Only after these matters were arranged could he leave with Xu Fu with peace of mind.

So that night, only Xu Fu remained in the hall, sitting at the table and flipping through bamboo slips.

Oh, learning two more witchcraft spells might come in handy.

Zhao Cheng brought water to Xu Fu's side. He stood there for a long time, hesitating, his expression changing back and forth, until even Xu Fu couldn't stand it anymore and couldn't help but look up and ask, "Is there something you want to tell me?"

"This servant is worried about the Shuzhang." Zhao Cheng lowered his head and asked in a low voice, "May I ask if the Shuzhang has... had a falling out with the King?"
