Is amnesia really that easy to come by? However, this didn't stop Xu Fu from creating an illusion for Xiong Yi, making him believe that only a Xu Fu who had lost his memory could possibly betray the King of Qin.

A look of deep thought appeared on Xiong Yi's face.

Xu Fu glanced at him and sighed inwardly. On this point alone, Xiong Yi was far inferior to Ying Zheng, and even inferior to himself. Xiong Yi's originally privileged background made his ability to handle pressure very low. So, after encountering setbacks, although he did strengthen himself, he also indulged his spirit in descending into another dark abyss. Even today, he could not properly hide his emotions; his strengths and weaknesses were obvious. It was no wonder that Ying Zheng and the others didn't take him seriously, because Xiong Yi was indeed unlikely to pose any real threat to Ying Zheng.

It was just that during this process, an accident occurred: Xiong Yi had obtained all of Zheng You'an's knowledge from the future. Xu Fu should be thankful that Xiong Yi wasn't smart enough; otherwise, he could have fully integrated this knowledge to create things sufficient to dominate this era.

Xiong Yi glanced at Jianjia. "I'll let him go in a few days." Xiong Yi's mouth curved into a smile. "When I retake Ye City."

Xu Fu's perception was extremely keen. Xiong Yi said "in a few days"... and also "when I retake Ye City"... It was evident that in his mind, "in a few days" was when he would retake Ye City. Why was his tone so certain? Could it be that he had some secret weapon he hadn't unleashed yet?

"Do you know who Meng Tian is?" Xu Fu suddenly spoke, his words seemingly irrelevant.

Xiong Yi didn't know what Xu Fu was aiming for and could only smile: "How could I not know Meng Tian?" They had both been people in Xianyang City, and their family backgrounds were not low; not only did they know each other, but they had also had some interactions.

"Who is Meng Tian's father? Who is his grandfather? Famous generals of Qin! He has been nurtured by his family since childhood and possesses outstanding talent. ...Can you take Ye City from his hands?" Xu Fu's tone was very flat, without any disdain or contempt, but the flatter it was, the more unbearable it sounded to Xiong Yi.

"Why not? Even if his father is capable, and his grandfather is capable, so what? It doesn't mean he is capable!" Xiong Yi sneered. "How do you know I can't defeat him now?"

Because I can see it!

Although Xu Fu was not versed in military affairs and knew nothing about troop formations or the intricacies of ancient warfare, he could keenly perceive that when the Zhao army and the Qin army faced off, the Zhao army was clearly at a disadvantage, and their formations were a complete mess. Xiong Yi might be somewhat intelligent, but his intelligence was not reflected in warfare. How could he compare to Meng Tian? Unless he held something in his hands that could completely crush Meng Tian.

Xu Fu's unmoved demeanor caused the suppressed fire in Xiong Yi's heart to ignite. His heart was screaming: Show him, show him, let him know that I am not lacking anything compared to the King of Qin... If it weren't for the King of Qin, I could have been better...

"You don't believe me?" Xiong Yi smiled. "I'll take you to see it, and then you will believe." Xiong Yi even thought that perhaps after seeing it, Xu Fu would be terrified on the spot and might even be unable to resist begging him... Xiong Yi's imagination ran wild, while Xu Fu looked at him with cold eyes.

Xu Fu found that he was increasingly unable to understand what Xiong Yi was thinking.

"Let's go." Xiong Yi put away those fantasies and said to Xu Fu in a low voice.

Xu Fu, however, stepped over to Jianjia's side. "Untie the ropes." Xu Fu had discovered that the worse his attitude toward Xiong Yi was, the better Xiong Yi's attitude became toward him. If someone else had been as bossy and arrogant as he was, they would have certainly been beaten up, but Xiong Yi wasn't angry; instead, he followed him over and whispered: "No, he..."

"He's just a child. Do you want to keep him tied up here until he dies?" Xu Fu said expressionlessly while lifting Jianjia's sleeve, revealing faint red marks where the ropes had been. In truth, such marks were unavoidable after being tied up for a long time, but the way Xu Fu looked at Xiong Yi made the other man feel as if he had committed a heinous crime.

Anyway, the person was in the camp, and there were many guards outside the tent. Just as Xu Fu said, he was just a brat; what great ability could he have? He might be skilled, but could he be better than an army? He wasn't Xu Fu; he didn't have Xu Fu's incredible abilities. Xiong Yi glanced at Jianjia. Jianjia's beautiful appearance immediately worked to his advantage, making him look completely harmless. Xiong Yi waved for the soldiers to untie him.

Jianjia just sat on the ground without getting up, looking exceptionally weak.

Someone came in to bring him some water and food, and Jianjia immediately grabbed them and ate.

Xu Fu didn't look at him again and followed Xiong Yi outside.

Xiong Yi noticed that Xu Fu was still cradling a small, broken tripod in his arms. Xiong Yi frowned. "What is this?"

"For divination. Do you want to try?"

Xiong Yi laughed. "Don't try to fool me. I am also skilled in divination; how could I not know that this object is not used for divination?"

Xu Fu wasn't nervous. He glanced sideways at Xiong Yi. "And how do you know this isn't a new method of divination I've invented?"

Xiong Yi was choked by the response. He recalled the rumors about Xu Fu over the past few years; it was true that his divination methods were different from others, yet his methods were convenient and accurate. That this was what he used for divination... it wasn't impossible. Xiong Yi suppressed his doubts and led Xu Fu toward the back of the camp. Soldiers followed behind them, but they didn't dare to get too close.

As they walked, Xu Fu realized they were almost leaving the camp's perimeter. Didn't Xiong Yi say he was going to show him something? What could he see outside the camp?

But soon, Xu Fu knew why they were heading this way.

Not far from the back of the camp, a hillside could be seen. Xiong Yi led him up the hill, and the soldiers all stopped, guarding the front of the hill and not advancing further. After crossing the hill, Xu Fu saw a cave. So, everything was inside the cave? If Xiong Yi hadn't brought him here, the Qin army might not have found this place for a long time. He really had to thank Xiong Yi for being so conceited; his personality was truly very similar to that of Zheng You'an. Otherwise, he really wouldn't have discovered this place so quickly.

Xiong Yi didn't know what Xu Fu was thinking. He led Xu Fu into the cave, and as they reached the entrance, Xu Fu faintly smelled the scent of mercury.

Xu Fu's expression changed slightly; he almost wanted to turn around and leave.

Xiong Yi had already walked in first. Seeing Xu Fu hesitating, Xiong Yi couldn't help but smile slightly. He turned back and asked: "Scared? It's really not easy to see you scared. Come in, don't be afraid."

Xu Fu was afraid; he was afraid of dying.

A place like this was practically a sweatshop, with no safety measures whatsoever. Who knew when someone might die?

Xu Fu cut off the hesitation in his heart and stepped inside. Even if this cave collapsed, he would definitely drag Xiong Yi down to be his cushion.

As they walked deeper, light gradually appeared.

Dim firelight illuminated the interior of the cave. Xu Fu heard the clanging of metalwork and a faint smell of sulfur hit his nose. Xu Fu's heart sank. Had Xiong Yi already solved the problem of gunpowder? The invention of gunpowder wouldn't happen until the Tang Dynasty! Xu Fu roared internally, but his face remained completely calm.

"Do you hear that sound?"

"Hmm." Xu Fu responded perfunctorily.

"That is the sound of new weapons being forged." The firelight flickered, reflecting on Xiong Yi's face, making his expression look somewhat insane. Xu Fu could clearly see the burning ambition in his eyes.

Xiong Yi moved aside, and Xu Fu walked forward two steps, then saw soldiers wearing thin undergarments, drenched in sweat, their faces dark and red, standing by the furnaces forging weapons. Zhao was not a country with high iron production; he didn't know how Xiong Yi obtained these things or how he got them here. Xu Fu didn't know much about weapons, but looking at the shapes taking form in the men's hands, the terms in Xu Fu's mind quickly matched them one by one.

Shields, armor, caltrops, ring-pommel swords, dragon-whisker hooks... there were even things that looked like firelocks.

Seeing this, the trepidation in Xu Fu's heart suddenly vanished.

With the level of this era, these things simply couldn't be made. Even if they were made, they would at most just have the shape. To make these things, it wasn't enough to just have blueprints; one needed evolving technology. After all, you weren't doing the work yourself; you had to find craftsmen to do it. The craftsmen might not have the sufficient skill to make them, and the lack of raw materials might cause their power to be greatly reduced—just like that dud bomb from before. Forcing the use of technology from thousands of years in the future with the level of several thousand years ago was sometimes not only a waste of effort but could also lead to a disastrous defeat because of blind trust in the power of the weapons in hand, while ignoring other aspects.

Xu Fu walked deeper and indeed saw people researching gunpowder. But was gunpowder so easy to develop? Xu Fu actually knew how to make it, because there were ancient records that the alchemist who discovered that sulfur could produce explosives was an alchemist. Ancient alchemy always used sulfur. This was easy to make, but to create lethality, was it something you could just do by holding a blueprint and finding some materials? Were these craftsmen geniuses?

Xu Fu's gaze swept over them and then glanced to the side.

Someone was smearing mercury onto swords.

Xu Fu was even more speechless.

Did Xiong Yi think mercury was poison? Did he really think that by smearing it on, stabbing someone in the stomach, or grazing a wound, he could poison the opponent? Don't joke. Never mind whether it could kill the Qin soldiers; the first to die would definitely be these soldiers smearing the mercury. Xu Fu examined them closely, and sure enough, from their complexion, hair, and other signs, it was clear that their bodies were already very unhealthy.

Xu Fu didn't intend to stay here any longer. They weren't afraid of death, but he was.

Mercury is toxic in its gaseous form; when it is a liquid, gas evaporates from it. Once you inhale too much, you're just waiting to die. Xu Fu turned to walk out, a thought even faintly crossing his mind. He had originally been wondering how to kill Xiong Yi, but now a ready-made method had been presented.

Seeing Xu Fu turn to leave without a word, Xiong Yi couldn't help but feel smug. He thought Xu Fu had been stunned and was fearful of these weapons, which was why he didn't dare stay here any longer. Xiong Yi curled his lips and hurriedly followed.

Only after exiting the cave did Xu Fu suddenly feel much more comfortable.

He breathed out slowly and, using the light outside, examined Xiong Yi.

Compared to the young nobleman he used to be, Xiong Yi's skin was now darker, and because he was prone to anger, his face was shrouded in a gloomy air, making it easy to overlook his features and complexion. Now, looking closely, Xu Fu realized that Xiong Yi actually had obvious signs of poisoning. His complexion was sallow and dark, his eyes were dull, his eyeballs were red, he was manic and irritable, and his breathing was heavy. Weren't these signs of poisoning? It seemed that after obtaining these things, Xiong Yi liked them too much; he probably went to see them every day, and perhaps even held them in his arms... Xu Fu's mouth twitched. Otherwise, the poisoning wouldn't be this severe.

Xu Fu felt a stir in his heart. If he added a little more force on top of this foundation... what would happen to Xiong Yi?

He knew that some sulfide poisoning could damage a person's central nervous system, damage the respiratory tract and throat, and even affect vision... As for mercury, it could also cause skin ulceration, and until it led to more serious illnesses, death wouldn't be far off.

He still had to restrain himself and observe a bit more to see exactly what stage Xiong Yi was at.

If he didn't strike, he wouldn't; but once he did, he had to ensure a hit.

Xu Fu rubbed the body of the tripod in his arms.

This was perfect; he didn't have to rack his brains to figure out how to feed it to Xiong Yi.

Xiong Yi led Xu Fu further and further away from the cave. Xiong Yi narrowed his eyes slightly, his tone carrying a hint of intoxication. "How is it? This place, it's something the Qin state doesn't have, something no state has! The things I can make, none of them can! I am a descendant of Chu; in the future, I will make Chu the hegemon and destroy the Qin state!"

Xiong Yi seemed to have hypnotized himself; his tone was three parts intoxicated, as if that day would arrive soon. Looking at his appearance, Xu Fu really wanted to tell him that this daydream shouldn't be taken lightly. There were so many people in history who wanted to be kings and hegemons; Xiong Yi really didn't rank among them. All those people failed, and he still wanted to destroy the Qin state? This dream was just like Zheng You'an's desire to become the First Emperor... very silly and very naive.

Xu Fu didn't say a word. Xiong Yi was a little disappointed by his lack of response, but thinking that this was Xu Fu's nature, he immediately felt relieved and even spontaneously made an excuse for him. He must have been startled just now, which was why he couldn't speak for a long time.

"Are you worried for the King of Qin?" Xiong Yi asked with a sour tone. If he had gotten his hands on Xu Fu back in Xianyang, then the person Xu Fu followed now would be him. Thinking about what Ying Zheng possessed, Xiong Yi felt an intense jealousy.

Xu Fu neither nodded nor shook his head. Meeting Xiong Yi's gaze, he quickly looked away.

I'm thinking about how to kill you... How could I tell you that?

Upon returning to the camp, a soldier rushed in front of Xiong Yi. "General... General! The, the person has escaped!" The soldier was very nervous, drenched in sweat, his face bright red, and his look toward Xiong Yi was filled with fear.

"Who?" Xiong Yi paused, then suddenly realized. "That Qin person?"

"Yes..." the soldier stammered.

Xiong Yi kicked the soldier in the chest, and the soldier stumbled and fell to the ground, not daring to get up for a long time.

This kick was so sudden that even Xu Fu was stunned.

Xiong Yi's wounds hadn't healed yet, and making such a large movement naturally tore them. His face turned deathly pale. Looking at the soldier again, Xiong Yi's temper became even more explosive. "Drag him away," Xiong Yi said coldly. By comparison, the soldier losing the person made Xiong Yi even angrier than Jianjia escaping.

Xu Fu felt that Xiong Yi was evolving more and more toward mania, both physically and mentally. If someone like this had discovered something was wrong earlier and received treatment, it wouldn't have reached this point, but if he continued to indulge himself, it would undoubtedly get worse and worse until he killed himself.

The soldier was quickly dragged away. Xu Fu didn't know what consequences he would face, but he could clearly see the terror in the eyes of the other soldiers. They were all afraid of Xiong Yi, yet Xiong Yi didn't trust these Zhao soldiers. With such deep conflicts between the general and his soldiers, it was no wonder Xiong Yi found it hard to fight a good war. In the Qin army, if nothing else, the rapport between generals and soldiers was perfect, and with excellent generals and fierce soldiers, it was no wonder the Qin state could expand its territory step by step.

Xiong Yi then turned back to look at Xu Fu gloomily. "He escaped; you should be happy now."

"Naturally, I am happy." Xu Fu's posture was open and honest. The person used to threaten him had escaped; how could he not be happy?

Xiong Yi used great effort to suppress the surging emotions in his chest.

Xiong Yi called for people to chase after Jianjia, but he himself didn't put much more effort into it. Originally, capturing Jianjia was just to lure Xu Fu into the trap; now that Xu Fu was here, it didn't matter anymore. Xiong Yi brought Xu Fu to his own tent. For the past few days, Xu Fu had been separated from him, but today, Xiong Yi didn't mention having soldiers take Xu Fu back to his tent at all. Xu Fu's heart tightened. What was Xiong Yi planning to do?

Seeing his hand holding the small broken tripod tighten, Xiong Yi couldn't help but smile. In his view, this was a sign of Xu Fu's inner insecurity. But in reality, Xu Fu was still pondering how to kill him.

"Do you really have to hold this thing in your arms? Why not put it down?"

Xu Fu glanced at him coldly.

Xiong Yi showed an indulgent, doting expression. Xu Fu got goosebumps.

Xiong Yi walked to the bed and sat down. He patted the bed and said to Xu Fu, "Come here."

Xu Fu's footsteps stopped there, with no intention of moving. "I want to go back to my tent."

"From now on, this will be your tent." Xiong Yi was full of smiles. "I don't dare let you go back; otherwise, you'll run away again. What should I do? I don't care about your attendant running away, but you cannot escape."

"The Zhao army guards are strict; how could I run away?" Xu Fu remembered that he had even discovered caltrops on the outskirts of the camp. If one stepped on that, the feeling would definitely be "extraordinarily refreshing." He didn't know if Jianjia had stepped on one when he came.

"Is there anything you can't do?" Xiong Yi smiled, with no intention of letting Xu Fu go back.

Xu Fu could only sigh lightly in his heart.

Xiong Yi, oh Xiong Yi, this is you delivering yourself to me to be finished off.

Xu Fu walked to the side of the bed and said calmly, "Then if I sleep here, are you going to sleep on the floor?"

The expression on Xiong Yi's face stiffened. "Naturally, we will sleep together."

"You have wounds on your body; if I accidentally..." Xu Fu stopped halfway.

Xiong Yi's expression stiffened again. Of course, Xiong Yi cherished his life very much now. Who could say for sure that if he slept on the same bed as Xu Fu, who would be the one to end up in trouble? Perhaps before he could do anything to Xu Fu, he would die at Xu Fu's hands first. Xiong Yi had to grit his teeth and hesitate. "...Then, then you sleep on the bed."

"Good." Xu Fu replied quickly, and then calmly ordered the soldiers to bring him hot water.

While washing up simply, Xu Fu put down the tripod in his hand.

When Xu Fu left, Xiong Yi was curious about the tripod. He glanced at Xu Fu's back, couldn't help but walk over to the small tripod, and lifted the mismatched lid. Then he discovered some liquid flowing inside, sparkling and beautiful under the candlelight, with some broken dried flower petals floating on top, emitting a faint fragrance. Xiong Yi was truly baffled; could this be used for divination?

Not long after, Xu Fu came out. Xiong Yi pointed to the small tripod and asked Xu Fu: "How is this used for divination?"

Xu Fu glanced at him sideways. "You want to try?"

The joy on Xiong Yi's face grew stronger. "You're willing?"

"Not willing." Xu Fu coldly rejected him and then walked to the side of the bed naturally, lying down in his robes to sleep.

Watching his figure, Xiong Yi could only helplessly choose to... sleep on the floor.

Xu Fu heard the rustling sound behind him. He felt he was quite something; Xiong Yi was clearly the villain threatening him, but he had been forced by himself to sleep on the floor, while he, the one being threatened, could sleep comfortably on the bed...

Xu Fu closed his eyes and fell asleep quickly.

Xiong Yi had been away from Xianyang for almost six years. With Xu Fu sleeping not far away, Xiong Yi felt as if he had been instantly pulled back to the Xianyang City of the past. At that time, he was still Young Master Xiong Yi of the Fengchang Temple, and no one dared to offend him. Even the King of Qin had to treat him politely. At that time, Xu Fu was just someone he liked because of his appearance, a dispensable existence. But after great changes and the passage of time like flowing water, his obsession with Xu Fu had grown deeper and deeper. Now, Xu Fu was within his reach, and hatred and love struggled in his heart.

How could Xiong Yi still sleep? He got up and sat on the edge of the bed, staring blankly in Xu Fu's direction. After a while, a rich fragrance attracted him. It turned out that the curtain had been lifted by the wind, and the wind had blown in, dispersing the scent from the small tripod. Xiong Yi couldn't help but walk over.

The scent smelled very comfortable; Xiong Yi even faintly felt that Xu Fu had such a scent on him. He couldn't help but be a little intoxicated. After smelling it for a while, Xiong Yi noticed that his throat was a bit parched, so he quickly turned around and called for a soldier to bring him water. Xiong Yi picked up the water and gulped it down. The cold water felt stinging as it went down his throat, and he even choked uncomfortably.

"What did you give me to drink?" Xiong Yi's face changed, and he grabbed the soldier's collar with a manic expression.

The soldier was stunned and stammered: "...It, it's just water."

Xiong Yi opened his mouth to curse, but his throat stung uncomfortably. He couldn't help but vomit all the water out. The firelight illuminated the ground outside the tent, and Xiong Yi caught a glimpse of faint bloodstains inside. A sudden panic rose in Xiong Yi's heart. He released the soldier and roared: "Catch him!"

The soldier was flustered and fell to his knees. "General! General, I didn't do anything... General!"

Other soldiers swarmed up and dragged the man away from the ground.

Xiong Yi grabbed the curtain, lowered his head, and poked his throat. He spat out some saliva.

It was mixed with blood.

He didn't know if his throat was torn or if he was vomiting blood internally. And what made Xiong Yi panic even more was that he couldn't even taste the blood. He licked his lips, and his whole body was covered in a feeling of soreness. He hadn't been able to eat properly recently because his appetite was worse than before, and his sense of taste was indeed not as sharp as before. Xiong Yi was a little panicked and suddenly thought of something. Wasn't this how Li Xin looked when he was poisoned? Could it be that he was also poisoned by mercury?

A look of fury flashed across Xiong Yi's face.

How could this be? He hadn't drunk that thing!

Could it really be the water? Xiong Yi's face was ferocious, gritting his teeth, wishing he could kill the soldier immediately. He hurriedly called for a military doctor and ordered him to boil medicine quickly. After returning to the tent, Xiong Yi felt his whole body go limp, and with his wounds being very painful, he sat on the ground, dizzy and with a gloomy face. When the military doctor arrived at the tent, he was startled by Xiong Yi's appearance. He looked truly terrifying. The doctor carefully squatted beside him and began to examine his body, his face growing uglier by the second.

Xiong Yi's heart sank suddenly. "...What? Is it serious?"

How could the doctor dare to answer that it was serious? He just stammered: "I have never seen such an illness before..."

Xiong Yi whispered: "Get out."

How could the doctor dare to say another word? He scrambled out as fast as he could. Who in the army didn't know Xiong Yi was cruel? Who wanted to touch his bad side? Even if he said nothing, that was safer than saying too much.

Such poison was indeed difficult to cure. Xiong Yi's heart grew colder. He had used this to deal with others before, so he naturally knew the severity of it. According to his current state, he had been poisoned for some days... Xiong Yi gritted his teeth, wondering who had plotted against him!

It doesn't matter, I have the antidote... Xiong Yi closed his eyes and repeated the words of self-comfort in his heart countless times.

Xu Fu was still sleeping soundly on the bed, completely unaware of what had happened to Xiong Yi. Xiong Yi struggled to get up, looked at Xu Fu for a while, then looked at Xu Fu's tripod, and then put the lid back on. Xiong Yi fell asleep in a daze.

After Xu Fu woke up, he got up quickly. The air was still filled with the faint scent of mercury and the fragrance of flowers. Xu Fu walked to the table and saw that the tripod he had placed there had been moved. He knew that Xiong Yi couldn't resist his curiosity and had taken a look. Normally, a normal person would be able to smell that something was wrong, but Xiong Yi had smelled it too many times, and his sense of smell had long since become numb. Moreover, with sulfide poisoning, there were symptoms of declining taste and smell. Plus, Xiong Yi had a preconceived notion that it was used by Xu Fu for divination; although he felt the object was strange, he never thought that what was inside was the very thing he used to harm others.

And since Xu Fu hadn't fed it to him, Xiong Yi naturally wouldn't think that what was inside was the thing he had originally given to someone else, ordering them to harm Huan Qi.

His thinking was fixed on the idea that one could only be poisoned by drinking mercury; he had no idea that what truly caused poisoning was vaporized mercury.

Xu Fu glanced at Xiong Yi sleeping on the floor; his face was faintly purple.

Xu Fu knew very well that before long, he would develop the same symptoms as Huan Qi, and although Xiong Yi held the formula for the antidote, the process of this antidote was far less effective than his own. He feared that before any improvement, Xiong Yi would die first.

Xiong Yi's eyelids suddenly moved, and then he struggled to crawl up from the floor. He was breathing heavily, his vision was blurred, and due to the physiological and psychological pressure, he now looked like he was shrouded in a sense of decay.

The expression on Xiong Yi's face was first dazed, then became ferocious. He sternly called for soldiers and the military doctor. The doctor's hands trembled as he presented the medicine. The medicine was still a bit hot, but Xiong Yi couldn't care about that anymore; he cherished his life and just wanted to survive. Xiong Yi hurriedly gulped the medicine down his throat, not caring how hot it was.

Xu Fu sensed that his consciousness was actually no longer clear.

Xu Fu's heart felt as if it were being tightly gripped by a pair of large hands. He was a little nervous and a little afraid. It wasn't fear of what Xiong Yi might do. He just thought of the historical records about the First Emperor of Qin; perhaps he died like this in his later years. At that time, the First Emperor was cruel and obsessed with elixirs, and some even suspected whether he was poisoned by the harmful substances in the elixirs. The more he looked at Xiong Yi's appearance, the more determined Xu Fu became to change history. He would never let Ying Zheng become the First Emperor of Qin as recorded in later history.

Xiong Yi breathed heavily, and then his gaze landed on Xu Fu nearby.

Xiong Yi faintly knew in his heart that he might die, and the hatred and madness in his heart were pushed to the peak. If he died, wouldn't Xu Fu be able to return to Ying Zheng's side? Xiong Yi sneered, his expression looking strange and somewhat ferocious. Supported by soldiers, he climbed up. "Go... go call for battle!" "Bring him." Xiong Yi looked in Xu Fu's direction.

Although the soldiers were puzzled, they did as they were told.

Xu Fu was roughly dragged out of the tent.

Xu Fu wasn't angry. He watched Xiong Yi hurriedly assemble troops and generals, and took him onto the war chariot.

"Go, tell people to take the things and follow closely behind. Today, we must take Ye City," Xiong Yi said coldly.

Xu Fu's heart tightened slightly. Xiong Yi had moved up the plan to take Ye City because he knew he might not have long to live? Xu Fu's heart was full of tension, but on the other hand, it was full of anticipation. Because he knew that perhaps today he could return to the Qin army.

The war chariot moved forward, and about half an hour later, they arrived at the battlefield.

The Qin army had already engaged in battle, with Meng Tian in the lead and Ying Zheng in the back. Xu Fu saw Ying Zheng's figure almost at a glance. Because the distance was slightly far, Xu Fu could only faintly glimpse Ying Zheng's outline. He could almost guess that Ying Zheng's face must be exceptionally dark, wishing he could kill Xiong Yi immediately.

And Xiong Yi, on the contrary, became much more spirited at this moment, looking even a bit high-spirited. Xu Fu was really worried whether this was a "flash of brilliance" before death.

"Bring it up." Xiong Yi waved his hand to order the people behind him.

The soldiers struggled to carry a large box forward. Inside the box were black round balls that were very familiar to Xu Fu. Were they those dud bombs again? No, it wasn't. Xiong Yi looked so confident; could he have improved these bombs?

Xu Fu felt that pushing Xiong Yi into a desperate situation didn't seem very good. He couldn't help but worry whether Xiong Yi would do something insane later. They were all people who valued their lives; the most feared thing was when an opponent no longer cared about their own life.

"Light it." Xiong Yi said in a deep voice.

The Qin army didn't know what was happening on this side, so they were full of confusion and patiently waited for the Zhao army to make their next move.

Warfare in this era was like this; not everyone would rush up to fight together; they had to follow a code.

But Xu Fu felt... Xiong Yi didn't seem to intend to follow the code anymore.

The soldiers hurriedly lit those round balls.

Xu Fu's heart skipped a beat.

What was he planning to do? Blow everyone up? Or throw them all at the Qin army?

"What do you want to do?" By the time Xu Fu came to his senses, he found that he had asked the question without realizing it.

"It's a pity, I thought I could keep you by my side..." Xiong Yi murmured in a very low voice. As his words fell, the soldiers had already thrown the round balls in their hands.

The Qin army knew that those round balls had no power, just to scare people. Seeing this, they even sneered and didn't dodge.

Xu Fu's face changed. "These things... you've improved them?"

Xiong Yi didn't speak.

Xu Fu shouted, "Everyone, get out of the way!"
chapters.title: 第181章
第182章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu’s shout had been too sudden, and many were unable to react in time. Ying Zheng, sharing an incredible tacit understanding with him, immediately ordered Meng Tian to lead the troops in a retreat the moment the cry left Xu Fu’s lips. Neither of them had expected Xiong Yi to start throwing those spheres without a word. No matter how fast Ying Zheng’s reactions were, they couldn't outpace the falling spheres.

Once the spheres hit the ground, any soldier touched by the sparks would quickly burst into flames.

With a "boom," that entire area was swallowed by fire.

Xu Fu’s heart felt as if it had jumped into his throat in an instant; he didn't dare look closely at what was happening on the side blocked off by the fire. Worry and fierce anger enveloped him simultaneously. He gripped his palms tightly, wishing he could stomp the man beside him into the ground. Was this Xiong Yi’s plan? If he couldn't survive, he would just drag everyone else down with him?

Xu Fu hadn't expected that he had underestimated Xiong Yi’s level of madness. Listening to the screams of the Qin soldiers, the smile on his face grew even brighter.

He whispered, "Continue."

A soldier nearby couldn't help but remind him, "General, we only have so many... if we use them all up..."

"This is a military order," Xiong Yi said coldly.

The soldier didn't dare to persuade him further and had no choice but to start bringing out more spheres.

Xu Fu felt a sense of fear, but also a sliver of relief. If Xiong Yi, in his madness, used up all his secret weapons without leaving a single one for the Zhao state, then the Zhao state would remain nothing to fear in the future. On the contrary, once the Qin state obtained these new technologies, its military power would reach a new level.

...But those were things for later. If Xiong Yi dealt a ruthless blow today—he didn't need to kill many people, just endanger Ying Zheng’s life—then today would be a massive victory for Xiong Yi.

The spheres were thrown out one after another; at a glance, it looked like a thunderstorm of lightning falling from the sky.

These spheres not only burned quickly, but many also emitted explosive sounds, scattering the flames and widening the range of impact. However, since there was no shrapnel or similar material inside, the destructive power wasn't lethal enough to be catastrophic.

Wails rose throughout the Qin army, and there were many cases of friendly fire among the Zhao troops as well. The Zhao soldiers looked at Xiong Yi with increasing awe and terror.

Xiong Yi wrapped his arm around Xu Fu’s waist. Xu Fu struggled twice, and Xiong Yi, accidentally pulling at his wound, was forced to loosen his grip.

The smile on Xiong Yi’s face was grim. He shouted, "Zhao Zheng, if you want to save Xu Fu, I want you to walk out through that ring of fire."

Xu Fu’s expression darkened.

This classic trope from television dramas... it was truly unbearable! He had no desire to be the weak heroine waiting to be rescued by the male lead.

Xiong Yi pulled out a sphere and placed it on Xu Fu’s shoulder. "Zhao Zheng, if you don't come out, I will set Xu Fu on fire. You had better think carefully: do you choose to walk through the fire yourself, or let Xu Fu walk through it?"

Hearing this, Xu Fu couldn't help but sneer.

See, this was Xiong Yi’s so-called love. He knew that in a moment like this, Xiong Yi would be more than willing to use him to threaten Ying Zheng.

But would he give him that chance? Xu Fu drew the dagger from his sleeve and stabbed Xiong Yi in the waist. The wound on Xiong Yi’s waist was reopened, and he couldn't help but let out a miserable, angry cry. As he reached out to grab Xu Fu, Xu Fu slammed into his waist and flipped off the chariot.

The movement looked extremely cool, but when he hit the ground, pain swept through Xu Fu’s entire body. The ground was too hard, not to mention the gravel.

"Catch him!" Xiong Yi’s eyes were bloodshot, his expression hideous. He roared and prepared to flip off the chariot to follow him.

The surrounding Zhao soldiers swarmed forward, attempting to capture Xu Fu.

Xu Fu gripped the cloth strip on his wrist tightly.

If you don't listen to me now, I’m going to die here!!!

Xu Fu had calculated how to kill Xiong Yi and how to steal his technologies, but he had failed to consider how he would escape once everything was done.

The soldiers’ gazes were vicious, as savage as Xiong Yi’s. Xu Fu even felt that in that instant, their eyes were glowing red.

"Ying Zheng!" Xu Fu shouted sharply, no longer caring how hoarse his voice was. "Wait for me over there!" His tone was full of command, leaving no room for rebuttal, his aura reaching its peak.

On the other side of the fire, Ying Zheng paused, his expression dark, his hand gripping the Qin sword at his waist.

Meng Tian and the others were ready for battle, and the situation wasn't as dire as Xiong Yi had imagined.

Xu Fu’s warning shout just now had played a major role.

Because of the training over the past few days, and the fact that Xu Fu was still in the enemy camp, the Qin army was filled with rage and fighting spirit, no longer fearing those strange spheres.

"Turn! Go that way!" Meng Tian didn't care about formation anymore. He led the soldiers to flank through a side path. If he didn't see Xu Fu soon, not to mention the King, even he felt an unbearable, extreme tension in his heart.

The Qin army immediately changed course.

Meanwhile, the Zhao army had surrounded Xu Fu, and it looked like he wouldn't be able to fly away even with wings.

Xiong Yi’s sanity had crumbled to a terrifying degree. He stared fixedly at Xu Fu, his jealousy and madness making his features increasingly hideous.

"You’re going to die." At such a moment, after standing up from the ground, Xu Fu was surprisingly no longer nervous.

Xiong Yi sneered, "I know."

"Why don't you ask me if I can save you?"

Xiong Yi gritted his teeth fiercely. "How could you save me? Your heart is full of Zhao Zheng; I’m afraid you’d kill me for him in a heartbeat..."

When the name "Zhao Zheng" was mentioned, Xu Fu didn't react for a moment.

"To survive, I would naturally save you." Xu Fu felt his life could still be salvaged.

Xiong Yi smiled, "No, you wouldn't. You aren't that kind of person. I know your pride better than anyone... you’re trying to trick me..."

Xu Fu: "..."

How the hell did I not know I had such "pride"?

A reputation for being aloof really kills people!

I just want to live right now!

Xu Fu roared in his heart, but Xiong Yi couldn't hear these words. Even if he said them out loud, Xiong Yi wouldn't care, because in Xiong Yi’s mind, his image was already fixed—he was the aloof and steadfast Xu Fu. So no matter what he said now, Xiong Yi would stubbornly believe in the image from his memories.

Xu Fu tugged at the cloth on his wrist. Oh well, if the worst comes to the worst, I’ll just be a hero again in the next life.

Anyway, he had already put on enough of a show in the Warring States period... his legend was already all over the world. Everyone has to die eventually. Being able to die with the villain, Xu Fu felt he was quite heroic; perhaps his name would even appear in future history books.

Xiong Yi got off the chariot and walked slowly toward him. He smiled slightly, "Didn't you say you would only betray Zhao Zheng if you lost your memory? I’ve thought of a way to make you lose all your memories." He squeezed the sphere in his hand.

By now, the Qin army had circled around, met the Zhao army, and were locked in combat.

The spheres the Zhao army had thrown earlier hadn't caused many casualties to the Qin army; instead, it had ignited their fighting spirit, making them even more ferocious and formidable. A sharp army like that was hard for the Zhao troops to block.

Screams soon erupted within the Zhao ranks.

Xiong Yi, however, acted as if he heard nothing. He didn't give any tactical orders, nor did he even turn his head to look.

He walked slowly to Xu Fu and ordered someone to bring a torch over.

Xu Fu looked at the sphere bomb in his hand, and a thin layer of cold sweat gradually seeped onto his back. Was Xiong Yi going to light it?

How could Xu Fu know that his act of getting off the chariot and telling Ying Zheng not to come over had completely triggered Xiong Yi? So, regardless of whether Ying Zheng came or not, Xiong Yi had decided to take him down as a cushion.

"Once you leave with me in the fire, everything will be fine. How could a dead person still have memories? Don't you agree? Perhaps we will meet in the underworld. By then, you will have forgotten Zhao Zheng and will only belong to me." The expression on Xiong Yi’s face was unexpectedly calm, but after hearing his words, Xu Fu couldn't remain calm at all.

Xiong Yi is a total psychopath!

Ying Zheng approached on horseback and asked sharply from across the way, "Xiong Yi, what are you doing?"

Everyone who heard the name looked blank.

Only Xiong Yi burst into laughter.

Zhao Yi? That wasn't him at all! He was Xiong Yi, the son of Lord Changping! A descendant of the Chu royal family! His grandfather was the Crown Prince of Chu! He was once the most favored junior of the Empress Dowager Huayang of Qin! He was the Young Master Xiong Yi in Xianyang whom no one dared to offend...

Xiong Yi looked at Ying Zheng with bloodshot eyes and reached out to grab Xu Fu, pulling him close. "What am I doing? I’m taking him with me to die!"

Riding a horse wasn't suitable for the battlefield because there were no stirrups or saddles, making it hard to steady one’s body. If one relied on charging on horseback, it was very likely they would fall off and die. But at this moment, Ying Zheng didn't care about anything. He galloped his horse toward Xiong Yi. Despite the short distance, the Zhao soldiers blocking the way made the path feel incredibly long.

"Light it," Xiong Yi said coldly.

The soldier beside him froze, his face pale, his lips purple, trembling as he said, "General... this... no..."

"Light it!" Xiong Yi roared. "When that King of Qin comes over, perhaps we can kill him too. Such a good opportunity, how can we let it pass?" After all, Xiong Yi wasn't a Zhao native, and the soldier was naturally more tempted by the prospect of killing the King of Qin. He gritted his teeth, obeyed Xiong Yi, and used the torch in his hand to light the sphere.

Xiong Yi held Xu Fu firmly. No matter how much Xu Fu kicked or struck his wounds, Xiong Yi didn't budge.

Xu Fu felt as if he could hear the sizzling of the fuse being lit, each sound knocking against his heart. His heart pounded wildly to that rhythm, and Xu Fu even felt he couldn't catch his breath for a moment.

This guy is even more brutal than that gang boss!

Xu Fu felt his death this time was quite unjust...

Seeing that Xu Fu seemed to have given up struggling and that sparks were already jumping on the sphere, Ying Zheng watched as Xiong Yi held the sphere in his hand without letting go. The flames scorched his palm, but he seemed to have lost all sensation, showing no intention of releasing it.

Ying Zheng stared at this scene, his eyes splitting with rage.

In his eyes, anger and murderous intent seemed ready to erupt.

He jumped off his horse, regardless of the danger, using the Zhao soldiers as stepping stones to lunge straight toward Xiong Yi.

No matter what, he had to at least take Xu Fu out of Xiong Yi’s arms.

The Qin army also lunged at the Zhao army like madmen.

Originally, there was no such way to fight, but today Xiong Yi had already broken the rules, so they didn't care about anything else. Under their brutal tactics, the blood of the Zhao army soon stained the land. Meng Tian also followed Ying Zheng’s example, riding his horse and trying to jump over to help rescue Xu Fu.

The sphere burned more and more fiercely.

Xu Fu could clearly feel a wave of heat rushing toward him—the heat wave released as the sphere burned.

The feeling of death looming over him was truly unbearable.

Only at this moment did Xu Fu realize that he had been lying to himself. He didn't want to die at all... he couldn't bear to die. His mind was filled with Ying Zheng, Fusu, Huhai, Wei Liao, Li Si... many people flashed through his mind in rapid succession. He actually couldn't bear it. How could he, with such a wonderful life, die with someone like Xiong Yi?

Xu Fu gripped the dagger in his sleeve.

The sharp blade cut his finger.

Dotting with cinnabar, forming a human shape...

The blood on his finger rubbed against the small cloth strip...

Xiong Yi thought he was going to use the dagger to attack him again, so he reached out and grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist tightly. He whispered, "Don't struggle, you have no chance left..."

With a "whoosh," something darted past at high speed.

Xu Fu felt his wrist loosen.

The sphere expanded and then suddenly exploded, fire filling the sky—no, perhaps it just filled his eyes. Xu Fu squinted, his heart tightening violently.

The sound of the explosion startled everyone.

The Qin sword in Ying Zheng’s hand pierced Xiong Yi’s waist and abdomen. He reached out to grab Xu Fu, but the flames and heat wave rushed toward him after the explosion. Everyone stared blankly at the scene. They didn't know if it was their imagination, but the power of this sphere seemed stronger than all the others.

Xiong Yi smiled, but the smile on his face only lasted for a second.

A huge black shadow sprang up from behind Xu Fu, like a giant net, covering him in the middle. Xiong Yi was sent flying by a fierce force, the Qin sword still stuck in his stomach.

That black shadow stood, crawled, and curled up.

Although it made no sound, it gave the illusion that it was roaring fiercely.

The Zhao army had already collapsed in terror.

No flame could get near Xu Fu. The scene Xiong Yi had imagined—dying wrapped in fire with Xu Fu, or setting Ying Zheng on fire—none of it came to pass. Oh wait, one thing did: he was covered in fire, poisoned even more severely, his face blue and purple, blood gushing from his wounds. He was a dead man!

It’s just that Xu Fu wasn't dying with him.

If Xiong Yi, who could throw fireballs and was impervious to blades, was already terrifying, then Xu Fu, who was impervious even to fire, was even more so.

In their eyes, it was as if the flames were bowing to Xu Fu.

Although in Xu Fu’s eyes, such a puppet was indeed magical, in the eyes of others, it was equivalent to the power of a god.

Xiong Yi lay on the ground, gradually being swallowed by the fire. Everyone knew he couldn't possibly survive.

The Qin army had already charged over, their general was dead, and there was such a god-like figure... the fear in the hearts of the Zhao army grew, almost completely consuming their minds. Once a hint of panic spread, it easily infected everyone. They had no general left to lead them out of such panic.

Some couldn't help but kneel on the ground, choosing to abandon their weapons, and their actions spread to others.

One after another, people discarded their weapons.

The Qin army watched this scene, stunned, and then felt disdain. If it were them, no matter what, they would never abandon their weapons and admit defeat like that! It was no surprise that the Zhao army was repeatedly defeated.

Their eyes turned toward Ying Zheng and Xu Fu.

To them, Xu Fu was a god-like existence to be worshipped, and the King’s actions just now made them feel his decisiveness and his humanity. The King was not cold and cruel. The scene of the King saving someone just now ignited the emotions in their hearts.

The Qin soldiers’ gazes were exceptionally burning; they almost wanted to kneel down in their direction immediately.

Once people lost their fighting spirit, it was very difficult to pick it up again.

In the end, the Zhao army had all surrendered, and those who didn't were all executed.

Xu Fu touched his wrist; it took a long time before he felt the shadow behind him disappear. Xu Fu slowly exhaled, his legs as soft as noodles. Fear and exhaustion made it hard for him to walk steadily.

Ying Zheng stepped forward at the right time, scooped him up, and carried him back into the Qin army.

The casualties on both sides and the Zhao prisoners were quickly organized and counted.

Ying Zheng took Xu Fu onto his horse and slowly led his men toward the Zhao camp. Xu Fu didn't look back at Xiong Yi once. For someone who brought him such bad memories, unless he was a masochist, he wouldn't keep thinking about him.

Xu Fu leaned into Ying Zheng’s arms.

The chest, unchanged as always, was not soft.

But Xu Fu felt very comfortable, and a sense of stability quickly rose in his heart.

Ying Zheng kept his face tight and didn't speak; he just gripped Xu Fu’s hand.

Meng Tian caught up, also letting out a slight sigh of relief.

After the count was finished, the Qin army didn't rest; they headed straight for the camp. The Zhao camp didn't have many people left guarding it, so it wasn't difficult for the Qin army to attack their defenses. Once the Qin army surrounded them, the Zhao soldiers inside panicked slightly before grabbing their weapons to stand their ground.

Xu Fu pinched the back of Ying Zheng’s hand. "Don't let them advance yet."

Ying Zheng didn't doubt his words at all and immediately passed the order to Meng Tian. Meng Tian also had extreme trust in Xu Fu, so he immediately ordered them to stop.

"Outside the Zhao camp, there is medicinal powder and caltrops. If you aren't careful, you’ll be hit. You can have the soldiers surround the perimeter, but don't move forward. Everyone else should enter through the main gate." The Zhao camp looked well-defended, but in reality, the loopholes were too obvious.

Because the Zhao soldiers themselves needed to enter and exit, there was nothing set up at the gate. So the Qin army just needed to go through there.

Although the entrance was narrow, and there was a saying about one man holding the pass, Xu Fu really looked down on these Zhao soldiers, especially after staying in the Zhao camp for a while. If they wanted to stop the Qin army, it would be truly difficult.

Once Xu Fu’s meaning was conveyed, Meng Tian immediately knew how to attack.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng stayed in the rear. In less than half an hour, the Qin army had broken through the camp, and all surviving Zhao soldiers became prisoners.

Xu Fu struggled out of Ying Zheng’s arms and jumped off the horse.

Ying Zheng followed closely behind, walking slowly into the main tent.

Inside the main tent, that little broken tripod was still sitting in the center of the table. Xu Fu walked up, lifted the lid, and saw the shimmering liquid inside—quite beautiful. Xu Fu covered it expressionlessly. He called a soldier in and gave the tripod to him.

Ying Zheng was surprised to see the small tripod. "Isn't this a very important item of yours? Is it okay to let a soldier carry it?"

"It’s not that important, I just kept it to kill Xiong Yi," Xu Fu said lightly. "The stuff inside is poisonous, don't let anyone else touch it."

The soldier shivered, nodded repeatedly, and hurried out, holding it carefully, not daring to bump it at all.

Ying Zheng stroked Xu Fu’s cheek with a complex expression. "You’ve worked hard." He didn't want to worry about whether or not to stop Xu Fu anymore. Heartache, worry—he swallowed it all. It was enough that he could come to clean up the mess. It would be even better if the opponent wasn't someone like Xiong Yi who had ulterior motives toward Xu Fu!

The two of them working together to pacify the six states was actually a pretty good feeling.

Ying Zheng was immersed in his own thoughts; he was almost moved by his own tolerance and gentleness toward Xu Fu. In his life, he had never poured these emotions into anyone else.

Xu Fu tugged his sleeve. "Order someone to search Xiong Yi’s body, then call Meng Tian. I want to take you all to a place."

Ying Zheng had to stop his train of thought.

Xu Fu took him out of the tent, and since Meng Tian happened to be outside, Xu Fu called him along, and they brought some soldiers as well.

"Let’s go." Xu Fu led them out of the camp and over a hillside.

Everyone was confused, but no one questioned Xu Fu. They kept their mouths shut and followed him honestly until they reached a cave.

Meng Tian asked first, "Shuzhang, what is this?"

"Do you know where those strange weapons of the Zhao state were made?" Xu Fu pointed at the dark cave entrance. "Right inside here."

Everyone was shocked. Right inside here? In this gloomy-looking cave?

Xu Fu walked in front, Ying Zheng following closely by his side to support his waist, in case he collapsed from exhaustion. This intimate and ambiguous posture didn't make the Qin soldiers feel anything was wrong; on the contrary, they thought the scene was very beautiful and harmonious.

The people inside didn't know what had happened; they could faintly hear the sounds of shouting while forging iron.

A gust of wind blew from inside, and a foul odor drifted out. Smelling such a scent for the first time, everyone couldn't help but frown, and some even had the urge to turn around and leave.

"Come here," Xu Fu whispered to the soldier holding the tripod.

The soldier walked over.

"Carry it inside. When you’re about to see people, pour the contents on the ground, then come out immediately, understand?"

The soldier nodded. "Understood." His hand holding the small tripod was miraculously steady.

Xu Fu also ordered people to find soil. Once the people inside reacted and collapsed, they would use the soil to cover the mercury liquid when they went in, to prevent the drifting odor from poisoning them too. Although it was their first time smelling it and it might not cause major harm, it was always better to be careful.

The soldiers did as he ordered. Meng Tian and the rest of the soldiers waited quietly outside the cave.

Ying Zheng looked at Xu Fu’s side profile as he gave orders seriously, his heart feeling as if it were being stirred by a pair of hands, his love unable to calm down for a long time.

...Extremely charming! Ying Zheng thought secretly.

Not long after, Xu Fu estimated that the time was about right, so he let the soldiers go in to fill the soil, and then they walked into the cave entrance.

Just like when Xu Fu first came, they walked with some trepidation. But since there were many of them, it bolstered their courage. After several turns, Xu Fu led them deep into the cave.

The Zhao soldiers who had been making the weapons had already collapsed on the ground, the symptoms of poisoning becoming increasingly obvious. Just by looking at them, Xu Fu knew they wouldn't live much longer.

Xu Fu felt that when it came to cruelty, Ying Zheng really couldn't compare to Xiong Yi.

Of course, if Ying Zheng didn't have him by his side, after obtaining those methods from Zheng You'an, he might have gone down this path too. Not regarding the lives of ordinary people as anything would eventually lead to trouble.

Xu Fu pointed to the things still being refined and introduced them in a low voice.

Meng Tian and Ying Zheng were both very knowledgeable; they knew the value of these things, so after hearing about them, they couldn't help but be tempted. If they had these things, the Qin state would definitely be able to use them better than the Zhao state. They would use these things to exert maximum power and sweep away the six states!

Xu Fu said, "If we can find the records, I might even be able to improve these things. Xiong Yi didn't do a good job, and besides, he used the lives of his subordinates to trade for it. Look at them; the soldiers here are all poisoned." Xu Fu pointed to a pool not far away. "Look, this cinnabar, once liquefied, will emit gas. Smelling this gas for a long time will cause poisoning."

Meng Tian fell silent.

They all understood what Xu Fu meant.

Xu Fu didn't want to use the lives of soldiers or craftsmen as stepping stones like Xiong Yi, even though many kings didn't consider that a big deal. What did the death of ordinary people matter? As long as it was a contribution to the country, it was meaningful.

As soon as he finished speaking, a soldier hurried in and said, "King, General, a bundle of silk cloth was found on the enemy general."

The expression on Xu Fu’s face softened immediately.

He knew this thing existed!

Ying Zheng saw Xu Fu’s joy at a glance. He held Xu Fu’s hand and walked out first. Meng Tian didn't intend to stay long either, following behind with the soldiers while ordering them to clean up the cave.

Someone presented the silk cloth.

Xu Fu grabbed the silk cloth and flipped through it hurriedly. It was actually the incredibly familiar simplified Chinese characters, accompanied by illustrations. Xu Fu didn't know whether to laugh or cry. No wonder Xiong Yi’s creations were so rough and simple. Because he didn't recognize some of the simplified characters, he could only guess based on the illustrations, which naturally led to errors. Now that Zheng You'an was dead, by some twist of fate, he was the only one left in the world who could understand this.

Ying Zheng stared at the silk cloth for a while, frowned, and said coldly, "What kind of junk is this?" Ying Zheng thought it was useless.

Xu Fu said calmly, "I recognize the characters on it, but others don't... no, perhaps apart from me, no one else will recognize them."

Hearing this, although Ying Zheng was surprised, he didn't worry at all about what would happen if Xu Fu betrayed him in the future... At this moment, his heart was filled only with pride—pride for Xu Fu. Only he could recognize the characters; wasn't that something to be proud of? Ying Zheng felt that what Xu Fu said to him back then was truly correct.

After the bitterness comes the sweetness; misfortune departs and fortune arrives.

This good fortune was just following him like this.

Ying Zheng’s gaze toward Xu Fu suddenly became so gentle it seemed like it could drip water. Xu Fu, suddenly receiving such a gaze, wasn't quite used to it. According to past experience, shouldn't Ying Zheng be looking at him with extreme displeasure? Could it be that after many blows and injuries, Ying Zheng had become accustomed to him acting so recklessly? Xu Fu felt a faint sense of loss, accompanied by a touch of melancholy.

Xu Fu put away the silk cloth and couldn't help but ask in a low voice, "Aren't you curious why only I can understand it?"

Ying Zheng hugged his waist, applying force. "A-Fu is intelligent, naturally different from others." In fact, Ying Zheng occasionally wondered, was Xu Fu really not a god incarnate? So many magical things happened around him; perhaps he really was a god...

Hearing this reason, Xu Fu felt deeply defeated.

Was it really "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"? Ying Zheng had already found excuses for all his abnormal behavior, and he didn't need to rack his brains to think of how to explain it.

They didn't stay long in the Zhao camp. Ying Zheng couldn't wait to take Xu Fu back to the Qin camp. If it weren't for Xu Fu’s excessive loss of energy, Ying Zheng would have already wanted to keep Xu Fu and eat him from inside out to satisfy his longing.

When the Qin camp heard the news of Xu Fu’s safe return, Jianjia was the first to rush out.

"Is the Master alright?" Jianjia was full of guilt. He still felt that Xu Fu had fallen into the enemy camp because of him. But in reality, Xu Fu had already had this idea; he only used his own method after failing to get it through Jianjia. And in fact, Xiong Yi really hadn't guarded against him.

Jianjia couldn't help but ask hurriedly, "Is Xiong Yi dead?"

"Dead," Xu Fu nodded.

Jianjia opened his mouth wide. "Did the Master kill him? The Master is truly amazing!"

"He was poisoned by his own desires."

Jianjia looked blank.

Xu Fu reached out and patted his head without explaining further. He could talk about these things in detail with Ying Zheng, but there was no need to explain to others.

Others only cared that Xu Fu was safe, so naturally, they wouldn't ask more, and they hurried to drag Jianjia away.

Sangzhong looked back at this direction with reluctance. Xu Fu gave him a gentle look, and Sangzhong’s eyes reddened as he left without looking back.

This time, it could be considered a lucky accident; it actually helped Sangzhong resolve the shadow in his heart, at least so he wouldn't dwell on his disappearance in the tent. After all, this time, he had given Sangzhong a chance to save him. For Sangzhong, that was doing something he had failed to do before—he had saved Xu Fu, and in doing so, he had saved himself.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng returned to the camp. After bathing, Xu Fu leaned softly against Ying Zheng, and only then did he tell Ying Zheng in detail about what happened in the Zhao camp. He said that Xiong Yi hadn't done anything to him, that he had made Xiong Yi go sleep on the floor, and how Xiong Yi had died.

Ying Zheng was amazed. "If cinnabar is poisonous, then why do elixirs need to be made with cinnabar?"

"Taking too much cinnabar is inherently bad. Once it becomes liquid, the harm to people is even greater. What the predecessors left behind isn't necessarily correct. In my opinion, elixirs don't need these things at all."

Regardless of whether the predecessors were right or not, Xu Fu was right at this moment.

Ying Zheng nodded, indicating his agreement with Xu Fu.

"This poison acts very slowly. At first, I didn't think Xiong Yi was already poisoned. I just needed to add a little fire, and he would die." The stuff in that little tripod was actually just the final straw that broke the camel’s back.

"At first, I thought if his poisoning was very slow, I would lure him into fortune-telling for me, or make him think there was a way to make me lose my memory. I deliberately wrote the wrong method on the silk cloth. If he discovered it, he would go find sulfur and other things... he thought it was something that could make me lose my memory, but I could turn them into things that kill..."

Xu Fu used his limited brain capacity to think of limited ways to kill, but he had made countless assumptions in advance, thinking he must kill Xiong Yi while he was confused in front of him.

"...I just forgot, after killing Xiong Yi, how was I supposed to escape."

Ying Zheng’s expression darkened. "..." If Xiong Yi hadn't been insane enough to bring people to the battlefield, Ying Zheng might not have been able to save Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but reach out to cup Xu Fu’s neck, then leaned down and kissed him deeply. Sure enough, no matter how intelligent Xu Fu was, he still had to have him, the King.
