For Ying Zheng, looking down on Xu Fu was now the same as looking down on him.

With Young Lord Yuan’s attitude toward Xu Fu being so malicious, how could he expect to be treated with gentleness? He should have realized what he was the moment he stepped into Xianyang!

The envoy was somewhat panicked and hurriedly tugged at Young Lord Yuan’s robe.

Young Lord Yuan ground his teeth in anger, but he wasn't foolish enough to be beyond saving. After Ying Zheng displayed extreme displeasure, Young Lord Yuan finally realized that whether he liked it or not, he had to pay his respects to Xu Fu today. In Young Lord Yuan’s view, this was perhaps the Qin State trying to trample on the face of Han. He bent his back once more, but this time it was directed at Xu Fu.

"...Young Lord Yuan pays his respects to the Shu Zhang." His tone was very stiff, and he hadn't even fully masked the expression on his face.

Xu Fu looked at the expression on his face and could almost immediately tell what Young Lord Yuan was thinking.

Oh... perhaps he was saying, "This damned male favorite." Perhaps he was also saying, "The King of Qin is so bewitched by male beauty that he’s lost his mind. Male beauty ruins men! As a young lord of Han, how can I bow to such a person?"

It wasn't that Xu Fu possessed mind-reading powers, but rather that Young Lord Yuan’s expression was simply too transparent.

Ying Zheng, of course, also saw Young Lord Yuan’s reluctance. He suppressed the surging anger in his heart and did not make Young Lord Yuan do it again. No matter how many times he did it now, Young Lord Yuan would still not respect Xu Fu; even making him kowtow would be meaningless. Once the State of Han was gone, Young Lord Yuan wouldn't even have a place to kowtow. At that time, he would be nothing, and could he still expect to see the Shu Zhang of the Qin State?

After Young Lord Yuan and the envoy stood up, Ying Zheng didn't pay much attention to them.

Young Lord Yuan presented the map and the documents, then could only wait honestly below.

Ying Zheng grasped the documents in his hand with an unreadable expression. Young Lord Yuan tried his best to find some sign of joy on his face, but found none. Young Lord Yuan felt uneasy, not knowing whether this posture of Ying Zheng’s meant he was satisfied or not.

"King of Qin..." the envoy finally couldn't hold back and spoke up.

"I know. You may leave," Ying Zheng said coldly.

The envoy gritted his teeth; he ultimately didn't dare to press Ying Zheng further and had to take Young Lord Yuan away. If Young Lord Yuan were a sensible and clever person, Ying Zheng naturally wouldn't be stingy about treating them better, but since Young Lord Yuan was so clueless, Ying Zheng had no need to give him a pleasant look.

The hall soon became quiet.

Ying Zheng’s expression softened considerably. He turned his head and asked Xu Fu in a low voice, "That person offended you just now; do you still feel unhappy?"

"Why would I bother with him?" Xu Fu brushed it off and reached out to grab the map by his side. Such an action would normally be considered highly disrespectful, but the palace attendants nearby just watched.

What was grabbing a map without saying a word? At least he didn't reach out to scratch the King, the attendants thought with extreme composure.

"Let me see, what land did Han offer?" Xu Fu had no impression of this period of history. Now that he had been by Ying Zheng’s side for a long time, Xu Fu could recognize ancient maps. The territory drawn on it was Nanyang. Xu Fu had no impression of other places, but he did have some impression of Nanyang. Nanyang was one of the five capitals of the Han Dynasty. What were the five capitals of the Han? Nanyang, Luoyang, Linzi, Handan, and Chengdu. Xu Fu even vaguely remembered that Nanyang had built famous water conservancy projects during the Han Dynasty, which were later known as one of the three major irrigation areas alongside Dujiangyan and the Zheng Guo Canal.

Hmm, it seemed that if water conservancy were developed, it should be a good place.

"Not bad," Xu Fu said aloud unconsciously.

Ying Zheng glanced at it but didn't speak; he didn't think much of this piece of land. Xu Fu knew why he didn't think much of it—because Ying Zheng was eyeing the entire State of Han anyway.

"When the time comes, we will go to Han to receive this land. Will you go with me?" Ying Zheng had learned a method: blocking is not as good as diverting. He would take Xu Fu with him whenever he went out. He knew Xu Fu’s temperament very well; after tossing about outside for a while, Xu Fu would feel tired and would long to return to Xianyang to live in peace.

"Alright." Xu Fu was quite looking forward to that day.

It would be like a king inspecting his own territory. That feeling must be great.

...

Young Lord Yuan was arranged to stay in the Qin palace. The treatment given to him was no better than that of Young Lord Jia back then, but at least it wasn't as remote. However, Young Lord Yuan’s temper was far less patient than Young Lord Jia’s. Once he found that his living quarters were not to his liking, he immediately started making a scene. But the courtyard full of palace attendants and servants ignored him and let him make his scene. When Young Lord Yuan tried to discipline them, they would nimbly hide away, leaving him no chance to lay a hand on them.

Young Lord Yuan was not clever enough; seeing that no one paid him any mind when he made a scene, he simply left the courtyard.

When Xu Fu ran into him, he had just been caught by the palace guards.

The Qin palace was not a place to wander about aimlessly. Moreover, since Young Lord Yuan was from Han, the guards naturally wouldn't go easy on him.

As Xu Fu approached, he could hear Young Lord Yuan’s wailing.

"What is this for?" Being pinned to the ground was, after all, somewhat embarrassing for Young Lord Yuan. Regardless, he was a young lord of Han; this appearance made the Qin State look too much like a bully... well, although the Qin State had always been a bully.

Seeing Xu Fu, the guards immediately paid their respects and said in a low voice, "This person was acting too suspiciously, so we apprehended him."

"Let him go; he is a young lord of Han," Xu Fu said. In fact, the guards might not have been unaware of his identity, but in the Qin palace, no matter who you were, they would first pretend not to know you and catch you anyway.

As soon as the guards let go, Young Lord Yuan immediately scrambled up from the ground, looking at Xu Fu with hateful eyes, and sneered, "Oh, it’s the Shu Zhang..." His tone sounded truly mocking.

Xu Fu really wanted to crack open his head to see if it was filled with straw.

He glanced coldly at Young Lord Yuan, "Has the young lord never been taught manners?"

Young Lord Yuan’s face changed instantly, "...You dare, you dare to speak to me like this?"

Xu Fu thought to himself, what is there not to dare? I even dare to lecture the King of Qin; what are you? You have to respect others to receive respect in return. A person like Young Lord Yuan didn't deserve his respect.

"Take him back to where he came from," Xu Fu ordered the guards directly.

The guards nodded and immediately stepped forward to surround Young Lord Yuan. Young Lord Yuan hadn't expected them to actually dare to take action. This Shu Zhang could freely command the palace guards? Had the King of Qin’s brain been kicked by a donkey? It was all the fault of the man in front of him, whose appearance was too bewitching! With such a face, if he wasn't a disaster, what was he?

Young Lord Yuan shouted loudly, "What are you? I am a young lord of Han, and you are but a Shu Zhang! A mere male favorite! Do you really think of yourself as the second Lord Longyang? Serving others with your looks, and you don't even feel shame!"

A burst of footsteps approached and then suddenly stopped.

Xu Fu turned his head to look.

Young Lord Yuan followed his gaze, and upon seeing that it wasn't the cruel King of Qin, he immediately breathed a sigh of relief. He stiffened his neck, putting on an appearance of cold, firm pride.

And Xu Fu was already struggling to keep from laughing out loud.

Not only was Young Lord Yuan’s head full of straw, but his luck was truly rotten.

Those who had stopped were Jianjia, Sangzhong, and Lord Longyang, with Han Fei and Yao Jia not far behind.

Oh, setting the others aside.

Lord Longyang!

You used him as an example right to his face, saying that serving with male beauty was a bad thing. If Xu Fu hadn't known what kind of person Lord Longyang was before, he knew very well now: Lord Longyang had high-level methods and was vengeful—exceptionally vengeful. Just think about what the State of Wei had been turned into; his handiwork was definitely involved. To say Lord Longyang served with his looks was more like saying the muddled King of Wei relied on Lord Longyang.

At this moment, there was no expression on Lord Longyang’s face, and his eyes were filled with coldness.

Beside him, Jianjia’s expression was even more unpleasant. If Xu Fu hadn't been standing there and hadn't spoken yet, Jianjia would have long since stepped forward to knock the blabbering Young Lord Yuan to the ground and give him a sound beating.

Seeing that Xu Fu remained silent for a long time, Young Lord Yuan thought he was rendered speechless by his anger, so he immediately wore a look of triumph and turned to leave.

These people wanted to drag him away, but he didn't even deign to stay in the same place as this Shu Zhang. It would only dirty the ground in front of him. Young Lord Yuan thought with full malice.

But without Xu Fu’s word, Young Lord Yuan could neither advance nor retreat. The guards were still surrounding him, and after the string of insults Young Lord Yuan had just spewed, the guards were also looking at him with angry faces, wishing they could skin him alive. Young Lord Yuan knew far too little about the Qin palace, and he knew far too little about the status Xu Fu held in Ying Zheng’s heart and how he was admired in the Qin palace.

If people had brought up Xu Fu being with Ying Zheng in the beginning, it might have had some effect, and someone might have said it was shameful for Xu Fu to serve as a male favorite. But so much time had passed, the ministers didn't dare to say a word, the Empress Dowager didn't interfere, the King of Qin’s concubines were happily enjoying their single lives, and the two sons had joyfully accepted Xu Fu as their father... Even the people of Qin believed that Xu Fu and Ying Zheng being together was a match made in heaven! In everyone’s eyes now, Xu Fu was an immortal who brought good luck; what did it matter if he messed with the King of Qin’s sexual orientation?

Who do you think you are? Is it your place to slander him like this?

Almost in that instant, everyone thought the same thing.

Young Lord Yuan was completely unaware that he had incurred public wrath.

Xu Fu looked at him and sighed lightly, his tone flat: "Young Lord Yuan, the State of Han will surely be destroyed by your hands in the future."

This sentence did not carry a harsh tone, but it was cold and detached, causing Young Lord Yuan to break into a cold sweat. Unwilling to admit that the aura on Xu Fu was too powerful, he stiffened his neck and shouted, "Audacious! What do you mean by that?"

"I said, if the State of Han is destroyed, it will surely be because of this mouth of yours," Xu Fu repeated coldly.

At this time, Han Fei and Yao Jia walked closer.

Han Fei looked surprised but did not greet Young Lord Yuan. Instead, when Young Lord Yuan saw him, he grabbed onto him like a life-saving straw and shouted, "Stutterer, come save me! This person is being rude to me! You must report this to the King of Qin and teach him a lesson!"

Han Fei’s face looked ugly, and he didn't speak.

And Xu Fu truly curled the corners of his mouth, revealing a smile.

He really couldn't hold it in anymore.

This child, why is he so stupid?

Knowing that Han Fei was the only one with blood ties to him who might save his life, he opened his mouth and called him "Stutterer." Such disrespect to an elder brother—he must have been like this back in Han. But this was not Han; this was the Qin State.

Xu Fu reminded him coldly, "Who is the young lord calling?"

"Han Fei, of course!"

"What nonsense is the young lord speaking? Han Fei died long ago," Lord Longyang stepped forward and said slowly.

Young Lord Yuan turned to look at him, thinking that this person was quite handsome, but those eyes were too chilling.

Young Lord Yuan couldn't help but shiver.

Ye... yes... Han Fei... wasn't he dead?

"You, you..." Young Lord Yuan cowered, unable to say a word for a long time.

"Why are you stuttering now?" Lord Longyang sneered, "I think this young lord of Han won't be able to leave this place in the future. Why would the King of Qin be willing to let such a dog out? What is the State of Han?" Lord Longyang reached out and pinched Young Lord Yuan’s chin; because of the force, Young Lord Yuan’s chin quickly turned red.

Lord Longyang cursed in a low voice, "You dog, you can't even see the situation clearly; you are truly stupid. Even if I smashed you and fed you to the vicious dogs, the dogs wouldn't want to eat you."

Xu Fu watched this scene: ...

At this moment, Lord Longyang looked truly... incredibly dominant!
chapters.title: 第184章

chapters.translated_text:
Lord Longyang and Jianjia both looked like they would draw their swords at the slightest provocation. Xu Fu thought for a moment; Gongzi Yuan could not die just yet.

"Take him away, and do not let Gongzi Yuan walk outside from now on." Xu Fu’s tone was light and calm, sounding like an elder gently soothing an unreasonable child.

"What do you mean?" Gongzi Yuan keenly sensed a crisis, his expression changing. The guards did not let him continue speaking; they stepped forward, grabbed him, and dragged him back. Gongzi Yuan wanted to struggle, but mindful of his royal dignity, he could only remain stiff. By the time he finally steeled himself to cast aside etiquette and decorum, he had already been dragged far away.

Lord Longyang sneered, "Actually, killing him wouldn't matter. As long as we say he was left here, the King of Han wouldn't dare reach out to ask for him. Once he's chopped up, who would ever know?"

Murder was nothing more than a casual remark in his mouth.

Although Xu Fu had long known how fierce he was, he was still startled by Lord Longyang’s blunt ruthlessness.

Seeing Xu Fu silent, Lord Longyang smiled, "What you did is just right, Sir. A dead person is no fun; he must be kept alive so he can learn his lesson properly."

Xu Fu agreed with Lord Longyang’s words from the bottom of his heart.

No matter how foolish Gongzi Yuan was, the fact that Han had submitted was set in stone. It probably wouldn't be a year before he was no longer a prince of Han.

Han Fei and Yao Jia had come to meet the King, and Han Fei was led away by Yao Jia, his face pale. Lord Longyang and the others had entered the palace to find Xu Fu.

"How will you thank me, Sir?" Lord Longyang clapped his hands, and Jianjia stepped forward, revealing what had been hidden within her sleeves.

A small, exquisitely crafted tripod was immediately revealed.

Xu Fu was surprised; he hadn't expected Lord Longyang to remember this. He had actually found him a new tripod—this must have been from years ago, right? Xu Fu took the tripod and toyed with it; it had the same familiar feel and shape, though the patterns carved on it were different from the previous one.

There were tiny bumps on the body of the tripod, with textures resembling tightly packed grains of rice.

It was the "powdered rice" pattern, one of the twelve imperial ornaments.

It looked impressive enough to fool people, but it was precisely because of this texture that it had lost its value. The twelve ornaments were formed during the Zhou Dynasty; how long had it been since the Zhou Dynasty? In other words, this thing couldn't even be considered an antique. What could something that wasn't an antique be worth? It couldn't be linked to any mysterious legends.

But Xu Fu had never figured out the magical effect of using the tripod to grind medicine, so after a moment of hesitation, he accepted it.

"Is there anything you need from me, Lord Longyang?" Xu Fu paused, "I naturally won't refuse."

Lord Longyang nodded, "I didn't really have anything to ask of you, Sir, but there is one thing right now."

"Oh? What is it?" Xu Fu also felt that Lord Longyang wouldn't need to ask him for anything. With Lord Longyang’s abilities, what could there be that he couldn't do himself?

"Jianjia refuses to share a room with me, what should I do?" Lord Longyang smiled slightly as he threw out this sentence.

Jianjia’s face turned bright red, and she gritted her teeth.

"This..." Xu Fu turned his head, pretending not to see the ferocious expression on Jianjia’s face, "Jianjia, what do you think should be done about this?"

Jianjia’s face grew redder and redder, and then she suddenly rushed forward, hoisted Lord Longyang onto her shoulder, and ran out of the palace.

Everyone was shocked.

Xu Fu: ...

He felt that, until now, who was on top and who was on bottom between Jianjia and Lord Longyang remained a mystery.

Jianjia ran off, and Sang Zhong, left behind, felt a bit awkward. After exchanging a few simple words with Xu Fu, he also took his leave.

Xu Fu stood there alone for a while, blinked, and simply returned to his sleeping quarters to fuss over Fusu and Huhai.

After that day, Gongzi Yuan, much like Gongzi Jia before him, almost vanished from the palace. The Han envoys didn't dare ask about his whereabouts, and when the envoy returned to his country to report, Ying Zheng told him that Gongzi Yuan would remain in Qin from then on.

The Han envoy initially thought the Qin King, who favored men, had taken a fancy to Gongzi Yuan, but as soon as the envoy saw Xu Fu’s face, he felt that was absolutely impossible. If the appearance of this Siche Shuzhang was like the stars in the sky, then his own prince’s appearance was like the mud on the ground. That was not an exaggeration in the slightest.

The envoy sighed inwardly, worried that Gongzi Yuan had offended the Qin King and might lose his life. But the envoy was of low status; in front of the Qin King, no matter how glib his tongue or how brilliant his diplomatic skills, he couldn't use any of them.

The Han envoy could only return, feeling stifled and aggrieved.

After nightfall that day, Gongzi Yuan began to make a scene in the palace. He hadn't expected the Qin state to really mean it when they said they wouldn't let him go. During these few days in the Qin palace, life was hardly fit for a human. A dignified prince of Han, having nothing he wanted, crying out to heaven and earth with no response, even the palace servants didn't hold him in any regard.

Gongzi Yuan tasted the bitterness of being looked down upon, but he still didn't know what he had done wrong.

Xu Fu called someone over to ask, and upon hearing that Gongzi Yuan was still unrepentant, he immediately lost any desire to be kind.

Fusu sat to the side, frowning at the mention of Gongzi Yuan’s name. Growing older, Fusu was increasingly able to discern people’s thoughts. He knew Xu Fu didn't like this person and immediately asked, "Where is he?"

The servant replied with the name of the courtyard, and Fusu nodded without saying anything else, turning back to talk to Xu Fu about gunpowder and new weapons, speaking with great interest. Xu Fu found it quite strange. After all, he remembered the historical Fusu as being the exact opposite of Qin Shi Huang; this eldest prince was soft-hearted and benevolent, which were not traits for the next Emperor of Qin, which is why Fusu was so easily killed by his brothers later on.

Xu Fu pushed these doubts out of his mind.

Perhaps history had its inaccuracies too.

"Brother..." Huhai ran in from outside the hall at some point and dragged Fusu away after a short while.

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief and sat at his desk, racking his brain to recall what high-tech knowledge he had from his past life—at least something that could help Ying Zheng.

Thinking and thinking, Xu Fu fell asleep. When he woke up the next day, he heard the palace servants talking about Gongzi Yuan. After washing up, Xu Fu called them over while eating breakfast and asked, "What happened to Gongzi Yuan?"

"He didn't want to stay in that courtyard and tried to climb over the wall in the middle of the night regardless of the consequences. Who knew... he fell from the wall. He had been making a fuss in the courtyard all day, and after he fell, someone heard the noise but didn't go to check. It wasn't until daytime that they called for a physician. The physician said that his lower body is afraid... afraid it might never regain feeling..."

That meant he was paralyzed, right?

Xu Fu had originally wanted to take a look, but thinking of Gongzi Yuan’s face, he gave up the idea.

Xu Fu always felt there was something eerie about this, but it was fine if Gongzi Yuan was crippled; at least he wouldn't be making trouble in the palace anymore. Those who know the times are wise, but unfortunately, Gongzi Yuan never understood this truth.

"...Please ask Physician Li to go and take a look." Physician Li’s medical skills were quite good; if even he couldn't do anything, then Gongzi Yuan would just have to pay a heavy price for his words.

The servant nodded and withdrew.

About half a month later, the servant reported Gongzi Yuan’s recent situation to Xu Fu again.

"Physician Li says it cannot be cured," the servant said helplessly. "After Gongzi Yuan learned his leg was injured, he made even more of a fuss, not even resting properly, and refusing to take his medicine. If this continues, let alone being cured, he will likely be left with a chronic illness and will be in pain in the future."

Regarding this Gongzi Yuan, Xu Fu could only say he was truly courting death. He waved his hand to dismiss the servant and stopped asking.

A good opportunity had been placed before Gongzi Yuan, but he had squandered it himself; who could he blame?

Xu Fu tossed aside the bamboo slips and took his servants to Fusu’s side hall.

Xu Fu was becoming more and more at home in the palace, coming and going without even needing to announce himself, so when he walked outside the side hall, he happened to hear the voices coming from inside.

It was Ying Zheng talking to Fusu.

"You are growing older and wiser, and your methods of doing things have become sharper than before..."

Xu Fu’s footsteps approached, and Ying Zheng’s voice immediately stopped. He turned his head, saw Xu Fu, and the expression on his face softened instantly; there was no trace of the stern father from just a moment ago.

Fusu also smiled at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was still thinking about what Ying Zheng had just said to Fusu. Fusu’s methods could be sharp too? Xu Fu looked at Fusu and finally confirmed that this Prince Fusu was far removed from the historical description.

After Xu Fu sat down, Ying Zheng continued talking to Fusu.

"...After the new year, you will follow Meng Tian..."

"Wait." Xu Fu had to interrupt Ying Zheng, "Fusu is going to follow Meng Tian? What can Fusu do by following him?"

"Fusu is not young anymore; it is only natural that he should follow and see what the Qin state is like. Following Meng Tian could not be better." Ying Zheng had absolute trust in the Meng brothers, not to mention that Meng Wu had once tutored Fusu.

Xu Fu also knew that Fusu would never learn much by staying in the palace all day. But at Fusu’s current age, in his past life, that would be the level of a first-year middle school student. Just like that, he was going to run around outside and learn the way of ruling?

As Fusu’s former teacher and current father, Xu Fu felt a tiny bit of guilt; he hadn't really intervened much in Fusu’s growth. Fusu was too independent, and reaching this point was already something many of his peers couldn't compare to.

Ying Zheng had already made up his mind to send his son away, and he chose a different way to persuade Xu Fu, "Soon, we will be heading to Han, and Fusu would have to be left in the palace again. We cannot always leave him alone in the palace..."

Xu Fu’s cold, hard heart had long since softened with the passage of time, and Fusu’s position in his heart was much higher than it had been initially. He pondered Ying Zheng’s words carefully, and the more he thought about it, the more he felt it was right; it was truly too cruel to Fusu. As parents, they were not qualified at all, and if this continued, it would indeed be bad for Fusu’s physical and mental health...

"Hmm." Xu Fu replied in a low voice, "Just be careful in everything while you are alone outside."

The smile on Fusu’s face was exceptionally genuine. He reached out and grabbed Xu Fu’s sleeve, asking in a low voice, "Is Father worried about Fusu’s safety?"

"Naturally." Fusu had spent several years with him day and night, and Xu Fu wasn't truly cold-blooded; he naturally had feelings of affection for Fusu.

Emotions flashed in Fusu’s eyes but were quickly hidden. He gripped Xu Fu’s sleeve tightly, then quickly let go, whispering, "Father, do not worry. Fusu will take care of himself. As for Huhai..."

Ying Zheng did not want Huhai to be raised with any ambition, so he naturally wouldn't let Huhai follow him. He said nonchalantly, "Huhai is young; it is better for him to stay in the palace and be cared for by others."

Fusu nodded quickly, "Everything as Father the King says."

Xu Fu’s mind pictured Huhai’s little face; eating and drinking was enough for him. Leaving him in the palace wasn't bad; just have more people accompany him. Wait until Huhai is older, and if there is another trip, take him along.

After so many experiences, Xu Fu knew they were prone to attracting trouble; if they took Huhai, he would actually become a burden.

Thus, Huhai, who was sleeping like a little pig in his side hall, had no idea he had been left behind in the palace just like that.

In the blink of an eye, it was August.

Li Xin and Huan Yi both returned to the court.

Ying Zheng intended to promote Li Xin, so he ordered him to lead troops to Han to receive the ceded land. Afterward, Ying Zheng threw the state affairs to Li Si and the others again, took Xu Fu, packed his things, and set off.

They traveled with Li Xin’s army, bringing only two or three attendants with them.

After they set off, a continuous light rain began to fall, and the muggy weather made Xu Fu feel unbearable. Remembering the great drought in Qin, it felt like a lifetime ago. They passed through a small town, and Li Xin led the army to camp outside the city, while Xu Fu and Ying Zheng went to an inn in the town to rest.

Xu Fu finally got a chance to catch his breath.

After bathing, Xu Fu went downstairs with Ying Zheng to eat.

There were still many locals in the lobby chatting. They were speaking the local dialect, which Xu Fu couldn't quite understand, but he felt he vaguely heard someone mention his name. Who would mention his name? Xu Fu glanced over there.

While the waiter was serving the dishes, Xu Fu stopped him and asked, "What are they talking about?"

The waiter saw that Xu Fu was extremely handsome and that the person beside him also looked like someone of great importance, and they spoke with a Xianyang accent, so how could he dare to be negligent? He immediately said, "Hey, this is a strange thing. Recently, everyone in town has been talking about it. At first, there was a merchant who came to town and chatted with people, talking about Han Fei of Han. Do you know Han Fei? The one they call Han Zi. Didn't he die a long time ago? This matter even spread back to Han, and wasn't it because of this that the King of Han was scared into ceding land to our King?"

The waiter smiled triumphantly and quickly pulled back the straying topic.

"This merchant said..." the waiter lowered his voice, "that Han Fei is alive!"

Xu Fu’s face turned cold, Ying Zheng’s expression was identical to his, and the attendants behind them couldn't help but change their expressions slightly.

Xu Fu said coldly, "Tell me in detail."

The waiter had never seen such a good-looking person as Xu Fu, and seeing Xu Fu still asking him, his cheeks turned red, and he whispered, "Actually, it’s just those few words. Some say Han Fei is alive because someone changed his fate."

"Changed his fate?"

"Yes, and it is said that the person who changed his fate is the current Siche Shuzhang of Qin... Xu Junfang." The waiter whispered.

In this era, one could not call people by their names directly, so people outside naturally referred to Xu Fu by his "courtesy name."

Xu Fu’s heart skipped a beat, instinctively feeling that something was wrong.

Ying Zheng coldly ordered the waiter to step back.

Although the waiter was confused, he obediently left.

Ying Zheng’s face was extremely ugly, and his voice carried a sharp chill, "Someone did this on purpose."

"I don't know who it could be..." Xu Fu frowned. Logically, the fact that Han Fei was still alive was a secret known only to them, Yao Jia, Li Si, and the people in the palace. Xu Fu knew how tightly Ying Zheng controlled the Qin palace. How could such news leak out?

Ying Zheng said coldly, "Even if we knew who was behind it, it would be useless. Since such news could be heard by us, we don't know where that merchant has traveled or how many people he has told."

Xu Fu immediately understood.

It didn't matter who said it; what mattered now was the series of troubles that would follow the spread of the news.

Being able to change someone’s fate sounded incredible, but Xu Fu’s reputation was well-known—something Ying Zheng had deliberately promoted—so no one would think Xu Fu couldn't do it. Once the matter of changing fate was pinned on Xu Fu, everyone would just take it for granted. But this was truly terrifying to think about.

Wouldn't everyone dissatisfied with their current fate hope to find Xu Fu to change it? At that point, they wouldn't care whether Xu Fu actually had such ability; they would all be willing to try. Interests drive people. In history, Qin Shi Huang had done so many foolish things in pursuit of immortality, let alone others.

To survive, to change their fate, who wouldn't want to get their hands on Xu Fu?

Xu Fu was clearly being pushed to the forefront of the storm!

Xu Fu gradually didn't dare to think anymore, his face already turning pale. Becoming a "hot commodity" for such a reason was really not a good thing. Thinking of the common tropes in countless Mary Sue novels, where whoever gets XX can rule the world, Xu Fu felt a chill. He didn't want to become such a Mary Sue himself.

"Don't worry, I will handle this matter." Ying Zheng comforted him gently, covering the back of Xu Fu’s hand and conveying a warm touch.

"Hmm." If he had known this would happen, he would have brought more attendants with him. Now, his safety was really hard to guarantee. It was hard to ensure he wouldn't run into someone insane.

Ying Zheng seemed to see what he was thinking and whispered, "I will immediately order someone to send a message back, ordering Bo Zhou and the others to come quickly."

Xu Fu was used to dealing with them and felt more at ease having them by his side. Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief, didn't eat much, and hurriedly went upstairs with Ying Zheng to rest.

By the next day, Xu Fu had no desire to stay, so he hurriedly set off with Li Xin’s army to continue their journey to Han.

Nothing happened along the way, which made Xu Fu feel much more at ease.

As long as nothing happened, it was fine.

After a month, they arrived in Nanyang.

It was September, and the weather was gradually turning cool.

They entered the city of Nanyang’s administrative seat, and the people in the city looked at them blankly as they entered, showing no sign of resistance at all.

After entering the city, a group of people approached Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng whispered in his ear, "That person is the King of Han." There was an unavoidable tone of disdain in Ying Zheng’s words. The King of Han was cowardly, refusing to use Han Fei because he stuttered, and shortsightedly sending Zheng Guo to Ying Zheng. It was no wonder Ying Zheng looked down on him.

Xu Fu looked in that direction and saw a man wearing bamboo-green royal robes, supported by palace servants, walking slowly toward them. The man was over fifty and looked quite aged; his body was stout, and the wrinkles on his face were somewhat obvious. It was really hard to find any trace of Han Fei on his face. These years of trembling in fear had made him look nothing like a monarch.

The King of Han’s gaze scanned the team and finally landed on Ying Zheng and Xu Fu.

Who else could it be, given their outstanding appearance and temperament? Although the King of Han was cowardly, he wasn't stupid enough to be blind. He could see at a glance that Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were different. He took the initiative to step forward and whispered, "Welcome, King of Qin."

That posture could be described as extremely low.

"The King of Han need not be like this." Ying Zheng said coldly and then didn't speak again.

Ying Zheng saying this, of course, was not to let the King of Han relax, telling him not to be polite and to be casual. Ying Zheng just said it casually, and the King of Han naturally listened casually, eagerly leading them into the administrative office. With the King of Han here, the officials of Nanyang were all obedient, and everything that needed to be presented was presented.

Li Xin led his troops to take over Nanyang, and just an hour later, the entire Nanyang administrative seat was under Li Xin’s control.

After the King of Han explained what needed to be explained, he left immediately. He felt extremely oppressed staying with the King of Qin for even a moment. The King of Han even forgot to ask about his son who was left in Xianyang. Anyway, as long as Han was still there and he was still alive, it was fine. He had so many sons that he didn't care about that one.

After the King of Han left, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng rested well for a night. The next day, Ying Zheng took Xu Fu to ride through the city, taking Xu Fu to see this land that had been ceded. Males are always happy to show their powerful and robust side to their partners. Ying Zheng was naturally very happy to let Xu Fu see the territory he had conquered and to show off his abilities.

Xu Fu was also very happy.

Not everyone could stand side-by-side with Qin Shi Huang, inspecting the land ceded by Han.

They walked through the city and outside the city, and the people of Han looked up at them cautiously, only feeling that Xu Fu, who was riding on the horse, looked so beautiful that he didn't seem like a person of the mortal world, and some even whispered if he was a god.

It could even be exaggerated to say that because of Xu Fu’s arrival, it became much easier for them to accept the entry of the Qin state.

Having a good face really does have privileges.

Xu Fu’s existence invisibly reduced their tension and resistance.

Li Xin had shown more and more of his bravery in the war, and Ying Zheng was naturally reluctant to leave Li Xin here; the Qin state still needed such generals to expand its territory. So Ying Zheng appointed another person, someone he trusted deeply, who had once been in charge of Xianyang’s security, holding the title of Neishi, known as Neishi Teng.

Ying Zheng appointed him as the governor of Nanyang Commandery and then prepared to return to Xianyang after resting for a few days.

Now that the rumors about Xu Fu outside were becoming more and more exaggerated, Ying Zheng could no longer safely leave Xu Fu in Nanyang. No matter how many people outside wanted to get Xu Fu, as long as he brought him back to the Qin palace, those people would have no way. The Qin palace was not a place that was easy to enter!

Actually, Ying Zheng felt a faint joy in his heart, though he knew this thought was too wicked.

What he had simulated countless times in his mind—locking Xu Fu by his side—could finally be realized. As long as the six states existed, these rumors would not disappear. For Xu Fu’s safety, he could completely use this as an excuse to keep Xu Fu by his side until the world was unified, at which point Xu Fu could travel freely.

By then, Ying Zheng could also accompany him out.

After the world was unified, although there would still be many complex affairs, the King of Qin would need to go out for inspections, and taking Xu Fu along would be just right.

The more Ying Zheng thought about it, the more wonderful it felt.

But Xu Fu was extremely unhappy. He had been full of expectations for Nanyang, originally intending to "travel on public funds" and experience the customs of Nanyang, but who knew such a thing would pop up midway. Even if he had to return to Xianyang early for the sake of safety, Xu Fu couldn't be happy.

Because Ying Zheng was in Nanyang, Neishi Teng had to consult Ying Zheng on everything to avoid doing anything wrong and angering the King.

After Ying Zheng was invited away by Neishi Teng, Xu Fu walked outside the administrative office, followed by two or three attendants.

He looked at the street in front of him and the people of Han walking on the street, feeling truly disappointed.

A sound of horse hooves suddenly approached, and Xu Fu looked up, only to find Li Xin passing by on horseback. Perhaps seeing him, he reined in his horse and stopped outside the door.

"Why is the Shuzhang standing here?" Li Xin asked in a low voice.

"Nothing, just came out to take a look." Xu Fu covered the look of regret in his eyes. Although it was a pity, he knew Ying Zheng was doing it for his own good. Xu Fu cherished his life; his life in Qin was very good now, and he didn't intend to change it, nor did he want any outside force to try to change it.

Xu Fu turned to go inside, but Li Xin suddenly clamped the horse’s back from behind, bent down, reached out, and scooped Xu Fu onto the horse’s back.

Xu Fu was caught off guard and didn't even have time to react before watching Li Xin take him away. His attendants were even more caught off guard; who could have imagined that Li Xin would act as soon as he said he would? By the time they came to their senses, Li Xin had already ridden far away. The attendants looked at each other, not knowing if they should report to the King at this moment. In the time they hesitated at the door, Li Xin had already taken Xu Fu far away.

"What are you doing?" Xu Fu asked coldly. He thought of the fate-changing matter almost instantly. Li Xin wouldn't be doing something to him because of this rumor, would he?

Was Li Xin really that stupid?

"Does the Shuzhang want to walk around the city?" Li Xin asked in a low voice.

Xu Fu leaned against his chest, and because of the horse’s jolting, he bumped into Li Xin’s chest several times. This feeling made Xu Fu feel very bad, as if he were cheating on Ying Zheng. He reached out to push against Li Xin’s chest and said coldly, "I have no such intention."

The expression on Li Xin’s face was somewhat disappointed, "Did I misunderstand the Shuzhang’s intention?"

"Naturally, I have already walked through the city and outside the city; why would I need to see it again?"

"There is one place the Shuzhang has not been to." Li Xin became even more enthusiastic, driving the horse and taking Xu Fu forward.

"Li Xin, what exactly are you doing?" Xu Fu’s voice grew colder.

Li Xin said nothing and took Xu Fu straight out of the city.

Xu Fu’s heart sank further and further. If Li Xin really had ulterior motives, then Ying Zheng really couldn't use such a person in the future! Xu Fu thought of this first. Only then did he worry about his own safety.

Xu Fu could almost clearly hear his heart pounding.

Beat by beat, as if it were about to jump out of his chest.

The horse galloped from the city gate and finally arrived at a forest. Deep in the forest, there was a cave and a small waterfall, which was indeed very beautiful. But Xu Fu had no interest in admiring this. Li Xin took him off the horse and brought him to the entrance of the cave.

Li Xin whispered, "I heard that the Shuzhang is looking for a small tripod. I learned from the people in the city that there is a strange tripod here, with an ancient and exquisite appearance; it might be the one the Shuzhang is looking for."

Xu Fu was truly stunned.

Li Xin brought him here just to show him this tripod? How many people knew he was looking for a tripod? Xu Fu had stopped looking for any tripods for such a long time. Xu Fu felt inexplicably that perhaps this had something to do with the news of him being able to change fate. But guesses were just guesses after all. Xu Fu suppressed his thoughts and asked coldly, "Is this the purpose for which General Li brought me here?"

"That’s right."

"General Li, do you know who you are and who I am?" You take the Qin King’s lover and carry him away just like that—how big is your courage! How big must the hole in your brain be!

Li Xin didn't feel anything was wrong and argued, "What does that have to do with anything? I saw that the Shuzhang was not in high spirits, so I brought the Shuzhang here." He frowned, "Does the Shuzhang not like me doing this?"

Of course I don't like it!

The expression on Li Xin’s face was even more disappointed, "I thought that after I became a general of Qin, I could be closer to the Shuzhang, but who knew it would become even colder and more distant."

Xu Fu remembered the words he used to fool Li Xin when he first met him.

Could this have become Li Xin’s motivation to strive?

Li Xin whispered, "The Shuzhang’s prediction was very accurate; I did become a general of Qin. Before, it was the Shuzhang who rushed to Handan to save me. I want to repay the Shuzhang, but I can't find an opportunity." His voice lowered, " ...That’s why I was a bit reckless. I hope the Shuzhang will forgive me."

Xu Fu scanned his face, always feeling that something was wrong with Li Xin, but what he said didn't seem wrong, and Xu Fu had long learned from Huan Yi that Li Xin was indeed quite impulsive. If explained this way, doing such a reckless thing wasn't entirely incomprehensible.

"Let’s go, let’s go in and take a look." Xu Fu withdrew his gaze and walked into the cave.

Just now, he was observing Li Xin to see if his physiognomy had changed.

Xu Fu could judge whether someone had malicious intent by observing their physiognomy. After a careful look just now, Li Xin’s face was open and honest, his eyes were clear, and there was indeed no sign of a villain. Xu Fu felt slightly relieved.

Li Xin bent down to look for it in the cave, and finally came out with a frown, "The tripod... is gone..."

Xu Fu walked forward and suddenly stepped into a dirt pit. He quickly retracted his leg and looked down, finding faint traces of where the tripod had been placed in the pit. He looked closely and found tiny bugs crawling around in the pit. Xu Fu shuddered in disgust and quickly stepped back a few paces. Some patterns were carved on the stone wall opposite; Xu Fu glanced at them and found that they were carved in the shape of a tripod, and the general meaning was that this was a tomb where the tripod was buried.

Xu Fu felt a chill. It turned out that someone had treated the tripod as an evil object. The rice-sized bumps carved on the tripod’s body were considered disgusting by the local people.

But Xu Fu’s face darkened as he thought of the tripod Lord Longyang had given him.

It must be the same one.

It turned out that Lord Longyang had gotten his hands on it long ago...

Li Xin had wasted his effort.

"Since there is no tripod, let’s go." This time, Xu Fu walked out first, and Li Xin followed closely behind. But after walking only a few steps, Xu Fu suddenly couldn't hear any footsteps. He couldn't help but look back at the dark cave entrance, but there was no one there.

Xu Fu’s heart pounded wildly, and he even held his breath instantly.

...Where is Li Xin?

"General Li." Xu Fu whispered.

His voice echoed in the cave, but no one answered him.

The feeling of suddenly being left alone gave Xu Fu goosebumps all over.

Where is he? Could a living person suddenly disappear? He hadn't noticed anything wrong when he entered the cave just now.

Xu Fu hesitated whether to go back and check or just go straight out of the cave.

He hesitated for only three seconds and then immediately lifted his feet to walk out.

Xu Fu wasn't so overconfident; he couldn't guarantee his own safety, let alone find Li Xin, so it was safer to get out of the cave first. He figured that once Ying Zheng discovered he was gone, he would immediately come after him, and then with more people, it would be easier to find Li Xin.

Xu Fu quickened his pace and soon reached the cave entrance.

The bright daylight outside formed a sharp contrast with the inside of the cave.

Xu Fu’s footsteps suddenly stalled; he felt his nose and mouth stifled, suddenly unable to breathe, and then a large hand reached out from behind his neck and roughly pressed him to the ground.

Xu Fu’s heart pounded wildly.
