燕国使臣几乎是逃一样地离开了秦国，他们深深地认识到了秦王不好惹这句话。而那日那个开口的人，他们再也没见过，死了还是活着，他们不知道，也不敢问秦王要……待回到燕国之后，他们怕是也不敢提起的。燕王的凶残并不下于秦王，若是让燕王知道，他们在秦王面前这般畏惧，甚至还丢了一个人，就连公子丹身体有异，都不敢对秦王提出抗议……他们怕是要受到燕王责罚，轻则丢官，重则丢命的！
而秦国在此时对外宣布，燕国将驷车庶长送回了秦国。
为什么呢？因为驷车庶长一身神通，燕国压不住这般厉害人物，唯有秦王方能做他的君主。
此话出来后，秦国百姓自是与有荣焉，而燕国却是气得够呛，颇有点丢了西瓜也丢了芝麻的倒霉味道。
燕王在听闻过后，果然迁怒了公子丘，令人将他关在府中不许任何人出入，并将府中人抓了起来，严刑拷打，等公子丘察觉到徐福从未有过和他合作的心思之后，已经迟了……
燕王一边对徐福愤恨，但一边却又想念徐福手中的药丸。
他发觉到自己近来的身体不如以往健壮了……徐君房是当真诓了他，还是并未诓他，离开燕国，只是一个意外呢？
燕国使臣归来后，只告知了燕王，那秦王是如何宠爱徐福的，燕王听了过后，心中已经有了一个想法——徐君房一定是对秦王政动了真心！他是当真爱上了秦王，因而才对我燕国提出的种种好处都视而不见。
燕王自觉找到了原因，他又灵机一动，想到了离间这二人的法子。
那燕王做着什么样的白日梦，徐福是不知晓的。
转眼已是深冬时节。因地动受灾的百姓，便被派往去修建水渠了，好歹还能得一口饱腹的粮食，得一件御寒的棉衣。
相比从前，今年秦国哪怕经历了地动，也并不算什么伤筋动骨的大事，全国上下一派喜气，他们都认为，是徐福为带来了这些福气。这样的言论难免流传到他国去。
燕王听说之后，又是好一阵气得呕血，暂且不提。
冬日清晨，徐福迷迷糊糊地伸出手来，从床榻起身。身边被窝温热，却不见人影，“王上呢？”
宫人笑道：“王上在殿中呢。”
徐福坐起身来，才看见坐在不远处的身影。宫人服侍着他起了身，往嬴政的方向走去，待走近了之后，徐福惊讶地看着桌案上的铁链……
“这是什么？”
嬴政头也不抬，声音低沉道：“为了不让你再被他国人带走，寡人自然要做条铁索，将你绑在宫中才好。”
徐福知道嬴政也就嘴上说说，他劈手夺过了铁链，“新武器？”
“不错，你师兄为寡人寻来一人。”
“嗯？”
“据说是墨子后人。”嬴政顿了顿道，“韩非曾赞墨子擅工巧，凡他手中所出的工具，在战场上都能发挥起大作用。这墨子后人学到了几分本事寡人不知，便将之前你画出的图交予了他一些，令他选择一件武器来制作，他便做了这个呈了上来。”
“这个派不上用场，他怎么选了这个的图？”徐福凑近了在嬴政身边坐下，“若他真有本事，便让他将如今的弩再做改进，做出杀伤力更强，范围更为密集的连发弩好了。”
嬴政双眼微亮，“阿福与寡人心意相通。”
徐福心中动了动，却不是为嬴政这句话，他是想到了墨家的本事，墨家弟子不就相当于后世的科学家吗？他们富有想象力，更具有创造力和实干的本事。徐福手中光有图，那半分作用也没有，还须得他们来出力那才能制成。
徐福甚至有些好奇，当初郑有安或熊义若是寻了墨家弟子来做这些东西，哪里还会轮得到徐福将这些东西抓在手里呢？要怪就怪，当初郑有安太过自大，以为自己一力可以揽下所有的事，而熊义又一心只记着报复嬴政，哪里还会考虑到这般周详？
当然墨家不如儒家、法家那般入世，墨家本就神秘，墨家后人也是难寻的。
说起来……他和尉缭两个人，身为鬼谷弟子，也是很难寻到的存在啊……嬴政手底下如今有王翦，蒙氏兄弟，荀子两大弟子，还有鬼谷弟子，如今更有墨家后人……
他不成功，谁能成功？
“多寻些墨家后人来才好。”徐福低声道，这样的话，以后便可以致力于发明各种各样后世的东西了。想到不必再过这样的“原始生活”，徐福就感觉到自己的身体内充满了力量。
但是一切都还要等到秦国一统。如今最重要的还是统一天下为先。
徐福安慰了自己一番，现在就当是先苦一苦心志和体肤吧。
“这是自然。”嬴政的大掌抚弄过他的头顶，他顿了顿，突然道：“寡人将李信派到韩国去了。”
“嗯？”
“韩国虽献了地，但寡人要的是从此世上无韩国。”嬴政低声道。当然还有后半句话，他没有当着徐福的面说出来。李信前往战场，若是侥幸拿得胜利，且活了下来，那就让他多活上一些时日，权当以功抵过。若是没活下来，便当是偿他自己莽撞的苦处了。若是活下来却未胜利，嬴政自然也有借口处置他了。
徐福点点头，并未对此事多加评判。
韩国覆灭是必然的……
不仅他知道，几千年后的所有人都知道啊！
两人间的气氛正好，一宫女跌跌撞撞地扑倒在门边，口中抽噎道：“王、王上……”
一阵杂乱的脚步声响起，许久未见的昌文君自殿外走来，粗暴地推开那宫女，高声道：“华阳太后病得起不来身了！请王上去瞧一瞧！”
昌文君方才的举动未必没有借故发泄的意思。
嬴政深深地看了他一眼，昌文君不自觉地往后缩了缩，看向嬴政和徐福的时候，眼底掩藏着几分憎恨的目光。
嬴政起身快步向外走去。
徐福慢慢走在身后，路过那昌文君身旁的时候，才冷声道：“昌文君就算是惊慌，也应当注意规矩。”一句话就说得昌文君变了脸色。徐福知道昌文君对自己怀有敌意，不，不止是对自己，他对嬴政都是怀有敌意，只是他轻易不敢表露出来。
昌文君在秦国越发地没有存在感了，只能日日往华阳太后跟前凑，偏偏华阳太后年纪大了，已经不想再插手秦国的事务，昌文君心中如何能不恨呢？
可你恨归恨，跑到嬴政跟前来撒什么野？
徐福冷傲地从他面前走过，再也不看昌文君一眼，仿佛多看一眼都脏了自己的眼睛。
昌文君气得呕血，冷哼一声，挥手叫上那软倒在地的宫女，赶紧跟了上去。
徐福其实有些迟疑要不要随嬴政前去，毕竟他好像没有什么身份立场……但是等他走上前以后，嬴政就已然抓住了他的手掌，徐福挣脱不开，就跟着去了。
徐福对华阳太后的印象已经模糊了，只隐约记得，华阳太后模样雍容华贵，可以看出年轻时是个绝世的美人儿。她的语气是温柔的，就连见到他同嬴政携手，也并不觉惊奇。那是个经历过风雨，且分外聪明的女人。
很快，他们就走到了华阳太后的寝宫外。
寝宫的门口已经跪了一地的宫人，他们战战兢兢不敢抬头。等跨进去后，还能看见跪在地上的侍医，见嬴政来了，侍医抖得更是厉害。
“华阳太后可还能听见人声？”嬴政转头问那侍医。
侍医点头。
嬴政带着徐福直接走到了围屏后，他们见到了躺在床榻上的华阳太后。
毕竟年纪太大了，华阳太后瞧上去瘦弱了不少，面上覆着一层蜡黄色，可见的确是病得有些重了。
听见人声，华阳太后便撑开了眼皮。
当然在徐福和嬴政的眼中，她也不过是撑开了一条眼缝而已，她还能清醒地人出人，她伸出手冲嬴政招了招，“王上，过来。”
嬴政三步并作两步上了前。
嬴政待她，向来都是怀着报恩的心思。不过王宫之中，嬴政没了父母，更没有妻子，他身边唯一个徐福，膝下唯扶苏和胡亥，再往上，便只剩下一个华阳太后了。
就是再冷漠的人，相处许久自然也会多一些感情，何况华阳太后从不给他找事，颇合嬴政的心思胃口呢。
嬴政动了动唇，面上还有些担忧，“……祖母。”
华阳太后面上的神色软了软，道：“这是什么时候了？”
徐福出声，“巳时。”
嬴政也道：“……这是十六年了。”
华阳太后点了点头，“……一转眼也是这么久了。”她费力地瞪大眼，看了看徐福，“还是那个少年吗？”
“是。”
“好模样啊好模样……如今王宫中可有王后了？”华阳太后的话题蹿得还挺快。
“并无。”
“日后不立后了吗？”华阳太后又问。
徐福在一旁听得心中怪异，总好似在听华阳太后交代后事一样。
“自然要立的。”嬴政沉声道。
徐福面色一冷，眉头紧皱，忍不住伸手掐了嬴政一把。
嬴政面上带笑，表情都不带变一下的。
徐福心头极为不快，冷笑连连，呵呵，立后？立谁？
华阳太后不知二人之间的暗潮汹涌，她点着头道：“好，好……那我为你留一件东西……日后给王后便是……”
嬴政并未怎么放在心上。华阳太后与他之间或许有两分情谊，但毕竟不是亲生的祖孙，何来深厚的感情值得她留下什么东西给自己的王后？
“他……叫什么？”华阳太后又问起了徐福。
“他的字君房。”
“君房啊……”华阳太后念叨了一回。大约是精神不济了，她靠在床榻上久久没有说话。
昌文君姗姗来迟，进到殿内，见了华阳太后那副模样，吓得三魂七魄都差点没了。若是华阳太后当真去了，他在秦国便是真的没有立足之地了！
昌文君忍不住哭喊道：“太后！您要保重身体啊……”
华阳太后一下子又被喊得清醒了过来，但她却并未看那昌文君一眼，反而是又冲徐福招招手，“过来。”
徐福一头雾水地走近了。
华阳太后抓住了徐福的手。
老太太的手已经皱了，甚至看上去还枯瘦，干巴巴的。
不过徐福被她握住的时候，倒是没有什么别的感觉。倒是嬴政的眉头一跳，有些不快。尽管抓着徐福手的那是个老太太……
华阳太后将嬴政的手也抓了过去。
昌文君眉头也是一跳，他有些难以理解，为什么华阳太后看也不看他一眼，反而在这里做着这些有的没的事儿。如此有半分意义吗？
华阳太后笑了笑，“君房与王上相互扶持，日后定然能走得更远……秦国有王上，会成为霸主的……”“我老了，记不住多少话，便今日与你们说了……”
华阳太后说的话的确有些散乱。
“王上便交予君房了，王宫之中，除我之外，便剩君房与两位公子还是王上的亲人了……”华阳太后语气温柔，叫起“君房”二字的时候，显得格外亲昵。
徐福无父无母，更未见过什么长辈，头一次听人这般温柔地唤他，他心中有些怪异，但还有点儿暖意。当华阳太后说到，“王上便交予君房”的时候，徐福心底还真的有了点责任感压肩的感觉。
华阳太后说到一半就又不说话了，她困倦地合上眼，手也松开了。
嬴政赶紧将徐福的手抓在了自己的掌心中。
徐福忍不住低声道：“好。”算是应了华阳太后。
嬴政此时心底的感觉也格外的复杂。
他有了恋慕的人，本该是告诉自己的母亲，但他的生母满心只有她的情人，视儿子为无物。而徐福之上只有尉缭、姜游，也无父母长辈。双方竟是都未曾有过这样的体验——被长辈叫到跟前来，送与祝福，还有嘱咐。
一段感情，连长辈也认同的滋味，还是有点儿甜的。
嬴政抓紧了徐福的手背，低声道：“再去请侍医。”
徐福迟疑了一下，“……不若去请姜游师兄吧？”
嬴政看了他一眼，“嗯，寡人令人去寻。”
徐福忍不住道：“这几日，便由我来盯着吧。”
若是换做他人，嬴政自然不会允，但是今日……他沉默一会儿，道：“寡人陪你便是。”
昌文君在一旁，硬生生成了个隐形人，面色好不扭曲！华阳太后，那是他楚国人……
chapters.translated_text:
Li Xin, Ji Dan, Gongzi Qiu, and the King of Yan... these four men had unfortunately been etched into the Qin King's mind.

Xu Fu smoothed his robes, thinking to himself that the latter three had actually been pretty much ruined by his own hand.

"...I gave the King of Yan a type of medicine. This medicine makes him increasingly irritable, makes it difficult for him to remain clear-headed for long, and is addictive. I added Sichuan peppercorns to it—oh, you don't know what Sichuan peppercorns are. Adding them masks the taste of other ingredients." For example, cinnabar.

Everyone knew that this was an essential ingredient for alchemy.

Once Xu Fu had gained more freedom in the State of Yan, he added new things to the mixture.

All of them could catalyze a fatal outcome, but they were all slow-acting.

At that time, Xu Fu didn't want the King of Yan to die from his pills before he had managed to leave the State of Yan.

Xu Fu whispered, "The King of Yan is arrogant and selfish; for the sake of talk about destiny, he handed over his most excellent son. He even asked me if the immortality recorded in ancient texts truly exists. Of course, it does not." After saying this, Xu Fu stared intensely at Ying Zheng, "...In the future, you must not be like the King of Yan and be deceived by other alchemists."

In history, Qin Shi Huang was immersed in the pursuit of immortality and had committed many absurd and foolish acts. Xu Fu did not want these things to repeat themselves with Ying Zheng.

The reason the historical Qin Shi Huang was like that was because he didn't have him by his side. Now that Ying Zheng had him, he would definitely brainwash him at every opportunity, telling him that immortality was impossible!

Hearing this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but laugh, "As long as A-Fu stays by my side, I naturally will not trust other alchemists. No matter how capable an alchemist may be, in my heart, they cannot compare to A-Fu."

Xu Fu had heard enough cheesy lines that he could now take them in stride. He glanced at Ying Zheng sideways and nodded with an "Mm," which served as his reply to Ying Zheng, telling him that he would indeed stay by his side.

Xu Fu continued, "After I leave this time, the King of Yan might still vent his anger on Gongzi Qiu. It’s a pity; he didn't come to provoke me, yet he is to be implicated."

"What's a pity about that?" Mentioning Gongzi Qiu, Ying Zheng's expression immediately soured. This man dared to flirt with Xu Fu; it would be no pity if he died!

Xu Fu glanced at him, vaguely guessing what was on Ying Zheng's mind.

He knew that in this era, human life really didn't count for much. He just did his best to do what he thought was right; he couldn't force himself to twist Ying Zheng's worldview to one of universal equality. He wasn't crazy. The concepts of this era and the future were separated by thousands of years!

Once the State of Qin unified the land, he could try to shift some of the more backward concepts.

But that was at least twenty years away.

Xu Fu cleared his head and asked about the land the State of Wei had offered.

"The land offered by the State of Wei has been designated as Liyi by me. The one who has ascended the throne of Wei is Wei Zeng, the son of King Anxi of Wei, known as King Jingmin of Wei. This boy has some talent, but as a ruler, he is still far off. He's not even as good as his father was in his youth. As soon as he ascended the throne, fearing that I would attack him while the State of Wei was in internal chaos, he immediately offered up the ceded land." Ying Zheng’s tone was slightly disdainful.

If he wore this expression in front of other monarchs, he would definitely be asking for a beating, but in front of Xu Fu, Xu Fu thought it was... quite... handsome...

"And what about the earthquakes in the State of Qin?"

"Your seismoscope was a huge help." Speaking of this, Ying Zheng was in an extremely joyous mood and couldn't help but lower his head to cup Xu Fu's face and give him a peck.

Xu Fu: ...

If you have the ability, don't use your mouth!

"This object did not come from me, but from someone else." Xu Fu still deflected the credit.

Ying Zheng didn't listen, however, and laughed, "I know how much effort you put into it; why be so modest? Now in the State of Qin, everyone knows you are exceptionally gifted and can predict earthquakes at any time. They don't even say you're like an immortal anymore..."

"I wish I were an immortal, but unfortunately, I'm not." Xu Fu quipped casually.

Ying Zheng hugged him tighter, his eyes deep, and whispered in his ear, "I don't want you to be an immortal." If you became an immortal, what would I do?

Xu Fu replied lazily, "Mm, that's why I'm not."

Ying Zheng couldn't help but want to press him down... and flip the covers...

Xu Fu suddenly said "Ah," "...I haven't told you yet, I had Ji Dan arranged to stay in Gongzi Yuan's courtyard."

Ying Zheng didn't even remember who Gongzi Yuan was, so he nodded, "If you think it's good, then it's good. Once the Yan envoys leave, this Yan prince will cease to exist."

Ying Zheng kept the Qin palace under very strict control. Even if the King of Yan had sent people to follow Ji Dan to keep an eye on his situation, they probably wouldn't even be able to pass on a single word.

Xu Fu lit a candle for Ji Dan in his heart.

The next day, Ying Zheng received the Yan envoys in the palace. The Yan envoys had long expected that the State of Qin's attitude wouldn't be very friendly. After all, they had snatched the other party's Siche Shuzhang to be their State Preceptor! Anyway, the person was in the State of Yan! Ha, even if the State of Qin was furious, there was nothing they could do! The Yan envoys felt quite smug. However, when the day came for them to be summoned by the King of Qin, they couldn't be happy anymore.

The prince was nowhere to be seen.

They didn't have Prince Dan in their hands; how were they to answer to the King of Qin? What if the King of Qin thought the State of Yan had deliberately deceived him?

They entered the palace full of worry, while the palace guards and servants glared at them with hostility.

If it were just one person looking at them like that, it wouldn't be a big deal, but with so many people doing it, and being on someone else's turf, they couldn't help but tremble with fear and dare not meet their eyes. Only then did they realize what an important position the current State Preceptor of Yan held for the State of Qin, and how many people were his supporters.

They walked tremblingly into the great hall where the banquet was being held.

The Qin officials had already learned to cooperate; they were very skilled at treating the Yan envoys as if they didn't exist. The Yan envoys found their seats and were left out in the cold; no one spoke to them, and even the Qin palace servants were icy.

The Yan envoys were a bit nervous. Was the King of Qin going to use this opportunity to lash out? But it didn't matter if he did; they had to hold on! That Siche Shuzhang was now the State Preceptor of Yan! The King of Qin was just angry and jealous! The envoys comforted themselves.

Before long, he saw an attendant leading a man in luxurious clothing into the hall.

The envoy looked closely and almost overturned the table in front of him in shock.

This... isn't this Prince Ji Dan?

"Prince... how could the Prince be here?" The envoy stood up to greet him, looking at Ji Dan's pale and gaunt face, a thousand thoughts flashing through his mind.

Ji Dan moved his lips, his heart filled with endless hardship he wanted to pour out, but the moment he thought about how his father had been the one to send him to Qin as a hostage, what else was there to say? Should he lose face in front of the Yan envoys? He was a Prince of Yan! His dignity... even if his father no longer cared for it, he had to maintain it himself.

In the end, Ji Dan said nothing, walked straight past the envoy, and sat in a seat near the front.

The envoy couldn't help but shiver, feeling that something had changed about Prince Dan, but he couldn't put his finger on it. The envoy shook his head, deciding it must be his imagination. Prince Dan was just a bit thin and tired; could it be the journey was too exhausting? And he was brought straight into the palace after arriving in Xianyang? The envoy instinctively felt something was wrong, but couldn't figure out what.

At this moment, an attendant announced, "The King of Qin arrives."

The officials knelt, and the envoys followed suit in a daze.

Ji Dan couldn't help but stand straight, looking toward that direction, only to see a tall and heroic man wearing black robes, his expression cold and stern, his aura majestic, his right hand resting on the sword at his waist as he walked into the hall. And his left hand was gripping someone's wrist.

That wrist was fair and slender.

Ji Dan looked up along the arm, and the feeling in his heart became indescribably complex.

This person was not slender at all!

Who else could be following at Ying Zheng's side but Xu Fu? He was also dressed in black robes, his delicate brows covered in a layer of frost, his expression serious and unsmiling, his thin frame exuding a daunting aura, somewhat similar to the King of Qin. Compared to his laziness in the State of Yan, this version of him was more like his true self.

Ji Dan clenched his fists involuntarily, his nails digging deep into his palms.

Although he was unwilling to admit it, the two of them walking together looked exceptionally well-matched. As if they were born to be together.

Ji Dan felt an indescribable, murky jealousy in his heart.

Had the State of Yan ever treated Xu Junfang poorly? Yet he was always thinking of the State of Qin... and even took the opportunity to harm him.

Ji Dan’s heart was filled with resentment and jealousy, while the Yan envoys were filled with terror; they overturned their tables and almost fell flat on their faces.

"...Th-that, isn't that the State Preceptor? Shouldn't the State Preceptor be in... the State of Yan? H-how could he be here?" They doubted their own eyes.

But they stared for a long time and finally confirmed that they weren't seeing things; that was indeed the State Preceptor who should have been staying in the State of Yan!

"State Preceptor..." someone gasped. Perhaps it was because they were too panicked to suppress the sound.

Ying Zheng stopped in his tracks. He turned his head, looked at the person who had spoken with a cold, piercing gaze, and said gloomily, "What did you say? How could there be a State Preceptor in the State of Qin?"

The man didn't dare to meet Ying Zheng's gaze. He hurriedly lowered his head and stammered, "...The person by the King of Qin's side is clearly the State Preceptor of Yan." He couldn't help but swallow hard after saying it.

Ying Zheng sneered; what a fool to come looking for death!

"What nonsense are you spouting? The person by my side is the Siche Shuzhang of Qin! What State Preceptor of Yan? Where would you get a State Preceptor in the State of Yan? Guards, drag this man who speaks nonsense away and execute him!" Ying Zheng commanded sternly.

As soon as his words fell, guards entered the hall and dragged the man out directly.

The man was stunned, then realized he might lose his life, so he began to wail. The guards gagged him and dragged him out of the hall just like that; he was drenched in cold sweat, leaving a trail on the floor.

The Yan envoys didn't even dare to breathe; they were stunned by this turn of events.

The King of Qin was clearly teaching them a lesson, yet they didn't dare to utter a single word.

The King of Qin's reputation for cruelty was widespread; it was said he was a man who recognized no kin, that he would even take action against his own Zhongfu, birth mother, and brothers... If they accidentally provoked the King of Qin, there was no telling what kind of fate awaited them.

The Qin officials were already used to this; they were neither surprised nor panicked, kneeling in Ying Zheng's direction and calling out "King of Qin." Even with Xu Fu standing beside Ying Zheng, there was no strange look on their faces, as if they were already accustomed to the King of Qin walking with his lover.

The Yan envoys felt their perception being challenged.

As the King of Qin's lover, shouldn't he be disliked by the officials in the State of Qin? Why did he enjoy such treatment!

Could this be the reason the State Preceptor returned to the State of Qin? Was his status in Qin even greater than being the State Preceptor of Yan?

The envoy was confused. Of course, he was even more curious: why was the State Preceptor here? Had something happened in the State of Yan? The envoy couldn't get an answer and felt like he was sitting on pins and needles.

Ying Zheng's cold gaze swept over them. Although his expression was unpleasant, he was actually extremely pleased inside. He had sternly told the people of Yan that Xu Fu belonged to him, Ying Zheng!

No matter how much the people of Yan deluded themselves, they would get nothing.

Ying Zheng and Xu Fu walked together to the dais and took their respective seats.

Xu Fu sat in the position below Ying Zheng, unique and singular.

No wonder... the favor the King of Qin showed him was indeed supreme! Perhaps in the entire State of Qin, besides the King of Qin, he was the highest. Ji Dan laughed mockingly in his heart; no wonder he looked down on the position offered by the State of Yan. Even if they gave him all the gold and silver in the world, what of it? Staying by the King of Qin's side, the King of Qin was probably eager to offer him all the good things in the world.

Ji Dan's gaze lingered on Xu Fu's face for a while before moving away.

Yes...

What a beautiful face.

How could the King of Qin not be captivated?

Even he and his father had been played in circles by this man; it was easy to imagine that the King of Qin had likely been hooked by him, heart and soul. The future of the State of Yan... no, what future did the State of Yan have left... This man was highly capable, extremely cunning, and even knew how to use poisons and gu-insects; could his father live much longer? With his help, the King of Qin would probably destroy the State of Yan sooner or later. The King of Qin already didn't want to see the State of Yan continue to exist. After all, the State of Yan had once abducted Xu Junfang...

Ji Dan's mind raced.

Would he deceive the King of Qin? Would he wait until the King of Qin destroyed all the states, only to die by his hand?

Ji Dan looked at Xu Fu as if he were looking at a venomous beauty.

Xu Fu could feel Ji Dan's gaze, but he didn't take it to heart. Ji Dan’s resentment and unwillingness were inevitable; a dignified Prince of Yan, once a noble child of heaven, had fallen to such a state—how could he not hate him? If that gaze could be turned into a blade, Xu Fu would probably be dead already.

But there were so many people in the world who hated him and Ying Zheng, yet they couldn't do anything about them now. Why should he take Ji Dan to heart?

Because Ying Zheng had given them a show of force right from the start, the intimidated Yan people didn't dare to provoke him, and even when they spoke, they weighed every word carefully. And Ji Dan had nothing to say at all.

If one had to use a word to describe his current state, it would probably be "despair."

Abandoned by the State of Yan and suppressed by the King of Qin, Ji Dan could no longer see his own future.

If it were envoys from other states, Ying Zheng would at least ask a few symbolic questions, but for the Yan envoys, Ying Zheng didn't even mention their names. The Yan people were left in the cold to the extreme, making it hard to believe that this banquet was held for them.

Xu Fu leaned into Ying Zheng's ear and whispered, "Are you truly going to treat the Yan delegation like wood today?"

Ying Zheng whispered back, "If I didn't need to let them know who A-Fu belongs to, I wouldn't even have held this banquet." Ying Zheng's voice was low and his tone gentle. Xu Fu even felt a hint of flirtation in it, because when Ying Zheng's breath sprayed against his ear, Xu Fu felt his heart racing wildly, difficult to calm down.

Ying Zheng's overbearing attitude actually gave him a mysterious... thrill.

Ah, it felt faintly good...

This feeling of being needed, of being possessed.

Xu Fu lowered his eyes, picked up the wine vessel in front of him to his lips, took a shallow sip, and then, pretending to be nonchalant, raised his hand and placed it on Ying Zheng's knee.

Because of the cover of the table and the distance, no one noticed the movement, and the surrounding palace servants and attendants, even if they noticed, wouldn't say anything. Ah, it's just touching a knee, flirting—how normal...

Ying Zheng didn't mind either.

Instead, he reached out and covered the back of Xu Fu's hand, asking in a low voice, "What is it? Are you bored?"

Xu Fu shook his head, "Waiting to watch the dancing."

Ying Zheng said unhappily, "What's there to watch?"

Xu Fu was also unhappy, "I've lived in the palace for several years; how many dances have I actually seen?"

You were the one who said there was nothing to watch before. Ying Zheng shut his mouth and accompanied Xu Fu to wait for the dancers to enter the hall. If he wants to watch, let him watch; anyway, those dancers aren't as good-looking as I am.

The King of Qin was as thick-skinned as ever today.

Xu Fu pulled his hand away from Ying Zheng's large palm. Just as Ying Zheng was about to put on an even more displeased expression, Xu Fu's hand suddenly pressed against the inside of his thigh. Ying Zheng's body trembled imperceptibly; he gritted his teeth, his face dark, but he said nothing.

Ying Zheng looked extremely majestic; no one would look at him and think of anything else.

The music started, and the dancers stepped into the hall.

The Yan envoys and the others had no heart to enjoy it; they were anxious and couldn't focus their attention anywhere.

And Ying Zheng... was no longer in the mood either.

Xu Fu's hand slid down to his lower parts.

Xu Fu thought, since Ying Zheng had teased him just now, he had to tease him back.

Ying Zheng felt that Xu Fu had actually stirred up his desires right in front of so many people... He had to admit, the more he was in a place like this, the more he felt the beast of desire within him howling. He truly longed to push Xu Fu onto the table before them, drench his lean, fair body in wine, and then cover him, letting everyone see exactly how he possessed him. Of course... this could only remain a thought. Ying Zheng was far from being that reckless and insane.

He grabbed Xu Fu’s wrist, "Returning to the palace?"

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, then refused, "...I haven't finished watching yet."

Still watching?

You still want to watch the dancing girls?

Ying Zheng’s heart was restless, as if a flame were about to erupt from within.

Ying Zheng suddenly stood up, his face cold as he said, "You all enjoy your food, wine, and beauties... I shall not remain here any longer." After saying this, he pulled Xu Fu up with him. When Xu Fu saw his arm reaching for his waist, he slapped it away, then turned and followed Ying Zheng out of the hall.

As their figures passed by Ji Dan, he caught a glimpse of a faint blush on Xu Fu’s cheek, and the emotions in his heart churned even more violently.

Ji Dan could imagine...

Why the King of Qin had whisked Xu Fu away in such a hurry...

The music and voices in the hall were left behind them. Once they were out of the hall, Ying Zheng could no longer restrain himself; he scooped Xu Fu up and strode toward the palace. The palace attendants and servants tried to follow, but dared not get too close. Fortunately, they were already quite experienced, so this little problem didn't stump them.

After Ying Zheng carried Xu Fu into the bedchamber, the thoughtful attendants closed the palace doors for them.

Xu Fu lay in his arms, asking in confusion, "What are you doing?"

Seeing the clarity in his eyes, Ying Zheng assumed he was merely feigning innocence.

Every inch of Xu Fu’s body was clearly seducing him!

Although they were no longer in the hall, Ying Zheng still pressed him onto the table.

Once Xu Fu realized his situation, he finally thought of three words: I’ve gone too far...

"Back in the hall, weren't you touching me quite enthusiastically?" Ying Zheng gripped his wrists, pressing his palms against his own body.

Xu Fu blinked, his face expressionless as he said something entirely contradictory, "...You really wanted to push me down just now?"

"I did." Ying Zheng pulled open his robes, no longer suppressing the desire in his heart.

...

·

The Yan envoys left the State of Qin as if fleeing for their lives. They had deeply realized the truth that the King of Qin was not to be trifled with. As for the man who had spoken up that day, they never saw him again; whether he was dead or alive, they did not know, and they dared not ask the King of Qin... Once they returned to Yan, they likely wouldn't dare mention it either. The King of Yan was no less cruel than the King of Qin. If the King of Yan learned that they had been so fearful before the King of Qin, even losing a man, and that they hadn't dared to protest even when Prince Dan was physically compromised... they would surely be punished by the King of Yan—at best losing their official positions, at worst losing their lives!

Meanwhile, the State of Qin announced to the outside world that the State of Yan had returned the Siche Shuzhang to Qin.

Why? Because the Siche Shuzhang possessed divine abilities, and the State of Yan could not contain such a formidable figure; only the King of Qin was worthy of being his sovereign.

When this news broke, the people of Qin naturally felt a sense of pride, while the State of Yan was furious, feeling like they had lost both the watermelon and the sesame seeds.

Upon hearing this, the King of Yan vented his anger on Prince Qiu, ordering him to be confined to his residence with no one allowed in or out. He had the people in the residence arrested and interrogated under torture. By the time Prince Qiu realized that Xu Fu had never intended to cooperate with him, it was already too late...

While the King of Yan harbored resentment toward Xu Fu, he also found himself missing the pills Xu Fu had provided.

He noticed that his health had not been as robust as before... Had Xu Junfang truly deceived him, or had he not? Was his departure from Yan merely an accident?

After the Yan envoys returned, they only told the King of Yan how much the King of Qin doted on Xu Fu. Hearing this, the King of Yan formed an idea—Xu Junfang must have truly given his heart to King Zheng of Qin! He had genuinely fallen in love with the King of Qin, which was why he turned a blind eye to all the benefits the State of Yan had offered.

Believing he had found the reason, the King of Yan had a flash of inspiration and thought of a way to sow discord between the two.

What kind of daydreams the King of Yan was having, Xu Fu did not know.

In the blink of an eye, it was deep winter. The people affected by the earthquake were sent to build water channels, where they could at least earn enough food to fill their stomachs and receive cotton-padded clothes to ward off the cold.

Compared to the past, this year in Qin, even with the earthquake, was not a catastrophic blow. The entire country was in high spirits, and they all believed that it was Xu Fu who had brought them this good fortune. Such sentiments inevitably spread to other states.

When the King of Yan heard this, he was so angry he nearly vomited blood, but that is a story for another time.

On a winter morning, Xu Fu groggily reached out as he rose from the bed. The spot beside him was warm, but there was no sign of anyone. "Where is the King?"

An attendant smiled and said, "The King is in the hall."

Xu Fu sat up and saw the figure sitting not far away. The attendant helped him dress, and he walked toward Ying Zheng. As he approached, Xu Fu looked in surprise at the iron chain on the table...

"What is this?"

Ying Zheng didn't look up, his voice low: "To ensure you aren't taken away by people from other states again, I naturally had to make an iron chain to keep you tied to the palace."

Xu Fu knew Ying Zheng was just talking, so he snatched the chain away. "A new weapon?"

"Indeed. Your senior brother found someone for me."

"Oh?"

"It is said he is a descendant of Mozi." Ying Zheng paused. "Han Fei once praised Mozi for his skill in craftsmanship; any tool that came from his hands could play a major role on the battlefield. I don't know how much of that skill this descendant has learned, so I gave him some of the diagrams you drew and ordered him to choose one weapon to craft. He made this and presented it."

"This one isn't very useful. Why did he choose this diagram?" Xu Fu sat down close to Ying Zheng. "If he truly has talent, have him improve the current crossbows to create a repeating crossbow with greater lethality and a denser range."

Ying Zheng’s eyes brightened. "A-Fu and I share the same mind."

Xu Fu’s heart stirred, though not because of Ying Zheng’s words. He was thinking about the skills of the Mohists. Weren't the Mohist disciples the scientists of the future? They were imaginative, creative, and practical. Having the diagrams in his hands was useless; he needed them to put in the work to make them a reality.

Xu Fu was even curious: if Zheng You'an or Xiong Yi had sought out Mohist disciples to make these things, would it have ever been Xu Fu’s turn to hold them? If one were to blame, it was that Zheng You'an was too arrogant, thinking he could handle everything himself, while Xiong Yi was only focused on revenge against Ying Zheng—how could he have considered things so thoroughly?

Of course, the Mohists were not as involved in the world as the Confucians or Legalists; the Mohist school was inherently mysterious, and their descendants were hard to find.

Come to think of it... he and Wei Liao, as disciples of Guigu, were also very hard to find... Under Ying Zheng’s command now were Wang Jian, the Meng brothers, two disciples of Xunzi, and now Guigu disciples, and even Mohist descendants...

If he didn't succeed, who could?

"We should find more Mohist descendants," Xu Fu said softly. That way, they could dedicate themselves to inventing all sorts of things from the future. Thinking that he wouldn't have to live this "primitive life" anymore, Xu Fu felt his body filled with strength.

But everything had to wait until Qin unified the land. For now, the most important thing was the unification of the world.

Xu Fu comforted himself; for now, he would just consider it tempering his heart and body.

"That goes without saying." Ying Zheng’s large hand stroked his head. He paused and suddenly said, "I have sent Li Xin to the State of Han."

"Oh?"

"Although Han has offered its land, what I want is for there to be no State of Han in this world from now on," Ying Zheng said in a low voice. Of course, there was a second half to his sentence that he didn't say in front of Xu Fu. If Li Xin went to the battlefield and luckily won and survived, he would let him live a while longer to atone for his mistakes with merit. If he didn't survive, it would be the price for his own recklessness. If he survived but didn't win, Ying Zheng naturally had excuses to deal with him.

Xu Fu nodded, not offering any judgment on the matter.

The fall of Han was inevitable...

Not only did he know it, but everyone thousands of years later knew it too!

The atmosphere between the two was perfect when a palace maid stumbled and fell by the door, sobbing, "Y-Your Majesty..."

A flurry of footsteps sounded, and Changwen Jun, whom they hadn't seen in a long time, walked in from outside. He shoved the maid aside roughly and shouted, "Empress Dowager Huayang is so ill she cannot rise! I beg the King to go and see her!"

There was likely a desire to vent his frustrations in Changwen Jun’s actions just now.

Ying Zheng looked at him deeply. Changwen Jun shrank back involuntarily, his eyes filled with hidden hatred as he looked at Ying Zheng and Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng stood up and walked quickly outside.

Xu Fu walked slowly behind. As he passed by Changwen Jun, he said coldly, "Even in panic, Changwen Jun should mind his manners." One sentence made Changwen Jun’s expression change. Xu Fu knew Changwen Jun held hostility toward him—no, not just toward him, but toward Ying Zheng as well, though he dared not easily show it.

Changwen Jun had less and less presence in Qin and could only hover around Empress Dowager Huayang every day. But Empress Dowager Huayang was old and no longer wanted to interfere in the affairs of Qin. How could Changwen Jun not hate that?

But hatred is one thing; why come and act wild in front of Ying Zheng?

Xu Fu walked past him coldly, never looking at Changwen Jun again, as if looking at him for even a second would dirty his eyes.

Changwen Jun was so angry he nearly vomited blood. He snorted coldly, waved for the maid who had fallen to the ground to follow, and hurried after them.

Xu Fu was actually hesitant about whether to follow Ying Zheng, as he didn't seem to have any standing... But after he walked up, Ying Zheng had already grabbed his hand. Xu Fu couldn't break free, so he went along.

Xu Fu’s impression of Empress Dowager Huayang was already blurred. He only vaguely remembered that she was graceful and noble, and one could tell she had been a peerless beauty in her youth. Her tone was gentle, and she hadn't even seemed surprised to see him holding hands with Ying Zheng. She was a woman who had weathered storms and was exceptionally intelligent.

Soon, they arrived outside Empress Dowager Huayang’s bedchamber.

The entrance was already filled with kneeling attendants, trembling and not daring to look up. Once they stepped inside, they could see the court physician kneeling on the floor. Seeing Ying Zheng arrive, the physician shook even more violently.

"Can Empress Dowager Huayang still hear voices?" Ying Zheng turned to ask the physician.

The physician nodded.

Ying Zheng led Xu Fu directly behind the screen, where they saw Empress Dowager Huayang lying on the bed.

Being of such advanced age, she looked much thinner, her face covered in a waxy yellow hue, showing she was indeed quite ill.

Hearing voices, she forced her eyelids open.

Of course, to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, she had only opened a slit. She could still recognize people clearly, and she reached out and beckoned to Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, come here."

Ying Zheng reached her in three strides.

Ying Zheng had always treated her with a sense of gratitude. But in the palace, Ying Zheng had no parents, and even less a wife. Beside him was only Xu Fu, and beneath him were only Fusu and Huhai. Beyond that, there was only Empress Dowager Huayang.

Even the coldest person would develop some affection after living together for so long, and Empress Dowager Huayang never caused him trouble, which suited Ying Zheng’s temperament well.

Ying Zheng moved his lips, his face still showing concern, "...Grandmother."

The expression on Empress Dowager Huayang’s face softened. "What time is it?"

Xu Fu spoke up, "The hour of the snake (10 AM)."

Ying Zheng also said, "...It has been sixteen years."

Empress Dowager Huayang nodded. "...In the blink of an eye, it has been so long." She struggled to widen her eyes and looked at Xu Fu. "Is he still that same young man?"

"He is."

"A fine appearance, a fine appearance... Is there a Queen in the palace now?" Empress Dowager Huayang’s topic jumped quite quickly.

"There is not."

"Will you not appoint a Queen in the future?" she asked again.

Xu Fu felt strange listening from the side; it felt as if Empress Dowager Huayang was giving her final instructions.

"Naturally, I will," Ying Zheng said in a deep voice.

Xu Fu’s face turned cold, his brows furrowed, and he couldn't help but pinch Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng smiled, his expression not changing in the slightest.

Xu Fu was extremely unhappy, sneering repeatedly. Heh, appoint a Queen? Appoint whom?

Empress Dowager Huayang was unaware of the undercurrents between the two. She nodded and said, "Good, good... Then I will leave something for you... to give to the Queen in the future..."

Ying Zheng didn't take it to heart. Perhaps there was some affection between him and Empress Dowager Huayang, but they were not blood-related grandmother and grandson; what deep sentiment could there be to warrant her leaving something for his Queen?

"What... is his name?" she asked about Xu Fu again.

"His courtesy name is Junfang."

"Junfang..." Empress Dowager Huayang murmured. Perhaps her energy was failing; she leaned back against the bed and remained silent for a long time.

Changwen Jun arrived late. Entering the hall and seeing Empress Dowager Huayang in that state, he was so frightened his soul nearly left his body. If she were to pass away, he would truly have no foothold in Qin!

Changwen Jun couldn't help but cry out, "Empress Dowager! You must take care of your health..."

Empress Dowager Huayang was jolted awake by the shouting, but she didn't even look at Changwen Jun. Instead, she beckoned to Xu Fu again. "Come here."

Xu Fu walked over, bewildered.

Empress Dowager Huayang grabbed Xu Fu’s hand.

The old woman’s hand was wrinkled, even looking withered and dry.

However, when Xu Fu was held by her, he didn't feel anything else. Ying Zheng’s brow twitched, feeling somewhat displeased. Even though the one holding Xu Fu’s hand was an old woman...

Empress Dowager Huayang also grabbed Ying Zheng’s hand.

Changwen Jun’s brow also twitched. He couldn't understand why she wouldn't even look at him, instead doing these pointless things here. Did this have any meaning at all?

Empress Dowager Huayang smiled. "Junfang and the King support each other; you will surely go far in the future... With the King, Qin will become a hegemon..." "I am old and cannot remember much, so I will say this to you today..."

Her words were indeed a bit scattered.

"I leave the King to Junfang. In the palace, besides me, there is only Junfang and the two princes left as the King’s family..." Her tone was gentle, and when she called out "Junfang," it sounded exceptionally intimate.

Xu Fu had no parents and had never known any elders. Hearing someone call him so gently for the first time, he felt strange, but also a bit warm. When she said, "I leave the King to Junfang," Xu Fu truly felt a sense of responsibility pressing down on his shoulders.

Empress Dowager Huayang stopped speaking halfway through. She closed her eyes wearily, and her hand loosened.

Ying Zheng quickly grabbed Xu Fu’s hand into his own palm.

Xu Fu couldn't help but whisper, "I will." It was his response to Empress Dowager Huayang.

Ying Zheng’s feelings at this moment were also exceptionally complex.

He had someone he loved, and he should have told his mother, but his birth mother only had eyes for her lover and treated her son as nothing. And Xu Fu had only Wei Liao and Jiang You, with no parents or elders. Neither of them had ever experienced this—being called before an elder, receiving blessings, and instructions.

The feeling of a relationship being acknowledged by an elder was actually quite sweet.

Ying Zheng tightened his grip on the back of Xu Fu’s hand and said in a low voice, "Go and call the physician again."

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment. "...Why not call Senior Brother Jiang You?"

Ying Zheng looked at him. "Very well, I will have someone find him."

Xu Fu couldn't help but say, "For these next few days, I will keep watch."

If it were anyone else, Ying Zheng would naturally not allow it, but today... he was silent for a moment and said, "I will accompany you."

Changwen Jun stood to the side, becoming an invisible man, his face twisted in frustration! Empress Dowager Huayang—she was a person of his State of Chu...

chapters.title: 第193章
chapters.translated_text:
Empress Dowager Huayang’s illness seemed to have no end in sight.

Xu Fu would visit her palace whenever he had a spare moment, keeping a constant watch on the changes in her condition. Ying Zheng, burdened with heavy state affairs, would only find time to check on her once he had finished his work.

Xu Fu vaguely remembered a saying from his past life: "There is no filial son before a long-term sickbed." Lord Changwen had been very attentive to Empress Dowager Huayang in the past, but now he gradually stopped coming. He likely realized that he could no longer expect to gain anything from her.

It would have been fine if he simply stayed away, but he insisted on making snide remarks to provoke Xu Fu: "Always hovering around the Empress Dowager, what are you hoping for? Do you really think of yourself as a woman..."

At first, Xu Fu ignored him, feeling that it would be inappropriate to kill Lord Changwen outside the Empress Dowager’s palace. However, Xu Fu was never one to endure such things, and he had no interest in being a pushover. As he turned to leave the palace, he called the attendants over: "Take him down."

Lord Changwen was stunned: "...You, what are you doing?"

"Lord Changwen is making a scene outside the sleeping quarters, causing the Empress Dowager great anger and worsening her condition. Why haven't you seized such an unfilial and disloyal person yet? If the Empress Dowager’s condition deteriorates further, who can bear the responsibility?" Xu Fu scolded sharply.

The palace attendants were mostly under Xu Fu’s command, so how could they refuse? They didn't care that he was Lord Changwen; in the royal palace, anyone causing a disturbance was to be apprehended without exception.

"You have such audacity! What do you think you're doing? Who do you think you are? To be so arrogant in the Qin palace..."

Xu Fu felt genuinely irritated; Lord Changwen’s face had become repulsive in his eyes. "Drag him away."

The attendants nodded, grabbed Lord Changwen by his robes, and dragged him away roughly.

"You villain! A plaything who serves with his looks! How dare you treat me like this..." Lord Changwen cursed.

Before Lord Changwen could finish his words, a powerful force suddenly struck him, knocking his head to the side. The metallic taste of blood instantly filled his mouth. Dazed by the blow, he shook his head, but before he could look up, Ying Zheng’s voice sounded in his ear: "Lord Changwen accidentally fell and is unable to speak. Take him back to rest properly."

Lord Changwen suddenly felt a chill run through his body; his mouth opened and closed, but he couldn't squeeze out a single word.

The attendants dragged him outside the palace and pushed him toward his own servants, relaying Ying Zheng’s words. The servants broke into a cold sweat and hurriedly took Lord Changwen away.

Did Lord Changwen still think it was the past, when he held great power, had backing, and had others to shield him? Now, Lord Changping was dead, the Empress Dowager was critically ill, the State of Chu was declining, and his own power had been stripped away. What advantage could he possibly have over Xu Fu? Not to mention that Xu Fu was now a Siche Shuzhang; even if Xu Fu were nothing, it wouldn't be his place to slander him.

Ying Zheng watched as Lord Changwen was dragged away, then turned and returned to Xu Fu’s side.

While the Empress Dowager was lucid, they went in to see her once more.

"There is no need to come during this time... do not catch the illness..." After muttering a few words, the Empress Dowager fell asleep again.

Ying Zheng took Xu Fu’s hand and led him back to their sleeping quarters. Once Jiang You arrived in Xianyang, he took charge of the Empress Dowager’s treatment. As the Empress Dowager had requested, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng visited her chambers less frequently.

In just a short time, Xu Fu had become quite exhausted. He slept soundly in his chambers for a few days, finally feeling the fatigue fade away.

Xu Fu couldn't deny that spending a long time with an elderly person nearing the end of their life also brought his own mood down.

After returning to his chambers, Fusu would often come to see him, and over time, those negative emotions naturally drifted away.

In the 17th year of King Zheng of Qin, Neishi Teng led troops to attack the State of Han.

Before leaving Xianyang, Li Xin lingered outside the palace many times, and each time, the palace attendants reported it to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng. Xu Fu’s attitude was firm; he would not move a single step for Li Xin. Ying Zheng’s jealousy naturally dissipated after a while.

Besides, the battlefield was dangerous, and Ying Zheng didn't want to bicker with Li Xin at such a moment.

Li Xin soon led his troops toward Han.

Xu Fu couldn't help but worry about Han Fei. They all knew this day would come sooner or later, but what about Han Fei? Did he know? Was he still dreaming that offering land would preserve the State of Han?

To avoid further trouble, Xu Fu took a carriage out of the palace to visit Yao Jia’s residence in person.

Although Han Fei had once again caught Ying Zheng’s eye, Yao Jia’s resentment toward him had not faded, and he stubbornly kept Han Fei at his residence. Ying Zheng thought it wouldn't be bad to let Han Fei suffer a bit and have Yao Jia keep him in check, so he never inquired about Han Fei’s living situation.

Even if Han Fei felt stifled, he had no choice but to stay at Yao Jia’s residence.

When Xu Fu arrived, the steward of the Yao residence was standing with his back turned to a man in white, saying, "Oh, you cannot do this... no, no..."

The man in white remained silent.

The steward sighed, "It won't do, my master said... it's not allowed."

The attendant beside Xu Fu stepped forward and knocked on the door panel: "Is Han-zi here?"

The man in white turned around; it was none other than Han Fei.

Xu Fu saw that his brows were tightly furrowed, his face pale with anxiety: "...Xu, Shuzhang Xu."

The steward also recognized Xu Fu, hurriedly bowed, and then consciously stepped aside.

"Where does Han-zi intend to go?" Xu Fu asked.

Han Fei was a bit nervous; he pressed his lips tightly together: "To, to see, to see the King."

"If it is about the State of Han, I think there is no need; the King will not see you. Han-zi must know that one only has one choice; once you make a mistake, there is no turning back. One must give up something to gain something; one cannot be greedy." Han Fei wanted his own ambitions, but he also wanted the country that had abandoned him. How could there be such a good thing in the world? To have both.

Han Fei’s body stiffened, his face turning even paler: "...Shuzhang is, is right." He gritted his teeth, turned around, and stood there without moving.

Xu Fu knew that Han Fei was incapable of lying. Since he had stopped in his tracks, he would not be ungrateful.

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief.

Fortunately, Han Fei was not as stubborn as before; was this the result of Yao Jia’s discipline?

Xu Fu did not step forward to comfort Han Fei.

The attack on Han was already a fact; why should he go and nag Han Fei about it? It would only end up being like twisting a knife in Han Fei’s heart.

"Let's go," Xu Fu instructed the attendant beside him.

The steward hurriedly stepped forward: "Is Shuzhang leaving already? Won't you stay a while longer? My master went out, but he will be back shortly."

Xu Fu waved his hand and was about to step out when he saw Yao Jia entering, holding medicine in his hand.

...For Han Fei?

Xu Fu couldn't help but look back. He had been taking medicine for so long; was he still not better?

"Shuzhang Xu." Yao Jia bowed to Xu Fu, and after a moment of surprise, a smile appeared on his face: "Why has Shuzhang come today?"

"To check on Han-zi." Xu Fu pointed to the medicine in his hand: "How is it? Is Han-zi’s health still not fully recovered?"

Yao Jia laughed: "For the past few days, Han-zi hasn't been able to eat, and he cannot sleep at night. His face is pale and his body is weak, so I had to go get the medicine for him myself."

Yao Jia would take such good care of Han Fei? Xu Fu felt surprised.

Hearing their conversation, Han Fei turned around and glared at Yao Jia, but immediately sheepishly withdrew his expression.

Xu Fu felt the atmosphere between the two was truly strange, but he couldn't ask further. He chatted with Yao Jia for a few moments, praising his contributions in his diplomatic missions until Yao Jia’s face beamed with joy, and only then did Xu Fu depart.

Xu Fu was usually cold and arrogant, and no one would think he was someone who would easily offer praise. Therefore, when he praised Yao Jia with a calm expression, it seemed all the more sincere. How could Yao Jia not be happy? When he saw Xu Fu off, Yao Jia’s demeanor was even more attentive.

After returning to the palace, Xu Fu continued to study the items Zheng You’an had left behind. As he flipped through the silk cloth in his hands, his gaze suddenly froze. Xu Fu saw a symbol; others might not understand it, but he could. It was written as "①"—an Arabic numeral one inside a circle. He absolutely had not misread it!

Where there is a one, there is a two, and perhaps even a three.

Xu Fu frowned and looked over the silk cloth again and again, but there was only that one mark on the entire piece.

"What's wrong?" Ying Zheng’s voice suddenly sounded behind him.

Xu Fu almost dropped the silk cloth in his hand.

"Why do you walk without making a sound?" Xu Fu complained coldly without looking up.

Ying Zheng’s large palm rested on Xu Fu’s smooth neck: "It is you who were too engrossed; you didn't hear the attendants calling you."

Xu Fu pushed his hand away and pointed to the silk cloth: "I discovered something strange."

Ying Zheng’s expression became serious: "What is strange?"

Seeing his serious look, Xu Fu hurriedly said: "...It's not a major matter, I just discovered that there might be more than one piece of silk left by Zheng You’an."

The look on Ying Zheng’s face relaxed: "Why did you suddenly discover this?"

"It's..." Xu Fu stopped halfway; how could he explain Arabic numerals to Ying Zheng? To this day, he still hadn't told Ying Zheng why he could clearly understand the simplified characters Zheng You’an had left behind.

Ying Zheng noticed Xu Fu’s abrupt silence, his eyes flickered, and he consciously changed the subject: "Did you rest well today? I will take you out of the palace."

The more considerate Ying Zheng was, the more uncomfortable Xu Fu felt, feeling a bit like he was being ungrateful.

"...Yes, I rested well." Xu Fu stood up, unable to resist wanting to hold onto Ying Zheng’s sleeve. Only by grasping it did he feel his heart settle.

Ying Zheng put his arm around Xu Fu as they stepped out of the hall, and the two boarded a carriage, heading out of the palace.

Once they arrived, Xu Fu knew what Ying Zheng had brought him to see.

"The descendants of the Mohists have been here for several months. I have already prepared to use the things they have created in the army. Li Xin took some with him when he left Xianyang," Ying Zheng whispered in Xu Fu’s ear.

The guards in front opened the gate, and a wave of heat rushed toward them.

They stepped through the gate and walked down the corridor, where they could hear the sound of "clanging."

This was the first time Xu Fu had seen so many finished weapons; compared to the scale of Xiong Yi’s operation, it was much larger. Long and short weapons, projectiles, crossbows... it was almost everything one could imagine. However, some weapons that appeared ahead of their time still differed from those of later generations due to a lack of constant practical improvement and raw materials.

Walking a few steps further, Xu Fu saw a repeating crossbow.

This was a reinforced repeating crossbow; its range and reach had been enhanced. It required much less arm strength than a heavy crossbow, but at the same time, its lethality was not as great.

"Li Xin took this," Ying Zheng said from the side.

Xu Fu reached out to touch the repeating crossbow, but someone slapped his hand away with a "smack." Xu Fu had fair skin, and the back of his hand immediately turned red. Ying Zheng’s face darkened as he looked at the person: "What are you doing?"

The person shrank back and muttered: "...I, I was just, just worried about accidentally hurting him."

Xu Fu withdrew his hand and looked at the man. He was wearing dusty, simple clothes without even sleeves, though this attire was much more convenient.

"What is your name?" Was this person a descendant of the Mohists?

"...Er, Er’er." The man swallowed hard while staring at Xu Fu, his cheeks flushing red.

Er’er?

What kind of name was that? Had his parents been that lazy when naming him?

Ying Zheng turned his head and whispered: "Most of them have hidden their names; 'Er’er' is his ranking from when he joined the Mohists."

So that was it.

Xu Fu looked at the man again; he was quite unkempt, and seeing him look over, the man hurriedly smiled at him.

Seeing Xu Fu staring for too long, Ying Zheng pulled him: "Let's go."

Xu Fu nodded and followed him out: "Has Senior Brother been here to see this?"

"He has. After seeing these weapons, the Guowei didn't know what inspiration he had received, and he left in a hurry."

Xu Fu looked back at the place.

If the weapons here could be popularized... the Qin army would truly be unstoppable. But the premise was... there had to be sufficient national strength to support it. If they blindly consumed national strength in war, there would be major problems once Qin unified the land.

Xu Fu could no longer remember why the people had suffered so much during the Qin Dynasty, leading to the uprising of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang. Was it because of the cruelty after Fusu’s successor took the throne, or were the hidden dangers planted during the time of Qin Shi Huang?

The two returned to the carriage.

Seeing that Xu Fu’s expression was not as pleasantly surprised as others, but rather serious, Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask: "Is there a problem with these weapons? Or are you unhappy about something?"

"It's not the weapons, and I am not unhappy." Xu Fu shook his head, deciding to voice his concerns, even if Ying Zheng might have already been prepared. "Has Ah-Zheng thought about what will happen when all six states are destroyed and the world is unified? If national strength is exhausted by war, and we are forced to increase taxes, what will happen if the people become dissatisfied?"

Xu Fu’s words were like a bucket of cold water poured down when someone was at their happiest.

If it had been anyone else, it would have surely enraged Ying Zheng, but the person speaking was Xu Fu. After the initial displeasure, joy began to well up in Ying Zheng’s heart. That Xu Fu was so worried for him and willing to think about these things—wasn't that because he was completely in his heart? If Xu Fu were still as heartless as before, why would he bring these things up to him?

Ying Zheng was not someone who couldn't listen to advice, especially when the person speaking was Xu Fu.

"You are right." A lack of material resources would become a major hidden danger in the future. Many countries had been brought down by the drain on their resources. "I will think about it carefully; you don't need to dwell on such troublesome matters." Ying Zheng reached out and gently stroked the top of Xu Fu’s head.

Only after saying it did Xu Fu realize his words were a bit of a mood-killer, but since they were already out, he couldn't take them back. He looked up at Ying Zheng’s face, which held a smile and soft eyes... Xu Fu felt a weight lift from his heart.

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu to his side, letting him rest in his arms.

For a moment, the carriage was quiet.

Xu Fu closed his eyes in a daze; he suddenly thought of the State of Yan.

He hadn't heard news of Ji Dan and Gongzi Yuan for some time. Perhaps they were dead, or perhaps they were still alive, but Xu Fu didn't intend to ask anymore.

Ying Zheng looked down at Xu Fu’s face and reached out to gently stroke his chin.

Xu Fu felt nothing.

The carriage swayed as it moved forward...

·

At the hour of the dragon (7-9 AM), while Xu Fu was still groggy, he vaguely heard Fusu’s voice. In a short while, his quilt was pressed down heavily, and Fusu leaned close to his cheek, breathing warmly: "...Father."

Xu Fu was forced to open his eyes: "What is it?"

Fusu’s face showed disappointment: "Has Father forgotten?"

Xu Fu met his gaze: "...Forgotten what?" Xu Fu sat up from the bed and pulled Fusu in front of him, pinching his cheek—he had lost some weight...

"My..."

"Birthday?"

Fusu’s eyes brightened, and he nodded repeatedly.

Xu Fu stood up, wanting to bend down to hug him, but sadly realized he could no longer easily lift Fusu. Fusu was very self-aware and hurriedly patted Xu Fu’s hand, whispering: "I've grown up, I don't need it, I don't need it..."

The corners of Xu Fu’s mouth couldn't help but curl up; he took Fusu’s hand and walked to the side: "Have you washed up?"

Fusu nodded.

"Have you eaten?"

Fusu shook his head: "...Waiting for Father."

Xu Fu felt that he was incredibly well-behaved, and couldn't help but pinch his cheek again before calling the attendants to help him dress and wash. Once everything was done, the two sat down to have breakfast together. Each had a bowl of soup in front of them.

Hu Hai was frail, and Xu Fu was not much better off; tonic soups had become an essential part of their breakfast. Only when the weather was dry and their vitality was at its peak would they skip the tonics, lest they over-nourish themselves.

Before they had even finished their tonic, an attendant came to request an audience.

Xu Fu let the man in. The attendant was brimming with excitement, and before he could even kneel to speak, a clamor suddenly erupted outside the hall. Ying Zheng strode in, his face glowing with wild joy; the palace servants behind him could barely keep up with his pace, forced to trot along.

Xu Fu hurriedly stood up, "Is there news of victory?"

The smile on Ying Zheng's face could no longer be contained. He laughed heartily in front of Xu Fu without any restraint, "Victory in Han! No, there is no more Han!"

In the seventeenth year of King Zheng of Qin, Li Xin and Neishi Teng swept through like a hot knife through butter, capturing Xinzheng, the capital of Han, in one fell swoop and taking King An of Han prisoner. Only Shangdang refused to surrender to Qin and defected to the State of Zhao.

This was the first of the Seven Warring States that Ying Zheng had annihilated; from this day forth, there would be no more King of Han in the world.

Xu Fu’s heart pounded, and he opened his mouth, but for a long while, he could not utter a word.

The course of history had taken a massive leap forward right before his very eyes...

Hu Hai stood up as well, "Congratulations, Father! Since you have received such good news today, does that mean my gift will be even bigger?"

Ying Zheng was in a great mood. Hearing this, he walked over and patted his head, "You little rascal... what do you want?"

"Father, give Fusu brother to me." Hu Hai licked his lips.

Xu Fu turned to look at him, "What do you want Fusu for?"

"To serve me! When I was little, Fusu brother would hold me like this, but now I can’t even see him..." Hu Hai pouted unhappily, "I don't even see him on my birthday."

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng, who didn't seem angry. He laughed and patted Hu Hai's head again, "What nonsense are you spouting? Aren't there enough people serving you all day long? You still want a Prince of Qin to serve you!"

Ying Zheng’s gaze fell upon the unfinished meal on the table, and he said, "Hurry up and finish eating."

Hu Hai reluctantly sat back down with Xu Fu, muttering, "...Are you taking me out of the palace for my birthday today? I haven't been out, I'm about to become a country bumpkin."

Is that really how the term "country bumpkin" is used?

Xu Fu’s brow twitched, and he couldn't help but interrupt his mischief, "We took you out of the palace when you were young; how can you say you’ve never been out?"

"That was when I was little, I don't remember it at all, so that means I haven't been out," Hu Hai argued stubbornly.

When they returned from the State of Yan, Xu Fu had thought Hu Hai looked much more mature, but seeing him now, he was still that same little dumpling who only knew how to eat, play, and pester Fusu.

Ying Zheng sat down beside Xu Fu and asked with narrowed eyes, "So, between Fusu and going out of the palace, which do you choose?"

Hu Hai’s movements paused, "...I choose going out of the palace."

Xu Fu really couldn't help it, "...Hahaha."

Is Fusu not even worth as much as a chance to leave the palace?

Ying Zheng was also left between laughter and tears, "I shall grant you that wish."

Hu Hai nodded and rubbed his belly, "Father, I'm full."

"Then let's go." Xu Fu stood up, but suddenly saw Fusu standing at the entrance of the hall. Because of the backlight, the expression on his face was dark and unreadable. Hu Hai followed Xu Fu’s gaze and almost dropped his spoon.

"...Ah, Fusu brother." Hu Hai ran over with an innocent look and hugged Fusu’s leg, as if he hadn't just been the one who chose to leave the palace.

Fusu was held so tightly by Hu Hai that he could barely even bow, and could only call out "Father" and "Father" verbally.

Ying Zheng was somewhat surprised, "When did you return?" At this time, he should have been with Meng Tian.

Fusu moved his leg expressionlessly, but couldn't budge, "...I arrived in Xianyang an hour ago."

Xu Fu found it somewhat amusing.

Hu Hai was clingy with his words, but he would cast Fusu aside the moment he got the chance. Fusu didn't say anything, but he still rushed back in time for Hu Hai’s birthday.

Xu Fu walked over and pinched Hu Hai’s cheek, "That’s enough, let’s go."

Since the accident with Jiang You, the four of them rarely traveled together, even if it was just for a walk in Xianyang City. However, now that Fusu and Hu Hai were no longer children and wouldn't be helpless in the face of danger, there were no restrictions on leaving the palace today.

They boarded a carriage and left the palace.

They stopped and went along the way. When they passed by the residence of Wei Liao, the servants recognized the accompanying guards and hurried forward to invite Xu Fu inside.

Xu Fu naturally couldn't just abandon Ying Zheng and the others to go inside. He was about to politely decline when he saw Wei Liao walking out quickly.

"Junior brother." Wei Liao approached, his stern expression slowly melting into a smile, "It is Hu Hai’s birthday, and I have nothing worthy to give." "Someone, bring the items to the Shu Zhang."

The servant on the side hurried forward, holding three bamboo slips in his hands.

Xu Fu thought to himself, here we go again...

Over the past few years, for his birthday, or Hu Hai’s or Fusu’s, Wei Liao would always send gifts in the name of an elder, and the gifts were inevitably bamboo slips—sometimes one, sometimes two or three. Only on Ying Zheng’s birthday would Wei Liao give nothing. But it made no difference, because these bamboo slips were the culmination of Wei Liao’s hard work and would eventually end up in Ying Zheng’s hands.

Wei Liao never explicitly expressed his submission to Ying Zheng, but the act of sending these bamboo slips undoubtedly represented his softening.

How could such bamboo slips be called "nothing worthy to give"?

If these weren't worthy, then he truly didn't know what would be.

"Thank you, Senior brother."

Wei Liao waved his hand, and because Ying Zheng was still in the carriage, he quickly retreated back into his residence.

Xu Fu’s mouth twitched, and he handed the bamboo slips to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng took the slips, looked them over, and then handed them to Fusu, "Can you understand them?"

Fusu nodded earnestly, "I can try."

Xu Fu and Hu Hai, completely out of the loop, glanced at them, eventually gave up on trying to get involved, and turned their attention back to the interesting trinkets on the street.

After playing wantonly in Xianyang City for a day, although there wasn't anything particularly interesting, Xu Fu still felt a sense of lingering enjoyment. He roughly understood the meaning of the phrase, "It doesn't matter what you do, it matters who you are with." In his past life, he was all alone and couldn't taste any of these flavors; in this life, he had tasted them all.

...

·

After Hu Hai’s birthday passed, the King of Han surrendered. Ying Zheng immediately established the Han territory as Yingchuan Commandery, appointed Neishi Teng as the Commandery Governor, and then Li Xin returned with his troops.

The one who received a warm welcome was naturally Li Xin alone.

For a time, he was the center of attention in the court. Everyone said he might be the next Wang Jian. With so much praise, it inevitably carried the suspicion of "killing with kindness," but Li Xin didn't care. He was promoted in rank and rewarded with wealth. After thanking Ying Zheng in the hall, his gaze involuntarily fell upon Xu Fu.

Xu Fu gave him a cold glare, and only then did Li Xin look away.

Wei Liao was also observing this man, and when he noticed his gaze lingering on his junior brother, Wei Liao immediately felt displeased.

A mere greenhorn? Daring to covet his junior brother? Just because he won two battles, he thinks he’s something special?

Ying Zheng also felt somewhat displeased, but since they had just conquered Han, he naturally couldn't send Li Xin out again. This wasn't for Li Xin’s sake, but because the national strength couldn't withstand such continuous consumption. Qin also needed to rest before it could fight again. However, Qin had a tradition of supporting war with war, so it recovered quite quickly.

Li Xin accepted his rewards and stepped aside, standing with Meng Tian and the others, receiving the bold, scrutinizing gazes from all directions.

At this moment, Wei Liao stepped forward, "...Your Majesty, General Li Xin abandoned his post last year and went missing for nearly half a year. How should he be punished?"

The people of Qin all thought Li Xin had gone alone to the State of Yan to save Xu Fu. Because of this, there was a heroic legend about Li Xin in Qin. With this great victory in Han, Li Xin was even more popular among the people, and everyone believed he would become another guardian deity of Qin.

If it weren't for the fact that the Meng brothers couldn't be easily sent out, it probably wouldn't have been Li Xin’s turn.

Compared to that annoying man from the Meng family, Wei Liao found Li Xin even more annoying.

Suddenly, all eyes were fixed on Li Xin. Even Xu Fu looked at him. Yet Li Xin didn't move, his expression firm and unchanged, as if the person Wei Liao was talking about wasn't him at all.

Even Xu Fu had to admire that if Li Xin’s temperament were further honed, he would surely become a rare military talent! But if he remained so impulsive, his talent would inevitably be worn away.

Ying Zheng had also long wanted to find a way to deal with Li Xin, but there was nowhere to strike. This was a rare occasion where Ying Zheng and Wei Liao reached a consensus and coordinated perfectly.

"The State Lieutenant is right. Rewards should be given, but punishments must also be meted out." Ying Zheng paused and said coldly, "Order Li Xin to supervise the construction of the irrigation canal at Hukou, and fine him five hundred shi of grain." Ying Zheng said the latter part with great reluctance, "However, as Li Xin has merit in rescuing the Shu Zhang, his rank shall only be temporarily revoked."

Supervising the construction of an irrigation canal was hard work, and one careless move could lead to disputes with the common people.

How could that compare to the benefits of being on the battlefield?

Everyone cast sympathetic glances at Li Xin, and that fine of five hundred shi was quite substantial!

Yet Li Xin remained neither humble nor arrogant, and thanked Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu shook his head secretly.

Supervising the canal was hard, but it was a great benefit to the people! If the Zheng Guo Canal was completed after he went there, then Li Xin would be credited with a great achievement.

Ying Zheng probably hadn't thought of this, only focused on letting Li Xin suffer.

After the small court session ended, Li Xin didn't talk to those around him. With a solitary attitude, he strode out of the hall and followed closely behind Xu Fu.

Seeing that something was wrong, Wei Liao hurriedly followed. Although he didn't like the King of Qin, he liked this kid even less! If his junior brother’s relationship with the King of Qin was ruined because of him, that would be a disaster! He would have to chop this man up!

When a monarch is angry, a million corpses fall.

Li Xin better not mess around!

While Wei Liao’s thoughts were racing, Li Xin had already caught up to Xu Fu, "Is the Shu Zhang well recently?"

"I would be well if General Li didn't keep trying to lure me away."

As soon as Wei Liao approached, he heard this and was shocked. Luring him away? This is outrageous! How can Li Xin be so tactless? To think such a person could lead troops and even capture the King of Han! Is the defense of Han made of dung?

Li Xin’s face showed no embarrassment. He just knelt down with a "thud" in front of Xu Fu, "That day was my recklessness. So much time has passed, is the Shu Zhang still unwilling to forgive Li Xin?"

Xu Fu was startled by him, and other officials couldn't help but look over.

They had truly become a spectacle of gossip.

"...General Li rescued me in Ji City, so that cancels everything out."

Li Xin stood up and suddenly said, "...No, it doesn't have to be that way. The Shu Zhang went to Ji City because of me; how can the two cancel each other out? What Li Xin owes the Shu Zhang, I will repay in the future. If the Shu Zhang won't forgive me, then don't."

Xu Fu: ???

Li Xin is telling him not to forgive him? What kind of god-like logic is this?

Xu Fu really couldn't understand.

"Since General Li is aware that he has harmed someone, why do you keep pestering the Shu Zhang? General Li, please leave quickly and stop being an eyesore." Wei Liao finally reached the two of them.

The officials passing by shook their heads secretly.

The State Lieutenant’s words are still as sharp as ever.

Li Xin was also stunned, probably having never met someone like Wei Liao.

Xu Fu pulled Wei Liao back, fearing that he might get excited and knock Li Xin to the ground, "Go." These words were clearly meant for Li Xin.

Li Xin looked at Wei Liao with burning eyes, and there was even a sense of battle intent in them.

Finally, hindered by the fact that Xu Fu was standing there, Li Xin obediently left.

Wei Liao looked around, and the others hurried to put away their gossiping expressions and followed Li Xin away. After they left, Wei Liao said to Xu Fu, "Is this person admiring you?"

"...Perhaps."

"Since you are the lover of the King of Qin, you naturally cannot be ambiguous with others, otherwise, you will be the one to suffer in your relationship with the King of Qin."

"I know..."

"This person is very reckless, knows no etiquette, and acts as he pleases. He is not fit for great use!" Wei Liao frowned, looking very displeased, just like when he first met Ying Zheng, wishing he could scold him from head to toe. However, in recent years, Wei Liao knew his physiognomy skills weren't as good as Xu Fu’s, so he didn't dwell on Li Xin’s face.

"His ability cannot be underestimated. That is precisely why I feel he shouldn't be discarded; it would be a pity."

Wei Liao snorted, "Where is he needed? If we have Meng Tian, how would it ever be his turn?"

Xu Fu blinked, "...Senior brother is not scolding Meng Tian today?"

Wei Liao’s face looked ugly, "Li Xin is even more detestable than him."

So it was just because of a comparison? Xu Fu scanned Wei Liao and nodded, noncommittally.

The good senior brother, having finished lecturing his junior brother, waved his hand with satisfaction, "Go, and remember not to get too close to others."

Xu Fu nodded, "Okay, Senior brother, remember to stay five zhang away from me next time."

Wei Liao’s face turned red. Eh? Wasn't he doing this for his junior brother’s own good?

Xu Fu was just joking. He turned around, and a faint smile couldn't help but appear on his lips.

Senior brother and Meng Tian are quite interesting...

Xu Fu walked slowly toward the hall where Ying Zheng handled state affairs. Upon entering, he saw Ying Zheng frowning, looking displeased. It couldn't be because of Li Xin, could it? Xu Fu walked up and saw someone kneeling before Ying Zheng. That person had an expression completely opposite to Ying Zheng’s—he was full of joy.

Seeing Xu Fu enter, Ying Zheng beckoned him over, "The news that just arrived: there was an earthquake in the State of Zhao."

Xu Fu was surprised.

No wonder the messenger looked so happy; if the enemy suffers, isn't it a blessing for their side?

However, thinking of the common people who were suffering, Xu Fu couldn't bring himself to smile.

"Why is Your Majesty worried?"

"The area where the earthquake occurred in Zhao borders Qin. I am worried that Qin will also be affected."

"Have you tested it with the seismoscope?"

"There was no sound."

"Then send someone to that area and order the local officials to pay close attention to the seismoscope’s reaction. If there is the slightest movement, evacuate in time."

Ying Zheng hesitated and said, "Zhao does not have a seismoscope, and they don't have you by their side like I do. After this earthquake, their national strength will surely be greatly reduced. I intend to send Meng Tian to retake Shangdang."

Shangdang... that was the place in Han that refused to surrender to Qin.

"If Your Majesty thinks it is feasible, I will naturally support it." Ying Zheng was right; this was indeed a good opportunity. But at the same time, no one knew if the Qin army would encounter an earthquake while on the march.

"If I send Meng Tian, Fusu will surely follow..."

Xu Fu finally understood where Ying Zheng’s true worry lay, "Are you worried about Fusu?"

"Indeed. He is still a bit young after all. I do not want him to get involved in such things, but for the past few years, I don't know why, Fusu has been wanting to find an opportunity to go to the battlefield with Meng Tian, saying that he needs to be tempered. Only after seeing the cruelty of the battlefield can he know the difficulty of my unification. Since Fusu is so sensible, I find it hard to refuse." Moreover, Ying Zheng had high hopes for Fusu in his heart.

Since he and Xu Fu were destined to have no more offspring, Ying Zheng poured all his heart and soul into Fusu. It was naturally good that Fusu was motivated.

But after all, he was his son, and when a son is away, parents inevitably worry.

"If I follow..."

Ying Zheng had thought of this too, but he felt that if Fusu and Hu Hai both went, wouldn't his worries only increase?

"...How is Hu Hai learning from you?" Ying Zheng suddenly asked.

Xu Fu looked at him in disbelief, "You, you aren't planning to let the two brothers go together, are you?" If Hu Hai went to the battlefield, Fusu would probably be looking after him the whole time. And Xu Fu really didn't think Hu Hai had learned anything at all.

Ying Zheng’s idea was simply insane!
