燕国使臣一路紧赶慢赶到达了咸阳，个个都灰扑扑的不成模样了。他们以为秦王大喜之下，会立即招他们入宫。而实际上，迎接他们的只有一名内侍，伴几名侍从。
当然，这些使臣不会知晓，他们眼中的小内侍，其实正是赵高，赵高来接他们，也不算是辱没他们了。
之所以打发了赵高前来，嬴政不过是觉得赵高脑筋活，让他先来瞧一瞧燕国使臣可有不对劲之处。
燕国使臣一行人极为不忿，原本前来秦国献地，他们就是满腔怨气，此时见秦国如此怠慢，胸中的怒火更是一层又上一层楼。
“秦国便是如此待我等吗？”其中一人忍不住怒道。
赵高凉凉地瞥了他一眼，没说话。
此时那人身边站着的男子，伸手拽了他一把。男子穿着分外宽大的衣袍，面无表情，双目冰冷，仔细去瞧，却又觉得他那双眼分明是空茫的。别的却是看不清了。只因那男子脸上还裹着布条，瞧上去像是重伤未愈一般。
赵高问道：“那人是谁？”
有人答道：“荆轲。”
赵高冷笑一声，转身离去，竟是连他们送也不送进去。
燕国使臣一行人再难遏制心中怒气，不由得厉声道：“秦国待客之道正是让我等好生领教到了。”
赵高面上冷色不改，刺了回去，“你们燕国胆敢派出刺客刺杀我大秦的驷车庶长，如今还期望得到什么温和态度？”赵高轻蔑道：“未将你们扫出咸阳，先让你们吃个苦头，已经是不错了。”
对面的人涨红了脸，气得说不出话来。
赵高也不再多留，迅速带着人撤离了此处。等回到咸阳宫后，他便匆匆到了嬴政的跟前。
“如何？”徐福倒是比嬴政更关注那些从燕国来的使臣。
赵高躬身笑道：“目前瞧来，是没有什么不对劲之处的。”
徐福点头，也并不觉得意外。若是看一眼就能揪出刺客，那历史上荆轲又怎会差点得手呢？
“……快了。”嬴政合上面前的竹简，抬手覆住徐福的手背，语气沉静，带着足以安抚住人的力量，“就看明日了。”
徐福嘴角微微上翘。
赵高抬头瞧了一眼，总觉得徐福像是在笑，但又像是自己的错觉。
有什么……值得开心的吗？
chapters.title: 第221章
chapters.translated_text:
Ying Zheng was furious. Before the assassin could raise his hand to strike again, he lunged forward with his long sword.

The Qin King’s sword was about a meter long, while the blade in the assassin’s hand was far shorter. The tip of the sword pierced through the assassin’s shoulder first. In pain, the assassin withdrew his hand, and the blade fell to the ground. The guards nearby finally swarmed forward and subdued him.

Before long, soldiers and guards sealed off the entire street, searching everywhere to see if he had any accomplices.

Ying Zheng’s cold gaze swept across the street and finally landed on Xu Fu. He wrapped his arms around Xu Fu with a firm yet gentle motion and whispered, "Are you hurt?"

Xu Fu had just shaken his head when he felt a sharp pain in his ankle and calf. However, after a moment's thought, he smoothed out his brow, which had furrowed from the pain, and appeared as if nothing were wrong. Ying Zheng, relieved, then took Xu Fu back to the Xianyang Palace.

The soldiers were left behind to handle the aftermath.

Regardless of whether the assassin had accomplices, it would be impossible for them to succeed again in the short term.

After Ying Zheng and Xu Fu returned to the palace, the captured assassin was brought up shortly thereafter. At this time, it was not yet popular to hide poison sacs in one's teeth to commit suicide upon capture. Therefore, when the assassin was tied up before Xu Fu, he had only the wound inflicted by Ying Zheng, which was not fatal. This meant he could be interrogated for a long time without dying easily. The assassin likely realized his situation; his face turned uncontrollably pale, his gaze became unfocused, and he lacked any of the spirit of a heroic martyr.

This man could not be Jing Ke.

Xu Fu concluded with disappointment in his heart.

If it wasn't Jing Ke, did that mean there would be more assassination attempts? Xu Fu’s gaze toward the assassin inevitably carried a hint of disgust. Perhaps this assassin believed he was killing an enemy of his state, someone who had cheated the Yan state, and that this was a righteous, heroic act. But in Xu Fu’s eyes, he had no "saintly" sentiments toward an enemy who tried to profit from him, failed, and then sent people to kill him out of spite. If the other party wanted him dead, then he wanted the other party dead.

"Did the King of Yan send you?" Ying Zheng asked, almost directly pinning the crime on the King of Yan.

The assassin gritted his teeth and remained silent, his attitude appearing very resolute.

Ying Zheng’s attitude, however, was even more resolute. He gestured, and a nearby attendant understood. The attendant, holding a small knife, bowed his head and cleanly severed the assassin’s little finger. The assassin’s scream immediately echoed through the entire palace.

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu closer into his arms and said, "If you feel uncomfortable, go back and rest. I will handle this."

Xu Fu shook his head.

The assassin wanted him dead, and he wanted the assassin dead; why bother pretending not to have the heart to watch?

Upon hearing this, Ying Zheng said nothing more. He stopped questioning the assassin, acting as if he had forgotten him, and simply held Xu Fu in his arms, toying with a stylus knife. The sharp tip of the knife made one feel a chill, a fear that in the next moment, it might be plunged into one's own body.

Initially, the assassin hadn't been that terrified, but he hadn't expected the King of Qin to be so brutal. Without a word, he had ordered his little finger to be cut off. The pain of the fingers being connected to the heart surged into his bones in an instant. Then came the unbearable silence; everyone stopped speaking, and he could only hear the sound of his own blood flowing. What was terrifying was not death, but the fear of the unknown. He didn't know what else the King of Qin would do, or in what way he would die...

The assassin blinked his sore eyes and opened his mouth: "It... it was the King of Yan... he told me to kill the State Preceptor, no, he is no longer the State Preceptor..."

Only his voice filled the empty hall, and after the sound faded, the King of Qin did not respond to him.

The assassin panicked, an inexplicable fear gripping his heart.

He couldn't help but open his mouth again, spilling everything out like beans from a bamboo tube...

Xu Fu was truly speechless.

This assassin had no professional ethics, let alone any heroic spirit.

However, although the assassin said a lot, very little of it was useful. Xu Fu only gathered one thing: the King of Yan was determined to kill him.

This feeling of drawing away the hatred on behalf of Ying Zheng... Xu Fu felt he was quite something!

By the time the assassin finished speaking, he was already lying on the ground due to excessive blood loss, his gaze even more unfocused.

Ying Zheng didn't even glance at him, saying coldly, "Kill him." After a pause, he added, "Post a public notice: whoever assassinates the Si Che Shu Zhang shall have their entire clan exterminated." Hidden within his calm tone was this message: it didn't matter if they were from another state; once that state was conquered, their clan would be exterminated all the same.

Xu Fu reached out and pressed down on the hand Ying Zheng was using to hold the stylus knife. It was a simple gesture, yet it seemed to press back Ying Zheng’s killing intent as well.

"That won't do. If it's to deter others... there's no need to ruin your own reputation." It is understandable to seek revenge, but slaughtering an entire clan will inevitably invite criticism.

Ying Zheng, however, didn't care at all. "Only this method can deter these people. They may not care about their own deaths, but they must consider that their entire clan will die with them." Saying this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but sneer, "Besides, haven't I long been known as 'brutal' among the states? Since that is the case, why should I bother pretending to be a good person!" A look of disdain flashed across his face as he added, "Families that can produce such assassins are likely not good families either!"

Xu Fu: "..." What kind of twisted logic is this? You almost convinced me.

Yet, for a moment, he couldn't think of a perfect reason to refute it, so Xu Fu gave up and stared at Ying Zheng, saying, "I don't allow it." Three words, exceptionally stubborn.

Ying Zheng wouldn't listen to any other argument, but this one... he listened.

Ying Zheng frowned, but finally called out to the attendant who was about to deliver the order, "Then just write down his crimes, state his wickedness, and let him be haunted by a bad name even after death!"

The attendant carefully glanced at Xu Fu, feeling immense admiration while nodding repeatedly to accept the order.

After the attendant stepped out of the palace gate, Ying Zheng turned to ask Xu Fu, "Do you feel better now?"

Xu Fu didn't answer, instead saying, "The King of Yan sent someone to assassinate me; I am the victim. But if we slaughter their entire clan, we become the perpetrators. Perhaps some assassins will retreat because of such harsh punishment, but others will only believe more firmly that killing you and me is a heroic act. Why should we create a righteous excuse for those assassins?" Xu Fu paused and said calmly, "I am not willing to let that happen."

Ying Zheng sighed softly, "I understand."

Xu Fu lifted his leg and took the opportunity to say, "My leg hurts."

Ying Zheng’s expression changed slightly. Without hesitation, he reached out, lifted Xu Fu’s leg, bent over, and pulled up the robe, revealing the grazed ankle and calf. Xu Fu stared at the blood-stained wound and blinked; it must have been grazed when he jumped from the carriage.

It didn't hurt much, well within his tolerance, but Xu Fu didn't know why he couldn't help but want to complain about the pain.

In the end, such unmanly words didn't manage to escape his lips.

Instead, Ying Zheng’s brows were knotted together, looking as if he were the one who had been injured. He supported Xu Fu’s waist, picked him up, and carried him straight out. The court physician, who had just arrived, had to trot along on short legs to keep up.

The injury on Xu Fu’s leg wasn't serious to begin with, and after treatment, it was of no concern.

Soon, a notice was posted on the city walls, detailing the assassin’s background and his sinister intentions. The people, upon seeing it, were all filled with utter contempt. To the Qin state, Xu Fu was already a figure who brought good fortune; how could they allow people from other states to come and assassinate him?

When the news reached other states, no one praised the assassin as a hero. In secret, some even said that the move the King of Yan made was truly too stupid.

But regardless of how others discussed the matter, the King of Yan was truly determined to kill Xu Fu. Afterward, assassins attempted to sneak into Xianyang one after another, but Ying Zheng had made full preparations, so every one that came was captured. Eventually, few assassins were tempted by gold or silver to dare come and assassinate Xu Fu. The King of Yan had intended to wait until Xu Fu left the palace and the city of Xianyang to strike, but those assassins lurked outside the city for days without even catching a glimpse of Xu Fu.

How could they know that a person who stays indoors can go a whole year without leaving a city?

In the blink of an eye, several months passed.

A palace servant trotted into the hall and bowed to Xu Fu, saying, "The yarrow stalks have grown." After speaking, an attendant nearby presented a tray, and on the tray lay the yarrow stalks.

Yarrow divination: the number of the Great Expansion is fifty, of which forty-nine are used; divide them into two to represent the two poles, hang one to represent the three, count them by fours to represent the four seasons, return the remainder to the fingers to represent the leap month; every five years there are two leap months, so return the remainder twice before hanging.

Xu Fu knew this formula, but he had never tried to use it for divination in earnest.

In the eyes of people from later generations, it was just a pile of weeds; how could it be used for divination? It sounded like a joke.

Xu Fu took one yarrow stalk to symbolize the Taiji, then took forty-nine and divided them into two piles to symbolize the two poles. He took one from the left pile and placed it between his right fingers, then used his right hand to take from the left pile in groups of four, the four symbolizing the four seasons. After taking the stalks from both sides in this manner, the sum of the remaining stalks on both sides was eight.

The palace servants watching were already dazzled, having no idea what Xu Fu was doing. In their eyes, the movement of Xu Fu’s ten fingers was like a magic trick.

"Father, what is this?" Hu Hai scurried over and snatched the yarrow stalks.

Xu Fu’s face darkened: ...

Hu Hai had no idea he had caused a mess. He licked his lips and said excitedly, "Father, this can be used to cast curses on people!"

Xu Fu: ...

Hu Hai stuffed the yarrow stalks into his pocket, "Father, can I take them back to play with?" he asked earnestly, blinking his eyes.

Xu Fu couldn't even get angry anymore, he could only wave his hand, "Go on, take them and play." As long as Hu Hai wasn't doing anything reckless. Xu Fu directly ignored the comment; if things like curses weren't considered reckless, what was?

Hu Hai happily tucked the yarrow stalks away and rolled off to play. Before long, he attracted mosquitoes and was bitten several times. Soon, Hu Hai himself became a crybaby. His skin was tender, and he swelled up after a few bites. The itching made Hu Hai’s tears stream down.

Xu Fu stared at him, not knowing how to comfort him.

A palace servant had a sudden idea and went to find Fusu. After Fusu arrived, he simply dragged Hu Hai away.

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief. Only when he came to his senses did he realize that with Hu Hai’s interference, he had forgotten the purpose of his divination.

Xu Fu had no choice but to order people to go and pick more yarrow stalks.

Before long, the first to return was not the servant picking yarrow, but Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng wore a look of obvious joy, and the domineering and arrogant look between his brows had grown even more intense. He was truly in high spirits.

He strode over, wrapped his arms around Xu Fu, and said, "The King of Yan originally had times of fear... He dared to send people to assassinate you, but now he has softened his knees." A look of disdain flashed across Ying Zheng’s face; he was exceptionally disgusted by the King of Yan.

Xu Fu was puzzled, "Why do you say that?"

"The King of Yan has sent envoys to offer me land."

Offering land was naturally a good thing, but Xu Fu suddenly couldn't feel happy; it was an instinctive resistance. Xu Fu’s heart sank, and he asked, "What land is being offered?"

"Dukang, this is the fertile land of the Yan state. For the King of Yan to be willing to offer this land, he must truly be intimidated by Wang Jian’s momentum." Since the King of Yan sent assassins to kill Xu Fu, Ying Zheng had immediately mobilized Wang Jian and others to lead a large army northward, an unstoppable force.

Xu Fu couldn't hear anything else at this moment. His mind was echoing with that sentence from his old school textbooks: "Respectfully beheading Fan Yuqi, and presenting the map of Dukang of Yan, sealed in a box, the King of Yan bowed and sent it to the court, sending an envoy to inform the Great King."

The so-called "at the end of the map, the dagger is revealed" (tu qiong bi shou jian) — wasn't that map the map of Dukang of Yan?

From the perspective of understanding history, Xu Fu didn't believe for a second that the King of Yan was sincerely offering the map. Not to mention his experience dealing with the King of Yan, he knew that the King of Yan was not someone willing to bow his head easily, unless Wang Jian had truly led his men to the city of Ji and the King of Yan was in danger himself, only then would he surrender.

Offering Dukang was nothing but a temporary measure, all to arrange for Jing Ke to enter Qin and assassinate Ying Zheng!

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more a fire burned in his chest, scorching him. But the King of Yan had voluntarily submitted, and the Qin state could not refuse. Regardless of whether the King of Yan was truly bowing his head or faking it, in the eyes of other states, they would think the King of Yan was truly afraid of Qin’s power. This move could also achieve the effect of deterring other states. If there were other timid rulers like the King of Han, they might just offer their land too. Such an opportunity to display the might of Qin was something not only Ying Zheng couldn't bear to refuse, but Xu Fu himself admitted he couldn't bear to either!

Xu Fu’s mind raced with a thousand thoughts. Finally, he composed his expression and asked nonchalantly, "Have the Yan envoys already set off?"

Ying Zheng nodded, "They have already set off."

Then they could only receive the Yan envoys. No matter what tricks they used, in the end, they would not only seize the Dukang map but also teach the assassin a hard lesson. Then, by killing the chicken to scare the monkey, everyone would know that the King of Qin was not so easily assassinated. If they wanted to deceive the King of Qin, they might end up shooting themselves in the foot!

Xu Fu didn't tell Ying Zheng any of these thoughts. He compromised, frowning, "I have had a bad premonition for the past few months, so I have been performing divination once a month. Today’s divination gave me a bad hexagram. A few months ago, the King of Yan wanted my life at all costs, and now, after only a few months, he is so quick to admit defeat and bow his head. I don't think it fits the King of Yan’s character. A-Zheng, you must be on guard."

Such words, of course, only Xu Fu dared to say in Ying Zheng’s ear.

After the news of the King of Yan offering Dukang spread, most of the ministers were busy being happy, their words full of praise for Ying Zheng. Those who felt something was wrong didn't dare to dampen Ying Zheng’s spirits at such a time.

The smile on Ying Zheng’s face gradually faded, and he said in a deep voice, "A-Fu is right. I must not be blinded by momentary success. If the King of Yan is unwilling, then this offer of Dukang must have a very sinister plot behind it! When the day comes, I will certainly make careful arrangements. No matter what conspiracy the King of Yan has, it will have no result in the end."

It was good that Ying Zheng was vigilant. Xu Fu breathed a secret sigh of relief and didn't dwell on the matter anymore.

He knew this history, so avoiding it shouldn't be difficult... Xu Fu thought to himself. But he didn't expect the first problem to stump him very quickly.

·

The attendant placed bronze swords, which were exquisite yet radiated a sharp, cold air, one by one in front of Xu Fu.

The swords worn in the Qin state were made quite long, a meter, or even 1.4 meters long.

Just looking at those 1.4-meter-long swords made Xu Fu’s teeth ache. How was it written in the school textbook?

"He drew his sword, but the sword was long, so he grabbed the scabbard. At that urgent moment, the sword was stuck, so it could not be drawn immediately."

It meant the King of Qin tried to draw his sword, but the sword was too long, so he couldn't pull it out and was left holding the empty scabbard. In his haste, he tried again, but the sword was stuck too tightly, and he still couldn't draw it.

Xu Fu vaguely remembered laughing out loud in his heart when he first learned this. Because the sword was too long and almost killed him—wasn't that a joke?

But now, Xu Fu couldn't laugh at all. He didn't want this scene to play out in the palace hall again.

Xu Fu shook his head and looked at the attendant, "Are there any shorter swords?"

"Yes!" the attendant replied crisply. Not long after, he really came back holding swords.

Who would dare to make such a fuss without Ying Zheng’s permission? So many swords placed in the palace were absolute lethal weapons. If it were anyone else, they would likely have been treated as having ulterior motives and dealt with.

When Ying Zheng returned to the hall, a pile of swords was already in front of Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng’s brows jumped heavily. He was truly worried that Xu Fu would accidentally cut himself, so he stepped forward quickly and pulled Xu Fu from his seat, "Have you looked at them?"

Xu Fu pointed to the short swords he had selected, "A-Zheng, why don't you try them?"

Ying Zheng picked up a sword and looked at him, confused.

Xu Fu said, "Is it easy to draw?"

"Of course it is easy." Ying Zheng smiled and drew them out without any burden.

Xu Fu sized up Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng was tall enough; even if a 1.4-meter sword were hung on him, it would still be easy. But in such a critical situation, how could Ying Zheng’s arm reach that far?

Xu Fu thought for a moment and took the shortest one, "How about using this as your sword?"

Ying Zheng was stunned, never expecting Xu Fu to say such a thing. He thought Xu Fu had ordered people to find swords to test new results, but in the end, he was just picking a sword for him? Ying Zheng was moved, but he still smiled and refused, "Why did you suddenly think of picking a sword for me? I already have one, so this is unnecessary."

"How can that sword compare to this one?" Xu Fu raised an eyebrow and squinted at him.

Ying Zheng felt his heart itch from that look, "Yes, it cannot compare."

"Then change it!"

Ying Zheng smiled and patted Xu Fu’s head, "There are rules for the length of a sword. Although I like what A-Fu picked, I cannot change it at will." Perhaps to please Xu Fu, Ying Zheng consciously lowered his stance.

Xu Fu was so choked he almost vomited blood. There were rules for the length of a sword? Did it mean the higher the status, the longer the sword? This kind of rule should be abolished as soon as possible!

Xu Fu’s expression turned cold, "Your sword is so long, how can you draw it? If you encounter danger, what will you do?"

Ying Zheng wasn't stupid and soon realized what Xu Fu meant. He knew Xu Fu was preparing for the day the Yan envoys arrived. Ying Zheng laughed, "I have already made arrangements, A-Fu need not worry. If you treat this as a major matter, wouldn't you just be restraining yourself?"

Xu Fu knew what Ying Zheng meant. If it were an idiom, it would be saying he was being too "suspicious of every bush and tree."

However, how did history evaluate Jing Ke’s assassination of the King of Qin? It was said to be the closest attempt to succeed in assassinating the King of Qin.

Seeing Xu Fu’s unhappy expression, Ying Zheng had to grab a long sword from the side, grip the hilt, and draw it out easily... Ying Zheng smiled, "If the King of Yan really prepared men to assassinate me at the banquet, I fear that before they could even get close, the long sword in my hand would have already subdued them."

Xu Fu looked at the long sword.

...It seemed there was logic to it being long.

Those assassins would never be arrogant enough to bring long swords in. Of course, even if they wanted to, they couldn't bring them in. So didn't the long sword in Ying Zheng’s hand have the advantage?

Xu Fu’s gaze couldn't help but linger on Ying Zheng’s arm and waist, "Is A-Zheng’s arm strength sufficient?"

Ying Zheng laughed loudly, threw the long sword aside, stepped forward, and picked Xu Fu up, "Hmm? Does A-Fu know how my arm strength is now?"

Seeing Ying Zheng like this, Xu Fu knew he really didn't take the King of Yan’s tricks to heart. Monarchs are often arrogant, and Ying Zheng had enough capital to be arrogant, or even conceited. Xu Fu blinked; so be it, long sword it is. If he couldn't draw it, he would just draw it for him. Ying Zheng wouldn't have the same imposing manner with a short sword, but he was different. Anyway, he wasn't as tall as Ying Zheng, so a short sword suited him just fine.

Xu Fu patted Ying Zheng’s arm, "Put me down."

Ying Zheng took the opportunity to kiss Xu Fu’s forehead before putting him down. The palace servants quickly lowered their heads, preferring to look at the murderous weapons scattered all over the floor.

Xu Fu picked up the short sword that Ying Zheng had dismissed, "This one belongs to me."

"Good." Ying Zheng, of course, wouldn't have a single word of objection. Even if the ministers were dissatisfied, he had his own ways to appease them.

The attendant came in and carefully cleared away the swords.

Ying Zheng said, "What do you think of the sword in your hand?"

"Hmm?"

"This is not a bronze sword, but an iron sword obtained after the craftsmen improved it based on the drawings you provided."

At this time, iron swords already existed, but they were not as good as the improved craftsmanship of later generations. Moreover, the methods for mining iron ore at this time were also very primitive. Xu Fu had recorded them and given them to Ying Zheng, but he hadn't expected that in the blink of an eye, there would be a finished product. That was perfect... it would be used on the assassin when the time came.

"We'll see if the craftsmen have been lazy when we test it then."

Seeing that the expression on Xu Fu’s face had relaxed quite a bit, Ying Zheng finally felt relieved. As long as he could coax Xu Fu, it was fine.

·

The Yan envoys rushed all the way to Xianyang, all of them looking dusty and disheveled. They thought that the King of Qin, in his great joy, would immediately summon them into the palace. In reality, they were greeted by only one attendant and a few servants.

Of course, these envoys wouldn't know that the little attendant in their eyes was actually Zhao Gao. Zhao Gao coming to greet them was not an insult to them.

The reason Ying Zheng sent Zhao Gao was simply because he felt Zhao Gao was quick-witted and wanted him to see if there was anything suspicious about the Yan envoys.

The Yan envoys were extremely indignant. They were already full of resentment for coming to Qin to offer land, and seeing Qin’s neglect, the anger in their chests rose higher and higher.

"Is this how the Qin state treats us?" one of them couldn't help but say angrily.

Zhao Gao glanced at him coldly and said nothing.

At this time, the man standing next to him reached out and pulled him. The man was wearing exceptionally wide robes, expressionless, his eyes cold. If one looked closely, one would feel that his eyes were clearly vacant. Nothing else could be seen, only because the man’s face was wrapped in cloth strips, looking as if he were still recovering from a serious injury.

Zhao Gao asked, "Who is that?"

Someone replied, "Jing Ke."

Zhao Gao sneered and turned to leave, not even bothering to escort them in.

The Yan envoys could no longer suppress their anger and couldn't help but say sharply, "We have truly learned a lesson about the Qin state’s hospitality."

Zhao Gao’s expression remained cold as he retorted, "Your Yan state dared to send an assassin to kill our Great Qin’s Si Che Shu Zhang, and now you expect a gentle attitude?" Zhao Gao said contemptuously, "It’s already generous that we haven't swept you out of Xianyang and made you suffer a bit first."

The man opposite flushed red, too angry to speak.

Zhao Gao didn't stay any longer and quickly led his men away. After returning to the Xianyang Palace, he hurried to Ying Zheng’s side.

"How was it?" Xu Fu was more concerned about the envoys from Yan than Ying Zheng.

Zhao Gao bowed and smiled, "As it stands, there is nothing suspicious."

Xu Fu nodded, not feeling surprised. If one could spot an assassin just by looking, how could Jing Ke have almost succeeded in history?

"...It’s almost time." Ying Zheng closed the bamboo slip in front of him and placed his hand over the back of Xu Fu’s hand, his tone calm, carrying enough power to reassure anyone, "We shall see tomorrow."

The corners of Xu Fu’s mouth curled up slightly.

Zhao Gao looked up and felt that Xu Fu seemed to be smiling, but it might have been his imagination.

Was there anything... worth being happy about?

The next day, Ying Zheng held court as usual. The delegation from the State of Yan had been waiting until they were anxious, yet they still failed to receive an audience with the King of Qin. It wasn't until the palace banquet was held that Zhao Gao finally led people to summon the Yan envoys. The envoys were filled with indignation, but they had no choice but to suppress it.

All around them were Qin soldiers, holding weapons and clad in iron armor, their entire presence radiating a sharp, icy coldness that made people tremble uncontrollably.

Even if the Yan envoys were filled with resentment, they could not say a word.

Soon, they entered the palace. The further they walked, the more Qin soldiers they saw. These soldiers were all clad in iron armor, their faces as cold as iron, their momentum imposing. One person in the delegation couldn't help but have his legs shaking, his face revealing fear.

Zhao Gao turned back and scolded the man, "Why are you so unseemly?"

The man named Jing Ke also turned back and gave the man a cold look, "Keep up."

The man let out a breath, nodded hurriedly, and followed Jing Ke inside.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were already seated. Although the Qin ministers were dissatisfied with Xu Fu's special status, they could console themselves by thinking of him in the Queen's seat; after all, he couldn't be the Queen of Qin, so this was actually a slight to him. The simple-minded ministers fell into this straightforward, naive line of thinking.

On the contrary, after the Yan envoys entered the hall and saw Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, they felt extremely strange. They thought to themselves, no wonder he refused when the King of Yan offered him the title of State Preceptor. It turned out that in Qin, although he was a Shu-Zhang of the Four-Horse Chariot, he actually sat with the King of Qin, his status a cut above other ministers! Wouldn't the other ministers be dissatisfied because of this? These Yan people could never figure it out.

They were not allowed to continue walking forward.

More guards stepped forward to search them for weapons. A look of annoyance at being humiliated flashed across the faces of the Yan people.

Xu Fu sat high up and could see further, his line of sight enough to encompass everything before him. He tugged on Ying Zheng's sleeve and whispered, "Look at one of them; his legs are shaking and his expression is flustered. There must be something fishy."

Just then, the guards finished their search; they had no weapons or sharp objects on them.

Ying Zheng said in a deep voice, "Who is presenting the map?"

The man stepped out and said loudly, "Jing Ke and Qin Wuyang have come to present the map!" After he finished speaking, the flustered young man beside him also walked out, barely managing to steady his wavering gaze.

Xu Fu remembered that in the story of Jing Ke assassinating the King of Qin, there was a person who almost ruined Jing Ke's plan. Could it be this young man? Xu Fu withdrew his gaze, looked at Jing Ke, and said coldly, "Why are you covering your face with a cloth?" For some reason, Xu Fu always felt that something had been overlooked; the whole thing felt strange.

"Upon arriving in Qin, I suffered from the change in climate and developed malignant sores on my face, so I dare not show this face to the King of Qin," Jing Ke said in a deep voice.

A flash of inspiration crossed Xu Fu's mind. He couldn't help but squint and examine Jing Ke closely, finally realizing what was wrong. Xu Fu felt both shocked and inexplicably amused. He turned to look at Qin Wuyang beside him; under his gaze, Qin Wuyang's face turned blue and white, his legs so weak he was almost collapsing.

Not having the guts, yet wanting to assassinate the King of Qin?

Xu Fu sneered in his heart.

The attendants on both sides shouted, "Why has this envoy changed his expression?"

Jing Ke actually smiled, his tone relaxed as he brushed it off, "He is just a crude countryman who has never seen someone as heroic as the King of Qin. Being awed by the King's presence, he naturally became flustered. I ask for the King's forgiveness for his lack of decorum."

"Is that so?" Ying Zheng's tone was also quite playful, clearly not taking Jing Ke's words to heart. Ying Zheng waved his hand, ordering someone to take Qin Wuyang away. Qin Wuyang was already scared witless; when he was dragged away by the Qin soldiers, he didn't even dare to struggle.

"Present the map in your hand," Ying Zheng said in a low voice.

Jing Ke was followed by a group of Yan people who could only be blocked at the foot of the steps in shame and anger.

Jing Ke walked up the steps slowly, the map in his hand gradually unfurling.

Xu Fu held his breath unconsciously; he wanted to see what kind of tricks this person was going to play.

Just as it was written in the textbook—the map was revealed, and the dagger appeared!

The map rolled to the ground, but the poisoned dagger was gripped tightly in Jing Ke's hand as he lunged at Ying Zheng. The crowd fell into chaos instantly. The remaining Yan people were flustered and retreated repeatedly, while the guards swarmed up and apprehended them all.

At this moment in the hall, Xu Fu's expression changed slightly, and he was about to draw his sword, but Ying Zheng pressed a hand on him, instead easily drawing his own sword and wounding Jing Ke. Jing Ke was furious, a fierce look flashing in his eyes. He raised his hand and threw the dagger, but missing his target, he lost his final weapon.

Everything ended too quickly; the ministers were a bit dazed, and the captured Yan people were also somewhat confused.

Xu Fu heaved a sigh of relief.

He wondered if he would still hear Jing Ke leaning against a pillar and cursing after his failed strike?

Xu Fu frowned at Jing Ke, seeing him retreat to a pillar and laugh, "The reason the matter did not succeed was that I wanted to take you alive."

How similar to the words in the language textbook. Xu Fu's brow furrowed even tighter. Seeing this, Ying Zheng stood up, not even looking at him, and said, "Take him away."

The attendants stepped forward, grabbed Jing Ke, and dragged him out. Xu Fu walked straight down the steps and followed them out of the main hall.

The ministers hadn't recovered yet, and after a long while, they stammered, "...Your Majesty?"

Ying Zheng's expression turned cold, and he threw his table, "The State of Yan is detestable! I will definitely capture King Xi of Yan alive!"

The ministers hurriedly knelt and bowed, not daring to advise him otherwise.

Meanwhile, Xu Fu followed the attendants outside the hall. Seeing that the attendants were about to drag him away, Xu Fu hurriedly spoke up to stop their actions, "Bring him over."

The attendants looked at each other, not knowing whether to obey or not. But at this moment, Xu Fu had already turned and left, so the attendants had no choice but to grit their teeth and follow, dragging Jing Ke along. Xu Fu beckoned an attendant over, "Find a quiet place."

The attendant didn't understand why, but he still followed Xu Fu's wishes and found a nearby palace.

Xu Fu had always been able to move freely in the royal palace; the guards outside the hall not only didn't stop him but bowed and let him in.

The attendants pushed Jing Ke inside. Seeing that Jing Ke was still standing and not kneeling, the attendant beside him looked displeased and was about to draw his sword to force him, but Xu Fu interrupted him directly, "You wait outside."

"Shu-Zhang!" The attendant's eyes widened, not complying, fearing that Jing Ke would attack Xu Fu again.

Xu Fu shook his head, his attitude firm, "Retreat. He has no weapons on him; how could he hurt me?"

The attendants had no choice but to grit their teeth and retreat.

Jing Ke chuckled, raised his hand, and tore off his face mask, revealing the face underneath. His face was covered in something unknown, looking black and disgusting, truly as if he had malignant sores as he had claimed. If it were anyone else, they would have believed it, but Xu Fu's medical skills were becoming increasingly excellent; how could he not see that the person in front of him was faking it?

"Tell me exactly what is going on, General Li," Xu Fu said coldly.

Jing Ke smiled again, raised his hand to wipe away the black stuff on his face, and finally revealed the familiar face underneath... it was Li Xin!

Li Xin had been missing since the capture of Huan Yi, and Xu Fu never expected that he would appear in front of him in such a way, staging a historical scene. Xu Fu even felt that when he pulled the dagger from the map, for a moment, the fierce light in his eyes didn't look fake. However, it was useless to dwell on that now. Xu Fu was just curious: why did Jing Ke become Li Xin? Did the person Jing Ke not exist at all?

Seeing Xu Fu's cold expression and the gaze like a knife, Li Xin hurriedly smiled and said, "I captured Huan Yi, and as for that Jing Ke, I captured him too."

Xu Fu's expression softened slightly, "Did you intentionally swap Jing Ke?"

Li Xin nodded, "Huan Yi fled to the State of Yan, and I pursued him closely. I heard that Prince Dan was spending his family fortune to recruit brave men to accompany the envoys to assassinate the King. Later, someone recommended Jing Ke to Prince Dan, so he visited Jing Ke's residence. Jing Ke's martial arts were extremely high, so I used a scheme to replace him, letting Prince Dan believe I was Jing Ke. Later, I successfully returned to Qin with them."

"And what about Jing Ke?"

"He should be in the King's hands by now."

Xu Fu's expression was strange.

In other words, Ying Zheng had sensed it early on? No wonder when Zhao Gao reported to him that he hadn't found anything wrong, he remained as steady as a mountain! Xu Fu secretly gritted his teeth; it was only after he saw Li Xin and felt that his physique was different that he vaguely guessed his identity. After all, a person's physique might be substituted due to similarity, but a person's destiny and fortune could never be swapped. In Xu Fu's eyes, whether Li Xin was disguised or not made no difference.

It wasn't just this that was different from history; even the head of Fan Yuqi from history was gone!

Because Crown Prince Dan died? So he couldn't get Fan Yuqi's head?

Xu Fu was puzzled, but then he heard Li Xin say, "They wanted Huan Yi's head as a stepping stone to see the King. Huan Yi naturally refused, and he took the initiative to find me. That was how Prince Dan's plan was ruined." Li Xin never had the habit of taking credit for others' work; since Huan Yi had made a contribution, he would tell it exactly as it was.

Xu Fu suddenly realized.

Huan Yi was Fan Yuqi.

This deviation from history... was really not small at all.

After finishing speaking, an attendant walked to the outside of the palace and bowed to Xu Fu, "Shu-Zhang, this servant has been ordered by the King to bring some clothes."

"Come in."

What the attendant was holding were the robes Li Xin usually wore. Li Xin turned to wash his face and changed into the robes, completely shedding the shadow of Jing Ke. Li Xin returned to his cold, iron-faced demeanor, making it hard for anyone to associate him with the previous Jing Ke.

Xu Fu led Li Xin out. The attendants on both sides looked at Li Xin in surprise, but in the end, they all wisely kept their mouths shut.

Xu Fu returned to the hall as if nothing had happened, then watched as Ying Zheng scolded the State of Yan severely. The ministers were so shocked they couldn't say a word. After Ying Zheng had said enough, the two of them left the hall together.

The ministers breathed a sigh of relief and were about to discuss it with their colleagues when they suddenly noticed—huh? When did Li Xin appear? Wasn't he missing after pursuing Huan Yi?

The ministers were confused for a long time.

But Wei Liao, who had seen through the trick, kept his mouth shut and left alone, waving his sleeves.

After Xu Fu and Ying Zheng left the hall, they heard Ying Zheng laugh, "I feel it wasn't worth holding a banquet for the State of Yan!" Ying Zheng's tone carried contempt and two parts arrogance.

He had already solidified his determination to take the State of Yan.

Xu Fu habitually wanted to answer him, but he got stuck halfway through his sentence.

Without Xu Fu's response, Ying Zheng's joy couldn't last long. He restrained the expression on his face and said in a low voice, "Does A-Fu think I deliberately deceived you?"

Xu Fu didn't even shift his gaze.

"I did not deceive you," Ying Zheng said in a deep voice, "I didn't know the assassin brought by the State of Yan would be Li Xin either. It wasn't until I was in the hall that I realized something was wrong, so I ordered a search of the post house, and thus I found the real Jing Ke and Huan Yi in the post house."

Xu Fu's cold gaze softened a little, "Is that really so?"

"It is indeed so."

Ying Zheng answered firmly, and Xu Fu stopped asking. If Ying Zheng ever learned to lie, he would find it strange. Originally, he just had a bit of pent-up anger, but now that he had been smoothed over, there was naturally nothing wrong. Compared to questioning Ying Zheng, Xu Fu's attention was now on Jing Ke and Huan Yi. One was a famous assassin of the Warring States period, often called a hero by later generations, and the other was a traitorous Qin general who appeared in language textbooks. Xu Fu was really curious about what happened to Huan Yi that made him become the "traitorous Qin general Fan Yuqi" known to later generations.

"Where is Jing Ke now?"

"In the palace." Without waiting for Xu Fu to continue, Ying Zheng already understood his meaning, "I will take you to see him." Ying Zheng's tone was very flat; it seemed that from the beginning, he had never taken the State of Yan's methods seriously. Even Jing Ke was not in his eyes.

Although Ying Zheng didn't understand why Xu Fu was always interested in strangers, since it was Xu Fu's wish, he would try his best to fulfill it. It was just seeing a person; it was no big deal.

The two turned a corner and walked toward the other side.

The palace servants behind them were a bit dazed. Eh? Was the coldness on the Shu-Zhang just now an illusion? How did the tense atmosphere disappear all of a sudden?

Jing Ke was locked in a desolate little courtyard; the former Prince of Han had also been locked here.

Just as Xu Fu stepped in, Ying Zheng pulled him, and Xu Fu, unprepared, fell directly into Ying Zheng's arms. Ying Zheng whispered in his ear, "No one has lived here for a long time, and weeds have grown on the roadside. Be careful when you walk."

Xu Fu nodded and slowed his pace.

The palace servants behind immediately looked up at the sky.

After entering the small courtyard, Xu Fu heard a familiar male voice ask, "When will I be able to see the King?"

Xu Fu walked forward, signaled the guards to open the door, and said, "General Huan Yi, long time no see."

Huan Yi stiffened, looked up abruptly, and met Xu Fu's gaze. He couldn't help but feel ashamed, his tone dropping suddenly, "...Shu-Zhang."

After all, having saved his life before, Xu Fu was not surprised by Huan Yi's reaction. His gaze went straight past Huan Yi and looked directly at another person.

The man was sitting on the ground with his back to them. Even when he heard the sound, he didn't move, only asking coldly, "Where is Li Xin?"
chapters.title: 第222章
chapters.source_text:
翌日，嬴政如常上了朝，燕国使臣一行人等得上了火，也未能等到秦王的召见。直至宫中举宴，赵高才领着人上门去唤燕国使臣了。燕国使臣多有不忿，但也只能强行压下。
四周都是秦国士兵，手中执有兵器，身穿铁甲，一身都泛着凌厉寒光，直教人战栗不已。
燕国使臣就算心中再为不忿，也什么都说不出来。
很快，他们入了宫。越往里走，他们便见着了越来越多的秦国士兵，这些士兵皆是铁甲在身，面如寒铁，气势威武。使团中有一人忍不住两股战战，面上流露出了惧色。
赵高回头来，斥责那人：“怎么这般无状？”
名为荆轲的男子，也回头冷冷地看了一眼那人，“跟紧了。”
那人吐出一口气，匆忙点头，跟着荆轲往里走去。
徐福和嬴政已经坐在座位上了，秦国大臣虽对徐福的特殊有所不满，但是将他换到王后的位置上一想，倒也能自我安慰了呢，如此一想，他反正又当不了秦国王后，这样还是委屈了他呢。单纯的大臣们陷入了这样的一根筋淳朴思维中。
反倒是燕国使臣一行人进到殿中后，见了徐福和嬴政，顿觉怪异不已，心下暗道，难怪燕王封他做国师也不干，原来在秦国，虽为驷车庶长，而实际上却是和秦王同坐的，地位比起其他大臣竟是高出一截来！其他大臣难道就不会因此心生不满吗？这些燕国人始终都想不明白。
他们没能继续往前走去。
又有守卫上前来，搜寻他们身上的兵器。燕国人的脸上顿时闪过了被羞辱的恼色。
徐福坐得高，看得也更远，视线足以囊括眼前的一切。他扯了扯嬴政的衣袖，低声道：“你看他们中有一人，两股战战，神色慌张，定有蹊跷。”
恰好此时守卫搜寻完了，他们身上都无兵器利器。
嬴政沉声道：“何人献图？”
男子踏出来，高声道：“荆轲，秦舞阳，二人来献图！”说罢，他身边有些慌乱的青年也跟着走了出来，勉强稳住了虚晃的目光。
徐福记得荆轲刺秦一段里，是有一人差点坏了荆轲的事，难道便是那青年？徐福收起目光，看向荆轲，冷冷道：“你为何以巾遮面？”不知为何，徐福总觉得有什么地方被自己忽略了，这事儿透着点怪异。
“至秦时，水土不服，面生恶疮，不敢以此面目见秦王。”荆轲沉声道。
徐福脑子里飞快地闪过了点儿灵感，他忍不住眯眼细细打量荆轲，终于发觉到了不对劲的地方。徐福心中又是震惊又是说不出的想笑，他转头去看一旁的秦舞阳，秦舞阳在他目光的梭巡下，面色又青又白，怂得都快软腿了。
没那个胆子，还想来刺杀秦王？
徐福心中轻嗤了一声。
两边侍从高声喝道：“这位使者为何变了脸色？”
荆轲竟是笑了，语气轻松地带过道：“他一介粗野乡下人，未曾见过秦王这般英武的人，为王上气势所慑，自然慌乱了些，还请王上原谅他的失仪。”
“是吗？”嬴政的口气也很是玩味，显然未曾将荆轲的话放在心上。嬴政一挥手，让人将那秦舞阳带下去，秦舞阳已然被吓傻了眼，被秦兵拉下去的时候，连挣扎也不敢。
“将你手中的地图献上前来吧。”嬴政低声道。
荆轲身后跟着一干燕人，只能羞愤地被阻挡在台阶之下。
荆轲缓步上了台阶，手中的图缓缓展开。
徐福不自觉地屏住了呼吸，他就看看这人要玩儿什么花样。
正如课文中曾写到的那样——图穷匕首见！
地图翻转过来落在地上，淬了毒的匕首却被荆轲紧握在手中，朝着嬴政刺来。众人登时大乱，其余燕人慌乱不已，连连后退，守卫涌上来，将他们全数拿下。
此时殿上，徐福脸色微变，正要拔剑，嬴政却一手摁住了他，反倒轻松抽出随身佩剑，将荆轲刺伤，荆轲怒极，眼眸中闪过厉色，他抬手掷出匕首，一击不中，他却就此失去了最后的武器。
一切结束得太快，大臣们都有点懵，被拿住的燕人们也有些懵。
徐福松了一口气。
也不知这回他还能听见，荆轲一击不中后的倚柱笑骂吗？
徐福皱眉看向荆轲，见他退至柱子旁，笑道：“事所以不成者，乃欲以生劫之。”
跟语文课本上何其相似的话，徐福的眉头皱得越来越紧，嬴政见状，这才站立起来，看也不看他，道：“拿下。”
侍从上前来，抓住荆轲往外退去，徐福却直接下了台阶，跟着他们出了大殿。
满朝大臣还没能回过神来，半晌才讷讷道：“……王上？”
嬴政面色一冷，摔了桌案，“燕国可恶！寡人定要活捉燕王喜！”
大臣们忙跪地俯身，不敢劝。
而这头徐福跟着侍从走到殿外，眼见侍从们要将他拖下去，徐福忙出声阻断了他们的动作，“将人带过来。”
侍从们对视一眼，不知该从还是不从。但此时徐福已然先行转身离去了，侍从们只得咬咬牙，押着荆轲跟上去。徐福招手叫来一名内侍，“寻个安静的地方。”
内侍不明所以，但还是遵从了徐福的意思，就近找了处宫殿。
徐福在王宫中向来是畅通无阻的，殿外的守卫不仅没拦他，还弯腰躬身，放了他进去。
侍从们将荆轲推了进去，见荆轲还直立不跪，一旁的侍从面色不虞，正待拔剑逼之，徐福却直接打断了他，“你们在外等候。”
“庶长！”侍从瞪大眼，并不依从，生怕荆轲再对徐福出手。
徐福摇头，态度坚决，“退出去。他身上再无利器，如何能伤我？”
侍从们只得咬着牙退了出去。
荆轲轻笑一声，抬手扯去面巾，露出下面的脸庞。他的脸上不知覆有何物，看上去黑乎乎的，极为恶心，倒真像是如他所说那样生有恶疮般。若是旁人也就这样以为了，但是徐福的岐黄之术越加出色，又怎会瞧不出面前的人是装的？
“究竟如何一回事，劳烦李将军细细与我说一说。”徐福冷声道。
荆轲又是一笑，抬手抹去面上黑乎乎的玩意儿，方才露出了下面那张熟悉的面孔……正是李信！
李信在捉捕桓齮时失踪至今，徐福却怎么也没想到，他会以这样的方式，在自己的面前出现，并且上演了一幕历史桥段。徐福甚至觉得，当时他从地图中抽出匕首时，有一瞬间，眼底的凶光不似作伪。不过如今再去纠结那些也没用了，徐福只好奇，为什么荆轲变成了李信，难道荆轲其人本就是不存在的吗？
李信见徐福面色冰冷，投过来的目光更如刀般凌厉，李信忙笑了笑，道：“桓齮被我拿住了，那荆轲么，也被我拿住了。”
徐福神色微微松缓，“是你故意调换了荆轲？”
李信点头，“桓齮逃至燕国，我紧追而去，听闻公子成变卖身家重金求勇夫，随使臣前来刺杀王上。后来有人向公子成举荐了荆轲，他便拜访到了荆轲的府上。荆轲功夫极高，我便使计换下了他，让公子成以为我为荆轲，后来便顺利地与他们回到了秦国。”
“那荆轲呢？”
“此时应当在王上手中了。”
徐福神色怪异。
也就是说，嬴政早先便有所察觉了？难怪赵高回来禀报他，没有发现什么不对劲，他也依旧稳坐如山！徐福暗暗磨牙，反倒自己直到见了李信后，觉得身形有异，方才隐约猜出了他的身份。毕竟一个人的身形或许可以因相似互相顶替，但是一个人的命格气运，是无论如何也无法交换的。在徐福眼中，李信做不做伪装，倒也没得差了。
只是不仅这点儿与历史不同了，就连历史上的樊於期的头，竟然也没了！
因为太子丹死了？所以就没能拿到樊於期的头？
徐福心头正疑惑，却听李信又道：“他们想要桓齮的人头，以作求见王上的敲门砖。桓齮自然不愿，他主动找到了我。这才让公子成的计划破灭了。”李信向来没有贪人功劳的癖好，既然桓齮立了功，他便会原原本本地说出来。
徐福恍然大悟。
桓齮，樊於期也。
这和历史的出入……还真不是一般的大啊。
话说完，一内侍走到殿外，朝着徐福躬身道：“庶长，奴婢领了王上的命来送衣裳。”
“进来吧。”
内侍手中捧着的正是李信往日惯穿的衣袍，李信转身洗了脸，换上衣袍，他便全然从荆轲的影子中脱离出来了。李信恢复到铁面冷然的模样，很难再让人将他同之前的荆轲联系起来。
徐福带着李信走出去，两边的侍从惊讶地打量了李信一眼，最后又都聪明地紧紧闭上了嘴。
徐福若无其事地回到了殿中，然后看着嬴政对燕国大加斥责一通，大臣们被惊得一句话也说不出来，待嬴政说够了之后，两人便一同离开了大殿。
大臣们松了一口气，正要与同僚议论，却骤然发现——嗯？李信什么时候出现的？他不是追捕桓齮失踪了吗？
大臣们半晌都摸不着头脑。
而看出门道来的尉缭，却是闭紧了嘴，又孤零零一人挥袖离开。
这头徐福和嬴政出了大殿后，便听见嬴政笑道：“为燕国举宴寡人都觉不值！”嬴政的口气中带着轻蔑，还有两分狂妄。
他已然坚定了要拿下燕国的决心。
徐福原本习惯性地想要回答他，但是话说到一半就卡住了。
没有徐福接话，嬴政那点儿喜色也就维持不了多久了，他收敛起脸上的表情，低声道：“阿福可是以为寡人故意蒙骗了你？”
徐福连目光都没挪过去一下。
“寡人并未蒙骗你。”嬴政沉声道：“先前寡人也不知燕国带来的刺客会是李信，还是等到上殿之后，寡人这才发觉不对，便令人去搜寻驿馆，遂从驿馆中搜得了真正的荆轲，还有桓齮。”
徐福冰冷的目光这才缓和了些，“当真如此？”
“确实如此。”
嬴政答得坚定，徐福便也不再追问了。嬴政要是哪一天真学会撒谎了，他才会觉得奇怪。本来他也只是心中一股郁气，现在被顺毛捋了，自然也就没什么事儿了。相比质问嬴政，徐福现在的注意力都放在了荆轲和桓齮的身上。一个是战国时期的著名刺客，后人常以英雄称他，而另一个是语文课本上出镜的秦国叛将。徐福实在好奇，桓齮身上到底发生了什么，才会成为后世称的秦叛将樊於期。
“荆轲现在何处？”
“宫中。”不消徐福再说下去，嬴政便已经明了他的意思，“寡人带你去瞧他。”嬴政口吻极为平淡，想来从一开始，他便未曾将燕国的手段放在眼中。甚至包括荆轲，都不被他看在眼中。
嬴政虽然不解徐福为何总能对一些陌生人抱有兴致，但既是徐福的意愿，他尽力达成便是。瞧个人而已，也没甚大不了。
两人拐了个弯儿，朝着另一边走了过去。
身后一干宫人有点懵，诶？刚才庶长身上的冷意是错觉吗？原本紧张的气氛怎么一下子便没了？
荆轲被关在了一处荒凉的小院中，曾经那位韩国公子便是被关在这边的。
徐福刚踏足的时候，嬴政便拉了他一把，徐福毫无准备，直接就跌进了嬴政的怀中，嬴政在他耳旁低声道：“此处久不住人，路边杂草都生了不少，你走路的时候小心些。”
徐福点点头，放缓了脚步。
后面的宫人立即抬头看天。
待走进小院子后，徐福便听见有一道熟悉的男声，问道：“何时才能见到王上？”
徐福走上前，示意守卫将门打开，一边道：“桓齮将军，许久不见了。”
桓齮僵了僵，猛地抬起头来，正对上徐福的目光，却忍不住满面愧色，语调都霎地低了下去，“……庶长。”
毕竟从前救过他的性命，桓齮会有这样的表现，徐福并不意外，他的目光直接越过了桓齮，直直地看向了另一个人。
男子背对着他们坐在地上，哪怕听见声音，也没有动弹，只是冷声问道：“李信何在？”

徐福淡淡应道：“李信不在此处。”
荆轲嗤笑了一声，不再说话。
嬴政瞥了一眼荆轲的背影。高大，不羁。但还是不及自己。自己更高大英武！就荆轲这样的，还是不能吸引住徐福多少视线的。嬴政放下了心。
“李信不在此，但寡人在此。”嬴政的口吻和徐福如出一辙的平淡。
荆轲浑身一颤，几乎是迫不及待地起身，转身，看向门口的嬴政。他目光锐利如刀，只可惜目光又不能杀人，所以哪怕他气势再盛，也拿嬴政无法。
嬴政依旧拥着徐福，二人姿势半点都没变换。他们浑身上下都透着一股气息，“我没将你荆轲放在眼中。”
荆轲自然是感觉到了这一点。他心中并不以为然，若是国君都气势低弱，那才奇怪。只可惜……只可惜他错过了刺杀秦王的机会，若非桓齮、李信二人，他同公子成的计划，也不会就此被破坏。
“我未能杀你，并非我无能，也并非你秦国得天助。只不过是李信耍了诡计而已。”荆轲盯着嬴政冷声道。
徐福凉凉地插嘴道：“别人使了诡计，你便输了，那不是你无能是什么？”
荆轲被噎了一下，扭头不言。显然并未将徐福看在眼中。
哦，估计在他们眼中，徐福这样的，就是助纣为虐的人物，自然不被他们这样的英雄瞧得上了。
徐福将他又仔细地打量了一番。生得好模样，气质也极是出众，偏就是这样的人物，却非要做刺杀的勾当！什么英雄？不过为了一己私欲，哪里当得上是英雄？历史上的太子丹蠢，这次派出荆轲来的公子成也蠢。徐福才觉得自己瞧不上他们呢。
徐福倒是想起了一句话。
卿本佳人，奈何从贼。
“我倒是想见识一番荆轲的功夫，可惜以后没机会了。”
荆轲闻言，反而笑了起来，“是可惜了，原本今日你们就该瞧着秦王死于我手下的。”
“既已失败，现在又何必来放狠话呢？”因着瞧荆轲不顺眼，徐福更甚至觉得历史上，荆轲失败时笑骂的话，也不过是见事不成，便逞口舌之快而已。
“纵死，也是痛快死，我有何不能说？”
“不过愚蠢之行，你倒是觉得光荣了起来。”徐福冷笑起来，看向荆轲的目光更为锐利。
嬴政瞧着徐福难得失态与人吵起来的模样，心底渐渐蔓开了笑意……若非为他，徐福又怎么会与荆轲争执这样的问题？换做其他时候，徐福定是连搭理都懒得与他搭理的。
“既是不懂，便勿要妄言！”荆轲厉声斥道。
“我确是不懂，你明为卫国人，如今替着燕国公子杀人，又来的哪门子的爱国情怀？若是如韩非那样的，我还能敬佩几分，但如你这样的，可不是蠢吗？你倒是不怕，出手杀人不成，全族跟着遭殃。”
荆轲气极，不由得打断了他，“秦王残暴，人人都欲取他性命，跟我是哪国人无关。”
“分明是公子成变卖了身家换成钱财给你，你拿人手短，这才不得不来刺杀秦王。什么残暴？残暴到你头上去了吗？”
荆轲更气，“他攻打赵、燕，让百姓陷入战火之中，难道不是残暴吗？”
“明是为一己私欲，何必来寻借口？若以此定残暴，那谁人不残暴？昔日赵、魏为霸主时，他们手中的城池难道不是通过打仗得来的吗？你怎么不去杀了赵王，不去杀了魏王？燕王倒是想要攻秦，只可惜他没这个本事罢了！昔日打得赢秦国时，便嘲讽秦国国弱，如今他们打不赢秦国了，便又道秦王残暴，世上哪有这样的道理？话倒是都被你们说尽了！”徐福嗤笑一声，气势强盛，直直压下了荆轲，“那公子成但凡有点血性，便应当操练兵马，联合他国，先强燕国，方能抵御我大秦！偏他不如此，只一心寻勇士来刺杀我秦王上。不过是个懦夫罢了！”
徐福脑中甚至隐约还能记起，昔日曾见《史记》记载，“太子日造门下，供太牢具，异物间进，车骑美女恣荆轲所欲，以顺适其意。”
大意就是太子丹每天前去问候荆轲。供给他丰盛的宴席，备办奇珍异宝，还不时进献车马和美女任荆轲随心所欲，以便满足他的心意。
徐福越想越觉得荆轲不要脸。
明明是你享用了好处，方才觉得过意不去，遂来刺杀秦王，何必装作义愤填膺的模样？真以为，死了嬴政，天下便是太平的天下，百姓便可衣食无忧，生活富足了吗？
国君若如赵、魏两王，百姓哪里能过好日子？而嬴政手下却是有能之士极多，有他们襄助，自然能为百姓带来更好的盛世。
几国王室仓皇不已，不过是害怕失去尊贵的地位和权势罢了。何必寻些冠冕堂皇的借口，非要将嬴政说成必须处死的一大恶人。
“你……”荆轲被噎得说不出话来。
“不过是燕国王室贪生怕死，这才寻了你这么一个人，前来刺杀。若是你成了，他们便自然能安稳地继续过王室生活，而你的命自然是留在秦国了。若你不成，反正死的还是你，他们一时又死不了。偏你还一心觉得自己所为乃是义举。不过愚蠢作为罢了！”徐福说得赤裸裸。不管公子成有没有这样龌蹉的心思，反正在他看来，便是如此！
荆轲张嘴正要反驳，却再次被徐福截断了。
“何为英雄？至少，这不是英雄！”徐福冰寒锐利的目光逼视着他。
荆轲一时间什么话都忘记了，掏空了肚皮，他也应不上徐福的话来，最后只能勉强挤出二字，“……歪理。”
“打不赢，便说我们残暴。如今你说不过我，便说我的是歪理。”徐福凉凉道，“这般可笑逻辑，我倒是头一次见着。”
“你……”
徐福又笑道，笑容比荆轲还要肆意上几分，“不如我让王上也赐你高门府邸，再赠以珠宝黄金，再赐你车马美女。你也替王上去杀那公子成如何？”
徐福这话说得实在太过辛辣尖锐了些，荆轲色变，怒发冲冠，一跃而起。
桓齮色变，当即阻拦在荆轲之前，嬴政也快手将徐福拉了过去，“寡人少见你有如此嘴利的时候。”还少见你笑的时候。如此一笑，竟是对着荆轲……寡人心痛。
“谁让他胆敢刺杀你呢？”徐福脸上笑容已然不见，嘴上只如此淡淡道。但嬴政心中反倒觉得欢喜了起来。
荆轲急急地喘了几口气，怒道：“不过佞宠也，我不与你辩！”
嬴政的脸色瞬间便阴沉了下来。徐福抬手握住了他的手腕，将他往后推了推，傲然道：“我乃秦国驷车庶长，而你在之前，却是喜爱与一干酒徒在街头饮酒撒疯，倒不知你何来的底气嘲讽我？不与我辩，不过是辩不过我的托词罢了。”
其实史记中写他，荆轲虽游于酒人乎，然其为人沈深好书。不过这个时候总要拿话来刺他的。
嬴政道：“杀了便是，何须再与他费口舌。”
徐福抬手拦了一把，“听闻荆轲剑术极高，且留着他吧，改日龙阳君或许有兴与他切磋。”
荆轲初闻之，倍觉羞辱，但是突然间反应过来，“龙阳君还活着？”
“自然活着。”
“魏国之臣，却降了秦？”荆轲皱眉。
“魏王多可恶，龙阳君为何不能降秦？”
荆轲也算是明白了，今日他是说不过徐福的，于是干脆闭了嘴。闭嘴后，他不知又想起了什么，突然道：“……李信何在？”哦，又回到了最初的问题上。
他对李信的执念倒是大，约莫是在李信手中栽得狠了，心中不服气吧。
“他乃秦将，你乃刺客，他自然不会见你。”
“他做出这等事来，确实不敢见我。”荆轲冷笑一声，遂不再言语。
徐福的脸色却变得有些怪异，这等事？哪等事？改日还得好生问一问李信才是。见荆轲一身傲骨仍在，不像是脆皮到能被他气死的模样。徐福顿时安心了，转头对桓齮道：“此处不便说话，桓齮将军，请吧。”徐福可不希望让外人看了秦国的笑话。
全程都是徐福在说话，嬴政一直未曾插嘴，哪怕此时听见徐福仍称桓齮为将军，他也什么话都未说。
桓齮低下头，拢了拢袖子，跟着徐福出去了。
屋子里很快便只剩下了守卫和荆轲，荆轲顿觉胸口堵得慌，一撩衣袍，又坐了回去。
守卫嘴角一抽，……地脏，且凉啊，何必非要装得跟坐牢一样呢？
·
桓齮有些不安，他走在徐福的身后，徐福甚至觉得自己能听见他喘息的声音，那是紧张才会发出的声音。瞧桓齮这般模样，徐福便觉不解。他究竟为何才会叛逃？
将人引进殿中后，嬴政慢慢走到了桌案前坐下，居高临下地审视着桓齮。桓齮被人带进宫后，便一直是这个打扮，穿着平民着的衣袍，衣角多有磨损脏处。可见他的逃亡生活并不如意。
“说吧，为何杀人？”
桓齮咬了咬牙，面上闪过屈辱之色，“自去岁战败，致丢了粮草，秦兵死伤无数后，我便领命在家中休息。”
徐福耐心等待他继续说下去。
“被杀之人家中与我家中乃是姻亲……”
徐福正想着，难道是那家人瞧着桓齮没本事了，便不将女儿嫁给他了，谁晓得听下去才知，哪里是那家人不肯嫁女儿，而是桓齮独女嫁到大夫家中。桓齮兵败，那家人怕遭牵连，便将人赶出来了，转头还有人送了几名姬妾上来。桓齮的女儿回去后没多久便死了。桓齮疑心她受了虐待，便上门寻个道理。桓齮欲将此事闹到嬴政的跟前来，但那大夫家中却是极不要脸，与桓齮当场起了冲突，桓齮本是个武夫，冲动之下便宰了人，人一宰，又不甘心为其陪葬，便匆匆逃离了咸阳。
那大夫家中为何如此惊慌，忙不迭撇清关系？
都是因秦律极严，像桓齮这样败得惨的，全家因此遭难都是有可能的。嬴政虽一时免了他的死罪，但谁知道嬴政会不会之后与他算账呢？当然谁都不想沾上桓齮了。
相比之下，徐福更觉得惊奇的是……桓齮竟然年纪大到已经有女儿了！
嬴政听罢，冷声道：“你不能再为将了。”
桓齮跪地苦笑不语。
那大夫家中被屠的不止那大夫一人，还有其子，以及儿子的姬妾。那家人确实做事不地道，有此劫都是一个因果报应。但是桓齮杀人，不仅是复了仇，他还挑战了秦王的颜面。在咸阳城中，你一个战败之将，便能随意杀人，杀人后又逃窜到别国去。嬴政总不能因他有冤，便放过了他。若都是如此，那还了得？
嬴政迅速便定下了他的结局。
秋季过后，便会施以死刑。这已经算是轻饶他了。从他杀了人，逃出咸阳那一刻开始，严酷的刑法便加在他的身上了。
徐福觉得有些可惜，但最终还是什么都没说。桓齮这件事儿的确做错了，而他也再没了翻盘的机会。只是……只是荆轲一事……徐福想一想都觉得好笑。历史上，桓齮，也就是樊於期，可是自杀了，愿以自己的头颅为敲门砖，让荆轲见到秦王。不过那时，秦王屠尽了他的家人。而这世，嬴政并未直接斩杀他的家人，而是派出李信去捉。于是桓齮反倒不肯将头给荆轲了……
这算是有功吗？
好像也说不上。
看来桓齮也必须得为自己做过的事付出代价了。徐福面上再度闪过了可惜之色。曾经到军营中，他为桓齮解毒时，还是挺瞧得上此人的。现在落到这一步，再忆起往日缘分，饶是徐福，都不由觉得世事变迁，实在太快！令人措手不及。
想到这里，徐福突然觉得脑袋有点疼，他眉头紧紧锁了起来，眼前甚至阵阵发晕。
嬴政脸色微变，抬手扶住了他，“怎了？”那跪在下面的桓齮，已然不被他放在心上了。
但晕眩也是一瞬间的功夫，待徐福清醒过来，他便立即摇了摇头，“……无事了。”
徐福隐隐觉得，他的反常，似乎与师兄尉缭口中的常年失忆有关。

Xu Fu replied indifferently, "Li Xin is not here."

Jing Ke sneered and said nothing more.

Ying Zheng glanced at Jing Ke’s back. Tall and unbridled. But still not as good as himself. He was taller and more heroic! Someone like Jing Ke couldn't possibly capture much of Xu Fu's attention. Ying Zheng felt relieved.

"Li Xin is not here, but I am." Ying Zheng’s tone was as flat as Xu Fu’s.

Jing Ke shuddered, rising almost impatiently to turn and face Ying Zheng at the door. His gaze was as sharp as a blade, but unfortunately, looks couldn't kill, so no matter how imposing his aura was, he could do nothing to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng continued to hold Xu Fu, the pair not changing their posture in the slightest. Their entire demeanor exuded a single message: "I do not hold you, Jing Ke, in any regard."

Jing Ke naturally sensed this. He didn't think much of it; it would be strange if a monarch lacked such an imposing air. It was just a pity... a pity he had missed the chance to assassinate the King of Qin. If not for Huan Yi and Li Xin, his plan with Prince Cheng would not have been ruined.

"My failure to kill you is not due to my incompetence, nor is it because your Qin state is blessed by heaven. It is merely because Li Xin played a trick," Jing Ke said coldly, staring at Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu interjected coolly, "If you lost because someone else played a trick, what is that if not your own incompetence?"

Jing Ke was choked by the retort and turned his head away, remaining silent. Clearly, he did not hold Xu Fu in any regard.

Oh, he probably viewed someone like Xu Fu as an accomplice to a tyrant, and naturally, heroes like them would look down on such a person.

Xu Fu examined him carefully once more. He had a fine appearance and an outstanding temperament, yet a man like this chose to engage in assassination! What kind of hero was this? It was nothing more than for his own selfish desires; how could he be called a hero? Prince Dan in history was foolish, and this time, Prince Cheng who sent Jing Ke was also foolish. Xu Fu felt he was the one who looked down on them.

Xu Fu recalled a line.

"You were a beauty, why did you turn to banditry?"

"I actually wanted to witness Jing Ke's martial arts, but unfortunately, there won't be a chance in the future."

Upon hearing this, Jing Ke laughed instead, "It is a pity. Today, you should have been watching the King of Qin die by my hand."

"Since you have already failed, why bother spouting harsh words now?" Because he found Jing Ke unpleasant, Xu Fu even felt that the mocking words Jing Ke uttered in history upon his failure were merely a way to vent his frustration after failing to achieve his goal.

"Even if I die, I will die with satisfaction. Why shouldn't I speak?"

"It was nothing but a foolish act, yet you feel proud of it," Xu Fu sneered, his gaze toward Jing Ke becoming even sharper.

Ying Zheng watched as Xu Fu rarely lost his composure to argue with someone, and a smile gradually spread in his heart... If it weren't for him, why would Xu Fu bother arguing with Jing Ke over such matters? At any other time, Xu Fu would be too lazy to even acknowledge him.

"If you don't understand, then do not speak nonsense!" Jing Ke scolded sharply.

"I certainly don't understand. You are clearly a man of the Wei state, yet now you are killing people for a prince of the Yan state—where does this 'patriotism' come from? If you were like Han Fei, I might respect you a little, but like you? Isn't that just foolish? You don't even fear that if your assassination fails, your entire clan will suffer the consequences."

Jing Ke was furious and could not help but interrupt him, "The King of Qin is cruel, and everyone wants his life. It has nothing to do with which state I am from."

"It is clear that Prince Cheng sold his family assets to give you money. You took his money and felt obligated, so you had to come to assassinate the King of Qin. What cruelty? Has his cruelty reached you personally?"

Jing Ke was even angrier, "He attacked Zhao and Yan, plunging the people into the fires of war. Is that not cruel?"

"It is clearly for your own selfish desires, why look for excuses? If you define cruelty by this, then who is not cruel? When Zhao and Wei were the hegemons in the past, were the cities in their hands not acquired through war? Why didn't you go kill the King of Zhao or the King of Wei? The King of Yan wanted to attack Qin, but he simply lacked the ability! When they could defeat Qin in the past, they mocked Qin for being weak; now that they cannot defeat Qin, they call the King of Qin cruel. Where in the world is there such logic? You have said all there is to say!" Xu Fu sneered, his imposing aura directly suppressing Jing Ke. "If that Prince Cheng had any backbone, he should have trained his troops and allied with other states to strengthen Yan first, only then could he resist our Great Qin! Instead, he did not do so, focusing only on finding warriors to assassinate our King of Qin. He is nothing but a coward!"

Xu Fu could even vaguely recall the records in the *Records of the Grand Historian*: "The Crown Prince visited him daily, providing him with grand feasts and exotic treasures, and from time to time presented him with carriages, horses, and beautiful women to satisfy his every whim."

The gist was that Crown Prince Dan visited Jing Ke every day, providing him with lavish banquets, rare treasures, and occasionally offering carriages and beauties to satisfy his desires.

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more he felt Jing Ke was shameless.

You enjoyed the benefits, and only then felt obligated to come and assassinate the King of Qin—why pretend to be filled with righteous indignation? Do you really think that if Ying Zheng died, the world would be peaceful, the people would be free from worry, and their lives would be prosperous?

If the monarchs were like the Kings of Zhao and Wei, how could the people live well? But under Ying Zheng, there are many capable people, and with their assistance, they can naturally bring about a better golden age for the people.

The royal families of those states are panicked only because they fear losing their noble status and power. Why look for such high-sounding excuses, insisting on painting Ying Zheng as a great villain who must be executed?

"You..." Jing Ke was choked into silence.

"It is just that the Yan royal family is cowardly and fears death, which is why they found someone like you to come and assassinate him. If you succeed, they can naturally continue their royal life in peace, and your life will naturally be left in Qin. If you fail, you die anyway, and they won't die for a while. Yet you still think your actions are a righteous deed. It is nothing but a foolish act!" Xu Fu spoke bluntly. Regardless of whether Prince Cheng had such sordid thoughts, in his eyes, that was exactly how it was!

Jing Ke opened his mouth to retort, but was cut off by Xu Fu again.

"What is a hero? At the very least, this is not a hero!" Xu Fu’s cold, sharp gaze bore into him.

Jing Ke forgot everything he wanted to say. He racked his brains but could not respond to Xu Fu, and in the end, he could only squeeze out two words: "...Sophistry."

"When you can't win, you call us cruel. Now that you can't out-argue me, you call my words sophistry," Xu Fu said coolly. "This is the first time I've seen such ridiculous logic."

"You..."

Xu Fu smiled again, his smile even more unbridled than Jing Ke's, "Why don't I ask the King to grant you a grand mansion, gift you gold and jewels, and bestow upon you carriages and beauties? How about you go kill that Prince Cheng for the King instead?"

Xu Fu's words were truly too sharp and biting. Jing Ke’s expression changed, his hair standing on end with rage as he leaped up.

Huan Yi’s expression changed, and he immediately blocked Jing Ke. Ying Zheng also quickly pulled Xu Fu away, "I rarely see you being so sharp-tongued." And rarely see you smile like that. To smile like that, and at Jing Ke... my heart aches.

"Who told him to dare to assassinate you?" The smile on Xu Fu's face had already vanished, and he spoke only these words faintly. But Ying Zheng felt happy in his heart.

Jing Ke panted heavily, shouting angrily, "You are nothing but a sycophant, I will not argue with you!"

Ying Zheng’s expression instantly turned gloomy. Xu Fu raised his hand to hold his wrist, pushing him back slightly, and said proudly, "I am a Siche Shuzhang of Qin, while you, before this, loved to drink and act wildly on the streets with a bunch of drunkards. I don't know where you get the confidence to mock me? Not wanting to argue with me is just an excuse because you cannot win."

In fact, the *Records of the Grand Historian* wrote that although Jing Ke wandered among drunkards, he was deep and fond of books. But at this moment, he had to use words to prick him.

Ying Zheng said, "Just kill him, why waste more breath."

Xu Fu raised a hand to stop him, "I heard Jing Ke’s swordsmanship is extremely high. Keep him for now; perhaps Lord Longyang might be interested in sparring with him another day."

When Jing Ke first heard this, he felt deeply humiliated, but suddenly realized, "Lord Longyang is still alive?"

"Naturally, he is alive."

"A minister of Wei, yet he surrendered to Qin?" Jing Ke frowned.

"The King of Wei is so detestable, why shouldn't Lord Longyang surrender to Qin?"

Jing Ke finally understood that he couldn't win an argument against Xu Fu today, so he simply shut his mouth. After closing his mouth, he didn't know what he thought of, and suddenly said, "...Where is Li Xin?" Oh, back to the original question.

His obsession with Li Xin was quite large; he probably suffered a heavy defeat at Li Xin's hands and was unwilling to accept it.

"He is a Qin general, and you are an assassin; he naturally will not see you."

"He did such a thing, he surely doesn't dare to see me," Jing Ke sneered and said no more.

Xu Fu’s expression became a bit strange. Such a thing? What kind of thing? He would have to ask Li Xin properly another day. Seeing that Jing Ke still had his pride and didn't look like he would die from being angered, Xu Fu felt relieved. He turned to Huan Yi and said, "It is inconvenient to talk here. General Huan Yi, please." Xu Fu did not want outsiders to see Qin's jokes.

Xu Fu had been doing all the talking, and Ying Zheng had not interjected once, even when he heard Xu Fu still calling Huan Yi "General," he said nothing.

Huan Yi lowered his head, gathered his sleeves, and followed Xu Fu out.

The room was soon left with only the guards and Jing Ke. Jing Ke felt a tightness in his chest, flicked his robes, and sat back down.

The guard’s mouth twitched, "...The floor is dirty and cold, why act like you're in prison?"

·

Huan Yi was somewhat uneasy. He walked behind Xu Fu, and Xu Fu felt he could even hear his breathing—the sound of nervousness. Seeing Huan Yi like this, Xu Fu felt puzzled. Why on earth did he defect?

After leading him into the hall, Ying Zheng slowly walked to the desk and sat down, looking down at Huan Yi. Since being brought into the palace, Huan Yi had been dressed like this, wearing commoner's robes with worn and dirty hems. It was evident his life in exile had not been easy.

"Speak, why did you kill?"

Huan Yi gritted his teeth, a look of humiliation flashing across his face, "Since the defeat last year, which led to the loss of grain and countless Qin soldiers dying, I have been ordered to rest at home."

Xu Fu waited patiently for him to continue.

"The family of the person I killed was related to my family by marriage..."

Xu Fu was thinking, did that family look down on Huan Yi for being incompetent and refuse to marry their daughter to him? Who knew that upon listening further, it wasn't that the family refused to marry their daughter, but that Huan Yi’s only daughter had married into that official's family. After Huan Yi’s defeat, that family feared being implicated and drove her out, turning around to accept concubines from others. Huan Yi’s daughter died shortly after returning. Huan Yi suspected she had been abused, so he went to their house to seek justice. He wanted to bring the matter to Ying Zheng, but the official's family was extremely shameless and clashed with him on the spot. Huan Yi, being a martial man, killed them in a fit of impulse. Once he had killed, he was unwilling to be executed for it, so he hurriedly fled Xianyang.

Why was the official's family so panicked and eager to distance themselves?

It was because Qin law was extremely strict. For someone like Huan Yi who had suffered such a disastrous defeat, his entire family could suffer for it. Although Ying Zheng had temporarily spared him from the death penalty, who knew if Ying Zheng would settle accounts with him later? Naturally, no one wanted to be associated with Huan Yi.

By comparison, what surprised Xu Fu more was... Huan Yi was old enough to have a daughter!

After hearing this, Ying Zheng said coldly, "You can no longer be a general."

Huan Yi knelt on the ground, smiling bitterly without a word.

It wasn't just the official who was slaughtered in that house, but also his son and his son's concubines. That family had indeed acted dishonorably, and this disaster was a form of karmic retribution. But Huan Yi’s killing was not just revenge; he had challenged the dignity of the King of Qin. In Xianyang, a defeated general could kill at will and then flee to another state. Ying Zheng could not let him go just because he had a grievance. If everyone did this, what would become of the state?

Ying Zheng quickly determined his fate.

After autumn, he would be executed. This was already a light punishment. From the moment he killed and fled Xianyang, the harsh laws had already been applied to him.

Xu Fu felt it was a pity, but in the end, he said nothing. Huan Yi had indeed done wrong, and he no longer had a chance to turn things around. It was just... the Jing Ke affair... Xu Fu found it funny just thinking about it. In history, Huan Yi, also known as Fan Yuqi, had committed suicide, willing to use his own head as a stepping stone for Jing Ke to see the King of Qin. But at that time, the King of Qin had slaughtered his entire family. In this life, Ying Zheng had not directly executed his family, but sent Li Xin to capture him. Thus, Huan Yi refused to give his head to Jing Ke...

Could this be considered a merit?

It didn't seem so.

It seemed Huan Yi would have to pay the price for what he had done. A look of regret flashed across Xu Fu’s face again. When he had gone to the military camp to detoxify Huan Yi, he had quite admired the man. Now that he had fallen to this point, recalling their past connection, even Xu Fu couldn't help but feel that the changes in the world were too fast! It caught people off guard.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu suddenly felt a headache, his brows furrowing tightly, and he even felt a wave of dizziness.

Ying Zheng’s expression changed slightly, and he reached out to support him, "What's wrong?" The kneeling Huan Yi was no longer on his mind.

But the dizziness was only for a moment. Once Xu Fu cleared his head, he immediately shook it, "...It's nothing."

Xu Fu vaguely felt that his abnormality seemed related to the chronic amnesia mentioned by his senior brother, Wei Liao.
