Xu Fu did not directly rebuke him today, nor did he flatly refuse him. Instead, he said, "I will consider this matter. If Master Tian Wei truly has the ability, then by next year, I will hand this position over to you."

Tian Wei was struck by this sudden good news, and the expression on his face almost failed to hold its composure.

"Then I thank you in advance, Shuzhang."

Having received the answer he wanted, Tian Wei naturally wouldn't continue to pester him. He still felt a lingering fear from Ying Zheng's cold demeanor, so it was better to leave early!

Once Tian Wei left, Ying Zheng felt much more at ease. In fact, Xu Fu felt much the same—the air even seemed fresher.

Over there, Wang Liu had just finished presiding over the Wax Festival and intended to look toward Xu Fu to get an evaluation from his gaze. Who knew that as soon as he turned his head, he would catch sight of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walking side by side, moving further and further away from him...

Wang Liu could only suppress the disappointment in his heart and leave with Su Yi.

And as Ying Zheng and Xu Fu walked side by side, what was he saying to Xu Fu?

"Tian Wei's background cannot be traced; he is like someone who appeared out of thin air."

"How could anyone appear out of thin air? There are always people and events connected to them." Xu Fu paused. "Unless Tian Wei is vastly different from his former self, and after a complete transformation, he reinvented himself as the current Tian Wei, so no one knows anything about his past."

Ying Zheng said indifferently, "You are right. The only information found is that he appeared in Yu City, then drifted through several countries until he came to Xianyang and was introduced to Feng Quji."

"Wait..." Xu Fu interrupted him impatiently.

Ying Zheng looked at him in surprise; he had never seen Xu Fu look like this.

"He appeared in Yu City?"

"Yes, is there something wrong with this place?"

How could there be such a coincidence? Xu Junfang had been to Yu City, and Tian Wei also appeared from Yu City. Yu City was a small place; Xu Fu had never even heard of it before, yet they had both appeared there. If there was no underlying reason for this connection, Xu Fu wouldn't believe it.

The words "Yu City" remained in Xu Fu's mind.

He wanted to go to Yu City!

"Nothing, the name of this place just sounds quite familiar to me." Xu Fu changed the subject.

"Divination... regardless of whether your abilities fade or not, you are the only State Preceptor of Great Qin." Ying Zheng said in a deep voice, likely worried that Xu Fu was overthinking because of Tian Wei's words.

"Hmm, I know." Xu Fu's expression was very calm. Ying Zheng examined him carefully and confirmed that Xu Fu truly hadn't taken Tian Wei's words to heart. That was good...

To him, Xu Fu had long since become more than just the Grand Diviner who could perform divination.

Once they got back into the carriage, they didn't mention Tian Wei again. At a time like this, there was no need to let the name Tian Wei ruin their mood.

"A-Fu." Ying Zheng suddenly grabbed Xu Fu's wrist again, his rough fingers rubbing against Xu Fu's wrist bone. "As of today, we have known each other for ten years."

"Ah..." Xu Fu was dazed for a moment. It seemed, it really was that long.

Ten years... had it gone by that fast? Xu Fu could vaguely remember when he was first with Ying Zheng, his mind was full of questions like: when I break up with the King of Qin, where should I run? What can I do if I'm no longer the State Preceptor? At that time, Ying Zheng was almost synonymous with a human-shaped massager in his mind. How many years had it been since he last thought about those things? Xu Fu couldn't even remember clearly himself. Time makes certain memories blur. Now, Xu Fu's mind was filled only with how to conquer the six states, how to help Ying Zheng unify the land, how to change the historical records regarding his tyranny, how to make Great Qin prosperous... Beyond that, it was occupied by how to raise Fusu and Huhai, as well as matters of divination.

And then, he never thought about the phrase "if I leave Ying Zheng" ever again...

Ying Zheng didn't speak again. He narrowed his eyes, staring intently at the expression on Xu Fu's face, not missing a single detail. Ying Zheng's gaze gradually became infatuated. He could roughly guess what Xu Fu was thinking through the subtle changes in his expression. Was he finding it incredible? From the very beginning, Ying Zheng knew that Xu Fu's heart had never truly settled. But time always changes a person's thoughts.

Ten years, what a wonderful phrase.

It changed Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng reached out and pulled Xu Fu into his arms, savoring the feeling of holding Xu Fu at this moment.

Even if a hundred years passed, he would never be willing to let go.

Xu Fu didn't push him away. They were each lost in their own thoughts, appearing to be daydreaming, but at this moment, the distance between them had been pulled incredibly close.

What Ying Zheng didn't expect was that it wasn't just Xu Fu who had changed in ten years; he had too. Hadn't he also slowly changed his nature and come to want to possess Xu Fu for a lifetime?

How could the Ying Zheng of the past have thought of such things?

The carriage continued to sway along.

The officials and commoners had all gone home, passing by the carriage with looks of awe.

Inside the carriage, Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu tighter, his voice deep and charming, like a bewitching spirit. "A-Fu, let's get even closer."

Xu Fu's mind had already interpreted this. Closer... how much closer could they get? Negative distance?

Just as he was thinking this, Ying Zheng truly made the distance between them negative.

The attendant driving the carriage vaguely felt that the carriage seemed to be bumping a bit more violently, but since the King didn't rebuke him, the attendant honestly continued to drive. After all, carriages were always bumpy.

Inside the carriage, through a layer of curtain, some light leaked in, flickering on Xu Fu's face. He narrowed his eyes involuntarily and pinched Ying Zheng, "...We should be close to the palace gate, right? What will you do?"

Ying Zheng didn't speak, instead leaning down to kiss Xu Fu's earlobe.

A tingling sensation suddenly surged through Xu Fu's body. He almost couldn't control a sound from escaping, so he kept a cold face and pinched Ying Zheng again, this time on his thigh. Unfortunately, it wasn't strong enough, and pinching the muscle had no effect on Ying Zheng at all.

Just then, the carriage stopped. The curtain stopped swaying, the light could no longer leak in, and Xu Fu's face fell into darkness.

Ying Zheng raised his hand to pinch the soft flesh behind his neck. "Shh."

The soldiers naturally didn't dare look at the people inside the carriage. After confirming the attendant was correct, they let them in. The carriage started moving again.

Ying Zheng took off his own robe and draped it directly over Xu Fu. The black robe was stepped on by Xu Fu inside the carriage, but in the end, it still wrapped him up.

Ying Zheng gently touched his forehead. "A-Fu is sick again."

"..." Xu Fu pursed his lips and said nothing.

Fine, the tenth anniversary could barely count as an anniversary; he'd let Ying Zheng have his way this once.

It was just that Ying Zheng's movements were so gentle that Xu Fu felt an intense itch in his heart, even having a desire for the other to treat him more roughly. Xu Fu felt his brain wasn't very clear today!

Soon, the carriage stopped again.

The attendant said in a low voice, "Your Majesty, Shuzhang, we have arrived."

"Lift the curtain."

The person outside hurriedly lifted the curtain upon hearing this.

Xu Fu's lower body was almost bare. Although his undergarments were still on and he was wrapped in a large robe, Xu Fu still felt a sense of shame at being seen.

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu tighter into his arms and then easily carried him down.

The palace servants were not surprised by this, as the Shuzhang had often been sleeping since winter began. This had happened frequently in previous years, so what was there to be surprised about? However, the servants sighed inwardly again—the King was so good to the Shuzhang! Carrying him back personally when he fell asleep!

Someone nearby thought to themselves, "What's this? Today I even saw the King bend down to tie the Shuzhang's sword for him, hmph!"

...

Xu Fu clutched the clothes on Ying Zheng's chest and was carried into the palace.

Huhai and Fusu arrived a step late and were ruthlessly blocked outside by the main gate.

Huhai sighed, "Is Father being intimate with the King again?"

Fusu's brow twitched, and he turned to ask Huhai, "Who taught you this?"

Huhai blinked. "You did." He almost habitually added "Zhao Gao" out of reflex.

Zhao Gao didn't know he had escaped another round of questioning.

Fusu was slightly stunned. "Me? When did I teach you that?" Fusu frowned, already believing Huhai was lying.

"There are bamboo slips in your palace that say so!" Huhai said righteously.

Fusu had a splitting headache and dragged him away. "If you are lying to me, I will..."

"Do bad things to me?" Huhai blinked his bright, watery eyes, looking at him pitifully.

Fusu felt that this was too... strange. His face darkened. "Could it be that this was also from the bamboo slips?"

Huhai nodded heavily. "Really, if you don't believe me, I'll go find the book for you..." After saying this, Huhai broke free from Fusu's arm and ran away. Fusu had no choice but to chase after him. After chasing for a while, Fusu remembered that those bamboo slips... probably, possibly, maybe, were sent to him by the King. He wasn't young anymore... it was customary for him to be exposed to those things... but Fusu never expected Huhai to have looked through them.

The habit of Huhai entering his palace freely had to change!

·

On the night of the Wax Festival, the four of them sat around the hall as usual, eating some food casually. However, this year, the Sichuan peppercorns that Xu Fu had contributed were used to develop a new dish, and the taste was barely passable.

Fusu was no longer young; he drank wine with Ying Zheng, and even Xu Fu had a small cup. Only Huhai pouted, indignantly gnawing on the dough in his hand.

Ah!

This is Fusu's hand!

This is Fusu's head!

Bite!

Xu Fu glanced at Huhai's appearance and found it hilarious. If he hadn't spared his life back then, it would have been a pity. Looking at Huhai now, it was clear that people are raised with care. If taught poorly and allowing treacherous people to take advantage, they would naturally grow crooked. But if taught well, they were good children!

Xu Fu was a bit tipsy from the wine and rubbed Huhai's head. "It feels very good, like a cloth doll."

Huhai grabbed Xu Fu's hand and wouldn't let go, and this action continued until nightfall.

Ying Zheng had originally planned a beautiful night, but it was ruined by Huhai. Huhai cried until his face was covered in snot and tears, insisting on sleeping with Xu Fu. Xu Fu was a bit drunk, sitting there with a cold face and not speaking, but he allowed Huhai to grab him. Comparing the two, it seemed as if Huhai was the one who was drunk. Ying Zheng couldn't really tear Huhai away, so in the end, he could only let Huhai cling to Xu Fu and get into bed together.

The moon climbed to the treetops.

Ying Zheng lay on the bed and glanced at Huhai.

It would be better to just throw this son away!

He looked at Xu Fu again. Forget it, as long as A-Fu is here...

Fusu leaned against the palace door. Am I the only one left??? He turned back to the palace servants with a cold face and asked, "Is there any precedent in Qin for someone in their teens to still sleep with their father?"

"No... I don't think so..."

·

After the Wax Festival, Xu Fu instigated Ying Zheng to issue an order for Tian Wei to join the Fengchang Temple as a Grand Diviner. The position of Grand Diviner was very low, and for Tian Wei, it was naturally beneath him. But he didn't dare vent his anger on Ying Zheng, so after entering the Fengchang Temple, Tian Wei began to target Wang Liu. He provoked Wang Liu at every turn, often disagreed with Wang Liu's views, and loved to make Wang Liu lose face during divination. Yet Tian Wei was very good at disguising himself; he had a good demeanor and spoke in a gentle and elegant way. By comparison, Wang Liu's mouth was much more venomous. After a few rounds, Tian Wei actually gained the upper hand.

Xu Fu thought about going to the Fengchang Temple to see Tian Wei's performance. On the day he arrived, he happened to see Tian Wei squeezing Wang Liu out.

Seeing Wang Liu so angry at Tian Wei, Xu Fu felt a bit disappointed.

Wang Liu's combat effectiveness wasn't weak; how could he be angered into such a state by Tian Wei? Now Xu Fu actually missed the unreasonable, arrogant, and domineering Wang Liu of the past!

"Master Wang, Master Tian."

The two turned their heads at the same time.

Wang Liu still had anger on his face, but because of Xu Fu's arrival, he seemed to restrain his emotions. Tian Wei, on the other hand, turned his head unhurriedly and smiled faintly at Xu Fu. "Shuzhang."

Xu Fu didn't look at Tian Wei; his attention was entirely on Wang Liu.

Wang Liu seemed very unwilling to expose his cold arrogance, irritability, and bad temper in front of Xu Fu. He was trying very hard to draw a line between himself and his past self in front of Xu Fu. It was precisely because of this that Wang Liu appeared weaker in front of Tian Wei.

However, Xu Fu didn't think Wang Liu would remain weak forever. Wang Liu's arrogance was innate; he could tolerate Tian Wei once or twice, but he couldn't tolerate him forever.

"Shuzhang came at the right time. I was just about to compete with Master Wang, and I ask Shuzhang to be a witness," Tian Wei said.

A look of disdain flashed across Wang Liu's face.

Tian Wei, someone whose name he had never even heard of—would he be afraid?

Xu Fu's voice was very cold. He didn't even look at Tian Wei, expressing his disregard completely. "Grand Diviner Tian, remember your status. You are not yet qualified to challenge Master Wang."

Tian Wei smiled. "But wasn't Shuzhang the same back then?"

"Grand Diviner Tian must have remembered wrong." Wang Liu no longer hid his contempt. "When Shuzhang and I sparred back then, we were both Grand Diviners in the Fengchang Temple. But now, Grand Diviner Tian wants to overstep his rank, and that won't work."

"Did Shuzhang not overstep his rank back then?" Tian Wei was surprised. "I thought that Master Liu, Assistant Hou..." Speaking of this, Tian Wei's voice stopped abruptly, as if he had suddenly realized he had said something he shouldn't have.

In fact, the words were nothing more than an attempt to satirize Xu Fu.

"You misunderstood." Wang Liu blocked him with one sentence. Wang Liu was extremely impatient. He couldn't read faces; he couldn't see how strange or important Tian Wei's face was. He only felt that Tian Wei was truly annoying. If such a person didn't know his place while staying in the Fengchang Temple, he would definitely find an opportunity to punish him.

Xu Fu looked at Wang Liu, his expression softening slightly. "Master Wang, do as you see fit. I just came to take a look."

Wang Liu knew this was Xu Fu's tacit approval. He bowed and replied, "The bamboo slips have already been sent to your palace."

"Good." Xu Fu left after saying this.

Tian Wei wasn't angry either. He watched Xu Fu's back, his desire for power reaching its absolute peak.

He looked up at the sky and then smiled at Wang Liu. "Master Wang will agree to my request."

Wang Liu cursed mercilessly, "You're brain-damaged!"

Tian Wei: ...

·

The twentieth year of King Zheng of Qin, early spring.

At first, there was a gentle spring rain in Xianyang, but later, it turned into a torrential downpour.

By late spring and early summer, after a clap of thunder, heavy rain began to fall again, and this rain, once it started falling from the sky, almost never stopped.

The people of Xianyang watched the rain falling incessantly and couldn't help but frown, saying that this was not a good omen!

Xu Fu was also awakened from his sleep by a chill. He climbed out of bed, his ears filled with the sound of rain beating against the eaves, roof, and leaves. Xu Fu couldn't help but frown.

The weather was indeed unusual. If this rain were allowed to continue, it might eventually lead to flooding, drowning the city of Xianyang. He wondered how the drainage system was at this time. As Xu Fu thought about this, he couldn't sleep anymore. He quickly put on his robes and went to see Ying Zheng.

Just as Xu Fu was about to step out of the hall, he saw a figure approaching under an umbrella.

The person closed the umbrella, soaked through. He looked up and happened to see Xu Fu.

"Shuzhang, this servant came specifically to see you."

"Zhao Gao?"

chapters.source_text:
徐福并不意外赵高的到来，他的目光淡淡地从赵高身上扫过，“恭喜中车府令。”
赵高有些惊讶，“先生的消息来得这样快？”
赵高已经重新将权利把握在手中了。他本来就没什么大错，一直以来为嬴政鞍前马后办了不少事，算得上是鞠躬尽瘁，何况他一直陪嬴政走到现在，那点儿君臣情谊还是较为深厚的。所以，从上次乐师事件出了后，徐福差不多就能猜到，嬴政非但不会怀疑赵高，反而还会过不久就将他提回到原来的位置上。
让徐福唯一没想到的是，赵高这次主动来见，竟然又恢复了从前的称呼。
“先生。”
就和桑中等人一样，始终不变对他的称呼。
徐福盯着赵高的面孔，暗暗道，若是你始终不变，没有过强的野心，那就好了。
“奴婢有话与先生说。”
其实赵高已然不用自称“奴婢”了，但是在徐福的跟前，他依旧将姿态放得极低，和过去没有什么差别。
“进来吧。”徐福转头进去。
进去之后，徐福便屏退了其他宫人，殿中只余他们二人。
赵高拜了一拜，道：“自打头一次见先生，至此已有十年了。在先生未来之前，奴婢也是花了好几年的功夫，才得以站在王上身边伺候。那时王上年少……”
赵高口吻平淡地说起，在徐福来到秦国之前，没有见过的东西。
初时，徐福还以为赵高是想说明，他于嬴政的重要性，但到了后来，徐福才发现，赵高似乎没有半点邀功和以此威胁的意思。
末了时，赵高才道：“先生是忧心奴婢有害于王上吗？奴婢怎会如此呢。奴婢的今日都是王上给的。”他顿了顿道：“奴婢与弟赵成生于隐官，后入了王上殿中做一名内侍。那时，权柄掌于吕不韦之手，宫人若非他的人，便是太后的人。唯奴婢过于愚钝，才叫那些人忽视了，也因而接近到了王上身边。一待便是十几年。先生怎能疑心奴婢待王上的忠诚呢？”
徐福看着赵高的模样，心底淡淡地接了一句，人心是易变的。
“先生如此提防奴婢，不必也不知该如何方能证自身清白。”
“赵成是如何一回事？”徐福出声问道。
“什么？”
“赵成救过我，我是极为感激，但我并不蠢笨，赵成接近我是故意为之，他难道不是受你指使吗？”
赵高脸色微变，“实在冤枉，奴婢与弟赵成关系并不亲厚，宫人们都是知晓的。奴婢怎会指使他？若说赵成会如此，那……那倒也是有可能的。”
“为何如此说？”徐福紧盯着赵高的面孔，为了确认他有没有说谎。
“奴婢的母亲曾因触犯刑法而被处刑，身体残缺后便入了隐官。”赵高尴尬道：“或许，或许赵成便是因此心中，心中有些难以接受吧。但……”
见赵高面露急色，徐福才出声道：“他救了我，这些便算作没发生。”
赵高苦声道：“若先生还不肯信奴婢，那便也在奴婢身上施以咒术就是。”
“你是王上的臣子，不是我的臣子，我怎敢如此擅为？”哪怕徐福心中再担忧，他也不能擅自动赵高，这是一直以来，徐福保留着的想法。他并不想因为赵高而令嬴政不愉。赵高说得不错，他的确是陪着嬴政走过了太多事。在完全没有证据的情况下，他不能对赵高如何。
这辈子已经有些历史发生变动了，那么日后赵高还会不会是那个奸臣，谁也不能确定。
不能因为一个人可能会做的事，而选择抹杀这个人。
这句话，徐福已经提醒了自己无数次。
他实在拿赵高无法了。
赵高点头道：“乃是奴婢自愿为之，如此若是能令先生放心，那也值了。”
徐福忍不住再打量起了赵高，他竟然如此笃定，难道他真的是没有异心？
“让我来试试！”胡亥的声音在殿中响起。他不知何时到了这里，外面的宫人竟然也没有通报。
胡亥走到赵高的身旁，扬起头看了他一眼，“我给你下咒。”
赵高点头应道：“诺。”竟是十分配合地低下了头。
胡亥摸了摸他头上的帽子，嘴里叽里咕噜也不知念了些什么，然后一巴掌拍在了赵高的肩上。等这一系列动作做完，徐福都还没能反应过来。
而后，胡亥板着一张小脸，认真地将当初胡亥说与徐福的话，又给赵高复述了一遍，“若你胆敢有二心，定然会会肠子断成一节一节，脏器都成碎肉，外表还是完好的，直到死后，浑身的皮肉脱落……死也难有全尸。”
徐福看向了赵高，带着略微责怪的目光。
你现在知道你把胡亥带得有多歪了吗？
赵高没有注意到徐福的目光，反而冲着胡亥微微一笑，道：“胡亥公子说的是，奴婢日后定然不会有二心。”
徐福觉得自己有些恍惚了。
这二人的对话竟然这般淡定，他们难道不觉得何处不对吗？赵高不会害怕，不会愤怒，不会惶恐吗？
最后与赵高的谈话，在胡亥的咒术中画上了句号。
赵高弯了弯腰，行过礼后，才退了出去，他撑着伞，又顶着大雨出去了。他的身影渐渐模糊在雨幕中。徐福轻叹了一口气。像赵高这样的人，若是没有二心，那便是一个好的助手，但若是有了二心，那便是最大的杀器。
赵高走后，徐福本想陪一会儿胡亥，等雨小些再去寻嬴政，谁知雨却一直没有要小下来的意思。这一等，便等到了天黑。而这时，嬴政也归来了。
雨这时才小了些。
嬴政一进殿门，徐福便注意到了他脸上的冷色。
“雨如此一直下着，实令人心烦。”嬴政顺着徐福的目光，往窗外看了一眼，顿时道。
“奉常寺传来的消息如何说？”
“若是他们说出个所以然了，寡人也不会如此生气了。奉常寺只道春末夏初向来如此，雨水多，并无任何不正常之处。但是……”
“但是咸阳城中已经有不好的言论传出了？”徐福接口道。在这个时代待得久了，对于这些东西，徐福渐渐也变得敏锐起来了。从大雨不停歇开始，徐福差不多就猜到这点了。
“百姓认为是蜡祭未能求得神灵先祖护佑。”
“此事，能解决的。”徐福淡淡道，说着走到了嬴政的身后，虽然他身高不及嬴政，但微微踮脚，倒还可以抬起手给嬴政揉揉额角和太阳穴。
嬴政全然没想到徐福会做这样的动作，徐福的手指触到他的皮肤后，他不自觉地颤了颤，然后抬手握住了徐福微凉的手指。
“今日田味又来求见寡人了，说是他能解决此事。依你看，如何处置？”嬴政当然舍不得让徐福举着手给自己揉额头，他反手一拉，就将徐福拉到他面前去了。
徐福挡在嬴政的面前，感受着窗外刮来的凉风。“……”
嬴政今天的心情已经不好到了，需要拿他挡风的地步了吗？
雨丝飘进来落在徐福脸上，徐福道：“让田味跟我一起去便是。”
嬴政动了动手指，“还留着他钓鱼？”
“留着，起码也要等我，研究出他的面相才好。”
嬴政借机低头吻了吻他的耳廓，“嗯。”真不知寡人与面相卜筮，孰轻孰重……
·
这一场雨断断续续地下了七天，咸阳城中的百姓多有怨言。雨水堆积，哪怕有排水系统的也不太顶事了。百姓们都忧心，咸阳会不会被涨起来的大水淹没。
一辆马车摇晃着出了宫门。
车轮滑过水坑，溅起了水。
这个时候，雨停了。没有雨声敲击在耳边，坐在马车内的徐福觉得安静极了。这种滋味让他觉得很舒服。
田味坐在一旁，不时打量着徐福。
他以为徐福闭着眼，便不会知晓他的小动作了。
徐福的睫毛忽然颤动两下，紧接着他便睁开了眼眸，田味心中一惊，忙别过了头，但心跳却是骤然加快了。
他紧张地蜷了蜷手指，觉得在徐福的跟前有些难以自持。
徐君房太优秀了……
他心底五味杂陈。
“田太卜瞧什么？”
“没什么。”田味故作淡定地道。
徐福目光冰冷地扫过他，“……哦。”
田味感受着那道冰冷的目光，从身上渐渐扫过去，而奇怪的是，这次他没有了鸡皮疙瘩的感觉，反而是……反而是心中带起了莫名舒畅的滋味。
走了个神的功夫，他们的马车就已经到了。
“准备好了吗？”徐福冷声问。
田味滞了滞，“好了。”
徐福当先撩起车帘走了下去。
田味看了一眼徐福的背影。
着白袍，却气质高冷如山尖上的那抹雪，仿佛生来就是叫人仰望的一般。
作者有话要说：　　隐官：收容刑满释放人员的地方。
隐官中人，其身份在没有爵位的什伍、公卒和庶人之下一等，在奴隶之上。
chapters.title: 第232章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu was not surprised by Zhao Gao's arrival; his gaze swept over Zhao Gao indifferently. "Congratulations, Zhongchefuling."

Zhao Gao was somewhat surprised. "How did you receive the news so quickly, Sir?"

Zhao Gao had already regained his grip on power. He had never committed any major errors to begin with, and having served Ying Zheng diligently all this time, he could be considered to have given his all. Moreover, having stayed by Ying Zheng's side until now, the bond between sovereign and subject remained quite deep. Therefore, ever since the incident with the musician, Xu Fu had almost guessed that not only would Ying Zheng not suspect Zhao Gao, but he would also restore him to his former position before long.

The only thing Xu Fu did not expect was that Zhao Gao, in taking the initiative to see him this time, had actually reverted to his old form of address.

"Sir."

Just like Sang Zhong and the others, his way of addressing him remained unchanged.

Xu Fu stared at Zhao Gao's face and thought to himself, If only you remained unchanged and lacked such overwhelming ambition, that would be for the best.

"This servant has something to say to you, Sir."

In truth, Zhao Gao no longer needed to refer to himself as "this servant," but in front of Xu Fu, he still kept his posture extremely low, no different from the past.

"Come in." Xu Fu turned and walked inside.

Once inside, Xu Fu dismissed the other palace attendants, leaving only the two of them in the hall.

Zhao Gao bowed and said, "It has been ten years since I first met you, Sir. Before you arrived, it took me several years of effort just to be able to stand by the King's side and serve him. At that time, the King was young..."

Zhao Gao spoke in a flat tone about things that had happened before Xu Fu came to the State of Qin.

At first, Xu Fu thought Zhao Gao wanted to emphasize his importance to Ying Zheng, but later, Xu Fu realized that Zhao Gao did not seem to have the slightest intention of claiming credit or using this as a threat.

At the end, Zhao Gao said, "Are you worried, Sir, that this servant might harm the King? How could I ever do such a thing? Everything I have today was given to me by the King." He paused and continued, "My younger brother Zhao Cheng and I were born in the Yin Guan, and later entered the King's palace as attendants. At that time, power was in the hands of Lu Buwei; if palace servants were not his people, they were the Queen Dowager's. Only because I was too dull were those people ignored, and thus I was able to get close to the King. I have been there for over a dozen years. How could you doubt my loyalty to the King, Sir?"

Xu Fu looked at Zhao Gao's expression and added faintly in his heart, Human hearts are easily changed.

"Since you are so wary of me, Sir, I do not know what I must do to prove my innocence."

"What is the story with Zhao Cheng?" Xu Fu asked aloud.

"What?"

"Zhao Cheng saved me, and I am very grateful, but I am not stupid. Zhao Cheng's approach was intentional; was he not acting under your instructions?"

Zhao Gao's expression changed slightly. "I am truly wronged. It is well known among the palace servants that I am not close to my brother Zhao Cheng. How could I have instructed him? If you say Zhao Cheng would do such a thing, then... then that is indeed possible."

"Why do you say that?" Xu Fu stared intently at Zhao Gao's face, trying to confirm if he was lying.

"My mother was once punished for violating the law, and after her body was mutilated, she was sent to the Yin Guan." Zhao Gao said awkwardly, "Perhaps, perhaps that is why Zhao Cheng finds it difficult to accept. But..."

Seeing the anxious look on Zhao Gao's face, Xu Fu said, "He saved me, so let those matters be considered as if they never happened."

Zhao Gao said bitterly, "If you still refuse to trust me, Sir, then please place a curse upon me as well."

"You are the King's subject, not mine. How could I presume to do such a thing?" Even if Xu Fu was worried, he could not act against Zhao Gao on his own; this was a principle Xu Fu had always held. He did not want to displease Ying Zheng because of Zhao Gao. Zhao Gao was right; he had indeed accompanied Ying Zheng through too many things. In the complete absence of evidence, he could not do anything to Zhao Gao.

Some history had already changed in this lifetime, so no one could be certain if Zhao Gao would still become that treacherous official in the future.

One cannot choose to destroy a person because of what they might do.

Xu Fu had reminded himself of this sentence countless times.

He really could do nothing about Zhao Gao.

Zhao Gao nodded and said, "It is my own wish. If this can put your mind at ease, Sir, then it is worth it."

Xu Fu couldn't help but size up Zhao Gao again. He was so certain; could it be that he truly had no ulterior motives?

"Let me try!" Fusu's voice rang out in the hall. He had arrived at some point, and the palace attendants outside hadn't even announced him.

Fusu walked to Zhao Gao's side and tilted his head to look at him. "I will cast a curse on you."

Zhao Gao nodded and replied, "Yes." He lowered his head in a very cooperative manner.

Fusu touched the hat on his head, muttered something unintelligible, and then slapped Zhao Gao on the shoulder. By the time this series of actions was finished, Xu Fu hadn't even had time to react.

Afterwards, Fusu kept a straight face and earnestly repeated to Zhao Gao what he had once said to Xu Fu: "If you dare to have a double heart, your intestines will surely break into pieces, your organs will turn into minced meat, while your exterior remains intact, until after you die, when your skin and flesh will fall off... even in death, you will not have a whole corpse."

Xu Fu looked at Zhao Gao with a slightly reproachful gaze.

Do you realize now how much you've warped Fusu?

Zhao Gao did not notice Xu Fu's gaze; instead, he smiled slightly at Fusu and said, "Young Master Fusu is right. I will certainly never have a double heart in the future."

Xu Fu felt a bit dazed.

The conversation between these two was so calm; did they not feel that something was wrong? Would Zhao Gao not be afraid, angry, or panicked?

The final conversation with Zhao Gao ended with Fusu's curse.

Zhao Gao bowed, performed a salute, and then retreated. He opened his umbrella and headed out into the heavy rain. His figure gradually blurred into the curtain of rain. Xu Fu sighed softly. A person like Zhao Gao, if he had no ulterior motives, would be a good assistant, but if he did, he would be the deadliest weapon.

After Zhao Gao left, Xu Fu had intended to keep Fusu company for a while and wait for the rain to lighten before seeking out Ying Zheng, but the rain showed no signs of letting up. This wait lasted until nightfall. And by then, Ying Zheng had returned.

The rain had only just begun to ease.

As soon as Ying Zheng entered the hall, Xu Fu noticed the cold look on his face.

"For the rain to continue like this is truly vexing." Ying Zheng followed Xu Fu's gaze to the window and remarked immediately.

"What news came from the Fengchang Temple?"

"If they had come up with a reason, I wouldn't be this angry. The Fengchang Temple only says that the transition from spring to summer is always like this, with much rain, and there is nothing abnormal about it. However..."

"However, bad rumors have already begun to spread in Xianyang City?" Xu Fu interjected. Having stayed in this era for so long, Xu Fu had gradually become sensitive to these things. From the moment the rain became incessant, Xu Fu had guessed as much.

"The common people believe that the La Sacrifice failed to secure the protection of the spirits and ancestors."

"This matter can be resolved," Xu Fu said calmly. As he spoke, he walked behind Ying Zheng. Although he was not as tall as Ying Zheng, by standing on his tiptoes, he could reach up to massage Ying Zheng's temples and forehead.

Ying Zheng had not expected Xu Fu to do such a thing. When Xu Fu's fingers touched his skin, he trembled involuntarily, then raised his hand to grasp Xu Fu's slightly cool fingers.

"Tian Wei came to see me again today, saying he could resolve this matter. In your opinion, how should it be handled?" Ying Zheng certainly couldn't bear to let Xu Fu hold his hands up to massage his forehead, so he pulled back, drawing Xu Fu in front of him.

Xu Fu stood in front of Ying Zheng, feeling the cool breeze blowing in from the window. "..."

Had Ying Zheng's mood today become so bad that he needed to use him as a windbreak?

As the mist of rain drifted in and landed on Xu Fu's face, he said, "Let Tian Wei go with me."

Ying Zheng moved his fingers. "Still keeping him around to fish?"

"Keep him, at least until I have finished studying his physiognomy."

Ying Zheng took the opportunity to lower his head and kiss his earlobe. "Hmm." I really don't know which is more important to me: you or physiognomy and divination...

·

This rain fell intermittently for seven days, and the people of Xianyang were full of complaints. Rainwater accumulated, and even the drainage systems were no longer effective. The people were worried about whether Xianyang would be submerged by the rising floodwaters.

A carriage rattled out of the palace gate.

The wheels slid through a puddle, splashing water.

At this moment, the rain stopped. With no sound of rain beating against his ears, Xu Fu, sitting inside the carriage, felt it was extremely quiet. This feeling made him feel very comfortable.

Tian Wei sat to one side, sizing up Xu Fu from time to time.

He thought that since Xu Fu had his eyes closed, he would not be aware of his small actions.

Xu Fu's eyelashes suddenly fluttered twice, and then he opened his eyes. Tian Wei was startled and hurriedly looked away, but his heart began to beat rapidly.

He nervously curled his fingers, feeling unable to control himself in front of Xu Fu.

Xu Junfang is too outstanding...

His heart was filled with mixed emotions.

"What is the Grand Diviner looking at?"

"Nothing." Tian Wei feigned calmness.

Xu Fu's gaze swept over him coldly. "...Oh."

Tian Wei felt that cold gaze sweep over his body, and strangely, this time he didn't get goosebumps; instead... instead, he felt an inexplicable sense of comfort in his heart.

In the time it took to lose himself in thought, their carriage had already arrived.

"Are you ready?" Xu Fu asked coldly.

Tian Wei hesitated. "I am."

Xu Fu was the first to lift the carriage curtain and step down.

Tian Wei looked at Xu Fu's back.

Dressed in white robes, yet his temperament was as cold and aloof as the snow on a mountain peak, as if he were born to be looked up to.

Author's note: Yin Guan: A place for housing those released from prison.

The status of those in the Yin Guan is one rank below commoners and soldiers without titles, and above slaves.

chapters.title: 第233章
chapters.translated_text:
When Xu Fu appeared, the commoners were stunned at first, and then their faces were flooded with a look of incredulous joy. They could not believe their eyes. How could this man, who should only walk within the royal palace, suddenly appear on the streets of the common people? What was he here for?

At that moment, everyone was extremely excited and also extremely curious.

"...Shu-zhang?" Someone called out first, and then the momentary silence was broken.

"Why has the Shu-zhang come here?"

"The Shu-zhang must have come to pray for our blessings, right?"

"Has the Shu-zhang also discovered something wrong with this heavy rain?"

"Shu-zhang..."

The commoners began to chatter, but they all remained in their original positions, not daring to get too close to Xu Fu, as if such behavior would profane him.

Tian Wei slowly approached, and seeing this scene, the feeling in his heart became even more complicated. Tian Wei clearly had no clear sense of Xu Fu's reputation in the Qin State... until this moment.

Tian Wei's appearance was not bad; to be precise, his features were softer and more approachable than Xu Fu's. Coupled with his outstanding temperament, he should have been the center of attention even when walking behind Xu Fu. But the facts disappointed him.

In the eyes of these commoners, there was absolutely no sign of him.

They didn't even glance at him.

Tian Wei felt a bit stifled.

He glanced at Xu Fu's back again. Was something wrong? Was his temperament not "immortal" enough?

Tian Wei tried very hard to imitate Xu Fu's temperament, but in the end, no commoner noticed him. Tian Wei stared intently at Xu Fu. What was still lacking?

Xu Fu was guarded by more than just Tian Wei. Because of the special nature of Xu Fu's status, he was always accompanied by others when he went out—attendants skilled in martial arts and thoughtful eunuchs. Tian Wei, mixed in among them, seemed a bit out of place.

The eunuch beside Xu Fu spoke, the gist being: "The heavy rain in Xianyang City has not stopped for several days. The Shu-zhang learned that the people in the city were uneasy, so he came specifically to see what was going on with this rain and to set everyone's hearts at ease."

The eunuch spoke concisely, and the commoners understood immediately, becoming even more excited: "Many thanks, Shu-zhang!"

Xu Fu turned his head and called the eunuch over, "First, go and count the households that have suffered damage. For the more serious cases, I will visit them personally."

This behavior was actually similar to leaders in later generations rushing to the front lines to visit the masses. It could, to some extent, serve to stabilize people's hearts.

The eunuch nodded, silently remarking on the Shu-zhang's benevolence, and turned to find the person in charge of the matter.

Xu Fu walked casually up to a man and said, "With the heavy rain these past few days, are you afraid in your hearts?"

The man was extremely excited, trembling so much he could barely form complete sentences, "We are afraid. We all say that the heavens have sent down endless rain because they are angry and are punishing us. This heavy rain has destroyed many ridges, and we can't even set up stalls on the street. We don't know how many people's livelihoods have been ruined."

Again, the theory of divine punishment weighed on them, and at the same time, the heavy rain hindered travel and their ability to earn money. If it continued to get worse, they feared even their lives would be at risk. How could this not make people afraid? It looked like a minor matter of rain, but it was extremely easy for it to develop into a great disaster.

"Do not worry, this matter will certainly be resolved." Xu Fu seemed to say something trivial, but for these people of Xianyang, it was the greatest comfort; they trusted Xu Fu implicitly.

Others had spent great effort and could not appease these commoners, yet Xu Fu gained their trust with a single sentence. It was no wonder some were extremely jealous and envious of this.

Tian Wei had originally boasted to Xu Fu that he could solve this matter, but when it truly came to this moment, he realized that Xu Fu had no use for him at all. This small disaster was not tricky for Xu Fu in the slightest; he could solve it easily and use it to gain the people's adoration once again. The only person affected by this was that Wang Fengchang.

Just a Wang Fengchang... Tian Wei was a bit disappointed. His ambition did not allow his gaze to linger on this position; what he wanted was not this.

"Keep up." A cold voice suddenly rang in Tian Wei's ear. Tian Wei came back to his senses and noticed that Xu Fu's words were directed at him. Tian Wei hurriedly stepped forward to follow, and only then was he noticed by the commoners.

"Who is that person?"

"Is he the Shu-zhang's student?"

"The Shu-zhang is so young, how could he have a student?"

...

Xu Fu had already walked some distance away before these commoners dared to whisper. Although Tian Wei also looked good, to the commoners, he was just a stranger, so why would they need to be particularly careful?

Tian Wei's expression remained unchanged, but waves were rising in his heart. Even though Xu Junfang was quite young, had his status in the hearts of these people reached such a level? Tian Wei couldn't help but feel a trace of doubt. Could he still take down Xu Fu? He no longer dared to be so certain.

Xu Fu had only walked a few steps when he saw Wang Liu and Su Yi. They were also startled when they saw Xu Fu.

"Shu-zhang?" Wang Liu's eyes were bloodshot, and he looked somewhat weary.

It was understandable; this Wax Sacrifice was supposed to be the best opportunity for Wang Liu to stand out, but who could have expected such a thing to happen this year? It was inevitable that some people with ulterior motives would link it to the Wax Sacrifice, and Wang Liu naturally could not distance himself from it. Therefore, before Xu Fu even left the palace, Wang Liu had already come to investigate the matter. But his ability to appease the masses was truly not as good as Xu Fu's; instead, because he was not eloquent, he had nearly come into conflict with the people here.

Wang Liu felt that these commoners were truly difficult to reason with, but he had to lower his status and try hard to communicate with them. This communication had lasted until now.

"Has the Shu-zhang also come because of the heavy rain?" Su Yi asked.

"Indeed."

Su Yi looked ashamed, "It has caused the Shu-zhang worry."

Wang Liu pursed his lips and said, "It is my fault."

Su Yi immediately shook his head, "How can you say that? I also contributed during the Wax Sacrifice; wouldn't that mean I am also at fault?"

It was rare for Xu Fu to see the two of them talking like this, and he found it quite fresh, so he looked them both up and down, "Are you finished?"

"Finished." Wang Liu's face flushed, and he quickly shut his mouth. Su Yi also stopped.

"At this time, arguing about whose fault it is is useless. If you feel quite guilty in your hearts, then follow them and go appease the disaster-stricken people."

"Understood." Wang Liu nodded, his expression relaxing a little.

Tian Wei watched from a distance, and a flash of jealousy suddenly crossed his heart, which startled even him. In his eyes, Wang Liu and the others were extremely useless people, yet these were the very people who could converse with Xu Junfang as equals. When Xu Junfang looked at them, there must have been no coldness, detachment, or contempt in his eyes, right?

Tian Wei gave Wang Liu a cold look before following Xu Fu again.

Most of the disaster victims in the city were poor, and their houses could not withstand the continuous heavy rain. When Xu Fu entered the door, his shoes immediately sank into a puddle. Xu Fu rarely had such embarrassing moments; the wet, soggy feeling clinging to his feet immediately made him feel extremely uncomfortable.

An old woman sitting on the steps inside the courtyard gate stood up tremblingly, "Who... who is it?" The old woman's eyesight was not good, and she could not see who had stepped through the door.

A middle-aged man rushed in and hurriedly supported the woman, saying, "Mother, it's the Shu-zhang, the Shu-zhang who cured the plague in the city that year..."

The old woman realized a beat late, lifted her foot and stepped into the puddle, but as if she didn't notice, she walked straight up to Xu Fu and grabbed the back of his hand with her rough, dark, calloused hand. Xu Fu was startled and almost pulled back sharply. The middle-aged man was also shocked to see this and raised his voice, "Mother, what are you doing?"

"Our roof, the house has collapsed, can it... can it be saved?" The woman said with trembling lips, and two lines of murky tears flowed from the narrow slits of her eyes.

The middle-aged man was about to scold his mother for being too rude, but suddenly heard Xu Fu say, "It can."

In such times, Xu Fu was always patient; he just had to treat these people as clients.

Tian Wei still stood behind Xu Fu. He watched the old woman tightly clutching Xu Fu with her mud-stained hand, the black and white forming a sharp contrast. Tian Wei felt a surge of anger. If it were him, he would definitely have scolded the old woman for her rudeness. Since Xu Junfang was known as an "immortal" in the Qin State, he should maintain the posture of an immortal; how could he be so close to these commoners? If he were this tolerant, what majesty would he have in the future? How could he awe these people?

Tian Wei strongly disapproved of Xu Fu's composure at this moment.

His gaze could not help but fall on the old woman's hand.

Why hadn't she taken her hand away yet?

Tian Wei felt that just looking at it was unbearable. Such a pair of hands... how could such a pair of hands touch Xu Junfang?

After Xu Fu spoke a few words to the old woman, he walked to the next house. It wasn't just that old woman; among poor families, there were truly few who could keep themselves clean. Moreover, with the heavy rain these past few days, their houses had collapsed; where would they have the mood to worry about whether they were clean or not?

Fortunately, except for the old woman with poor eyesight, the others looked at Xu Fu with fearful eyes. They did not dare to approach Xu Fu and could only kneel and kowtow in the direction of Xu Fu as he walked away.

Tian Wei thought to himself, that's how it should be.

The sun gradually shifted, and Tian Wei finally spoke, "Shouldn't the Shu-zhang rest now?"

Hearing him say this, Xu Fu stopped in his tracks and only then felt a sense of fatigue.

Tian Wei said in a low voice, "After spring, the Shu-zhang's energy recovered, so you are squandering it like this again?"

Xu Fu's gaze turned slightly cold, and he glanced at him sideways.

Tian Wei was quite bold at this moment, and he said, "Shu-zhang, do not forget what I once said to you."

Tian Wei had said a lot since coming to Xianyang; how could Xu Fu remember what he had said?

"Shu-zhang, do not abuse your abilities. Is it worth it to be like this?" Tian Wei said in a low voice. He looked as if he were earnestly advising Xu Fu.

Xu Fu pursed his lips.

Oh. With Tian Wei emphasizing this, had he discovered something?

"Did Grand Diviner Tian see something?" Xu Fu asked directly.

Tian Wei hesitated for a moment and said, "Within a year, the Shu-zhang will taste the feeling of his abilities fading."

"Is that so? Then I look forward to it." Xu Fu replied in a cold tone. He did indeed have a feeling; for instance, with this heavy rain, he had not sensed any signs, so he could only remedy it now. But did Tian Wei think that because of this, he would be afraid, would shrink back, and would voluntarily give up his position? Tian Wei was thinking too wishfully.

Seeing that there was not a trace of panic on Xu Fu's face, a sense of frustration welled up in Tian Wei's heart.

What would it take to see his expression change? Tian Wei gritted his teeth hard.

Xu Fu called for the eunuch to drive the carriage and take him back to the royal palace.

This day had come to an end.

Afterwards, in order to test the results of his divination, Xu Fu specifically performed a few more divinations. He wrote the results on silk, and apart from himself, no one else knew. He was just waiting to compare them one by one to see if he would make a mistake. If he did, it was no big deal; he would just have to avoid divining for Ying Zheng in the future to prevent any mishaps.

As he thought, he looked down at the silk again. Several lines were written on it, and to avoid being seen by others, he used simplified characters: 1. Small rain will return in two days, stop after one day and night, and there will be no rain for half a month.

2. The matter Fusu requested will be successful.

3. The war to attack Yan will suffer a setback.

4. Within a month, Huhai will have a minor illness.

5. ...

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment before picking up his brush to add the last line.

Five, Xu Fu will face disaster.

The precognitive ability he had previously acquired was still working, but this time he saw nothing; he could only feel that while no one else was in any danger, he himself seemed to be on the verge of disaster.
chapters.source_text:
当徐福出现的时候，百姓们先是一怔，紧接着他们的脸上涌现了不可置信的惊喜之色。他们不敢相信自己的眼睛。这个本该只能行走在王宫的人，怎么会突然出现在平民的街头呢？他是来做什么的？
那一刻，大家激动极了，也好奇极了。
“……庶、庶长？”不知是谁先唤了一声，紧接着这瞬间的沉寂便被打破了。
“庶长来到此处是为何事？”
“庶长一定是来为我们祈福的吧？”
“庶长也发现那大雨的不对劲之处了吗？”
“庶长……”
百姓们七嘴八舌了起来，只不过他们始终都站在原位置上，并不敢向徐福靠得太近，似乎这样的行为会亵渎了徐福一般。
田味慢慢走近了，看着这样一幕，心底的滋味更复杂了。田味对于徐福在秦国的声望显然并没有一个明确的感受……直到这一刻。
田味容貌生得并不差，准确的说，他的模样比之徐福更显柔和，更容易让人亲近。加上他的气质也分外出众。因而，哪怕是走在徐福身后，他也应当是备受瞩目的。但是事实令他失望了。
就是这些平民百姓的眼中，竟然完全没有他的身影。
他们连看他一眼也无。
田味有些憋气。
他又瞥了一眼徐福的背影，是哪里不对吗？气质还不够仙？
田味很努力地模仿着徐福的气质，但最后还是没有百姓注意到他的身上。田味紧紧盯着徐福，是哪里还不够呢？
徐福身后拱卫着不止田味一人。因为徐福身份的特殊性，他出行时身边必然是会跟人的，会武艺的侍从，还有体贴周到的内侍。田味夹杂在中间，倒是显得有些异类。
徐福身边的内侍出了声，大意便是“咸阳城中几日大雨不止，庶长得知城中百姓心下难安，便特地前来，瞧一瞧这大雨是如何一回事，以安大家的心。”
内侍说得简练，百姓们也听了个明白，当即更为激动，“多谢庶长！”
徐福转头将那内侍叫了过来，“先去统计可有受灾的人家，严重些的，我便亲自走一趟。”
这个行为，其实跟后世的领导奔赴第一线探望群众是差不多的。多少都能起到安定人心的效果。
内侍点头，暗道一声庶长仁慈，转头便去寻负责事宜的人了。
而徐福随意走到了一男子跟前，道：“这几日大雨，你们心中可害怕？”
那男子分外兴奋，哆嗦得差点不成完整的语句，“是害怕的，咱们都说天降大雨不歇，那是上天有怒气，才降罪下来的。这一场大雨，田埂毁了不少，小的们连在街边摆摊都无法。也不知毁了多少人的营生。”
又是降罪论压在身上，同时大雨又阻碍了人的出行，阻碍了他们赚钱，若是等到更严重些，怕是连小命都堪忧。这如何能教人不害怕？瞧上去不过是个下雨的小事，但却极为容易发展成大灾难。
“不必忧虑，此事定然会得到解决。”徐福看似说了句不痛不痒的话，但是对于这些咸阳百姓来说，已经是最大的慰藉了，他们无比地信任徐福。
别人花了大工夫都安抚不住这些平民百姓，而徐福简单一句话就获得了他们的信任。也难怪有人对此极为嫉妒和羡慕了。
田味原本在徐福跟前夸口，说此事他能解决，但真正到了这个时候，他才发现，徐福根本用不上他。这点儿小灾祸对于徐福来说，半点也不棘手，他轻松就能解决，并且以此再次获得民众的追捧爱戴。唯一因此事而受影响的，便只有那王奉常。
一个王奉常而已……田味有些失望。他的野心并不允许他的目光停留在这个位置上，他想要的，不是这个。
“跟上。”冷淡的声音骤然响在田味的耳边，田味回过神来，这才注意到徐福那两个字是对他说的。田味忙拔腿跟上，到这时，他才算是被百姓们注意到了。
“那人是谁？”
“庶长的学生吗？”
“庶长那样年轻何来的学生？”
……
徐福已经走得有些远了，这些百姓才敢低声议论起来，田味虽然瞧上去也生得好模样，但对于百姓们来说，他就是个陌生人而已，哪里需要什么格外的小心呢？
田味脸色不变，心底却是泛起了波涛。尽管徐君房年纪颇轻，但在这些人的心中，地位已经高到那般地步了吗？田味不由得生起了一丝怀疑。他还能拿下徐福吗？他如今再也不敢那样笃定了。
徐福走了没几步，便见着了王柳和苏邑的身影，他们见着徐福，也是一惊。
“庶长？”王柳眼底布着血丝，瞧上去有些萎靡。
想来也是，这次蜡祭本是王柳崭露头角最好的机会，但谁能想到到了今年就出了这样的事，难免被一些有心人往蜡祭上扯，王柳自然就脱不开关系了。所以不等到徐福出宫，王柳就已经先来调查此事了。但他安抚民众的能力实在不比徐福，反倒还因为口拙，险些与这里的百姓起了冲突。
王柳觉得这些百姓实在难以说通，但是他又不得不放下身段，努力地去和他们沟通，这一沟通，便到了现在。
“庶长也是为大雨之事而来？”苏邑问道。
“不错。”
苏邑面露愧色，“让庶长忧心了。”
王柳抿唇，道：“是我之过。”
苏邑立即摇头，道：“怎能如此说？蜡祭之时，我也有出力，那岂不是我也有过错？”
徐福难得见他们二人如此对话，顿时还觉得有些新鲜，于是将他们二人来回打量了一番，“说完了吗？”
“说完了。”王柳脸上一红，忙住了嘴。苏邑也随之停住了。
“此时争论是谁之过都无用，你们若觉得心中颇为罪过，那便随他们一起，去安抚受灾的百姓。”
“诺。”王柳点头应了，面上表情松缓了一些。
田味不远不近地瞧着，心底陡然掠过了一丝嫉妒之情，他自己都惊了一跳。那王柳等人在他看来，是极为无用之辈，但就是这些人，却能和徐君房平等地交谈。徐君房看向他们的时候，眼底一定没有冷漠疏离和蔑视吧？
田味冰冷地看了一眼王柳，才有再次跟上了徐福。
城中受灾的多是家贫之人，那屋子顶不了接连的大雨，徐福进门的时候，鞋履便立即陷入了水坑之中。徐福少有这样窘迫的时候，湿哒哒的感觉缠绕着他的足部，顿时让他觉得难受极了。
院门内坐在台阶上的老妇人，颤巍巍地站了起来，“是……是谁？”老妇人的眼神不大好，看不清踏进门的人是谁。
一个中年汉子冲了进去，忙扶住那妇人，道：“娘，是庶长啊，那年在城中治了疫病的庶长啊……”
那老妇人慢半拍地醒过神来，抬脚踩进了水坑里，但她却恍若未觉一般，直直走到了徐福的跟前，粗糙黑黝的大手，抓住了徐福的手背。徐福一惊，差点猛地抽回去。那中年汉子见状也吓了一跳，拔高了声音道：“娘，你做什么？”
“我们家屋顶，房子塌了，也能……能救吗？”那妇人嘴唇哆嗦着道，狭小的眼缝里还流出了两行浊泪。
那中年汉子正要斥责母亲太过无礼，却突然听徐福道：“能的。”
在这种时候，徐福向来是耐心的，只要将这些人都看做是客户就好了。
田味依旧站在徐福的身后，他看着那老妇人用带着污泥的手紧紧攥住徐福，黑白形成鲜明的对比，田味看得好一阵火光。若是他，他定然会斥责那老妇人的无礼。既然徐君房在秦国素来有“神仙”之称，那他便应当拿出神仙的架子才是，又怎能与这些平民百姓，这般接近？若是如此宽容，那日后还有何威严？如何震慑这些人？
田味对于此时徐福的不动声色，颇为不赞同。
他的目光不可抑制地落在了那老妇人的手上。
她怎么还不将手拿开呢？
田味觉得他光是瞧着，便觉得难以忍受了。那样的一双手……那样的一双手怎么能触碰徐君房？
徐福与那老妇人说过几句话后，便又拔腿走到了下一家。不止那名老妇人，穷苦人家，实在少有将自己收拾得干干净净的人。何况这几日大雨，他们屋子都垮了，哪里还有心情去顾忌自己干净不干净。
不过好在除了那眼神不好的老妇人以外，其他人看向徐福时都是畏惧的目光，他们并不敢接近徐福，只能在徐福走出去的时候，他们才对着徐福的方向跪地叩头。
田味暗道，这样才对啊。
日头渐渐地偏移了，田味终于开口说话了，“庶长难道不应当休息了吗？”
听他这样一说，徐福顿住脚步，这才感觉到了倦意。
田味低声道：“庶长入春以后，精力恢复了，便又这样挥霍了吗？”
徐福目光微冷，斜睨了他一眼。
那田味此时胆子倒是大起来了，他道：“庶长勿要忘记我曾与庶长说过的话。”
田味自打来了咸阳，话说了不少，徐福怎么记得他说的什么话。
“庶长勿要滥用能力啊。如此这般，可值得？”田味低声道。瞧上去，他倒像是在语重心长地劝诫徐福一样。
徐福抿了抿唇。
哦。田味这般强调，难道是他发现了什么？
“田太卜是看见什么了吗？”徐福直接了当地问出了声。
田味犹豫了一下，道：“不出一年，庶长便能体会到能力消退的滋味了。”
“是吗？那我倒是期待着。”徐福口吻冷淡地应道。他确有所感，就好比这次大雨，他便没有感受到任何征兆，于是只能到现在才去补救。但是田味以为这样，他便会畏惧，会退缩，会主动让出位来吗？那田味未免想得太过美好了。
见徐福脸上半点惊慌也无，田味心底顿时涌现了一阵挫败感。
要怎么样，才能看见他变脸色呢？田味狠狠地咬了咬牙。
徐福叫来内侍，驾着马车送他归了王宫。
这一日算是划上了句号。
之后徐福为了试验卜筮结果，特意又卜了几卦，他将结果写在绢布上，除却他自己之外，再无他人知晓。他就等着一一对照，看自己究竟会不会出错。若是会出错，那也没什么大不了的，只是以后他得避免再为嬴政卜筮了，免得反误了事。
他想着想着又低头看了一眼那绢布，绢布上书了几行字，为了避免被他人瞥见，他都是用的简体字：1.两日后复小雨，持续一天一夜后停，半月不再有雨。
2.扶苏所求之事，成。
3.攻燕之战有失利。
4.一月内，胡亥会生一场小病。
5.……
徐福犹豫一下，还是提笔添上了最后一句。
五，徐福有祸。
他之前获得的预感能力，现在还在运作中，只不过这一次他什么也没看见，只能感觉到，谁都没什么祸事，反倒是自己，像是要祸事临头了。

chapters.title: 第234章
chapters.source_text:
以前徐福也没少经历过这样的等待时刻，但是都没有这样难熬过。
他静静地听着耳边的雨声，滴滴答答敲打在外面的石阶上。
颇有节奏的雨声实在太过催眠，徐福没一会儿便困意袭来，不知不觉地睡着了。黑暗将他笼罩在了其中，他仿佛化身一抹孤魂，在这个空间里漫无目的地飘荡了起来。初时，徐福以为是自己又要看到未来会出现的画面了，但是他瞪大眼等了许久，也什么都没能看到。
直到一阵脚步声传入耳中，徐福惊了一跳，不自觉地睁开了双眼。
亮光泄入了黑暗中，徐福陡然清醒了。
嬴政俯在他的身上，专注地盯着他，徐福睁开眼的时候，正好四目相对。
“你睡得太沉了。”嬴政皱了皱眉，“寡人唤了你许久也未能醒来。”
宫人还守在一旁，徐福微微一怔，转头问那宫人：“我睡了多久？”
“五个时辰了。”
五个时辰？
差不多相当于他用过早膳之后，就靠在小榻上睡着了，一直睡到嬴政归来，中间他半点也未曾醒过。
老毛病又犯了？徐福实在摸不着头脑，不过他却注意到耳边没有雨声了。
雨停了。
徐福缓缓舒出了一口气。
雨停就好。说明他没看错。不过观测天象并不能作数，毕竟只要稍有些经验的人，都能瞧出来第二日是晴还是雨，除却个别的时候，天公不作美，非要变个脸。
“没事了，我有些饿了，用饭吧。”徐福轻描淡写地将自己的异状带过去了。
而嬴政竟然也当真没有追问，他点点头，勾着徐福的腰，将人带了起来。坐起来后，宫人们也就在小榻前直接摆了食物。睡得浑身软绵绵的徐福，倒是正好就这样进食了。食物摆上来之后，徐福正要转头与嬴政说话，让他放心雨不会再造出事端了，但是要出口的话，却突然被堵在了嗓眼儿里。
嬴政竟然在发呆！
徐福从来没见过嬴政这副模样，他在想什么，才会让他陷入呆滞之中。
“阿政？”
徐福的声音响起，嬴政立即回了头，“这几日寡人也有些疲累，先用饭吧。”
“嗯。”徐福应了声，一边却准备再炼些药丸出来，最好是能凝神静气的。
因为雨停的缘故，徐福的心情还不错，哪怕他又变得嗜睡了些，但至少现在说明，田味那些话都是故意膈应他的。
用完饭食之后，二人在宫中散了散步。但是嬴政一直有些神游，徐福倒也无法和他聊天了，只能沉默着走完，然后洗过澡，就一起上了床榻。说来也怪，白日里睡了那么长的时间，这个时候徐福竟然还能睡得着。
如此过了两天，徐福却没能等来预料中的小雨。
他抬头，看见的是金灿灿的日光。他几乎可以联想到那些百姓们，在见到日光后，面上灿烂的笑容。
天气预测出错是正常的，君不见后世天气预报也有放人鸽子的时候呢。
徐福安了安心，等待着下一个卜筮结果的印证。
扶苏被嬴政派去督水利了，回王宫的时候越发少了，不过前段日子他回来的时候，面带愁色，似乎为什么所难。
这次便看他能否解决那事吧……
·
秦王政二十年，嬴政令王贲率军攻楚，同时又派出大军，李信、羌瘣领军，增援王翦。
徐福没有等到攻燕之战失利，也没有等到扶苏回宫来。结果如何，他竟是半点也不知晓……
眼看着，一个月的时间溜走了。
胡亥打着小喷嚏，抽着鼻子走到了徐福的跟前，“父亲，头痛……”
胡亥贪凉，不慎染上了风寒，他刚吃了药，从被窝里爬起来，脸蛋烧得通红，眼睛红红，鼻子也红红，看上去可怜到了极点。往日都是扶苏照顾他的，现在扶苏不在，胡亥便自动寻到了徐福这里。
生了病的胡亥瞧上去倍加脆弱，让人心底顿时就化成了一滩水。
徐福抚了抚他的脸颊，让胡亥窝进了自己的怀中。
这个算是应验了吧？
徐福全然没发觉到，自己心底已然种下了怀疑的种子。
他越是在心底强调，其实能力削减也没什么大不了，而另一边就越是加深心底对能力削减的肯定。他已经从潜意识里认同田味的话了。
抱着胡亥，徐福忽然间想起了很早以前的事。
上辈子的时候，他那半吊子的师父告诉他。给人算命，那就是在透支自己的性命。知道了不该知道的东西，前生你能通过此道获得荣华富贵，但后生你却是要拿命来换的。别妄想逃脱，谁都逃不掉的……
谁都逃不掉吗？
瞥一眼怀中的胡亥，再想到在外的扶苏，和此时还在累于案牍的嬴政。
……这辈子不一样了，这辈子他不太想用性命去交换。
而且还有那么多疑惑未能解开！
徐福轻轻拍了拍胡亥的头。
他还是改日再翻翻古籍，瞧一瞧有没有相关的记载吧。能力消退他不害怕，他怕没命。
都说算命人不自算，但他却能预见到自己的危险，这是不是一个不好的信号呢？徐福不知道，毕竟以前他从前没体验过。
等胡亥病渐渐好转的时候，徐福也翻了不少书了，不过很可惜，半点相关的记载也没有。
徐福又想起了侯生。
若是他在的话，或许他能知道一些？
毕竟都是做卜筮行业的，侯生应当会比他了解得更多。
但是无论徐福花了多大的力气，都始终寻不到侯生。
他的脑子里闪现过当初侯生的面孔，有些遗憾。
柏舟在一旁低声道：“如今战乱起，那侯太卜丞，说不准……许是死了。”这是柏舟说的最有可能的结果。
徐福倒是不希望他死。
徐福偶尔也会想要和人切磋，但他想要切磋的对象绝不是韩终那样的人，更不是田味这样的人。只有侯生才当得起！
“再去找找吧……”
柏舟并未再劝，他点点头，应下了。不管主子给的什么命令，他都应该遵从。
徐福的心情有点说不出的郁结，他挥手叫来了胡亥，揉一把毛茸茸的脑袋。这倒是舒服些了。而胡亥还极为乖巧地任由他揉弄，那就更舒服些了。
……
不久，王翦攻燕传来了捷报。
徐福不知是该笑还是该哭。
捷报，按理来说，他是该为嬴政高兴的；但是，另一方面来说，它也证明自己卜出的失利是个出错的结果。
徐福揉了揉额角，将手拿下来的时候，他才发现自己的指尖微微颤抖着。
他的心底在害怕吗？
徐福搁下膝盖上的绢布，走到了一处小榻旁，倒上去睡着了。
而这时，徐福又做了一个梦。
这次会梦见什么？徐福隐隐还有些激动和期待。
梦境中还是一片黑暗，他不知道过了有多久……
电闪雷鸣，狂风大作，异象陡生，仿佛有什么上古巨兽发出了震动天地的怒吼声，然后天地就真的被震动了。
山崩地裂，大概便是如此。
借着电闪雷鸣间的亮光，徐福看见那座耸立的宫殿崩塌了，以摧枯拉朽的姿态……场面极为骇人。
徐福发现自己动也不动了，只能眼睁睁地看着那坍塌的宫殿，将自己压在下面。
他的嗓子眼儿里骤然迸发出了一声惊呼。
“唰”，他睁开了眼。
身下的小榻微微颤动了起来。
是他自己控制不住地在颤抖吗？等宫人发觉徐福醒了，匆匆走进来的时候，徐福已经恢复如常了，半点看不出他刚才展露出了惊恐。
徐福支起身子，看了一眼窗外。
日光正好，半点天灾人祸的现象都没有。
但那个梦境……
徐福怔了会儿，只听见耳边的宫人突然惊叫道：“庶长？您……您流血了？”
“流血？”徐福低头一看，黑袍上面被什么染透了。……是血。
徐福抬起手。
滴答——
血又落在了手掌上，白皙的手掌和鲜红的血，形成了鲜明的对比。那宫人已经惊骇得不能自已了，连忙快步奔出去，高声道：“快！快去请侍医！庶长受伤了！”
宫中登时就沸腾了起来。
反倒是徐福自己没什么太大的感觉。他抬手摸了摸鼻子，血是从那儿流下来的。不过徐福猛地想起了一个细节。
梦境之中，他眼睁睁看着那宫殿坍塌下来的时候，他感觉到了一阵强烈的压迫感，随后好像也有什么滴落在了他的手背上，好像是黑色的……或许也是血……
那个梦太真实了！
徐福实在难以忽视。
他强自镇定下来，坐在小榻上半天没挪动位置。
侍医是连滚带爬进到殿中来的，他一见坐在那里的徐福，气质一如既往的高冷，俊美的五官依旧迷人。
但是……这、这也没哪儿受伤啊？
侍医一头雾水地走近，这才看清，徐福的嘴上沾了点儿血。
这是吃东西不小心咬破嘴唇了？
那侍医仔细盯着徐福的唇瞧了一会儿，红红嫩嫩，饶是侍医这个年纪了，也依旧觉得看得脸红。
徐福瞧面前的老头儿面色怪异，不由得道：“我没受伤，只是突然鼻中滴了血出来。”
老头儿恍然大悟，“那应当只是心火过旺，才导致流了鼻血。”说完，他顿了顿，问道：“庶长可需要我拿药？”他是知道徐福会炼丹药的，就不知徐福是否会看上他的药了。
“嗯，备一些给我吧。”现在徐福哪里顾得上去炼药。
“诺。”老头儿应了声，叫来宫人，与她嘱咐一番，便令宫人去取药了。
“你叫什么？”徐福见老头儿有些面生，便随口问了一句。
老头儿道：“夏无且。”
夏无且？
“庶长，可是何处不对吗？”夏无且小心问道。
徐福摇了摇头，令人送他出去了，还特地令人打赏了他一番。若是没自己，这夏无且就该飞黄腾达了。毕竟史书里，写到荆轲刺秦一节，有一句是“是时，侍医夏无且以其所奉药囊提轲”。夏无且在那场刺杀中可是立了大功，后来颇得秦王重视，得了重赏。
但是如今荆轲都被换了个人，夏无且便也没有出场的机会了。
夏无且走后不久，嬴政许是也听说了徐福受伤的消息，后脚便进门来了。
“怎么回事？”嬴政眉头紧蹙，大步走到了徐福的跟前，伸手直接将徐福捞起来搂在了怀中。
宫人们见到王上这般失态的模样，也并不觉得惊奇。
一宫女走上前，低声向嬴政解释了。得知只是流了鼻血，嬴政方才松了一口气。
徐福瞧着嬴政担忧的模样，总觉得哪里不对。
蜡祭那日田味胡言的话，是不是嬴政也上心了？因而他才对自己的状况这般忧心？徐福感觉自己跟嬴政似乎一样，被紧紧拴在了一根线上，那根线哪怕是轻轻一抖动，自己和嬴政都会仿佛惊弓之鸟。
他还是得找回徐君房的记忆才行啊。
徐福轻叹一口气，他现在整个人都笼在迷雾里，什么都看不清，这种滋味真是太难受了。
“正好，有事与你说。”
“嗯，你说。”嬴政严肃地盯着他，静静等着徐福往下说。
“我忧心咸阳会地动。”
徐福并不怀疑那个梦。在这个时代，天灾太常见了。饥荒、地动、洪水……都是有可能的。徐福自己光是想一想都觉得艰辛。他们躲过了洪水，但是却还有另外的灾难。
嬴政拧起眉，口吻有些不赞同，“你又卜筮了？”
“没有，是预见到的。”
嬴政果然是对那日田味的话上了心。
“寡人知道了，你放心，寡人自会安排下去。”
嬴政对徐福的信任是毋庸置疑的，哪怕是徐福突然告诉他，天要塌下来了，嬴政也会相信的。
“好。”徐福擦了擦鼻血，喝了些水，便又接着睡觉了。
从前他们就曾经合作过，发布出地动的讯息。这次自然也一样。而且有了徐福的名头，那些百姓毫不怀疑地相信了。
城中百姓组织了转移。
而大臣们也早就见识过徐福的能力，根本不敢拿自己的小命来开玩笑，于是也组织着转移了。
咸阳城外搭建起了临时的住所，士兵们护卫着嬴政和徐福走了进去。
嬴政见徐福的脸色并不大好看，不由得问道：“怎么？”
“总觉得哪里不对。”徐福心中始终放不下。他已经驱散百姓了，但为什么心底还始终蒙着一层阴翳？
“别忧心。”嬴政摸了摸他的头顶，转头道：“将田味带过来。”
“做什么？”徐福一怔。
侍从已经出去了，很快那侍从就领着田味进来了。
田味面带微笑，问道：“王上传田味前来，可是有何事？”
嬴政对旁边的侍从使了个眼色，那侍从立即拔剑，利刃对准了田味的脖颈，田味全然没想到对方一言不合就拔剑要割他脖子，田味惊得差点变了脸色，他费了好大的劲儿，才遏制住了自己想要逃跑开的冲动。
“王……上这是何意？”
“田味先生说一说，你有何依据，说庶长能力会削减？”嬴政的口吻听上去漫不经心，但是田味却注意到嬴政的目光是冰寒的，看着他的时候，仿佛看着一个死人。田味毫不怀疑，如果自己说出口的话，不够让对方满意，很有可能下一刻自己就血洒大地了。
“这一点，庶长自己应该也清楚吧。只不过这个后果，在庶长的身上会更强烈罢了。因为庶长从前的能力太强了，他为多少个人卜筮过，为多少个人看过面相，他自己恐怕都记不清了。这次地动，又是来自庶长的卜筮结果吧？庶长明知后果，为何还要如此呢？”田味惋惜道：“这次卜筮，不仅会损害庶长本身，恐怕弄不好，卜筮的结果还会出错。”
田味的口气让嬴政极为厌恶。
“那你可知解决的办法？”嬴政冷声道。
田味身后的侍从也立即将剑逼得更近了，田味甚至感觉到了皮肤被割开的刺痛感。
一定是流血了！
田味暗暗咬牙，隐晦地憎恨了嬴政一眼，嘴上却是乖顺地道：“我也是希望庶长能恢复如常的，但是这是常态。不止庶长会如此，日后我也会如此。”
那侍从冷笑一声，欲用剑割了他的脖子。
田味吓出了一身冷汗，忙又补充道：“唯有一个法子！”
“什么法子？”
“自然是再也不用卜筮的能力，做个普通人到老便不会再损耗心力了。”
徐福闻言，在心底暗暗说了句，个屁！
但嬴政却认真思考起了这个可能性，他倒是希望如此，但他也比所有人都清楚，放在徐福的身上，徐福是决不可能做到的。
“将此人扣押起来。”嬴政终于撕去了耐心的面孔。
徐福轻叹道：“可惜了。”
田味背后的人都还没出来呢。
“不可惜。”嬴政淡淡接口道：“外人只会知晓田味在此次事件中，获得了寡人的青睐，被提了官职。他们哪里会知道田味被寡人扣押了呢？”
徐福怔了怔，“也是。”本来他们就只是为了做给别人看的，那么只要制造假象就行了，哪里管田味究竟会不会受苦呢。
“等抓到背后之人，我倒是要好好问一问田味，他那一身能力又是传承自谁，他的面相又怎么会如此诡异。”徐福道。
嬴政闻言，没有说话。
看吧，现在徐福的第一反应都是想到这些，可想而知，要从他身上剥离开卜筮的能力，那就好比剥离徐福赖以生存的东西一样，怎么可能做得到呢？
徐福说完，也发觉自己有点好笑。
将此事抛到脑后，他们直接在帐中休息了起来。
百姓们遥遥瞥见这边的帐子，纷纷安下了心。
如此过了一夜。
平安无事。
嬴政并不惊奇，依旧勒令大家在城外等候，确认完全安全无事后，方能回到城中。百姓们知道这都是为了他们好，哪里敢有异议？
那田味可就不好受了，他没想到自己一不小心装逼装过头，把自己给装进小黑屋里去了。昨日侍从将他带下去之后，便直接将他捆绑了起来，没有吃的，没有喝的，被捆起来之后冷风一吹，他就直打哆嗦。田味已经很久没有吃过这样的苦了，这个时候他才知道，秦王和那徐君房，都不是可以随意招惹的。
这一招惹，就得出事儿啊！
田味无奈，只得嘶声道：“我，我有话与秦王说！”
守在外面的士兵根本不搭理他。
“我有非常重要的话要与秦王说！与庶长有关！”
那士兵这才动了，他回头看了一眼田味，恶声道：“等着！王上见不见你，可说不准！”
田味哆嗦了一下，是冷的。
他靠着杆子，脑海中又浮现了那一日，在宫殿上空看见的异象。
他们都看不见……
就连徐君房也看不见。
田味微微一笑，不知怎的，脑中还浮现了大雨那几日，徐君房去安抚那些百姓的身影。
瞧上去还挺圣洁的，但是田味不得不说，圣洁得太碍眼了。
这些愚民，何必那样对待呢？只要对他们稍加恩惠，他们不是便会匍匐在你的脚边，将你奉若神明吗？
在等待秦王的时候，田味脑子里想了很多。
他甚至还意淫了一把，自己若是坐在至高无上的位置上，那会如何……到那时，他大约会留着徐君房吧。
秦王这样的人太过危险，倒是不能留着。
徐君房生的分明就是菟丝花的模样，失去卜筮的能力，做个普通人才好……
田味还在进行毫无边际地意淫。而这时，徐福却和嬴政一起踏了进来。
“说吧。”开口的是徐福。
田味扬起头来，还是没能从徐福的脸上看见半点渴求，又或是焦灼。田味颇觉可惜，不过他还是毫无保留地说了出来，“有一日，我前去见王上与庶长时，在殿外瞥见了异象。”
“什么异象？”徐福几乎是本能地觉得，那异象应当跟自己有关。
“宫殿的上空，黑云密布，那一块儿的天都是低垂且灰蒙的，如同一张大口，要将整个宫殿吞噬进去一般。庶长应当也见过不少异象了。这样大凶的异象，庶长应该知道，绝不是什么好征兆。”
光是听田味的描述，就会容易让人觉得毛骨悚然。
自己站在宫殿里，那不就跟站在怪物口中一样吗？
不过徐福很清楚，这可不是恐怖片或者奇幻片的世界，他半点恐惧也无。田味说得不错，这样的异象他应该是知道的。这个异象，还是他上辈子的时候，曾经在山门中见过。
那是山门中有个师傅快死了，才会出现的异象。
古籍中倒是有记载说，这种异象的出现，代表上天要收回什么东西了，或许你的灵气，或许你的能力，或许是你的性命……
反正给人算卦的相师少有长命的，因而这种异象，从来引不起什么惊奇。
徐福还在沉思中，倒是嬴政脸色变得更厉害。
当然，这时的古籍，也有对异象的记载。但是关于异象的记载呢，大部分都是这样的。红光、吉祥鸟、彩虹……都是吉兆。而这种黑气、阴云、仿佛凶兽的大口，那都是凶兆！
“这预兆了什么？”嬴政冷声问道。
“我……我也不敢确定，但会带来祸患是定然的。”田味顿了顿，还小心地补充道：“若是弄不好，或许还会牵连旁人。”他这句话说得实在太有深意，其中暗含的意思大约便是，可能会牵连到嬴政的身上。
但是嬴政根本感受不到个中的深意。
就算是感受到了，嬴政也半点不会畏惧。若是他那般畏惧多疑，又哪里会成就如今的秦王？
“没事，别紧张。”徐福突然出声了。
他先出口的话，竟然是先安抚嬴政的。
嬴政的脸色冷了冷。
“异象又如何？我为那么多人卜筮过，又怎么会乐意让天来把持我的命运呢？”
从前徐福是觉得这些东西都不可抗的，但是现在不一样了，现在他更想要试一试，如何打破那种禁锢。
嬴政脸色稍缓，“嗯，你说得对。”说罢，他紧握住徐福的手，将人带了出去。
田味愣了愣，“王上！请王上放了我！”
然而徐福和嬴政一转眼便没了影子，任他怎么嘶吼都没用。守着他的士兵似笑非笑地看了他一眼，里面分明夹杂着嘲讽。
田味死死咬牙。
他就不信徐福当真能那样强悍地挺过去！
总会再回来寻他的！
·
风吹动帐子，远处的百姓频频往这边看来，他们已经没有太多的耐性了，他们都很着急，这样一直在城外等下去实在不是个办法。
他们还要生存，还要做生意，要开店，要上工摆摊糊口。
同样的，大臣们也无比想念那舒适的府邸。一直在城外，他们都无法进行正常的生活，更没有了小朝可上。
几日尚可，但长久下去，整座城池都会受到巨大的影响。
有大臣忍不住来到了嬴政的跟前，问道：“王上，这……这样下去也不是个办法啊，庶长可知那地动究竟是何时来？”
徐福就站在一旁，他没有说话。
难道这次预测也出错了？但那个梦……
他不该这样依赖于预测的能力，徐福在心底轻叹了一口气，等那大臣被打发走之后，他才转头问嬴政：“地动仪可有动静？”
“寡人差人去看了。”
徐福点点头，静静等待了起来。
现在他俨然陷入了一个两难的境地。选择让这些人回去，还是不回去？如果地动是真的，只是迟迟未来，那他们贸然回去，因此损失惨重，那该如何？可若是并无地动，这样耽误着众人，届时徐福承受得了那样的指责吗？他辛苦经营到现在的声望，到那时会不会骤然崩塌？
没多久，被派遣出去的人回来了。
那人擦了擦额上的汗，小心翼翼道：“地动仪，并、并无动静。”
徐福坐在那里没有说话。
这期间谁也不敢开口，生怕触怒了徐福，而嬴政则是担忧徐福产生自我怀疑。
“回去吧。”徐福沉声道。
如果继续耽搁下去，城中的生产链就会断裂，这对于咸阳城，包括城中百姓来说，可都不是什么好事。
两者取其一，既然地动仪没有异象，那他们就回去吧。
如今相比之下，或许那地动仪比他的预测和卜筮更为可靠些。
“回去之后，也嘱咐众人夜晚小心些，熬过这个月便没事了。”徐福低声道。
嬴政担忧地看了一眼徐福，最后却是应道：“好。”徐福如何说，他便如何做就是了。现在这样拖延着确实不是个办法，这或许是最好的处理方式了。百姓们如今应当也熟练地掌握逃难方法了，届时若是地动来临，他们应当知晓往哪里走了。
做了决定之后，徐福心底就松了口气。
不管之后会引起什么样的后果，他都会承担。
决定都做下了，自然是很快，嬴政也亲自下了命令，于是一行人又开始往城中挪。
徐福独自坐在帐中，有些懊恼。
这次他是太着急了，被那梦境骇得并不加核实，就匆匆告诉了嬴政。若是当真被那预测能力给坑了，他也怪不了别人，只能说是吃个大教训了。
命令一下，自然有不解的，甚至还有隐隐埋怨的。
这样大费周章地让他们迁出来了，他们出于对庶长的信任也就老实出来了，但是现在，却又让他们再回到城中，什么地动，根本没有！实在令人恼火！白提着心这么久！
不过多数百姓倒没想那么多，他们松了一口气，只觉得是好事。
没有地动来，那他们的房屋就不会垮塌，他们不会受灾，不会无家可归，也不会有人受伤生病，那可不是个好事儿吗？虽然是折腾了些。但是因为有过上次不相信徐福的经历，这一次大家反倒是对徐福极为信任的，哪怕是被这样折腾，这些百姓也并没有指责徐福的意思。
前几天下大雨，还是庶长来安抚的他们咧！
在士兵的组织下，他们安然有序地回到了咸阳城中。
秦国官员们和他们的王上一起，落在了最后进城。
徐福和嬴政坐在马车中，慢慢往城门的方向接近。徐福的情绪有些低落，嬴政瞥了一眼，忍不住伸手握了握他的手背。
此时田味还被绑在柱子上，而那根柱子由两个士兵抬着，就这样将田味，像是抬猪一样，给抬进城去了。中途还有不少人打量他，田味不愿丢脸，便刻意遮了遮，于是倒没人知道他是谁，只当是有人惹怒了王上，才被这样捆住了。
中途还有不懂事的小孩儿冲着他讥笑起来。
田味心头窝火至极。
难道这些百姓，这些大臣，就不怨恨徐福吗？怎么还有空来讥笑他？
那些被他惦记着的大臣们走在了前面。
尉缭和蒙恬走在一处，尉缭眉头紧锁，久久不语。
蒙恬问他：“可是心下忧心这地动？”
“我并非忧心此事，我忧心的是君房，君房近来……不太对劲。”
“勿要忧心，君房有王上护着，自然不会出事。”蒙恬虽然不明所以，但还是出声宽慰道。
尉缭正要点头，却听前面两名大臣，低声交谈道：“王上对那徐君房，是不是太过信任了些？”
“不是向来如此么？王上对他倍加宠信，这有何奇怪之处？”
“不，我说的不是这个！你们难道就不担忧吗？王上对徐君房信任至此，日后怕是会酿成大祸啊！”
“何出此言？”
“你们想想，从前那昌平君是如何出事的？你们再想想，后来徐君房失踪，王上是如何对待的？徐君房想如何，王上便迁就着他如何，甚至不顾自身安危，也要去保住徐君房，这还了得？现在又因为徐君房一句话，王上便不加思考，让我们从城中迁出，到现在却成了个笑话！细细一想，难道你们不会觉得恐惧吗？”
……
尉缭的脸色登时变得极为难看。
蒙恬也是跟着脸色一冷。
而那大臣还在说话。
大臣摇摇头，一脸痛色道：“这样下去，徐君房还不是一句话，便能要了我等性命？他与那褒姒、妲己，有何区别？”
若是徐福听见大臣此言，定会忍不住笑出声来。
哈！
把他比做妲己、褒姒！
真是瞧得起他！
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu had experienced many such moments of waiting before, but none had been as agonizing as this.

He listened quietly to the sound of rain against the stone steps outside.

The rhythmic patter of the rain was far too hypnotic, and before long, sleepiness washed over Xu Fu, and he drifted off without realizing it. Darkness enveloped him, and he felt as if he had become a lonely soul, drifting aimlessly through this space. At first, Xu Fu thought he was about to see visions of the future again, but he kept his eyes wide open for a long time and saw nothing at all.

It wasn't until the sound of footsteps reached his ears that Xu Fu was startled and involuntarily opened his eyes.

Light spilled into the darkness, and Xu Fu suddenly became clear-headed.

Ying Zheng was leaning over him, staring intently; when Xu Fu opened his eyes, their gazes met.

"You were sleeping too soundly," Ying Zheng frowned. "I called you for a long time, but you wouldn't wake up."

The palace attendants were still standing by, and Xu Fu was slightly stunned. He turned to ask the attendant, "How long have I been asleep?"

"Five hours."

Five hours?

That was roughly the time since he had finished breakfast and leaned back on the small couch to nap; he had slept until Ying Zheng returned without waking once.

Was his old ailment acting up again? Xu Fu was truly baffled, but he noticed that the sound of rain had stopped.

The rain had stopped.

Xu Fu let out a slow breath.

As long as the rain had stopped, it meant he hadn't been wrong. However, observing celestial phenomena wasn't foolproof; after all, anyone with a little experience could tell whether the next day would be sunny or rainy, except for those rare times when the heavens were in a bad mood and insisted on changing their face.

"It's nothing. I'm a bit hungry, let's eat," Xu Fu said, brushing off his strange condition.

Surprisingly, Ying Zheng didn't press him further. He nodded, hooked his arm around Xu Fu's waist, and helped him up. Once they were seated, the attendants laid out food directly in front of the couch. Feeling soft and limp from his long sleep, Xu Fu simply began to eat. After the food was served, he was about to turn and speak to Ying Zheng to reassure him that the rain wouldn't cause any more trouble, but the words he meant to say suddenly got stuck in his throat.

Ying Zheng was actually zoning out!

Xu Fu had never seen Ying Zheng like this; what could he be thinking about to make him fall into such a stupor?

"A-Zheng?"

At the sound of Xu Fu's voice, Ying Zheng immediately turned his head. "I've been a bit tired these past few days. Let's eat first."

"Mm," Xu Fu replied, though he was already planning to refine some pills—preferably ones that could calm the mind and spirit.

Because the rain had stopped, Xu Fu was in a fairly good mood. Even though he had become more prone to sleepiness, at least it now seemed that Tian Wei’s words had been intended to irritate him.

After the meal, the two took a walk in the palace. However, Ying Zheng remained somewhat distracted, so Xu Fu couldn't chat with him. They finished their walk in silence, bathed, and went to bed together. Strangely enough, despite having slept for so long during the day, Xu Fu was still able to fall asleep.

Two days passed like this, but Xu Fu did not see the light rain he had expected.

He looked up and saw golden sunlight. He could almost imagine the smiles on the faces of the common people when they saw the sun.

It was normal for weather predictions to be wrong; after all, even weather forecasts in later generations sometimes failed.

Xu Fu calmed his heart, waiting for the verification of his next divination.

Fusu had been sent by Ying Zheng to oversee water conservancy and returned to the palace less and less. However, when he had returned a while ago, he looked worried, as if troubled by something.

Let's see if he can resolve that matter this time...

·

In the twentieth year of King Zheng of Qin, Ying Zheng ordered Wang Ben to lead an army to attack Chu, and simultaneously dispatched a large force under Li Xin and Qiang Hui to reinforce Wang Jian.

Xu Fu did not wait for the defeat in the war against Yan, nor did he wait for Fusu to return to the palace. He had no idea what the outcome was...

In the blink of an eye, a month slipped away.

Huhai walked up to Xu Fu, sneezing and sniffling. "Father, my head hurts..."

Huhai had been greedy for the cool air and accidentally caught a cold. He had just taken his medicine and crawled out of bed; his cheeks were flushed red, his eyes were red, and his nose was red—he looked pitiful to the extreme. Usually, Fusu took care of him, but with Fusu away, Huhai automatically sought out Xu Fu.

The sick Huhai looked even more fragile, making one's heart melt instantly.

Xu Fu stroked his cheek and let Huhai nestle into his arms.

Does this count as a fulfillment?

Xu Fu didn't realize that the seeds of doubt had already been planted in his heart.

The more he emphasized to himself that a reduction in his abilities was no big deal, the more he deepened his conviction that his powers were indeed waning. He had subconsciously accepted Tian Wei's words.

Holding Huhai, Xu Fu suddenly remembered something from a long time ago.

In his past life, his half-baked master had told him that fortune-telling was an overdraft of one's own life. Knowing things you shouldn't know—you might gain wealth and status through this path in your previous life, but you would have to pay with your life in the next. Don't dream of escaping; no one can escape...

Can no one escape?

He glanced at Huhai in his arms, then thought of Fusu away on duty, and Ying Zheng, who was still laboring over documents.

...This life is different; he didn't really want to trade his life for it in this one.

And there were still so many mysteries left unsolved!

Xu Fu gently patted Huhai's head.

He would look through ancient texts another day to see if there were any relevant records. He wasn't afraid of his abilities fading; he was afraid of losing his life.

They say fortune-tellers don't divine for themselves, but he could foresee his own danger—was this a bad sign? Xu Fu didn't know; he had never experienced it before.

By the time Huhai’s illness gradually improved, Xu Fu had flipped through many books, but unfortunately, there were no relevant records at all.

Xu Fu thought of Hou Sheng again.

If he were here, perhaps he would know something?

After all, they were both in the divination business; Hou Sheng should know more than he did.

But no matter how much effort Xu Fu spent, he could never find Hou Sheng.

The image of Hou Sheng’s face flashed through his mind, and he felt a sense of regret.

Bo Zhou whispered from the side, "With the wars breaking out now, that Grand Diviner Hou... he might be dead." This was the most likely outcome Bo Zhou could think of.

Xu Fu didn't want him to be dead.

Xu Fu occasionally wanted to exchange ideas with someone, but the person he wanted to spar with was definitely not someone like Han Zhong, and certainly not someone like Tian Wei. Only Hou Sheng was worthy of that!

"Keep looking..."

Bo Zhou didn't try to persuade him otherwise; he nodded and accepted the order. Whatever his master commanded, he would obey.

Xu Fu felt an indescribable melancholy. He waved for Huhai to come over and rubbed his fluffy head. That felt better. And since Huhai was being extremely obedient and letting him rub it, it felt even better.

……

Not long after, news of victory came from Wang Jian’s attack on Yan.

Xu Fu didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

A victory—logically, he should be happy for Ying Zheng; but on the other hand, it proved that his own divination of defeat was a wrong result.

Xu Fu rubbed his temples, and when he took his hand away, he noticed his fingertips were trembling slightly.

Was his heart afraid?

Xu Fu set aside the silk cloth on his lap and walked over to a small couch, collapsing onto it to sleep.

And this time, Xu Fu had another dream.

What would he dream of this time? Xu Fu felt a faint sense of excitement and anticipation.

The dream was still a void of darkness, and he didn't know how much time had passed...

Lightning flashed and thunder roared, a great gale blew, and strange phenomena emerged, as if some ancient beast had let out a roar that shook the heavens and the earth, and then the world truly shook.

Mountains crumbling and the earth splitting—that was likely what it was like.

By the light of the lightning, Xu Fu saw the towering palace collapsing, with a force that destroyed everything in its path... the scene was terrifying.

Xu Fu found that he couldn't move, and could only watch helplessly as the collapsing palace pressed down on him.

A gasp of shock burst from his throat.

"Swish," he opened his eyes.

The small couch beneath him was trembling slightly.

Was he trembling uncontrollably? By the time the attendants noticed Xu Fu had woken up and hurried in, Xu Fu had already returned to normal, showing no signs of the terror he had just displayed.

Xu Fu propped himself up and looked out the window.

The sunlight was perfect; there was no sign of any natural or man-made disaster.

But that dream...

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, only to hear the attendant beside him suddenly scream, "Shuzhang? You... you are bleeding?"

"Bleeding?" Xu Fu looked down and saw his black robe stained with something. ...It was blood.

Xu Fu raised his hand.

Drip—

Blood fell onto his palm again; the fair palm and the bright red blood formed a sharp contrast. The attendant was so terrified that she quickly ran out, shouting, "Quick! Go get the imperial physician! The Shuzhang is injured!"

The palace was instantly in an uproar.

Xu Fu himself didn't feel much. He raised his hand to touch his nose; the blood was flowing from there. But Xu Fu suddenly remembered a detail.

In the dream, when he watched the palace collapse, he felt a strong sense of pressure, and then it seemed something dripped onto the back of his hand, it seemed black... perhaps it was blood too...

That dream was too real!

Xu Fu found it hard to ignore.

He forced himself to remain calm, sitting on the small couch for a long time without moving.

The imperial physician came scrambling into the hall. When he saw Xu Fu sitting there, his demeanor as cold and aloof as ever, his handsome features still charming.

But... this, there was no injury anywhere?

The physician walked closer, confused, and only then saw the blood on Xu Fu's lips.

Had he accidentally bitten his lip while eating?

The physician stared at Xu Fu's lips for a while; they were red and tender, and even at his age, the physician felt himself blushing.

Seeing the old man's strange expression, Xu Fu couldn't help but say, "I'm not injured, my nose just suddenly started bleeding."

The old man suddenly realized, "That must be due to excessive internal heat, causing a nosebleed." After speaking, he paused and asked, "Does the Shuzhang need me to get some medicine?" He knew Xu Fu could refine pills, so he didn't know if Xu Fu would even look at his medicine.

"Mm, prepare some for me." Xu Fu was in no state to refine medicine now.

"Nuo," the old man replied, calling an attendant to give instructions before sending her to fetch the medicine.

"What is your name?" Xu Fu asked casually, seeing the old man was a stranger.

The old man said, "Xia Wuju."

Xia Wuju?

"Shuzhang, is something wrong?" Xia Wuju asked cautiously.

Xu Fu shook his head, had him escorted out, and even specifically ordered a reward for him. If not for him, this Xia Wuju would have risen to great heights. After all, in the history books, the section on Jing Ke’s assassination attempt on the King of Qin contained the line, "At this time, the imperial physician Xia Wuju threw his medicine bag at Ke." Xia Wuju had performed a great service in that assassination and was later highly valued and heavily rewarded by the King of Qin.

But now that Jing Ke had been replaced by someone else, Xia Wuju had no chance to make an appearance.

Not long after Xia Wuju left, Ying Zheng, having likely heard the news of Xu Fu’s injury, followed him in.

"What happened?" Ying Zheng frowned deeply, strode to Xu Fu’s side, and reached out to pull him into his arms.

The attendants were not surprised to see the King in such a state of agitation.

A palace maid stepped forward and whispered an explanation to Ying Zheng. Upon learning it was just a nosebleed, Ying Zheng finally breathed a sigh of relief.

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng’s worried expression and felt something was wrong.

Had Ying Zheng taken Tian Wei’s nonsense on the day of the Wax Festival to heart? Was that why he was so worried about his condition? Xu Fu felt as if he and Ying Zheng were tied to the same string; even if that string were to tremble slightly, both he and Ying Zheng would be like startled birds.

He still had to recover the memories of Xu Junfang.

Xu Fu sighed softly; he was currently shrouded in fog, unable to see anything clearly, and this feeling was truly unbearable.

"Actually, I have something to tell you."

"Mm, tell me." Ying Zheng stared at him seriously, waiting quietly for Xu Fu to continue.

"I am worried there will be an earthquake in Xianyang."

Xu Fu did not doubt the dream. In this era, natural disasters were too common. Famine, earthquakes, floods... all were possible. Xu Fu felt the hardship just thinking about it. They had escaped the flood, but there were other disasters.

Ying Zheng knitted his brows, his tone somewhat disapproving. "You divined again?"

"No, I foresaw it."

Ying Zheng had indeed taken Tian Wei’s words from that day to heart.

"I understand. Don't worry, I will make the arrangements."

Ying Zheng’s trust in Xu Fu was unquestionable; even if Xu Fu had suddenly told him the sky was falling, Ying Zheng would have believed him.

"Good." Xu Fu wiped his nosebleed, drank some water, and went back to sleep.

They had cooperated before to issue warnings about earthquakes. This time was naturally the same. And with Xu Fu’s reputation, the common people believed it without a doubt.

The people in the city organized an evacuation.

The officials had also witnessed Xu Fu’s abilities and dared not gamble with their own lives, so they also organized their own evacuations.

Temporary shelters were set up outside Xianyang, and soldiers escorted Ying Zheng and Xu Fu inside.

Seeing Xu Fu’s poor complexion, Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask, "What is it?"

"I just feel something is wrong." Xu Fu couldn't let it go. He had dispersed the people, but why was there still a shadow over his heart?

"Don't worry." Ying Zheng patted his head and turned to say, "Bring Tian Wei here."

"What for?" Xu Fu was startled.

The attendant had already gone out, and soon led Tian Wei inside.

Tian Wei smiled and asked, "The King has summoned me, is there something you need?"

Ying Zheng gave a look to the attendant beside him, who immediately drew his sword, the sharp blade pointed at Tian Wei’s neck. Tian Wei had never expected the other party to draw a sword to cut his throat without a word. He was so shocked his face almost changed color, and he used all his strength to suppress the urge to run away.

"What... what is the meaning of this, Your Majesty?"

"Mr. Tian, tell me, what evidence do you have to say that the Shuzhang’s abilities will diminish?" Ying Zheng’s tone sounded nonchalant, but Tian Wei noticed Ying Zheng’s gaze was icy, as if looking at a dead man. Tian Wei had no doubt that if his answer didn't satisfy the other party, he might be bleeding out on the ground the next moment.

"The Shuzhang should know this himself. It’s just that the consequences will be more severe for him. Because the Shuzhang’s abilities were too strong before; he has divined for so many people, read so many faces, he probably can't even remember them all himself. This earthquake is also from the Shuzhang’s divination, right? Knowing the consequences, why would the Shuzhang do this?" Tian Wei said with regret, "This divination will not only harm the Shuzhang himself, but if things go wrong, the result of the divination might also be incorrect."

Ying Zheng found Tian Wei’s tone extremely disgusting.

"Then do you know a solution?" Ying Zheng said coldly.

The attendant behind Tian Wei immediately pressed the sword closer, and Tian Wei even felt the stinging pain of his skin being cut.

It must be bleeding!

Tian Wei gritted his teeth, harboring a hidden hatred for Ying Zheng, but said submissively, "I also hope the Shuzhang can recover, but this is the norm. It’s not just the Shuzhang who will be like this; I will be too in the future."

The attendant sneered, wanting to cut his throat.

Tian Wei broke into a cold sweat and hurriedly added, "There is only one way!"

"What way?"

"Naturally, to never use divination abilities again and live as an ordinary person until old age; then there will be no more drain on your spirit."

Hearing this, Xu Fu thought to himself, "Bullshit!"

But Ying Zheng seriously considered this possibility. He wished it were so, but he also knew better than anyone that for Xu Fu, this was absolutely impossible.

"Lock this man up." Ying Zheng finally dropped his patient facade.

Xu Fu sighed lightly, "What a pity."

The people behind Tian Wei hadn't even appeared yet.

"It’s not a pity," Ying Zheng said calmly. "Outsiders will only know that Tian Wei has gained my favor in this incident and has been promoted. How would they know that Tian Wei has been locked up by me?"

Xu Fu was stunned, "That’s true." They were just doing this for show anyway, so as long as they created the illusion, it didn't matter if Tian Wei suffered.

"When we catch the person behind him, I want to ask Tian Wei properly who he inherited his abilities from, and why his face looks so strange," Xu Fu said.

Ying Zheng didn't speak upon hearing this.

See, Xu Fu’s first reaction was to think about these things. It was clear that stripping away his divination abilities would be like stripping away the very thing Xu Fu relied on to survive—how could that be possible?

After saying this, Xu Fu also found himself somewhat amusing.

Putting the matter behind them, they rested directly in the tent.

The common people glimpsed the tents from afar and felt relieved.

Another night passed.

Nothing happened.

Ying Zheng was not surprised and still ordered everyone to wait outside the city, only returning when they were confirmed to be completely safe. The people knew this was for their own good, so how could they have any objections?

Tian Wei, however, was having a miserable time. He hadn't expected that by showing off too much, he would end up in a dark room. After the attendant took him away yesterday, he was tied up without food or drink, and the cold wind blowing on him made him shiver. Tian Wei hadn't suffered like this in a long time, and only then did he realize that the King of Qin and that Xu Junfang were not people to be trifled with.

Provoking them led to trouble!

Tian Wei had no choice but to rasp, "I... I have something to tell the King of Qin!"

The soldiers guarding outside ignored him.

"I have something very important to tell the King of Qin! It concerns the Shuzhang!"

The soldier finally moved, looked back at Tian Wei, and said viciously, "Wait! Whether the King sees you or not is not up to me!"

Tian Wei shivered; it was the cold.

Leaning against the pole, the vision he had seen in the sky above the palace that day appeared in his mind again.

They couldn't see it...

Even Xu Junfang couldn't see it.

Tian Wei smiled slightly. For some reason, the image of Xu Junfang comforting the people during those days of heavy rain also appeared in his mind.

He looked quite saintly, but Tian Wei had to say, it was too saintly to be pleasant.

Why treat these foolish people like that? If you just give them a little favor, wouldn't they crawl at your feet and worship you like a god?

While waiting for the King of Qin, Tian Wei thought about a lot.

He even fantasized about what it would be like if he were sitting in the supreme position... By then, he would probably keep Xu Junfang.

A person like the King of Qin was too dangerous and couldn't be kept.

Xu Junfang clearly looked like a dodder flower; it would be better if he lost his divination abilities and lived as an ordinary person...

Tian Wei was still lost in his wild fantasies when Xu Fu and Ying Zheng walked in.

"Speak," Xu Fu said.

Tian Wei raised his head, still unable to see any craving or anxiety on Xu Fu’s face. Tian Wei felt it was a pity, but he spoke without reservation, "One day, when I went to see the King and the Shuzhang, I glimpsed a strange phenomenon outside the hall."

"What phenomenon?" Xu Fu felt instinctively that it should have something to do with him.

"Above the palace, dark clouds were dense, and the sky in that area was low and gray, like a giant mouth, as if it wanted to swallow the entire palace. The Shuzhang must have seen many strange phenomena. You should know that such an ominous sign is definitely not a good omen."

Just listening to Tian Wei’s description was enough to make one’s skin crawl.

If you were standing in the palace, wouldn't that be like standing in the mouth of a monster?

However, Xu Fu knew very well that this wasn't a horror or fantasy movie world, and he felt no fear at all. Tian Wei was right; he should know this phenomenon. He had seen this phenomenon in his past life at the mountain gate.

It was a phenomenon that only appeared when a master in the mountain gate was about to die.

Ancient texts recorded that the appearance of this phenomenon meant that the heavens were about to take something back—perhaps your spiritual energy, perhaps your abilities, or perhaps your life...

In any case, few fortune-tellers lived long, so such phenomena never caused much surprise.

While Xu Fu was lost in thought, Ying Zheng’s expression became even more severe.

Of course, at this time, ancient texts also had records of strange phenomena. But regarding these records, most were like this: red light, auspicious birds, rainbows... all were good omens. And this black mist, dark clouds, like the mouth of a fierce beast—those were all bad omens!

"What does this portend?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.
