第240章
chapters.source_text:
那几个乞丐见徐福一来，便将他们挡在了后面，哪里还有乞讨的机会？看着徐福的目光登时就变得凶恶了起来，他们站起身，正欲将徐福驱逐走。
周围旁观的人，不由得吊起了心。
此时在两旁摆摊的摊主，对视一眼，起身猛地扑将上去，将那几名乞丐按倒在了地上，口中大骂：“若要讨饭，到一边去！碍着我们作甚！”
摊主心知徐福站在那里，才能为他们带来更多的客人，而乞丐蹲在那里，却是会将想要前来的客人都吓跑。毕竟谁会愿意往乞丐的方向跑呢？
那几个乞丐被踩在地上的时候就已经怂了，等摊主松开他们的时候，他们连看也不敢多看徐福一眼，赶紧跑了。若论看人眼色，没有比他们更利害的了，既然现在占不到便宜，那也只有赶紧跑了，好歹免了一顿打。
徐福：“……”他还全然没反应过来呢，事情竟然就已经结束了？
乞丐被赶走以后，徐福当然就能回到昨日的位置上，继续摆摊了。
两边的摊主对于他要卜筮算卦，半点不感兴趣，毕竟大家又都不是同行，前来卜卦的人少，但是会被他们摊子吸引走的可就多了。
没一会儿，摊主们脸上便挂满了笑容。对比之下，徐福这边就显得清冷多了。徐福顿觉自己噎了一口老血。明明这些客人都是被自己吸引来的，怎么最后都买了别人家的东西？
这一日，徐福又是枯坐一日，好奇的人倒是增多了，但却唯独没有前来找他卜卦的人，更没有凑到他跟前，说“你好眼熟”的人。直到日落西山，徐福收拾起东西打算回客栈休息了，他面前的人群也变得寥落了起来。
此时却有一名女子紧张地攥了攥裙子，走到了徐福的跟前。
“先、先生，我能，能卜一卦吗？”
“请。”徐福本意是想请她先坐，但是低头一看，哦，面前连块布都没有，总不能让人家一屁股坐在地面上吧。
女子倒是并未觉得有何不对，她一撩衣裙，跽坐下来，动作还挺标准的，如果忽略掉她屁股底下就是地面的话。
徐福欣赏地看了她一眼。
女子方才虽然表现得很是紧张，但这样的时候却极是大方，说坐就坐，不拘小节。
女子被徐福这一眼瞧得有些脸红，她低声道：“我想请先生为我，卜一卦姻缘。”
噢。
就是算桃花运嘛。
徐福指了指面前的道具，“姑娘择其一。”
当然，徐福根本不会用到这些东西，只是这个逼还是要装的。
女子大约是觉得龟甲看起来最为了不得，于是指了指龟甲那黝黑的背，“这……这可以么？”
“可以。”徐福装模作样地借了隔壁的火盆，用龟甲卜了一卦，实际上他说的却是根据那女子面相得出的结论，“姑娘可是急于求到另一半？”
纵然那女子再大方，说到这样的事，她还是羞红了脸。
幸好周围的人都离得远，倒也不会在听见之后，而让那女子觉得尴尬。
女子低声道：“嗯。”
“姑娘的姻缘不能急，还需等候，不出三年便会到来。而这三年之内，姑娘自然不是白白等着，姑娘还要扭转一下运道，方能得一个好姻缘。”其实一般面对算姻缘的姑娘，徐福都会劝她们不要急。这世上，有些东西是万万急不得的，尤其是姻缘。有几个匆匆结了婚的人，能落到一个好结局的？这般人生大事，是值得等待的，一时心急迷了眼，那可就是大麻烦了。
女子先是有些失落，尔后双眼一亮，道：“如何扭转？”
“姑娘家中可是有布坊？”
女子眨了眨眼，满面惊讶之色，“先生怎会知晓？”
因为你一身染料的味道啊。
“自是卜出来的。”徐福道。
女子面上敬佩之色更浓，毕竟谁都知道徐福是个生面孔，打外地来的，他怎么会知道这城中的人，家中都是做什么的了？那也只有卜筮可得了。
“扭转之法极为简单，姑娘努力经营家中布坊，运道也会随之往上走，那时，姑娘的姻缘说不得便要提前了。”徐福告诉她不出三年，而实际上从女子的面相来看，一年多便会到来。之所以要说三年，徐福是希望面前的姑娘，到时候哪怕姻缘来了的，也应多加思虑，而不是贸然走入婚姻。
“这……这样简单？”那女子呆了呆，没想到对方什么也未让她买。
“是，就如此简单，这法子可是半点妨害也无，姑娘可以试一试。”徐福淡淡道。
其实这个所谓的扭转之法跟卜筮相术根本扯不上关系。悉心经营布坊，不过是为了让女子变得更为独立，不管是精神还是金钱上。如此过不了多久，女子就会变得更为坚韧，更为聪慧。而且有句话是如何说的？认真起来的人最可爱。不分男女，各自都有专注的事业时，精神面貌都是极为出彩的。到那时，优秀又聪明的女子，怎么会寻不到自己的姻缘？
虽然想一想上辈子，很多女性变得优秀之后，反倒不需要姻缘了。
徐福在心底轻咳一声，将这些联想从脑子里扔了出去。
女子欢天喜地站起身来，冲着徐福躬腰道：“我信先生！”对方说得不错，这种扭转运道的法子，又半点没有妨害，试一试又如何？
女子掏出了钱币，放了一把到徐福的跟前，问道：“先生，如此可够了？”
“够了。”徐福说完，用绢布包了些土灰递给了女子。
“这？”
“拿着吧，有它辅助，自会更好。”
那土灰，里头有木屑，也有龟甲壳，还有点儿泥土。龟甲通灵，木屑为木，木生火，泥土，土生金。火和金，自然都是好的寓意。这不过是个再简单不过的，帮助运势升腾直上的法子。当然，这样的辅助也很容易被破坏。不过对于女子来说，现在够用就行了。
女子笑得极为灿烂，她将绢布捏在手中，转身离开了。徐福当然不会知晓，那女子转过身去后，心头还念叨了好一会儿，为什么自己的姻缘不是这个男子呢？她上前本来就只是为了，先与对方搭上话而已，哪里是正经去卜姻缘的，没想到倒是真得了这么嘱咐。
见女子做了第一个吃螃蟹的人，其他人便有些躁动了，不过他们又不卜姻缘，因而也没有急于动作。倒是有对夫妻，盯着徐福瞧了半天。
徐福耳尖，听见他们小声道：“他瞧起来好生眼熟啊……”
“是啊……”
徐福冲着他们招了招手，“二位，瞧我眼熟？”
那对夫妻一听徐福对他们说话了，登时反倒有些慌张了，“没、没有，许是、许是看错了……”那对夫妻说完，便赶紧离开了，像是后头有什么在追一样。
徐福无奈。难道他以前还在城中做过什么坏事吗？徐福的心往下沉了沉，不至于吧。徐君房应当不是个坏人啊，而且他的日记中也并没有写……呃，好吧，或许是写了，但是绢布被毁得差不多，他自然也就看不见了。徐福按捺下心中的担忧，收拾起东西先行离开了。
他还是继续等等看吧。
可惜这时阿武不在身边，徐福虽然不待见阿武，但他也知道阿武的武力值不错，若是有阿武在身边，他就不用担忧那么多了，可以放心大胆地继续摆摊，而不会担忧徐君房过去有没有得罪过城中的人。
这一夜，徐福睡得不太安稳，他甚至频频梦到嬴政。
醒来后，徐福在床榻上呆坐了许久。何时他会这样思念嬴政了？
徐福揉了揉额头，翻身起来。
他是真的想要快点回咸阳，或许还是出于直觉吧，徐福总觉得频频梦到嬴政，并不是什么好的征兆。
第三日，徐福又来到了那个摊位上。
这一日围观的人变少了。因为就算徐福长得再好看，他们也不至于将目光死死黏在徐福的身上，并且为了打量徐福，而放弃正常的生活。
徐福坐在那里都觉得有些百无聊赖了。幸好墙底下，日光并不算强烈，不然他还当真等不下去了。
就在上午快要过去的时候，徐福长舒一口气，低头整理跟前的东西。
一个略略苍老的声音骤然响起了，“你、你……”
你什么？
徐福被惊了一跳，他面色冷淡地抬头看过去，只见跟前站着一个穿着朴素的老妇人，那老妇人走路都有些不稳，眼皮也耷拉了下来，只留出两条缝来看东西，满脸的皱纹像是橘子皮一般。老妇人这般模样，实在有些吓人。但是徐福可以看出，对方没有恶意。
“你……”徐福刚开了个口，老妇人就突然冲着他跪下来了。
徐福这次是真的被吓着了，这老妇人做什么？
周围的人也被老妇人出乎意料的举动吓了一跳，忙围上前来，高声道：“陈阿婆你干什么啊？”虽然徐福长得好看，但是当他和老人摆在一起的时候，其他人当然自发地认为，徐福是不是欺负了老人。
接收到周围人谴责的目光，徐福：“……”他还什么都没做呢。
那老妇人挥开了身边想要上前去扶她的人，她死死盯着徐福，用年老嘶哑的声音道：“您又回来了！没想到，我在死前还能再见您一面！”
周围的人都惊呆了。
“陈阿婆你说什么啊？”
“陈阿婆你认识他吗？”
徐福也惊了惊。他等到第三日了，原以为线索都等不来了，谁知道突然出来一个老妇人，竟然开口便说出了这样的话。这老妇人定然是认识他的，她曾经见过徐君房！并且还和徐君房有着不小的接触！
有人注意到陈阿婆称呼对方，语气都极为客气尊敬，这些人颇有些摸不着头脑，此人究竟是谁啊？陈阿婆在他们城中可是颇有名气的，谁人都知晓陈阿婆，现在因着陈阿婆的缘故，也对跟前的人更为好奇了。
“您认识我？”徐福出声问她，尽管此时徐福心底再惊讶，他面上也丝毫不显，连说话的语速都依旧不紧不慢的。
陈阿婆看着他，眼中闪过怀念之色，道：“您与过去并没有多少变化。只是我老了太多，您是认不出我了吧。”
徐福没说话。
陈阿婆笑了笑，露出了漏风的牙齿。
她的模样看起来实在不怎么慈祥，但是徐福却莫名地从她的身上感觉到了温柔。
“多谢您当初尽心尽力的指点，虽然最后我那儿子还是死了，但我对您的感激仍在。我听人说城中来了一位卜卦的先生，便猜到应当是您，于是便独自前来了。”陈阿婆又道。
指点过她儿子？
徐福心中疑惑堆积到了一起，但面上却是不显，他淡淡点头，道：“多年前的事，不足以提。”
陈阿婆又笑了，“您还是如此。”她顿了顿，道：“您如今住于何处？若是不嫌弃，便还是到我家中住下吧。”
徐福心中一动，“好。”
“您还是那样爽快。”
每次听到陈阿婆说“还是那样”的时候，徐福心底就升起了怪异感，因为他很清楚自己和徐君房是分割开的两个灵魂，会听到这样的话，还真是奇特。不过想一想，或许徐君房在陈阿婆的心底原本就是个神化的形象，所以恐怕不管自己做什么、说什么，陈阿婆都会觉得自己不曾改变。
等到了想要的东西，徐福当然也不会继续摆摊下去了，他收拾起了东西，道：“在此处等我。”
陈阿婆点了点头。
徐福回到了客栈，很快办了退房，同时也拿走了所有的行李包袱。那客栈距离他摆摊的地方并不远，不过等徐福出来的时候，陈阿婆身边已经有两名妙龄女子，将她堪堪扶住了。那两名女子穿得倒是并不俗，而且模样在这样的城中，也算得上是美人了。
这难道是陈阿婆的女儿？
徐福瞧着觉得极为怪异。那陈阿婆的穿着打扮和她们可全然不一样啊。前者像是贫苦之家出来的，后者却像是富家小姐。
“先生，您先请。”陈阿婆见徐福出来了，便立即对徐福做了个请的手势。
这时，其他人看着徐福的目光微微变了，忍不住低声议论起来，“陈阿婆跟他什么关系啊？”“多年前陈阿婆的儿子是他救的吗？”“这人真的那么厉害吗？早知道我也找他卜一卦试试了。”“是胡说吧，他不过是个方士，又不会岐黄之术，怎么救人？”“但是陈阿婆不会说谎啊……”
这些议论声都收入了徐福的耳中，他想，陈阿婆的儿子是怎么一回事，到时候应该能从陈阿婆的口中问出来。说不定陈阿婆口中还能说出更多关于徐君房的事。
虽然要从别人的口中知道关于自己的事，听起来很怪异，但是徐福也的确只有这样的渠道了。
徐福走在前，那两名妙龄女子在他身后指路。很快，他们就停在了一座府邸之外，徐福仰头一看，上面并没有牌匾，但是光从外面看，徐福就能看出这府邸应该是有钱人家才能住的。那陈阿婆的确并非贫穷之家出来的。她作如此打扮，应该也只是年老了，便不重这些身外之物了。
“先生请。”妙龄女子道。
徐福踏了进去，等进门之后，徐福才发现，外面看起来气派，但里头，却不如尉缭、姚贾他们的府邸那般。因为这府中的花草树木明显是没有专人打理，而且进门之后，徐福也没有见着什么下人。这倒是奇怪了。
陈阿婆叹道：“我那儿子去后，我便将下人都遣散了。香儿，玥儿，都是我后来收养的孤女。”陈阿婆笑了笑，“香儿，玥儿，你们都得多谢先生，若无先生，你们与我便也没有这个缘分了。”
两名女子闻言，立即朝着徐福躬身见礼了。
“收养之事，是我与你说的？”
“是啊，我那儿子造了太多孽，便只有我来还债了。当初先生便是让我多做善事，总能得到心中所求的。如今我也的确得到了，她们二人极为乖巧，如今便也如同我亲生女儿一般了。”
徐福点了点头，并不说话。
徐君房这般作为，倒是和他不谋而合了。若是他，他也会对陈阿婆说出这样的话，就如同他提点找他算姻缘的女子一般。
府邸虽大，人却不多，除却这两名女子以外，府中还有几个幼童，还有一个十来岁的小姑娘。他们都是由陈阿婆收养来的。
徐福差不多也能想到，为什么之前在街上，那些百姓那样担忧他欺负了陈阿婆。都是因为陈阿婆做了太多善事，这城中的百姓也将她记在心中了。如今陈阿婆在城中的地位，说一句德高望重也不为过。
香儿、玥儿都去为徐福准备房间了，而徐福则是和陈阿婆坐在了厅中，陈阿婆絮絮叨叨地说起了过去的事。
“如今十多年过去了，当初认得先生的人，现在都不太爱出门了。这些人眼拙得很，都认不出先生来。”陈阿婆生气地说。
徐福自己倒是根本不在意，“无妨，我此次回来，是为了寻找记忆。”
“什、什么？”陈阿婆一怔，没听明白徐福的意思。
“我回来是为了寻找记忆。”徐福决定干脆坦白说出来，“当初我在舆城做过什么，我都不记得了。”
陈阿婆脸上闪过哀色，“是因为……因为如您曾经说的那样，泄露了太多的天机，便会遭到反噬吗？”
徐福惊讶，这话徐君房也跟他们说起过？
陈阿婆叹了口气，细细说起了徐君房到舆城后发生的事，只要是陈阿婆知道的，她都统统说出来了。“那时先生也是这般进了城，然后在路边摆了摊。城中早已有了个方士，因而初时没有多少人相信先生，先生便在城中说，每日第一个来的人，你都可以不要钱，为其相面。有人想着反正也不花钱，于是第一日，来了个人找您卜卦。当时我就在旁边瞧着。我是第二个人……”
“那时您也是这般，不爱与人说话，目光也是冰冷的，但我知道您是个极为良善的人……”
“……后来有一日，我带着儿子到您那里去的时候，却遇见有个疯子口中囔囔着让您改命，那疯子还想要砸了您的摊子，我才邀您到了家中来住。可惜没两日您便离开了，那之后，不出一月，我儿子便也死了。”
囔囔着改命的疯子？
就是那个被徐君房记在日记中的疯子？
“你们城中原来有个方士？”
“是啊，不过那个方士如今已经不在城中了。”
徐福点了点头，并未放在心上，“你可知那疯子是谁？”
陈阿婆细细想了会儿，“人老了，不太记得了，您若是要问，那便到府邸外，不远处有个卖饼的人那里问问。”
徐福也不过随口问一问，“我过去在舆城可有留下什么东西？”
陈阿婆摇头，“这个倒是没有。”
徐福突然间，倒是有点儿说不出的怅惘。他想知道的，现在都已经知道了。这些就是他在舆城的记忆。但是除了这些之外呢？就没有别的更有用的东西了吗？徐福觉得，关于徐君房为何为失忆这一点，依旧是个谜。而且当初他重生过来的时机也很怪异，按照他对徐君房的认知，当初就算徐君房算命算到了秦始皇的头上，也不可能被吓得心肌梗塞而死，而那时除了失忆症以外，徐君房也并没有什么疾病，所以徐君房不死，自己的灵魂又是怎么占据这具身体的呢？
联合陈阿婆与他说的话，徐福心底的怪异感越来越浓，他几乎克制不住脑子里那个奇怪的念头了。
……假如、假如他和徐君房就是一个人呢？假如他根本没有什么重生穿越，他只是在失忆后，所有关于这个时代的记忆都被回档了呢？
徐福不免有些毛骨悚然。
坚持了许久的认知，一朝被颠覆的感觉可一点也不好。
“先生？”
见徐福久久不说话，陈阿婆不由得出声了。
“当年那人冒犯了先生，我一直以为先生是受了伤，这才不愿留在城中离开的。”陈阿婆叹道，“不知如今先生可还要离开此地？”
“要。”当然要。嬴政还在咸阳等他呢！
徐福此时倒是想起了一件事，“城中可有能传信的地方？”
“传信？”
“不错，我要传信到咸阳。”
陈阿婆摇头，“传不过去的，太远了。何况如今秦国和楚国，说不准什么时候便会打起来。”
虽然早有预料，但徐福还是免不了有些失望。他几乎闭上眼就能想象得到，在他失踪之后，嬴政该是何等震怒的模样。
“您可是累了？”陈阿婆注意到徐福的倦色，忙关心道。
“嗯，我去歇息一下。”
“对了。”陈阿婆突然又出声道：“那个冒犯了先生的疯子，可惜在先生走后不久就失踪了，不然如今先生归来，我等还能为先生出一口恶气。”陈阿婆言语间对那个疯子极为厌恶。
徐福淡淡一笑，从厅中出去了。
那两名女子已经将房间为他收拾好了，徐福踏进去之后，便顿觉放松了不少。这房间比客栈可要好上数倍，虽然摆设家具都有些老了，但是被子却是新的，而且房间极为干净。
徐福靠在了床榻之上，或许是这几日思虑过多，他真的有些累了，竟然合衣便睡着了。
朦胧中，他像是梦见了那一日的场景。
太阳快要下山的时分，有个疯疯癫癫、衣着褴褛的男子走到了他的跟前，男子似乎站立不稳了，直接摔倒在了徐福的跟前，他的脸凑近了，分外惊悚，将徐福吓得险些叫出声来。
“你会算命？那给我算一卦吧！”
他的脸在梦境中格外的清晰。
皮肤发红，脸上布有脓疮，看上去极为恶心。
但是梦中的徐福却并没有皱眉，而是极为淡定地看着他，就跟看路边的石头没有什么区别，他淡淡道：“欠有巨债，又身有恶疾，活不长久了。”
那男子闻言，登时崩溃大吼，“你胡说！我怎么……怎么可能活不长久！”
徐福依旧稳坐如山，“我并未胡说，你应当知晓自己的情况。你走吧，你的命不用再算了。”
男子踉跄着爬起来，憎恶地看着徐福，“凭什么？天下这么多人，凭什么我的命这样差呢？你不是很有本事吗？那你一定会改命吧！你会改命吧！”
“胡说的人是你。”梦中的徐福终于厌恶地皱起了眉，“改命这个说法你从何处听来的？哪有什么改命之说！”
“能改的！一定能改的！为什么你不肯为我改命？为什么？”男子激动地掀翻了他跟前的摊子，甚至还凑拢上前，似乎要伸手打徐福。
梦中的徐福立即起身躲避，厉声喝道：“你的面相如此丑陋！如何改命？”
“丑陋？”男子怔了怔，“丑陋那就将它变得不丑陋啊！只要改了它，我不就好了吗！你为什么见死不救？”
“面相哪里说改就能改的？你的脸是天生的，如何改？”
男子当真疯魔了，他嘻嘻笑道：“你说，我脸上何处丑陋？那便切了它！鼻子丑，那就切了鼻子，眼睛不好，那就剜了眼睛，若是整张脸都不够好，那就剥掉脸皮……”
徐福和梦中的徐福在这一刻似乎重叠了，他们对上男子的目光，忍不住打了个寒颤。
恶心！
徐福实在是说不出的恶心！
大约是实在被恶心得狠了，徐福一下子就从梦中惊醒过来了。
他扶着床榻坐起来，忍不住喘息频频。
窗外一阵凉风吹进来，徐福控制不住地打了个哆嗦，那股寒气仿佛一直渗到了骨子里去。
那人果然是个疯子！
徐福咬牙切齿地想。徐福遇见过的人千千万万，但他也没遇见过这样的，整个人一出场，就跟上演恐怖片差不多了。徐福闭了闭眼，靠在床榻上调整呼吸，好将那些恶心的画面从脑子里挥出去。
他的呼吸渐渐平稳下来，而就在此时，徐福脑中突然灵光一闪，他立即坐了起来。
那个疯子的脸！
那个疯子的脸跟阿武的脸何其相像！都是那样可怖又恶心！只不过阿武是变成了压抑后的冷酷，而那个人则是完全释放出来，最后变成了一个疯子。
这……会是巧合吗？
徐福不得不又想到了阿武口中的方士，那个方士总不会是自己吧？不不不，不可能，年纪对不上。徐福立时又否决了。不知道那个疯子后来还活着吗？
徐福现在又有点后悔自己给惊醒过来了，如果没有惊醒的话，他是不是可以在梦境中，继续走一遍徐君房经历过的事，起码可以将当时关于那个疯子的后续找到。
徐福躺回去，试着再睡着，再入梦。但是他闭上眼睛许久都没有再等到那个梦境。徐福无奈，只有爬起来了。
改命、改面相……
徐福觉得这简直成为了一个谜。之前还有人传他会改命呢？假如他当时被燕国太子丹掠走的时候，告诉姬丹，要改命得把脸皮剥下来，燕丹会不会吓得立即将他送回去？
徐福想一想，自己又觉得颇为好笑。
不过就算是改面相，也并不是这样血腥。换脸术放到后世的科技还可行，但在这时，换一张脸你差不多就可以去见阎王爷了。那这时为什么还会有改面相的说法呢？是谁传出的？还是说古籍中确有记载？
徐福只要一联想到，那个疯子将自己的脸切割剁开，眼珠挖出，就觉得恶心又可怖。
“……还是去找一找他？”徐福有些犹豫。
那个疯子脸上的病症，和阿武究竟是不是出自一处，他都很好奇。毕竟当初观察阿武脸上的脓包，徐福实在说不出那究竟是什么病。他觉得什么病都不像。
就在这时，屋门被敲响了。
徐福往窗外看去，才发现这时天已经大亮了。原来他靠在床榻上，竟然入神地想了这么久吗？
他穿好衣袍，这才起身去打开了屋门，外面站着的是玥儿。玥儿站在他跟前，脸红红地道：“阿婆说您要用些食物，我给您拿过来了。”
“多谢，放在那里便是。”徐福指了指屋中的桌案。
玥儿小心翼翼地进了门，放下东西之后，香儿又端着水来了。
这时徐福才感觉到了些微的不自在。人家相当于是陈阿婆的女儿，却来如下人一般伺候他。而且人家还是女子呢。
“辛苦了，你们出去吧。”
香儿倒是二话不说地出去了，玥儿临走的时候，还娇羞地看了一眼徐福。
徐福：“……”虽然嬴政并不会知道此处发生了什么，但是徐福还是有种莫名的心虚感。嬴政此时应当还在咸阳为他担忧，而他竟然在舆城招惹桃花。
换个位置，假如是嬴政在舆城，他在咸阳。
那简直光是想象一下，徐福都觉得难以接受。
于是用完食物之后，徐福便主动与陈阿婆说，不需要两位姑娘来伺候他了。初时陈阿婆并不同意，徐福也不与她讲道理，只说这般太不适应，若是如此，他便回客栈去。为了挽留住恩人，陈阿婆只得让两名女子不再去了。
玥儿当时就站在一旁，闻言好不失落。
徐福见状，心底却道了一声幸好。可不是幸好吗？明眼人都能看得出来，这姑娘对他有两分意思，若是再让人家经常见着他，那还不得更加对他上心？
年少慕艾是很正常的事，只要及时打住，那些心思总归会慢慢消散。
解决此事之后，徐福便出府了，他按照陈阿婆口中所说的，找到了那个卖饼的人。那是个老头儿，老头儿见了徐福，惊诧地瞪大了眼。这也就罢了，他还举起油乎乎的手擦了擦眼，或许是油进了眼睛，等他放下手的时候，两眼都开始往外渗泪了。
“原来真的是先生啊！”老头儿高声道。
他这一嗓子太过响亮，于是立马便有人看过来了。
徐福忽略掉耳边的那些议论声，直接了当地问道：“你还记得我？”
“这是自然！”老头儿激动地道。
“那还记得我曾经在舆城的时候，有一个疯子叫嚷着让我给他改面相，那个疯子去哪里了？”
“您要找他啊，当年这个疯子自知惹怒了您，不久后就没踪影了啊，城中的人都以为他死了。”
“死了？”
“这也只是猜测，毕竟连个尸骨都没见着呢。”
徐福眼底流露出了失望之色，老头儿似乎很不愿见到徐福失望，忙又道：“虽然我不知晓那疯子的踪迹，但我知晓他住在哪儿，他若是活着，说不准还会回去吧……”
徐福没说话。若是那人不改命，那么他也的确应该早就死了。除非他改了命，才能活到现在。但若是这世上有其他人能轻易为个穷苦的疯子改命，那这也太吓人了！因为这说明，对于对方来说，这改命非常简单便捷，所以可以毫不顾忌，随意为人改命。
那老头儿说完，连生意也不做了，他将自己的饼摊交给旁边的人看管，然后便领着徐福往城西去了。
“这边住的都是些穷苦人。”老头儿絮絮叨叨地说起了那个疯子的过往。
原来那疯子早就患有恶疾了，他还是个赌徒，还是个贼，令人所不齿，因而他的住处与所有人都分割开来，他住在一个单独的茅草屋中，那茅草屋破烂不堪，十年过去，连屋顶都没了，也不知是被哪一阵大风给刮走了。
老头儿往前一走就傻眼了，“这……这……”他尴尬地笑道：“这，许多年未曾来过，所以就……我也不知会如此……”
“无妨。”徐福面不改色地径直往前走，“你回去吧，我一人便可。”
老头儿犹豫一下，虽然他尊敬面前的人，但是他那饼铺也很让他挂心啊，于是老头儿还是挪着步子离开了。
徐福走近那草屋，闻见了一股霉味儿，还夹杂着一股难闻的不知道是什么的味道，差点让徐福将早上吃的食物全都吐出来了。
他驻足在草屋前，往里面探了一眼。因为屋顶都被掀没了的缘故，那草屋中便光线十足，令徐福一览无遗。
要不要进去呢？十来年，里面就算有留下什么东西，也早就没了吧。
徐福脑子里回想着老头儿说的话。疯子早就患有恶疾，但是阿武的异状，却是在那个方士给他治好原本的病之后，才生出来的。这和那疯子不大相像啊。
徐福一边想着，一边就不自觉地踏足进了草屋。
一进去，徐福就差点控制不住想要转身狂奔。或许真的没什么人来这里，这屋子里的东西竟然没有挪动过，包括多年前的破棉被，破烂的容器等等都还在。当然，这些都不可怕，可怕的是，那屋子里，有两具骸骨！
对，是两具！
上面的肉遭啃噬得差不多了，如今再看骸骨，污迹斑斑，还带着陈年血色，实在恶心。
这两具中会有那个疯子吗？
徐福实在憋不住了，还是选择了转身先出来。等出来之后，徐福长长地吐出了一口气。他可不想变成来查案的。不知城中可否能报官？
chapters.translated_text:
Seeing Xu Fu arrive, those beggars blocked the path behind them, leaving no room for begging. Their gazes turned vicious the moment they saw Xu Fu, and they stood up, intending to drive him away.

The onlookers nearby couldn't help but feel anxious.

The stall owners on both sides exchanged glances, then suddenly lunged forward, pinning the beggars to the ground while shouting, "If you want to beg, go somewhere else! Why are you getting in our way?"

The stall owners knew that only with Xu Fu standing there could they attract more customers, whereas the beggars squatting there would scare away anyone who wanted to approach. After all, who would want to walk toward a group of beggars?

The beggars were already intimidated when they were pinned to the ground. By the time the stall owners released them, they didn't even dare to glance at Xu Fu and scrambled away. When it came to reading the room, no one was better at it than them; since they couldn't gain any advantage, running away was the only way to avoid a beating.

Xu Fu: "..." He hadn't even reacted yet, and it was already over?

With the beggars driven off, Xu Fu was naturally able to return to his spot from yesterday and continue setting up his stall.

The stall owners on either side had no interest in his fortune-telling; after all, they weren't in the same trade. While few people came for divination, many were drawn to the area by his presence, which in turn benefited their stalls.

Before long, the stall owners were beaming with smiles. In contrast, Xu Fu’s side seemed much colder. Xu Fu felt a surge of frustration. Clearly, these customers were attracted by him, so why did they end up buying things from others?

That day, Xu Fu sat idly once again. While the number of curious onlookers increased, no one came to him for a reading, nor did anyone approach him to say, "You look so familiar." By the time the sun set behind the mountains, Xu Fu packed up his things, intending to return to the inn to rest, as the crowd in front of him thinned out.

Just then, a young woman nervously clutched her skirt and walked up to Xu Fu.

"S-sir, may I... may I have my fortune told?"

"Please." Xu Fu intended to ask her to sit, but looking down, he realized there wasn't even a mat in front of him; he couldn't just let her sit on the bare ground.

The woman didn't seem to mind. She lifted her skirt and knelt down, her posture quite standard, if one ignored the fact that she was sitting directly on the ground.

Xu Fu gave her an appreciative look.

Although the woman had appeared very nervous earlier, she was quite generous in this moment; she sat down without fuss, unconstrained by minor details.

The woman blushed under Xu Fu’s gaze and whispered, "I would like to ask you, sir, to tell my fortune regarding marriage."

Oh.

So, she wanted to know about her romantic prospects.

Xu Fu pointed to the items in front of him, "Choose one, miss."

Of course, Xu Fu wouldn't actually use these things, but he still had to keep up the facade.

The woman probably thought the tortoise shell looked the most impressive, so she pointed to its dark back, "This... is this okay?"

"It is." Xu Fu pretended to borrow a brazier from next door and performed a divination with the shell, though in reality, his words were based on the conclusions he drew from her physiognomy. "Is the young lady anxious to find a partner?"

Even as open as she was, the woman blushed at the mention of such matters.

Fortunately, the people around were far enough away that she didn't feel embarrassed after hearing it.

The woman whispered, "Yes."

"A young lady's marriage cannot be rushed; it requires patience. It will come within three years. In these three years, you should not wait idly; you must turn your fortune around to secure a good marriage." In fact, when facing young women asking about marriage, Xu Fu usually advised them not to rush. In this world, some things simply cannot be hurried, especially marriage. How many people who marry in haste end up with a happy ending? Such a major life event is worth waiting for; becoming blinded by impatience is a recipe for great trouble.

The woman looked disappointed at first, then her eyes brightened, "How do I turn it around?"

"Does your family own a cloth workshop?"

The woman blinked, her face full of surprise, "How did you know, sir?"

Because you smell like dye.

"I divined it, of course," Xu Fu said.

The woman’s admiration deepened. After all, everyone knew Xu Fu was a stranger from out of town; how could he know what the people in this city did for a living? It must have been through divination.

"The method to turn it around is very simple: work hard to manage your family's cloth workshop, and your fortune will rise accordingly. When that happens, your marriage might even come sooner." Xu Fu told her it would be within three years, but based on her physiognomy, it would actually arrive in a little over a year. He said three years because he hoped that even when the marriage prospect arrived, the young lady would think carefully rather than rushing into it.

"It... it's that simple?" The woman was stunned, not expecting him to ask her to buy anything.

"Yes, it is that simple. This method has no drawbacks at all; you can give it a try," Xu Fu said calmly.

In truth, this so-called method of turning fortune around had nothing to do with divination or physiognomy. Diligently managing the cloth workshop was merely to help the woman become more independent, both mentally and financially. Before long, she would become more resilient and intelligent. Besides, how did that saying go? People are most attractive when they are focused. Regardless of gender, when one has a dedicated career, their spirit is incredibly vibrant. By then, how could an excellent and intelligent woman fail to find her own marriage?

Although, thinking back to his past life, many women didn't even need marriage once they became excellent.

Xu Fu coughed lightly in his heart and cast these thoughts out of his mind.

The woman stood up happily, bowed to Xu Fu, and said, "I believe you, sir!" The other party was right; this method of turning fortune around had no drawbacks, so why not give it a try?

The woman took out some coins, placed a handful in front of Xu Fu, and asked, "Sir, is this enough?"

"It is enough." After saying this, Xu Fu wrapped some dirt and ash in a piece of silk and handed it to her.

"This?"

"Take it. With its assistance, things will naturally go better."

That dirt and ash contained wood shavings, tortoise shell fragments, and soil. The tortoise shell was spiritually sensitive, the wood shavings represented wood (which feeds fire), and the soil represented earth (which produces metal). Fire and metal were both auspicious symbols. This was just a simple method to help fortune rise. Of course, such assistance could easily be broken, but for the woman, it was enough for now.

The woman smiled brightly, clutched the silk in her hand, and turned to leave. Xu Fu, of course, would never know that after she turned away, she was still wondering why her destined marriage wasn't with this man. She had approached him only to strike up a conversation, not to seriously ask about marriage, yet she had received such advice.

Seeing the woman be the first to "eat the crab," others became restless, but since they weren't asking about marriage, they didn't act immediately. However, one couple stared at Xu Fu for a long time.

Xu Fu had sharp ears and heard them whisper, "He looks so familiar..."

"Yes, he does..."

Xu Fu beckoned to them, "You two, I look familiar?"

Upon hearing Xu Fu speak to them, the couple became flustered, "N-no, perhaps... perhaps we were mistaken..." After saying this, they hurried away as if something were chasing them.

Xu Fu felt helpless. Had he done something bad in this city before? Xu Fu’s heart sank—surely not? Xu Junfang shouldn't have been a bad person, and his diary didn't mention... well, perhaps it did, but the silk was mostly destroyed, so he couldn't see it. Xu Fu suppressed his worries and packed his things to leave first.

He would just have to keep waiting and see.

It was a pity that A-Wu wasn't by his side. Although Xu Fu didn't particularly care for A-Wu, he knew A-Wu had decent combat skills. If A-Wu were here, he wouldn't have to worry so much and could continue setting up his stall boldly without fearing whether Xu Junfang had offended anyone in the city in the past.

That night, Xu Fu didn't sleep well; he even dreamed of Ying Zheng repeatedly.

After waking up, Xu Fu sat blankly on the bed for a long time. Since when did he miss Ying Zheng so much?

Xu Fu rubbed his forehead and got up.

He truly wanted to return to Xianyang quickly. Perhaps it was intuition, but Xu Fu always felt that dreaming of Ying Zheng so frequently was not a good omen.

On the third day, Xu Fu returned to that same spot.

The number of onlookers had decreased that day. Even if Xu Fu was good-looking, they wouldn't keep their eyes glued to him and abandon their normal lives just to stare at him.

Xu Fu felt bored sitting there. Fortunately, the sunlight wasn't too intense under the wall, otherwise, he really wouldn't have been able to wait any longer.

Just as the morning was coming to an end, Xu Fu let out a long sigh and lowered his head to tidy up his things.

A slightly aged voice suddenly rang out, "Y-you..."

You what?

Xu Fu was startled. He looked up with a cold expression and saw an old woman in simple clothing standing before him. The old woman walked unsteadily, her eyelids drooping so low that only two slits remained to see through, and her face was covered in wrinkles like orange peel. The old woman’s appearance was quite frightening, but Xu Fu could tell she had no ill intent.

"You..." Xu Fu had just started to speak when the old woman suddenly knelt before him.

Xu Fu was truly shocked this time; what was this old woman doing?

The surrounding people were also startled by the old woman’s unexpected action and hurried over, shouting, "Granny Chen, what are you doing?" Although Xu Fu was handsome, when he was placed next to an old woman, others naturally assumed he had bullied her.

Receiving the condemning gazes of the crowd, Xu Fu: "..." He hadn't done anything yet.

The old woman waved away those who tried to help her up. She stared fixedly at Xu Fu and said in an aged, raspy voice, "You have returned! I never expected to see you again before I died!"

The onlookers were stunned.

"Granny Chen, what are you saying?"

"Granny Chen, do you know him?"

Xu Fu was also shocked. He had waited until the third day, thinking the leads wouldn't come, yet suddenly an old woman appeared and said such things. She must know him; she had seen Xu Junfang! And she must have had significant contact with him!

Some noticed that Granny Chen’s tone when addressing him was extremely polite and respectful, leaving them puzzled—who exactly was this man? Granny Chen was quite famous in their city, and everyone knew her. Because of her, they became even more curious about the man before them.

"You know me?" Xu Fu asked. Despite the surprise in his heart, he showed nothing on his face, and his speaking pace remained unhurried.

Granny Chen looked at him, a flash of nostalgia in her eyes, and said, "You haven't changed much from the past. It's just that I have grown too old; you wouldn't recognize me, would you?"

Xu Fu didn't speak.

Granny Chen smiled, revealing a toothless gap.

She didn't look particularly kind, but Xu Fu inexplicably felt a sense of gentleness from her.

"Thank you for your heartfelt guidance back then. Although my son died in the end, my gratitude toward you remains. I heard someone say a fortune-teller had arrived in the city, and I guessed it must be you, so I came alone," Granny Chen added.

Guided her son?

Doubts piled up in Xu Fu's heart, but he showed nothing on his face. He nodded faintly and said, "It was many years ago; it is not worth mentioning."

Granny Chen smiled again, "You are still the same." She paused and said, "Where are you staying now? If you don't mind, why not stay at my home?"

Xu Fu’s heart stirred, "Very well."

"You are still as straightforward as ever."

Every time he heard Granny Chen say "still the same," Xu Fu felt a sense of strangeness, as he knew very well that he and Xu Junfang were two separate souls. Hearing such things was truly peculiar. But thinking about it, perhaps in Granny Chen’s heart, Xu Junfang had always been a deified figure, so no matter what he did or said, she would feel he hadn't changed.

Having obtained what he wanted, Xu Fu naturally wouldn't continue setting up his stall. He packed his things and said, "Wait for me here."

Granny Chen nodded.

Xu Fu returned to the inn, quickly checked out, and took all his luggage. The inn wasn't far from where he had been setting up his stall, but by the time Xu Fu came out, two young women were already by Granny Chen’s side, supporting her. The two women were dressed quite elegantly and could be considered beauties in this city.

Were these Granny Chen’s daughters?

Xu Fu found it very strange. Granny Chen’s attire was completely different from theirs; the former looked like someone from a poor family, while the latter looked like young ladies from a wealthy household.

"Sir, please go first," Granny Chen said, gesturing for Xu Fu to lead the way as soon as she saw him.

At this moment, the way others looked at Xu Fu changed slightly, and they couldn't help but whisper, "What is his relationship with Granny Chen?" "Did he save Granny Chen’s son years ago?" "Is he really that capable? I should have asked him for a reading." "It must be nonsense; he's just a fangshi, he doesn't know medicine, how could he save anyone?" "But Granny Chen wouldn't lie..."

These discussions reached Xu Fu’s ears. He thought that he should be able to find out about Granny Chen’s son from her later. Perhaps she could tell him even more about Xu Junfang.

Although it sounded strange to learn about himself from others, it was indeed the only channel Xu Fu had.

Xu Fu walked in front, with the two young women guiding him from behind. Soon, they stopped in front of a mansion. Xu Fu looked up; there was no plaque, but just from the exterior, he could tell it was a residence for the wealthy. Granny Chen clearly didn't come from a poor family. Her attire must have been due to her old age, making her indifferent to such worldly possessions.

"Please, sir," one of the young women said.

Xu Fu stepped inside. Once he entered, he realized that while it looked grand from the outside, the interior was not like the mansions of Wei Liao or Yao Jia. The flowers and trees in the courtyard were clearly untended, and he didn't see any servants after entering. This was strange.

Granny Chen sighed, "After my son passed, I dismissed all the servants. Xiang'er and Yue'er are orphan girls I adopted later." Granny Chen smiled, "Xiang'er, Yue'er, you both must thank this gentleman. Without him, you and I would not have this bond."

Upon hearing this, the two women immediately bowed to Xu Fu.

"Was it I who told you to adopt them?"

"Yes. My son committed too many sins, so I had to repay the debt. Back then, you told me to do more good deeds, and I would eventually get what I sought in my heart. Now I have truly received it; these two are very sensible, and they are like my own daughters now."

Xu Fu nodded without speaking.

Xu Junfang’s actions were in line with his own. If it were him, he would have said the same thing to Granny Chen, just as he had advised the woman who asked about her marriage.

Although the mansion was large, there were few people. Besides the two women, there were several young children and a girl of about ten. They were all orphans adopted by Granny Chen.

Xu Fu could more or less guess why the townspeople had been so worried that he might have bullied Granny Chen earlier on the street. It was all because Granny Chen had done so many good deeds that the people of this town held her dear in their hearts. To say that Granny Chen’s status in the town was one of high virtue and prestige would not be an exaggeration at all.

Xiang’er and Yue’er both went off to prepare a room for Xu Fu, while Xu Fu sat in the main hall with Granny Chen, who rambled on about things from the past.

"Now that over ten years have passed, those who knew you, Sir, back then don’t really like to go out much anymore. These people have poor eyesight; they can’t even recognize you, Sir," Granny Chen said indignantly.

Xu Fu himself didn’t care at all. "It’s fine. I returned this time to search for my memories."

"W-what?" Granny Chen was startled, not quite understanding what Xu Fu meant.

"I returned to search for my memories." Xu Fu decided to just be blunt. "I don’t remember anything I did when I was in Yucheng."

A look of sorrow flashed across Granny Chen’s face. "Is it because... because as you once said, leaking too many secrets of heaven leads to a backlash?"

Xu Fu was surprised. Xu Junfang had told them this too?

Granny Chen sighed and began to recount in detail what had happened after Xu Junfang arrived in Yucheng, telling him everything she knew. "At that time, you, Sir, entered the city just like this and set up a stall by the roadside. There was already a fangshi (alchemist/diviner) in the city, so at first, not many people believed in you. You then announced in the city that for the first person who came each day, you would read their fortune for free. Some people thought it didn't cost anything anyway, so on the first day, someone came to you for a divination. I was watching from the side at the time. I was the second person..."

"Back then, you were also like this—not fond of talking to people, and your gaze was icy, but I knew you were an extremely kind-hearted person..."

"...Later, one day when I brought my son to see you, we encountered a madman who was shouting for you to change his fate. That madman even wanted to smash your stall, which is why I invited you to come stay at my home. Unfortunately, you left within two days, and not a month after that, my son died."

A madman shouting about changing fate?

Was it that same madman recorded in Xu Junfang’s diary?

"Was there already a fangshi in your city?"

"Yes, but that fangshi is no longer in the city now."

Xu Fu nodded, not taking it to heart. "Do you know who that madman was?"

Granny Chen thought carefully for a while. "I’m old and don’t remember very well. If you want to ask, you should go outside the residence and ask the person selling pancakes not far from here."

Xu Fu had only asked casually. "Did I leave anything behind when I was in Yucheng before?"

Granny Chen shook her head. "That, I’m afraid not."

Suddenly, Xu Fu felt an indescribable sense of melancholy. He now knew everything he had wanted to know. These were his memories of Yucheng. But besides these, was there nothing else more useful? Xu Fu felt that the reason for Xu Junfang’s amnesia remained a mystery. Moreover, the timing of his own rebirth was also very strange. Based on his understanding of Xu Junfang, even if Xu Junfang had calculated the fortune of Qin Shi Huang himself, he wouldn't have been scared to the point of dying from a myocardial infarction. At that time, apart from amnesia, Xu Junfang had no other illnesses. So, if Xu Junfang didn't die, how did his own soul occupy this body?

Combining this with what Granny Chen had told him, the sense of strangeness in Xu Fu’s heart grew stronger; he could barely suppress the bizarre thought in his mind.

...What if—what if he and Xu Junfang were the same person? What if there was no rebirth or transmigration at all, and he had simply experienced a system rollback of all his memories regarding this era after losing his memory?

Xu Fu couldn't help but feel a chill run down his spine.

The feeling of having a long-held perception overturned in an instant was not pleasant at all.

"Sir?"

Seeing that Xu Fu had been silent for a long time, Granny Chen couldn't help but speak up.

"That man offended you back then, and I always thought you were injured, which is why you didn't want to stay in the city and left," Granny Chen sighed. "I wonder if you still intend to leave this place now, Sir?"

"I do." Of course he did. Ying Zheng was still waiting for him in Xianyang!

At this moment, Xu Fu remembered something. "Is there a place in the city to send messages?"

"Send messages?"

"Yes, I need to send a message to Xianyang."

Granny Chen shook her head. "It can’t be sent; it’s too far. Besides, it’s uncertain when the Qin and Chu states might go to war."

Although he had expected this, Xu Fu couldn't help but feel disappointed. He could imagine, just by closing his eyes, how furious Ying Zheng must have been after he went missing.

"Are you tired, Sir?" Granny Chen noticed the weariness on Xu Fu’s face and asked with concern.

"Yes, I’ll go and rest for a while."

"Oh, right," Granny Chen suddenly added, "That madman who offended you, it’s a pity he went missing shortly after you left. Otherwise, now that you’ve returned, we could have vented your anger for you." Granny Chen spoke of that madman with extreme disgust.

Xu Fu smiled faintly and left the hall.

The two women had already tidied up the room for him. Once Xu Fu stepped inside, he felt much more relaxed. This room was several times better than the inn; although the furniture was a bit old, the bedding was new, and the room was extremely clean.

Xu Fu leaned against the bed. Perhaps because he had been thinking too much over the past few days, he was truly tired and fell asleep fully clothed.

In a hazy state, he seemed to dream of the scene from that day.

As the sun was about to set, a disheveled, ragged-looking man walked up to him. The man seemed unable to stand steadily and fell directly in front of Xu Fu. His face leaned in close, looking exceptionally horrifying, scaring Xu Fu so much he nearly cried out.

"You can tell fortunes? Then tell me one!"

His face was exceptionally clear in the dream.

His skin was red and covered in pustules, looking extremely disgusting.

However, the Xu Fu in the dream did not frown; instead, he looked at him with extreme calmness, no different from looking at a rock by the roadside. He said indifferently, "You owe a huge debt and suffer from a malignant disease; you won't live much longer."

Upon hearing this, the man immediately broke down and roared, "You’re lying! How... how could I not live much longer!"

Xu Fu remained as steady as a mountain. "I am not lying; you should know your own situation. Go now, there is no need to calculate your fate anymore."

The man staggered to his feet and looked at Xu Fu with hatred. "Why? There are so many people in the world, why is my fate so bad? Aren't you very capable? Then you must be able to change fate! You can change fate, right!"

"The one who is lying is you." The Xu Fu in the dream finally frowned in disgust. "Where did you hear this talk of changing fate? There is no such thing as changing fate!"

"It can be changed! It must be possible! Why won't you change my fate? Why?" The man excitedly overturned the stall in front of him and even leaned in, as if he were about to strike Xu Fu.

The Xu Fu in the dream immediately stood up to dodge and shouted sternly, "Your physiognomy is so ugly! How could it be changed?"

"Ugly?" The man was stunned. "If it's ugly, then make it not ugly! As long as it's changed, won't I be fine! Why won't you save me?"

"Physiognomy cannot be changed just like that. Your face is born that way, how can it be changed?"

The man had truly gone mad. He giggled, "Tell me, which part of my face is ugly? Then cut it off! If the nose is ugly, cut off the nose; if the eyes are bad, gouge out the eyes. If the whole face isn't good enough, then peel off the skin..."

Xu Fu and the Xu Fu in the dream seemed to overlap at this moment. As they met the man’s gaze, they couldn't help but shudder.

Disgusting!

Xu Fu felt an indescribable sense of disgust!

Perhaps because he was so thoroughly disgusted, Xu Fu woke up from the dream with a start.

He sat up, leaning on the bed, unable to stop gasping for breath.

A cool breeze blew in from the window, and Xu Fu couldn't help but shiver; that chill seemed to have seeped into his very bones.

That man really was a madman!

Xu Fu thought, gritting his teeth. He had met thousands of people, but he had never met anyone like that; his mere appearance was like a scene from a horror movie. Xu Fu closed his eyes and leaned against the bed, adjusting his breathing to clear those disgusting images from his mind.

His breathing gradually steadied, and at that moment, a flash of inspiration struck Xu Fu, and he immediately sat up.

That madman’s face!

That madman’s face was so similar to A-Wu’s! Both were so terrifying and disgusting! It was just that A-Wu had turned into a repressed, cold person, while that man had completely unleashed it, eventually becoming a madman.

Could this... be a coincidence?

Xu Fu couldn't help but think of the fangshi A-Wu had mentioned. Could that fangshi be himself? No, no, impossible, the age didn't match. Xu Fu immediately dismissed the thought. He wondered if that madman was still alive.

Xu Fu now regretted waking up. If he hadn't woken up, could he have continued to walk through the events Xu Junfang had experienced in the dream? At the very least, he might have found out what happened to that madman afterward.

Xu Fu lay back down, trying to fall asleep and re-enter the dream. But he closed his eyes for a long time and never waited for that dream again. Helpless, Xu Fu had no choice but to get up.

Changing fate, changing physiognomy...

Xu Fu felt this had become a mystery. Hadn't people rumored that he could change fate before? If he had told Crown Prince Dan of Yan, when he was abducted, that to change his fate he would need to peel off his skin, would Yan Dan have been scared into sending him back immediately?

Xu Fu thought about it and found it quite amusing.

However, even changing one's physiognomy shouldn't be this bloody. Face-swapping surgery might be feasible with the technology of later generations, but in this era, if you swapped a face, you might as well go see the King of Hell. So why was there talk of changing physiognomy? Who started it? Or were there records of it in ancient texts?

Whenever Xu Fu imagined that madman cutting and chopping his own face, gouging out his eyeballs, he felt disgusted and terrified.

"...Should I go look for him?" Xu Fu hesitated.

He was curious whether the ailment on that madman’s face and A-Wu’s condition came from the same source. After all, when he had observed the pustules on A-Wu’s face, Xu Fu couldn't say what kind of disease it was. It didn't look like any disease he knew.

Just then, there was a knock on the door.

Xu Fu looked out the window and realized it was already broad daylight. Had he really been lost in thought for so long while leaning on the bed?

He put on his robe and got up to open the door. Standing outside was Yue’er. She stood before him, blushing as she said, "Granny said you needed to eat, so I brought some food for you."

"Thank you, just leave it there." Xu Fu pointed to the table in the room.

Yue’er carefully entered the room, and after putting the things down, Xiang’er brought in some water.

Only then did Xu Fu feel a slight sense of unease. These girls were practically Granny Chen’s daughters, yet they were serving him like servants. And they were women, too.

"Thank you for your hard work. You may leave."

Xiang’er left without a word, but as Yue’er was leaving, she cast a shy glance at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu: "..." Although Ying Zheng wouldn't know what was happening here, Xu Fu still felt an inexplicable sense of guilt. Ying Zheng should still be in Xianyang worrying about him, and here he was, attracting romantic attention in Yucheng.

If the roles were reversed, if Ying Zheng were in Yucheng and he were in Xianyang...

Just imagining it made Xu Fu feel it was unacceptable.

So, after finishing his meal, Xu Fu took the initiative to tell Granny Chen that he didn't need the two girls to serve him. At first, Granny Chen disagreed, but Xu Fu didn't argue; he simply said he wasn't used to it and if it continued, he would return to the inn. To keep her benefactor, Granny Chen had no choice but to tell the two women not to go anymore.

Yue’er was standing to the side at the time and looked very disappointed upon hearing this.

Seeing this, Xu Fu sighed in relief in his heart. Wasn't it a good thing? Anyone with eyes could see that this girl had a bit of an interest in him. If he let her see him often, wouldn't she become even more attached?

Young love was normal; as long as it was stopped in time, those feelings would eventually fade away.

After resolving this, Xu Fu left the residence and found the pancake seller as Granny Chen had described. It was an old man, and when he saw Xu Fu, he stared in astonishment. That wasn't all; he raised his greasy hand to wipe his eyes—perhaps some oil got in—and when he lowered his hand, both eyes were leaking tears.

"It really is you, Sir!" the old man exclaimed loudly.

His voice was so loud that people immediately looked over.

Ignoring the whispers around him, Xu Fu asked directly, "Do you remember me?"

"Of course!" the old man said excitedly.

"Then do you remember when I was in Yucheng, there was a madman who kept shouting for me to change his physiognomy? Where did that madman go?"

"You’re looking for him? Back then, that madman knew he had offended you, and not long after, he vanished. Everyone in the city thought he had died."

"Died?"

"That’s just a guess, since no one ever saw a corpse."

A look of disappointment appeared in Xu Fu’s eyes. The old man seemed unwilling to see Xu Fu disappointed and quickly added, "Although I don't know the whereabouts of that madman, I know where he lived. If he’s still alive, he might go back there..."

Xu Fu didn't speak. If that man hadn't changed his fate, he should have died long ago. Unless he had changed his fate, he couldn't have lived until now. But if there were others in this world who could easily change the fate of a poor madman, that would be too terrifying! Because it would mean that for the other party, changing fate was very simple and convenient, so they could do it for anyone without any hesitation.

After the old man finished speaking, he didn't even care about his business; he left his pancake stall for someone else to watch and led Xu Fu toward the west of the city.

"Poor people live around here," the old man rambled on about the madman’s past.

It turned out that the madman had long suffered from a malignant disease and was also a gambler and a thief, despised by all. Therefore, his dwelling was separated from everyone else’s. He lived in a solitary, dilapidated thatched hut. Ten years later, even the roof was gone; no one knew which gust of wind had blown it away.

The old man walked forward and was stunned. "This... this..." He laughed awkwardly, "This, I haven't been here in many years, so... I didn't know it would be like this..."

"It’s fine." Xu Fu walked straight ahead without changing his expression. "You can go back; I can go on alone."

The old man hesitated. Although he respected the person before him, he was also worried about his pancake stall, so he shuffled away.

Xu Fu approached the hut and smelled a musty odor, mixed with an unpleasant, unidentifiable scent that almost made him vomit everything he had eaten that morning.

He stopped in front of the hut and peered inside. Because the roof had been blown off, the hut was well-lit, giving Xu Fu a clear view.

Should he go in? After ten years, even if anything had been left behind, it would be long gone.

Xu Fu recalled what the old man had said. The madman had long suffered from a malignant disease, but A-Wu’s abnormality only appeared after that fangshi had cured his original illness. This didn't seem much like that madman.

While thinking, Xu Fu unconsciously stepped into the hut.

As soon as he entered, Xu Fu almost couldn't stop himself from turning and running. Perhaps no one had really come here; the things in the room hadn't been moved, including the old, tattered cotton quilt, broken containers, and so on. Of course, these weren't the scary parts; the scary part was that there were two skeletons in the room!

Yes, two!

The flesh on them had been mostly gnawed away, and now looking at the skeletons, they were stained with dirt and dried blood, truly disgusting.

Could that madman be one of these two?

Xu Fu couldn't hold it anymore and chose to turn and leave first. Once outside, Xu Fu let out a long breath. He didn't want to become someone investigating a case. He wondered if one could report this to the local authorities?

chapters.title: 第241章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu had no idea how to report to the authorities in this era, nor did he know where the government office was located. Therefore, after leaving the hut, he had no choice but to find the old man from before. Seeing him approach, the old man immediately dropped his work, rubbed his hands together, and asked, "Sir, did you find what you were looking for?"

Xu Fu shook his head.

The old man looked disappointed, but his expression changed immediately when Xu Fu said to him, "I found human remains inside the hut."

The old man was startled, his mouth agape, unable to speak for a moment. After a while, he recovered and shook his head, saying, "It seems that madman really did die in there. No one has been to check in so long, who knows what state they're in now..."

"There is more than one set of remains inside," Xu Fu had to interrupt the old man's lament.

"Wh-what? So how many people died?"

"Two. It's currently impossible to determine if one of them is the madman's. I don't know how to handle this, so I had to come find you. I'll have to trouble you to notify someone to deal with the remains," Xu Fu said calmly.

The old man nodded blankly. "Y-you wait here, I... I'll go call someone over right now." The old man entrusted his pancake stall to someone nearby once again, then took off running. His legs, at this moment, had become remarkably nimble.

The person entrusted with the stall raised an eyebrow. "What's he up to now? Running so fast!" After saying this, he shook his head, turned to look at Xu Fu, and asked curiously, "You're not from Yucheng, are you?"

"No."

"Then what are you doing in Yucheng?"

Xu Fu did not answer him.

The man didn't mind, just muttered to himself in a low voice, "When did the old man get to know someone like this? Strange! Strange!"

Before long, the old man returned with a group of people. The men behind him were wearing plain clothes; Xu Fu took a look and couldn't tell at all if they were official government uniforms. Were these the civil servants of the Chu State?

Those men glanced at Xu Fu, not paying him any mind, and only said to the old man, "Where is it? Take us there!"

The old man caught his breath and hurried forward again. Xu Fu followed without a word, and the men didn't rebuke him for it. Soon, they reached the hut, and the old man pointed inside. "The remains are in there."

Because so many people had gathered outside the hut, the locals in the area were stirred up. They couldn't help but poke their heads out, curiously eyeing Xu Fu and his group, even pointing and whispering among themselves.

The men went inside to inspect for a while and soon came out. Frowning with expressions of disgust, they said coldly, "It seems the one who died is Wang He."

Wang He? Xu Fu guessed this must be the name of the madman. But how could these people be so certain the deceased was Wang He?

Just as he was wondering, he heard them add, "The other set of remains must be that outsider!"

Xu Fu realized then that these men were clearly just spouting nonsense.

"How do you gentlemen conclude that the deceased is Wang He and an outsider?" Xu Fu couldn't help but ask. He had truly never seen such a crude way of handling a case.

And facts proved to Xu Fu that these people were even cruder.

The man questioned by Xu Fu gave him a cold look and said, "If someone dies in Wang He's hut, who else could it be but Wang He?"

Xu Fu: "..." Your logic is impeccable.

"And since there are no missing persons in Yucheng, the other one is naturally an outsider."

Xu Fu was completely convinced. Who exactly died in the hut clearly didn't matter to them at all, nor did how they died. They just needed to quickly assign identities to them to call it a day.

"Just bury these two sets of remains," the man said, effectively ending the matter.

The men behind him immediately moved to lift the remains upon hearing this.

Xu Fu felt truly helpless. If he let them bury them just like that, he would never get any information from the remains; after all, he didn't have the skill to dig up graves.

"Could you allow me to take one more look?" Xu Fu spoke up.

The men looked at Xu Fu suspiciously and asked sharply, "Why are you so curious about this? Could it be that you..."

Before the other party could suspect him of being the murderer, Xu Fu used his presence to overwhelm them and interrupted, "I only came to find Wang He; he can vouch for me." Xu Fu pointed at the old man nearby.

The old man nodded repeatedly.

Although these men didn't trust a new face like Xu Fu, they still trusted the old man. So the man snorted coldly and said, "Oh, looking at you, you must be an outsider too. Be careful, lest you end up like this." This remark was clearly intended to make things difficult for Xu Fu.

Xu Fu pretended not to hear the sarcasm in his tone, bypassed them, and walked back into the hut. He suppressed his urge to vomit and leaned in close to examine the two sets of remains carefully.

Because the remains had been gnawed on, they were extremely incomplete, but Xu Fu still discovered that these two bodies had been mutilated even before being gnawed upon. Especially on the faces; one could see that the jawbones had been hacked, and parts like the nose had varying degrees of damage. This forced Xu Fu to think again of what the madman Wang He had said to him in his dream. Perhaps that wasn't a dream; it was a memory belonging to Xu Junfang, a true, vivid memory.

"Are you done?" the people outside urged.

Xu Fu stood up straight, let out a breath, and walked out.

Thinking of the madman's appearance now, Xu Fu still felt a chill down his spine. He didn't even dare to dwell on why these remains had ended up in such a state.

The two sets of remains were quickly taken away by those men. They would likely be buried soon, and Xu Fu couldn't expect to gain any more information from them. After they left, the old man walked to Xu Fu's side unconsciously and whispered, "Are you disappointed, sir?"

"It's nothing. Thank you, you can go back now." After saying this, Xu Fu paused, took out some coins, and handed them to the old man. "Take these." He had truly troubled the man a lot; the old man hadn't even been able to attend to his pancake stall. How could he accept the man's kindness for nothing?

The old man didn't dare reach out to take the money and shook his head repeatedly. "N-no, there's no need."

"Take it." Xu Fu's tone was firm. The old man froze, not daring to argue, and had to accept the coins.

"You can go back now," Xu Fu said again.

The old man followed his instruction instinctively and walked back honestly.

After they had all left, the other onlookers dispersed as well. Two people had died; that was enough to be a topic of conversation for them for a while, and there was no need to keep watching.

Moreover, they all unanimously agreed that the handsome man standing in front of the hut was not to be trifled with. Better not to look too much.

Soon, the area around Xu Fu returned to silence.

He stood outside the hut for a while, then couldn't help but walk back inside. He wanted to see if there were any other clues left behind. Perhaps he should thank those irresponsible Chu people; they had taken the remains away so cleanly but hadn't touched anything else in the hut, which now made things convenient for Xu Fu.

Xu Fu struggled to search for what he wanted in the chaotic hut.

He moved his feet carefully, but the floor of the hut was in such a bad state that he didn't know what he stepped on and almost slipped, scaring the soul right out of his body. He didn't want to slip at all; he didn't want to touch the ground—ghastly corpses had lain here!

Xu Fu barely managed to grab the dilapidated table nearby to steady himself and stood up quickly. Only then could he look down to examine what had almost caused him to slip. It looked like a piece of silk fabric crumpled into a ball, black and grimy, half-buried in the mud.

Could Wang He afford silk? Xu Fu was very doubtful.

However, if it really was silk, it was likely used for recording things. If there was silk here, it must contain exactly what Xu Fu needed! Xu Fu was a bit excited; he carefully bent down and picked up the silk.

Xu Fu slowly unfolded the silk.

He was disappointed.

The preservation of the silk was truly poor. Perhaps it had been mixed with the mud and weathered by the elements... Xu Fu couldn't see anything clearly.

Just as Xu Fu was about to discard the silk, it suddenly slipped, and a layer fell off.

Were there two layers?

Xu Fu picked up the silk again.

Why not take it back and wash it with water to see if there were any remaining traces of ink? Just as Xu Fu was thinking this, his gaze was suddenly drawn to an unusual spot on the silk.

Stuck to it was a small clump of dark red...

Xu Fu brought the silk closer to look again carefully. He was suddenly horrified; his hand loosened, and the silk fell to the ground.

No! That wasn't silk at all!

There were remnants of flesh and blood stuck to it. Because it had been so long, the bloodstains had turned dark red. Xu Fu could almost imagine how this thing had been peeled off another person's face.

These were two human face skins!

One of them even had an eyeball still attached!

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more disgusted he felt. He had already experienced many strange things; even A-Wu's face hadn't made him vomit, but at this moment, he felt his stomach churning violently.

He couldn't hold it back anymore!

Xu Fu rushed out of the hut, for the first time disregarding his etiquette and composure. Of course, no one would notice him at this time anyway.

Once outside, Xu Fu wanted to vomit but couldn't. His vision seemed to be covered in a layer of blood, and in his mind, he couldn't help but imagine how those two bodies had been skinned while they were still alive. One of them, due to excessive force, had even had an eyeball ripped out along with the skin.

How bloody! How cruel!

Was this what Wang He called "changing one's physiognomy"?

He really was a madman!

Xu Fu stood there for a long while before he managed to calm his emotions.

After calming down, Xu Fu could make logical guesses. He believed that neither of the two sets of remains was likely Wang He. Why were these remains missing certain parts, missing facial features and skin? This coincided perfectly with what Wang He had once said to Xu Junfang. And they just happened to appear in Wang He's hut. How could this be a coincidence? The best explanation was that after Wang He was rejected by him, he had taken matters into his own hands to perform the transformation. He had lured people into his hut and, while they were still alive, attempted to use their perfect parts to replace his own ugly ones.

But why, after taking the skin, did he not use it, but instead leave it in the hut?

Could it be that Wang He had regained his sanity at the end? And realized the skin couldn't be used?

Wang He wouldn't have peeled off the other person's face while sane, then peeled off his own, and then died from blood loss before he could transplant them, would he?

Xu Fu felt he couldn't even think for a moment.

But he could be certain that changing one's physiognomy definitely wasn't done through such a brutal method. So, as long as Wang He's fate remained as Xu Junfang had divined for him, Wang He couldn't have lived until today.

So, was Wang He dead, or had he succeeded in changing his fate and was still alive?

Xu Fu urgently wanted to see this madman.

But finding people wasn't his specialty. If nothing else could be found in Yucheng, he would have to leave, return to Xianyang, and entrust Ying Zheng to send people to find this Wang He. Wang He might be able to hide from him, but he definitely couldn't hide from a search backed by imperial power.

Xu Fu sighed softly and stared at the hut for a long time. In the end, he didn't have the courage to step into that hut again. He thought he needed to calm his mind.

Xu Fu left the hut and returned directly to Chen Apo's residence.

As soon as he entered, Yue'er walked over. "Sir, Apo is waiting for you," she whispered.

Xu Fu didn't even look at her and walked straight in.

Yue'er bit her lip but didn't say anything.

Xu Fu felt a sense of relief in his heart; it was better to keep people at a distance with coldness, as this could avoid certain situations.

Chen Apo was sitting in the hall. As soon as she saw Xu Fu step through the door, she immediately stood up, leaning on Xiang'er's arm. "I heard that two people died in the city. You didn't encounter any trouble outside, did you?" The worry on Chen Apo's face didn't seem fake.

"I went to find that madman and ended up finding two corpses in his hut," Xu Fu said calmly.

The two women nearby covered their mouths upon hearing this, their faces full of shock and fear.

"H-how could this happen?" Chen Apo was also quite shaken. "It's been so many years since anyone died in the city."

"Those two must have died a long time ago, perhaps right after that madman went missing."

Chen Apo was speechless for a long time. Finally, she opened her mouth and said, "You must be careful. You're tired, aren't you? Shall I have some food prepared? I remember you usually eat at this time." Chen Apo smiled and cast the matter of the corpses to the back of her mind.

Hearing Chen Apo's clearly nostalgic tone, Xu Fu felt a bit strange again.

Yes, eating lunch was his habit, but did Xu Junfang have such a habit too? Xu Fu knew very well that in this era, people mostly ate two meals a day; there would never be a habit like his.

Of course, if Xu Junfang also came from the modern era, perhaps he would have chosen to bring his modern eating habits to this time as well.

Xu Fu pushed these messy guesses out of his mind.

He would eventually be able to verify what the connection between him and Xu Junfang was.

"Let's eat," Xu Fu said calmly.

Chen Apo smiled happily upon hearing this and immediately ordered food to be brought.

Only then did Xu Fu notice that there were indeed servants in the residence. The man who brought the food was middle-aged, though Xu Fu hadn't seen him yesterday.

The man placed the food on the table in front of Xu Fu, then looked up at him. A look of surprise flashed across his face, and he couldn't help but exclaim, "It's you!"

It seemed this man had been a servant in the residence for a long time? Otherwise, how would he remember him?

Xu Fu nodded. The man didn't say much else, but a light flashed in his eyes before he bowed and backed out. Xu Fu didn't pay much attention to the man; he was very familiar with that look in the man's eyes. It was a look of reverence.

After eating, Xu Fu returned to his room to rest. Chen Apo thought he was tired and ordered people not to disturb him.

Back in his room, with no other leads, Xu Fu simply lay down on the bed. It would be best to have another dream... at least one where he could dream about what else Wang He said or did. And how did he leave Yucheng back then?

Xu Fu closed his eyes, these questions swirling in his mind.

But unfortunately, Xu Fu didn't dream of anything. Instead, Ying Zheng made a forceful appearance in his mind—just for a blink of an eye, and then he was gone. Upon waking, the sun was setting. What was deeply etched in Xu Fu's mind was the icy coldness in Ying Zheng's eyes during that fleeting glance. Even now, just recalling it, Xu Fu could vividly feel Ying Zheng's powerful presence and the sense of being pinned to the spot by that single look.

Xu Fu didn't feel fear; instead, an indescribable feeling welled up in his heart—perhaps... a bit of sweetness?

Ying Zheng's strength made him feel happy involuntarily.

Xu Fu propped himself up on the bed, washed his face, and walked out of the room. He had slept for quite a while, and the food he had eaten at noon hadn't fully digested, so Xu Fu had to go out of the residence and walk a few more steps to help with digestion.

He walked along the streets of Yucheng, drawing countless gazes. Although Xu Fu had never cared much about such attention, at this moment, he felt an indescribable sense of irritation. Perhaps it was because his mind was tangled in too many mysteries, and yet, lacking any knack for decryption or deduction, he felt as if something were stuck in his throat.

To be affected by emotions—this was a rare occurrence for Xu Fu.

He hesitated for a moment, then chose to turn into a smaller side street. There were few people here, and he could finally escape those prying eyes.

His gaze gradually swept across the street.

Yucheng should have been a familiar place to him, but now, everything appeared extremely strange in his eyes. Amnesia was truly a terrifying thing.

As he walked, Xu Fu turned into a dead end.

Sensing something was wrong, Xu Fu immediately spun around and demanded sharply, "Who is following me?"

A man emerged from the corner and smiled at Xu Fu, "Sir, I... I have come to ask you for a divination."

Xu Fu let out a slight sigh of relief. At least it wasn't a thug. It seemed that because he hadn't set up his stall today, someone had sought him out instead. Xu Fu found it amusing, but he still looked at the man before him seriously, "What do you wish to divine?"

The man grinned, "Can you read faces, sir? Please, read my face."

Hearing this, Xu Fu felt less inclined to speak.

He didn't need to look closely to see that the man’s physiognomy was poor—one might even say it was terrible. Xu Fu hesitated, wondering if he should say it aloud. A person's face could change, but for an adult, it was extremely difficult. In childhood, a person was like a blank sheet of paper, and anything could be altered, but once adulthood was reached, many things were set in stone and hard to change.

With the man’s face looking so wretched, if Xu Fu were to speak the truth, wouldn't it make the man feel as though he would never be able to turn his life around?

Xu Fu’s thoughts wandered for a moment. Perhaps in the past, he would have spoken the truth without reservation. But now, thinking of the madman Wang He, Xu Fu could not bring himself to be blunt.

Seeing that Xu Fu remained silent, the man grew anxious. He stretched his neck and asked urgently, "Is my face... is it bad?"

Xu Fu still said nothing.

The man continued on his own, "Yes! My face is bad! I knew it! No matter what I do, I lose money! It’s all because of my face... my face... I’ve even ended up alone now, my wife and children have abandoned me... it’s all because of this face!" His emotions were quite volatile, and as he spoke, his expression grew somewhat twisted, with spittle flying from his lips as they moved.

Xu Fu instinctively took a step back, frowning secretly.

Why another madman?

Xu Fu really wanted to curse out loud.

With the man so agitated, he certainly couldn't speak the truth. From what the man said, it was clear he attributed all his life's misfortunes to his physiognomy. Such self-pity and blame-shifting revealed a character that was cowardly, impulsive, irresponsible, and prone to extreme emotions. How could such a person have a good face? Even if it had been decent at first, it would have been gradually corrupted by his own malice.

It is very difficult for a person's face to change for the better, but it is all too easy for it to change for the worse.

After the man finished venting his emotions, he looked up at Xu Fu. He stared fixedly at him, his gaze overlapping with that of the madman from his dream.

He said in a low voice, "I have been looking for you for a long time, sir. Change my fate for me."

Xu Fu’s heart skipped a beat. Could this man be Wang He?

"Sir, why have you stopped speaking?" The man’s body trembled slightly—not from fear, but from agitation and excitement. His eyes glowed as he looked at Xu Fu; Xu Fu felt as if he had become a precious treasure in the man's eyes.

"Say what?" Xu Fu said coldly. "What fate-changing? I don't know what you are talking about."

"How could you not know, sir?" The man became even more agitated, waving his hands as if he might pounce on Xu Fu at any moment. "How could you not know! How could you! You are lying to me!"

Xu Fu retreated further. While he appeared to be staring at the man, his eyes were actually scanning the path, calculating how to escape if the man truly went berserk.

Although he had taken a wrong turn, Xu Fu could still hear the sounds of people outside, meaning this alley was close to the main road, and people outside might notice any commotion.

Xu Fu thought to himself that he would never wander aimlessly in an unfamiliar place again. Not only did it fail to trigger any memories, but it had also attracted a madman.

"You are lying to me! I saw it!" the man insisted.

"Saw what?" Xu Fu kept his tone calm, attempting to use it to influence the man opposite him. Unfortunately, the man seemed entirely lost in his own world and did not perceive Xu Fu’s calmness or indifference.

He shouted excitedly, "I saw it all! I saw Wang He! Back then, Wang He also came to you to change his fate! He came to you to change his fate! It was you who changed his fate!"

A wave of dizziness washed over Xu Fu, and he nearly lost his composure.

What did he mean by "It was you who changed his fate"? Was what this man said true or false? Could it be that after Wang He was rejected, he hadn't given up and found Xu Junfang, and that Xu Junfang had actually changed his fate? Just thinking about it made Xu Fu feel sick.

If it were him, he would never have changed Wang He's fate!

Like this madman today, they didn't look for the root cause of their problems but blamed everything on their physiognomy. Did a change in face really change a person? Wasn't Tian Wei the best example? He possessed a near-perfect face, but due to his character, his face was now subtly changing, shifting in a negative direction.

No... wait!

Xu Fu bit his lip, using the pain to keep his mind clear.

Tian Wei...

That's right!

Just like Tian Wei!

Why did Tian Wei have such a face? Why was there such an eerie disconnect between his face and his true self? Could it be that Tian Wei’s face wasn't originally like that? That this near-perfect face was actually the result of having his physiognomy altered?

"You could change it for Wang He, why can't you change it for me? I can pay you! Once my face is changed, I can keep paying you!" The man said, moving closer to Xu Fu.

"Do you truly want to know if your face is good or not?" Xu Fu interrupted him.

In truth, the best solution would be for Xu Fu to tell him his face was excellent and use his knowledge to deceive the man, praising him to the heavens. But there were risks. Given the man's behavior, he was already convinced his face was bad. If Xu Fu lied, the man might assume Xu Fu was simply unwilling to help, leading him to fly into a rage—Xu Fu couldn't imagine what he might do then.

Besides, Xu Fu generally didn't like to lie.

Except for the unlucky King of Yan, whom he had completely bluffed.

"I do! I want to know how my face is! Between Wang He and me, who is worse?" the man gritted his teeth.

Xu Fu: ...

Even at a time like this, the man was still thinking about comparing himself to Wang He?

"Wang He," Xu Fu said. Of course, Wang He was worse. When Wang He had come to him, his face had shown signs of impending death. As for the man in front of him, although his face was ugly, his spirit listless, and his eyes murky—clearly indicating a poor physiognomy—at least he showed no signs of imminent death.

The man grinned, then said with fanatical intensity, "Sir, change my face! I want to get rid of this damned fate! My life is rotten! I don't want to live like this! You changed Wang He's face, so why can't you change mine?"

"I never changed Wang He's face. I am not skilled in such arts," Xu Fu said coolly. "Isn't there another occultist in the city? Why don't you seek him out?"

"That fraud has already left Yucheng!" the man said excitedly. "I looked for him, but he was useless! I know, it's only you, only you can change it. I saw it! I saw everything, you changed Wang He's face..." The man lowered his head, neurotically repeating the last sentence.

"I saw it with my own eyes..."

"You changed his face, I know it. Wang He is still alive, he is living well, it was all your doing. You can change my face too, why won't you do it? Why won't you help me!"

The man said.

The more Xu Fu heard, the more goosebumps he felt. If he kept listening, he felt his own speculations would be overturned and thrown into chaos by this man.

"Enough! This matter... I will consider it further. Changing one's physiognomy is no small matter. You should go back for now." Xu Fu put on a grand air, lifting his chin and casting a cold, arrogant glance at the man.

The man’s agitated state was strangely calmed by that look. He said with a trembling voice, "You are right, you are absolutely right... this is a major matter... yes... I, I will wait... I will wait for you."

"I will wait for you." These four words seemed to linger on his tongue, spoken with extreme lightness, while his gaze toward Xu Fu became even more fanatical.

Xu Fu suppressed the urge to shudder and cursed "madman" in his heart. Was Yucheng a breeding ground for madmen?

The man smiled and turned to leave. He walked away as happily as a child who had received a piece of candy, showing no signs of the terrifying, frantic state he had been in just moments before.

Xu Fu let out a small sigh of relief and then set off to leave.

Having stood there with tense muscles for so long, Xu Fu felt his legs were a bit weak as he walked.

Throughout the journey, Xu Fu’s mood could not settle. The man’s roaring voice kept repeating in his ears, and he chewed over the words again and again—"I saw it all, it was you who changed Wang He's face."

Was it... me?

Xu Fu clenched his fists, finding it truly hard to accept this conclusion.

If he had really changed Wang He's face back then, what about Tian Wei? Surely he hadn't changed Tian Wei's too? Xu Fu felt an indescribable sense of absurdity, as if he had spent all his effort trying to find the villain behind the scenes, only to discover that he was the villain himself.

As he walked down the street, some people still couldn't help but approach him, perhaps wanting to ask for a divination, but Xu Fu now had a shadow over the practice. He had no desire to divine for anyone in Yucheng, and with his current state of mind, how could he? Xu Fu ignored them entirely and walked all the way back to Granny Chen’s residence.

As soon as Xu Fu entered the door, Granny Chen and the others ran out.

"Where did you go, sir? We haven't seen you for so long. We were scared to death," Xiang'er said, being the quickest to speak.

"My apologies, I slept a bit late this afternoon and wanted to take a walk in Yucheng, hoping it might trigger some memories," Xu Fu’s expression was grim. "Who would have thought I would run into another madman."

"Another madman?" Granny Chen clutched her clothes. "How, how could this be? Are you hurt, sir? Sir... please take someone with you tomorrow, that way you can avoid such madmen."

Xu Fu shook his head and blurted out, "No, I am leaving."

Yes, he had to leave.

He had already obtained what he needed here, and the rest was only danger. He had no Wu by his side, nor any attendants. If something were to happen... no, he couldn't even imagine what would happen if he met with misfortune.

The moment he thought that if he died here, Ying Zheng would never know, Xu Fu felt a sharp pain in his chest.

At this moment, Xu Fu missed Ying Zheng immensely—missed Xianyang, missed everything in the palace... In the past, even when he went out without Ying Zheng’s company, Ying Zheng was effectively by his side. Because his attendants and eunuchs were all from Ying Zheng, sent under his orders to care for him. That was why Xu Fu could always act without worry and do what he pleased.

But this time, he was all alone.

His skills were of no use here.

Xu Fu felt his mood was terrible, like a child who had been wronged outside and was desperate to return to the embrace of an adult for comfort.

Xu Fu was slightly dazed, and he didn't hear a word of what Granny Chen was excitedly saying in his ear.

Granny Chen didn't notice Xu Fu’s distraction; she looked at his cold, unchanging expression and sighed.

"I knew you wouldn't stay here for long," Granny Chen said, sounding a bit sad. Perhaps when people grow old, they miss the past and fear parting.

Xu Fu’s gaze softened as it landed on Granny Chen. "Thank you for your care during these days."

Granny Chen said helplessly, "It has only been two days... that you are leaving so soon is truly... sigh..."

"I need to avoid that madman."

Hearing this, Granny Chen dared not persuade him further, only saying, "Please take care of yourself."

"I will," Xu Fu nodded.

Granny Chen had dinner prepared, and Xu Fu sat down to eat with them. The sadness on Granny Chen’s face lessened quite a bit. She personally saw Xu Fu back to his room. "To be able to share a meal with you after more than ten years is already a rare blessing. I suppose when I die, I will be able to remember your face as I pass."

Hearing this, Xu Fu didn't feel happy; instead, a chill washed over him.

You don't need to think of me when you die.

Thinking of that made him feel cold all over.

Wanting to avoid the madman, Xu Fu decided to leave Yucheng first thing the next morning, hoping the city gates would be open by then.

There were no alarm clocks, and no one would wake him, so Xu Fu decided to sleep early to ensure he could wake early. After washing up, he lay on the bed, forcing down the myriad thoughts in his mind, whispering Ying Zheng’s name until he gradually fell asleep.

When Xu Fu woke the next day, it was not yet bright, but he didn't go back to sleep. He got up, washed, packed his belongings, and without saying goodbye to anyone, headed straight for the gate. Just as he reached the entrance, he saw Yue'er. Her eyes were slightly swollen, as if she hadn't rested well last night. She looked at Xu Fu and asked with reluctance, "Must you leave, sir?"

"Yes."

Yue'er bit her lip, "But... but I have feelings for you, sir..."

Xu Fu didn't even think before saying, "My home is in Xianyang, Qin. I cannot stay in Yucheng."

Yue'er had already interpreted his words. She widened her eyes, trying hard to keep her tears from falling, and said, "Ah, so you already have a wife and family, sir?"

Wife... and family?

Wife... Ying Zheng?

Family... Fusu, Huhai?

Oh, perhaps also Senior Brother Wei Liao...

"Yes," Xu Fu said softly.

"I... I understand. Then, then please go, sir." Once she knew, she didn't say anything like "I am willing to be a concubine." It seemed Granny Chen had taught her well.

For a woman to fall for a man was the most natural thing in the world, and her graceful retreat only made her seem more intelligent and refined.

Dealing with such a girl, Xu Fu felt a sense of relief in his heart.

He bid farewell to Yue'er and walked out through the open gate.

In the distance, there was already a faint glow.

The sun was rising...

Xu Fu felt his mood comforted significantly. However, his good mood didn't last long.

"You lied to me!" A voice, gritted with teeth, rang out not far from him. Xu Fu turned his head to look.

...It was that madman again!

How did he know he was leaving?
