始皇二十四年，秦始皇擢升廷尉李斯为丞相，随后将朝政暂交予太子扶苏，又令公子胡亥、丞相李斯、中车府令赵高、国尉尉缭、将军蒙恬协于太子。
同年，王翦告老归家，正式退出了秦朝的武将队伍。
始皇二十五年，春始，秦始皇携皇后、内侍、护卫，出巡郡县。
不久后，他们的队伍便到达了邹县。
长长的队伍停在了一座府邸之外，县令狗腿地将他们迎进了府中。
县令不知这位皇后的容貌，他只隐约知晓，据传陛下极为宠爱的皇后，却是个男儿。那县令好奇不已，他小心翼翼地抬起头去打量走在前头的人。
只见两人皆着黑袍，一个背影高大英武，一个背影挺拔孤冷。
二人身上散发出气质，都能震慑住人。
县令忙小心地低下了头去。
果然，陛下与皇后自是不同！
只是那县令心底实在好奇极了，好奇得仿佛有一双手在心底挠来挠去一般。
陛下之功盖五帝，这般厉害的人，能被他看中，站在他身侧，受他宠爱的人物，又该是何等绝色？
就在这时候，县令听见前面的二人开口了。
“口渴，肚饿，先在厅中歇一歇，也好让他们都去吃些东西。”
县令听见了这道声音，微微清冷，但嗓音却很是好听，无端让人想起天边仙乐。
“县令。”另一道声音响起了，威严低沉。
县令打了个激灵，当即反应过来这是陛下在叫他。县令忙几个碎步上前，蹭到了二人的跟前去，他躬下腰道：“陛下，臣下知晓，这便命人去准备。”说完，他便顺理成章地抬起了头，去打量对方的神色。
这些小地方的县令，哪有见着陛下的机会？更别说见着皇后了。
这一见，县令就有些傻眼。
这相貌，县令从前哪有机会见着啊？
实在面容英俊，气势逼人！
县令的目光稍稍往旁边一瞥，那就更不得了了！这人看上去年纪极轻，若非身量足够，说他是少年，怕是也有人信的，而且此人面容极为出色，竟是县令从未见过的绝色！只是此人身上气质淡漠，倒教人不敢接近了。
县令在心中暗自咋舌。
也只有这般的人物方才能配上陛下了！陛下也实在厉害，这样的美人儿也能揽入怀中。
县令压下了心底百般思绪，这时候下人已经来到了他的身边，县令马上就吩咐了下去。
徐福和嬴政没再管其它，他们径直走进了厅中坐下。
那县令吩咐完下人后，忙跟了进去，他进去一瞧，才发现陛下竟然连落座，都是与皇后一同，县令一面惊讶一面又感叹不已，怕是女子也少有受这般重视的。
县令刚感慨完便被打发走了，他有心想要多看陛下两眼，但却不敢不从，他顺从地退了下去，趁着这个时候，叫来人去整理房屋了。
……
徐福从未有过这样惬意的时候。
一身的重担都缷了下来。
一路和嬴政出巡，原本应当觉得劳累的路途，竟是变得极为轻松和惬意，嬴政有意迁就他，便将行程放得极慢。
嬴政道：“明日，我们便去登峄山。”
这是帝王必须要做的一件事，登山、祭天地。
徐福也隐约记得，历史上嬴政登了不少的山，而且似乎还留下了石碑。
徐福点头，“好。”虽然他体力不大好，但是登个山也不错，便当做是换一换眼前的风景了，古人不是还常说，登山开阔心胸吗？
很快，下人送来了食物和水。就连县令都没见过他们这样端方绝艳的人物，更莫说下人们了，下人退下去的时候，都还忍不住偷偷打量，又偷偷脸红。
徐福和嬴政坐在一处，慢腾腾地用了食物。
不久，天色微微暗了。
那头的县令还在为难，陛下来到邹县，他作为县令，自然应当是费尽一切力气，不遗余力地讨好陛下。那么常人的做法无非就是摆宴、请美人来献上歌舞。但是陛下那般宠爱皇后，他还会对美人有兴趣吗？县令左思右想，最后还是放弃了。他认为自己的判断没有错，他小心翼翼打量陛下和皇后的时候，能分明地感受到二人间的气氛，是不容他人插入的。县令便估摸着，就算是再好的美人，陛下也定是看不入眼的，当然，邹县之中也难寻一个比皇后长得更好看的美人啊。他擅自做出这样的举动，恐怕反会惹得皇后记恨。
一番衡量之后，县令放下了心。
他并不知道，正是他这样的行为，让他免去了一场被发作的灾难。
毕竟前头就有些不长眼的，还非往嬴政跟前献美人，还不等徐福吃醋了，嬴政就先醋起来了，当即就黑了脸，并且严斥了那些心思不正的官员。
吃过饭食后，徐福和嬴政在府中逛了两圈，这才选定了屋子，入住进去。
自是一夜好眠。
第二日，他们收拾好行装，县令作陪，队伍之后缀了队伍，其中还夹杂了些仰慕始皇风采的儒生。
这一行人往着峄山而去。
徐福走到半道便没力气了，嬴政想也不想，便躬下了腰，道：“阿福既然累了，那便让我带你上去。”竟是做出了要背徐福的姿势。
后面的宫人、侍从们吓得不行。
能让始皇陛下背人上山吗？那不行啊！还不如让几个侍从抬着上去呢！
他们哪里知晓这等献殷勤的情趣！自然不是几个侍从就能替换得了的！
只不过……徐福也并不希望真让嬴政来背自己就是了。
他不希望在这么多人的跟前，折损嬴政的威严。
“不必了，我身体不大好，正巧借此机会磨砺一番。”徐福淡淡道。
嬴政笑了笑，揽住了徐福的肩，好承住他的力气，带着他一块儿继续往前行。
若是从前，徐福早就不想登什么破山了，但今日倒也强迫着，硬生生地登上去了。登顶之后，便有儒生迫不及待地向嬴政进言道，请嬴政选石立碑，刻以碑文，述嬴政之功绩，以传后世。
徐福闻言，并未说话。
他其实认为这样挺好的。
留下碑文，不仅是留给后世考古一个凭据，同样的，也是让后人知晓，嬴政究竟如何厉害，究竟创下了何等的功绩。光是这般想一想，徐福心底都忍不住为之觉得自豪。
说做便做。
嬴政点头后，便看向了徐福，“阿福去选一块巨石。”
徐福也不推拒，特意选了瞧上去最有灵气的一块，指着道：“就它吧。”
儒生们忍不住打量了徐福好几眼，竟是有些对徐福替代嬴政选石而不满。
徐福当然不会理会他们。
他是秦朝国师，何必拉低自己的身段去与这些人计较呢？
选定石块后，便有儒生及工匠，合作在巨石上刻下碑文。
刻定碑文后，徐福还仔细检验了一遍，确认没有哪里不对之后，徐福的心情顿时变得更为松快了。
他们很快就下了峄山，并且准备离开邹县，儒生们不舍错过这样的机会，便向嬴政进言，说起祭天地之事，有儒生道，在泰山祭天、在梁父山祭地和遥祭名山大川。嬴政应允过后，这些儒生便自动黏了上来，跟随队伍前行。
徐福和嬴政离开邹县的这一日，县令遥遥将他们送出了老远，然后才不舍地回转身来。
见过了陛下和皇后的风采，这足以成为他这后半辈子的谈资了。
之后，邹县中不少人都从这位县令的口中，听闻了陛下与皇后的恩爱，此事更被部分人刻于石头上，记载于绢布、竹简上，甚至有人将它当做了故事流传下去，为后世还原这段历史的考据提供了不少的帮助……
·
离开邹县后，他们便径直前往了泰山，在泰山之上立石碑，筑起土坛，举行祭天盛典。
一路以来的好天气，却硬是在泰山手中被破坏了。
徐福等人下山的时候，遭遇了大风大雨，风雨迎面而来，教人们不自觉地眯起了眼。
这一场雨实在来得太突然，就连徐福都未能算到。
有儒生紧张地道：“莫非这是不详的预兆？”
那人的确是蠢笨了点儿，而且也的确被突如其来的风雨吓了一跳。但从他这样大胆地开口说出来以后，他便完蛋了。
徐福都不能容忍谁胡乱这样开口，他当即回头冷声道：“什么不详的征兆？风雨从何处来？从天而来！方才陛下才祭过了天地山川，天上便降下了雨水，雨水为何物？为甘露！可见这正是上天也为陛下的功绩所震动，又感陛下敬天地的赤诚之心，方才降下甘露。”
那儒生被徐福这样堵了一句，面色登时有些不大好看。
而旁的儒生什么也未说，就看着他一人出头。
其余的人，早就知道徐福的本事，此时听闻，心中不由觉得皇后（国师）才是真神仙！口中说出的话，实在令人佩服不已。皇后说得不错，这岂不正是陛下天命所归的意思吗？
嬴政忍不住微微一笑，转头满是柔情地瞥了徐福一眼，道：“阿福说得是。”
那儒生面色已然涨成了猪肝色。
见周围人都不为他出声，儒生也就只有咬咬牙，将话都吞下去了。
因为风雨实在太大，山上又路险，尤其是被雨冲刷着，还有大风刮着，就更难走了。他们毫无准备，此时撞上，就只能生生淋雨了。此时那儒生瞥见了一棵大树，他双眼一亮，心道自己挽回颜面的机会到了！
儒生出声道：“陛下，那处有一大树，风雨中能巍然不动，请陛下到树下避雨。”
旁人也跟着惊叹，“路遇这般奇异的大树，真乃是奇特至极！也唯有陛下方能遇见这般神木了。”
徐福差点忍不住翻白眼的冲动。
什么神木？哪里来的神木？
不就一棵树吗？
竟然还宣扬了这么多话！
徐福冷冷地截断，“不行，陛下不能前往树下躲雨。”
那儒生登时气得不行，心底更是暗暗将这位皇后，钉上了“祸水”“媚君惑上”“心思歹毒”“空有其表”等标签。
不过这时候儒生到底没蠢到底，他没敢冲着徐福愤慨大骂，他只是立即反驳道：“如此大的风雨，陛下不躲一躲，若是病了又该如何？我对陛下实乃一片赤诚之心，只愿陛下能安康。”
这话说得，就仿佛在说他对秦始皇一片真心一般。
徐福是怎么听怎么觉得别扭和膈应。
他冷冰冰地看了一眼那儒生。
徐福知晓自己这一眼通常有着什么样的威力，果不其然，那儒生连这一眼都承受不住，脸色顿时忍不住发起了白。竟是就这样便被徐福的气势慑住了。
儒生连忙后退了两步，等意识到他自己做了什么之后，儒生的面上又涨红了，显然这样的丢面子，让他觉得难以忍受，可对方偏偏又是皇后，哪怕是一个男皇后。
“寻一处稍平的地点，我和陛下躲进马车中。”
幸而他们上山时，死活驱赶了一辆马车上来，此时好歹能挡个雨。
至于其他人，徐福是当真顾不上了。
一辆马车当然只能容下他们二人，其他人也就只能淋着雨了。
侍从们闻言，当然是听从了徐福的话，将马车引到了平地上去。嬴政始终微微笑着，并不发言。他极为享受这样被徐福维护的时刻，至于那个儒生，谁会理他呢？嬴政可是从很早之前，便从徐福这里知晓，雨天是不能往树下躲的。
跟得久了的宫人、侍从也都是知晓这一点的。
哪怕他们不知道这一点，他们自然也是本能地选择信任徐福，而不是那个只顾着出风头的儒生。
儒生见这些人竟然全然不理自己，就连陛下都未曾多看他一眼。
皇后便了不起了吗？皇后说的话才能令人听从吗？不过是个男子！却做了皇后！实在耻辱！儒生恨恨地磨了磨牙。其他儒生比他识时务多了，都选择了听从安排，跟随着他们一块儿挪动位置。
儒生心中的恼恨在翻滚，他实在不甘心就这样轻易认输，于是他咬了咬牙，心道，你们偏要淋雨！那我就偏要躲雨！
那儒生转了个弯儿，直直走向了那棵大树。
而这一头，徐福正撩起车帘，仔细嘱咐外面的人，“勿要靠近大树。”
这些人本就是极为听从命令的，且不说徐福说得有没有道理，哪怕是胡乱说的，他们也都是会听从的。这些人连连点头，他们哪里会想到，一回头便见那儒生躲到了大树下，而且他还拉拽了另一名儒生同去。
徐福顺着看过去，登时也觉得又好气又好笑。
这人还当真不知死活！
不过念在总归是条人命的份儿上，徐福便出声道：“去，去告知他，躲在树下易遭雷击，会出人命。”
侍从点头，深一脚浅一脚地上去了。
嬴政在徐福身后淡淡道：“这般胆敢质疑阿福的人，他要死便让他去送死好了。”
那头侍从很快走到了树前，因为距离稍微有一些远，徐福并不能听清他们在说什么，不过他能瞥见那儒生脸上激动的神色，实在不知晓，这有何好激动的？
侍从与他说了许久，都不见儒生挪动位置。
大约是因为受了徐福的吩咐，那侍从倒也不肯轻易离开，看得徐福都忍不住拧眉，早知道便不将那侍从派过去了，还反倒累得侍从这般费口舌力气，说不准还被儒生气得够呛。
到最后，那侍从果然被那儒生油盐不进的态度气急了，忍不住怒道：“让你从树底下出来，你便出来！皇后说，在树下小心丢了命！”
那儒生大笑道：“躲在树下怎会丢命？”他虽没说完，但脸上明明白白地写着四个大字“无稽之谈”。
二人这段对话，因为声音大了些，周围的人都听了个清楚。
那儒生还未笑完，突然天空中一声轰鸣。
徐福抬头一看，就见半空中划过了一道紫色的闪电，徐福一个心道不好，那闪电便直直落在了大树上，在远处的人看来，那就是一道绚丽的光炸开了。然而站在树底下的人，却能清晰听见轰隆、噼嚓的声音，那棵大树被劈开了，雷电直接落到了树下二人的身上，并且雷电带出的火花还将大树下面未被湿透的树叶枝桠点燃了。
大火嗖地一下蔓延了两人的全身。
众人只听见紧接着响起了两人的怪叫声。
那站在树前的侍从呆了呆，拔腿便跑，显然被吓得不轻。
其他人也是一样，就像是被谁施了定身咒一样，半晌都不敢挪动。
大火和雷电很快将那两人烧焦了，惨叫声在耳边重复着，众人浑身都被雨水浸透了，忍不住狠狠打了个哆嗦。
太……太可怕了……
他们先是一阵庆幸，庆幸自己没有跟随那儒生走过去躲雨，而后又是一阵后怕，若是……若是陛下听从那儒生的话，走进了树底……他们根本不敢想象其后果。
他们又接连打了几个哆嗦，一面心底埋怨那死去的儒生，一面看向徐福的时候，目光便变了。
这些儒生看向徐福的时候，并非敬畏，而是恐惧，就如同见了什么可怕的怪物一般。
徐福对他们的目光全然不在意，待那侍从跑回来之后，徐福对他说了声，“受惊了，去歇息吧。”
那侍从便顿时觉得一身惊吓和疲惫都消去了，他忍不住笑了笑，道：“多谢皇后。”说罢，这就到一边去躲着了。
嬴政伸手将徐福拉了一把，将他拉到了身边来，并且还搂住了他，二人身上都湿透了，不过这样紧贴在一起，总能取些暖。这时候正是春时，春寒还未完全褪去，一场大雨下来，淋得人是有些受不了。
嬴政俯在他的耳边低声道：“那人竟敢得罪寡人的阿福，被雷火烧死，也算是便宜了他。”
徐福舒服地靠在嬴政怀中，淡淡道：“只可惜了那个被他拉过去的人。”
嬴政摇头，“不可惜，阿福都道不能去树下了，且不说阿福话中的对错，但他们身为秦的子民，而阿福乃是大秦的皇后，阿福所言，他们都应当遵守。这二人擅自妄为，往轻了说，是不遵从大秦的皇后，往重了说，那便是不服从于皇权。这样不忠之人，死了好。”
徐福竟然还觉得嬴政说得有点儿对。
徐福没再说话，他就这样靠着嬴政休息了起来。
马车外还伴随着大雨声和雷声，但是这一刻，徐福却觉得宁静得让人心底舒服。
好像人生追求便就是如此。
窗外下着雨，爱人在怀里。
马车外，那些儒生们凑到了一起，也不知在说些什么，不过经过那个儒生之后，剩下的宫人侍从及守卫士兵们，便都对这些儒生有些不满。
光会嘴上说，真的本事却半点没有！实在让人瞧不起！
更重要的是，他们竟然还敢不尊皇后！
儒生们还尚未意识到有哪里不对，毕竟他们向来身份不低，走到哪里都能受到优待呢，此时当然也不会分神去思考，自己是否有何处不妥，得罪了皇后和陛下。
……
这场雨来得快，去得也快，没多久，雨便停了。
众人舒了一口气。
那儒生惨死的画面带给他们的冲击太大，他们实在也有些忧心，自己会不会也死成那个模样。
徐福掀起车帘，和嬴政一同走了下去。
徐福当先往那棵树的方向瞥了一眼。
他们在山上本就离天很近，更被说大树高耸了，那真是……雷不劈他劈谁？
其他人见他们下了马车，忙唤道：“陛下，皇后。”
那些儒生们看向徐福的目光更为忌惮了。
嬴政对这些目光有些不快，于是不着痕迹地拧了拧眉。
“去瞧一瞧树下。”嬴政冷声道，他没再分给儒生们半点目光。
儒生们虽然觉得哪里有些怪异，但到底并未多想。
士兵们走上前去，拨弄了一下尸体又迅速退开。
那二人已然浑身焦黑，不成模样了。
士兵们也不免被吓了一跳。
那一幕可实在太震撼人了，等看见了尸体便更觉得可怕。幸而他们向来都极为听从皇后所言。
嬴政没说将人埋葬的事，直接就下令说继续下山。
埋葬？
就这样两人，还配入土为安吗？
嬴政冷着脸想道。
接下来倒是没遇见什么大雨了，他们平安地下了山。
只是徐福不知晓，历史上，嬴政还当真躲到了那棵大树之下，而嬴政有龙气护体，还当真没什么雷来劈他，嬴政躲完雨后，大喜之下，还赐封那棵树为“五大夫”。这一段故事还流传到了后世呢。
下了泰山之后，休息一日，他们便又再度启程了。
这一次他们前往了梁父山祭地，后又立碑刻文，曰：皇帝临位，作制明法，臣下脩饬。二十有四年，初并天下，罔不宾服……
之后他们又沿渤海岸往东走，途经黄县、腄县，后又登上成山的顶峰，登上之罘（ｆú，浮）山，皆树立石碑歌颂秦之功德，然后再离去。
这一路，他们便走了两个多月。
两个多月后，他们往南走，登上了琅邪山。
琅邪山比之从前的山峰，更为古拙大气，徐福和嬴政恰好都对此地较为偏爱，便借此机会，在琅邪山歇了下来。
琅邪山的风景极为美丽，徐福身置琅邪山中，甚至能缓慢地感觉到周身溢来的灵气，无论是错觉还是属真，徐福都选择了同嬴政住在山中。
于是琅邪山开始修建了琅邪台。
此处人烟稀少，显得有些清寂，嬴政为了寻人来打消这种状态，便下令，让三万户百姓迁来，在琅邪山下落地生根，繁衍生息。
徐福站在琅邪山上，逐渐见证着琅邪山的变化。
从琅邪台到迁来的众多百姓……
徐福觉得惊叹。
他与嬴政站在山巅之上，脚下云雾纷纷，隐约能瞥见山脚下和山腰新修起的房屋和百姓。
嬴政指了指脚下的云雾，笑道：“阿福可有羽化登仙之感？”
徐福错愕地低头去看，仔细感受一番，竟是还当真有此错觉。
嬴政兴致起，又唤来人，在琅邪山上立石碑，塑徐福之雕像，在石碑上刻碑文，大意便是君房在琅邪台，似要羽化登仙……云云，全篇都是赞颂徐福的。
徐福没想到嬴政想到便立即做了，他看着他和嬴政的石碑靠在一处，登时还真有些说不出话来。
他更没想到的是……
其实在他们从山巅往下望去的时候，那些百姓，也忍不住仰头往上看。
百姓们觉得自己瞧见了一黑一白两人，这两人衣袍飘飘，似神仙落入云雾间，引得百姓们争相叩拜，此后还编成了传说，传于后世……
甚至琅邪山上的雕像也影响到了其他地方的百姓，百姓们自发设石碑，塑雕像，颂扬国师君房与始皇陛下。
……此乃后事，便且不提。
chapters.title: 第263章
chapters.translated_text:
Ying Zheng brought Xu Fu up to the city walls. Xu Fu looked down from his vantage point at the commoners and officials below, and a faint suspicion began to rise in his heart. But wasn't this day coming a bit too suddenly? Xu Fu unconsciously pressed his lips together.

After Ying Zheng changed his title to "First Emperor," he hadn't issued many edicts, yet this one had become one of the few.

The attendant held the freshly minted "Imperial Edict," his voice rising involuntarily as if he felt a great sense of honor. "The First Emperor decrees: Qin possesses Junfang, who is like the pillar of the court and the bulwark of the nation..."

Xu Fu's heart beat a little faster, and his ears began to heat up and turn red of their own accord.

"...Qin hereby establishes the position of State Preceptor for the Xu clan's Junfang. Let this be proclaimed to the world, so that all may hear and know."

The general meaning was that Xu Fu was praised as the one and only person in heaven and earth, his achievements were unparalleled, and he possessed peerless wisdom, vast supernatural powers, and a handsome appearance (?). Thus, the Qin Dynasty had specifically created the position of State Preceptor for him, and from this day forward, he would be the State Preceptor.

Xu Fu felt as if he had been vividly praised into a Mary Sue flower.

Yet, even as a Mary Sue flower, he couldn't help but let the corners of his mouth lift slightly. His eyes were bright, and a smile appeared on his face. However, in the eyes of the people below the city wall, Xu Fu remained cold, aloof, and awe-inspiring. They strained their necks, unwilling to miss a single shred of his grace.

Then the attendant announced that on the day of the appointment of the State Preceptor, the people were permitted to feast and celebrate.

Counting carefully, aside from today, such permission for the world to gather and drink had only been granted during the appointment of the Queen and the unification of the world. With such an edict issued today, the whole world would know just how profound the favor bestowed upon the State Preceptor was.

After this proclamation to the world, Ying Zheng led Xu Fu down from the city wall and headed toward the Ancestral Temple.

With Su Yi presiding over the rites, Xu Fu followed Ying Zheng to worship the ancestors in a daze.

But the problem was... he was just a State Preceptor, why was he worshipping at the Ancestral Temple? This was the Ancestral Temple of the Qin royal family! Would those Qin ancestors really not be angered enough to "jump" right up?

However, Ying Zheng's expression was far too solemn, with no hint of a joke, so Xu Fu had no choice but to comply.

The two of them, dressed in similar sacrificial robes, worshipped the ancestors of Qin in the Ancestral Temple with the utmost sincerity and formality. The ministers stood outside the temple, their faces turning blue, but in the end, they couldn't utter a single word.

Originally, appointing Xu Fu as Queen had already been shocking enough. As time passed, they had gradually become accustomed to comforting themselves, even mocking him in private—after all, a man being treated as a woman wasn't a good thing, and he had even been stripped of the position of Si-Che Shu-Zhang. But being Queen, or even Empress, was one thing—everyone could comfort themselves that way—but to also be the State Preceptor, and then to enter the Ancestral Temple openly and legitimately???

Was this not going too far???

The ministers' faces turned an even deeper shade of blue, but they all knew that this was not the best time to oppose the Emperor. Now that the Emperor held absolute power and his prestige had reached its peak, he didn't even need to hesitate before executing someone. Who would dare to provoke Ying Zheng? At this time, the censors were far from having the status they would have in later generations, and given Ying Zheng's overbearing nature, he would never allow anyone to override his will.

Finally, Xu Fu finished kowtowing, and Ying Zheng supported him, standing up together with him.

When they turned to face the ministers again, the ministers could fully sense just how high-spirited and joyful their Emperor was—not much different from when he had unified the six kingdoms.

The ministers felt even more bitter in their hearts.

Seeing this, they dared not voice any opposition.

Just... let it be. They had to be thankful that Xu Fu was not someone who liked to interfere in state affairs; otherwise, if a "male beauty" were to disrupt the country and execute all the ministers he didn't like, that would be the real trouble.

After the ancestral rites, Ying Zheng took Xu Fu to the next location. The ministers followed along miserably. Of course, the commoners could not follow; if so many people crowded over, wouldn't there be a stampede?

The place Ying Zheng took Xu Fu to was another palace, but this one was built extremely high. Standing in front of it and looking up, one would have the illusion that it touched the sky.

Ying Zheng stood behind Xu Fu, his hand resting on his shoulder, and whispered, "This place represents the Ziwei Star at the pole of the heavens. I have named it the 'Xin Palace.' If A-Fu wishes to observe the celestial phenomena, this is the best location."

To put it more simply, this was Xu Fu's observatory.

Only Ying Zheng had the grand scale to build an observatory the size of a palace, and only he was willing to do so.

Xu Fu lowered his head, the strain on his neck relieved. He moved his lips, but in the end, he couldn't say anything.

The ministers were nearly fainting.

King Zhou of Shang built the Deer Terrace and Sand Mound for Daji, and King You of Zhou built the beacon towers for Baosi. Now, their Emperor had built the Xin Palace for a man!

A man!

At least those others were built for women. Why did their Emperor insist on not following the path of his predecessors and build one for a man?

"Follow me inside." Ying Zheng took Xu Fu's hand, showing his affection openly and without avoidance in front of his ministers.

The ministers were about to follow, but were ruthlessly blocked outside. They felt even more heartbroken.

As the power of the Qin State grew, there was naturally no lack of money or manpower to build palaces. The Xin Palace was built with exceptional grandeur. Once inside, Xu Fu could see tools for divination, and on both sides were large bookshelves piled with many classics that would definitely be fought over in later generations.

Xu Fu scanned them briefly and then followed Ying Zheng up to the small attic on the top floor of the Xin Palace. Standing there, Xu Fu indeed had a better perspective for observing the celestial phenomena. The old Grand Diviner's little tower was truly not worth mentioning compared to this.

Xu Fu unconsciously closed his eyes, feeling the wind brush against him...

He could clearly feel how much thought Ying Zheng had put into this, and how much heart he had poured into it.

How could Xu Fu not be moved in his heart?

He opened his eyes and moved his fingers, scratching Ying Zheng's palm.

"Let's go down," Xu Fu said.

In fact, at this moment, the emotions in Xu Fu's heart were layering upon each other, nearing a peak.

Ying Zheng took him to the Ancestral Temple to openly declare to the ancestors, the ministers, and even the world that the relationship between them was recognized—even to the point of being allowed into the Ancestral Temple.

Xu Fu understood the affection hidden within, and the more he understood, the greater the waves in his heart became.

"Alright, let's go." Ying Zheng gripped Xu Fu's hand tighter and led him downstairs.

After walking out of the Xin Palace, Xu Fu couldn't help but ask, "Are we going anywhere else?"

Looking at the ashen faces of the ministers, Xu Fu really couldn't bear to hurt them any further.

"No more." Ying Zheng leaned down and whispered in his ear, "Does A-Fu feel satisfied?"

"Satisfied," Xu Fu whispered.

He was satisfied. He had won the hearts of the people, suppressed the opposition of the ministers in the court, and conquered the Ministry of Rites. He had sat firmly in the position of State Preceptor, and no one could point fingers at his position anymore.

Now, sitting in the position of State Preceptor, Xu Fu was truly worthy of the name.

The ministers slowly breathed a sigh of relief and dispersed.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng boarded the carriage and returned to the Xianyang Palace.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but stroke the hair hanging behind Xu Fu's head. Because Ying Zheng had handled things so perfectly to Xu Fu's liking, hitting the mark in his heart, Xu Fu couldn't even bring himself to refuse, letting Ying Zheng continue to touch him.

Fortunately, the ministers had already left; otherwise, if they had seen this scene, they would surely have felt another heavy blow to their chests.

The carriage gradually moved away.

The Xin Palace stood there, towering and sharp in the cold wind.

...

The news of the Qin Dynasty establishing the position of State Preceptor quickly spread throughout the world, and everyone learned the name of this State Preceptor: Xu Junfang.

Those who had once received kindness from Xu Fu finally realized that the Xu-surnamed alchemist from back then was the current State Preceptor of the Qin Dynasty. And these people who had received his kindness were scattered everywhere, many of them even being from other states.

Such as Zhao, Wei, and others...

Once these commoners realized this, they immediately accepted this State Preceptor Xu Fu, and their resistance to Qin's unification actually decreased significantly. After all, their benefactor, and even their object of faith, was now the State Preceptor of Qin, and it was rumored that he had always been a high official of Qin. From the small to the large, from one person to a hundred, these commoners suddenly felt they could see the style of Qin officials through Xu Fu's actions. Perhaps the Qin Dynasty could truly lead them to a good life...

It wouldn't be any worse than before, anyway.

Thus, after the news of the State Preceptor's appointment spread, the governors were surprised to find that the commoners in various places had become much more docile. This was truly a miracle!

The process of Qin's unification of the people was greatly promoted as a result. Of course, that is a story for another time.

In short, the name of Xu Fu had spread throughout the world.

It was completely different from that other life in the Qin Dynasty!

·

In the 24th year of the First Emperor, the First Emperor of Qin promoted the Commandant of Justice, Li Si, to Chancellor, and then temporarily handed over state affairs to Crown Prince Fusu, ordering Prince Huhai, Chancellor Li Si, the Prefect of the Carriage Office Zhao Gao, the Commandant of the State Wei Liao, and General Meng Tian to assist the Crown Prince.

In the same year, Wang Jian announced his retirement due to old age, formally withdrawing from the ranks of Qin's military generals.

In the 25th year of the First Emperor, at the beginning of spring, the First Emperor of Qin, accompanied by the Empress, attendants, and guards, went on an inspection tour of the commanderies and counties.

Not long after, their procession arrived at Zou County.

The long procession stopped outside a mansion, and the county magistrate obsequiously welcomed them into the residence.

The magistrate did not know the appearance of this Empress. He only vaguely knew that it was rumored that the Empress, whom the Emperor favored greatly, was a man. The magistrate was extremely curious, and he carefully raised his head to observe the people walking in front.

He saw two people, both dressed in black robes. One had a tall and heroic back, and the other had a straight and aloof back.

The aura emanating from both of them was enough to awe anyone.

The magistrate hurriedly lowered his head carefully.

Indeed, the Emperor and the Empress were naturally different!

But the magistrate was truly curious in his heart, as if a pair of hands were scratching at him.

The Emperor's achievements surpassed the Five Emperors. What kind of peerless beauty could be favored by such a powerful man and stand by his side?

Just then, the magistrate heard the two in front speak.

"Thirsty and hungry. Let's rest in the hall for a while, and let them all have something to eat as well."

The magistrate heard this voice; it was slightly cold, but the tone was very pleasant, inexplicably reminding one of celestial music from the heavens.

"Magistrate." Another voice sounded, majestic and deep.

The magistrate gave a start, immediately realizing that the Emperor was calling him. He hurriedly took a few small steps forward, sidling up to the two, and bowed his waist. "Your Majesty, your servant understands. I will order people to prepare it immediately." Having said this, he naturally raised his head to observe the other's expression.

How would a magistrate of such a small place have the chance to see the Emperor? Let alone the Empress.

Upon seeing him, the magistrate was a bit stunned.

He had never had the chance to see such a face before!

Truly handsome, with an imposing aura!

The magistrate glanced slightly to the side, and that was even more incredible! This person looked extremely young; if not for his stature, one might believe he was a youth. Moreover, his face was extremely outstanding, a peerless beauty the magistrate had never seen before! It was just that this person's aura was indifferent, making one afraid to approach.

The magistrate clicked his tongue in his heart.

Only such a person could be a match for the Emperor! The Emperor was truly amazing to be able to hold such a beauty in his arms.

The magistrate suppressed the myriad thoughts in his heart. By then, the servants had already come to his side, and the magistrate immediately gave the orders.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng didn't pay attention to anything else and walked straight into the hall to sit down.

After the magistrate finished ordering the servants, he hurriedly followed them in. When he looked inside, he discovered that the Emperor was actually sitting together with the Empress. The magistrate was surprised and sighed endlessly; even women were rarely treated with such importance.

The magistrate was dismissed right after he finished sighing. He wanted to take another look at the Emperor, but he dared not disobey. He obediently retreated and took the opportunity to call people to tidy up the rooms.

...

Xu Fu had never felt so comfortable.

The heavy burden on his body had been lifted.

Traveling with Ying Zheng, the journey that should have felt tiring actually became very relaxed and pleasant. Ying Zheng intentionally accommodated him, keeping the pace very slow.

Ying Zheng said, "Tomorrow, we will climb Mount Yi."

This was something an emperor had to do: climb mountains and sacrifice to heaven and earth.

Xu Fu also vaguely remembered that in history, Ying Zheng climbed many mountains and seemed to have left stone tablets behind.

Xu Fu nodded, "Alright." Although his physical strength wasn't great, climbing a mountain wouldn't be bad. He would treat it as a change of scenery. Didn't the ancients often say that climbing mountains broadens the mind?

Soon, the servants brought food and water. Even the magistrate had never seen such upright and stunning figures, let alone the servants. When the servants retreated, they couldn't help but peek and blush secretly.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng sat together and ate their food slowly.

Not long after, the sky grew slightly dark.

The magistrate on the other side was still in a dilemma. With the Emperor coming to Zou County, as the magistrate, he should naturally do everything in his power to please the Emperor. The common practice would be to set up a banquet and invite beauties to perform songs and dances. But with the Emperor favoring the Empress so much, would he still be interested in beauties? The magistrate thought left and right, and finally gave up. He believed his judgment was correct; when he carefully observed the Emperor and the Empress, he could clearly feel the atmosphere between them, which did not allow anyone else to intervene. The magistrate reckoned that even the best beauty would not catch the Emperor's eye. Of course, it was hard to find a beauty in Zou County better-looking than the Empress anyway. If he made such a move without authorization, he might instead incur the Empress's resentment.

After some weighing, the magistrate felt relieved.

He did not know that it was precisely this behavior that saved him from a disaster.

After all, there had been some blind people before who insisted on offering beauties to Ying Zheng. Before Xu Fu could even get jealous, Ying Zheng got jealous first, immediately darkening his face and severely reprimanding those officials with ulterior motives.

After eating, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng strolled around the mansion twice before choosing a room to stay in.

It was, of course, a good night's sleep.

The next day, they packed their luggage. The magistrate accompanied them, and the procession was followed by another, which included some Confucian scholars who admired the First Emperor's style.

This group headed toward Mount Yi.

Xu Fu ran out of energy halfway up. Ying Zheng didn't even think about it and bowed his waist, saying, "Since A-Fu is tired, let me carry you up." He actually made a gesture to carry Xu Fu on his back.

The palace attendants and servants behind were terrified.

Could they let the First Emperor carry someone up a mountain? That wouldn't do! It would be better to have a few servants carry him up!

How could they understand this kind of romantic gesture! Naturally, it couldn't be replaced by a few servants!

However... Xu Fu didn't really want Ying Zheng to carry him either.

He didn't want to diminish Ying Zheng's majesty in front of so many people.

"No need. My body isn't very good, so I'll just take this opportunity to temper myself," Xu Fu said lightly.

Ying Zheng smiled and put his arm around Xu Fu's shoulder to support his weight, leading him forward together.

If it were in the past, Xu Fu would have long since refused to climb any mountain, but today he forced himself to climb it. After reaching the top, some Confucian scholars couldn't wait to advise Ying Zheng to choose a stone to erect a monument, carve an inscription on it, and describe the Emperor's achievements to pass on to later generations.

Xu Fu heard this and said nothing.

He actually thought this was quite good.

Leaving an inscription was not only a piece of evidence for future archaeology but also a way for later generations to know just how powerful Ying Zheng was and what kind of achievements he had created. Just thinking about it, Xu Fu couldn't help but feel proud.

No sooner said than done.

After Ying Zheng nodded, he looked at Xu Fu, "A-Fu, go and choose a giant boulder."

Xu Fu did not decline; he specifically chose the one that looked the most spiritually resonant and pointed at it, saying, "That one will do."

The Confucian scholars couldn't help but size Xu Fu up several times, actually feeling somewhat dissatisfied that he had taken it upon himself to choose the stone instead of Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu, of course, paid them no mind.

As the State Preceptor of the Qin Dynasty, why should he lower himself to haggle with these people?

Once the stone was selected, Confucian scholars and craftsmen worked together to carve the inscription onto the giant boulder.

After the inscription was carved, Xu Fu carefully inspected it one more time. Confirming that nothing was amiss, his mood became even more relaxed.

They soon descended Mount Yi and prepared to leave Zou County. The Confucian scholars, unwilling to miss such an opportunity, submitted advice to Ying Zheng regarding the rituals of sacrificing to Heaven and Earth. Some scholars suggested performing the sacrifice to Heaven at Mount Tai, the sacrifice to Earth at Mount Liangfu, and remote sacrifices to the famous mountains and great rivers. After Ying Zheng gave his consent, these scholars automatically latched onto them, following the procession as it moved forward.

On the day Xu Fu and Ying Zheng left Zou County, the county magistrate saw them off from a great distance before reluctantly turning back.

Having witnessed the grace of the Emperor and the Empress, this was enough to become a topic of conversation for the rest of his life.

Afterward, many people in Zou County heard from this magistrate about the deep affection between the Emperor and the Empress. This matter was even carved onto stone by some, recorded on silk and bamboo slips, and some even passed it down as a story, providing significant help to later generations in reconstructing this period of history...

·

After leaving Zou County, they headed straight for Mount Tai, where they erected a stone tablet on the summit, built an earthen altar, and held a grand ceremony to sacrifice to Heaven.

The good weather they had enjoyed along the way was ruined right there on Mount Tai.

As Xu Fu and the others descended the mountain, they encountered a fierce storm. The wind and rain lashed at them, forcing people to squint involuntarily.

This rain came so suddenly that even Xu Fu had not been able to foresee it.

A Confucian scholar said nervously, "Could this be an ominous omen?"

That man was indeed a bit foolish, and he had truly been startled by the sudden storm. But from the moment he boldly spoke those words, he was finished.

Xu Fu could not tolerate anyone speaking such nonsense. He immediately turned back and said coldly, "What ominous omen? Where does the wind and rain come from? It comes from Heaven! His Majesty has just sacrificed to the Heaven, Earth, and mountains, and now Heaven has sent down rain. What is this rain? It is sweet dew! It is clear that Heaven itself is moved by His Majesty's achievements and, touched by his sincere heart in revering Heaven and Earth, has sent down this sweet dew."

The Confucian scholar was blocked by Xu Fu's retort, and his expression immediately turned unpleasant.

The other scholars said nothing, simply watching him stand out alone.

The rest of them had long known of Xu Fu's abilities. Hearing this now, they couldn't help but feel that the Empress (State Preceptor) was indeed a true immortal! The words he spoke were truly admirable. The Empress was right; wasn't this exactly the sign that His Majesty was the one ordained by Heaven?

Ying Zheng couldn't help but smile slightly. He turned his head and cast a glance full of tenderness at Xu Fu, saying, "A-Fu is right."

The Confucian scholar's face had already turned the color of a pig's liver.

Seeing that no one around him would speak up for him, the scholar had no choice but to grit his teeth and swallow his words.

Because the wind and rain were so fierce and the mountain paths were dangerous—especially with the rain washing over them and the strong winds blowing—it was even harder to walk. They had no preparations, so when they hit this, they could only endure the downpour. Just then, the scholar caught sight of a large tree. His eyes lit up, thinking that his chance to regain his dignity had arrived!

The Confucian scholar spoke up, "Your Majesty, there is a large tree over there that stands firm in the wind and rain. Please, Your Majesty, go under the tree to take shelter."

Others exclaimed in wonder, "To encounter such a miraculous tree on the road is truly extraordinary! Only Your Majesty could encounter such a divine tree."

Xu Fu almost couldn't resist the urge to roll his eyes.

What divine tree? Where did this divine tree come from?

Isn't it just a tree?

To think they would go on and on about it!

Xu Fu coldly cut them off, "No, His Majesty must not go under the tree to take shelter from the rain."

The Confucian scholar was instantly furious, and in his heart, he secretly pinned labels on this Empress: "siren," "bewitching the monarch," "malicious intentions," and "all show and no substance."

However, the scholar wasn't completely stupid at this moment; he didn't dare to lash out at Xu Fu. He simply retorted immediately, "With such heavy wind and rain, if His Majesty doesn't take shelter and falls ill, what then? My heart is truly sincere toward Your Majesty; I only wish for Your Majesty's health."

The way he said this made it sound as if he were the only one with a sincere heart toward the First Emperor.

Everything about it felt awkward and grating to Xu Fu.

He gave the scholar a cold, icy look.

Xu Fu knew the power that this look usually held. Sure enough, the scholar couldn't even withstand this gaze; his face instantly turned pale. He was completely cowed by Xu Fu's aura.

The scholar retreated two steps in a hurry. Once he realized what he had done, his face flushed red again. Clearly, such a loss of face was unbearable to him, yet the person he was facing was the Empress—even if he was a male Empress.

"Find a relatively flat spot; the Emperor and I will take shelter in the carriage."

Fortunately, they had insisted on bringing a carriage up the mountain, so at least it could block the rain.

As for the others, Xu Fu truly couldn't spare the energy to worry about them.

A single carriage could, of course, only hold the two of them, so the others would just have to get wet.

Upon hearing this, the attendants naturally followed Xu Fu's instructions and led the carriage to a flat area. Ying Zheng remained smiling slightly, not saying a word. He thoroughly enjoyed being protected by Xu Fu like this. As for that Confucian scholar, who would pay him any mind? Ying Zheng had known from Xu Fu long ago that one should not take shelter under a tree during a rainstorm.

The palace servants and attendants who had been with them for a long time also knew this.

Even if they didn't know it, they would instinctively choose to trust Xu Fu rather than that Confucian scholar who was only interested in showing off.

The Confucian scholar saw that these people ignored him completely, and even the Emperor hadn't spared him a second glance.

Is being an Empress so great? Does only what the Empress says deserve to be followed? He's just a man! Yet he became Empress! It's truly a disgrace! The scholar gnashed his teeth in hatred. The other scholars were much more sensible than him; they all chose to follow the arrangements and moved along with them.

The resentment in the scholar's heart churned. He was truly unwilling to admit defeat so easily, so he gritted his teeth and thought, "You insist on getting wet! Then I insist on taking shelter!"

The scholar took a turn and walked straight toward that large tree.

On this side, Xu Fu was lifting the carriage curtain, carefully instructing the people outside, "Do not go near the large tree."

These people were extremely obedient to orders. Regardless of whether what Xu Fu said made sense, even if it were nonsense, they would still listen. They nodded repeatedly. How could they have imagined that when they turned back, they would see the scholar hiding under the large tree, and he had even dragged another scholar along with him.

Xu Fu looked over and immediately felt both angry and amused.

This person truly had no regard for his own life!

However, considering it was a human life after all, Xu Fu said, "Go, go tell him that hiding under a tree is prone to lightning strikes and will cost them their lives."

The attendant nodded and made his way over, stumbling through the mud.

Ying Zheng said coldly from behind Xu Fu, "For someone to dare to question A-Fu like this, if he wants to die, let him go and seek his own death."

The attendant soon reached the tree. Because the distance was a bit far, Xu Fu couldn't hear what they were saying, but he could see the excited expression on the scholar's face. He really didn't know what there was to be excited about.

The attendant spoke with him for a long time, but the scholar wouldn't budge.

Perhaps because he was following Xu Fu's instructions, the attendant was unwilling to leave easily. Xu Fu couldn't help but knit his brows; if he had known, he wouldn't have sent the attendant over, only to have him waste his breath and effort, and likely be infuriated by the scholar to boot.

In the end, the attendant was indeed exasperated by the scholar's stubborn attitude and couldn't help but shout angrily, "I told you to come out from under the tree! The Empress said that hiding under a tree is dangerous and you might lose your life!"

The scholar laughed loudly, "How could hiding under a tree cost one's life?" Although he didn't finish his sentence, his face clearly displayed the words "absurd nonsense."

Because their voices were a bit loud, everyone around heard the conversation clearly.

The scholar hadn't even finished laughing when there was a sudden roar in the sky.

Xu Fu looked up and saw a purple bolt of lightning streak across the sky. Xu Fu thought to himself, "Oh no," and the lightning struck straight down onto the large tree. To those far away, it looked like a brilliant burst of light. However, those standing under the tree could clearly hear the rumbling and crackling sounds. The tree was split open, and the lightning struck the two people directly beneath it. Furthermore, the sparks from the lightning ignited the dry leaves and branches under the tree that hadn't been soaked through.

The fire spread over the two men in a flash.

Everyone heard the strange screams that followed immediately after.

The attendant who had been standing in front of the tree froze for a moment, then turned and ran, clearly terrified.

The others were the same; it was as if someone had cast a freezing spell on them, and for a long while, no one dared to move.

The fire and lightning quickly charred the two men. Their screams echoed in everyone's ears. Everyone was soaked to the bone by the rain and couldn't help but shiver violently.

Too... too terrifying...

They first felt a sense of relief that they hadn't followed that scholar to take shelter under the tree, and then a lingering fear: if... if His Majesty had listened to that scholar and walked under the tree... they couldn't even imagine the consequences.

They shivered again and again. While blaming the dead scholar in their hearts, their gazes changed when they looked at Xu Fu.

When these scholars looked at Xu Fu, it was not with reverence, but with fear, as if they had seen some terrifying monster.

Xu Fu didn't care about their gazes at all. After the attendant ran back, Xu Fu said to him, "You've been startled, go and rest."

The attendant immediately felt all his fright and fatigue vanish. He couldn't help but smile and say, "Thank you, Empress." With that, he went to the side to take shelter.

Ying Zheng reached out and pulled Xu Fu toward him, wrapping his arms around him. Both of them were soaked through, but pressing close together like this provided some warmth. It was spring, and the spring chill had not yet fully faded; after being caught in such a heavy rain, it was hard for anyone to bear.

Ying Zheng whispered in his ear, "That man dared to offend my A-Fu; being burned to death by lightning is getting off easy."

Xu Fu leaned comfortably in Ying Zheng's arms and said calmly, "It's just a pity for the person he dragged along with him."

Ying Zheng shook his head, "Not a pity. A-Fu said not to go under the tree. Regardless of whether A-Fu was right or wrong, they are subjects of Qin, and A-Fu is the Empress of Great Qin. They should have obeyed what A-Fu said. These two acted willfully; to put it mildly, they disobeyed the Empress of Great Qin, and to put it severely, they defied imperial authority. For such disloyal people, it is good that they are dead."

Xu Fu actually felt that Ying Zheng was somewhat right.

Xu Fu didn't speak again; he just leaned against Ying Zheng and rested.

Outside the carriage, there was still the sound of heavy rain and thunder, but at this moment, Xu Fu felt a peace that made his heart feel comfortable.

It seemed that this was what one pursued in life.

Rain falling outside the window, and one's lover in one's arms.

Outside the carriage, those Confucian scholars gathered together, not knowing what they were saying. However, after what happened to that scholar, the remaining palace servants, attendants, and guards were all somewhat dissatisfied with these scholars.

All they could do was talk, but they had no real ability! It was truly contemptible!

More importantly, they actually dared to disrespect the Empress!

The Confucian scholars hadn't yet realized that anything was wrong. After all, they had always held high status and received preferential treatment wherever they went. Naturally, they wouldn't spare any thought to whether they had done anything improper or offended the Empress and the Emperor.

……

This rain came quickly and went quickly. Before long, the rain stopped.

Everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

The impact of the scene of the scholar's tragic death was too great, and they were truly worried that they might also die in such a manner.

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain and stepped out with Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu first glanced in the direction of the tree.

They were already very close to the sky on the mountain, not to mention the tree was towering. It was truly... if the lightning didn't strike it, who would it strike?

Seeing them step out of the carriage, the others hurriedly called out, "Your Majesty, Empress."

The Confucian scholars looked at Xu Fu with even more apprehension.

Ying Zheng was somewhat displeased by these gazes, so he frowned imperceptibly.

"Go and take a look under the tree," Ying Zheng said coldly, not sparing the scholars another glance.

Although the scholars felt something was strange, they didn't think too much of it.

The soldiers walked up, poked at the corpses, and quickly retreated.

The two were already charred black and unrecognizable.

The soldiers couldn't help but be startled.

That scene had been truly shocking, and seeing the corpses made it feel even more terrifying. Fortunately, they had always been extremely obedient to what the Empress said.

Ying Zheng didn't mention burying them, simply ordering them to continue down the mountain.

Bury them?

Did these two even deserve to be laid to rest?

Ying Zheng thought with a cold face.

They didn't encounter any more heavy rain and safely descended the mountain.

It was just that Xu Fu didn't know that in history, Ying Zheng had indeed taken shelter under that large tree. And because Ying Zheng was protected by dragon qi, no lightning had struck him. After the rain stopped, Ying Zheng, in his great joy, had even bestowed the title of "Grand Master" (Wudaifu) upon that tree. This story had even been passed down to later generations.

After descending Mount Tai and resting for a day, they set off again.

This time they headed to Mount Liangfu to sacrifice to Earth, and later erected a tablet with an inscription that read: "The Emperor ascended the throne, established laws and regulations, and the ministers rectified their conduct. In the twenty-fourth year, he first unified the world, and all submitted..."

Afterward, they traveled east along the Bohai coast, passing through Huang County and Chui County, then climbed to the peak of Chengshan, and ascended Mount Zhifu, all while erecting stone tablets to praise the merits of Qin before departing.

This journey took them more than two months.

Two months later, they traveled south and ascended Mount Langya.

Mount Langya was more ancient and majestic than the previous peaks. Xu Fu and Ying Zheng both happened to have a preference for this place, so they took the opportunity to rest on Mount Langya.

The scenery of Mount Langya was extremely beautiful. Situated on the mountain, Xu Fu could even slowly feel the spiritual energy overflowing around him. Whether it was an illusion or reality, Xu Fu chose to stay on the mountain with Ying Zheng.

Thus, construction of the Langya Terrace began on Mount Langya.

This place was sparsely populated and seemed somewhat lonely. To dispel this state, Ying Zheng ordered thirty thousand households to relocate here to take root and multiply at the foot of Mount Langya.

Xu Fu stood on Mount Langya, gradually witnessing the changes in the mountain.

From the Langya Terrace to the many relocated commoners...

Xu Fu felt amazed.

He and Ying Zheng stood on the summit, with clouds and mist swirling beneath their feet. They could vaguely glimpse the newly built houses and the commoners at the foot and on the slopes of the mountain.

Ying Zheng pointed at the clouds and mist beneath their feet and laughed, "A-Fu, do you have the feeling of becoming an immortal and ascending to heaven?"

Xu Fu looked down in surprise. After carefully sensing it, he actually had that very illusion.

Ying Zheng, in high spirits, called for people to erect a stone tablet on Mount Langya and sculpt a statue of Xu Fu. On the tablet, he had an inscription carved, the gist of which was that Junfang was at Langya Terrace, appearing as if he were about to ascend to heaven... and so on, with the entire text praising Xu Fu.

Xu Fu hadn't expected Ying Zheng to do it the moment he thought of it. Looking at his and Ying Zheng's tablets standing side by side, he was truly speechless for a moment.

What he didn't expect even more was...

Actually, when they looked down from the summit, those commoners couldn't help but look up.

The commoners felt they saw two figures, one in black and one in white, their robes fluttering as if immortals had descended into the clouds and mist, leading the commoners to compete to kowtow. This was later turned into a legend and passed down to later generations...

Even the statue on Mount Langya influenced commoners in other places. The people spontaneously set up stone tablets and sculpted statues to praise the State Preceptor Junfang and the First Emperor.

...This is a later matter, so it need not be mentioned here.
