徐福同嬴政在琅邪山过了三个月的逍遥日子。
清晨，伴随着鸟鸣声、落水声醒来，宫人小心地敲响了木门，多余的声音倒是不敢发出，生怕不小心惊扰了门内的人。
琅邪山上的居所多是木头搭建，只要小心些别走了水，住着便是别有一番滋味的。
徐福嗅着木头味儿，晨露味儿，还有点儿清冷的花香味儿，从梦中缓缓醒来了。
琅邪山上虽有多处不便，但空气、风景实在都是一绝啊！
徐福在床榻里磨蹭了会儿，一转头便正对上嬴政的脸庞，嬴政不知何时已经醒了。徐福仔细想一想，发觉大部分时候，嬴政似乎都是比自己先醒。若是哪一日他没有先行醒来，那定然是他累到极致了。
嬴政一手抚了抚徐福的面颊，一边转头冲着木门外的宫人道：“备水。”
门外的宫人得到吩咐，这才安心地退了下去。
徐福不大想起身，哪怕只是这样躺着嗅一嗅木头的香气，他都觉得特别舒服。
奈何嬴政直接伸手从背后，将徐福提了起来，他的手臂足够有力，要将徐福抱起来实在太容易了。嬴政就这样抱着徐福下去了，宫人们小心翼翼推门进来的时候，嬴政还没有将徐福放下来，瞥见这一幕的宫人们，抿了抿嘴角，压下了笑意，忙将洗漱用具一应摆好。
内侍站在一旁，躬腰道：“陛下，有人上书。”
“谁？”嬴政正在帮着徐福穿衣袍呢，于是连头都没抬。
那内侍早就习惯了嬴政的这般模样，道：“齐地有方士上书。”
齐地？
嬴政不由得转头看了一眼徐福，道：“从前你便是那处的。”
徐福总觉得嬴政这句话还暗含了什么意思，他微微一怔，突然想到了有件事。历史上，在这个时间段，是有人上书了，好像还就是他上书的，告诉嬴政追求仙山之类的玩意儿，而后嬴政便将方士们都喊到了咸阳。
“拿来朕瞧一瞧。”嬴政道。
内侍点头，小心地从袖中取出了竹简。
还真是竹简……
也不知道在送来的过程中经历了多少麻烦。
嬴政展开竹简，简略地扫了一眼，随后转头看向徐福，笑道：“有人上书，说大海之中有三座仙山，分别名为蓬莱、方丈、瀛洲，那里居住着仙人。若有人愿意带三千童男童女出海寻仙山，便可求得长生不老之灵药。”
徐福：“……”真是好生熟悉的台词啊。
这不是就是他口中说出来的话么！
没想到他改变了历史的轨迹，最后却也还是有人，上书说了和他同样的话。
嬴政合上了竹简，随手丢弃了在一旁，笑道：“若是阿福如此上书，我定然心动不已，但若是旁的人，从何而来都不知，我自是不信了。”
这意思……便是不打算按照历史来派人出海寻仙山了？
徐福虽然松了一口气，但同时心底还隐隐有些可惜。
毕竟这流传到后世，也差不多能成个传说了。
想一想，自己从前竟然还是传说中的人物，徐福还顿觉有种说不出的滋味呢。
二人很快洗漱完毕。
齐地方士上书，当然只是一个插曲罢了。徐福和嬴政谁都不会将之放在心上。那些方士怕是要失望了。
只不过这也到了他们该离开的时候了。
他们在琅邪山停留三月，实在是花费了不少的时间。徐福虽有不舍，但也觉得应当离开了。美好的地方越是留恋，恐怕越是不舍，便干脆直接离开。人生那样长，说不准日后还能再和嬴政到此处来。当然，还有一个原因，徐福担忧留了胡亥在咸阳，他会闹出些什么事来。
宫人们收拾好了东西，一行人便这样离开了琅邪山，离开的时候，徐福还从车帘中往外瞧了瞧，看了看那些从外地搬迁而来的百姓。百姓们虽是到了一个陌生的地方，但出人意料的是，他们的脸上并没有沮丧和担忧，反而满满都是欣喜，而且徐福还隐隐发现，他们看向旁边琅邪山的时候，眼底里闪烁着崇敬与渴望的光芒。
嬴政见状，凑到徐福耳边，低声道：“阿福又多了一些信徒。”说这话的时候，他脸上闪烁着的是喜色和自豪之色。
信徒？
徐福觉得有点怪怪的，感觉自己就像是招摇撞骗的江湖术士一样。
队伍很快离开了琅邪山。
他们下一个将要前往的地方，乃是彭城。据说这里曾是黄帝的都城，彭祖曾于此建立了大彭氏国。
嬴政低声道：“传闻夏王大禹铸造的九鼎，便在彭城之中。”
“九鼎？”徐福微微惊讶。有些意思！这个东西，他是早就听闻过大名的，九鼎甚至可以算作是风水物，只不过它是顶级的风水物。旁的连它半根毫毛都及不上。不过徐福对风水研究得并不多，因而也就并不知晓这九鼎有多少功效作用。
“你不是好鼎吗？我便令人去将鼎都寻来。”嬴政笑道，似乎并未将这传说中的九鼎放在心上。
“上辈子，找到了吗？”徐福搜寻了一番记忆，却并没能搜寻到这九鼎的身影。
“未能。”嬴政道，“那鼎在河中，我曾令人入水寻找，却遍寻不得，反而一路乘舟而下，过了淮河，到了湘山祠。”
“湘山祠？”
嬴政说起此地都依旧觉得不大痛快，他道：“所谓湘山祠，便是供奉湘君的祠，据传是是尧的女儿，舜的妻子，埋葬在了此处，于是便有人建起了湘山祠。我到湘山祠时，竟是连河也不能渡了，那河面上刮起了好大的风。”
过去他的性子可远没有这样好，但是听人说起，是什么湘君的祠，他登时便怒了，令人发配了囚犯前来，把湘山上的树砍了个干净，红色的土地都转为了赭红色，当时背后定然少不了微词，但那时的嬴政全然不顾，根本不将那点儿不顺耳的话听进去。将树砍光后，他又命人去打捞九鼎，却依旧不得，最后只得放弃，便从南郡经由武关回到了咸阳。
嬴政也不隐瞒，便将这些都说与了徐福，只是他口吻颇为轻描淡写，将自己曾经的暴怒都掩埋了。
徐福当然不会听出来，只是忍不住问道：“那我们还从河上渡？”
嬴政道：“可在彭城停留几日，询问城中人，仔细打听九鼎的传闻，之后再做决定。”
徐福点了点头。
做下决定后，他们便歇在了彭城中。
只是他们入住的当夜，彭城便下起了大雨。
雨声噼里啪啦地敲打在房檐上，徐福反倒睡得更香了。这时候正值夏日，雨后的清凉袭来，让徐福觉得舒服极了。
第二日，徐福和嬴政起床用饭食，便听门外下人低声议论起了什么，而且情绪还相当的激动，只是教人听不出究竟是喜还是悲。
徐福往外瞥了一眼，嬴政登时会意，唤来了门外的下人，问道：“可是出什么事了？”
这下人都是彭城中人，见贵人将他们唤了进来，忙躬着腰，诚惶诚恐地应道：“昨夜、昨夜大雨，淋了湘山祠……”
湘山祠？这不就是嬴政口中的那个供奉湘君的祠吗？
徐福拍了拍嬴政的手臂，示意他继续用饭，于是二人便颇有耐心地，一边用饭一边等那下人将舌头捋直。
“……湘山祠破、破了，雨水灌了进去，湘君的神像涕出了血泪，湘山也满山泛着红……那情形，实在可怖得很嘞！”说着那下人都忍不住自己先打了个哆嗦。
血泪？漫山遍野的红？
徐福与嬴政对视了一眼，然后挥退了那名下人。
“那山上的土不就是红色吗？这有何可怖的？”徐福不解。还有什么涕血泪的把戏，如今电视剧都不爱演这一套了，实在过时得很了，半点也唬不住徐福。
嬴政道：“莫急，我们过去瞧一瞧便是。”
徐福点了点头。
二人慢慢用完饭食，便坐上了马车朝着湘山的方向而去。有一拨人跟随着他们前往湘山，好护佑皇帝陛下的安危，而另一拨人被派出去打听九鼎的传闻了。
马车很快到了湘山脚下，湘山脚下还有着三两农户，而此时农户已经被淹没了。湘山脚下围了太多的人，他们几乎将路堵了个水泄不通，徐福相当怀疑彭城大半的人，都聚到此处来了。也不知道被派出去打听的人，还能不能问到什么东西。
马车的车帘被掀起，侍从道：“陛下，我们走不前去了。”
这时候还下着雨，但这些人恍若未觉一般，顶着淅沥的小雨，他们仰头看着湘山，竟是异常地起劲。
这么些人挡路又如何？嬴政下令道：“分开百姓。”
侍从们会意，握紧了腰间的剑，走上前去，开始分人群。百姓们虽然八卦兴味浓，但此时他们更畏惧侍从们手中的兵器，于是他们震惊地睁大了眼，纷纷往后退去，生怕那剑冲着自己而来。
就是这样粗暴又简单的，人群分开了。
侍从笑了笑，驾着马车继续前行。
马车前行了没多久，便停在了上山的入口处。
“可要上山一观？”嬴政道。
徐福此时却并未听他说话，反而是掀起车帘，身子微微歪斜，他在听那些百姓低低的议论声。也亏得他的耳力出众，方才能听见百姓们压低的声音。
“……好端端的，湘君怎会流血泪呢？”
“山怎么会变色呢？”
“昨夜那一场雨实在太可怕了……”
“会不会是预兆着，秦王统一乃是受神灵抵触的？”
“你胡说什么？当心你的小命！”
徐福很好地将这一段对话收入了耳中，徐福早就料到会有这样的对话出现了。这并没什么稀奇的，每逢天灾人祸，总有些人会站出来，将这牵扯到当政者的身上，尤其是部分有心人更会利用这一点，一旦有这样的传言疯传，那便说明是有人欲造反了。当然，现在应当并非如此，毕竟说话的只有那么零星几个人，只有他们胆敢联想到如何的皇帝陛下身上，其他人对此都不敢随意胡言，可见背后并无什么造反的阴谋。
但，尽管如此。
徐福也并不乐意，听到这些人出声质疑嬴政，哪怕是质疑半分也不成。
徐福收回目光，坐直了身子，沉声道：“走，上山。”
嬴政并不知徐福为什么，突然间变得这样坚决。不过上个山而已啊。
徐福当先掀起车帘走了下去，嬴政紧随其后。二人今日都是着黑衣。徐福不着白衣的原因很明确，不耐脏。只不过就算是黑衣，被溅上泥点后也依旧脏得不行。
当然，这些细节并不会影响到二人的气质，尤其是当有人瞥见他们的面容之后，百姓中立时发出了大大小小的惊呼声。
他们哪里见过这样好看的人？
“他们是谁？”
“他们看上去很有来头诶……”百姓间免不了又议论开了，只不过见着了徐福二人的面容后，这些百姓更不敢上前了，生怕自己亵渎了对方似的。
当徐福和嬴政直直朝着山上而去，百姓们再度惊了。这些人是不要命了么？这等异状，也敢直直闯上山去！他们可是都不敢动的！
“要不要拦下他们啊？”“我们怕是拦不下啊。”“是啊……”百姓中间有了争议。
就在徐福已经踏上上山的路之后，有个年轻姑娘站了出来，道：“你们不能上去！”
徐福推了推嬴政握着伞的手，转过身来，问道：“为何不能上去？莫非这山有何禁令？”
咋一直面徐福这张脸，那姑娘不由得往后退了半步，脸蛋也红了红，声音不自觉地降小了些：“山上……山上的土都变红了，你没瞧见么？你小心些，勿要再往前行了。”
徐福道：“变红又如何？”
“那定然是湘君发怒了呀。”姑娘不解地应道，她不解徐福为何如此问，……他应当是打外地来的吧，所以才不知晓。
姑娘又道：“湘君是夏王大禹的女儿，她死后被葬于此，守护九鼎。多年来彭城都平稳得很，偏偏昨夜出了这样的异状，那定然是湘君发怒了！所以你要小心呀……人、人怎么能与神斗呢？”
徐福不急不慢地反问道：“可我又并非惹怒湘君之人，湘君又怎会迁怒我呢？湘君为何会发怒，定是因为大雨摧毁了湘山祠，那我便更应该前去瞧瞧了，若是有破损处，我便代为修补一二，那湘君自然就不会发怒了，彭城便还可继续过安稳日子。”
姑娘被徐福这番话说得微微愣住了。
“你、你说得似乎也有几分道理……”姑娘皱起眉，似乎陷入了纠结之中。
此时嬴政有些不满了。阿福怎能用这般温柔的语气，与那姑娘说话？而且这话说得也太长了些！嬴政拽了一下徐福的胳膊，而后便大大方方地伸手，从背后揽住了徐福的肩，光明正大地宣告着他的所有权。左右二人已然成婚，此时做起来这样的动作，也并未有何处不妥。
姑娘微微有些错愕，张了张嘴，最后却是什么都没说。
“走吧。”嬴政温柔地出声催促道。
或许是那姑娘看了嬴政一眼，发觉嬴政也长得极为英俊，与徐福正是相配得很，那姑娘便只是好奇地多打量了两眼，别的却是未再说。
其他百姓也多少被镇住了。他们这些没甚文化的人，当然想不出什么溢美之词，便只能望着徐福和嬴政等人离去的背影，淡淡道：“好气度呢！真是好像仙人下凡呢……”
那姑娘怔怔道：“说不准便是仙人呢，不然怎么敢这般胆大，还主动上山去为湘君修祠呢？”
……
因为没人敢上山，他们上山的路就变得极为宽敞了。这段时日，徐福总跟着嬴政登山，体力倒是也增长了一些，此时要爬个湘山倒算不得什么。不过他们一边往山上走，便一边能瞥见脚下地皮翻了过来，露出了红色的泥土，红土被浸泡过后，看上去便像是被一汪汪血水浸过了似的。
不少士兵瞧上几眼，都觉得实在忍不住哆嗦。
若是一处泛红也就罢了，若只是红色泥土那也就罢了，偏偏如今是满山的鲜红色啊，那形成的视觉冲击，实在有些过于刺激。
不久，有侍从道：“前面便是湘山祠了。”
徐福抬头望了一眼，只能隐约瞥见一抹褐色。
嬴政道：“阿福不会当真要为那湘君修祠吧？”言语间竟是还对那湘君有些不满。
徐福道：“过去瞧一瞧再说。”他还想看一看清楚，那湘山祠究竟是如何一回事，那湘君落泪又是如何一回事。
“既然无人敢上山，怎么有人知晓湘君落下了血泪？”徐福突然想到了这一茬，便转头问起了身边的侍从。
“那是山上的守祠人见着的，见着以后便赶紧跑下山了，据说因为跑得太急，还将腿也摔断了呢。”
徐福点点头，继续拔腿向前。
嬴政捏紧了徐福的手，低声道：“我不许你为湘君修祠。”
“为什么？”
嬴政厚着脸皮淡淡道：“那湘君可是阻拦过我去捞九鼎，这般欺负我，难道阿福还要助她吗？”
什么叫“这般欺负我”？谁敢欺负他？堂堂秦始皇，口中竟然还能说出这样的话来！
徐福顿时又觉得好气，又觉得好笑。
沉默一会儿，徐福最终还是决定顺从了嬴政的意思，“好，听你的。”
简短的四个字，轻易地取悦了嬴政，嬴政脸上阴翳散去，立即浮现了笑容。当真是比胡亥还要幼稚上几分。
就简短对话的时候，他们已然走到了湘山祠外。
湘山祠修建得并不高大，更不宏伟，瞧上去普普通通，甚至还有些矮小，经历风吹雨淋之后，这座湘山祠看上去显得朴素古拙了许多。徐福当先走了进去，嬴政紧随其后，侍从和士兵们都有些紧张，想喊又不敢喊住他们。虽说他们也知晓皇后的本事，更知晓没有什么诡奇的事件，但心底总归会忧心陛下的安危。
这头徐福踏进湘山祠，地上还有些枯叶和碎掉的瓦片，看上去实在有些破败，哪里像是供奉神的地方？徐福挪开目光，看向了湘君的塑像。
湘君的塑像其实吧……做得也挺丑的，甚至丑得有点让人辨不清男女。只是诡异的是，那湘君的眼眶之中，还当真流下了血泪来。
嬴政当即道：“去瞧瞧那血泪是什么做的？”
侍从不敢犹豫，当即上前查探，侍从摸了一把，回转身来，“……不知为何物？”侍从面色赧然，为自己的知识面狭隘敢绝到了羞愧。
徐福凑上前瞧了一眼，其实他也不知道这是何物。
不过徐福顺手也沾了点儿，来闻，顿时一股土腥味儿窜进了鼻子里。看来也是红土了。
徐福拍了拍手，嬴政忙往他手里塞了条绢布，徐福就着绢布擦了擦手，道：“是土，应当是从顶上掉下来的。”徐福话音刚落，嬴政正要嗤笑原是这样一回事，便突然听祠外的士兵惊叫了一声。
徐福和嬴政赶紧往外走去，并让人将那士兵叫了过来。
“出了何事？”嬴政沉声问。
“陛下，那、那边……”士兵指向了另一面。
徐福和嬴政想也不想，便齐齐拔腿往那边走去，可以说，胆子不是一般的大。当然，对于他们来说，也确实不知何为畏惧。一个整日与“封建迷信”的玩意儿打交道，一个又是身负龙气的千古帝王，谁会畏惧这些呢？
等他们走了过去，徐福这才看清，原是一条红色泥流，顺着往山坡下滑去了，那山坡之下，正好便是一条河流。
嬴政挑眉，指着河流道：“这便是我当初渡过的那条河，正是在此处，我便再不得前进了，随后士兵发现了湘山祠。”
徐福微微惊讶。这可真是有些奇妙了。
当然这山上不可能有鬼，也未必有什么湘神的指示。只是这条泥流实在显得怪异了些，为什么偏偏正好就朝着这个方向下去了呢？当然世间万物，有些玄妙是说不清的。徐福看了一眼嬴政，他从嬴政的眼底得到了相同的答案，嬴政道：“沿着山坡下去，捞九鼎。”
士兵们都知晓他们的皇帝陛下在寻九鼎，而儒生们更是清楚，这九鼎有着何等的含义！于是难免跟着激动了一些。
众人都沿着山坡下去了。
反倒是徐福和嬴政慢悠悠地走在了最后。
士兵顺着这片水域下去，忽觉狂风大作，甚至被迷得睁不开双眼，但他们还是生生下了水，水底浑浊不清，不过对于夏日的士兵们来说，这片水域正好还可以让他们清凉一下。紧接着，儒生们为了现个风头，也跟着下了水。徐福和嬴政站在上头，就能听见接连不断的“噗通”声，能跳的基本都跳下水去了。
人多力量大，徐福和嬴政站在岸上等了等会儿，便听人叫道：“找、找到了！”一士兵高托起手中之物，明明是从河中捞起的，但那小鼎身上竟然找不到半点污泥，看上去很是干净。
徐福心中啧啧称奇。
捞到了一只鼎，自然便有人去捞第二只，众人激动不已，忙继续潜水往下捞，头上还在飘着小雨都不算什么了。
那些儒生们，终于直面了自己的体弱，在捞而不得的情况下，还是选择回到了岸上，并进行了自我安慰，他们又并非那些粗莽的武夫，自然是捞不到鼎的，但方才他们那般积极地下水，便已经是向陛下表明一片赤诚忠心了啊！
只是令他们失望的是，他们并没能再捞到第二只鼎。
众人不死心地继续捞了下去……依旧没有，他们叹了口气，只得起身。
儒生马上冲上前去，从士兵的手中接过了鼎，随后高举着鼎，便要往坡上爬，口中还喊道：“陛下！这便是九州鼎没错！”
被他抢了鼎的士兵一脸懵。
徐福也不由得皱了皱眉，这儒生之中怎么偏有那么几人，这样混账？
那儒生可不知徐福和嬴政对他的嫌弃，他兴奋地举着鼎，便要往上爬，只可惜爬了没几步，又是一阵大风刮来，那儒生一个站立不稳，竟是就这样倒栽葱倒了下去，“噗通”一声入了水，其他人惊了一跳，忙又下水去捞，当然，不是捞那儒生，而是去捞鼎啊！
刚才费了大力气才捞到鼎的士兵们，在心底里臭骂了那儒生一通。
这搅事的玩意儿！
站在山坡上的嬴政，也是面色一沉，道：“朕便应当挖个坑将这些坏事的给埋了！”反正也不是没埋过！
听见嬴政这般不悦的口吻，徐福不由得伸手轻抚过了他的手背，算是安抚了他一通。
嬴政身上暴戾的气息稍有平息，总算没立即下令让人将儒生们都给摁进水里去，淹死一个算一个。
士兵们下水打捞了好一会儿，脸色一个比一个难看，岸边的儒生忍不住瑟瑟发抖了，也不知是害怕，还是一身淋湿了之后被大风给刮的 。
那个落进水里的儒生倒是顽强，自己扑腾两下，爬起来了，就是头上还带了点血。从那么高被吹下来，落在水面上也就跟落地面差不多了，不出血才奇怪。不过出血也实在是他自己活该。
士兵竟是再也没有捞到那只鼎，那只鼎连徐福的手掌都还没挨一下，就这样又落回水中去了。徐福和嬴政谁的脸色都好看不起来，士兵更甚，之前捞出鼎来的那名士兵，直接上前拎住了那名抢着表现的儒生。儒生回过神来，有些腿软，见士兵面色阴沉地拎住了自己，儒生便更加慌张了。
“你……你做什么？”儒生打了个哆嗦。
士兵咬了咬牙，没说话，提着他就往徐福和嬴政的方向走。
其他士兵也是愤怒地看向了儒生，他们不能谴责所有的儒生，但用目光杀死这个儒生还是可以的。
这些士兵都是上过战场，沾过人命的，身上的杀气哪里是这个儒生所能承受的？
儒生吓得崩溃大叫出声，道：“陛下，不是我啊！陛下，这乃是那湘君为了阻拦我等带走九鼎，方才放出了大风，故意将我吹倒下去啊！”
嬴政心中对那湘君固然厌烦，但此时他对这做错了事，想要抢功，还敢推卸责任，喋喋不休的儒生，更是恼怒和憎恶！儒家果真少有些成才的！
“将人带上来。”嬴政冷声道，说完便牵着徐福转身了。
徐福回头冷漠地瞥了一眼那儒生，他也有些厌烦这样的人。
想要表现自我没问题，但至少功劳是属于你的。擅自从士兵手中抢过九州鼎，以为借此机会便可在嬴政跟前露脸，实在是大错特错！尤其是此时还力图狡辩，以求保命，那嘴脸更是令人恶心。
一个九鼎对于徐福来说，虽然稀奇，但并没有到可以令他为之勃然大怒的地步，倒是这儒生，实在让徐福觉得连看一眼都觉不快。
儒生被带了上来，他浑身湿透了，头上还带着血迹，看上去颇为狼狈。
有儒生看不过眼了，便道：“请陛下饶恕他的罪过吧。”不过这人倒是不敢赖湘君。
嬴政没搭理他。
儒生颤巍巍地道：“陛下……”
身后的儒生也跟着道了声，“陛下。”
徐福觉得这些人实在是烦透了，怎么半点眼力见儿都没有呢？他们不死谁死？
“来人，将湘山上的树都砍了。”嬴政的确是心中不痛快，尤其是对于他这样的，手握大权的帝王来说，又怎么能允许什么湘神凌驾于他之上呢？一场大风算什么？他便要如前世一样，砍了这山上的树！破了那湘山祠！教那湘君无处可依！
士兵们自然是遵守嬴政的吩咐，当即便要去伐树。
徐福眼皮一跳。
这可不行。
不是冒犯湘君不行，而是树木全都砍伐走，用什么来留住水土呢？日后再下大雨，岂不是要造成山体滑坡？彭城还会有安宁和平稳吗？湘君不重要，儒生也不重要，重要的是这城中的无辜百姓！现在徐福都还能想起山下那个年轻姑娘的模样，这些人淳朴的人可不能因为别人而被牵连。
毕竟砍树又如何？也并不能对那湘君进行实质的报复，且九鼎已经再度落到水中去了，砍了树那鼎也不会回来。
徐福便直接反握住了嬴政的手，道：“等等。”
士兵们都知晓，除却陛下的话以外，谁的话都可以不听，但皇后的话必须听！
“树不能砍。”徐福淡淡道，“给那湘君周身糊上一层红土便是。”
士兵们动也不动，静静地等待着最终的决定。
嬴政抿了抿唇角，出声道：“……便按皇后说的去做。”
士兵们点头应是，他们其实也不想砍树，毕竟这可是个花功夫的活儿。士兵们立即拿了工具去挖红土，准备将祠中的湘君塑像给糊上厚厚一层。
徐福转头看向嬴政，低声解释道：“树砍了，以后大雨下起来，没有树木留住土壤和雨水，城中的百姓便要遭殃了。”
嬴政点头，原来如此，原来阿福是为了寡人着想。嬴政面上不由带出点点喜色。
徐福接着又道：“糊上一层红土，那湘君像不再现于人前，无法再受供奉，那便是对她最好的羞辱了。”虽然羞辱一位女性有点不大道德，但这一阵又一阵吹来的风，也的确有点折腾人啊。便算作小惩了。总不会比砍光这里的树更过分了。
嬴政点头，面上神色更是轻松，显然已经被徐福的话说服了，他道：“阿福说的是。”
此时，儒生对视一眼，终于完全确定，他们的陛下极为听从这位男皇后的话了。
那个狼狈的儒生，也明悟过来，看向徐福的目光便如同抓住了什么救命稻草一般……
“陛下，皇后……”
chapters.translated_text:
Xufu spent three carefree months with Ying Zheng at Mount Langya.

Awakening in the early morning to the sound of birds chirping and water splashing, palace attendants gently knocked on the wooden door, not daring to make any extra noise for fear of inadvertently disturbing the person inside.

Most of the dwellings on Mount Langya were built of wood; as long as one was careful not to cause a fire, living there had a uniquely charming flavor.

Breathing in the scent of wood, morning dew, and a hint of cool floral fragrance, Xufu slowly awoke from his dream.

Although Mount Langya had several inconveniences, its air and scenery were truly peerless!

Xufu lingered a while longer under the covers, then turned his head to find himself face-to-face with Ying Zheng, who had already woken up at some point. Xufu thought about it carefully and realized that most of the time, Ying Zheng seemed to wake up earlier than he did. If there was ever a day when Ying Zheng didn't wake up first, it was definitely because he had been exhausted to the extreme.

Ying Zheng stroked Xufu’s cheek with one hand while turning his head to tell the attendants outside the wooden door, "Prepare water."

Only after receiving the order did the attendants outside quietly step back.

Xufu didn't really want to get up; even just lying there like this, smelling the fragrance of the wood, made him feel exceptionally comfortable.

Yet Ying Zheng directly reached out from behind, lifting Xufu up. His arms were strong enough that picking Xufu up was effortless. Ying Zheng carried Xufu down just like that. When the attendants carefully pushed the door open, Ying Zheng hadn't put Xufu down yet. Catching a glimpse of this scene, the attendants pressed their lips together to suppress a smile and busily set out all the washing utensils.

An eunuch stood to the side, bowing as he said, "Your Majesty, someone has submitted a memorial."

"Who?" Ying Zheng was in the midst of helping Xufu put on his outer robe, so he didn't even raise his head.

The eunuch, long accustomed to Ying Zheng's demeanor, replied, "A fangshi from the Qi territory has submitted a memorial."

The Qi territory?

Ying Zheng couldn't help turning his head to glance at Xufu, saying, "You were from those parts in the past."

Xufu always felt that Ying Zheng's remark carried some hidden meaning. He was slightly startled as a thought suddenly occurred to him. Historically, around this time, someone *had* submitted a memorial—it seemed it was even submitted by *him*—telling Ying Zheng to seek out immortal mountains and the like, after which Ying Zheng summoned all the fangshi to Xianyang.

"Bring it here for Us to see," Ying Zheng said.

The eunuch nodded and carefully retrieved the bamboo slips from his sleeve.

It really was bamboo slips...

One could only wonder how much trouble it had gone through during delivery.

Ying Zheng unrolled the bamboo slips, glanced over them briefly, and then turned to look at Xufu with a smile, saying, "Someone has submitted a memorial stating that there are three immortal mountains in the midst of the great sea, named Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou respectively, where immortals dwell. If someone is willing to lead three thousand boys and girls across the sea to seek these immortal mountains, they can obtain the elixir of immortality."

Xufu: "..." Such a terribly familiar line.

Wasn't this the very thing he himself used to say!

He hadn't expected that even though he had altered the course of history, someone in the end would still submit a memorial saying the exact same things he had.

Ying Zheng rolled up the bamboo slips, tossed them aside casually, and smiled, "If Ah-Fu had submitted such a memorial, I would naturally be deeply moved. But coming from some unknown person whose origins are entirely unclear, I naturally do not believe it."

This meant... he had no intention of following history by sending people out to sea to search for immortal mountains?

Although Xufu breathed a sigh of relief, a faint trace of regret lingered in his heart.

After all, handed down to later generations, this could have become quite a legend.

Thinking about how he was once supposed to be a legendary figure, Xufu felt a strange, indescribable sensation.

The two of them quickly finished washing up.

The Qi fangshi's memorial was, of course, merely a brief interlude. Neither Xufu nor Ying Zheng would take it to heart. Those fangshi were likely going to be disappointed.

However, this also meant it was time for them to leave.

They had stayed on Mount Langya for three months, which truly took up a lot of time. Though Xufu felt a pang of reluctance, he knew they ought to leave. The more one lingered in a wonderful place, the harder it probably became to leave, so it was best to depart directly. Life was long; who was to say they couldn't come back here with Ying Zheng in the future? Of course, there was another reason: Xufu worried about what kind of trouble Huhai might stir up if left alone in Xianyang.

The attendants packed their belongings, and the entourage departed from Mount Langya. As they left, Xufu peeked out through the carriage curtain to look at the commoners who had been relocated from other places. Although these people had arrived in an unfamiliar land, unexpectedly, there was no frustration or worry on their faces; instead, they were filled with joy. Moreover, Xufu faintly noticed that when they looked at Mount Langya nearby, their eyes flickered with a light of reverence and longing.

Seeing this, Ying Zheng leaned close to Xufu's ear and whispered, "Ah-Fu has gained a few more believers." As he said this, his face radiated joy and pride.

Believers?

Xufu felt a bit weird, feeling somewhat like a swindling charlatan from the jianghu.

The procession quickly departed from Mount Langya.

Their next destination was Pengcheng. It was said that this had once been the capital of the Yellow Emperor, and Peng Zu had established the state of Da Peng right here.

Ying Zheng murmured, "Rumor has it that the Nine Cauldrons cast by King Yu of Xia are in Pengcheng."

"The Nine Cauldrons?" Xufu was slightly surprised. How interesting! He had long heard of the great fame of these items; the Nine Cauldrons could even be considered feng shui objects, except they were the supreme feng shui objects. Everything else couldn't even compare to half a hair of them. However, Xufu didn't study feng shui extensively, so he didn't know how many functions and effects these Nine Cauldrons possessed.

"Aren't you fond of cauldrons? I will have someone go and search for them all," Ying Zheng said with a smile, seeming not to take these legendary Nine Cauldrons very seriously.

"In the past life, were they found?" Xufu searched his memories, but failed to find any trace of the Nine Cauldrons.

"They were not," Ying Zheng replied. "The cauldrons were in the river. I once ordered men to enter the water to search for them, but searched everywhere in vain. Instead, we drifted downstream by boat, crossed the Huai River, and arrived at the Xiangshan Shrine."

"Xiangshan Shrine?"

Whenever Ying Zheng spoke of this place, he still felt displeased. He said, "The so-called Xiangshan Shrine is a shrine dedicated to the Xiang Goddess. Legend has it that she was the daughter of Yao and the wife of Shun, and was buried here, so people built the Xiangshan Shrine. When I arrived at the Xiangshan Shrine, I couldn't even cross the river; a massive gale blew across the water's surface."

In the past, his temper was far from being this good, but upon hearing people say it was some Xiang Goddess's shrine, he instantly flew into a rage. He ordered convicts to be sent there to cut down every single tree on Mount Xiang until the red earth turned a dusty crimson. At the time, there must have been plenty of whispered criticisms behind his back, but the Ying Zheng of that day completely ignored them, refusing to listen to a single unpleasing word. After clearing the trees, he ordered people to dredge for the Nine Cauldrons, but still found nothing. In the end, he had to give up, and traveled from Nanjun back to Xianyang via Wuguan.

Ying Zheng made no attempt to hide it and told all of this to Xufu, though his tone was quite understatement-laden, burying his past outbursts of fury.

Xufu certainly wouldn't read too much into it, but couldn't help asking, "Then are we still crossing via the river?"

Ying Zheng said, "We can stay in Pengcheng for a few days, inquire among the townspeople, carefully gather rumors about the Nine Cauldrons, and then make a decision."

Xufu nodded.

Having made their decision, they rested in Pengcheng.

Yet on the very night they checked in, torrential rain began to fall over Pengcheng.

The sound of rain pattered rhythmically against the eaves, causing Xufu to sleep all the more soundly. It was the height of summer, and the coolness that followed the rain made Xufu feel exceptionally comfortable.

The next day, as Xufu and Ying Zheng got up to have a meal, they heard the servants outside whispering about something with quite excited emotions, though one couldn't tell whether they were happy or sorrowful.

Xufu glanced outward, and Ying Zheng immediately understood. He called the servants from outside and asked, "Has something happened?"

These servants were locals of Pengcheng. Seeing the noble figures summon them inside, they hurriedly bowed and answered with fearful trepidation, "Last night... last night's heavy rain drenched the Xiangshan Shrine..."

Xiangshan Shrine? Wasn't this the shrine dedicated to the Xiang Goddess that Ying Zheng had just mentioned?

Xufu patted Ying Zheng's arm, signaling him to continue eating, so the two of them patiently ate while waiting for the servant to untangle his tongue.

"...The Xiangshan Shrine was broken, broken open, and rainwater poured inside. The statue of the Xiang Goddess shed tears of blood, and the entire Mount Xiang turned crimson all over... That sight was truly terrifying!" As he spoke, the servant couldn't help shivering first.

Tears of blood? Crimson as far as the eye could see across the mountains?

Xufu exchanged a look with Ying Zheng and then waved the servant away.

"Isn't the soil on that mountain naturally red? What's so terrifying about that?" Xufu was baffled. As for the tricks about shedding tears of blood, even TV dramas nowadays didn't bother with that cliché anymore; it was thoroughly outdated and couldn't bluff Xufu in the slightest.

Ying Zheng said, "Don't rush, we'll just go over and take a look."

Xufu nodded.

After finishing their meal leisurely, the two of them boarded a carriage and headed in the direction of Mount Xiang. One group of guards followed them to protect His Majesty the Emperor's safety, while another group was sent out to inquire about the rumors of the Nine Cauldrons.

The carriage soon arrived at the foot of Mount Xiang. There were usually two or three farming households at the foot of the mountain, but by this time, the area had been flooded. Too many people had gathered at the foot of Mount Xiang, blocking the road almost impassably. Xufu strongly suspected that most of Pengcheng's population had congregated here. He wondered if the people sent out to gather information would still be able to find out anything at all.

The carriage curtain was lifted, and an attendant reported, "Your Majesty, we cannot go any further."

It was still raining at the moment, but these people seemed entirely unaware of it. Braving the drizzling rain, they tilted their heads upward to gaze at Mount Xiang with unusual eagerness.

What did a crowd blocking the road matter? Ying Zheng ordered, "Separate the people."

The attendants understood. Clasping the handles of the swords at their waists, they stepped forward and began parting the crowd. Although the commoners had a strong appetite for gossip, they feared the weapons in the attendants' hands even more. Wide-eyed with shock, they retreated backward in haste, terrified that the swords might be directed at them.

Just like that, roughly and simply, the crowd was split apart.

The attendant smiled and drove the carriage forward.

After moving a short distance, the carriage stopped at the entrance leading up the mountain.

"Shall we go up the mountain for a look?" Ying Zheng asked.

At that moment, Xufu wasn't listening to him. Instead, he lifted the carriage curtain, leaned his body slightly forward, and listened to the low murmurs of the commoners. Thanks to his exceptional hearing, he was able to catch the subdued voices of the people.

"...For no good reason, why would the Xiang Goddess shed tears of blood?"

"How could the mountain change color?"

"Last night's rain was truly terrifying..."

"Could it be a sign that the King of Qin's unification is resented by the deities?"

"What nonsense are you uttering? Watch your neck!"

Xufu took in this conversation quite clearly, having long anticipated that such talk would emerge. There was nothing strange about it; whenever natural and man-made disasters struck, there were always people who would step forward to tie it to those in power, especially certain scheming individuals who would exploit this. Once such rumors ran wild, it meant someone intended to rebel. Of course, that probably wasn't the case right now, given that only a sparse few were speaking and dared to link it to His Majesty the Emperor, while others didn't dare chat idly about it. This showed there was no underlying rebellious conspiracy.

But even so.

Xufu was not happy to hear these people voicing doubts about Ying Zheng—not even by a fraction.

Pulling back his gaze, Xufu sat up straight and said in a deep voice, "Let's go, up the mountain."

Ying Zheng didn't know why Xufu had suddenly become so resolute. It was just climbing a mountain, after all.

Xufu took the lead, lifting the carriage curtain and stepping out, followed closely by Ying Zheng. Both of them were dressed in black today. Xufu's reason for not wearing white was clear: it showed dirt easily. Yet even in black, once splashed with mud, it still looked a mess.

Of course, these details didn't detract from their aura. Especially when someone caught a glimpse of their faces, gasps of various sizes immediately erupted from the crowd.

When had they ever seen people this handsome?

"Who are they?"

"They look like they come from extraordinary backgrounds..." The commoners inevitably started whispering again. However, upon seeing the faces of Xufu and the other, they dared not step forward, as if fearing they might desecrate the two.

When Xufu and Ying Zheng marched straight toward the mountain, the commoners were shocked all over again. Were these people out of their minds? With such strange anomalies, they dared to barge straight up the mountain! Not one of them dared to make a move!

"Should we stop them?" "I'm afraid we can't stop them." "Yeah..." Contention arose among the commoners.

Just as Xufu stepped onto the path up the mountain, a young woman stood out and said, "You cannot go up!"

Xufu nudged the hand Ying Zheng was using to hold the umbrella, turned around, and asked, "Why can't we go up? Could it be that this mountain has some sort of ban?"

Facing Xufu's face the whole time, the young girl involuntarily took half a step back, her cheeks flushing red as her voice lowered unconsciously: "The mountain... the soil on the mountain has turned red, didn't you see? Be careful, do not go any further."

Xufu said, "So what if it turned red?"

"That must mean the Xiang Goddess is furious," the girl replied in bewilderment. She didn't understand why Xufu would ask such a thing... he must have come from out of town, which was why he didn't know.

The girl continued, "The Xiang Goddess is the daughter of King Yu of Xia. After her death, she was buried here to guard the Nine Cauldrons. Pengcheng has been peaceful for many years, but last night such an anomaly occurred—that must mean the Xiang Goddess is angry! So you must be careful... How, how can humans ever fight against gods?"

Xufu unhurriedly retorted, "But I am not the one who angered the Xiang Goddess, so why would she vent her anger on me? As for why she is angry, it must be because the heavy rain destroyed the Xiangshan Shrine, which makes it all the more reason for me to go take a look. If there are any damaged parts, I can help repair them a little, and naturally the Xiang Goddess won't be angry anymore, allowing Pengcheng to continue living in peace."

The girl was slightly stunned by Xufu's words.

"You, what you're saying sounds somewhat reasonable..." The girl frowned, looking as though she had fallen into a dilemma.

At this point, Ying Zheng grew somewhat displeased. How could Ah-Fu use such a gentle tone to speak with that girl? And what's more, that speech was way too long! Ying Zheng gave Xufu's arm a pull, then openly reached out from behind to wrap an arm around Xufu's shoulders, blatantly declaring his ownership. The two of them were married anyway, so performing such an action right now wasn't inappropriate in the least.

The girl was slightly startled, opened her mouth, but ultimately said nothing.

"Let's go," Ying Zheng urged gently.

Perhaps because the girl glanced at Ying Zheng and found him exceptionally handsome and a perfect match for Xufu, she merely looked a couple of times out of curiosity and said nothing else.

The other commoners were also somewhat awed. Lacking in culture, they couldn't think of any flowery words, so they could only watch the retreating figures of Xufu, Ying Zheng, and the others, murmuring, "Such grace! They really look like immortals descending to the mortal realm..."

The girl dazed and said, "Who's to say they aren't immortals? Otherwise, how could they be so bold as to proactively go up the mountain to repair the shrine for the Xiang Goddess?"

...

Because no one dared to go up the mountain, their path was exceptionally clear. Lately, Xufu had often followed Ying Zheng in mountain climbing, so his stamina had increased somewhat; climbing Mount Xiang at this moment didn't pose much of a challenge. However, as they walked up, they could catch glimpses of the ground along their path turning over, exposing red soil. Drenched by the rain, the red earth looked as if it had been soaked in pools of blood.

Quite a few soldiers felt a shiver run down their spines just looking at it.

If only one patch were red, it would be fine; if it were merely red dirt, that too would be fine. But now the entire mountain was a vivid crimson, creating a visual impact that was a bit too stimulating.

Soon, an attendant reported, "Ahead is the Xiangshan Shrine."

Xufu looked up and could only vaguely glimpse a patch of brown.

Ying Zheng remarked, "Ah-Fu isn't actually going to repair the shrine for that Xiang Goddess, are you?" His tone showed he still held some grievance toward the Xiang Goddess.

Xufu said, "Let's go take a look first." He also wanted to see clearly what was going on with the Xiangshan Shrine and how the Xiang Goddess shed tears.

"Since no one dared to go up the mountain, how did anyone know the Xiang Goddess shed tears of blood?" Xufu suddenly thought of this and turned to ask the nearby attendant.

"That was seen by the shrine keeper on the mountain. After seeing it, he hurried down the mountain; it's said he was running so fast he even broke his leg."

Xufu nodded and continued putting one foot in front of the other.

Ying Zheng squeezed Xufu's hand and whispered, "I forbid you from repairing the shrine for the Xiang Goddess."

"Why?"

Ying Zheng brazenly replied, "That Xiang Goddess once tried to stop me from dredging the Nine Cauldrons. Bullying me like this—does Ah-Fu still want to help her?"

What did he mean by "bullying me like this"? Who would dare bully him? The dignified First Emperor of Qin was actually capable of uttering such words!

Xufu instantly felt both exasperated and amused.

After a moment of silence, Xufu ultimately decided to yield to Ying Zheng's wishes. "Fine, I'll listen to you."

Those four brief words easily pleased Ying Zheng. The gloom on his face vanished, replaced immediately by a smile. He was truly a bit more childish than Huhai.

Amidst this brief conversation, they had already walked outside the Xiangshan Shrine.

The Xiangshan Shrine was not built tall or grand; it looked ordinary, even somewhat short. Having endured wind and rain, the shrine appeared much simpler and more archaic. Xufu walked in first, followed closely by Ying Zheng. The attendants and soldiers felt somewhat nervous, wanting to call out to stop them but not daring to. Although they knew the Empress's abilities and that there were no bizarre supernatural events, they still worried about His Majesty's safety in their hearts.

Stepping into the shrine, Xufu saw scattered dead leaves and broken tiles on the ground, making it look rather dilapidated—where was this like a place to worship gods? Xufu shifted his gaze and looked at the statue of the Xiang Goddess.

The statue of the Xiang Goddess... actually looked rather ugly, so ugly that it was somewhat difficult to distinguish its gender. The eerie part was that from the eye sockets of the Xiang Goddess, tears of blood were indeed flowing down.

Ying Zheng immediately ordered, "Go see what those tears of blood are made of!"

Without hesitation, an attendant stepped forward to inspect them. He touched the substance and turned back, looking sheepish: "...I don't know what it is." The attendant's face flushed with embarrassment, ashamed of the limits of his knowledge.

Xufu stepped forward to take a look, though he didn't know what it was either.

However, Xufu casually touched a bit of it and brought it to his nose to smell; an earthy, muddy odor instantly rushed into his nostrils. It seemed to be red earth after all.

Xufu clapped his hands. Ying Zheng hurriedly shoved a silk cloth into his hand, which Xufu used to wipe his fingers. "It's dirt, probably falling down from the ceiling." Just as Xufu finished speaking and Ying Zheng was about to scoff that it was just that simple, a soldier outside the shrine suddenly let out a startled scream.

Xufu and Ying Zheng hurried outside and had the soldier brought over.

"What happened?" Ying Zheng asked in a deep voice.

"Your Majesty, over... over there..." The soldier pointed in another direction.

Without a second thought, Xufu and Ying Zheng strode together toward the indicated direction. Their boldness was truly extraordinary. Of course, for the two of them, they genuinely didn't know what fear was. One constantly dealt with "feudal superstition," while the other was an ancient emperor carrying dragon Qi—who would fear such things?

When they walked over, Xufu finally saw clearly that it was a stream of red mud sliding down the slope toward a river right below the hillside.

Ying Zheng raised an eyebrow, pointed at the river, and said, "This is the river I crossed back then. It was right here that I could go no further, after which the soldiers discovered the Xiangshan Shrine."

Xufu was slightly surprised. This was indeed rather marvelous.

Of course, there couldn't possibly be ghosts on this mountain, nor necessarily any guidance from the Xiang deity. It was just that this stream of mud looked rather bizarre—why on earth did it flow precisely in this direction? Yet among all things in the world, some mysteries defied explanation. Xufu glanced at Ying Zheng and received the same answer in Ying Zheng's eyes. Ying Zheng said, "Down the slope, dredge for the Nine Cauldrons."

The soldiers all knew their emperor was searching for the Nine Cauldrons, and the Confucian scholars were even more aware of what the Nine Cauldrons signified! Thus, they inevitably grew a bit excited.

Everyone headed down the hillside.

Instead, Xufu and Ying Zheng walked leisurely at the very rear.

As the soldiers waded into the water area, they suddenly felt a fierce gale blowing, blinding them so they could barely open their eyes. Yet they forced themselves into the water anyway. The riverbed was murky and turbid, but for soldiers in the summer heat, this stretch of water offered a refreshing coolness. Shortly after, the Confucian scholars, eager to show off and catch the spotlight, also entered the water. Standing above, Xufu and Ying Zheng could hear a continuous series of "splash" sounds; almost everyone who could jump in had done so.

There was strength in numbers. After Xufu and Ying Zheng waited on the bank for a while, someone shouted, "Found... found it!" A soldier held an object high above his head with both hands. Although it had been fished out from the river, not a single speck of mud could be found on the small cauldron; it looked exceptionally clean.

Xufu clicked his tongue in wonder inwardly.

Having fished out one cauldron, naturally someone went to fish for a second. The crowd was thrilled and hurriedly continued diving to dredge deeper, ignoring the drizzle still drifting from the sky.

Those Confucian scholars finally confronted their own physical weakness. Unable to dredge anything up, they chose to return to the bank and comfort themselves: after all, they weren't crude, brawny warriors, so naturally they wouldn't catch a cauldron. But their proactive plunge into the water just now was already proof enough of their unswerving loyalty to His Majesty!

To their disappointment, however, they failed to fish out a second cauldron.

Refusing to give up, the crowd continued dredging... still nothing. Sighing, they had no choice but to get out of the water.

A Confucian scholar immediately rushed forward, took the cauldron from the soldier's hands, held it high, and started climbing up the slope while shouting, "Your Majesty! This is indeed the Jiuzhou Cauldron!"

The soldier whose cauldron had been snatched looked utterly dumbfounded.

Xufu couldn't help frowning either. Why were there always a few such outrageous scoundrels among these Confucian scholars?

That Confucian scholar was oblivious to Xufu and Ying Zheng's disgust toward him. Excitedly holding the cauldron high, he hurried to climb up. Unfortunately, after only a few steps, another fierce gust of wind blew past. Losing his footing, the Confucian scholar tumbled head over heels, plunging into the water with a loud "splash!" The others jumped in shock and hurriedly rushed back into the water—not to save the scholar, mind you, but to save the cauldron!

The soldiers who had exerted great effort to fish out the cauldron cursed that Confucian scholar to the core in their hearts.

What a troublemaking nuisance!

Standing on the hillside, Ying Zheng's expression darkened as well. He declared, "I should just dig a pit and bury these troublemakers!" It wasn't like he hadn't buried people before!

Hearing Ying Zheng's displeased tone, Xufu reached out to gently stroke the back of his hand, soothing him.

The violent aura on Ying Zheng subsided slightly, and he ultimately refrained from immediately ordering his men to shove the Confucian scholars into the water and drown them one by one.

The soldiers fished around in the water for quite a while, their complexions growing uglier by the second. The Confucian scholars on the bank trembled uncontrollably, unsure whether it was from fear or from being chilled by the strong wind after getting soaked.

That Confucian scholar who had fallen into the water proved quite tenacious; he thrashed about a couple of times and hauled himself up, though his head was stained with blood. Falling from that height and landing on the water's surface was practically no different from hitting solid ground; it would be a miracle if he didn't bleed. But bleeding was entirely his own fault.

The soldiers failed to fish out that cauldron after all; the vessel hadn't even brushed against Xufu's palm before slipping back into the water. Neither Xufu nor Ying Zheng wore pleasant expressions, and the soldiers looked even worse. The soldier who had originally retrieved the cauldron marched straight up and grabbed the meddlesome Confucian scholar by the collar. Regaining his wits, the scholar felt his legs turn weak; seeing the soldier's gloomy expression as he hauled him up, the scholar panicked all the more.

"What... what are you doing?" The scholar shivered.

Clenching his teeth in silence, the soldier dragged him directly toward Xufu and Ying Zheng.

The other soldiers also glared angrily at the scholar. While they couldn't condemn every single Confucian scholar, murdering this one with their glares was entirely possible.

These soldiers were veterans of the battlefield who had taken lives; the killing intent they radiated was not something a mere Confucian scholar could withstand.

Terrified to the point of a breakdown, the Confucian scholar shrieked, "Your Majesty, it wasn't my fault! Your Majesty, it was because the Xiang Goddess wanted to stop us from taking away the Nine Cauldrons that she unleashed a fierce wind to deliberately blow me down!"

While Ying Zheng loathed the Xiang Goddess in his heart, his anger and hatred toward this Confucian scholar—who had messed up, tried to steal the credit, and now dared to shirk responsibility while babbling endlessly—were far greater! Confucianists truly produced very few capable individuals!

"Bring him up," Ying Zheng said coldly, turning around to take Xufu's hand.

Xufu cast a cold, indifferent glance back at the scholar, growing equally weary of such people.

Wanting to showcase oneself was fine, but at least the achievement had to be genuinely yours. Snatched the Jiuzhou Cauldron from the soldiers' hands in hopes of shining before Ying Zheng—what a colossal mistake! Especially now, resorting to sophistry to save his skin; that ugly mug was truly nauseating.

A single cauldron, though rare, wasn't enough to make Xufu fly into a rage. However, this Confucian scholar made Xufu feel that even looking at him was unpleasant.

The Confucian scholar was dragged up, soaking wet and bleeding from the head, looking utterly disheveled.

A Confucian scholar could no longer bear to watch and said, "Please spare his life, Your Majesty." Yet this person didn't dare blame the Xiang Goddess.

Ying Zheng ignored him.

Trembling, the Confucian scholar pleaded, "Your Majesty..."

The other Confucian scholars behind him chimed in, "Your Majesty."

Xufu thought these people were utterly exasperating. How could they lack situational awareness to such a degree? If they didn't die, who would?

"Men, cut down all the trees on Mount Xiang." Ying Zheng was indeed deeply displeased. Especially as an emperor holding supreme authority, how could he allow any Xiang deity to lord over him? What was a mere gale? He would do just as he had in his past life: cut down every tree on this mountain, smash the Xiangshan Shrine, and leave that Xiang Goddess nowhere to dwell!

The soldiers naturally obeyed Ying Zheng's command and immediately moved to fell the trees.

Xufu's eyelids twitched.

That would not do.

It wasn't that offending the Xiang Goddess was unacceptable, but if all the trees were chopped down, what would hold the soil and water in place? If heavy rains came again later, wouldn't it cause landslides? Would Pengcheng still have peace and stability? The Xiang Goddess didn't matter, and the Confucian scholars didn't matter; what mattered were the innocent commoners in the city! Even now, Xufu could still recall the young girl at the foot of the mountain; these simple-minded folks could not be implicated because of others.

Besides, what good was cutting down the trees? It wouldn't inflict any substantive revenge on the Xiang Goddess, and since the Nine Cauldrons had fallen back into the water, chopping down the trees wouldn't bring them back either.

Xufu directly gripped Ying Zheng's hand back and said, "Wait."

The soldiers knew that aside from His Majesty's words, anyone else's could be ignored—but the Empress's words had to be obeyed!

"The trees cannot be cut down," Xufu said calmly. "Just plaster a layer of red mud all over the Xiang Goddess instead."

The soldiers didn't move, quietly awaiting the final verdict.

Ying Zheng pressed the corners of his lips together and stated, "...Do as the Empress says."

The soldiers nodded in assent. Truth be told, they didn't want to cut down trees either, as it was laborious work. They immediately grabbed tools to dig up red mud, preparing to slap a thick layer of it over the statue of the Xiang Goddess inside the shrine.

Xufu turned to look at Ying Zheng, explaining in a low voice, "If the trees are cut down, when heavy rains fall later, there won't be any trees to hold the soil and water, and the commoners in the city will suffer."

Ying Zheng nodded. So that was it—Ah-Fu was looking out for him. Joy blossomed uncontrollably on Ying Zheng's face.

Xufu continued, "By plastering a layer of red mud so the statue of the Xiang Goddess can no longer manifest before people or receive offerings, that will be the greatest humiliation inflicted upon her." Although humiliating a female deity wasn't entirely moral, those gusts of wind blowing in succession had been rather bothersome. Consider it a minor punishment, and far less excessive than stripping the mountain of all its trees.

Ying Zheng nodded, his expression relaxing further, clearly convinced by Xufu's words. "Ah-Fu is right," he agreed.

At this moment, the Confucian scholars exchanged glances, finally confirming entirely that their emperor was utterly subservient to this male empress.

That disheveled Confucian scholar also had a sudden awakening; the gaze he cast toward Xufu was as desperate as if he had grabbed onto a life-saving straw...

"Your Majesty, Empress..."
