By the time Xiang Yu revolted, it was already the reign of the Second Emperor of Qin.

Ying Zheng shook his head. "What? Who is this person?" Having said that, Ying Zheng frowned; if he was a dangerous figure, they could simply chop his head off.

Xu Fu did not directly state that this person would overthrow the Qin Dynasty. After all, once Xu Fu said that, from Ying Zheng's perspective, regardless of how old Xiang Yu currently was, and regardless of how naive and innocent he still might be, in order to nip future troubles in the bud, he would definitely deal a fatal blow to Xiang Yu directly. To Ying Zheng, Xiang Yu was like an ant, and such a life was not worth his concern.

Therefore, Xu Fu compromised somewhat and said, "This person possesses quite a bit of talent in military command and marching, and he is also naturally gifted with divine strength and extraordinary martial prowess."

Ying Zheng had always deeply admired such figures. He smiled and said, "If it is as A-Fu says, then in the future he can also be kept as a major pillar of support for Fusu."

Xu Fu imagined the scene of the Hegemon-King of Western Chu serving as a subordinate to Prince Fusu, and for some inexplicable reason, it felt delightfully surreal!

The two did not stay in the main hall for long. Once Ying Zheng finished dealing with official matters, he went together with Xu Fu to the side hall to check on Huhai. Human hearts always had degrees of closeness; over the years, Huhai had long since washed away the naturally unappealing background and heritage he had brought with him. Even if Ying Zheng didn't treat him as well as Fusu, it was still far better than treating him like an outsider. Naturally, Ying Zheng wanted to go and see if Xiang Yu had the gall to displease Huhai.

Harboring this thought, the two had just stepped across the threshold of the hall when they heard the sound of Huhai's loud laughter.

It wasn't enough that Huhai was laughing heartily; after finishing his laughter, he even let out fangirl-like shrieks, continuously showering praise: "Big Brother Xiang Yu, you're amazing!"

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng exchanged a helpless glance—they had worried over Huhai for nothing; at this point, they should have been worrying about Fusu instead. With Huhai acting like an ungrateful wretch who called anyone who caught his eye "big brother," if Fusu were to hear this, it wouldn't be strange if he died of anger.

As they walked further inward, an attendant whispered a reminder to the people inside that His Majesty and the Empress had arrived. Yet the occupants inside were perhaps too excited, as they didn't notice at all, let alone come out to greet them. When Xu Fu and Ying Zheng drew closer, they finally saw clearly what the people inside were fussing over that had caused Huhai to be so excited.

It turned out that young Xiang Yu, with his small frame, was actually lifting the large bronze tripod in Huhai's hall all by himself using just his right hand.

Originally, there was only a small incense burner in the room, but Huhai had deemed it insufficiently imposing, so he had a bronze tripod refitted to burn incense instead. This tripod was rather heavy; Xu Fu vaguely remembered that it had previously taken four eunuchs working together to carry it in. And now, it was being hoisted up by a ten-year-old child?! If those eunuchs were to see this, they would probably blush with shame.

Seeing Xiang Yu display such divine strength, Xu Fu finally got a bit of the feeling of witnessing the Hegemon-King of Western Chu.

Upon seeing Xiang Yu's performance, Ying Zheng's eyes lit up, and he thought to himself that it was indeed just as A-Fu had said—it was truly quite interesting.

A beat slower, Huhai noticed their arrival. He pulled Xiang Yu and turned around. Xiang Yu lowered the tripod in his hands shyly, his face flushed red as he said, "I—I was just lifting it to play." He looked as though he was afraid Xu Fu and Ying Zheng would scold him for recklessly touching someone else's things; from this, it could be seen that his upbringing was quite good. Xu Fu's mind settled slightly more. This Xiang Yu had quite a few similarities with historical records, but also entirely dissimilar aspects. As long as he was strictly supervised during his childhood, he naturally wouldn't grow up warped.

Ying Zheng fancied good raw talent like Xiang Yu, so he called him forward to question him in detail, and also asked him if he would be willing to reside in the palace long-term from then on.

Ying Zheng wanted to make Xiang Yu a sharp blade at Fusu's side.

Xiang Yu was somewhat shy, his face flushed pink, his eyes flickering as he said softly, "O—Okay then. To stay in the palace and be Huhai's bodyguard?"

Huhai hadn't been very happy earlier because Xiang Yu's arrival had stolen Royal Father's attention, but hearing Xiang Yu put it this way, Huhai immediately said happily, "Okay, okay! Royal Father, let him be my attendant!"

Ying Zheng had originally intended to leave Xiang Yu for Fusu, but now that his younger son was pleading aloud, Ying Zheng naturally couldn't rebuff Huhai either. He remembered A-Fu saying that children cared about face and should be cherished when they sought affection, so Ying Zheng changed his tune on the spot: "Then... then follow Huhai."

Perhaps due to his young age, Xiang Yu had no idea what being an attendant entailed. He only knew that Huhai had been extremely supportive of him just now, and such an admiring gaze was something Xiang Yu was experiencing for the very first time! Moreover, based on the mindset instilled by the upbringing he usually received, he thought Huhai was too good-looking and definitely needed someone to protect him; someone like himself was the absolute best fit! Little Xiang Yu, who could lift tripods and wield swords, was filled with confidence, his eyes shining brightly.

"Thank you, Royal Father!" Huhai smiled, revealing his teeth, "Thank you, Father!"

Ying Zheng smiled involuntarily, patted Xiang Yu, and said, "Then practice your martial arts in the palace from now on." As for studying literature, Ying Zheng wouldn't bother with that. Reading too much was sometimes not necessarily a good thing. If Xiang Yu remained this formidable and grew up into an easily controllable brute, that would be even better. Of course, Ying Zheng kept all these thoughts hidden in his heart; whether he could achieve what he desired in his heart would simply be left to nature.

Seeing that everything was fine, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng made the trip and then returned to their palace hand in hand.

Over the next few days, Xiang Yu truly began practicing kung fu in the palace. Shy as he was, he wasn't actually afraid of people and carried himself quite adeptly within the royal palace, not treating it like a solemn and majestic royal court at all. Under his influence, the lazy Huhai couldn't help following along to learn a couple of moves himself.

As for what kind of mood the eldest son Fusu felt upon seeing all this, neither Xu Fu nor Ying Zheng bothered to pay attention to it anymore.

Over on this side, Xiang Liang sent word that the mastermind behind the scenes had been caught.

When the roster of those captured this time was reported, it made Ying Zheng's complexion turn pitch black.

Leftover fish from the royal house of the State of Zhao, descendants of the nobility of the State of Yan, and a group of fangshi.

To be precise, there was a distinction between fangshi and scholars. Although the term was occasionally used to mean fangshi, at this time it was mostly used to refer to Confucian scholars.

In other words, yet another group of remnants of the Six States and Confucian scholars who were courting death had bumped right into Ying Zheng's hands—truly courting their own demise. Xu Fu felt a sudden bad premonition in his heart. His original intention was that he didn't want to see the burying of Confucian scholars; he would protect as many as he could. Even if future history books found fault with it, Ying Zheng walked an upright and honest path, and surely someone would eventually find this history to vindicate him. Yet who could have predicted that there would always be some people utterly devoid of tact who had no idea what an emperor's power and majesty were, and insistently sought death? In that case, Xu Fu truly had no way to help them.

He wasn't some holy savior; since these people had pushed things to this extent, they only had themselves to die.

Xu Fu suppressed the emotion in his eyes, feeling a slight sense of lament—he was now able to remain unmoved by human lives.

Upon hearing the reports from Yao Jia and Xiang Liang, Ying Zheng sneered, "Treat them as prisoners and order them to go build the water canals!"

Hearing this, Xu Fu was somewhat surprised. They weren't digging a pit to bury them this time? But on second thought, it made sense—digging a pit to bury them would waste the soldiers' physical strength and also ruin good farmland; burying them wasn't even as useful as planting a couple of cabbages!

Only, Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief far too early at this moment.

This group of remnants and Confucian scholars thoroughly demonstrated to everyone what it meant to court death with one's life.

Just as Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had packed up their things once more and prepared to head out, another piece of news arrived, stating that those remnants and Confucian scholars who had been reduced to prisoners for hard labor were spreading rumors everywhere locally, blackening the emperor's name, and loudly proclaiming that the emperor was tyrannical, enslaving and whipping the common people for his own selfish desires, making the people suffer exhausting hardships to build water canals, with countless people having died of exhaustion. Under such brutal governance, the common people had nowhere to voice their grievances; these men had merely been petitioning on behalf of the people, yet all of them had been exiled to do hard labor. If the people showed the slightest bit of dissatisfaction, they would suffer the exact same fate as them, with shackles locked around their hands and feet... and so on.

This time, they were blatantly talking utter nonsense with their eyes open to smear Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu truly could not bear it any longer!

When dealing with this group of people, Xu Fu had only three words filling his mind!

Bury! Bury! Bury!

In the 26th year of the First Emperor, some of the laborers building the canal disappeared mysteriously. Rumor had it that the First Emperor was cruel and had them buried in pits, while others claimed it was not laborers but Confucian scholars who were buried. However, the reason behind the First Emperor's actions remained a subject of heated debate, with no definitive answer.

...

As the red snow gradually ceased, Xu Fu heard Ying Zheng mention that those Confucian scholars and former officials had already been dealt with.

Xu Fu looked up at the sky, which was slowly turning a deep blue. He wondered if future generations would claim that it was precisely because the First Emperor had buried people alive and slaughtered the innocent that the heavens sent down red snow—the red snow serving as a divine indictment of his cruel deeds.

But there was no use dwelling on it now.

Who can control what happens after they are gone? Since it cannot be controlled, one might as well enjoy the present and live life to the fullest.

With the incident of the red snow concluded, Xiang Liang had proven his worth before them. Ying Zheng, naturally, was not stingy and bestowed a position upon him, while Xiang Yu remained in the palace. After all, while Xiang Liang made Ying Zheng feel uneasy, Xiang Yu was far too young to stir up any trouble, so Ying Zheng felt at ease.

Xu Fu did not pay much attention to Xiang Yu. He had previously been wary of Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, and Lü Zhi, but he had never considered that at this moment, Xiang Yu was only eleven years old. What could he possibly do? Nothing at all.

After leaving Xiang Yu in the palace, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng once again set out on their eastern inspection tour.

Since Xiang Yu was young, perhaps staying in the palace and being subtly influenced would allow him to change his fated destiny, much like Huhai.

·

Once the heavy snow stopped, the period of melting began, and the time when snow melts is the coldest.

As the carriage traveled along the imperial road, Xu Fu curled up inside, wrapped in robes and blankets, with a human furnace behind him, who had tucked a smaller hand warmer into his arms. Although it was cold outside, being huddled together like this, feeling warm all over, had a unique charm.

Not long after the carriage started, an attendant outside spoke cautiously through the curtain: "Your Majesty, Empress, the weather looks like it is turning bad again." The implication was that he hoped Xu Fu would take a look, as only Xu Fu in the entire entourage could discern the changes in the sky.

Xu Fu struggled a bit in Ying Zheng's arms before laboriously poking his head out from under the curtain.

Seeing him emerge, the attendant outside breathed a sigh of relief.

Xu Fu looked up at the sky; it was indeed heavy, but it was likely just the change of seasons, causing the sky to look different than before. Xu Fu squinted into the distance, where he could faintly see the snow-capped peaks.

"Stop moving forward. Find a cave to rest," Xu Fu said in a low voice.

The attendant asked in surprise, "Empress, is there truly something wrong with the weather?"

Xu Fu shook his head. "The weather is fine, but the thick snow ahead hasn't melted yet. If we go now, we'll likely get stuck. Let's rest for the night and organize men to clear the road tomorrow." They had been traveling for most of the day; although the soldiers were generally strong, they shouldn't be forced to clear roads in such weather. Physical exertion consumes energy quickly in the cold, and if they exhausted themselves, it would be troublesome.

Naturally, if they were to camp out in such cold, they had to choose a cave rather than setting up camp on the spot.

A cave would at least provide shelter from the cold.

Of course, Xu Fu wouldn't explain these trivial reasons in detail to the attendant. The attendant already had immense faith in Xu Fu, so he didn't ask further and immediately summoned men to carry out Xu Fu's orders.

After speaking, Xu Fu was pulled back into the carriage by a pair of large hands.

Ying Zheng raised his hand to stroke Xu Fu's cheek, whispering, "You're frozen red."

In his previous life, Xu Fu would have been a shut-in who rarely went out. His skin was naturally fair, and being physically weak made him look even paler. It was rare to see his face flushed with cold, which gave him a strangely beautiful, rose-like color.

Just from Ying Zheng's body language, Xu Fu knew exactly what he wanted to do.

Fortunately, in such cold weather, there weren't many braziers to light, and Xu Fu was wrapped up so tightly that there was no room to maneuver. Although Ying Zheng was stirred, he ultimately restrained himself.

Ying Zheng wrapped Xu Fu tightly, buried his face in the crook of Xu Fu's neck, and said in a hoarse, low voice, "A-Fu's neck is truly warm."

Xu Fu's mind wandered slightly. He wanted to say there was a warmer place on his body and perhaps reach down to touch him, but he thought better of it, deciding it was too lewd and didn't suit his temperament, so he gave up.

Ying Zheng nuzzled his neck for a long while, his actions quite erotic. Soon, they heard the eunuch outside call out: "Your Majesty, Empress, a cave has been found."

The carriage moved only a few steps before coming to a halt.

Ying Zheng lifted the curtain and looked out; sure enough, there was a cave with a small opening not far away.

The attendant jumped down from the cave entrance and hurried over, reporting in a low voice: "There are no signs of wild beasts living inside."

Ying Zheng nodded and picked Xu Fu up horizontally.

Xu Fu raised an eyebrow, his expression cooling slightly.

Ying Zheng leaned into his ear and explained affectionately, "There is snowmelt on the ground. What if your shoes and socks get wet? It's better if I carry you in."

Xu Fu's heart inevitably softened.

Although the posture was a bit excessive in front of everyone, Ying Zheng was always unwilling to let him suffer, so what could Xu Fu say? He silently accepted the gesture of affection.

In truth, Xu Fu was overthinking it. Their behavior had become more high-profile with each passing year, and everyone was long accustomed to it. Besides, their Emperor was tall and heroic, and the Empress and State Preceptor was exceptionally handsome; the two of them together were a perfect match. It was such a pleasing sight that no one would complain about seeing more of it!

The two soon entered the cave.

Although the entrance was small, the interior was surprisingly spacious, with plenty of room to move around.

The eunuch busied himself laying down blankets to prevent Xu Fu and Ying Zheng from catching the dampness from the ground. Then, the soldiers began to light a fire and set up the cave. Even if they were only staying for one night, they had to be meticulous.

Ying Zheng sat on the blankets with his arm around Xu Fu, pointing at the cave and whispering, "This must have been excavated by predecessors." He then pointed to some blurred markings on the cave wall and said, "Those are ancient characters."

Xu Fu clicked his tongue in wonder.

The power of the ancients was indeed not to be underestimated. Not to mention the Dujiangyan, the Zheng Guo Canal, or the future Great Wall and Lingqu... just looking at such a large cave, excavated entirely by human labor, how could one not marvel at the magnitude of human strength? No wonder it is said that among all things in the world, only human power and wisdom are truly terrifying.

Ying Zheng seemed to have some knowledge of these ancient characters. He held Xu Fu and began to explain them in a low voice.

This caused Xu Fu to look at him twice more.

The First Emperor's vast knowledge was no boast!

He usually browsed through many official bamboo slips, but he also read quite a few ancient texts!

Before long, the soldiers had lit a fire, and torches were hung on the cave walls. A small tent was even set up inside the cave.

Then, they began to prepare food...

The food, having undergone improvements, was becoming increasingly flavorful. The aroma slowly drifted out, causing Xu Fu to twitch his nose involuntarily.

"Will this attract wild beasts?" Xu Fu couldn't help but whisper.

"No," Ying Zheng said while rubbing Xu Fu's palms. Xu Fu had a cold constitution, and he felt this was the only way to help him retain heat; it was also a form of intimate contact. "It is winter now, and many wild beasts do not come out. Besides, in winter, scents are weakened."

Xu Fu nodded, leaning into Ying Zheng's arms, suddenly feeling a bit lazy.

This kind of life really felt like retirement. Xu Fu didn't know if, in history, Ying Zheng had traveled his land alone with only soldiers and ministers. But Ying Zheng's current behavior made Xu Fu feel that he wasn't as obsessed with power as he was once thought to be.

"What are you thinking about?" Seeing Xu Fu slightly distracted, Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask.

If they were in the Xianyang Palace, he would have already taken advantage of Xu Fu's distraction to get handsy. It seems there are downsides to traveling.

"Hungry," Xu Fu said concisely.

Ying Zheng smiled helplessly and ordered someone to bring food.

The aroma grew richer, and Xu Fu truly felt hungry. Soon, the food was brought over. Just as Xu Fu took a bite, he heard a soldier outside the cave entrance turn and say, "Your Majesty, Empress, something seems to be approaching from afar."

It was already getting dark, gray and gloomy, making it hard to see what was in the distance, but it was precisely because it was blurry that it was concerning.

Ying Zheng was not in a hurry. He said calmly, "Watch carefully and report back in a moment."

The soldier shouted his acknowledgment and sent a few men to investigate.

Xu Fu wasn't worried either. Ying Zheng was by his side, surrounded by attendants and soldiers. Their group wasn't large, but every one of them was fierce, capable of taking on a hundred men. Ordinary incidents were not worth worrying about, and major incidents were impossible, as all the armies in the world now belonged to Qin. Who else could muster enough men to deal with them?

Xu Fu lowered his head and continued eating.

After a while, most of the food was prepared, and the soldiers gathered around to eat.

The soldier guarding outside the cave suddenly let out a strange cry, and his voice became urgent: "Your Majesty! It seems someone is coming towards us!" He hesitated and added, "There are quite a few of them..."

Xu Fu blinked. Could it be such a coincidence? He had just thought it impossible for a large group to attack them, and now someone was here? Was he being slapped in the face so quickly?

Upon hearing this, Ying Zheng remained calm, cutting the roasted meat in his hand. After cutting a piece, he fed it to Xu Fu before saying, "Let those who went out return. If those approaching the cave have the ability, let them come up."

Ying Zheng naturally had the confidence to say this. Not to mention the elite soldiers, the cave's geographical position made it easy to defend and difficult to attack. If anyone were foolish enough to attempt something, they would be coming to their deaths.

Xu Fu frowned secretly.

Nowadays, apart from the remnants of the six states, no one would want to attack their party. After all, the Great Qin was currently flourishing, there were few people inciting riots, and not many laborers were dying at the foot of the Great Wall. The common people naturally had no desire to rebel.

The more he thought about it, the more Xu Fu loathed those remnants of the six states.

They were truly too troublesome!

Can't you just live your lives properly? Why must you use the banner of "the people" to seek your own interests? Isn't it disgusting?

It was rare for Ying Zheng to see Xu Fu's face all scrunched up, and he couldn't help but laugh. "Is the taste strange?"

"No..." Xu Fu was about to say it wasn't strange, but before he could finish, the rest of his words were blocked by Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng leaned down and kissed Xu Fu's lips. The kiss was brief, and no one around them noticed their actions.

Ying Zheng licked Xu Fu's lips, withdrew his tongue, and said, "Does it taste better now?"

"Better." Xu Fu had no doubt that if he said it didn't, Ying Zheng would hold him and kiss him again. Although Xu Fu never rejected any intimate actions, they were outside, and such indulgence was truly not quite right. Thinking of the phrase "if the upper beam is crooked, the lower ones will be too," Xu Fu felt a faint pang of heartache.

At this moment, a few soldiers entered the cave; they must have been the ones sent out to investigate.

Their hair was damp, and they had some snow on them, likely from branches falling on them.

The soldiers briefly reported what they had discovered.

"It seems to be a group of people, but they were too far away to see their attire clearly." The soldier looked a bit embarrassed. "We could see they were holding weapons, but they looked very disorganized."

Xu Fu thought to himself that these were probably some kind of ragtag army.

Ying Zheng waved for them to go eat, then continued to whisper sweet nothings to Xu Fu.

By the time they finished their meal, the armed men still hadn't arrived. The soldiers went out in groups to fetch water. They couldn't just wait for those people; they had to do what they needed to do—fetch water, sleep, and so on. It wouldn't be worth it to be anxious over some insignificant ants.

When the soldiers returned with water, the guard at the cave entrance specifically counted the number of people.

No one was missing.

It seemed those people were still lurking, not even daring to pick off a single person.

Just as he was thinking this, a shout suddenly rang out in the cave: "Who are you?" The voice was extremely stern and loud, startling everyone in the cave into turning their heads.

Xu Fu also looked over and saw a soldier grabbing another by the collar, questioning him loudly.

Xu Fu's heart skipped a beat, and he exchanged a glance with Ying Zheng; both vaguely guessed what was happening.

That group wasn't as cowardly as they had imagined; on the contrary, they were quite bold. They had waited until someone went out for water, then sent men to pick off the straggler and replace him with one of their own... but did they think they could fool the Qin army? The Qin army had its own strict discipline, so as soon as the person was replaced, someone immediately recognized it.

"Take him down," Ying Zheng said calmly.

Hearing Ying Zheng's words, three or four soldiers pounced and began to fight the man.

The rest of the people watched from the sidelines; they wouldn't all pounce at once. After all, too many people rushing in would only cause trouble and get in the way.

Before long, the man was subdued.

Two soldiers dragged the man before Xu Fu and Ying Zheng. The man was forced to kneel and lift his head.

Xu Fu saw the man's face.

He had a full beard and looked somewhat disheveled, but his muscles were knotted, and his appearance was quite intimidating.

"Who are you?" Ying Zheng asked. His voice was cold, and he didn't even look at the bearded man; in his eyes, the man was not worth mentioning.

The bearded man didn't speak. Not only did he not answer, but he also looked at Xu Fu, his gaze even lingering on him. Ying Zheng looked up and caught the look of amazement in the bearded man's eyes. His face darkened, and he said coldly, "Execute him."

Upon hearing this, the bearded man struggled violently. But the straggler he had replaced had been caught off guard; now that the soldiers had the upper hand, how could they let him escape? No matter how he struggled, he couldn't break free from the soldiers' grip. The bearded man's face turned bright red, and he didn't care even if he hurt himself in the struggle.

"You... don't you want to know where the others are?" the bearded man said with a ferocious expression.

Ying Zheng said coldly, "No."

Did he need to know? Sending all the soldiers out to surround and slaughter them all at once—it might be a bit bloody, but it was very efficient.

Xu Fu had long known of Ying Zheng's ability to shut people down, and he struggled to hold back his laughter.

The bearded man was stunned, and he hurriedly said, "But... but they have a conspiracy..."

Xu Fu sighed inwardly; this baiting was a bit too obvious.

The bearded man didn't look like someone who would easily betray his own side, yet he was so quick to offer information and even bring up a conspiracy. Even if he were afraid of death, he wouldn't spill the beans so quickly, would he? To him, the bearded man's initial refusal to even give his name when first captured was his true nature.

When things are abnormal, there must be a demon.

Without even thinking, the bearded man's deliberate mention of a conspiracy was the real conspiracy!

"Take him away." Ying Zheng didn't even look at the bearded man, though he didn't have him killed immediately. He and Xu Fu exchanged a glance, both believing that this bearded man might be the leader of that group. After the bearded man was taken out, Ying Zheng ordered someone to find the whereabouts of the straggler.

After being dragged out, the bearded man began to shout again, this time acting like a complete scoundrel.

The soldiers tied him to a carriage parked outside the cave.

Of course, not the one Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were sitting in.

After all, if it were accidentally damaged by this person, it wouldn't be worth it!

How could a thief be worthy of being tied to that carriage?

After tying him up, they ignored him, not even posting a guard, and returned to the cave entrance to continue their watch. The bearded man widened his eyes again, stunned. He cursed a few times, but still didn't get a single glance from the Qin soldiers.

The bearded man immediately looked miserable. "What should I do... I haven't done anything yet. Those blocks of wood, they won't just attack the cave, will they?"

Inside the cave, it gradually became quiet.

After Xu Fu and Ying Zheng washed up, they embraced and wrapped themselves in the quilt. Because the fire was nearby, they didn't feel cold even inside the cave.

"Will they come tonight?" Xu Fu asked, muffled in Ying Zheng's arms.

"Yes." Ying Zheng's large palm pressed against Xu Fu's cheek, pulling him closer. "Don't worry, nothing will happen. Once the night passes, everything will be gone."

Xu Fu's mouth twitched.

He always felt like Ying Zheng was about to unleash some ultimate move—killing everyone in one go?

But Ying Zheng's embrace was too comfortable. Xu Fu closed his eyes and fell asleep without realizing it.

The howling wind outside gradually faded from Xu Fu's ears...

Ying Zheng also held him and fell asleep.

Ying Zheng's vigilance was extremely high; even while sleeping like this, if anyone approached, he would wake up immediately.

The fire crackled with small sounds, and the guards at the cave entrance began to feel sleepy, so they leaned against the cave wall. The firelight flickered, casting shadows on their faces.

Gradually, in the shadows cast by the cave walls, someone seemed to move.

Someone whispered, "They should all be unconscious, right?"

"Did you put the medicine in?"

"Let's test them first."

"Go!"

The brief conversation ended, and the group walked straight to the cave entrance. They quietly entered the cave and then said in loud voices: "See if they're awake!" "They shouldn't be!" "These people look like wealthy folks! We've made a profit this time!"

Xu Fu was awakened by their loud voices. After hearing their conversation, he couldn't help but twitch his mouth.

Seeing that Ying Zheng hadn't moved, Xu Fu kept his eyes closed and continued to pretend to be asleep.

Those people walked back and forth in the cave boldly. After a while, one said: "There's a little girl here, she's quite pretty..." The person next to him drooled: "Indeed, she's beautiful. I've never seen anyone this beautiful before." "Why don't we take her back to be the chieftain's wife!"

Xu Fu: "..."

Little girl? Where would there be a little girl in this cave? Could this group be... blind... Just as he thought this, Xu Fu froze.

They couldn't possibly be... mistaking him for some little girl, could they?

A surge of anger and displeasure rose from the depths of Xu Fu's heart.

Ying Zheng naturally heard this conversation as well. He was even more sensitive to these words and even more infuriated. When Ying Zheng was displeased, he wouldn't hold it in. He opened his eyes, held Xu Fu, and asked slowly, "Who do you want to take back to be your chieftain's wife?"

"Oh! So there's one who isn't unconscious!" The group turned around in unison and looked at Ying Zheng.

Upon seeing their attire and hearing their tone, Ying Zheng knew they were bandits. But with just one glance, he could see that most of them were just for show, and the only one who might be useful was the bearded man. But what could he do alone? In the hands of the Qin army, these people were truly only fit to be slaughtered.

"It's fine that you're not unconscious," the bandit laughed disgustingly, pointing at Xu Fu in Ying Zheng's arms. "Maybe we can watch how our chieftain handles your wife!"

Ying Zheng's expression turned cold, his gaze lingering on the bandit's hand.

At this moment, Xu Fu opened his eyes. He was almost disgusted to death by the bandit's words. Since coming to Qin, he had never heard such disgusting and disrespectful words. Thinking about it, Ying Zheng had protected him too well. How could Xu Fu tolerate such an insult?

His eyes flashed with cold light. "Better worry about your own lives first."

"Another one awake?" The bandit was shocked, but not panicked. Instead, he spat. "Why is it a man? He's so good-looking, why is he a man?"

At this moment, the soldiers and attendants who had been sleeping in the cave opened their eyes and rolled over. They drew their weapons, the sharp blades gleaming in the firelight, causing the bandits to feel a flicker of fear.

The bandits finally changed their expressions and couldn't help but retreat, but the cave was only so big, and it was full of soldiers and attendants. Where could they retreat to?

"You... you didn't pass out?" the bandit shouted sternly, seemingly trying to win with volume.

Ying Zheng's expression was cold. "Take this one down first." He pointed at the one who had spoken most disrespectfully.

The bandit broke out in a cold sweat, but as he panicked, the soldiers began to move.

In the cave, the sound of clashing weapons, the sound of blades piercing bodies and tearing clothes, and the sound of screams immediately erupted...

The bandit in front had already been knocked to the ground.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng stood up and walked over to the bandit, so close that the bandit's face was pressed against Ying Zheng's boots.

Ying Zheng's loathing for this person had reached its peak. He wouldn't show any mercy and kicked him heavily in the face. The kick had enough force that the bandit's head was knocked to the side, his teeth were loosened, and he spat out a lot of blood. In just a moment, the man's cheek swelled up purple.

The bandit was enraged and began to curse.

Ying Zheng drew a knife from his side, had someone hold the bandit's arm, and asked in a cold, low voice, "This was the arm that pointed, right?"

The cold sweat on the bandit's forehead increased.

By this time, the others had almost finished the battle.

How could a mob resist the elite of Great Qin? It didn't take much effort for them to be subdued, and each one was pressed to the ground. If they didn't behave, they were kicked in the face—the goal was to trample their self-esteem and humiliate them!

They began to wail.

Until they saw the extremely handsome man with a powerful aura standing in front of one of their brothers with a knife.

The man raised his hand and brought the knife down. They heard their brother let out a miserable scream, and blood splattered in that instant...

Shadows flickered in the cave.

The hearts of the bandits sank, and the timid ones even wet their pants.

How could they have imagined that this man would be so cruel?

Xu Fu stood by and watched as Ying Zheng chopped off the man's arm. Xu Fu knew the anger in Ying Zheng's heart, and he wasn't happy either. So, even though Ying Zheng was full of murderous intent, he didn't step forward to stop him.

At this moment, Ying Zheng said something that made the bandits even more terrified: "This is the first."

W-what did that mean?

Was he going to chop them all up?

Even the most ferocious bandit couldn't help but tremble.

Naturally, Ying Zheng didn't need to do it himself anymore. He said coldly, "Bring the bandit leader over, cut off their limbs, and bury them alive."

Limbs... they weren't even being treated as human beings.

The bandit leader naturally referred to the bearded man.

This was what Ying Zheng had deduced from the conversation and the bearded man's behavior.

The soldiers nodded and immediately went to find the bearded man.

Xu Fu was slightly shocked. After all, he rarely saw such scenes. Ying Zheng's actions were a bit bloody for him, but he said nothing. Ying Zheng's rage was merely a result of his protection of him. These bandits were truly too stupid; if they had only wanted to steal money, they wouldn't have died so miserably...

For the soldiers, dealing with a few bandits was extremely easy. Having killed people on the battlefield like cutting vegetables, how could they care about these few lives?

They worked together to drag the wailing bandits out.

How could they dare to slaughter people's arms right in front of Xu Fu? The scene was too bloody, and it wouldn't be good to frighten the Empress.

Soon, the cave returned to silence, but the silence was somewhat chilling.

The bloodstains on the ground were still there.

A soldier ran in with a smile, picked up the severed arm on the ground, and said apologetically, "Forgot this." With that, the soldier ran out in a flash.

This left Xu Fu feeling a bit amused; the bloody smell seemed to have been diluted by the soldier's actions.

The eunuchs and attendants began to clean up the mess in the cave. Soon, the blankets and quilts were back in place, and the fire was relit. Ying Zheng hugged Xu Fu and asked in a low voice, "Do you want to wash up? That bloody smell must have gotten on you." Ying Zheng's expression was exceptionally gentle, completely different from before.

Xu Fu felt something in his heart.

Ying Zheng's behavior was likely because he didn't want Xu Fu to see him as the First Emperor of his previous life.

After all, his appearance just now did indeed overlap with the image of the First Emperor of the previous life.

Xu Fu pretended not to know Ying Zheng's thoughts, hugged his waist, and buried himself in his arms, saying naturally, "I'm sleepy."

Ying Zheng felt an indescribable joy. He held Xu Fu tightly and responded, and then the two lay down to sleep. The faint smell of blood still lingered in Xu Fu's nose, but in Ying Zheng's arms, he slowly ignored it. Before long, Xu Fu fell asleep.

Ying Zheng looked down at Xu Fu's face in his arms and couldn't help but raise his hand to gently stroke his cheek.

His eyes were deep, as if he had something to say, yet as if he couldn't say anything at all.

The fire in the cave was still flickering, the soldiers had all fallen asleep, and the bandits' screams had faded away...

In the early morning, Xu Fu opened his eyes groggily and looked outside. The sun had risen early, and the sunlight shining into the cave finally brought some warmth. It seemed the snow would melt today.

Xu Fu was still staring at the scenery outside when Ying Zheng, who had also woken up early, leaned over and kissed his neck.

"Are you getting up?" Ying Zheng asked in a low voice.

Ying Zheng's voice in the morning was extremely charming.

Xu Fu's eyes flashed, and he pushed off his shoulders, struggling out of his arms.

The two got up and soon washed up.

The eunuch brought food, and after a simple meal, Xu Fu walked out of the cave. The air outside was fresh, but as soon as Xu Fu looked down, he couldn't help but see the bloodstains on the ground.

Large patches of it, like beautiful flowers blooming on the ground.

It was just that these flowers were a bit terrifying.

Just as Xu Fu was about to look away, he suddenly felt that something was wrong with the ground. Looking closely, he realized the ground seemed to be bulging slightly, only to collapse again.

Ying Zheng walked out, stood by Xu Fu's side, and followed his gaze. He explained, "They didn't bury them firmly."

So the soil was loose, allowing the people underneath to struggle and push the soil up.

Which meant that those bandits were still alive...

Xu Fu felt a bit disgusted and looked away.

In the cold weather, blood doesn't flow out easily. It seemed that was why those bandits hadn't died from blood loss.

...This punishment was enough to make them remember it until they died.

At this moment, a soldier ran up and said, "Your Majesty, these bandits have a stronghold, and there are people they kidnapped inside..."

Xu Fu was surprised.

It seemed these bandits had done many evil deeds!

It looked like they would have to stay here tonight.

But saving people was a good thing, so Xu Fu naturally didn't mind.

Ying Zheng ordered a search and rescue, and then he took Xu Fu for a walk around the area to enjoy the scenery.

Some soldiers were sent to save people, while others remained to guard them.

Not long after, another attendant came and said that news had arrived from Xianyang.

Author's note:

Historical records:

In the 31st year, in the 12th month, the First Emperor traveled incognito to Xianyang with four warriors. At night, they encountered bandits at Lanchi. Seeing they were in a difficult situation, the warriors killed the bandits, and a massive search was conducted in Guanzhong for twenty days.

The general idea is that he traveled incognito and encountered bandits. I changed it here to the 26th year, encountering bandits on the eastern inspection tour.
chapters.title: 第268章
chapters.source_text:
始皇二十六年，修建水渠的部分劳工离奇消失，据传始皇残暴，将劳工都挖坑埋之，也有人传埋的并非劳工而是儒生。但对于始皇为何有此举，却一直争论纷纷，不得其原因。
……
红雪渐渐停了的时候，徐福便听嬴政说起，那些儒生和遗臣都已经处置了。
徐福仰头瞥了一眼渐渐转为蔚蓝的天空，也不知道后世会不会说，正因为始皇挖坑埋了人，滥杀无辜，才导致天降红雪，红色的雪，便正是老天对他残暴行为的控诉。
不过现在多想也无用了。
谁能管得了身后事呢？既然管不了，那便干干脆脆如今爽上一把，活得快意便好。
红雪的事告一段落，项梁也在他们的跟前证明了自己的能力，嬴政当然也不会吝啬给项梁派个职务，项羽倒是就此留在了宫中。毕竟项梁令嬴政觉得不快，但项羽的年纪却是无论如何都掀不起风浪的，自然嬴政就放下了心。
徐福对项羽倒也不是很在意，他之前一直对项羽、刘邦、吕雉有所提防，但却从未想到过，这时候的项羽才刚刚十一岁，能做得了什么？什么也做不了。
将项羽留在宫中之后，徐福方才和嬴政一同再度踏上了东巡的路途。
项羽如今年纪小，说不准留在宫中潜移默化的，日后也能像胡亥那样，改变其既定的命运。
·
大雪一停，便进入了融雪期，而融雪的时候最为寒冷。
马车在官道上行着，徐福便蜷缩在了马车之中，身上裹着衣袍和毯子，身后还贴了个人肉火炉，火炉还往他怀中又塞了个小火炉。外头虽然是冷了些，但能这般依偎在一处，浑身暖融融，倒是更有不一样的滋味。
马车行了不久，隔着一层车帘，外头的侍从小心翼翼地道：“陛下，皇后，这天气瞧着像是又不大好了。”言下之意，其实就是希望徐福能出去瞧上两眼，毕竟队伍之中也唯有徐福，能够一双眼瞧出不同来了。
徐福在嬴政怀中挣扎了两下，而后才艰难地从车帘底下探出了头去。
见人一出来，外面的侍从顿时松了一口气。
徐福抬头瞥了一眼天，是有些沉，但这应当是要换季了，所以天色变化比之从前有所不同了。徐福眯起眼往远处看了看，隐约还能瞥见远处山峰上的皑皑白雪。
“别往前行了。寻个山洞歇息。”徐福沉声道。
那侍从惊异道：“皇后，果真天色有异吗？”
徐福摇头，“天色没甚问题，只是前方厚雪还未化完，此时前去怕是要被堵在这头，休息一晚，明日再组织人手去清理道路吧。”他们已经行了大半天的路了，虽说士兵们身体大都强悍，但也不可在这样的时候去清理道路，本来天气冷的时候体力消耗就快，到时候若是消耗个干净，那才麻烦。
自然，他们要在这样冷的时候在外露宿，也只能选择山洞，而不能就地扎营。
山洞好歹能御寒。
当然这些琐碎的原因，徐福不会细细说给那侍从听，侍从本身对徐福又是极为信服的，闻言便也不多问，立即招来人手，让他们按照徐福的吩咐去做事了。
徐福说完话，便被一双大手给拖回了马车中去。
嬴政抬手摩挲了两下徐福的面颊，低声道：“都冻红了。”
换在后世，徐福就是个死宅，平时少有出门的时候，他的肤色本就白，加上体弱，也就显得更白了，难得被冻红了脸，看上去反倒有了点儿不一样的瑰美色彩。
徐福单是从嬴政这个肢体动作中，就知晓了他想做什么。
不过幸好，这样冷的天，没有那么多的火盆可点，徐福包裹得严严实实的，也施展不开，嬴政虽有情动，但是到底还是将自己克制住了。
嬴政将徐福裹得紧紧的，然后埋进了徐福的脖颈处，还沙哑着嗓子，沉声道：“阿福的脖颈处实在暖和极了。”
徐福脑子里的思维稍微有些发散。他想说你身上有个地方更暖和，顺便再摸一把裆。但是徐福想一想，觉得这样实在太过猥琐了，实在不符合他的气质，于是就干脆放弃了。
嬴政在他脖颈间磨蹭了好一会儿，动作颇有些情色味道。不久便听外面的内侍喊道：“陛下，皇后，山洞已经寻到了。”
那马车走了没几步，也就停住了。
嬴政伸手掀起了车帘，往外一看，果真不远处有个开口较小的山洞。
侍从从山洞口跳了下来，三两步到了他们的跟前，低声汇报道：“里面并无猛兽生活过的痕迹。”
嬴政点了点头，直接将徐福打横抱了起来。
徐福挑眉，面色冷了冷。
嬴政俯在他耳边亲昵地解释道：“地上有雪水，若是你下脚湿了鞋袜可怎么好？便不如我将你抱进去了。”
徐福心中不可避免地软了软。
虽然姿势在众人面前，显得是有些过分了些，但是嬴政处处舍不得他吃苦，徐福还能说什么？自是不动声色地敛下这份感动。
其实徐福实在是多想了，毕竟他和嬴政之间的行为，早就是一年高调过一年，众人实在是见怪不怪了。而且他们的陛下生得高大英武，皇后兼国师又生得俊美非常，二人凑在一处，那岂不是极为相配吗？这是何等赏心悦目的画面啊！谁都不会嫌多！
二人很快进了山洞。
这山洞开口虽小，但里头却是别有洞天，活动空间相当的足够。
内侍忙铺下了毯子，免得徐福和嬴政坐下来的时候，沾了底下的湿气。而后士兵们又开始生火，布置山洞。虽然只停留一夜，但也要悉心对待才是。
嬴政揽着徐福在毯子上坐下，指着山洞低声道：“此处应当乃是前人挖掘留下的。”说着他又指了指山洞壁上一些模糊不清的痕迹，道：“那是古文字。”
徐福微微咋舌。
古人的力量果然是不可小觑的，且不说如今的都江堰、郑国渠，以及未来的长城和灵渠等……单看这样大的山洞，却是在之前全靠人工挖掘出来的，如何能不让人感叹人的力量之大？难怪都说世间万物，唯人的力量和智慧最为可怕。
嬴政似乎对这些古文字有些了解，他拥着徐福，还一边低声讲解了起来。
倒是引得徐福多看了他两眼。
始皇帝的博闻强识倒不是吹嘘的！
他平时浏览的公务竹简多，但看的古籍也不少！
不多时，士兵们便燃起了火堆，洞壁之中还挂起了火把。洞中甚至还搭建了一顶小小的帐篷。
而后便是开始做食物……
如今的食物经历过改良之后，倒是越加有滋味儿了，香气缓缓飘出来，让徐福不自觉地动了动鼻子。
“会引来猛兽么？”徐福忍不住低声道。
“不会。”嬴政一边揉搓徐福的手掌一边道。徐福体寒，他觉得只有这样，方才能帮着徐福留住热度，当然也是亲密接触的一种方式。“此时正值冬日，许多猛兽都不会出来。而且冬日里，味道也会被削弱。”
徐福点了点头，靠在嬴政怀中，突然变得有些懒怠了起来。
这样的生活，实在有些像是退休生活啊。徐福不知道历史上，嬴政是否孤身一人，只带了士兵和大臣便开始巡游他的国土。但如今嬴政的行为，反倒让徐福生出了，嬴政并不是那样重于权柄不肯脱手的感觉。
“在想什么？”见徐福微微走神，嬴政不由得问道。
若是在咸阳宫中，他便早借着徐福走神的时候，上下其手了。可见出来游玩，也是有不足之处的。
“饿了。”徐福简洁利落地道。
嬴政无奈一笑，令人去取食物了。
香气在鼻间渐渐变得更为浓郁了，徐福是当真觉得有些饿了。很快食物拿了过来，徐福下口咬了咬，便突然听洞口外的士兵转头来道：“陛下，远处似乎有什么东西在接近。”
此时天色已经有些黑了，灰蒙蒙、阴沉沉，实在不大能看清远处是什么，但正是因为看得模糊，才更令人上心。
嬴政并不急，他淡淡道：“仔细瞧着，一会儿再报。”
士兵高声应了，还派出了几人前去查探。
徐福也不着急，反正嬴政在他的身旁，周边还围了侍从和士兵，他们这支队伍人算不上多，但却绝对个个凶悍，拎出去都是以一敌百的好手，寻常的事故实在不消在意，而大的事故也不可能出现，毕竟如今天下兵马皆归于秦，还有谁能拿出许多人手来对付他们？
徐福低头继续吃着手中的食物。
过一会儿，食物大部分都做好了，士兵们也纷纷围下来，准备开始吃东西。
守在山洞外的士兵，突然间怪叫了一声，随即声音急促了起来，道：“陛下！似乎有人朝我们过来了！”那人又斟酌了一下，道：“人数有些多……”
徐福眨了眨眼，不是这样凑巧吧？他才刚想着，绝不可能有什么大的队伍来攻击他们，于是此时便有人来了？打脸这样快？
嬴政闻言，倒是依旧面不改色地切着手中的烤肉，切好之后，便往徐福口中塞了一块，随后他才道：“让方才出去的人都回来，那些接近山洞的人，若是有本事便让他们上来好了。”
嬴政说这话自然是有底气的，且不说士兵精锐，光是这山洞的地理位置，也显得很是易守难攻，若是真有不长眼的人要企图对他们做些什么，那便是前来找死来了。
徐福暗暗皱眉。
如今除了六国遗臣，也没什么人会想要攻击他们的队伍了，毕竟此时大秦正是一派欣欣向荣之时，没有太多人煽动暴乱，更没有多少劳工死在长城脚下。那些百姓自然不会有什么反叛之心。
越是想到这一点，徐福便越是厌恶那些六国遗臣了。
实在太能作妖！
好好过你的日子不行吗？非要打着为民的旗号来为自己谋利益，恶心不恶心？
嬴政难得见徐福五官都皱一块儿的表情，他忍不住笑了，“味道很奇怪？”
“不……”徐福刚想说个不奇怪，谁知道才冒出来一个字，剩下的话便统统被嬴政堵回去了。
嬴政低头吻住了徐福的唇，这个吻倒是浅尝辄止，身边都没什么人注意到他们的动作。
嬴政舔了舔徐福的唇，这才收起舌，道：“现在味道好了吗？”
“好了。”徐福毫不怀疑，若是他说没好的话，嬴政还会扣着他再来一个吻。虽然徐福向来不排斥任何亲密动作，但如今毕竟是在外头，这样放肆着实有点不大好。现在徐福想到“上梁不正下梁歪”这句话，都还有点淡淡的心痛。
这时候，洞口外进来了几名士兵，想来正是刚才被派出去查探情形的。
士兵们头发都打湿了，身上还顶了点雪，想来是树枝上掉下来，便落在他们身上了。
士兵们简单说了他们出去后查探到的东西。
“那应当是一群人，只是距离太远了些，看不清是什么打扮。”士兵有些赧然，“他们手中持有兵器是能瞧见的，不过显得很是杂乱。”
徐福心道，这大概便是杂牌军一类的人物。
嬴政挥手让他们用饭食去了，随后继续低声和徐福甜腻腻。
等到他们用完食物后，都没等到那些手持兵器的人前来。士兵们便结伴出去寻水了。他们自是不可能一直等待那些人前来，当然是该做什么便做什么，打水得打水，睡觉也得睡觉。若为一些不足为提的蝼蚁，反倒弄得自己惶然不已，那便实在不划算了。
等士兵们打了水回来，洞口处的士兵还特意数了一下人数。
人倒是没少。
看来那些人还在蹲守，连挑单个的下手都不敢。
正想着呢，洞中突然响起了一声惊呼，“你是谁？”这一声极为严厉，声音也足够响亮，登时震得洞中的人都转过了头去。
徐福当然也看了过去，只见这话是一名士兵，揪住了另一名的衣领，高声质问出来的。
徐福心中一动，与嬴政对视一眼，二人都隐约猜到了是怎么回事。
那群人并不是他们想象得那样胆小，相反，他们还很胆大，他们蹲守到人出去寻水之后，便派出了人，挑选落单的下手，然后用己方的人来替代……但他们以为这样便可蒙混过关，好来个里应外合了吗？秦军治军向来有自己的一套，所以当换了人之后，士兵中便立即有人认出来了。
“拿下。”嬴政淡淡道。
听到嬴政的话，周围三两个士兵扑了上去，和那人打了起来。
剩下的人便在一旁看戏了，他们当然不会齐齐扑上去。毕竟那么多人涌上去，反而添了不少事端碍手碍脚。
不多时，那人便被拿下了。
两名士兵将那人押到了徐福和嬴政的跟前，那人被迫跪了下来，也被迫抬起了头。
徐福见着了这人的面容。
满面大胡子，看上去模样有些邋遢，但这人肌肉虬结，模样看上去倒是很能唬人。
“你是何人？”嬴政出声问道。他的声音很是冷淡，连看都没看那大胡子一眼，毕竟大胡子在他眼中实在太不值得一提了。
大胡子并没有说话，他不仅不回话，反而还看向了徐福，甚至是将目光都黏在了徐福的身上。嬴政抬起头来看了他一眼，顿时从大胡子的眼中捕捉到了惊艳之色，嬴政面色一黑，冷声道：“将他斩了。”
大胡子闻言，奋力挣扎了起来。但之前能被他解决掉的落单士兵，那是并未设防，而此时士兵们已经占了先机，又怎么会让他逃走呢？不管那大胡子如何挣扎，他始终都无法挣脱那士兵的桎梏。大胡子面色没一会儿便涨得通红了，哪怕他在挣扎中伤害到了自己，他也并不在意。
“你们、你们不想知道那些人在何处吗？”大胡子面容狰狞地道。
嬴政冷声道：“不想。”
还用知道吗？将士兵全都派出去，将人圈起来一次绞杀，血腥是血腥了点儿，但极为省事。
徐福早就知道嬴政这等噎人的本事，在旁边辛苦地憋住了笑意。
那大胡子被堵得也有些傻眼，他忙道：“可……可他们还有阴谋……”
徐福心中暗暗叹了一口气，这钓鱼可就钓得有些明显了啊。
这大胡子看上去并不像是会轻易投敌的人，但偏偏他就是这样轻易地要供出自己，甚至还拉扯出了阴谋，就算是怕死，也不至于这样快地抖落出来吧？以他来看，刚被抓到的时候，那大胡子桀骜不驯地连名字都不愿报上，方才是他真正的本性。
事出反常必有妖。
想也不用想，着大胡子故意说有什么阴谋诡计，那才是真的阴谋！
“将人带走。”嬴政看也没看那大胡子一眼，不过倒是没再直接让人杀了他。他和徐福对视了一眼，彼此都认为这大胡子，说不准是那拨人中的领头人。大胡子被带出去之后，嬴政便让人去寻那落单士兵的下落。
大胡子被拖出去后，便又囔囔叫了起来，这回表现得极为无赖。
士兵将他绑在了山洞外停靠着的马车之上。
当然并不是徐福和嬴政坐的那辆。
毕竟若是不慎被这人给毁了，那实在不值！
一个贼人，怎配与那马车拴到一起呢？
将人拴住以后，他们也不理会，连个看守的人都不派，就直接回转身到山洞口继续看守了。那大胡子再度瞪大了眼，又有些傻眼了。他在后头骂了几句，却仍旧没得到秦军一个回眸。
那大胡子登时一脸苦相，“这可怎么办哟……啥都还没做，那群木头，不会直接攻到洞中去吧？”
这头山洞里渐渐安静了下来。
徐福和嬴政洗漱过后，便相拥着裹在了被子里，因为旁边便是火堆的缘故，因而哪怕是在山洞之中，他们也并不觉得寒冷。
“夜晚他们会来吗？”徐福埋在嬴政怀中，瓮声道。
“会。”嬴政的大掌贴在了徐福的面颊上，将他又往怀中按了按，“放心吧，什么事也不会有，一夜过去，便什么都没了。”
徐福嘴角微抽。
总觉得嬴政像是要放什么大招一般，一出手就全部搞死吗？
但是嬴政的怀中实在太过舒服，徐福闭上眼，不知不觉便睡着了。
外面呼啸的寒风都渐渐从徐福的耳畔远去了……
嬴政也拥着他在一同入睡。
嬴政的警惕性极高，就算是这般入睡，一旦有人前来，他还是会立时醒过来。
火堆燃烧着发出细小的噼啪声，洞门口的守卫渐渐也来了困意，于是他们倚住了洞壁，山洞内的火光明明灭灭，在他们的脸庞上落下了一片阴影。
渐渐的，山体掩映的阴影之下，似乎有什么人动了。
有人在低语，“他们应该都晕了吧？”
“药下好了吗？”
“先去试探一番。”
“走！”
短暂的对话结束了，这群人直直走到了山洞外，他们悄然走入了山洞中，然后大着嗓门儿道：“你看看他们醒了吗？”“应该没醒吧！”“瞧上去这些人都是富贵人呐！这回倒是赚了！”
徐福是他们的大嗓门吵醒的，吵醒以后听见他们的对话，徐福不免嘴角一抽。
只是见嬴政一直没有动作，徐福便依旧闭着眼，继续装睡。
那些人在山洞中大着胆子来回行走，过了会儿，有个人道：“这里有个小姑娘，生得倒是漂亮……”旁边的人跟着流口水，“的确生得好看啊，我从前就没见过这样好看的人。”“不如带回去给寨主做个媳妇！”
徐福：“……”
小姑娘？这山洞里哪来的小姑娘？这群人莫不是……眼瘸……刚想到这里，徐福就僵住了。
他们总不至于是将他……当做了劳什子小姑娘吧？
一股怒火和不快，登时从徐福心底深处拔了起来。
嬴政自然也将这段对话收入了耳中，嬴政对这些话更为敏感，也更为憋火，当嬴政不快的时候，他当然不会憋着下去了，嬴政睁开眼来，拥着徐福慢条斯理地问道：“你们想要谁去给你们寨主做媳妇？”
“哟！原来还有个没昏过去呢！”那些人齐齐转过身来，看向了嬴政。
嬴政一见这行人的打扮，和说话的口吻，便知晓这伙人应当是强盗，但也就是一个照面，嬴政便能瞧出来，这群人之中花架子居多，真正顶用的，那大胡子算是一个。但光他一人又如何？这些人在秦军手底下，还当真只有被斩杀的份儿。
“没昏过去也好。”强盗恶心地笑着，指了指嬴政怀中的徐福，“说不定正好瞧一瞧我们寨主是如何搞你媳妇的！”
嬴政面色一冷，他的目光在强盗的那只手上打了个旋儿。
此时徐福也睁开了双眼，他差点被那强盗的话给恶心死。从他到秦国以来，还真没有听过这样恶心不客气的话。此时想一想，倒是嬴政将他护得太好了。此时徐福怎能容得了这样的侮辱？
他目露寒光，道：“不如先担心你们自己的小命。”
“又一个醒了？”强盗大惊，但也并不算惊慌，反倒还啐了一口，“怎么是个男的？长得这般好看，怎的是个男的？”
此时山洞中原本睡着的士兵和侍从等人，都睁开眼翻起了身，他们还从怀中抽出了兵器，利刃在火光下显得熠熠生辉，让人不自觉地生出了些微的害怕。
那些强盗终于变了脸色，甚至还忍不住往后退，但这山洞就这么大，里面全是士兵和侍从等人，哪里还有他们的退路？
“你们……你们没晕过去？”强盗厉声喝道，似乎他们试图从音量上来取得胜利。
嬴政面色微冷，“先将这人拿下。”嬴政当先指的便是之前那最先出言不逊的人。
那强盗登时急出了一头的汗，但就在他焦急的时候，士兵们已经开始动手了。
山洞之中，立时便响起了兵器碰撞的声音，还有捅穿身体撕裂衣帛的声音，其中还混杂着惨叫声……
跟前的那个强盗，已经被撂翻在地了。
徐福和嬴政站起身来，走到了强盗的跟前，近到强盗的脸就贴着嬴政的鞋面。
嬴政心底对此人的厌恶已然升到了极点，他可不会有半分手软，当即重重一踢，便直直踹在了那人的面颊上，这一脚力道十足，那强盗的脑袋当即被踹得偏转了过去，牙都被踹得松动了，嘴里呸出不少血来。也就一会儿的功夫，这人的面颊便紫胀起来了。
那强盗被激怒了，当即大骂起来。
嬴政从旁拔出刀来，让人按住他的手臂，眼眸微微低垂，嗓音冰冷地问道：“方才是这只手臂指的对吧？”
强盗脑门上的冷汗更多了。
这时候其他人也差不多结束战局了。
一群乌合之众如何抵得过大秦精锐？没花多少工夫，他们便被拿下了，而且个个都按在了地面上，一不老实就照脸踹，就是要将他们的自尊踩到脚底下去，就是要羞辱他们！
他们哀声叫了起来。
直到他们看见那个极为英俊，气势也极为强烈的男子，拎着一把刀站在了他们其中一个兄弟的面前。
男子手起刀落，他们听见那个兄弟发出了凄惨的叫声，那瞬间鲜血也跟着迸溅了出来……
山洞中影子晃动。
一群强盗的心也渐渐沉了下去，胆子小的甚至尿了裤子。
他们怎么会想到，这个男子竟然凶残至此？
徐福站在一旁，亲眼看着嬴政剁掉了那人的手臂。徐福知道嬴政此时胸中的怒火，其实他心头也不大高兴。因而哪怕此时嬴政满面戾气，他也并未上前阻止。
而此时嬴政说了一句让那些强盗更为胆寒的话，“这是第一个。”
什、什么意思？
他要把他们都剁了吗？
再凶残的强盗，此时也忍不住颤抖了起来。
接下来当然不用嬴政再亲力亲为了，他冷声道：“将那匪首带过来，都斩去前肢，再挖坑活埋之。”
前肢……这是都不拿他们当人看待了啊。
匪首指的自然是那大胡子了。
这是嬴政从这些人的对话中，以及那大胡子的言行中推出来的。
士兵点头，当即便去寻那大胡子了。
徐福心中稍微有些惊。毕竟他少有见到这种场面的时候，嬴政此举对于徐福来说，还是稍有些血腥了，但他还是什么都没说。嬴政之所以如此勃然大怒，不过是出自对他的维护。这些强盗也着实太蠢，若只是想要谋个财，死得也不至于这样惨……
对于士兵们来说，处置几个强盗是极为容易的事。在战场上杀人如同砍菜瓜的人，又怎么会将这么些人命看在眼中？
他们合力将哀嚎不断的强盗拖了出去。
他们哪里敢在徐福的跟前，就这样大咧咧地宰人胳膊呢？场面那般血腥，惊着了皇后可不好。
很快，山洞中便恢复了宁静，只是这时候的宁静难免让人觉得有些悚然。
那地上的血迹都还在呢。
此时一个士兵笑眯眯地跑进来，捡起了地上断掉的手臂，不好意思地笑笑，“忘拿了。”说罢，那士兵便一溜烟地跑出去了。
弄得徐福反倒颇为哭笑不得，方才的血腥气似乎都被这名士兵的举动给冲淡了。
内侍和侍从开始收拾山洞中的乱摊子，很快，毯子和被子都归位了，火堆也重新燃起来了。嬴政搂着徐福，低声问道：“可要擦洗一番？那些血腥气染到你身上了罢？”嬴政的神色分外温柔，与方才的模样全然是两个模样。
徐福心中似有所感。
嬴政这般表现，应当是不希望自己将他又当做前世的秦始皇。
毕竟他方才的样子，的确和前世的秦始皇形象有所重叠。
徐福装作不知晓嬴政的心思一般，抱住了嬴政的腰身，主动埋入了他的怀中，无比自然地道：“我困了。”
嬴政心中有点说不出的愉悦，他将徐福紧紧抱在怀中，应了一声，然后两人便又躺下去准备继续入睡了。徐福的鼻间还萦绕着那股淡淡的血腥气，但是身处嬴政的怀中，慢慢的，他倒是将那股味道给无视了。没多久，徐福便睡着了。
嬴政低头凝视着怀中徐福的面容，忍不住抬起手，轻轻抚弄过了徐福的脸颊。
他的眸光有些深沉，像是有什么话要说，却又像是什么都说不出。
洞中火光还在摇晃着，那些士兵们也相继入了睡，强盗们的惨叫声渐渐远去了……
清晨时分，徐福迷迷糊糊地睁开双眼，往外面看了一眼，竟是早早地便日出了，日光投射进山洞来，总算多了些暖意，看来今日那些雪能够化掉了。
徐福还盯着洞外的景色呢，谁知晓嬴政也早早就醒了，这时候便正好凑上前来，吻在了徐福的脖颈上。
“起身吗？”嬴政沉声问。
嬴政晨起时的嗓音极为迷人。
徐福眸光闪了闪，撑着他的肩膀，从他怀中挣扎了出来。
两人起了身，很快洗漱好。
内侍做好了食物送到二人的跟前，徐福简单用了食物，便走出了山洞。外面的空气倒是清新得很，只是徐福一低头，便不可避免地瞥见了地面上洒的血迹。
一大片一大片的，就像是在地上绽开了美丽的花。
只不过这花实在有些惊悚了些。
徐福正要挪开目光，突然间他又觉得，那地面上似乎有点不大对劲。徐福仔细一瞧，才发现地面竟然似乎微微往上鼓了起来，只是鼓一点便又塌下去了。
嬴政走出来，站在徐福身侧，顺着他的目光看了过去，见状便解释道：“他们并没有埋瓷实。”
所以土是松的，所以下面的人可以挣扎，可以将土撑起来。
也就是说明，现在那些强盗都还是活的……
徐福觉得有些恶心，便挪开了目光。
寒冷的气候里血不容易流干，看来正是因为这样，那些强盗才没因失血过多而亡。
……这惩罚可足够令他们强盗到死都铭心刻骨了。
此时一名士兵跑上前来，道：“陛下，这些强盗有个寨子，寨子中有他们抢回去的人……”
徐福有些诧异。
看来这些强盗作恶不少啊！
今夜怕是又得在此地停留了。
不过救人本是好事，徐福当然不会在意。
此时嬴政也下令让人去搜救了，随后他便带着徐福在这处地方转悠了起来，散散步，也当做瞧一瞧风景。
一部分士兵被派了出去救人，一部分当然仍旧留下来守着他们。
没多久，又一名侍从来到了跟前，说咸阳传来了消息。
作者有话要说：　　历史记载：
三十一年十二月，始皇为微行咸阳，与武士四人俱，夜出逢盗兰池，见窘，武士击杀盗，关中大索二十日。
大意就是微服出行碰上强盗了。
这里被我改了改，变成了二十六年，东巡路上遇强盗。

chapters.title: 第269章
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu originally thought it was some news about the court affairs, but who knew that the person delivering the message was staring straight at Xu Fu. If he hadn't been certain that this person lacked the sheer audacity, Ying Zheng would have flown into a rage on the spot.

"What is it?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.

The messenger knelt on the ground and respectfully handed over a piece of silk cloth.

Due to Ying Zheng's extremely strong desire for control, most matters in Xianyang were delivered to his hands by fast horses every couple of days. Therefore, it wasn't particularly strange that this man made a special trip just to hand-deliver a message to Xu Fu.

Xu Fu unrolled the silk cloth in puzzlement and discovered that it was a message from Wang Liu. Normally, he had very little contact with Wang Liu, and Wang Liu certainly wouldn't bother someone to deliver a message from thousands of miles away like this.

Could it be that he had divined something unusual in the Fengchang Temple?

Xu Fu calmed his mind and read it carefully. He found that between the lines, Wang Liu seemed somewhat panicked. He stated that half a month ago, a group of fangshi (alchemists/mages) had come to Xianyang, presenting themselves to the Fengchang Temple, and a few days ago they had offered a book of charts and records, claiming it was sought from overseas. After the Fengchang Temple accepted it, who would have thought that upon opening and inspecting it, they were frightened to the extreme. Wang Liu dared not easily judge its authenticity and even suspected for a moment that his own eyes were playing tricks on him. How could he dare to conceal such a major event? After careful deliberation, he reported the matter to the Commandant of the Guards (Guowei), who secretly detained those fangshi. On the other hand, Wang Liu wrote this silk cloth and ordered someone to deliver it by fast horse.

The content in that book of charts and records that made Wang Liu's expression change drastically could be summarized in just a few words.

Just at this moment, Ying Zheng also leaned closer and thus caught that line of text in his eyes.

After reading it, the complexions of Xu Fu and Ying Zheng turned cold in unison.

——"Those who destroy Qin are the Hu."

Xu Fu immediately thought of Huhai.

In history, it seemed... vaguely... that there was such a record. Some fangshi presented a book of charts and records, which had this sentence recorded on it. Only at that time, Qin Shi Huang didn't associate it with Huhai, so he let it pass. At this moment, Ying Zheng probably still hadn't associated it with Huhai. After all, until his death in his past life, he might not have known that Huhai, Zhao Gao, and others were the ones pulling strings behind the scenes.

A knot of indescribable discomfort tightened in the bottom of Xu Fu's heart.

He was already improving the original historical trajectory, so why did this thing still appear? Could it be that Qin was still destined to perish in the hands of Huhai? The image of Huhai flashed through Xu Fu's mind, and he immediately dismissed the thought. No, Huhai had already changed.

At this time, Ying Zheng's face had already darkened, and he said coldly, "Who dares to destroy my Great Qin?" In his past life, he could beat those Hu people until they cried for their fathers and mothers, and this lifetime would naturally be the same.

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment, but still chose to remain silent.

He couldn't gamble on how much familial affection Ying Zheng still held for Huhai in his heart. If he spoke of it now, given Ying Zheng's temper, it didn't seem entirely impossible that he would directly execute Huhai. Xu Fu simply suppressed the matter. He had already tried his utmost to steer history onto another track; if it still didn't work, he had done his best and would have no regrets. No matter in which generation Qin perished, Ying Zheng would always remain that Emperor Through the Ages.

Ying Zheng ordered someone to fetch a piece of silk cloth and a charcoal pencil, and then ordered the person kneeling in front of him to use his back as a desk. Ying Zheng then raised his pen and hastily jotted down a few strokes on it, saying, "Hand this over to Crown Prince Fusu."

The man nodded carefully, straightened up, tucked the silk cloth into his bosom, pressing it against his chest, and then bowed to Xu Fu and Ying Zheng before hurriedly leaving. The essence of transmitting information lies in the word "timely," so the man naturally dared not delay even a bit.

The horse hurried over and hurried away again, but everyone looked upon this as nothing out of the ordinary.

Soon, a soldier came to report that the bandits' stronghold had been found.

Ying Zheng's expression was somewhat cold. He had originally thought it was just a simple group of bandits, but he didn't expect them to actually have a stronghold of their own, entrenching themselves as a domain. What did they want to do? Could it be that they wanted to stir up some rebellions at the beginning of the establishment of the Qin Dynasty? Of course Ying Zheng wouldn't fear a mere group of bandits, but the other party's bold actions still made Ying Zheng feel that his majesty had been violated. This was something no emperor could tolerate.

It truly fit the saying: you cannot pluck the tiger's whiskers.

Disliking that the road was difficult to walk and fearing it would be bad if Xu Fu got tired, the two simply waited in a cave, waiting only for the soldiers to rescue the people and destroy the stronghold in one fell swoop. For these battle-hardened elites, destroying a stronghold was truly too easy a task.

It took a day's effort, but the stronghold was destroyed, and a group of women and children were led out of the forest by the soldiers.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng stood at the entrance of the cave and gazed into the distance, but did not step forward to look. Saving the people was good enough; naturally, there was no need for them to crowd around. Perhaps because they had saved quite a few people over the years, Xu Fu felt quite peaceful in his mind watching this scene.

Just as Xu Fu was slightly lost in thought, a pair of hands suddenly reached out from behind, trapping Xu Fu in an embrace. Ying Zheng rubbed against his shoulder and said in a low voice, "There is still some chill outside, let's go inside."

Xu Fu nodded and followed Ying Zheng inside to continue living their decadent and lazy life.

However, Xu Fu always felt that Ying Zheng's mood seemed a bit off again somewhere, but upon careful distinction, he couldn't tell where this mood came from. Ying Zheng was, after all, the Emperor Through the Ages, and even Xu Fu found his thoughts difficult to fathom. Much like before, Ying Zheng had recovered his memories of his past life ahead of him, while he had still been kept in the dark, knowing nothing at all.

Xu Fu's trust in Ying Zheng nowadays could no longer be compared to the past. Even if he sensed something unusual about Ying Zheng at this moment, Xu Fu wouldn't feel angry or annoyed because of it. He waited with great patience for the day when Ying Zheng would speak to him about it, just as Ying Zheng had waited with patience for him to reveal his origins.

Leaning in Ying Zheng's embrace, Xu Fu couldn't help but turn his body slightly, then took the initiative to reach out and wrap his arms around Ying Zheng's waist. A smile appeared on Ying Zheng's face. He reached out to hug Xu Fu tighter and said in a low voice, "Our trip this time will pass by the seaside..."

Ying Zheng's voice was low and charming. He spoke softly to Xu Fu about the interesting things along the coast, showing that after realizing Xu Fu had a considerable interest in local customs and anecdotal trivia, he had spent a fair amount of effort on this to please Xu Fu.

The two of them gradually indulged in this quiet atmosphere.

It wasn't until a soldier returned to report on the follow-up disposition of those women and children that the atmosphere between the two was broken.

The soldier unconsciously shrank his neck, feeling as if some danger was lingering behind his neck, but upon careful sensation, it was gone. He secretly thought to himself: How could there possibly be any danger in front of His Majesty the First Emperor? It must be an illusion! The soldier raised a smiling face and rattled off the matters like bamboo tubes spilling beans.

Xu Fu realized that this soldier was the very one who had forgotten to take his arm yesterday. Looking at this face now, no matter how he looked at it, he found it unspeakably funny.

"I know. Go down and rest." Ying Zheng waved his hand, extremely unwelcoming of anyone coming to disturb him and Xu Fu.

Just as Xu Fu and Ying Zheng snuggled together in the cave, turning even hardship into sweetness.

On the other end, the letter was still flying rapidly toward Xianyang.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng's group rested in the cave for another day, and it was such a coincidence that when they set off again, the snow in front had all melted cleanly, and the weather was gradually starting to warm up. Along the way, Xu Fu witnessed the beauty and wonder of spring returning to the earth; seeing it with one's own eyes and reading about it in textbooks were completely two different experiences. At this moment, Xu Fu once again felt one of the great joys of being an empress. Traveling outside like this probably only the First Emperor possessed such grand strokes and such sufficient confidence.

One must know that many emperors of later generations wouldn't even step out of the imperial city. The reasons were simple: first, it wasn't safe outside the imperial city; second, the dragon chair under their bottoms wasn't safe outside the imperial city.

Meanwhile, as the years piled up, Ying Zheng's personality grew increasingly domineering and confident. He could fully grasp all affairs in his hands, so he had not the slightest worry. After pacifying the six states, whenever Xu Fu wanted to go out, he dared to cast aside state affairs at any time to accompany Xu Fu out, even if a tour lasted a year or two, it didn't matter at all.

Ying Zheng had complete mastery over the imperial court.

He truly made being an emperor feel as natural as eating and drinking. He might look exhausted, but he would never sacrifice everything for the sake of court affairs.

To be able to pick up and put down—that is truly a presence to be admired!

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more he realized that he seemed to be endlessly praising Ying Zheng in his heart. He blinked, tugged at Ying Zheng's robe, and then retreated further into his embrace. Heh, this way I won't have to be seen with my ears turning red and my eyes flashing.

But given Ying Zheng's understanding of Xu Fu, how could he possibly miss such a scene?

A certain place in the depths of his heart grew even softer, and he couldn't help but knead Xu Fu closer into his arms.

Ah Fu being like this, how could I ever bear to let go? I couldn't bear to in the past life, and it's the same in this lifetime...

Ying Zheng concealed the ripples in his eyes and continued to speak softly to Xu Fu about things along the seaside.

Along this journey, the two didn't experience any more winds and waves. After taking three months, they arrived at the coast. Upon entering the city, Xu Fu even felt a faint salty and fishy scent rushing at him in the wind. That should be the smell of the ocean.

"Do you feel any discomfort?" Ying Zheng asked in a low voice.

Xu Fu shook his head. Although he wasn't very interested in seafood, having taken ships and cruise liners in his past life, he didn't feel anything amiss.

Hearing this, Ying Zheng instead showed a rather regretful expression.

Xu Fu was somewhat puzzled. What did he mean by this? Could it be that he regretted missing a chance to take care of himself?

After thinking about it, once he got off the carriage, Xu Fu took the initiative to lean against Ying Zheng. At first glance, anyone who didn't know better would think he was suffering from acclimatization and thus appeared a bit frail.

Seeing such a huge change in him all of a sudden, Ying Zheng was genuinely startled and had to ask, "Is somewhere on your body feeling unwell?" At this moment, the look in Ying Zheng's eyes was entirely filled with care and nervous tension.

"I'm fine." Seeing him like this, Xu Fu was even more puzzled. Since Ying Zheng didn't want to see him looking sickly, why did a look of regret flash by when he saw him shake his head? Xu Fu didn't hide his musings and asked straight to the point, "What was A-Zheng regretting just now?"

Ying Zheng lowered his gaze and said in a deep voice, "You probably don't remember." He leaned close to Xu Fu's ear and said, "In your past life, you stubbornly insisted on going out to sea to search for immortal mountains and the elixir of life. If you couldn't adapt to this ocean, then naturally, I wouldn't have to worry about when you'd start thinking about going out to sea again."

There was no expression on Ying Zheng's face, but at this moment, having no expression surpassed all expressions; a plain tone surpassed everything.

Xu Fu suddenly found himself somewhat speechless.

Bringing up old scores really wasn't a good habit. Once old scores were brought up, whenever Ying Zheng thought of what Xu Fu had once done to him, he wished nothing of it had ever happened. And once Xu Fu remembered that it was he who had tricked Qin Shi Huang into seeking immortality, tricked him into taking the elixir, and even tricked him into saying he wanted to go to sea to find immortal mountains for him... piece by piece, item by item, Xu Fu still felt a tiny bit guilty.

After all, who could imagine that a lover who was once killed by one's own hands could remain calm and collected without a single ripple?

Sensing the thoughts in Xu Fu's heart, Ying Zheng couldn't help but raise his hand to gently stroke Xu Fu's hair, saying, "All those matters of the past life have passed. As long as A-Fing doesn't leave me in this lifetime, that will be enough. Otherwise, I truly wouldn't know what to do back then."

Xu Fu pressed his lips together and said feignedly and casually, "If that's the case, then A-Zheng shouldn't have brought me to the seaside." Although he wouldn't decide to take a boat out to sea just after taking one look at the ocean, given Ying Zheng's domineering temperament, shouldn't he have directly prevented him from coming to the seaside? With the memories of his past life, wouldn't Ying Zheng feel panicked and distressed upon seeing the ocean?

Hearing this, Ying Zheng instead raised his hand to familiarly flick the bridge of Xu Fu's nose, and said, "Didn't you take a boat away from the Yue tribe before, wanting to try what it feels like to ride a boat on the sea? Since you were bound to come anyway, it's better that I brought you here, which is much better than you coming alone in the future." This was clearly the first time Ying Zheng had made such a childish gesture toward Xu Fu, yet he did it very skillfully, and Xu Fu also instantly forgot to dodge such a childish action.

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment.

That's right, Ying Zheng was domineering, but beneath that dominance was his consideration for Xu Fu in all things; even principles as unyielding as iron seemed to make way for it because of this.

An irrepressible sweetness rose in the depths of Xu Fu's heart.

Ying Zheng stared intently at Xu Fu's face, his eyes seeming to hide many things, filled entirely with obsession toward Xu Fu.

Obsessed for two lifetimes, of course I won't repeat the mistakes of the past, Ying Zheng thought to himself.

Then he picked Xu Fu up from the carriage.

Their entourage, naturally, once again checked into a local luxury mansion. The local officials of various ranks wished they could kneel and beg them to stay in their own homes.

Resting in the residence for a day, Ying Zheng did not delay and immediately took Xu Fu to the seaside.

There were many fishing villages by the sea, and aside from the fishing villages and beaches, there wasn't much else.

The closer they walked, the more they could smell that fishy ocean scent.

Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng's expression and couldn't read anything from it, but after thinking about it, he still reached out and took Ying Zheng's hand. Would doing this slightly transmit a sense of security to Ying Zheng?

The peaceful little fishing village was thrown into a boil by their arrival. When had a small fishing village ever had the opportunity to see people like them? Hearing people at the entrance of the village say that a group of people with magnificent clothing and looks resembling immortals had arrived, many people in the fishing village immediately came out with the mentality of watching the spectacle.

Some people originally wanted to crowd closer to take a look, but upon seeing that their bearings were extraordinary and their looks were too handsome to belong to mortal beings, not a single person dared to step forward anymore.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had long been accustomed to such scrutiny from others, so they walked straight ahead.

The people in the fishing village widened their eyes as they watched them walk in the direction of the seawater.

For most fishing villages, they each carved out their own territories, meaning they wouldn't allow outsiders to encroach upon their land. Without a doubt, Xu Fu's group were outsiders in their eyes. However, the usually fierce fishing village didn't dare to lock horns with them at this moment; not only that, they even stepped back a bit.

Xu Fu didn't pay any attention to this corner at all.

Several soldiers carried a boat into the water. The boat had been improved, incorporating the craftsmanship of the Yue tribe and the improvements and reinforcements of the Qin. Now this small boat was very stable. If they hadn't been unable to build large ships in such a short time, the boat they rode on today would have been an even more majestic and domineering large vessel.

The boat was set properly in the water, and Xu Fu didn't hesitate or show any fear. He leaned on Ying Zheng's arm and stepped onto the small boat, followed closely by Ying Zheng, along with two attendants who were extremely skilled in water.

The small boat bobbed and drifted out onto the sea surface.

Exclamations rang out from this corner of the small fishing village. Their accents were rather heavy, and when they muttered and spoke, their speed was extremely fast, making it impossible for the soldiers guarding the coastline to understand what they were saying.

...

The small boat gradually drifted further away, and the attendants paddled beside it without exerting too much effort.

The bobbing and drifting sensation of the boat was extremely comfortable. Xu Fu leaned in the boat and unconsciously closed his eyes.

Ying Zheng leaned close to his ear and said in a low voice, "After I died in my past life, did you heartlessly take a boat and sail far away?"

Xu Fu moved his lips. "...Mn." That couldn't be blamed on him either. It was really because Ying Zheng at that time was too crude and aggressive, and the two of them hadn't journeyed together through thick and thin. Relying solely on a first impression of each other's appearance, followed by forced favors, it would have been strange if Xu Fu had just turned the other cheek and submitted!

Ying Zheng sighed softly, "I know you wanted to go out to sea; there's probably not much difference between the past life and this one."

Xu Fu nodded hesitatingly and said, "A-Zheng has taken me across the beautiful rivers and mountains of Great Qin, so naturally, I will want to go to even more distant places in the future. Does A-Zheng know what lies on the other side of the ocean?"

Ying Zheng shook his head. He knew that in this respect, his knowledge was inferior to Xu Fu's, so he simply watched Xu Fu and listened quietly as he continued. He wanted to hear what on earth was on the other side of the ocean that could make Xu Fu unable to forget it.

"Over there, there are islands and other nations, each with their own kings... There are also many ownerless lands, lands containing treasures that have never been mined by anyone. Whoever occupies those lands first can become their master..." Xu Fu blinked his eyes, "Doesn't A-Zheng want them?"

Unexpectedly, Ying Zheng didn't find it very interesting. He said in a low voice, "Barbaric lands, how can they be incorporated into Great Qin? How can those subjects be considered Qin people in the future?"

Was this disdain?

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, and then couldn't help but want to laugh.

"What if those people covet the wealth of Great Qin in the future and want to make a move against Great Qin?"

Ying Zheng remained confident and proud, his tone carrying a trace of self-satisfaction as he said, "Just look at what happened to the Xiongnu? And take a look at how the Meng brothers beat those Hu people into scattering and unable to form an army this time." The implication was that even if those people coveted the wealth of Great Qin, so what? They still wouldn't be able to do anything to Great Qin, and instead might end up being beaten until they wet their pants, ultimately gaining no benefits at all.

Xu Fu roughly envisioned the scenario Ying Zheng described. Actually, thinking about it, it was quite thrilling.

Only Qin Shi Huang could speak with such confidence.

"But they live on islands and deal with water all year round, so their naval warfare is extremely formidable. What should we do then?" Xu Fu couldn't help asking.

Ying Zheng frowned slightly, pondered for a moment, and said, "What is there to fear about this? If there are deficiencies, we will set about changing those deficiencies!" When Ying Zheng said this, he was remarkably calm. In his current view, perhaps there was nothing left that could make him frown and worry. This wasn't arrogance on Ying Zheng's part, but rather the sediment left after experiencing many things.

Xu Fu stroked his chest, his brow furrowing slightly.

This wasn't good.

He actually found Ying Zheng extremely charming at this moment, and every word he spoke was charming.

Xu Fu: "..." Perhaps his senses had malfunctioned.

The small boat gradually drifted further.

The people in the fishing village muttered and chattered even more fiercely, causing the Qin soldiers to look over at them frequently. Alas, still unable to understand what they were saying, the Qin soldiers could only frown and turn back around themselves.

On this end, Xu Fu was still whispering with Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu kept his attention on Ying Zheng's facial expression all along. He could see that Ying Zheng's expression had gradually softened from its initial coldness and vigilance. In his past life, this place should have been an extremely hateful place for him, to the extent that calling it a psychological shadow wouldn't be an exaggeration. But now, as the two of them drifted together on the sea, the slight manic restlessness in the depths of Ying Zheng's heart was gradually dissolved.

This very moment reminded him that the future was different. They had changed; they could possess a better life instead of being unable to shake off the word "intense" from their first encounter to their death, like in the previous life.

Ying Zheng held Xu Fu with satisfaction. In his heart, he vaguely felt that this trip hadn't been in vain after all.

At this instant, Ying Zheng's heart seemed to be overwhelmed by a fervent love, and he couldn't help blurting out, "If, in the future, when you and I are older, I will accompany you out to sea together. Whatever immortal mountains or elixirs you want to seek, I will walk side by side with you."

As soon as these words came out, an unusual wave of emotion rose in Xu Fu's heart, but at the same time, he felt a bit guilty.

What immortal mountains and elixirs...

They were all nothing more than excuses he had desperately used in his past life to escape from Ying Zheng's side. Ying Zheng probably knew, but he wouldn't bring it up again.

Right at that moment, as if something icy had fallen onto his cheek, Xu Fu opened his eyes and realized that fine threads of rain were falling from the sky, and the wind and clouds in the sky seemed to be shifting. Xu Fu frowned slightly; this was truly something he had failed to calculate—well, of course, it was indeed hard for him to calculate, since the weather on the sea was the most unpredictable of all.

Xu Fu sat right up from Ying Zheng's embrace and said in a low voice, "Return!"

The attendant acknowledged the order and immediately began preparing to turn back.

Although they hadn't traveled very far, for Xu Fu, satisfying his craving a bit was already good enough, and this trip had been worth it. Neither he nor Ying Zheng grew angry because of this sudden weather change; on the contrary, their faces carried extremely peaceful expressions.

Seeing this scene, the attendants felt it was truly a bit incomprehensible: How could His Majesty still have the corners of his mouth upturned with a smile?

Suppressing their thoughts, the attendants rowed back with all their might.

Just at that moment, a sudden crack of thunder split the sky, and the weather darkened at a breathtaking speed. A bolt of lightning almost split the sky in two. Such a sight was extremely terrifying, and even the Qin soldiers on the shore grew slightly anxious.

Nothing must happen to their Majesty and Empress!

The Qin soldiers even wanted to go into the water, but after all, not many knew how to swim, so they exercised restraint and didn't act rashly.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng on the other end were actually quite calm and collected.

Ying Zheng grasped Xu Fu's wrist without saying a word, but just this simple action alone was enough.

Suddenly, changes also occurred on the sea surface, and waves began to swell...

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were caught unprepared as a wave crashed over. The small boat was sturdy enough, but Xu Fu was knocked over into the water by the wave, and naturally, Ying Zheng went down with him. The two attendants gripping the oars were dazed for a moment, hesitating whether or not they should let go of the oars.

They shouted loudly, "Your Majesty! Empress!"

Subsequently, one of them went down while the other continued to steady the small boat. He couldn't let the boat capsize; although they hadn't traveled far, they couldn't just swim back through the seawater either. Not to mention physical exhaustion, the cold seawater alone could freeze a person to death.

Xu Fu was a bit dazed by suddenly falling into the water.

Instantly, the memories of his past life flooded back: he struggled powerlessly in the river water, slowly suffocating, slowly losing consciousness...

After entering the water, Ying Zheng didn't let go of Xu Fu's wrist either. Watching Xu Fu struggle a few times in the water before suddenly stopping all movement,

in that instant, Ying Zheng's heart felt as if someone had abruptly and forcefully squeezed it.

A shadow suddenly loomed over Ying Zheng's head.

It was truly difficult to exert force underwater, but Ying Zheng still mustered his strength, desperately pulling Xu Fu toward himself and letting Xu Fu lean against his embrace. "A-Fu, A-Fu..."

After shouting twice, Ying Zheng inevitably swallowed a mouthful of seawater and had to try his best to hoist Xu Fu upward again.

It was precisely these two shouts from Ying Zheng that abruptly pulled Xu Fu out of the memories of his past life.

The desire to survive rapidly occupied Xu Fu's brain, and Xu Fu tried his utmost to cooperate with Ying Zheng in swimming upward.

Yet the moment Ying Zheng pulled him over, he locked him tightly within his embrace. "A-Fu..."

His voice was slightly hoarse, and upon close listening, a hint of trembling could be detected.

A sharp pang gripped Xu Fu's heart, and he involuntarily recalled the time in his past life when he coldly left Great Qin by boat...

At this moment, even the pet name, usually uttered so harshly, was endowed with a different flavor.

Hearing Ying Zheng call him "A-Fu," Xu Fu couldn't help but feel his heartstrings tremble slightly.

Ying Zheng held him tightly as the two rose and sank in the seawater.

The attendant found them and was about to step forward to help, intending to hoist their Empress up first. But who would have thought that the moment he made a move, the Emperor's hand suddenly shot out, clamped onto his wrist, and forcefully shoved him aside. As if that wasn't enough, at that instant their eyes met; the Emperor's gaze was dark, cold, and fierce, as if about to devour someone alive. The attendant couldn't help shivering. He had no doubt his wrist was already bruised—the Emperor's grip strength was simply too formidable!

This possessiveness was simply too strong!

The attendant was torn between tears and laughter; he could only withdraw his hand and swim alongside Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, acting as their guard for any unexpected contingencies.

Ying Zheng forcefully pushed Xu Fu up onto the small boat, and only then grabbed the gunwale and hoisted himself up after him.

The other attendant on the small boat finally breathed a sigh of relief at this.

As long as His Majesty and the Empress were safe and sound, that was all that mattered.

Meanwhile, Ying Zheng's state wasn't actually very good. Even after boarding the small boat, he still kept Xu Fu tightly imprisoned in his arms, his gaze still carrying an indescribably devouring quality.

Ying Zheng kissed the outer rim of Xu Fu's ear.

Actually, at this moment, he wanted to bite down.

But Xu Fu coughed twice, coughing up a couple of mouthfuls of seawater.

After he finished coughing, Xu Fu said, "A-Zheng, my hand..."
