In the span of just over a year, climbing countless mountains with Ying Zheng had still been somewhat useful. At least, after being fished out of the sea, Xu Fu did not catch a cold; it was just that the sudden shock was a bit too much, causing Xu Fu to choke on a couple of gulps of water, and afterwards he felt a bit exhausted, with nothing else amiss. After drinking some cold-prevention medicine and wrapping himself in a quilt for a good sleep, he was completely fine.

It wasn't until this day that Xu Fu finally learned that what the fishermen had been shouting on the shore was actually something like, "The weather is about to change drastically, how can they be so bold as to head out?"

It was just that back then, no one could understand the fishermen's dialect, and the fishermen didn't dare to get close. As a result, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng ran into bad luck not long after setting out to sea.

When it came to maritime meteorology, Xu Fu really didn't understand as much as the local fishermen.

After the incident, Ying Zheng no longer took Xu Fu to that stretch of sea. Although nothing major happened this time, it was ultimately not safe enough.

"I will send troops here to train a navy and build large ships. When the sea is completely safe, I will accompany you out to sea then," Ying Zheng said to Xu Fu.

Hearing this, Xu Fu was a bit surprised.

He had thought that after this event, Ying Zheng would develop a sense of awe toward the sea and no longer be willing to take him out on it. However, upon a little careful thought, Xu Fu could guess Ying Zheng's mentality.

It was all for his sake, after all.

"Let's talk about that later then." Whatever Xu Fu wished to pursue, it could not compare to this little life of his. Well... nor could it compare to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu to sit by the table, having the servants bring food and water.

Fiddling with the food on the table, Ying Zheng said casually, "What was that phrase you said the other day?"

"What?" Xu Fu was startled.

"That day you said, 'Me too.' Me too what?" Ying Zheng picked up a bowl and handed it to Xu Fu's lips; it was filled with water.

Xu Fu took a small sip, and only then did he sluggishly recall what "me too" from Ying Zheng's mouth was actually about. A faint flush swept across Xu Fu's cheeks. "Ah..." If the atmosphere hadn't been just right that day, he absolutely would not have said such words.

Ying Zheng pressed his lips together. "Unwilling to say it again?"

"What is there to say?" Xu Fu took another sip of water, refusing to meet Ying Zheng's gaze at all.

A look of regret flashed across Ying Zheng's face, and his hand gripping the chopsticks seemed to grow much weaker.

Although Xu Fu knew clearly that given Ying Zheng's temperament, he would never have such a dejected mood, his heart was nonetheless thrown into turmoil by it.

Xu Fu gripped his chopsticks, took another sip of water, and let out a muffled sentence from his throat, "I... I can't lose you either."

Ying Zheng sharpened his focus; he had been waiting right there for Xu Fu to speak these words. Originally, he hadn't held much hope, given that Ying Zheng knew Xu Fu's temperament very well—he knew Xu Fu was too aloof to ever say such things. But precisely because he hadn't held much hope, the pleasant surprise received at this moment was all the greater.

Ying Zheng felt that he hadn't heard quite clearly, so he couldn't help reaching out to pull Xu Fu into his embrace. "A-Fu, say it once more; I didn't hear clearly just now."

Suppressing the urge to give him a cold glare, Xu Fu picked up a piece of food with his chopsticks and shoved it directly into Ying Zheng's mouth, saying coldly, "Eat." After finishing their meal, it would be time for them to leave this place. Unable to go out to sea, this place had lost its appeal to Xu Fu, let alone the fact that they had already walked through every corner of the city, leaving no need to stay.

This place simply couldn't compare to Mount Langya. On Mount Langya, at least Xu Fu could smell the fresh fragrance, whereas here he smelled the fishy stench of the ocean. If they stayed any longer, Xu Fu felt he wouldn't be able to bear it.

Ying Zheng unconsciously licked his lips. "Mmm."

Actually, getting that one sentence from Xu Fu was enough. Only at this moment could Ying Zheng be completely certain that they had embarked on a path entirely different from his past life.

Suppressing his emotions, Ying Zheng accompanied Xu Fu through their meal. Afterwards, a eunuch entered the room and reported, "Your Majesty, Empress, everything has been packed."

Half-embracing Xu Fu, the two of them walked out side by side. "Return to Xianyang."

By now they had toured quite a few places, so they would set off directly for Xianyang from here.

Xu Fu did not voice any objection to cut him off; he had stayed outside long enough, and it was indeed time for them to head straight back.

When the carriage pulled up, Ying Zheng picked Xu Fu up and carried him inside directly.

Once inside the carriage, Ying Zheng laid Xu Fu down in his arms, then reached out to roll back Xu Fu's sleeves. After rolling them up, Ying Zheng couldn't help reaching out to stroke Xu Fu's wrists, a dark, gloomy light flashing deep within his eyes.

Moving his wrists with a trace of discomfort, Xu Fu said flatly, "It's already fine."

Without a word, Ying Zheng took out the medicine box and continued applying ointment to Xu Fu.

Xu Fu stared at the medicine box for a moment.

Who knows what he was thinking when he made the medicine back then, actually using the exact same containers for the body lotion and the medicinal ointment. Now Ying Zheng had to take out the medicine box every day to apply the ointment, but every time he saw it, Xu Fu's thoughts would involuntarily drift in a certain direction.

Paying no attention to where Xu Fu's gaze had fallen, Ying Zheng meticulously finished applying the medicine. Then, as the ointment on his fingers melted away, his fingers inevitably became a bit greasy. He picked up a silk cloth to wipe his fingers, his movements somewhat slow.

This scene invisibly grew somewhat ambiguous.

Turning his face away, Xu Fu picked up a bamboo slip to distract himself.

As he wiped, Ying Zheng suddenly thought of something. He tossed the silk cloth aside, raised a hand to pull Xu Fu even closer into his embrace, casually slipped his hand inside Xu Fu's robes, and murmured near his ear, "Is there another place that needs me to apply medicine?"

"..." It turned out he wasn't the only one whose mind was wandering.

"There's no water," Xu Fu was forced to remind him of this cruel reality.

Ying Zheng sighed softly. "As expected, we still need to return to Xianyang early."

The corners of Xu Fu's lips twitched upward involuntarily. Then he shifted his position, sliding down slightly so that the back of his neck rested right on Ying Zheng's lap, and continued reading his bamboo slip. With a helpless sigh, Ying Zheng put away the medicine box and went back to wiping his fingers.

Meanwhile, on another front, General Meng Tian led an army of 300,000 north to attack the Hu people, and a fierce battle unfolded. It was precisely in this war that Meng Tian's reputation grew increasingly prominent, gradually replacing the veteran general Wang Jian of the past.

In the twenty-sixth year of Qin Shi Huang, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng returned to Xianyang.

Taking two months, Meng Tian beat the Hu people to a pulp and captured the land south of the Yellow River. Soon, Meng Tian made a triumphant return. By this time, the fame of the Meng brothers throughout the Qin Dynasty had become exceedingly illustrious.

To celebrate the conquest of the Hu people, Ying Zheng held a banquet in the palace, inviting all civil and military officials to attend.

Some officials were delighted to attend such a grand feast; they finally had the opportunity to use the occasion to say things the Emperor loved to hear, thereby showing off.

Palace Assistant Zhou Qing took the lead in praising Ying Zheng's achievements. With exceptionally fluent eloquence, he praised Ying Zheng as unprecedented in the past and unmatched in the future, surpassing even the Emperor through the Ages. Hearing this, the others thought: since Zhou Qing has shamelessly exhausted all the words of flattery, what else is left for us to suck up with? Their complexions turned terribly ashen, one and all.

Sitting beside Ying Zheng, Xu Fu found it rather amusing. It seemed that under the rule of any monarch, there was never a shortage of officials who seized the opportunity to flatter their way up. These flattering words, when spoken, were indeed pleasing to the heart. Therefore, Xu Fu only smiled inwardly and didn't really think Palace Assistant Zhou Qing's character was all that base.

Yet right at this banquet, someone just had to step up and ruin the mood.

Imperial Academician Chunyu Yue raised his cup to toast Ying Zheng, but instead began lecturing him on the matters of Confucian scholars and feudal lords.

Chunyu Yue still maintained that Ying Zheng should establish feudal states and respect Confucian scholars.

"The Yin and Zhou dynasties ruled the realm for over a millennium because they enfeoffed their sons and meritorious ministers to assist themselves. Now Your Majesty's sons are mere commoners. If ministers who plot to murder rulers like Tian Chang of Qi or the Six Ministers of Jin were to appear, who would come to the rescue without the assistance of feudal lords?" Chunyu Yue argued with seemingly impeccable logic.

But at this moment, Xu Fu found it even more comical.

This Chunyu Yue was much funnier than Zhou Qing.

Why didn't he take a look at how Qin itself used to be a feudal state? Now Qin had established the Qin Dynasty and unified the realm, and the King of Zhou had perished beyond all perishing—which showed what use feudal states were for! If ministers truly rebelled, the feudal states would likely be the very first to surround them, join in to overthrow the suzerain state, and then declare themselves kings.

Such a simple truth, yet Chunyu Yue simply refused to understand it.

A monarch certainly needed assistance, but he must never rely on the power of ministers or feudal states, because ministers and feudal states would always change. Only by making oneself strong, firmly grasping power in one's own hands, and suppressing everyone with an imposing posture could a monarch ensure that ministers and feudal states dared not harbor secondary motives. And even if they did harbor secondary motives, so what? The monarch was that sharp blade, and with a wave of his hand, he could execute the disloyal.

Xu Fu turned his head to look at Ying Zheng. Sure enough, Ying Zheng's expression had already darkened.

Yet Chunyu Yue remained oblivious.

Ying Zheng said coldly, "I have stated before not to bring this matter up again. Great Qin will never have feudal states! Why does Academician Chunyu deliberately bring this up again? Do you harbor doubts about my decision?"

Chunyu Yue's lips moved. Xu Fu guessed he probably wanted to say "I do have doubts," but upon receiving Ying Zheng's icy glare, Chunyu Yue unconsciously swallowed the words back down.

Xu Fu hadn't expected Chunyu Yue to lose his nerve so quickly, and couldn't help the corners of his mouth twitching.

At this point, Li Si stepped forward with a cold expression. "The systems of the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties each differed inherently, and the system established by our Great Qin naturally differs from those of the ancients as well. But His Majesty is brilliant and martial; with a new system, he can likewise govern the country well and establish achievements that will endure for all eternity. Why must one obsess over the establishment of feudal states? Besides, those decadent Confucian scholars cannot understand His Majesty. Instead of relieving His Majesty's worries, they only add trouble for our Great Qin. Confucian doctrines have spread across the world, influencing the common people through these ideas. If we speak of threats, I fear it is not future ministers who might rebel, but these very Confucian scholars."

As Xu Fu listened to Li Si continue, the more Li Si spoke, the more alarmed Xu Fu became.

Was Li Si about to propose... burning books and burying scholars?

"In the past, when feudal lords contended with one another, the various states widely recruited wandering lobbyists. But now the realm is pacified, and laws and decrees emanate from His Majesty alone. The common people should devote themselves to agricultural and industrial production, while scholars should study laws and prohibitions. Yet today's scholars do not study contemporary matters, but instead insist on imitating antiquity to slander the present age and bewitch the minds of the people. How many scholars employ empty rhetoric to throw names and realities into confusion? They praise what they learn privately in secret while turning around to criticize the systems established by the court. Now that His Majesty has unified the realm, how can he permit such people to use private schools to wildly criticize the laws and blacken the reputation of the court?"

To be fair, Li Si's words were quite reasonable.

Since ancient times, Confucian scholars had possessed an exceptionally powerful ability to agitate public opinion. If their mouths could be sealed, it would indeed reduce the possibility of a great deal of trouble. That was precisely why certain emperors pursued policies of keeping the people ignorant.

"Entering court, these scholars criticize in their hearts; leaving court, they gossip in the alleys. They deliberately boast before the sovereign to seek fame and profit, intentionally uttering eye-catching remarks to elevate themselves, and then take the lead in fabricating slander among the common people. If such vicious conduct is not prohibited, your majesty's majesty will decline, and the power of their cliques will form. Over the long run, this will surely brew disaster!" Li Si bowed deeply. "Therefore, Li Si believes that Confucianism should be prohibited so that they no longer have any possibility of creating chaos!"

Ying Zheng had heard these exact words in his past life as well.

In fact, in this lifetime, Ying Zheng completely agreed with Li Si's words. He still wanted to bury those scholars alive and burn those Confucian books that were poisoning the minds of the people.

Noticing with acute sensitivity that Ying Zheng's expression was growing increasingly cold, Xu Fu couldn't help reaching out to gently clasp Ying Zheng's hand as a signal for him to think calmly. Having experienced the annoyance of Confucian scholars himself, Xu Fu would no longer blindly obstruct Ying Zheng's decision. If future generations were destined to subject Ying Zheng to criticism, they might as well be carefree and unconstrained—deal with whatever needed dealing with. Never mind how later generations would judge it; as long as the achievements of Great Qin could be stabilized right now, that was all that mattered.

"Li Si believes that any texts not belonging to the state of Qin should be gathered up and burned, leaving them no possibility of influencing the common people or being held in the hands of Confucian scholars to wreak havoc on the state." With that, Li Si stared fixedly at Ying Zheng, awaiting his reaction.

"At the same time, those who use the past to criticize the present should have their entire households executed, so as to teach those people not to dare give rise to slanderous thoughts again."

Viewed through the lens of a modern person like Xu Fu, this point felt truly excessive—devoid of even a shred of democracy and freedom. But when he thought of those keyboard warriors in future generations who ran amok on the internet, relying on the web to casually smear, slander, and shirk responsibility, Xu Fu felt that such punishments were indeed warranted. He knew that two different eras could not be placed together for comparison. Upon careful reflection, Xu Fu gradually came to agree with Li Si's words in his heart.

"Anyone who discusses the *Classic of Poetry* or the *Classic of History* should be put to death. Those who fail to burn their books within thirty days of the decree being issued shall be tattooed on the face and exiled to the frontier, guarding the city by day and building walls by night. Only books on medicine, agriculture, and divination shall be spared from burning. As for those who wish to study the laws and decrees, let officials be their teachers." As Li Si spoke with mounting excitement, he looked quite triumphant. "In this way, the harm brought by Confucianism can be halted."

Li Si's argument carried far more weight than Chunyu Yue's, and the reasons he presented were much better grounded and defensible. A careful pondering of his words left one with no choice but to agree.

Xu Fu squeezed Ying Zheng's hand again. "...The books cannot be burned."

Because of the distance, no one else knew what he and Ying Zheng had said to each other.

Legend had it that the Four Books and Five Classics were originally the Four Books and Six Classics, but the *Classic of Music* among them had been burned in the fires of Qin, causing a precious piece of human cultural wealth to vanish forever and drawing endless criticism from later generations.

Of course, according to historical records, many books vanished in the burning of books, though even more were burned by Xiang Yu's fire. This point was difficult for later historians to determine with absolute certainty, and naturally Xu Fu didn't dare be certain either. But whether certain or not, books could not be burned at will. If these were passed down to future generations, they would all be peerless treasures of the world!

Books were the crystallized effort and wisdom of past generations. Regardless of right or wrong, only by preserving books could a new generation of capable talents be cultivated.

Seeing that Ying Zheng remained silent, Xu Fu couldn't help leaning down to murmur in his ear, "The Confucian scholars can be killed, but the books cannot be killed. Holding these books in his hands, A-Zheng can easily cultivate a new generation of Confucian scholars who are truly aligned with his heart later on."

Ying Zheng's lips moved, and he said, "I understand. We shall follow the Chancellor's proposal: anyone who dares to criticize the court and lead public slander among the people shall be put to death. As for the burning of books, I have my own judgment on the matter. First, order the entire country to collect ancient texts, gather them in Xianyang, and store them within the palace." Having said this, Ying Zheng suddenly turned his head to look at Xu Fu, smiling as he said, "With A-Fu's deep love for reading, how could I ever order them burned?"

Xu Fu suddenly thought of another matter. "If we're collecting books from across the country, we might as well recall those manuscripts of mine that have circulated outward." That kind of stuff was what truly ought to be burned; henceforth, aside from the Ministry of Fengchang, not a single external copy should remain.

Ying Zheng nodded.

After that, neither Zhou Qing nor Chunyu Yue dared to approach Ying Zheng to speak again.

Although a flash of regret crossed Li Si's face, his emotions were well-concealed—at least he didn't lose his composure like Zhou Qing and Chunyu Yue. He sat back down in his seat and calmly continued his meal.

The rest of the banquet proceeded smoothly, with no one else coming forward to displease Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng and Xu Fu sat in their seats whispering to each other, paying no further heed to the officials in the court.

As the banquet drew near its end, the conversation between Xu Fu and Ying Zheng finally concluded. By this time, Ying Zheng also announced orders for Wang Ben to lead troops in subduing Baiyue. This Baiyue was far thornier and more troublesome than the Yue tribes. However, Ying Zheng had some experience now, and this lifetime would certainly not be as tragic as the previous one.

At court the next day, Ying Zheng punished the judges who had failed to enforce the law impartially. It was also on this day that Ying Zheng initiated the project to build the Great Wall. Those punished officials were the ones dispatched to construct the wall.

Standing in the imperial court and watching these officials being led away, Xu Fu thought to himself: It seems that in Ying Zheng's mind, officials and commoners are no different at all. Aside from those conscripted, everyone else sent to build the Great Wall consisted of criminal officials and commoners. And even those who were conscripted received pay. What reason did anyone have to use the construction of the Great Wall to accuse Ying Zheng of being cruel and tyrannical?

Xu Fu could not figure it out, nor did he intend to.

The further he walked with Ying Zheng, the more strangely calm Xu Fu became, as if no storm could trouble him any longer.

After the morning court session, Xu Fu walked alongside Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng looked hesitant, as if he were deliberating over something and unsure whether to tell Xu Fu. Seeing him like this, Xu Fu knew it couldn't be anything major. If it were truly important, Ying Zheng would never hesitate; he would make a swift decision on whether to speak or not.

Therefore, Xu Fu asked without any mental burden: "What is A-Zheng thinking about?"

Ying Zheng glanced at Xu Fu and said, "Do you still remember that in my previous life, I built a palace in the forest park south of the Wei River? It was named 'Epang'."

Epang Palace?

Xu Fu immediately felt a bit unwell. He remembered those memories; he had personally heard Qin Shi Huang tell him that the palace was built for him. Even now, thinking about it made Xu Fu shiver.

Can you imagine that feeling?

The Epang Palace, known to everyone in later generations, was actually built by Qin Shi Huang just to please you.

This feeling is like coming to the Qin Dynasty and discovering that the reason Qin Shi Huang placed terracotta warriors in his imperial mausoleum was simply because you liked figurines.

It was truly shocking, and there was a sense of being so thunderstruck that one felt numb, as if one had suddenly transformed into a "femme fatale" bringing disaster.

"In my previous life, I died before it was finished, and you left by sea without ever looking back at Epang Palace again."

As soon as these words were spoken, Xu Fu felt as if he had become the "scumbag" who walked away without looking back the moment Ying Zheng died...

Xu Fu shook his head and said, "Resources are currently being consumed by many, how can we spend them on this?" Xu Fu couldn't tell Ying Zheng directly that he didn't like it, so he had to find an excuse.

Ying Zheng smiled faintly and did not refute, but he also didn't explicitly say that he would stop building the Epang Palace.

Xu Fu glanced at him from the corner of his eye and couldn't discern any emotion on Ying Zheng's face, so he simply gave up.

Upon returning to the palace, Ying Zheng remembered the Nine Cauldrons and asked Xu Fu: "What does A-Fu intend to do with them?"

Now that the nine cauldrons were gathered, Xu Fu had played with each of them and said, "Since the Nine Cauldrons are meant to stabilize the mountains and rivers, let us find skilled craftsmen to repair them, and then use them to stabilize the Great Qin's territory."

The Nine Cauldrons were indeed magical—even the medicine ground within them was extraordinary—but Xu Fu felt that placing them to stabilize the Great Qin's mountains and rivers was the best way to utilize their purpose.

Ying Zheng laughed: "Is A-Fu willing to do this for me?" In Ying Zheng's eyes, this move by Xu Fu was undoubtedly done with his interests in mind.

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment and said calmly, "Naturally."

A look of intense joy appeared on Ying Zheng's face. He pushed the Nine Cauldrons off the table, scattering them around, and then Xu Fu was pressed onto the table.

Xu Fu: "..." What did he say that triggered Ying Zheng?

...

As for finding craftsmen to repair them, Xu Fu truly found people. By the time the Nine Cauldrons were repaired, the Baiyue War, which should have lasted several years, had ended early. Wang Ben had pacified Baiyue, and subsequently, Ying Zheng established the commanderies of Guilin, Xiang, and Nanhai, sending exiled individuals there to defend them.

Not long after, the Xiongnu, sensing the growing national strength of Great Qin, could not help but attack the borders.

Ying Zheng dispatched the Meng brothers, whose prestige in the court grew day by day.

This could also be considered as Ying Zheng paving the way for Fusu's future.

·

Xu Fu sat in his bedchamber. The attendants delivered the repaired Nine Cauldrons to him. Without hesitation, Xu Fu handed them to Ying Zheng, telling him to place them in various regions to stabilize the dragon aura of Great Qin. After receiving the cauldrons, Ying Zheng could not suppress his joy and ended up flipping Xu Fu over and over again.

What delighted him was naturally not the Nine Cauldrons, but the fact that these cauldrons represented the deepening affection Xu Fu held for him.

What could be more joyful than knowing one's lover loves them back? Especially for Ying Zheng, who had sought this in vain in his previous life.

After they spent a few days in indulgence, a group of fangshi (alchemists/mystics) arrived in Xianyang.

Among this group were those who had previously submitted memorials requesting Ying Zheng's permission to sail the seas in search of fairy mountains, as well as those who had presented illustrated books. These people came from all over the country, gathering here partly to serve Ying Zheng and partly to see Xu Fu, the legendary National Master, and perhaps spar with him.

Xu Fu, however, did not care.

If there were capable fangshi, they could stay in the Fengchang Temple; if they were incompetent, they could be expelled. If they wanted to stir up trouble, Xu Fu felt that Ying Zheng would likely be happy to dig a pit and bury them.

The fangshi arrived outside the Xianyang Palace, requesting an audience with His Majesty.

Upon hearing this, Xu Fu sat up lazily on his bed. For the sake of the Fengchang Temple, he had to go and take a look. Thus, he washed and ate with Ying Zheng, then headed to the main hall together to summon the fangshi.

The fangshi had long heard of Xu Fu's name; it could be said that the current Xu Fu was their rival.

Some fangshi knew that the Empress and the National Master were the same person and naturally had no ulterior motives, but others who were unaware already felt a sense of resistance toward the National Master before even meeting him.

When the fangshi walked into the hall and saw Xu Fu dressed in black, his face handsome and cold, like a god high above in the heavens, they guessed that he was the National Master.

After all, Xu Fu's outstanding appearance had long been known throughout the world.

Xu Fu could feel the gazes landing on him—some contemptuous and disdainful, some cautious and wary... there were few who truly admired or revered him. It was clear that among his peers, there were indeed many enemies!

The fangshi paid their respects and then proceeded to spout the usual nonsense about elixir pills and fairy mountains to Ying Zheng.

Although Xu Fu had once spouted such nonsense to Qin Shi Huang himself, their stances were different. Back then, he was trying to escape Qin Shi Huang, whereas these people were trying to deceive Ying Zheng in pursuit of fame, wealth, and power. This naturally made Xu Fu despise them.

Xu Fu's expression grew colder, his gaze like a blade, causing some of the fangshi to lose their composure on the spot, nearly collapsing to their knees. Although they managed to maintain their posture and etiquette in the end, their faces could not help but turn slightly pale.

Xu Fu did not hold these people in high regard.

Among those in the hall, how many could compare to Hou Sheng? Not to mention him, how many could compare to Han Zhong? If they couldn't even compare to them, where did they get the nerve to spout such nonsense?

After listening to them one by one, Xu Fu secretly noted down a few who were relatively capable, thinking they could be selected for the Fengchang Temple; as for the rest, he didn't even bother to look at them twice.

Once they had finished their presentations, Ying Zheng nodded and said, "Then I shall grant you the opportunity to refine elixir pills and sail the seas in search of fairy mountains."

The fangshi were naturally overjoyed upon hearing this.

Xu Fu, however, could not help but frown. What did this mean? Could it be that Ying Zheng was still interested in immortality?

Soon, the fangshi were led away by attendants and were actually settled within the palace.

Xu Fu's expression turned even colder. As soon as the people left, he immediately asked Ying Zheng: "A-Zheng, why did you grant their request just now?"

Ying Zheng looked at Xu Fu calmly and unhurriedly. He gripped Xu Fu's shoulders, looked into his eyes, and said slowly, "A-Fu, have you never noticed one thing?"

"What?" Xu Fu was somewhat confused.

Ying Zheng pulled Xu Fu into his arms. The attendants on both sides hurriedly lowered their heads.

"A-Fu, have you never noticed that your appearance has not changed in the slightest to this day?" After saying this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but smile bitterly. He reached out and held Xu Fu tighter, resting his chin on Xu Fu's shoulder, and murmured, "In this life, I have finally obtained you; how could I bear to leave you after only a few decades? When we are old, if I am white-haired and frail while you remain as youthful as ever, how painful would that be?"

Xu Fu was stunned, his mind feeling as if it had been struck by a heavy blow, and for a long while, he could not speak.

"But... but..."

At this moment, Xu Fu was truly speechless. If it were before, he could have argued eloquently. But now, tasting the words Ying Zheng had spoken, he felt an immense bitterness.

When we are old, if you are white-haired and I remain as youthful as ever...

Xu Fu found it truly difficult to imagine.

"The mountains and rivers of the world, the supreme power—I have possessed them for two lifetimes. Only you... in my previous life, I could not possess you. Must I leave you first in this life as well? Since we have the miraculous fate of being reborn, why can we not be immortal? If I were immortal alone, it would be extremely lonely, but if I could accompany you, I would never grow tired of it, no matter how many years pass."

Ying Zheng spoke softly, his low voice pouring into Xu Fu's ears. Xu Fu suddenly felt a heaviness in his heart, and he could no longer say anything.

"But..." Xu Fu bit his lip unconsciously, his expression slightly dazed, "But what can they do? Can they produce an immortality elixir? Can they really find the fairy mountains?"

Ying Zheng said lightly, "But we must try."

These few simple words weighed heavily on Xu Fu's heart.

Xu Fu pressed his lips together firmly, "If we are to search, then I should be the one to go."

Ying Zheng did not speak, but there were dark undercurrents hidden in his eyes.

How could he possibly let Xu Fu go? In both his past and present lives, he would never allow it.

Emotions surged within Ying Zheng, unable to settle for a long time, so he simply picked Xu Fu up horizontally and walked away, while the attendants kept their heads down and followed at a distance.

...

When Xu Fu woke up the next day, Ying Zheng had already gone to court. Because Xu Fu was sleeping so soundly, Ying Zheng did not pull him from under the covers to take him to court. In any case, Ying Zheng understood Xu Fu's temperament very well and knew he had no obsession with attending court.

Upon waking and seeing that Ying Zheng was not by his side, Xu Fu actually felt a slight sense of relief.

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment and ordered someone to bring a mirror. He could only vaguely see his reflection, but that was enough.

Both he and Ying Zheng were around thirty years old, yet his face was still as youthful as a teenager's, extremely fresh and without a single wrinkle. Xu Fu rubbed his temples in frustration. How could this be? Oh, right...

Xu Fu remembered that in his previous life, he truly had techniques for maintaining his youth. When he met Ying Zheng, Ying Zheng looked over forty, while he was in his thirties but still looked like a youth.

But why was he like this?

Xu Fu could not find a single memory of youth-preservation or immortality in his mind; it was filled with memories of how he had used the concept of immortality to trick Ying Zheng.

Xu Fu let out a long sigh, feeling that it was not good to keep feeling so depressed, so he got up and headed outside. Since he couldn't figure it out now, he would just give up. There were still decades of life left; he would surely find a solution!

Just as Ying Zheng said, the fact that they could be reborn was already miraculous; who knew what other miracles might happen? If... if there was truly no way, well... death wasn't actually such a painful thing. Xu Fu had long been prepared for an early death, so if he had to wait for Ying Zheng to grow old and pass away, he would simply accompany him.

These thoughts flashed through Xu Fu's mind. He didn't think it was such a big deal, and after self-comforting, he gradually became calm and composed.

After washing up, Xu Fu had food brought to the garden to eat. The attendants naturally wouldn't question this decision; they just went to prepare it.

There was a small pavilion in the garden. Because Ying Zheng no longer had a harem, this area was rarely visited, except when Fuhai came to play. The attendants hurriedly cleaned the pavilion, set up tables and other items, and even lit a brazier.

It was cold now, and the attendants dared not let Xu Fu catch a chill.

Xu Fu ate his meal while admiring the flowers and plants.

Before long, a person suddenly appeared in the garden—an old man in dusty robes.

The old man walked outside the pavilion and smiled: "Greetings, National Master."

Xu Fu looked up and glanced at him nonchalantly, "And you are?"

"I am one of the fangshi remaining in the palace." He did not state his name.

Xu Fu assumed he was there to challenge him, so he gave a hum and waited quietly for the old man to continue. If someone truly lacked eyes and wanted to challenge him, he wouldn't mind a fight; it might even help relieve his mood.

Seeing Xu Fu's cold attitude, the old man didn't mind. He smiled again and said, "The National Master comes from another place; would the National Master like to go back?"

"What?" Xu Fu frowned slightly. What was this old man talking about? He didn't quite understand.

"Is the National Master not from another world?" The old man's smile remained unchanged. Even though he still looked dusty and plain, Xu Fu felt that his aura had changed as he looked at him.

"What exactly are you trying to say?" Xu Fu was not a rash person, so he naturally had to ask for clarity first. Whether this old man was human or immortal, Xu Fu could not be easily deceived.

The old man said, "If the National Master wishes to return, you must gather the Nine Cauldrons to go back to the past."

Xu Fu's expression was strange as he said, "I have already gathered the Nine Cauldrons."

The old man was slightly surprised, his brows furrowed, "So fast?" Then Xu Fu heard him mutter under his breath: "How could it be so fast? This isn't right... History isn't like this..." Although the old man kept his voice very low, it did not escape Xu Fu's ears.

Xu Fu's heart skipped a beat, and his expression turned ugly.

What was the origin of this old man?

The old man seemed to see through his thoughts and hurriedly smiled: "Someone who repairs space-time."

Repairing space-time? Xu Fu suddenly felt as if he had fallen into a science fiction blockbuster.

"Since you have already gathered the Nine Cauldrons, I will tell you how to use them, and you can return."

Xu Fu felt a sense of irony in his heart. If this person had appeared when he first arrived in the Qin state and told him these things, he might have gone to gather the Nine Cauldrons without a second thought to return to the future. But now that this old man had popped up to say such strange things, why would Xu Fu listen? If he were to leave Ying Zheng... Xu Fu didn't even dare to think about it.

So Xu Fu sat there and said coldly, "Too bad, those Nine Cauldrons have already been gathered by me and handed over to the First Emperor, scattered across the states to stabilize the mountains and rivers of the nation."

Upon hearing this, the old man nearly choked on his breath. After a long while, he calmed his breathing and said anxiously, "This... what is to be done? Isn't this the 26th year of the First Emperor? Why... why did such a flaw occur?"

Xu Fu could almost guess why the flaw occurred.

The past and the present were not the same, and they were very different from historical records. Because of his appearance, the historical trajectory of Qin had been accelerated. So, things that should have happened ten years later had been brought forward. The Nine Cauldrons had also been gathered early. No wonder the old man was so devastated; he had fully expected to have calculated the time, but he had forgotten that the hardest thing to calculate is people.

Human change is extremely uncontrollable.

"This, this won't do!" the old man said, "These Nine Cauldrons were never meant to fall into the hands of the First Emperor!"

After all, the Qin Dynasty was supposed to fall in the second generation!

How could Qin Shi Huang obtain the Nine Cauldrons? When he failed to salvage them, didn't he order the trees on Xiang Mountain to be cut down?

The old man paced back and forth in anxiety.

Xu Fu sensed some extraordinary qualities in this person, so he put down his chopsticks and asked calmly, "Do you know the art of immortality?"

The old man looked up at Xu Fu and said, "I know, I know! You are the representative figure who promoted immortality on a grand scale!"

Xu Fu's gaze grew colder, making the old man shiver. He muttered to himself, "If I had known you would find them so quickly, I wouldn't have used dreams to drop clues."

Xu Fu was incredibly sharp and immediately connected these pieces of information.

So, the reason he had dreamed of the cauldron in the Shu region nearly being swallowed by a dragon was that the old man was trying to hint to him through dreams that it was the key to returning to the future? If there was anyone to blame, it was that Xu Fu had been living too well in the Qin Dynasty and had no intention of returning, so he never linked the Nine Cauldrons to that.

徐福脑中百转千回，最后道：“扣下他。”
这个他自是指这老叟。
两旁守卫闻言，一拥而上，将那老叟当即按翻在地，手上半点不留情。
老叟也是一懵，懵过之后，他便立即哀声叫了起来，“国师何必如此待我？我这身子骨，怕是经受不起这样的折磨！”
那老叟都已经自己抖落出身份了，此时徐福自然不会认为他还真是个老头子。既然敢自称乃“修补时空者”，那便绝不会脆弱到往地上摁两下便要死要活了。
徐福冷漠地看了老叟一眼，道：“此人出言不逊，冒犯于我，先关押几日，再行审问。”
老叟傻眼了，“这……这……这不行啊！国师你……”
见这老叟口吻没有半点尊重之意，守卫看向他的目光便更是厌恶不已，管他是何人，竟敢对国师不敬！那便应当受到惩罚！守卫二话不说便遵从了徐福的命令，直接将那老叟带了下去。
老叟一边挣扎，一边嘶喊“不可啊”。
徐福却没分给他半点多余的目光，徐福专注于眼前的食物，低头继续享用。
跟着嬴政久了，徐福就越来越沉得住气，懂得用这样的方式去得到自己想要的信息了。现下很明显，着急的是那老叟，又并非他，那他便晾他一晾，届时好从他口中得知更多的信息。若是徐福在听过老叟表明身份后，便立即放低身段去接触，怕是那老叟反倒要翘上天去，不给徐福好脸色了。
反正徐福如今也不知低头谦虚为何物，那便干干脆脆表现得冷硬且高傲一些，让老叟苦上几日再说。
徐福缓慢地用完了饭食，然后便让宫人陪着自己在宫中散散步，以消食。
因为方士们都被留在了宫中的缘故，宫中似乎因而显得热闹了许多，这不，徐福还没走上多久，便撞上几名方士了，那方士之中，为首的乃是一中年男子，留着短胡须，打扮倒是与仙风道骨沾两分边。
男子一见了徐福，眼底便飞速地掠过了三分敌意。
但毕竟尊卑摆在那里，男子躬身，当先道：“卢生见过皇后。”
后面两个字他咬得有些轻，不难听出其中带了几分轻蔑的味道。
只不过此时徐福的注意力根本不在此。
卢生！
这不就是之前他梦到另一世记忆时，那个道貌岸然接近他的方士卢生吗？徐福对此人的感官可实在不大好，于是此时他也并不掩饰自己的情绪，冷漠道：“嗯。”
卢生包括他身后的方士们，皆是忍不住一愣。
就“嗯”一声便算完了？
不是向来听闻秦国对待有能之士极为客气吗？这……这徐君房实在是可恶！莫非是瞧他们也同为方士，便故意给他们冷脸？
若是徐福知晓此时这些人心中所想，必然会道，“怀揣恶意的人，瞧谁都觉得有恶意。”不过是他们自己思维龌龊罢了，怎敢怪他冷脸？
这些方士之中，没一个是之前徐福看得入眼的，于是他没分给这波人注意力，带着宫人便转弯离去了。
他们见徐福走远，便有些心高气傲的忍不住了。这些人却是还不想想，徐福是什么身份？他们是什么身份？徐福有着何等的本事和性格的？而他们又有什么拿得出手的东西来？
“何必如此猖狂？不过都是方士罢了！”
“我们怎能与之比？”
“是啊，他可是皇后……哈……”
这口吻便是不加掩饰的，带上嘲讽之意了。
只是他们的得意实在没能持续多久的时间，一旁的守卫便陡然上前来，凶神恶煞地将他们全部扣住了，其中也包括了那个在那一世得罪徐福的人。一个都没落下！
守卫们冷哼道：“身在咸阳宫中，胆子倒是不小，连皇后都敢妄议！”
旁边还有人补了一句，“什么东西！”
短短两句话，登时将这群人吓得脸色发白又发红，实在好看！
蠢到这样的地步，所以徐福都不乐意搭理他们。
这样不分场合地猖狂，哪里需要徐福出手做什么？他们自己便能将自己生生作死。
不过不得不说，经过这么几个蠢货前来挑衅一番，徐福竟是觉得心情大好，走路都轻快了几分。他干脆去寻了胡亥，去瞧胡亥与项羽如今都捣鼓出什么玩意儿来了。
项羽此时才刚刚十来岁，年纪尚小，语言还稚嫩得很，偶尔说出来的话还令人觉得有两分好笑。
实在大大抹杀了他在徐福心目中留下的印象。
瞧着项羽借着天生神力的优势，表演了会儿“杂耍”，徐福方才心情愉悦地回到了殿中，休息前，他又照了照镜子。
皮囊本是父母所赐，虽然徐福不知自己的父母是谁，可他从来对自己的皮相极为满意。从前他都并不觉得有何处不妥，也就是现在，才骤然发觉，原来他的容颜真的数十年如一日，极少有变化。
若是在现代的话，他便能寻到原因了吧？或许还能寻到父母？
只可惜如今身在秦朝，而他也确实不愿离开此处。
徐福揉了揉额头，仰面躺倒在小榻之上。
嬴政悄然进了殿，以为徐福正在小憩，便不想脚步声将他吵醒。谁知等走近了，嬴政才发现原来徐福并未睡着，二人大眼瞪小眼，看了好一会儿，嬴政才伸手将徐福抱了起来。
既然徐福没有睡着，嬴政便直接与他说起了话。
“阿福可要随我去瞧一瞧长城的修筑？”
徐福双眼微亮，面色却是不显，他点点头，应道：“好。”
他也正想瞧一瞧，千年前的长城，由秦始皇主持修筑的长城，该是何等雄伟大气的模样！
嬴政知晓自己说了些话，令徐福心情不大愉悦，这才提出了去游长城的建议。见到徐福两眼微微放光的模样，嬴政心底顿时松了一口气。原本他是不打算告知徐福，他依旧想要命人研制长生不老药的。这样的事，让他在背后操心头疼便是，便不消徐福再多加关注了。
但是当徐福问起的时候，他还是牙关一松，便全部都说了出来。
他心底的不舍和霸道，都说了出来。
他说这些可不是为了影响徐福的心情，自然得找些法子来弥补。
嬴政却并不知晓，徐福哪有那样脆弱？自我调节一番便也无事了。世上本无难事，只怕有心之人。尤其是见了那老叟之后，这时候徐福的心可是正宽得很。
二人定下行程后，便先在宫中进行了几日没羞没臊的生活。
待到前往长城之前，徐福方才与嬴政说起了这个老叟，徐福没有半点隐瞒，就说这人知道自己是从后世穿越而来。
嬴政面色沉了沉，道：“那人现在何处？”
“我已经命人将他关押起来了，招来侍从一问便知在何处。”那日下令将老叟关押起来之后，徐福便没再如何上心了，连他具体被关在了何处都不知晓。
嬴政闻言，点了点头，直接将侍从叫了进来，侍从自然是一五一十地汇报了。
听过之后，嬴政的面色便难看到了极点。
那老叟在他眼中就是个什么性质的人物呢？就是个想要来拐带徐福的人！而且此人还态度恶劣，对徐福极为不尊！嬴政可不管他是什么来头，到了大秦，你就是条龙也得给我盘着！
侍从在前带路，嬴政携着徐福的手，一同来到了关押那老叟的地方。
老叟听见了脚步声，当即便站起了身，等看到嬴政与徐福同来的时候，老叟便又坐了回去。
嬴政冷声道：“见了朕，倒是好大的架子。”
老叟一惊，这才反应过来自己方才的行为实在太不妥当，于是他赶紧站立起来，冲着嬴政躬身，恭敬地道：“见过陛下。”
嬴政却没搭理他，他现在看着老叟，便如同看着眼中钉一样，自然不愿意轻易放过老叟。胆敢不尊徐福，肆意妄为，那便要承担妄为带来的这份后果。
“剁去他的手指。”嬴政道。
那老叟惊呆了，完全没想到嬴政口中会发出这样的指令。
“陛下，陛下！请陛下三思！”老叟怂得不行，立马就软倒地上了。
徐福有些好奇看了看他，“你的手指断了便接不回去了吗？”
老叟没点头也没摇头，他此时看着徐福和嬴政的目光都充满了惊恐，只敢暗暗在心头骂道，这二人实在可怖，难怪走一块儿硬生生凑成了一对！
“那便缝上他的嘴。”
老叟更惊悚了，“不！不我还有话要说……”
“没了嘴，你还有手，反正留着这张嘴也说不出什么话来，这般无用，不如割去！”
那老叟也知晓秦朝刑法的厉害，他打了个哆嗦，竟是连与嬴政直视的勇气都无。
人间帝王便是至尊的存在，他纵为修补时空者，怕是也无法吧？徐福心中暗道。所以这老叟才会如此畏惧嬴政。他也就只敢在背后说一说人的坏话罢了。
似乎正是为了印证徐福的猜测，那老叟极其没有骨气地朝着二人的方向跪了下来，口中忙道：“请陛下绕过我，若是陛下有何疑问，我定然都为陛下解决！”
其实徐福关押了他好几日，要的便也是老叟这句话。
但是偏偏老叟惹上了不该惹的人。
嬴政的脾气可不是那样好安抚下来的。
他冷声道：“可惜了，朕与皇后都不想知晓。”
老叟面上的表情僵了僵，隐隐有些六神无主了起来，“这……我、我对皇后当真没有恶意，我前来只是问一问皇后，九鼎可集齐了。”他也知道自己没有卖关子的资格了，此时唯有赶紧张嘴说出有用的东西来，或许秦始皇还能绕过他。
来到一个世界便要遵循一个世界的规则，来到秦朝，若是秦始皇要斩杀他，那他便也只有被斩杀的份儿。
“集齐九鼎又如何？”
“如此皇后便可返回后世了。”
嬴政冷笑一声，“诱拐皇后，应当死罪！”
老叟傻了眼，忙不得不道：“我我我不敢！何况如今九鼎已经被皇后交到您的手中了不是吗？九鼎本是皇后返回到后世的关键，如今送到了陛下的手中，想来便是能保陛下功业千秋的！”老叟也是被吓急眼了，这才想出了主意来——拍秦始皇的马屁。
夸什么功业千秋，其实都没用处。
这样的话，嬴政听得还少了吗？
不过老叟这番话倒也算是误打误撞了个正着！
嬴政听这段话的时候，重点便在于，徐福抛下了集齐九鼎回到后世的机会，转而选择了留在了他的身边，并且将九鼎给了他，让他用于镇家国山河。个中情谊，如何能教嬴政不欢悦？
嬴政面色稍霁，转头问徐福：“阿福有什么话要问此人？”
徐福盯着老叟，还是问了那日的话，“你对长生不老之术可有了解？”
chapters.translated_text:
Xu Fu's mind raced through countless thoughts before finally saying, "Lock him up."

This "him" naturally referred to the old man.

Hearing this, the guards on both sides swarmed forward and immediately pinned the old man to the ground, showing not the slightest bit of mercy in their hands.

The old man was stunned for a moment, and once the daze passed, he immediately cried out in grievance, "Why must the State Preceptor treat me like this? This old body of mine probably cannot withstand such torture!"

Since the old man had already revealed his own identity, Xu Fu naturally no longer believed he was just a regular old man. Since he dared to claim to be a "spandrel-time mender," he certainly wouldn't be fragile enough to drop dead just from being pressed to the ground twice.

Xu Fu gave the old man a cold glance and said, "This man spoke impertinently and offended me. Lock him up for a few days, then interrogate him."

The old man was dumbfounded. "This... this... this won't do! State Preceptor, you..."

Seeing that the old man's tone lacked even a shred of respect, the guards looked at him with even greater disgust. Whoever he might be, how dare he show disrespect to the State Preceptor! That deserved punishment! Without another word, the guards obeyed Xu Fu's order and dragged the old man away directly.

The old man struggled while shouting, "You cannot do this!"

Xu Fu, however, didn't spare him a single extra glance, focusing instead on the food before him and lowering his head to continue enjoying it.

Having been with Ying Zheng for so long, Xu Fu had grown increasingly composed and knew how to use such tactics to get the information he wanted. Right now, it was obvious that the old man was the anxious one, not him. Therefore, he would leave the old man hanging for a bit so that he could extract more information from him later. If Xu Fu had lowered his stance and engaged with him immediately after the old man revealed his identity, the old man probably would have grown arrogant and refused to give Xu Fu a pleasant look.

Anyway, Xu Fu currently had no idea what humility was, so he might as well just be straightforwardly cold and arrogant, and let the old man suffer for a few days first.

Xu Fu slowly finished his meal, then had the palace attendants accompany him for a walk around the palace to help digest it.

Because the alchemists had all been kept in the palace, it seemed to have become much more lively as a result. Sure enough, before Xu Fu had walked very far, he ran into several alchemists. Among them, the leader was a middle-aged man with a short beard whose attire bore a two-tenths resemblance to that of an immortal sage.

As soon as the man saw Xu Fu, a flash of hostility quickly crossed the depths of his eyes.

But after all, the hierarchy was there; the man bowed and spoke first, "Lu Sheng greets the Empress."

He bit down rather lightly on the last two syllables, and it wasn't hard to hear a hint of contempt mixed within.

It was just that Xu Fu's attention wasn't on this at all right now.

Lu Sheng!

Wasn't this the sanctimonious alchemist Lu Sheng who had approached him in his dream of memories from another lifetime? Xu Fu's impression of this person was truly not good, so he didn't bother to mask his emotions at the moment, saying coldly, "Mn."

Lu Sheng and the alchemists behind him couldn't help but freeze.

Just a "Mn" and that was it?

Hadn't it always been rumored that the Qin State was extremely courteous to talented individuals? This... this Xu Junfang was simply hateful! Could it be that, seeing they were fellow alchemists as well, he was intentionally giving them the cold shoulder?

If Xu Fu knew what these people were thinking at the moment, he would definitely say, "Those who harbor malice see malice in everyone." It was just their own minds that were filthy; how dare they blame him for giving them a cold face?

Not a single one of these alchemists caught Xu Fu's eye, so he didn't spare this group any more attention and turned away with his attendants.

Seeing Xu Fu walk away, a few arrogant ones couldn't help themselves. These people didn't stop to think: What was Xu Fu's status? What was their status? What kind of ability and temperament did Xu Fu possess? And what did they have to bring to the table?

"Why be so arrogant? Aren't we all just alchemists!"

"How can we compare to him?"

"Yeah, he is the Empress... Ha..."

This tone was completely unmasked and carried a mocking intent.

Yet their smugness didn't last long before the guards nearby suddenly stepped forward and menacingly pinned all of them down, including the one who had offended Xu Fu in that other lifetime. Not a single one was left out!

The guards sneered, "Being in Xianyang Palace, you certainly have a lot of nerve to dare to openly gossip about the Empress!"

Someone nearby even added, "Who the hell do you think you are!"

Just two short sentences instantly frightened this group until their faces turned pale and red—a truly magnificent sight!

They were so stupid to such a degree that Xu Fu couldn't even be bothered to deal with them.

Being arrogant so indiscriminately without regard for the occasion—where was the need for Xu Fu to lift a finger? They were perfectly capable of digging their own graves.

However, it had to be said that after being provoked by a few fools like this, Xu Fu actually felt his mood improve greatly, and his steps felt a bit lighter. He simply went to look for Hu Hai to see what kind of contraptions he and Xiang Yu were tinkering with these days.

Xiang Yu was only just over ten years old at this time, still very young, and his speech was quite childish. The things he said occasionally even felt somewhat amusing.

It thoroughly shattered the impression he had left in Xu Fu's mind.

Watching Xiang Yu leverage his innate supernatural strength to perform "acrobatics" for a while, Xu Fu finally returned to the hall in a pleasant mood. Before resting, he looked into the mirror once more.

The physical vessel was originally bestowed by one's parents. Although Xu Fu didn't know who his parents were, he had always been extremely satisfied with his looks. In the past, he hadn't felt anything was amiss; it was only now that he suddenly realized his appearance truly remained unchanged through decades, showing very little variation.

If he were in modern times, would he be able to find the reason? Perhaps he could even find his parents?

It was just a pity that he was now in the Qin Dynasty, and he truly didn't want to leave this place.

Xu Fu rubbed his temples and lay flat on the small couch.

Ying Zheng quietly entered the hall. Thinking Xu Fu was taking a nap, he didn't want his footsteps to wake him. Who would have thought that upon walking closer, Ying Zheng would discover Xu Fu wasn't actually asleep. The two stared at each other with wide eyes for quite a while before Ying Zheng reached out and picked Xu Fu up.

Since Xu Fu wasn't asleep, Ying Zheng directly started talking with him.

"Would Ah Fu like to accompany me to see the construction of the Great Wall?"

Xu Fu's eyes brightened slightly, though his expression remained unbothered as he nodded and replied, "Okay."

He also wanted to see what the Great Wall of a thousand years ago—the Great Wall built under the auspices of Qin Shi Huang—would look like in all its majestic grandeur!

Ying Zheng knew that some of the things he had said earlier had made Xu Fu unhappy, which was why he proposed the suggestion of touring the Great Wall. Seeing the slight glimmer in Xu Fu's eyes, Ying Zheng let out a mental sigh of relief. Originally, he hadn't planned to let Xu Fu know that he still wanted people to research the elixir of immortality. Such matters were heavy enough for him to worry about and handle behind the scenes; there was no need for Xu Fu to pay extra attention to them.

But when Xu Fu asked about it, his guard slipped, and he blurted everything out anyway.

His reluctance to let go and his domineering possessiveness deep in his heart had all been spoken aloud.

Saying those things hadn't been meant to ruin Xu Fu's mood, so naturally, he had to find some ways to make up for it.

Ying Zheng didn't know that Xu Fu wasn't that fragile; after a bit of self-adjustment, he would be fine. There were no truly difficult tasks in the world, only those with a determined heart. Especially after meeting that old man, Xu Fu's mind was completely at ease right now.

After setting their itinerary, the two spent a few days of uninhibited intimacy within the palace.

Before setting off for the Great Wall, Xu Fu finally brought up the old man to Ying Zheng, holding back not a single detail and stating that this person knew he had traveled through time from a later era.

Ying Zheng's expression darkened. "Where is that man now?"

"I've already ordered him to be locked up. A quick question to an attendant will tell us where." After giving the order to lock the old man away that day, Xu Fu hadn't paid much attention to it and didn't even know where specifically he was being held.

Hearing this, Ying Zheng nodded and directly called an attendant in, who naturally reported everything truthfully.

After listening, Ying Zheng's expression turned ashen beyond belief.

What kind of figure was this old man in his eyes? He was simply someone trying to abduct Xu Fu! Moreover, this person had a terrible attitude and was extremely disrespectful to Xu Fu! Ying Zheng didn't care what his background was; once in Qin, even if you were a dragon, you had to coil up for him!

The attendant led the way in front, and Ying Zheng, holding Xu Fu's hand, walked together to the place where the old man was imprisoned.

Hearing footsteps, the old man immediately stood up. When he saw Ying Zheng and Xu Fu coming together, the old man sat back down.

Ying Zheng said coldly, "Such a grand attitude upon seeing Us."

The old man was startled, only then realizing how inappropriate his previous behavior had been. He hurriedly stood up, bowed toward Ying Zheng, and said respectfully, "Greetings, Your Majesty."

Ying Zheng ignored him. Looking at the old man now was like looking a thorn in his eye; naturally, he wasn't going to let him off easily. If he dared to disrespect Xu Fu and act willfully, he would have to bear the consequences of that willful behavior.

"Chop off his fingers," Ying Zheng commanded.

The old man was dumbfounded, completely not expecting Ying Zheng to issue such a directive.

"Your Majesty, Your Majesty! Please reconsider, Your Majesty!" The old man turned out to be utterly spineless and instantly collapsed onto the ground.

Xu Fu looked at him with some curiosity. "Can't your fingers be reattached once they're cut off?"

The old man neither nodded nor shook his head. At this moment, his gaze toward Xu Fu and Ying Zheng was filled with terror, and he only dared to curse inwardly: These two are truly terrifying, no wonder they got together and formed a match made in hell!

"Then sew his mouth shut."

The old man was even more horrified. "No! No, I still have things to say..."

"Without a mouth, you still have hands. Anyway, since keeping this mouth doesn't yield any useful words, it's as useless as can be—might as well cut it off!"

The old man knew the severity of Qin penal laws. He shivered and didn't even have the courage to look Ying Zheng in the eye.

Mortal emperors were supreme existences; even as a spandrel-time mender, he probably couldn't do anything about it, right? Xu Fu thought to himself. That was why this old man feared Ying Zheng so much; he only dared to speak ill of people behind their backs.

Seemingly to verify Xu Fu's guess, the old man completely discarded his backbone and knelt in the direction of the two, hurriedly saying, "Please spare me, Your Majesty! If Your Majesty has any questions, I will certainly resolve them all for Your Majesty!"

Actually, Xu Fu had locked him up for several days precisely to get these words out of the old man.

But unfortunately, the old man had provoked the wrong person.

Ying Zheng's temper wasn't so easily appeased.

He said coldly, "Pity, neither I nor the Empress wish to know."

The expression on the old man's face stiffened, and he vaguely began to panic. "This... I—I truly harbor no malice toward the Empress. I only came to ask the Empress whether the Nine Cauldrons have been gathered." He knew he no longer had the qualification to drag things out; right now, he had to quickly speak up and offer useful information, perhaps then the First Emperor would spare him.

Coming to a world meant following that world's rules. Coming to the Qin Dynasty, if the First Emperor wanted to execute him, he would only have the fate of being executed.

"So what if the Nine Cauldrons are gathered?"

"That way the Empress can return to later generations."

Ying Zheng sneered, "Abducting the Empress is a capital offense!"

The old man was dumbfounded and hurriedly blurted out, "I—I—I wouldn't dare! Besides, haven't the Nine Cauldrons already been handed over to you by the Empress, Your Majesty? The Nine Cauldrons were originally the key for the Empress to return to later generations, but now that they have been delivered into Your Majesty's hands, I imagine they can ensure Your Majesty's achievements endure for a thousand autumns!" The old man was frightened out of his wits, which was why he came up with this idea—flattering the First Emperor.

Praising someone's millennial achievements was actually completely useless.

Had Ying Zheng heard such words any fewer times?

Yet this speech by the old man hit the mark by sheer coincidence!

When Ying Zheng heard this passage, his focus was entirely on the fact that Xu Fu had abandoned the chance to gather the Nine Cauldrons and return to later generations, choosing instead to stay by his side and giving the Nine Cauldrons to him so he could use them to pacify the country and mountains. How could such deep affection fail to make Ying Zheng overjoyed?

Ying Zheng's expression cleared up slightly. He turned to ask Xu Fu, "Is there anything Ah Fu wants to ask this person?"

Xu Fu stared at the old man and asked the same question from that day: "Do you have any understanding of the art of immortality?"

chapters.title: 第272章
chapters.source_text:
老叟苦着脸，“我早已说过了啊，你便是最擅此道的啊！若是陛下要求长生，便应当寻你才是。”
不待徐福说话，嬴政已然冷声道：“你在说谎。”
老叟惊了惊，“我、我没有……”
“还是割掉他的嘴吧。”嬴政立即道。
老叟这次反倒骨气上来了，当即躺下去道：“若是陛下认为我在胡言，那杀了我便是！”
徐福皱了皱眉，看来什么都能说，唯独长生不能说？徐福总觉得这老叟有些怪异，但又找不出他哪里怪异，此时杀了他又觉得有些可惜。毕竟这老叟来历奇妙，谁能说得准，他身上还有多少东西没被挖出来呢？
嬴政与徐福心有灵犀，闻言便道：“割唇，抽筋，锁起来。”简单干脆利落七个字，却包裹着浓浓的血腥味道。
老叟瞪大了眼，“你你你……”
“走吧。”徐福拉着嬴政当先转了身。
嬴政回头看了老叟一眼。
老叟还未出口的话，登时就被掐没在了嗓子眼儿里，整个人都倒仰下去，跌坐于地，甚至是满头大汗，好不狼狈！
嬴政揽着徐福走远了。老叟这才重重地喘了两口气。方才……方才秦始皇望向他的眼神，竟是、竟是那般可怖，让他对上一眼，就不自觉地遍体生寒。
他……他是不是知道了什么？
老叟想到这里，陡然色变。
……
走出来之后，嬴政笑道：“长生不老之术，哪有这样容易获得？问不出便也罢了。”
徐福没再说话。他也觉得那老叟在说谎，或者说他在掩盖什么。
“嗯，陪我吃些食物吧。”徐福很快将这些甩到了脑后去。
“好。”嬴政揽着徐福继续往前走。
徐福跟嬴政并肩走了会儿，发现路上再没有碰见什么方士了，不免有些惊讶，“那些方士呢？”
“有方士胆敢在背后议论，我便将他们处死了。”嬴政淡淡道：“还有若是出现这人这般的状况，胆敢肆意到你跟前胡说，我也会处死。”大意便是，严令之下，那些人自然就不敢出现了。
这算是将那日宴上说的话，直接了当地实践了。
徐福想了想，还是没说什么。
胆敢在王宫里胡言乱语的人，死了倒也不冤枉。
只是待到两日后，徐福才发觉，原来这波处理的人中，就有那卢生，上辈子还活得挺长的卢生，这辈子竟是这样轻易丢了性命。不过想一想他辈子的做派，徐福心底浮现了三个大字，“死得好”。
接下来嬴政安置了一番政务，再度将大权移交到了扶苏的手中，并且抛下了小可怜胡亥，随后便和徐福高高兴兴出门去了。
“要去瞧长城，那不如再去个地方。”坐上出城的马车之后，徐福一边展开书简，一边漫不经心地道。
嬴政给他倒好了水，方才问道：“何地？”
“泗水。”
“泗水？泗水是何处？”嬴政一脸疑惑。
徐福被噎了一下。
不过泗水本就是个小地方，嬴政不知晓也实属正常。
“在沛县。”
“沛县？”嬴政似乎有了些记忆，毕竟他看过舆图之后，记性是非常好的，要从记忆的犄角旮旯里翻出来，倒也不难。
“嗯。”
“为何突然想去那里？”
“去找一个人。”去找刘邦。虽然还不知如今刘邦多大岁数，但应当是比项羽大的。徐福记得他与吕雉成亲的时候，可算得上是老光棍了。
“谁？”嬴政拧眉，目光一下子就危险了起来。能令徐福念念不忘牵挂于心的人物，嬴政是当真好奇。
“一个市井混混。”
嬴政闻言，顿时就放下了心。他很清楚徐福的眼光，以徐福的眼光，区区市井混混，他又怎么能看得入眼呢？这样的人应当也与徐福成不了朋友。既然不是朋友，那就应当是仇人了。
“阿福可是要杀了此人？”
徐福犹豫着点了点头。若他找到了刘邦，能像留下胡亥、项羽这般留下他吗？徐福觉得自己是做不到的，到时候他应当是想要直接出手杀了刘邦，以绝后患。
在这一点上，徐福做不到善良。
嬴政道：“要杀此人何其容易！今日我便可下令，让人找出此人杀死。”
徐福摇头，“我要到泗水走一趟。”
见徐福这般坚定，嬴政忍不住问道：“他是何处得罪阿福了？”若是太过可恶，那便不是死那样简单了。
徐福对上嬴政认真询问的目光，面色有些怪异。
“他……以后你便知晓了。”
嬴政笑了笑，“好。”说罢，顺手往徐福的嘴里塞了食物。
·
抵达临洮后，徐福和嬴政先行休息了一日，补了个眠。之后方才在当地负责人的带领下，前往了长城。
徐福在去往之前，做了无数的心理准备。
将要看到古长城，当然是一件令人忍不住激动的事。
未经后世再度修筑的长城，该是什么模样？是不是带着浓郁的秦国建筑风格呢？
“陛下，皇后，这边请。”引路的人恭恭敬敬地带着他们走上了另一条小道。
这边的道路实在不平整，光是走一走，徐福都能想象到，那些劳工在修筑的时候，该是经历过了多少的艰难困苦。
这时候的劳工还是挺伟大的。
若是秦国国力足以支撑，倒是应当让这些劳工至少吃得饱一些。古时的百姓所求，不就是温饱二字吗？
走着走着，他们便踏上了一处高处。
引路的人恭敬地道：“陛下，皇后，不便再向前了，当心那些贱民碰伤了二位。”
嬴政谈不上是多么爱子民的人，但此时听见引路人口中所言，当场就变了脸色，厉声道：“依朕来看，你倒是连贱民也不如。”
那引路的人面色僵了僵，这才知晓自己说错了话，忙跪地求饶。
嬴政可从来不是求求饶便能心软的人。
“拖下去。”嬴政看也不看那人，冷硬道。
徐福皱了皱眉，“长城在何处？”
嬴政指了指前方。
徐福一看。
这是长城？？？
还那么光秃秃！
气势恢宏在哪里？？？
chapters.translated_text:
The old man pulled a wry face. "I have already said it, you are the most adept at this! If His Majesty desires immortality, he should be looking for you instead."

Before Xu Fu could speak, Ying Zheng already said coldly, "You are lying."

The old man was startled. "I-I am not..."

"Cut out his tongue then," Ying Zheng said immediately.

This time, the old man suddenly grew a spine, slumped to the ground, and said, "If Your Majesty believes I am spouting nonsense, then just kill me!"

Xu Fu frowned. It seemed anything could be discussed except immortality? Xu Fu always felt this old man was a bit bizarre, yet he couldn't quite pinpoint what was strange about him, and killing him right now felt a bit of a waste. After all, the old man had a mysterious background; who could say how much more information remained unmined within him?

Ying Zheng and Xu Fu shared a tacit understanding, and upon hearing this, he said, "Sever his lips, pull his tendons, and lock him up." Seven simple, crisp, and decisive words, yet laden with a heavy stench of blood.

The old man's eyes widened. "You, you, you..."

"Let's go." Xu Fu pulled Ying Zheng and turned away first.

Ying Zheng looked back at the old man.

The words the old man was about to utter were instantly choked back in his throat. His entire body reeled backward, he slumped into a sitting position on the ground, and he was even drenched in cold sweat—what a miserable sight!

Ying Zheng put his arm around Xu Fu and walked away. Only then did the old man draw two heavy breaths. Just now... just now, the gaze the First Emperor of Qin cast upon him was actually, actually so terrifying that merely meeting it made his whole body involuntarily break out in a chill.

Did he... did he know something?

Thinking of this, the old man's expression changed abruptly.

......

After walking out, Ying Zheng smiled and said, "How can the art of immortality be so easily attained? If we can't get an answer out of him, so be it."

Xu Fu didn't speak again. He also felt that the old man was lying, or rather, concealing something.

"Well, accompany me to eat something." Xu Fu quickly cast these thoughts to the back of his mind.

"Alright." Ying Zheng put his arm around Xu Fu and continued walking forward.

After walking side by side with Ying Zheng for a while, Xu Fu noticed that they didn't encounter any more fangshi on the road, and couldn't help being somewhat surprised. "Where are those fangshi?"

"Some fangshi dared to gossip behind my back, so I executed them," Ying Zheng said indifferently. "And if anyone behaves like that man, daring to spout nonsense right in front of you, I will execute them as well." The implication was that, under strict orders, those people naturally wouldn't dare to show up.

This could be considered a direct and straightforward putting into practice of what was said at the banquet that day.

Xu Fu thought about it and didn't say anything in the end.

Those who dared to talk nonsense within the royal palace didn't die unjustly.

It was only two days later that Xu Fu realized that among this batch of people dealt with was Lusheng—the Lusheng who had lived quite a long life in his past life had so easily thrown away his life in this one. But thinking about his demeanor in his past life, three large characters surfaced in the depths of Xu Fu's mind: "Served him right."

Afterward, Ying Zheng arranged some state affairs, handed over supreme authority to Fusu once again, abandoned poor little Huhai, and then happily went out with Xu Fu on a trip.

"If we're going to see the Great Wall, we might as well go to another place," Xu Fu said casually while unfolding a bamboo slip after getting into the carriage leaving the city.

Ying Zheng poured him some water before asking, "Where?"

"Sishui."

"Sishui? Where is Sishui?" Ying Zheng looked puzzled.

Xu Fu choked slightly.

However, Sishui was just a small place, so it was completely normal for Ying Zheng not to know it.

"In Peixian."

"Peixian?" Ying Zheng seemed to have some memory of it. After all, having looked over maps, his memory was exceptionally good; digging it out from the dusty corners of his memory wasn't difficult.

"Mhm."

"Why suddenly want to go there?"

"To find someone." To find Liu Bang. Although he didn't know how old Liu Bang was now, he should be older than Xiang Yu. Xu Fu remembered that when Liu Bang married Lü Zhi, he could well be considered an old bachelor.

"Who?" Ying Zheng furrowed his brows, his gaze instantly turning dangerous. Ying Zheng was truly curious about any figure who could make Xu Fu linger in his thoughts and care about them so much.

"A marketplace scoundrel."

Hearing this, Ying Zheng immediately set his mind at ease. He knew Xu Fu's standards very well; with Xu Fu's standards, how could he possibly look favorably upon a mere marketplace scoundrel? Such a person probably couldn't become friends with Xu Fu either. Since they weren't friends, they must be enemies.

"Is Ah Fu going to kill this person?"

Xu Fu hesitated and nodded. If he found Liu Bang, could he spare him the way he spared Huhai and Xiang Yu? Xu Fu felt he couldn't do it; by that time, he would probably want to kill Liu Bang directly to nip future troubles in the bud.

On this point, Xu Fu could not afford to be benevolent.

Ying Zheng said, "How easy it is to kill this person! Today I can issue an order for someone to track him down and kill him."

Xu Fu shook his head. "I want to make a trip to Sishui."

Seeing Xu Fu so resolute, Ying Zheng couldn't help asking, "How has he offended Ah Fu?" If the offense was too heinous, then death wouldn't be the only simple outcome.

Meeting Ying Zheng's serious and inquiring gaze, Xu Fu's expression turned somewhat odd.

"He... you'll know in the future."

Ying Zheng smiled. "Alright." With that, he casually stuffed some food into Xu Fu's mouth.

·

Upon arriving in Lintao, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng rested for a day first to catch up on sleep. Afterward, led by the local official in charge, they headed to the Great Wall.

Before going, Xu Fu had made countless mental preparations.

Going to see the ancient Great Wall was naturally something that made one unable to suppress their excitement.

What would the Great Wall look like without later generations rebuilding it? Would it carry a strong Qin Dynasty architectural style?

"Your Majesty, Empress, this way please," the guide respectfully led them onto another path.

The road here was truly uneven; just walking on it, Xu Fu could imagine how much hardship those laborers must have endured while building it.

The laborers of this era were truly great.

If the national strength of Qin was sufficient to support it, those laborers should at least be allowed to eat their fill. Wasn't what the common people of ancient times asked for just the two words "food and warmth"?

As they walked, they stepped up to a higher vantage point.

The guide respectfully said, "Your Majesty, Empress, it is inconvenient to proceed further. Please be careful lest those lowly commoners bump into and injure the two of you."

Ying Zheng wasn't someone who loved his subjects dearly, but upon hearing what the guide said, his expression changed on the spot, and he sternly said, "In my view, you are even inferior to those lowly commoners."

The guide's expression stiffened. Realizing only then that he had said the wrong thing, he hurriedly knelt down to beg for mercy.

Ying Zheng was never someone who would soften his heart just because someone begged for mercy.

"Drag him away," Ying Zheng said coldly, without even looking at the man.

Xu Fu frowned. "Where is the Great Wall?"

Ying Zheng pointed ahead.

Xu Fu took a look.

This is the Great Wall???

And it's so barren and bald!

Where is the grand and majestic momentum???

chapters.source_text:
沉默在空气中蔓延。
半晌，嬴政不由得问道：“阿福，怎么了？”怎么突然之间沉默了？
“长城就是这般模样？”徐福的声音差点控制不住颤抖。
嬴政看出了他的失望，不由道：“不然呢？”
徐福这才意识到自己之前想得太过美好了！长城本就该是这般模样的，因为这时候……它！还！没！修！好！啊！
“没事了。”徐福摇头，缓缓吐出一口气来。要见到秦长城，起码还得等到几年后吧？这时所能见到的，不过是个雏形罢了。想一想，还觉得有些难耐。
毕竟后世所见到的长城，都是在明朝修筑过后的模样了。
嬴政看出了徐福的兴致不高，便道：“可是觉得没见着什么？”
徐福点头。
嬴政大笑道：“这有何妨？长城自西周时便开始修建了，只是各自零散，且有些实在不成样子，现在我只是命人将它们修筑并连通起来，这才能形成统一的防线，教外族不敢侵秦。”
徐福点头，原是如此啊……竟是从西周时便有了。
“若是你要瞧从前修筑的城墙，此时便能带你去看。”
徐福闻言，迟疑一下，倒是摇了摇头。从前的，却不是在嬴政手底下修建起来的，似乎……似乎倒也没那样吸引他了。“四处走一走便可。”徐福出声道。看长城，倒不如先去看一看那些劳工，他很好奇他们的生活，若是能借机改善一下，那便更好了。
修筑长城，十万劳工，这些人若是起了异心，那实在是个大麻烦！
徐福可不希望出现孟姜女哭长城的情况，后世多少人借此来讽刺嬴政啊。只要安抚住了劳工，他倒要看看还哪来的孟姜女！
“怎么走神了？”嬴政握了握徐福的手。原本他带着徐福就要往前走的，谁知晓徐福竟然站在那里动也不动。
徐福回过神来，只得道：“在想泗水的那人。”
嬴政无奈一笑，轻抚了抚徐福的头顶，“别急，等过几日，我便带你过去寻这人。”嬴政倒是不舍徐福出手杀人，届时寻着了人，他手刃之便是。
徐福点了点头，与嬴政巡视起了还在建造中的长城。而这一巡视，徐福没想到还当真巡视出了问题来。
如之前那带路的人嘴脸一样，此处不少监工竟是都将自己当做了大爷，将劳工当作了贱民。
这些劳工之中，犯过罪的人是不少，但更多的却是被征召来的，这些人何其无辜，凭什么被当做贱民？徐福越巡视，神色越冷。他忍不住反握住了嬴政的手，甚至还用了用力，道：“这些人倒是比阿政的架子还要大。”
嬴政闻言，免得也不由一冷，“此事我会叫人前来处理。”嬴政对百姓或许没有太多的怜爱之心，但他百姓为他的子民，嬴政的性格便注定了他不允许旁人来欺负他的子民。
见嬴政态度也这般坚决、不容沙子，徐福便放下了心。所以说后世一直传秦始皇残暴不仁，是如何传出去的？身为雄才伟略的一代帝王，又并非魏王、赵王等人可比，秦始皇又怎会如此短视呢？若说错，也不过是秦时刑法的确严苛。而秦始皇主持了几项工程的修建，动用了不少劳工。
且说那刘邦又高尚得到哪里去呢？他放走了逃犯，因而被定罪，于是便借此起义。
放在后世，你有本事，你放几个杀人犯试试？
更别说那刘邦做了皇帝之后，可是立即斩杀了手下的功臣啊。嬴政与他一比，都实在不如他心狠手辣！若是嬴政也那样多疑，李斯、赵高还能有害死他的机会？还会有胡亥成为秦二世的历史吗？
徐福心中愤懑之下，竟是不自觉地越想越远了，他忙收住思绪，拉了拉嬴政的手，“走吧。”
嬴政点头，立即带着徐福离开了这里。这里尚在修建之中，灰尘漫天，还是不适合久留的。
回去之后，嬴政便立即叫来了负责人，连通他的官位一起夺了，之后又临时抽调了官员前来，并且还将蒙毅都调来了。文官难免镇不住场子，而蒙毅手握大军，与他兄长一样的脾气，他同文官协手，要管住这些人可就容易多了。
换了一大批人之后，被换下的人也迎来了他们的结局。
杀这么多人，嬴政向来采用极为粗暴的方式，挖坑、掩埋之。徐福听过之后，也只是轻轻一叹。难怪后世总说他坑儒了。老挖坑埋人，传来传去的，自然便成了坑儒。
徐福与嬴政商量着提高了部分劳工的待遇之后，方才启程前往了沛县。
chapters.translated_text:
Silence spread in the air.

After a long while, Ying Zheng couldn't help asking, "Afu, what's wrong?" Why had he suddenly fallen silent?

"Is this what the Great Wall looks like?" Xu Fu's voice almost trembled uncontrollably.

Sensing his disappointment, Ying Zheng asked, "What else?"

It was only then that Xu Fu realized his previous imagination had been way too rosy! The Great Wall was supposed to look like this, because at this time... it! Was! Not! Finished! Yet!

"It's nothing," Xu Fu shook his head, slowly exhaling a breath. To see the Qin Great Wall, he would probably have to wait at least a few years, right? What could be seen at this moment was merely a rudimentary form. Just thinking about it felt a bit hard to bear.

After all, the Great Wall seen by later generations was the version reconstructed during the Ming Dynasty.

Noticing Xu Fu's low spirits, Ying Zheng said, "Do you feel like there's nothing much to see?"

Xu Fu nodded.

Ying Zheng laughed heartily, "What harm is there in that? The Great Wall has been under construction since the Western Zhou Dynasty, only that the sections were scattered and some were truly in a wretched state. Now I have simply ordered people to repair and connect them, so that a unified defense line can be formed to deter foreign tribes from daring to invade Qin."

Xu Fu nodded. So that was how it was... it had actually existed as far back as the Western Zhou Dynasty.

"If you want to see the walls built in the past, I can take you to see them right now."

Hearing this, Xu Fu hesitated, but shook his head. The old walls hadn't been built under Ying Zheng's direction, and somehow... somehow they didn't seem quite as appealing to him anymore. "Just taking a walk around will do," Xu Fu said aloud. Rather than looking at the Great Wall, he'd rather go look at the laborers first. He was very curious about their lives, and if he could take the opportunity to improve them, that would be even better.

Building the Great Wall involved one hundred thousand laborers; if these people harbored evil intentions, it would truly be a huge trouble!

Xu Fu certainly didn't want a situation like Meng Jiangnü weeping at the Great Wall to happen, which so many people in later generations used to satirize Ying Zheng. As long as the laborers were appeased, he'd like to see where any Meng Jiangnü would come from!

"Why are you zoning out?" Ying Zheng held Xu Fu's hand. He had originally intended to walk forward with Xu Fu, who knew the latter would just stand there without moving at all.

Recovering his senses, Xu Fu had no choice but to say, "I was thinking about that person from Sishui."

Ying Zheng smiled helplessly and gently stroked the top of Xu Fu's head. "Don't rush. In a few days, I will take you to find this person." Ying Zheng was reluctant to let Xu Fu dirty his hands with killing; when the time came and the person was found, he would execute him himself.

Xu Fu nodded and patrolled the still-under-construction Great Wall with Ying Zheng. And during this patrol, Xu Fu didn't expect that they would genuinely patrol and uncover problems.

Just like the attitude of the guide from earlier, quite a few overseers here actually regarded themselves as lords and treated the laborers as lowly scum.

Among these laborers, quite a few had committed crimes, but many more had been conscripted. How innocent these people were—by what right were they treated as lowly scum? The more Xu Fu inspected, the colder his expression became. He couldn't help tightening his grip on Ying Zheng's hand, even applying some force as he said, "These people put on even bigger airs than Azheng."

Hearing this, Ying Zheng's expression inevitably turned cold as well. "I will have people deal with this matter." Ying Zheng might not have had excessive benevolence toward the common people, but they were his subjects; his personality dictated that he would not allow others to bully his subjects.

Seeing that Ying Zheng's attitude was equally resolute and intolerant of evildoers, Xu Fu's heart settled. So how had the rumors that Qin Shi Huang was brutal and inhumane been spread down through later generations? As a monarch of grand talent and great vision, incomparable to the Kings of Wei or Zhao, how could Qin Shi Huang have been so short-sighted? If there were any faults, it was merely that the penal laws of Qin were indeed harsh, and Qin Shi Huang had overseen the construction of several projects, employing numerous laborers.

Besides, how noble was that Liu Bang anyway? He had let a fugitive escape and was thus convicted, so he used that as a pretext to start a rebellion.

Put in the context of later generations, if you've got the ability, try letting a few murderers go and see what happens!

Not to mention that after Liu Bang became emperor, he immediately executed the meritorious ministers who had served under him. Compared to him, Ying Zheng wasn't ruthless enough! If Ying Zheng had been that paranoid, would Li Si and Zhao Gao have had the opportunity to harm him? Would there have been the history of Huhai becoming the Second Emperor of Qin?

Filled with indignation in his heart, Xu Fu unconsciously let his thoughts wander further and further. He hurriedly reined in his thoughts and tugged at Ying Zheng's hand. "Let's go."

Ying Zheng nodded and immediately led Xu Fu away from the place. Since it was still under construction and dust filled the air, it was still not a suitable place to linger for long.

Upon returning, Ying Zheng immediately summoned the person in charge and stripped him of his official rank as well. Afterward, he temporarily transferred other officials over, and even brought Meng Yi along. Civil officials inevitably struggled to command respect and hold the ground, while Meng Yi held military command and shared the same temperament as his elder brother; with him cooperating with the civil officials, keeping these people in line would be much easier.

After a large batch of people was replaced, those who were replaced also met their respective ends.

When it came to executing so many people, Ying Zheng had always adopted an extremely brutal method—digging pits and burying them. After hearing about it, Xu Fu could only let out a soft sigh. No wonder later generations always said he buried Confucian scholars alive. Constantly digging pits to bury people, passed on from mouth to mouth, naturally turned into burying Confucian scholars.

After discussing with Ying Zheng to improve the treatment of some of the laborers, Xu Fu finally set off for Peixian.
