The path of lust, once touched, is enough to intoxicate a person, especially when the object of that desire is someone you particularly adore. Thus, Xu Fu truly experienced what it meant to be unable to get out of bed.

Having stayed in Xianyang Palace for a month, compared to when he first arrived, Xu Fu already carried a different aura about him. No matter how cold his eyes were, one could still sense the deep, hidden spring of desire within. Xu Fu was unaware of the changes in himself, but he was extremely fond of the crimson hickeys on his body. Whenever they began to fade after a few days, Qin Shi Huang would imprint them again; his behavior was truly overbearing to the extreme.

By this moment, Xu Fu realized that his ability to live in Xianyang Palace was not because Qin Shi Huang favored him, nor was it for him to refine elixirs or practice divination. This "favor" was truly something else entirely!

Was he to become the Emperor's plaything?

Just thinking about it made Xu Fu feel as if his flesh were being carved away.

Xu Fu adopted an extremely uncooperative stance, yet Qin Shi Huang still had ways to deal with him. The disparity in physical strength made it easy for Xu Fu to be pinned down, and the more he resisted, the more often he was pinned down. On the desk, in the great hall, on the rug, on the small couch... even in the garden, in the pavilion, in the Xianyang tavern... Xu Fu could clearly feel that Qin Shi Huang was telling him this was a punishment; the less cooperative he was, the more severe the consequences would become.

In the blink of an eye, it was the end of the year, the time of the La sacrifice. Qin Shi Huang fed Xu Fu some wine, and unable to hold his liquor, Xu Fu fell drunk into his arms. After Qin Shi Huang carried him back and naturally removed his clothes to enjoy him, Xu Fu displayed a completely different charm while intoxicated, and his body even cooperated quite a bit. After a night of pleasure, when he woke up the next day, Xu Fu saw his long-lost tortoise shells and alchemy furnace.

Xu Fu felt it was truly ironic; it was as if he had served Qin Shi Huang well, and in return, Qin Shi Huang had bestowed a reward upon him.

But life in Xianyang Palace was truly unbearable, and only these things could help Xu Fu find a sense of familiarity. Qin Shi Huang gave him partial freedom; he could linger in the palace or head to the alchemy room.

Xu Fu desperately wanted to divine where his future lay, but he could divine nothing at all. Xu Fu could only wait, waiting for the days to pass by without purpose.

This peace was soon broken.

When Xu Fu was able to walk out of the palace, he saw Qin Shi Huang's offspring, the princes of Qin. Walking in front was Prince Fusu. The aura Fusu carried was completely different from Qin Shi Huang's; it was hard to imagine he was Qin Shi Huang's son. Xu Fu couldn't help but look at him with surprise.

Fusu clearly saw him as well. Fusu naturally knew of Xu Fu's identity, but who his father chose to favor was not something he could interfere with. Fusu merely gave Xu Fu a faint smile, then led his younger brother away in another direction.

Xu Fu also wanted to head in that direction, but unfortunately, his range of movement ended there. Xu Fu stared at that side for a long time before finally turning around. "Let's go back."

The palace attendants behind him lowered their heads, following Xu Fu in silence as they escorted him back to the palace.

Xu Fu suddenly felt incredibly bored.

No one to talk to, nothing to do, and nowhere to go.

Xu Fu felt that living such days was too suffocating; he didn't even doubt that he would be suffocated to death just like this.

After returning to the hall, it was another dull afternoon. Xu Fu stayed there for the afternoon, the sunlight and autumn breeze brushing his face, and he fell asleep on the small couch without realizing it.

Xu Fu was awakened by a forceful kiss, and at the same time, a large hand reached into his robes, vigorously kneading his buttocks. Xu Fu woke up with a start, but once awake, he couldn't break free from the shackles of the other's embrace. By then, the other's kisses had already spread to his neck. Xu Fu couldn't help but frown, angrily saying, "What are you doing?"

Qin Shi Huang pressed him tightly beneath him and whispered, "You stared at Fusu for a long time today. Why?"

Xu Fu's mind went blank, unable to process the question for a moment. "...What?"

Ignoring the confusion on his face, the other man pinned him down and stripped off his robes. Xu Fu understood immediately; this was another punishment. For what? Oh, for taking one extra look at Prince Fusu during the day? But who was Fusu? Fusu was his son! Did he have to control this too? Xu Fu was so angry his chest hurt. But soon, he had no energy left for chest pain, because what followed was pain in his rear.

Xu Fu was pinned to the small couch and fucked until he was limp, then carried to the bed.

From then on, Xu Fu knew exactly how terrifying Qin Shi Huang's possessiveness was. Later, he didn't believe it and tried it again. That day, after Qin Shi Huang returned to the hall, Xu Fu was still sitting at the desk. Qin Shi Huang strode over, pinned him to the desk, and fucked him again.

Xu Fu held his breath, but he never dared to try that again.

Qin Shi Huang didn't reason with him either. Before starting, he would ask, "Did you stare at XX all day today?" or "Did you talk to XX today?"... This barely counted as a reminder of what Xu Fu had done, and then he would say nothing more, not even a threat like, "If I catch you again, I'll fuck you to death."

Xu Fu once suspected that he actually enjoyed seeing him step outside the lines of the rules, because it gave him an opportunity to impose punishment.

Xu Fu gritted his teeth in anger, but what could he do? Xu Fu fell silent.

In the blink of an eye, it was the twenty-ninth year. The First Emperor went on an inspection tour and encountered bandits. In his fury, he ordered a large-scale search across the country for the escaped thieves.

It was precisely at this moment that Xu Fu suddenly thought of something.

These people had come to kill the First Emperor. The First Emperor was also a man; he would grow old, and he would die. If he died... would he be able to leave this confining cage?

This thought planted a seed in the depths of Xu Fu's heart, waiting for the day it would grow into a towering tree. When a person has already harbored the intent to kill, what can stop him?

Xu Fu didn't know if there had been any emotional change after having this thought, but later, when Qin Shi Huang returned to the hall, he seemed not to notice anything amiss with Xu Fu at all. During this inspection tour, he had suffered a minor injury; a blade had grazed his arm. The imperial physician knelt before him to apply medicine. He was bare-chested, and the wound on his arm looked all the more gruesome in contrast to the surrounding unblemished skin.

Xu Fu sat not far away, watching this scene indifferently.

Qin Shi Huang seemed completely unaware of his gaze. He beckoned to Xu Fu, his voice low and hoarse: "Come here."

Xu Fu hesitated, but thinking of the methods Qin Shi Huang would use once his wound healed, Xu Fu got up and walked over.

When it came to humiliating people, if Qin Shi Huang dared to claim second place, no one would dare claim first. Xu Fu truly did not want to be pinned down in the great hall again with palace attendants standing around.

Xu Fu walked up to Qin Shi Huang. Qin Shi Huang reached out, pulled him to sit on the edge of the bed, and then his other uninjured arm wrapped firmly around Xu Fu. His embrace was tight, carrying that familiar sense of oppression. Xu Fu struggled but couldn't break free.

Qin Shi Huang's arm went around his neck, his fingers gently stroking his cheek and chin. Looking at him, his eyes were deep, giving Xu Fu a feeling of being unable to breathe.

In that instant, he actually felt, ridiculously, that the person before him was filled with deep affection.

After the wound was bandaged, Qin Shi Huang dismissed the physician, and before Xu Fu could recover his senses, he was pushed down again. Xu Fu's eyes were blank for a moment.

He told himself that the look just now was an illusion; how could Qin Shi Huang have a side of deep affection? Rather than affection, it was more like desire. Xu Fu closed his eyes and cooperatively went through the motions.

Life continued on, unhurriedly.

One day, Qin Shi Huang began to bring up the elixir of immortality with Xu Fu again. It turned out that the other alchemists Qin Shi Huang had recruited had no real skill and could not refine the elixir. Qin Shi Huang came to talk to Xu Fu, holding him tightly in his arms, whispering, "I want to live forever with you."

Xu Fu remained silent, but Qin Shi Huang didn't mind; he just waited slowly, waiting for the day Xu Fu would make the immortality elixir.

Time passed even faster.

Xu Fu was truly sick of this life. Qin Shi Huang saw his depression and took him on an eastern inspection tour. Leaving the palace, leaving Xianyang, Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief. When he saw the vast world outside, Xu Fu even faintly felt that the time for him to leave had arrived. Xu Fu meticulously planned an escape.

Qin Shi Huang had an attendant named Zhao Gao, and Zhao Gao had a younger brother named Zhao Cheng. It was with this person's assistance that Xu Fu escaped the camp. He rode his horse, galloping all the way. After reaching the next town, Xu Fu hurriedly ate some food and continued to flee, not daring to stop even when heavy rain began to fall from the sky...

On this journey, Xu Fu traveled for half a month. His white robes were stained gray, and his handsome face was hidden beneath a disheveled appearance. Xu Fu even thought that even if Qin Shi Huang came here, he probably wouldn't recognize him now. Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief. He found an inn to stay in.

He bathed, ate, and had his first good night's sleep in a long time.

When he woke up comfortably, very good, there was no sign of Qin Shi Huang by the bed.

Xu Fu stayed at the inn for three days, his entire being relaxed to the extreme. However, he didn't expect that after cleaning up, revealing his true appearance, he quickly attracted many gazes. To avoid news of him spreading from this town, Xu Fu decided to stay one more night and leave early the next day. For this, Xu Fu settled the bill with the owner in advance.

This night was still comfortable.

Early the next morning, Xu Fu woke up groggily, propping himself up on the bed to sit up. But who would have thought that his hand would press against warm skin? Xu Fu woke up instantly. He turned his head to look at the person beside the bed.

A tall figure with a cold expression, now sleeping with eyes closed, looking very exhausted.

It was Qin Shi Huang!

In a daze, Xu Fu thought he was dreaming.

His movement of getting up eventually woke Qin Shi Huang. Qin Shi Huang sat up, his voice slightly hoarse: "Awake?"

Xu Fu opened his mouth, wanting to ask why he was here, but after thinking about it, he felt this question was truly powerless. With the First Emperor's abilities, it didn't seem strange that he had found him.

Just as Xu Fu was slightly distracted, Qin Shi Huang leaned over and pinned him down.

In the inn, Xu Fu was again fucked until his legs were weak, and in the end, it was Qin Shi Huang who carried him onto the carriage.

"You stayed at the inn for a few days, and I guarded you at the inn for a few days," Qin Shi Huang said nonchalantly. But Xu Fu had been with him for so long that he could clearly feel the suppressed anger and madness in Qin Shi Huang. He wouldn't erupt at the inn, but what about after they returned?

This eastern inspection tour ended without success.

Qin Shi Huang brought him back to Xianyang, and Xu Fu, in a daze, began a life of nightly revelry.

Xu Fu's range of activity was narrowed; he could no longer leave the great hall. Whatever he needed, the palace attendants would bring to him, but the attendants would not speak to him, not even a word of idle chat. Only when Qin Shi Huang returned to the hall would Xu Fu have the illusion of coming back to life. By this time, Xu Fu's heart had sunk.

What was the difference between Qin Shi Huang's behavior and taming a beast?

Would he wait a few more years until all his cold pride was worn away, until he was willing, or even longing, to submit beneath Qin Shi Huang? Because only Qin Shi Huang would speak to him; if even words were denied, that would be truly terrifying. Could that still be considered human?

Xu Fu finally understood why people often said Qin Shi Huang was tyrannical. He wasn't just tyrannical; he was cruel. So cruel that the thought of wanting to kill him rose in Xu Fu's heart once more.

Only if Qin Shi Huang died could the possibility of him being caught again be truly prevented.

·

Xu Fu's gaze lingered on the immortality elixir for a long time; this was the only way he could kill Qin Shi Huang. He had no strength to truss a chicken, and he had no poison in his hands. Only with this could he tamper with things without being discovered. But Xu Fu himself was unwilling to use his alchemy skills to harm others.

To make the desire in his heart firmer, Xu Fu spoke to Ying Zheng about one thing.

"I want to sail east to find the Divine Mountain," Xu Fu said calmly.

Qin Shi Huang laughed: "Divine Mountain? Does Junfang not know that you cannot even leave Xianyang Palace?"

"Don't you want the immortality elixir? Only by finding the Divine Mountain can this medicine be made."

The smile on Qin Shi Huang's face gradually faded. He looked truly terrifying, and Xu Fu couldn't help but purse his lips. Then he heard Qin Shi Huang say: "I will send people to find the Divine Mountain, but that person will not be you."

Xu Fu lowered his eyes, his expression even more indifferent.

See? He restricts your freedom and won't allow you to leave this place even an inch! What is there to be reluctant about in killing such a person? Xu Fu's breathing gradually became lighter.

Qin Shi Huang was unaware of his change.

In the days that followed, Xu Fu began to provoke others even more intensely, because Xu Fu's appearance was truly too outstanding; anyone who saw him couldn't help but admire that beauty. But in Qin Shi Huang's eyes, this was absolutely intolerable. He also began to punish Xu Fu even more severely.

One day, in the great hall, with ministers present, Qin Shi Huang pinned him to the desk. The minister was so frightened that his legs went weak and he knelt on the ground, thinking the Emperor was about to fly into a rage. The palace attendants kept their heads down, unmoved by this. Only after a while did the minister hear a moan. He was startled and carefully looked up, only to see that extremely young-looking person pinned to the desk, with only a glimpse of fair skin exposed, enough to make anyone who saw it harbor wild thoughts.

The minister dared not look again, hurriedly keeping his head down, trembling incessantly.

Xu Fu's dignity was completely torn to shreds and trampled underfoot.

When pleasure and pain intertwined in his heart, Xu Fu's mind was incredibly clear. He could finally make up his mind completely to kill this man.

Since then, Xu Fu became much more well-behaved and disciplined, and occasionally even gave Qin Shi Huang a faint smile. His smile was truly rare; one smile could wash away all of Qin Shi Huang's displeasure and suspicion.

As time went on.

Xu Fu presented the medicine to Qin Shi Huang. Qin Shi Huang did not doubt him; whatever he gave, he took.

Xu Fu stayed by his side for a long time. He remembered the pain Qin Shi Huang had brought him every day. Under such constant suggestion, Xu Fu's heart became harder and harder.

In the 37th year of the First Emperor, Qin Shi Huang took Xu Fu on an eastern inspection tour, accompanied by his youngest son Huhai, Chancellor Li Si, and the Chief of the Carriage Office Zhao Gao.

That year, the First Emperor reached Pingyuanjin and fell seriously ill. Xu Fu waited by his side day and night without drinking. Qin Shi Huang felt extreme tenderness in his heart and forced Xu Fu to eat. In his view, although he had fallen ill, he had finally waited for what he wanted. He had completely obtained Xu Fu.

The First Emperor's condition gradually improved.

They stayed in Shaqiu. With Xu Fu by his side, Qin Shi Huang was in no hurry to return to Xianyang.

He would occasionally look at Xu Fu and sigh, "I am still growing old, while Junfang is still as he was when we first met. If I go first, where will Junfang go?"

Xu Fu was dazed for a moment, but then he thought of sailing east.

Leaving the Qin Dynasty, going to a more distant place. If he could gain freedom, that would be his great fortune; if he unfortunately died at sea, it would be his retribution for killing a man.

Qin Shi Huang laughed at this moment: "If I die, Junfang, you shall be buried with me. We will be buried together in the imperial mausoleum, never to be separated in life or death."

Xu Fu opened his mouth but said nothing.

This man was still so selfish.

While at Shaqiu, the First Emperor's illness recurred, and he became bedridden. Xu Fu still guarded his side, day and night without rest.

Xu Fu sat by his bed, silently counting the days.

Five days, four days...

It was this day; he should die.

What Qin Shi Huang saw in his eyes as deep affection was merely Xu Fu's anxiousness to confirm his death.

In the 37th year of the First Emperor, on the Bingyin day of the seventh month, the First Emperor passed away at Shaqiu.

The last words he said before he died still echoed in Xu Fu's ears: "If I die, Junfang, you must follow!" "I cannot rest easy about you..." "Junfang..."

Junfang...

Xu Fu looked back at him once; the First Emperor's mouth still held a faint smile, and then he left without looking back. Zhao Gao and the others thanked Xu Fu for his cooperation and ordered people to send him away from the Qin Dynasty, to sail east to a more distant place. To prevent anyone from knowing how the First Emperor died, Li Si and Zhao Gao strictly ordered everyone not to mention Xu Fu again, and to claim that this person had left the Great Qin in the 28th year of the First Emperor to search for the three immortal mountains: Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou.

Afterward, they ordered all the manuscripts and notes Xu Fu had left behind to be burned.

Since then, there has been very little historical record of this person.

Where he went after sailing east, who knows?

…

[The First Emperor's original name was Zhao Zheng, born in Handan, Zhao State, where he spent a difficult childhood. After growing up, Zhao Zheng was first oppressed by Lu Buwei, then plotted against by his mother Zhao Ji and the villain Lao Ai, and his younger brother Chengjiao also raised an army to rebel... The young king who ascended the throne at thirteen had already had all his sentimentality worn away. He exiled Lu Buwei, killed Lao Ai, threw Zhao Ji's son to his death, and executed Chengjiao... As he grew older, his temper became increasingly patient and increasingly ruthless.

He spent twenty-six years unifying the six states. He became the first First Emperor.

With power firmly in his hands, Zhao Zheng became increasingly tyrannical and lawless; no one under his command dared to resist him. Even his most favored Prince Fusu, when he angered him, would be sent away to supervise construction.

In the 28th year of the First Emperor, Zhao Zheng met the Guigu disciple Xu Junfang, fell in love at first sight, and wished he could use every means in the world to love him.] Author's note: Meeting the right person at the wrong time still turns out wrong.

chapters.source_text:
秦王在，主心骨便在。
嬴政的气势在那一刻迸发出来，也算是激起了其他人的斗志。老秦人是彪悍骁勇的，他们能吃苦，能隐忍。哪怕他们是秦国的文职官员，也是被逼急了能提着刀上阵的人物，他们随手抄起兵器工具，就与来人拼杀在了一起。
因为嫪毐的借口便是徐福为贼人，那些府兵自然第一个是要擒了徐福，再趁乱杀死嬴政。
他们看徐福冷冷清清、精致秀美的模样，便第一眼就从心底里小瞧了他，认为一人便能将他制服。凶恶的府兵，手持长戈便要朝徐福的腰腹上刺去。徐福躲避不及，被长戈狠狠撞击在腰腹上，对面的府兵洋洋得意，等着而看徐福摔倒在脚边，然后轻轻松松将人提走。徐福原本也做好了被刺中的准备了，谁知道预想中的疼痛并没有到来。
府兵也感觉到手中的长戈抵上了什么坚硬的东西，被狠狠地挡了挡，反倒是震得他掌心一阵发麻。
就在府兵懵了懵的时候，徐福抬脚狠狠一踹，将毫无防备的府兵踹翻在地，随后迅疾地抽走了府兵手中的长戈，然后调转方向，将尖尖的长戈那头对准了地上的府兵。
徐福没有杀过人，他不知道杀人是什么滋味儿。
但对于嬴政来说，不是你死便是我亡，半点没有怜悯可讲，他长剑刺翻一个敌人，转身便从后握住徐福的手臂，往前一推，也并未怎么用力，但那长戈就这样扎进了对方的腹腔之中。
鲜血喷洒！
徐福不自觉地往后退了一步，刚好撞进嬴政的怀里，嬴政也没将徐福推开，反倒是将欲走的徐福反手往怀里搂了搂，带着他就往宗庙后方撤，那边还有后门可以走。
赵高等人也反应相当快地跟了上去，他们相继往后撤退。
明明前面被嫪毐的人堵住了，嬴政当然不会真的带着人硬冲，只要麻痹嫪毐一会儿就足够了。
嫪毐眼看着嬴政的身影就要脱离视线，登时怒喝一声，“还不快追上去？”
府兵们听命，正要往前冲，谁知道那些听了嬴政悬赏令的宫人侍从，还有雍城中的普通武夫，又或是挥舞锄头的农民，竟然也大着胆子闯进来了，与那些府兵们缠斗在了一起。
雍城府兵大都是雍城人，他们敢为了荣华富贵，为了主人家的命令而对秦王下手，但他们未必敢对雍城的平民百姓下手，因为谁也不知道其中是否有自己的亲人。一时间，他们就落了下风，自然也分不出神来去追嬴政一行人。
嫪毐大怒，但是这个时候怪罪也不来及了，他担心被嬴政逃脱之后，死的就是自己。
今日一战，势必要让嬴政丢了性命！
于是嫪毐带着自己的侍从就冲了上去，又另外有侍从匆匆跑出宗庙去请兵。嫪毐虽然见识短浅了些，但他倒不算过分愚蠢，更何况他手底下还吸纳了不少门客，这些门客总是会给他出主意的。为了确保起事万无一失，嫪毐又从赵姬处取了太后印，以赵姬的名义，调了最近城郡的卒兵前来，说是防止秦王冠礼出差错，保护蕲年宫安危。另还有嫪毐所属的太原郡发兵前来，虽然路途远了些，但在总能起到威慑作用。
嫪毐一边狞笑一边咬牙，“我就不信，这样还能被你逃过去！”
徐福被嬴政带着跌跌撞撞地出了后门，外面是一条小巷，众人迅速往外冲去。
有大臣恨恨咬牙道：“快回蕲年宫！嫪毐总不至于胆大到连蕲年宫也敢闯！”
徐福心头忍不住发笑，回蕲年宫？赵姬如今和嫪毐一个鼻孔出气，回到蕲年宫之后，说不定赵姬便正好和嫪毐一起关上门围攻呢。
“回蕲年宫。”嬴政低沉的声音在徐福耳边响起，带着几分喘意。
徐福愣了愣。秦始皇会考虑不到那一点吗？不可能考虑不到！除非……除非是他早有准备，他是故意的？他就是要回到蕲年宫？徐福压下心中的惊讶。顺手从怀中掏了个八卦盘出来，递给了嬴政。
嬴政愣了下，“将这给寡人做什么？”
刚才在怀中替徐福挡了那长戈的是卜筮所用的龟甲，那一下子顶上去，也不过是让龟甲背上多了条裂纹，其余的却是半点伤口也无。徐福始终惦记着从龟甲上占卜所得的信息，就算秦始皇早已将一切都算计好了，那他也要尽量减少秦始皇受伤的可能。不然，历史出了意外，秦始皇翘了，那他可怎么办？
“八卦盘，放于胸前可作护心镜。”徐福一本正经地道。
其余大臣听罢，也纷纷劝嬴政收下。
今日本是为加冠而来，谁会穿盔甲，谁会带武器？和叛军比起来，他们就像是一群手无寸铁的羔羊，任人宰割。现在能有个东西顶替护心镜，不管之后是否有作用，现在也能给大家吃一颗定心丸，保障住秦王的安危，那他们才能放心。
嬴政挑了挑眉，深深地看了一眼徐福，随后将那八卦盘揣进了怀中。
嬴政此时想的是，原来徐福固执地要将那么多东西都带上，原来是早有准备。
徐福接收不到嬴政内心对其的称赞，他抬手按了按怀中的龟甲，拔腿快步与嬴政一起往前疾走，他们上了车驾，急速朝着王宫而去，这时倒是没有谁会指摘不合礼宜了。等拉着车驾的马儿跑得力气用尽，他们也终于抵达了王宫。
“王上？”宫门口的守卫士兵觉得很是诧异，他们可没想到自己会迎来狼狈的秦王和朝中大臣。
有大臣嘴快，忙喊道：“嫪毐谋反！尔等还不带人前去阻击？”
这些守卫们却是互相对视一眼，低下了头。
大臣只是以为那些守卫是只听从秦王的，便也没觉得可疑。而嬴政看也没看那守卫一眼，下了车驾，疾步朝里走。徐福也加快了脚步，心脏在胸腔中砰砰直跳。他脑子里有根弦一直绷得紧紧的，却不敢有丝毫松懈，见着嬴政往前走，他便立刻跟上。剩下的人犹豫几秒，也只能跟了上去。
待到嬴政等人入了蕲年宫以后，那王宫的守卫却是突然拔高嗓门，道：“关宫门！”
关了一道还有另一道，嫪毐便是带着人从另一道宫门进来了，而这一道宫门之所以会关上，不过是为了防止嬴政等人发觉不对，逃离蕲年宫而已。
可以说，为置嬴政于死地，嫪毐花了不少的功夫。
进入蕲年宫后，众人以为得救，便跪坐于地，互相检查伤处，稍作休息。
唯有嬴政下巴紧紧绷着，站在殿内最高的台阶上，望着殿门之外，那一头是另一扇宫门处。
徐福就站在嬴政下首的位置，他深吸一口气，缓缓道：“要来了。”
嬴政向徐福投去了诧异的一眼，他没想到徐福看出了他的用意。
嫪毐余党，除去带到宗庙的人以外，更多的存于蕲年宫中，他为了这一年，想来是布了不少的手段，要绞杀嫪毐，当然是要将他的全部势力顺带一起绞杀。嬴政曾赐嫪毐山阳地，又以河西太原郡更为毐国。嫪毐在这些处的势力，看似庞大，但却属于鞭长莫及的范围，只要嫪毐在这里被嬴政拿下，他的势力自然就能全部打散。
所以嬴政不做便已，一出手便要将嫪毐毫无遗漏地一次解决。
徐福初时看不出来，那是因为他对这些本身并不敏锐，更何况，他从来不觉得自己能猜透秦始皇的心思。只是毕竟他和秦始皇相处也有一段时间了，总能推测出一二来，于是渐渐的便窥得了整个布局的全貌。
若他没有猜错，嬴政的后手应该也要到了，到时候瓮中捉鳖，瓮还是这个蕲年宫，但鳖却会变成嫪毐。
随后又是一阵脚步声，和兵甲摩擦声渐渐近了。
众人惶惶不安，互相搀扶着站起身，齐齐看向嬴政，“王上，这……”他们不知道那是援兵，还是叛军。
嬴政没有说话，他目光冰寒地盯着殿门口。而接着很快，众人的疑惑也得到了解答，因为那得意洋洋进门而来的还是嫪毐和他的党羽……
不少人都慌了。
嫪毐怎么会来得如此之快？难道王宫之中还有里应外合之人吗？
徐福不自觉地握紧了手中的长戈。他其实挺想直接捅到嫪毐头上去的，奈何他没有其他穿越主角的武力光环。
这时他听见嬴政颇有闲心地转头笑问：“你猜援兵何时来？”
听到援兵二字，徐福就知道自己心中的猜想得到了验证，他握着长戈的手不由得松了松。心态陡然一变，也跟着轻松起来，他转头回应嬴政，嘴角还微微噙着笑意，“我数十声。”
嬴政忍不住笑了，“你如此笃定？”
“是。”
远远地看见站在高阶上的嬴政还能露出轻松的笑容，嫪毐顿时感受到了侮辱，憋住火气，道：“到了如此地步，王上还能发笑？”他不明白，为什么他都已经逼到跟前，嬴政还能维持轻松之态？嬴政的临危不乱令他觉得羞辱，而嬴政站在那里的王者气势，又令他颇为嫉妒。那是出身市井的他，怎么也无法与之相比的。
嬴政的存在就是讽刺他的，正应了那句，穿上龙袍也不像太子的话。
“大胆嫪毐！竟敢公然谋反！你可知你犯下的是何等大错？”有人义愤填膺地出声。
嫪毐冷笑不已，“待我做了秦王，哪里还有什么大错？你们才是大错！”
王宫守卫、嫪毐侍从，还有从邻县赶过来的士兵，这些都成为了嫪毐的底气，他不再掩饰自己的狼子野心，将丑陋的面容瞬间暴露无遗。
嬴政一直没有开口。与嫪毐对话，他都觉得自降身份。
徐福没再沉默，他冷睨着嫪毐，缓缓道：“刚才不是问王上为何发笑吗？不止王上想笑，我也想笑。我想笑你的愚蠢。进了蕲年宫，如此耀武扬威，实在像是民间耍把戏的。”
见徐福见他比做耍把戏的，又想起之前徐福和嬴政联手耍了他的事儿，嫪毐脸上挂不住，双眼里迸射出恶毒的光芒来，他抓紧了手中的长剑，怒吼一声，“给我杀了他们！”
徐福突然转头，低声对嬴政道：“十下，我数到了。”
他话音刚落，殿外突然响起了厮杀声，嫪毐不得不顿住脚步，转身去看，这一看，他才发觉那些被他纠集着去搅乱冠礼的贵族府兵和门客们，个个都愤怒地与他的人厮杀在一起，口中还骂着“嫪毐小人”。嫪毐顿时被气得七窍生烟。
这些个狗腿子，如何骂他是小人？
他嫪毐最恨别人骂他小人！
怒极失去理智的嫪毐当即发作，“把那人的嘴给我撕下来！”他的侍从踌躇不前，低声道：“长信侯可勿要被奸人挑拨，这些人为何突然叛离，还要先问个原因啊！”
嫪毐也还真的就冷声问了，“你们竟然敢骂我是小人？叫你们主子来！”
那些人却更是愤怒，“就是主人吩咐我等前来的，嫪毐小人欺人太甚！若不是为了钱银，谁愿意与你干这档子买卖？偏偏你言而无信，将我们主人肆意玩弄于鼓掌中，不仅半分钱不见，还命人嘲笑我等，眼皮子浅，下等人！呸！谁不知道你长信侯才是真正的下等人出身！如今我们不如捉了你，朝秦王要个赏钱！”
嫪毐听得懵了，他何时言而无信了？又何时命人去嘲笑他们了？这群人竟敢揭他伤疤！还妄想拿下他去讨赏钱？
嫪毐又怒又急，但是没等他想个明白，已经有手快的，扔了把弯刀过来，直直朝着嫪毐的脸上扎来，嫪毐仓皇躲过，弯刀却是划伤了他的脖颈，留下一道浅浅的血痕，嫪毐暴跳如雷，模样又十分狼狈，哪里还找得回刚才半分的得意姿态？
徐福憋不住笑了。
嫪毐说要给那些贵族们分的钱，不会就是想要从“常姓商人”那里得到吧？那派去辱骂府兵和门客的人，应当也是秦始皇派去的。他还真是从前到后，都将嫪毐和赵姬好好坑了一把啊！
要玉玺没玉玺了，要助力没助力了，还反倒将助力得罪了。
“给我杀！全部杀了！”嫪毐气疯了，倚着侍从，狂舞着双手下令。
兵卒们一扑而上，混乱至极。
这时却又有马蹄声和脚步声近了，徐福只听得殿外一声怒喝，“蒙武、李信在此！擒拿叛军首领嫪毐！”
那轰轰的马蹄声和沉重的脚步声，都化作了一记强有力的战鼓，瞬间唤醒了所有人的斗志，内外呼应，殿内的人和殿外的人对嫪毐一行人，形成了夹击之势。
李信年少气盛，率着兵卒在前开路，硬生生杀出一条路来，直接冲到了嬴政的面前，随后将嬴政等人团团护在包围圈里，嫪毐的人马再难接近分毫。
前一刻，还仿佛胜券在握的叛军，这一刻变成了待宰的羔羊。
嫪毐没有半点军事素养，骨子里本来就不过是个小人，除了媚上逢迎，真正遇到这样的情况，很快便慌乱了起来，嘴里还胡乱喊着让侍从逃出去寻太后来救场。
嫪毐是真的怕死，他怕自己输了，被嬴政弄死，所以他需要赵姬来保他一命。
可此时，连赵姬也是自身难保。
蒙武彪悍，将嫪毐擒于马下，他身材高大，直接嫪毐提了起来，面向其余叛军，高喊一声，“尔等还不速速投降？”
余下叛军茫然四顾，正纠结于放不放下兵器的时候，已经被一旁的兵卒按倒在地，不服从者一刀斩首，鲜血很快铺满了整个蕲年宫的殿门。
徐福有些不自在地别过了脸。这样一幕带给他的冲击力还是太大了。
嬴政也没觉得什么，他只当是方士有一颗怜悯之心。
而从头至尾，嬴政都维持着那副高高在上，半分不乱的姿态，徐福都不得不感叹，实在不是谁都能做始皇的！光是这副姿态，已经将太多人远远甩在其后了。
至此，嫪毐之乱，被平定了。
蒙武和李信两员大将，上前来向嬴政见礼。
就是在这样的一座被鲜血染红的宫殿之中，嬴政淡然面对众人，声量不大，但却足够铿锵有力地道：“即日起，寡人亲政。”
秦国被赵太后和嫪毐分走的政权，即将回到嬴政的手中，嬴政对于秦国的掌控力也开始走向高峰。
这是秦始皇在未来统一六国之前，迈出的第一步。
徐福觉得自己莫名其妙都被影响得燃起来了，他扔下了手中握了许久的长戈，手指还隐隐有些酸疼，那是因为之前用力太过留下的后遗症。
此时，众人拜服。
劫后余生的众人倒是一时忽视了，还有个唯一与嬴政同站在高阶上的——徐福。他们突然跪拜而下，倒像是连着徐福也跪了一样。
这等细节没有人会去在意了。
雍城中的厮杀也逐渐接近了尾声，剩下逃窜的叛军，被雍城百姓和其余府兵围剿了个干净。
嬴政理了理衣袍，突然对徐福道：“陪寡人再一趟太后宫中。”
嬴政心中的滋味也很复杂。他怎么会想到，在他收服权利的过程中，会是徐福从头陪他到尾？赵太后宫中的事并不适合让太多人知道，嬴政这时当然是带亲信过去最好。
见证了一出胜仗的徐福心情正好，想也不想便点了头。
于是身上还沾染着淡淡血腥气的秦王政，在行过成年礼后第一次踏入了母亲赵姬的宫殿。
*
“侍医可来了？侍医来了吗？”宫女不断探头往外看，慌慌张张地问。
另外几名宫女也急得脸色悲苦，牙齿紧咬，“这可怎么办才好……太后身下可是见红了……”
有个年纪小的宫女怯怯地问：“会不会落胎呀？”
“胡说什么？”年长的宫女一巴掌扇到她的脸上，“太后怎是你能诅咒的？”
小宫女委委屈屈地捂住脸，幼时她曾见过家中长姐也如此模样，可不像是要落胎么？
赵姬有气无力地靠在床上，身下慢慢渗出血来，她只能感觉到隐隐的抽痛和腿间滑腻的感觉，顿时惶恐到了极点，她厉声问：“侍医呢？死哪里去了？”话出口，她突然痛得低呼一声，气息一下子就降了下去，气弱得也发不了脾气了。
“太、太后，侍医不、不见踪影。”宫女战战兢兢地跪在她的床前。
一定是他，一定是嬴政故意为之，才让她找不到侍医。赵姬这时终于想起了嬴政，她死死地捏住宫女的手腕，“你快去，快去见王上，告诉他，说我病得厉害，让他……让他过来……让他遣个侍医来……”
“是、是……”宫女被赵姬脸上略略凶狠的表情吓得连连点头，刚想要挣开赵姬站起身来，就听见背后的有人哆嗦着喊了声，“王上。”
赵姬一下子就松开了宫女的手腕，她看向了围屏的方向，嬴政和徐福一前一后走了过来，其后还有赵高等人。
赵姬脸色微变，“政儿，政儿！你带这么多人闯我的寝宫，是什么意思？”赵姬感觉自己被冒犯了，她仍旧没有认清形势，都这个时候了还撂下了脸子。
“母后不是派人要寻我吗？”嬴政笑了笑，反问赵姬。
赵姬立刻痛呼出声，“政儿，快为我遣侍医来……”
嬴政倒是答应得爽快，转头对赵高道：“将人带上来。”
那侍医正是被赵姬和嫪毐买通的人，只不过他此刻却抖成了个筛子，几乎是爬到了赵姬床边。
嬴政居高临下地瞥了一眼赵姬，先是给赵姬造成了不小的心理压力，随后才轻飘飘地说了一句，“嫪毐谋反，已经被寡人拿下。”
赵姬猛地抬头看向嬴政，脸色一白，身体颤抖，她目光复杂地瞪着嬴政，语不成调。
嬴政转身走了出去。
这一招实在漂亮啊！徐福暗自咋舌，随即也跟着转身出去。等他们刚刚跨出寝宫，就立刻听见了赵姬凄声尖叫的声音。嬴政并没有急着离开，而是站在宫殿外的台阶上，目光看着不知道何方。随着寝宫内传出的叫声越发地响，嬴政的脸色也越来越冷。
徐福知道这个时候他的心理应该经历了一段曲折的变化。不过徐福不太擅长灌心灵鸡汤，所以就只能收紧下巴，眼观鼻鼻观心。两人都是沉默冷清地站着，落日逐渐西下，余晖披洒在他们的身上，仿佛罩上了一层微红的光。赵高和其余侍从站在一旁，他们看着嬴政和徐福方向，顿觉这两人仿佛要羽化登仙了一般。
良久过去，里头才跑出来一名小宫女，往地上一跪，“王上……孩子、孩子生出来了。”
“哦？”嬴政头也不回地应了一声。
那小宫女却是继续往下道：“可是，可是没一会儿，便、便夭折了……”
嬴政更像是早在预料之中一般，他冷冷地吐出一句话来，“母后重病，雍城不宜再住，即日起迁往贡阳宫修养。”这段话被他不带感情地念完，就算是定下了赵姬的命运。
徐福对这段历史只隐约记得个轮廓，碍于曾经的母子情谊和血缘关系，历史上的嬴政似乎的确只是将赵姬逐出了咸阳宫。
对于一个已经享乐已久，贪恋舒适荣华的女人来说，失去如今地位为她带来的一切，便是足够狠的惩罚。
宫女或许是转身进殿以后便将这段话转述给了赵姬，里面竟然传出了赵姬破口大骂的声音。
回到蕲年宫以后，嬴政并未做停留，他下令带着叛军，马上回到咸阳，并对嫪毐施车裂之行，嫪毐闻言，也气得对嬴政破口大骂，只不过他嘴上骂的话比赵姬骂得要脏多了。昔日的长信侯落魄后竟是如此模样，其余人都忍不住露出了嫌恶的表情。这样的市井混混，也不知道是哪里来的勇气，竟是妄图抢夺秦王之位！
等紧绷的神经松下来之后，徐福就发现自己长时间没进食的胃不太配合了，它开始隐隐作痛了。
偏偏嬴政已经上了车驾，其余人也都是拿出干粮在路上吃，而完全没有干粮这玩意儿的徐福愣住了。还是赵高走了过来，微笑着递给了徐福食物。递来的食物虽然难吃至极，不过好歹能果腹，徐福也不讲究那么多了，低声道了谢，便开始吃了起来。
他刚刚咬了一口，还没来得及嫌弃那饼实在咯牙，道路两旁突然杀出了一队人来，直直奔着后方的嫪毐而去。
徐福心脏一紧，顿时想到了自己某句还没实现的批语。
或许真的是命中注定的怎么也躲不过。
俗话说秦桧还有仨朋友呢。纵使是嫪毐这样的人，也有拼死前来救他的人，这些人趁着队伍毫无防备之时下手，经历了一天的惊心动魄，走在回咸阳的路上，众人多少都有些松懈，自然被钻了措手不及的空子。
赵高与侍从等人牢牢护卫在嬴政周围，徐福低头看了看自己的身板，他觉得自己不用去挡着秦始皇了，他身体那么脆弱，还是站远一点，到时候躲快一点，保命为上。
徐福正想着呢，偏偏那些贼人就跟疯了一样，见营救嫪毐无望，径直朝他冲了过来。徐福的表情僵了僵，连忙后退躲避，嬴政见状，伸出长臂将徐福一捞，搂着他的腰就带到了车驾上，所有人都怔了怔，没想到嬴政会有此举。那贼人高举着的兵器欲上前，却已经被其余涌上来的兵卒用长戈刺倒在地，鲜血迸溅。
徐福的心脏狂跳不已，没想到刚才死亡距离自己那么近。
背后的嬴政突然“嘶”了一声，似乎是倒抽了一口气。
不是吧？真的受伤了？徐福连忙挣开嬴政的手臂，回转身去看他，只见嬴政沉着脸从腰间拔下了一只青铜制的矛头，竟然是刚才无意中飞来的兵器尖端部分。
徐福有点哭笑不得，这样也能受伤？还真是契合了那句话。
腰腹受伤，却无悔意。
秦始皇想要除掉的都已经除掉，目的皆已达到，而这个乌龙意外并不算什么，他当然不会有什么悔意。可以说这次蕲年宫之变，已经在秦始皇的处理下，解决得十分到位了。
落在队伍后面的李信带兵上前来，将这些贼人全部镇压，一个不留地处理了个干净。
徐福没回头去看杀人的场面，他僵在了嬴政的身旁，他这才想起自己被拦腰抱到属于秦王的车驾之上，怪不得其他人看自己的眼神那样的怪异。他继续做出面不改色的模样，装作淡定地跳下了车驾，仿佛刚才什么也没发生过。而嬴政脸色黑沉，他捂着腰侧的伤口，冷声道：“将嫪毐赶到前面去，若是走得慢了，便用鞭子抽打。若是又有贼人前来营救，全部就地格杀。”
“是！”众人齐齐应了声，声音震天响，将后面的嫪毐惊得脸色发白，两股战战，最后是被人跌跌撞撞地推到队伍前去的。
刚才那些贼人的尸首挂在后面囚车上示众，之后哪里还敢有人来劫嫪毐，或是刺杀嬴政？
嫪毐被鞭子抽打着往前走，仿佛真的驱逐着牲畜一般，徐福时不时就能听见他的哀嚎惨叫之声，只不过，不会有人同情他。
徐福在心中骂了句嫪毐活该，一低头，就看见自己右手还攥着食物呢。刚才那么危机的关头，都没忘记紧紧握住。徐福顿了顿，低头又咬了起来。
嬴政坐在车驾之上，原本腰侧的伤口疼得有些让人难以忍耐，谁知道他无意中一低头，偏看见了徐福淡定无恙低头吃饼的模样。
嬴政：……
好像疼痛都在一瞬间缓解了呢。

始皇九年，嫪毐作乱，秦王早有闻，发卒攻毐，斩杀无数叛军。太后迁于贡阳宫。
为了完全平复嫪毐的叛乱，捉拿余党，嬴政又命昌平君及昌文君前往河西太原郡镇压。
嫪毐则是被带进了咸阳宫中。
他是被人用车推进来，不是对他的待遇变好了，只是嫪毐被鞭子抽得浑身血肉模糊，双脚发软，难以再迈出一步，再往下抽，说不定就活活抽死了。
嫪毐为嬴政心头大恨，怎么可能让他如此轻易地就死去？
嬴政沐浴换衣，又上了伤药，这才在殿内召见已经半死不活的嫪毐。而徐福此时捂着肚子默默去了茅厕。哦，水喝少了，难受。等徐福再回来时，刚好听见赵高宣读嬴政的命令。
“车裂以徇，灭其宗。及其舍人，轻者为鬼薪。及夺爵迁蜀四千余家，家房陵。”
听到车裂二字，嫪毐顿时就慌了，他躺在地上挣扎不已，那一小块地方都被他身上的血蹭得脏污至极。
“不！不要杀我！不！”嫪毐畏惧死亡，连忙没有尊严地在嬴政面前求饶。之前他一心畅想着占据秦王位，嬴政性命也被他捏在手中的一幕。那时，他可是半分没有想到，他失败了，等待着他的就是这样严酷的刑罚。
徐福走进殿来，打量嫪毐一番，面色略略怪异。
据传闻说嫪毐那物巨大，更能转动车轮而毫发无损，不知道车裂的时候，会不会顺便也将他那物绑上。太污了……徐福连忙打住自己的联想。
或许是无比惊惧之下，嫪毐竟然失禁了，难闻的味道在宫殿内弥漫开，那些宫人都朝他投去了鄙夷的目光。不过此时嫪毐也顾不上觉得羞耻或恼怒了，命都要丢了……他口中还连连喊着让嬴政放他一条狗命。
不过徐福觉得么，说他是狗命，那都侮辱了狗啊！
嬴政皱起眉，不想再见嫪毐的丑态，多看一眼都觉得伤眼，于是他命人将嫪毐带下去，“车裂前，先将其它刑具也供长信侯享受一番。”
此话一出，嫪毐顿时挣扎得更厉害了，口中发出凄厉惨叫声，侍从堵上他的嘴，很快将人抬出去了。
已是入夜时分，徐福被宫人带着去沐浴换洗一番后，便回到了嬴政的寝宫，在这一场叛乱之中，嬴政耗费了不少的心力，也只有在这个时候，刚刚加冠成年的秦王才会露出些微疲惫的神色来。
他揉了揉额角，与徐福一同躺在床上，因为累极，倒是很快便入睡了。
还是这一晚，仍旧有很多人无法安眠。
负责刑讯的狱卒们，嫪毐逃窜在外的党羽们，还有曾经巴结过他的贵族们……
*
翌日，徐福缓缓从睡梦中醒来，在宫女的伺候下洗漱、用膳，没有一个人敢怠慢他。而嬴政早就起了，这是他亲政后第一次上朝，意义至关重要。
徐福用过早膳之后，便有常跟在赵高身后的内侍走了进来，冲他弓腰道：“我送徐先生回去。”
回去？
徐福怔了一下，这才想起自己的住所并不是王宫，只是恰好因为冠礼之事，才被秦始皇留在宫中的，秦始皇那时都只是为了避免让他走漏消息。现在冠礼顺利结束，他自然该回到奉常寺。
徐福站起身来，冲内侍浅淡地笑笑，“好。”
内侍备了马车，徐福坐上去后，很快便抵达了奉常寺的大门口。
他下了马车，抬头看了看奉常寺的牌匾，明明才不过大半月，却好像是多年没踏足过了一样。
徐福整了整身上的衣袍，抬脚踏了进去。
chapters.translated_text:
As long as the King of Qin was present, the spiritual pillar of the state remained.

Ying Zheng’s imposing aura burst forth at that exact moment, effectively igniting the fighting spirit of the others. The old Qin people were fierce and valiant; they could endure hardship and exercise forbearance. Even though they were civil officials of Qin, when pushed to the limit, they were the kind of people who would draw their swords and take to the battlefield. Snatching up weapons and tools at random, they began to fight desperately against the intruders.

Because Lao Ai’s excuse was that Xu Fu was a criminal, those garrison troops naturally sought to capture Xu Fu first, and then take advantage of the chaos to kill Ying Zheng.

Seeing Xu Fu’s detached, delicate, and exquisite appearance, they underestimated him from the very bottom of their hearts at first glance, believing that a single person could subdue him. A ferocious garrison soldier, holding a long halberd, lunged to stab Xu Fu in the waist and abdomen. Xu Fu failed to dodge in time, and was struck hard in the waist and abdomen by the halberd. The garrison soldier opposite him was immensely proud and smug, waiting to see Xu Fu collapse at his feet and then effortlessly lift him away. Xu Fu had originally prepared himself to be stabbed, but who would have thought that the anticipated pain did not arrive.

The garrison soldier also felt that the long halberd in his hand had pressed against something hard and was blocked fiercely, sending a tingling numbness up the palm of his hand instead.

Just as the garrison soldier was stunned for a moment, Xu Fu raised his foot and kicked out fiercely, sending the unprepared garrison soldier tumbling to the ground. He then swiftly snatched the long halberd from the soldier's grasp, reversed its direction, and aimed the sharp tip of the halberd at the soldier on the ground.

Xu Fu had never killed anyone before; he did not know what it felt like to kill a person.

But for Ying Zheng, it was a matter of life and death, with not the slightest bit of pity to be spared. With his long sword, he stabbed and flipped over an enemy, then turned around to grip Xu Fu’s arm from behind and pushed it forward. He didn't use much force, but the long halberd thus pierced straight into the opponent's abdominal cavity.

Fresh blood sprayed forth!

Xu Fu instinctively took a step back, crashing right into Ying Zheng’s embrace. Ying Zheng did not push Xu Fu away either; instead, with a reverse motion, he pulled the retreating Xu Fu tighter into his arms and took him retreating toward the back of the ancestral temple, where there was still a back door they could use.

Zhao Gao and the others also reacted quite quickly, following closely behind as they retreated one after another.

Clearly, the front was blocked by Lao Ai’s men, and Ying Zheng certainly wouldn't actually lead people to charge through it head-on. Lulling Lao Ai into a false sense of security for just a little while was enough.

Seeing Ying Zheng's figure about to slip out of sight, Lao Ai immediately roared in anger, "Why aren't you chasing after him?!"

Obeying the order, the garrison troops were about to charge forward when—who would have thought—those palace attendants who had heeded Ying Zheng's reward proclamation, along with ordinary martial men in Yongcheng or farmers wielding hoes, also boldly barged in and began entangling themselves in a fierce battle with those garrison troops.

The Yongcheng garrison troops were mostly locals of Yongcheng. They might dare to take action against the King of Qin for the sake of glory, wealth, and their master's orders, but they might not dare to take action against the ordinary citizens of Yongcheng, because no one knew if their own family members were among them. For a time, they fell into a disadvantageous position and naturally could not spare the energy to pursue Ying Zheng's party.

Lao Ai was furious, but it was too late to lay blame at this point. He was afraid that if Ying Zheng escaped, the one who would die was himself.

Today's battle must result in Ying Zheng losing his life!

Therefore, Lao Ai rushed forward with his personal attendants, while other attendants hurriedly ran out of the ancestral temple to request reinforcements. Although Lao Ai was somewhat short-sighted, he wasn't excessively foolish, especially since he had absorbed quite a few retainers under his command, and these retainers would always offer him ideas. To ensure the uprising went off without a hitch, Lao Ai took the Queen Mother's seal from Zhao Ji and, in Zhao Ji's name, mobilized the garrison troops from the nearest commandery, claiming it was to prevent any mishaps during the King of Qin's capping ceremony and to protect the safety of Qinian Palace. Additionally, troops from Taiyuan Commandery, to which Lao Ai belonged, were dispatched to come. Though the distance was somewhat far, they could still serve as a deterrent in the end.

Gritting his teeth with a grim smile, Lao Ai said, "I refuse to believe you can still escape me this way!"

Brought by Ying Zheng, Xu Fu stumbled out the back door, and outside was a narrow alley as the group rushed swiftly outward.

A minister gritted his teeth bitterly and said, "Hurry back to Qinian Palace! Surely Lao Ai wouldn't be bold enough to storm Qinian Palace as well!"

Xu Fu couldn't help but laugh internally. Return to Qinian Palace? Zhao Ji and Lao Ai were currently singing from the same hymn sheet; once they returned to Qinian Palace, Zhao Ji and Lao Ai might just close the doors and launch a coordinated siege.

"Return to Qinian Palace." Ying Zheng’s deep voice sounded beside Xu Fu’s ear, carrying a hint of breathlessness.

Xu Fu was stunned. Could the First Emperor of Qin fail to consider that point? It was impossible he hadn't considered it! Unless... Unless he had been prepared all along, and he was doing this on purpose? He actually *wanted* to return to Qinian Palace? Xu Fu suppressed the astonishment in his heart, casually fished a Bagua compass out of his robe, and handed it to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng was taken aback. "Why are you giving this to Us?"

The thing that had blocked that long halberd for Xu Fu inside his robe just moments ago was the tortoise shell used for divination. That hard thrust had merely added a crack to the back of the tortoise shell, leaving not even the slightest scratch otherwise. Xu Fu had kept thinking about the information obtained from the divination of the tortoise shell; even if the First Emperor of Qin had already calculated everything, he still wanted to minimize the possibility of the First Emperor getting injured. Otherwise, if history suffered an accident and the First Emperor kicked the bucket, what on earth would he do?

"The Bagua compass. Placed against the chest, it can serve as a heart-protecting mirror," Xu Fu said with a deadpan expression.

Hearing this, the rest of the ministers also successively urged Ying Zheng to accept it.

Today was originally meant for the capping ceremony; who would wear armor or carry weapons? Compared to the rebel army, they were like a flock of lambs without the strength to truss a chicken, at the mercy of others. Now that there was something to substitute for a heart-protecting mirror—regardless of whether it would be useful later—it could serve as a mental anchor for everyone right now. As long as the King of Qin's safety was guaranteed, they could set their minds at ease.

Ying Zheng raised an eyebrow, gave Xu Fu a profound look, and then tucked the Bagua compass into his robes.

What Ying Zheng was thinking at that moment was: So the reason Xu Fu had stubbornly insisted on bringing so many things along was because he had been prepared all along.

Unable to receive Ying Zheng's internal praise, Xu Fu pressed a hand against the tortoise shell in his robes, lifted his legs, and walked swiftly forward alongside Ying Zheng. They boarded the carriage and galloped rapidly toward the royal palace, and this time no one bothered to point out any breaches of etiquette. When the horses pulling the carriage ran out of breath, they finally arrived at the royal palace.

"Your Majesty?" The guards at the palace gates felt extremely surprised; they certainly hadn't expected to welcome a disheveled King of Qin and the court ministers.

A sharp-tongued minister hurriedly shouted, "Lao Ai is rebelling! Why haven't you men gone forth to intercept them?!"

However, these guards merely exchanged glances with one another and lowered their heads.

The minister simply assumed those guards only took orders from the King of Qin and thus felt no suspicion. Meanwhile, without even glancing at the guards, Ying Zheng alighted from the carriage and strode rapidly inward. Xu Fu also quickened his pace, his heart pounding heavily in his chest. A string in his mind remained tightly taut without a moment of slack, and seeing Ying Zheng walk forward, he immediately followed. The remaining people hesitated for a few seconds before they could only follow as well.

After Ying Zheng and the others entered Qinian Palace, the guards at the royal palace suddenly raised their voices and shouted, "Close the palace gates!"

If one gate was closed, there was another. Lao Ai had entered through a different palace gate with his men, and the reason this palace gate was being closed was simply to prevent Ying Zheng and the others from realizing something was wrong and escaping Qinian Palace.

It could be said that to send Ying Zheng to his death, Lao Ai had put in a great deal of effort.

Upon entering Qinian Palace, believing they were saved, the group sat on the knees on the ground, checked each other's injuries, and rested briefly.

Only Ying Zheng stood with a tightly clenched jaw on the highest set of steps within the hall, gazing out beyond the hall doors toward the direction of the other palace gate.

Xu Fu stood in the position just below Ying Zheng, took a deep breath, and slowly said, "They're coming."

Ying Zheng cast a surprised glance at Xu Fu; he hadn't expected Xu Fu to see through his intentions.

Aside from the men brought to the ancestral temple, more of Lao Ai’s remnants existed within Qinian Palace. For this year, he had likely laid out quite a few methods. To crush Lao Ai, he naturally had to crush all of his forces along the way. Ying Zheng had once bestowed Shanyang land upon Lao Ai and later used Hexi and Taiyuan commanderies to rename it the state of Ai. Lao Ai's forces in these places, though seemingly massive, fell into the category of being too far away to help. As long as Lao Ai was captured here by Ying Zheng, his forces could naturally be completely scattered.

Therefore, if Ying Zheng wasn't going to make a move, once he did, he would resolve Lao Ai completely and without omission in a single stroke.

Xu Fu hadn't been able to see it at first because he wasn't inherently keen on these matters, and furthermore, he never felt he could guess the First Emperor's thoughts. However, having spent some time with the First Emperor after all, he was always able to deduce a thing or two, and thus gradually caught a glimpse of the entire layout.

If he guessed correctly, Ying Zheng's contingency plan should be arriving soon. At that time, it would be catching turtles in a jar—the jar would still be this Qinian Palace, but the turtle would turn out to be Lao Ai.

Soon after, another sound of footsteps and the friction of armor gradually drew closer.

Panic-stricken, the group helped each other up and collectively looked toward Ying Zheng. "Your Majesty, this..." They didn't know whether those were reinforcements or rebel troops.

Ying Zheng did not speak, his icy gaze fixed on the hall entrance. Soon enough, everyone's doubts were answered, because the people swaggering through the doors were still Lao Ai and his faction...

Quite a few people panicked.

How could Lao Ai have arrived so quickly? Could there be someone inside the royal palace working from the inside out in coordination with him?

Xu Fu involuntarily tightened his grip on the long halberd in his hand. Actually, he really wanted to stab it straight into Lao Ai's head, but alas, he lacked the martial arts halo of other transmigrated protagonists.

At that moment, he heard Ying Zheng ask with rather leisurely amusement as he turned his head, "When do you guess the reinforcements will arrive?"

Hearing the word "reinforcements," Xu Fu knew his internal guess had been verified, and the hand gripping the halberd relaxed somewhat. His mindset shifted abruptly, becoming relaxed as well. He turned to reply to Ying Zheng, a slight smile lingering at the corners of his mouth, "I'll count to ten."

Ying Zheng couldn't help laughing. "You are so certain?"

"Yes."

Seeing from afar that Ying Zheng, standing on the high steps, could still display a relaxed smile, Lao Ai instantly felt insulted. Suppressing his anger, he said, "To reach such a state, Your Majesty can still smile?" He didn't understand why, even when he had forced his way right up to him, Ying Zheng could still maintain a relaxed demeanor. Ying Zheng's composure in the face of danger made him feel humiliated, while the regal aura Ying Zheng exuded as he stood there made him quite envious. That was something he, coming from a humble background, could never hope to compare with.

Ying Zheng's very existence was a satire of him, truly fitting the saying that even if one put on a dragon robe, one wouldn't look like a crown prince.

"Audacious Lao Ai! How dare you openly rebel! Do you know what kind of grave crime you have committed?" Some official spoke out with righteous indignation.

Lao Ai sneered incessantly. "Once I become the King of Qin, what grave crime is there? *You* are the ones committing the grave crime!"

The royal palace guards, Lao Ai's attendants, and the soldiers who had rushed over from neighboring counties—these all became Lao Ai's source of confidence. No longer concealing his wild ambitions, he instantly exposed his ugly visage without reservation.

Ying Zheng had not spoken the entire time. Conversing with Lao Ai felt like lowering his own status.

Xu Fu did not remain silent any longer. Giving Lao Ai a cold glare, he slowly said, "Didn't you just ask why His Majesty was smiling? It's not just His Majesty who wants to smile; I want to smile too. I want to laugh at your stupidity. To enter Qinian Palace and act so flauntingly and triumphantly truly looks like a street-corner juggler."

Seeing Xu Fu compare him to a street juggler, and recalling how Xu Fu and Ying Zheng had previously joined forces to play him for a fool, Lao Ai lost face. A vicious light burst from his eyes as he gripped his long sword tightly and roared, "Kill them for me!"

Xu Fu suddenly turned his head and said in a low voice to Ying Zheng, "Ten. I've counted to ten."

The moment his voice fell, the sounds of slaughter suddenly rang out from outside the hall. Lao Ai had to halt his steps and turn to look. Only upon looking did he realize that those aristocratic garrison troops and retainers he had gathered to disrupt the capping ceremony were all angrily fighting to the death with his men, shouting "Lao Ai, you petty villain!" as they did so. Lao Ai was instantly so furious that steam practically came out of his seven orifices.

These lackeys—how dare they curse him as a petty villain?!

Lao Ai hated nothing more than others calling him a petty villain!

Driven to loss of reason by extreme anger, Lao Ai immediately flew into a rage. "Rend that man's mouth off for me!" Hesitating and lingering, his attendants lowered their voices and said, "Lord Changxin must not be provoked by treacherous people! We must first ask why these people suddenly turned on us!"

Lao Ai actually asked in a cold voice, "How dare you curse me as a petty villain?! Bring your master here!"

Those people grew even more furious. "It was our master who instructed us to come! Lao Ai, you petty villain, you went too far! If it weren't for the money, who would be willing to do this kind of business with you? Yet you broke your word, wantonly playing our master in the palm of your hand! Not only is there not a single coin in sight, but you even ordered people to mock us, calling us short-sighted and low-class! Bah! Who doesn't know that you, Lord Changxin, come from truly low-class origins?! Now, we might as well capture you and demand a reward from the King of Qin!"

Lao Ai was dumbfounded by what he heard. When had he broken his word? And when had he ordered people to mock them? How dared this group of people pick at his scars! And they even dared to daydream about capturing him to collect a reward?!

Lao Ai was both furious and anxious, but before he could figure it out, someone with quick hands threw a curved saber, which flew straight to stab at Lao Ai's face. Lao Ai dodged in a panic, but the saber grazed his neck, leaving a shallow bloody scratch. Flying into a towering rage and looking thoroughly disheveled, Lao Ai could no longer muster even a fraction of the smug posture he had a moment ago.

Xu Fu couldn't hold back his laughter.

The money Lao Ai claimed he would distribute to those nobles—could it be that he intended to get it from the "Merchant surnamed Chang"? And the people sent to insult the garrison troops and retainers should also have been sent by the First Emperor. He really had played both Lao Ai and Zhao Ji for fools from start to finish!

They had no imperial seal left, no reinforcements left, and instead ended up offending the very forces they were relying on.

"Kill them! Kill them all!" Driven completely mad by rage, Lao Ai leaned against his attendants and gave the order while flailing his hands wildly.

The soldiers rushed forward in utter chaos.

At that moment, however, the sound of horse hooves and footsteps drew near. Xu Fu heard a furious roar from outside the hall: "Meng Wu and Li Xin are here! Capture the rebel leader Lao Ai!"

Those rumbling horse hooves and heavy footsteps both transformed into a powerful battle drum, instantly awakening everyone's fighting spirit. With a response from both inside and out, the people inside the hall and the people outside formed a pincer movement against Lao Ai's faction.

Young and vigorous, Li Xin led the soldiers to open the way at the front, forcefully carving out a path to charge straight before Ying Zheng. He then surrounded Ying Zheng and the others tightly within a protective perimeter, making it impossible for Lao Ai's men to approach even an inch closer.

The rebel army, which had seemed to have victory in their grasp just a moment before, had now turned into lambs waiting to be slaughtered.

Lao Ai possessed not a shred of military capability; deep down, he was merely a petty villain. Aside from sycophancy and pandering to superiors, when genuinely confronted with such a situation, he quickly panicked, shouting wildly for his attendants to escape and find the Queen Mother to save the day.

Lao Ai was truly terrified of death; he was afraid that if he lost and was killed by Ying Zheng, he would need Zhao Ji to save his life.

Yet at this moment, even Zhao Ji herself was barely able to protect her own skin.

Valiant and fierce, Meng Wu captured Lao Ai beneath his horse. Being tall of stature, he hoisted Lao Ai up directly, faced the remaining rebel soldiers, and shouted at the top of his lungs, "Why haven't you all surrendered yet?"

Looking around blankly and hesitating over whether to drop their weapons, the remaining rebel soldiers were already pinned to the ground by the nearby soldiers; those who resisted were beheaded on the spot, and fresh blood soon flooded the entire doorway of Qinian Palace.

Xu Fu averted his gaze somewhat uncomfortably. The impact of such a scene was still far too great for him.

Ying Zheng didn't feel anything of the sort; he simply assumed the fangshi possessed a compassionate heart.

Throughout the entire ordeal, Ying Zheng maintained that lofty, completely unruffled posture, prompting Xu Fu to inwardly marvel that not just anyone could be the First Emperor! This bearing alone left far too many people trailing endlessly behind him.

With this, the Lao Ai Rebellion was suppressed.

Meng Wu and Li Xin, the two major generals, stepped forward to pay their respects to Ying Zheng.

Right here in this palace stained red with blood, Ying Zheng faced the crowd calmly, his voice not loud, but resolute and powerful enough as he stated: "As of today, We shall personally assume rule."

The political power of the Qin State that had been carved up by Queen Mother Zhao and Lao Ai was about to return to Ying Zheng's hands, and Ying Zheng's grip on the Qin State began to peak.

This was the first step the First Emperor of Qin took before unifying the six states in the future.

Xu Fu felt inexplicably fired up by the influence of it all; he discarded the long halberd he had gripped for so long, his fingers still faintly aching—an aftereffect of exerting too much force earlier.

At this moment, everyone bowed in submission.

In their survival from the jaws of death, the crowd momentarily overlooked the only person standing on the high platform alongside Ying Zheng—Xu Fu. As they suddenly dropped to their knees in prostration, it almost looked as though they were bowing to Xu Fu as well.

No one would care about such details now.

The slaughter within Yongcheng was also drawing to a close, and the remaining fleeing rebels were thoroughly wiped out by the commoners of Yongcheng and the rest of the garrison troops.

Ying Zheng straightened his robes and suddenly said to Xu Fu, "Accompany Us to the Queen Mother's palace once more."

Ying Zheng's feelings at this moment were also very complex. How could he have anticipated that in the process of reclaiming his power, it would be Xu Fu accompanying him from start to finish? Matters within Queen Mother Zhao's palace were not suitable for too many people to know, so bringing a trusted confidant along was naturally the best course of action for Ying Zheng at this time.

Xu Fu, whose spirits were high after witnessing a victorious battle, nodded without even thinking.

Thus, the King of Qin, Ying Zheng—still bearing the faint scent of blood on his person—set foot into the palace of his mother, Zhao Ji, for the first time since his coming-of-age ceremony.

*

"Has the court physician arrived? Has the court physician come yet?" A palace maid repeatedly peered outside, asking in a panic.

Several other palace maids also looked distressed and sorrowful, their teeth clenched tight. "What on earth are we to do... The Queen Mother is bleeding down below..."

A younger palace maid asked timidly, "Could she be miscarrying?"

"What nonsense are you babbling?" The older palace maid slapped her across the face. "How is the Queen Mother someone you can curse?"

The young palace maid aggrievedly covered her face. In her childhood, she had seen her eldest sister look just like this; wasn't that the sign of a miscarriage?

Zhao Ji leaned against the bed feebly, blood slowly seeping out from below. Feeling only a dull, cramping pain and a slippery sensation between her legs, she was suddenly gripped by the utmost terror. She demanded in a harsh voice, "Where is the court physician? Where the hell has he died off to?" As the words left her mouth, she suddenly let out a low gasp of pain, her breath instantly failing her, growing too weak to even throw a tantrum.

"Q-Queen Mother, the court physician is n-nowhere to be found." The palace maid knelt tremblingly before her bed.

It must be him; it must be Ying Zheng's deliberate doing that prevented her from finding a court physician. Zhao Ji finally remembered Ying Zheng at this moment, and she grabbed the palace maid's wrist with a death grip. "Hurry, go see the King. Tell him... tell him I am gravely ill, have him... have him come over... have him send a court physician..."

"Y-Yes..." Terrified by the slightly ferocious look on Zhao Ji's face, the palace maid nodded repeatedly. Just as she wanted to break free from Zhao Ji and stand up, she heard someone behind her trembling as they called out, "Your Majesty."

Zhao Ji instantly released the palace maid's wrist and looked toward the folding screen. Ying Zheng and Xu Fu walked over one after the other, followed by Zhao Gao and the others.

Zhao Ji's expression shifted slightly. "Zheng'er, Zheng'er! What is the meaning of you barging into my bedchamber with so many people?" Zhao Ji felt herself violated; she still failed to recognize the situation, putting on airs even at a time like this.

"Didn't Mother send someone to look for Us?" Ying Zheng smiled and countered Zhao Ji's question.

Zhao Ji immediately let out a cry of pain. "Zheng'er, quickly send a court physician for me..."

Ying Zheng agreed readily enough, turning his head to tell Zhao Gao, "Bring the man up."

That court physician was precisely the person bribed by Zhao Ji and Lao Ai, but at this moment, he was shaking like a sieve, practically crawling to the side of Zhao Ji's bed.

Ying Zheng glanced down at Zhao Ji from on high, first inflicting no small amount of psychological pressure upon her before casually dropping a single sentence, "Lao Ai has rebelled and has already been captured by Us."

Zhao Ji jerked her head up to look at Ying Zheng, her face turning pale and her body trembling. She glared at Ying Zheng with a complex gaze, her words disjointed.

Ying Zheng turned and walked out.

This move was truly brilliant! Xu Fu clicked his tongue inwardly, and immediately turned to follow him out. As soon as they stepped out of the bedchamber, they instantly heard Zhao Ji's shrill, piercing screams. Ying Zheng did not rush to leave; instead, he stood on the steps outside the palace, his gaze fixed on some unknown direction. As the cries echoing from within the bedchamber grew louder and louder, Ying Zheng's expression also grew increasingly cold.

Xu Fu knew that his psychological state must be undergoing a torturous change at this time. However, Xu Fu wasn't very good at serving up chicken soup for the soul, so he could only tighten his jaw, keeping his eyes on his nose and his nose on his heart. The two of them stood in silence and detachment as the setting sun gradually sank in the west, casting its remaining glow over them and bathing them in a faint reddish light. Zhao Gao and the other attendants stood off to the side, looking toward Ying Zheng and Xu Fu, suddenly feeling as though these two were about to ascend to immortality.

After a long while, a young palace maid ran out from inside and dropped to her knees on the ground. "Your Majesty... the child... the child has been born."

"Oh?" Ying Zheng responded without even turning his head.

The young palace maid continued, "However, however, a mere moment later, i-it unfortunately perished..."

As if he had anticipated it long ago, Ying Zheng coldly spat out a single sentence: "The Queen Mother is gravely ill; Yongcheng is no longer suitable for residence. As of today, she is to be transferred to Gongyang Palace to recuperate." With this emotionless recitation, Zhao Ji's fate was sealed.

Xu Fu only vaguely remembered the outline of this history; hampered by the former bonds of mother-and-child affection and blood ties, the historical Ying Zheng indeed seemed to have merely banished Zhao Ji from the Xianyang Palace.

For a woman who had indulged in pleasure for long and was greedy for comfort and glory, losing everything that her current status brought her was a punishment severe enough.

Perhaps the palace maid had relayed these words to Zhao Ji right after turning back into the hall, for the sound of Zhao Ji cursing bitterly could actually be heard coming from within.

Upon returning to Qinian Palace, Ying Zheng did not linger. He ordered the rebel troops to be taken back to Xianyang immediately, and for Lao Ai to be subjected to the punishment of dismemberment by chariots. Upon hearing this, Lao Ai flew into a rage, cursing Ying Zheng vehemently as well—except the words coming out of his mouth were far filthier than Zhao Ji's curses. For the former Marquis of Changxin to end up in such a wretched state upon his downfall left everyone else unable to suppress expressions of disgust. Such a common street ruffian—where on earth did he get the audacity to covet the throne of the King of Qin!

Once his tense nerves relaxed, Xu Fu found that his stomach, which had gone without food for a long time, was uncooperative, beginning to ache faintly.

To make matters worse, Ying Zheng had already boarded the chariot, and everyone else took out dry rations to eat along the way. Xu Fu, who completely lacked such a thing as dry rations, was left stunned. Fortunately, Zhao Gao walked over and smilingly handed food to Xu Fu. Although the handed-over food tasted utterly wretched, it at least filled the stomach; Xu Fu didn't bother being picky anymore, murmured his thanks, and began to eat.

He had just taken a bite and hadn't even had time to despise the cake for being truly hard on the teeth when a squad of people suddenly rushed out from both sides of the road, heading straight for Lao Ai at the rear.

Xu Fu's heart tightened instantly, reminding him of a certain unfulfilled prophecy of his own.

Perhaps some things were truly destined and impossible to escape no matter what.

As the saying goes, even Qin Hui had three friends. Even someone like Lao Ai had people willing to risk their lives to rescue him. These people struck while the convoy was completely unprepared; having gone through a thrilling day, everyone walking the road back to Xianyang was more or less let down their guard, naturally leaving them caught off guard by a surprise attack.

Zhao Gao and the attendants tightly guarded Ying Zheng in the center. Xu Fu looked down at his own physique and decided he didn't need to shield the First Emperor of Qin; his body was so fragile that he'd better stand further back and dodge quickly when the time came—preserving his life was paramount.

Just as Xu Fu was thinking this, those scoundrels went utterly mad. Seeing no hope of rescuing Lao Ai, they charged straight toward him. Xu Fu's expression froze as he hastily stepped back to dodge. Seeing this, Ying Zheng reached out a long arm, scooped Xu Fu up by the waist, and pulled him onto the chariot. Everyone was startled, not expecting Ying Zheng to make such a move. The weapon raised high by the scoundrel intent on stepping forward had already been stabbed to the ground by other rushing soldiers using long halberds, blood splashing everywhere.

Xu Fu's heart hammered wildly; he hadn't expected death to be so close to him just now.

Behind him, Ying Zheng suddenly hissed, appearing to draw in a sharp breath.

No way? He actually got hurt? Xu Fu hurriedly broke free from Ying Zheng's arm and turned around to look at him, only to see Ying Zheng pulling a bronze spearhead out from his waist with a dark expression—it was shockingly the tip of the weapon that had inadvertently flown over earlier.

Xu Fu didn't know whether to laugh or cry. You could get injured even like this? That really matched that prophecy.

Injured in the waist and abdomen, yet harboring no regrets.

The First Emperor of Qin had already eliminated everyone he wanted to get rid of, and his goals had all been achieved. This absurd accident was nothing, so naturally he wouldn't harbor any regrets. It could be said that this upheaval at Qinian Palace had been resolved quite thoroughly under the First Emperor's handling.

Li Xin, who had lagged behind the procession, brought his troops forward and completely suppressed these scoundrels, disposing of every last one without leaving a single survivor.

Xu Fu didn't look back at the scene of the slaughter; he stood frozen beside Ying Zheng. Only then did he remember that he had been scooped up by the waist and hauled onto the chariot belonging to the King of Qin. No wonder the others looked at him with such strange expressions. Maintaining his poker face, he pretended to be calm as he jumped down from the chariot, acting as if nothing had just happened. Meanwhile, Ying Zheng's face was dark and gloomy as he clutched the wound at his waist, saying coldly, "Drive Lao Ai to the front. If he walks too slowly, whip him. If any more scoundrels come to the rescue, execute them all on the spot."

"Understood!" Everyone shouted in unison, their voices shaking the heavens. The sound turned Lao Ai's face pale with fright, his legs shaking so badly he could barely stand, and in the end, he was stumbled and shoved toward the front of the procession.

With the corpses of the previous scoundrels hung on the prison cart behind as a warning, who would dare come to rescue Lao Ai or assassinate Ying Zheng after that?

Lao Ai was whipped forward as if he were truly being driven like livestock, and Xu Fu could hear his wails and screams from time to time. However, not a single person would sympathize with him.

Xu Fu cursed Lao Ai as deserving in his heart, and upon lowering his head, he caught sight of the food still gripped tightly in his right hand. Even in such a critical moment of crisis, he hadn't forgotten to hold onto it firmly. Xu Fu paused for a moment before lowering his head to take another bite.

Sitting on the chariot, Ying Zheng found the wound at his waist starting to ache with a nearly unbearable intensity. Who would have thought that when he casually lowered his head, he would happen to see Xu Fu calmly and unconcernedly lowering his head to eat his cake.

Ying Zheng: ……

It seemed the pain had eased away in a single instant.

*

In the ninth year of the First Emperor, Lao Ai revolted. The King of Qin, having long heard of it, dispatched troops to attack Ai, slaying countless rebels. The Queen Mother was transferred to Gongyang Palace.

To completely pacify Lao Ai's rebellion and round up the remaining party members, Ying Zheng further ordered Lord Changping and Lord Changwen to head to Hexi and Taiyuan Commandery for suppression.

As for Lao Ai, he was brought into the Xianyang Palace.

He was pushed in on a cart—not because his treatment had improved, but because Lao Ai had been whipped until his whole body was a bloody mess, his legs so weak he could no longer take a single step. If they whipped him any further, he might just be beaten to death on the spot.

Lao Ai was the target of deep-seated hatred in Ying Zheng's heart; how could he possibly let him die so easily?

Ying Zheng bathed, changed his clothes, and applied medicine to his wounds before summoning the half-dead Lao Ai in the hall. Meanwhile, clutching his stomach, Xu Fu quietly slipped off to the outhouse. Ah, he hadn't drunk enough water; it was uncomfortable. By the time Xu Fu returned, he happened to hear Zhao Gao proclaiming Ying Zheng's decree.

"To be dismembered by chariots as a public warning, and his entire clan executed. As for his retainers, the minor offenders are to be sentenced to firewood-gathering labor. Furthermore, their titles are stripped, four thousand-plus households are relocated, and they are to be settled in Fangling."

Hearing the words "dismembered by chariots," Lao Ai panicked instantly. He struggled relentlessly on the floor, staining that small patch of ground utterly filthy with the blood from his body.

"No! Don't kill me! No!" Terrified of death, Lao Ai immediately groveled and begged for his life before Ying Zheng without a shred of dignity. Previously, he had been wholeheartedly fantasizing about seizing the throne of the King of Qin, imagining the scene where Ying Zheng's life was held right in the palm of his hand. At that time, he hadn't thought for a single second that if he failed, such a harsh punishment would be waiting for him.

Xu Fu walked into the hall and sized Lao Ai up, his expression turning slightly bizarre.

Rumor had it that Lao Ai's member was enormous and could even spin a carriage wheel without sustaining any damage. He wondered if, when he was dismembered by chariots, that thing of his would be tied up as well. Too filthy... Xu Fu quickly halted his train of thought.

Perhaps gripped by ultimate terror, Lao Ai actually lost control of his bowels, and a foul odor permeated the palace hall. The palace attendants all cast looks of utter contempt toward him. However, Lao Ai was in no state to feel shame or annoyance now—he was about to lose his life... He kept crying out, begging Ying Zheng to spare his dog's life.

Yet Xu Fu thought that calling his life a dog's life was an insult to dogs!

Frowning, Ying Zheng had no desire to look upon Lao Ai's ugly state any longer, feeling that laying eyes on him for even a second was an offense to his sight. Thus, he ordered the guards to drag Lao Ai away: "Before he is dismembered by chariots, have the Marquis of Changxin experience the rest of the torture instruments first."

At these words, Lao Ai struggled even more violently, letting out shrill, miserable screams. The attendants stuffed his mouth and quickly carried him out.

By now it was already nighttime. After being led by palace attendants to bathe and change into fresh clothes, Xu Fu returned to Ying Zheng's bedchamber. During this rebellion, Ying Zheng had expended a great deal of mental and physical effort; it was only at moments like this that the newly crowned King of Qin would reveal a trace of weariness.

Massaging his temples, he lay down on the bed alongside Xu Fu, and due to sheer exhaustion, quickly fell asleep.

Yet this was still a night when countless people found themselves unable to sleep.

The prison guards responsible for the torture, Lao Ai's fugitive partisans, and the nobles who had once curried favor with him...

*

The next day, Xu Fu slowly awakened from his dreams, washing up and dining under the attendance of palace maids—not a single person dared to show him the slightest neglect. Meanwhile, Ying Zheng had already risen long before. This was his first court session since personally assuming rule, and its significance was paramount.

Once Xu Fu finished breakfast, an eunuch who usually followed closely behind Zhao Gao walked in, bowed deeply to him, and said, "I shall escort Master Xu back."

Back?

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, only then remembering that his residence was not the royal palace. He had merely been kept in the palace by the First Emperor because of the capping ceremony—something the First Emperor had done solely to prevent news from leaking out. Now that the capping ceremony had successfully concluded, it was naturally time for him to return to the Fengchang Temple.

Xu Fu stood up and smiled faintly at the eunuch. "Alright."

The eunuch had a carriage prepared, and after Xu Fu boarded it, they quickly arrived at the grand gates of the Fengchang Temple.

Stepping down from the carriage, he looked up at the plaque of the Fengchang Temple. Even though it had only been a little over half a month, it felt as though he hadn't set foot here for years.

Xu Fu straightened his robes, lifted his foot, and stepped inside.

chapters.source_text:
宫殿绵延巍峨，气势恢宏，带有浓厚的时代色彩。因为夜色沉暮，这座王城看起来就像是一只狰狞又威严的巨兽，让人望而生怯。
这是徐福在来到这个世界以后，第一次完完整整地看见这个地方的全貌。可惜他历史学得糟糕，也判断不出这是哪个朝代。
倒是想到王上叫那个白净宫人的名字为“赵高”，听起来好像很耳熟啊。
“走快些。”正想着呢，赵高就回头冷睨了他一眼。
徐福不得不收回自己土包子一样的视线，老老实实地做回自己出尘脱俗的姿态，跟在一行人身后，不再分神。
等进了宫殿，嬴政落座，徐福忍不住抬眼望去，只见这位王上手中把玩着一张玉牌，那双手骨节分明，一定是相当有力的。这个时候，徐福才发觉，对方的气势竟然能将自己笼罩住。这个男人好霸气，用师傅的话来说，生为天子命格，又气势如虹的男人，那岂不是可能会成为千古一帝？
徐福心中暗惊。
嬴政开口，“过来。”他的声音微微暗哑，却带着极强的威慑性。
徐福挪动步子，缓缓走到嬴政的桌案前。嬴政锐利的目光将徐福从头到脚一寸寸梭巡了个遍，徐福顿时被看得浑身发毛。
难道这个王上是个断袖吗？徐福曾经听说古代将龙阳之事视为风雅，他不会也看上自己的脸了吧？
“你怎么知道寡人会有血光之灾？”嬴政终于收起了打量的目光，冷声问道。
徐福张了张嘴，正要说话，嬴政却又突然添了一句，“寡人要听实话，如若你有半句虚言，看见那儿了吗？”嬴政遥遥一指，徐福转头顺着他指的方向看过去，那是一根桅杆，耸立在大殿之外。
“寡人就将你绑在上面，受烈日暴晒。”嬴政慢悠悠地补充道，手中的玉牌骤然碎成了两半。
雾草，好残暴！徐福忍不住打了个激灵。
大概是徐福装逼的功底太过深厚，嬴政没能从他脸上发现一丝惊惶害怕的神色，嬴政暗自皱眉，难道这个江湖术士真的有什么依仗吗？
“吾出自鬼谷子门下，名徐福，师门授以看面相、占祸福、观天气之术，吾学成以后，便想要四处行走，为人看相测祸福。相逢即是有缘，吾能遇到王上，那是吾之幸啊！吾之前的批语句句属实，绝无虚言。”徐福勉强模仿了一下古人说话的方式。
至于出自鬼谷子门下……
他师门连个名字都没有呢，哪来的鬼谷子门下？反正也就胡诌一下，显得自己来历很深，比较高大上嘛。
“鬼谷子门下？”嬴政勾了勾唇角，似乎来了点儿兴趣，但他怎么可能是好糊弄的人？“你如何证明你有真本事？”
“之前的批语不能算作证明吗？”徐福倒是直接和嬴政讨价还价起来了。
赵高在旁边忍不住嘀咕，这少年胆子实在大！
“一次，也许只是巧合，要让寡人真正相信你的本事，那必须得再拿出一个证据来。”嬴政的表情有些冷漠。
徐福毫不怀疑，如果自己无法证实，那自己将真的被挂在桅杆上，然后晒成咸人干。
见徐福眉头微蹙。
美人蹙眉，总是说不出的赏心悦目，嬴政忍不住嘴上软了软，直接给徐福指了条路，“你不是说你善于观测天气吗？那你现在就出去观测观测。”
徐福双眼一亮，对啊，他可以马上预测一下天气啊，只要能证实自己是有真本事，就能保得住命了啊。
他没再犹豫，转身就往宫殿外走，嬴政示意赵高跟上。
赵高小跑着跟上徐福一起出了宫殿。
这就是古代的夜景，天空上群星点缀，看上去顿生梦幻之感。
实在漂亮！
赵高撇撇嘴，对这江湖术士有些看不起，“怎么样？可看出什么了？”
“哪有这么快的？”徐福头也不回地反驳，然后抬头慢慢观测起天上的景象来。
虽然夜幕低垂，但徐福用自己超高的视力辨出了，西边的云由远及近，而且有大块大块的积云，近处则是有些薄絮状的云团。晚上实在光线不好，这个时代也没有个电灯啊，望远镜什么的。徐福只能粗暴地判断。
明日有雨！
对，明日应该是有雨的。
徐福一旦下了判断，就不会再怀疑自己，他转过身，正对上赵高那一脸不屑的表情。
等这次也应验了，他倒要看看，这个赵高的脸色会如何变幻？哼。徐福端足架子，神色淡漠地绕过赵高就往里走。
赵高没想到他这么快就看完了，徐福已经先往里走了，他只能迈着一双短腿费力地跟在徐福身后，心里不知道将徐福骂了多少遍。
“如何？”见徐福进门来，嬴政身子微微前倾，倒是有些期待从他口中听到答案。
“据吾观天象所得，明日必有大雨，王上出入定会觉得闷热无比。”后半句是放在一起凑数的。毕竟下大雨嘛，一般空气都很闷热啊。
见徐福一脸坚定，赵高已经忍不住先笑开了。他还当这个江湖术士真的有点儿本事呢，原来真是胡诌的！
嬴政转头看向赵高，“赵高，你说呢？”
赵高脸上挂着笑容，那是对徐福的鄙视，他佝着腰，恭敬答道：“回王上，奴婢看这人就是个骗子，之前肯定只是碰巧说中而已。”
徐福和赵高比起来，嬴政当然更相信近侍赵高的话，他的面色微沉，“哦？为什么这么说？”
“他在看天象的时候，奴婢也在看，但据奴婢所观，今夜夜色大好，明日必定是个晴朗天气，怎么可能……”赵高说着忍不住嗤笑一声，“怎么可能如他所说，会下大雨？”
嬴政的面色更沉了，他最恨别人欺骗，于是加重了语气，“徐福，你还有何话可说？”
事关性命，徐福当然不会让步，他转身冲赵高拱手，问：“敢问赵公公，你是做什么的？”
在嬴政面前，赵高当然是露出一脸与有荣焉的表情，道：“奴婢是伺候王上的，掌王上一切贴身事务。”
“哦，你也说了，你就是个负责伺候人的，你专业是伺候啊，不是观天象啊。我才是专业人士。你说明天是晴天，难道明天就一定是晴天了吗？”徐福眨了眨眼，淡定反驳。
虽然嬴政和赵高都没听明白，什么专业不专业人士的，但他们都听出了徐福话里的意思。
赵高被气得脸色发青，但碍于嬴政在此，他只能恨恨地瞪了一眼徐福。
徐福神经粗，瞪一眼也不在乎，哪怕赵高再多瞪几眼，他也没什么特别的感觉。
“你说得倒也有几分道理。”嬴政的脸色稍稍缓和了，在他看来，也觉得徐福胆子够大，现在也依旧临危不乱，到了这种地步，还能保持镇静，口舌伶俐反驳赵高，那他话里的可信度应该还是有几分。“寡人这里倒是有个最直观判别的办法，等到明日，自然有所分晓。”
“好。”徐福一口答应，这个办法的确最直观，到时候直接拿事实来抽这位赵公公的脸，看他还有什么好说。
嬴政点头，“那就将他带回大牢去吧。”
徐福骤然瞪大眼，“不，等等！我还要回大牢？”
“当然，如果明日无雨，你就不用再出来了。”嬴政慢条斯理地说道，说出来的话却足以教人遍体生寒。
徐福很相信自己的判断，他确信自己不会丢了小命，但他是真的不想回大牢啊！
“咕叽。”
肚子一声响。
在侍从上来将他拖走之前，徐福伸出了手，“等等，我能吃个饭再走吗？”
chapters.title: 第3章
chapters.translated_text:
The palaces stood tall and majestic, exuding a grand momentum with a strong historical flavor. Because of the gathering twilight, this royal city looked like a ferocious yet dignified giant beast, inspiring awe and timidity in those who gazed upon it.

This was the first time Xu Fu had seen the full view of this place in its entirety since coming to this world. Unfortunately, his history was terrible, and he couldn't tell which dynasty this was.

However, he happened to think of the fair-skinned palace attendant whom the King called "Zhao Gao," which sounded rather familiar.

"Walk faster." Just as he was thinking, Zhao Gao turned around and cast a cold glance at him.

Xu Fu had no choice but to withdraw his bumpkin-like gaze, obediently resume his otherworldly and refined posture, and follow behind the group without letting his mind wander again.

Once they entered the palace and Ying Zheng took his seat, Xu Fu couldn't help lifting his eyes to look. He saw this King toying with a piece of jade in his hands, those hands with distinct knuckles that must be quite powerful. It was at this moment that Xu Fu realized the other man's aura was actually capable of enveloping him. This man was so overbearing. In his master's words, a man born with the destiny of a Son of Heaven and an overwhelming aura—wouldn't he potentially become an emperor through the ages?

Xu Fu was secretly startled in his heart.

Ying Zheng spoke, "Come here." His voice was slightly hoarse, yet carried an extremely strong deterrent force.

Xu Fu moved his steps, slowly walking up to Ying Zheng's desk. Ying Zheng's sharp gaze scanned Xu Fu from head to toe inch by inch, and Xu Fu instantly felt his entire body break out in goosebumps.

Could this King be a cut-sleeve? Xu Fu had once heard that the affairs of Longyang were regarded as refined in ancient times; surely he hadn't taken a fancy to his face, had he?

"How did you know We would face a bloody disaster?" Ying Zheng finally withdrew his scrutinizing gaze and asked in a cold voice.

Xu Fu opened his mouth, just about to speak, when Ying Zheng suddenly added another sentence, "We want to hear the truth. If you utter even half a falsehood, do you see that over there?" Ying Zheng pointed a far distance away. Xu Fu turned his head to look in the direction he pointed, and saw a mast towering outside the grand hall.

"We will tie you to it and expose you to the scorching sun," Ying Zheng added leisurely, the jade plaque in his hand suddenly shattering into two halves.

Holy crap, how tyrannical! Xu Fu couldn't help shivering.

Probably because Xu Fu's facade of acting cool was too profound, Ying Zheng failed to find a trace of panic or fear on his face. Ying Zheng frowned inwardly; could this wandering Daoist really have something to rely on?

"I am a disciple of Guiguzi, named Xu Fu. My sect taught me the arts of reading physiognomy, divining misfortune and fortune, and observing the weather. After completing my studies, I wished to travel everywhere and read fortunes for people. To meet is to have affinity; being able to encounter the King is my fortune! My previous prophecies are true in every word, without the slightest falsehood." Xu Fu barely managed to imitate the way ancient people spoke.

As for being a disciple of Guiguzi...

His sect didn't even have a name, so where would a disciple of Guiguzi come from? Anyway, he was just spouting nonsense to make his background sound profound and high-end.

"A disciple of Guiguzi?" Ying Zheng hooked the corners of his lips, seeming to develop a bit of interest, but how could he be someone easily fooled? "How can you prove you have genuine skills?"

"Couldn't the previous prophecy be considered proof?" Xu Fu simply started bargaining with Ying Zheng instead.

Zhao Gao couldn't help muttering aside that this youth was truly audacious!

"Once might just be a coincidence. To make Us truly believe in your skills, you must produce another piece of evidence." Ying Zheng's expression was somewhat cold.

Xu Fu had no doubt that if he couldn't prove it, he would really be hung on that mast and dried into a salted human jerky.

Seeing Xu Fu's brows furrow slightly.

A beauty frowning was always unspeakably pleasing to the eye. Ying Zheng couldn't help softening his tone and directly pointed out a path for Xu Fu, "Didn't you say you are skilled at observing the weather? Then go out and observe it right now."

Xu Fu's eyes lit up. Right, he could predict the weather right away! As long as he could prove he had real skills, he would be able to save his life.

Without further hesitation, he turned and walked out of the palace. Ying Zheng motioned for Zhao Gao to follow.

Zhao Gao trotted to keep up and went out of the palace with Xu Fu.

This was the ancient night view, the sky dotted with stars, instantly generating a sense of fantasy.

Truly beautiful!

Zhao Gao curled his lips, looking down somewhat on this wandering Daoist, "How is it? Can you make anything out?"

"How could it be that fast?" Xu Fu retorted without looking back, then raised his head to slowly observe the scene in the sky.

Although night had fallen, Xu Fu used his superior eyesight to discern that the clouds in the west were coming from afar to near, and there were large chunks of cumulus clouds, while closer by were some wispy cloud clusters. The lighting at night was really poor, and this era didn't have electric lights or telescopes. Xu Fu could only make a crude judgment.

It will rain tomorrow!

Yes, there should be rain tomorrow.

Once Xu Fu made a judgment, he would no longer doubt himself. He turned around, running straight into Zhao Gao's look of utter disdain.

Once this prediction also came true, he wanted to see how Zhao Gao's expression would change! Humph. Xu Fu put on a full pose, with a detached expression as he bypassed Zhao Gao and walked inward.

Zhao Gao didn't expect him to finish observing so quickly. Xu Fu had already walked ahead, so he could only use his short legs to follow laboriously behind Xu Fu, cursing Xu Fu in his heart不知道 how many times.

"How is it?" Seeing Xu Fu enter the door, Ying Zheng leaned forward slightly, somewhat expecting to hear the answer from his mouth.

"According to what I have gained from observing celestial phenomena, there will definitely be heavy rain tomorrow, and the King will certainly feel extremely sultry when going out." The second half of the sentence was added just to pad the numbers. After all, when it rains heavily, the air is generally very sultry.

Seeing Xu Fu's resolute expression, Zhao Gao couldn't help laughing first. He had thought this wandering Daoist really had some skills; it turned out he was truly talking nonsense!

Ying Zheng turned to look at Zhao Gao, "Zhao Gao, what do you say?"

A smile hung on Zhao Gao's face, expressing contempt for Xu Fu. He hunched his waist and respectfully replied, "Reporting to the King, this servant sees this person as nothing more than a swindler. The previous hit was definitely just a lucky guess."

Compared to Xu Fu, Ying Zheng naturally believed the words of his close attendant Zhao Gao. His expression sank slightly, "Oh? Why do you say that?"

"When he was observing celestial phenomena, this servant was also watching. But according to this servant's observation, tonight's night view is magnificent, and tomorrow will definitely be clear weather. How could it..." Zhao Gao couldn't help sneering as he spoke, "How could it rain heavily as he claimed?"

Ying Zheng's expression sank even further. He hated being deceived the most, so he intensified his tone, "Xu Fu, what else do you have to say?"

With his life at stake, Xu Fu naturally wouldn't back down. He turned, cupped his hands at Zhao Gao, and asked, "Dare I ask, Eunuch Zhao, what is your profession?"

In front of Ying Zheng, Zhao Gao naturally revealed a look of profound honor, saying, "This servant serves the King and is in charge of all the King's personal affairs."

"Oh, you also said it yourself, you're just responsible for serving people. Your profession is serving, not observing celestial phenomena. I am the professional. You say tomorrow is a sunny day, does that mean tomorrow must definitely be sunny?" Xu Fu blinked and calmly retorted.

Although neither Ying Zheng nor Zhao Gao understood what "professional or non-professional" meant, they both understood the meaning behind Xu Fu's words.

Zhao Gao was so angry his face turned pale, but hindered by Ying Zheng's presence here, he could only glare fiercely at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu had thick nerves and didn't care about a glare. Even if Zhao Gao glared a few more times, he wouldn't feel anything special.

"What you say does make some sense." Ying Zheng's expression eased slightly. In his view, he also felt that Xu Fu was bold enough to remain calm in the face of danger.
