Wang Liu, who had originally expected Xu Fu to say something, suddenly felt a mouthful of old blood stuck in his throat—neither able to spit it out nor swallow it back. He was genuinely so furious that his blood boiled upward.

"Ever since you arrived at the Fengchang Temple, you haven't done a single proper thing all day long. By what virtue and ability are you qualified to hold the post of Chief Diviner? I have served as a diviner for over a year. In terms of seniority and family background, how can you possibly compare to me?" Wang Liu raised a hand to clutch his chest, looking almost as if he were about to faint from anger at Xu Fu, yet he stubbornly forced himself to put up a fight against Xu Fu. In this regard, he was vastly superior to Qiu Ji and Grandmaster Liu.

At least one could barely say he had a bit of backbone and persistence.

"Oh, and so?" Xu Fu still maintained a nonchalant expression.

Wang Liu was secretly vexed. He clenched his teeth hard and said harshly, "Do you dare to compete with me? If your skills are inferior to mine, naturally you cannot be this Chief Diviner!"

"Why should I compete with you? The one who made me Chief Diviner is the King. Could it be that you are dissatisfied with the King's decision?" Xu Fu lifted his chin slightly, his gaze piercing through his dense eyelashes, carrying an inherent sense of contempt and mockery.

The positions between the two instantly reversed.

Only then did everyone realize that Xu Fu's previous indifference toward them was simply because he hadn't taken them seriously yet. Now, Xu Fu was beginning to reveal his prickly side; whoever reached out to probe him might just end up getting slashed bloody.

This person was not without pride; it was just that his pride was hidden deep within his bones.

The others subconsciously shrank their necks, even less daring to step forward and test Xu Fu's edge.

"Xu Fu, you... you... you coward!" Wang Liu was truly choked with nothing left to say by Xu Fu. People of their background could not curse freely like street ruffians, which was why he could only squeeze out these few words after a long while.

Xu Fu was merely teasing Wang Liu to vent some steam. If it really came down to a contest of skills, Xu Fu wouldn't fear him by even a fraction. Oh, as the saying goes, no matter what you lose, you must never lose your momentum. Since someone had already hopped right to his doorstep, he would just slap them back with genuine skill and beat the opponent until they were completely incapacitated.

"How do you want to compete?" Xu Fu suddenly spoke up and asked.

Wang Liu was startled. "...What?" Xu Fu's attitude changed so abruptly that he was caught off guard. It was like trying your hardest to get someone to agree to something, only for them to casually consent the moment you finished exerting all your effort.

Wang Liu once again had the urge to vomit blood.

"How do you want to compete?" Xu Fu repeated.

"Naturally... a contest of divination arts!"

"Tortoise shell divination?" Xu Fu asked. Actually, Xu Fu wasn't all that skilled at tortoise shells; after all, this technique had been passed down from far too ancient times, and many of its inner essences were not necessarily things one could comprehend. Relatively speaking, Xu Fu was actually a step inferior to these proper ancient sorcerers. Moreover, most of those who served as Chief Diviners, Grand Historians, and Grand Invokers inherited their craft from their ancestors, and some even came from renowned families.

What was Xu Fu? In this era, he had zero foothold. If he casually blurted out that he was a disciple of Guiguzi, who would actually take it seriously?

But none of that mattered.

What he was truly best at was bullshitting, after all.

Wang Liu sneered, "Other than tortoise shell divination, what else did you think there was?"

Xu Fu pressed down the disdain in his heart. Little buddy, if you haven't seen the world, don't boast; I can totally crush you, okay? Face reading, character analysis, fortune drawing, divination, and exorcism—oh wait, there's no exorcism option. Well, aside from that, he (did) know (not) a (master) thing (of) or (all) everything (sorts), alright?

"Have you ever heard of character analysis through writing?"

Wang Liu froze for a moment, then sneered with disdain, "What kind of heretical sorcery is that? Never heard of it! Why bother fabricating it to deceive me?"

Xu Fu: ......

Heretical sorcery? If you put that under a pedestrian overpass, the fact that you use tortoise shell divination would also be called heretical sorcery—that goes against the scientific view of development, you know that?

If you don't understand learning and progress at all and only know how to stick to outmoded conventions, then you won't be wronged in the slightest if you lose to me. After finishing his internal rant, Xu Fu looked at Wang Liu with a calm expression and asked, "Then who shall act as the adjudicator?"

Wang Liu smiled, "Naturally, we shall invite Grandmaster Liu."

I'd have to be crazy to let you invite your partner-in-crime to be the adjudicator! Xu Fu sneered inwardly, but on the surface, he raised a smile—one that was rarely ever so brilliant. Who knows how many people were dazzled by this smile in that single instant, thinking to themselves that this person was completely like two different styles of art when smiling versus when not.

"In my view, how about we invite the King to act as the adjudicator?" Xu Fu was usually cold, detached, and restrained, yet suddenly smiling like this—and smiling so brilliantly—as if mocking Wang Liu for biting off more than he could chew.

Wang Liu suddenly felt the smile was too glaring. He clenched his teeth and said hatefully, "The King... how could he get involved in such a matter?"

"Just say whether you think it's feasible or not." Xu Fu then mercilessly mocked, "It's not like I'm asking you to go beg the King to come; I know you couldn't beg him anyway."

Bystanders could only catch glimpses of how graceful Xu Fu's posture was, how charming his smile was, and how Wang Liu's expression twisted and turned ferocious. How could they know that from Wang Liu's angle, he could catch the mockery and triumph hidden deep within Xu Fu's eyes?

Now, the positions of the two had truly been swapped.

Look how Wang Liu had mocked and despised him earlier—it was being returned so quickly.

"The King then, let it be the King." After saying this, Wang Liu immediately sneered, terrified of losing momentum: "But can you actually manage to invite the King?"

"As for that, naturally you don't need to worry." A single sentence from Xu Fu blocked Wang Liu's mouth. When he turned around, all other emotions had vanished from the depths of his eyes, and the earlier mockery and contempt seemed like nothing more than an illusion.

The others had watched enough of the excitement and also prepared to disperse.

After taking two steps, Xu Fu suddenly turned back to remind Wang Liu, "Don't forget to clean my room."

Wang Liu held back a breath. At that moment, he felt as though he could physically feel the burning gazes cast from all around.

But every cause has its effect. If Wang Liu hadn't played dirty in the first place, he wouldn't be eating the bitter fruit of his own actions today.

Grabbing his appointment order and official robes, and feeling utterly starved with his complexion slightly pale, Xu Fu walked slowly toward the side. Su Yi suddenly strode to his side and asked, "You've offended them thoroughly—how will you get by in the Fengchang Temple in the future?"

Xu Fu turned his head, stared at Su Yi's deadpan face for a few seconds, and then said in a profound, earnest tone, "Since it was doomed from the beginning that we wouldn't get along, why should I wrong myself to accept it? If you're going to offend someone, you might as well offend them all the way, lest they harbor resentment against you and instead treat you like a soft persimmon, bullying you even worse in the future. Oh, do you know Shakespeare? This quote was said by the celebrity Shakespeare." Having smoothly finished dishing out this bowl of chicken soup for the soul, Xu Fu turned around and asked someone to bring him a soft cushion.

I wonder if sitting at the doorway would be a bit strange?

Meanwhile, Su Yi over there was somewhat dizzy. "...Kill-speare? What celebrity? Why have I never heard of him?"

Of course he hadn't heard of him. Because these words were said by Xu Fu, not Shakespeare. Xu Fu thought this with extreme irresponsibility.

Leaving Su Yi behind to struggle over who this celebrity was, Su Yi pondered in secret for a moment and felt that what Xu Fu said made a tremendous amount of sense. Immediately, he cast an obscurely respectful gaze toward Xu Fu's direction.

Yet another person fell under the spell of Xu Fu's casual rambling.

At this moment, Xu Fu was quietly counting in his heart.

One, two, three...

Ten, eleven...

Why hasn't he come yet? Could it be that he guessed wrong this time? Just as Xu Fu was feeling puzzled, he suddenly heard someone over there cry out in startled uncertainty, "Eunuch Zhao?"

Xu Fu stood up, patted away the completely nonexistent dust on his body, proactively took a few steps forward, and quietly awaited Zhao Gao's arrival.

The remaining people in the Fengchang Temple who hadn't dispersed yet froze once again.

They hadn't expected that within a single day, the Fengchang Temple would be graced by the King's close attendant twice.

Zhao Gao hurried over to Xu Fu. Seeing his pale complexion, his heart sank, and he quickly said, "Please, Chief Diviner Xu, take a trip with me."

The others were clueless and exchanged confused glances, left only to watch Xu Fu's leisurely retreating figure alongside Zhao Gao. In their hearts, they sighed—this newcomer truly had an extraordinary background; thank goodness they hadn't neglected him.

Su Yi, however, was even more astonished. In his view, Xu Fu's divination arts were already beginning to show results; otherwise, how could he have dared to say he would invite the King to act as adjudicator? Unless he had already known that this Eunuch Zhao would come to escort him to the royal palace.

He truly possessed real skill!

*

Acting on Ying Zheng's order, Zhao Gao had gone to the Fengchang Temple to deliver the appointment order and new official robes to Xu Fu, and then immediately returned to the Xianyang Palace to report to Ying Zheng about the affairs within the Fengchang Temple. Did Ying Zheng want to know the entanglements behind it? It wasn't hard to find out. Soon, he learned that Xu Fu's previous residence had been maliciously vandalized, and Ying Zheng's face immediately elongated into a grimace.

During the capping ceremony, Xu Fu was a meritorious subject—this was beyond doubt. He was far superior to those aristocratic scions who came from prominent families yet could never figure out where their loyalties lay. Now that Xu Fu was being bullied, wasn't that equivalent to slapping the dignified King of Qin across the face? Learning further that Xu Fu hadn't even eaten his meal before getting so angry as to go argue with people, and linking this to when Xu Fu was in the Xianyang Palace with him—was there anything he lacked to eat?

Ying Zheng instantly felt that Xu Fu had suffered immensely!

Moreover, that room hadn't been cleaned up yet; once night fell, where would Xu Fu go?

Ying Zheng completely overlooked the fact that Xu Fu, now the Chief Diviner, could have simply spoken a single sentence to change rooms.

Thus, he dispatched Zhao Gao out once more, ordering him to bring Xu Fu back to the palace. Zhao Gao wasted no time and promptly left the palace to pick up Xu Fu.

By the time Xu Fu entered the palace riding a dusty carriage, Ying Zheng had already ordered meals to be prepared.

After alighting from the carriage, Xu Fu was led directly by Zhao Gao to the dining hall. Xu Fu was already thoroughly familiar with this place; he walked in with a natural posture and immediately caught sight of Ying Zheng sitting on his knees before the low table.

"Your Majesty." Xu Fu finally remembered to offer a salute, after which he found his former seat, promptly sat down, and then... waited for dinner to be served.

He was indeed starved past the limit; his stomach lacked nourishment, and his complexion was completely pale.

Yet Ying Zheng had no inkling of what he was thinking. The moment he saw Xu Fu's pale complexion, he couldn't help frowning and asked, "Are you ill? Zhao Gao, go summon the royal physician."

Complying with the order, Zhao Gao bowed and was about to step out of the palace gates.

"No, no..." Need to.

The latter word was forced back down his throat.

When Ying Zheng looked at him, his face was practically plastered with three words: "Don't speak."

Xu Fu: "..." But I'm hungry! I'm starving! Hungry!

However, Xu Fu didn't want to dampen the Qin King's enthusiasm for caring for his subordinates, so he could only grit his teeth and hold it in. If he wanted to see a doctor, so be it; he could just treat it as getting a routine physical check-up. Anyway, being hungry for a little while wouldn't make him pass out.

The imperial physician did not arrive quickly. Xu Fu waited on pins and needles. After a short while, he finally saw an elderly man enter with trembling steps. After offering a salute to the King of Qin, the old man sat on his knees to the side and took Xu Fu's pulse.

Zhao Gao explained from the side, "This is a highly skilled imperial physician within the royal palace."

Thank you so much for not brushing me off and specially inviting an "old" traditional Chinese medicine doctor for me! Oh, heavy emphasis on the word "old".

Xu Fu restrained his gaze from wandering toward the food.

After a moment, the old imperial physician kowtowed to the floor before stating, "This gentleman is..."

Before he could even finish, Xu Fu suddenly felt a buzzing in his ears and his vision blurring. He shook his head, and then his body unconsciously listed to one side and he collapsed. Everyone was startled, and the old imperial physician's voice was forced to cut off abruptly.

Xu Fu's head happened to knock against Ying Zheng's bony knees.

Ying Zheng hurriedly stretched out a long arm and scooped Xu Fu up. When he looked again, Xu Fu had already fainted, and right on his forehead, a patch of skin that should have been fair was now topped with a small bruised mark.

Ying Zheng inexplicably felt a slight sense of guilt.

The old imperial physician huffed and puffed for a couple of breaths before continuing, "This gentleman... has simply gone without food for too long, resulting in excessive physical exertion and Qi-and-blood deficiency, causing him to faint."

Ying Zheng gave a light cough. So his pale face was because he was starving, huh? "...Then... then how should this be resolved?"

The old imperial physician replied matter-of-factly, "Pinch his philtrum, and feed him back to health."

Ying Zheng instantly felt even more guilty.

Zhao Gao also felt like he had done a bad thing with good intentions, and quickly led the old imperial physician back out.

Ying Zheng lowered his head to look at Xu Fu resting against his knees. Because of the unconsciousness, his facial features softened considerably, and his long, ink-black feathered eyelashes formed a striking contrast with his pale skin. Yet Ying Zheng felt slightly troubled: how does one pinch a philtrum? If Your Servant's hand pinches down, will the force be too great?

When Zhao Gao returned after seeing the old imperial physician out, what he saw was Ying Zheng with an "earnest" expression, staring down at the Xu Fu in his arms.

A shock ran through Zhao Gao's heart, and he silently kept his mouth shut.

Ying Zheng raised his head and swept his gaze around the room. Seeing that none of the others had any intention of stepping up to take over, Ying Zheng did not realize that the palace attendants knew better than to disturb his "gazing" at Xu Fu, fearing they might provoke his wrath.

After hesitating for a moment, Ying Zheng ultimately chose to reach out his hand and pinch the philtrum of Xu Fu.

That sensation was truly refreshing!

Xu Fu was jolted awake by the pain. If he hadn't dazedly opened his eyes straight into Ying Zheng's face, he probably would have instinctively bolted straight up. And if he really hadn't been able to hold back, the cold and aloof persona he had painstakingly maintained for so long would have been completely ruined!

Xu Fu secretly breathed a sigh of relief, then climbed up feebly, only to notice for the first time that he had just been lying in Ying Zheng's arms.

Xu Fu: "..." To dare lie in the arms of China's First Emperor and enjoy the sensation of "sleeping drunk upon a monarch's knees"—he must be the very first person to ever pull this off, right?

Ying Zheng ordered the palace maids to set the dishes.

Xu Fu breathed another sigh of relief; he could finally eat.

He didn't hesitate any longer, picked up his chopsticks, and began to eat. Ying Zheng hadn't eaten dinner yet either due to being caught up in reviewing piled-up state affairs, so he simply joined Xu Fu just like that. Compared to the tasteless meals of before, this meal tasted vastly more flavorful.

Ying Zheng didn't think too much of it, merely figuring that perhaps when a person was exceptionally hungry, they wouldn't be picky about anything.

After finishing the meal, Xu Fu remained in the Xianyang Palace.

Xu Fu asked in a low voice, "Am I still sharing quarters with the King?"

Zhao Gao answered with absolute certainty, "Naturally!"

Head lowered as he flipped through bamboo slips, Ying Zheng had no idea that his close attendant Zhao Gao had already very "considerately" nudged Xu Fu closer to his side.

When Ying Zheng got busy, he had a bit of a workaholic streak in him. Once Xu Fu was full and well-fed, he felt listless and deeply drowsy. At this time of year, sleeping on the small couch at night would already bring a chill, and Xu Fu just wanted to go to bed and get a proper night's sleep. He circled around Ying Zheng a few times; the candlelight cast his silhouette drifting back and forth within the hall, making him look less like an immortal-like sage during the day and somewhat more like a male ghost accompanied by gusts of eerie wind.

No matter how obtuse Ying Zheng was, he felt it. He put down his writing brush and knife, raised his head to look at Xu Fu, and asked, "Sleepy?"

Xu Fu nodded without the slightest hesitation, and conveniently dished out another bowl of soul chicken soup for the First Emperor: "There's never an end to work. Proper rest is the only way to ensure efficiency... the only way to complete tasks faster. Your health is paramount." Xu Fu forcefully made a sharp turn right at the word "efficiency".

This was the first time Ying Zheng had ever heard such words. After all, ancient times lacked internet slang and chicken soup peddlers.

Ever since he ascended the throne, the Dowager Zhao rarely cared for him, and he had never been close to his father, King Zhuangxiang of Qin, having never experienced the feeling of being cared for since childhood. After becoming the King of Qin, his only remaining belief was how to reclaim the supreme power belonging to the King of Qin as early as possible. How could he still spare any mind for whether his body was healthy or not?

Xu Fu had no idea that a casual bowl of chicken soup of his had irrigated the barren, un-nurtured emotional field of the First Emperor.

Ying Zheng was extremely decisive in his actions; he promptly stood up, "Let's go. Wash up and retire."

Xu Fu immediately walked out together with Ying Zheng.

When Xu Fu very consciously followed him into the bedchamber, very skillfully spread out his arms to let the palace maids dress him down, and then very obediently climbed onto the bed, Ying Zheng abruptly realized... actually, now that the capping ceremony had passed, Xu Fu no longer needed to share a bed with him, nor did he need to worry about Xu Fu leaking anything out.

But Xu Fu had already spontaneously tucked himself in.

Ying Zheng's lips twitched for a moment, but he finally pressed them together, changed and washed up, and climbed onto the bed as well.

Ying Zheng stared at the top of the bed canopy for a while before slowly closing his eyes.

After a period of conditioning, the so-called poisonous incense had long since gradually faded from Ying Zheng's body. However, after closing his eyes, Ying Zheng always felt as though he could still faintly catch a wisp of fragrance at the tip of his nose—a light, refreshing fragrance.

He couldn't open his eyes, feeling only as though he had once again wandered into that dream.

This time, however, he caught a glimpse of that figure completely shedding his robes...

Faint candlelight flickered in his eyes, and by the dim, warm light, he could clearly make out the smooth skin on the other person's body, and even catch a glimpse of a small mole on his neck, hidden among the strands of hair and contrasting against the fair skin.

Ying Zheng found his throat moving involuntarily.

That person seemed to have noticed his gaze, and actually turned around, his entire figure seemingly shrouded in a layer of mist as he approached Ying Zheng in a hazy silhouette.

Perhaps due to being too emotionally stirred, Ying Zheng lost his composure and snapped awake from the dream. The moment he came to, Ying Zheng realized that his entire back was drenched in sweat, and as a cool breeze blew past, he involuntarily shuddered, slowly calming his mind.

Ying Zheng wasn't quite sure about the face in his dream, but the one thing he was certain of was that that person definitely had a flat chest.

It was a youth, and even from afar, one could sense his graceful and elegant appearance.

Ying Zheng uneasily twisted his neck, bracing his hand on the edge of the bed, only to happen to touch a small patch of warm skin, causing him to turn his head involuntarily.

Xu Fu was still sleeping soundly, completely unaffected.

Only two candles were lit in front of the bed, their light weak. When the bed curtains swayed from Ying Zheng's movement of getting up, the candlelight reflecting on Xu Fu's face swayed along with them. Ying Zheng's gaze was involuntarily drawn over. Following the shadow cast by the candlelight on the curtains, his aggressive gaze slowly extended all the way down to Xu Fu's neck.

The lighting was simply too dim.

Ying Zheng kept feeling like he caught a glimpse of a mole on the back of Xu Fu's neck as well, but in the dimness, it seemed like it might just be his own imagination.

"Your Majesty?" At some point, the palace attendant was startled awake, hurriedly scrambled up, walked to the bedside, and called out softly.

Ying Zheng snapped back to his senses, realizing only then that he had been staring at Xu Fu for a bit too long. He raised a hand to touch his forehead, which felt damp and cold to the touch.

Upon seeing this, the palace attendant hurriedly bowed and said, "This servant will go prepare hot water right away."

Ying Zheng uttered an "en" without saying anything else. His mind and soul still seemed to linger within that overly wondrous dream, unable to fully pull away. Ying Zheng twitched his nose, but smelled nothing at all. Driven by a sudden impulse, he bent down and lowered his head, wanting to sniff the scent on Xu Fu's body, but halfway through the action, he felt it was inappropriate and quickly straightened his posture.

Just as the palace attendant brought in the prepared hot water, Ying Zheng let out a breath, shed his outer robes, and simply took a bath. Before he knew it, it was the hour of Mao (5:00 - 7:00 AM).

The night outside had not yet dissipated, but Ying Zheng no longer felt any sleepiness, so he draped a robe over himself alone and began browsing through bamboo slips on the side.

While Xu Fu was still in a hazy, sleepy state, he was jolted awake from his dream. He suddenly sat straight up in bed, startling Ying Zheng, who turned to stare at him, thinking Xu Fu had suffered from a nightmare.

Who would have thought that Xu Fu would lift his chin, open a pair of drowsy eyes, and say to Ying Zheng, "Please, Your Majesty, make a judgment for me."

"What judgment?" Ying Zheng asked, setting aside the bamboo slips.

Who knew? Perhaps Xu Fu was truly still asleep; he suddenly lay flat back down, burrowed further into the quilt, fluttered his eyelids, and closed them again.

Ying Zheng, who had been waiting earnestly for a long while: ......

*

"Master Xu, Master Xu..." A palace maid softly woke Xu Fu up from the bed.

Xu Fu opened his eyes and turned to look—there was no longer any trace of Ying Zheng.

Did he oversleep? Xu Fu rubbed his temples and slowly got up from the bed. Seeing his disheveled clothes, the palace maid involuntarily blushed a little. She helped Xu Fu dress.

Hesitating for a few seconds, Xu Fu asked, "Is His Majesty here?" He clearly remembered giving himself a stern reminder last night to definitely remember to bring up the matter of the judgment with Ying Zheng, so how could he have forgotten it entirely by morning?

However, the palace maid lowered her head and remained silent.

Knowing that these people didn't dare to speak recklessly about His Majesty's whereabouts, Xu Fu stopped pressing the matter. The palace maid led him to have breakfast alone. After hastily finishing a meal that tasted like sawdust, Xu Fu felt somewhat torn: should he leave early, or wait for Ying Zheng to return?

"What time is it now?" Xu Fu asked.

"It is already the hour of Si (9:00 - 11:00 AM)."

Xu Fu's expression instantly became somewhat complicated. He had even missed the office reporting time at the Ministry of Rites (Fengchang Si)! Since he had already missed it anyway, a little longer wouldn't make a difference. Xu Fu instantly grew calm and very familiarly instructed the palace attendants to bring over a small daybed for him to rest on.

When Ying Zheng returned, what he saw was Xu Fu lounging leisurely and contentedly in his palace chambers.

"Your Majesty." As his gaze brushed against Ying Zheng's figure, Xu Fu naturally got up from the daybed in an instant.

Ying Zheng cast a glance at Xu Fu, signaling him to speak if he had something to say.

"I would like to ask Your Majesty to make a judgment for me." Xu Fu stated his purpose directly.

Ying Zheng's expression was slightly complex—it was word for word identical to last night. "What judgment?" Ying Zheng asked again. After asking, Ying Zheng couldn't help but simultaneously size up Xu Fu's expression. Surely he wasn't still half-asleep with hazy eyes even now?

However, what Ying Zheng met was a pair of eyes as clear as water.

Ying Zheng felt relieved.

Xu Fu had no idea what kind of mental scenarios Ying Zheng had run through in just a short span of time; he smoothly and unreservedly recounted his wager with Wang Liu.

After listening, Ying Zheng pondered for a moment. "Then We shall make this judgment." Pausing for a second, he added, "Have you two set the stakes?"

"Not yet." Xu Fu shook his head.

"We might as well add a stake for you. If you win, We shall further promote your official rank and order you to enter and leave the palace freely, serving solely as Our diviner. That way, no one will dare to look down upon you."

A flash of bright light crossed Xu Fu's eyes.

Everything else was unimportant; he had heard the words "promote your official rank"!

Isn't the capital for establishing oneself and making a living in any era having sufficient power and wealth? Well, although he didn't have power or wealth just yet, he would definitely have them eventually! Look, isn't getting a promotion an important step toward the future?

"Then it's settled!" Xu Fu agreed readily.

Ying Zheng nodded. "Go back and prepare for a few days. When the time comes, We will summon you and Wang Liu into the palace." Saying this, Ying Zheng paused. "Zhao Gao, send Master Xu back."

"Understood." Zhao Gao bowed in acknowledgment, then smiled at Xu Fu and said, "Master Xu, please."

Xu Fu finally understood now—"Master Xu" was a relatively affectionate form of address. Titles like "Grand Historian Xu" or "Grand Diviner Xu" were rigid official titles called out for outsiders to hear. For Ying Zheng to dispatch Zhao Gao to personally send him back could be considered a special honor at the time. The nature of it was akin to a mayor in later generations sending his own secretary to drive you home. The face given was simply too generous!

With Zhao Gao being so close to Xu Fu, the people in the Ministry of Rites would naturally have to weigh carefully whether Xu Fu was someone they could bully easily.

Ying Zheng was well aware that within the Ministry of Rites, there were many whose official ranks were higher than Xu Fu's. Qiu Ji and Wang Liu were nothing special, but if those veterans of long standing took notice of Xu Fu and quietly began to scheme against him, that would be troublesome. After all, Xu Fu's official position was too small; as the King of Qin, Ying Zheng couldn't possibly monitor Xu Fu at all times or aggressively step in to back him up in the Ministry of Rites.

Zhao Gao's displays of closeness with Xu Fu were only a temporary measure. The wager delivered right to their doorstep this time was the truly useful tool!

After all, Xu Fu had not yet displayed an overwhelming amount of ability. If he could crush Wang Liu miserably this time, it would be much easier for him to elevate Xu Fu's rank further. No matter how much favor and affection he bestowed upon Xu Fu, it couldn't compare to an actual promotion in rank. Only status and power held in one's own hands were real. This was Ying Zheng's personal realization.

One had to admit that at a certain moment, Xu Fu's train of thought coincided with Ying Zheng's. Xu Fu also believed that relying on Qin Shi Huang alone wasn't reliable—one still had to rely on getting promoted!

……

Zhao Gao cleared the path ahead, led Xu Fu out of the palace, and then escorted Xu Fu straight into the Ministry of Rites.

That Official Liu had learned to be smart; he no longer came out to stir up trouble. After the others quickly swept a glance at Xu Fu, none of them were tactless enough to accuse Xu Fu of arriving late.

Xu Fu's objective of establishing his authority was achieved under the dual assistance of Zhao Gao and Ying Zheng!

Having delivered the person safely, Zhao Gao took his leave.

When Xu Fu returned to the grand hall where official business was handled, his workspace had long since been cleaned to a pristine condition. As he approached, there were no longer any blatant sneers around him, nor any whispered, backstabbing slanders.

Xu Fu's mood instantly grew much more pleasant. When the day came to an end and he returned to his living quarters, that room had also been entirely refurnished, leaving not a single trace of its previous grime.

Indeed, some people just needed a beating to behave. Xu Fu gave a soft snort, finished his meal, and went to bed early.

For the next few consecutive days, Xu Fu maintained a leisurely posture, sitting in the grand hall all day long, flipping through ancient texts and cramming his knowledge. Whenever Wang Liu saw him thereafter, he would cast a cold, ambiguous glance at him before quickly looking away.

The atmosphere between the two soon reached a hair-trigger state.

Within the Ministry of Rites, those with high official ranks were watching the spectacle, while those with low ranks didn't dare to get involved. Everyone quietly awaited the arrival of the day of the trial.

However, before that day even arrived, Wang Liu had already grown deeply dissatisfied.

Xu Fu's daily behavior of wholeheartedly browsing ancient texts seemed to Wang Liu to be nothing more than clasping Buddha's feet at the last minute—completely useless. Wang Liu was bent on exposing Xu Fu's "pretense" of being a high-level expert, so today, right in front of everyone, Wang Liu ran his mouth again and stepped up to provoke Xu Fu.

"Didn't you say you were going to ask His Majesty to make a judgment? How is it that after so long, there's not the slightest ripple of movement? Could it be that Grand Diviner Xu is more adept at empty boasting with his mouth?" Grabbing the hard-earned opportunity, Wang Liu spoke up without showing any mercy.

The rest of the people, who had been silently observing the undercurrents surging between them, all turned their heads in unison to look at the two of them.

Everyone had thought that Wang Liu would give up on tangling with Xu Fu. Sure enough, peace was only temporary! With Wang Liu's intensely proud nature, how could he tolerate Xu Fu stepping over his head?

"Has Grand Diviner Xu nothing to say?" Seeing that Xu Fu remained silent for a long time, Wang Liu finally vented the pent-up frustration in his heart, pressing his advantage with gleeful satisfaction.

"What's the rush?" Xu Fu raised his head, sweeping a nonchalant glance over him, looking entirely as if he didn't take Wang Liu seriously in the slightest.

From his perspective, Wang Liu had planted this flag way too fast. Now, he was dying to lecture him, completely unaware that he would be the one getting his face slapped later on.

"Grand Diviner Xu is certainly in no rush." Wang Liu sneered. He initially wanted to use even sharper words to attack Xu Fu, but considering the persona he usually projected in front of others, he forcefully suppressed this urge.

"Liu'an can just wait patiently." Xu Fu offhandedly brushed him off and lowered his head again to read his ancient texts.

Xu Fu adopted this impenetrable attitude once more, instantly rendering Wang Liu's attacks ineffective. If he kept pushing aggressively, it would only make him look increasingly ridiculous. Wang Liu at least possessed this bit of self-awareness; to salvage his dignity, he put on a cold and arrogant facade and walked back to his seat.

Wang Liu secretly planned that if Xu Fu still made no moves by the second day, he would openly mock Xu Fu for being cowardly and fond of lying. When that time came, he'd see how he could make Xu Fu lose all face.

Unfortunately, Wang Liu's self-satisfied triumph didn't even last for a single day.

"If he's unwilling to admit defeat, that's one thing, but he just has to pretend he has deep ties with the royal palace..." Wang Liu chuckled softly, speaking in a jocular tone to the person beside him.

The person next to him gave a fake laugh, not daring to echo him in any real way.

Xu Fu was already the Grand Diviner, and it was an established fact that he stood above them. To deliberately go and make things difficult for Xu Fu—what if Xu Fu harbored a grudge and retaliated? What would they do then?

Xu Fu had brushed him off, and the rest of the people refused to pick up his conversational threads. Wang Liu's expression turned rather unsightly; he pressed his lips tightly together, a freezing glint gleaming in the depths of his eyes.

A flurry of footsteps suddenly sounded in the hall. Everyone raised their heads to look, and instantly stood up in unison.

It turned out that the person entering was none other than Official Liu!

Why had this great Buddha come here again? The others were completely baffled.

However, they very quickly heard Official Liu open his mouth to dispel their doubts: "His Majesty has summoned Grand Diviner Xu and Grand Diviner Wang to Xianyang Palace." Upon finishing, Official Liu looked with a mixture of shock and suspicion toward the direction of Wang Liu and Xu Fu. In his heart, he probably assumed that Xu Fu had gone and lodged a complaint. He instantly felt a lingering sense of fortunate relief that he hadn't offended Xu Fu too severely; even if anything had gone wrong previously, it could all be blamed on the instigations of those two villains Wang Liu and Qiu Ji.

Official Liu washed his hands clean of any blame in his own mind, thinking that this would spare him from Xu Fu's retaliation.

Over on Wang Liu's side, an unmaskable look of shock hung on his face.

Even if Zhao Gao treated Xu Fu with utmost courtesy, so what? Even if Zhao Gao had escorted him into the palace, so what? That didn't mean Xu Fu truly had connections with His Majesty. From the very beginning, Wang Liu had been dead certain that Xu Fu was spouting tall tales; it was absolute nonsense that Xu Fu could summon the dignified King of Qin to make a judgment. He himself rarely even got a chance to see the King of Qin, let alone Xu Fu!

Yet as luck would have it, the heavens seemed to be deliberately working against him.

Wang Liu cast a dark gaze toward Xu Fu, and could even catch a glimpse of Xu Fu smiling at him in an ambiguous, unreadable manner.

Gritting his teeth fiercely, Wang Liu said, "Grand Diviner Xu, after you."

Xu Fu loved seeing Wang Liu's expression of pent-up rage while having no way to deal with him. He generously took the lead and walked ahead. Once outside, Xu Fu caught sight of the young junior court eunuch waiting there.

That young eunuch recognized Xu Fu, so his attitude toward him was naturally even softer. He smiled and said, "Grand Diviner Xu, this way please." As for Wang Liu? He was naturally ignored completely.

Afterward, when Wang Liu cast numerous cold glares at the young eunuch, the eunuch was utterly bewildered. Wang Liu hadn't looked like much to begin with, and the moment they stepped outside, he was completely overshadowed by Grand Diviner Xu's radiance—naturally, he hadn't noticed Wang Liu. He hadn't done it on purpose.

The young eunuch felt deeply aggrieved.

Returning to the matter at hand, Wang Liu walked glumly behind Xu Fu, and the group entered Xianyang Palace together.

It had been a long time since Wang Liu last had the fortune of catching a glimpse of the young King of Qin. At that time, the King of Qin had not yet seized full power, and the Wang family hadn't taken this King of Qin seriously either. If it weren't for Lao Ai later emerging to contend for power with Lü Buwei, causing the Wang family to waver, the Wang family probably would have already pledged allegiance to Lü Buwei long ago. Now, having witnessed the King of Qin's methods, the Wang family had honestly sworn allegiance to the King of Qin, and even Wang Liu had been repeatedly instructed at home to seize the opportunity to catch the King of Qin's eye.

Ying Zheng sat formally on his knees behind the desk, his expression solemn and cold. Wang Liu, someone usually extremely arrogant, found himself involuntarily lowering his head the moment he saw Ying Zheng's face, not even daring to take an extra look.

At this moment, Xu Fu, walking ahead of him, displayed a unique aura.

Completely devoid of fear, Xu Fu strolled leisurely into the hall and saluted Ying Zheng. Compared to Wang Liu, who turned somewhat cowering the moment he stepped onto a real stage, Xu Fu clearly looked more like someone born into a prominent scholarly clan, as if he had received a fine upbringing in etiquette since childhood, making every gesture of his brimming with an ethereal grace.

Comparing the two, Ying Zheng didn't even need to watch how Wang Liu displayed his skills to already hold a lower opinion of this man in his heart.

"Summoning the two of you here today is because We heard that the two of you have a wager to compete in the art of tortoise-shell divination." Throughout the entire process, Ying Zheng's gaze remained fixed entirely on Xu Fu, not sparing even a shred of extra attention for Wang Liu. The truth was, Ying Zheng simply didn't feel Wang Liu was worth looking at.

Not daring to raise his head to look at Ying Zheng, Wang Liu assumed Ying Zheng was glaring straight at him, and instantly felt as though a fine, dense layer of cold sweat had broken out all over his back.

The aura was simply too overwhelming.

Wang Liu swallowed hard, involuntarily.

In truth, if he had just raised his head for a second and noticed Ying Zheng and Xu Fu engaging in a deep (wide-eyed) quiet (staring) match (staring each other down), he surely would have vomited blood from anger, furious that his presence was so utterly negligible that he wasn't even worth a glance from the King of Qin.

"Have you two agreed upon the stakes?" Ying Zheng asked again.

Regaining his spirit at this moment, Wang Liu preemptively spoke up: "If Grand Diviner Xu loses, I ask that he voluntarily resign from his post."

Standing nearby, Zhao Gao mentally cursed him as an idiot.

Wasn't this Wang Liu a complete fool?

For Xu Fu to serve as Grand Diviner was by command of the King of Qin. If Xu Fu lost, wouldn't that also be equivalent to accusing the King of Qin of being blind for choosing such a talentless person as Grand Diviner?

Regardless of whether Wang Liu had a private grievance with Xu Fu, using this as a wager meant going against the King of Qin. How could Wang Liu possibly come out ahead?

No matter how displeased Ying Zheng was inwardly, it wouldn't show on his face. He merely cast a cold glance at Wang Liu and asked, "And if you lose, what then?"

Startled for a moment, Wang Liu gritted his teeth and said, "If I lose, I will likewise voluntarily resign from the post of Grand Diviner and leave the Ministry of Rites."

Xu Fu chuckled from the side. "Why bother resigning from the post of Grand Diviner? In my view, if you lose, how about you become a servant to me?"

Wang Liu stared in disbelief, never expecting Xu Fu to be so impudent right in front of the King of Qin. "Grand Diviner Xu's demands are truly excessive!" Having said that, Wang Liu bravely raised his head, looking toward the direction of the King of Qin in an attempt to have the wise, martial, and sagacious King of Qin make a ruling in his favor.

Unfortunately, Ying Zheng consistently failed to receive his signals.

It was rare to see Xu Fu smile, and Ying Zheng's gaze was involuntarily drawn over.

With a beauty to look at, who the hell would look at you, Wang Liu?

A ruling in your favor?

My ass!

隐约眼里有烛火在跳动，借着昏黄的光，他能看清对方身上光洁的皮肤，甚至还能瞥清楚他的脖颈上有一点痣，隐藏在发丝之间，衬映在白皙的皮肤之上。
嬴政发现自己不自觉地喉头动了动。
那人似乎注意到了他的目光，竟是转过身来，整个人影都仿佛蒙在一层面纱之中，影影绰绰地朝着嬴政而来。
或许是情绪太过激动，嬴政一个没绷住，从梦中惊醒了过来，清醒过来的那一瞬间，嬴政便发觉自己整个后背都被汗水浸湿了，凉风吹拂而过的时候，嬴政还不自觉地打了个寒颤，慢慢的，心绪就恢复了平静。
嬴政不太敢确认梦中的面孔，但他唯一可以确定的是，那人当然是平胸。
那是个少年，远远的，便能令人感觉到姿容秀丽。
嬴政不自在地扭了扭脖子，手在床边撑了撑，却刚好摸到了一小块温热的皮肤，他不自觉地转过了头。
徐福还在熟睡之中，全然没有受到影响。
床前只点了两根蜡烛，烛光微弱，床畔帷帘因为嬴政起身动作而摇晃的时候，连带着映在徐福脸上的烛光也晃了晃。嬴政的目光被不自觉地带了过去，他顺着那道烛光照映帷帘留下的阴影，一直蔓延而下，富有侵略性的视线慢慢地延伸到了徐福的脖颈处。
光线实在太暗了。
嬴政总觉得自己瞥见徐福的脖颈后面也有一点痣，但影绰间似乎又只是自己的错觉。
“王上？”不知何时宫人被惊醒了，连忙爬了起来，走到床边，低声叫道。
嬴政猛然惊醒，这才觉得自己盯着徐福看的时间有些久了，他抬手摸了摸额头，触手一片湿冷。
宫人见状连忙俯身道：“奴婢这便去准备热水。”
嬴政“嗯”了一声，没说其他的话。他的心神似乎还留在那个过于瑰美的梦境中，没能完全抽离出来。嬴政抽动了一下鼻子，却是什么也没嗅到了。鬼使神差的，他弯腰低头，想要去嗅徐福身上的味道，但是动作做到一半，他又觉得不妥，很快直起了身子。
刚巧宫人准备了热水抬进来，嬴政呼出一口气，脱去衣袍干脆泡了个澡，不知不觉，便是卯时。
外面夜色还未散去，嬴政却已经没了睡意，于是独自披上衣袍于一旁翻阅书简。
徐福睡得迷迷糊糊的时候，陡然从睡梦中惊醒过来，他突然从床上坐了起来，嬴政被他的动作惊了一跳，转头盯着徐福，以为徐福这是被魇住了。
谁知道徐福抬着下巴，睁着一双朦胧的眼，对嬴政道：“请王上为我做个裁决。”
“什么裁决？”嬴政搁下书简问。
谁知道徐福或许是真的未睡醒，他又猛地躺了下去，还往被子里缩了缩，眼皮动了动，又闭上了。
认真等待半晌的嬴政：……
*
“徐先生，徐先生……”宫女轻声唤醒了床上的徐福。
徐福睁开双眼，转头再看时，已经没有嬴政的踪影了。
他睡过头了？徐福揉了揉额角，慢慢从床上起来，宫女看着他衣衫凌乱的模样，不自觉地红了红脸。宫女为徐福穿好衣。
徐福犹豫几秒，问：“王上可在？”他明明记得昨夜他好好提醒了自己一番，一定要记得向嬴政提起裁决之事，怎么早上却忘得一干二净？
宫女却是低头不语。
知道这些人不敢妄言王上去处，徐福也就没再追问。宫女领着他单独用了早膳。食不知味地匆匆用完之后，徐福便有些纠结，他是早些离开呢，还是等待嬴政回来。
“现在是几时了？”徐福问。
“已是巳时了。”
徐福的脸色顿时有些复杂。他连奉常寺上班的时间都给错过了！反正都错过了，也不在乎这一会儿了。徐福顿时淡定了下来，又十分熟稔地招呼宫人搬来小榻供他休息。
等嬴政回来时，见着的便是徐福在他宫中悠然自得的模样。
“王上。”目光触及到嬴政的身影，徐福当然一下子就从小榻上起来了。
嬴政递了一道目光给徐福，示意他有话便说。
“我想请王上为我做个裁决？”徐福直接了当地说出了自己的目的。
嬴政的神色微微复杂，倒是和昨夜分毫不差的话，“什么裁决？”嬴政又问了一次。问完之后，嬴政还忍不住同时去打量徐福的神情，他不会到现在还未睡醒，两眼朦胧吧？
不过嬴政对上的却是一双清澄如水的眼。
嬴政放心了。
徐福不知道嬴政短短时间内，都脑补了些什么东西，他从善如流地将自己与王柳的赌约，毫无保留地交代了出来。
嬴政听过之后，沉吟半晌，“那寡人便来做此裁决。”说完，他顿了顿，“你们可定下赌注了？”
“还未。”徐福摇头。
“寡人不妨再给你加一点赌注，若是你赢了，寡人便再升你的官职，命你出入宫中，独为寡人占卜。如此，便无人敢小瞧你了。”
徐福眼眸里闪过一道亮光。
其它的都不重要了，反正他听见了升官两个字！
在一个时代安身立命的资本，不就是拥有足够的权势和财富吗？呃，虽然现在权势和财富他还都没有，但总是会有的嘛！看，升官不就是迈向未来的重要一步吗？
“那便就此说定！”徐福一口应了。
嬴政点头，“你且回去准备几日，届时，寡人便召你与王柳进宫来。”说到这里，嬴政顿了顿，“赵高，你送徐福回去。”
“喏。”赵高躬身应了，随后对徐福笑道：“徐先生，请。”
徐福现在算是感受到了，“徐先生”算是比较亲近的叫法了，“徐太史”“徐太卜”一类，硬邦邦地叫着官职，那都是叫给外人听的。嬴政将赵高派出来亲自送他，换在当时也算是一种殊荣了。性质就像是后世的市长派自己的秘书送你回家一样。脸给的太足！
赵高与徐福如此亲近，奉常寺里的人自然要好好掂量一番，徐福是不是他们能轻易欺侮的。
嬴政很清楚，一个奉常寺里，也多有比徐福官职更高的。邱机和王柳都不算什么，徐福若是被那些老资历的记在眼中，他们不动声色地收拾起人来，那才麻烦。毕竟徐福的官位太小，在奉常寺里，嬴政身为秦王，也不可能时时关注徐福，强横地为他出头。
赵高与徐福的亲近只是暂时之计。这次送上门来的赌约才是真正有用处的！
徐福毕竟还未展现出过多的能力，若是这次能将王柳碾压得凄凄惨惨，他要再升徐福官位，就容易多了。他就算给徐福再多的荣宠，都比不上一个升官。只有握在手中的地位和权利才是真实的。这是嬴政的切身体会。
不得不说，徐福的思维在某一瞬间和嬴政重合了。徐福也认为，光靠秦始皇是靠不住的，还得靠升官！
……
赵高在前开路，引着徐福出了宫，之后又将徐福给送到了奉常寺内去。
那刘奉常倒是学聪明了，不再出来作妖了，其余的人快速扫了徐福一眼后，却也没谁不识相地指责徐福来迟了。
徐福立威的目的，在赵高和嬴政的双重辅助下，达到了！
将人送到，赵高便离去了。
徐福回到处理公务的大厅之中，他的位置早就被清理得干干净净，在他走近之后，周围也没有什么明目张胆的嘲讽，或是窃窃私语的暗地中伤了。
徐福的心情顿时愉悦了不少。等到当天结束以后，他重新回到住处，那间屋子里也统统换了新，再也看不出一点之前脏污的痕迹。
果然人都是欠抽的。徐福轻哼一声，用过饭食之后，就早早睡觉了。
其后连续几天，徐福都是悠哉哉的姿态，整日坐在大厅里，翻阅古籍，恶补知识。那王柳见着他以后，都是不阴不阳地冷冷瞥他一眼，便快速移开目光。
两人之间的气氛不多时便到达了剑拔弩张的地步。
奉常寺里，官位高的都在看笑话，官位低的都不敢掺合，众人都静静待着比试的那一天到来。
只是还没先等到那天的到来，王柳就已经多有不满了。
徐福每日潜心翻阅古籍的行为在王柳看来，不过是临时抱佛脚，没有卵用罢了，王柳一心想要拆穿徐福那一派高人的“伪装”，于是这日当着众人的面，王柳又嘴贱，上前撩徐福了。
“你不是说要去请王上来做裁决吗？怎的这么久了半点动静也无？莫非徐太卜更擅长嘴上逞能？”好不容易逮住机会，王柳毫不留情地出声。
原本都默默观察着他们之间暗潮汹涌的其余人，此时都不约而同地转头去看他们。
众人都以为王柳要放弃和徐福折腾了，果然，平静都只是暂时的！以王柳十分骄傲的性子，怎会容忍徐福踏在他的头上呢？
“徐太卜无话可说了？”见徐福久不说话，王柳心中憋屈许久的心情终于得到了宣泄，他快意地乘胜追击道。
“急什么？”徐福抬起头，漫不经心地从他身上扫过，一派全然没将他放在眼中的模样。
在他看来，王柳这flag立得实在太快，现在迫不及待地想要数落他，却不知道之后被打脸的还是自己。
“徐太卜是不急。”王柳冷笑一声，原本想用更为尖锐的话来攻击徐福，但随即考虑到他一向在众人面前扮演的模样，便生生将这股欲望压了下去。
“柳安心等等便是。”徐福随口应付了一句，继续低头看自己的典籍。
徐福又是这样一副油盐不进的模样，王柳的攻击顿时都失了效，他再咄咄逼人下去，只会将他衬得越发可笑。王柳好歹还有这个自知，为了挽回自己的姿态，他又故作冷漠高傲地回了位置。
王柳暗自计划着，若是第二日徐福仍旧没有什么动静，他便要嗤笑徐福懦弱，还喜好撒谎了。到那时，看他如何让徐福没脸。
只可惜王柳的暗自得意维持了一天都没到。
“不愿认输也就罢了，还非要装作与王宫关系深厚……”王柳低声笑了笑，用说笑的口吻同身旁的人说道。
旁边那人假笑两声，却也没敢如何附和。
徐福都已经是太卜令，踩在他们头上已成事实，非要去与徐福为难，若是徐福心生报复可怎么好？
徐福敷衍他也就罢了，其余人也不接他的话茬，王柳的脸色这就不太好看了，他紧紧抿着嘴，眼底透着冰寒之色。
一阵脚步声图突然在厅中响起，众人抬头看了一眼，顿时齐齐起身。
原来进来的是刘奉常！
这尊大佛怎的又来了这里？其他人都摸不着头脑。
不过很快他们就听见刘奉常开口为他们解去了疑惑，“王上召徐太卜与王太卜入咸阳宫。”刘奉常说完，都惊疑地看向了王柳和徐福的方向，大概在他心底，以为徐福这是告了状了。心底顿时还暗自庆幸不已，没有将徐福得罪得太狠，就算有何处不对，那也是受了王柳和邱机俩小人的挑拨。
那刘奉常在心底将自己的罪责推得一干二净，以为这样便能免受徐福报复了。
那边王柳脸上掩不住震惊的神色。
虽然赵高待徐福十分礼遇，那又如何？就算赵高带着他进了宫又如何？那又不代表徐福真的便与王上有交情了。从一开始，王柳就是笃定徐福在说大话，徐福定然不可能请到堂堂秦王来做裁决。他都难见秦王一面，何况徐福？
偏偏老天似乎专与他作对。
王柳目光沉沉地看向徐福，还能瞥见徐福对他若有似无地笑了笑。
王柳狠狠咬牙，“徐太卜，先请。”
徐福就喜欢看王柳一脸憋着气，又拿他没办法的模样，他大大方方走在了前面，走出去以后，徐福便一眼看见了候在那里的小内侍。
那小内侍是认识徐福的，对徐福的态度当然更为柔和了，他笑了笑道：“徐太卜，这边请。”而王柳呢，自然是被他无视了。
事后王柳对那小内侍多有冷眼时，小内侍也十分想不明白，那王柳本来长得不出彩，一出门来便被徐太卜夺取了光辉，自是注意不到他了。他也不是故意的。
小内侍感觉到很委屈。
再说这头，王柳憋屈地走在徐福身后，几人一同进了咸阳宫。
王柳还是许久以前有幸得见少年秦王一面，那时秦王还未掌权，王家也未将这位秦王放在眼中，若不是后来多出了个嫪毐与吕不韦争权，导致王家摇摆不定，恐怕王家早就向吕不韦示好了。如今见识到往秦王的手段之后，王家便老老实实效忠秦王了，连王柳在家中也多被嘱咐，要找机会入了秦王的眼。
嬴政跽坐于桌案前，神色肃穆冷然，王柳平日里十分傲气的一人，却在见了嬴政的脸之后，不自觉地就低下了头，甚至不敢多看一眼。
这时，走在他前头的徐福就显露出独到的气场了。
徐福浑然无惧，闲庭信步地走到了殿中，向嬴政行了礼，比起真正上了台面便显得有些畏畏缩缩的王柳，徐福显然更像是出身某个士族之家，仿佛从小就接受着良好的礼仪教育，因而举手投足才满是仙气。
两相对比，嬴政不需要看王柳如何展露本事，便已经心中对这人低看一眼了。
“今日召你二人来，是寡人听闻你二人有一赌约，要比试龟甲占卜之术。”嬴政全程目光都放在了徐福的身上，连一丁点多余的目光都没分给王柳。实在是嬴政不觉得王柳有什么值得可看的。
王柳不敢抬头去看嬴政，还以为嬴政正盯着他呢，登时觉得背后仿佛铺满了一层细密的冷汗。
气势太过强盛了。
王柳不自觉地咽了咽口水。
其实如果他要是抬一下头，注意到嬴政与徐福深（大）情（眼）悄（瞪）对（小）视（眼）之后，肯定得被气吐血，不服于自己的存在感竟是如此之低，还不值得秦王看上一眼。
“你们可约定赌注了？”嬴政又问。
王柳这时来了精神，抢先道：“若是徐太卜输了，便请他自辞其位。”
赵高在旁，心底暗骂了句蠢。
这王柳可不是蠢么？
徐福做太卜令，那是秦王之令，若是徐福输了，那岂不是也相当于在指责秦王瞎了眼，选了这么一个没本事的人做了太卜令。
不管王柳与徐福有无私怨，以此做赌注，都是在与秦王过不去，王柳岂能讨得了好？
嬴政心中再不快，面上也不会显露出来，他只是冷冷地瞥了一眼王柳，问道：“若是你输了，又如何呢？”
王柳怔了怔，咬牙道：“若是我输了，便也自辞太卜一职，离开奉常寺。”
徐福在旁边笑了，“何必辞去太卜之位呢？我瞧，若是你输了，不如与我做个仆人可好？”
王柳不可置信地瞪大眼，没想到徐福会在秦王面前便对他这样无礼，“徐太卜要求实在过分！”说完王柳还勇敢地抬起了头，看向秦王的方向，企图让英明神武睿智的秦王为自己做主。
只可惜，嬴政一直接受不到他的信号。
难得见徐福笑一次，嬴政的目光不自觉地就被牵引过去了。
有美人儿看，谁还看你王柳啊？
做主？
做屁！

chapters.translated_text:
Seeing that Ying Zheng remained silent, Wang Liu unhappily stretched his neck forward a bit more, desperately trying to catch Ying Zheng's attention. Where was there any trace of his usual arrogant and lazy demeanor? He truly looked rather ridiculous.

Only then did Ying Zheng spare him a glance.

Ying Zheng was never stingy with his appreciation for talented individuals, but for those he looked down upon, he was stingy even with his gaze and a pleasant expression.

When facing Xu Fu, Ying Zheng had become increasingly unlike the King of Qin he was when they first met, but now facing Wang Liu, he returned to the position of the King of Qin—majestic, cold, sharp-gazed, and merciless in his reprimand: "You demanded that Grand Diviner Xu resign from his post as Grand Diviner if he lost—was that not excessive? Yet Grand Diviner Xu merely asked you to be his servant. What kind of nerve do you have to feel that he is being excessive? This is the first time Gu has ever seen someone so selfish."

Hearing this string of rebukes, Wang Liu felt his legs go soft and he suddenly dropped to his knees. "Your Majesty... Your Majesty, Liu did not mean it that way, it's just..." It was just that he had indeed wanted to trick Xu Fu, not get tricked himself. If he really lost, how could he willingly be Xu Fu's servant? Wouldn't that be throwing away all his face and ruthlessly trampling his dignity into the dirt?

Wang Liu suddenly felt that Xu Fu possessed terrifying scheming skills, using a tactical retreat before the King to set him up so harshly!

He turned his head to look at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu innocently blinked. He had indeed wanted to humiliate Wang Liu. Wasn't this exact method used by Wang Liu back then when he deliberately gave Palace Attendant Liu the idea to spare him and assign him to scrub the latrines? It looked like he was thinking for the other person, but in reality, it trapped them even worse. He was putting what he learned into practice right away on Wang Liu. How could Xu Fu know that in Wang Liu's mind, he had already been imagined as a scheming bitch.

"The bet is thus set, and if you lose, you must fulfill it. Gu will personally supervise," Ying Zheng decided with a single word, leaving Wang Liu no chance to change it.

"Have you considered the process for the competition?" Ying Zheng asked again.

Xu Fu didn't speak, leaving the opportunity to Wang Liu; this kind of complex mental activity was not suited for him.

True to form, Wang Liu didn't waste Xu Fu's "good intentions," and hurriedly said, "Your Majesty, tortoise shells have been used since ancient times to divine good and bad fortune, and misfortune and blessings. Liu, lacking in talent, has achieved some initial understanding, and thus thought to divide the entire competition into three stages: easy, difficult, and extremely difficult divination. These three stages."

"Divining what?"

Hearing Ying Zheng reply with these three words, Wang Liu immediately said, "Naturally, it is to divine..."

Xu Fu mercilessly interrupted him. "Naturally, it should be up to Your Majesty to decide."

Wang Liu choked for a moment, but didn't dare to contend with Ying Zheng for the right to speak, so he could only echo, "Let Your Majesty decide."

"Someone, bring the tortoise shells," Ying Zheng suddenly instructed the palace attendants.

The palace attendants went down and fetched the tortoise shells, brought a brazier, and brought wooden strips, placing them one by one in front of Xu Fu and Wang Liu.

"As it happens, then divine Gu's recent fortune and misfortune," Ying Zheng said calmly.

Wang Liu hadn't prepared in time and was stunned upon hearing this. "This... this, Your Majesty, Liu is more accustomed to using ancestral items."

"Oh, where are they? Gu will have someone go fetch them," Ying Zheng still showed no intention of letting them prepare for a few days first.

Wang Liu nodded stiffly, then still lowered his voice to say, "Your Majesty, before divination, one must burn incense and bathe, and also offer sacrifices to ancestral spirits."

In the past, Ying Zheng didn't know the process of divination either; it was only after seeing Xu Fu use tortoise shells for divination that he learned those prophecies of misfortune and blessings came from such a method. Hearing Wang Liu describe the process as so complicated, Ying Zheng unconsciously frowned. "Tortoise shell divination is this complex beforehand?"

Everyone is the same; when talking about the field they excel in, they become animated and smug. Wang Liu unconsciously straightened his back and discoursed eloquently, "The method of tortoise shell divination has been passed down since ancient times. There are records stating that tortoise shell divination uses the shell as a medium to obtain instructions from ancestral spirits. Every time we sacrifice to ancestors, the rules are extremely elaborate. Now, to ask the ancestors to guide us on misfortune and blessings, we naturally also need to burn incense, bathe, and sacrifice to ancestral spirits before we can sincerely obtain the final result."

Xu Fu stood nearby, his gaze not even flickering.

Divination truly requires sincerity; in certain solemn ceremonies, burning incense and bathing are basic tasks.

However, by later generations, the process of tortoise shell divination had long been greatly simplified, and there was no way to verify whether its efficacy had weakened. Moreover, later generations believed that tortoise shell divination was not asking ancestors for instructions, but rather asking all the gods in the heavens for guidance. Tortoise shells are spiritually attuned; a millennium-old tortoise shell gathers the spiritual energy of heaven and earth, and naturally can communicate with the gods.

Xu Fu didn't know which statement was correct; anyway, he had been doing divination this way for many years and couldn't change it now. Besides, if every divination were that troublesome, it would be better to just casually search for an online divination website and cast a lot there, wouldn't it?

After finishing, Wang Liu even glanced sideways at Xu Fu.

Looking at Xu Fu's appearance, he didn't look like someone from a prominent family. A self-taught fellow, what kind of foundation could he possibly have? And who would have taught him the rules? Compared to himself, wouldn't Xu Fu's actions by then be as crude and unrefined as a country bumpkin?

Wang Liu's heart immediately settled a great deal. Even without any preparation, he would definitely be able to crush Xu Fu. When Xu Fu slunk away in disgrace from the Bureau of Palace Attendants, that would truly be deeply satisfying!

Xu Fu couldn't help turning his head to look at Wang Liu. "Why are you staring at me? Are you suffering from an inferiority complex because you're too ugly?" Wang Liu was acting like he had a sudden fit, fixing a tight gaze on him with a smile at the corners of his eyes. No matter how he looked at it, it felt wretched, practically ruining that greasy, powdered face to the point of extreme ugliness.

The smile on Wang Liu's face stiffened and his mouth opened, but he couldn't very well pick a fight with Xu Fu openly in front of the King of Qin.

With a single sentence, Xu Fu blocked the other man back, and finally, the guy stopped frequently shooting those disgusting gazes at him. Xu Fu was extremely satisfied, turned his head back, and continued to maintain his own unshakeable composure.

Ying Zheng immediately sent people to fetch Wang Liu's customary items.

"Then does Grand Diviner Xu still need to prepare anything?" Zhao Gao considerately asked from the side.

Xu Fu shook his head. "No need."

Wang Liu felt deep contempt in his heart, but constrained by Ying Zheng's presence, he still suppressed the impulse to mock Xu Fu. However, images of Xu Fu losing face terribly in front of the King of Qin had already begun to well up in his mind.

An agonizing silence spread across the hall.

Wang Liu was itching with eagerness, dying to teach Xu Fu a lesson quickly, while Xu Fu's mind was wandering far away, thinking: If it were before, it would be time for lunch by now, and standing here, he was actually a little hungry. Xu Fu felt somewhat resentful toward Wang Liu; if it weren't for this fellow making a fuss, he could at least openly move a small couch to rest inside Emperor Shi Huang's hall, with palace maids serving snacks at his hand.

Just as they were each preoccupied with their own thoughts, an attendant brought over Wang Liu's customary items.

Afterwards, a palace maid led Wang Liu away to burn incense and bathe.

Xu Fu slightly frowned and shifted his position; standing in this posture for too long was somewhat uncomfortable.

A small couch was brought to Xu Fu's side. The palace maid seemed to understand Xu Fu's thoughts very well and smiled shyly, "Sir Xu, please."

Ying Zheng glanced at the palace maid, his gaze growing slightly dark. Then he looked at Xu Fu, his voice unconsciously turning a bit gentler, "If you feel tired, you might as well go behind the screen to rest for a while. That Wang Liu will probably take some time to fuss around."

Of course Xu Fu wouldn't refuse Ying Zheng's good intentions. He went behind the screen to rest as before, and the palace maid thoughtfully served food.

On the other side, while Wang Liu was bathing with a sense of guaranteed victory and blooming joy, Xu Fu was leisurely leaning against the small couch, savoring his food, not taking this competition to heart in the slightest.

There were two main principles in the tortoise shell divination Xu Fu had learned: first, rarely divine recent misfortune and blessings; second, it is difficult to divine future great fortunes.

The meaning was that because the time was too close and the requests too detailed, divining short-term fortune and misfortune easily led to inaccuracies. Second, trying to divine events a hundred or even a thousand years later was practically impossible, because neither your ancestors nor the gods were so omnipotent that they could know everything and tell you everything.

Therefore, when Xu Fu generally performed divination, he would match hexagrams with some nonsense and ultimately arrive at a result.

As for how to be a hundred percent certain—let alone Xu Fu, even the most famous necromancers in history could hardly achieve that!

Xu Fu didn't care about competing with Wang Liu. He had already defeated too many people just relying on his tongue; what could Wang Liu possibly count as?

By the time Wang Liu had finished his preparations, an hour had already passed.

Ying Zheng repeatedly shook his head. "If divination matters always require such a huge fuss, what should be done in a critical moment?" During the capping ceremony, if the person beside him hadn't been Xu Fu, but another Grand Diviner, I'm afraid with all this tossing and turning, any preemptive opportunity would be lost. By the time the divination was finally completed, the events would have already happened—what use would it be then?

Zhao Gao chimed in from the side, "Sir Xu is still much more adept."

Zhao Gao originally just wanted to flatter Xu Fu who was resting behind the screen, but who would have thought that after pondering for a moment, Ying Zheng would earnestly agree with Zhao Gao's words: "Gu thinks so too."

Zhao Gao was stunned for a moment, thinking to himself: This Wang Liu is bound to lose sooner or later; whose heart the King favors is already a matter clear at a glance.

Xu Fu slowly walked out from behind the screen and sat down at Ying Zheng's feet. Because of the large movement, his robes were slightly disheveled. But someone with good looks is just that willful; no matter how messy his clothes were, it wouldn't give off a desolate or sloppy feel, but instead generated three parts of casualness and laziness.

"Wang Liu should be arriving," Xu Fu said.

The palace maid understood and immediately went inside to remove the small couch and food.

Before long, Wang Liu's figure indeed appeared at the hall entrance. He had changed into a new set of robes—not looking like the later generations' bagua vestments, but instead dressed in brocades and fine silks, as if he were going to attend some kind of banquet.

Seeing Xu Fu sitting on his heels in the lower seat of Ying Zheng, Wang Liu felt internal disdain, viewing Xu Fu as a sycophantic flatterer.

He bowed to Ying Zheng, hoping that when Ying Zheng cast his gaze upon him, it would carry a hint of admiration. It was a pity Ying Zheng didn't even look at him, directly waving his sleeve and saying, "Let us begin."

Wang Liu's full anticipation was doused by a basin of cold water, and the expression on his face couldn't help but stiffen.

Xu Fu didn't have time to deal with him, directly calling palace maids to move the items over, and then repeating his previous actions—tossing the wooden strips into the brazier, picking them out, and placing them into the circular holes of the tortoise shell.

This tortoise shell wasn't the life-saving one that had protected him once; this was a new one Ying Zheng had ordered people to find. Xu Fu touched the surface of the shell; its texture wasn't as comfortable as the previous one. Although the last one looked ancient and worn, it was indeed a rare find.

However, Xu Fu didn't want to put on airs like Wang Liu, going through so much trouble just to cast a lot. He wondered if, when his divination turned out wrong, Wang Liu would be so ashamed and angry that he would strip off his clothes and go on a crazy naked run through the Xianyang Palace.

Xu Fu was wildly complaining in his heart, but his expression remained completely unchanged, and his movements were extremely steady.

When Wang Liu saw that his operational process was so simple, he couldn't help laughing out loud.

The technique was amateurish, full of errors, and how could he treat a tortoise shell so crudely? How could he possibly divine a hexagram?

Wang Liu truly couldn't hold back anymore and said, "I really don't know whose school of thought Grand Diviner Xu comes from!" The mockery in his tone was far too thick, essentially suspecting that Xu Fu was a total amateur.

Xu Fu was indeed an amateur, but he couldn't help the fact that he was a formidable amateur.

Without even lifting his eyelids, Xu Fu calmly dealt with it. "Are you really that curious about my lineage? Could it be that Grand Diviner Tai has fallen under the spell of my robes and decided to join my school as well? But what a pity, my teacher doesn't like your type. Grand Diviner Tai had better stop looking at me..." Xu Fu paused, pulling out a wooden strip as he spoke and turning to meet Wang Liu's instantly changing face, "...because I've already finished divining."

Wang Liu was furious. "Nonsense! How could you possibly be this fast? Tortoise shell divination requires sincerity, concentration, and meticulousness! Have you achieved even one of these? Could it be that knowing you couldn't divine anything, you just casually perfunctorily brushed it off, attempting to hoodwink His Majesty?" With that, Wang Liu turned his head to look at Ying Zheng, attempting to get his brilliant, wise, and sagacious King of Qin to uphold justice for him and speak a fair word.

Then Ying Zheng indeed spoke up, saying with an unpleased expression to Wang Liu, "Before Gu, why all the noise? Grand Diviner Xu took it calmly, whereas you haven't made a move for ages. Such empty posturing—could it be that you've grown fearful in your heart?"

Xu Fu cast a hint of an appreciative glance at Ying Zheng.

Emperor Shi Huang could talk trash too!

This eloquence was simply too good!

A pale, ashen expression covered Wang Liu's face. He was still somewhat dazed, unable to understand why he had drawn the King's reprimand once again.

Wang Liu aggrievedly lowered his head and began fiddling with the objects in his hands.

With a particularly mischievous intent, Xu Fu stood up and said to Ying Zheng, "I have already divined it, so I will speak first. Later on, Grand Diviner Tai must remember to divine something different from me, otherwise there might be a suspicion of plagiarism."

Wang Liu's face turned even paler and ashen, and he gritted his teeth hard. "That goes without saying!"

Xu Fu nodded. "Then that's good." He paused, then continued, "According to the tortoise shell hexagram, Your Majesty has a joyous event coming recently."

Wang Liu couldn't help but let out another sneer.

Mentioning joyous events first when fortune-telling and divining—isn't this just what street-wandering Jianghu charlatans loved to say? He had said it all along: this Xu Fu had no real skills!

Little did he know that the very first sentence Xu Fu had spoken on the street had nothing whatsoever to do with a joyous event. Therefore, hearing Xu Fu say, for once, that he had a recent joyous event, Ying Zheng was somewhat taken aback.

"Whence comes this joy?" Ying Zheng asked with rising interest.

"Probably..." Xu Fu paused for a few seconds before honestly speaking out, "You're about to happily become a father." After saying this, Xu Fu felt as though these three words he uttered seemed to carry some other meaning as well, but suddenly he couldn't remember what it was, so he stopped right there.

Happily become a father?

Ying Zheng: ......

Very few people knew about Lady Hu's pregnancy; Xu Fu couldn't have heard it from elsewhere. There was only one possibility: he had genuinely divined it. But the child in Lady Hu's womb was not his bloodline... Previously, Xu Fu had clearly seen this, and even brought up the words "green hat" again. Why on earth was he saying now that he had a joyous event?

The gaze Ying Zheng cast at Xu Fu grew increasingly complex.

Wang Liu refused to accept this. How could anyone use tortoise shell divination to figure out that someone was about to have a son immediately? That was impossible!

"Does Grand Diviner Xu dare to explain what the hexagram on the tortoise shell is? Why would you say Your Majesty has a joyous event?"

Xu Fu turned his head and used a single sentence to block him right back. "Want to steal my techniques? Sorry, unique secret skills are never passed on to outsiders. Since I have already calculated the result, why hasn't Grand Diviner Tai hurried up and finished your divination? Could it be that you really intend to plagiarize me?"

Having repeatedly failed in his bouts with Xu Fu, Wang Liu already had a ball of fire pent up in his chest. Now, seeing Xu Fu spout nonsense so casually, his sense of grievance reached its peak. He raised his voice and rebuked, "What does Grand Diviner Xu not dare to say? Could it be that you're just spouting utter nonsense? What unique secret skill? Never seen before! And you dare to pull it out and use it! Shameless!"

"Of course you've never seen it, because my method is the authentic technique passed down from ancient times, whereas yours is merely later generations haphazardly adding their own understanding to form today's divination methods. But speaking of its subtlety, how can it compare to the ancient methods? Look, you still haven't divined it yet. Doesn't Grand Diviner Tai feel ashamed?" Xu Fu opened his mouth and started bluffing again.

"You!" Wang Liu couldn't find a single retort. A mouthful of blood instantly choked up in his throat. He silently swallowed it back, glared with a pair of bloodshot eyes, and once again accelerated the movements of his hands.

About half an hour passed. In this weather, Wang Liu actually worked up a sweat all over. Finally letting out a breath of relief, he put down the tortoise shell in his hand, raised his hands in a bow, and said, "Your Majesty will recently experience both blessings and misfortune."

"Speak."

"Your Majesty's inner palace will certainly acquire beauties recently—this is the blessing."

Ying Zheng frowned, and unconsciously glanced toward Xu Fu, feeling a nameless sense of a guilty conscience in his heart.

Ying Zheng was not a lustful person; whether beauties were added to the inner palace made no difference to him. Furthermore, at this time he was just beginning to wield supreme power, and had even less inclination to waste his energy on the inner palace. Wang Liu's flattery had truly missed the mark.

"And what about the misfortune?" Ying Zheng asked in a cold voice.

Wang Liu didn't notice the chill in Ying Zheng's words, and secretly felt proud in his heart that he had divined one more item than Xu Fu; no matter what, his skill was superior to Xu Fu's. Thus, Wang Liu continued, "Your Majesty's side will likely face chaos and turmoil recently. Your Majesty needs to take good care of yourself."

After saying this, Wang Liu once again waited for his brilliant, wise, and sagacious King of Qin to lavishly praise him.

"Oh?" Ying Zheng's voice grew even colder. "Turmoil by Gu's side? Since that's the case, then from now on, Grand Diviner Tai shall remain in the palace and carefully look out for this turmoil for Gu."

Eh?

Wang Liu was dumbfounded once again.

Why... why was this completely different from what he had imagined?

Xu Fu remained calm. Even though Wang Liu had divined two things, Xu Fu didn't show any extra facial expressions.

Actually, Xu Fu was secretly feeling thrilled inside: *Aha, Wang Liu is finally going to experience being detained in the palace just like he was back then!*
chapters.source_text:
见嬴政不语，王柳不甘心地又往前抻了抻脖子，拼了命地企图引起嬴政的注意。哪里还有平日里的半分倨傲懒散之态？模样实在有些可笑。
嬴政这才分了一点目光给他。
对于贤才，嬴政并不吝啬自己的赏识，但是对于他不大瞧得上的人，他连目光和好脸色都吝啬给。
嬴政面对徐福时变得越来越不像当初初见的那个秦王，但是现在面对王柳，他又回到了秦王的位置上，气势威严冷厉，目光锐利，说出口的斥责也是毫不留情，“你要求徐太卜输了便辞去太卜令之位，便不过分了吗？而徐太卜只是命你做他仆人，你又何来的脸觉得他过分？寡人倒是头一次见到如此自私之人。”
王柳听完这串斥责，脚下一软，陡然跪地，“王上……王上，柳并非此意，只是……”只是他的确想要坑徐福，而不是想坑到自己身上。若是真输了，他怎么会甘愿给徐福做仆人？那岂不是丢尽脸面，将他的尊严狠狠扔在地上踩！
王柳顿觉徐福好生可怕的心机，在王上面前以退为进，竟是这样将他狠狠坑了一把！
他转头看向徐福。
徐福无辜地眨了眨眼。他的确是想羞辱一下王柳来着，当初王柳故意出主意让刘奉常放他一马，排他去洒扫茅厕，用的可不就是这样的招数吗？看似为对方着想，实际却是将对方坑得更厉害。他现学现卖，就用在王柳身上了。徐福哪里知道，自己在王柳的心中，已经被脑补成了一个心机婊。
“赌注就此定下，输了便要履行，寡人会亲自监督。”嬴政一口决定，没留给王柳更改的机会。
“比试过程可考虑好了？”嬴政又问。
徐福没说话，将机会留给了王柳，这种复杂的脑力活动不适合他。
王柳果然没浪费徐福的“心意”，急急道：“王上，龟甲自古以来，测吉凶，测祸福，都有所应用。柳不才，初有所得，遂思考将整个比试分为三个阶段。容易，困难，极难占卜。这三个阶段。”
“卜什么？”
王柳听见嬴政回应了三个字，马上便道：“自然是卜……”
徐福毫不留情地打断了他，“自然应由王上说了算。”
王柳被噎了噎，倒是不敢跟嬴政抢话，只能跟着道：“由王上说了算。”
“来人，取龟甲来。”嬴政突然吩咐宫人道。
宫人下去拿了龟甲，端了火盆，带了木条来，一一摆放在徐福和王柳的面前。
“正好，那便测寡人近日的吉凶祸福吧。”嬴政淡淡道。
王柳准备都来不及，闻言愣了愣，“这……这，王上，柳更惯于用家传之物。”
“哦，放在哪里？寡人命人前去取来便是。”嬴政依旧没有开口让他们先行准备几天的意思。
王柳僵硬地点了点头，随后还是低声道：“王上，占卜之前，需得焚香沐浴，还要祭祀先灵。”
从前嬴政也并不知占卜的过程，还是见了徐福用龟甲占卜之后，他才知道原来那些祸福吉凶的批语，是从这样的方式中得来的。如今听王柳将过程说的如此繁复，嬴政不自觉地皱了皱眉，“龟甲占卜之前如此复杂？”
所有人都一样，谈及自己擅长的领域，都会眉飞色舞、洋洋得意，王柳都不自觉地挺直了腰背，侃侃而谈道：“龟甲占卜的方式从上古流传而来，曾有记载言，龟甲占卜，便是以龟甲为媒介，获得祖宗先灵的指示。每逢祭祀祖先时，规矩都十分繁复，如今要请祖先指点祸福吉凶，自然也要焚香沐浴、祭祀先灵，方能诚心求得最后的结果。”
徐福站在旁边，目光都不带闪一下的。
占卜的确需要诚心，在某些庄重的仪式上，焚香沐浴是基础工作。
但是到了后世，龟甲占卜的流程早已被简化了许多，也无从验证其效力是否减弱。而后世更认为，龟甲占卜并非是请祖先指示，而是请满天神明指点一二。龟甲通灵，千年龟甲聚天地之灵气，自可与神明相通。
徐福也不知道究竟哪个说法是对的，反正他都这样占卜好多年了，改也改不过来了，更何况若是每次占卜都那样麻烦，那还不如上网随便搜个在线卜卦网，来卜一卦不就好了？
王柳说完之后，还瞥了一眼徐福。
他看徐福的模样，就不像是从高门出来的，一个自学成才的家伙，身上哪有什么底蕴？又哪会有老师教他规矩？和自己一比，到时候徐福的举动岂不是就如同乡民一般粗陋？
王柳顿时定心不少。哪怕毫无准备，他也定然可以压过徐福，那时徐福灰溜溜地从奉常寺离开，那才叫大快人心！
徐福忍不住转头看着王柳，“你盯着我做什么？因为自己太丑，自卑吗？”王柳就跟突然犯病了一样，目光紧紧盯着他，眼底还带着笑容。怎么看都怎么觉得猥琐，可算是将那张油头粉面的脸，给破坏得难看至极了。
王柳脸上的笑容僵了僵，张了张嘴，但也不好在秦王面前公然与徐福掐起来。
徐福一句话把对方给堵回去了，终于不再拿那恶心的目光频频看向自己了，徐福满意不已，将头扭回去，继续维持自身的淡定如斯。
嬴政马上派了人去给王柳取他惯用的物件。
“那徐太卜可还需准备什么？”赵高从旁体贴地问。
徐福摇头，“不必。”
王柳心中轻视不已，不过碍于嬴政当前，他还是压住了嘲讽徐福的冲动。只是他的脑海里已经随之涌现了，徐福在秦王面前丢了大脸的画面。
难耐的安静在殿内蔓延开来。
王柳摩拳擦掌恨不得赶快给徐福一个教训，徐福却是神游天外，想的是，换做以前，这个点儿都该吃午饭了，站在这里他还真的有点饿。徐福有点埋怨王柳，若不是这家伙作妖，他一个人在秦始皇的殿内，好歹还能大大方方搬个小榻休息，手边还有宫女送上小食。
就在他们心思各异之时，有内侍取来了王柳惯用的物件。
之后便有宫女带着王柳焚香沐浴去了。
徐福微微皱眉，挪了挪步子，这个姿势站得久了不太舒服。
一张小榻被送到了徐福的身边，那宫女似乎很了解徐福的心思，羞涩一笑，“徐先生请。”
嬴政朝那宫女看了一眼，目光微沉。随后他才看向徐福，声音不自觉地温和了几分，“若是觉得累了，还是到围屏后去休息一会儿。那王柳想必还要折腾些功夫。”
徐福当然不会推拒嬴政的好意，他依旧到围屏后去休息，宫女贴心地送上了食物。
那头王柳正胜券在握、心花怒放地沐着浴时，徐福却是一派悠闲地倚着小榻，品着食物，半点没将这场比试放在心上。
徐福所学到的龟甲占卜中有两个讲究，一是少占近日祸福，二是难测未来鸿运。
意思就是呢，因为时间挨得太近，所求太细，短期内的祸福吉凶测出来，便很容易不准确。二是，要测百年甚至千年后的事，那几乎是测不出来的，因为不管是你祖先还是神明，也没有神通广大，什么都能知道，什么都能告诉你的地步。
所以徐福一般占卜之时，都是卦象配上几句胡扯，最后得到一个结果。
要说如何百分百的笃定，莫说徐福了，就算是历史上再出名的术士，也很难做到这一点！
徐福是不在乎与王柳比试的，他靠着一张嘴已经赢过太多人了，王柳又能算什么？
等王柳做好了准备，已经是一个时辰之后的事了。
嬴政连连摇头，“若是占卜之事都需如此大动干戈，危急时刻又该如何？”加冠礼时，若跟在他身边的不是徐福，而是另外的太卜，恐怕被这样一折腾，什么先机也都不占了，等到好不容易占卜出来时，事情都已经发生了，还有何用？
赵高从旁附和，“还是徐先生更高一筹。”
赵高原本就是夸一夸在围屏后休息的徐福，谁知道嬴政沉吟一阵，还很认真地应了赵高这句话，“寡人也如此认为。”
赵高愣了愣，心道，这王柳将来不输都得输了，王上的心偏向谁，已是一目了然的事。
徐福慢腾腾地从围屏后走出来，绕到嬴政脚边坐下，因为幅度过大，他的衣袍还稍稍有些凌乱，但是颜好的人，就是如此任性，哪怕衣衫再凌乱，也不会给人以落拓邋遢之感，反倒还生出三分潇洒与慵懒。
“王柳应该要到了。”徐福开口说。
宫女会意，立刻进去撤了小榻和食物。
没过一会儿，王柳的身影果然出现了殿门口，他换了一身衣袍，并不像是后世的八卦服，反倒打扮得锦衣华服，好像要去参加什么宴会一般。
王柳看到徐福跽坐在嬴政下首，心中不屑，将徐福视为了阿谀奉承之人。
他朝嬴政拜了拜，希望嬴政将目光落到他身上时，带出几分赞赏之意来，只可惜嬴政连看也没看他一眼，直接挥袖道：“这便开始吧。”
王柳满心的期待又被一盆冷水浇中，脸上的表情忍不住僵了僵。
徐福没空理他，直接叫宫女搬来东西，然后重复着上次的动作——将木条扔入火盆，拣起，放入龟甲圆孔之中。
这龟甲并不是那个护了他一命的保命龟甲，这是嬴政命人新寻来的。徐福摸了摸龟甲的表面，没上一个质地舒服。上一个虽然看上去古老又破旧，但确实不可多得。
不过徐福也不想像王柳那样装逼，卜个卦还要搞那么多麻烦事，也不知道等他卜错了的时候，会不会羞愤地扒掉自己身上的衣服，疯狂地在咸阳宫里的裸奔。
徐福内心疯狂吐槽，面上神色却是丝毫未动，手上的动作更是十分稳健。
王柳见他操作过程如此简单的时候，便忍不住笑出了声来。
手法稚嫩，错误颇多，对待龟甲何等粗暴？又怎么能卜出卦来？
王柳实在忍不住了，便道：“真不知徐太卜是出自何人门下？”语气中的嘲讽味道实在太浓，意思其实就是在怀疑徐福压根就是个半吊子。
徐福的确是个半吊子，但抵不住人家是个厉害的半吊子啊。
徐福连眼皮都不带掀的，淡定应对，“我出自什么师门你很好奇吗？王太卜莫非是拜服于我的袍服之下，决心也要投入我的师门了？不过可惜，我的老师不喜欢你这样儿的。王太卜还是不要再看我了……”徐福顿了顿，说着抽出木条，转头对上王柳瞬间变色的脸，“因为我已经卜完了。”
王柳气极，“胡说八道？你怎么可能如此之快？龟甲占卜，需要诚心，精心，细心！你何曾有一样做到？莫非是知晓自己卜不出来了，便如此随意敷衍，企图蒙蔽王上吗？”说完王柳又转头看向了嬴政，企图他英明神武睿智的秦王为他做个主，说句公道话。
然后嬴政的确开口了，他脸色不虞地对王柳道：“寡人之前，吵闹什么？徐太卜安然处之，反倒是你半天未见动手，如此虚张声势，难道是心生惧意了？”
徐福隐隐用赞赏的目光看了一眼嬴政。
秦始皇也会嘴炮啊！
这口才简直不要太好啊！
王柳脸上一片青白之色，他还有些懵逼，他想不明白，为何自己招来的还是王上斥责？
王柳憋屈地低下头，开始捣鼓手中之物。
徐福特别坏心眼儿地站起身来，对嬴政道：“我已卜出，我就先说了，等会儿王太卜可要记得与我卜出不同的事来才好，不然恐有抄袭之嫌。”
王柳脸色更加青白，狠狠咬牙，“这是自然！”
徐福点头，“那便好。”他顿了顿，接着道：“据龟甲卦象显示，王上近日有喜事。”
王柳实在忍不住又嗤笑了一声。
算命卜卦先说喜，这不是的街头招摇撞骗的江湖术士才爱说的话吗？他就说，这徐福没什么真本领！
他却不知道，当初在街头徐福第一句说的，可跟喜事完全没有关系。所以嬴政听见徐福难得说一句，他近日有喜事，都有些发怔。
“喜从何来？”嬴政兴起，连忙问道。
“大概就是……”徐福沉默几秒，还是老老实实地说了出来，“要喜当爹了吧。”说完之后，徐福又觉得自己说的这三个字好像还有别的含义，但是徐福又突然记不起了，便点到这里就打住了。
喜当爹？
嬴政：……
胡姬有孕之事，知晓之人甚少，徐福不可能从别处听来，只有一种可能，他是真的占卜出来了。但胡姬腹中之子，并非他的血脉……之前徐福明明也看出来了，甚至又重提“绿云”二字，如今为何又要说他有喜事呢？
嬴政看着徐福的目光愈发复杂了。
王柳不服气，哪有人用龟甲占卜，能算出说你马上要生儿子了？这不可能！
“徐太卜可敢说一说，龟甲上是何卦象？为何你会说王上有喜事？”
徐福转头又一句话把他堵了回去，“想要偷师？不好意思，独门绝技，概不外传。我既然已经算出结果，王太卜还不加紧卜算出来？难道真的要抄袭我？”
与徐福过招屡屡战败，王柳心中已经憋着一团火了，如今见徐福张口就来，他心中的不忿更是达到了顶峰，他拔高了声音，斥责道：“徐太卜有何不敢说的？莫非是信口胡诌？什么独门绝技？见所未见！也敢拿出来用！恬不知耻！”
“你当然没见过，因为我的手法是上古流传下来的正宗手法，你的不过是后人胡乱加入自身理解，才有了如今的卜卦之法，但论其精妙，如何能与古法相比？你瞧，你还没卜出来。王太卜不觉得丢人吗？”徐福张嘴又开始忽悠。
“你！”王柳一句也对不出来，喉咙里登时又哽了一口血，他默默咽下，瞪着一双布满血丝的眼，再度加快了手上的动作。
大约过去了半个时辰，王柳在这个天气竟是忙出了一头热汗，他终于松了一口气，放下手中龟甲，抬手拜道：“王上近日有福有祸。”
“说。”
“王上近日后宫必得美人，此乃福。”
嬴政皱起了眉，他还不自觉地往徐福那边瞥了一眼，心中莫名觉得心虚。
嬴政并非好色之人，后宫添不添美人，并没有什么区别，何况这时他初掌大权，更没有那个心思将精力浪费在后宫中了。王柳这个马屁可谓是拍在了马腿上。
“那祸呢？”嬴政冷声问。
王柳没察觉到嬴政话中的冷意，心中还暗自得意自己比徐福多卜出一项来，无论如何，他的本事都比徐福要厉害，于是王柳继续道：“王上近日身边恐有祸乱，王上需要多加保重才是。”
王柳说完之后，又继续等待着他英明神武睿智的秦王好好夸奖他一番。
“哦？”嬴政的声音更冷了，“寡人身边有祸乱？既如此，那接下来便请王太卜留于宫中，好好为寡人注意这番祸乱吧。”
诶？
王柳又懵逼了。
这……这为何和想象中全然不一样啊？
徐福依旧淡定，王柳就算卜出两件事来，他也没有多余的表情变化。
其实徐福正在心中暗爽，哎呀，王柳终于也要经历一次当初他被扣留在宫中的事了！

chapters.title: 第35章
chapters.translated_text:
Stay in the palace?

At first, Wang Liu considered this an honor, but when he suddenly came to his senses, he realized that staying in the palace was just a disguised form of detention.

It was not surprising that the King of Qin would take such a measure; after all, matters of calamity were not things to be spoken of lightly. They could be trivial or grave, and if it were a grave matter, how could he not be suspected? Cold sweat broke out on Wang Liu’s forehead instantly. He had only been thinking about bickering with Xu Fu and had completely overlooked this point. Only now did he feel regret. The more he regretted it, the more he blamed Xu Fu. Upon reflection, he felt even more convinced that Xu Fu had deliberately provoked him to make him speak so irrationally.

Xu Fu was truly calculating!

……

Xu Fu stood to the side, feeling speechless under the frequent hateful glares cast by Wang Liu. How was Wang Liu mentally whipping him, this "villain," again? It was Qin Shi Huang who said he would be detained, not him. Was there something wrong with Wang Liu’s brain? He was still looking at him! Still glaring at him with such resentment!

Xu Fu felt a bit like teaching Wang Liu how to behave again, but by the time he turned his head, Wang Liu had already withdrawn his gaze.

Xu Fu: "..."

Wang Liu probably knew he couldn't escape the fate of being kept in the palace. Anyway, he wasn't being kept as a eunuch, so there was nothing to fear. Thus, the desire to defeat and humiliate Xu Fu took over his entire mind again. He took the initiative to court death by asking Ying Zheng: "Since both Liu and Grand Diviner Xu have divined the same omens of fortune and misfortune, how shall we judge who wins and who loses?"

"Wait," Xu Fu interjected, "When the event occurs, won't we know then?"

Wang Liu’s reflex was to snap at Xu Fu, "What kind of lousy method is that?" but then he thought, besides letting facts verify it, what other method could serve as a basis for judgment? Should they compare who divines faster? Wouldn't Xu Fu still win?

Wang Liu gritted his teeth, suppressing the displeasure in his chest, "Then... then we shall wait a few days."

"Mm, take your time, I'm not in a hurry," Xu Fu said magnanimously.

Wang Liu could barely maintain his superficial etiquette and composure. You're not in a hurry! I am! Watching you serve as the Grand Diviner makes my heart ache!

Ying Zheng nodded and finally gave his verdict, "Then we shall follow what Grand Diviner Xu said." He paused, then added, "Grand Diviner Xu shall also stay in the palace these days."

Before Wang Liu could gloat, he heard Ying Zheng suddenly add, "During the day, just let Zhao Gao send an attendant to take you to the Fengchang Temple to perform your duties."

Thinking of being able to experience the luxurious and comfortable palace life for a while longer, the corners of Xu Fu’s eyes curved, and a faint smile appeared on his face, as if ice and snow were beginning to melt. "Nuo," he replied crisply.

Ying Zheng, behind the desk, suddenly felt as if his heart had been tapped, neither too lightly nor too heavily.

A tingling sensation.

Truly strange...

Meanwhile, in Wang Liu’s heart, it felt as if someone had struck him with a heavy hammer; the heartbreak was enough to crush him.

Why was Xu Fu’s treatment different from his?

Xu Fu and Wang Liu had occupied Ying Zheng’s time for long enough; Ying Zheng waved his hand and had the palace servants take them away.

Although there was no strict rule against outside men entering the inner palace at this time, someone like Wang Liu naturally couldn't wander around at will. A tall, stern-faced, and fierce-looking attendant blocked Wang Liu’s path, "This way, please."

Then, Wang Liu watched helplessly as Xu Fu, led by the King’s personal attendant, walked toward another majestic palace.

Wang Liu, feeling severely unfairly treated: ...

*

Xu Fu was indeed brought by a palace maid to Ying Zheng’s sleeping quarters. When he stepped inside, he was stunned for a moment.

Was he really going to sleep in the same bed as Qin Shi Huang again?

And what about Wang Liu?

Xu Fu had thought Qin Shi Huang would play the same game with Wang Liu—the trick of a monarch and subject sleeping side by side. So it turned out Wang Liu didn't have the opportunity to be recorded in history books for this! Probably because... he was too ugly?

After Xu Fu walked in, he bathed and changed clothes. Then, a palace servant found some ancient texts for him. Xu Fu flipped through the bamboo slips to pass the time, waiting for Ying Zheng to return for dinner. As for the Fengchang Temple, he was openly skipping work again.

Ying Zheng, having just grasped all the power of the Qin State, was extremely busy. Xu Fu’s eyes grew sore from reading. He lifted his head to rub his temples, and when he looked outside, he saw the moon was already high in the sky. He didn't even know when the candles had been lit in the hall.

Just as he was about to ask the palace servant if the King had returned, he heard footsteps.

Ying Zheng walked in from outside, his tall figure blocking much of the candlelight. As soon as he stopped in front of Xu Fu, Xu Fu was completely shrouded in his shadow.

Due to the oppressive feeling from the other man, Xu Fu stood up immediately. Instead of calling him "Your Majesty," he asked, "Is it time to eat?" After asking, Xu Fu was stunned himself. He realized he had been so dizzy from reading the bamboo slips that he had blurted that out.

Ying Zheng didn't think much of it; he assumed Xu Fu was truly hungry, so he took Xu Fu to dine.
