"M-Mr. Xu?" Seeing Xu Fu standing there and hesitating to board the carriage, the attendant couldn't help but call out nervously.

Xu Fu pulled up the carriage curtain with a dark expression. He paused, then turned and walked back into the Fengchang Temple. "Wait for me here."

The attendant didn't dare say anything, only nodding dumbly.

Su Yi had originally been about to follow him out and happened to bump into Xu Fu, who was walking back in. "What’s wrong?" Su Yi immediately stopped in his tracks and asked.

It was rare for Xu Fu to show Su Yi a faint smile. "I must trouble you to keep an eye on something for me." With that smile, his features seemed to come alive.

Feeling that he had been entrusted with an important task, Su Yi’s heartbeat quickened slightly, and his voice turned hoarse. "...What is it?"

"Keep an eye on the person responsible for the security, the person who made the wager with me, and anyone you believe to have an intimate understanding of the inner workings of the Fengchang Temple..." Xu Fu said slowly. In truth, this scope wasn't small, but there couldn't be many people who would reveal telltale signs; identifying the target shouldn't be too difficult.

Even if that person couldn't be found, they would eventually reveal their intentions. Was it merely to steal the bamboo slips and watch Xu Fu’s anxious appearance, or did they have another use for them after taking them?

"Alright." Su Yi agreed directly.

Xu Fu nodded, giving him a look of trust, before leaving the Fengchang Temple again.

After a busy day, he was now so hungry he felt like his chest was sticking to his back. He didn't have the energy to stir up trouble with those people in the Fengchang Temple again; hungry and angry, why make things difficult for himself?

After Xu Fu came out, the attendant hurriedly lifted the carriage curtain. Xu Fu nodded slightly at him before boarding the carriage.

Upon returning to the palace, Xu Fu did not pause. As soon as Ying Zheng appeared, he handed over the bamboo slips. Ying Zheng, however, had little interest in perusing them. Without lifting his head, he said, "We shall proceed according to the auspicious date you divined."

Xu Fu felt a bit helpless. If he were the only one submitting bamboo slips, he would naturally have set the date himself. But since someone had deliberately challenged him to a contest, if he were to just brush it off, there was no guarantee it wouldn't spread and become a handle for others to use, painting him as someone who abused his position for personal gain.

Thinking this, Xu Fu pushed the bamboo slips toward Ying Zheng.

Only he would dare to be so "willful" when the King of Qin had clearly refused.

Ying Zheng had no choice but to set down his stylus and pull the bamboo slips closer. Perhaps even he hadn't realized that his indulgence toward Xu Fu was growing with each passing day.

He flipped through them casually and recognized Xu Fu’s unique "handwriting" at a glance. He picked up the bamboo slips to read them, naturally ignoring the other set. Ying Zheng did not believe there was anyone currently whose abilities surpassed Xu Fu’s.

"The twenty-first?" Ying Zheng looked up at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu nodded. "In the twelfth month, it is difficult to find an auspicious day; most are unsuitable for various matters. However, nothing is absolute. There is no absolutely auspicious day, nor an absolutely ominous one. The twenty-first is just right. On this day, the Winnowing Basket star is on duty. When the Winnowing Basket star is on duty, the year is prosperous; it is auspicious for sacrifices and repairing graves. It also carries the meaning of fields, silkworms, cattle, and horses covering the mountains, and gold, silver, jade, and grain filling the granaries. It perfectly aligns with the requirements of the La sacrifice. This day forbids weddings and breaking ground, which does not conflict with the La sacrifice."

Ying Zheng already trusted Xu Fu enough, and now, after reading the bamboo slips and hearing Xu Fu’s detailed explanation, he naturally had no complaints.

He set the bamboo slips down, having no intention of flipping through the other set. "That is very good."

Xu Fu walked over, unfolded the other bamboo slips, and said, "This person chose the twenty-ninth." He then fell silent.

Ying Zheng only glanced at it and felt that the person’s narrative was chaotic, deliberately pretentious, and annoying. He immediately lost interest in reading further. He waved his hand, his brow slightly furrowed. "No need to look further; this person’s level is far behind yours."

Since Ying Zheng had already said as much, Xu Fu naturally wouldn't ask him to take a closer look.

After all, they weren't his bamboo slips; what did it have to do with him?

Xu Fu collected the bamboo slips and handed them to the attendant nearby.

Ying Zheng buried himself in state affairs for a long time. When the sun set and the sky grew dark, a palace servant came forward to knead Ying Zheng’s shoulders to relieve his fatigue. Ying Zheng set aside his work, remembered that he had neglected Xu Fu, and hurriedly asked, "How long did it take you to carve the characters on the bamboo slips?"

"Two days."

"Why so long? In the future, you may order your subordinates, or the attendants and palace servants, to carve them for you," Ying Zheng said without a second thought.

Xu Fu was not willing to be someone who suffered in silence. Since there was trouble, why hide it? Xu Fu said calmly, "It could have been finished in one day, but when I went to the Fengchang Temple today, I learned that my bamboo slips had been stolen. With no other choice, I had to pick up the stylus and start all over again."

Upon hearing this, all the other matters Ying Zheng had been contemplating vanished. His expression changed, and his eyes were tinged with anger. "Your bamboo slips were stolen? Things locked inside the Fengchang Temple can be stolen? Does that mean there is no safety at all in this Xianyang Palace?"

Xu Fu remained silent.

His official position in the Fengchang Temple was still too low; he couldn't even make a scene without restraint. Since he didn't have the entire temple in the palm of his hand, he was naturally much more passive in some matters.

After Ying Zheng’s outburst, he quickly regained his composure. He called the attendant holding the bamboo slips to his side. "Tomorrow, you shall go to the Fengchang Temple and conduct a thorough investigation into this matter."

The attendant nodded in acknowledgment.

Xu Fu felt much more relaxed. With the First Emperor intervening, he would surely get a result.

After giving instructions to the attendant, Ying Zheng stopped dwelling on the matter. He moved with Xu Fu to another palace to dine. Fusu had also been brought over by his wet nurse. He stood in the hall, refusing to sit, and only after Ying Zheng entered with Xu Fu did Fusu hurriedly pay his respects before taking his seat.

During the meal, Ying Zheng had become accustomed to his gaze drifting toward Xu Fu involuntarily.

Xu Fu held his chopsticks, but because he had used his fingers too forcefully over the past two days, his hand holding the chopsticks was trembling slightly. Xu Fu couldn't help but frown inwardly. If only there were a spoon; at least he wouldn't look so shaky—where was the immortal aura in that?

Even the slightest movement from Xu Fu caught Ying Zheng’s attention. Ying Zheng’s gaze swept over and landed on Xu Fu’s hands.

Ying Zheng’s brow immediately furrowed. He couldn't help but recall when Xu Fu had entered the palace to report the auspicious date to him; his hands had looked even more pitiful then. He wondered how many times the stylus had poked his hands and how many blisters had been worn into them.

The injuries on Xu Fu’s hands now were surely caused by the theft of the bamboo slips, right?

Ying Zheng’s expression darkened further.

Fusu had originally looked up happily, about to speak to his father, but when he happened to meet such a face on Ying Zheng, his little face immediately changed color. He whispered, "Why is Father angry?"

Xu Fu also stopped struggling with his chopsticks. He looked up at Ying Zheng and met those dark, bottomless eyes. Xu Fu was stunned for a moment and looked away uncomfortably. "What is wrong, Your Majesty?"

Ying Zheng ordered an attendant to summon the imperial physician, then answered Xu Fu’s question. "I saw that your hands were injured, and thinking of the theft at the Fengchang Temple, I am naturally displeased."

Fusu’s gaze fixed on Xu Fu, suddenly turning strange.

Xu Fu himself felt the atmosphere become strange in an instant.

"Many thanks, Your Majesty." After thinking for a long time, Xu Fu could only come up with these four words.

Ying Zheng, however, felt even more displeased. Xu Fu’s gratitude didn't seem very sincere.

The imperial physician was quickly summoned, and the meal had to be interrupted. After the physician examined and applied medicine to Xu Fu’s hands, he said, "It is nothing serious. Once the blisters break, the wounds will feel painful when they touch water for a short time, but they will be fine in a few days."

Ying Zheng’s expression did not soften; his gaze remained glued to Xu Fu’s hands.

Xu Fu’s hands were coated with a greenish herbal paste, making them look a bit messy and ugly, but in Ying Zheng’s eyes, they didn't seem so. The fair, slender fingers were slightly curled, marked with red traces and green medicinal stains, which only served to make his hands look as white as jade.

Ying Zheng suddenly thought of the new imperial seal he had ordered to be made—lustrous, uniform in texture, and beautifully translucent.

It was just like Xu Fu’s hands.

To compare a person to jade—this was a first.

Even with such injured hands, they could stir up restless feelings in the depths of Ying Zheng’s heart. Ying Zheng felt he was truly ill, and quite severely! He was almost like a beast in heat!

Ying Zheng’s face grew darker, and he lost his appetite. He slapped his chopsticks down and suddenly stood up. "I have other matters to attend to. Fusu, you shall keep Mr. Xu company for the rest of the meal."

Fusu nodded, not understanding why, his expression obedient.

Xu Fu also watched Ying Zheng walk out with a confused expression.

However, Ying Zheng’s early departure wouldn't hinder Xu Fu’s appetite.

*

A youth had been standing at the entrance of the Fengchang Temple for a long time. When Su Yi came from behind, he caught sight of that figure at a glance, dressed in official robes, his color like spring flowers.

Why was he standing there in a daze? Su Yi was puzzled and called out, "Grand Diviner Xu."

Xu Fu’s expression was still somewhat dazed. At Su Yi’s call, he immediately snapped back to reality, pretending to have been deep in thought about life and the future at the gate. He gave a shallow "Hmm" and lifted his feet to walk inside. Su Yi was fooled by Xu Fu’s appearance, and his own doubts vanished. He followed Xu Fu inside, saying, "Today, we will surely be able to catch the thief."

"Thank you for the trouble," Xu Fu said.

Su Yi’s heartbeat quickened again, and he couldn't speak for a long while.

Xu Fu’s mind was not on the theft at all. He reached his seat, sat down, and picked up the cup on the desk, holding it in his palm, but his thoughts drifted to the startling dream of last night.

He knew that the First Emperor often had dreams after nightfall. Every time the First Emperor woke up in a fright, he would sense it, but the winter nights were cold, and Xu Fu was too lazy to struggle to get up. At that time, he had buried his questions in his heart, wondering why the First Emperor had such frequent dreams and what kind of terrifying dreams they were. But last night, Xu Fu finally experienced that bitterness himself.

A magnificent and topsy-turvy dream, entangled with lust.

It was truly terrifying.

The fearless Xu Fu finally understood why the First Emperor was so miserable every time he woke up in a fright. The feeling of being unable to control one’s body and being dominated by desire was truly terrible.

As Xu Fu thought about this, his face turned sallow.

The others in the hall assumed he was still angry about the theft of the bamboo slips, and the atmosphere was so cold that everyone unconsciously became careful even when walking.

Only one person was bold enough to walk straight up to Xu Fu and ask with a slight bow, "Grand Diviner Xu, I wonder which day the King has chosen as the auspicious date?"

Xu Fu raised his eyes and glanced at him sideways. Because he was in a bad mood, his voice was naturally much colder. "The twenty-first."

The person in front of him was the one who had made the wager with him. Originally, Xu Fu couldn't remember his name, but after Su Yi started keeping an eye on him, he mentioned the name in Xu Fu’s ear.

His name was Zhao Yi. His family had some connection to the Qin royal family, but that connection was too distant, and it was difficult for Zhao Yi to gain favor before the King of Qin. Relying on the protection of his ancestors, he entered the Fengchang Temple. He held people like Wang Liu in contempt, and he was extremely unconvinced by Xu Fu. Once Wang Liu fell, Xu Fu was riding high. So, before the La sacrifice, Zhao Yi couldn't wait to jump out.

Zhao Yi could barely be called good-looking. The expression on his face had originally been very calm, but after hearing those four words from Xu Fu, Zhao Yi couldn't suppress the change in his expression, and a look of resentment flashed across his face.

He was unwilling to accept it. That day, when Wang Liu was arguing fiercely with Xu Fu in the hall, he had heard every word Wang Liu said. Wang Liu had hinted that Xu Fu’s looks were extraordinary, and he used them to gain the King of Qin’s favor. After Zhao Yi took it to heart, the more he thought about it, the more he felt it was so. Otherwise, given Xu Fu’s youth and weak abilities, how could he sit in the position of Chief Diviner without a clear background? In his view, he was merely relying on the King of Qin’s favor.

Now, seeing this result, Zhao Yi immediately felt that Xu Fu must have pulled some strings behind the scenes, or that the King of Qin, because of Xu Fu, hadn't even looked at his bamboo slips before setting the date.

Xu Fu looked at Zhao Yi with a cold gaze. He asked unhurriedly, his voice cold, "Grand Diviner Zhao seems to know when I chose the auspicious date?"

Zhao Yi met Xu Fu’s gaze and smiled. "The twenty-first was not my choice, so naturally, it was Grand Diviner Xu’s choice."

Xu Fu withdrew his gaze and said nothing more.

Currently, Zhao Yi was the most likely suspect, whether in terms of familiarity with the Fengchang Temple, his relationship with the guards, or his motive. But Zhao Yi hid it well; at least Xu Fu couldn't find anything wrong with him.

Having asked for the result, Zhao Yi turned and left. As soon as he turned, his expression darkened. Naturally, he was dissatisfied with this result.

The others had long expected this scene and only treated it as a joke.

From the Wang Liu incident, they knew it wasn't easy to deal with Xu Fu, so why were there still people who didn't know their own limits?

Zhao Yi had chosen the twenty-ninth, which was not long after Xu Fu’s date. Ordinary people might think that with the dates so close, how could one distinguish between good and bad? But in the method of calculating auspicious dates, let alone two different days, even two consecutive hours could have completely opposite auspicious or ominous meanings.

If Xu Fu knew what Zhao Yi was thinking, he would surely burst into laughter.

With this level of skill, he dared to compare himself to him?

Xu Fu had a unique advantage in this era. What he had learned was the essence of the ancients. Although some methods and techniques had gradually been lost in the long river of history, it was undeniable that in his era, divination, fortune-telling, and face reading had evolved to an advanced level.

For example, while others only used turtle shells for divination, how did they calculate auspicious dates? They would take every day of the month and seek out the omens to know if the day could be used. The speed was naturally much slower, and if one was not careful, it was easy to make mistakes.

Turtle shell divination was something that worked occasionally but often failed.

No matter how spiritual something was, if you asked too often, that spirituality would be worn away.

Xu Fu had his own method of calculating auspicious dates; he would have to be crazy to use turtle shells. So, while it looked like he was using turtle shells that day, he was actually just calculating silently in his heart. He quickly eliminated many ominous days and then chose the most suitable day from the auspicious ones, which was both fast and reliable. Who won and who lost had basically been decided from that moment.

At this time, someone brought the ceremonial robes—the robes to be worn by the selected Diviners, Historians, and Invokers at the La sacrifice, with the Invoker’s ceremonial robes being the most exquisite and solemn.

Naturally, this drew another round of envious or jealous gazes.

Among them, Xu Fu and Su Yi were the ones who attracted the most hatred.

Xu Fu and Su Yi were both newcomers. Su Yi was fine; he got along well with everyone. But Xu Fu was always elusive, and his temperament was noble, making him incompatible with them. How could people not be jealous of such a person who was rising the fastest?

Of course, if these people knew that Su Yi being selected was also just a stroke of Xu Fu’s pen, they would surely be jealous of Su Yi as well.

Hugging the big thigh, hugging the big thigh—they had actually succeeded in hugging it!

However, after waiting for a while, everyone put away their jealousy, and some even secretly laughed in their hearts.

Everyone had been handed their sacrificial robes, so why was Xu Fu's the only one missing? Was it an omission, or was Xu Fu going to be removed from the list of attendees for the La sacrifice?

Never mind the others, even Su Yi's expression shifted slightly, though it wasn't appropriate for him to step forward and ask Xu Fu at that moment. What if there really had been a mishap? Asking him right then would be like twisting a knife in Xu Fu's heart.

A stormy tide of shock and suspicion raged within Xu Fu's heart as well, but what kind of blows hadn't he taken? Nothing could possibly be worse than last night's dream. Xu Fu's expression remained calm and indifferent, without the slightest hint of being shaken.

Those who had originally intended to watch a joke unfold now found themselves forced to wipe the smiles from their faces.

Regardless of how resentful they were that Xu Fu had secured the position of Grand Astrologer, just looking at Xu Fu's demeanor at that moment left them trailing far behind. What point was there in continuing to mock him?

The crowd exchanged awkward glances and returned to their respective places.

It was at this moment that Xu Fu summoned the guard on duty. The onlookers, who had thought the show was over, suddenly felt their hearts leap back into their throats. Was the Grand Astrologer about to play for keeps?

Once the guard arrived, he dropped to his knees at Xu Fu's feet. Had Xu Fu's expression not been so ice-cold, the man might have grabbed Xu Fu's legs and begged for mercy.

"Grand Astrologer Xu, this matter truly has nothing to do with me..." the man bitter-clung to his defense.

"You were responsible for the watch, yet you neglected your duty. Putting aside whether the thief has any connection to you, how can you brazenly claim this has nothing to do with you?" Xu Fu looked down at the man from on high, his heart not softening in the slightest just because the other party showed a weak, pleading side.

Due to years of fortune-telling, Xu Fu's thinking was, in certain respects, relatively rational. People or matters that could evoke his sympathy and softness were exceedingly rare.

For someone like the guard, Xu Fu felt no sympathy whatsoever.

You take the pay, you do the job.

Since he held this position and enjoyed a stipend from the Qin state, he ought to give it his all and fulfill his duties. If he failed to do so, he naturally had to bear the responsibility. Did he really think a kowtow and a plea for mercy would let him off the hook? If acting pitiful could buy exemption, wouldn't everything descend into chaos?

"I..." The man was left completely speechless by Xu Fu's retort. He had simply assumed Xu Fu would put on an air of broad-minded magnanimity, let him off with a warning, and focus strictly on catching the thief.

The guard's expression immediately turned bitter, his heart consumed by extreme anxiety and dread.

"Relate what happened that day in detail. When did you check? Before what time were the bamboo slips still there? After what time did you discover they were missing? What were you doing at the time? Tell me every single thing clearly," Xu Fu said in a cold, hard voice.

The guard involuntarily shivered, his gaze darting this way and that.

"That day... that day, after nightfall, I remained on guard duty at the Bureau of Ceremonies. At the Hour of Chou (1–3 AM), I checked once, and the bamboo slips were still there. At the Hour of Yin (3–5 AM), I went to fetch some water and checked again; the slips were still there. By three quarters past the Hour of Mao (5–7 AM), the slips were... were gone..."

"What were you doing at that time?"

"...I... I carelessly fell asleep." The guard shivered again as he spoke.

Xu Fu looked at him coldly, his gaze piercing. "And you still call this having nothing to do with you? If my attitude hadn't been strict, were you planning to just gloss over it?"

The guard lay prostrate on the ground, his body trembling, not daring to utter another word.

"Grand Astrologer Xu, spare me this once! I truly don't know how those bamboo slips were lost! The slips are of no use to me either... I..."

Xu Fu interrupted him. "Did you see any shady characters?"

"N-no."

Before Xu Fu could speak again, Su Yi stepped forward. His lean and wiry frame suddenly burst with strength as he effortlessly hoisted the guard up by his collar with a single hand. "Whether you did or not, you'd better choose your words carefully."

Pushed to his absolute mental limit, the guard finally snapped and shrieked, "Y-you treating me like this! This is nothing less than extorting a confession through torture!"

Su Yi loosened his grip, dropping the guard back to the floor. The rest of the onlookers involuntarily winced at the sight, as if they could feel the sudden, painful impact themselves.

"He's lying," Su Yi said with certainty. "We might as well just send him to the prison for an interrogation."

Hearing the word "prison," the guard instantly panicked, a flurry of emotions—panic, terror—flitting across his face one after another.

While Su Yi was pressing him with severe interrogation, Xu Fu quietly swept his gaze around the hall. A thief was bound to feel guilty; no matter how well they masked it, flaws would always show unless their psychological fortitude was exceptionally strong.

As Xu Fu thought this, he withdrew his gaze empty-handed.

That "thief" really did have extraordinarily strong psychological fortitude! Not a single flaw was showing!

No wonder he was able to steal the bamboo slips right out from under the Bureau of Ceremonies—he certainly had some skills.

"Send him to the prison." Dropping these three words, Xu Fu ordered people to seize the guard and drag him out.

The guard finally cracked completely and yelled, "No, I'll talk! I'll talk! I'll say everything!"

Deep down, Xu Fu actually shared a striking resemblance to Ying Zheng: you piss me off, and do you think you can just wrap things up whenever you please? Stop joking. Playing games with me comes at a price. Without even blinking an eye, Xu Fu said, "Drag him out." He delivered the word "drag" with such chilling coldness that the rest of the onlookers couldn't help but shiver, not even daring to watch the drama anymore, lest they end up on Xu Fu's blacklist.

As it turned out, in the future they would simply have to badmouth Xu Fu quietly in their own hearts; even speaking ill of him behind his back wasn't safe. This man Xu Fu truly could not be offended... truly could not be offended... must not be offended!

Su Yi walked past Xu Fu and lowered his voice. "Rest assured, Grand Astrologer Xu, I will continue to keep an eye on this matter."

Su Yi was being so attentive that Xu Fu was somewhat surprised. Although he had instructed Su Yi to do so, he hadn't actually expected Su Yi to take the matter to heart—after all, their friendship wasn't that deep. Who would treat someone else's affair as their own and constantly worry about it?

"Then I am deeply grateful," Xu Fu was forced to offer his thanks once more.

Over at the prison, once the guard was delivered and checked in, he happened to cross paths with the inner palace attendant sent by Ying Zheng to investigate. With a few instructions given to the officials in charge, the guard was in for a rough time. The thief was not far from being dragged out into the light.

After making a proper fuss over the guard, Xu Fu left the Bureau of Ceremonies.

He still hadn't figured out what was going on with those sacrificial robes.

Faced with the Grand Astrologer leaving early, the crowd—who had just been thoroughly intimidated—collectively turned a blind eye.

Xu Fu's face had practically become the universal pass of Xianyang Palace; even without an inner attendant accompanying him, the guards and servants were long used to seeing him roam the royal palace.

Walking outside the Qin King's bedchamber, a palace attendant spotted him and gasped, "Master Xu?!"

Xu Fu nodded. "I'm here to rest." Mid-sentence, he suddenly paused. Xu Fu abruptly realized that he had already started treating the royal palace like his own home! Not to mention coming and going every day, sleeping here every night, and eating every meal here as well... When he didn't want to serve at the Bureau of Ceremonies and wanted to slack off, his choice had actually been to return to the royal palace.

In what way did the Qin King's bedchamber look like it belonged to Qin Shi Huang? Why did it invisibly feel more and more like it belonged to him instead?

"Master Xu?" The attendant looked at his cool, aloof profile and couldn't help calling out again.

Xu Fu gave the attendant a slight nod, stepped across the threshold into the hall, and not a single palace attendant or servant tried to stop him.

Xu Fu once again realized something was amiss.

He had grown accustomed to living in the royal palace and had stopped overthinking it, but yesterday's terrifying dream seemed to have dragged everything he hadn't re-evaluated in days right back to the forefront of his mind.

He moved unhindered through Qin Shi Huang's palace, and the attendants treated him practically as the master of the estate. Clearly, he no longer needed to stay in the palace—at least not to follow Qin Shi Huang around constantly by his side—yet over the past few months, he had somehow continued to sleep in the same bed as Qin Shi Huang? Even Qin Shi Huang's two sons had been squeezed off into the side hall by him.

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more wrong it felt.

Could that dream be some kind of portent? A sign that he was about to embark on the path of a southern-style broken sleeve (homosexuality)?

Xu Fu silently shivered. He knew his appearance was exceptional and made it terribly easy to win others' favor with his face, but he didn't want to be a cut-sleeve at all!

He wondered if there was a poison called "cut-sleeve poison" hidden in that incense. Xu Fu's imagination ran wild. He felt an urge to immediately rush to a private place, pull out his little brother, and stroke it to check: is it still holding up okay?

Xu Fu stopped in his tracks, turned, and headed toward the alcove in the side hall where the chamber pot was kept. The alcove was shielded by a curtain, so that should keep him out of sight.

Although the attendants were puzzled as to why he suddenly changed direction mid-walk, out of habit, they followed behind Xu Fu until they were blocked outside by the curtain.

Palace attendants were right outside.

Xu Fu gritted his teeth, gripped by an indescribable, faint sense of shame.

But this matter had been weighing on his mind for far too long. Gritting his teeth against the shame, Xu Fu reached out and groped his crotch.

An attendant suddenly hurried over, calling out in a low voice, "Master Xu, His Majesty is looking for you."

How did Qin Shi Huang know he was back in the palace? Oh right, this was Qin Shi Huang's territory; was there anything the man didn't know?

Startled, Xu Fu almost grabbed his own little Fu. He put on a calm expression, pulled up his trousers, straightened his robes, and struck a dignified pose, instantly radiating an otherworldly aura. Yes, exactly—with that face, even if he had just emerged from the outhouse, he would still look thoroughly celestial.

He lifted the curtain and stepped out. An attendant glanced up at him.

Master Xu was truly different. Even after using the outhouse, he still looked as though he hadn't touched a speck of dust, and you couldn't catch even a whiff of any foul odor.

If Xu Fu knew what the attendant was thinking at that moment, he would surely be dumbfounded.

Real immortals didn't use outhouses; using the outhouse naturally meant it smelled! Even Qin Shi Huang's business must stink, right? Maybe he could take a whiff another day... Ugh, bah! What kind of sniffing is that? How could handling basic biological functions ever be tied to an otherworldly aura?!

...

Ying Zheng was waiting for him in the bedchamber. As soon as Xu Fu walked back in, his gaze landed on Ying Zheng's tall figure. A flash of imagery from that dream streaked across his mind; Xu Fu shuddered, hastily banishing the scene from his thoughts, suppressing his guilty conscience and faint sense of shame, and slowly walked behind Ying Zheng.

His mind had been wandering far too much. He got too close and failed to stop his steps in time just as Ying Zheng happened to turn around.

Xu Fu crashed squarely into Ying Zheng's chest.

Good grief... it was hard!

The impact made Xu Fu's nose sting with soreness, but he still had to struggle to maintain his composure. So he forced his eyes open, pressed his lips together, and stood unshaken even as tears welled up in the corners of his eyes.

Ying Zheng was startled, and his own heart felt even guiltier at that moment.

After all, Xu Fu didn't know how many times he had been bumped into because of him; the bruising on his forehead had only just barely faded.

The old injury had just healed, and now a new one was about to be added?

Ying Zheng grabbed Xu Fu's wrist and reached out to lift his chin. "You bumped yourself! Let Us take a look."

Xu Fu was dazed, looking frail (and bewildered) as he allowed Ying Zheng to tilt his chin up just like a male lead flirting with a maiden in a movie. Goosebumps broke out all over Xu Fu's body; he felt as though his image in front of the attendants had collapsed in that single instant...

"It's nothing," Xu Fu recovered his wits and quickly averted his face, intending to slip past Ying Zheng's fingers. Who would have guessed that Ying Zheng suddenly exerted force, pinching Xu Fu's chin tight.

Pinched! Tight!

Qin Shi Huang, do you actually think you're flirting with a beauty?!

"Your Majesty," Xu Fu called out with added weight in his voice, a layer of ice instantly coating his face.

Oh, can you imagine what it's like to look into a pair of misty eyes—made hazy because his nose was bumped and aching—staring at you with shimmering tears?

Can you imagine a face that usually radiated pure chill, never sparing anyone a single extra smile or showing a single fraction of weakness, now wearing the exact opposite expression?

Ying Zheng suddenly felt like he was beyond saving.

Perhaps he had been struck by an incurable poison...

Meeting Ying Zheng's seemingly majestic gaze—which was actually drifting all over the place—Xu Fu couldn't help furrowing his brow. He had to take matters into his own hands, forcibly grabbing Ying Zheng's wrist and pulling his hand away with a blank face.

The attendants kept their heads lowered, eyes fixed on their noses and noses on their hearts, plunging into temporary blindness.

Snapping out of his trance as if waking from a dream, Ying Zheng turned around as if nothing had happened and pointed to the robes held by the attendant beside him. "The sacrificial robes worn by the Grand Astrologer were far too crude, so Us had another set made for you."

So the reason they hadn't sent the sacrificial robes wasn't because they forgot him, but because something better was waiting!

Xu Fu stepped forward and picked up the robes. The embroidery was exquisite, and the ancient totems embroidered upon them carried a heavy, solemn aura. They were indeed vastly superior to the sacrificial robes delivered to the Bureau of Ceremonies.

He was probably the only person in the world to enjoy such treatment.

Xu Fu's heart tightened slightly.

Was Qin Shi Huang treating him this well really not out of some ulterior motive? But when he had disguised himself as Qin Shi Huang's favorite concubine, he hadn't noticed Qin Shi Huang reacting in any special way. Or was all of Qin Shi Huang's behavior merely meant to grant him the treatment a meritorious official deserved?

Historically, Qin Shi Huang didn't seem like a petty person; thinking about it that way, it was entirely possible.

Xu Fu didn't want to appear too narcissistic; if he misunderstood, wouldn't he become the laughingstock of everyone? Temporarily burying his doubts, he motioned for the attendant to pack up the robes.

No sooner had the robes been put away than another inner attendant slowly entered, dropped to his knees, and reported, "Your Majesty, the matter concerning Grand Astrologer Xu has been resolved."

"Report." When facing official business, the aura around Ying Zheng changed instantly—serious and majestic, as if the person who had just pinched Xu Fu's chin while zoning out wasn't him at all.

Presenting the bamboo slips, the attendant said, "There is a man named Zhao Yi in the Bureau of Ceremonies. Having made a wager with Grand Astrologer Xu to pry into the results of the Grand Astrologer's divination, he colluded with the guard and another Grand Historian in the Bureau of Ceremonies to steal the bamboo slips."

It really was him!

Xu Fu frowned; Zhao Yi was simply too good at putting on an act, leaving not the slightest trace to be seen.

After hearing the attendant out and skimming the bamboo slips, Ying Zheng immediately said in a cold voice, "Go take Zhao Yi into custody."

"No, wait." Xu Fu spoke up to interrupt Ying Zheng.

Beads of sweat broke out on the attendant's forehead, thinking that Grand Astrologer Xu was truly daring to outright cut off His Majesty's words.

Ying Zheng, however, turned to look at Xu Fu with immense patience. "Do you have other plans?"

Xu Fu nodded. "Taking him into custody right now has no real meaning. Even if we arrest him, he will surely remain resentful in his heart and might even smear me as someone abusing public office for private revenge to deliberately retaliate against him. With the La sacrifice imminent, there's no need to stir up unpleasantness over this person. After the La sacrifice, when the date I divined and the date he divined are compared, which is better and which is worse will be obvious at a glance. He can accuse me of falsifying it, but surely he can't blame the heavens for falsifying it too."

What was the point of brutally locking someone away in a prison? The best way to strike down an opponent was naturally to target their psychology first—making them lose confidence, realize the gap between them, and lose their fighting spirit amid shock. That was the most severe punishment!

Kneeling on the floor, the attendant thought secretly: he's actually teaching His Majesty how to handle things.

Ying Zheng had always been able to take advice from others, let alone words spoken by Xu Fu. After a moment of contemplation, he said, "Do as the Grand Astrologer says."

The attendant was stunned. Still sweating profusely, he looked up in shock, gave an acknowledgment, and retreated out of the hall.

Ying Zheng waved his hand, dismissing everyone else.

Xu Fu's heart tightened. Huh? What was he about to do?

Instead, he saw Ying Zheng wearily rub his brow and say in a cold voice, "Us has brought Grand Empress Dowager Zhao back to the palace."

That troublemaker Zhao Ji was back again?!!!!

赵太后被驱出咸阳，移居贡阳宫一事，虽为王室秘辛，但实际只是大家彼此心中有数，却并不提起罢了，毕竟担心损了嬴政的脸面。只是正逢蜡祭，一国太后却未在宫中，传到六国去岂不是成了笑话？
齐人茅焦对嬴政道：“秦方以天下为事，而大王有迁母太后之名，恐诸侯闻之，由此倍秦也。”
嬴政不愿在蜡祭前惹出事端，这才前往贡阳宫，悄然将赵姬接了回来。
那夜嬴政一身风雪归来，便是前去贡阳宫了。
嬴政对母亲赵姬的最后一丝温情也被消磨了，赵姬在贡阳宫中并不安分，一面派人来求嬴政，一面却又在贡阳宫中享受最后的疯狂荒唐，更甚至在宫人面前大骂嬴政，哪里还有半分太后应有的姿态？赵姬如此做派，又岂能唤得嬴政心软？
赵姬被接回宫后，嬴政便不再理睬了，赵姬不复往日风光，在宫中又如何撒泼，嬴政也丝毫不管了。在咸阳宫中，不管赵姬如今做了什么，也不会泄露出去，只是将赵姬衬得越发如同可笑了。
原本徐福还在想，嬴政怎么与他说起了赵姬的近况，紧接着，他便又听嬴政道：“赵太后回宫，必然会寻人发作，若是不慎与你撞上，你不与她计较便是。”
如今嬴政对赵姬的称呼如此疏远冷淡，言语间更是如此嫌恶赵姬。
做人母亲做到这个份儿上，也实在太过失败了。
徐福点头应道：“这是自然，我会避着太后些的。”
嬴政“嗯”了一声，便不再言语了，徐福能瞥见他眼角隐隐透着的倦色。秦王之位尚且不好坐，不知等到秦始皇一统天下后，又该肩负如何压力。想到这里，徐福又突然觉得自己太奇怪了，他岂能用常人来揣度秦始皇呢？
没一会儿便有内侍前来请嬴政了，想来还有什么事等着嬴政去处理，嬴政一走，徐福倒是心底暗自松了一口气。
若是嬴政继续留下来，他必然感觉无所适从，毕竟昨夜的梦境还时时回荡在他的脑中。
宫人点了火盆，又给徐福送来了食物，徐福顿时将那些思绪都抛开了，冬日里，想那么多都没什么用，还是惬意处之最为实在。身为一个职业神棍，他得时时保持冷静才对呢。
只是等到当晚入夜后，嬴政回到寝宫中，却不见徐福身影。
“徐先生呢？”嬴政挑了挑眉梢问道。他倒是没太在意徐福不见踪影的事儿，毕竟徐福日日留于寝宫中，不仅徐福习惯了，就连他也习惯了。
宫人不敢抬头，低声道：“徐先生说这几日睡得不太安稳，让我们给收拾了偏殿出来，刚刚睡进去了。”
原本这样的事，当然要嬴政做主同意，徐福才能挪进去的，但是宫人们见往日嬴政对徐福的态度，便也不好怠慢徐福，连忙就为他收拾出来了。
嬴政的神色微微有些复杂，他沉默半晌，才开口，“徐福若是入睡了，那今日便如此吧。”
他不知为何徐福突然想要搬到偏殿去，但是嬴政最先想到的便是，徐福发现了自己对着他夜夜春梦的事？
正好，他也需要短时放松一番，仔细思量思量那诡异的梦境。
那边徐福一夜未入梦，醒来之后，徐福登时神清气爽不少。
说不定是秦始皇的那张床被下了降头……徐福如此想着，顺便还决定多翻一翻古籍，找出个破解之法来。
嬴政早早离了寝宫，徐福因为睡得太过香甜，醒来后又错过奉常寺的时间了，徐福磨蹭了一会儿，正准备去用早膳，他还没来得及踏出殿门，就见宫人急急忙忙跑过来，高声道：“太后到了。”
其余人怔了怔，连忙跪地迎接。
唯剩下徐福跟个桩子似的，特别显眼地站在那里。
但徐福真不想跪地，更不想匍匐。
他对赵姬喜欢不起来，自然也不乐意用如此大礼迎接她。
很快，赵姬便带着一群宫人朝这边来了。赵姬不如之前那样姿容妍丽了，她眼角松弛，头上隐约能瞥见白发，但不可否认的是，她依旧是风韵犹存的，一身宫装套上身，雍容华贵、容色妍丽。
赵姬还未踏进殿来，便口中问道：“扶苏呢？”
宫人应道：“在偏殿呢。”
赵姬还要再问，目光却陡然从徐福身上掠过，立时滞住了。
“又是你？”赵姬恨恨咬牙，看着徐福的目光登时就变得不善起来了。之前在蕲年宫中，嬴政如何羞辱于她，此人也是在场的！“见了我为何不跪？”赵姬拔高声音，厉声斥责道。
如今的赵太后，也就只能在徐福面前耍耍威风了。
徐福淡定道：“太后来得突然，徐福准备不及。”
还反过去怪她了？赵姬心中不快，冷笑道：“不过是政儿身边一男宠，也敢对我不敬？谁人给你的胆子？”其中赵姬心中更不忿的是，嬴政能找男宠，却不许她养面首吗？
宫人们心都齐齐提了起来，无比紧张地望着这两人，生怕出了什么意外。当然，他们更担心的是，赵太后会不会伤到徐福。如今这两人中，王上更重视谁，那还真不好说。
徐福依然淡定，他很清楚，赵太后就算再猖狂，也不可能拿他如何，顶多拿话来刺一刺他罢了，徐福听过的流言蜚语还少了吗？又岂会惧怕这些？
还没等赵姬继续作威作福，又一阵脚步声近了。
只见扶苏身后跟着宫人，小小的身子跌跌撞撞地朝着这个方向快步走开，他怯怯地唤了一声赵姬为“祖母”。之前他还跟着郑妃时，赵姬便偶有刁难郑妃的时候，那时在扶苏心中，便种下了畏惧的种子。
赵姬也顾不上徐福了，她原本的目标就是扶苏。
赵姬蹲下身来，抓着扶苏的小手，露出温柔的笑容来，“扶苏，祖母问你，你可知祖母宫中的小姐姐去哪里了？”
扶苏眨了眨眼，露出懵懂无知的表情来，“扶苏不知道呀。”
赵姬暗暗咬牙，又问：“那你在宫中可还见过其他小孩儿呀？”
徐福在旁边，心中却是微微一沉。
赵姬说他胆子大，依他看，胆子大的人是赵姬才对！赵姬问的应该是她与嫪毐那私生女的下落吧？她知道嬴政不会再心软，竟是跑到寝宫来，利用起扶苏一小孩子了。
当真是愚蠢之极……
chapters.translated_text:
The matter of Queen Mother Zhao being driven out of Xianyang and relocated to Gongyang Palace was a royal secret, but in reality, everyone just understood it tacitly without speaking of it aloud, after all, out of fear of damaging Ying Zheng's pride. However, it just happened to be the La Sacrifice, yet the Queen Mother of the state was not in the palace; wouldn't it become a laughingstock if word spread to the six states?

Mao Jiao of Qi said to Ying Zheng, "Qin is just beginning to concern itself with the empire, and Your Majesty has the reputation of banishing the Queen Mother. I fear that if the feudal lords hear of this, they will turn away from Qin as a result."

Unwilling to stir up trouble before the La Sacrifice, Ying Zheng finally went to Gongyang Palace and quietly brought Zhao Ji back.

That night Ying Zheng returned amidst wind and snow; that was when he had gone to Gongyang Palace.

The last shred of tenderness Ying Zheng held for his mother Zhao Ji had also been worn away. Zhao Ji was not behaving herself in Gongyang Palace; on one hand, she sent people to plead with Ying Zheng, while on the other hand, she indulged in her final moments of wild extravagance within Gongyang Palace, and even cursed Ying Zheng furiously in front of the palace attendants—how was this fractionally like the demeanor a Queen Mother ought to have? How could such behavior from Zhao Ji ever soften Ying Zheng's heart?

After Zhao Ji was brought back to the palace, Ying Zheng simply ignored her. No matter how Zhao Ji threw tantrums in the palace, having lost her former glory, Ying Zheng paid her not the slightest heed. Inside Xianyang Palace, no matter what Zhao Ji did nowadays, it would not be leaked outside, only making Zhao Ji appear all the more ridiculous.

Xu Fu had originally been wondering why Ying Zheng was bringing up Zhao Ji's recent situation with him, when he immediately heard Ying Zheng say, "Upon her return to the palace, Queen Mother Zhao will inevitably look for someone to vent her spleen on. If you happen to bump into her, just don't bicker with her."

By now, Ying Zheng's address toward Zhao Ji was so distant and cold, and his words were filled with such abhorrence for her.

To fail so utterly at being a mother was truly pathetic.

Xu Fu nodded in response and said, "Naturally. I will steer clear of the Queen Mother."

Ying Zheng gave an "en" and said no more. Xu Fu could catch a glimpse of the faint exhaustion lingering at the corners of his eyes. The throne of the King of Qin was already not an easy seat to occupy; he could only wonder what kind of pressure would rest upon his shoulders once Qin Shi Huang unified the empire. Thinking of this, Xu Fu suddenly felt he was being very strange; how could he measure Qin Shi Huang using the standards of ordinary people?

Before long, a court eunuch came to summon Ying Zheng, presumably because there were still matters awaiting his attention. The moment Ying Zheng left, Xu Fu breathed a silent sigh of relief in his heart.

If Ying Zheng had continued to stay, he undoubtedly would have felt at a complete loss, especially since the dream from last night was still echoing in his mind.

The palace attendants lit the brazier and brought food to Xu Fu. Xu Fu instantly cast those thoughts away—in the winter, thinking so much was of no use, and taking things in stride was the most practical course of action. As a professional charlatan, he ought to maintain his composure at all times.

However, when night fell that evening and Ying Zheng returned to his bedchamber, Xu Fu was nowhere to be seen.

"Where is Mister Xu?" Ying Zheng asked, raising an eyebrow. He did not care too much about Xu Fu being out of sight; after all, with Xu Fu staying in the bedchamber every day, not only had Xu Fu grown accustomed to it, but even he had gotten used to it.

Not daring to raise his head, a palace attendant lowered his voice and said, "Mister Xu said he hasn't been sleeping very soundly these past few days, so he had us tidy up the side hall. He just went in to sleep."

Ordinarily, for a matter like this, Ying Zheng's consent and decision would certainly be required before Xu Fu could move in. However, seeing the attitude Ying Zheng had shown toward Xu Fu in the past, the attendants did not dare to neglect Xu Fu either, and hurriedly tidied it up for him.

Ying Zheng's expression turned slightly complicated. He remained silent for a long while before speaking, "If Xu Fu has already fallen asleep, then leave it be for today."

He did not know why Xu Fu suddenly wanted to move to the side hall, but the very first thing that crossed Ying Zheng's mind was: could Xu Fu have discovered that he had been having erotic dreams about him night after night?

Just as well, he also needed a short respite to carefully ponder over that bizarre dream.

Over on the other side, Xu Fu did not experience a single dream all night. Upon waking up, Xu Fu instantly felt much more refreshed.

Perhaps that bed of Qin Shi Huang's was cursed... Xu Fu thought to himself, while also deciding to flip through more ancient texts to find a method to break it.

Ying Zheng had left the bedchamber early. Because Xu Fu had slept so soundly, he woke up and missed the time for the Bureau of Ceremonies once again. After lingering for a bit, Xu Fu was just about to go have his breakfast when, before he even had a chance to step out of the hall doors, he saw a palace attendant running over in a flurry, shouting loudly, "The Queen Mother has arrived!"

The rest of the people were startled and hurriedly knelt to welcome her.

Only Xu Fu was left standing there like a wooden stake, making him particularly conspicuous.

But Xu Fu truly did not want to kneel, let alone prostrate himself.

He could not warm up to Zhao Ji, and naturally had no desire to welcome her with such grand obeisance.

Soon, Zhao Ji came toward them with a group of palace attendants. Zhao Ji was no longer as fair and radiant as before; the corners of her eyes were slack, and white hairs were faintly visible on her head. Yet, undeniably, she still retained her charm. Draped in court robes, she was dignified, luxurious, and striking in appearance.

Before even stepping into the hall, Zhao Ji asked aloud, "Where is Fusu?"

An attendant replied, "He is in the side hall."

Zhao Ji was about to ask further, but her gaze suddenly swept past Xu Fu and instantly halted.

"It's you again?" Zhao Ji gnashed her teeth in hatred, her gaze toward Xu Fu turning instantly unfriendly. Back in Qinian Palace, when Ying Zheng humiliated her, this person had also been present! "Why do you not kneel when you see me?" Zhao Ji raised her voice and rebuked him harshly.

The Queen Mother Zhao of today could only throw her weight around in front of Xu Fu.

Xu Fu said calmly, "The Queen Mother arrived so suddenly that Xu Fu was unprepared."

Was he turning it around to blame her instead? Displeased in her heart, Zhao Ji sneered, "Merely a male favorite by Zheng'er's side, yet you dare to show disrespect to me? Who gave you the gall?" What angered Zhao Ji even more in her heart was: Ying Zheng was allowed to keep a male favorite, yet she wasn't permitted to keep gigolos?

The hearts of the palace attendants all leaped into their throats as they watched the two of them with utmost tension, terrified that some accident would occur. Of course, what they worried about even more was whether Queen Mother Zhao would hurt Xu Fu. Between these two people now, it was truly hard to say whom the King valued more.

Xu Fu remained calm. He was very well aware that no matter how unbridled Queen Mother Zhao was, she couldn't possibly do anything to him, at most resorting to harsh words to sting him. Had Xu Fu heard few enough gossips and slanders? How could he fear these?

Before Zhao Ji could continue lording it over others, another wave of footsteps drew near.

They saw Fusu followed by palace attendants, his small figure stumbling and hurrying quickly in this direction. He timidly called out "Grandmother" to Zhao Ji. Back when he was still following Consort Zheng, Zhao Ji had occasionally given Consort Zheng a hard time; seeds of fear had been planted in Fusu's heart during those times.

Zhao Ji no longer had the mind to deal with Xu Fu; her original target was Fusu.

Zhao Ji squatted down, grasped Fusu's small hand, and wore a gentle smile as she asked, "Fusu, Grandmother asks you, do you know where the little older sisters from Grandmother's palace have gone?"

Fusu blinked his eyes, revealing a clueless and innocent expression, "Fusu doesn't know."

Zhao Ji gritted her teeth inwardly and asked again, "Then have you seen any other little children in the palace?"

Standing nearby, Xu Fu felt his heart sink slightly.

Zhao Ji had said he was bold, but in his view, the truly bold person was Zhao Ji! What Zhao Ji was asking about must be the whereabouts of her illegitimate daughter with Lao Ai, right? Knowing that Ying Zheng would no longer soften his heart, she had actually run all the way to the bedchamber to make use of a child like Fusu.

Truly utterly foolish...
chapters.title: 第44章

chapters.source_text:
担心扶苏应付不了赵姬，徐福正要站出来，却听扶苏继续用天真无邪的语调，将赵姬的话直接堵了回去，“祖母在说什么？扶苏从来都是只待在这里呀，扶苏很听话，不会乱跑，哪里会看见其他人呢？哦……扶苏只见过一个……”
“谁？”赵姬的双眼唰地就亮了起来。
徐福心中暗自觉得好笑。
他猜到扶苏要说什么了。
“喏，就是他呀。”扶苏转过头，指着宫人手中抱着的襁褓，还生怕赵姬不明白似的，还特地解释道：“胡姬给我生的弟弟哦。”
赵姬的脸色骤然变了，哪怕是在小孩儿的面前，她也毫不掩饰地露出了不快的神色来。赵姬感觉到自己被一个小孩儿给愚弄了，若不是因为扶苏乃嬴政长子，赵姬深知扶苏地位，恐怕已经忍不住狠狠教训扶苏了。
她原本气势汹汹地转身欲走，但她拉长了的脸上又突然浮现了几分怪异的表情。
赵姬快步走了过去，动作近乎粗暴地将那宫人拽了一把，宫人惊了一跳，差点失手摔了怀中的孩子。赵姬看了看那孩子的面容，顿时神色更加难看，徐福甚至还能隐约瞥见赵姬眼中一闪而过的失望。
赵姬是在失望什么？难道她以为，那会是她生下的那个孩子？
徐福觉得实在可笑。
赵姬若是聪明一些，若是真为她的私生儿女着想，她就应该好生乖觉一段时间，起码先博得秦始皇些许的心软，那时再私底下去寻他们的下落，总比她现在大张旗鼓跑到秦始皇寝宫中来，企图从小孩嘴里套话要好。
赵姬的确没有死心，她不相信嬴政会对自己那么狠。
但是再不死心也无法了，她找不到她那双儿女的下落。
她生下来的儿子，真的死了……
嬴、政。
赵姬神色恍惚地从殿中走了出去，也顾不上再对徐福发作了，徐福倒也算是逃过一劫。宫人们恭送着赵姬离开，心中也暗自松了一口气，一旁有人则是悄悄向嬴政报告去了。
秦始皇这flag立得太快，前一日还跟他提起要避开赵太后，后一日自己就跟赵姬撞上了。
徐福暗自吐槽完，压住想要打呵欠的冲动，又困又饿的，他还是先去吃饭比较好。
他刚一拔腿，扶苏就抱住了他的大腿，紧紧地抓住他的衣摆，一脸紧张地道：“徐先生，我、我有些害怕……”
扶苏话音才刚落下，那头胡亥就像是要呼应他似的，跟着也哇哇大哭了起来。
都被赵姬吓唬一遍了，神经居然迟钝到现在才哭……
扶苏受到胡亥的影响，抬头看着徐福的那双大眼也变得水汪汪了起来。
胡亥哭得更大声了……
宫人们乱作一团，安抚不住。
扶苏的表情更加可怜了……
徐福：“……”秦始皇你快回来带你儿子啊！
也不知道嬴政是不是真的与他有心有感应，徐福冷着一张脸，盯着扶苏的发旋儿，不为所动（不知所措）的时候，他终于听见宫人的声音在殿外响起。
“王上！”
嬴政回来了！
徐福难得一回如此期待嬴政归来。
嬴政跨进殿门，原本脸色阴沉面孔冷凝，却在注意到徐福和扶苏怪异的姿势之后，脸上的表情也瞬间变得怪异起来了。
尽管嬴政生出了点笑意，但他还是口吻严肃地冲扶苏道：“扶苏，还不放开徐先生？”
那头的胡亥直接被遗忘了，他还紧紧攥着宫人胸前的衣领嚎啕大哭，哭得久了，总算获得了嬴政的些许关注。
嬴政微微皱眉，问宫人：“哄不住胡亥吗？”
宫人畏惧地低下头，“胡亥公子年纪小，不易哄……”
胡亥的嗓子哭得已经有些哑了。
嬴政丝毫没有要将胡亥接过去的意思，扶苏弱弱小声道：“他哭得好厉害……扶苏能抱他吗？”
扶苏才多大？要抱起一个胡亥实在太吃力，那宫人脸色发白，也不敢交给扶苏。
嬴政没有要将胡亥马上弄死的意思，当然也不会同意让扶苏去抱。
徐福有些忍不了了，哪怕秦始皇再厉害，他也搞不定俩孩子啊！那怎么办？要是有什么清心咒和消音咒就好了，他一定贴在胡亥的脑门上。
徐福心中叹了口气，瘫着一张脸，伸手将胡亥抓到了自己的怀里。
诶，那个清心咒怎么念的？
徐福从古籍上见到过，不过他觉得十有八九没什么用，而且清心咒多出自佛家，佛教道教不两立，他来念，能有用？
徐福还在努力回忆清心咒是什么样的，却听一旁的宫人，诧异地指着他怀中的胡亥，道：“胡亥公子不、不哭了？”
徐福和嬴政同时地低头看去，胡亥的确恹恹地张着嘴打了个呵欠，抽噎两下，便不再继续往下哭了。
扶苏张大嘴，“徐先生比奶娘还要厉害吗？”
徐福：“……”
他只是在抱胡亥的那瞬间，仿佛回到了还在师门的时候。那个时候师门偶尔也会从孤儿院抱来几个小孩儿，他们那个地方较为落后，手续简陋也可以领养回家，只是许多人都利用这一点，将小孩儿带走后便折断手脚，装成被抛弃的残疾人在街边讨钱。师门有不忍之心，也想要将师门技艺传授下去，便会在经济能力尚能承受的情况下，带些孩子回来收做徒弟。
徐福早入师门，偶尔也会抱一抱那些师弟师妹。
只是他并不怎么喜欢孩子，所以经常抱上一会儿便丢开了。
徐福可没想到，这点随手学来的技能，也能被用到这上面来。
徐福又低头看了怀中的胡亥许久，胡亥连续张着小嘴打了几个呵欠，然后就闭上双眼了，小小的眉头还皱到了一块儿去，脸颊上还带着未干的泪痕，看上去还有那么一小点儿可怜。
胡亥抓着徐福的袖子便不放开了。
嬴政眉头却不见松开，反倒是更紧了。
他对胡亥别说是喜欢了，不厌恶便是很好了，如今见胡亥霸占了徐福的怀抱，嬴政很快就发觉自己心中有些不快了。
“将胡亥抱走。”嬴政十分无情地命令宫人道。
宫人小心地从徐福怀中将胡亥接走，人倒是抱过去了，就是手还抓着徐福的袖子呢。
宫人露出了为难的神色，看向嬴政，“王上，这……”
嬴政干脆利落地抽出随身佩剑来，再动作利落地一斩，刺啦一声，布料直接被斩开。
徐福抬起手臂，看着自己破损漏风的袖子，“……”
秦始皇今天是吃了火药吗？
扶苏见状，不自觉地打了个哆嗦。他毫不怀疑自己亲爹火气上头很可能会把剑捅自己肚皮上。
扶苏连忙撒开手，小声道：“父王，扶苏去照顾弟弟吧。”说着他就连忙转身，抓着宫人的衣角摇了摇，“我们抱胡亥出去。”
宫人见了嬴政手中佩剑也正忐忑不已，闻言连忙看向嬴政。
嬴政点了头，那宫人才敢带着人退出去。
扶苏和胡亥两个噪音源一消失，徐福顿时觉得头上的压力减轻了不少。
徐福的脸色微微有些发白，早起顾不上用早膳，他都很容易出现这样的症状，不等嬴政开口，他就先一步道：“王上，能先让我用口饭吗？”
被赵姬那么一打岔，徐福现在都隐隐有些发晕了。
嬴政脸色瞬间变得严肃起来，他叫来内侍，“传膳。”
徐福心底松了一口气。
等到用了一些饭食过后，徐福才抬头看向嬴政，“王上可是有话说？”
“赵太后为难你了？”嬴政眼底闪过一丝不易令人察觉的厌恶之色。
“没有。”徐福摇了摇头。在他看来，真正能为难到他的人，的确没有。他心思豁达，自己也有足够强的能力，他还会被谁为难到呢？不管是邱机、王柳或赵毅，甚至是如今的赵姬，他都并未放在眼中过。
将他们一一分个等级，不过是从小怪到大怪的过程，但赵姬这个大怪已经被秦始皇打得掉血快掉光了，他还有何惧？
嬴政却不信徐福之言。
在贡阳宫中，他便亲身领教到了赵太后言辞能恶毒到何种地步，对自己儿子尚且如此，若是对徐福，赵太后岂不是更为气焰嚣张？
嬴政早就用过膳，此时他也未动筷，只是坐在那里，静静地望着徐福的脸。
徐福的性子太过好了。
过分纯善，又直言不讳，不记仇怨，更不屑背地里的手段。如此这般的人，他能自己护住自己吗？
嬴政脑子里冒出了一个怪异的想法来。
若是他，定能将徐福护个周全。
徐福迅速用过了早膳，他放下筷子，喝了点水，忍不住问道：“王上，以后赵太后便一直住在宫中吗？”
倒不是他介意赵姬找自己麻烦，随便赵姬怎么蹦跶都成，他又不傻，怎么会任由赵姬欺负到自己头上来。
相反的，他更担忧的是秦始皇。
思及茅焦对秦始皇说的话，徐福便怎么都消不去这股担忧。
有时候他这双眼睛就是太过灵敏了，那赵姬踏入殿来以后，他一眼就看出了笼罩在赵姬眉间的霉运，若是霉运扩大，转变为死气，甚至将她整个人都笼罩其中，届时赵姬说不得便会出现什么危及生命的意外。
嬴政与赵姬不合现在已成为众人心底皆有数的事，到时候赵姬在咸阳宫一蹬腿，嬴政不是便成为了最大怀疑对象吗？别人心中或许不说，但其余六国呢？其余那些前来投靠秦国的人呢？他们会如何想？如今大行其道的儒家搞不好也会更提前与秦国作对。
既然他已经从赵姬身上看出来，那还是要早提醒秦始皇为上。
嬴政并不知徐福心中所想，他心中微沉，心道，果然赵太后还是为难徐福了。
“她会一直住在甘泉宫。”直到死。嬴政在心底默默道。
闻言，徐福只有直说自己所见了。
“王上，今日赵太后前来，我无意中从她身上看见……”
“看见什么？”挥挥手让宫人撤了食具，嬴政转头看向徐福。
徐福也不再卖关子，当即道：“赵太后眉间阴郁，眼角多皱纹，眼底多血丝，这段时间定然日日暴躁难安，我再见她眉宇间笼有黑气……”
“有祸事？”已经熟悉徐福这套说辞的嬴政当即就接了话。
徐福点头，“确有祸事，不知是人祸，还是自身。我瞧赵太后如今的模样，恐怕很容易出现什么急症。”
嬴政眼底闪过一道晦涩的光芒，“哦？是吗？”
徐福并未发觉到嬴政的不对劲，点头道：“我没有看错，应当是如此的，若是不提早防着，到时候赵太后出了意外，王上……又该如何自处？”
嬴政怔了怔，才发觉原来徐福这一番提醒是为了他。
他脸色顿时轻松不少，“寡人知晓了，有劳你。”
徐福根本没将这点事儿放在心上。
他吃喝住全是花的秦始皇的，他的本职自然包括为秦始皇分忧。
嬴政陪着徐福用完了早膳，见徐福的确没有因为赵姬之事烦忧，这才离开。
等出了殿门，嬴政顿住脚步，突然将门口的宫人叫到跟前来，“等会儿你们将徐先生偏殿里的东西都收拾了，若等到日落后，他又要住进偏殿里去，你们便找个借口推脱了。”
宫人们一脸早知会如此的表情，笑着道：“喏。”
随后便退下去了。
那边用完早膳精神大好的徐福去寻了本古籍来，翻开竹简，里面上书：降头术。
徐福很认真地看了起来。
他真的觉得搞不好秦始皇那张大床被下了一睡觉就会做噩梦的降头呢。
待到日落时分，徐福想要提前用晚膳，被宫人委婉地拒绝了，徐福也并未觉得有什么不对，这里本就是秦始皇的地盘，他一个客人，哪来那么多唧唧歪歪的毛病？
能吃便吃，不能吃那便等秦始皇回来好了。
好不容易折腾到嬴政归来，两人又一同用了晚膳，酒足饭饱之后，徐福便向宫人道：“带我去偏殿吧。”
谁知那宫人一福身，委婉道：“偏殿里的床被都收拾起来了呢，蜡祭在即，那偏殿里不能再住人了。”
徐福觉得有一道晴天霹雳劈在了自己头上。
他又要和嬴政同床共枕了？
他又要忍受那个梦了？
徐福脸上的表情依旧冷冷清清毫无变化，他转过了身，对上了嬴政探究的双眼，徐福不自觉地移开了目光。
待那宫人退下之后，徐福才陡然想起来。
住偏殿与蜡祭有什么关系？
这两者分明没关系啊！
但是徐福也不可能将人再叫回来了，那宫人会如此说，莫非是收到了秦始皇的命令？秦始皇也没理由拦着他啊。
难道秦始皇爱上了和人同床的感觉？或者是漫漫黑夜，秦始皇一个人会觉得寂寞孤独？
徐福嘴角微抽，觉得自己越想越歪了。
既然已经被拒绝了，那也只有服从了。接受能力极强的徐福只是默默在心中决定，明日还是好好研究一番那降头术吧。不然去找本解毒的医术来看也好……
*
从一个行业跨到另外一个行业是极不容易的，徐福本职是算命的神棍，要让他去研究降头和医毒，途中困难自然是重重的。这令徐福很不解，现代都市之中，处处可见打着活神仙的招牌，言明自己可前知五百年后知五百年，能算命解签看相，还能瞧风水斩鬼妖。
如此全能，跨界如此之多，他们是如何做到的？
转眼到了蜡祭之日。
而徐福已经备受春梦困扰了。
夜夜长湿裤满裆的感觉，真是太糟糕了。
不过到了这一日，徐福就算精神再糟糕，也会强打起来。这仅是出于职业道德，该他做的，那便要做好。
晨起，焚香沐浴。
这是难得一次，徐福比嬴政起得要早上许多。
嬴政醒来时，便能从光影间瞥见宫人为裸着背的徐福披上衣衫，烛光影影绰绰，晃花了他的视线，他不得不从床上坐起来，却只来得及看见徐福脖子和背上那一小截裸露在外的肌肤。
徐福脖颈后一点痣，明明是在昏暗的烛光下，但那一瞬，嬴政却觉得格外清晰地印进了他的眼眸之中。
嬴政心中一惊，神情都恍惚了一阵。
曾经做过无数次的梦似乎都与此刻的画面相重叠了。
“王上？”床边的宫人小心地唤出声来，惊醒了嬴政。
嬴政装作不经意地将视线从徐福身上扫过，再收回，然后起身由宫人服侍着沐浴穿衣。
待他拾辍完之后回到寝殿中，徐福刚将那全套的祭祀大礼服穿上身。
衣色为黑，图腾为红，上印有夸张的图腾纹路，徐福也不知究竟是象征着什么，但就是这样一套礼服穿上身，很快便为徐福原本清冷的气质笼上了一层神秘感和瑰丽感。
就像是古时神庙中的祭祀。
徐福不自觉地想。
嬴政见到徐福的模样之后，也有短暂的失神。
革带束在徐福的腰间，他的领口也是整整齐齐、妥妥帖帖地交叠在一起，嬴政觉得自己又犯病了，第一时间生出的想法竟是，想要扯开革带，撕开领口……
嬴政不自觉地轻咳一声，掩下心中思绪。
徐福注意到嬴政到来。
宫人上前为嬴政更衣，黑色的冕服披在嬴政的身上，徐福也不自觉地摒了摒呼吸。
不愧是秦始皇。
通体黑色，被他穿得贵气又威严十足，嬴政表情冷然，哪怕他此刻只是往那里一站，也让徐福觉得，他仿佛高高在上，坐在那王座之上，俯瞰众生。
两人对视一眼，又视线分开。
嬴政淡淡道：“备齐了吗？”
内侍答道：“已齐了。”
另外又有内侍走到徐福跟前来，躬身道：“劳烦徐先生先与我出宫了。”
徐福身为奉常寺太卜令，虽有随行之权，但他毕竟不可能同嬴政一起从王宫出发，若真是那样，徐福的存在还不在秦国朝堂上下掀起轩然大波。
这一日，他们是不能提前用膳的。
蜡祭之上祭鬼神，唯有等到祭了鬼神之后，送走神灵们，他们才方能开始进食。
徐福掐了自己掌心一把，保持着绝对的清醒，然后便与那内侍一同离开了王宫。
一道奉常寺，苏邑便立刻迎了出来。
“我还当你出了事。”苏邑微微松了一口气，他的动作并不显眼，不过还是被徐福收入了眼中。
徐福不好意思告诉人家，他只是冷得不行，又懒得不行，又不想这么快见到赵毅，所以才未来奉常寺。
“无事。”徐福只能继续装作高冷地回了两字，便踏入了奉常寺中。
此时苏邑也注意到了他身上的祭服，苏邑心底再度松了一口气，道：“果然只是送衣物来的那人疏漏了吧。”
徐福嘴角噙着淡淡笑意，却没多做解释。
嬴政特地命人为他另做衣袍的事，并不适宜大肆宣扬。
跨进奉常寺之后，徐福那身与众不同的祭服，立刻迎来了大肆打量的目光，那些目光或羡慕或嫉妒，当然也有平平淡淡并不以为然的。
徐福一眼就看见了厅中的赵毅。
赵毅脸色并不太好看，甚至是还有几分憔悴，他深深地看了一眼徐福，很快便移开了目光，那目光什么情绪也没有。
见徐福注意到了赵毅，苏邑忙又在他耳边道：“这几日你未来，赵毅脸色一日比一日难看。”
徐福心道，心有惶惶，脸色难看可不稀奇。
“或许是难过于他卜出的吉日未被选上吧。”徐福嘴上一笔带过。
现在还不到揭露赵毅的时间，他还会让赵毅多轻松两日，不过也就这两日了。
苏邑点点头，理了理身上的祭服，脸上难得带出了些微笑意来，那张平日里较为严肃刻板的脸上涌现了笑意，反差十分大。
不多时，便由太祝令带着其余人，准备前往咸阳宫外，跟上蜡祭队伍。
太祝令出现之后，带着寥寥几人往外走去，就这几人确实赚足了奉常寺内不少的目光。
众人之中，徐福唯独与苏邑较为熟悉，走在路上，苏邑倒还会和徐福偶尔交谈一两句，也不至于太过冷清孤寂。
很快的，他们便抵达了咸阳宫外。
队伍齐聚，有士兵与侍从将队伍牢牢护起来，徐福站得远远的，连嬴政的车驾都看不真切。
徐福的内心突然有些复杂。
往日里，他都是与嬴政同进同出，可以说除却嬴政贴身伺候的宫人与内侍，还有他那些如花似玉的后宫们，便是他与嬴政最为亲近了。
之前在加冠礼上，他都是站在嬴政身侧，甚至还为嬴政捧冠。
而如今，他却只能站得远远的，遥望一眼，还什么都看不到个名堂。
一行人先是浩浩荡荡前往咸阳城的祭祀庙中，那里摆放着祖先灵位，虽然不如雍城齐全，但在蜡祭时拜一拜便已足以。
这时徐福才有了上前的机会。
太祝立于嬴政身后，太祝之后便是太史、太卜。
徐福便站在其中，他与苏邑恰好站在一起。
两人都是身着黑色祭服，站在一起时，却能让人很容易分辨出，谁人身上的祭服更为精致。
嬴政区别于往日在徐福跟前的模样，他毫不掩饰自己身上的威严与霸气，身形高大往庙中一站，便令人望而生畏。
大臣们再也不敢小看嬴政，都是规规矩矩排在之后，用真切的目光仰望着嬴政。
太祝口中唱词。
很快，嬴政便祭祀完了先祖。
一行人便又撤出来，前往咸阳城外的田埂间。
待到嬴政再次从车驾中出来，他已经换了一身衣服，黑色冕服脱去，他身着白色素服，头戴鹿皮所做的皮弁，手持榛木手杖，模样看上去挺奇怪的，像是要进行某种宗。教。仪式般。
嬴政并不大适合白衣，白衣穿在身上，将他身形过于高大，肤色微微黝黑都衬作了缺点。
明明是极富男子气概的英俊模样，偏偏与白衣的气质相排斥。
不过不管如何，秦始皇终究是秦始皇，哪怕是穿着气质不符的衣袍，他身上的威严霸气也未减分毫。
此时田埂间已经聚了不少的百姓。
百姓们身着黄色野服，头戴斗笠，分立两旁，站于外围。
徐福站在包围圈之中，顿觉气势浩大。
又见太祝唱词。
“土反其宅！水归其壑！昆虫毋作！草木归其泽！土反其宅！水归其壑！昆虫无作！丰年若土，岁取千百！”
待他唱完之后，嬴政便开口唱了起来。
徐福并不太能听懂唱的是什么，但嬴政开口声音低沉，极富磁性，歌声由低及高，仿佛有木槌轻轻叩在徐福心上，一点一下，一点一下。
甚是醉人。
百姓们也高歌而和之，吟唱歌谣。
田埂间登时飘散开了众人的声音，有男有女，有高有低。
莫名的令徐福感觉到了几分浑身血液沸腾味道，就好比上辈子他在师门里，借着那根效果并不太好的天线，在每年除夕夜看着春晚时一般，明明并没有什么好看的，却就是莫名会跟着十二点钟声敲响而激动起来。
钟鼓之乐紧随响起。
也不知道过了多久，钟鼓乐声慢慢低了下去，而嬴政也收了声，百姓们的声音也逐渐消失。
与后世过春节不同，过春节时，人人面带喜气，而蜡祭礼上，人人都面色威严，不苟言笑。
这或许是因为习俗的不同。
蜡祭是为了祭鬼神，他们自然要展露出庄严一面，才能迎来鬼神，做到无半点冒犯。
之后有几名穿着稀奇古怪衣袍的男子，摇摇晃晃从人群中穿出来，士兵和侍从都并未拦他们。
他们戴着模样狰狞怪异的面具，在田埂间摆出各种祭祀。
随后有宫人与百姓手捧酒肉等珍贵食物送到这些人的脚边，那些人也不客气，捡起酒肉便开始吃喝，徐福也很难看清那些面具之下的人，究竟长得什么模样。
钟乐声停住。
太祝口中又唱，“祭八神。”
八蜡神。
即先啬，司啬，农，邮表啜，猫虎，坊，水庸，昆虫。
祭过八蜡神之后，才又听见太祝口中唱：“蜡祭礼毕！神灵已醉，送诸神灵还天去也！”
钟乐便又响起，送鬼神与先灵离开。
待到钟声再度停下，宫人们忙上前将祭祀之物撤下，分发于众，接到祭祀之物的百姓们这才展露笑颜。
徐福不自觉地将目光投向了嬴政的方向，他看见嬴政脸上的表情也松了松，而且嬴政似乎注意到了他的目光，竟然突地转头来，与徐福对视了一眼，周围人太多，徐福也不知道那一刻为何自己竟然有些许心虚，迅速撤开了目光。
也有食物分到了徐福的手中，徐福接在手中愣了愣。
他之前翻看典籍，只知道蜡祭礼上，自己身为太卜并不需要做额外的事，却并不知还有这样一个环节。
苏邑在旁边附耳道：“怎么不吃？不合胃口，也要吃下。蜡祭后，这些祭祀之物都是十分好的东西。”
徐福不再犹豫，抬手吃了下去，就是普通的米，嚼在嘴里也没有特别的味道。
百姓们高呼一声，各自散去，大臣们竟然也陆续散去。
徐福怔了怔，苏邑在旁边又道：“蜡祭便算作结束了，蜡祭之后还有宴饮，不知你家可在咸阳城中，若是不在，与我一同回去，宴饮一番也极好。”
徐福原本正要一口应下，却突然想到了嬴政。
大臣们都各自退去了，那秦始皇呢？蜡祭之后，他也会举办宴席吗？那又会有谁去参加？
“……不了，我已有安排。”徐福还是推拒了苏邑。
若是秦始皇早已安排妥当，他再跟着苏邑走了，得罪了秦始皇那可不好。
众人都散得差不多了，士兵和侍从便护着秦王车驾往咸阳城内回去，徐福也不起眼地跟在了身后。
当然只是他以为的不起眼罢了。
徐福容貌出众，怎么可能当真做到不起眼？早有人注意到徐福其人，只是蜡祭之后便是举国狂欢，谁还有闲心去关心别人呢？
车驾很快回到咸阳宫中，徐福也从善如流地跟了进去。
嬴政此时在车驾之中，面色并算得喜悦，甚至他的表情还紧绷着。
赵高不知嬴政为何不喜，只当嬴政是想到宫中的赵太后，便觉得蜡祭之后的宴席没有什么意思了。
只可惜年年蜡祭之后的宴饮是必然要进行的，赵太后也定然会赴宴，也不知到时可还会闹出些麻烦来。
谁也不知嬴政此时不过心中不悦于，那蜡祭礼上，他竟见一人与徐福举止极为亲密，两人还时常附耳交谈。
嬴政心中不屑，道那人如此做派，定不是什么君子。
但不管他心中如何不屑，那人与徐福之间默契的模样，都让嬴政心中膈应得难受，脸色怎么也好不起来。
车驾缓缓停在宫殿外。
徐福也顿住了脚步。
嬴政脸色沉沉地下了车驾，也不知那人是否会邀徐福共同前去宴饮？若是徐福一时心软答应了怎么办？
嬴政原本还正想着呢，谁知他一个回头，便看见了云淡风轻，姿态超然，站在车驾之后的徐福。嬴政心中隐约有什么地方被触动了一下。
他令内侍将徐福请上前来，低声道：“此时你必然无法回师门了，今日便与寡人一同宴饮吧。”
徐福没什么好拒绝的，并不多想，直接点了点头。
宫人们已经备好宴席，有人前去请扶苏公子，也有人前去请赵太后，就连后宫中的女人也一个没落下。
这一日，宫中同席便不再过分讲究身份地位，若是非要讲究地位，除却郑妃，那些女人还都不能与嬴政同席。
徐福和嬴政身上的衣袍都未换，他们直接入了大殿之中。
大殿中点着香炉和火盆，还温着酒，殿外雪花飘摇，寒风呼啸而过，能将人冻得手脚木木的。等进了殿，徐福便顿觉一股暖意袭来，身上极为舒适。
嬴政坐于上位，随后便将身边下首的席位赐给了徐福。
若是往年，那里坐着的必然是吕不韦。
赵高犹豫一阵，道：“太后……”
嬴政顿时记起，还有赵太后的位置。
但今年他实在不愿与赵太后相对，于是便命人放置围屏于身后，单独给赵太后摆了桌案，到时赵太后到围屏后坐着便是。
徐福跽坐而下，面前已经有宫女为他倒好了酒水，盛好了食物，满桌案的食物，十分之丰盛。
赵姬到得极早，两人才落座不久，便见赵姬穿着华丽宫装，打扮得十分艳丽，带着宫人进了殿门，赵姬神色冷艳，瞥见嬴政下首的徐福时，还不阴不阳地冷笑了一声，随后便走到了嬴政跟前。
嬴政站起身来，冷淡地朝她行了礼，之后便让人带赵姬到围屏后去。
一听自己要坐到围屏后，赵姬当即就变了脸色。
她低低地笑了一声，说了三个字，“好儿子！”然后才恨恨咬牙，带着人绕到围屏后去了。
扶苏紧跟着也到了，他小小的身子艰难地迈过殿门，身后跟着宫人，那宫人连胡亥也抱来了，其后还紧跟着一名奶娘。
扶苏朝嬴政和徐福都见了礼，倒是围屏后的赵姬，也不知他是真的未看见，还是小小年纪便已如此机灵，直接将赵姬无视了。
众人落座之后。
那殿门外便是莺莺燕燕的娇声响起来了。
随后徐福便见十来名美人，带着宫人跨进殿来。
这些美人宫装在身，精致美丽，她们身段窈窕，却唯独脸上的妆画得有些可怕。
徐福不自觉地别了别脸。
也不知道嬴政对着她们涂脂抹粉丝毫不讲求技巧的脸，是如何忍得下去的？
嬴政见徐福紧紧盯着那十来名美人，心中登时一紧。

Worried that Fusu wouldn't be able to handle Zhao Ji, Xu Fu was about to step forward when he heard Fusu continue in an innocent tone, blocking Zhao Ji's words right back: "What is grandmother talking about? Fusu has always stayed right here. Fusu is very obedient and doesn't run around, how could he see anyone else? Oh... Fusu has only seen one..."

"Who?" Zhao Ji's eyes lit up instantly.

Xu Fu found it rather amusing inwardly.

He had guessed what Fusu was going to say.

"Well, it's him, of course." Fusu turned his head, pointing at the swaddling clothes held in the court attendant's arms. As if afraid Zhao Ji wouldn't understand, he specifically explained, "The younger brother that Lady Hu gave birth to for me."

Zhao Ji's expression changed abruptly. Even in front of a child, she made no effort to conceal her displeasure. Zhao Ji felt she had been made a fool of by a child. If not for the fact that Fusu was Ying Zheng's eldest son, and she was well aware of his status, she probably would have couldn't help but give Fusu a harsh lesson.

She had originally turned around aggressively, ready to leave, but a strange expression suddenly surfaced on her elongated face.

Zhao Ji walked over briskly and, with a nearly violent motion, yanked the attendant. The attendant was startled and almost dropped the baby in her arms. Zhao Ji looked at the infant's face, and her expression immediately became even uglier. Xu Fu could even vaguely catch a flash of disappointment in her eyes.

What was Zhao Ji disappointed about? Could it be that she thought this would be the child she had given birth to?

Xu Fu found it utterly ridiculous.

If Zhao Ji were a bit smarter, if she truly cared for her illegitimate children, she should have behaved herself obediently for a while, at least winning a shred of the First Emperor's softness first. Only then would looking for their whereabouts in secret have been better than marching triumphantly into the First Emperor's bedchamber now, attempting to extract words from a child's mouth.

Zhao Ji indeed had not given up; she refused to believe that Ying Zheng could be so ruthless to her.

But even though she hadn't given up, there was nothing she could do—she couldn't find the whereabouts of her son and daughter.

The son she had given birth to was truly dead...

Ying, Zheng.

With a dazed expression, Zhao Ji walked out of the hall, no longer in any state to vent her anger on Xu Fu, who could thus be considered to have escaped disaster by the skin of his teeth. The attendants respectfully saw Zhao Ji off, breathing quiet sighs of relief inwardly, while someone nearby went off to report to Ying Zheng in secret.

The First Emperor had jinxed himself far too quickly; just the day before he had mentioned to him the need to avoid Dowager Zhao, and the very next day he had run right into Zhao Ji himself.

After inwardly ranting to himself and suppressing the urge to yawn—sleepy and hungry as he was—Xu Fu decided it would be best to go get some food first.

The moment he set off, Fusu hugged his thigh, grabbed tightly onto the hem of his robe, and said with a nervous expression, "Mr. Xu, I-I'm a little scared..."

Just as Fusu's voice trailed off, Hu Hai over there seemed to echo him, bursting into a loud wail.

Having been frightened by Zhao Ji, his nervous system was actually so slow that he was only crying now...

Influenced by Hu Hai, the large eyes Fusu raised to look at Xu Fu also became watery.

Hu Hai cried even louder...

The attendants fell into a chaotic mess, unable to soothe him.

Fusu's expression became even more pitiful...

Xu Fu: "..." First Emperor, hurry back and take care of your son!

Not knowing whether Ying Zheng truly had a telepathic connection with him or not, just as Xu Fu wore a cold face, staring at Fusu's crown and remaining unmoved (and at a loss), he finally heard an attendant's voice ring out outside the hall.

"Your Majesty!"

Ying Zheng was back!

It was a rare occasion for Xu Fu to look forward to Ying Zheng's return this much.

Stepping across the threshold, Ying Zheng's expression was originally gloomy and cold, but upon noticing the bizarre posture between Xu Fu and Fusu, the look on his face instantly turned bizarre as well.

Even though a trace of a smile arose in Ying Zheng, he still spoke to Fusu in a stern tone: "Fusu, why haven't you let go of Mr. Xu?"

Hu Hai over there was completely forgotten; he was still clutching tightly to the collar of the attendant's garment and howling at the top of his lungs. Having cried for so long, he finally garnered a modicum of Ying Zheng's attention.

Ying Zheng frowned slightly and asked the attendant, "Can't you coax Hu Hai?"

The attendant lowered her head fearfully, "Young Master Hu Hai is young, and not easy to coax..."

Hu Hai's voice had already grown somewhat hoarse from crying.

Ying Zheng showed no intention whatsoever of taking Hu Hai over himself, while Fusu weakly and quietly said, "He's crying so terribly... Can Fusu hold him?"

How old was Fusu? It was simply too strenuous for him to lift Hu Hai. The attendant's face turned pale, and she didn't dare hand him over to Fusu either.

Ying Zheng had no intention of doing away with Hu Hai immediately, and naturally would not agree to let Fusu hold him.

Xu Fu couldn't bear it any longer. No matter how formidable the First Emperor was, he couldn't handle two kids! What should he do then? If only there were some sort of Mind-Clearing Mantra or Silence Mantra, he would definitely slap it right onto Hu Hai's forehead.

Sighing inwardly with a deadpan face, Xu Fu reached out and scooped Hu Hai into his own arms.

Uh, how did that Mind-Clearing Mantra go again?

Xu Fu had seen it in ancient texts, but he figured nine times out of ten it was useless. Besides, Mind-Clearing Mantras mostly originated from Buddhism, and Buddhism and Taoism didn't mix—would it do any good if he recited it?

While Xu Fu was still struggling to recall what the Mind-Clearing Mantra was like, he heard an attendant nearby point in astonishment at Hu Hai in his arms and say, "Young Master Hu Hai has s-stopped crying?"

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng lowered their heads at the same time. Hu Hai indeed opened his mouth listlessly, let out a yawn, let out a couple of hiccups, and stopped crying altogether.

Fusu's mouth widened, "Is Mr. Xu even more amazing than a wet nurse?"

Xu Fu: "..."

The moment he held Hu Hai, it just felt as though he had returned to his days in the sect. Back then, the sect would occasionally take in a few children from orphanages. Their area was rather backward, and one could adopt children home with simple procedures; however, many people took advantage of this point, breaking the children's limbs after taking them away and pretending to be abandoned disabled people begging on the streets. Out of a sense of compassion and a desire to pass down the sect's skills, the sect would bring back some children to take in as disciples whenever they could still bear the financial burden.

Having entered the sect early on, Xu Fu would occasionally hold those junior martial brothers and sisters.

It was just that he didn't care much for children, so he would usually put them down after holding them for a short while.

Xu Fu hadn't expected that this casually learned skill could actually be put to use here.

Xu Fu lowered his head to look at Hu Hai in his arms for a long while. Hu Hai repeatedly opened his little mouth to yawn a few times, then closed his eyes. His tiny brows were still scrunched together, and his cheeks were stained with un dried tear tracks, making him look just the tiniest bit pitiful.

Hu Hai grabbed onto Xu Fu's sleeve and refused to let go.

Ying Zheng's brow didn't loosen at all; instead, it furrowed even tighter.

Far from liking Hu Hai, not feeling disgust toward him was already quite a lot. Now, seeing Hu Hai hog Xu Fu's embrace, Ying Zheng quickly realized that some displeasure was stirring in his heart.

"Take Hu Hai away," Ying Zheng commanded the attendant ruthlessly.

The attendant carefully received Hu Hai from Xu Fu's arms. She took him away alright, except that the child's hand was still clutching Xu Fu's sleeve.

The attendant wore a troubled expression as she looked at Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, this..."

Ying Zheng decisively drew the sword at his waist and chopped down with a clean, fluid motion. With a *rip*, the fabric was sliced right open.

Xu Fu raised his arm and looked at his torn, drafty sleeve, "..."

Had the First Emperor eaten gunpowder today?

Seeing this, Fusu involuntarily shivered. He had no doubt that if his biological father's temper flared up, he might very well thrust the sword right into his own belly.

Fusu hurriedly let go and said in a small voice, "Father, Fusu will go take care of younger brother." With that, he hastily turned around, grabbed the corner of the attendant's garment, and shook it. "Let's carry Hu Hai out."

The attendant was already feeling nervous upon seeing the sword in Ying Zheng's hand; hearing this, she quickly looked at Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng nodded, and only then did the attendant dare to take the others and withdraw.

The moment the two noise sources, Fusu and Hu Hai, vanished, Xu Fu instantly felt the pressure on his head lighten considerably.

Xu Fu's complexion was slightly pale. Whenever he failed to have breakfast in the morning, he was prone to such symptoms. Before Ying Zheng could speak, he took the initiative to say, "Your Majesty, can you let me have a bite to eat first?"

Interrupted by Zhao Ji like that, Xu Fu was currently feeling faintly dizzy.

Ying Zheng's expression instantly turned serious. He summoned an attendant, "Serve the meal."

Xu Fu let out a mental sigh of relief.

After partaking in some food, Xu Fu raised his head to look at Ying Zheng, "Does Your Majesty have something to say?"

"Did Dowager Zhao give you a hard time?" A trace of hard-to-detect disgust flashed across the depths of Ying Zheng's eyes.

"No," Xu Fu shook his head. As far as he was concerned, there was truly no one who could give him a hard time. With his open-minded disposition and sufficiently strong abilities, who could possibly trouble him? Whether it was Qiu Ji, Wang Liu, Zhao Yi, or even the current Zhao Ji, he had never taken any of them to heart.

Grading them was merely the process of progressing from small monsters to big monsters, but the big monster Zhao Ji had already been drained of health so quickly by the First Emperor—what was there for him to fear?

Yet Ying Zheng did not believe Xu Fu's words.

In Gongyang Palace, he had personally experienced the extent to which Dowager Zhao's words could turn vicious. If she was like that toward her own son, wouldn't her arrogance be even more overbearing when facing Xu Fu?

Ying Zheng had already eaten earlier and did not touch his chopsticks this time; he simply sat there, quietly gazing at Xu Fu's face.

Xu Fu's temperament was simply too good.

Excessively pure and kind, yet speaking his mind without restraint, bearing no grudges, and disdaining underhanded methods. Could a person like this protect himself?

A bizarre thought popped into Ying Zheng's head.

If it were him, he would definitely be able to keep Xu Fu thoroughly protected.

Xu Fu finished his breakfast quickly. Putting down his chopsticks and drinking a little water, he couldn't help asking, "Your Majesty, will Dowager Zhao continue to live in the palace from now on?"

It wasn't that he minded Zhao Ji finding trouble for him—she could jump around all she wanted, as he wasn't foolish enough to let Zhao Ji bully him.

On the contrary, what worried him more was the First Emperor.

Thinking of Mao Jiao's words to the First Emperor, Xu Fu found himself completely unable to shake off this anxiety.

Sometimes this pair of eyes of his was simply too perceptive. After Zhao Ji stepped into the hall, he had spotted at a glance the bad luck shrouding her brow. If the bad luck expanded and turned into death energy, even enveloping her entire person, then by that time Zhao Ji might suffer some life-threatening accident.

The discord between Ying Zheng and Zhao Ji had already become an open secret among everyone. If Zhao Ji were to kick the bucket in Xianyang Palace, wouldn't Ying Zheng become the primary suspect? Others might not voice it in their hearts, but what about the other six states? What about those people who had come to seek refuge in Qin? What would they think? The currently thriving Confucianism might even ally with Qin to oppose them sooner.

Since he had already foreseen this from Zhao Ji, it would be best to remind the First Emperor early on.

Unaware of what was passing through Xu Fu's mind, Ying Zheng sank into a slight inward gloom, thinking to himself that Dowager Zhao had indeed troubled Xu Fu after all.

"She will live in Ganquan Palace forever." Until she dies. Ying Zheng added silently in his heart.

Hearing this, Xu Fu had no choice but to speak frankly about what he had seen.

"Your Majesty, when Dowager Zhao came today, I inadvertently saw on her..."

"Saw what?" Waving his hand to have the attendants remove the tableware, Ying Zheng turned to look at Xu Fu.

No longer keeping him in suspense, Xu Fu stated directly, "Dowager Zhao's brows are gloomy, the corners of her eyes have many wrinkles, and her eyes are bloodshot. She must be irritable and restless day after day during this period. Furthermore, I saw black qi lingering around her brows..."

"Disaster?" Already familiar with Xu Fu's phrasing, Ying Zheng immediately took over the words.

Xu Fu nodded, "Indeed, there is disaster, though I know not whether it is man-made or from within herself. Judging by Dowager Zhao's current appearance, she is likely prone to some acute illness."

A murky light flashed through the depths of Ying Zheng's eyes, "Oh? Is that so?"

Not noticing anything amiss with Ying Zheng, Xu Fu nodded and said, "I did not see wrong; it should be thus. If we do not guard against it early, and an accident befalls Dowager Zhao when the time comes, Your Majesty... how will you conduct yourself?"

Ying Zheng was stunned for a moment, only then realizing that Xu Fu's warning was for his sake.

His expression immediately relaxed quite a bit, "I am aware. Thank you for your trouble."

Xu Fu hadn't taken this matter to heart at all.

Since his food, drink, and lodging were all provided by the First Emperor, his job naturally included sharing worries for him.

Ying Zheng accompanied Xu Fu through breakfast, and seeing that Xu Fu truly wasn't troubled by the affair with Zhao Ji, he took his leave.

Upon stepping out of the hall doors, Ying Zheng paused his steps and suddenly called the attendants at the entrance over to him: "Later on, clear out everything in Mr. Xu's side hall. If sunset arrives and he wants to sleep in the side hall again, find an excuse to brush him off."

Wearing expressions that showed they had long expected this, the attendants smiled and said, "Nuo."

Then they withdrew.

Meanwhile, Xu Fu, whose spirits were greatly revived after breakfast, went to find an ancient text. Unrolling the bamboo slips, it was inscribed with: *The Art of Jiangtou (Sorcery).*

Xu Fu began to read it very earnestly.

He genuinely felt that perhaps the First Emperor's large bed had been cursed with some sort of sorcery that made one have nightmares the moment they fell asleep.

When dusk arrived, Xu Fu wanted to have his evening meal early, but was politely declined by the attendants. Xu Fu didn't find anything amiss with this; this was the First Emperor's territory after all, and as a guest, where did he get so many picky complaints?

He would eat if he could; if not, he would just wait for the First Emperor to return.

After finally struggling through until Ying Zheng's return, the two of them partook in the evening meal together. Fully wined and dined, Xu Fu said to the attendants, "Take me to the side hall."

Who would have thought that the attendant would curtsy and tactfully say, "The bedding in the side hall has already been packed away. With the La Festival approaching, nobody can stay in that side hall anymore."

Xu Fu felt as though a bolt of lightning from a clear blue sky had struck him on the head.

He was going to share a bed with Ying Zheng again?

He was going to endure that dream again?

The expression on Xu Fu's face remained cold, clear, and completely unchanged. He turned around to meet Ying Zheng's probing gaze, and involuntarily looked away.

Only after the attendant had retreated did Xu Fu suddenly remember.

What did staying in the side hall have to do with the La Festival?

These two things clearly had nothing to do with each other!

But Xu Fu couldn't very well call the person back. For the attendant to say such a thing, could it be that she had received orders from the First Emperor? Yet the First Emperor had no reason to block him.

Could it be that the First Emperor had fallen in love with the feeling of sharing a bed with someone? Or perhaps through the long, dark nights, the First Emperor felt lonely and solitary by himself?

The corners of Xu Fu's mouth twitched slightly, feeling that his thoughts were drifting further and further off course.

Since he had already been rejected, he had no choice but to submit. Possessing an extremely high capacity for acceptance, Xu Fu silently decided to properly study that sorcery art tomorrow. Otherwise, finding a medical text on detoxification to read would also do...
