Crossing over from one industry to another is extremely difficult. Xu Fu's primary profession was a fortune-telling charlatan; asking him to research sorcery and medical poisons naturally meant facing numerous obstacles along the way. This puzzled Xu Fu greatly: in the modern metropolis, one could see people everywhere hanging up signs as "living immortals," declaring themselves capable of knowing five hundred years into the past and five hundred years into the future, telling fortunes, drawing divining sticks, reading physiognomy, and even handling Feng Shui to slay ghosts and demons.

So omnipotent and spanning so many cross-industries, how on earth did they pull it off?

In the blink of an eye, the day of the La Festival arrived.

And Xu Fu had already been plagued by wet dreams.

The feeling of waking up night after night with wet pants and soaked crotch was truly terrible.

However, when this day arrived, no matter how wretched his spirits were, Xu Fu would force himself to perk up. This was simply out of professional ethics—what was his duty must be done well.

Rising in the morning, burning incense and bathing.

This was a rare occasion where Xu Fu got up much earlier than Ying Zheng.

When Ying Zheng woke up, he could catch glimpses through the light and shadow of attendants draping garments over Xu Fu’s bare back. The flickering candlelight blurred his vision, forcing him to sit up in bed, though he was only in time to catch sight of that small patch of bare skin on Xu Fu's neck and back.

There was a tiny mole at the nape of Xu Fu's neck. Even in the dim candlelight, at that exact moment, Ying Zheng felt as though it had been exceptionally clearly imprinted into his eyes.

A shock jolted through Ying Zheng's heart, leaving him in a daze for a moment.

The countless dreams he had experienced seemed to overlap with the scene before him.

"Your Majesty?" The attendant beside the bed called out cautiously, snapping Ying Zheng out of his reverie.

Ying Zheng feigned casualness as his gaze swept past Xu Fu and then retracted, before rising to let the attendants assist him in bathing and dressing.

By the time he finished dressing and returned to the bedchamber, Xu Fu had just put on the full set of grand ceremonial robes.

The garments were black with red totters, and printed with exaggerated totem patterns. Xu Fu had no idea what they ultimately symbolized, but wearing such a set of ceremonial robes instantly cast a layer of mystery and magnificence over his originally cold and detached demeanor.

Much like a sacrificial priest in an ancient temple.

Xu Fu thought to himself unconsciously.

Upon seeing Xu Fu's appearance, Ying Zheng also experienced a brief moment of distraction.

A leather belt was fastened around Xu Fu's waist, and his collar was neatly and impeccably overlapped. Ying Zheng felt as though his old affliction was acting up again, as his very first thought was to pull at the leather belt and tear open the collar...

Ying Zheng unconsciously gave a light cough, suppressing the thoughts in his mind.

Xu Fu noticed Ying Zheng's arrival.

Attendants stepped forward to dress Ying Zheng. As the black ceremonial crown robes were draped over him, Xu Fu also unconsciously held his breath.

As expected of the First Emperor of Qin.

The pitch-black attire was worn by him with such nobility and absolute majesty. Ying Zheng's expression was cold and stern; even if he were merely standing there at that moment, he gave Xu Fu the impression that he was sitting high above on his throne, looking down upon all living beings.

The two exchanged a glance before looking away.

Ying Zheng said indifferently, "Are preparations complete?"

An inner attendant replied, "They are complete."

Another inner attendant walked over to Xu Fu, bowed, and said, "I must trouble Master Xu to leave the palace with me first."

As the Grand Astrologer of the Ministry of Rites, though Xu Fu had the right to accompany the procession, it was impossible for him to set out from the royal palace alongside Ying Zheng. If that were truly the case, Xu Fu's existence would have stirred up a massive uproar throughout the Qin court.

On this day, they were not permitted to eat in advance.

The La Festival sacrificed to ghosts and deities; only after the sacrifices were completed and the spirits seen off could they begin to partake in food.

Xu Fu pinched his own palm to maintain absolute sobriety, and then departed from the royal palace together with the inner attendant.

As soon as he reached the Ministry of Rites, Su Yi immediately hurried out to greet him.

"I thought something had happened to you." Su Yi let out a slight sigh of relief. His movement was not conspicuous, but it was still caught by Xu Fu's eyes.

It was hard for Xu Fu to tell him that he was simply freezing cold, too lazy to move, and reluctant to see Zhao Yi so soon, which was why he hadn't come to the Ministry of Rites earlier.

"Nothing happened." Xu Fu could only continue to put on a cold and aloof front as he gave those two words in reply, and stepped into the Ministry of Rites.

At this point, Su Yi also noticed the ceremonial robes he was wearing. Su Yi felt another wave of relief deep down and thought, "As expected, it was just an oversight by the person who delivered the clothes."

A faint smile hung on the corners of Xu Fu's lips, though he offered no further explanation.

The fact that Ying Zheng had specially ordered a separate robe to be made for him was not suitable to be widely publicized.

Upon stepping into the Ministry of Rites, Xu Fu's distinctive ceremonial attire immediately drew intense, sweeping gazes. Those gazes were filled with envy or jealousy, and naturally some were indifferent and unimpressed.

Xu Fu spotted Zhao Yi in the hall at a single glance.

Zhao Yi's complexion did not look too good; he even appeared somewhat haggard. He gave Xu Fu a deep look before quickly looking away, his gaze devoid of any emotion.

Seeing that Xu Fu had noticed Zhao Yi, Su Yi hurriedly whispered in his ear, "Zhao Yi's expression has grown uglier day by day during the days you haven't been here."

Xu Fu thought to himself, with panic in his heart, an ugly complexion was hardly surprising.

"Perhaps he is grieving that the auspicious date he divined was not chosen," Xu Fu brushed the matter off with a word.

It was not yet time to expose Zhao Yi; he would let Zhao Yi have a few more days of ease, but those days were numbered.

Su Yi nodded, straightened his ceremonial robes, and a rare trace of a smile appeared on his face. The smile breaking across features that were usually rather stern and rigid created a stark contrast.

Before long, the Grand Administrator of Rites led the rest of the group to prepare to head outside Xianyang Palace to join the La Festival procession.

After the Grand Administrator of Rites appeared, he led a sparse few people outward, and these few individuals certainly captured a great many gazes within the Ministry of Rites.

Among the crowd, Xu Fu was only relatively familiar with Su Yi. As they walked along, Su Yi would occasionally exchange a word or two with Xu Fu, keeping things from feeling too desolate and lonely.

Soon enough, they arrived outside Xianyang Palace.

The procession gathered, with soldiers and attendants strictly guarding the ranks. Xu Fu stood far away, unable to even clearly see Ying Zheng's carriage.

Xu Fu's heart suddenly felt somewhat complex.

In the past, he always came and went alongside Ying Zheng. It could be said that aside from Ying Zheng's close palace attendants and inner servants, as well as the beauties of his inner palace, he was the one closest to Ying Zheng.

Previously at the capping ceremony, he had stood right by Ying Zheng's side and even held the crown for him.

Yet now, he could only stand far off, gazing from afar without being able to make out anything of significance.

First, the grand procession marched toward the ancestral temple in Xianyang city, where the ancestral spirit tablets were housed. Although not as comprehensive as the ones in雍城 (Yongcheng), paying homage here during the La Festival was already sufficient.

Only then did Xu Fu have the opportunity to step forward.

The Grand Diviner stood behind Ying Zheng, followed by the Grand Historian and the Grand Astrologer.

Xu Fu took his place among them, standing right beside Su Yi.

Both wore black ceremonial robes, but standing together, it was easy for anyone to tell whose robes were far more exquisitely crafted.

Unlike the demeanor he usually showed in front of Xu Fu, Ying Zheng made no effort to conceal his majesty and dominance. Standing tall in the temple, his towering figure inspired awe.

The ministers no longer dared to underestimate Ying Zheng; they all lined up obediently behind him, gazing up at him with genuine reverence.

The Grand Diviner chanted the sacrificial words.

Soon, Ying Zheng completed the sacrifices to his ancestors.

The procession then withdrew and headed toward the farmland ridges outside Xianyang city.

When Ying Zheng emerged from his carriage once again, he had changed his clothes. Having cast off the black crown robes, he wore plain white garments, a deerskin ceremonial cap on his head, and held a hazelwood staff in his hand. His appearance looked rather peculiar, as if he were about to conduct some sort of religious ritual.

Ying Zheng was not particularly suited for white. Wearing white magnified the flaws of his overly towering stature and slightly tanned skin.

Despite having a strikingly masculine and handsome appearance, it somehow clashed with the inherent vibe of white attire.

Regardless, the First Emperor was ultimately the First Emperor. Even clad in robes that mismatched his temperament, the majesty and dominance he radiated did not diminish by a single fraction.

By this time, quite a few commoners had gathered along the farmland ridges.

The commoners wore yellow peasant garments and conical hats, standing in separate groups on either side along the outer perimeter.

Xu Fu stood within the inner circle, instantly feeling the grand and imposing atmosphere.

Once more, the Grand Diviner chanted the sacrificial lyrics.

"Earth, return to your dwelling! Waters, return to your beds! Insects, do no harm! Plants and trees, return to your marshes! Earth, return to your dwelling! Waters, return to your beds! Insects, do no harm! May the harvest be like rich soil, yielding thousands and hundreds each year!"

As soon as his chant ended, Ying Zheng began to sing.

Xu Fu could not entirely understand the meaning of the chant, but Ying Zheng's voice was deep and extremely magnetic. The song rose from a low pitch to a high one, as if a wooden mallet were gently tapping against Xu Fu's heart, beat by beat.

It was utterly intoxicating.

The commoners also joined in chorus, chanting the folk song.

The voices of the crowd suddenly drifted across the farmland ridges—male and female, high and low.

Unaccountably, it made Xu Fu feel as though his blood was boiling, much like when he was back in his master's sect in his past life, watching the Spring Festival Gala on New Year's Eve with the help of that poorly functioning antenna. Even though there was nothing particularly worth watching, he would inexplicably get excited as the clock struck midnight.

The music of bells and drums immediately followed.

How much time had passed, no one knew, but the chime and drum music gradually subsided. Ying Zheng also ceased his singing, and the voices of the commoners slowly died away.

Unlike the celebration of the Lunar New Year in later generations, where everyone wore joyful expressions, during the La Festival rites, everyone's expression was stern and unsmiling.

This was perhaps due to a difference in customs.

The La Festival was held to appease ghosts and deities, so naturally they had to display a solemn countenance to welcome the spirits without the slightest offense.

Afterward, several men dressed in bizarre, eccentric garments staggered out from the crowd, unrestrained by the soldiers and attendants.

Wearing fierce and grotesque masks, they struck various ritual poses along the farmland ridges.

Then, palace attendants and commoners holding precious foods like wine and meat stepped forward to lay them at these men's feet. Those men stood on ceremony, picking up the wine and meat to eat and drink; it was difficult for Xu Fu to make out what the people beneath those masks actually looked like.

The bell and drum music stopped.

The Grand Diviner chanted again, "Sacrifice to the Eight Gods."

The Eight La Gods.

Namely: Xianse (God of Agriculture), Sishi (God of Seeds), Nong (God of Husbandry), Youbiaochuo (God of Roads and Boundaries), Maohu (God of Cats and Tigers), Fang (God of Dikes), Shuiyong (God of Ditches and Canals), and Kunchong (God of Insects).

After sacrificing to the Eight La Gods, the Grand Diviner was heard chanting once more: "The La Festival rites are concluded! The deities are intoxicated; send all the spirits back to heaven!"

The bells and drums struck once again to bid farewell to the ghosts, deities, and ancestral spirits.

When the sound of the bells finally ceased once more, the attendants rushed forward to clear away the sacrificial offerings and distribute them among the crowd. The commoners who received the offerings finally broke into smiles.

Unconsciously, Xu Fu cast his gaze toward Ying Zheng's direction. He saw that the expression on Ying Zheng's face had also relaxed. Furthermore, Ying Zheng seemed to have noticed his gaze, suddenly turning his head to lock eyes with Xu Fu. With so many people around, Xu Fu did not know why he felt a momentary pang of guilt at that instant, and quickly averted his gaze.

Some of the food was also distributed into Xu Fu's hands, leaving him momentarily dazed as he held it.

Having browsed through ancient texts earlier, he only knew that as the Grand Astrologer during the La Festival, he had no extra duties to perform, but he had been unaware of this particular step.

Su Yi whispered into his ear from the side, "Why aren't you eating? Even if it doesn't suit your palate, you must consume it. After the La Festival, these sacrificial offerings are considered exceptionally auspicious items."

Xu Fu hesitated no longer; he raised his hand and ate it. It was simply ordinary rice, with no special taste as he chewed it in his mouth.

The commoners shouted out in cheers and dispersed in all directions, and the ministers likewise began to scatter one after another.

Xu Fu stood in a daze before Su Yi spoke up again beside him, "The La Festival can be considered over. There will be a banquet following the ceremony—is your home located within Xianyang city? If not, you might as well return with me; attending the feast together would be wonderful."

Xu Fu was on the verge of agreeing outright when he suddenly thought of Ying Zheng.

All the ministers had retreated to their homes, but what about the First Emperor? Would he also host a banquet after the La Festival? And who would be attending?

"...No need, I already have arrangements." Xu Fu ultimately declined Su Yi.

If the First Emperor had already made arrangements and he instead went off with Su Yi, offending the First Emperor would not be wise.

Once the crowd had mostly dispersed, the soldiers and guards escorted the King of Qin's carriage back into Xianyang city, and Xu Fu inconspicuously followed behind.

Of course, it was only inconspicuous in his own mind.

With Xu Fu's striking appearance, how could he possibly remain truly unnoticed? People had already taken note of him, but since the end of the La Festival marked a nationwide revelry, who had the leisure to care about others?

The carriage soon returned to Xianyang Palace, and Xu Fu followed smoothly inside.

Inside the carriage at that moment, Ying Zheng's expression was far from joyful; in fact, his features remained tightly drawn.

Zhao Gao had no idea why Ying Zheng was displeased, assuming instead that Ying Zheng was thinking of Empress Dowager Zhao in the palace and thus finding the post-La banquet uninteresting.

It was just a pity that the post-La banquet was an inevitable yearly event, and Empress Dowager Zhao would certainly attend. He wondered what kind of trouble might flare up by then.

Little did anyone know that Ying Zheng was simply annoyed because during the La Festival rites, he had witnessed a certain individual interacting with Xu Fu with extreme intimacy, the two whispering into each other's ears repeatedly.

Ying Zheng felt a sense of disdain in his heart, thinking that such behavior meant the man was certainly no gentleman.

Yet no matter how much disdain he harbored, the tacit understanding between that man and Xu Fu made Ying Zheng feel intensely uncomfortable, leaving his complexion impossible to improve.

The carriage slowly came to a halt outside the palace hall.

Xu Fu also halted his steps.

With a dark expression, Ying Zheng stepped down from the carriage. Would that man invite Xu Fu to the banquet together? What if Xu Fu agreed out of sudden softness of heart?

Ying Zheng was still mulling this over when he turned his head and caught sight of Xu Fu standing unhurriedly and transcendently behind the carriage. Something deep within Ying Zheng's heart was stirred.

He instructed an attendant to invite Xu Fu forward, and said in a low voice, "You surely cannot return to your sect at this hour; join Us for the banquet today."

Xu Fu had no reason to refuse. Without overthinking it, he simply nodded.

The attendants had already prepared the banquet. Messengers had been sent to invite Prince Fusu, Empress Dowager Zhao, and not a single woman from the inner palace was left out.

On this day, status and rank were no longer strictly emphasized for seating in the palace. If status truly had to be observed, aside from Lady Zheng, none of the other women were qualified to share a mat with Ying Zheng.

Neither Xu Fu nor Ying Zheng had changed their robes; they walked straight into the grand hall.

Incense burners and firepots were lit inside the hall, and wine was being warmed. Outside the doors, snowflakes drifted and cold winds howled past, chilling one's hands and feet into numbness. Upon entering, Xu Fu instantly felt a wave of warmth wash over him, making his body immensely comfortable.

Ying Zheng took his seat in the highest position, and then bestowed the seat of honor beside him upon Xu Fu.

In previous years, that seat would undoubtedly have been occupied by Lü Buwei.

Hesitating for a moment, Zhao Gao said, "The Empress Dowager..."

Ying Zheng immediately remembered that there was also a place for Empress Dowager Zhao.

However, this year he truly wished to avoid facing Empress Dowager Zhao, so he ordered a folding screen to be placed behind him and a separate table set up exclusively for her, so that she could sit behind the screen when she arrived.

Xu Fu knelt down to take his seat. Palace maids had already poured wine and served food before him—a table entirely laden with exceptionally sumptuous dishes.

Zhao Ji arrived remarkably early. Not long after the two had taken their seats, Zhao Ji was seen entering the hall doors, dressed in gorgeous palace attire and heavily made up in bright, vivid colors, accompanied by attendants. With a cold and haughty expression, she cast a sour, mocking smirk upon catching sight of Xu Fu seated beside Ying Zheng's lower rank, before walking up to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng stood up, offered her a cold bow, and then had someone escort Zhao Ji behind the folding screen.

Upon hearing that she was to sit behind a folding screen, Zhao Ji's expression changed instantly.

She let out a low laugh and spat out three words, "Good son!" Then, gritting her teeth in bitter resentment, she led her people around behind the screen.

Fusu followed closely behind. His small figure labored across the threshold, followed by attendants—one of whom was even carrying Hugai, trailed closely by a wet nurse.

Fusu paid his respects to both Ying Zheng and Xu Fu, though as for Zhao Ji behind the screen, whether he truly failed to notice her or was simply too astute for his young age, he directly ignored her entirely.

Once everyone was seated.

The flirtatious, melodious voices of women rang out from outside the hall doors.

Soon afterward, Xu Fu saw a dozen beauties stepping into the hall, flanked by attendants.

These beauties were dressed in palace gowns, delicate and lovely with slender figures, save for the fact that their facial makeup was painted rather frightfully.

Xu Fu unconsciously averted his gaze.

He wondered how Ying Zheng managed to endure looking at faces where makeup was applied with such a complete lack of skill.

Seeing Xu Fu staring intently at the dozen beauties, Ying Zheng's heart instantly tightened.
chapters.title: 第45章

chapters.translated_text:
Lady Zheng was among these dozen or so beauties. Although her status was slightly higher than the others, her attire was no different from theirs. Lady Zheng was so quiet, gentle, and low-key that if not for her exceptional height, Xu Fu might not have been able to pick her out of the crowd at a single glance.

The beauties took their seats one after another. Even though Fusu was right at the head, Lady Zheng didn't even raise her head, nor did she glance in Fusu's direction.

Xu Fu suppressed the astonishment in his heart and withdrew his gaze.

Food and fine wine were served onto the low tables, and the beauties stopped restraining themselves. Pouring their own wine, they raised their cups in a distant toast to Ying Zheng.

It was just that the gazes of these beauties would sweep toward Xu Fu from time to time. Unlike the Hu women, they didn't have such a strong sense of warry self-defense. At this time, the seven states favored handsome men, and compared to the Qin King's heroic and martial looks, they were more easily intoxicated by Xu Fu's delicate and ascetic face.

The moment Ying Zheng picked up the rhinoceros-horn wine vessel on his table, his expression sank abruptly.

Xu Fu didn't feel anything was amiss. He was often bathed in the gazes of others; what did this little bit amount to?

Xu Fu calmly raised his cup in follow-up.

The beauties finally withdrew their gazes as well, and smilingly offered a few words of blessing to Ying Zheng, which were nothing more than hoping for favorable weather in the coming year. As soon as they finished speaking, all gazes immediately fell upon Xu Fu.

Did he have to speak too?

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment. Meeting Ying Zheng's gaze, he almost blurted out, "May your longevity be as southern mountains and fortune as eastern seas."

Xu Fu held it in for a moment, and finally said just seven understated words: "May Your Majesty's wishes be fulfilled."

A trace of a smile faintly surfaced on Ying Zheng's face. His gaze stared fixedly at Xu Fu, with not the slightest intention of sparing a fraction of his attention for anyone else.

The crowd raised their cups to drink merrily. The wine tasted astringent and harsh as it entered the throat, and wasn't very good. Xu Fu was never good at drinking to begin with, so he merely took a hasty sip and put down the wine vessel in his hand.

The atmosphere inside the hall was joyous and cheerful.

Only behind the folding screen, as Lady Zhao listened to the laughter and cheers outside, she suddenly felt as if a ball of fire was burning fiercely in her chest. Not only was there not the slightest trace of joy on her face, but her eyebrows were raised and her gaze was ferocious. She actually dug her fingers into the tabletop and hard-heartedly snapped off a small section of a fingernail.

The palace attendants beside her held their breath in fear, not even daring to utter words of comfort.

They knew that ever since the Queen Mother left Yongcheng, she had completely changed—irritable and prone to anger. Even the King of Qin never directly conflicted with Queen Mother Zhao face-to-face; how could lowly servants like them dare to provoke the Queen Mother?

Perhaps after a few cups of wine went down, their courage truly grew, for the gazes the beauties cast at Xu Fu became even more uninhibited.

Xu Fu inadvertently caught a glimpse of the gloomy expression on Ying Zheng's face, and his heart skipped a beat. His head, which had been somewhat dizzy, instantly cleared up.

He had no intention of putting a green hat on the First Emperor of Qin...

Thinking of Lao Ai and Lü Buwei's fates, Xu Fu felt that being remembered in this way by the First Emperor of Qin was not good at all.

The food that he should have been thoroughly enjoying suddenly became tasteless in his mouth.

At this moment, shouldn't he immediately show his loyalty?

Xu Fu feigned casualness as he stood up, holding the rhinoceros-horn wine vessel, and slowly walked to Ying Zheng's feet, raising the vessel to invite Ying Zheng to drink together.

Ying Zheng fixed his gaze on Xu Fu, lingering relentlessly, and raised his wine vessel along with him.

What was originally a pleasing picture was abruptly shattered.

A bronze wine vessel was smashed onto the ground, rolling out from behind the folding screen and coming to a stop right at Ying Zheng's feet. Ying Zheng's expression subsequently turned cold and stern, but he still calmly drained the wine in the rhinoceros-horn cup first.

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, then also raised his cup and took a small sip.

A palace maid behind the folding screen let out a shrill scream, "Queen Mother!"

Originally, Xu Fu thought Lady Zhao couldn't help but make a huge scene at a time like this. But who would have thought that after that wine vessel was thrown out, not a sound from Lady Zhao was heard from behind the screen for a long time? Just as Xu Fu was puzzled, he saw the palace maid who had screamed running out, her face drained of color. Slipping underfoot, she tumbled directly to a sprawl at Ying Zheng's feet, stammering, "Y-Your, Your Majesty... The Queen Mother... The Queen Mother she..."

That palace maid was panting heavily, her expression terrified. Perhaps due to excessive shock, she failed to complete that sentence for a long time.

Subsequently, palace attendants also ran out one after another. One of them groveled on the ground, her body shaking uncontrollably, and wailed, "...The Queen Mother has suffered a sudden severe illness and collapsed to the ground. Your humble servants did not dare to touch the Queen Mother at will."

Xu Fu was also dumbfounded.

When had his words ever come true this fast? He almost felt like he was a crow with an ominous mouth! How could Lady Zhao kick the bucket just when she said she would? Wasn't she quite capable of bouncing around?

Xu Fu couldn't help but raise his head to look at Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng's face bore an expression of sullen anger. He flicked the hem of his robe and stood up, walking quickly around behind the folding screen, and shouted loudly, "Summon the court physicians!"

The hall instantly plunged into chaos.

Xu Fu didn't dare to go behind the screen at will either, not knowing what state Lady Zhao had actually turned into. Yet not even the slightest sound could be heard, so Xu Fu figured Lady Zhao must be in a very bad way...

The beauties who had just moments ago been full of interest and frequently stealing glances at Xu Fu were now every bit as silent as cicadas in winter, sitting in their seats without even daring to move, terrified of carelessly getting tangled up in this troublesome matter.

In times like these, if one were implicated and lost their life, that would truly be an unjust death.

The court physician arrived quickly, and he immediately ordered people to remove the folding screen.

Only then did Xu Fu see the scene behind the screen.

The table was extremely scattered, with patches of blood lingering on the side. Lady Zhao was currently collapsed beside the table, her face livid, though there was not the slightest trace of blood at the corners of her mouth; only her fingernails were somewhat damaged, and the blood had originated from there.

A dignified Queen Mother, collapsed on the ground, yet no one dared to go help her up.

Even though it was a moment when one should be furious and anxious, Xu Fu felt a bit amused in his heart.

Could it be that Lady Zhao was this era's professional expert at extortionate framing? She made the palace attendants too afraid to touch her, and Ying Zheng merely stood coldly to the side until the court physician ordered people to lift Lady Zhao up.

The court physician immediately reached out to feel Lady Zhao's breath.

At this touch, the court physician's expression changed.

With a pale face, he knelt on the ground, kowtowing to plead for mercy: "Your Majesty, the Queen Mother... the Queen Mother has probably passed away..."

The palace attendants were so frightened that they hurriedly knelt on the ground in tandem, not even daring to raise their heads.

The rest of the people in the hall also reacted and kowtowed along with them.

After all, Xu Fu wasn't a person of this era; he found it hard to adapt to the rhythm of kneeling at a moment's notice, so he stubbornly stood his ground.

Up and down the grand hall, only he and Ying Zheng were suddenly left standing.

A look of deep sorrow flashed across Ying Zheng's face, and the corners of his eyes quickly stained with bloodshot red. For a long time he couldn't utter a single word, and no one else dared to speak again; the hall was as silent as a graveyard.

Originally, Xu Fu also felt a little sympathy for the First Emperor of Qin.

Being the King of Qin was not easy. Celebrating the La Festival only to have such a bloody matter erupt—even though Lady Zhao was quite detestable, she was, after all, the mother who had once depended upon the First Emperor of Qin for survival, and now she died of a sudden illness...

Xu Fu attempted to convey his gaze to comfort the First Emperor of Qin.

But the moment his gaze locked onto Ying Zheng's pair of black eyes, he abruptly sensed that within those eyes, there was no grief whatsoever; instead, the icy coldness within was bone-chilling.

And rightly so.

Lady Zhao had already worn away the warmth in the First Emperor's heart. How could the First Emperor of Qin possibly feel grief for her now? The expression on the First Emperor's face just moments ago must have all been put on.

The Queen Mother of a state had died of a sudden illness; how could the banquet possibly continue?

The palace attendants hurriedly cleared away the food and wine.

The beauties also silently returned to the inner palace. Fusu was swiftly taken away by palace attendants, and Huhai, despite being very young, didn't cry either, being ignorantly carried back by palace attendants once more.

Xu Fu shifted his steps, just about to walk in Ying Zheng's direction, when he suddenly felt as if his brain had been struck by a dull hammer the moment he took two steps. Xu Fu's footsteps swayed, and he collapsed to the ground.

Ying Zheng turned back around and hurriedly reached out to scoop him up. Xu Fu leaned limply against Ying Zheng's chest, fainting completely.

Before passing out, Xu Fu couldn't help but curse inwardly.

You don't have the fate of a female lead, so what the hell kind of female lead disease are you catching...

Ying Zheng's expression turned even uglier. He raised his foot and kicked the court physician: "Get up! Go check on Mr. Xu!"

The court physician was dazed for a moment, scrambled up, and flung himself directly at Ying Zheng's feet.

Lady Zhao's body was carried out from behind.

Ying Zheng's gaze locked tightly onto the face of Xu Fu in his arms, without even turning his head back once.

The vast difference in attitude between the two instances caused the palace attendants to vaguely sense something. Their hearts grew cold as they groveled on the ground, yet no one dared to think any further.

The court physician pinched Xu Fu's wrist, his expression shifting back and forth, unable to reach a conclusion for a long time.

Seeing this, Ying Zheng's expression grew even gloomier. Feeling the suddenly intensified pressure bearing down on him, the court physician raised his head tremblingly and gritted his teeth: "Mr. Xu's symptoms are bizarre."

"How bizarre? Speak!" Ying Zheng's expression was even uglier, deeply suspecting whether Xu Fu had contracted some bizarre poison, or accidentally caught some incurable disease.

"Deficient Qi and blood, depleted essence." The court physician shook with fear and blurted out six characters.

Deficient Qi and blood?

Depleted essence?

The expression on Ying Zheng's face instantly became extremely bizarre, and his mind involuntarily plunged into a certain kind of reverie.

The court physician lowered his voice to recount methods for supplementing the body one by one, but Ying Zheng couldn't calm his mind to listen. The attendant beside him, however, carefully and meticulously noted down every single word.

Once the instructions were finished, Ying Zheng personally picked up Xu Fu and walked toward the bedchamber.

The attendant behind him was stunned and asked hesitatingly, "As for the Queen Mother..."

"Although it is during the La Festival, the Queen Mother's sudden demise must still be proclaimed to the whole of the State of Qin." Ying Zheng's expression was calm as he casually brushed the matter aside, entirely failing to show that the person who had just died of a sudden illness was his mother.

Remembering the past actions of Queen Mother Zhao, the attendant sighed inwardly and nodded: "Understood." I'm afraid that even if Queen Mother Zhao were alive, in the end she would only be destined to die.

*

When Xu Fu woke up, his stomach was on the verge of rumbling out loud. Clutching his stomach, which felt like it was caving in toward his back, he sighed inwardly: being an ancient person is truly not easy; who knows how many people died of stomach ailments.

Just as Xu Fu was about to call for a palace attendant, the moment he sat up from the bed, he bumped right into Ying Zheng face-to-face.

It turned out that Ying Zheng had been sitting by the bed the whole time, and the white unlined commoner's garment on his body hadn't even had time to be changed yet. He looked somewhat haggard, and his eyes were bloodshot.

Being able to see such an expression on the First Emperor of Qin's face was rare enough!

Xu Fu subconsciously mythologized the First Emperor of Qin in his heart. Only at this moment did he think: Oh, the First Emperor can be tired, can be weary, and can have joy, anger, sorrow, and delight.

Regaining his senses, Xu Fu asked, "What illness do I have?" After asking, Xu Fu himself suddenly felt a wave of bizarreness.

Of course, Ying Zheng didn't know that scolding people could include saying "you are sick."

"It is not an illness."

"Then what is it?" Could it be that his halo really was assigned wrong, accidentally adding a female lead halo?

Ying Zheng's expression turned complex.

Xu Fu's heart also tightened involuntarily, even though he still maintained a calm expression on the surface.

"Deficient Qi and blood, depleted essence." Ying Zheng recounted the court physician's words to Xu Fu completely, without a single omission, in a dull tone.

A streak of lightning flashed across Xu Fu's mind, illuminating his dumbfounded soul.

Essence... Qi... Depleted...

Xu Fu looked at Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng also looked at him.

The two of them looked at each other, neither able to utter a word.

Xu Fu actually felt a bit guilty; the matter of experiencing a nocturnal emission from a wet dream while sleeping in the First Emperor's bed was simply too humiliating.

Thus Xu Fu could only continue pretending to be calm and aloof, with the four large characters "I don't understand" written across his face.

Ying Zheng also came to his senses, figuring Xu Fu was probably feeling embarrassed, so he re-explained the court physician's words to Xu Fu: "The court physician said that you were young in the past, and your body had not yet fully matured. Now... it is a normal phenomenon... Coupled with the fact that there was poison in the incense previously, after you inhaled it, the toxicity inevitably lay dormant in your body until it erupted right up to now, which can only be considered as prematurely making you understand worldly matters."

A normal phenomenon?

The effect of the incense?

Xu Fu let out a long sigh of relief in his heart. He had always been broad-minded, yet he had tangled himself up over this matter for so long, to the point of generating the thought of running off to the side hall—making it increasingly appear in the Xianyang Palace that he was relying on the Qin King's power to act wildly and arbitrarily.

If that was the case, then he didn't need to trouble himself with needless worry anymore.

It was all caused by external factors; it seemed he truly had no romantic thoughts about the First Emperor, which was just great.

Ying Zheng didn't know the psychological changes in Xu Fu; if he had known, he would inevitably have instantly given birth to regret for what he had just said, wishing he could vomit a mouthful of blood.

"Thank you, Your Majesty, for worrying about me." Xu Fu finally spoke up.

Ying Zheng's expression softened somewhat, and a hint of a smile involuntarily curved the corners of his mouth. "I heard the court physician say that you must eat some food that replenishes Qi and blood every morning. How could there be Qi-and-blood-replenishing things in the Fengchang Temple? In my view, you might as well stay permanently in the palace; every morning when you wake up, palace attendants will naturally deliver the food right to your side."

Hm?

Hm?!

When Xu Fu first heard Ying Zheng speak, he didn't pick up on much, only feeling that the First Emperor was truly attentive to him—a monarch who valued his subjects this much was none other than the First Emperor! Who would have thought that before Xu Fu even finished praising him inwardly without costing a cent, he heard the second half of the sentence.

Stay permanently in the palace?

Every morning upon waking up, having palace attendants deliver lavish, Qi-replenishing food?

Such a huge pie dropped from the sky and smashed onto his head!

Xu Fu should have been overjoyed, but a keen sense of awkwardness arose deep within his heart. Was his ability really so high that it was enough to make the First Emperor treat him with such exceptional favor?

Xu Fu always had a cold and detached appearance. Even seeing that Xu Fu showed no reaction at all right now, Ying Zheng didn't find it strange. Tucking the quilt in for Xu Fu, he stood up and walked outward. The candle flames lit inside the hall were blocked behind him, and his face instantly plunged into a patch of shadows.

Perhaps it was an illusion caused by light and shadow.

With that single glance, Xu Fu caught a glimpse of a ferocious and murderous aura on Ying Zheng's face, a gaze that made one's whole body turn freezing cold.

To a certain extent, that was highly likely a portent.

Xu Fu's heart suddenly startled, and he sat straight up from the bed. He opened his mouth to say something to Ying Zheng, but before he could speak, Ying Zheng had already strode away.

Right! Lady Zhao...

Xu Fu suddenly thought of that Lady Zhao, whose life or death was unknown.

What was Ying Zheng going to do by going there? Was he going to deal with Lady Zhao? Xu Fu hurriedly called the palace maid not far away to the bedside. "How is the Queen Mother?" As soon as he finished asking, he froze.

Because that palace maid was wearing plain white mourning clothes, with not a single hair ornament or hairpin on her head.

"The Queen Mother... has... has passed away..." The palace maid knelt on the ground, speaking in a low voice, and let out a sob along with it.

Lady Zhao really died?!

Countless scenes flashed rapidly through Xu Fu's mind.

The dim and obscure look in Ying Zheng's eyes when he told Ying Zheng that Lady Zhao would bring disaster; the calm look when Ying Zheng replied to him that Lady Zhao would live permanently in the palace; the look when Ying Zheng was angry yet took no substantive action upon learning Lady Zhao came to the bedchamber to cause trouble; as well as the look at the banquet when the court physician said Lady Zhao had passed away, while Ying Zheng wore a face full of grief yet had icy-cold pupils; and Ying Zheng's face just now as it fell into the shadows...

A thought couldn't help but arise in Xu Fu's mind.

Ying Zheng had long known of the impending disaster, yet he took no action, and even turned a blind eye to Zhao Ji's reckless behavior.

Was it because he had long been confident of success?

From the moment Zhao Ji stepped back into Xianyang Palace, had she actually already stepped onto a path to her death?

Could the deathly aura he saw on Zhao Ji's face actually originate from Qin Shi Huang himself? That would explain why Qin Shi Huang reacted so strangely when he mentioned the deathly aura.

All of this had been planned by Qin Shi Huang!

Xu Fu was almost certain of it in his heart.

During the banquet after the La sacrifice, with so many people in the hall, Zhao Ji had thrown a tantrum and then suddenly died; although a screen blocked the view, it was still effectively in front of everyone.

No one would ever link Zhao Ji's death to Qin Shi Huang.

Although it sounded cruel, at such a time of nationwide celebration, with the Queen Dowager Zhao dead, perhaps the resentment in the hearts of the people across the country outweighed their grief.

Queen Dowager Zhao was too distant from them.

If the King of Qin had kicked the bucket, the people of Qin would certainly have wept in sorrow, but with Queen Dowager Zhao, who never had a good reputation, passing away on this day, how much grief could the people feel? Because of her passing, the year-end feast they had waited so long for would be cut short; how could they be happy?

After all these various emotions, who would still pin Zhao Ji's death on the King of Qin?

And those people from the six states who came to seek refuge in Qin, would they still harbor resentment toward the King of Qin because of this?

Zhao Ji was dead, the negative impact on the Qin state had been minimized, and before long, few would remember this Queen Dowager Zhao.

...Qin Shi Huang would no longer have any shackles binding him!

Xu Fu was startled.

"Master Xu?" The palace maid knelt on the ground with her head lowered; after a long while, hearing no sound from Xu Fu, she couldn't help but cautiously lift her head.

"It is nothing." Xu Fu lay back down.

Whatever Qin Shi Huang had done behind the scenes was none of his business.

Xu Fu closed his eyes; he might as well sleep again, and when he woke up, it should be when the dust had settled.

It was just that Xu Fu didn't manage to sleep until dawn; not long after he fell asleep, he was awakened by the palace maid.

"The King has returned," the palace maid said by his ear.

Shouldn't Qin Shi Huang be busy with Zhao Ji's funeral arrangements right now?

Xu Fu had to get up from the bed, and after stepping down, he suddenly realized that his outer robe had been thoughtfully removed.

The palace maid hurriedly fetched a robe to drape over Xu Fu; fortunately, there was a brazier lit in the hall, so he wouldn't be hit by a full blast of cold wind.

Ying Zheng strode in, his expression relaxed, and he said to Xu Fu, "It is time to eat."

Ying Zheng had indeed returned specifically to dine with Xu Fu.

Regarding his mother Zhao Ji, Ying Zheng felt he had already done his duty; now, by comparison, he preferred returning to his sleeping quarters to share a meal with Xu Fu rather than handling Zhao Ji's funeral affairs.

Xu Fu followed Ying Zheng out of the sleeping quarters, but halfway there, Ying Zheng suddenly turned back and blocked Xu Fu, "The wind outside is too harsh; it would be better to set the table inside the sleeping quarters."

Hearing this, the servants immediately turned to set the table and bring the food.

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment, then nodded and calmly turned back. He felt it was quite good not to have to go out and blow in the cold wind.

The previous banquet had been a total mess, so this could be considered making up for it.

There were no beauties filling the hall, not even Fusu or Huhai, just two tables placed very close together, and the food on the tables was much richer than it had been in the hall.

It could also be considered a make-up New Year's Eve dinner.

A New Year's Eve dinner without dumplings and without a gala.

Xu Fu picked up his chopsticks, feeling a warmth in his heart; the matter of Zhao Ji's death had been completely cleared from his mind.

Xu Fu filled his stomach first, and only then did he hear Ying Zheng speak: "Do you know that the Queen Dowager has passed away?"

The servants were all standing far away, and no one could hear what they were saying.

Xu Fu felt slightly relieved and nodded, "I asked the palace maid."

Ying Zheng kept his head low, his chopsticks tightly gripped by his well-defined fingers, but he didn't pick up any food. "Queen Dowager Zhao was not supposed to die."

Xu Fu's heart tightened. Why was Qin Shi Huang telling him this?

"I also did not expect that your thoughts would coincide with mine."

"What thoughts?" Xu Fu blurted out.

"That the Queen Dowager would suddenly die of a sudden illness."

Xu Fu's heart tightened even more.

He knew what Qin Shi Huang was referring to. When he told Qin Shi Huang that Zhao Ji was in danger, he had said that based on her current state, it was very easy for her to have a sudden illness that might be impossible to save her from. Had Qin Shi Huang already been planning to use the excuse of a sudden illness to ensure Zhao Ji died completely?

Did Qin Shi Huang think he had seen through his plan?

Could Qin Shi Huang's sudden insistence that he stay in the palace be a disguised form of coercion?

Xu Fu's hair stood on end, and his heart grew cold.

Ying Zheng continued to stare down at the chopsticks in his hand.

The image of Ying Zheng's cold, grim face suddenly appeared in Xu Fu's mind.

The more he thought about it, the more he felt it was true, directly ignoring the fact that if Ying Zheng truly feared him, he could have simply killed him brutally; a Grand Diviner disappearing in the palace could certainly be done without leaving a trace.

And at this moment, the head-lowered Ying Zheng had a smile playing on his lips.

Xu Fu's ability was indeed not weak; when he heard what Xu Fu said, he was indeed a bit stunned. He hadn't expected Xu Fu to be able to see even that, but Ying Zheng had no guard against Xu Fu, so he didn't change his plan. It was just that in his planning, he hadn't intended for Zhao Ji's death to ruin the entire La sacrifice. Zhao Ji's temper had been too volatile lately, inducing a heart-toxin, and it just so happened that she died of extreme rage during the banquet.

Ying Zheng could only regret that at such a moment, he hadn't been able to enjoy more time with Xu Fu.

Now that it was made up for, Ying Zheng's regret had disappeared, and his mood was naturally much lighter and more pleasant; he tapped his chopsticks on the table.

Over there, Xu Fu felt a chill behind his back.

But then he saw Ying Zheng suddenly look up at him, his expression eerily gentle, "Are you full?"

"Full... yes." Xu Fu, who had expected Ying Zheng to say something threatening or make a harsh remark, was a bit bewildered.

Ying Zheng said "Hmm," and then asked nonchalantly, "Then how do you intend to deal with Zhao Yi?"

Xu Fu shook his head, "The time has not yet come; there is no rush."

Yet, Ying Zheng could not suppress that sense of impatience in his heart.

Perhaps he really had taken an interest in Xu Fu, and seeing Zhao Yi provoke Xu Fu so much, and even steal Xu Fu's bamboo slips, Ying Zheng felt an uncontrollable surge of anger, wanting to get rid of Zhao Yi once and for all.

But Ying Zheng knew better: Xu Fu was usually cold and seemed not to take many things to heart, but in reality, his pride was hidden in his bones. He disdained to compete with Zhao Yi at this moment, and he certainly wouldn't be happy if Ying Zheng dealt with Zhao Yi behind his back. Xu Fu wanted to use his own strength to slap Zhao Yi hard in the face.

That was how Xu Fu was with Wang Liu.

Otherwise, from the moment Wang Liu walked into the palace, Ying Zheng could have ensured he never walked out again.

Actually, what Xu Fu was thinking wasn't really about taking it slow and slapping Zhao Yi in the face...

He just thought that in this cold weather, he didn't really want to leave the palace and head to the Fengchang Temple.

If he had to brave the cold wind just to deal with Zhao Yi, wouldn't that mean he was truly in love with Zhao Yi?

So Xu Fu decisively gave up; when the weather warmed up a bit, it would just happen to be after the date Zhao Yi had calculated had passed, and it would be the perfect time to slap his face.

Just let that Zhao Yi live with a guilty conscience, unable to sleep peacefully for a while.

Anyway, he wasn't the one doing the dirty work, so why should he be in a hurry? He was in the palace, and no matter how much Zhao Yi jumped around, he couldn't jump to where he was.

Without realizing it, Xu Fu had eaten quite a bit of food. He put down his chopsticks and was about to serve some soup; the moment he opened his hand, Ying Zheng raised his hand and placed the soup bowl into his hand.

Xu Fu was stunned, but without hesitation, he looked up and drank the soup.

This meal was much more comfortable than the one at the banquet. After eating and drinking his fill, he felt a bit sleepy. Over the past few days, Xu Fu had indeed lost a lot of energy, and having prepared so much for the La sacrifice, his sleep had been disturbed by nightmares and was insufficient. Now that Zhao Ji was dead and the La sacrifice was over, the suddenly relaxed Xu Fu couldn't wait to go to bed and get some good rest.

Ying Zheng saw the fatigue on Xu Fu's face and said, "Come and rest with me; on the day of the Queen Dowager's burial, I will need you to perform the divination."

"The King is also going to rest early today?"

A rare smile appeared on Ying Zheng's face, "Yes."

Having seen the small mole on the back of Xu Fu's neck, Ying Zheng had some sense of his nightly dreams; although he hadn't figured it out completely, he had gained some understanding.

In such a state of mind, sleeping on the same bed with Xu Fu felt completely different.

Xu Fu, upon hearing about sleeping, couldn't help but ask, "Did the palace physician prescribe any medicine for me today?"

"Only dietary supplements."

Xu Fu was a bit disappointed; if the medicine worked quickly, he wouldn't have that dream again tonight. But even without medicine, he had to sleep.

After the two quickly washed up, they got onto the bed together.

And at this time, Lu Buwei, who had not long left Xianyang City and was still on his way to the Shu region, also heard the news of the Queen Dowager's sudden death.

Lu Buwei was stunned on the spot, unable to move for a long time.

"...Husband?" Lady Lu called out to him.

Lu Buwei came back to his senses, his face pale, "Ying Zheng... is truly ruthless..." Lao Ai was dead first, and now Zhao Ji was dead; he didn't know when it would be his, Lu Buwei's, turn.

Lu Buwei felt panicked, and with a numb expression, he continued on the road to the Shu region under urging.

*

Perhaps it was a psychological effect, but once Xu Fu set his mind at ease, he had no dreams all night.

Ying Zheng, however, entered a dream again.

It was completely different from the vague, unclear dreams of the past.

On the large bed, behind the curtains, this was the first time he had seen the youth's face with such clarity.

The youth was dressed in black sacrificial robes, with a leather belt tied gently around his waist, making the youth look infinitely elegant. The contrast between black and white made the tyrannical desire in Ying Zheng's heart grow even stronger; he wished he could tear the youth's robes to shreds and then savagely bite into his snow-white neck.

How could Ying Zheng not recognize that sacrificial robe?

He had personally ordered it to be made.

Worn on Xu Fu, it was noble and mysterious. During the La sacrifice, countless people were captivated by his grace, and even at the banquet, the concubines in the harem couldn't help but blush in front of Xu Fu.

Ying Zheng felt anger in his heart, but he clearly knew that his anger was not directed at Xu Fu.

How could those heavily made-up, slender concubines compare to Xu Fu?

...

Perhaps because he was in a dream, Ying Zheng found his thoughts a bit chaotic.

His mind was full, one moment of Xu Fu's neck, the next of him standing on the ridge of a field side-by-side with Su Yi, and then again of the uncontrollable longing for Xu Fu in his heart...

So he acted; he lay beside the youth, following his inner desire, reaching out to peel back his robes, revealing the smooth and fragile neck. He raised his hand, and his rough fingers caressed the youth's neck, a small mole leaking out from between his fingers.

Black and white, distinct.

It gave one an urge to kiss it.

Ying Zheng lowered his head, kissing, licking, biting.

Ying Zheng felt that his eyes could no longer contain such magnificent color.

Beautiful things always make one unable to stop from feeling a fondness for them.

Ying Zheng felt he was very strange; at first, his feeling for Xu Fu was purely just fondness, but later, he didn't know when it gradually turned into a deeper desire.

He would actually one day suddenly think of the way Xu Fu lay on the bed, giving him the illusion of having intimate relations with him.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but reach deeper, groping downwards.

The robes were parted.

The kisses on his neck became more forceful.

A hand suddenly stretched out from nowhere.

Ying Zheng was stunned, meeting Xu Fu's eyes, which were shining in the dark night, as if studded with all the stars in the sky.

Ying Zheng's hand froze involuntarily.

There were two voices clamoring in his heart; one was saying, you've been discovered, you've been caught! The other was clamoring even harder, urging him to rush up more directly, pin the person to the bed, and if he wanted to tear the robes, just tear them...

Before the voices in Ying Zheng's heart could reach a conclusion, that hand suddenly withdrew.

Xu Fu closed his eyes.

Ying Zheng let go of Xu Fu's neck and took a breath.

It was cold.

Ying Zheng suddenly became much clearer.

What dream?

Was it a dream? Was it not a dream?

In that instant, Ying Zheng couldn't distinguish between dream and reality.

He closed his eyes, and it took a long time to calm the desire in his heart.

The moon slowly hid behind the clouds, time passed, and in the blink of an eye, it was the next morning.

Xu Fu fell asleep quickly and went to bed early, so he woke up exceptionally early today. When he opened his eyes, the sky was just beginning to brighten. When the palace maid served him and helped him put on his robe, he didn't know what happened, but she suddenly lowered her head, her face flushed red.

Xu Fu looked puzzled.

Could it be that after a night's sleep, his charm had increased again? Oh, perhaps sleep helps increase one's beauty value.

Xu Fu put on his robe and washed up. Before Ying Zheng woke up, the servants had already brought food, which was specifically for replenishing energy and blood.

Qin Shi Huang really wasn't joking, was he?

It was indeed true that he had food to enjoy as soon as he got out of bed!

Xu Fu couldn't figure out what was in Ying Zheng's mind, so he sighed and, inside the warm sleeping quarters, set up the table and enjoyed some of the nourishing food first.

At the hour of the dragon (7-9 AM), Ying Zheng woke up. He pressed his temples, turned over, and got out of bed, immediately seeing Xu Fu sitting at the table.

Xu Fu left him with his back turned.

Ying Zheng stared for a while, and a certain desire in his heart had already become clear.

After Ying Zheng also changed and washed up, he slowly walked to Xu Fu's side. Seeing that Ying Zheng had woken up, Xu Fu immediately stood up from his seat, "Your Majesty."

In Qin Shi Huang's territory, acting more like the master than Qin Shi Huang himself, Xu Fu was really worried that if he continued to be so extravagant, one day Qin Shi Huang wouldn't be able to tolerate it and would kill him.

But he couldn't refuse such high-level treatment from Qin Shi Huang.

Xu Fu sighed inwardly.

Ying Zheng had originally kept last night's dream to himself, but his gaze suddenly froze on Xu Fu's neck.

...There was a patch of red marks there, the traces of kisses were quite conspicuous.

A storm surged in Ying Zheng's heart; had he mixed up reality and dreams last night? The person he held in his arms wasn't the youth from his dream, but clearly Xu Fu!

Those marks were the best proof!

Ying Zheng had an urge to strip off Xu Fu's robes to see what was going on, but he forced it down, turned his head away, and said in a hoarse voice, "Accompany me today; after we eat, we will go see the Queen Dowager first."

Xu Fu chewed the food in his mouth and gave a vague response.

Going to see how miserable Zhao Ji was could be considered revenge, right?

"Would the King like to dine together?" Xu Fu pointed to the table in front of him.

Ying Zheng didn't shy away and sat down directly in Xu Fu's previous spot.

Xu Fu: ...

Then where was he supposed to sit?

The palace maid giggled incessantly and hurriedly went to fetch another table and cushion. Only then did Xu Fu lift his robe and sit down. Perhaps because his movement was a bit too large in that instant, he couldn't help but cover his neck.

Did I get a stiff neck from sleeping?
chapters.title: 第46章
chapters.source_text:
这十余名美人之中也包括了郑妃，郑妃尽管比其余人地位更高一些，但她的打扮与她们并无不同，郑妃太过静婉低调了，若不是她个子出挑，徐福还未必能一眼将她从人群中认出来。
美人们相继落座，明明扶苏就在上首，郑妃却连头都没抬一下，连看都没朝扶苏的方向看一眼。
徐福压下心中惊讶，收回了目光。
食物与美酒端上桌案来，美人们也不再拘束，自己倒上酒，便举杯遥敬嬴政。
只是这些个美人儿的目光，时不时会往徐福身上扫去。她们与胡姬不同，她们没有胡姬那样强烈的提防心理。此时七国大行美男之风，比较起秦王的英俊神武，她们更易为徐福那张精致又禁欲的脸而感觉到迷醉。
嬴政刚端起桌案上的兕觥酒器，脸色就登时沉了下去。
徐福并未觉得有何不对，他常常接受到来自他人的目光洗礼，这又点儿又算得了什么？
徐福淡定地跟着举杯。
美人们终于也收回了目光，还笑盈盈地朝嬴政说了几句祝词，无非就是希望来年风调雨顺之类的话。待她们说完之后，顿时所有目光就都落在了徐福的身上。
他也要说？
徐福怔了怔，对上嬴政的目光，险些脱口而出一句，“寿比南山福如东海”。
徐福憋了一会儿，最后只轻描淡写地说了七个字，“愿王上得偿所愿。”
嬴政脸上隐隐浮现了一丝笑容，他的目光紧紧盯着徐福，半分没有要分点目光到其他人身上去的意思。
众人举杯欢饮，酒水入口艰涩，味道并不怎么样，徐福原本也不善喝酒，只匆匆抿了一口便将手中酒器放下了。
殿内一派气氛欢畅。
唯有那围屏之后，赵姬听着外面的欢声笑语，顿觉胸中有一团火在狠狠灼烧，她脸上不仅不见半点欢颜，反倒还眉毛扬起，目光狰狞，竟是将手指扣在桌面上，硬生生地折断了一小节指甲。
她身旁的宫人噤若寒蝉，就连劝慰的话也不敢说。
他们知道，自从赵太后从雍城离开，便整个人都变了，暴躁易怒，就连秦王也从不正面与赵太后起争执，他们这些做奴婢的，又哪里敢触怒赵太后呢？
或许是几杯酒下了肚，便真的壮了胆，美人们望着徐福的目光倒是变得更为放肆了。
徐福无意中瞥见嬴政脸上阴沉的神色，心中登时咯噔一下，原本有些发晕的头，顿时就清醒了过来。
他可没有想要给秦始皇头上造绿云的意思……
想一想嫪毐和吕不韦的下场，徐福就觉得被秦始皇如此惦记上，可一点也不好。
原本应该好好享受的食物顿时吃进嘴里也变得无味了。
此时，他是不是应该立刻表示一下忠心？
徐福装作不经意地起身，手执兕觥，缓缓走到嬴政脚边去，举起酒器邀嬴政共饮。
嬴政将目光放到徐福的身上，流连不已，他跟着举起酒器。
原本是赏心悦目的画面，却偏偏被打破了。
青铜酒器被砸到了地面上，还从围屏后咕噜噜地滚了出来，刚好顿在了嬴政的脚边，嬴政的脸色随之冷凝起来，但他还是淡定地先将兕觥之中的酒水一饮而尽。
徐福怔了一下，也跟着举起来抿了一口。
围屏之后宫女失声惊叫，“太后！”
原本徐福以为赵姬会忍不住在这种时刻，大闹起来，可谁知道，那只酒器被砸出来之后，围屏后却半晌没有赵姬的声音响起，徐福正疑惑不解时，就见那失声惊叫的宫女跑了出来，花容失色，脚下一滑，直接扑倒在了嬴政的脚边，“王、王王上……太后……太后她……”
那宫女气喘吁吁，表情惊骇，或许是受到的惊吓太过，竟然半天都未能将那句话完整说出来。
随后，里面也接二连三地跑出了宫人，其中一人匍匐在地，身体抖动不已，哀声道：“……太后突发急症，倒地不起，奴婢们不敢随意触碰太后。”
徐福也呆了一下。
他的话何时灵验得这么快了？他都快觉得自己是乌鸦嘴了！赵姬怎么说玩完就要玩完了，不是挺能蹦跶吗？
徐福不由得抬头朝嬴政看去。
嬴政脸上带着愠怒之色，他一掀衣袍站起身来，快步绕到围屏之后去，高声道：“传侍医！”
殿中登时便乱作了一团。
徐福也不敢随意到围屏后去，也不知那赵姬到底变成什么模样了，只是连半点声音都听不见了，徐福便觉得赵姬定然十分不好了……
方才还饶有兴致频频偷瞧徐福的美人们，这时也都个个噤若寒蝉，坐在位置上连动也不敢动，生怕一不小心就跟这麻烦事儿扯上关系。
在这样的时间里，若是被牵连了，丢了性命，那可真是冤死了。
侍医很快便赶到了，他当即命人撤了围屏。
这时徐福也才看见围屏后的景象。
桌案上甚为散乱，边上还带着点点血迹，而赵姬此刻正倒在桌案旁，脸色发青，嘴角倒是半点血迹也没有，只是她的指甲有些破损，血迹正是从那里出来的。
堂堂太后，倒在地上，却无人敢去扶她。
明明是该又怒又急的时刻，徐福却觉得心中有些好笑。
难道赵姬就是这个时代的实力碰瓷专业户？搞得宫人都不敢去碰她了，嬴政也只是冷冷立于一旁，还是侍医命人将赵姬扶了起来。
侍医立刻伸手去探赵姬的呼吸。
这一探，侍医的脸色便变了。
他面色惨白地跪在地上，叩地请罪，“王上，太后……太后恐是已经去了……”
宫人们被吓得连忙跟着跪在地上，连头也不敢抬。
殿中其余人也反应过来，跟着叩地。
徐福毕竟不是这个时代的人，他难以适应说跪就跪的节奏，于是硬挺着站在那里了。
大殿上下，登时就剩下他与嬴政二人还站着。
嬴政脸上闪过沉痛之色，眼底很快染上血丝，半晌都未能说出一句话来，众人也不敢再开口，殿内鸦雀无声。
原本徐福也有点心疼秦始皇。
秦王不好当，过个蜡祭，也搞出这么血腥的事来，尽管赵姬挺讨厌的，但那毕竟也是曾与秦始皇相依为命的母亲，如今猝死……
徐福企图用传递自己的目光去安抚秦始皇。
但是等他目光一对上嬴政的那双黑色眼眸，他骤然感觉到那双眼里，毫无悲痛，反倒是里面的冰寒之色，冷得刺骨。
也是了。
赵姬已经消磨掉秦始皇心中的温情，如今秦始皇又怎么会为她而感觉到悲痛呢？方才秦始皇脸上的神色，应当都只是装出来的吧。
一国太后猝死，宴饮哪里还能继续进行下去？
宫人忙不迭地撤了食物酒水。
美人们也都默默回了后宫，扶苏更是迅速被宫人带走，胡亥年纪小小，倒也不哭，懵懵懂懂地便又被宫人抱回去了。
徐福挪了挪步子，正要朝着嬴政的方向走过去，谁知道他刚走两步，就感觉到脑子里像是被一记闷槌敲了一下，徐福脚步晃了晃，摔倒在地。
嬴政回转身来，连忙伸手将他捞起，徐福软绵绵地靠在嬴政胸膛前，晕了个彻底。
晕过去之前，徐福还忍不住在心底骂了句。
不是女主角的命，你特么得个什么女主角的病啊……
嬴政脸色变得更为难看，他抬脚就踹那侍医，“起来！给徐先生瞧瞧！”
那侍医懵了懵，爬起来后直接扑到了嬴政的脚边。
身后的赵姬被人抬了出去。
嬴政的目光紧紧锁在怀中徐福的脸庞上，连头都没有再回一次。
两厢态度差异之大，宫人们隐隐察觉到了什么，他们心中发冷，匍匐在地面上，却谁也不敢再往下想去。
那侍医捏着徐福的手腕，脸上神色来回变幻，半晌都没有得出一个结果来。
嬴政见状，脸色越加阴沉，侍医感觉到身上压力陡然加大，战战兢兢抬起头来，咬牙道：“徐先生症状诡异。”
“如何诡异？说！”嬴政脸色更加难看，深以为徐福是否中了什么奇毒，又或是一不小心染上了什么不治之症。
“气血虚，精气亏。”侍医吓得一抖，脱口而出六个字来。
气血虚？
精气亏？
嬴政脸上的表情瞬间变得极为怪异，脑子里还不自觉地陷入了某种遐想之中。
侍医低声将补身之法一一道来，只是嬴政却静不下心去听，身旁的内侍倒是小心又仔细地一字不落地记下了。
待嘱咐完之后，嬴政便亲自将徐福抱起来，往寝宫里走了。
身后内侍怔了怔，犹豫问道：“太后那里……”
“虽是蜡祭之时，但太后突然薨逝，也是要昭告秦国上下的。”嬴政神色淡淡，口中轻描淡写地将此事带过，全然瞧不出刚刚猝死的人，是他的母亲。
思及往日赵太后的作为，那内侍心中直叹气，点头道：“喏。”恐怕赵太后就算是活的，最后也只能死了。
*
徐福醒来时，肚子差点咕叽咕叽叫出声来，他捂着快要前胸贴后背的肚子，心中感叹了一声，身为古人也真是不容易，不知道有多少个得了胃病死的。
徐福正要唤宫人来，谁知道刚从床上坐起，就与嬴政打了个照面。
原来嬴政一直坐在床边，身上的白色野服都还未来得及换下，他的模样看上去有些憔悴，眼眸布满血丝。
能在秦始皇的脸上看见如此神色，也足够稀奇了！
徐福心中都不自觉地将秦始皇神化了。此时才会觉得，哦，秦始皇会累，会倦，会有喜怒悲欢。
徐福回过神来，问：“我是什么病？”问完之后，徐福自己顿时感觉到一阵怪异。
嬴政当然不知道骂人还有骂你有病这种说法。
“并非病症。”
“那是什么？”难道还真的是他身上的光环加错了，一不小心加成女主光环了？
嬴政神色变得复杂起来。
徐福的心也不自觉地紧了紧，尽管他的面上还是维持着淡定之色。
“气血虚，精气亏。”嬴政丝毫不带删减的，十分完整的，语气寡淡地将侍医的话转述给了徐福。
一道闪电从徐福脑中滑过，照亮了他懵住的心灵。
精……气……亏……
徐福看着嬴政。
嬴政也看着他。
两个人你看我我看你，谁也说不出话来。
徐福其实有些心虚，睡在秦始皇的床上因为一夜春梦发情这种事，实在太过羞耻。
于是徐福只能继续装着淡定冷然，脸上写着“我听不懂”四个大字。
嬴政也回味过来，徐福许是觉得尴尬，于是便将那侍医解释的话语，又转述给了徐福，“侍医说你从前年少，身体还未长开。如今……是正常现象……加上之前熏香之中有毒，你吸入过后，难免会有毒性潜伏于体内，直至如今爆发出来，也只当是提前使你知人事罢了。”
正常现象？
熏香作用？
徐福心中长长地舒了一口气，他向来心胸宽阔，却偏偏为此事纠结于心这么久，都闹得他生出想法跑到偏殿去，在咸阳宫中越发显得他仗着秦王之势，肆意妄为。
若是如此，那他也不必再庸人自扰了。
皆是外物所致，看来他果然对秦始皇是没有想法的，真是太好了。
嬴政不知徐福心理变化，若是知晓了之后，必然会对自己刚才所言陡然生出后悔之意，恨不得呕出一口血来。
“多谢王上为我担忧。”徐福总算开了口。
嬴政脸色缓和一些，嘴角不自觉地带上了点笑意，“寡人听侍医所言，你每日晨起必然要食一些补气血的食物。那奉常寺中何来补气血之物？依寡人看，你不如便长留宫中，每日晨起，自有宫人将食物送至你跟前。”
嗯？
嗯？！
徐福刚听嬴政开口的时候，没听出个什么来，还只觉秦始皇对自己可真够上心的啊，这样重视臣子的帝王，也就秦始皇了！谁知道徐福心中不要钱的夸奖还没跨完呢，便听到了后半句话。
长留宫中？
每日晨起，还有宫人送来补气血的丰盛食物？
天降如此大一个馅饼，砸在他的头上！
徐福原本应该喜出望外的，但他心底却敏锐地升起了一股别扭感。他的能力真的有高到，足够让秦始皇对他特殊至此吗？
徐福常常都是冷冷清清的模样，哪怕见徐福此刻毫无反应，嬴政也并不觉得奇怪，他为徐福压了压被角，站起身来往外走，殿内点着的烛光被他挡在身后，他的脸庞顿时陷入了一片阴影之中。
也许是光影造成的错觉。
徐福那一眼，却是从嬴政的脸上瞥见了凶戾之像，目光令人遍体生寒。
从某种程度上来说，那极有可能是一种预兆。
徐福心中陡然一惊，从床上坐直了身体，他张了张嘴，要对嬴政说什么，但是没等他开口，嬴政已经大步离去了。
对了！赵姬……
徐福突然想到了那个生死不知的赵姬。
嬴政此去是做什么？去处理赵姬吗？徐福连忙将不远处的宫女叫到床边来，“赵太后如何了？”他话刚问完，就僵住了。
因为那宫女着一身素服，头上无半点钗饰。
“赵太后……已……已薨逝……”宫女跪在地上，低声道，还随之抽噎了一下。
赵姬真的死了？！
徐福脑子里快速闪过之前的无数画面。
他向嬴政说起赵姬有祸时，嬴政眼底光芒晦暗不清的模样，嬴政回应他赵姬会常住宫中时那淡定的模样；得知赵姬前来寝宫找麻烦，嬴政虽怒，却并无实质行动的模样；还有就是在宴席之上，侍医言赵姬已去，嬴政满面悲痛，却眸光冰冷的模样；以及方才嬴政落入阴影中的脸……
徐福脑子里不得不生出了一个想法来。
嬴政早知有祸，却无动作，更对赵姬猖狂举动视若无睹。
是因为他早就胸有成竹？
从赵姬踏回咸阳宫开始，其实她已经如同踏在一条死路上了？
他从赵姬脸上见着的死气，会不会其实正来源于秦始皇呢？所以秦始皇才会听见他说起死气之后，反应那样奇怪。
这一切都是秦始皇谋划好了的！
徐福几乎已经在心底确定了。
蜡祭过后宴饮之时，那么多人身在殿中，赵姬大发脾气，却引起自己猝死，尽管有一围屏挡住，但也算是在众目睽睽之下了。
不会有任何人将赵姬的死与秦始皇扯上关系。
虽然说起来有些残忍，但在这样举国上下欢庆的时刻，赵太后死了，全国上下，或许心中怨怼是多于哀痛的。
赵太后距离他们太过遥远。
若是秦王翘辫子了，秦国百姓定然还会悲痛而哭，而名声一向不大好的赵太后在这一日薨逝了，百姓们能有多少悲痛之情？因为赵太后的薨逝，他们好不容易等来的年终欢宴也将因此被终结，他们又如何能高兴得起来？
种种情绪之后，谁还会将赵姬的死盖在秦王头上呢？
那些前来投奔秦国的六国人，又岂会再因此而对秦王心生芥蒂呢？
赵姬已死，对秦国的负面影响却已经降到最低，不久之后，便很少会有人再记起这位赵太后。
……秦始皇身上将再无束缚之力！
徐福惊了惊。
“徐先生？”宫女跪在地上低着头，半晌也听不见徐福的声音，不由得小心地抬起了头。
“无事了。”徐福又躺了下去。
不管秦始皇在背后做了什么，都不归他管。
徐福闭上眼，不如再睡一觉，等醒来后，应当就是尘埃落定的时候了。
只是徐福并没能达到一觉天明的目的，他入睡后不久，便被宫女唤醒了。
“王上回来了。”宫女在他耳畔道。
秦始皇现在不是应该正在忙于赵姬的身后事吗？
徐福不得不从床上起来，下来之后，他才骤然发现，自己身上的外袍被贴心地脱去了。
宫女忙又取来袍子披在徐福的身上，所幸殿内点着火盆，倒不至于被寒风灌个满怀。
嬴政阔步踏来，脸上神色轻松，他朝徐福道：“该用膳了。”
嬴政的确是特地回来同徐福一起用饭的。
对待母亲赵姬如何，嬴政自认早已仁至义尽，如今相比起来，处理赵姬身后事，他更乐意回到寝宫中，与徐福同坐一席用些饭食。
徐福跟在嬴政身后迈出寝宫，等走到一半，嬴政又突然回转身来，将徐福挡住了，“外面寒风太烈，不如便摆在寝宫中吧。”
宫人们闻言，立刻转身去摆桌案，上饭食。
徐福愣了下，点头，跟着又淡定回转身来。不用出去吹冷风，他觉得也挺好的。
之前的宴席被搞得一塌糊涂，如今也算是补回来了。
没有满殿的美人，连扶苏和胡亥也没有，只有两人摆得极近的桌案，和桌案上的食物，比当初在殿内时还要丰富得多。
也当时补了个年夜饭了。
补了个没有饺子，没有春晚的年夜饭。
徐福执起筷子，心中暖了暖，赵姬身亡的事已经彻底从他脑子里清理出去了。
徐福先填了填肚子，随后才听见嬴政出声道：“你可知太后已薨逝了？”
宫人们都站得远远的，谁也听不清他们这边在说什么。
徐福心下稍安，点头道：“问过宫女了。”
嬴政低着头，手中的筷子被他骨节分明的手指紧紧捏住，却并没有夹菜。“赵太后本没有死。”
徐福心中紧了紧。秦始皇跟他说起这个做什么？
“寡人也未想到，你会与寡人的想法不谋而合。”
“什么想法？”徐福脱口而出。
“太后突发急症猝亡。”
徐福的心顿时揪得更紧了。
他知道秦始皇是在指什么了。他向秦始皇说起赵姬有祸时，便说观赵姬如今之状，极容易突发急症，很可能一时救不回来。在这之前秦始皇是不是就已经在谋划，以急症之籍口，让赵姬死得透透的呢？
秦始皇以为自己窥得了他的谋划？
秦始皇突然让他长留宫中，不会也是一种变相要挟吧？
徐福浑身汗毛直立，心中凉了凉。
嬴政依旧低头盯着手中的筷子。
徐福脑子里顿时浮现了嬴政面目阴冷的模样。
越想便越觉得是这样，徐福直接忽视了若是嬴政真心忌惮他，大可以直接粗暴地杀了他，一个太卜令在王宫中消失，保管可以不留痕迹。
而此时低着头的嬴政，嘴角还噙着笑意。
徐福本事果真不弱，当时他听见徐福所言，的确有些怔住，他没想到徐福连这也能瞧出来，但嬴政对徐福并无提防，于是也未更改计划，只是在他的谋划之中，没想让赵姬的死破坏掉整个蜡祭，赵姬近来脾气太过暴躁，诱发心尖毒，偏偏恰巧在宴席之上怒极而亡。
嬴政只能可惜一下，如此时刻，却未能同徐福多享受上一会儿。
现在补回来了，嬴政遗憾也已消失，心情自然轻松愉悦不少，他将手中筷子叩在桌案之上。
那头徐福背后隐隐发寒。
却见嬴政突然抬起头来，看着他，神色温和得诡异，“饱腹了吗？”
“饱……了。”以为嬴政会说出什么威胁之言，或者放出狠话来的徐福，有些懵。
嬴政“嗯”了一声，又漫不经心地问：“那赵毅你欲如何处置？”
徐福摇头，“时辰未到，不急。”
嬴政心中却按捺不下去那股急躁感。
许是真的对徐福上了心，再见赵毅如此挑衅徐福，更甚至偷走徐福的竹简，嬴政心中便止不住地涌动着的怒意，想要将赵毅弄死，一劳永逸。
但是嬴政更清楚，徐福平日冷淡，好似许多事都不放在心上，但实际上，徐福的骄傲是藏在骨子里的，他不屑此时与赵毅争个高低，他当然更不会乐意让嬴政背后直接将赵毅处置了，徐福想用实力狠狠扇赵毅一记耳光。
对那王柳，徐福便是如此。
若不然，王柳从走进王宫后，嬴政便能叫他再也出不去。
其实徐福心中想的还真不是要慢慢来，给赵毅重重扇一记耳光之类的想法……
他只是想到大冷天的，他不太想离开王宫，前往奉常寺啊。
就为了处置赵毅，他就得冒着寒风前去，那他对赵毅还不得是真爱啊？
所以徐福果断放弃，等天气回暖一些，正好那时，赵毅所算的日子也过去了，他再去打脸也正好。
就且让那赵毅心中做贼心虚，日日难以安眠一段时日。
反正做亏心事的不是他，他急什么？他在王宫之中，那赵毅再蹦跶，也蹦跶不到他跟前来。
徐福不知不觉便吃了不少食物，他放下手中筷子，正要去盛汤，手刚一张开，嬴政便抬手放了汤碗到他手中。
徐福怔了怔，也不犹豫，直接抬头喝汤。
这顿饭倒是比宴席之上要吃得舒服多了，吃饱喝足之后便会有些犯困，这几日，徐福的确是亏了不少精气，又为蜡祭准备良多，睡眠受噩梦所干扰，也有不足，现在赵姬一死，蜡祭一结束，陡然放松下来的徐福，便恨不得立即睡到床榻上去，好生休息一番。
嬴政看出了徐福脸上的倦色，出声道：“同寡人去休息，太后下葬之日，还需你来卜算。”
“王上今日也要早早歇下？”
嬴政脸上罕见地露出笑容来，“是。”
见了徐福脖颈后的小痣，嬴政对自己夜夜入梦已有所感，虽然没能弄个透彻，却也已有几分明悟。
如此心境之下，再与徐福同睡一榻，滋味便变得截然不同了。
徐福倒是一听要睡觉，忍不住问：“今日侍医可曾给我开了药？”
“只有食补之法。”
徐福有些失望，吃了药若是见效快，今晚他便不会再做那梦了。不过就算没有药，他也得睡觉。
两人迅速洗漱过后，便一同上了床榻。
而此时，刚刚离开咸阳城不久，还在前往蜀地路上的吕不韦，也听闻了太后暴毙而亡的消息。
吕不韦当即就怔住了，久久无法挪步。
“……夫君？”吕夫人出声唤了唤他。
吕不韦回过神来，脸色发白，“嬴政……果真心狠……”嫪毐先亡，赵姬也已死，不知何时，便会轮到他吕不韦？
吕不韦心中惶然，表情麻木地在催促下，同吕夫人继续踏上往蜀地而去的路。
*
不知是不是心理作用，徐福放下心来，便一夜无梦。
嬴政却又入了梦。
与往日里那样模糊不清的梦境全然不同。
大床之上，帷幔之中，这是他头一次将少年的面容瞧得无比的清晰。
少年身着黑色祭服，腰间革带轻轻一束，将那少年显得风华无限，黑与白的相互映衬，让嬴政心底的暴虐欲望越发强烈，恨不得将少年身上的衣袍撕个粉碎，再凶蛮从他雪白的脖颈间啃噬而过。
那件祭服，嬴政又怎么会认不出呢？
他亲自吩咐人做来的。
穿在徐福的身上，高贵又神秘，蜡祭之时，便有无数人为他的风姿所倾倒，就连在宴席之上，后宫姬妾也忍不住在徐福跟前羞红了脸。
嬴政心中是有怒意，但他却清晰得知，自己的怒意并非冲着徐福而去。
那些妆容厚重，身段窈窕的姬妾，怎能与徐福相比？
……
也许是因为在梦中的缘故，嬴政发觉自己的思绪有些混乱。
满脑子，一会儿是徐福的脖颈，一会儿是他站在田埂间与苏邑并肩而立的模样，一会儿又是心中止不住对徐福的渴望……
于是他动手了，他趴在少年的身旁，遵从内心的渴望，伸手，剥开他的衣袍，露出光洁又脆弱的脖颈来，他抬起手，粗糙的手指摩挲过少年的脖颈，一点小痣从指间漏出。
黑白分明。
让人有一种想要吻上去的冲动。
嬴政低下头，亲吻，舔舐，啃咬。
嬴政觉得自己的眼中已经装不下如此瑰丽之色。
美的事物总是让人止不住心生好感的。
嬴政觉得自己很奇怪，初时他对徐福本也只是纯粹的好感罢了，到了后来，却不知何时渐渐变成了更深的欲望。
他竟然会在有一日，骤然想起，徐福躺在床榻上的模样，让他有种临幸的错觉。
嬴政忍不住将手探得更深，摸索向下。
衣袍被分开。
脖间的亲吻变得更加用力。
一只手突然横空伸来。
嬴政怔了怔，正对上徐福那双眼眸，在黑夜里，熠熠生辉，仿佛缀满了漫天星辰。
嬴政的手不自觉地僵住了。
心底有两个声音在叫嚣，一个在道，你被发现了，你被抓住了！一个却在更用力地叫嚣，让他更直接地冲上去，将人摁在床榻之上，想撕开衣袍就干脆撕开……
没等嬴政心底的声音争论出个结果来，那只手突然又收回去了。
徐福闭上了眼。
嬴政松开徐福的脖颈，吸了一口气。
凉的。
嬴政陡然清醒了不少。
什么梦？
是梦？不是梦？
那瞬间，嬴政有些分不清梦境与现实了。
他闭上双眼，半天才平息下来内心的欲望。
月亮慢慢躲在了云层之后，时间流逝，转眼便是翌日清晨。
徐福入睡快，睡得又早，今日便醒得也格外的早，他睁开眼时，天刚蒙蒙亮，宫女服侍着他起身，为他披上衣袍的时候，也不知是怎么了，突然间就满面通红地低下了头。
徐福一脸莫名。
难道睡了一觉起来之后，他浑身的魅力又增加了？哦，或许是睡觉有助于美貌值增加吧。
徐福穿上衣袍，洗漱干净，没等嬴政醒来，宫人便已经送来了食物，正是补气血用的。
秦始皇还真没开玩笑啊？
的确是他一起床便有食物享用啊！
徐福摸不清嬴政心中所想，慨叹一声，就在暖融融的寝宫之内，搭上桌案，先享用了些食补之物。
辰时，嬴政醒来，他按了按额角，翻身起床，一眼便看见了桌案前坐着的徐福。
徐福留了个背影给他。
嬴政盯着瞧了一会儿，心底某个欲望已然变得清晰起来。
嬴政同样更衣洗漱后，才缓缓走到徐福的身旁，见嬴政醒了，徐福立刻从位置上站了起来，“王上。”
在秦始皇的地盘上，比秦始皇还像主人，徐福真担心自己这样骄奢下去，哪一日秦始皇容忍不了，就弄死他了。
但是秦始皇这样的高级待遇，偏偏他又拒绝不了。
徐福心中暗自叹气。
嬴政原本只将昨夜的梦暗自记在心中，但他的目光却陡然凝滞在了徐福的脖颈之上。
……那里一片的红痕，亲吻的痕迹相当显眼。
嬴政心中掀起了惊涛骇浪，昨夜他将现实与梦境弄混了？他抱在怀中的哪里是梦中的少年，分明就是徐福！
那些痕迹便是最好的证明！
嬴政心中有股想要扒掉徐福衣袍看个究竟的冲动在作祟，他强制压下，将头偏转过去，声音暗哑道：“今日与寡人同行，用过膳后，便先去见一见太后。”
徐福嚼了嚼口中的食物，含糊地应了一声。
去看一看赵姬多么惨，也算是报仇了吧啊？
“王上可一同用膳？”徐福指了指面前的桌案。
嬴政也不避讳，直接就着徐福之前的位置跽坐而下。
徐福：……
那他坐哪里去？
宫女窃笑不已，忙又去搬了桌案与软垫来，徐福这才掀袍坐下，或许是那瞬间动作幅度稍微大了些，他忍不住捂了捂脖子。
睡一觉，我落枕了不成？
