Zhao Yi woke up feeling a vague sense of unease. Even though his servants stood by his side calling him for a long time, he remained in a daze. Zhao Yi had heard from his clan that those who deal with divination year-round often develop a certain sensitivity to fortune and misfortune. He didn't know if this was what he was experiencing now. Suppressing his anxiety, he hurriedly sent someone out of the manor, "Go and notify Young Master Xiong Yi."

After everything was prepared, Zhao Yi arrived at the Fengchang Temple.

Upon entering, he didn't feel that anything was amiss.

Xu Fu had still not arrived.

Zhao Yi secretly breathed a sigh of relief, though he didn't realize that his own heart had already lost half its composure. He found his seat and sat down, pretending to be nonchalant. Before he could fully relax, he heard a faint commotion coming from outside the hall.

What kind of matter could cause such a fierce reaction?

Zhao Yi gripped the bamboo slips in his hand, and fine beads of sweat began to form on his forehead involuntarily.

Several people walked in quickly from outside the hall. Zhao Yi turned his head to look and saw the guard being shoved in violently, nearly collapsing onto the floor of the hall as his legs gave way.

The cold sweat on Zhao Yi's forehead instantly increased.

The guard looked nothing like his usual self.

Zhao Yi knew the Qin laws were harsh, but he hadn't expected the guard to be in such a state just for being taken away as a suspect.

His hair was disheveled, his face covered in blood, and he looked haggard beyond recognition...

Zhao Yi looked further out and saw several cold-faced jailers standing at the entrance, reeking of blood, looking completely out of place in this setting. No matter how many schemes Zhao Yi had in his heart, how could he compare to jailers who dealt with darkness and bloodshed year-round? Zhao Yi's aura involuntarily faltered, and his heart couldn't stop trembling.

After the jailer shoved the guard inside, he immediately spoke in a stern voice: "By order to apprehend the thief! Do not interfere!"

What did it matter how good one's background was? In front of Qin law, everyone had to kneel.

They all turned their heads in unison, pretending to be blind. At this moment, no matter what happened, it was not their place to discuss it.

"Where is Dong You?" the jailer demanded sternly.

Upon hearing this, Zhao Yi felt a sudden sense of relief, and even a faint urge to laugh. Could it be that some unlucky fellow was taking the fall?

But before Zhao Yi could fully relax, he heard the jailer say: "Where is Zhao Yi?"

Zhao Yi's heart skipped a beat. He stood up, feigning calmness, just in time to see Xu Fu walking in from outside, looking at him with a smile in his eyes. Could Xu Fu know? Impossible! Perhaps Xu Fu just didn't like him and wanted to take the opportunity to harm him.

Zhao Yi felt much steadier. He stood up and walked outside together with the man named Dong You.

Dong You was shorter than him, looked timid, and his face was pale, giving off an immediate impression of guilt.

Zhao Yi felt disdain in his heart, but his expression remained indifferent, faintly carrying the arrogance of someone who had been wronged.

He was acting quite convincingly, Xu Fu thought. No wonder he had been worried about wrongly accusing Zhao Yi before and hadn't pinned the crime directly on him. Who would have thought that Zhao Yi was simply better at pretending?

After Zhao Yi and Dong You had both left the hall, Xu Fu cast a light glance at everyone inside.

But no one felt that his glance was light.

Everyone's heart tightened involuntarily, and they instantly felt as if they were being suppressed by his aura.

A simple display of power was enough. Xu Fu turned around and followed the jailers to another spacious open area. No one in the Fengchang Temple dared to come and interfere, and even Liu Fengchang acted as if he knew nothing.

Zhao Yi didn't even look at Xu Fu. With clear eyes, he asked, "May I ask why you have called me out?"

The jailer sneered, "It is not your turn to speak here."

The jailer's attitude was arrogant and hostile. Zhao Yi's face turned cold, but he still smiled at the jailer. Only by enduring what others could not could he have reached this point. Although the jailer was nothing, he was here under the King's order, and no one could afford to offend him.

The jailer first turned to look at Dong You.

Dong You was already covered in sweat.

Zhao Yi knew this man. Although his family background was extraordinary, he was the son of a concubine, was at odds with the eldest son, and had a very reclusive personality, which was why he had entered the Fengchang Temple. Usually, he was bullied by Wang Liu and his group, and Zhao Yi and the others looked down on him.

Zhao Yi laughed to himself, wondering if this man had really been mistaken for the culprit. If so, he could only blame his own lack of fortune.

"Was what you said before true?" the jailer asked.

Dong You's body trembled as he said, "It is true."

The jailer nodded and said, "Then point out the thief to us."

Upon hearing this, Zhao Yi felt a surge of alarm and almost couldn't suppress the change in his expression.

Sure enough, Dong You looked up and pointed right in his direction: "That morning, I arrived at the Fengchang Temple very early, and I... I saw him conspire with the guard, and then steal Grand Diviner Xu's bamboo slips..."

He had been seen?!

Zhao Yi never imagined that Dong You had been called out not because he was a suspect, but on the contrary, he was the only witness!

The guard knelt on the ground and made a hoarse sound: "I can also testify... the person who stole... *cough*, it is indeed Grand Diviner Zhao Yi."

The guard's words were as clear as could be. The charge of theft was instantly and firmly pinned on Zhao Yi. The jailer's cold, sharp gaze shot toward him. The sudden attack caught the previously relaxed Zhao Yi off guard. He looked at Xu Fu, who looked leisurely and couldn't be bothered to even look at him twice.

"...Nonsense!" Zhao Yi calmed himself and retorted sternly, his face showing the indignation of someone who had been insulted.

If someone didn't know the truth, they would truly believe Zhao Yi had been wronged.

But those jailers already knew the trickery involved. They had come today just to help Grand Diviner Xu scare Zhao Yi. How could they be moved by his one-sided story just because he pretended to be innocent?

The jailers sneered repeatedly and scolded: "Do you think it's nonsense just because you say so? Now that there are witnesses, what else do you have to say?"

Zhao Yi still stiffened his neck and said stubbornly: "Witnesses? Witnesses can be distorted, and besides, there is no physical evidence now. How dare you say I am guilty? Even if the King himself were here, I would still say I am innocent."

Never mind Xu Fu, even the jailers looked at each other, feeling that Zhao Yi was truly hard-headed. Even when pushed to the brink, he didn't give an inch and could still perform such a fearless act. It made them feel both ironic and, in a way, forced to admire him.

"How about it? Nothing to say? I, Zhao Yi, dare to say I am innocent! If you want to convict me, you must produce stronger evidence." Seeing that the jailers didn't speak for a long time and Xu Fu was standing by like a spectator, Zhao Yi suddenly gained confidence and shouted defiantly.

The jailers were about to open their mouths to threaten him.

Xu Fu suddenly spoke calmly: "Is Grand Diviner Zhao truly so unyielding?"

In fact, at this point, even without physical evidence, Zhao Yi's crime could be established. Once the crime of theft was established, he would face very harsh punishments: stripping of his official position, loss of status, and even death. Along with the guard, and even colleagues who were very close to Zhao Yi, they might also be punished.

Xu Fu couldn't quite understand where Zhao Yi's unyielding attitude came from.

The results of the First Emperor's investigation couldn't be wrong. That could only mean that either Zhao Yi's psychological quality was indeed too strong, or he had someone to rely on behind his back.

Although Zhao Yi had some connection to the Qin royal family, it went back many years, and besides, what was bloodline worth in the royal family? Zhao Yi wouldn't be stupid enough to rely on that.

So who could Zhao Yi rely on?

Xu Fu lowered his eyes slightly. He must use this move to draw out the person behind him, so as not to dispose of Zhao Yi in a hurry and leave a hidden danger behind. A fortune-teller finds it hard to calculate their own fate; if it were to erupt at an unknown time and endanger himself, that would be a big problem.

If Xu Fu had been as fierce as the jailers, Zhao Yi would definitely have continued to stiffen his neck and act unyielding. But Xu Fu's indifferent, unhurried manner made Zhao Yi feel a bit unsettled.

"This is only natural." Zhao Yi suppressed his inner unease and insisted firmly.

...

At this moment, a guest arrived outside the Fengchang Temple. The person stepped out of a carriage, smilingly rested his hand on the arm of a maid, and walked slowly to the entrance.

Someone inside the Fengchang Temple saw him and blurted out: "Attendant Xiong?"

The young man was handsome, and when he smiled, the maid beside him couldn't help but blush.

The young man ignored the person who had called him and went straight into the Fengchang Temple. His entourage did not have the qualifications to follow him inside and stayed by the carriage.

After entering the Fengchang Temple, the young man went straight to find Liu Fengchang.

Once he left, someone couldn't help but shake their head and say: "I didn't expect him to come back..."

"Can he not come back? Those two, one dead and one gone, his father can once again be favored by the King of Qin..." Someone said half of this in a low voice and then stopped abruptly.

...

To deal with a shameless person, Xu Fu didn't mind being a bit shameless himself.

He had no reason to order his men to raid Zhao Yi's home directly and couldn't get the bamboo slips, but it wasn't difficult to use this as evidence.

Xu Fu suddenly changed the subject and asked: "Now that the Wax Sacrifice has passed, and today happens to be the day chosen by Grand Diviner Zhao, why doesn't Grand Diviner Zhao tell us whose chosen day was more appropriate?"

Zhao Yi had already acted out the image of being unyielding and upright enough; now, after hesitating for a moment, he stopped pretending.

Since Xu Fu wanted him to say it, he would just say it straight. Zhao Yi laughed inwardly and immediately said bluntly: "Naturally, I prefer the day I chose. Although I don't know why Grand Diviner Xu is asking now, since Grand Diviner Xu has asked, I will certainly speak boldly. Grand Diviner Xu chose the 21st, and on the 21st, the Queen Dowager passed away. Can this be considered an auspicious day?" Zhao Yi paused, his inner sneer growing stronger, almost showing on his face: "Grand Diviner Xu knew this day was not right, yet he stubbornly chose it..." Zhao Yi stopped and didn't continue.

It was nothing more than creating the illusion for others that Xu Fu had ulterior motives and deliberately chose this day.

Xu Fu smiled for once.

Once his cold, clear face broke the ice, it bloomed like flowers.

Zhao Yi paused, his disdain growing even greater. He didn't have the great reverence for the current King of Qin that others did. Looking at Xu Fu's appearance, it was no wonder he could bewitch the King of Qin to the point of ignoring the auspicious day of the Wax Sacrifice, choosing such a day in a daze! Ridiculous!

What was wrong with the day he chose?

"Oh? How does Grand Diviner Zhao know that I wrote not only 'fortune' but also 'misfortune' in the bamboo slips? Could it be that Grand Diviner Zhao has already seen my bamboo slips, which is why you say I knew it was not right yet stubbornly chose this day?" Xu Fu knew that Zhao Yi wouldn't let this point go. Zhao Yi would definitely hold onto this pigtail tightly, attempting to save himself at a critical moment, and incidentally splash dirty water on Xu Fu. No matter what, it was enough to portray Xu Fu as someone with ulterior motives.

Zhao Yi hadn't thought of one point at all.

He had already seen the contents of the bamboo slips, so his thinking would naturally follow the contents of the slips without further reflection. How could someone who hadn't seen the slips say such things?

Zhao Yi certainly wouldn't admit it easily. The expression on his face stiffened, and he asked in confusion: "Why does Grand Diviner Xu slander me so? I clearly only saw that this day was not auspicious, so I..."

Xu Fu interrupted him directly: "If you only saw that this day was not auspicious, that means my divination was wrong. Shouldn't you be accusing me of lacking skill and deliberately showing off, causing the Wax Sacrifice to go wrong? Why accuse me of knowing there was misfortune yet stubbornly choosing this day? Grand Diviner Zhao, that doesn't make sense."

Xu Fu blocked Zhao Yi's words.

Beads of sweat seeped out on Zhao Yi's forehead.

Xu Fu was usually an aloof and cold person. Even when Wang Liu bullied him, he hadn't seen him tear Wang Liu apart. How could such a person have any eloquence? And how much did he understand about scheming? Sitting in the position of Grand Diviner in the Fengchang Temple, he should have been firmly under his control!

However, the person he looked down upon in his heart, once the disguise was torn off, was not clumsy in speech or too proud to argue.

Before Zhao Yi could think of a rebuttal, Xu Fu suddenly asked again: "Does Grand Diviner Zhao still insist that he is innocent?" Xu Fu's voice was mixed with a hint of laughter, as if mocking Zhao Yi's overestimation of himself.

Zhao Yi didn't understand.

Why did Xu Fu repeat the question?

His inner unease grew stronger.

Suddenly, he saw Xu Fu raise his hand and point from afar: "Grand Diviner Zhao, what is that?"

"What?" Zhao Yi was stunned, unable to react, and looked blankly in the direction Xu Fu was pointing.

As he lowered his head, Zhao Yi was almost scared out of his wits.

How could it be here? No, impossible! Zhao Yi's body suddenly stiffened, and he didn't even dare to touch it.

Inside his wide sleeve, a bamboo slip was hidden, and a black ribbon was floating out from it. All bamboo slips from the Fengchang Temple presented to the King of Qin had this mark. This black ribbon was issued by the Fengchang Temple, with strict regulations, and could never be forged; there would be no more and no less.

What was inside it went without saying.

The jailer looked contemptuous, walked over, used force, pulled Zhao Yi's arms apart, and forcefully pulled the bamboo slip out of his sleeve, shaking it open to look.

The signature was "Fu" (Fortune).

The jailer sneered: "How about it? Does Grand Diviner Zhao still refuse to admit it? Now not only are there witnesses, but there is also physical evidence! And caught on the spot! Does Grand Diviner Zhao still want to argue? If Grand Diviner Zhao is still not convinced, then we shall go before the King. But then, what awaits Grand Diviner Zhao might be the Five Punishments or the death penalty." The jailer's voice seemed to be soaked in ice, and his tone was extremely venomous.

Zhao Yi's heart suddenly went cold, and his guilt became even more intense.

Never mind him, even Dong You was scared pale, as if the Five Punishments would be used on him.

Zhao Yi gritted his teeth hard.

Admit it? Not admit it?

Why the bamboo slip had appeared in his sleeve so strangely, he couldn't explain! Why he had said those things to rebuke Xu Fu, he couldn't explain! The guard and Dong You's testimonies both pointed to him, and he still couldn't explain it!

If there were only the guard and Dong You's accusations, he might have a chance to save himself by arguing, but now with all three added together...

Zhao Yi's face was dark, and his legs felt weak.

But like Wang Liu, how could he be willing to admit defeat? He stubbornly believed that the day Xu Fu chose was wrong; how could he be willing to be stepped on by Xu Fu like this?

As the atmosphere reached a stalemate, a burst of footsteps approached, instantly breaking the deadlock.

Xu Fu said to himself.

Finally here!

He turned his head and saw Liu Fengchang wiping the sweat on his forehead, arriving in a hurry.

Didn't Liu Fengchang only have some friendship with Wang Liu? Didn't he avoid things quite quickly before and learn to be smart? Why was he standing out for Zhao Yi now? Xu Fu felt something was wrong and scanned again. Instantly, his gaze couldn't help but freeze.

Behind Liu Fengchang stood a young man dressed in black robes, his face powdered, his eyes like peach blossoms—exactly the kind of handsome man women loved these days.

Seeing Xu Fu examining him, the man even curled his lips at Xu Fu and smiled slightly, his face rippling with a seductive charm.

What a handsome man!

Xu Fu withdrew his gaze.

Was he the one Zhao Yi relied on? After all, in the Fengchang Temple, Xu Fu only found this person to be a new face.

"Grand Diviner Xu, I have something to ask you," Liu Fengchang said coldly.

Xu Fu said disdainfully in his heart: "A weathercock."

Wasn't Liu Fengchang a weathercock? He leaned toward whoever was powerful. Now he didn't know who was driving him to come and make trouble for him again. Liu Fengchang didn't even have the brains to think about it. Being used as a gun by others, what good end could he have later? Offending people back and forth, in the end, he was the one who would suffer!

"Liu Fengchang, we are acting under the King's order to interrogate Zhao Yi and Dong You. Grand Diviner Xu is the victim, so I'm afraid he cannot go with you," the jailer immediately stood out and confronted Liu Fengchang fearlessly. Those who had spent years in prison might respect those with high official positions on a daily basis, but so what? It didn't mean they feared these people. In their eyes, no matter how high an official you were, if the day came when you ended up in prison, weren't everyone the same? Who cared if you were a Prime Minister or a small soldier before?

The jailer's attitude was too tough, forcing Liu Fengchang's face to turn black.

At this time, the man behind Liu Fengchang also spoke.

"Is this Grand Diviner Xu?" the man looked at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu nodded, "And you are?"

Liu Fengchang couldn't wait to interject: "This is the Attendant of the Grand Ancestral Temple, who was also once the Grand Diviner."

His official position was higher than his own? And it shouldn't be just a little higher! Xu Fu reacted quickly in his heart.

The man didn't show off his official position but smiled: "Xiong Yi."

"Xiong Yi" (Chest/Bra), Xu Fu thought to himself, what a good name.

Xiong Yi then unconsciously swept his gaze over Zhao Yi and said: "Coincidentally, Liu Fengchang is looking for Grand Diviner Xu for something, and I am also looking for Grand Diviner Zhao for something. How about we put the interrogation on hold for now?"

Xu Fu had originally thought that the jailers would scold Xiong Yi, but when he glanced back, he happened to see the look of surprise on the jailers' faces that they couldn't hide. The jailers looked at each other; they, who had dared to snap back at even Liu Fengchang, were now becoming hesitant.

No wonder Zhao Yi had such backing; this person must have a high status, right? Xu Fu was not familiar with Qin history and couldn't guess what Xiong Yi's identity could be, or what the surname Xiong represented.

However, he had made up his mind today to slap Zhao Yi's face hard, so he must slap it hard and would absolutely not retreat a single step!

"Oh, Attendant Xiong, what a coincidence. The evidence of Grand Diviner Zhao's theft is conclusive. I'm afraid there are only two places he can go now," Xu Fu replied calmly.

A flash of interest crossed Xiong Yi's face: "Oh? Which two places?"

"One is prison, and the other is before the King." Xu Fu's expression was cold when he said this. Zhao Yi couldn't help but feel his heart drum, while Xiong Yi was not discouraged at all and smiled again: "Why go to such trouble? If he has already been convicted, I suppose it won't hurt to wait a moment, right?"

Xu Fu thought to himself, it would hurt.

If he let go and let Xiong Yi take Zhao Yi away, could he still bury Zhao Yi in the ground in one breath and never let him climb out of that pit again?

"Attendant Xiong, no need to say more. No matter who it is, they must be dealt with according to the law," Xu Fu turned back and reminded the jailers: "Trouble you all to take Grand Diviner Zhao away."

The jailers woke up as if from a dream and immediately stepped forward to hold Zhao Yi, and the guard was also lifted from the ground.

Xiong Yi cast a cold glance at Dong You, making Dong You tremble slightly.

Zhao Yi panicked instantly.

Xu Fu hadn't guessed wrong; his backing did come from Xiong Yi, but how could he have expected that even in front of Xiong Yi, Xu Fu would dare to be so disrespectful and forcefully send him to prison?

"Attendant Xiong..." Zhao Yi finally couldn't help it. His disguise cracked, and his voice revealed a slight nervousness.

Xiong Yi frowned, and after his gaze touched Xu Fu, he couldn't say anything more.

He had long heard from Zhao Yi that there was a person in the Fengchang Temple who served the King of Qin with his looks, thus obtaining the position of Grand Diviner, and then acted arrogantly, not putting Zhao Yi in his eyes, and even secretly taking away Zhao Yi's spot for the Wax Sacrifice. Xiong Yi had seen the King of Qin, Ying Zheng, and he didn't believe Zhao Yi's words—who could fool the King? But he didn't know that the person Zhao Yi spoke of looked like this.

Xiong Yi liked men, so how could he bring himself to make things difficult for Xu Fu now?

Xu Fu's lack of respect made him feel annoyed, but compared to Zhao Yi, Xiong Yi was a bit hesitant. Moreover, Zhao Yi had done a stupid thing and was caught in the act! How could he help him? Xiong Yi's face darkened: "Grand Diviner Zhao, then go with them."

Zhao Yi was stunned.

His mouth opened slightly. He never thought even in death that things would develop to this point.

Hadn't he and Xiong Yi talked it over well? Why did he suddenly change his mind? With Xiong Yi and Liu Fengchang here, could Xu Fu really turn the world upside down? Why did Xiong Yi suddenly give up on saving him? If he hadn't had such high hopes before, he wouldn't have felt like a bolt from the blue now.

Upon hearing this, Xu Fu was also a bit surprised. He thought he would have to argue with Xiong Yi, but he gave up so easily?

Turning to see the shock and panic in Zhao Yi's eyes, Xu Fu knew that Xiong Yi's attitude shouldn't be fake.

The jailers received the order and immediately grabbed Zhao Yi's arms, dragging him out. In this way, Zhao Yi's face and reputation in the Fengchang Temple were completely lost. Not to mention that his life was now in jeopardy, even if he lived to come out of prison in the future, he would become a big joke in the Fengchang Temple!

Zhao Yi struggled and finally remembered to save himself. He shouted loudly: "Xu Fu! You slander me so! Xu Fu..." Zhao Yi was still struggling to act, attempting to maintain his image of being unyielding and indomitable.

A faint smile appeared on Xu Fu's face.

Did Zhao Yi think this was the end? That was underestimating him too much. Zhao Yi could still have the mood to act now, but after he entered prison, he would soon have no mood to act.

Thinking of this, the smile on Xu Fu's face paused. When he returned to the palace, he would have to thank the First Emperor properly. If it weren't for the First Emperor's help, how could he, a newcomer to Qin who was unfamiliar with the place, have the ability to mess with Zhao Yi?

The jailers were still a bit hesitant, but seeing that Xiong Yi had let go, their fierce aura returned. Seeing Zhao Yi making a scene, they grabbed a rag from a passerby and stuffed it into Zhao Yi's mouth.

The person whose rag was snatched away was stunned, watching the jailers take the man away, and then muttered: "...That... that was just used to wipe the threshold..."

Zhao Yi had a mouthful of sand and dirt. Where had he ever suffered such hardships? Even if Xu Fu had tortured him mentally, he wouldn't necessarily be weak, but physical torture made him feel unbearable, and even sorrow welled up...

Just as Zhao Yi was about to step out of the Fengchang Temple gate, he suddenly heard Xu Fu smile and say: "Grand Diviner Zhao carefully chose today, so Grand Diviner Zhao must enjoy it well."

What did he mean?

Zhao Yi's thoughts were chaotic, and he didn't have time to think deeply before he was dragged out. He could no longer hear Xu Fu's voice behind him.

After they were far from the Fengchang Temple, Zhao Yi finally understood what Xu Fu meant.

Zhao Yi's fingernails dug deep into his palms.

He had chosen today as an auspicious day.

How ironic! He was also caught on this day! It was called an auspicious day, but it had turned into his day of misfortune!

Xu Fu was mocking him! Ridiculing him! Humiliating him severely!

...

Zhao Yi's figure gradually faded away, and Xu Fu also breathed a sigh of relief. Having dealt with one trouble, he felt much lighter. The bamboo slip taken from Zhao Yi's sleeve had been taken away by the jailers, and the guard had also been dragged away. Apart from a few spots of the guard's blood, there was nothing else in the open area.

Xiong Yi stared at Xu Fu wiping his fingers in a leisurely manner, his throat moving, and a fire seemed to be burning fiercely in his heart.

Zhao Yi losing to him was not unjust...

Xiong Yi thought involuntarily.

Only Liu Fengchang stood awkwardly to the side, his face burning. He had originally wanted to curry favor with Xiong Yi, but who knew that by now, the person who was supposed to find trouble for Xu Fu had suddenly stopped? How was he supposed to handle himself?

Liu Fengchang looked at Xiong Yi frequently, attempting to get an explanation from him.

Xu Fu turned and said calmly: "Does Liu Fengchang have anything else to say? If not, I will take my leave."

Liu Fengchang became even more anxious.

At this moment, he received Xiong Yi's gaze.

Liu Fengchang was stunned. Still continue? Wasn't Zhao Yi already taken away? What was the point of continuing? Liu Fengchang didn't understand, but he didn't dare to ask Xiong Yi, so he immediately put on a serious face and said coldly: "Of course, there is something else to ask you."

Xu Fu nodded and stood there without moving. He would listen to what kind of trouble Liu Fengchang wanted to make.

Liu Fengchang suddenly raised his voice and said viciously: "Xu Fu, do you know your mistake? The Wax Sacrifice, such an important ceremony! How did you treat it?"

Xu Fu was confused. Did Liu Fengchang want to accuse him of miscalculating the auspicious day?

That auspicious day was overseen by the First Emperor. How brain-dead would these people have to be to find fault with the auspicious day? If they said the day was wrong, wouldn't that be equivalent to saying the First Emperor was blind?

Xu Fu didn't respond.

Liu Fengchang felt even more awkward and had to raise his voice higher, scolding: "The ceremonial robes for the Wax Sacrifice are official! They all follow the strict rites! Why is yours the only one different from others? Grand Diviner Xu, did you accidentally damage your robe and find another one to fill in? Such disrespect to the Wax Sacrifice! According to the law, you should be punished with the Five Punishments! Strictly punished!"

The Five Punishments?

Xu Fu now understood what the Five Punishments of the Qin State were.

Corporal punishment, amputation, tattooing, nose cutting, and castration.

These Five Punishments were all extremely harsh!

Liu Fengchang was trying to kill him with this opening?

The First Emperor had also killed him. Xu Fu never expected that a set of sacrificial robes could be used by Liu Fengchang to make such a big deal out of it!

Where did the robe come from? Should he say it or not? Xu Fu hesitated. If he said it, people might be wary, but they would definitely be even more jealous! How could his current status bear more jealousy?

"Grand Diviner Xu! Why don't you speak?" Liu Fengchang continued sternly.

Xu Fu frowned, feeling extremely troubled.

He didn't expect Liu Fengchang to be waiting for him here. He was completely unprepared. What perfect strategy could he have now?

Just as Xu Fu was about to tell the truth, he heard Xiong Yi say: "Why is Liu Fengchang so angry? If this matter wasn't exposed at the time, let it be. Why bother to make things difficult for Grand Diviner Xu now?" Xiong Yi's face was smiling, and no malice could be seen.

Xu Fu looked at him with extreme wariness.

What did Xiong Yi mean?

Liu Fengchang hit him with a stick, and Xiong Yi wanted to come out and be the good guy?

Wasn't Xiong Yi here to stand up for Zhao Yi? What was the meaning of this now? Was it to seek justice for Zhao Yi?

Upon hearing this, Liu Fengchang became even more severe: "This rampant trend cannot be indulged! Please explain to me, Grand Diviner Xu, otherwise, I will have to send you to prison! Grand Diviner Xu, don't argue with me. If you are truly unconvinced, the result will be the same when you go before the King."

Xu Fu laughed inwardly.

I am afraid of many things, but I am really not afraid of you taking me before the First Emperor!

Compared to Xiong Yi, Liu Fengchang's behavior made Xu Fu realize that these two were singing a duet.

"Liu Fengchang accused me as soon as he came up. I really don't know where I went wrong? If you are talking about the sacrificial robe, it was sent by the attendant later. How can you say I damaged the robe and found another one to replace it?" Xu Fu learned the trick of playing the rogue that Zhao Yi had just used: "Liu Fengchang is so firm, you must have evidence in your hand. Please show me the evidence."

Liu Fengchang was stunned.

If it were an ordinary person, wouldn't they have panicked between his and Xiong Yi's pincer attack?

Why was Xu Fu such an anomaly?

Liu Fengchang gritted his teeth secretly, thinking of Xu Fu's struggle with Wang Liu and Zhao Yi, and realized: Yes, how could Xu Fu be someone so easily subdued?

Liu Fengchang couldn't help but look at Xiong Yi, attempting to get Xiong Yi to make a move and subdue Xu Fu.

Xiong Yi did indeed speak at this time. He shook his head and said in a gentle tone: "Why does Grand Diviner Xu have to be like this? Even if there is a mistake, you can correct it later. I don't think Grand Diviner Xu did it on purpose. Can't you just correct it later?"

Was this just ignoring whatever he said and insisting on pinning the hat on him?

Xu Fu sneered in his heart.

He didn't intend to just take it.

Xu Fu suddenly shouted loudly: "Someone!"

Liu Fengchang and Xiong Yi were both startled by his shout, not knowing what Xu Fu was going to do.

As the voice fell, a person with an unremarkable appearance walked over, but seeing his attire, not to mention Liu Fengchang, even Xiong Yi didn't dare to look down on him.

This person was a palace attendant!

Liu Fengchang then remembered that when Xu Fu returned to the Fengchang Temple just now, someone seemed to have followed him, but because the fight between Zhao Yi and Xu Fu was so attractive, they had all forgotten about this person.

Xu Fu smiled.

The smile was still the kind that seemed to dazzle people's eyes.

"Then let's go before the King now," Xu Fu said.

Liu Fengchang was stunned.

Really... really going?

得了官职之后，赵高只领命将徐福送到了奉常寺的居所去，第二日还是要徐福自己前往报道的。
翌日清晨时分，徐福压抑住打呵欠的冲动，推开了面前的门，然后迈出一只脚，“请问，这里是奉常寺吗？”
不管是忙成一锅粥的还是清闲得拍苍蝇的，全部齐齐回头看向了门口的少年。
少年穿着一身稍显宽大的红色官服，越发衬得他面如桃花，唇红齿白，真是秀丽得不像凡间人物，望一眼真让人顿生脱俗之感。
“尔是？”其中一名中年男子开口问了。
嗯？什么耳屎？徐福一阵茫然，“我来报道，这里是奉常寺吗？我来做奉常。”
中年男子狠狠地会皱了皱眉，看向徐福的目光顿时带上了敌意，“这里是奉常寺，既然过来了，那就……”那男子随手一指，“就先去整理那堆东西吧。”
徐福高冷地点了点头，缓步走过去，然后……撸起袖子整理竹简。
中年男子忍不住问旁边的人：“你以前可见过他？难道又是哪个世家的公子？”
旁边的人连连摇头，“我也没见过，可能是吧。”
中年男子强自压下心中不满，看向徐福的目光就跟看一个讨厌的走后门的狗屎富二代一样。
徐福动作看上去不疾不徐的，但整理东西还挺快，他做完以后，就找出了一个竹简，拖过垫子坐下来慢慢看起来。竹简上记载的都是年历和过往的大事件，徐福越看越惊心。他没猜错，他真的到了秦朝！哦不，现在还只是秦国。那位少年老成的王上，正是还未行加冠礼的秦王嬴政！
嬴政啊！
徐福历史学得再烂，却也知道这位历史上的千古一帝。他大概记得这位帝王在历史上，知人善用，揽了不少六国良才，而且秦始皇似乎在后期十分重用方士，他记得还有个方士特别出名来着，叫什么来着……哦，想不起了。
想不起来，徐福也没再纠结，他合上竹简，心情愉悦了不少，他觉得自己离梦想蓝图更近了一步。
一阵脚步声突然近了，徐福抬头一看，只见那中年男子正面色不豫地看着自己，男子嘴角一撇，大声斥责徐福，“这点小事你也要做上半天，真不知道是怎么选进来的。”
你意思是怪你家王上眼瞎咯？
徐福心中吐槽，面上倒是出奇的淡定，丝毫没有要跟这个中年男子计较的意思。
石块扔下去连个水花都打不起来，中年男子顿觉丢脸，于是变得更加颐气指使了，“你知道你过来是干什么的吗？不是吃白饭的，是要干活的，去，将那堆东西清理干净。”
徐福不知道这放在现代，叫做职场欺压。他不是会任人随意欺负的性格，骨子里还带点执拗，现在听这个老男人口气恶劣，他当然也没什么好态度。
“我来奉常寺是掌天气观测的，不是过来给你干活儿的。”你算什么东西？徐福瞥了一眼男子，眼眸里透着几分骄矜。
男子稍微有些心虚，他猜不出徐福究竟是什么来头，而他自己的背景也只能算尚可，以前在奉常寺里没少被一干贵公子欺负，现在见了徐福，顿时觉得来了个更好欺负的对象，便迫不及待地想要下手捏软柿子了。
这傻子却没想过，这柿子里头藏着尖锐石子，把手硌出口子来怎么办？
也不知道中年男子哪根筋搭错了，将徐福的淡定漠然当做了软弱，他越发恶气起来，“掌天气观测？你也配？你可知道，奉常寺中掌天气、卜筮的大人，都是出自世家！”
这玩意儿还要讲究个世家传承吗？徐福无语。
那中年男子越发来劲，“来到奉常寺，你就得听我们几位的。不过一介小小新人，竟是半点规矩都不通。自然是我叫你做什么，你就要做什么……”
徐福实在懒得听对方在自己面前耀武扬威了。
“你是做什么的？”徐福打断他的话。
中年男子愣了愣，“我掌祭祀衣冠。”
徐福暗自嘀咕，这奉常寺到底是个什么鬼地方，怎么什么人都有？掌祭祀衣冠的又是什么玩意儿？
徐福摸不清来头，就“哦”了一声，便不再说话。
中年男子愣了愣，顿时脸色臊红，显然他认为刚才徐福问他的话，是在故意戏耍他，男子怒从心起，“还愣着干什么？去整理东西！没看见大家都忙不过来吗？”
秦王即将行加冠之礼，奉常寺作为掌陵庙群祀、礼乐仪制、天文术数衣冠之属，自然忙得团团转，谁也不敢怠慢分毫。其中以观天、卜筮为职的巫祝大人们，却是最悠闲的，他们这些打杂的羡慕嫉妒恨，心中忿忿，现在正好发泄到徐福的身上。
反正在他们看来，徐福是个生面孔，又极为年轻，长得还细皮嫩肉弱唧唧的，突然空降过来就要做巫祝，不欺负他欺负谁？
给你脸，还不要脸了？
徐福目光冷了冷，将那中年男子从头梭巡到脚。
中年男子被看得总觉得身上发凉，他不由得再度出声呵斥徐福，“小儿，看什么？”
“你有病。”徐福突然吐出三个字。
中年男子因为职场生涯的长期不如意，性格暴躁易怒，听见这三个侮辱他人身的字眼，哪里还能忍？他因为愤怒而鼻翼微动，“大胆，你才有病！”
真像只河马。
徐福有点嫌弃。
哦不，说他像河马，都侮辱河马了。
徐福清了清嗓子，面色漠然，颇有一番世外高人的风范，“听我说，你是真的有病了，暴躁易怒，双眼血丝密布，眼下乌黑，额间多有细纹，喘气粗急……可不是有病吗？当然这些都不重要，最重要的是，你乌云罩顶，恐有大祸啊……”
“胡说八道！”中年男子满心都是被侮辱嘲笑的感觉，他彻底被激怒，袖袍一挥，竟是粗暴地将徐福面前的桌案都掀翻了，其中还包括之前徐福整理出来的竹简，“你、你到底是从哪里来的？你竟敢在奉常寺撒野！待我秉明刘奉常，定将尔等败类驱出奉常寺！”
其实也就中年男子一个人在激动，其他人全都是一副看笑话的表情，这些人不仅漠视徐福，对待这名中年男子也是极为轻蔑的。
中年男子就如同一个跳梁小丑，迫不及待地在徐福面前上蹿下跳。
徐福低下头，拾起竹简，依旧稳坐如山，“你不信就算了。”
嘁，纸老虎，这个老男人敢冲上来揍他，都算是血性男儿，但他只会跳脚怒骂，拽两句规矩。看周围人的目光就能知道，男人也不可能是什么官，那他又哪里来的底气在自己面前作妖？
送他一句批语，那都是自己心善了。
中年男子完全威胁不了徐福，更拉拢不到同仇敌忾的同事，他有些慌张，但他手无缚鸡之力，更是不敢对徐福动手，于是只能恨恨地罢了手，一边往外走，一边高声喊：“我这就去见刘奉常。”
徐福心中轻嗤。以为自己今年五岁吗？骂不赢还要告老师？
作者有话要说：
关于历史考据。正文中已经说明，天文术数等都是归奉常寺管，奉常隶属于三公九卿中的九卿之一。这个官是很大的，可惜徐福过去做的并不是这个官。然后巫祝是瞎编的。古典记载，巫祝是负责卜筮和祭祀。这里就拿来做官职好了，因为实在查不到具体的职位。只能作者君自己闭门造了。
最后，秦朝能入朝做官的方士大都是有背景的人物，像徐福这样空降的，小透明嫉恨他，走后门的轻视他，所以本章又名#同事都是我敌人可怎么办？全部掀翻这样好吗？急！在线等#
chapters.title: 第5章
chapters.translated_text:
After receiving his official title, Zhao Gao only took the order to escort Xu Fu to the residence of the Fengchang Temple. Xu Fu would still have to report for duty himself the next day.

Early the next morning, Xu Fu suppressed the urge to yawn, pushed open the door in front of him, and then stepped out with one foot, "Excuse me, is this the Fengchang Temple?"

Whether busy as a beehive or so leisurely they were swatting flies, everyone turned their heads in unison to look at the youth at the door.

The youth was wearing a slightly oversized red official robe, which only served to make his face look like peach blossoms and his lips red and teeth white. He was truly so exquisite that he didn't look like a mortal, and just one glance instantly gave one a sense of transcendence from the mundane world.

"Who are you?" one of the middle-aged men asked.

Huh? What earwax? Xu Fu was momentarily dazed, "I'm here to report for duty. Is this the Fengchang Temple? I'm here to serve as the Fengchang."

The middle-aged man furrowed his brow fiercely, and the gaze he directed at Xu Fu instantly carried hostility, "This is the Fengchang Temple. Since you're here, then..." The man pointed casually, "Go tidy up that pile of things first."

Xu Fu nodded coldly and aloofly, walked over slowly, and then... rolled up his sleeves to sort out the bamboo slips.

The middle-aged man couldn't help asking the person next to him, "Have you ever seen him before? Could he be the young master of some noble family again?"

The person beside him shook his head repeatedly, "I haven't seen him either. Probably."

The middle-aged man forcefully suppressed the dissatisfaction in his heart, looking at Xu Fu as if he were looking at a detestable, connection-pulling, silver-spooned rich second-generation brat.

Xu Fu's movements looked unhurried, but he was actually quite fast at tidying things up. After he finished, he found a bamboo slip, dragged a cushion over, sat down, and began to read slowly. The bamboo slips recorded annual calendars and past major events, and the more Xu Fu read, the more alarmed he became. He hadn't guessed wrong; he had really arrived at the Qin Dynasty! Oh no, right now it was still just the State of Qin. That precosious young ruler was none other than the King of Qin, Ying Zheng, who had not yet undergone his capping ceremony!

Ying Zheng!

No matter how poor Xu Fu's history was, he still knew about this emperor through the ages in history. He vaguely remembered that this emperor in history was good at knowing and using people, recruited many talents from the six states, and furthermore, the First Emperor of Qin seemed to heavily employ fangshi (alchemists/warlocks) in his later years. He remembered there was a particularly famous fangshi, what was his name again... Oh, he couldn't remember.

Unable to remember, Xu Fu didn't dwell on it further. He closed the bamboo slip, feeling much more cheerful. He felt he was one step closer to his blueprint for his dreams.

A burst of footsteps suddenly drew near. Xu Fu looked up and saw the middle-aged man looking at him with an unhappy expression. The man curled the corner of his mouth and loudly scolded Xu Fu, "You took half a day just to do this trivial task. I really don't know how you got selected."

Do you mean to blame your king for being blind?

Xu Fu complained inwardly, but on the surface he was surprisingly calm, showing no intention of arguing with this middle-aged man.

Throwing a stone down couldn't even stir up a ripple. The middle-aged man suddenly felt he had lost face, so he became even more bossy and dictatorial, "Do you know what you're here to do? You're not here to get a free meal; you're here to work! Go, clean up that pile of stuff."

Xu Fu didn't know that in modern terms, this was called workplace bullying. He was not the type of person to be bullied arbitrarily, and deep in his bones, he still carried a bit of stubbornness. Now hearing this old man's bad tone, he naturally had no good attitude either.

"I came to the Fengchang Temple to be in charge of weather observation, not to do chores for you." Who do you think you are? Xu Fu glanced at the man, his eyes revealing a hint of arrogance.

The man felt slightly guilty; he couldn't guess what kind of background Xu Fu actually had, while his own background could only be considered passable. In the past at the Fengchang Temple, he had frequently been bullied by various young aristocrats. Now, seeing Xu Fu, he instantly felt that a softer target to bully had arrived, and could not wait to pinch the soft persimmon.

Yet this fool didn't think: what if this persimmon had a sharp stone hidden inside, and you bruised your hand on it?

Who knew which nerve of the middle-aged man was misfiring, but he mistook Xu Fu's calmness and indifference for weakness, and he grew even more vicious, "In charge of weather observation? You're worthy? Do you know that the lords in charge of weather and divination in the Fengchang Temple all come from noble families!"

Does this stuff even require a noble family heritage? Xu Fu was speechless.

The middle-aged man grew even more spirited, "Coming to the Fengchang Temple, you have to listen to the few of us. Merely a tiny newcomer, yet you don't understand the rules at all. Naturally, whatever I tell you to do, you must do..."

Xu Fu was truly too lazy to listen to the other party showing off before him.

"What is your job?" Xu Fu interrupted him.

The middle-aged man was stunned, "I am in charge of sacrificial attire."

Xu Fu muttered to himself, what kind of ghost place is this Fengchang Temple anyway, how come it has all sorts of people? What kind of nonsense is being in charge of sacrificial attire?

Unable to figure out his background, Xu Fu just let out an "oh" and stopped talking.

The middle-aged man was stunned for a moment, and his face instantly turned flushed. Clearly, he thought that Xu Fu's question just now was deliberately mocking him. Anger rose from the man's heart, "What are you still standing there for? Go tidy things up! Didn't you see everyone is overwhelmed with work?"

The King of Qin was about to hold his capping ceremony, and the Fengchang Temple, being in charge of imperial mausoleums and temple sacrifices, rituals and music, astronomy, divination, and attire, was naturally spinning around in a flurry, and no one dared to slack off even a fraction. Among them, the shaman-priests whose duties were stargazing and divination were the most leisurely. These odd-job workers were green with envy and filled with resentment, and now they just happened to vent it all on Xu Fu.

Anyway, in their view, Xu Fu was an unfamiliar face, extremely young, and with his tender and delicate, frail appearance, he had suddenly parachuted in to become a shaman-priest. If they didn't bully him, who would they bully?

I'm giving you face, yet you refuse to want it?

Xu Fu's gaze turned cold, and he swept his eyes over the middle-aged man from head to toe.

Being looked at like that made the middle-aged man feel a chill running through his body, and he couldn't help shouting at Xu Fu again, "Brat, what are you looking at?"

"You're sick." Xu Fu suddenly spat out three words.

Due to long-term frustration in his workplace career, the middle-aged man had a quick-tempered and irritable personality. Hearing these three words that insulted his character, how could he possibly endure it? His nostrils flared slightly with anger, "Audacious! You're the one who's sick!"

He really looks like a hippopotamus.

Xu Fu felt a bit of disgust.

Oh no, saying he looked like a hippopotamus was an insult to the hippopotamus.

Xu Fu cleared his throat, his expression indifferent, maintaining quite a bit of the demeanor of an otherworldly master, "Listen to me, you really are sick. Irritable and quick-tempered, your eyes are dense with bloodshot veins, there is dark skin under your eyes, many fine lines between your brows, and your breathing is rough and hurried... Isn't that being sick? Of course, none of this matters. The most important thing is, you have dark clouds shrouding your head, and you're afraid of meeting a great catastrophe..."

"Nonsense!" The middle-aged man was filled with the feeling of being insulted and mocked. He was completely provoked, and with a wave of his sleeve, he actually brutally knocked over the desk in front of Xu Fu, which still held the bamboo slips Xu Fu had just sorted out earlier, "You, where on earth did you come from? How dare you run wild in the Fengchang Temple! When I report this to Liu Fengchang, I will definitely have scum like you driven out of the Fengchang Temple!"

Actually, only the middle-aged man was agitated; everyone else wore an expression of watching a good show. Not only did these people ignore Xu Fu, but they also held this middle-aged man in extreme contempt.

The middle-aged man was just like a clown, eagerly jumping up and down in front of Xu Fu.

Xu Fu lowered his head, picked up the bamboo slips, and remained as steady as a mountain, "If you don't believe it, forget it."

Tch, a paper tiger. If this old man had dared to rush up and beat him up, he would still count as a man of mettle, but he only knew how to stamp his feet, curse angrily, and throw around a few rules. Judging by the looks of the people around him, this man couldn't possibly be any sort of high official either, so where on earth did he get the confidence to act the fool in front of him?

Granting him a character assessment was already a sign of his own kindness.

The middle-aged man couldn't threaten Xu Fu at all, nor could he rally any colleagues to share his hatred. He panicked a bit, but he had no strength to truss a chicken and didn't dare to lay a hand on Xu Fu, so he could only angrily stop, and while walking out, shouted loudly, "I'm going to see Liu Fengchang right now."

Xu Fu sneered inwardly. Does he think he's five years old? If you lose an argument, you go tell the teacher?

Author's note:

Regarding historical research: As stated in the main text, astronomy, mathematics, and arts are all managed by the Fengchang Temple. The Fengchang belongs to the Nine Ministers under the Three Ducal Ministers and Nine Ministers. This official position is very high, but unfortunately, the job Xu Fu went to do was not this official position. Then, the shaman-priests are made up. According to classical records, shaman-priests were responsible for divination and sacrifices. I'm just using it here for the official title because I really couldn't find a specific position. The author just had to invent it behind closed doors.

Finally, most of the fangshi who could enter court as officials in the Qin Dynasty had backgrounds. Someone like Xu Fu who parachuted in—the minor transparents envy him, and those who used connections look down on him. Therefore, this chapter is also titled: #What to do when all my colleagues are my enemies? Is it really okay to flip all of them over? Urgent! Waiting online!#

chapters.title: 第50章
chapters.translated_text:
Liu Fengchang instantly turned into a wooden stake, standing there stiffly, his facial expression frozen and his mouth unable to open.

Xu Fu had long anticipated such a reaction from Liu Fengchang. He, Xiong Yi, and even Zhao Yi, were all fierce in their clamoring to go before the King to seek a judgment of right and wrong, but in reality, they were just posturing. When it actually came to going, it was uncertain if any of them dared to do so.

Opposite him, Xiong Yi frowned imperceptibly.

Liu Fengchang had chickened out far too quickly!

"Why must Grand Diviner Xu speak such angry words?"

Since Liu Fengchang’s combat effectiveness was insufficient, Xiong Yi smiled slightly and interjected. A handsome man, if he treats you with elegance, speaks in a very gentle tone, and is full of protection in his words, his appearance is naturally moving.

But Xu Fu was a man.

No matter how Xiong Yi performed, it was just a show for a blind man.

Xu Fu lowered his eyes and asked indifferently, "What does Liu Fengchang think?" He ignored Xiong Yi entirely, facing Liu Fengchang directly instead, turning the situation around and taking control of it in his own palm.

Liu Fengchang’s words were originally just meant to intimidate Xu Fu; how could he dare to actually go before the King with him? Xiong Yi might be fine, but if he brought trouble upon himself and couldn't extricate himself later, who could he turn to?

The expression on Liu Fengchang’s face became extremely strange. He felt more and more that his position as Fengchang was meaningless, unable to exert even the slightest bit of official authority.

"Liu Fengchang?" Xu Fu urged again.

Weren't you just being aggressive? Weren't you just demanding he plead guilty? Weren't you going to send him to prison for the five punishments? How could your momentum fade so quickly?

Xiong Yi was also somewhat stunned. He had never heard of this person named Xu Fu, so he subconsciously regarded him as someone inexperienced. Even if he had lucked out in the Fengchang Temple and gained the favor of the King of Qin, he might not necessarily have much ability himself. Ever since seeing Xu Fu, Xiong Yi had defined him as someone who was gold on the outside but rotten on the inside. For such a person, wouldn't a fierce confrontation to intimidate him lead to his immediate submission?

Even if Xu Fu could trouble Zhao Yi, Xiong Yi had previously attributed Xu Fu’s confidence to the King of Qin.

Yet, Xu Fu was neither panicked nor quick to yield. He appeared arrogant and cold, seemingly turning a blind eye to everything, which only made Xiong Yi feel more restless. That was true, too—if he yielded easily, it wouldn't be interesting at all.

People in the Fengchang Temple were already unable to resist looking over at them.

Xiong Yi spoke again, "What is the point of standing here like this? Why not follow Liu Fengchang first, and we can slowly clarify this matter..."

Xu Fu always felt that Xiong Yi’s slight smile held no good intentions, especially when Xiong Yi’s gaze swept over him inch by inch, making him feel as if goosebumps were rising all over his body. Under such circumstances, how could Xu Fu agree to them? In any case, they wouldn't get anything good out of this. Did they dare to forcibly take him away here?

They dared not!

"No need. Since Liu Fengchang questions me, then please, at that time, invite the Clothing Bureau and the attendants who delivered the sacrificial robes here, and then determine my guilt." Xu Fu mimicked the exact toughness Zhao Yi had shown earlier. Zhao Yi wanted to escape punishment but couldn't, and while Xu Fu was using his own methods against him, he himself was clean and innocent; no matter who came, they couldn't convict him.

Liu Fengchang choked, "You... you..." He couldn't utter a complete sentence for a long time.

Xu Fu knew the other party was at a loss for words, and Xiong Yi was still observing, not knowing what exactly he wanted to see from him. Xu Fu couldn't be bothered to deal with them anymore, bid them farewell, and left quickly.

The young attendant who had been standing beside Xu Fu stared at Liu Fengchang, smiled slowly, and said, "If Liu Fengchang wants to pass judgment, I’ll come join the fun when the time comes."

Join the fun?

You, an attendant by the King of Qin's side, coming to the Fengchang Temple—can that be called joining the fun? Who knows how many people will directly interpret your attitude as the King of Qin's attitude!

Liu Fengchang gritted his teeth in secret, not expecting Xu Fu to have brought such a complete set of helpers.

But on second thought, it wasn't that he didn't want to help Xiong Yi now; it was that he simply couldn't.

Once Xu Fu left, Liu Fengchang showed a troubled and awkward expression to Xiong Yi, "Xu Fu is arrogant and difficult to tame. He has been like this since he arrived at the Fengchang Temple. I... I have no way to deal with him."

If Xu Fu were still here, he would realize that Liu Fengchang’s tone of "applying eye drops" (slandering) was exactly the same as when Qiu Ji had complained to Liu Fengchang before.

Indeed, petty people in the world have common traits!

"He is just a Grand Diviner, but in the end, isn't he managed by you? You are the Fengchang; if you can't even handle him, what is there to boast about?" Xiong Yi glanced at him coldly, blocking all of Liu Fengchang’s words.

Liu Fengchang became even more awkward. His position was already unstable, and he relied entirely on Xiong Yi...

"Then... Zhao Yi?" Liu Fengchang hesitated.

Xiong Yi had almost forgotten the purpose of his visit. Zhao Yi was a drinking buddy, so there was some friendship, but to say it was deep would be a joke.

Xiong Yi was not a man without a sense of justice. Given how much Zhao Yi had done to please him in the past, now that Zhao Yi was in prison, he had to offer some help. As for what result Zhao Yi would eventually face, that was none of his business.

Xiong Yi looked in the direction Xu Fu had left, sighed softly, not knowing what he was regretting, and then turned to walk away, "Today’s matter is settled. I will handle Zhao Yi’s affair separately. You don't need to intervene; just keep your position secure."

Liu Fengchang couldn't help but ask, "Then when will Young Master Xiong Yi return to the Fengchang Temple?"

"Tomorrow."

Liu Fengchang muttered to himself. He hadn't appeared at the Fengchang Temple for a long time, yet now he was suddenly coming back... Could it be because of Zhao Yi’s affair?

Liu Fengchang couldn't figure it out, only thinking to himself that holding onto Xiong Yi’s thigh was enough.

On the other side, Zhao Yi had already been taken to the prison. He was shoved and left standing stiffly in the dark corridor of the prison.

The endless darkness made fear rise in his heart uncontrollably.

Even Xiong Yi had no way to deal with Xu Fu...

Could it be that he was really going to fall at the hands of Xu Fu today?

When he was taken away, the sound of Xu Fu’s malicious mockery still echoed in his ears. Today... today was the auspicious day he had personally chosen! Zhao Yi felt as if he were vomiting blood from frustration.

"Still not moving?" the jailer glared.

Zhao Yi didn't dare to walk inside. He gritted his teeth hatefully and said indignantly, "It was clearly that Xu Fu who framed me, yet you all are helping the villain! Truly shameful!"

Without Xiong Yi, how could the jailer look at Zhao Yi with any respect?

The jailer looked at Zhao Yi with pity, smiled sarcastically, and asked, "Then tell me, how did Grand Diviner Xu frame you?"

"I did not steal Grand Diviner Xu’s bamboo slips! How could I, Zhao Yi, be such a petty person? Those bamboo slips must have been planted by someone to frame me..."

Such far-fetched words were too much for the jailers to listen to.

"Frame you? How did he frame you? By forcibly stuffing the bamboo slips into your sleeves? Hahahaha... Grand Diviner Zhao actually has the face to say such absurd words..." The jailer laughed loudly, his sarcastic tone like slaps across Zhao Yi’s face. Especially when the surrounding jailers joined in the laughter, Zhao Yi, caught in the middle and feeling isolated and helpless, felt a surge of grief and indignation.

The mocking laughter was endless, and insults followed. Zhao Yi was pushed into the corridor. He pressed his lips tightly together and felt grit in his mouth. Zhao Yi’s face turned dark, remembering the rag that had been stuffed in his mouth earlier, and a wave of nausea surged in his heart. He couldn't help but retch a few times, but nothing came out.

"So useless?" the jailer behind him sneered again, taking pleasure in his pain.

Zhao Yi finally understood why the guard had confessed everything after just one stint in prison.

A sense of fear rose faintly in his heart—a fear of the unknown that instantly enveloped him. His limbs went weak involuntarily, the urge to vomit grew stronger, and his mind was muddled, losing the ability to think. He couldn't understand why those bamboo slips had appeared in his sleeves... Clearly, clearly he remembered putting the bamboo slips back into the study before he left... Could he have remembered wrong?

Zhao Yi panted, his legs gave way, and he fell to the ground.

Just then, rapid footsteps echoed in the corridor.

A man walked over quickly and asked loudly, "Is Grand Diviner Zhao Yi here?"

The jailer replied, "He is here! What is it?"

The man said, "I have come specifically to tell Grand Diviner Zhao Yi that a fire has broken out in his home..."

Zhao Yi raised his head abruptly and took two steps forward, but because his legs were weak, he fell to the ground again. He cried out, "What did you say?"

"A fire has broken out in Grand Diviner Zhao’s home!" the man raised his voice and said again.

"My home... my home..." Zhao Yi’s ears were buzzing, his face deathly pale. After falling to the ground, he had no strength to pull himself up for a long time, looking utterly disheveled!

Seeing this, the jailers looked at each other with contempt.

If you knew it would come to this, why do it in the first place? You can't even take this? If you wait for what comes later, wouldn't life be worse than death?

Seeing Zhao Yi’s devastated appearance, the man stammered, "It’s nothing, it’s nothing... just two rooms were lost..."

Zhao Yi took a heavy breath, his complexion gradually easing. He suddenly realized something and said tremblingly, "Which two rooms were lost?"

"Grand Diviner Zhao’s study and the resting area..." The man only had time to say this much before he was shouted away by the jailer who came up behind him.

Xu Fu’s words echoed in Zhao Yi’s ears once again.

"Grand Diviner Zhao carefully selected today, so Grand Diviner Zhao must enjoy it well."

Enjoy it well...

In these four short words, Zhao Yi had deeply felt the malice.

What a Grand Diviner Xu! This was a blatant mockery! This was gouging his flesh! Zhao Yi dug his fingers into the ground, his mind wandering, and he didn't even feel it when his fingers were dug until they bled. It wasn't until the jailer suddenly grabbed his collar and hoisted him up from the ground that Zhao Yi’s neck was constricted. After standing steady, he panted violently, his thoughts slowly returning, and only then did he feel the piercing pain in his fingers.

Zhao Yi grimaced in pain and was shoved directly into the prison cell.

In his twenty-plus years of life, when had he ever encountered such a situation?

Fear, indignation, and shock wrapped tightly around him, leaving him unable to spare any energy to think about how those bamboo slips had come to be.

...

"Where is Zhao Yi?" Seeing Xu Fu step in, Su Yi couldn't help but walk to his side and ask in a low voice.

"He was taken away." Xu Fu noticed that many eyes around him wanted to size him up but didn't quite dare. This was probably thanks to him knocking Zhao Yi down? Did these people fear him now?

A flash of disgust crossed Su Yi’s face, "Caught red-handed and still trying to argue. Truly disgusting!"

Xu Fu didn't expect Su Yi to have such an upright side. He lowered his eyes to hide his surprise and nodded.

Someone once said that the bonds between men are nothing more than having been classmates, having carried guns together, or having visited brothels together.

Su Yi had participated in the struggle between Xu Fu and Zhao Yi, helped watch Zhao Yi for a while, and now, speaking indignantly about Zhao Yi with Xu Fu, had invisibly deepened their colleague bond. In his previous life, Xu Fu was mostly surrounded by fellow disciples and rarely had close friends, so he couldn't quite understand this, but it didn't hinder him from drawing closer to Su Yi.

After Xu Fu sat down, he suddenly remembered something.

Su Yi was a native of Qin and should know more about this place than him. Su Yi should know about Xiong Yi’s identity...

"Does Yi know what background the Xiong official in the Fengchang Temple has?" Xu Fu asked immediately.

Su Yi hesitated for a moment and said, "Are you talking about Young Master Xiong Yi? Has he returned to the Fengchang Temple?"

"It should be him." Xu Fu didn't know any "Young Master Xiong Yi." He had very little knowledge of Qin history to begin with; knowing Qin Shi Huang, Fu Su, and Hu Hai was already quite impressive. However, he did know that at this time, not everyone was qualified to be called "Young Master."

Su Yi’s expression became complicated, "Young Master Xiong Yi is the eldest son of Lord Changping."

Seeing the confusion still in Xu Fu’s eyes, Su Yi felt a bit of doubt but had to continue explaining, "Does Grand Diviner Xu know who Lord Changping is?"

"Who?" Lord Changping? It sounded familiar. In a flash of lightning, Xu Fu suddenly remembered that Lord Changping was the person who had blocked his and Qin Shi Huang’s carriage last time! That Lord Changping’s servants were very arrogant.

He didn't know who Lord Changping was, but he felt that someone who could be called that shouldn't be an ordinary person.

Sure enough, he heard Su Yi lower his voice and say, "Lord Changping, surname Mi, clan Xiong."

Seeing Xu Fu still looking confused, Su Yi was anxious and had to make it clearer, "The Mi surname is a great noble surname of the Chu State. Lord Changping’s father was once the Crown Prince of Chu, and his mother was once a Princess of Qin."

Before Su Yi could continue, Xu Fu was already stunned.

With a father who was a Crown Prince and a mother who was a Princess, how strong must this background be!

"Then he is the King’s..." Xu Fu hesitated.

Counting it up, this Lord Changping should belong to some relative of Qin Shi Huang, right? No wonder his son could be called a Young Master, and no wonder even the Fengchang didn't dare to offend that Xiong official easily.

"He should be... the King’s uncle," Su Yi said awkwardly, his voice dropping even lower.

Xu Fu sighed slightly in his heart. It seemed he couldn't afford to offend Xiong Yi for the time being. No wonder Zhao Yi was so confident. Zhao Yi had the son of Lord Changping behind him, while he had Qin Shi Huang behind him. Regardless of whose weight was greater, Xu Fu didn't think he could make Ying Zheng give up his peaceful coexistence with Lord Changping to stand up for him.

It didn't matter. Zhao Yi was already in prison, and just letting him suffer was satisfying enough. As for what would happen later, who could have guessed?

Xu Fu thought with a very broad mind.

Su Yi seemed to think this bolt from the blue wasn't heavy enough and emphasized it in Xu Fu’s ear, "Young Master Xiong Yi is the eldest son of Lord Changping, handsome and talented. In his childhood, he was almost assigned to be a playmate for the King. Lord Changping and Empress Dowager Huayang both came from the Chu State. Because of Empress Dowager Huayang, Lord Changping’s talent gradually became apparent in Qin. King Zhuangxiang once entrusted the young King to Lord Changping. After the late King passed away, Empress Dowager Huayang also greatly appreciated Young Master Xiong Yi. Therefore, after Young Master Xiong Yi entered the Fengchang Temple, he was quickly given important responsibilities."

In other words, this pair of father and son were quite powerful in Qin?

Su Yi added, "After Lu Buwei moves to the Shu region, the Chancellor of Qin will likely be replaced by Lord Changping... Naturally, this is just everyone’s speculation. But in any case, Lord Changping and Young Master Xiong Yi are people who cannot be offended."

The more Xu Fu read the three characters "Lord Changping," the more familiar they felt. Xu Fu remembered again that after the rebellion of Lao Ai, among those sent by Qin Shi Huang to attack the Ai State, wasn't Lord Changping one of them? Later, Lu Buwei intervened and also went to suppress the rebellion, but after returning, Lord Changping received rewards, while Lu Buwei received a sword hanging over his head.

"I understand." Xu Fu nodded and then thanked him.

Only Su Yi was willing to tell him these things.

The twists and turns of officialdom and family backgrounds were not things he could get from ancient books. Even if he asked others, he wouldn't get anything, and if he were careless, he would be seen as having ulterior motives toward that Xiong official. If he were reported, that would be trouble. Now, Xu Fu didn't underestimate the ability of people in the Fengchang Temple to cause trouble at all.

Xu Fu had already raised his guard, but seeing him still looking so calm and composed, Su Yi couldn't help but sigh inwardly.

Grand Diviner Xu is broad-minded and naturally wouldn't harbor such dark matters in his heart! That leaves only... only that he must secretly consider more for Grand Diviner Xu... A sense of responsibility suddenly welled up in Su Yi's heart.

Xu Fu did not know that he had once again refreshed the impression others had of him. He calmly finished handling the tasks that had accumulated over this period, and in the blink of an eye, it was sunset. The others had basically all dispersed, but Su Yi had actually stayed and accompanied him until now.

Xu Fu squeezed his arms and stood up, his legs numb.

It was truly too torturous; couldn't they just provide a stool to sit on properly? Having to kneel to sit, his legs would be ruined sooner or later!

Su Yi walked out of the Fengchang Temple with him. The attendant waiting by the carriage for Xu Fu immediately panicked the moment he saw Xu Fu's appearance.

"What happened to Master Xu?" the attendant asked hurriedly. If something went wrong, it would be troublesome upon returning to the palace.

"It's nothing." Xu Fu waved his hand, bade farewell to Su Yi, and boarded the carriage.

The attendant, however, secretly took note of Su Yi's face.

Hmm, this person is highly suspicious! Must report this to the King!

And so, Su Yi was innocently marked by Ying Zheng and became a target of long-standing resentment in Ying Zheng's heart—though that is a story for another time.

When Xu Fu returned to the palace, Ying Zheng had been waiting for him for a long time. Seeing Xu Fu step through the door, Ying Zheng immediately asked, "How did it go? Has that Zhao Yi been imprisoned?"

Xu Fu nodded, finally showing a hint of a smile even toward the First Emperor of Qin, "Many thanks to the King, Zhao Yi has already been sent to prison." He truly needed to thank the First Emperor properly. To ensure he could decisively deal with Zhao Yi once the person behind him appeared, he had made full preparations from the start, including that bamboo slip.

After the First Emperor's men discovered the bamboo slip in Zhao Yi's mansion, they didn't take it immediately so as not to alert him. However, Xu Fu had immediately forged a bamboo slip and easily obtained that piece of black cloth from the First Emperor to tie it up. Later, during the scuffle with the jailers, he had Dong You slip it into Zhao Yi's sleeve. Zhao Yi had been cornered by Xu Fu at his doorstep at the time; how could he have the presence of mind to notice such details? By the time he was caught red-handed in a daze, even if he knew it was impossible for a bamboo slip to appear there, he couldn't provide a strong rebuttal.

After all, he was indeed the one who stole the bamboo slip!

Was he supposed to tell the jailers that the bamboo slip was still in his own study and couldn't possibly be here?

In his panic, Zhao Yi was caught completely unprepared and fell straight into the trap Xu Fu had dug.

Once Xiong Yi appeared, it didn't matter how much he talked; Zhao Yi had been caught red-handed. Theft was a very serious crime in the State of Qin. Even if Xiong Yi wanted to save Zhao Yi, he had to weigh how much trouble it would cause to go against Qin law.

As soon as Zhao Yi entered the prison, the study was set on fire to burn the original bamboo slip, making the one in the jailer's hand the "stolen" original.

Zhao Yi knew the appearance of the bamboo slip was a frame-up, but so what? Xu Fu wanted him to swallow this unjust loss, and the more unwilling he was, the better. Only by making Zhao Yi feel resentful could he make him regret his actions even more. The taste of lingering remorse must be unbearable, and that was the best revenge.

Perhaps in a few days, Zhao Yi would figure out the connections. He would realize that from the very beginning, a King of Qin stood behind Xu Fu. To go against Xu Fu and try to frame him was a foolish idea!

But by then, it would be too late.

Xu Fu's mood improved significantly. Did Zhao Yi really think he was easy to bully? He wondered if Zhao Yi was enjoying this "auspicious gift" thoroughly.

Ying Zheng looked up and saw the faint smile on Xu Fu's face and the pride in his eyes, and he couldn't help but feel a sudden sense of relief himself. "That is good." He didn't know who Zhao Yi was, but regardless of who it was, anyone who dared to steal would have to pay a heavy price.

"The guards, Zhao Yi, and those who conspired with him, along with the person who hid the bamboo slip for him—let them be punished with the nose-cutting penalty," Ying Zheng said indifferently.

The nose-cutting penalty?

Cutting off the criminal's nose?

Xu Fu felt a bit of pain just hearing about it. The severity of Qin law was truly not a joke! Xu Fu didn't feel too much sympathy; if he, an outsider, didn't understand Qin law, that would be one thing, but didn't Zhao Yi know? Didn't he know how serious the consequences of theft were? He knew, but he was just harboring a fluke mentality, or perhaps his resentment and jealousy had taken the upper hand.

Jealousy is a truly terrifying thing; it can make people lose their reason and disregard life and death.

The attendant acknowledged the order and withdrew, seemingly to convey the King's decree.

Xu Fu observed a moment of silence for Zhao Yi in the prison.

Afterwards, he remembered something and asked, "How is Young Master Huhai?"

Ying Zheng said with a strange expression, "...He should be better, I suppose."

Hearing Ying Zheng's tone, Xu Fu instantly knew that Ying Zheng must have been busy all day and hadn't paid any attention to the young Huhai. What an irresponsible father... Xu Fu glanced at Ying Zheng indifferently. He had never had parents and didn't know what parents should be like toward their children, but as the First Emperor's youngest son, did he really ignore him so much? It seemed he didn't care much for Fusu either.

Was the First Emperor such a deadbeat dad that it led to Fusu having a completely different personality and constantly angering him, while Huhai grew up to be a spoiled brat who ended up ruining the entire Qin Dynasty in one go?

Xu Fu thought to himself, since he had arrived in this era and knew the fate of the Qin Dynasty, why not help the First Emperor? At the very least, help him not be a deadbeat dad?

Thinking about the image of the First Emperor raising his children properly, Xu Fu found it quite interesting.

"Your Majesty, may I go to visit Young Master Huhai?" Xu Fu asked Ying Zheng very politely.

Ying Zheng also stood up quite actively and said, "I shall go with you."

Xu Fu nodded, and the two tidied up before taking the palace servants to the side hall.

The imperial physicians had not slept for a long time. They had been kneeling by the bed, and seeing Ying Zheng enter, they immediately stiffened and paid their respects. They had difficulty even getting up, their limbs stiffened severely.

Although Huhai was not favored by Ying Zheng, the physicians dared not be negligent; if Huhai lost his life, they would be in trouble.

Xu Fu stepped forward a few paces and finally saw Huhai's appearance.

Huhai was wrapped in a small blanket, his cheeks flushed, eyes tightly closed, with long eyelashes; his delicate features made him look more like a doll. With his rosy, cute cheeks, he didn't look as terrifying as he had the night before. He should have made it through, right?

Ying Zheng was already asking the physician, "How is Huhai?"

The physician replied, "Young Master Huhai is out of danger. With careful care, he should be stable in a day or two."

Ying Zheng nodded and suddenly said, "Take a look at Master Xu as well."

Both the physician and Xu Fu were stunned at the same time.

The physician hadn't expected that after caring for his own son, the King would immediately turn his concern to a minor Grand Diviner. As for Xu Fu, it took him a long while to remember his own embarrassing illness.

Xu Fu remained calm and extended his hand to the physician, "Go ahead." Although he felt embarrassed, thinking about it, he hadn't had that dream recently, and with the tonic the First Emperor had ordered for him, how could he still be deficient in blood and vital energy?

The physician knelt on the ground, moved his knees with difficulty, came before Xu Fu, and grabbed Xu Fu's wrist.

Ying Zheng's gaze didn't scan toward Huhai on the bed at all; instead, his eyes fell involuntarily on that section of Xu Fu's wrist.

Perhaps just as Xu Fu found Huhai cute, he looked much the same in Ying Zheng's eyes at this moment.

Once Ying Zheng's gaze landed there, he couldn't move it away.

So white and tender, held in the physician's hand... Ying Zheng suppressed the displeasure in his heart, inexplicably wanting to take a bite. Ying Zheng moved his lips, his teeth grinding together involuntarily. Have I eaten too little meat during the Wax Festival?

The physician quickly let go of Xu Fu's wrist and said, "Grand Diviner Xu is also fine; just supplement his blood and vital energy a bit more."

Ying Zheng's tense expression finally relaxed slightly.

The physician felt a bit strange and couldn't help but mutter to himself, did he see wrong? After reporting Grand Diviner Xu's condition, the King seemed even more pleased than when he saw Young Master Huhai pass this hurdle? It must have been his eyes playing tricks on him.

"Father." Fusu's voice sounded at the hall entrance, carrying a hint of timidity, perhaps because Huhai's appearance over the past two days had frightened him.

Ying Zheng's expression remained extremely cold, showing no sign of gentleness upon seeing his eldest son.

"Come in," Ying Zheng said.

Only then did Fusu dare to walk in. He paid his respects to Xu Fu and held out the bamboo slips he had been clutching to his chest toward Xu Fu. "Master Xu, Fusu has finished reading them."

So fast!?

Truly worthy of being the son of Qin Shi Huang!

Xu Fu grabbed the bamboo slips and flipped through them. Even he didn't have the patience to finish reading some of them; had Fusu really read them all?

"You've read them all?"

Fusu nodded, neither arrogant nor impatient, and asked, "What should Fusu do next?"

Xu Fu racked his brains, trying to think of some bamboo slips that might stump him, but heard Ying Zheng beside him say indifferently, "I have some scrolls there; I will have an attendant bring them to you."

Fusu's eyes brightened, and he looked at Ying Zheng with a face full of filial affection. "Thank you, Father."

Seeing Fusu's pitiful appearance, Xu Fu felt a faint sense of guilt. Why did he feel like he had really snatched the father of two bratty kids?

"An attendant will deliver them to your palace; you need not come here anymore, lest Huhai pass his illness to you."

Fusu nodded cautiously, always feeling a trace of coldness in his father's eyes. Why would his father treat Huhai like this? Fusu couldn't understand it, but when his gaze swept to Xu Fu at the side, a warm, soft smile immediately appeared on his face again. "Master Xu, Fusu will take his leave now."

"Hmm, go ahead." Xu Fu didn't know how to get along with children, but fortunately, Fusu was very self-aware, and with Qin Shi Huang there to handle the trouble, Xu Fu suddenly felt that being a teacher wasn't as terrifying as he had imagined.

Fusu left, looking back every few steps.

At this moment, Huhai also woke up from the couch. He slowly opened his eyes, blinked twice, and soon saw Xu Fu by the bedside. Huhai immediately broke free from the constraints of his little quilt, stretched out his bare arms, and reached out to Xu Fu for a hug.

The imperial physician hurriedly picked up Huhai, wanting to wrap him in his quilt, but was kicked in the cheek by Huhai.

The physician's movements stiffened.

Huhai then began to wail.

Ying Zheng frowned, feeling his fingers itch; he wanted to pinch the little guy to death.

Huhai had suffered quite a bit in the past few days. Xu Fu thought about it and signaled for the physician to hand Huhai over to him. As soon as Huhai was in his arms, he stopped crying.

The physician felt a bit aggrieved.

Could it be that even a toddler's preference for someone depends on their face?

Once in Xu Fu's arms, Huhai grabbed the fabric on his chest tightly, blowing bubbles with his mouth. *Pop*, it burst, and drool smeared his own face. Where could one still see the half-dead, pitiful appearance from last night?

Xu Fu didn't know how to coax children, at most he would hold him and pat his bottom, and since Huhai happened not to cry, it saved him a lot of trouble.

After a while, a palace maid brought in Huhai's food, all of which was mushy stuff. Xu Fu felt disgusted just looking at it. Thinking that Huhai had to eat this kind of thing, Xu Fu suddenly felt that Huhai was quite pitiful... and he held him for a little longer.

Huhai leaned in his arms, being fed the mush by the palace maid, spitting out half of every bite.

Xu Fu's expression turned cold.

This was the only thing about children that was disgusting. That was why he had vowed in his past life to remain a virgin forever; it would be best to avoid finding a woman to have children with. His only ambition was to carry forward his own skills.

Perhaps Huhai sensed the coldness coming from him, for he licked his lips and stopped acting up.

At this time, Xu Fu noticed that the gaze Ying Zheng cast upon him was exceptionally intense, and he smiled inwardly. It was actually quite easy to stop Qin Shi Huang from being such a jerk...

"Does Your Majesty wish to hold Young Master Huhai?" Xu Fu very generously handed Huhai over.

Ying Zheng: "..." Who wants to hold Huhai?

Ying Zheng met Xu Fu's eyes and suddenly couldn't say anything. Since he had chosen to keep this "green cloud" (a metaphor for a burden/nuisance) back then, he had to endure it even if he wasn't happy. Ying Zheng took Huhai. He suddenly remembered the last time he held Huhai with the wrong posture, and Xu Fu had corrected him personally.

Ying Zheng's hand slipped, and he was about to drop Huhai.

Xu Fu didn't notice at all, and by the time he reached out, it was too late. However, the physician nearby acted very selflessly, throwing himself onto the floor to serve as a human cushion for Young Master Huhai.

Seeing a clumsy physician ruin his perfectly good plan, Ying Zheng's expression turned sour. He directly scooped Huhai back into his arms with a swift motion, as if performing acrobatics.

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief.

The physician also breathed a sigh of relief. Don't let Young Master Huhai's young age fool you, he wasn't light. If he had really crashed down, the physician might have had to say goodbye to his straight waist.

When Lady Hu was pregnant with Huhai, she had never stinted on her unborn son. She was naive, thinking that since Ying Zheng doted on her, he would also dote on Huhai. Later, during labor, because Huhai was too large, Lady Hu was tortured quite a bit; this could be considered bringing it upon herself.

That is a story for another time.

Ying Zheng was unhappy at this moment, so he threw Huhai back to the physician. Huhai stretched out his arms, swaying, and started blowing bubbles again, accurately spitting them onto Ying Zheng's chest.

Ying Zheng's face darkened; he felt his fingers itching even more.

Xu Fu was quick-witted; he grabbed a cloth from a palace servant and wiped Ying Zheng's chest.

With the warm, soft palm pressed against his chest, Ying Zheng could still feel the heat from Xu Fu's palm. The anger that had just been stirred up in Ying Zheng leaked away as quickly as a punctured ball...

Little did he know he had escaped a disaster; Huhai, held in the physician's arms, struggled unhappily and *pfft, pfft, pfft*, sprayed the physician's face with drool again.

The physician wiped his face with a bitter expression and continued to assist the palace maid in feeding Huhai.

Ying Zheng had no desire to continue watching this unlucky child. Xu Fu felt it was about enough after watching for a while. At worst, when Huhai grew a bit older, he would whisper in his ear every day about how much his father, his brother, and his whole family loved him, letting Huhai soak in a fake honey pot of happiness to prevent him from going astray.

The two stepped out of the side hall and walked a few paces.

A flash of inspiration suddenly struck Xu Fu's mind. "So that's how it is!" he said aloud unconsciously.

"How what is?" Ying Zheng asked immediately.

Xu Fu, however, closed his mouth and said nothing.
