By the time the entire city of Dujiangyan had recovered, Xu Fu had also fully recuperated. Only then did he have the chance to wander around the city under the clear sky, truly experiencing the charm of Dujiangyan as it was a thousand years ago.

Xu Fu emerged from his room, but he could not find Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou anywhere.

Although he could go out for a stroll alone, if he were to run into someone asking for fortune-telling on the street and get surrounded, he wouldn't be able to escape.

Xu Fu wandered around the inn and happened to see an attendant from Ying Zheng’s side. Xu Fu quickly called out to him, "Have you seen Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou?"

The attendant pointed to another door, "They are inside."

Xu Fu strode over and pushed the door open. With a "clatter," a cup rolled right to his feet. What was going on? Xu Fu looked up in confusion, only to see Ying Zheng standing in the room, with Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou prostrate on the ground, not daring to lift their heads. Another attendant gave Xu Fu an awkward smile and hurried over to pick up the cup.

Was this... a reprimand?

"Your Majesty, have Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou committed some error?" Since he had already stumbled upon this, Xu Fu could not turn around and pretend he hadn't seen anything. Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou had been guarding him for some time, and there was some sentiment there after all.

Ying Zheng pressed his lips tightly together, his face showing signs of anger, but upon hearing Xu Fu’s question, he relaxed his lips slightly, intending to answer him.

Before Ying Zheng could speak, Sang Zhong had already said in a low voice, "Master Xu, it is Bo Zhou and my fault for failing to protect you properly, which caused you so much suffering and nearly led to you being harmed by Liu Er."

Having been interrupted by Sang Zhong, Ying Zheng became even more displeased and cast a cold glance at him.

Sang Zhong, who had been quick to admit his fault, felt somewhat aggrieved by that look, thinking to himself that His Majesty must be extremely furious about this matter, and now even admitting his mistake was not enough to earn His Majesty's forgiveness.

"Liu Er?" Xu Fu suddenly remembered Liu Er, who had been taken to the county office. "Where is that Liu Er now?"

Bo Zhou lifted his head and said, "I heard from the county magistrate that when the flood came, Liu Er couldn't escape and was drowned."

At the mention of Liu Er, Xu Fu still felt disgusted. He frowned, making no effort to hide his loathing, "Drowning was too good for him."

Ying Zheng had never seen Xu Fu express his likes and dislikes so clearly, so he couldn't help but ask, "After you were separated from Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou, did Liu Er do anything?" When Ying Zheng asked this, he was thinking the same thing—that Liu Er had gotten off too easily. If this had been in Xianyang, he would have definitely subjected him to the five punishments before executing him!

Xu Fu did not want the name "Liu Er" to ruin his mood, so he quickly returned to his usual calm expression and said indifferently, "When I woke up, Liu Er had moved me under a tree. Perhaps he wanted to do something to me then, but I woke up too quickly, and he didn't find an opportunity. Later, I found a cave with him to hide from the rain. I was running a high fever and felt dizzy, so I leaned against the fire to rest. When he saw me close my eyes, he came at me with a knife. I woke up in shock and managed to subdue him. After I grabbed the knife, I threatened him into carrying me down the mountain toward Dujiangyan."

Xu Fu omitted the part where Liu Er had actually been lusting after him.

Talking about such things would, in any case, damage his masculine pride.

Xu Fu did not know that if he had mentioned it, Liu Er would certainly not have been left with a whole corpse.

The way Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou looked at him suddenly became filled with awe.

Master Xu usually looked so frail and powerless, yet he was able to snatch a knife from someone like Liu Er and threaten him—he was truly impressive!

Ying Zheng had not thought of it that way at all.

From those few words, he could already picture the dangerous situation in his mind. He had originally thought that suffering from a high fever, deliriously muttering in his sleep, and still forcing himself to comfort the city's people was already a great hardship for Xu Fu. Who would have thought there were such twists and turns in between? If there had been the slightest carelessness, he would not have been able to see Xu Fu when he arrived in Shu.

The more Ying Zheng thought about it, the gloomier his face became.

Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou both had the feeling that their lives were about to be forfeit.

"Do you know why that Liu Er attacked you?" Ying Zheng asked, his voice dark and inexplicably filled with a murderous aura.

Xu Fu let out an "um," "I suppose I'd have to ask the corpse to find out."

Xu Fu was just saying it casually, but Ying Zheng said quite seriously, "Even if he has become a corpse, there are ways to make him speak."

Xu Fu felt a bit horrified. How could a corpse speak? Was there some kind of witchcraft to resurrect him?

Ying Zheng did not dwell on this topic. Since it was a painful experience, why repeat it? He would naturally investigate it later.

"Well, have those two finished their punishment? I want to go out for a walk, and I need to take them with me," Xu Fu said.

Upon hearing this, Ying Zheng strode over to Xu Fu’s side, "In that case, I will accompany you."

"And them..."

"Bring them along too."

Ying Zheng naturally had to bring attendants when going out, so Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou escaped a disaster and hurriedly followed behind Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, keeping a low profile.

Xu Fu was still worried when he went out: if the commoners asked him for fortune-telling, what should he do? He didn't have the energy for fortune-telling right now, let alone the peace of mind. To his surprise, after walking down a street, the people only quietly observed him and Ying Zheng, with no intention of coming forward.

Xu Fu was a bit puzzled and turned to look at Ying Zheng’s face.

Could it be that the First Emperor's aura of authority was too intimidating? Or was his facial expression too fierce?

But the First Emperor's face didn't look scary.

Xu Fu remained very confused.

People were already setting up stalls on the street, and the shops on both sides had opened their doors wide.

The aroma of food lingered in the air.

Before he knew it, Xu Fu had wandered outside that medical clinic. He paused and said to Ying Zheng, "When I arrived at the city gate and fainted, I was sent to this clinic." Xu Fu froze for a moment and suddenly said, "I haven't paid them yet!"

Ying Zheng immediately waved for an attendant, "Go inside, thank the people in the clinic, and pay them."

The attendant nodded and was about to step inside.

Xu Fu, however, felt that passing by without entering was quite impolite. Since they had saved his life, he should show gratitude. Only by thanking them in person could he be considered truly courteous.

"Why don't we go in together?" As he said this, Xu Fu walked past the attendant.

The attendant looked at Ying Zheng, stunned, not knowing what to do.

Ying Zheng did not hesitate and stepped inside as well.

Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou exchanged glances.

This is bad!

Upon entering the clinic, they could hear a woman’s hearty laughter.

Before Xu Fu and Ying Zheng could get close, they happened to hear someone ask, "Miss Feng, you didn't accept that young man from the Liu family—is it because you've taken a fancy to Master Xu, who just arrived in the city?"

Master Xu, who just arrived in the city?

Who else could it be?

Ying Zheng’s expression changed instantly, reeking of jealousy.

As if that weren't enough, Miss Feng replied with a smile, "That's right, I just happen to prefer the likes of Master Xu."

Others laughed, "But Master Xu is an official, isn't he? He'll be returning to Xianyang later. What will you do then, Miss Feng?"

"Then I'll just follow him..." Miss Feng laughed, not caring at all. "Of course, that's assuming he likes me back..."

Ying Zheng scoffed in his heart.

He would never like you.

Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou sensed the cold air radiating from Ying Zheng and broke into a cold sweat simultaneously.

A shop assistant finally noticed their arrival and exclaimed, "Master Xu?!" The assistant only recognized Xu Fu and did not recognize Ying Zheng beside him. Who would have thought that the person walking next to Xu Fu was the King of Qin himself?

The conversation inside came to an abrupt halt.

The door curtain was lifted, and Miss Feng walked out. Originally, upon hearing the assistant's shout, she had a beaming smile on her face, but when she came out and saw Ying Zheng following Xu Fu, the smile on her face vanished completely.

"Is Master Xu’s illness better?" Miss Feng asked with concern first.

And in Ying Zheng’s eyes, this act was clearly transformed into something with ulterior motives! A hidden agenda!

"I have fully recovered, and I have come to thank you, Miss Feng." As he spoke, Xu Fu turned to call the attendant, who was holding Qin coins. Xu Fu said, "This is the consultation fee."

Miss Feng’s expression changed slightly again; she felt that Xu Fu was keeping her at a distance. But from another perspective, she felt that Xu Fu was truly appropriate in his conduct, polite, and generous... a whole basket of good qualities.

"Then I will accept it. Master Xu, you just arrived in the city; was it because time was tight that you couldn't walk around? Why don't I show you around the city now?" Miss Feng took the Qin coins and weighed the cloth bag; it was quite heavy.

Xu Fu had heard the conversation between Miss Feng and the others clearly just moments ago. If he didn't avoid suspicion now, he would either be a fool or someone wanting to take advantage of the young woman. Xu Fu was neither, so he declined and used Ying Zheng as an excuse, "My friend and I will stroll for a while; there is no need to trouble you, Miss Feng."

Miss Feng felt as if she had swallowed a mouthful of blood, and her gaze toward Ying Zheng became complicated.

Ying Zheng even pretended to be cold and aloof as he glanced at Miss Feng.

Miss Feng gritted her teeth in secret: What grudge do I have with you? Why do you sabotage me every time?

Xu Fu had expressed his thanks and paid the money, even though the one paying was Ying Zheng. In any case, the favor had been returned. His goal achieved, it was not appropriate to stay any longer.

"Miss Feng, I have other matters to attend to today and shouldn't disturb you further. I shall take my leave." With that, Xu Fu walked out with Ying Zheng. Ying Zheng felt much lighter in his heart and couldn't be bothered to make things difficult for the young girl, so he left with Xu Fu without saying a word.

Miss Feng sighed, "Why doesn't my beauty trap work anymore?"

The patient behind her burst into laughter, "Miss Feng, you have to put on makeup, flick your hair, adjust your dress, and show off your graceful figure—that's what you call a beauty trap..."

Miss Feng was unconvinced, "Could the person next to Master Xu be a woman disguised as a man? He only looks at him and doesn't look at me." After saying that, she couldn't help but mutter to herself, "I've never seen such a tall and sturdy woman either..."

·

There wasn't much food on the street suitable for Xu Fu to eat. Having just recovered from illness, he couldn't consume greasy or coarse food. So he could only glance at them, and to maintain his image, he had to quickly turn his head away and continue looking cold and composed.

Ying Zheng had no interest in food, so naturally, he wouldn't buy any. Thus, the two walked past in a hurry, failing to experience any of the local customs.

By the time they had finished walking down the street, they happened to run into Li Bing, who was inspecting the area.

Seeing the two, Li Bing was startled. He bowed slightly, which counted as a greeting to Ying Zheng, and then asked, "Is Master Xu’s illness better?"

Li Bing was only hindered by being in public and not daring to call Ying Zheng "Your Majesty," and not knowing what else to say, he asked about Xu Fu’s condition. But this similar line, echoing in Ying Zheng’s mind, made him feel slightly unhappy again.

How many people had Xu Fu met on this trip?

Why was everyone so concerned about him?

Asking if he was better the moment they met? Who was on such good terms with you?

Li Bing did not know he had inadvertently stepped on Ying Zheng’s landmine and continued to chat with Xu Fu with great enthusiasm.

Xu Fu also learned from Li Bing why the commoners on the street no longer asked him for fortune-telling.

Previously, Xu Fu only had the image of a divine fortune-teller, so naturally, many people wanted to ask him for a reading. But now, he had been transformed into the image of a "god," and everyone was in awe of him—how could they dare to trouble him further? Thus, Xu Fu became someone in the eyes of the people who could only be viewed from a distance.

Actually, Li Bing was always like this, gentle with everyone, but now in Ying Zheng’s eyes, he had become a thorn that was unpleasant no matter how he looked at it.

Li Bing was pondering whether to invite the King of Qin to his home for a small banquet, and he opened his mouth.

"The county magistrate is busy with official duties, so there is no need to stay. Xu Fu and I have other matters to attend to..." So you can leave.

Ying Zheng said this nonchalantly, and Xu Fu felt it sounded somewhat familiar.

Bo Zhou, behind them, sighed in his heart: Isn't this exactly what Master Xu said to that Miss Feng just now?

...

Li Bing froze, and it took a long while for him to realize that the King’s words meant he didn't want to see him. Li Bing was filled with fear, not knowing where he had offended the King, but since the King had already spoken, he couldn't make him more dissatisfied. He led his attendants and hurriedly said his goodbyes.

Ying Zheng was satisfied, secretly planning in his heart that he might as well take Xu Fu and leave here early tomorrow morning for the administrative center in Chengdu.

There were no Miss Fengs in Chengdu, nor was there an old Li Bing who loved to smile gently at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu felt that going out for a walk with the First Emperor was quite boring, so he cooperated with Ying Zheng and returned to the inn. After the two had eaten, there was nothing to pass the time, so Xu Fu took out the tripod and played with it in his hands.

Someone in the inn saw this and asked with a smile, "Master Xu, are you going to use this tripod to refine alchemy?"

Knowing that the people in the city already regarded him as a divine being, Xu Fu bragged without even blinking, "Yes, alchemy. Refining immortal pills, the kind that makes people live forever."

The man smiled and walked away.

Ying Zheng, who was on the side, actually believed it.

He secretly noted this hobby of Xu Fu’s. Even if Xu Fu couldn't refine immortal pills, he would order people to prepare all the materials and reference ancient texts for him.

Ying Zheng couldn't figure out what Xu Fu wanted the tripod for, but now that he heard Xu Fu say this, he felt that only such a reason could make Xu Fu willing to risk coming to Shu.

Xu Fu played with it for a long time without any results. He suppressed the urge to yawn, put down the small tripod, and stood up, saying, "I'm a bit tired."

"Go back and rest." Ying Zheng stood up as well. As the two went upstairs, Ying Zheng asked, "Is there anything else to do here?"

Xu Fu shook his head, "Nothing left."

Ying Zheng said no more. He personally escorted Xu Fu back to his room before returning to his own.

When Xu Fu woke up the next day, he was still a bit dazed.

He blinked, seeing not the top of a bed, but the roof of a carriage.

Xu Fu sat up, clutching his quilt, and saw Ying Zheng sitting not far away, who turned his head and smiled slightly, "Awake?"

Even the impact of the First Emperor smiling was not as great as the shock of waking up to find he had changed locations.

"We left the city?" Xu Fu asked.

Ying Zheng nodded, "I cannot stay long in Shu. After handling the affairs here, I must return to Xianyang early. There are no skilled imperial physicians in Shu, and how could some small clinics diagnose your condition? I cannot rest easy; it is better to return to Xianyang early and have the imperial physicians take a look at you."

Xu Fu had no objections.

His goal had been achieved, and there was no reason he had to stay.

Only...

"I haven't washed up yet." Xu Fu frowned. Waking up without washing his face or brushing his teeth—that feeling... was too terrible.

Ying Zheng, however, had been prepared. He pulled two buckets from the side of the carriage; one held water for washing his face, and the other was for dirty water, which would be taken away later and poured under a tree by the road.

Xu Fu sighed, thinking that following the First Emperor naturally came with different treatment, and then he began to wash up.

Having resolved this small matter, he had no complaints about rushing back to Chengdu.

This group of people had come in a hurry and left in a hurry. Only, when they arrived, they were under the rain, and when they left, the sun was shining brightly. The air in Shu was fresh, as if the previous disaster had never happened.

·

It was already too late when Miss Feng learned that Xu Fu had left the inn.

Someone couldn't help but advise her, "That Master Xu is clearly not an ordinary person; we can't reach that high... relax, relax, just don't think about it..."

Miss Feng held back her frustration and said in a low voice, "I just feel stifled..."

Ever since that strange man arrived, she had found it hard to get within a foot of Master Xu.

She hadn't even had a chance to pursue him.

Sighing melancholically, Miss Feng continued to grind the medicine in her hand, thinking that it must not have been meant to be...

·

Gone was the arduousness of their previous journey; on the way to Chengdu, they no longer needed to abandon their carriages or horses. Xu Fu sat comfortably and steadily inside the carriage, sleeping soundly every day. Once he woke, food was delivered right to him. Aside from the carriage bed being a bit hard and the inability to bathe properly, he was already living a life of ease.

This day, Xu Fu was startled.

The treatment he enjoyed inside the carriage made him seem more like the King of Qin than Ying Zheng.

He hadn't noticed before, but now that he paid attention, he realized he had been acting like a tyrant in the carriage, pushing Qin Shi Huang to the side.

Xu Fu coughed lightly.

It was fortunate that no one around Qin Shi Huang wanted to eliminate this bold, disrespectful little man.

"Has Your Majesty been resting well lately?" Out of guilt, Xu Fu took the initiative to show concern for Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng had indeed not been resting well these past few days. The carriage was only so wide, and thinking that Xu Fu had suffered a great deal and had just recovered from illness, he had left a considerable amount of space for him. Xu Fu slept comfortably, but the long-legged and tall Ying Zheng had to curl up, which was quite uncomfortable. Thinking about it, ever since he shed his status as a hostage in Zhao and returned to Qin, he hadn't suffered such hardship.

But no matter how uncomfortable he was, how could Ying Zheng ever voice it?

When would the King of Qin ever have a moment of weakness?

Ying Zheng wore an indifferent expression and said, "Very well."

Xu Fu stared at the expression on his face for a while, then finally lifted the quilt, revealing the space beside him. "Xu Fu has monopolized Your Majesty's carriage, and I am filled with guilt. I invite Your Majesty to sleep with me."

I invite Your Majesty to sleep with me...

Sleep together...

Even though the two of them slept together every night in the Xianyang Palace, hearing it from Xu Fu's lips today still made Ying Zheng's heart flutter.

It was a different feeling.

Ying Zheng said naturally, "Then let it be so."

The two shared the quilt, and night soon fell. The carriage stopped on the side of the road, and the attendants lit a fire and gathered around. The night was like water, and Ying Zheng, who hadn't shared a bed with Xu Fu for a long time, had countless thoughts flashing through his mind.

But none of these thoughts were ultimately carried out.

Ying Zheng fell asleep.

The exhaustion of the past few days was something even an iron-willed person couldn't withstand. Now, sleeping beside Xu Fu, he relaxed suddenly and inevitably fell into a deep slumber.

At this moment, it was Xu Fu who was exceptionally clear-headed.

Xu Fu turned his head to glance at Ying Zheng's face, and just this one look made it hard for him to look away. People are always drawn to look a few extra times at beautiful things. Ying Zheng's appearance might not be considered popular among men and women in this era, but according to the aesthetic standards Xu Fu brought from his past life, Ying Zheng was extremely handsome.

He still remembered the shock he felt when he first saw Ying Zheng and observed his features.

Such a face, condensing heroic beauty and a superior destiny, was truly a face that made physiognomists love and hate it at the same time!

They loved it because such a destiny was hard to find; this appearance could almost serve as a textbook example in the art of physiognomy.

They hated it because, damn it, such a good destiny and such a good appearance were truly enviable and jealous-inducing...

Xu Fu stared for too long, and Ying Zheng seemed to sense it, twitching the corners of his mouth in his sleep.

Xu Fu moved his gaze away, not feeling that there was anything strange about staring at another man for so long.

The night was quiet. Xu Fu kept his eyes open and watched the carriage roof for a while, feeling bored, and eventually fell asleep without realizing it.

The next day, when the two woke up, the carriage was about to enter the city.

They washed up in the carriage and straightened their attire.

Soon, the carriage stopped outside the Chengdu government office.

Someone saw the carriage daring to stop there and came up to drive them away, but was driven off even more fiercely by Ying Zheng's attendants. How could these small soldiers compare to the attendants brought from Xianyang Palace? Just in terms of aura, they were worlds apart.

Xu Fu lifted the curtain and stepped out of the carriage.

The people at the office saw him, paused, and hurriedly asked, "Are you Grand Diviner Xu?"

Xu Fu nodded and stepped aside, then Ying Zheng stepped out of the carriage, treading where Xu Fu had stepped before.

Seeing a more noble and imposing man step out of the carriage, these people were stunned, secretly guessing his identity while calling for someone to go inside and report.

Xu Fu asked the man first, "The flood—was Chengdu affected?"

The man nodded hurriedly, "Chengdu was flooded, but we were prepared early on, so there was no major loss."

As for the destruction of the commoners' farmland, in the eyes of these people, it didn't count as a major loss. If the Governor lost something, or they lost something, that would be a major loss.

As long as there were no casualties, it was fine. Xu Fu stopped talking after asking and made a gesture of invitation. "Let's go in first."

Seeing Xu Fu being so respectful to the tall man, the man felt even more awe and didn't dare to block them, only watching them walk inside. Halfway there, Xu Fu suddenly turned his head and pointed to the small carriage following behind, asking, "What is loaded in there?"

Ying Zheng smiled, but the smile was inexplicably cold. "Liu Er."

Qin Shi Huang had brought the corpse along?

Xu Fu felt a chill in his heart.

For all these days, Liu Er had been in the carriage behind? Thinking about it, it was still quite terrifying.

Qin Shi Huang brought Liu Er to the Chengdu government office—he wouldn't be planning to make this corpse actually "speak," would he?

The more he thought about it, the more disgusted he felt, and Xu Fu quickened his pace.

At this moment, Chen Hui had already come out with Xiong Yi.

"Is Grand Diviner Xu well?" Before they were even close, they could hear Chen Hui asking loudly.

"I am naturally well," Xu Fu said casually, while his gaze shifted behind Chen Hui.

After resting for this period, Xiong Yi had finally recovered his appearance as a handsome man; even this flood hadn't destroyed his charm in the slightest.

Seeing Xu Fu, Xiong Yi was about to speak, but his gaze suddenly fell upon Ying Zheng beside him. Xiong Yi's face changed drastically, his lips trembled, and fear rose involuntarily in his heart. "Your... Your Majesty?"

Chen Hui had been the Governor in Shu for several years, far from Xianyang. And Ying Zheng had changed a lot, so he didn't recognize him at first. Now, hearing Xiong Yi speak, he looked again—it really was the King of Qin! Chen Hui immediately knelt down, shouting "Your Majesty."

Everyone in the office was stunned, and before long, the courtyard was filled with kneeling people.

Many of these people would never have the chance to see the King in their entire lives, so seeing him now, they were naturally excited and terrified.

"Bring him up." Ying Zheng didn't even look at them, instead turning to instruct the attendant behind him.

"Yes." The attendant waved to the door, and two burly young men were seen dragging someone in. Yes, dragging.

Xiong Yi caught a glimpse of the limp person being dragged and couldn't help but frown, but because Ying Zheng was there, he didn't dare show an expression of disgust.

The two men let go, and the limp person fell to the ground, revealing his face.

Xiong Yi stared at the man and finally couldn't help but ask in confusion, "Isn't this... the person who went to Dujiangyan with Grand Diviner Xu?"

Ying Zheng looked at Chen Hui and asked, "I heard that this person was arranged by Governor Chen to accompany Grand Diviner Xu. Is that so?"

Chen Hui's mind was in chaos. He had been wondering why the King of Qin appeared here—was he here to kill Lu Buwei? Before he could figure it out, he suddenly saw Liu Er's pale, purple face. Chen Hui was so scared he took two steps back and almost fell to the ground.

"This... this..."

Xiong Yi was puzzled. "Your Majesty, is there a problem with this person?"

Ying Zheng said coldly, "This person intended to murder Grand Diviner Xu. If not for Grand Diviner Xu's wit, he might have perished at this man's hands. Governor Chen, do you have anything to say?"

Xu Fu understood Ying Zheng's intention. By bringing Liu Er's corpse, Ying Zheng was openly finding the person behind the plot.

His gaze swept over Xiong Yi and Chen Hui. Xiong Yi's expression was normal, but this Governor Chen had a strange look on his face, his eyes were panicked, and his mouth was tightly pursed—wasn't that the very manifestation of extreme nervousness?

Was it Chen Hui?

Xu Fu couldn't understand. How long had he been in Chengdu? This Chen Hui had been a governor for years; surely he wouldn't kill him just because he scolded him twice during breakfast? To be so enraged to this point, how small-minded must this Governor be to do such a thing?

Xu Fu thought about Chen Hui's background.

He had two masters behind him: one was the fake master Lu Buwei, and the other was the real master, Lord Changping.

Lu Buwei was now a stray dog. Although Lu Buwei must hate him, he wouldn't have the ability to command Chen Hui to kill him at this time, right? And Lord Changping—he hadn't even met him, let alone being thousands of miles away; how could he arrange for someone to kill him? After all, who would know in advance that after arriving in Chengdu, he would immediately find a local to take him to Dujiangyan?

With both possibilities ruled out, only one remained.

It was just Chen Hui himself who wanted to kill him.

Xu Fu cast his gaze on Chen Hui. Why, exactly?

Being stared at by so many eyes at once, one of which belonged to the King of Qin, one could imagine the pressure Chen Hui was under.

"Your Majesty..." Chen Hui began, but couldn't find words to argue.

Ying Zheng's gaze was like a blade. In this short time, if looks could kill, he would have already sliced Chen Hui into pieces.

Under such a gaze, the pressure in Chen Hui's heart grew heavier and heavier.

Xiong Yi wanted to reach out and save Chen Hui, but he was already out of favor with the King of Qin. If he spoke up for Chen Hui now, in this Shu region, he might end up meeting Yama along with Chen Hui.

"Does Governor Chen have nothing to say?" Ying Zheng asked in a deep voice.

Seeing that Ying Zheng's anger was no longer concealed, Chen Hui was panicked to the extreme, stammering, "Your Majesty, Your Majesty, this... this has nothing to do with me..."

"If it has nothing to do with you, then produce evidence. This Liu Er was assigned by you. He had never met Grand Diviner Xu before; why did he suddenly harbor evil intentions this time and dare to murder a Qin official? A stranger he had never met before! Governor Chen, are you speechless now?"

Chen Hui was questioned until he was covered in cold sweat, his governor's airs completely gone.

If Ying Zheng said that kneeling and begging for mercy would exempt him from his crimes, Xu Fu had no doubt that Chen Hui would immediately kneel and beg for mercy in a pathetic manner.

Such a petty person—no wonder he was on good terms with Xiong Yi's family.

And at this moment, a flash of inspiration struck Xu Fu.

Looking at Chen Hui nervously clutching his robes, he couldn't help but ask, "Governor Chen, your robes are finally worn more neatly today."

Chen Hui's face changed drastically, and his body shook even more violently.

And Xu Fu was certain of Chen Hui's motive for sending someone to kill him.

It was truly petty.

It was just a casual remark to scare him, but it happened to hit Chen Hui's sore spot. He must have been so guilty that he couldn't eat or sleep, and finally decided to kill him.

Ying Zheng also noticed Chen Hui's strange expression and asked, "What mystery is there in his robes?"

Xu Fu recalled the scene he saw that day in detail. "The collar was disheveled, the left and right lapels were crossed incorrectly, and he was in a great hurry when he came out..." Xu Fu paused. That day, there were also some marks on Chen Hui's neck; now that he thought about it, it seemed somewhat ambiguous.

That's not right. If Chen Hui slept with a woman, what was there to hide?

Unless he slept with someone else's wife and was exposed by his own disheveled appearance, making him feel guilty and afraid that he would know more. Whose wife could he have slept with to make him so panicked?

Since he had doubts, Xu Fu wouldn't hide them. Now that Qin Shi Huang was by his side, what was he afraid of?

"Governor Chen has good fortune with women. I wonder whose wife that was?" As soon as Xu Fu said this, everyone else was confused, but only Ying Zheng instantly understood what Xu Fu meant.

Ying Zheng sneered, "I know now."

"Huh?" Xu Fu turned back in confusion. Qin Shi Huang had just arrived in Chengdu today; how did he know?

He looked at Chen Hui again, and Chen Hui was already shaking so much he was about to collapse to the ground.

Ying Zheng's aura was intimidating. Chen Hui didn't even dare to argue, only making gurgling sounds in his throat, covered in cold sweat.

"Lu Buwei was driven by me to the Shu region. Lu Buwei treated you as his former guest, so he naturally came to rely on you. But you did not recognize the old friendship and drove Lu Buwei out of the Chengdu government office—that would be one thing. But Lu Buwei's wives must have all been slept with by you." Ying Zheng's face was cold, and by this point, it had turned into a sharp shout. "Truly a formidable Governor!"

Lu Buwei was a person who excelled at enduring and holding grudges. He was smarter than Lao Ai, and the friends he made were many times more numerous than Lao Ai's. Even if he arrived in Shu and lost his former status, he still had friends and former guests.

If the news that Chen Hui had toyed with his wives spread, would Chen Hui have any life left?

Chen Hui had witnessed Xu Fu's formidable nature, which was why he couldn't help but instruct Liu Er to find an opportunity to kill Xu Fu.

He hadn't expected that while he witnessed Xu Fu's formidable nature, Liu Er would naturally see it too. As a result, Liu Er didn't dare to act easily, and by the time he did, it was too late, and he ended up getting himself involved.

Xiong Yi was already stunned.

Losing a Governor of Shu was truly a pity.

The position of Governor was a good one!

Back then, when Lu Buwei was still the King of Qin's foster father, he could decide the candidate for the Governor of Shu Commandery, and even the King of Qin wouldn't say much. But now, even if Lord Changping had power, how could he dare to demand such a thing from the King of Qin? Losing a cultivated Chen Hui was like losing an arm.

Xiong Yi bit his lip hard, not daring to make a sound, fearing he would provoke Ying Zheng's anger.

Ying Zheng waved his hand, signaling the attendants to seize Chen Hui.

"As a Governor, you do not think of government affairs; the flood in Shu has not improved at all! You are narrow-minded, toy with other men's wives, and attempt to murder a fellow official, while suppressing the county magistrate of Dujiangyan, attempting to keep Dujiangyan firmly in your hands, treating the lives of the commoners like grass. Truly a good Governor recommended by Lu Buwei back then." Ying Zheng scolded him with a string of words, and Chen Hui's back was already soaked through.

He had come prepared.

The King had dealt with Lu Buwei, so he must have long found this Governor an eyesore...

Now it was his turn...

How great the King's control over the Shu region was could be seen from the fact that he had long known he had driven Lu Buwei away.

Chen Hui was panicked inside, almost anticipating his own end.

Would it be like Lao Ai, being torn apart by chariots?

"Your Majesty, I beg Your Majesty to spare my life!" Chen Hui finally squeezed out a cry from his throat.

He looked up, begging Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng walked past him and kicked him. "Such a Governor is worse than an animal."

Chen Hui's heart was already covered by fear. He hurriedly reached out, trying to grab Ying Zheng's hem, but Xu Fu followed and stepped on the back of his hand. Chen Hui let out a cry of pain. He wanted to curse Xu Fu but didn't dare, only glaring at him, wishing he could kill him with his eyes.

Xu Fu walked past Chen Hui with an expressionless face, following Ying Zheng's figure.

Chen Hui wanted to kill him; stepping on him was letting him off easy.

Entering the hall, Ying Zheng said to the attendant beside him, "Since Governor Chen has confessed, take him to apologize to Lu Buwei."

The attendant nodded and went out to order people to drag Chen Hui up from the ground and take him directly out of the Governor's mansion.

Xu Fu secretly thought Ying Zheng's methods were formidable.

If Lu Buwei knew he had been cuckolded, who knew how angry he would be? Chen Hui going to apologize was more like going to seek death. This move by Qin Shi Huang was killing two birds with one stone, letting these two dogs bite each other...

·

Pedestrians came and went outside the Governor's mansion. Seeing two burly men dragging the trembling Governor Chen out, they were all stunned, then began to laugh and spread the word. It was clear how unwelcome this Governor was in Shu.

Chen Hui had lost all his dignity and had to face the fear of death. His whole face turned pale as he watched the two men drag him toward where Lu Buwei lived.

If Lu Buwei found out...

Wouldn't he eat him alive?

Chen Hui shivered, only then realizing that from the moment he harbored the intent to kill Xu Fu, he had already stepped half a foot into hell.

"...Help!"

On this day, a scream suddenly rang out in a secluded alley, startling passersby into looking toward the courtyard. They could only catch a glimpse of a half-closed door and the hem of a robe flashing by. The passerby was shocked, thinking to himself, surely he hadn't just stumbled upon a murder?

A long time passed before two burly men pushed the door open and dragged out a man with a pale face and sweat-drenched hair. The robe the man wore was filthy, and he couldn't help but let out mournful cries as he was brought out, looking utterly wretched.

Unfortunately, the man was desperately trying to hide his face, and the passerby didn't have time to see clearly that the face belonged to none other than their Shu Commandery Governor.

The passerby peered into the courtyard again and saw a man with white temples leaning against a pillar, standing unsteadily. Not far from him, several beautiful women were sobbing softly.

The passerby muttered to himself, could it be they caught an affair? He shook his head and hurried away. If one accidentally got involved in such domestic matters, it could be deadly.

·

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng sat together in the main hall, and the servants of the Governor's mansion served tea with trembling hands. The people in the Governor's mansion still found it hard to believe they were seeing the King of Qin. But seeing how even Young Master Xiong Yi was extremely respectful, the fear in their hearts deepened, and they dared not doubt the identity of this man.

Those who had previously relied on the power of the Governor's mansion to bully others were now filled with anxiety, terrified that the King of Qin might crush them with a single finger.

Before long, a man walked into the hall and bowed to Ying Zheng, saying, "The person has been brought back."

Ying Zheng nodded. "Take him to the prison; we will bring him along when we depart for Xianyang. Issue an order for Li Bing to arrive and take office in three days."

The man acknowledged the order and withdrew.

Xu Fu was still curious about what Lü Buwei looked like when Chen Hui was brought over.

Just then, Ying Zheng spoke up: "You go on my behalf and retrieve the item..."

An item? What item?

"The Empress Dowager's Imperial Seal."

Xu Fu was stunned. "Wasn't it with Lao Ai back then?"

"It is not in Lao Ai's hands."

So the First Emperor of Qin wanted to take back the Empress Dowager's seal?

"Now that the Empress Dowager has passed away, although the seal is useless, it cannot remain in Lü Buwei's hands." Ying Zheng's face was gloomy, and his voice turned cold at the mention of Lü Buwei.

Ever since he witnessed Ying Zheng retrieve the seal from Zhao Ji only to smash it to pieces right in front of her, Xu Fu had seen Ying Zheng's domineering nature. Even if it were something he disdained to use, he would never leave it for anyone else.

Coincidentally, he also wanted to see what Lü Buwei looked like now...

Xu Fu nodded in agreement. "I'll trouble Your Majesty to send someone to guide me."

Ying Zheng called for someone, and the man bowed and led Xu Fu out. Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou exchanged a glance and followed Xu Fu.

·

With a creak, the courtyard door was pushed open again. The sensitive person in the courtyard immediately raised his head and shouted angrily, "Who is it?"

Xu Fu walked in front, leaning one hand against the door as he strolled in.

As soon as he met his face, Lü Buwei's expression changed.

"It's you..."

If one spoke of hating Ying Zheng, Lü Buwei probably loathed Xu Fu even more. Such a petty person appearing by Ying Zheng's side, inciting and bewitching him, was despicable; now, having become Ying Zheng's lackey, he was even more disgusting!

It was precisely after this person appeared that he could no longer control Ying Zheng.

His decline had begun to show signs from that very moment!

Xu Fu raised his eyes and caught sight of Lü Buwei leaning against a pillar.

Why had Lü Buwei aged so rapidly? A look of surprise flashed across Xu Fu's face.

They say only power keeps a man forever young. After losing power, was it inevitable for Lü Buwei to fall into rapid aging?

The high spirits had completely vanished from him. All Xu Fu could see were the white hairs at his temples, the deep wrinkles around his eyes and on his forehead, his sallow complexion, his cracked lips, and the malice and deep-seated fear in his eyes.

What was there left for Lü Buwei to fear now? He had lost everything that could be lost; what else could make him afraid? Was it because Chen Hui had cuckolded him that he had fallen into such a state of gloom?

Xu Fu walked forward slowly, watching this former hero reduced to his current state. However, his heart was calm, perhaps because Lü Buwei stood on the opposing side.

"What are you here for?" When Lü Buwei spoke, his lips were trembling slightly, and a look of shame and anger appeared on his face. Lü Buwei had heard that several people had arrived in Shu from Xianyang. At first, he was fearful, but after accidentally seeing Xiong Yi's face on the street, he felt much relieved. If Ying Zheng really didn't want him alive in Shu and sent someone to kill him, it certainly wouldn't be Xiong Yi.

But he hadn't expected that besides Xiong Yi, there would be Xu Fu... Who was Xu Fu? He was so close to Ying Zheng now; if there was anyone Ying Zheng still trusted, it would surely be him. If Ying Zheng was willing to let him come to Shu, wasn't the purpose obvious?

Lü Buwei's face turned slightly pale.

Xu Fu turned his head to look at the women still sobbing softly nearby.

These must be the concubines Lü Buwei had brought with him?

Lü Buwei's expression changed again, and he shouted sternly, "Take them away!"

Madame Lü walked out from inside. She didn't recognize Xu Fu, but looked at him with surprise, unable to understand why Lü Buwei was in such a rage. She called the servants to take the concubines away, then stepped back herself.

"I came here today to..." Before Xu Fu could finish, Lü Buwei's face had already turned extremely ugly. Xu Fu paused, carefully observing the expression on Lü Buwei's face, and then said, "Please, Master Lü, hand over an item."

To suppress the panic in his heart, Lü Buwei sneered and said loudly, "What could I, Lü Buwei, possibly have now that is worth coveting? To think you traveled all the way from Xianyang for it!"

Xu Fu lifted his eyelids, his expression indifferent, not taking Lü Buwei's posturing to heart at all. "Where is the Empress Dowager's Imperial Seal?"

"What Empress Dowager's Imperial Seal? Now that the Empress Dowager has passed away, you ask me for it? Ridiculous!" Lü Buwei scoffed, his gaze cold and sharp. This look actually had a bit of the demeanor of the former Chancellor Lü.

Xu Fu trusted what Ying Zheng said; since he said it was with Lü Buwei, it must be true. Xu Fu didn't argue with Lü Buwei, just said coldly, "Whether Master Lü hands it over or not, I am taking it today. But Master Lü can choose to hand it over voluntarily or have me search for it." Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou stepped forward, their presence sharp, their tall figures bringing an invisible sense of oppression.

Lü Buwei was no longer the Chancellor; if they really took action, he would have nowhere to seek justice.

His face shifted through several colors before Lü Buwei suddenly remembered something.

Chen Hui was the Governor of Shu; who would dare drag him here to humiliate him?

...Ying Zheng had also come to Shu?!

This thought flashed through Lü Buwei's mind, his throat suddenly turning dry and hoarse. The fierce demeanor he had forced himself to adopt was like a castle in the air, crumbling at a push.

"Did Ying... the King of Qin send you to ask me for the seal?"

Xu Fu glanced at him, his indifferent gaze carrying a hint of Ying Zheng's aura. "Not asking you, but giving Master Lü a chance."

Lü Buwei laughed after hearing this. "To think I, Lü Buwei, would have this day, bullied by a mere child like you." Lü Buwei could only resort to verbal bravado now. Enduring the humiliation, he gritted his teeth and took a cloth pouch from his sleeve; it turned out he had been carrying it with him all along.

Xu Fu raised an eyebrow, reached out to take the pouch, and opened it to see a small square of jade inside, looking quite exquisite. Xu Fu didn't examine it closely, as he couldn't tell the difference anyway, so he just glanced at it, closed the pouch, and tossed it casually to Bo Zhou.

Noticing the look of reluctance and unwillingness that flashed across Lü Buwei's face at that moment, Xu Fu was certain that the seal must be genuine.

With the seal in hand and having seen Lü Buwei's current state, there was no point in mocking him further. Xu Fu turned and walked out. By the time he led his men to the door, Lü Buwei behind him could no longer stand and collapsed to the ground.

Madame Lü let out a cry of alarm and hurried over to support him. Upon holding him, she was horrified to find that Lü Buwei's face was faintly tinged with a greenish hue.

Lü Buwei gritted his teeth, his eyes fixed on Xu Fu's retreating back, a mix of grief, indignation, and shame flashing across his face... He had actually collapsed in front of Xu Fu! What a disgrace!

Xu Fu heard the sound but didn't look back, walking straight out with Sang Zhong and Bo Zhou.

Once he left, Lü Buwei could no longer hold back and spat out a mouthful of blood. Madame Lü was terrified and shouted, "Someone! Someone..." Lü Buwei raised his hand and grabbed her wrist, the veins on his forehead about to burst. "It's nothing, help me... help me up..."

Madame Lü nodded in a panic and helped him up from the ground. Lü Buwei pushed her away and staggered toward the study. Once inside, he used all his strength to shut the door tightly, not wanting his wretched state to be seen by others again.

He closed his eyes, and in his ears, it seemed he could still hear the voices of people bowing and calling him "Chancellor Lü."

How could he have imagined he would fall to this point? He, Lü Buwei, considered himself a man of exceptional vision, the most successful merchant, who later became Chancellor and the King of Qin's foster father, holding the power of a nation, with three thousand retainers, author of the "Lüshi Chunqiu." He should have been a name revered by future generations in history books...

Why... why had it turned into this?

Ying Zheng had come to Shu; he was surely going to kill him... He couldn't tolerate him... Thinking of Hu Ji, thinking of the wretched Chen Hui, and then thinking of Xu Fu who had come here... and the faces of Lao Ai and Zhao Ji flashing through his mind... his fears had finally come true.

Zhao Ji was dead, and it would be his turn soon.

Lü Buwei's face suddenly twisted, but he refused to die at Ying Zheng's hands!

He stumbled to the table, grabbed the wine vessel, and drank it all in one gulp.
