寝宫之中，胡亥被宫人放在铺了绒布的地面上，爬来爬去，最后抱住了扶苏的腿，扶苏险些一脚踹过去，最后又硬生生地收住了，他抬头看向嬴政，“父王……”
嬴政头也不抬，道：“待徐先生来了，你将胡亥送予他便是。”
扶苏嘴角微抽，小小的脸上神色怪异。
父王，这是你儿子啊，说送人就送人……该不会有一日把我也送出去吧？
小小的胡亥全然不知发生了什么，口中咯咯笑着，然后撩起扶苏的裤腿便往上啃，扶苏被咬得差点嗷的一声叫出来。
扶苏红了红双眼，忙叫道：“父王……”他的话音刚落，便听宫人道：“徐先生！”
扶苏仿佛见了救星，忙拔高声音，“老师！”
徐福刚踏进殿中来，便听见了扶苏这一嗓子，如同被谁掐住了脖子一般，有点儿凄厉。难道秦始皇还虐待儿子？徐福拐了个弯儿，快步走进去，便见胡亥一嘴啃在扶苏腿脖子上，扶苏一脸哭相，终于褪去了那副小大人的模样，而极不靠谱的家长秦始皇正坐在不远处的桌案之后，面前放着竹简，俨然一副分不出神来带孩子的模样。
旁边的宫人倒是有些憋不住笑，全然将胡亥与扶苏之间的行为，看作了是兄弟间促进亲密感情的小打小闹。
“老师！”见徐福不为所动，扶苏不得不又叫了一声。
胡亥这时还不会说话，但闻言，也跟着朝徐福看去，“……四、四……”竟是在模仿着扶苏的音调，只是因为嘴里才冒了两颗小牙齿，如今一说话便漏风，一个完整的音也发布出来，看上去二了吧唧的，倒是显得呆萌了些。
哪怕是对小孩子谈不上喜恶的徐福，心中也微微软了软。
嬴政推开面前竹简，起身走到徐福身旁。原本想要去抱胡亥的徐福不得不顿住了动作。他以为秦始皇会问他升职的滋味如何，但下一刻，他却听嬴政问道：“奉常寺中夜宿可能入睡？”
你以为我会说难以入眠吗？
徐福眼底闪过一道精光，面上却是平平淡淡，道：“床榻舒适，轻松入眠。”说完，徐福突然觉得自己这话说得，像是在给奉常寺的床上用具打广告一样。
嬴政免不了有些失望。
那奉常寺如何能与王宫相比？但徐福去了一趟蜀地，似乎适应能力变强了一些，对于奉常寺的屋子，也并不如何挑剔了。
不过嬴政并不纠结于此，他命人摆了膳食，正欲将扶苏同胡亥打发走，徐福却突然弯腰将胡亥抱了起来。
胡亥在徐福怀中蹭了蹭，小脑袋点个不停，像是有些困倦了。
如今的胡亥，比起当初刚出生不久的模样，已经健壮了许多，胳膊和腿都变成了藕节，圆圆滚滚，白白嫩嫩。
也许正是这副模样太蠢了些，嬴政到了嘴边的话便拐了个弯儿，默许了胡亥留在寝宫之中。
饭食被摆上桌案，他们各自落座，形成三角之势。
徐福将胡亥放到一旁，胡亥摊着肚皮躺在小被子上，宫女将他裹得严实了一些，然后徐福才用起了自己的饭食。
不知不觉时间便流逝而过。
徐福不经意地一个抬头，发觉宫中气氛和谐，温馨，但怪异。
……怎么那么像一家四口的派头呢？
徐福皱了皱眉。
难道这也是秦始皇的阴谋？
一招温水煮青蛙！
徐福感觉到自己受到了挑战，于是他决定继续坚持本心，先不卑不亢一段时间，起码别那么容易进秦始皇的圈套。
吃过饭之后，便有内侍进门来，俯身道：“王上，太后病重。”
太后？什么太后？徐福愣了下，才想到内侍口中的太后，应当是那位与熊家有几分联系的华阳太后。
嬴政洗漱净手过后，才带人往华阳太后的宫中去了。
走时，嬴政嘱咐了徐福一句，“勿要离宫。”
“为何不能离宫？”见赵高站在殿中，徐福便问起了赵高。
赵高笑了笑，不急不忙道：“熊义公子身死，昌平君心有不满，如今徐先生做了典事，难免那昌平君不讲理，非要找徐先生的麻烦。”
这是担心他被迁怒？
徐福点头，“那我便暂时不去奉常寺了。”左右奉常寺中也无事，何况他翘班也不是一日两日了。
徐福突然顿住了。
不……他似乎忘记了自己与侯生的约定！
徐福不得不又叫住赵高，“劳烦为我叫个小内侍来，我需要请他办一件事。”
虽然徐福总是一副高高在上的模样，但赵高知晓，比起待人尊重，谁也比不过徐福。虽然他口气冷淡，但说出来的话，却总是令人觉得熨帖，忍不住为之付出全力来完成他交代的事。
赵高叫了内侍过来，徐福忙让那内侍去找侯生道歉。
赵高听见侯生这名字，惊讶道：“是他？他与徐先生有约定？”
徐福点头，问：“怎么？”
“此人难缠，若是与徐先生起了龃龉，徐先生万万不要埋于心中，王上定能为徐先生讨个公道的。”赵高不动声色地给嬴政脸上贴金。
徐福摇头，“侯太卜也不能做出什么来……”
赵高却是点到即止，不再多话徒惹徐福厌烦。
入夜后，徐福洗漱一番，更了衣上了床榻，却久久未能等到嬴政归来。
难道华阳太后那边实在不太好了？
徐福心中不自觉地担忧了几分。
若是从前，躺在床榻上他便满脑子都是困倦了，哪里还会分出点来为嬴政思量半分？如今他的心思早已发生了他自己都未注意到的变化。
等得有些烦躁的徐福强迫自己闭上双眼，总算睡着了。
第二日他醒来后，却也没能见到嬴政的身影，宫人伺候着他更衣洗漱用饭食。徐福正思索着自己要做何事来打发时间时，便有内侍进来，低声道：“昨日徐典事入了睡，便不敢前来打扰徐典事。那侯太卜有一物要交给徐典事。”
说着那内侍从袖中掏出了一竹简来。
徐福摊开竹简来一看，见上面刻着几句话，大意便是，侯生要与他玩一把大的，他们不占卜天气，不占卜国家祸福，他们只随意寻上一人，占卜那人的将来，待到数年之后，给那人的批语若是应验了，那届时，输的人也要承认自己技不如人。
几十年……
倒是比王柳更有耐心。
果然是要玩一把大的吗？
徐福来了兴致。
从来到秦国后，他认真相过面的，只有一人。那便是秦始皇。如今看来，恰好他还可以再寻一人来，仔细研究一番面相。
是瞧胡亥的呢？还是瞧扶苏的呢？
然而他早已知晓胡亥与扶苏的命运，那赵高……他虽然记得不清，但也知晓一二，说来没甚意思。
还有谁呢？徐福暂时想不起来，不如哪一日在街头随便遇上一人，便就挑那人好了。
徐福越想越觉得有些摩拳擦掌。
从蜀地回来后，正巧他也休养好了，如今正是测试相面水平的时候。
徐福在王宫之中有些待不住了，但是嬴政未回来，他并不想一点面子也不给秦始皇，撩起衣袍就走人。那岂不是没将秦始皇放在眼中吗？如今他这个最大的后门还没怎么开，便将秦始皇惹怒了，那多不划算。
徐福按捺住满腔躁动，干脆到偏殿去逗弄小胡亥了，伴随着扶苏的朗朗背诵声，时间倒也不知觉地过去了。
待到用晚膳时，徐福终于听见有内侍高喊一声，“王上！”
只见嬴政疾步跨进门来，不多时便走到了徐福的身旁，徐福抬起头来，眼里还没流露出点心疼来，假装安抚一下秦始皇，他便陡然发觉，秦始皇脸上并没有他想象中的悲苦烦恼之色，相反的——
面前的嬴政神采奕奕，眼眸含笑，嘴角也微微上扬。
他大手一挥，道：“将寡人搜寻来的物事带上来。”
有内侍应了一声，连忙躬身将一些东西倒在了徐福的跟前，徐福定睛一看，却是愣住了，奇形怪状的草药，颜色诡异的石头，还有殷红的朱砂，以及一些古时的竹简，其中一只竹简上还隐隐能瞥见二字：炼丹。
徐福呆了呆。
嬴政道：“你不是要用那鼎来炼丹吗？寡人便为你搜寻来了这些物事，若觉得不够好，寡人便再令人去搜寻。”
徐福愣住了。
他……他只是随口说着玩儿的啊……
忽悠了秦始皇会被做成兵马俑吗？
徐福原本要说出口的真相，就这样堵了回去。
罢了，连神棍都做了，炼丹有何不能做的？装模作样一番，那鼎也算派上用场了。只要他不将那些丹药给人吃便好。
当然，徐福也并不认为自己能炼出什么丹来。
扶苏窥见桌案前的物事，惊叹道：“老师博学，竟还会炼药之术。”
徐福装得淡定不惊，他拾起竹简随手翻了翻，然后便放了回去，“收起来吧。”
内侍忙将这些东西收了起来，却是就放在了嬴政的寝宫之中，俨然已经默认，徐福住的地儿，就是这里了。
徐福这才有空问那华阳太后，“王上，华阳太后如何了？”
嬴政并没有被打探的不悦，他在徐福身旁跽坐下来，道：“太后年迈，如今大病乃常事，只是昌平君想要在此事上做点文章，为他那儿子向寡人讨个公道。”
“熊义当真死了？”徐福将那熊义忘了个干净，并不知为何他们离开郡守府时，便不见了他的踪影。
“死了。”嬴政顿了顿，“蒹葭看着他死的。”
蒹葭？
想到他那张秀美如名字般的脸庞，徐福有些想象不能，这样一人，如何下手杀人。
“昌平君想要如何讨公道？”
嬴政阴沉沉地道：“昌平君向太后说，你与熊义同行，不管如何，你都脱不了关系。”他其实已经挑了好话来说了，要知道那昌平君当时说的话更为难听。言语间竟是指责徐福用美色祸了他的儿子，害了他儿子的性命，陈会有错，徐福也有错！
徐福也应当被下狱！
嬴政心中更加阴沉。
那昌平君如何想的，他如何不知？
不过是拼了命地想要挣扎着再拖个人下水，平一平心头之恨罢了？
嬴政越想越加恼火。
非我族类，其心必异！
昌平君早晚得死！
作者有话要说：
放一段史记资料：三十二年（前215），派韩终、侯公、石生去寻找仙人不死之药。
chapters.translated_text:
The sun set in the west, and the people in the Fengchang Temple had gradually dispersed.

After bidding farewell to Su Yi, Xu Fu strode toward another hall. As he stepped through the door, the rays of the setting sun shone into the hall, illuminating a figure slumped over a desk.

"Grand Diviner Hou," Xu Fu called out softly.

The figure at the desk raised his head, revealing a face with a solemn and rigid expression. "Grand Diviner Xu."

It was very difficult for Xu Fu to tell from Hou Sheng's face whether he was happy or unhappy.

"I have a question I would like to ask Grand Diviner Hou," Xu Fu said, kneeling beside him.

Hou Sheng lowered his head and continued flipping through the bamboo slips in his hand.

Xu Fu did not pause and continued, "Before I went to the Shu region, Grand Diviner Hou told me that the journey would be difficult. Did you truly divine something from the hexagrams, or did you only warn me because you thought the Shu region was dangerous?" Of course, there was another possibility: that Grand Diviner Hou had deliberately tried to scare him, but that question was not appropriate to ask aloud.

Hou Sheng finally cast aside the bamboo slips in his hand, his expression cold. "I did indeed divine some danger." He paused, then added, "But I am not like you; I did not calculate the great disaster in the Shu region. You are more refined than I am, and more resilient as well."

Hou Sheng's gaze was very complex.

He had once strictly obstructed Xu Fu, but now that Xu Fu had returned safely, he naturally felt he had lost face, as if he had been slapped hard by Xu Fu.

But could he refuse to admit it?

Hou Sheng did not usually show it on his face, but how arrogant was he deep down? Now, not to mention the books of divination, he had already lost to Xu Fu in terms of character alone. Xu Fu dared to do things he dared not, and the arrogance in his bones made him feel even more choked up.

He had lost the original intention he had when he first came to the Qin State!

He did not come just to be a Deputy Grand Diviner; he had ambitions and truly wanted to achieve something under the King of Qin, using the land of Qin to show his abilities to the various states and the world.

Yet now, he had fallen into such a narrow-minded state, fearing the wolf in front and the tiger behind. For the sake of his reputation, it was one thing to have a half-baked understanding of the hexagrams, but he had even suppressed the hexagrams of others. How was this behavior any different from those he used to look down upon?

Hou Sheng fell into shame and embarrassment, and now, looking at Xu Fu, he felt very uncomfortable.

Xu Fu could not see what was in Hou Sheng's heart from his face, so he could only say, "In that case, I will assume that Grand Diviner Hou was indeed doing it for my own good when you advised me so." Xu Fu's tone was not as gentle as his words.

Hou Sheng gritted his teeth and looked up. "Grand Diviner Xu, it was indeed my fault to have erased your annotations from the bamboo slips." Hou Sheng did not have the thick skin to ask Xu Fu to forgive his actions, and even if Xu Fu forgave him, he would only feel more awkward.

Only then did Hou Sheng realize how arrogant he had once been. He was well-known and thought he had a place among the seven states, but he never expected that there would truly be someone younger than him with greater ability.

Xu Fu was stunned for a moment. Hou Sheng was actually apologizing? Could it be that everyone in the Fengchang Temple had lost their minds today?

Xu Fu's disgust for Hou Sheng could not possibly disappear so quickly; he still remembered how furious he was when he found out his divination annotations had been deleted. So what if he apologized? He had the right to choose not to accept it.

Xu Fu nodded faintly, his gaze sweeping over the desk in front of Hou Sheng. "Since Grand Diviner Hou is very busy, I will not disturb you further." Xu Fu turned and walked out. He had come today just to let Hou Sheng see whether he had died or been crippled after his trip to the Shu region. He wanted Hou Sheng to know that his hexagram was the correct one, and Hou Sheng's was wrong.

Now that Hou Sheng had apologized so quickly, it was clear from his words that he already knew who was more capable.

There was no point in Xu Fu staying any longer.

Xu Fu walked out slowly and sighed softly. Hou Sheng had made him quite angry back then, but now there was no pleasure in taking revenge.

And as Xu Fu turned to walk away, Hou Sheng looked up almost simultaneously, secretly peeking at Xu Fu's back.

The moment Xu Fu's gaze had swept over him earlier, it had made him tremble with fear.

Ever since he learned that a great disaster had truly occurred in the Shu region, he had seemed to fall into a daze. He could not accept the result that he was inferior to Xu Fu, so he could not help but dig out many ancient books. At first, he wanted to prove that Xu Fu's divination method was unheard of and perhaps just a lucky guess, but later, he could not help but start frantically searching and learning, thinking that before Xu Fu returned, he could still crush him when they met again.

But he had failed...

Hou Sheng let out a long sigh and closed the bamboo slips in his hand.

After Xu Fu left the hall, he habitually started to walk out of the Fengchang Temple. Halfway there, he stopped and turned back. He had already told the people in the Xianyang Palace that he would not be returning today, so he could not go back on his word. Xu Fu turned around and walked slowly toward the room he had been assigned, which he had not yet stepped into.

He wondered what the room looked like after Wang Liu had people clean it up.

After becoming a Deputy Grand Diviner, Xu Fu's room had naturally been changed. Compared to when he first arrived at the Fengchang Temple, his treatment now had skyrocketed, rising by more than one level.

He pushed the door open and went in, seeing that the room was much larger, with a bed, a desk, cushions, a bathtub, and other items. The items inside were clearly much more refined, and the quilt on the bed did not look as rustic as before.

If the previous one was a standard room, this was a business suite.

Having gotten used to sleeping outdoors in the Shu region, sleeping in such a room was already quite good. Xu Fu fetched hot water to wash up, and without eating dinner, he went to the bed.

Outside the Fengchang Temple, the little attendant waited for a while and sighed involuntarily.

Just as the King said, he probably wouldn't be able to wait for him...

He drove the carriage back. He was puzzled, wondering why Grand Diviner Xu would want to sleep in a separate bed from the King for no reason...

·

Hou Sheng had come to the Qin State alone, with no belongings and no family, so he also stayed in the Fengchang Temple. When the sun set behind the mountains, he came out of the hall and hesitated before walking to the outside of Xu Fu's room.

Hou Sheng raised his hand and knocked on the door.

He still felt a sense of unwillingness in his heart.

He had practiced the art of divination for many years; how could he have so easily fallen behind a young man?

The arrogance in Hou Sheng's heart was at work.

Since that was the case, he would generously find Xu Fu to discuss the Dao, determine a winner, and only then would he be able to calm his heart.

Thinking of this, Hou Sheng's belief became even firmer. He knocked on the door again, but no one answered. Hou Sheng would not give up and stood outside knocking for a long time.

By now, night had fallen. Although it was already spring, the nights were always a bit chilly. Hou Sheng shivered and realized that his feet had gone numb from standing.

Hou Sheng gritted his teeth and left in anger. This Xu Fu must still be dissatisfied with him and was deliberately leaving him out in the cold... It was hateful... Yet, when Hou Sheng thought that this was his own doing, he felt even more stifled.

At this time, Xu Fu was lying on the bed, sleeping peacefully while hugging the quilt.

In the sleeping quarters of the Xianyang Palace, Ying Zheng lay on the bed and turned over, unable to see Xu Fu's calm face, and the place within reach was no longer warm skin. For Ying Zheng, who was used to taking advantage every day, returning to Xianyang City only to live such a lonely life made him sigh softly, and it took a long time for him to fall asleep.

·

At dawn, everyone in the Fengchang Temple had come to check in. When they walked into the hall, they saw a brown figure already sitting there.

Even though everyone was wearing brown robes, that person was different from everyone else. His temperament was unique, and one glance made people feel as if they had inadvertently caught a glimpse of gods and Buddhas in the nine heavens. Not only was his temperament otherworldly and eye-catching, but he also unintentionally exuded an aura that made everyone fearful.

As they got closer, they saw his face, which was still as fair as jade, and his handsome features. Truly, in the entire Fengchang Temple, no one could compare to him.

Even though he had been to the Shu region, he looked as if nothing had happened, looking even more pampered than those of them who stayed in the Fengchang Temple all day.

Everyone gritted their teeth secretly, thinking that there really was a big difference between people.

Usually, when Xu Fu was in the Fengchang Temple, it was rare to see him arrive early, which had attracted a lot of eager attention. After a while, Hou Sheng also came in. Hou Sheng's appearance made these people shut their mouths involuntarily.

They had already experienced how rigid and serious Hou Sheng was, and since their skills were not as good as his, they also held some admiration in their hearts. They knew about Hou Sheng erasing Xu Fu's hexagram, so now that they saw the two of them appearing together, they naturally felt very awkward and hurriedly turned their heads away, pretending they hadn't seen anything.

Hou Sheng walked up to Xu Fu. "Grand Diviner Xu." He spoke and realized his voice was too stiff. He paused and hurriedly tried to soften it, but his voice was perhaps naturally like that, always carrying a cold flavor.

"I would like to ask Grand Diviner Xu for guidance."

"Guidance on what?" Xu Fu was stunned, feeling a bit puzzled. What was Hou Sheng doing again?

"There is a method of proving the Dao in my school; please prove the Dao with me, Grand Diviner Xu." Hou Sheng said with a serious face. His voice was kept quite low, completely different from when Wang Liu deliberately looked for trouble with Xu Fu.

Although both of them harbored unwillingness in their hearts, Hou Sheng truly wanted to see Xu Fu's brilliance in its entirety.

Xu Fu had never refused such things; if he won, he would naturally become famous. Such a good opportunity had come to his door, why not take it?

"Okay..." Xu Fu had just agreed halfway when he heard an attendant coming with the King of Qin's order.

Everyone was stunned and hurriedly got up to rush to the courtyard.

It was the same attendant from last time. He stood in the courtyard, and seeing that everyone had arrived, he said loudly, "In the Divination Office of the Fengchang Temple, Grand Diviner Xu, for the safety of the country and the people, sacrificed himself and risked danger to go to the Shu region, saved several lives, and captured traitors. His merits are great, and he is now promoted to the position of Director."

Xu Fu himself was also slightly stunned.

Director?

Wasn't that Xiong Yi's position?

Hou Sheng's face changed instantly, and the look in his eyes was very complex. He had been in the Qin State for a while, but he hadn't been promoted as fast as this young man.

The others were also stunned or surprised...

Someone couldn't help but say, "Then Director Xiong..." There was already a Director Xiong in the Fengchang Temple. If there was another Director, wouldn't it cause the same awkwardness as the two Deputy Grand Diviners before?

At this time, some people didn't even think about Xiong Yi's life or death; they were filled with envy, jealousy, and hatred. If they had known that going to the Shu region would bring such honor and lead directly to the position of Director, they would have risked their lives to go... But these people only thought about it in their hearts; if it really came to that, they might not have dared to go.

"Director Xu, congratulations." The attendant no longer hid the eager smile on his face and laughingly placed the new official uniform into Xu Fu's hands.

"Thank you." Xu Fu nodded, unfazed by favor or humiliation.

He gripped the hem of the official uniform in his hand to confirm that this was not a dream. Xu Fu's mind was full of the position of National Master. After calming down, another sentence began to pop up in his mind. Could this be the sugar-coated bullet of the First Emperor of Qin?

The attendant came and went quickly. After the King's order was delivered, he left with his people.

The whole courtyard was quiet for a long time before returning to its previous state.

Liu Fengchang, who was on the side, carefully glanced at Xu Fu and felt more and more that Xu Fu's background was unfathomable and that he was highly favored by the King of Qin. Even the position of Young Master Xiong Yi could be squeezed out; this strength was probably not something he could afford to provoke. He had better be careful to keep his own position...

At this time, the panicked Liu Fengchang completely failed to remember that when he had angered Xu Fu, Xu Fu had already given him a prophecy.

·

Walking into the hall, Xu Fu, whose expression was slightly dazed, turned his head and caught a glimpse of the dazed Hou Sheng. It was really not easy to see such an expression on Hou Sheng's face.

After sitting in his seat for a long time, Xu Fu was tidying up his things, intending to change his office location again, when he heard Hou Sheng, who had finally come to his senses, say, "Today I will make an agreement with Grand Diviner Xu, no, Director Xu. Let's discuss the Dao tomorrow, how about it?"

This discussion of the Dao was, of course, not the discussion of the Dao in cultivation.

The Dao was something everyone had, which was the persistence in each person's heart.

Hou Sheng's Dao was perhaps the art of divination he had learned from his school.

And Xu Fu's Dao was to calculate if he could, and if he couldn't, to use his glib tongue to make up for it. Of course, he wouldn't say this in front of Hou Sheng. In a short period of time, Xu Fu had also seen through some of Hou Sheng's temperament; he was an extremely serious and stubborn person, and his love for the art of divination was perhaps even higher than his own.

How could such a person listen to such words?

What was difficult about discussing the Dao?

Just bluffing with his mouth and crushing with technique.

Xu Fu didn't even lift his head and said, "Okay."

The expression on Hou Sheng's face finally eased a little. After a long time, Xu Fu heard him say, "Congratulations, Director Xu."

"Thank you." Xu Fu considered himself quite polite. Even if he didn't like Hou Sheng, he would still show him respect. Hou Sheng had not respected him before and had already been slapped in the face. Now that his status was higher than his, Hou Sheng must be suffering even more than before, which was already the best revenge.

Xu Fu walked out of the hall.

Soon, someone took him to a new place.

This was a small hall with a small couch for resting, exquisite utensils, a wide desk, and a carpeted floor... Most importantly, in such a place, he was the only one.

And not far away, he could see Liu Fengchang at a glance.

This could be considered a position that countless people coveted, as he could reach the highest superior of the Fengchang Temple at his fingertips.

After entering the hall and the others retreated, Xu Fu showed a dazed expression without any concealment, recalling the huge difference between his treatment now and when he first arrived in the Qin State. At that time, he never imagined that his promotion speed would be so fast. Before, he didn't want to make a big fuss with Wang Liu, Qiu Ji, and others, just wanting to endure for half a year to get past the newcomer period, so as not to be suspected of being overly arrogant. Without any background, wouldn't he have died miserably then?

But there were always times when human calculations were not as good as heaven's.

He calculated and calculated, but he could not calculate his own destiny, which had been smooth sailing after experiencing such great twists and turns.

After sitting down, Xu Fu flipped through ancient books in the hall and waited for a while, but suddenly realized that although the position of Director was high, there was not much work to do. Very few people were willing to bother the Director. Xu Fu was a little puzzled; was this position just for show?

He frowned, feeling puzzled in his heart.

Unknowingly, the day passed.

When it was time to leave work, someone came in to clean the room, very thoughtful and attentive.

Xu Fu walked out of the hall and bumped into Wang Liu.

Wang Liu's face was flushed, and his eyes were also red. Xu Fu was startled. Would this Wang Liu be jealous and resentful again and come to find trouble with him? If Wang Liu came again now, he would be a real fool. He was a Director now, and even Hou Sheng couldn't provoke him...

Wang Liu caught his breath and said with a complex expression, "Congratulations, Director Xu."

He didn't have the slightest intention of provoking him.

Had Wang Liu really changed his temperament? Xu Fu raised his eyebrows and nodded slightly, accepting Wang Liu's congratulations.

The whites of Wang Liu's eyes were very red, densely covered with red bloodshot eyes. After saying that, Wang Liu fell silent, just silently staring at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was creeped out by the staring and left the Fengchang Temple without looking back.

And Wang Liu looked at Xu Fu's back, his heart filled with both sorrow and joy. No one wanted to see their former enemy become more outstanding than themselves, but he had to admit that Wang Liu secretly admired Xu Fu. When he realized that the gap between himself and Xu Fu was too large, he had to face his own failure.

Think about what Xu Fu looked like when he first arrived at the Fengchang Temple, like a bumpkin who only had a good skin but was green and immature in his bones.

But how long had it been? No one dared to look down on him anymore.

Every time it was so coincidental, it just happened to push Xu Fu to a higher position.

Thinking that he could be considered a witness to Xu Fu's promotion path, Wang Liu felt even more uncomfortable.

He hadn't intended to come to the Fengchang Temple today, but after some tossing and turning, he decided he couldn't fall too far behind Xu Fu, so he came to the Fengchang Temple to study ancient books carefully. Who knew that he would soon learn the news of Xu Fu's promotion to Director? Wang Liu hurried over, the cold wind blowing on his face, and his eyes were red.

...

Xu Fu walked to the gate of the Fengchang Temple and couldn't help but look back at Wang Liu, but he could only see Wang Liu's back.

A strange look flashed in Xu Fu's heart.

Could it be... Could it be... Wang Liu was still crying?

Xu Fu felt a shiver down his spine. Wang Liu's appearance when crying wasn't exactly delicate and charming.

While thinking, Xu Fu walked to his usual spot, where the Xianyang Palace carriage was parked, and the familiar little attendant was still in front of the carriage.

Seeing Xu Fu, the little attendant couldn't hide his surprise. He hurriedly bowed and said, "Grand Diviner Xu... I have waited for Grand Diviner Xu. No, no, it's Director Xu now." The little attendant hurriedly corrected himself.

Seeing that he had already walked here, Xu Fu didn't hesitate and immediately got into the carriage.

Now that the First Emperor of Qin had promoted him to Director, there should be reciprocity, and he always had to enter the palace to thank the First Emperor of Qin.

The carriage wheels rolled, moving away in the sunset, pulling out a long shadow...

And Hou Sheng walked to the outside of Xu Fu's room and raised his hand to knock on the door, then knocked again, and again...

His figure also pulled out a long shadow, but no matter how one looked at it, it felt a bit desolate.

Hou Sheng gritted his teeth.

Was Xu Fu deliberately blocking him outside again?

·

In the sleeping quarters, Huhai was placed on the floor covered with velvet by the palace servants, crawling around, and finally hugged Fusu's leg. Fusu almost kicked him away, but finally held back. He looked up at Ying Zheng. "Father..."

Ying Zheng didn't even lift his head and said, "When Master Xu comes, you can give Huhai to him."

Fusu's mouth twitched, and his small face had a strange expression.

Father, this is your son, you give him away just like that... Could it be that one day you will give me away too?

Little Huhai didn't know what was happening at all, giggling in his mouth, and then lifted Fusu's trouser leg and bit it. Fusu was bitten so hard he almost screamed.

Fusu's eyes turned red, and he hurriedly called out, "Father..." As soon as his voice fell, he heard the palace servant say, "Master Xu!"

Fusu seemed to have seen a savior and hurriedly raised his voice, "Teacher!"

Xu Fu had just stepped into the hall when he heard Fusu's shout, which sounded like someone was strangling his neck, a bit shrill. Was the First Emperor of Qin abusing his son? Xu Fu turned a corner and walked in quickly, seeing Huhai biting Fusu's leg, Fusu with a crying face, finally shedding his little adult appearance, while the extremely unreliable parent, the First Emperor of Qin, was sitting at the desk not far away, with bamboo slips in front of him, looking like he couldn't spare any attention to take care of the children.

The palace servants on the side couldn't help but laugh, completely seeing the behavior between Huhai and Fusu as a little squabble between brothers to promote intimate feelings.

"Teacher!" Seeing that Xu Fu was unmoved, Fusu had to call out again.

Huhai couldn't speak yet, but upon hearing this, he also looked at Xu Fu. "...Si... Si..." He was actually imitating Fusu's tone, but because he only had two small teeth in his mouth, he leaked air when he spoke, and couldn't make a complete sound. He looked a bit silly, but it made him look cute.

Even for Xu Fu, who didn't have much like or dislike for children, his heart softened slightly.

Ying Zheng pushed away the bamboo slips in front of him and stood up to walk to Xu Fu's side. Xu Fu, who originally wanted to hug Huhai, had to stop his movements. He thought the First Emperor of Qin would ask him how it felt to be promoted, but the next moment, he heard Ying Zheng ask, "Can you sleep at night in the Fengchang Temple?"

Do you think I would say it's hard to sleep?

A flash of light passed through Xu Fu's eyes, but his face was plain. "The bed is comfortable, and I fall asleep easily." After saying this, Xu Fu suddenly felt that what he said sounded like he was advertising the bedding in the Fengchang Temple.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but feel a little disappointed.

How could the Fengchang Temple compare to the palace? But after Xu Fu went to the Shu region, his adaptability seemed to have become stronger, and he was not very picky about the room in the Fengchang Temple.

However, Ying Zheng did not dwell on this. He ordered food to be served and was about to send Fusu and Huhai away, but Xu Fu suddenly bent down and picked up Huhai.

Huhai rubbed against Xu Fu's arms, his little head nodding constantly, as if he were a bit sleepy.

The current Huhai was much stronger than when he was just born, his arms and legs had become like lotus roots, round and chubby, white and tender.

Perhaps it was because this appearance was too silly, so the words that reached Ying Zheng's lips took a turn, and he tacitly allowed Huhai to stay in the sleeping quarters.

The food was placed on the desk, and they each took their seats, forming a triangular position.

Xu Fu placed Huhai aside, and Huhai lay on the small quilt with his belly exposed. The palace maid wrapped him up more tightly, and then Xu Fu started to eat his own food.

Time passed unknowingly.

Xu Fu looked up inadvertently and found that the atmosphere in the palace was harmonious, warm, but strange.

...Why does it look so much like a family of four?

Xu Fu frowned.

Could this also be the conspiracy of the First Emperor of Qin?

A trick of boiling a frog in warm water!

Xu Fu felt that he had been challenged, so he decided to continue to stick to his original intention and be neither humble nor arrogant for a while, at least not so easily fall into the trap of the First Emperor of Qin.

After eating, an attendant entered the room, bowed, and said, "Your Majesty, the Empress Dowager is seriously ill."

Empress Dowager? Which Empress Dowager? Xu Fu was stunned for a moment before he realized that the Empress Dowager in the attendant's mouth should be the Empress Dowager Huayang who had some connection with the Xiong family.

After Ying Zheng washed his hands, he took people to Empress Dowager Huayang's palace.

Before leaving, Ying Zheng gave Xu Fu an instruction: "Do not leave the palace."

"Why can't I leave the palace?" Seeing Zhao Gao standing in the hall, Xu Fu asked Zhao Gao.

Zhao Gao smiled and said unhurriedly, "Young Master Xiong Yi is dead, and Lord Changping is dissatisfied. Now that Master Xu has become a Director, it is inevitable that Lord Changping will be unreasonable and insist on finding trouble with Master Xu."

Was this worrying that he would be implicated?

Xu Fu nodded. "Then I won't go to the Fengchang Temple for the time being." Anyway, there was nothing to do in the Fengchang Temple, and he hadn't been skipping work for just a day or two.

Xu Fu suddenly stopped.

No... he seemed to have forgotten his agreement with Hou Sheng!

Xu Fu had to call Zhao Gao again. "Please call a little attendant for me; I need him to do something."

Although Xu Fu always had an aloof appearance, Zhao Gao knew that compared to respecting others, no one was better than Xu Fu. Although his tone was cold, the words he said always made people feel comfortable, and they couldn't help but give their all to complete the things he entrusted.

Zhao Gao called the attendant over, and Xu Fu hurriedly asked the attendant to go and apologize to Hou Sheng.

Hearing the name Hou Sheng, Zhao Gao said in surprise, "Him? Does he have an agreement with Master Xu?"

Xu Fu nodded and asked, "Why?"

"This person is difficult to deal with. If there is any friction with Master Xu, Master Xu must not bury it in your heart. The King will definitely be able to get justice for Master Xu." Zhao Gao calmly put gold on Ying Zheng's face.

Xu Fu shook his head. "Grand Diviner Hou can't do anything..."

Zhao Gao stopped at the right point and didn't say any more to annoy Xu Fu.

After nightfall, Xu Fu washed up, changed his clothes, and went to bed, but he couldn't wait for Ying Zheng to return for a long time.

Could it be that Empress Dowager Huayang's situation was really not good?

Xu Fu felt a bit worried involuntarily.

If it were before, he would be full of sleepiness when lying on the bed; how could he spare any thought for Ying Zheng? Now his thoughts had undergone changes that he hadn't even noticed himself.

Xu Fu, who was a little irritable from waiting, forced himself to close his eyes and finally fell asleep.

When he woke up the next day, he didn't see Ying Zheng, and the palace servants served him to change, wash, and eat. Just as Xu Fu was thinking about what to do to pass the time, an attendant came in and whispered, "Director Xu was asleep yesterday, so I didn't dare to disturb Director Xu. Grand Diviner Hou has something to give to Director Xu."

As he said this, the attendant took a bamboo slip from his sleeve.

Xu Fu spread out the bamboo slip and saw a few sentences engraved on it. The gist was that Hou Sheng wanted to play a big game with him. They would not divine the weather, nor the fortune of the country; they would just find a person at random and divine that person's future. After a few years, if the prophecy for that person was fulfilled, then the loser would have to admit that their skills were inferior.

A few decades...

He was more patient than Wang Liu.

Was he really going to play a big game?

Xu Fu became interested.

Since coming to the Qin State, there was only one person he had seriously read the face of. That was the First Emperor of Qin. Now it seemed that he could find another person to study their physiognomy carefully.

Should he look at Huhai's? Or Fusu's?

However, he already knew the fate of Huhai and Fusu, and that Zhao Gao... although he didn't remember it clearly, he knew a little bit, which was not very interesting.

Who else was there? Xu Fu couldn't think of anyone for the time being. It would be better to just pick someone he met on the street one day.

The more Xu Fu thought about it, the more he felt like rubbing his hands.

After returning from the Shu region, he had just recovered, and now was the time to test his physiognomy level.

Xu Fu couldn't stay in the palace, but Ying Zheng hadn't returned, and he didn't want to give the First Emperor of Qin no face at all, just lifting his robes and leaving. Wouldn't that be showing no regard for the First Emperor of Qin? Now that his biggest back door hadn't been opened much, if he angered the First Emperor of Qin, wouldn't that be a bad deal?

Xu Fu suppressed his restlessness and simply went to the side hall to tease little Huhai. Accompanied by Fusu's clear recitation, time passed unknowingly.

When it was time for dinner, Xu Fu finally heard an attendant shout, "Your Majesty!"

He saw Ying Zheng striding into the room, and before long, he walked to Xu Fu's side. Xu Fu looked up, and before he could show any heartache to pretend to comfort the First Emperor of Qin, he suddenly realized that there was no look of sorrow or trouble on the First Emperor of Qin's face; on the contrary—

The Ying Zheng in front of him was radiant, his eyes smiling, and the corners of his mouth slightly raised.

He waved his hand and said, "Bring up the things I have searched for."

An attendant responded and hurriedly bowed to pour some things in front of Xu Fu. Xu Fu looked closely and was stunned: strange-looking herbs, weird-colored stones, bright red cinnabar, and some ancient bamboo slips, on one of which the two words "Alchemy" could be faintly glimpsed.

Xu Fu was stunned.

Ying Zheng said, "Didn't you want to use that cauldron to refine alchemy? I have searched for these things for you. If you think it's not enough, I will order people to search for more."

Xu Fu was stunned.

He... he was just saying it for fun...

Would he be made into a terracotta warrior if he bluffed the First Emperor of Qin?

The truth that Xu Fu was about to say was blocked back.

Forget it, since he had already played the role of a charlatan, what was wrong with alchemy? If he put on a show, the cauldron would be put to good use. As long as he didn't give those pills to anyone to eat, it would be fine.

Of course, Xu Fu didn't think he could refine any pills.

Fusu saw the things on the desk and exclaimed, "Teacher is so knowledgeable that you even know the art of medicine."

Xu Fu pretended to be calm and unruffled. He picked up the bamboo slips, flipped through them, and put them back. "Put them away."

The attendant hurriedly put these things away, but they were placed in the First Emperor of Qin's sleeping quarters, as if it were already assumed that the place where Xu Fu lived was here.

Only then did Xu Fu have time to ask about Empress Dowager Huayang. "Your Majesty, how is Empress Dowager Huayang?"

Ying Zheng was not displeased by the inquiry. He knelt beside Xu Fu and said, "The Empress Dowager is old, and it is common for her to be seriously ill now, but Lord Changping wants to make a fuss about this matter to seek justice from me for his son."

"Did Xiong Yi really die?" Xu Fu had forgotten Xiong Yi completely and didn't know why he had disappeared when they left the County Governor's Mansion.

"Dead." Ying Zheng paused. "Jianjia watched him die."

Jianjia?

Thinking of that beautiful face that matched his name, Xu Fu couldn't imagine how such a person could kill someone.

"How does Lord Changping want to seek justice?"

Ying Zheng said gloomily, "Lord Changping told the Empress Dowager that you were with Xiong Yi, and no matter what, you cannot escape the relationship." He had actually chosen the better words to say; one had to know that what Lord Changping said at the time was even uglier. In his words, he was accusing Xu Fu of using his beauty to harm his son and causing his son's death. Chen Hui was wrong, and Xu Fu was also wrong!

Xu Fu should also be imprisoned!

Ying Zheng's heart was even gloomier.

How could he not know what Lord Changping was thinking?

Wasn't it just trying his best to drag someone else into the water to calm the hatred in his heart?

The more Ying Zheng thought about it, the more annoyed he became.

Those who are not of my race must have different hearts!

Lord Changping must die sooner or later!

Author's note:

A piece of historical data from the Records of the Grand Historian: In the 32nd year (215 BC), Han Zhong, Hou Gong, and Shi Sheng were sent to search for the elixir of immortality.

Xu Fu was not surprised; shameless people could always refresh your perception of their bottom line. Lord Changping had lost his most beloved son, so it would be strange if he didn't vent his anger now.

"Does he want me to offer a life to Xiong Yi? Or what exactly does he want?" Xu Fu asked unhurriedly.

Ying Zheng did not answer this question, instead saying, "Whether Lord Changping wants it or not, it depends on whether I am willing to give it." Ying Zheng’s tone was as flat as when he had first recounted the events, but having spent many days with him, how could Xu Fu fail to hear the chilling undertone in his words?

For some reason, he found it quite domineering...

Xu Fu looked away.

Ying Zheng did not mention Lord Changping again; mentioning such a person was merely annoying.

Xu Fu felt no concern for his own safety because he had given Ying Zheng his full trust. If there were anyone capable of killing him right under the nose of the First Emperor... well, generally, that "if" didn't exist, and those who did reach that point were eventually finished off by the First Emperor in various ways.

It was just that he wondered about Hou Sheng...

If Lord Changping refused to let things rest in a few days, he couldn't hide in the Xianyang Palace forever; he would eventually have to go out. At that time, he would go and fulfill his bet with Hou Sheng. Surely Hou Sheng could afford to wait a few days...

Xu Fu did not know that Hou Sheng, unable to catch a glimpse of him at the Fengchang Temple, was feeling incredibly stifled. It was as if he had made full preparations and gathered all his strength, only to land a punch on a pile of cotton.

...

Ying Zheng went to visit the Empress Dowager Huayang every day, so his time was naturally occupied. After a few days, Lord Changping claimed illness and stopped attending court, yet he spent every day outside the Xianyang Palace crying and wailing to Ying Zheng, making a scene and talking incessantly about his accidentally deceased son. Just looking at him, it was truly a heartbreaking sight. While Lord Changping was certainly resentful over Xiong Yi's death, it wasn't nearly as severe as he portrayed. What he was thinking about more was how to deal with Ying Zheng, how to extract benefits from him, how to drag others into the mess, and how to avenge Xiong Yi.

On this day, finding no way to reach Ying Zheng, Lord Changping took his grievances to the sickbed of Empress Dowager Huayang.

Empress Dowager Huayang was old. A few days prior, she had heard Lord Changping say his son had died, but she had been in a delirious state from illness with no energy to spare, so she hadn't heard it clearly. Only now did she realize that Xiong Yi was dead.

Because they were from the same state, Empress Dowager Huayang had been very fond of the handsome and dashing Xiong Yi. Standing in the position of an elder, she had cared for him quite a bit. Hearing this news, she was stunned on the spot.

"Xiong Yi... Xiong Yi..." Empress Dowager Huayang called out twice, but before she could catch her breath, she collapsed. The palace attendants were instantly thrown into a panic.

Lord Changping was also stunned.

He had come to cry and complain; he never expected such a consequence.

At this moment, Ying Zheng strode in, his face cold, and he sternly rebuked, "What is Lord Changping doing? Just because you lost a son, must you leave the Qin state without an Empress Dowager!"

This accusation was extremely severe, escalating the matter from a personal family affair to the level of the state.

Empress Dowager Huayang might not have been universally supported in Qin, but she was, after all, the Empress Dowager of the Qin royal family. Now that news of Lord Changping causing her to faint had spread, it would inevitably incite the dissatisfaction of the commoners, officials, and the royal clan.

Lord Changping had not considered this at all.

Or rather, he didn't care about the Empress Dowager's health; he was only calculating his own interests, so how could he have spared a thought for her condition? It was no surprise that things had reached such an awkward impasse.

"Your Majesty... Your Majesty..." Lord Changping stammered, the sorrow on his face not yet faded, but his recent actions had made that sorrow look ridiculous.

Ying Zheng summoned the imperial physicians to treat the Empress Dowager before turning his gaze to Lord Changping.

"It seems that Lord Changping acts as he pleases and no longer holds the Qin royal family in his eyes. In that case, please return home and rest for a while, and don't come back until your head is clear!" Ying Zheng's words were extremely harsh, much like someone in later generations telling another person they were brain-damaged and needed to take some medicine.

Lord Changping was dumbfounded; the muscles in his face twitched, unable to form a normal expression for a long time.

He hadn't expected Ying Zheng to show him so little face, rebuking him in front of so many palace attendants.

Yet Lord Changping didn't stop to think: he claimed illness to avoid court, yet ran to the Empress Dowager to make a scene—was that giving Ying Zheng any face? Since he didn't show respect, Ying Zheng didn't hesitate to slap him back hard.

An attendant stepped forward to escort Lord Changping out, and he had no choice but to leave in disgrace.

A day later, the news that Lord Changping had deliberately wailed before the Empress Dowager, causing her to fall seriously ill, spread throughout Xianyang City.

Lord Changping's prestige quickly plummeted.

In the past, Lord Changping could hold his own in court only because Ying Zheng was young and lacked power, and even then, he had to fear Lü Buwei and Lao Ai. Now that those two were gone, Lord Changping had lost his vigilance and acted recklessly, never imagining that the people of Qin would naturally support the Qin royal family—did he really think they would side with him, a member of the Chu royal family?

Once this happened, some even began to vaguely suspect that Lord Changping harbored ulterior motives and was plotting for the state of Chu. His past achievements were thus erased.

If only the officials were dissatisfied, it wouldn't have reached this point, but rumors began to circulate among the commoners. Soon, gossip about Lord Changping was everywhere in Xianyang. Using the power of the people to dismantle the good image Lord Changping had spent years building was effortless.

After returning home, Lord Changping quieted down. He knew that Ying Zheng's silence over the past few days wasn't out of guilt or concession, but because he simply didn't want to bother with him. Lord Changping gritted his teeth in secret. If he hadn't accidentally caused the Empress Dowager to faint, he wouldn't have ended up in this state. He had originally had a perfect excuse to pull Xu Fu, whom Ying Zheng was protecting, out of his grasp.

The mere thought of Xu Fu filled Lord Changping with bitter hatred.

They had gone to the Shu region together, yet only he returned—how could he not be hateful?

...

Xu Fu did not know how Lord Changping was plotting against him behind his back. Seeing that Lord Changping had quieted down, he went to the Fengchang Temple on schedule.

Hou Sheng finally caught up with him at the temple, but since they worked in different areas, it was hard to run into each other. Xu Fu wouldn't go out of his way to find Hou Sheng; looking at that rigid face wasn't exactly pleasant.

After finishing his daily tasks, Hou Sheng tried to find Xu Fu, but missed him again.

"There's a banquet today, does Director Xu have any free time?" Su Yi asked as he walked alongside Xu Fu toward the exit of the Fengchang Temple.

Su Yi had asked him several times already; he couldn't keep refusing. They had a good relationship, and they should interact more. Xu Fu didn't hesitate and nodded in agreement. After walking out of the temple, he was about to inform the attendant that he wouldn't be returning to the Xianyang Palace today, but the attendant smiled and said, "That's perfect, why don't I just take you both there?"

Su Yi had never ridden in a palace carriage before. After sitting down with Xu Fu, he couldn't help but frown, saying, "I'm riding with Director Xu; there shouldn't be any trouble, right?"

"What trouble could there be?" Xu Fu comforted him, "It's fine."

Xu Fu had come to see Su Yi's honest nature. At first glance, he seemed hard to get along with, but in reality, Su Yi was the most suitable person to be friends with. Su Yi came from a good background and was a staunch supporter of King Zheng of Qin. His temperament was neither hot nor cold; he could be stubborn and serious at times, but he was sincere to his friends and didn't care for showing off.

Counting it all up, he was full of virtues and was a perfect match for Xu Fu.

At the very least, in terms of political stance, they were both on the King of Qin's side.

Just as Xu Fu and Su Yi left, Wang Liu arrived and missed them as well.

When Xu Fu arrived at Su Yi's residence, the house was empty, save for the servants coming and going.

"It's spring, so my family often goes out to enjoy the season..." Su Yi explained, then led Xu Fu inside.

After they were seated, the servants quickly brought out food.

Su Yi asked, "Does Director Xu know that today, at court, His Majesty ordered a search for officials from the other six states serving in Qin, and once found, they are to be expelled from the Qin state..."

Xu Fu felt this sounded familiar; it seemed to be a part mentioned in history books.

Su Yi continued, "I wonder if it's because of the matter with Lord Changping..." Su Yi stopped there. Further than that, it wasn't for someone in his position to gossip about.

Expelling people from the six states?

The first person Xu Fu thought of was Hou Sheng. Didn't Hou Sheng come from the state of Han? Would he be expelled tomorrow? Would their bet be rendered void?

Su Yi didn't know what Xu Fu was thinking. The agreement between Xu Fu and Hou Sheng was unknown to anyone else in the Fengchang Temple. Their bet wasn't meant to make the other lose face; viewed with a normal heart, it was just a friendly exchange of skills.

"I have a friend I'd like to introduce to Director Xu another day..." Su Yi wasn't good at recommending friends and stopped halfway, perhaps feeling a bit shy.

Though, with Su Yi's face, one couldn't really see an expression of shyness.

"Sure." Xu Fu agreed quickly. Su Yi's friends shouldn't be people of low character.

In this era, friends introducing friends to each other was quite common; Xu Fu saw no reason to refuse.

Su Yi nodded and smiled, chatting about trivial things while they ate. He even asked what food Xu Fu liked and if he enjoyed flowers—strange questions... If it weren't for the fact that Su Yi's face showed no change in expression, Xu Fu would have suspected he was trying to set him up on a blind date. Why the sudden interest in these things?

Xu Fu didn't connect Su Yi's behavior to the "fan culture" of later generations.

Come to think of it, wasn't that exactly what fans did when chasing after their idols?

After the meal, Su Yi personally saw Xu Fu to the door and pulled a bamboo slip from his sleeve, saying, "It's of no use to me, but I hope it can be of use to you, Director."

He hadn't expected to get a free meal and walk away with a bamboo slip. It would be rude to open it right then, so Xu Fu tucked it away, bid farewell to Su Yi, and boarded the carriage. As the carriage traveled down the street, Xu Fu called for a stop when they passed a small stall.

Although the food in the palace was good, it couldn't compare to the many delicacies of his past life. Catching a whiff of a fragrant scent, Xu Fu lifted the curtain and told the attendant to go buy some snacks.

The attendant had been instructed by Ying Zheng to obey whatever Xu Fu requested.

So the attendant went to buy the food while Xu Fu watched from the curtain.

When the attendant returned, Xu Fu saw it was just a roasted pancake. He didn't know how the vendor made it, but it had a rich, savory aroma. He didn't plan on saving any for Ying Zheng.

The First Emperor wouldn't eat such roadside snacks, would he?

Xu Fu broke off a piece of the pancake and put it in his mouth.

The attendant secretly thought, "Director Xu bought a pancake... could it be to feed a dog?"

The attendant never imagined that Xu Fu, who had such a noble and ethereal face, possessed a heart that was so grounded and enjoyed the simple pleasures of life.

The carriage started moving again, but after a short while, Xu Fu heard someone calling from behind, "Wait... wait..."

Were they calling them? As Xu Fu wondered, the attendant stopped the carriage.

The attendant lifted the curtain and said, "Director Xu, someone is calling for you outside."

"Who?" Xu Fu poked his head out and saw a handsome young man walking quickly toward them, his gaze fixed directly on him.

When the young man drew near, he cupped his hands and asked politely, "Are you Director Xu?"

Xu Fu didn't nod immediately. He looked the young man over, confirmed he hadn't met him before, and asked, "And you are?"

The man smiled, his eyes filled with a scholarly air that made one feel at ease. "I once witnessed Director Xu's demeanor during the Wax Festival and have never forgotten it."

Xu Fu felt a flash of surprise. Could he actually be a fan?

"Is there something you need?" Xu Fu, unsure of the man's identity, asked cautiously.

"I wish to ask Director Xu to cast a divination for me." The man bowed from afar, his tone filled with just the right amount of expectation and reverence.

"You want me to cast a divination for you?" Xu Fu was even more surprised. It seemed this person had come fully prepared; not only did he know who he was, but he had tracked him down and dared to ask for a reading.

If it were any other diviner in the Fengchang Temple, they might have scolded the man and driven him away, but Xu Fu didn't feel it was shameful to read the fortune of an unknown person.

Xu Fu's mind flashed to his bet with Hou Sheng, and he became interested. He carefully studied the man's face and secretly formed an idea.

Divining a person's future.

Why not choose this person?

Xu Fu lowered the curtain and instructed, "Turn into the alley so we can talk."

The attendant nodded and hurried the carriage into a nearby alley. Seeing this, the smile on the man's lips widened slightly.

Once inside the alley, Xu Fu stepped out of the carriage and asked Li Si to come closer.

The man hadn't expected Xu Fu to be so easygoing, agreeing to the divination just like that. He suppressed the shock on his face and bowed to Xu Fu again. "Thank you, Director Xu."

"What kind of divination do you want me to perform?" Xu Fu asked while scanning his face.

The man accepted his scrutiny with poise and said, "I was once a minor official in another state, then studied under Master Xun, and later drifted to the Qin state. What I seek is merely to realize my ambitions. Yet, I have long failed to achieve my desires. I do not know if I am destined to never obtain what I seek. I ask Director Xu to cast a divination for my future."

Xu Fu withdrew his gaze and said calmly, "Looking at your mouth, nose, ears, and eyes—thin lips and long mouth lines—you have the face of an eloquent debater. With that mouth of yours, you should be able to rival an army of thousands."

The man was startled for a moment, then smiled. "Director, you jest. How could I compare to an army of thousands?"

Xu Fu ignored him and continued, "Straight nose—you are stubborn and firm in your heart. I see that even if you cannot achieve your desires now, you will not easily give up."

The man smiled, his face showing no embarrassment at having his pretense of sorrow seen through.

"Your eyes are clear, sharp, and steady; you can endure, and you can achieve great things."

The man smiled again.

"Achieve great things"—it sounded like the nonsense a street fortune-teller would use to fool people, but the man knew clearly that the person before him wasn't a fraud. His heart pounded in his chest; for once, the man felt a hint of nervousness.

Xu Fu added the second half of the sentence calmly, "However, the corners of your eyes are narrow; your heart is not as broad as your appearance suggests. You are prone to straying from the path and can be ruthless in your actions."

This was not a compliment.

The man's expression changed slightly, but he maintained his smile, looking as if he wanted to hear Xu Fu continue.

"Your eyebrows are full in shape but sparse; they cannot contain your momentum. In your later years, you will likely face great ups and downs."

"Your ears are thin, but the lobes are full—a sign of good fortune."

"The three regions and five peaks of your face indicate a path to high office."

"Your posture is upright, your demeanor is imposing—a sign of nobility."

...

The man slowly let out a breath, terrified that Xu Fu would say something like the previous remark again.

Finally, Xu Fu's gaze landed on the man's brow, the center of the life palace. Xu Fu said, "The life palace is slightly raised, a sign of abundance." Xu Fu paused, "The Ziwei star palace is in turmoil..."

Xu Fu stopped halfway through.

The man's appetite had been whetted; how could he refrain from asking? Even a composed person couldn't help but ask, "And what will happen?"

"With the help of a noble person, you will climb to a high position," Xu Fu finally said. Xu Fu felt a bit sour inside. He hadn't expected everyone's physiognomy to be so good; it was a pity he couldn't see anything on his own face. If only he had such a wealthy destiny, though that destiny of reaching the pinnacle of officialdom didn't suit him. At most, he would just be a State Preceptor.

"Thank you, Director Xu," the man bowed.

"Can you tell me your name now?" Xu Fu asked coldly.

The man finally realized that his failure to introduce himself had displeased Xu Fu and hurriedly said, "I am Li Si."

Li Si? Had he heard wrong? Or was this truly that Great Qin Chancellor?

Combining this with the physiognomy he had just seen, it seemed very likely...

Just as Xu Fu was stunned, he heard the man say, "I have one more thing to ask of Director Xu."

"What is it?" Xu Fu muttered to himself. He had already given the man the information he wanted in those words; was he still not satisfied?

The man suddenly bowed deeply to Xu Fu and said loudly, "Please, Director, be my noble person."

Xu Fu was startled and frowned, "Be your noble person? I am not the noble person you seek."

"No." The man said with resonant conviction: "Si's noble patron is the Dian-shi. Since the Dian-shi has cast this hexagram for me, the Dian-shi's prophecy is the word of my patron. I beg the Dian-shi to introduce me to the King; then, what the Dian-shi has said will immediately come to pass."

Xu Fu: ...

His expression was somewhat complex.

This man's mind was truly too clever!

It seemed now that the fortune-telling was a ruse, and the introduction was the true goal.

But why did he seek him out? Xu Fu felt puzzled.

"Si's noble patron is the Dian-shi; I beg the Dian-shi to introduce me," the man said again, showing no sign of shame.

"What could I possibly introduce you for? I am but a lowly Dian-shi who cannot even step into the royal court; how could I introduce you to anyone?" After saying this, Xu Fu turned to board his carriage.

The man, however, would not give up. He bowed his head and said, "If the Dian-shi leaves, Si will have lost his noble patron, and the Dian-shi's prophecy may never come to pass..." He paused, then added, "Is the value of the Dian-shi in the King's heart something that can be measured by whether or not one attends court?"

Xu Fu paused his steps. He felt that ever since he had glimpsed the thoughts of Qin Shi Huang, it seemed everyone was speaking well of the King.

Very well, if this truly was the historical Li Si, then he ought to meet Qin Shi Huang.

"I can introduce you, but what happens afterward is beyond my help." Xu Fu stepped into the carriage and lowered the curtain. "Come earlier than this tomorrow and wait for me at the gate of Xianyang Palace." With that, Xu Fu ordered the attendant to drive the carriage away.

The man let out a sigh of relief, the smile in his eyes lingering for a long time.

He... had won the gamble!

...

Once inside the carriage, Xu Fu cursed under his breath. What a forced sale!

He had read the man's physiognomy, and in the end, he had muddled his way into becoming the man's "noble patron." If he didn't lend a hand, it felt as if he would be disrupting the other's destiny.

He had never seen such a thing—you handle the fortune-telling, and you're expected to handle the job placement too!

Xu Fu felt stifled, but he had to admit that the man was truly clever, knowing how to seize the opportunity and stir things up to achieve his goal.

Then let him see if he truly was this man's noble patron, and if this man was indeed that future Chancellor, Li Si!

·

To make an introduction, he naturally had to notify Qin Shi Huang first. Xu Fu had become a frequent guest at Xianyang Palace and had become the "vermilion mole" on Qin Shi Huang's heart, but that didn't mean he could treat the place as his own territory.

He was even less than those women.

Those women could eventually enter the inner palace and could barely be considered future mistresses of Xianyang Palace.

He was nothing; just a temporary guest. Therefore, many things had to be done according to protocol so as not to disrupt the rules or become a nuisance. One should always know their place, no matter where they are.

Xu Fu returned to the palace quite late today. Ying Zheng had finished his evening meal alone with a dark expression, while Fusu was off to the side looking after the brat Huhai. When Xu Fu entered the hall, he saw Ying Zheng sitting coldly before his desk.

"Your Majesty," Xu Fu called out.

Ying Zheng looked up at him, his gaze softening slightly, but his tone remained somewhat cold. "Why so late today?"

Xu Fu considered whether to reveal Su Yi, but ultimately said vaguely, "A colleague invited me to a banquet, and on my way back to the palace, I encountered someone who stopped my carriage."

"Who was so bold?" Ying Zheng asked, displeased, thinking someone had offended Xu Fu.

Seeing Ying Zheng's unhappy expression, Xu Fu worried that the man might have a bad impression before even meeting the King, so he hurriedly said, "It was just someone seeking my help with a matter."

"Even if they seek your help, they shouldn't be so reckless." Ying Zheng frowned, but seeing that Xu Fu didn't take it to heart, he didn't press the matter further.

"Speaking of which, the matter he asked of me has something to do with Your Majesty."

"What is it?"

"The man's name is Li Si. He was once a minor official in another state, later studied under Xun Qing of Zhao, and then came to Qin to serve as a minor official. He is full of ambition but has no way to display it, so he asked me to introduce him to Your Majesty." Xu Fu didn't add any embellishments; he relayed exactly what the man had said to avoid the suspicion of intentionally promoting others.

If this Li Si truly had talent, he figured Qin Shi Huang wouldn't miss such a person.

"Studied under Xun Qing?" Ying Zheng became somewhat interested. Xun Qing was quite famous among the seven states, though Ying Zheng had a lukewarm opinion of Confucian theories; otherwise, he would have been even more interested in Li Si. "What great theory does he wish to present to me?"

Xu Fu shook his head. "I didn't ask. It's not my area of expertise, and even if he told me, I wouldn't understand it. I just told him to wait for me outside Xianyang Palace tomorrow."

Ying Zheng nodded. "I understand."

He would naturally have someone else investigate this Li Si. Once Li Si's background was verified, he would summon him to see what kind of talent he truly possessed.

Regardless of Li Si's actual ability, just the fact that Xu Fu had mentioned him was enough for Ying Zheng to give Xu Fu this favor.

After finishing the discussion about Li Si, Xu Fu went to bathe and change before getting into bed.

Ying Zheng sat on the other side, frowning.

The name Li Si... it seemed he had heard it from Fusu last time? But Fusu was just a child, how would he know Li Si? If Xu Fu hadn't mentioned him, he wouldn't have known this person either. Fusu must have just said it casually, right? Living in the royal palace, how would he know such a nobody? Ying Zheng stood up, preparing to bathe and change as well so he could sleep comfortably on the same couch as Xu Fu. But before he could even take off his robes, an attendant rushed in to report that the Empress Dowager Huayang was critically ill.

A dark glint flashed in Ying Zheng's eyes. He immediately rushed out of the door, taking his men toward the palace of Empress Dowager Huayang.

Xu Fu was tired today and didn't notice that Ying Zheng hadn't come to bed, drifting off into a hazy sleep.

The next morning, Xu Fu saw Ying Zheng just walking out from behind the curtain after bathing. It was spring, and with the charcoal burning in the palace, it wasn't cold. Ying Zheng was only loosely draped in his robe, and Xu Fu suddenly caught sight of Ying Zheng's long, bare legs, as well as his chest and abdominal muscles half-hidden behind the loose fabric. A powerful strength seemed to be hidden within his body.

Xu Fu had to objectively admit that it was quite intoxicating.

And yet, even a Qin Shi Huang like this had a mistress who cheated on him.

Could it be that his performance in bed was poor?

He looked like he had such a strong and powerful physique; he shouldn't be weak in that department...

Ying Zheng watched as Xu Fu stared at his body with a strange expression. He took two steps forward, his domineering aura enveloping Xu Fu. Xu Fu felt a bit sorry for himself; in front of Qin Shi Huang, he was still a bit short.

"Did you rest well?" Ying Zheng asked while reaching out to pull Xu Fu toward him.

Xu Fu dodged inadvertently, thinking to himself once again that this was another one of Qin Shi Huang's schemes! Bathing in the morning and dressing so seductively, just waiting for him to wake up—if this wasn't a scheme, what was? Hah, naive. Was he, Xu Fu, the type of person to be seduced by the flesh?

"Did Your Majesty leave the palace last night?" Xu Fu feigned nonchalance to steer the conversation, taking the initiative in the questioning.

"Yes, the Empress Dowager is critically ill." At this, Ying Zheng lost the smile on his face, his expression becoming somber.

As for this Empress Dowager Huayang, Ying Zheng respected her to a degree, but not much more. She was his father's foster mother, and it was because of her that his father was able to ascend the throne, which in turn allowed him to inherit the position of King of Qin. Otherwise, with his grandfather being so promiscuous and having so many heirs, it would never have been their branch's turn. Ying Zheng was not someone who didn't know how to repay kindness, so he had always given her sufficient respect, and no one in the palace dared to slight her.

But who could have imagined that Empress Dowager Huayang's illness was actually caused by being frightened by Lord Changping, who was from the same state as her?

If the Empress Dowager were to pass away, the label of offending her would be permanently stuck to Lord Changping.

But Ying Zheng shook his head inwardly. It wasn't time for Lord Changping to die yet. He had just been appointed Chancellor, and his abilities hadn't been fully utilized. Ying Zheng felt that letting him off so easily before squeezing him dry would be doing him a favor.

"Your Majesty has been very busy these days, please get some rest." Xu Fu suddenly turned around, pushed the unsuspecting Ying Zheng down onto the couch to sit, and then turned and walked out of the hall.

Ying Zheng, who hadn't expected Xu Fu to act so unpredictably: ...

Xu Fu went straight to the Fengchang Temple to report, then found Hou Sheng. The others were secretly surprised and puzzled.

Now that the expulsion order had been issued, it was clear Hou Sheng wouldn't be staying at the Fengchang Temple for much longer. In the past, when Hou Sheng was the Taibu-cheng, Xu Fu had always clashed with him. Now that Hou Sheng's position was worthless, Xu Fu seemed to be on good terms with him; it was truly unfathomable.

Seeing Xu Fu approach, Hou Sheng stood up immediately and asked in a low voice, "Dian-shi Xu, do you have a question?"

Xu Fu shook his head. "I have no questions. I came to tell Taibu Hou that I have selected the person." As he spoke, Xu Fu raised the bamboo slip in his hand. "The commentary is here; please have a look, Taibu Hou."

"...Dian-shi Xu, so fast?" Hou Sheng frowned slightly, somewhat incredulous. He took the bamboo slip and opened it, seeing things written there that he had never seen or heard of before.

At this time, the method of physiognomy was not popular, and there were even few mentions of it. Hou Sheng had studied the orthodox methods of divination, so he naturally found what was written on the bamboo slip extremely strange.

"This..."

"Taibu Hou, take your time reading. Oh, the man's name is Li Si. I believe you will see him soon." After saying this, Xu Fu left.

He left Hou Sheng alone facing the bamboo slip, filled with doubt and disbelief. He couldn't believe how such a crude method could be used for divination.

If Qiu Ji were here, he would certainly use his own experience to tell Hou Sheng that it was all true!

·

Before the sun had set, Xu Fu had already left the Fengchang Temple. Yesterday, because of the interruption by Li Si, he hadn't been able to take more than a few bites of the baked cake he bought. Once he reached the palace, he couldn't eat it anymore, so the attendant had thrown it away. Today, he wanted to buy some more early.

But today, after the attendant bought it, he didn't hand it to Xu Fu.

Xu Fu couldn't help but lift the carriage curtain and ask, "Why don't you give that to me?"

The attendant smiled and said, "Such things would dirty the sleeves of the Dian-shi. It's just something to take back to feed the dogs; I will hold onto it."

Feed the dogs... feed the dogs... feed the dogs...

This phrase circled in Xu Fu's mind.

Did this baked cake look like something meant for dogs? Didn't the attendant see the tooth marks he had left on the unfinished cake yesterday?

It was all because Xu Fu had built such an otherworldly image that no one believed he would lower himself to eat such food.

Xu Fu could only sigh lightly, close his mouth, and hold back his frustration.

Lucky for the stray dogs outside the palace...

Xu Fu had the attendant drive back to the palace. Before long, he saw Li Si outside the palace gate. Li Si was dressed in white, meticulously groomed, holding bamboo slips, and exuding an air of scholarship that made one feel an immediate sense of goodwill.

Temperament could be deceptive.

Just like himself, and just like this black-bellied Li Si.

Li Si bowed to Xu Fu: "Dian-shi Xu, I wonder if the King is willing to see me?"

Before Xu Fu could speak, he saw an attendant walking quickly out of the palace. The attendant first smiled and called out "Dian-shi Xu," then looked at Li Si and asked, "Are you Li Si?"

Li Si nodded.

The attendant then said briskly, "The King has summoned you; follow me."

Li Si was stunned for a moment; he hadn't expected the process to be so smooth. Then, with a smile on his lips, he bade farewell to Xu Fu and followed the attendant inside.

It seemed Qin Shi Huang had already arranged everything? It was good that he didn't have to worry about it. Xu Fu returned to the carriage, passed through the palace gate, entered the inner gate, and then got off the carriage to head toward the palace where the King of Qin handled state affairs. When Xu Fu was led inside, he found only Ying Zheng in the hall.

Where was Li Si?

Seeing the look of confusion on Xu Fu's face, Zhao Gao smiled and said, "Mr. Xu is looking for that Li Si, right? An attendant must have led him away to wash up. He is just a minor official; it's not that easy to enter the palace to see the King."

Xu Fu nodded, thinking to himself, why wasn't it that troublesome for him back then? But then he remembered that Qin Shi Huang had personally dragged him from the prison, so that step was probably skipped.

Li Si had the palace servants place a small couch and a table behind a screen. Xu Fu raised an eyebrow; this scene was very familiar.

Back when he and Qin Shi Huang were still wary of each other, he had spent his days in this hall, leaning on a small couch and eavesdropping on Qin Shi Huang's conversations with others. It seemed Qin Shi Huang had prepared this specifically for him, to make it convenient for him to eavesdrop on the conversation between the King and Li Si?

A palace maid smiled and led Xu Fu behind the screen.

Ying Zheng put down the bamboo slip in his hand and even comforted him, "Wait for me a little longer. There is an evening meal made from food brought from another state; we will be able to eat it soon."

Xu Fu nodded. He wasn't that obsessed with the evening meal, and now that he could listen to some gossip, what was wrong with that?

Xu Fu arrived behind the screen, and before long, Li Si was led in by an attendant.

Li Si bowed deeply to Ying Zheng, first expressing his respect for the King of Qin, then stood up. Although he kept his head slightly lowered to avoid looking directly at Ying Zheng and causing offense, his whole body exuded a sense of neither arrogance nor servility.

Ying Zheng had always appreciated such people, and his first impression was quite good.

"Since you have come to see me, if you have anything to say, speak your mind."

Li Si did not hide anything, stepped forward, and said: "Si once caught a glimpse of Your Majesty, and was captivated by your heroic bearing..."

Xu Fu felt strange listening from behind the screen.

Why did this opening sound so much like a confession of love?

But the ancients always spoke of admiration, affection, and infatuation... it was very cheesy. How many ancients had become soulmates by speaking like this? It wasn't strange for Li Si to speak this way. It was just that he felt it was weird... Xu Fu calmed his mind and continued to listen.

Li Si first praised Ying Zheng's achievements and actions, then concluded: "With such ambition, how could Your Majesty be satisfied with just strengthening Qin? The rulers of Qin have been wise and virtuous; who among the other six states can compare? Now that the six states are weak, it is the perfect opportunity!"

"Oh? What kind of opportunity?" Ying Zheng was not moved by these shallow words, so he remained in a state of observation.

Li Si still had a heart full of words left unsaid. Seeing Ying Zheng's indifferent attitude, he was not disappointed and continued: "Those who achieve great things are adept at seizing opportunities! During the time of Duke Mu of Qin, although Qin was strong, it failed to complete the great cause of unification, simply because the time was not yet ripe. Since Duke Xiao of Qin, the Zhou Emperor has completely declined, and the feudal states have been at war for years, while Qin has gradually grown stronger. Now that Qin is powerful and Your Majesty is virtuous, destroying the six states will be as easy as sweeping dust off a stove..."

Li Si spoke with a certain passion.

And Xu Fu, behind the screen, curled his lip in secret.

He had already used these words to fool Qin Shi Huang when he was competing with Wang Liu in fortune-telling; these empty words didn't work anymore.

Li Si did not know that long before him, there was a "cheater" named Xu Fu who had already spoken these words into Qin Shi Huang's heart, so this passionate speech could not elicit much of a reaction from Ying Zheng.

"...Now is the best time to complete the imperial cause and unify the world; Your Majesty must not miss it!" Li Si finished in one breath and looked up, but did not see Ying Zheng's eyes shining or his spirit stirred.

Failing to achieve the expected effect, Li Si was stunned.

But if he were to retreat easily, he wouldn't be Li Si. This was just an initial attempt to leave a good impression on the King of Qin.

Moreover, Li Si thought to himself, the King of Qin was truly composed. If it were the king of another state, just hearing this speech—regardless of whether it was practical—would have made them feel stirred, eager to draw their swords and sweep across the other states.

He didn't believe the King of Qin lacked such ambition; he could only say that the King of Qin was deep and calculating, not easily moved by external things. To move him, he would have to bring out more useful talent...

"I have heard these words from someone else before," Ying Zheng said.

Li Si was stunned. Had someone already beaten him to it? Faster than him? Who could it be? His rival?

Ying Zheng paused, then said slowly: "A few months ago, Dian-shi Xu of the Fengchang Temple cast a hexagram for me. Do you know what the hexagram was?"

"...What was it?" Li Si was confused and didn't understand. But hearing the name of Dian-shi Xu, his heart tightened involuntarily. Could it be that the person who beat him to it was Xu Fu? Li Si was astonished! He was clearly just a Taibu, yet he possessed such talent! His strategic vision must be incredibly far-reaching!

Such a person...

Li Si felt a slight excitement in his heart.

Sure enough, Qin was the place he should have come to!

Only here, by gathering the great talents of the world, could he display his abilities, conquer the states, and have the opportunity to realize his ambitions!
