龙阳君歪了歪头，看了一眼桑中。
桑中便立刻闭嘴，放下了车帘。做主的人是徐福，无论如何，他都不应该说出这样的话来。
徐福倒是点了点头，“我的确无处收留龙阳君。”王宫并非他的住所，他无权将龙阳君带进去。这时徐福才想起来，顺手把龙阳君带出来，倒成了个麻烦。
徐福不由得看向了蒹葭。
蹲在马车口的蒹葭无辜回望徐福。
他也不管龙阳君带走有什么后果。
……他只管带人走啊。
此时龙阳君才慢悠悠地道：“龙阳已随使臣离开大梁城，使臣如今却是不打算负半点责吗？”
负责？
蒹葭和桑中几乎是同时都竖起了耳朵。
徐福哪里是好撩拨的？龙阳再如何说，他也不会有半分为其所动。徐福淡淡地掀了掀眼皮，“我带你从魏王宫出来，一部分是为了看看你的命途还能有何变化，一部分是为了气一气那魏王。但你敢说，你当时心中没有半分主动吗？若是我强迫将龙阳君带出来了，我自然对龙阳君负责。”
从进了驿馆，徐福就觉得龙阳君身上的气息瞧上去有点不对劲了。等上了马车，龙阳君慢悠悠说出这句话来，徐福才发觉到龙阳君身上的违和之处在哪里。
什么冷漠，什么孤傲，都是在演戏。
这副模样才是隐藏其中的真面孔吧？
那院子究竟是不是龙阳君的住处，也有待商榷了。
龙阳君察觉到徐福的目光冷了冷，这才点头道：“既如此，我便只有自寻落脚的地方了。”
这么轻易就松口？徐福顿时便觉得自己的猜测，应该没有错了。
不过的确是他将人带出来的，徐福还没有那样过分，将人带走，便丢开不理了。
徐福指了指一旁的蒹葭，“若是蒹葭同意，龙阳君便可到蒹葭府中借宿。”
蒹葭有点懵，全然没想到，自己一个旁观者看戏看得好好的，怎么突然就被拉入战场中了。
龙阳君的目光随着徐福的动作，落到了蒹葭的身上，“那便有劳……”
蒹葭犹豫一下，还是点了点头。
他一个人住，多个人倒也无妨。
虽然定下了龙阳君的去向，但是徐福却对这个历史上记载的人更为好奇，也更为警惕了。龙阳君，“君”乃爵位。向来都是王室亲属才能称为“君”。能从魏王男宠晋升为魏国的龙阳君。他应该并不如表现出的那样形象单薄才是。
不过徐福对于龙阳君在历史的记载，了解并不多。
哪怕是在来到魏国之前，他都没想到龙阳君便是魏王的男宠。
将龙阳君放在蒹葭身边便最合适了。
蒹葭四人都是十分警惕之人，若是龙阳君有什么动向，蒹葭一定很快便注意到了。
徐福可以对龙阳君好奇，但他却不能因为一个龙阳君，把秦始皇给坑了。所以还是提防着些为好。
龙阳君像是并未注意到徐福的目光一般，他神色淡淡地靠在车厢上，妩媚的面容，因为骤然冷下来的神情，倒是显得更为迷人了。
徐福忍不住将目光又落在了龙阳君的脸上。
龙阳君与郑妃倒是有些相似。
都是命途坎坷，变化极大的人，只是郑妃眼看着便是有吉讯了，而龙阳君却全然相反，是凶兆。
若不是惋惜这样的美人，可能会因一场大病而夭亡，徐福怎么可能多嘴去提那样一句话？
大约是徐福盯着瞧的时间久了一些，龙阳君转过头来，忍不住问：“使臣，可是还有话要说？”
徐福面色不改地瞎扯，“瞧着你脸上厚重的妆容，有些晃眼。”
龙阳君笑道：“那如此看来，以后使臣也应当不会喜欢女子，而是偏爱男子了。”
徐福点头，不是以后，是他已经被掰弯了。
“使臣自己便生得如此出色，日后哪里还寻得着能与之相配的男儿呢？”
“自然不会是龙阳君这样的。”
龙阳君摇了摇头，脸上闪过惋惜之色。
……
他们一行人朝着另一座小城狂奔而去，马车一路颠簸，徐福就一边看着龙阳君卸下脸上的妆容，再脱下身上简陋的长裙，陡然便换了副模样。
不知不觉马车便停住了。
龙阳君放下袖子来，倒是又狠狠将人惊艳了一番。
龙阳君的相貌实在太好了。
徐福心中感叹一句。
蒹葭掀起车帘，请他们下车。
马车停在了一家小客栈外，客栈老板见了他们一行人，双眼登时就一亮。哪怕是千年前，客栈老板也无师自通，知道“名人效应”。虽然徐福和龙阳君都并非名人，但他们容貌出色啊，往门口一站，便能吸引来无数人。
李斯下了马车，大摇大摆地付了钱，带着人进了客栈去。
龙阳君见状，好奇道：“你们如此张扬，便不忧心魏王寻上门来吗？”
这早就是徐福与李斯计划好了的，徐福淡淡应道：“心虚之人才会忧心，我们又不心虚，为何要忧心？”徐福顿了顿，突然转过头来，“倒是你的脸应该遮挡一二。”
龙阳君闻言，点了点头，于是突然靠进了徐福的怀中，“如此便没有人瞧见了……”
龙阳君身量比徐福还要高出一些，不过或许因为二人容貌都十分出色的缘故，看上去丝毫没有违和之处。
只有人叹息一声。
生得如此俊美，却偏是好男风的。
徐福猝不及防，全然未能来得及推开龙阳君，他身后的四名侍从脸色已经变了，差点忍不住上前直接将龙阳君扒拉开。
徐福原本也想将龙阳君推开的，但是他犹豫了一下，将龙阳君揽在跟前，二人一同走了进去。
“如此看来，龙阳君还是作女子打扮更好。”
龙阳君反问：“使臣不会觉得瞧着我脸上的妆容，便难受了么？”
徐福没说话，他带着龙阳君径直上楼进了屋子。
而后李斯匆匆进来，见了龙阳君，脸上闪过惊骇之色，对，是惊骇，不是惊艳。魏国少有能生得如此夺目之人。
李斯的面色有些凝重，他忙问徐福：“这位是？”
龙阳君看了一眼李斯，丝毫不遮掩自己的身份，“龙阳。”
……龙阳？
李斯差点吓得打个跌。
“……龙阳君？”李斯的声音都微微变了。徐福或许不知，但李斯明显更清楚这位龙阳君在魏王身边是何地位。曾经专宠魏王宫，轻易取得魏王信任，后来更被封了爵位，出使他国。
世人皆赞其妩媚风采和睿智无双，但又厌恶其获得君王专宠，以男色侍人，不是什么好东西。
龙阳君身上褒贬不一。
这也是李斯头一次见到这位龙阳君。
虽然近年来，因为魏国内部算不得安稳，而魏王又越发昏聩，越发喜好美人，龙阳君逐渐失了宠爱。甚至龙阳君一走，魏国甚至还会有人拍手称快。但那龙阳君也不是能说带走就带走的人啊！
怎么好好的，便出现在他们身边了？
徐典事还将人直接从魏王身边抢走了？
真是……
真是……
真是好大的魄力！李斯憋了半天最后从心底里憋出这样一句话来。
不得不说，将龙阳君给拐走了，那就是给魏王一记重击，要知道如今魏国已不再是魏王一个人说了算了，魏国之中，龙阳君与信陵君都逐渐坐大，也只有魏王还拿龙阳君当个呼之即来挥之即去的男宠，反而心中对于信陵君多有不信任。
李斯心中暗暗琢磨，徐典事会有此做法，莫非心中暗暗有何打算？
……
龙阳君看了看李斯，问徐福：“这人是？”
“与我一同前来的使臣，长史李斯。”
龙阳君点了点头，并未放在心上。
这时他在七国之中已经颇负盛名，而李斯却籍籍无名，自然是瞧不上李斯的。
李斯一心认为徐福是另有打算，便也未再过问龙阳君之事，众人在客栈中用过饭食，沐浴休息。待到第二日天还未亮，众人便起了床，然后就驾着车马从客栈离去了。
而此时魏王还派着人四处搜罗使臣和龙阳君的下落。
魏王不得不联想到一个可能性上去，“难道秦国使臣将寡人的龙阳君掳走了？真是好大的胆子！”魏王盛怒之下，在朝堂之上扬言要向秦国讨个公道。
此时信陵君站了出来，温言劝解，建议魏王先寻到人再说，若是此时贸然与秦国起了冲突，有何误会便不好了。
魏王盛怒之下，哪里肯听，便问朝臣，可有谁愿意出使秦国的。
有一人主动站出来，愿为魏王分忧解难。
若是李斯在此，便会认出，那人正是与自己交谈过其中一官员。
此人高高兴兴地从魏王此处领了命。
而信陵君却是皱了皱眉，不再掺合进去。
·
马车之中，徐福从蒹葭怀中取过了乔装用品，“蒹葭怎么还随身带着这些？”
蒹葭道：“时时要用上的。”
徐福随即便想到了自己。
自己不也是出门便要将所有用具都放在胸前揣着吗？唯有这样，才能令他觉得毫无后顾之忧，想来蒹葭也是如此了。
都是出于职业特性。
徐福将乔装用品放在了龙阳君的面前。
龙阳君看了蒹葭一眼，“今日要我自己动手乔装吗？”
徐福摇头，“不，我为龙阳君上妆。”
龙阳君愣了愣，随即笑道：“荣幸之至。”
chapters.title: 第75章

chapters.translated_text:
Face powder, rouge, eyebrow ink... all lined up in front of Xu Fu.

Actually, Xu Fu was a bit out of his depth, but even if he hadn't eaten pork, he'd seen pigs run, right? Recalling the classical makeup styles from the television dramas of his past life, Xu Fu quickly sketched out a rough sequence of actions in his mind.

He grabbed the face powder with full confidence.

No matter how bad it turned out, it would still be better than Jianjia’s attempt.

Lord Longyang sat there without moving, acting as a very professional model—or perhaps he was simply curious and enjoying this unprecedented experience.

Xu Fu knelt in front of Lord Longyang and reached out to press down on his shoulders.

There wasn't anything to moisturize the skin at the moment. Xu Fu pinched some powder, frowned, and turned to ask Jianjia, "Is there water?"

"Yes." Jianjia hurriedly handed over the gourd hanging from his waist.

Xu Fu took the gourd, opened the stopper, and poured some water into his palm. Lord Longyang suddenly had a bad premonition and couldn't help but shrink back, but Xu Fu had already pressed one hand onto his shoulder and slapped the other directly onto Lord Longyang's face.

Everyone in the carriage was stunned.

Xu Fu explained without changing his expression, "Rubbing it in helps with hydration." As he spoke, he pretended to be skilled, rubbing the water into Lord Longyang's face.

Jianjia swallowed involuntarily, feeling a bit guilty.

...There was probably his own saliva in that water.

After rubbing it in, Xu Fu patted a thin layer of powder onto Lord Longyang's face, then grabbed the rouge to apply to the corners of his eyes and lips. Jianjia’s eyes widened suddenly, "Sir, you can't do that..."

Xu Fu glanced at him sideways.

Jianjia immediately shut his mouth.

Xu Fu picked up the eyebrow ink and began to draw Lord Longyang’s eyebrows.

He looked quite focused, his eyelids slightly lowered, giving the illusion of deep affection. Lord Longyang looked up at him, the corners of his mouth twitching upward as he said, "The way the envoy draws eyebrows is truly enough to make one's heart flutter..." Just as he finished speaking, Xu Fu’s hand slipped, and the eyebrow ink left a long black line across Lord Longyang’s face.

Xu Fu put away the ink and continued to talk nonsense, "...Hmm, it looks quite uniquely beautiful."

Jianjia couldn't help but turn his face away; this was even worse than his own attempt...

Lord Longyang grinned, "If the envoy says it's good, then it is good."

Jianjia’s expression was even more unbearable to look at.

Lord Longyang could really endure!

Even Xu Fu couldn't help but look at Lord Longyang with surprise.

Along the way, they inevitably passed through some small towns, and Lord Longyang would stiffly wear this face while getting off the carriage with Xu Fu. Perhaps the people in these small towns had a penchant for the bizarre, as they were actually mesmerized by such a face.

Lord Longyang stood up straight and walked into the inn with Xu Fu.

But as soon as Lord Longyang’s figure was fully revealed, everyone felt a sense of horror and stammered, "...What a sturdy woman."

Xu Fu and his group quickly booked rooms at the inn. Since they had traveled far enough, they no longer needed to rush. Xu Fu went to take a comfortable bath, and the others dispersed to rest.

By the time Xu Fu shivered and woke up from his daze in the water, it was already quite late. He got up, draped a robe over himself, and stepped out. At a glance, he saw Lord Longyang eating downstairs, but there was a stranger sitting opposite him.

The man was wearing a grey robe, with a handsome face and a beard on his cheeks. Although there was some fatigue from long-distance travel on his face, he appeared mostly composed and serious—a man who seemed wise, steady, and calm.

Xu Fu felt a slight sense of vigilance. What was this man’s relationship with Lord Longyang? Why was he sitting in front of him?

Xu Fu walked down the stairs, softening his footsteps as he approached.

Once close, Xu Fu heard the man say to Lord Longyang, "...Observing your physiognomy, I fear you will soon fall into a great illness. This illness may very well change your life. Meeting you today is fate, so I offer you a word of advice."

Xu Fu was stunned.

These words sounded so familiar...

Weren't these the things he usually liked to say?

Was this... running into a colleague?

Xu Fu’s expression couldn't help but become a bit strange.

At this moment, the man noticed Xu Fu’s arrival, a look of surprise flashing across his face as he stood up.

Lord Longyang stood up immediately after.

"Who is this?" Xu Fu looked at Lord Longyang.

"We happened to meet, and this gentleman said the exact same things as you," Lord Longyang said with a slight smile.

Hearing this, the other man was also surprised. He looked deeply at Xu Fu and asked, "Said the same things as me?"

Xu Fu nodded, "I didn't expect such a coincidence."

The man shook his head, "It is not a coincidence."

What did that mean? Xu Fu didn't understand the deeper meaning, but he wasn't curious enough to pursue it, so he let it go.

The man turned his head back and continued to say to Lord Longyang, "Although your destiny has already changed, you should still be cautious. Especially within this year, you should change some of your temperaments, act with low profile, and step out of confined places more often to see the world. Otherwise, wasting your talent and charm due to a moment of melancholy and an illness—wouldn't that be a pity?"

At this time, Li Si also came out. Seeing the man, he frowned and said, "You look very familiar." As he spoke, he moved unobtrusively to block Xu Fu, worried that this person might be here to cause trouble.

The man shifted his gaze away without a trace, "Oh, really? I have never met you all. I shall take my leave now." With that, the man left first.

Xu Fu asked Lord Longyang, "Was he fortune-telling for you just now?"

Lord Longyang nodded, and added something that surprised Xu Fu, "Like you, he only took one look at me before saying all that."

Only one look?

Could that person also read physiognomy?

Xu Fu looked up hurriedly in the direction the man had left, but the man had already exited the inn, and he couldn't even catch a glimpse of his back.

Sure enough, even a thousand years ago, there were people beyond people, and heavens beyond heavens. He shouldn't underestimate this era...

He just didn't know if he would ever have the chance to meet that man again.

With a sense of anticipation, Xu Fu’s group soon hit the road again. As it happened, not long after they set off, near the border of Qin, they ran into that man again. The man rode his horse into Qin territory without looking back, while Xu Fu and his group took a detour toward Han.

Xu Fu had already sent Gantang and Bozhou back to Xianyang City.

Regardless of whether the King of Wei would make trouble, they had to strike first and prepare a sufficient excuse for the envoy’s early departure.

As for why the envoy left, the King of Wei shouldn't have been shameless enough to approach Xu Fu; if he got slapped in the face, he deserved it. As long as they held onto this point and kept Lord Longyang well-hidden, the King of Wei would never go to war with Qin over this. If Qin then took the initiative to appear magnanimous and engaged with the arriving envoys, they could make the alliance look like a legitimate affair.

Compared to forming an alliance the moment they arrived in Wei, having a conflict first and then forming an alliance would make other countries believe it more. After all, Wei had always looked down on Qin and had significant grievances with them.

At the very least, Han would be bluffed and wouldn't be able to seek help from Wei.

With Wei as a precedent, it would be much easier to deal with Han.

Li Si dealt with the officials of Han with ease, while Xu Fu no longer appeared with Li Si, instead taking Lord Longyang to search for the whereabouts of the tripod.

"The envoy is actually so interested in a tripod? Can the Qin palace not produce one?" Lord Longyang asked, puzzled. He had spent the first half of his life dealing with power struggles and diplomacy; how could he understand the leisure of searching for a tripod?

"The Qin palace naturally has countless tripods, but none of them are the one I am looking for."

"Oh? Does that tripod have any unique features?" Lord Longyang’s interest piqued, and he couldn't help but ask.

"Small and exquisite, can be held in the hand, with complex patterns on it, elegant and grand, and engraved with ancient characters."

"Isn't such a tripod common?" Lord Longyang laughed. Having been by the King of Wei’s side, he had naturally seen countless treasures; how could such a tripod be rare?

Xu Fu shook his head and turned to call, "Sangzhong."

Sangzhong stepped forward, gave Lord Longyang a wary look, and then took a small tripod out from his bosom.

Saying it could be held in the hand was a slight exaggeration; although it was small and exquisite, it still had to be cradled in one's arms.

Lord Longyang’s gaze touched the tripod, and a look of wonder flashed in his eyes, "There are certainly tripods more ornate than this, but they cannot compare to the heavy, ancient aura emanating from this one. It is indeed interesting. Is this the kind of tripod the envoy is looking for?"

Xu Fu nodded, "Exactly."

The coldness on Lord Longyang’s face vanished completely. He reached out to stroke the tripod and then said, "I seem to have seen a tripod similar to this."

"Where did you see it?" Xu Fu asked immediately, the only time he would drop his cold, aloof exterior.

Lord Longyang withdrew his hand, "I seem to have put that tripod away, but it is not with me; it is still within the borders of Wei."

"In Wei?" So it was in Wei, not Han.

Xu Fu frowned, thinking to himself that Li Si’s information wasn't very reliable.

"The envoy need not worry. If you really need this thing, I can have someone send it over."

"Can you still return to Wei?"

Lord Longyang lowered his eyelids and said nonchalantly, "I don't need to return for it to be sent to you. But if the envoy takes my things, what will you give in exchange?"

Xu Fu said shamelessly, "I saved your life. Isn't Lord Longyang’s life worth more than that tripod?" Lord Longyang might be digging a hole for him to jump into; why should he be so honest and promise to exchange something for it later?

Lord Longyang nodded, "Then my life is in the envoy’s hands."

Xu Fu glanced at him, feeling that his behavior was strange, but he couldn't pinpoint exactly what was odd about it.

Since the whereabouts of the tripod were clear, Xu Fu didn't linger outside with Lord Longyang, and they soon returned to the inn. Lord Longyang was still dressed as a woman, and Xu Fu’s makeup skills had improved by more than one level. When Lord Longyang walked out, apart from his height which was slightly taller than Xu Fu’s, his face looked like that of a charming woman, completely different from his true temperament.

Wang Liu walked the streets and alleys, looking for people to tell fortunes.

Only Jianjia and Sangzhong stayed honestly outside Xu Fu’s door, while Lord Longyang, with no one following him, would occasionally sit downstairs for a drink, yet no one dared to approach him.

After nightfall, the inn became quieter. Then, with a creak, Li Si entered, covered in the dampness of the night. His expression was not relaxed, and Lord Longyang glanced at him, not surprised, and asked directly, "It seems Chief Clerk Li has failed in his negotiations."

"Failed?" Xu Fu came downstairs and frowned.

It was hard to find true talent in Han these days; could it be that the officials of Han were even harder to move than those of Wei, such that even Li Si’s silver tongue couldn't persuade them?

Li Si walked over with long strides, his expression grave as he said to Xu Fu, "I must trouble the Director to discuss this with me."

Li Si knew that Lord Longyang was a man of talent, but he was, after all, a male favorite of Wei who had served as an envoy to other countries to further Wei’s interests; some things could not be said in front of him. Li Si had great trust in Xu Fu, and he believed that discussing this with him would surely yield results.

The two went upstairs, with Jianjia and Sangzhong guarding the door.

"Did you encounter difficulties?" Xu Fu asked.

Li Si sighed, "I never expected the people of Han to be so shallow."

"How so?"

"The officials of Wei value power, status, and future advancement. But these officials of Han value gold, silver, and jewels." Li Si shook his head, "To cooperate with them, they ask for money as soon as they open their mouths."

That was truly vulgar and practical.

Although the officials of Han seemed more mercenary and lacked the grand ambitions of the Wei officials, one had to admit that their demands were more practical. If you want to talk to me, bring money first; only when I get actual benefits can I help you. If you talk to me about promotion or the future, I won't listen.

But in Li Si’s eyes, it was infuriating.

With such short-sighted officials, it was no wonder Han was becoming less and less like its former self.

"Then just find some gold and silver jewels."

Li Si shook his head, "When we left, I didn't ask the King to prepare a large amount of wealth." Moreover, Li Si looked down on these officials and wasn't very willing to spend money on them.

During the reign of King Huiwen of Qin, there was Zhang Yi, who could talk his way through the world.

Now that he thought about it, he had overestimated himself.

Li Si sighed softly.

He could think of ways to sow discord between rulers and ministers, but he hadn't considered that officials in different countries were different, and the interests that could move them were naturally different; one had to prescribe the right medicine for the right illness.

"That’s simple." There was no trace of anxiety on Xu Fu’s face.

"Why do you say that?" Li Si was startled.

"Lord Longyang has money. Just borrow it from him."

Li Si frowned, "He left Wei in a hurry; would he be carrying any?"

Xu Fu hummed softly, "He might not be carrying it, but his attendants are. Do you really think he came with us all alone?" Xu Fu hadn't realized it before, but it was only when Lord Longyang said those things while searching for the tripod today that he became certain of his thoughts.

Li Si nodded, "We cannot return empty-handed from this trip. We will change our plan; taking down just one person will be enough."

"Remember to bring Wang Liu."

Li Si smiled, relieved, "That goes without saying."

However, after Li Si stepped out of the room, he suddenly remembered that Lord Longyang was cold and arrogant by nature, even harder to talk to than Director Xu, and since Lord Longyang was also a silver-tongued person, why would he obediently lend him money?

As Li Si was secretly phrasing his words, he walked two steps forward and saw Lord Longyang standing opposite him, looking up with a smile, "Does Chief Clerk Li have something to say?"

Li Si didn't beat around the bush and bowed immediately, "I have a request..."

"Asking to borrow money?" Lord Longyang seemed to have foreseen it.

But thinking that Han and Wei had a good relationship in the past, and that Lord Longyang had even served as an envoy to Han, Li Si didn't find it strange.

"Exactly."

"Borrowing money is fine, but the Chief Clerk must also ask the envoy for me: what will he give in exchange?" Lord Longyang said lightly, "A life of Longyang cannot be worth that much."

Xu Fu happened to come out of the room at this moment and heard Lord Longyang say this. He was even more puzzled; why did Lord Longyang insist on him exchanging something? Did he want him to owe him a favor? Xu Fu stared at Lord Longyang’s face for a while.

Both of them had poker faces, and neither could tell who was winning.

Xu Fu couldn't see anything, so he could only nod, "Lord Longyang, please keep it in mind. If there is an opportunity in the future, I will certainly repay you."

Seeing this, Li Si hurriedly said, "This is a debt I owe Lord Longyang; how can it be recorded under the Sir?"

"It doesn't matter."

Li Si was expanding territory and winning hearts for the King of Qin. Although he had only slept with the King of Qin a few times, essentially, he was closer to the King of Qin now; what was wrong with him paying a little? If he owed Lord Longyang today, wouldn't it be the King of Qin owing him when he returned to Xianyang City?

This kind of deal was quite cost-effective.

Lord Longyang then smiled, "The envoy is straightforward. I have already ordered people to search for that tripod. As for the money Chief Clerk Li needs, I have already ordered it to be prepared. Chief Clerk Li might as well go back to your room and take a look."

So he had anticipated it all along? Xu Fu couldn't help but take another look at Lord Longyang.

He was older than Li Si, and sure enough, he was a bigger old fox than Li Si.

Rather than saying they had kidnapped Lord Longyang, it was more like Lord Longyang had his own schemes.

Li Si also looked deeply at Lord Longyang before turning to leave.

Regardless, the whereabouts of the tripod Xu Fu requested had been found, and the funds Li Si sought were also in hand. Li Si took Wang Liu with him, and after securing the person, their group hurriedly departed from the territory of Han.

Xu Fu had not expected the journey to be so calm; compared to the treacherous Shu region, the trips through Wei and Han had been surprisingly smooth.

While they were still on the road, the envoy dispatched by the State of Wei had already arrived in the State of Qin.

·

"Greetings to the King of Qin."

In the past, Wei officials might not have held the King of Qin in high regard, but their status had changed, and the envoy had an agreement with Li Si, so he was much more eager upon seeing the King of Qin. The envoy looked up at the King of Qin, only to find that this King of Qin appeared even more majestic than the previous one.

The envoy’s legs went weak involuntarily, and the instructions the King of Wei had specifically given him were immediately compromised and delivered in a euphemistic tone.

Sitting on the high throne, Ying Zheng’s expression was cold, his tone sharp, "I have yet to question the State of Wei for treating the envoy I sent in such a manner."

After Bo Zhou and Gan Tang returned, they recounted everything to Ying Zheng. After listening, it was already a miracle that Ying Zheng didn't want to crush the King of Wei to death immediately; now the King of Wei was still trying to provoke him. How much courage did that King of Wei have to dare to snatch someone away from him, Ying Zheng?

The King of Wei appeared very respectful toward Qin now, but from the King of Wei's actions, Ying Zheng knew that he still did not hold Qin in any regard.

Otherwise, how would he dare to lay a hand on a Qin envoy?

Was he truly so stupid that lust had clouded his mind?

The Wei envoy could not withstand Ying Zheng’s intimidation. Without needing Ying Zheng to say much more, he immediately conceded, kneeling and saying, "I will certainly convey the King of Qin's meaning to the King of Wei."

"Take him away." Ying Zheng ordered with a gloomy face.

The Wei envoy shivered, thinking, wasn't everything going well? The King of Qin wouldn't actually execute him, would he?

In the eyes of other states, Qin had always been perceived as barbaric and warlike. The Wei envoy could not help but feel terrified. Seeing the tall eunuch approach to escort him out, the Wei envoy, caught in the middle, trembled.

Ying Zheng watched coldly as the man was led away, his stylus nearly poking a hole through the desk.

If Bo Zhou hadn't already explained that this man had been won over by Li Si, he would certainly have taught this envoy a lesson.

The wrongs committed by the King of Wei would eventually have to be repaid.

Did those six states still think his Great Qin was the same Qin of the past?

Ying Zheng set down his stylus and called Bo Zhou to his side, "You said there was someone with Xu Fu; who is that person? Tell me in detail." Compared to talking to the spineless envoy from Wei, Ying Zheng was naturally more interested in asking Bo Zhou about Xu Fu's recent situation.

Bo Zhou vaguely knew the identity of Lord Longyang but dared not speak of it, so he could only vaguely say, "That person is extremely beautiful, with charming features, a tall stature, and came from the palace of the King of Wei..."

Even if Bo Zhou hadn't said it, Ying Zheng had already guessed the other's identity.

If the envoy had simply left in a hurry, why would the King of Wei send someone? It must be that the King of Wei had been slapped in the face repeatedly and felt so humiliated that he ordered someone to come and demand justice from him.

It’s just that... Ying Zheng sneered. Whatever Xu Fu had done, right or wrong, the King of Wei would never get justice from him.

"Is that person Lord Longyang?" Ying Zheng asked calmly.

Seeing Ying Zheng’s expression remain normal, Bo Zhou breathed a secret sigh of relief and nodded, "Exactly."

"Lord Longyang, whom the King of Wei relies upon..." Ying Zheng murmured.

Bo Zhou’s heart tightened involuntarily. Would the King be angry because of this?

But the next moment, he heard Ying Zheng laugh heartily, "Hahaha... Xu Fu has extraordinary courage to dare to abduct Lord Longyang to Qin; no wonder the King of Wei is jumping with rage."

Bo Zhou: ...

Why did he feel... as if... no matter what trouble Mr. Xu caused, the King was always proudly and smugly cleaning up the mess behind him?

It must be his imagination, right?

The King is so wise and martial; this move must have a deeper meaning. Perhaps he thinks Lord Longyang has extraordinary talent, and bringing him into Qin is a happy event...

However, although Ying Zheng said this, he still had to make some preparations in secret to prevent Xu Fu from blowing things out of proportion.

After making some arrangements, Ying Zheng couldn't help but ask Bo Zhou, "When did Xu Fu go to Han? How many days until he returns?"

Bo Zhou was stunned, "...At least a month, I should think." Having spent this time together, Bo Zhou understood Xu Fu's temperament; once the task was completed, Xu Fu would surely take his time on the return journey, deliberately stopping to admire the customs of other lands.

...At least... a month...

Ying Zheng felt this news was a much greater shock than hearing that Xu Fu had brought back a Lord Longyang.

Ying Zheng stood up and walked out of the hall.

Zhao Gao hurriedly followed, "Your Majesty..."

Ying Zheng said softly, "I have no appetite."

Zhao Gao wrinkled his face, thinking of a sycophantic method, "Perhaps invite a few dancing girls..."

Ying Zheng didn't even finish listening before interrupting him, "No need. How is Lord Changping doing with the rebellion suppression? Bring those reports to me."

Zhao Gao immediately swallowed all his words, his assessment of Xu Fu's status in his heart rising another notch. However, what Zhao Gao was thinking more about right now was whether this Director Xu would become another Lord Longyang...

Zhao Gao was not happy to see that.

He lowered his head, turned quickly to fetch the reports, and buried all the thoughts in his mind.

·

Noon.

After having some food, Xu Fu and the others drove their carriage along a desolate road.

As they were about to reach the border between Han and Qin, the road was blocked. A giant boulder obstructed their path, and the carriage could not pass. There must be people in the nearby towns who could come to repair the road, but it would take a long time to wait. Xu Fu and the others could not abandon the carriage in Han territory; there were too many prohibited items inside. If someone interested took a look, they could guess that a Qin official had been running around in Han.

Coming so discreetly, how could it not invite suspicion?

Thus, the group had to find another way, choosing a wider but even more desolate path.

That path was hidden behind the woods by the roadside. They didn't know where it led, but it was in the right direction, and they would eventually return to Qin.

But they traveled for a long time without seeing any signs of life. Spring had passed, and as summer arrived, the sun hung high in the sky, inevitably making people feel a bit irritable.

Xu Fu could only sigh to himself that the flag he had planted was being slapped down so quickly! Not long ago, he thought the trip through Wei and Han was extremely smooth, and now some trouble had arisen. However, when the moon is full, it begins to wane; it was normal for some trouble to appear after things had gone so perfectly.

Lord Longyang lifted the carriage curtain and glanced out, "We cannot go any further."

Sang Zhong also nodded, rarely not contradicting Lord Longyang, "It looks wrong ahead."

Xu Fu was surprisingly calm, "Encountering a giant boulder blocking the road while traveling is an ominous sign. But there is nothing to fear; just keep moving forward." This omen meant that one could not avoid it; after bypassing the boulder, it would be difficult to find the road ahead, which was exactly why one should face the difficulty head-on.

Lord Longyang was stunned, not expecting Xu Fu to say this. Lord Longyang had his own confidence, so he couldn't help but smile, "The envoy is so certain? What if we encounter disaster by moving forward?" After speaking, he paused and added, "The envoy looks as if he truly understands the art of divination."

Sang Zhong’s mouth twitched. He thought, the envoy in front of you not only understands the art of divination, but he can also calculate with extreme accuracy and precision!

Sang Zhong and Jian Jia naturally listened to Xu Fu. They were the ones driving, and now that Xu Fu had spoken, they naturally continued forward.

"The horses might not hold up," Wang Liu said, poking his head out from another carriage, frowning slightly.

What he said was the truth.

They had been traveling all the way; the people were well-rested, but the horses might not be. Moreover, upon arriving in Han territory, it wasn't just people who were prone to being unacclimated; horses were too. Now with the sun high in the sky, it was perfectly normal for the horses to be tired.

"It's fine, we will stop soon," Xu Fu said in his usual charlatan tone.

Lord Longyang was curious, wanting to know where Xu Fu got such certainty, so he stopped talking.

The carriage moved forward for a distance, and Xu Fu suddenly said, "Stop."

Everyone was stunned, and just as they were about to ask what they didn't understand, they saw a group of people emerge from the woods ahead.

In broad daylight, that group of people was holding torches and had their bodies smeared pitch-black, looking somewhat like the dancers at a wax sacrifice ceremony.

Lord Longyang was even more curious, "Does the envoy mean that since someone has come, we don't need to move forward?"

Xu Fu nodded, his eyes fixed on the group.

In fact, he could tell someone was coming not because of physiognomy, but because of his keen observation. Suddenly, many birds in the woods ahead were flapping their wings and flying away; either a giant animal was moving through, or someone was walking. But where would a giant animal come from here? The greatest possibility was people. As long as people appeared, they could rest, ask for directions, find the right way, or find a place to stay.

It was just that Xu Fu didn't expect the people who appeared to be dressed so strangely.

"Don't move yet."

"Retreat!"

Xu Fu and Lord Longyang said two completely different things.

The two couldn't help but look at each other.

Of course, they both felt that this group was dressed strangely and should not be provoked. If they ran into people who were unreasonable or spoke a different language, they might be in big trouble today.

Xu Fu hesitated for a moment. It was too late to retreat now; going back would still mean being blocked by the boulder, but rushing forward wasn't a good choice either.

"Wait to the side," Xu Fu said.

Lord Longyang couldn't help but ask, "Does the envoy not feel fear?"

Xu Fu was indeed very bold; he shook his head, "Where there is no worry, there is no fear."

Lord Longyang nodded and smiled, "Then I will trust the envoy once."

Xu Fu glanced at him, "Now that we are in the same boat, Lord Longyang must trust me whether he wants to or not."

In fact, Xu Fu was quite experienced in dealing with such emergencies. These people looked like they were going to perform some sacrificial activity. As a charlatan who had dealt with such feudal superstitions since childhood, couldn't Xu Fu handle this?

The group noticed Xu Fu and the others, their eyes scanning them viciously. One of them walked over quickly, holding a sickle, and asked, "Who are you?"

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief; although there was a heavy accent, he could at least understand what was being said.

Xu Fu’s face was highly deceptive. He leaned out and explained calmly, "We accidentally took the wrong road. Please point us in the right direction. Thank you."

"Where are you going?"

"The border of Han."

"Pass through this forest, but be careful not to damage it." Although the man looked fierce, he still answered Xu Fu's question earnestly.

Everyone was surprised that it had been so easy, so they thanked the man and drove the carriage toward the forest.

Xu Fu scanned the middle of the group and saw a few people who were not dressed in that manner.

They were a few old and frail women, being herded into the middle and taken to an open space not far away.

Some people had already gone to the open space, built a fire, set up a tripod, and were dancing in a circle.

"What is this?" Xu Fu had never seen such a custom and couldn't help but ask.

Lord Longyang showed an expression of sudden realization and whispered, "There is a custom very common in farming areas. It is called 'eating the mother'."

"'Eating the mother'?" Xu Fu’s expression changed slightly, "These people are going to eat their mothers?"

Lord Longyang shook his head, "Not exactly. 'Eating the mother' means using special witchcraft to transfer the mother's farming experience to her descendants so that they can farm the land well."

Witchcraft again?

"And how is this witchcraft performed?"

Lord Longyang shook his head, "I don't know either, I've only heard such rumors."

As soon as he finished speaking, he saw a tall man walk to the fire and push the old women into it. The women didn't even let out a scream. Xu Fu’s expression changed, and he grabbed the edge of the carriage, ready to jump out. Jian Jia and Sang Zhong’s expressions also changed drastically, but they had to protect Xu Fu’s safety, so they dared not act rashly.

Lord Longyang said sharply, "What does the envoy want to do? Sympathize with them?"

Li Si also looked grim, but out of reason, he said, "Local customs are usually passed down for many years. The people of this area will defend their customs, no matter how absurd they are. Once someone touches them, they will be attacked by the crowd."

Xu Fu understood this.

He also didn't consider himself a saint.

But watching the women being burned by the fire in front of him, and having to endure the screams because of the custom—how painful! And how ignorant! Wouldn't their souls scream? Could these people really watch their former family members be burned to death in the fire?

At this moment, the tall man, perhaps a shaman or something similar, held his staff high, tapping it over the heads of the women one by one, and then touching the heads of the surrounding people. It was probably meant to be a transfer.

But... what kind of hellish inheritance method is this?

Did they think the fire could burn the women's souls out, to be extracted by the staff and then given to these descendants?

How could these descendants endure the pain?

In that instant, countless thoughts flashed through Xu Fu's mind.

Let's treat this as a practice as well...

Xu Fu said to himself.

"I'll make a bet with Lord Longyang."

"What bet?" Lord Longyang frowned slightly; could it be that the envoy still wouldn't give up?

"I bet... I can change their custom! And make them not use this custom for a hundred, even a thousand years!" Xu Fu pointed into the distance, his gaze stern as he met Lord Longyang’s eyes.

"How to change it?" Lord Longyang was much more rational. Besides, was such a small matter worth the envoy doing this?

"Just watch." Xu Fu didn't say more, bypassed Sang Zhong and Jian Jia, jumped off the carriage, and walked toward that side without looking back. Li Si was shocked and hurriedly followed, while Sang Zhong and Jian Jia rushed up directly.

Lord Longyang rubbed his temples, "I really don't know if this envoy from Qin is truly bold, or if he has the capital to be bold..." After saying that, he didn't stay out of it either, but jumped off the carriage as well.

The movement here caught the attention of the people over there.

The group surrounding the fire immediately turned their heads, staring at Xu Fu with hostile, tiger-like eyes.

"What else do you want to do?" The man who had pointed the way for them asked coldly. It was as if Xu Fu’s group had invaded their territory, making them instantly tense.

Sang Zhong and Jian Jia looked back with even colder expressions.

The aura of Sang Zhong and Jian Jia was clearly much stronger, and the man couldn't help but step back, but he gripped the sickle in his hand tightly.

Xu Fu glanced at the women who had fallen into the fire and suddenly pointed at them, shouting, "Oh no! Look! Why don't you move them out quickly..."

The group remained unmoved, asking coldly, "What do you want to do? Go away!"

Xu Fu gave a look to Sang Zhong and Jian Jia, then resumed his charlatan act, "Are you doing this to make future farming smoother? To have a better harvest?"

The group still glared at him with vigilance and indifference, not moving at all.

"Can't you see? Doing this will only make your harvests worse and worse... In a few years, you won't even be able to have a full meal..."

"Nonsense!" The tall man stood out and loudly refuted Xu Fu's words.

Xu Fu didn't even look at him, turning to ask, "It started last year, didn't it... Last year the fields were barren, there was a severe lack of water, the harvest decreased, but the taxes were heavy. Were you all very panicked? That's why you adopted this custom passed down by your ancestors, determined to do this to exchange for a smooth coming year and a great harvest, right?"

"Tell me, is that it!" Xu Fu’s tone suddenly changed, asking sharply.
chapters.title: 第76章
chapters.source_text:
妆粉，胭脂，螺子黛……在徐福的面前一字排开。
其实徐福也稍微有一些苦手，不过没吃过猪肉还没见过猪跑么？回忆一番上辈子电视剧中的古典妆容，徐福脑子里很快便勾勒出个大致的动作来。
他信心满满地抓起了妆粉。
就算再糟糕，也总归比蒹葭打扮得好。
龙阳君坐在那里动也不动，很敬业地做着模特，或者说他是很好奇并享受这样从未有过的经历。
徐福跪俯在龙阳君的跟前，伸手将他的肩膀往下压了压。
这个时候也没有个滋润下肌肤的东西，徐福捏着妆粉，皱了皱眉，转头问蒹葭：“有水吗？”
“有。”蒹葭忙递上腰间的葫芦。
徐福接过葫芦，打开塞子，在掌心倒了一些水出来。龙阳君忽然有了不好的预感，不由得往后缩了缩，但是徐福一只手已经按了上来，另一只手直接拍在了龙阳君的脸上。
马车里所有的人都懵了懵。
徐福面不改色地解释道：“揉一揉，补水。”说着假装手法熟练地在龙阳君的脸上揉了起来。
蒹葭不自觉地咽了咽口水，有些心虚。
……那里边儿，好像还有他的口水吧。
徐福揉完之后，才往龙阳君的脸上薄薄地拍了一层粉，然后就抓起了胭脂往眼角和唇上涂抹，蒹葭骤然睁大双眼，“先生，这样不行……”
徐福回头斜睨了他一眼。
蒹葭立刻闭了嘴。
徐福又抓起螺子黛，给龙阳君画起了眉。
他的模样有些专注，微微低垂着眼睑，看上去给人一种深情的错觉。龙阳君抬眼看了看他，嘴角忍不住扬了扬，道：“使臣画眉的模样，实在教人有些动心……”他话音刚落下，徐福就不小心地手滑了，螺子黛在龙阳君的脸上画了道长长的黑线。
徐福收起螺子黛，继续胡扯，“……嗯，瞧上去也别有一番美丽。”
蒹葭不由自主地别过了脸，这还不如他呢……
龙阳君咧了咧嘴，“使臣说好，那便就如此好了。”
蒹葭更是一脸惨不忍睹的表情。
龙阳君当真能忍！
就连徐福都免不了诧异地看了看龙阳君。
中途他们免不了再经过一些小城镇，龙阳君便硬生生地顶着这张脸，跟着徐福下了马车。不知道是不是小城镇的人，审美也偏向猎奇，竟然对着这样一张脸，也能瞧得入迷。
龙阳君大大方方地站直身体，随着徐福进客栈。
只是龙阳君的身形一展示出来，众人就颇觉惊悚，讷讷地道：“……好生壮健的女子。”
徐福几人很快在客栈定了房间，因为跑得已经足够远了，他们也不用再急着赶时间了。徐福去舒舒服服地泡了个澡，其余人也各自散去休息。
等徐福迷迷糊糊地打了个冷颤，从水中醒来时，天色已经有些晚了。徐福起身披上袍子，跨出门来，一眼便看见了坐在楼下用饭食的龙阳君，只是龙阳君的对面还坐了个陌生男子。
那男子穿着一身灰袍，面容英俊，两腮留有胡子，虽然脸上有几分长途跋涉的疲色，但更多的是沉稳与严肃，看上去是个睿智又足够沉稳冷静的人。
徐福心中微微警惕，这人跟龙阳君是什么关系？他坐在龙阳君跟前是为了什么？
徐福走下楼梯，放轻脚步走近了一些。
等走近了，徐福才听见那男子对龙阳君道：“……我观阁下面相，不久之后恐将生一场大病，这场大病，很有可能会改变阁下的一生。近日遇见，便是有缘，我也劝解阁下一二。”
徐福愣了愣。
好生耳熟的话语……
这不就是他平常爱说的话吗？
这是……撞上同行了？
徐福的神色不由得怪异了几分。
而此时那男子也注意到了徐福的到来，脸上闪过惊讶之色，站起了身来。
龙阳君紧跟着也站了起来。
“这位是？”徐福看向龙阳君。
“恰好遇到，这位先生便说了同你一样的话。”龙阳君微微一笑，道。
对方闻言，也有些诧异，他深深地看了徐福一眼，问道：“和我说了同样的话？”
徐福点了点头，“没想到这样凑巧。”
对方却是摇头，“并非凑巧。”
什么意思？徐福听不明白其中深意，不过他对此也并不好奇，所以就放过了。
那人将头转回去，继续对龙阳君道：“阁下的命格虽已有变化，但也应该小心为上，尤其在这一年内，阁下还是改掉一些脾性，低调行事，多从禁锢的地方走出来，瞧一瞧外面，免得因为一时郁郁和一场病毁了一身才华风流，岂不可惜？”
此时李斯也出来了，李斯见了那人，皱眉道：“阁下瞧着好生面熟。”说着他便不着痕迹地挡在了徐福的面前，有些担心这人是不是来横生枝节的。
那人不着痕迹地挪开了眼，“哦，是吗？我与各位应当是未见过的，这便告辞了。”说着那人就先离去了。
徐福问龙阳君：“方才他在给你算命？”
龙阳君点了点头，而且还说了句令徐福有些惊讶的话，“他与你一样，只瞧了我一眼，便说出了这一番话来。”
只瞧了一眼？
难道那个人也会看面相？
徐福抬头忙朝那人离去的方向看去，但那人已经出了客栈了，连个背影也没能寻到。
果然，哪怕是在千年前，也是人外有人，天外有天的。他不应该小瞧了这个时代……
只是不知道，是否还会有缘与那个男子再见。
怀着期待的心情，徐福一行人很快又上了路，而刚好就是这样凑巧，他们行了没多久，在接近秦境的时候，又碰见了那位男子，那男子骑着马头也不回地入了秦国境内。而徐福等人却是临时拐道，转向了韩国。
只是徐福将甘棠与柏舟打发回咸阳城了。
不管魏王会不会发难，他们都得先倒打一耙，为使臣提前离去准备一个充足的借口。
为何使臣会离去，魏王先不要脸往徐福跟前凑，被打脸那也是活该。只要拿捏住这一点，再将龙阳君藏个结实，魏王怎么样也不可能会为此而同秦国大动干戈。秦国此时再主动做出大度的模样，与那前来的使臣接洽一番，将互盟之事做得看上去像那么回事儿。
比起刚到魏国，便与魏国结盟，如此先是一番矛盾，之后再结盟，那就更令他国相信了。谁让魏国从前都是瞧不起秦国的，且与秦国颇有嫌隙呢？
至少韩国会被唬住，没办法从魏国这里寻求帮助了。
有了魏国在前，韩国便好入手多了。
李斯从善如流地与韩国官员打着交道，而徐福却未再跟着李斯露面，而是带着龙阳君四处去寻那鼎的下落。
“使臣对鼎竟然还如此有兴致？难道秦王宫中拿不出鼎来吗？”龙阳君疑惑不解。他前半生与夺宠权谋、政治外交打交道，怎么能理解去寻一只鼎的闲心？
“秦王宫中自然有无数的鼎，但都不是我要寻的那一只。”
“哦？那鼎可有奇特之处？”龙阳君兴味浓了一些，不由得问道。
“小巧玲珑，可执于手，上有繁复纹理，精美大气，鼎上刻有远古文字。”
“这样的鼎，不是随处可见吗？”龙阳君失笑道。他跟在魏王身边，自然也是见过无数好东西的，这样的鼎哪里会少见？
徐福摇摇头，转头叫道：“桑中。”
桑中走上前来，暗暗警惕地看了一眼龙阳君，随后才从怀中掏出了一只小鼎来。
说是可执于手稍稍有些夸张了，虽然小巧玲珑，但也要捧在怀里才行。
龙阳君的目光触及鼎身，眸中闪过了惊叹的光芒，“比它华丽的鼎固然有之，但却比不上这鼎身上透出的厚重气息。果然有些意思，使臣要寻的，便是这样的鼎吗？”
徐福点头，“正是。”
龙阳君脸上的冷然退了个一干二净，他抬手抚弄两下那鼎，随后道：“我似乎见过与这相似的鼎。”
“在哪里见过？”徐福立刻问道，也只有这时候他才会稍稍放下那副高冷的外表。
龙阳君收回手，“那鼎似乎被我收了起来，不过并不在我身边，此时还在魏国境内。”
“在魏国？”原来在魏国并不在韩国。
徐福皱了皱眉，暗道那李斯的消息不太靠谱。
“使臣无须着急，若是真需要这玩意儿，我命人送来便是。”
“你还回得了魏国？”
龙阳君垂下眼睑，漫不经心地说：“不需要我回去，那东西自然也能送到使臣手中，但使臣取走我的东西，拿什么来换呢？”
徐福厚着脸皮道：“我救了你一命，难道龙阳君一命不如那鼎值价吗？”龙阳君话里说不定便是挖了坑给他跳，他何苦那么实诚，答应下来，说以后定拿东西来和龙阳君换。
龙阳君点点头，“那我的命便放在使臣手中了。”
徐福瞥了他一眼，总觉得他的表现有些怪异，但究竟何处怪异，却又突然间说不上来了。
既然已经清楚了鼎的下落，徐福也没有再与龙阳君在外久留，他们很快便回了客栈之中。如今龙阳君还是作女子打扮，而徐福的化妆技术已经上升了不止一个台阶，龙阳君走出去，除了那比徐福还要隐隐冒出一截来的身高，光是瞧面容，便已经像是个楚楚动人，与他真实气质全然不同的女子了。
王柳在外走街串巷，四处寻人来算卦。
唯有蒹葭和桑中老实守在了徐福的门外，而龙阳君无人跟随，时不时地坐在楼下喝个小酒，却硬是无人敢接近他。
待到入夜后，客栈中人渐渐少了起来，这时却听吱呀一声，裹着一身露水气的李斯进门来了。李斯的脸色并不轻松，而龙阳君扫了他一眼，并不奇怪，直接出声问道：“瞧来李长史应当是接洽失败了。”
“失败？”徐福下楼来，皱了皱眉。
韩国如今难寻真正的贤才，难不成韩国的官员比魏国的官员还要难打动，连李斯一张嘴也无法说动？
李斯大步走来，面色凝重地朝徐福道：“劳烦典事与我商量一二。”
李斯也清楚龙阳君是有才能之士，但他毕竟是魏国的男宠，曾经出使他国，他可都是在为魏王谋利益，有些话自然不能在他跟前说。而李斯胸中对徐福的信任已经十分之高，在他看来，此时与徐福商谈，定能有所获。
二人上了楼，蒹葭与桑中把守在外。
“可是遇见了难处？”徐福出声问。
李斯叹了口气，“我未曾想到，这韩国中人，眼皮子如此之浅。”
“如何浅法？”
“那魏国官员，看中权势地位，看中未来高升。而这韩国官员，看中的却是金银珠宝。”李斯摇头，“与他们合作，他们开口便要钱财。”
还真是俗得实际啊。
虽然说韩国官员显得市侩了些，不如魏国官员所求远大，但不得不说韩国官员所求更为实际。要与我谈，那便先取钱财来，我得到实际的利益了，我才能出手帮助你，你与我谈什么升官，谈什么未来，那我都不听。
只是放在李斯眼中，未免令他牙痒痒。
韩国官员目光如此短视，怪不得韩国越发地不如从前了。
“那便寻些金银珠宝来便是。”
李斯摇头，“走时，并未向王上要求准备丰厚钱财。”而且李斯心中多少有些瞧不上这些官员，并不十分乐意将钱花在他们身上。
秦惠文王时期，曾有张仪，一张嘴说遍天下。
如今想来，倒是他高看自身了。
李斯轻叹一口气。
他能想到君臣挑拨离间之法，却未曾想到，各国官员多有不同，能打动他们的利益自然也是不同的，要对症下药方才正确。
“这样简单。”徐福脸上丝毫焦急也无。
“何出此言？”李斯怔了怔。
“龙阳君有钱啊，问他借便是了。”
李斯皱眉，“他从魏国匆匆离去，身上可会携带？”
徐福轻哼一声，“他身上没有携带，但他的随从身上带了。你真当他一人孤身随我们而来吗？”之前徐福也未发觉，还是今天寻鼎时，龙阳君说了那一番话，才叫徐福坚定了心中所想。
李斯点头，“此行不能空手而归，我们改变计划，只拿下一人也足以。”
“记得带上王柳。”
李斯笑了笑，如释负重，“这是自然。”
不过等李斯迈出了屋子，才骤然想起，那龙阳君生性冷傲，比徐典事还要不好说话，何况龙阳君本身又是能言善道之辈，如何又会乖乖借钱给他呢？
李斯心中正暗暗措辞，等往前走上两步，便见龙阳君站在对面，抬头笑了笑，“李长史可是有事？”
李斯也不矫情，当即一拜，求道：“我有一求……”
“求我借钱？”龙阳君仿佛未卜先知一般。
不过想到韩魏两国从前关系不错，而龙阳君更是曾出使韩国，李斯便不觉得惊奇了。
“正是。”
“借钱可以，不过长史还要替我问一问使臣，这又拿什么来换？”龙阳君淡淡道：“龙阳一条命，可抵不了那么多的东西。”
徐福恰好此时也从屋子里出来，听见龙阳君如此说，心中更为疑惑，龙阳君为何非要让他拿东西去换？是想要自己欠他一份人情？徐福盯着龙阳君的面孔看了一会儿。
两个人都摆着一张面瘫脸，谁也分不出个胜负来。
徐福什么也瞧不出，只能点头，“龙阳君记下便是，日后若有机会，我定然还与龙阳君。”
李斯见状，忙道：“这算是我欠龙阳君的，怎么能记在先生身上？”
“无妨。”
李斯为秦始皇开疆拓土，笼络人心。而他虽然就与秦始皇睡了几觉，但本质上来说，他如今同秦始皇更为亲密一些，他付出一二又有何不可？今日他欠了龙阳君，改日回到咸阳城中，不就是秦始皇欠他了吗？
这等买卖做起来，还是相当划算的。
龙阳君这才笑道：“使臣爽快，那鼎我已命人去寻了。而李长史所求的钱财，我已经命人备好，李长史不如回屋子去瞧一瞧。”
原是早就预料到了？徐福忍不住多看了龙阳君一眼。
他年纪比李斯更为年长，果然也比李斯更老狐狸。
说是他们将龙阳君拐跑，还不如说是龙阳君另有谋算呢。
李斯也深深地看了龙阳君一眼，这才转身离去。
不论如何，徐福要求的鼎已经寻到了下落，李斯所求的钱财也拿到手了，李斯带上王柳前去，拿下一人后，他们一行人便又匆匆离开了韩国境内。
徐福未曾想到这一路会这般风平浪静，比起处处险阻的蜀地，魏国与韩国之行，竟是如此顺利。
他们还在路途上的时候，那头魏国派出的使臣已经抵达秦国了。
·
“拜见秦王。”
从前魏国官员未必能将秦王看在眼中，但如今地位不同了，而那使臣又与李斯有了约定，此时见了秦王，便热切了许多。使臣抬起头来，瞧了一眼秦王，却发觉这位秦王竟是比起从前的秦王，看上去更为威严。
使臣不自觉地腿软了一些，魏王特地嘱咐他的那些话，顿时都被他折中一下，用委婉的口吻说了出来。
而此时坐在高位之上的嬴政，面色微冷，口吻冷厉，“寡人还未询问魏国，如此对待寡人派去的使臣。”
柏舟和甘棠二人回来之后，一五一十地讲给了嬴政听，嬴政听完之后，没想着先把魏王捏死就不错了，现在魏王还要撩到他跟前来。那魏王多大的胆子，才敢与他嬴政抢人？
魏王如今看起来对秦国十分尊敬，但从魏王之举动，嬴政便能知晓，那魏王还是未将秦国放在眼中。
不然他怎么敢对秦国使臣下手？
当真是蠢得色欲将心窍都迷了吗？
那魏国使臣禁不住嬴政吓唬，不消嬴政多说上几句话，便立时认怂了，忙跪地道：“我定将秦王的意思转达魏王。”
“带他下去。”嬴政脸色阴沉地下了令。
那魏国使臣打了个哆嗦，心道不是说的好好的吗？那秦王总不至于宰了他吧？
秦国在他国眼中向来是野蛮又好战的形象，那魏国使臣不免心生惶恐，见那高大的内侍上前来将自己送了出去，被夹在中间的魏国使臣还抖了抖。
嬴政冷冷地看着人被带下去，手中的笔刀险些在桌案上戳个洞出来。
若不是柏舟早已交代过这人被李斯拉拢了，他必然也会给这使臣一个教训。
魏王做下的错事，总是要还的。
那六国还当他大秦是昔日那个秦国吗？
嬴政搁下手中笔刀，将柏舟叫到跟前来，“你说徐福身边跟有一人，那人是谁？与寡人细细说说。”比起与魏国来的软蛋使臣说话，嬴政自然更乐于向柏舟问起徐福的近况。
柏舟隐约知道龙阳君的身份，但却不敢说，于是只能含糊地道：“那人生得极为美貌，五官妩媚，身材高大，从魏王宫中出来的……”
哪怕柏舟不说，嬴政也已经猜到对方身份了。
如果只是使臣匆匆离去，哪会让魏王派人前来？必然是魏王被重重打了脸，觉得羞恼无比，这才命人前来与他讨个公道。
只是……嬴政冷笑一声。徐福做下的事，不论对错，那魏王也不可能从他这里讨到公道。
“那人可是龙阳君？”嬴政淡淡问道。
见嬴政面色如常，柏舟心底暗暗松了一口气，这才点头道：“正是。”
“魏王倚重的龙阳君……”嬴政低声念道。
柏舟的心不自觉地紧了紧，王上不会因此而发怒吧？
但下一刻，他却听嬴政大笑道：“哈哈哈……徐福敢将龙阳君拐到秦国来，也是魄力非凡了，无怪魏王跳脚。”
柏舟：……
他怎么觉得……有一种……不管徐先生捣了什么乱，王上都一脸骄傲且自豪在后面收拾烂摊子的感觉呢？
是他的错觉吧？
王上如此英明神武，此举应当是有深意的，说不定便是觉得那龙阳君才华非凡，纳入秦国也是一件快事……
不过嬴政虽然嘴上如此说，但暗地里还是要多做些准备，免得徐福将事情闹大发了。
嬴政做了一番部署之后，便忍不住问柏舟：“徐福何时去的韩国？几日方能归来？”
柏舟愣了愣，“……少说应当是一个月吧。”相处这段时间，柏舟也清楚了徐福的脾气，只要事情完成之后，在归途上，徐福必然会是慢悠悠的，还会特意去欣赏一番别国风情。
……少说……一个月……
嬴政觉得这个消息比听见徐福带了个龙阳君回来，带给他的冲击大多了。
嬴政起身往殿外走去。
赵高忙跟上去，“王上……”
嬴政轻声道：“寡人无食欲啊。”
赵高皱了皱脸，想了个损法子出来，“不若请几位舞姬前来……”
嬴政连听也未听完，便打断了他：“不必，那昌平君平叛平得如何了？将那奏报取来与寡人。”
赵高顿时就将所有的话都咽了进去，心中对于徐福地位的审估，又暗暗拔上了一个台阶。不过赵高此刻心中想的更多的是，这徐典事不会成为又一个龙阳君吧……
赵高并不乐于见到。
他低下头，快步转身去取奏报，将脑子里思绪统统掩埋了起来。
