午时。
用过一些饭食的徐福等人，驾着马车行在荒芜的道上。
眼看着便要到韩国与秦国接壤的边境处了，道路却被阻断了，那路上被巨石挡了去路，马车过不去，周围城镇定然有能前来修路之人，但不知要等上许久。徐福等人也不可能将马车丢弃在韩国境内，马车内有太多违制的东西，有心人看一看，便能猜到是秦国官员来韩国跑了一圈儿。
如此低调前来，那能不引人猜测吗？
于是一行人只能另辟蹊径，选了条更为宽阔，但也更为荒芜的道路。
那条道就隐藏在路旁的林子之后，他们也不知前方在何处，但总归是一个方向，总能回到秦国去的。
但他们走了许久，也不见人烟，如今春季已过，入夏时分，金乌当空，免不了让人生出几分烦躁来。
徐福只能暗自感叹，他立的flag，打脸这么快！不久之前还想着魏韩之行极为顺利，如今便生出些不顺来了。不过月满则亏，事情完成得如此圆满，会有些麻烦事出现，那才是正常的。
龙阳君掀起车帘往外瞥了一眼，“不能再往前了。”
桑中也点了点头，难得没反驳龙阳君的话，“前面瞧上去不对劲。”
徐福倒是出奇的淡定，“出行遇巨石阻路，不祥征兆。不过也没什么好怕的，往前走便是。”这种征兆代表，躲是躲不开的，绕过那巨石后，便难寻前路，也正是因为这个道理。迎难而上才是最后解决的方式。
龙阳君愣了愣，未曾想到徐福会如此说，龙阳君有自己的自信，他免不了笑道：“使臣如此笃定？往前走若是遇祸该如何？”说完，他顿了顿，又道：“使臣的模样，倒像是真的通卜筮之术一般。”
桑中嘴角微抽。心道，在你面前的使臣，他不仅通卜筮之术，还能算得极为准确精妙啊！
桑中和蒹葭二人自然是听徐福的，驾车的是他们，如今徐福发话，当然就继续往前走。
“马未必撑得住。”王柳坐在另一马车上，探出头来，微微皱眉道。
他说的倒也是实话。
他们一路奔波，人是休息好了，马却未必休息好了，而且来到韩国境内，容易水土不服的不止人，马儿也会。如今金乌当空，马儿会疲倦也是极为正常的。
“没事，我们就快停下了。”徐福还是一如既往的神棍口吻。
龙阳君心中好奇，想要知晓徐福何来如此笃定的底气，便也不说话了。
马车往前行了一段路，徐福突然出声，“停一停。”
众人怔了怔，正要问出心中不解，却就见前方的林子里钻出了一行人来。
那行人在大白天，却还手持火把，将自己浑身抹得漆黑，有些像是蜡祭礼上那些跳舞的人的打扮。
龙阳君更好奇了，“使臣的意思是，有人来，我们便不必往前走了？”
徐福点了点头，目光紧紧黏在那行人的身上。
其实他能看出有人来，跟相术并无关系，其中关系在于观察入微罢了。前方林子忽然有不少鸟儿扑腾着翅膀飞开，要么是巨型动物在其中穿行，要么就是有人在其中行走。但是这边哪来的巨型动物？最大的可能性就是人了。只要有人出现，他们也能歇一歇，问个路，寻个准确的方向，或者寻个落脚的地方了。
只是徐福没想到，出来的人打扮这样怪异。
“先别动。”
“往后撤！”
徐福和龙阳君说了两句全然不同的话。
二人不免对视了一眼。
他们当然都觉得这行人打扮怪异，不能与之冲撞，若是碰上蛮不讲理，又语言不通的人，说不定今天便有大麻烦。
徐福迟疑了一会儿，如今撤退已然来不及了，撤回去还是要被巨石挡过来，但是往上冲也不是个好的选择。
“到一边等着。”徐福道。
龙阳君不由得问道：“使臣不会觉得畏惧吗？”
徐福胆子的确很大，他摇了摇头，“无忧便无怖。”
龙阳君点头笑道：“那我便信使臣一回。”
徐福扫了他一眼，“如今同在一处，龙阳君不信也得信。”
其实处理这样的突发事件，徐福也较为驾轻就熟了。这些人看上去像是要去举行什么祭祀活动，这样与封建迷信扯上关系的活动，徐福这个从小与之打交道的神棍，还不能解决吗？
那行人注意到了徐福等人，目光凶恶地扫了过来，其中有一人，快步走过来，举着手中镰刀，问道：“什么人？”
徐福松了一口气，虽然带着浓重的口音，不过好歹能听明白说的是什么。
徐福那张脸具有极高的欺骗性，他探出头去，淡淡解释道：“我等不慎走错了路，烦请指个路，多谢。”
“你们要去哪里？”
“韩国边境。”
“穿过这片林子，你们小心些，不要破坏了林子。”那人虽然面容凶煞，但也还是认真回答了徐福的问题。
众人都没想到这样轻易便过了，于是忙对那人道了谢，驾着马车便要往林子去。
徐福往那行人中间扫了扫，却见着了几个并未打扮成这副模样的人。
那是几个年老衰弱的妇人，被夹在中间，带向了不远处的空地上。
有的人已经先前往那空地，架火，摆鼎，围着圈儿跳舞。
“这是什么？”徐福从未见过这样的习俗，不由得问道。
龙阳君倒是露出了恍然大悟的表情，低声道：“有一习俗，在农耕地极为常见。那便是‘吃母’。”
“吃母？”徐福脸色微变，“这些人要吃掉他们的母亲？”
龙阳君却是摇了摇头，“并非如此，吃母，乃是将母亲身上的农事经验利用特殊的巫术转至子孙身上，这样才能耕好地。”
又是巫术？
“那这巫术是如何使的？”
龙阳君摇头，“我也不知，只是曾听见这般传闻罢了。”
他话音刚落下，便见一身材高大的男子走到那火堆旁，将那几名年老的妇人推到了火堆之中，那几名妇人竟然连惨叫也未发出。徐福脸色一变，抓着马车的边缘便要跳出去。蒹葭和桑中也是脸色大变，但他们更要保护住徐福的安危，所以全然不敢轻举妄动。
龙阳君厉声道：“使臣想要做什么？同情她们吗？”
李斯同样面色难看，但却也不得不出于理智，道：“一地习俗通常流传多年，这地的百姓会维护他们的习俗，哪怕这个习俗再荒诞。一旦有人触碰，便会遭到人群起而攻之。”
徐福清楚这一点。
他也自认并非圣母。
但是看着妇人在跟前被烈火灼烧，却出于习俗的原因，还要死死地忍住惨叫声，何等痛苦！又何等愚昧！她们的灵魂难道不会发出嘶喊声吗？这些人真的就能眼睁睁看着昔日家人，于火中被烧死吗？
而此时那高大的男子，或许便是巫师之类的人物，他高举着手杖，从那些妇人头上挨个拍打而过，之后点在周围人的头上，大约便是传承之意了。
但是……这他妈什么鬼一样的传承方法啊？
难道他们以为烈火可以将妇人们的灵魂灼烧出来，最后由手杖抽走，再给予这些后代子孙吗？
这些子孙是如何忍得住痛苦的？
那一瞬间，徐福的脑中闪过了无数的思绪。
就将这一次也当做是修行吧……
徐福暗暗道。
“我与龙阳君打个赌。”
“什么赌？”龙阳君微微皱眉，难不成使臣还不死心？
“我便赌……我能改变他们的习俗！并且让他们百年，千年，都不再用此习俗！”徐福遥遥一指，目光凛然，与龙阳君对视。
“如何改变？”龙阳君便理智多了，何况这等小事，值得使臣如此吗？
“你且看着。”徐福也不再多言，直接越过了桑中和蒹葭二人，跳下马车头也不回地朝那方走去，李斯惊了一跳，忙跟着下了车，桑中和蒹葭更是直接奔了上去。
龙阳君揉了揉额角，“真不知道，这秦国来的使臣，是当真胆大，还是有资本胆大……”说罢，他倒也没有独善其身，而是跟着跳下了车。
这头的动静引起了那边人的注意。
围住火堆的一群人，立时便转过头来，虎视眈眈地紧紧盯着徐福。
“你们还要做什么？”原先给他们指路那人，冷声问道。就好像徐福一行人，入侵了他们的地盘，令他们瞬间紧张了起来。
桑中和蒹葭则是面色更冷地看了回去。
桑中和蒹葭身上气势明显强盛了不少，那人不由得往后退了退，但是却抓紧了手中的镰刀。
徐福扫了一眼在火堆中倒下的妇人，突然指着她们大喊了一声，“糟了！你们快看！还不快将人挪出来……”
那群人却不为所动，冷声问道：“你想做什么？走开！”
徐福朝桑中和蒹葭使了个眼色，随后便又扮演起了自己的神棍，“你们可是为了让以后的耕种更为顺利？收成更好？”
那群人依旧警惕且冷漠地瞪着他，动也不动。
“你们还看不出吗？如今你们这样做，只会令你们的收成，越来越糟……几年之后，连一顿饱饭也吃不上……”
“胡说八道！”那高大男子站出来，高声反驳徐福的话。
徐福看也不看他，转而问道：“是从去年开始的吧……去年良田荒芜，缺水厉害，收成减少，赋税却重，你们是不是十分慌乱？这才采用祖上流传下来的习俗，决心如此为之，以换来年平顺，收成大好，是吗？”
“说，是不是！”徐福的语气陡然一转，厉声问道。

chapters.translated_text:
When dealing with overbearing people, you have to be even more overbearing than them.

Xu Fu’s personality was never soft, so he was quite capable of being overbearing.

The people in front of him were stunned by his imposing manner and all took a step back. During this interval, Sang Zhong and Jian Jia had already stepped forward to rescue the women from the fire. However, flames were still licking at their clothes, so the two women decisively took off their outer garments and frantically beat out the sparks.

Seeing this, the shaman screamed, "What are you doing? Stop them! These people... these people will go to hell if they die! You are ruining the sacrifice! You are ruining the ritual! You are destroying the life of the entire village!"

That sounded even more exaggerated than his own swindling... Xu Fu mocked inwardly.

Only then did he realize that the tall, imposing shaman was not a man, but a woman; it was just that her voice was too hoarse, which had created the illusion.

Lord Longyang also stepped out from behind Xu Fu. He was still dressed as a woman, and because of his tall stature, he looked somewhat similar to the shaman.

The shaman froze for a moment, meeting Lord Longyang’s gaze, and then shrieked loudly, "Use witchcraft to sacrifice these people to the gods!"

"Unless you want to die!" Xu Fu turned his head to glance at her coldly, suddenly raising his voice to bark a sharp command that stopped them in their tracks.

At this moment, the sun was directly overhead and scorching. If not for the patch of woods nearby, even with all their might, Sang Zhong and Jian Jia would never have been able to extinguish the fire completely.

After the fire on the women was put out, they lay on the ground, dazed. Their throats still seemed to be gripped tightly, and no sound could be heard. Xu Fu could only catch glimpses of their trembling figures.

Xu Fu could more or less guess why they were like this.

One look at their reactions told him that the customs passed down from ancient times had poisoned them too deeply. They believed in such customs implicitly, convinced that through the "Mother-Eating" ritual, they could receive the inheritance of the clan’s older generation of women, and that even poor harvests caused by drought or heavy rain could be successfully resolved. This blind worship and trust not only made these descendants ignorant, but even these women themselves had become ignorant. When they were being scorched by the flames, they didn't even dare to scream, likely fearing that making a sound would be disrespectful to the gods and would appear as if they were resisting the ritual, which would then cause the ritual to fail.

There was likely no lack of sorrow and fear in their hearts, but they were driven more by the desire to sacrifice themselves for the clan, being pushed into the raging fire without a word.

Such things were not uncommon even in some backward regions in his previous life.

Their thinking was ignorant; they wouldn't have the slightest thought of resistance.

But was this really useful? Xu Fu scoffed.

He called himself a charlatan, but even he had never seen such unreliable "witchcraft."

That shaman was skulking about, wrapped in a black robe, which made Xu Fu feel unpleasant the moment he saw her. She definitely wasn't anything good! However, Xu Fu didn't intend to do anything to her. The shaman was just a blind follower; the existence of this ritual was the only reason shamans existed generation after generation. If one were to truly trace who was responsible for the deaths, not a single person here was innocent.

Whether these people lived or died wasn't important; what mattered was that if this ritual continued to be passed down, it would kill even more people.

If they killed a woman simply because she was old and frail, one day, these people would suffer a great loss!

...

Xu Fu reined in his thoughts, his face cold and his gaze like a torch. "This ritual is completely ineffective!"

Xu Fu said this the moment he opened his mouth. Lord Longyang, standing behind him, shook his head secretly. This wouldn't work; this wouldn't convince these people at all. On the contrary, because of his harsh tone, he was touching upon their faith, and it wasn't impossible that it might directly trigger a riot.

"What nonsense are you spouting? Outsider, what are you doing coming here and spouting nonsense? Get out! Get out!" Someone couldn't help but grab the sickle in their hand, rushing forward and reaching out to push Xu Fu.

Li Si was quick-witted and pulled Xu Fu back, beads of sweat faintly appearing on his forehead.

Anyone could be dealt with, and anyone was easy to handle, but these people were the hardest to deal with and impossible to reason with.

Xu Fu remained unfazed, saying calmly, "There is one part of this ritual that is wrong..." Of course, he wouldn't be stupid enough to reject the entire ritual outright. Even if he wanted to reject it, it had to be based on the premise that these people were already hooked by his deception. If he started by rejecting their customs and traditions, he wasn't just asking for abuse; he was practically asking for death.

The man gripped the sickle in his hand and stopped his steps. "...Y-you say, what is wrong?"

They were unwilling to doubt the customs passed down to them, but they couldn't help but wonder—the ritual indeed hadn't brought about any changes, so could it be that a step was accidentally passed down incorrectly during the transmission of the custom? The young man in front of them looked like he came from a wealthy family; surely he wouldn't... surely he wouldn't deliberately deceive them...

As long as one person’s mind wavered even slightly, more and more people would begin to waver.

Which part went wrong? At least that implied the custom itself wasn't wrong, just that one step in the middle was off...

By comparison, this explanation was naturally much easier to accept.

"Her performance of the witchcraft is incorrect."

Upon hearing this, before anyone else could say anything, the shaman flew into a rage, pointing at Qin Xi’s face and cursing loudly. Because it was mixed with too many accents and dialects, Xu Fu couldn't understand it, which was just as well—he didn't have to get angry over it.

Xu Fu didn't even glance at her.

At this moment, the knowledge of witchcraft and sorcery he had dug up in the Xianyang Palace finally came in handy.

"I have had the fortune to witness this ritual before. But their way of performing witchcraft is completely different from yours. You only know how to dance, but you do not know that the ritual requires an important vessel. Only with a vessel as a medium can the witchcraft power be manifested, and only then can the gods be summoned to satisfy what we seek." Xu Fu’s choice of words here was very subtle. When he said "we," he deliberately emphasized the tone. This was the invisible power of language, giving these people the illusion that he was standing on their side.

The man holding the sickle indeed relaxed his posture slightly.

This was already a sign that the other party was wavering.

"Heh, isn't my staff a vessel for transmitting witchcraft power?" The shaman sneered, holding her staff high.

In truth, calling it a staff was already giving it too much credit.

Xu Fu mocked unceremoniously, "How can such a piece of junk serve as a proper vessel?"

"You!" The shaman hadn't expected Xu Fu to start mocking her immediately, and she was rendered speechless on the spot.

After a long while, she sneered and retorted to Xu Fu, "Do you have a better vessel, then? Looking at you, you don't look like a shaman at all! Boy, don't go around smearing my reputation!"

The others lacked discernment, and hearing the shaman say this, they wavered again.

Xu Fu’s appearance indeed didn't look like that of a shaman.

Sang Zhong and the others secretly broke into a cold sweat for Xu Fu.

Just then, a woman said in a hoarse voice, "...H-he does."

Lord Longyang followed up, "Ancient records state that there were the Sichen, born beautiful and transcendent above the world. Whatever they thought in their hearts would turn into reality. They were a very powerful branch among the shamans."

The woman nodded, "Y-yes... that is so..."

The others didn't understand what "Sichen" meant.

But they knew what a "shaman" was.

A shaman meant a male sorcerer.

And this person had mentioned that whatever the Sichen thought would turn into reality.

Coupled with the woman’s acknowledgment, it undoubtedly confirmed this person’s identity—he must have a prestigious background! Although these people used the ritual to deprive mothers of their lives, they also trusted what the mothers said implicitly.

Seeing the situation turning increasingly unfavorable for her, the shaman became恼羞成怒 (embarrassed and angry), holding her staff high toward Xu Fu and shouting, "You filthy and ominous person, watch how I drive you away!" With that, she actually began chanting a spell at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu sneered, his posture cold and arrogant. "Jian Jia, use the move I taught you to deal with this third-rate shaman."

"Ah?" Jian Jia was stunned.

The move he taught?

Which move?

Upon hearing Xu Fu call her third-rate, the shaman became even more agitated, waving her staff wildly and chanting the spell even louder.

Lord Longyang chuckled, pulled Xu Fu back, and said with a smile, "Teacher, let me handle it."

Lord Longyang could tell at a glance that Xu Fu was just bluffing them.

That shaman did indeed look like a half-baked amateur; there was nothing to fear.

Lord Longyang was agile, and his movements were elegant—he looked more like he was performing witchcraft than the shaman did. In the blink of an eye, Lord Longyang snatched the staff from the shaman’s hand and kicked her to the ground. The shaman let out a miserable shriek. As she raised her head, she saw Lord Longyang easily snap the staff into two pieces. The shaman had just looked up when she was struck in the face by the pieces, causing her to shriek again.

It turned out that while the staff looked intimidating, it was made of cheap wood on the inside.

"You... you! You evil things! You should be burned to death!" The shaman screamed at the top of her lungs, only to be pinned to the ground by Lord Longyang’s foot, unable to even crawl away.

Xu Fu kicked the staff scattered on the ground and said coldly, "Take a look, is this what you call a vessel? Tsk, if I were a god, I wouldn't even want to descend. Is this what witchcraft is supposed to look like?"

Xu Fu walked right past the shaman and pulled an object from his sleeve.

He stopped by the bonfire.

The sun was high in the sky, and the fire was burning even more fiercely. As soon as Xu Fu approached, the heat hit his face, making him feel quite uncomfortable.

He really didn't know how those elderly women had endured it.

Xu Fu gripped the tripod in his hand.

Yes, a tripod!

It was the small tripod he carried with him. It was exquisitely crafted and looked more like a sacrificial object; however, taking it out to act as a vessel was enough to bluff them.

"Do you know what this is?" Xu Fu held the tripod high.

The crowd naturally didn't know, and some became restless. "What is this? Can this make the ritual error-free?"
chapters.title: 第77章
chapters.source_text:
对于横的人，你就得比他更横才行。
徐福性格从来不就软，所以他相当横得起来。
面前的人便被他的气势镇住，统统朝后退了退，就在这期间，桑中和蒹葭已经上前，将火中的妇人救了出来。只是她们身上还吞吐着火舌，两人当机立断脱下外套奋力去扑打着身上的火苗。
巫师见状，尖叫道：“你们干什么？快阻止他们！这些人……这些人死了是要下地狱的！你们破坏了祭祀！你们破坏了仪式！你们破坏了整个村庄的生命！”
说得比他忽悠人还夸张呢……徐福心中暗自嘲讽。
他这才听出来，那身形高大的巫师，并不是男子，而是女子，只是她的声音太过沙哑，才会给人造成错觉。
龙阳君也从徐福的身后走了出来，他还是作女子打扮，因为身材高大，瞧上去与那巫师倒是有几分相似之感。
那巫师怔了怔，对上龙阳君那张脸，尔后高声叫嚣着：“把这些人都用巫术祭神！”
“除非你们想死！”徐福转头冷冷地瞥了她一眼，陡然拔高声音，厉声将他们喝止住了。
此时金乌当头，阳光正烈，若不是这边有一片林子，桑中和蒹葭就是费了老劲儿，也不可能将火全部扑灭。
妇人们身上的火被扑灭之后，便呆呆地躺在地上，嗓子依旧像是被用力掐着一样，什么声音也听不见了，徐福只能瞥见妇人们微微抖动的身影。
徐福差不多能猜到为什么她们会这样。
看他们的反应就知道，古时流传下来的习俗，已经对他们荼毒太深，他们对这样的习俗深信不疑，深信通过“吃母”的仪式，就能够得到来自氏族老一辈妇人的传承，哪怕是干旱或大雨而造成的收成不好，也能顺利解决了。这样的盲目崇拜与信任，不仅将这些子孙后代变得愚昧了，就连这些妇人也变得愚昧了，她们被烈火灼烧时，甚至不敢叫喊出声来，应该是担心自己发出喊声，会是对神灵的不敬，会表现得如同反抗这个仪式，那么仪式就会遭到破坏。
她们心中未必没有悲伤和恐惧，但她们更怀着牺牲自我，献给氏族的心情，一言不发地被推入烈火。
这样的事，哪怕是在上辈子一些落后的地区，也并不少见。
她们的思维是愚昧的，根本不会有半点反抗的心思。
可这样真的有用吗？徐福嗜之以鼻。
他自称神棍，但他都没见过这么不靠谱的“巫术”。
那巫师藏头露尾，将自己裹在黑袍之中，徐福一看就不由心生不快。肯定不是什么好东西！不过徐福也没打算对人家怎么样。巫师也就是个盲目从众者，因为有了这个仪式的存在，所以才有了一代代巫师的存在。要真正论起来害死人的，这里一个人也不干净。
这些人死不死，都不重要，重要的是，这个仪式流传下去才会害死更多的人。
若是因为妇人年老体衰了，便杀死她，总有一日，这些人会吃大亏！
……
徐福收起思绪，面容冰冷，目光如炬，“这个仪式根本就是无效的！”
徐福张嘴就说这么一句话，龙阳君在其后暗自摇头，这样是不行的，这样根本说服不了这些人，反而会因为语气强硬，触及到他们的信仰，甚至直接引起这些人暴动，也不无可能。
“你胡说什么？外乡人，跑到我们这里来胡说什么？滚开！滚！”有人忍不住抓着手中的镰刀，冲上前来，伸手就要去推徐福。
李斯眼疾手快，将徐福往后拉了拉，额上隐隐冒出了些汗珠来。
谁都可以对付，谁都好对付，却独独这些人最难对付，也无从对付。
徐福巍然不惧，淡淡道：“这个仪式，有一个地方，错了……”他当然不会蠢到将整个仪式全盘否决，就算要否决，那也要建立在这些人被他忽悠住了的基础上，如果开口就否决人家的习俗、传统，这不是找骂，根本就是在找死。
那人握了握手中的镰刀，顿住了步子，“……你、你说，哪里错了？”
他们并不愿意去怀疑流传下来的习俗，但是他们会不自觉地去想，这个仪式的确没有带来变化，那会不会是习俗在流传的过程中，不小心传错了一节呢？眼前的少年，瞧上去也是富贵人家，总不至于……总不至于故意哄骗他们吧……
只要有一个人脑子里微微动摇了，那么就会有越来越多的人开始动摇。
哪一节出错，至少说明这个习俗并不是错误的，只是中间有一节出错了而已……
相比之下，这个说法当然更让人容易接受。
“她的巫术施展得不对。”
那巫师闻言，还不等其他人说什么，就已经暴跳如雷了，指着秦溪的脸，破口大骂，因为夹杂了太多口音和方言，徐福也听不明白，正好，也就不用为此生气了。
徐福看也没看她一眼。
此时，他在咸阳宫中翻出来瞧的什么巫蛊术，便在此时派上用场了。
“这个仪式，我也曾有缘见过。但他们与尔等施展巫术的方式全然不同。尔等只知舞蹈，却不知仪式之中需要重要的容器，唯有以容器为承载，巫力才能通过容器得以呈现，之后才能唤来神灵，满足我等所求之事。”这里徐福的用词也很微妙，他念到“我等”时，便刻意加重了一些语气，这是通过语言无形中的力量，带给这些人一种，他与他们站在一起的错觉。
握着镰刀的人果然稍微放松了肢体。
这已经是对方在动摇的一个信息了。
“呵，我的手杖不就是传递巫力的容器吗？”那巫师冷笑一声，高举起手中的手杖。
其实说是手杖，都是抬高了它。
徐福毫不客气地嘲讽道：“这等破烂玩意儿，如何能做上好的容器？”
“你！”巫师没想到徐福开口就放嘲讽，当即就被堵得说不出话来。
半晌她才冷笑一声，反问徐福：“难道你还有更好的容器吗？瞧你这模样，根本不像是做巫师的！小子勿要胡乱要往我头上盖污名！”
其余人难有分辨力，听巫师如此一说便又动摇了。
徐福的模样，看上去的确不像是做巫师的啊。
桑中等人暗自为徐福捏了把汗。
而此时却有个妇人，声音嘶哑道：“……有、有的。”
龙阳君接声道：“古时有记载，有斯辰，生而美丽，超脱于世，他们心中所想，便会化为事实。他们是觋之中力量极为强大的一支。”
妇人点头，“是……是如此……”
其余人听不明白，什么叫斯辰。
但他们知道觋为何物。
觋为男巫的意思。
而这人口中又提及，斯辰心中所想，便会化为事实。
加上那妇人开口认同，无疑是承认了这人的身份，定然是大有来头！这些人虽然用仪式剥夺母亲的生命，但同时他们也是极为信任母亲口中所言的。
巫师见场面对自己越发不利，恼羞成怒起来，高举起手中的手杖，对着徐福的方向，大喝一声，“你这等污秽不详之人，看我如何将你驱走！”说罢，她还真的对徐福念起了咒语。
徐福冷笑一声，姿态冷傲，“蒹葭，用我教你那一招，来对付这个不入流的巫师。”
“啊？”蒹葭愣了愣。
教的那一招？
哪一招啊？
那巫师在听见徐福骂她不入流之后，情绪更为激动，胡乱挥舞着手杖，口中念的咒语更为大声。
龙阳君嗤笑一声，将徐福往后拽了拽，笑道：“老师，还是我来罢。”
龙阳君一眼就能看出，徐福这是要糊弄他们呢。
那巫师瞧上去的确是个半吊子的玩意儿，没什么可畏惧的。
龙阳君身手利落，动作偏偏还优美，看上去比巫师更像是在施展巫术，也就眨了个眼的功夫，龙阳君就夺过了巫师手中的手掌，一脚将那巫师撂翻在地，巫师惨叫一声，抬起头来，就见龙阳君轻而易举地将那手杖掰成了两段，巫师刚一抬头就被砸了个照面，不由得又惨叫了一声。
原来那手杖瞧上去模样唬人，但内里却是木头做的。
“你……你们！你们这些邪物！应该烧死你们！”那巫师声嘶力竭地喊出声来，偏偏被龙阳君一脚踩在地上，爬都爬不起来。
徐福踹了一脚散落在地的手杖，冷声道：“瞧一瞧，这就是所谓的容器？嘁，若我为神灵，我都不愿降临。巫术何曾是这般模样的？”
徐福直接从那巫师身旁走过，从袖中掏出一物来。
他在火堆旁顿住脚步。
烈日当空，那火堆燃得越发旺了，徐福刚一走近，就是扑面而来的热气，熏得他有些难受。
真不知道那几个年老的妇人，是如何忍下来的。
徐福握了握手中的鼎。
对，鼎！
就是那只随身携带的小鼎，模样精致，瞧上去倒是更像祭祀之物，不过拿出来充当容器，倒也能唬人了。
“你们可知这为何物？”徐福高举手中鼎。
众人自然不知，有人躁动起来，“这是什么？难道这就能让仪式无误吗？”

chapters.title: 第78章
chapters.translated_text:
"A tripod is a vessel for cooking, and it also symbolizes abundance. What is it that you seek? You seek a good harvest, and isn't that so that you can have enough grain to fill your bellies in the coming year, and even for years to come?"

"Different vessels naturally serve different purposes. Each deity has their own duties; if you randomly pick something to serve as a vessel for shamanic power, how can you expect to reach the gods?"

The crowd’s expressions went blank, vaguely feeling that this logic seemed to hold up.

"The final step is even more egregiously wrong! If you push people into the fire, I fear they would be burned to death before the ritual even concludes."

The shaman sneered, "What nonsense are you spouting? How could they die? That isn't death at all; it is simply offering their souls to the gods!"

Xu Fu was very displeased that someone had interrupted him. He cast a cold, sharp glance at the shaman, his gaze so piercing it felt as if it could penetrate the black robe and skewer the person beneath it. The shaman involuntarily shrank her neck. Lord Longyang stomped down hard, "Shut your mouth." The shaman let out a miserable shriek, sweating profusely from the pain, and finally fell silent.

"Offering souls to the gods? The gods are arrogant; why would they ever look upon the souls of mortals? To communicate with the gods and obtain shamanic power, one needs items that are more spiritually resonant. A vessel is sufficient; why would you need a human?" Xu Fu wouldn't say that if a god required human lives, it wouldn't be worth a damn. In earlier times, the nature of gods was indeed cold and ruthless; if he tried to force the idea of a compassionate and kind deity onto them, these people would only think he was spouting nonsense.

"We do this for the sake of our heritage!" someone shouted, unconvinced.

"Why would heritage require such things? Shamanic rituals have many variations. You have already chosen the wrong vessel; is it not obvious that the final step of the ritual is also wrong?" Xu Fu spoke with great speed and force, giving them no time to think carefully.

"Jianjia, help them up," Xu Fu suddenly turned and ordered. "Have them sit around the fire, facing outward."

Sangzhong and Jianjia obeyed without a word, helping the women up and having them sit in an outer circle a bit further from the fire. The women were somewhat bewildered, looking at Xu Fu with a mixture of fear and awe.

"Close your eyes!" Xu Fu suddenly barked, his voice like a thunderclap exploding in their ears. Combined with his cold, detached tone, it sounded as if it had come from beyond the heavens, and everyone closed their eyes involuntarily.

The surroundings fell into a deep silence, with only the faint crackling of the fire audible.

A while passed, and still, there was no movement.

Lord Longyang hadn't closed his eyes at all, and he found himself wanting to laugh at the sight of Xu Fu.

The others opened their eyes one after another, only to see Xu Fu walking into the circle where the women were sitting. He held the tripod high, his shadow stretched long, making him look tall and majestic. This stunned the crowd into silence; no one dared to speak, even with their minds full of doubt and suspicion.

And Xu Fu, who had been treating himself like the Statue of Liberty and Dong Cunrui, finally remembered how the incantation went.

"Gods of the heavens, heed my plea..." Xu Fu paused, then suddenly switched to an English incantation.

The others were stunned the moment he opened his mouth. They couldn't understand a word he was saying, but seeing his serious and solemn expression, a sense of awe couldn't help but rise in their hearts.

Even Lord Longyang was somewhat taken aback.

At first, he thought Xu Fu was just babbling, but the more he listened, the more Lord Longyang felt that the words coming from Xu Fu’s mouth had a certain rhythm—perhaps it was... another language?

Lord Longyang felt a slight sense of shock in his heart.

It didn't sound like the language of any of the Seven States; even he had never heard it before.

This envoy truly had some impressive skills! This was interesting...

Xu Fu recited a long string of English. Since he finished it with fluent articulation despite the slightly off-key pronunciation, the crowd was left dizzy and confused, much like students who are baffled before they even finish a listening test in their past lives.

His ability to bluff was truly strong.

Then, Xu Fu loosened his grip, and the small tripod in his hand suddenly plummeted.

Everyone was startled, including Sangzhong and Jianjia, who were dumbfounded, amazed at the extent of Xu Fu’s sacrifice—he had actually thrown away his "beloved" tripod!

The crowd couldn't understand why he would throw the vessel away.

But in that split second, just as the tripod landed steadily in the middle of the fire, the tongues of flame were suddenly sucked away by the tripod, and the fire slowly began to retract and shrink. Looking at the handsome youth standing by the fire, his white robes fluttering in the heat, his expression cold and stern, no one could look more like a mysterious and lofty shaman than him.

Never mind the stunned crowd, even Xu Fu himself hadn't expected this. He had only intended to throw the tripod to put on a show, but who knew that as soon as it landed, it would trigger such a strange reaction? The eyes of those around him turned burning hot as they looked at the tripod, and their gaze toward Xu Fu became even more fearful.

No matter how the shaman performed her rites, she could never produce a reaction visible to the naked eye, but now that they could see such a miraculous change, they couldn't help but feel awe.

Once this foundation was laid, it would be much easier for Xu Fu to continue his charade.

"...The ritual is complete."

It took a long time for the crowd to snap out of their trance and hear that cold, clear voice conclude the ceremony.

"The heritage has now been passed to you, and what you seek will soon come to pass." Xu Fu stared at the fire and said faintly. No one knew that he was actually a bit worried about whether his tripod would be ruined by the heat; if it were ruined, what would he do?

"...It has already been passed?" These people didn't dare to make a sound for a long time, and only after hearing Xu Fu say this did they cautiously speak up, their faces still filled with wonder. This was completely different from the tribe’s rituals in previous years; was this really effective?

But Xu Fu’s performance was just too convincing.

He and Lord Longyang were so beautiful that they didn't look like people of this mortal world, and anyone who saw them would involuntarily lower their guard.

The shaman, still pinned under Lord Longyang’s foot, struggled unconvinced, "Just because you say it’s done, does that make it so?"

"Naturally. The gods have already heard your cries..." Xu Fu looked up at the sky. "Within two days, there will be heavy rain. The drought will be resolved. In two days, I will teach you another shamanic art that you can use whenever you encounter a drought, but remember not to use it too frequently, or the gods will visit their wrath upon you."

Lord Longyang frowned slightly.

Within two days?

Who would dare to make such a boast? If not for the second half of his statement, Lord Longyang would have thought Xu Fu was planning to leave immediately after his bluff. But based on the second half, he intended to stay here for two days? Was he crazy? Lord Longyang couldn't understand.

Sangzhong and Jianjia both felt their hearts tighten involuntarily.

Only Li Si watched Xu Fu’s back with burning eyes. Perhaps he was about to witness the miraculous nature of Envoy Xu once again...

"Th-thank you, my lord..." The people could no longer care whether Xu Fu’s words would actually come true. Just hearing that he would teach them a shamanic art made them so excited that they hurriedly bowed to him.

Who would ever easily teach shamanic arts to others?

In their eyes, Xu Fu instantly became glorious, tall, and selfless...

"Don't believe him! What 'within two days'? It's impossible!" the shaman sneered and shouted loudly.

"Whether I am right or wrong will be clear within two days; that is not long at all, is it?" Xu Fu paused. "If I am right, you must no longer let this person serve as your shaman. I will choose another from among you to pass on the arts."

"What right do you have..." The shaman struggled even more violently upon hearing this.

But the trust the others had in Xu Fu had already been raised quite high. They exchanged glances and immediately reached an agreement with him.

"After it is over, you will send one person to lead us out of this place."

"That is only natural!" the people agreed readily.

Their gaze toward Xu Fu was now filled with a sense of reverence, as if he were a god.

Someone from among them stepped forward to help the women up from the ground, then asked Xu Fu, "Does my lord wish to return with us?"

"Naturally, we shall return together," Xu Fu said calmly.

Lord Longyang’s shock deepened. Could this envoy truly be addicted to bluffing? How could he control whether it rained or not? If it didn't come to pass, how would he clean up this mess? Things had reached this point, and Lord Longyang couldn't stop him, so he could only sigh inwardly and keep his mouth shut.

This envoy’s temperament was still a bit too impulsive.

These people were all from a small village called Liang Village, the sound of which was the same as "grain," which showed how much this small village valued their crops.

It had been hard for Liang Village to see a real heavy rain in recent years, and the harvests were gradually becoming worse than before. For these farmers, this was a life-or-death matter. Their moral sense was weak; when the shaman proposed the ritual of "eating the mother" to inherit the wisdom of the older generation, they agreed, and the older women had no complaints, holding a fearless spirit as they prepared to sacrifice themselves for the village.

After hearing this, Sangzhong and Jianjia were both filled with sighs; they hadn't expected such customs to be practiced by anyone.

They followed the people of Liang Village through the woods.

Fortunately, the trees in the forest were not densely packed, so the carriage could barely squeeze through. After passing through the woods and climbing a slope, they saw a village. Smoke curled from the chimneys, and in a place that should have been lush and green, the trees and flowers showed signs of withering. It was easy to imagine that the fields were no better.

Among these people was a leading man named "A-Liang."

A-Liang’s house was relatively spacious, so he brought Xu Fu and the others to his home.

A-Liang’s small courtyard was just big enough to fit the carriage and the horses.

A-Liang didn't dare to offend Xu Fu, and after bringing him into the house, he hurried away, fearing that this shaman might be dissatisfied with him.

As soon as A-Liang left, Lord Longyang couldn't help but ask, "Where does the envoy get his confidence? If there is no heavy rain in two days, what then?" As he spoke, Lord Longyang frowned, saying with disapproval, "The envoy really shouldn't be so headstrong." Ever since Xu Fu insisted on moving forward, Lord Longyang had been quite disapproving of his actions.

Even Jianjia and Sangzhong cast puzzled glances at Xu Fu. Although they knew Xu Fu was capable, they couldn't help but worry.

Xu Fu turned to look at Li Si, who had been silent the whole time, and asked, "Does Chief Clerk Li know what I used to do at the Fengchang Temple?"

Li Si smiled, "Grand Historian, the Grand Historian is in charge of observing celestial phenomena. If it comes to predicting the weather, I imagine no one can compare to you." Clearly, he had great trust in Xu Fu.

"Grand Historian?" Lord Longyang raised an eyebrow. As far as he knew, even the Grand Historian was a relatively low-ranking official; how could he come to the State of Wei as an envoy? And to have a Chief Clerk treat him with such respect—there must be something extraordinary about him.

Sangzhong and Jianjia finally realized, "So the reason you said that earlier, sir, is because you had already observed the celestial signs?"

"Celestial signs combined with divination make it easy to deduce," Xu Fu paused, but he didn't say the rest of what was on his mind. In truth, let alone him, even advanced scientific instruments could easily make mistakes when predicting the weather. As the saying goes, the heavens are unpredictable; the weather is the hardest thing to forecast. Although he spoke with such certainty, it wasn't actually the case. His prediction carried a risk.

But he wouldn't mention the risk. Talking about it would only cause others to worry, and since they didn't understand the craft, it would be useless anyway.

Besides...

Did he look like someone who wouldn't have a backup plan?

Xu Fu remained perfectly calm, "Let us rest here for a while."

Lord Longyang’s interest grew, "Now I am even more curious about what official position the envoy actually holds in the State of Qin."

Li Si smiled, "Lord Longyang will naturally know when you arrive in the State of Qin."

Lord Longyang suppressed his curiosity, "I hope so."

It must be said that having a place to stop and rest was not bad. That night, the villagers brought some food—the best they could find. However, out of caution, Lord Longyang declined it, and Jianjia and the others said nothing. They had their own dry rations and didn't need to eat the villagers' food. The villagers had very little grain, and if they went hungry, there was no telling what crazy things they might do later.

When people are not well-fed, how can they afford to talk about propriety, righteousness, and shame?

After a night of rest, everyone woke up early, and the villagers sat outside their doors, waiting for the moment the rain would come.

Only Xu Fu remained lazily in bed, sleeping in comfortably. Once he was well-rested, he got up, ate some dry rations, drank some water, and then stepped out of the house.

When the villagers saw him, they hurriedly and cautiously bowed.

Just then, a woman walked quickly from a distance.

The woman was dressed in coarse hemp clothes and had an ordinary appearance; because her eyebrows were arched, she looked somewhat fierce. She walked over quickly, cast a cold glance at Xu Fu, and sneered, "Didn't you say there would be rain? Where is the rain? It is already dusk!"

When the woman spoke, Xu Fu realized she was the shaman, only she had removed the heavy black robe she had been wearing.

The woman’s voice drew the attention of other villagers. They all looked at Xu Fu with anxious and worried eyes, but no one dared to urge him. They were afraid that this shaman lord, in a fit of rage, would cast a spell on them. Xu Fu might not have achieved anything else, but making the villagers fear him was easy.

Xu Fu looked up at the sky, feeling even more confident.

He raised his hand and pointed far into the distance, "Look."

Everyone couldn't help but follow the direction he pointed.

Over there, clouds were rolling into balls, sweeping rapidly across the horizon. The entire sky looked like a pot of boiling water, and the cloud masses were like tumbling dumplings, crowding and pushing against each other. Because they were moving at an excessively fast speed, it looked as if a deity were casting a spell in the sky.

"Do not look for too long; that is the gods stirring the sky. When the sky settles, rain will naturally fall from above," Xu Fu began to spout nonsense again.

Yet these villagers believed him deeply. They looked up for a moment, then hurriedly lowered their heads, fearing that one extra glance would disturb the gods.

The shaman was furious but had no way to refute him.

The strange phenomenon in the sky did look quite terrifying and was indeed a sign of impending rain. Could it be... could it be that this person was actually right?

Lord Longyang was also quite surprised. He had thought Xu Fu was just spouting nonsense, but it turned out there was a basis for it...

Xu Fu didn't stay outside for long and soon turned back toward the house. At this point, the villagers only dared to steal glances at his back, not even daring to make a tiny sound.

It wasn't until later that someone whispered, "A noble person has come to our tribe..."

"Not a noble person, it's the Shaman Lord..." someone said worshipfully.

The others looked at the shaman with disdain, but since they were all of the same tribe, they just sighed and comforted her, "You just haven't learned enough. You should beg that lord to teach you more, and then it will be fine..."

The shaman snorted coldly and turned to leave.

Soon it was dusk, and the golden sun was quickly obscured by dark clouds as it dipped below the mountains.

The villagers stood outside their houses, not daring to move a single step. They swallowed hard, as if waiting together to witness the birth of a miracle.

The sun slowly disappeared from view, while the clouds continued to roll across the horizon. A wind picked up, causing the large trees outside the village to rustle loudly.

Xu Fu sat in the house, eating his dry rations and drinking water in a leisurely manner.

The villagers were still waiting foolishly.

Jianjia was the first to grow impatient. He couldn't help but ask Xu Fu, "Sir, will it really rain?"

Sangzhong reached out and patted him from behind, "What are you saying? What the master says is naturally accurate; if he says it will rain, it will rain."

Gradually, the hour grew late, and there was still no sign of rain. The villagers had been craning their necks for so long that A-Liang couldn't help but run into the courtyard, knock on the door, and ask, "...Shaman Lord, the rain... it hasn't fallen yet..." A-Liang’s face was flushed red. A tall, middle-aged man standing before the youth-like Xu Fu, he felt inexplicably shorter.

Everyone was anxious and wanted to ask Xu Fu, but no one dared to offend him.

But waiting was always agonizing.

Xu Fu remained calm, "Just go back and sleep. Two days haven't passed yet, why worry?"

He made it sound so easy, but it was hard for the villagers to do.

A-Liang didn't dare to ask again, and with no other options, he walked out and conveyed Xu Fu’s words to the crowd. They waited together for a long time, and until it was very late, they returned to their houses with heavy hearts. Of course, there were a few who whispered complaints about Xu Fu, but they didn't dare to say it out loud.

After washing up, Xu Fu immediately went to bed to rest.

The others looked at each other and also went to sleep on the floor mats in the room.

At this time, the shaman, wearing a dusty, dirty robe, snuck out of the courtyard and found a small hill to sit on. She snorted coldly, looked up, and stared intently at the dark, heavy sky...

"I will definitely catch you in your lies; I will definitely prove that you are a fraud." The shaman gritted her teeth, rubbed her sore neck, looked up, straightened her back, and watched the sky earnestly.

A few insects chirped in the distance.

...

*

In the Xianyang Palace.

The moon was high in the sky, and a palace maid carefully stepped forward to trim the candle wick.

Ying Zheng rubbed his neck, only then realizing his back was stiff. He closed the bamboo slips in his hand and stood up from his seat.

The palace maid was startled and hurriedly bowed, asking, "Your Majesty, shall I prepare hot water?"

Ying Zheng gave a grunt of acknowledgment, walked out of the hall, and returned to his sleeping quarters.

The maid in the sleeping quarters saw Ying Zheng enter and stepped forward, saying, "Your Majesty, today Prince Fusu came again to ask about the whereabouts of Official Xu."

Ying Zheng paused and frowned slightly, "I know."

Ying Zheng was in a foul mood and asked his attendant, "When did Bo Zhou say last time that Xu Fu would return?"

The attendant was sweating profusely, "I imagine, I imagine... it should be within these one or two days..."

Calculating it, it should indeed be within these few days. The longing in Ying Zheng’s heart surged like a tide. He suppressed his emotions, his mood becoming even worse, "Bo Zhou has deceived me. Since Xu Fu has not returned, order him to guard the city gates for these few days; he is not to leave until Xu Fu returns."

The attendant replied "Yes," bowing his head while mentally lighting a candle for Bo Zhou.

The maid had prepared the hot water.

Now that Xu Fu was not by his side at night, Ying Zheng naturally found sleeping to be dull. Coupled with his busy government affairs and his heart full of plans to conquer the six states, to alleviate the bone-deep longing he felt, Ying Zheng processed government affairs day and night. When it was late, he used hot water to relieve his fatigue.

Ying Zheng took off his robes and stepped into the bathtub. He closed his eyes and leaned against the side of the tub to rest. But before he knew it, Xu Fu’s face appeared in his mind. Ying Zheng’s heart stirred, and as he recalled the smooth skin of Xu Fu, he involuntarily reached his hand down...

“鼎，乃烹饪之器，鼎，有象征富足之意。你们所求为何？所求为农事，为的不就是来年，甚至日后年年都能有足够的粮食果腹吗？”
“不同的容器，自然是起不同的作用，众神灵各司其职，若是胡乱寻个东西当做巫力的容器，如何能求到神灵？”
众人的表情呆了呆，迷迷糊糊地觉得好像是这个道理。
“最后一步，更是大错特错！若是将人推进火堆之中，恐怕未等仪式结束，她们就先烧死了。”
巫师冷笑一声，“胡说什么？她们哪里会死？那根本就不是死，只是将灵魂献与神灵！”
徐福非常不高兴此刻有人来打断他，他冷冷地瞥了一眼巫师，他的目光冰冷又锐利，几乎要穿透那黑袍，将黑袍底下的巫师扎个透，巫师不自觉地缩了缩脖子。龙阳君重重踩了一脚，“闭上你的嘴。”巫师惨叫一声，疼得满头大汗，这才不说话了。
“灵魂献于神灵？神灵高傲，怎么会看得上凡人的灵魂？与神灵沟通，获得巫力，需要更通灵气的东西，有容器便可，何须要人？”徐福不会说，若是连人命都吃的神灵，那还算什么狗屁神灵。在更早的时期，神明的设定的确就是冷酷无情的，若是强行将神明往慈悲心善上靠，反而会让这些人觉得他在瞎扯。
“我们是为了传承！”有人不服气地嚷出声来。
“传承何须如此？巫术仪式有诸多变化，你们连容器都弄错了，仪式的最后一步，难道还不是错的吗？”徐福语速极快，又铿锵有力，根本不给这些人仔细思考的时间。
“蒹葭，将人扶起来。”徐福突然转头吩咐道，“让她们围着火堆坐下，面朝外。”
桑中和蒹葭自然是二话不说，便将人扶了起来，在距离火堆稍远的外圈沿着坐下。那几名妇人有些惶然，看着徐福的目光又惊惧又敬畏。
“闭眼！”徐福突然怒喝一声，如一道惊雷在众人耳边炸开，加之他声音清冷，就好像是从天外来的声音一般，所有人不自觉地闭上眼。
四周一片静寂，只能隐隐听见火堆燃烧的噼啪声。
一会儿的功夫过去了，还是什么动静也没有。
龙阳君压根没闭眼，他望着徐福的模样有些想笑。
而其他人此时也陆陆续续睁开了双眼，只见徐福走进了妇人围坐的圈子里，他高举着手中之鼎，影子被拉长，看上去高大又威严。倒是将一干人都镇住了，他们谁也不敢在此时出声，哪怕满腹的疑惑和怀疑。
而将自己当做自由女神像和董存瑞的徐福，终于想起了咒语是怎么念的。
“漫天神明，应吾之所求啊……”徐福顿了顿，突然改说了英文咒语。
其他人听他一开口就被镇住了，听了半天都没能听明白徐福说的什么，但是见徐福面色认真凝重，他们心中就不由得升起了一股敬畏之情。
就连龙阳君也有些被镇住。
初时他以为徐福是在胡言乱语，但是越听，龙阳君越觉得徐福口中说出的话是有条理的，或许是……另一种语言？
龙阳君心中微微有些惊骇。
听上去根本不像是七国任一国的语言，连他也从未听过。
这使臣实在本事不小！有些意思……
徐福念了番英文，这段英文还挺长的，所以等他虽然音不太准但口齿流利地念完，众人已经听得头昏脑涨，有些蒙圈儿了，就跟上辈子那些听力考试还没听完就先懵逼的学生一样。
忽悠能力真心强。
随后徐福手一松，手中那只小鼎骤然坠落了下去。
所有人都惊了一跳，包括桑中和蒹葭也目瞪口呆，惊讶于徐福的牺牲如此之大，竟然直接把他“心爱”的鼎给扔下去了！
众人想不明白他为什么要将容器扔下去。
但是刹那间，就在小鼎稳稳坠落在火堆中间的刹那间，火舌突然被那只鼎卷走了不少，然后火苗慢慢地开始收回、变小。再看那火堆旁站着的美貌少年，白衣被热浪掀起，面容冷厉，不会有人比他更像神秘又高高在上的觋了。
莫说是已经看呆了的众人，就连徐福自己也没想到。他要扔鼎，就只是装一装样子，谁知道鼎刚一落下去，就引起了这样怪异的反应，周围的人看向那鼎的目光变得灼热了起来，看向徐福的目光也更惊惧了起来。
那巫师不管如何作法，都难以有什么肉眼便能看到的反应，而如今他们肉眼就能看到如此惊奇的变化，他们便忍不住生出了敬畏之心。
一旦有了这个基础，之后徐福再要进行忽悠，就容易得多了。
“……仪式完成。”
众人恍惚了许久，才听见那道清冷的声音做了终结。
“现在传承已经到你们身上了，而你们所求之事很快便会应验。”徐福盯着那火堆，淡淡道，没有人知道，他此刻其实有些担心，自己那只鼎会不会给烤坏了，要是烤坏了，那得怎么办？
“……已经到了？”这些人半天不敢发出声音，现在听见徐福这么一说，这才小心地出声，他们的脸上还带着惊奇之色。这与族中往年的仪式大不一样，这样真的有用吗？
但徐福的表现实在太能忽悠人。
他和龙阳君的模样姣好得不似凡尘中人，任谁见了都会不自觉地放松警惕。
巫师被龙阳君踩在脚下，依旧不服气地挣扎着，“你说到了便是到了吗？”
“自然。神明也已经听见你们的呼喊……”徐福抬头看了一眼天空，“不出两日，便有大雨。干旱可解。两日后，我再教你们一项巫术，以后若是遇干旱，皆可用之，但切记勿要频繁使用，否则神明会降罪于尔等。”
龙阳君微微皱眉。
不出两日？
谁敢夸下这样的口？若是没有后面半句话，龙阳君便以为徐福忽悠完就要走人了，但是依后半半句话来看，他还要在此处停留两日？他疯了吗？龙阳君想不明白。
桑中和蒹葭都不自觉地心脏紧了紧。
唯有李斯，目光灼灼地望着徐福的背影。或许要又一次见到徐典事的神奇之处了……
“多……多谢大人……”那些人已经顾不上徐福所言是否真的会应验了，光是听见徐福说要教他们一项巫术，这些人便已经激动不已，连忙朝徐福拜下去了。
哪有人会轻易巫术教给别人？
徐福在他们的眼中，瞬间就变得光辉又高大且无私了起来……
“不要信他！什么不出两日？根本不可能！”巫师嗤笑一声，大声喊道。
“我说的对与不对，两日之内便见分晓，这不是很快吗？”徐福顿了顿，“届时我若说对了，你们便不得再让此人做巫师，我会从你们中间另挑一人，传授巫术。”
“你有什么权利……”巫师闻言，顿时更为激烈地挣扎起来。
但其他人心中对徐福的信任度已经拔得很高了，他们对视一眼，当即便和徐福达成了协议。
“结束之后，你们便派出一人，领我们走出这个地方。”
“这是自然！”那边的人答应得很爽快。
他们看着徐福的目光都有些敬若神明的味道。
他们中间走出人来，将妇人从地上扶了起来，随后才问徐福：“大人要跟我们回去吗？”
“自然一同回去。”徐福淡淡道。
龙阳君眼中震惊更甚，这使臣难道还真的忽悠上瘾了？下雨不下雨哪里是他能控制的？若是届时无法应验，他又要如何收场？事情已经到了这一步，龙阳君阻止也无法，只能心中轻叹一声，闭上了嘴。
这使臣的性子还是太冲动了一些。
这些人都是一个小村庄的人，村子叫良村，音同“粮”，足可看出这个小村子对于粮食庄稼的看重。
良村中人近年来很难真正下上一场大雨，庄稼收成渐渐不如以往，这对于这些庄稼人来说，简直就是要命的事，这些人道德感薄弱，巫师一提出用吃母的仪式，来得到老一辈身上的传承，这些人便答应了，而老一辈的妇人，也毫无怨言，并且怀着大无畏的精神打算为村庄牺牲了。
桑中和蒹葭听过之后，都各自感叹不已，没想到还会有这样被人奉行的习俗。
他们跟随着良村人穿过了树林。
所幸树林里的树木排布并不密集，马车也能勉强挤过去，等穿过树林，爬过一个坡之后，他们就看了一座村庄。村庄之中炊烟袅袅，原本应该山清水秀的地方，树木花草却有些枯萎的痕迹，想来那庄稼地里应该更好不到哪里去了。
这些人中有一为首的男子，名叫“阿良”。
阿良家的屋子比较宽敞，于是就将徐福等人带到了他的家中去。
阿良家的小院儿刚好能够放下马车和马儿。
阿良不敢轻易冒犯徐福，将徐福带到屋中之后，就匆忙离去了，生怕这位觋会对自己有所不满。
等阿良一走，龙阳君便忍不住问道：“使臣何来的底气？若是两日后，没有大雨，那该如何？”说着龙阳君还皱了皱眉，颇不赞同地道：“使臣实在不该如此一意孤行。”从之前坚持要往前走开始，龙阳君便颇不认同徐福的举动了。
就连蒹葭和桑中也朝徐福投去了不解的目光，虽然他们知晓徐福本事厉害，但总归免不了忧心。
徐福转头看向一旁一直一言不发的李斯，问道：“李长史可知从前我在奉常寺中是做什么的？”
李斯笑道：“太史令，太史，掌观天事宜。若要论对天气的预测，想来是没有人能比得过你了。”显然对徐福倍加信任。
“太史？”龙阳君挑了挑眉。据他所知，就算是太史令，那也应当是官职较低的，怎么会前来魏国做使臣呢？而且还能让一长史对他尊敬有加，想来，背后应该还有其它不凡之处。
桑中和蒹葭终于恍然大悟，“方才先生之所以会有如此之言，是因为先生已经观得天象了？”
“天象加上卜算，很容易便能得到了。”徐福顿了顿，却没说出心中的另一番话。其实莫说是他了，就连先进的科学仪器在预测天气时都容易会出错，更何况他呢？都说天有不测风云，最难预测的便是天气，他虽然看似笃定地说了这一番，其实却不然。他的预言背后，还有着一番风险。
但是他不会提及风险。说出来也不过是徒惹旁人担心罢了，他们又不通此道，说了也没有用。
何况……
他像是没有留后手的人吗？
徐福淡定十足，“就在此处稍作休息吧。”
龙阳君兴味更浓，道：“如今龙阳倒是越发好奇使臣究竟在秦国是何官职了。”
李斯笑道：“龙阳君日后到了秦国，自然便知晓了。”
龙阳君压下心中好奇，“希望如此吧。”
不得不说，有个停靠歇脚的地方倒也不错。当夜有村民送来了一些食物，都是他们所能寻来的，最好的食物了，不过谨慎起见，龙阳君便都推拒了，而蒹葭等人也未说什么。他们自己有干粮，的确不需要吃这些村民的口粮，他们本就粮食甚少，若是食不果腹，日后还不知道会做出什么疯狂的事来。
人在无法温饱的时候，哪里还有机会去讲什么礼义廉耻？
休息一夜之后，众人早早就醒了，而村中的人更是眼巴巴地坐在家门外，等待着大雨来临的时刻。
只有徐福还赖在床榻之上，舒舒服服地睡着懒觉。等他休息足了，这才起身吃些干粮，喝一些水，然后出了屋子去。
有村民见了他，忙小心翼翼地弯下腰。
而此时有一女子从远处快步走来。
那女子身着粗布麻衣，相貌平平，甚至因为眉毛上扬，瞧上去还有些凶恶。女子疾步走来，冷冷地横了徐福一眼，嗤笑道：“不是说有雨吗？雨在何处？此时可已是黄昏了！”
那女子声音一出，徐福这才知道，她就是那巫师，只不过此时她去除了身上裹得严实的黑袍罢了。
女子的声音还引来了其他村民的关注，村民们齐齐看向徐福，眸光焦急担忧，但他们谁也不敢催促徐福，他们害怕这位觋大人，一怒之下，会在自己身上下个咒术。徐福别的不一定做到了，但让村民们畏惧他，倒是轻易做到了。
而徐福此时抬头望了一眼天，倒是越发胸有成竹了。
他抬手遥遥一指远方，“你们看。”
所有人都不由得顺着他指的方向看过去。
那边云朵卷成团，飞快地从天边掠过，整个天空都如同一锅煮沸了的热水，而云团则像是翻滚的饺子，拥挤着，推搡着。因为它们掠过的速度实在快得有些过分，就像是有神仙在空中施法一般。
“不可久观，那是神灵在搅弄天空，待到天空沉下来时，自然会有雨从天上来。”徐福又开始了瞎扯。
偏偏这些村民非常相信他说的话，纷纷抬头望一眼，又匆匆低下头来，生怕多看一眼，会惊扰了神灵。
那巫师气极，却无从反驳。
天空中的异象看上去的确十分骇人，是有些像要下雨的征兆，难道……难道真的被这人说中了？
龙阳君也多有惊讶，他原以为徐福胡说的话，原来真的是有依据的……
徐福并没有在外过久停留，他很快就回转身往屋子里走去，这时，村民都只敢暗自打量他的背影，连一点细小的声音都不敢发出。
不知何时才有人低声说：“咱们族中来了个贵人哦……”
“不是贵人，是觋大人……”有人崇拜道。
其余人看向巫师的目光自然多有不屑了，不过好歹都是出自一族的人，他们也只是叹息几声，宽慰那巫师，“学得还不够好嘛，你就求那位大人多教一教你，那就好了……”
巫师冷哼一声，转身离去。
很快到了黄昏时分，金乌迅速被乌云遮挡住，从山上落了下去。
村民们站在屋子外，连步子都不敢挪一分，他们艰难地咽着口水，像是共同在等待见证一个奇迹的诞生。
金乌慢慢的便不见了踪影，而那云朵还在天边翻滚着，有风吹来，将村庄外的大树吹得发出稀里哗啦的响声。
徐福慢条斯理地坐在屋子里吃着干粮，喝着水。
村民们还在痴痴地等待。
倒是蒹葭最先等得有些不耐烦了，他忍不住对徐福道：“先生，真的会下雨吗？”
桑中从背后伸手拍了他一下，“说什么话呢？先生说的话，自然是准的，说下雨便是会下雨的。”
渐渐的，时辰渐晚，天空还没有要落雨的姿势，村民们仰着脖子等了许久，终于阿良也忍不住跑进院子来，敲开门问道：“……觋大人，那雨……半天没落下来呀……”阿良憋红了脸，一个身形高大的中年汉子站在少年模样的徐福跟前，却平白矮了一头。
谁都着急，他们都想来问徐福，但都谁也不敢冒犯徐福。
但是等待总是煎熬的。
徐福依旧淡定，“你们回去睡一觉便是。两日未至，何必忧心？”
话被他说得如此容易，但村民却是难做到的。
阿良却也不敢再问，又别无他法，只能走出去之后，将徐福的话传达给众人。众人又一起等了许久，直到天色渐晚，众人才情绪低落地回到了屋中，其中当然免不了几个低声埋怨徐福的，不过这几个人终究不敢大声说出来罢了。
徐福洗漱过后，便立刻上床休息了。
其余人面面相觑，也在屋中的地铺上睡下了。
而此时，那巫师穿着一身灰扑扑脏兮兮的袍子，悄悄从院子里跑了出来，随后找了处小山坡坐下，她冷哼一声，抬头紧紧盯着天空，黑沉沉的一片……
“我一定要抓住你的证据，一定要证明你才是骗子。”巫师咬牙，揉了揉发酸的脖颈，抬起头，挺得更直，认真地看着天空。
远处几声虫鸣。
……
*
咸阳宫中。
月上中天，宫女小心地走到跟前来，换了烛芯。
嬴政揉了揉脖颈，这才发觉到背脊都有些僵硬了，他合上手中的竹简，从位置上站了起来。
宫女被惊了一跳，忙俯身问道：“王上，可要备热水？”
嬴政“嗯”了一声，从殿中走出去，回到了寝宫中去。
寝宫中的宫女见嬴政进来了，小步迎上去，道：“王上，今日扶苏公子又前来询问徐典事下落了。”
嬴政怔了怔，微微皱眉，“寡人知晓了。”
嬴政心情有些不愉，问身边的侍从，“上次柏舟说的，徐福何时能归来？”
侍从满头大汗，“想来，想来……便是这一两日了吧……”
算一算，的确应该就是这几日左右了。嬴政心中的思念如潮水般汹涌袭来，他压下心中的情绪，心情越发不愉了，“柏舟竟然欺骗寡人，如今徐福未归，便令他这几日都去把守城门，守到徐福归来才能离去。”
侍从应了声“喏”，低头在心中为柏舟点了根蜡。
那头宫女备好了热水。
如今夜晚没有徐福相伴，嬴政自然也对于睡觉一事，觉得索然无味了，加之政务繁忙，他满心也都是征战六国的计划，为了排解食髓知味的刻骨相思，嬴政便日夜处理政务，夜深了时，便用热水来解乏。
嬴政脱去衣袍，跨进浴桶之中，他闭上眼，倚靠在桶壁上休息。但不知不觉，脑海里却出现了徐福的面容，嬴政心中一动，一边回忆起徐福身上滑腻的肌肤，一边不自觉地将手伸了下去……

chapters.title: 第79章
chapters.translated_text:
That night, there was neither moon nor stars above Liang Village.

The shamaness waited until she yawned, looking drowsy, her neck so stiff she could hardly turn it back. She didn't know what hour it was, but her heart was filled with excitement. She had said that man was definitely a liar!

Where had anyone ever seen a male shaman who looked like that?

"Shichen"? She had never even heard of such a name!

The shamaness smiled triumphantly, preparing to straighten her neck and return to her room for a comfortable sleep, expecting to see that man in a wretched state when she woke up the next day. Just as she raised her hand, a blinding flash of light suddenly streaked across the sky, accompanied by a muffled rumble of thunder that felt like a hammer striking her ears.

"Boom!"

"Rumble—"

Then came several more dull, heavy sounds, as if the entire small village were about to be struck.

Even the deepest sleeper would be jolted awake.

The whole village suddenly came to life. People exclaimed as they rose from their beds and hurriedly pushed open their windows. With sleepy eyes, they stared in astonishment at the flashes of light and the thunderbolts in the sky. The dense, dark clouds were churning violently, hanging so low it felt as if one could touch them by simply reaching out.

When the sky hangs that low, rain is sure to follow.

The villagers muttered the words Xu Fu had spoken during the day, their eyes fixed on the sky, unable to look away.

Finally...

The sound of rain pattered against the roofs, the leaves, and the tops of the carriages...

The livestock in the courtyards grew restless.

Meanwhile, the shamaness, sitting on the small hillside, was caught completely off guard by the downpour.

The heavy rain enveloped her, soaking her through in an instant. She didn't get to see Xu Fu's wretched state the next day, but she got to see her own wretched state right then and there. Her face changed drastically as she cursed the fickle weather, then she sprinted all the way home, never daring to mention causing trouble again.

Although the shamaness had a bad temper, she wasn't stupid enough to keep hitting a wall. Seeing the current situation, that young man clearly possessed some genuine ability; how could she dare to provoke him further? She still wanted to live a few more years.

With the rain pouring down, no one had the heart to sleep. They stared intently at the rain outside the window, terrified that if they fell asleep, they would wake up to find it had all been a dream.

Only Xu Fu slept more soundly than ever; the sound of the rain became his lullaby.

The next day, Xu Fu woke from his dream and moved his legs, feeling a bit uncomfortable. As a pure, innocent virgin, he had never experienced indulgence, but ever since he slept with Qin Shi Huang, Xu Fu realized that his desires had suddenly been unlocked by a key, pouring out in a torrent...

Oh, after saying all that, he had simply had a wet dream.

Xu Fu climbed out of bed with a blank expression, pondering how to quietly change his trousers, when he suddenly turned and stepped off the bed.

"The envoy is truly unfathomable in his calculations." Lord Longyang’s face was right in front of him. Lord Longyang looked much more serious now, having returned to his cold, detached expression, but his tone of praise sounded much more sincere.

Regardless of whether it was sincere or not, Xu Fu didn't appreciate being praised at this moment.

A faint sense of shame permeated Xu Fu’s heart.

Let me change my pants first, okay, Lord Longyang?

Lord Longyang didn't hear Xu Fu’s inner thoughts. Not only did he not step aside, but he pulled his robes closer and said, "Longyang is now even more curious: what will the sorcery you intend to teach them look like? Is that sorcery truly effective? Could it be that you, Envoy, are also a shaman?"

Xu Fu really didn't have the heart to chat leisurely with Lord Longyang, so he brushed it off with one sentence, "Won't Lord Longyang know when the time comes?"

With that, Xu Fu tried to walk past him.

Lord Longyang thought to himself, *Mysterious!*

Xu Fu’s demeanor appeared profound and inscrutable in his eyes.

Such a person, if he could be kept in the State of Wei, would surely bring prosperity to the nation... Kind and benevolent, calm and composed in his actions, and possessing marvelous arts. It was a pity; such a person—how could the increasingly foolish King of Wei ever hope to keep him?

After Xu Fu walked out, he ordered Jianjia to fetch him a change of clothes.

Since it was already raining, it wasn't an unforgivable thing for Xu Fu to boil some water for a bath. Sangzhong went to fetch a large bucket of water, heated it up, and carried it to the room next door. Xu Fu removed his clothes and settled into the tub.

When Lord Longyang came to look for Xu Fu, Xu Fu had just finished bathing. He had changed into a brand-new white robe, and as he walked, the gold patterns embroidered on the fabric seemed to shimmer.

Lord Longyang noticed his appearance and couldn't help but sigh; he was far less capable of enjoying life than Xu Fu.

Lord Longyang had suffered through hardships in his youth. Even after attaining high status and wealth, he rarely had time to enjoy himself. He spent his years traveling between various states, or maneuvering between the King of Wei and his concubines. Lord Longyang was weary of such a life. Even if he could kill the King of Wei if he wanted to, he had lost all desire for everything, so he was naturally too lazy to do it.

Had he known he would one day leave the State of Wei so easily, he would have slaughtered the King of Wei before leaving.

But that was just a thought for now...

If he really had killed the King of Wei, the State of Qin wouldn't dare to take him in.

Although the King of Wei wasn't good to his brother, Lord Xinling, Lord Xinling was extremely loyal to Wei. Besides, trading a fool for a wise monarch wasn't a profitable deal; if he wanted to be as comfortable as a fish in water in Wei, or even among the Seven States, that would be impossible.

Various thoughts flashed through Lord Longyang’s mind.

Xu Fu looked at Lord Longyang’s dazed expression, a trace of sympathy flashing in his eyes. Could it be that Lord Longyang had taken a fancy to his bathwater?

But unfortunately, he didn't intend to let Lord Longyang soak in it.

Mixing together like milk and water—that was too filthy.

He would feel guilty toward Qin Shi Huang if he did that.

Xu Fu pulled his robes together, and Sangzhong held an umbrella for him as the two walked out of the courtyard.

A while later, Jianjia came to move the water and saw Lord Longyang still standing at the door in a daze. Jianjia bypassed him and entered, carrying the large wooden tub, but when he reached the doorway, he found that because Lord Longyang was blocking the way, he was stuck at the door with the tub in his arms, unable to get out.

Jianjia frowned slightly, "Lord Longyang, please move aside."

Lord Longyang started, looking up to see Jianjia frowning at him.

"Do you need my help?" Lord Longyang hadn't heard the previous sentence clearly. Seeing Jianjia holding the tub and frowning at him, he assumed he was being asked for assistance. Without a word, Lord Longyang reached out to support the tub.

Lord Longyang had once been a famous sword master in Wei, but as he gradually retreated into the role of the King of Wei’s male favorite and a Wei envoy, people slowly overlooked this fact.

Jianjia was stunned for a moment and instinctively let go. As the tub fell...

With a "thud," the cold and arrogant Lord Longyang was almost knocked over by the tub right at Jianjia’s feet.

His face turned slightly pale.

Jianjia couldn't bear to watch, so he reached out and took the tub back, "You just need to move aside."

Lord Longyang, treated as an obstacle for the first time, moved away feeling dejected, then watched as Jianjia easily carried the tub away.

Lord Longyang: ...

·

Xu Fu and Sangzhong walked out of the courtyard and could immediately see the villagers gathered in the open space of the village. They weren't even holding umbrellas, just standing there, letting the rain wash over them; only this made them feel that it wasn't a dream.

Xu Fu didn't see the women; they must have already applied medicine to treat their burns.

Next, only the sorcery remained.

Xu Fu wondered what kind of incantation to write. Was he supposed to teach them English?

"Shaman..."

The villagers turned back and saw Xu Fu’s figure. They didn't care about the heavy rain or the muddy ground and knelt directly before him. They prostrated themselves on the ground, shouting something loudly, perhaps mixed with local dialects, which Xu Fu couldn't quite understand.

Perhaps it was a gesture of gratitude.

Although Xu Fu didn't like this group of people, he had at least achieved a good result.

The rain grew heavier, and the paper umbrella was clearly not going to hold up much longer. Xu Fu didn't hesitate, turned around, and walked toward the courtyard, "A-Liang, follow me."

A-Liang was stunned, then hurriedly followed Xu Fu. The others looked at A-Liang with envy. By now, no one dared to doubt Xu Fu’s identity or his actions. The people in the village were ignorant, but it was precisely because of their ignorance that they were more easily convinced by Xu Fu.

After entering the courtyard, Xu Fu asked him, "Are there any recommended people in the village? First, I must tell you, those chosen to learn sorcery must be young and have a clear mind; it doesn't matter if they are men or women."

Although this village was small, it at least didn't have any strong customs of favoring men over women, as evidenced by the fact that a woman could be a shaman.

A-Liang pondered for a while and smiled, "How about... how about you teach Qing Nü, Master?"

"Qing Nü?"

"She, she is the village shaman. She originally learned from her father. After her father passed away, she became the only shaman in the village. As for the others... they, they haven't been exposed to this stuff... learning, I'm afraid, I'm afraid they wouldn't be able to learn it..." A-Liang said awkwardly, glancing at Xu Fu’s expression as he spoke, fearing he might accidentally touch a nerve.

Xu Fu didn't particularly like that shamaness, but thinking about it, he didn't necessarily like the whole village either.

Wasn't it all the same?

Besides, he had just stripped her of her position as shaman; wouldn't that invite a lot of hatred?

"Then call her over," Xu Fu said coldly. "However, she must apologize to me. If she refuses to even bend her knee and lower her head, she will surely be too proud and difficult to tame in the future. How could I trust such a person with important matters?"

A-Liang nodded repeatedly, "Yes, yes..." With that, he hurriedly turned to find the shamaness.

Qing Nü likely inherited her father's traits; she was tall and somewhat sturdy, which would make one mistake her gender at first glance. Her voice was also somewhat hoarse, and she had been a shaman for many years, wrapped in black robes.

Because of her loneliness and her unique status, her temper was aloof and even somewhat bad.

However, she had lived with the villagers for many years, and since shamans were generally unable to marry, the villagers were naturally more tolerant of her. But the bigger reason was that the villagers relied on her, so they naturally accommodated her. Once Xu Fu left, everything would be fine, but Qing Nü had to remain in the village. Regardless of whether the rituals she presided over were effective, her identity as a shaman still commanded awe from the villagers.

When Qing Nü entered, her expression was still somewhat unpleasant.

However, A-Liang might have already spoken to her; now that the rain had arrived, Qing Nü was also awestruck by Xu Fu’s abilities.

Seeing Xu Fu now, even if she had resentment in her heart, she still bowed and apologized, "Please forgive my rudeness, Shaman."

Xu Fu knew she was unwilling, but since she had been chosen by the villagers, she would have to do!

"Come here, I will teach you the incantation first."

Qing Nü stepped forward and heard Xu Fu recite a string of strange sounds. By the time he finished, Qing Nü hadn't remembered a single word.

"...Wh-what?" Qing Nü blushed and stammered, "Are there no bamboo slips with it carved on them?"

"No," Xu Fu said coldly.

Was he supposed to carve English characters onto bamboo slips? Don't be ridiculous.

"I will say it to you a few times; memorize it," Xu Fu said coldly.

His tone was truly not very polite, and Qing Nü instinctively tightened her nerves, listening much more carefully.

Worried that she wouldn't remember, Xu Fu shortened the English sentence as much as possible. He repeated "byas" to Qing Nü over and over, struggling for most of the morning until he finally managed to get her to remember it. After Qing Nü went back, she specifically found bamboo slips and carved characters with the same pronunciation using the local script to facilitate memory and transmission.

Later, this passage was even carved onto bronze plates and passed down through the world as a mysterious incantation.

...Of course, that was a story for another time.

And this incantation was actually just something to be recited while bathing to increase one's strength.

Xu Fu thought it was useless, so it was perfect as a bluff. Qing Nü, however, treated it like a treasure. After memorizing the incantation, she came to ask Xu Fu about the ritual process that afternoon.

Xu Fu casually picked up a tree branch and drew a simple diagram in the mud of the courtyard.

Qing Nü was stunned, "What is this?"

"A vessel, a vessel needed for the ritual."

It was shaped like a drum and gong, and he explained in detail to Qing Nü what these two objects should be made of.

"Because your shamanic power is not as great as mine," Xu Fu lied shamelessly, "your process for praying for rain will be much more difficult and complex than mine. After making these two vessels, you must find a place behind the clouds where the airflow is strong..."

"What is a place where the airflow is strong? A place with strong wind?"

"..." Xu Fu was silent for a moment. His geography was truly not very good. How was he supposed to explain strong airflow or rising air currents? So he had to give up and lie, "Find a high place, the higher the better."

He remembered that in history, there seemed to be such precedents.

To pray for rain, one had to climb a high platform to increase the chances of success.

Qing Nü hurriedly took notes.

"Then use these vessels to strike and make sound; you must make a very loud sound so that the gods in the heavens can hear our call."

"After that, you must light a bonfire, and it must burn very brightly! With rolling heat waves!" This was nothing strange; in countless rituals, one had to light a bonfire to gain the opportunity to communicate with the gods.

And this step was exactly the backup plan Xu Fu had prepared.

When the heat waves rolled and the air currents rose to collide with the clouds, evaporating them into water vapor, it was highly likely that they would fall with dust, forming rain. This method wasn't absolutely guaranteed, but in the absence of sufficient conditions, it was a major option to use.

"Finally, you must make this object," Xu Fu said, drawing another shape on the ground. "This is also a vessel. Finally, place it on high ground and rotate it in this direction, rotating it continuously... while reciting the incantation, and you will be able to wait for the rain to fall."

That thing was called a rain-inducer in ancient times, and Xu Fu guessed it hadn't been invented yet.

This whole process looked very mysterious, leaving Qing Nü’s brain feeling like mush. Although she harbored hostility toward Xu Fu, at this moment, she felt more fear. This man truly had ability...

After giving instructions to Qing Nü, Xu Fu straightened his body.

"Have you learned it?"

Qing Nü still had some confusion in her heart, but she didn't want Xu Fu to look down on her, so she forced herself to memorize it and stammered, "I have remembered it."

"Call A-Liang over," Xu Fu said. Once this last thing was done, he could pack his bags and return to Xianyang City.

After a long time, he really did miss the comfortable and leisurely days in Xianyang.

Xu Fu felt his face ache slightly; he had slapped his own face too quickly. When he went to the Shu region, he had thought he wasn't suited for long journeys, but this time he had courted death by running all over the states of Wei and Han.

He instinctively reached up to touch his cheek, and A-Liang had already entered.

Seeing that Xu Fu had finished teaching Qing Nü, A-Liang treated Xu Fu with even more respect, his head almost bowing down to his waist.

"Shaman..."

"If you want to obtain the inheritance, just make a tripod like mine and perform the same ritual. After obtaining the inheritance, if you don't use it, it will gradually degenerate, so you must work harder at farming. When you encounter problems, you must consult your mothers in a timely manner. Your mothers have already received the blessings of the gods in the ritual and will naturally point you in the right direction. This is the only way for the inheritance to truly be carried forward," Xu Fu lied again.

It was actually a very simple principle.

If you want to improve farming techniques, it's practice—constantly farming and encountering difficulties, then drawing experience from the older generation. If there is no help from the older generation, they will naturally take many detours. The way of "eating the mother" (killing the elders), if called an inheritance, is more like cutting off the inheritance. How precious is the experience of the older generation? If you kill them directly, who else can provide experience to these people? At that time, a major crisis will likely occur in the clan.

But you couldn't say it so plainly.

Although these people were farmers and should be simple, if you spoke plainly to them, they wouldn't believe you at all, so you had to tie it to sorcery and make it sound like the real thing.

After hearing this, A-Liang thanked him repeatedly. By now, his trust in Xu Fu had gone deep into his bones.

"Send someone to see us off."

"I, I will do it," A-Liang said with a sycophantic smile.

"Hmm." Xu Fu put on a sufficiently cold and aloof air before going inside to tell them to pack their things.

Facts proved that although Xu Fu had appeared before them with a cold and punchable attitude from the beginning, the final result was that he was held in even higher regard.

"So soon?" Jianjia was stunned when he heard they were leaving.

Although the village was small, the scenery was nice, and Jianjia had been having quite a fun time wandering around these past few days.

Sangzhong slapped him on the back to make him shut up. Jianjia didn't want to go back; if the King found out, wouldn't he kill him?

After packing their things, the group quickly boarded the carriage.

The locals were indeed familiar with the roads; A-Liang sent them a long way, and they would be able to enter Qin territory after about another day of travel.

When parting, A-Liang took a deep breath and asked loudly, "May I ask for the Shaman's name! Everyone in Liang Village will surely remember your kindness..."

Xu Fu lifted the carriage curtain, revealing his cold, clear face, and said faintly, "Xu Fu."

A-Liang nodded heavily, firmly engraving this name in his heart.

But Xu Fu never expected that the people of Liang Village had such a heavy accent that his name would be garbled and passed down by A-Liang as "Xi Hu."

That is a story for another time, which we will not mention for now.

·

Walking on the road, Jianjia was still curious about how Xu Fu could calculate that it would rain within two days. He was young and had a more lively personality than Sangzhong and the others, so he couldn't help but ask.

Xu Fu had nothing to hide, so he explained it immediately, "To observe the sky, one must first observe the wind, the clouds, and the insects, fish, birds, and beasts."

"That day there was no wind, the temperature was sultry, the scorching sun was in the sky, and the cloud masses were huge, hanging in the air. It was noon, yet the clouds on the horizon moved from far to near, changing from few to many, the cloud layers intersecting and thickening, and drifting from afar. These were the omens of bad weather with wind and rain. And the birds were restless, and small insects coming out of their holes on the ground were also signs of the sultry weather turning into rain. Sometimes, the sultriness before rain is also a sign of rain. Moreover, after many days of drought, according to the time, it was naturally within these few days."

"So... it had nothing to do with that sorcery?" Jianjia asked blankly.

Sangzhong mocked Jianjia’s dullness without hesitation.

Of course, that sorcery was a bluff; did Jianjia really believe it after seeing the effect?

He was truly too young...

Lord Longyang couldn't help but smile and said, "I have learned of the Envoy’s methods and am quite impressed. In a few years, I believe the Envoy will become even more outstanding."

Did you need to tell me that? Xu Fu added to himself in his heart.

Over the next few days, Jianjia kept pestering Xu Fu to calculate the weather, calculate fortune and misfortune, or calculate if there were any big rocks ahead, all of which were ignored by Xu Fu.

Xu Fu was so pestered that he could only casually bluff, "I have observed your physiognomy; you should be a bit more restrained lately."

"Why?"

"Jianjia, you have peach blossoms on your face."

Jianjia hadn't gone to Dujiangyan with Xu Fu before, so he hadn't heard Xu Fu’s prediction about the peach blossom luck of the men along the way. He listened blankly, "What is peach blossom luck?"

Sangzhong smiled, "Someone is going to take a fancy to you."

"Eh?" Jianjia was dazed for a while, then sat in the corner of the carriage, not knowing what he was pondering, but he was finally dismissed.

Xu Fu closed his eyes. Because the temperature was getting hotter, he couldn't help but reach out and tug at his collar. After doing so, the face of Ying Zheng involuntarily appeared in his mind.

Xu Fu was puzzled.

Spring had already passed...

Hey, why am I still in heat?
