"Fusu is willing." Fusu didn't hesitate at all, which was exactly like Consort Zheng’s firm demeanor, "If Mother is ill, she should naturally go where she can be cured."

Xu Fu looked at the expression on Fusu’s face and discovered a very interesting detail.

Hearing that Consort Zheng was ill, Fusu showed no panic. He seemed to have expected it, or in other words, he seemed to know that his mother had someone else in her heart she couldn't let go of, and he also knew what the truth behind the excuse of needing medical treatment really was.

Fusu was truly too mature for his age.

Ying Zheng looked down at Consort Zheng and Fusu from his high position, "Then I will grant you this one chance. Go."

Consort Zheng kowtowed heavily several times, then took Fusu’s hand and led him out. Presumably, Consort Zheng still had things to tell Fusu.

Xu Fu blinked. The First Emperor of Qin was just letting them go like that?

Xu Fu naturally wouldn't know that while Ying Zheng was influencing him, his own existence was naturally influencing Ying Zheng as well. The reason Ying Zheng’s decision had changed was simply because of him.

"In the future, if anyone comes to you for help, you don't need to pay them any mind," Ying Zheng turned his head and looked at him.

Xu Fu smiled, "Your Majesty knows that I take money to tell fortunes for people."

Ying Zheng wasn't angry; instead, he said, "In the Qin palace, I can give you anything you want. How about you only tell fortunes for me for the rest of your life?"

Such a tempting offer, Xu Fu really wanted to agree. But if he only divined for Ying Zheng, he would never make any progress in his life. The fortune-telling trade required too much experience; reading a thousand books was not as good as seeing a hundred faces.

So Xu Fu smiled and deflected the comment calmly, "I didn't know Your Majesty could say such sweet things."

"I am always saying sweet things to you, you just haven't taken them to heart." Ying Zheng sensed Xu Fu’s rejection but didn't take it to heart. After saying this lightly, he took Xu Fu’s wrist and led him out.

Ying Zheng was in a rare mood for leisure today, so he took Xu Fu for a walk around the palace.

Finally, he wasn't dragging him to bed the moment he grabbed him.

Xu Fu breathed a sigh of relief.

Ying Zheng seemed to still be a bit unhappy, which led to this "maiden-like" behavior—oh, at least in Xu Fu’s eyes, it was quite maiden-like.

As they walked, Ying Zheng would speak to Xu Fu from time to time, which had a somewhat leisurely feel. It was just a pity that the sky was a bit overcast; if there had been sunlight, it would have been warm and cozy.

"That Wei Liao is indeed a disciple of Guiguzi." Speaking of this, a smile finally appeared on Ying Zheng’s face, "I will cover for you."

Xu Fu’s face darkened. He knew it; the First Emperor of Qin had known all along that he wasn't a disciple of Guiguzi.

However, Xu Fu kept a straight face and said, "It’s fine, I have nothing to fear."

The smile on Ying Zheng’s face deepened. In fact, he quite enjoyed the feeling of holding Xu Fu in the palm of his hand, "Someone recommended Wei Liao to me long ago. This man has some ability; he was already somewhat famous while still a disciple of Guiguzi. Later, as he traveled through various states, his reputation grew. It is a good thing for me that he has come to join Qin."

"Your Majesty, rest assured, I will not make things difficult for him."

Ying Zheng still smiled, "Yes, I am very assured." He had originally thought that if Xu Fu were exposed, he would surely lose face, but he hadn't expected Xu Fu to calm down so quickly. Thinking of this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but be curious: whose disciple was Xu Fu? Who could have taught such a wonderful person as him?

After walking for a while, they went back for dinner. After eating, when they went to sleep that night, Xu Fu took every possible precaution, wrapping himself up like a ball. Ying Zheng hadn't intended to touch him anyway. Seeing him, who usually acted so cold and aloof, now wrapped in a quilt in such a funny way, throwing away all his poise and temperament, Ying Zheng couldn't help but find it amusing. He reached out and pulled Xu Fu into his arms, and soon they fell asleep together.

The unpleasantness of that day simply dissipated just like that.

It was just that Ying Zheng hadn't realized that by instinctively driving Consort Zheng out of Xianyang, he had already moved toward the thought of keeping only Xu Fu by his side.

Where would a monarch find a deep-seated love? Ying Zheng’s education had never included such knowledge. He lacked this awareness, so naturally, he hadn't thought in that direction.

...

·

When Xu Fu woke up the next day, he was slightly dazed for a moment. He wasn't used to not having a lingering encounter with the First Emperor of Qin. What kind of problem was this? A post-estrus syndrome? Xu Fu rubbed his temples and asked the palace maid, "Where is Consort Zheng?"

The maid bowed, "Early this morning, Consort Zheng left Xianyang in a carriage to seek treatment for her illness."

As expected of the First Emperor of Qin, his efficiency was fast enough.

But Xu Fu still felt a bit down.

The words Wei Liao said yesterday—didn't that shatter Consort Zheng’s heart’s desire? And since he had previously said that Consort Zheng would surely get her wish, didn't that mean he had calculated wrong?

Xu Fu could accept anything, but he could not accept that he had calculated wrong.

When he told fortunes, he was always cautious. He never gave people hope for things he wasn't sure about, especially in matters like this, because if it didn't come to pass, it would only cause unnecessary pain.

Xu Fu was somewhat bothered by this result.

No, he had to keep an eye on news of Consort Zheng; he had to verify his prophecy!

Xu Fu frowned, got up, washed, and changed. By this time, Ying Zheng had already left. After having his tonic and breakfast, Xu Fu slowly took a carriage toward the Fengchang Temple.

Ever since Xu Fu left with Li Si, there had been those in the Fengchang Temple who were jealous and those who mocked him. Some thought that being able to travel with Li Si and serve as a Qin envoy represented the King’s favor, so how could they not be jealous? But others thought he was sick in the head—he was already a 'Dianshi' (official), and could have stayed comfortably in the Fengchang Temple enjoying his days, so why go out and suffer? Going so far away, if the mission wasn't completed, he might even incur the King’s disgust!

Hearing that Li Si had returned, everyone saw Wang Liu, but not Xu Fu. Unable to get anything out of Wang Liu, who had changed significantly from before, these people could only guess what had happened to Xu Fu with their own limited logic. They didn't know that Xu Fu was being treated very well in the palace and had no worries; what they thought was all just their own self-indulgent fantasies.

Xu Fu returned to the Fengchang Temple and first met with Su Yi.

Su Yi didn't know what had just happened, and his expression was ugly, but as soon as he saw him, his face lit up with joy, and he immediately came forward.

"When did Master Xu return?"

"Naturally, he returned with me." Wang Liu’s voice rang out not far away. Xu Fu turned his head and saw Wang Liu walking over with a not-so-good expression on his face.

The atmosphere between him and Su Yi was very stiff.

Wang Liu’s tone was truly impatient, and Su Yi naturally didn't have a good look for him either.

"How about this, if you have time, come over with me, and we can chat a bit." Xu Fu said this to Su Yi.

Su Yi didn't stand on ceremony and nodded immediately, following Xu Fu over.

"How was the trip?" Once inside, Su Yi asked immediately, "Li Si is a considerate friend. Are you getting along well with him, Master Xu?"

In Xu Fu’s eyes, Su Yi suddenly looked like a matchmaker.

It sounded as if the two of them were on a blind date.

Xu Fu said helplessly, "Chief Scribe Li is indeed very considerate. Traveling with him was very pleasant."

Su Yi was relieved, "I never expected such a coincidence in the world. I intended to introduce Chief Scribe Li to you, Master Xu, but you met him a step ahead."

Truly wonderful!

Xu Fu didn't know if his coming to the State of Qin was also something destined by fate.

After chatting with Su Yi for a while, they both felt quite happy, and then Xu Fu sent Su Yi away.

However, there were rarely any major events in the Fengchang Temple. Xu Fu had nothing to do, read ancient texts for a day, and then packed up to leave. But he came out a bit early today, and the little eunuch hadn't arrived yet. Just as Xu Fu was wondering whether to turn back, a figure slowly entered his line of sight.

...It was Wei Liao!

The coldness on Wei Liao’s face had faded quite a bit. He walked straight toward Xu Fu, "Follow me." After saying that, Wei Liao turned and walked to the other side on his own.

Xu Fu was confused, feeling that Wei Liao’s tone was truly impolite.

However, his curiosity got the better of him, so after a moment of hesitation, Xu Fu followed.

Wei Liao didn't walk far, just far enough away from the gate of the Fengchang Temple. The two stood by the side of the road, and Wei Liao finally turned around to face Xu Fu.

"What is going on between you and the King of Qin?" Wei Liao frowned and asked coldly.

Xu Fu felt even more displeased. Not only was Wei Liao’s tone very rude, but what he said was also truly impolite. Xu Fu’s eyes took on a look of detachment and resistance. He stepped back and asked coldly, "What right do you have to ask me that?"

Wei Liao’s expression turned strange instantly, "You forgot again?"

"What?" Xu Fu frowned as well. What on earth was this Wei Liao talking about? Rambling on without making any sense!

"You really did forget again. I was wondering, that day in the palace, why you asked me my name for no reason. When I saw you in the State of Wei before, you treated me like a stranger, and I thought you were just finding it inconvenient to recognize me." Wei Liao sighed.

Xu Fu felt a chill run down his spine.

Could it be that his original self had some kind of relationship with this person?

It couldn't be an old lover, could it?

Xu Fu shivered inwardly. He really wasn't into Wei Liao’s type.

He could accept the First Emperor of Qin, but Wei Liao...

Xu Fu stepped back again, looking at Wei Liao with even more vigilance. Wei Liao couldn't help but grit his teeth, "Your head—when will you ever be able to remember things!"

"Did you mistake me for someone else?" Xu Fu finally couldn't help but interrupt Wei Liao.

Anger surged on Wei Liao’s face, an expression of "iron not becoming steel," "I mistook you for someone else? When would I ever mistake you for someone else?"

It’s over... Xu Fu’s sense of foreboding grew even stronger. He felt that Wei Liao’s tone was just like an old lover coming to his door, and the things he said were quite ambiguous. But now, no old lover had anything to do with him. He would die before admitting it; he would just pretend the other person had the wrong person, or that he had amnesia.

"How long will it take for you to remember this time?" Wei Liao’s voice seemed to be squeezed out from between his teeth. His image of being steady and composed was completely destroyed.

Oh! He even thought of the excuse for him! Xu Fu was secretly pleased and, without changing his expression, lied, "Perhaps a few months..."

He didn't believe Wei Liao could keep an eye on him for months, could he?

Wei Liao reached up and rubbed his temples, "I hope so." After saying that, he lowered his hand, his expression suddenly becoming solemn, "You still haven't told me, what is going on between you and the King of Qin?"

Xu Fu looked at him without speaking. He felt that even if he didn't speak, Wei Liao could continue the conversation on his own.

Sure enough, Wei Liao didn't wait for him to speak and said, "Fine, you don't have to say it, I’ve already guessed a bit." Wei Liao’s face darkened, "I had no objection to you joining Qin, and I followed you to the State of Qin, but I have observed the King of Qin’s physiognomy these past few days..."

Xu Fu’s ears perked up instantly.

This person really knew how to read faces!

What conclusion would he reach after reading the First Emperor of Qin’s face? Would it be the same as his own? Xu Fu was slightly excited, and at the same time, he really wanted to know what the First Emperor of Qin looked like in other people’s eyes.

"The King of Qin has a bee-like nose, long eyes, a bird-like chest, and a jackal-like voice; his physiognomy is fierce. It shows he is mean-spirited and lacks grace; he has the heart of a tiger or wolf. When he is humble, he doesn't mind lowering himself to others, but when he is triumphant, if he is offended, he will surely devour people without spitting out the bones—he is extremely cruel! I am a mere commoner, yet he often lowers his status to respect me. If one day the King of Qin realizes his ambition to swallow the world, he will surely treat everyone in the world as his slaves. He lacks benevolence; one should not associate with such a person for long." Wei Liao said coldly, showing no mercy.

Xu Fu was stunned, and he cursed "fuck" in his heart.

You’re the one with long eyes, a chicken chest, and a jackal-like voice!

The First Emperor of Qin is so handsome and heroic, are you blind?

Xu Fu was so angry he felt suffocated. He stared coldly at Wei Liao and couldn't help but blurt out, "You’re blind."

Wei Liao frowned and said coldly, "I know you hold the King of Qin in high esteem, but Zhao Zheng is really no match for his grandfather! All the past Kings of Qin were warlike, and Zhao Zheng is even more so! His temper is violent; he is not an easy person to get along with! He is extremely good at enduring and is deep in his schemes! If you suffer because of him in the future, you won't even know why. How is such a monarch worth your service and loyalty? You should leave Qin with me quickly and go to another state. I think the State of Wei is quite good..."

Good my ass!

The King of Wei is sleazy and lustful!

He had already snatched away his male favorite, and he was going to run to the State of Wei? Was he asking to be eaten by the King of Wei?

Xu Fu’s anger grew even more, but he kept repeating in his heart: I am a civilized person, I don't curse.

But after all this, he still couldn't suppress the anger churning in his chest. Xu Fu had always believed his self-cultivation was excellent; no matter who came to provoke him, he could maintain a calm demeanor. But why... why was it that today, he found these words so grating and so unbearable?

"The person I think one shouldn't associate with is you."

Hearing this, Wei Liao’s expression changed drastically, "How can you say such things?"

"Am I wrong?" Xu Fu sneered, "I really can't understand your brain. Let me ask you, what is the reputation of Lord Xinling and Lord Chunshen among the seven states?"

Wei Liao didn't understand why, but he still answered, "These two were respectful to scholars, recruited guests widely, and were both virtuous men..."

Xu Fu immediately interrupted him, "What? According to your one-sided opinion, because they recruited guests widely and treated capable people with courtesy, they were 'respectful to scholars'? But when the King of Qin lowers his status and treats you with courtesy, it’s the heart of a jackal, full of schemes, good at enduring, and must be guarded against?"

He had never seen someone with such severe double standards!

When Wei Liao said this, did he feel any guilt?

Wei Liao did not agree with Xu Fu’s words, "My observation of the King of Qin’s physiognomy is just that; this person is narrow-minded. In the future, whoever offends him will surely be retaliated against in a thousand ways..."

Xu Fu interrupted him again, "If a villain bullies you, are you a saint? You won't retaliate? Are you going to thank him instead?"

"If someone provokes you and you retaliate, that is the act of a villain!" Wei Liao said sharply.

"Don't confuse the concepts. He is the dignified King of Qin; does he have the time to haggle over small things with people? If someone really offends him, offends the great matters of the King of Qin, shouldn't he retaliate? You say he is narrow-minded, so he is narrow-minded? But when I look at his physiognomy, I feel he is broad-minded, has the capacity to tolerate others, and has great courage. He can accept virtuous scholars; he is a good monarch!" Xu Fu paused, caught his breath, and added, "Not to mention that, what’s wrong with being a villain? Being a villain is what’s satisfying!"

Gentlemen are all hypocrites! Xu Fu complained in his heart.

Wei Liao was shocked and couldn't help but say, "Now that you have arrived in the State of Qin, you have actually... actually been influenced so severely! What did the King of Qin say to you? To make you believe in him so much?"

Xu Fu was unhappy again.

Wei Liao insisted on his own words, he insisted on what he said—what was wrong with that? He had his own persistence; did that mean he was blinded by the King of Qin?

In his opinion, Wei Liao was the one who was blinded! Insisting on splashing dirty water on the King of Qin—what for?

"Don't change the subject. You said you observed his physiognomy and reached this conclusion, but I observed his physiognomy and reached a completely different one. My conclusion is entirely different from yours." Xu Fu said sharply, his momentum actually suppressing Wei Liao.

Wei Liao was also quite angry, and he laughed out of extreme anger, "Then tell me, what is the physiognomy of the King of Qin that you observed?"

Xu Fu closed his eyes, and the image of the first time he saw the King of Qin appeared in his mind.

Those words seemed to be echoing in his ears.

Xu Fu looked at Wei Liao with burning eyes and said loudly, "The King of Qin’s physiognomy is noble beyond words!"

Wei Liao sneered.

Xu Fu then said the words he had buried in his heart but hadn't been able to say back then, now saying them exactly as they were, "Observe the King of Qin’s appearance: his spirit and energy are awe-inspiring! Observe the King of Qin’s forehead: his forehead is high and his head is square—noble beyond words! Observe the King of Qin’s eyes: his eyes are deep, his gaze is clear and sharp, and he is awe-inspiring without even being angry! Observe his five peaks, three pavilions, five sensory organs, and six storehouses—the dragon is about to transform; one day he will surely soar into the sky! His physique is heroic, his momentum is majestic! Where are the long eyes, the chicken chest, and the jackal-like voice you spoke of?"

Xu Fu sneered again, "Could it be that you are jealous of him? That’s why you are deliberately smearing him? King Zheng of Qin has such an appearance; his ambition to swallow the world will surely be realized! He may not be a benevolent monarch, but he can let the common people eat well, dress well, and live well—then he is a wise monarch!"

"Nonsense!" Wei Liao was furious and could only deny it dryly.

Xu Fu smiled, "Just you wait and see!"

Just you wait and see; one day, the First Emperor of Qin will become the Emperor of the Ages!

徐福和郑妃几乎是同时惊了一跳，一身汗毛都竖了起来。
徐福有一种在背后说人坏话，然后被人抓了个现行的羞耻感。而轮到郑妃这里就是结结实实的惊悚了，她不知道嬴政方才听见了多少，她身体僵直地坐在那里，动也不敢动，甚至忘记了按照规矩，她应当起身迎接王上的。
嬴政走近来，面色冷然，看不出是喜是怒。
但他仅仅只是站在徐福的身侧，就已经令人生畏了。
“不是有话要与寡人说吗？如今寡人在此，为何反倒闭口不言了？”嬴政低头看向郑妃，郑妃这才惊觉自己失了仪态，忙站起身来，讷讷道：“王上……”
事关男人尊严，不管今日郑妃说与不说，秦始皇定然会心中积火。
“初时，寡人以为，郑妃的愿望乃是希望扶苏将来能担大任。如今瞧来，郑妃的愿望并不是如此啊……”难得见到一向冷静聪慧的郑妃，做出这副模样来，嬴政心中不快更甚，不由得将声音压得更为低沉。
徐福心下一动，他方才什么都听见了？
郑妃的身子微微战栗，她忍不住咬了咬唇。
瞧上去方寸大乱的模样，越发将她的心思暴露无遗。
嬴政的耐心消耗殆尽，面色一冷，沉声问道：“那个人是谁？郑妃不愿留于王宫，多年隐忍不发，却唯独此时才急于离去。那人是什么时候进了宫中，与郑妃见了一面吗？”话到此处，嬴政的声音已经十分冰冷了。
那人敢出入秦王宫，是将秦王宫当做摆设了吗？
嬴政不能忍受这样的挑衅。
果然是什么都听见了。徐福心中轻叹一声，出声道：“那人是尉缭？”徐福在王宫之中也就见了他这个陌生人，何况当时他与尉缭撞见时，郑妃走来，尉缭就匆匆离开。
无论怎么瞧都太过巧合了些。
郑妃连忙摇头，“不是。”
大约是她心中明了瞒也瞒不住了，这才逐渐冷静了下来，但她如今的口吻已经是坐实了她心属别的男人。徐福都不由得为她捏了一把汗。
嬴政比徐福要敏锐多了，他紧紧盯着郑妃的面容，冷声道：“不是尉缭，那也必然是尉缭认识的人。近来王宫之中，光明正大出入的便只有他。若是另有其人，那寡人少不得要追究一番，郑妃与那人有何谋划了。”能悄无声息地进入秦王宫，置嬴政的安危于何处？
不管对方是出于什么目的，都已经冒犯到嬴政了，而避免危险的最好方式，就是直接剁了那人。
郑妃脸色微微一白，“啪”的一声，跪了下去。
声音沉得徐福听在耳中都觉得有些疼。
“王上。”郑妃咬了咬唇，狠下心，托出实话来，“确有此人，但并非尉缭，而是尉缭所识之人，昔日我曾见过尉缭，不料于宫中碰见，一眼便认出了他……我这才……忍不住生出妄想来。”
郑妃的神色实在不像是在撒谎。
“来人，去将尉缭传来。”嬴政面上冰寒未退，转头高声将宫人叫了进来，扶苏忐忑不安地将头伸进来，想要看清殿内发生了什么事。他见宫人面色发白、行色匆匆，心顿时便沉了下去，他抬脚想要进殿，却被内侍拦住了。
内侍微微一笑，“扶苏公子此时还是不要进去为好。”
扶苏心中不详的预感更甚，但他又不敢强吵着要进去，若是惹怒嬴政，局面只会更加糟糕。
徐福往扶苏的方向瞥了一眼。
这还是头一次，徐福看见扶苏对着自己露出了求救的目光。
徐福递给他一个稍安勿躁的眼神，然后便将头转了回去，静静等待那尉缭的到来。而徐福这时也骤然反应过来，尉缭应当便是那与他“同门”的师兄，正牌的鬼谷弟子。
原来他早就与他费心要躲开的人见上面了！
徐福心中惊讶不已，却没能看见扶苏脸上露出更为担忧的神色来。
徐福哪里会想到，自己常年伪装成冷漠的眼神，难以转变成安抚的味道，于是他刚才自以为是个稍安勿躁的眼神，实际上却是个十分冷漠的眼神，扶苏看了一眼，心就顿时凉了。
被派出去的内侍，终于将尉缭领了过来。
尉缭神色冷漠，大步跨进殿来，他朝嬴政简单行了礼，然后直起身子，便看见了嬴政两侧的徐福及郑妃，尉缭不由得皱了皱眉，问道：“王上唤我前来可是有何事？”
嬴政的脸色却是比他更为冷硬，他并未与尉缭说话，而是对郑妃道：“如今尉缭已在此，你便将方才的话，再说一次，寡人便要看看，事实是否当真如此。”
徐福也不由得抬头去打量尉缭脸上的表情。
尉缭面色冷漠，模样沉稳，看不出丝毫的破绽，的确不太像是郑妃心中的那人，若他真是的话，到了秦王跟前，怎么还能维持住与他无关的冷静姿态？除非是他的演技实在太好。
郑妃的身体又战栗了起来，她好半天才稳住了情绪，低声道：“王上，这样的话……我如何……如何再能复述一遍……”
嬴政冷漠地看着她，“那你便告诉尉缭，你心中所愿，究竟是什么。寡人也在此听着。”
郑妃又重重地咬了咬唇，这才吐出一口气，对着尉缭道：“不知尉缭先生可还记得我……”
尉缭倒也不隐藏，大大方方在嬴政跟前点了头，“记得。昔日游历郑国，与郑妃有过几面之缘。”后面半句听上去更像是解释给嬴政听的。
“我自入秦宫以来，心中有一愿望，我日夜因这个难以达成的愿望，辗转反侧，难以入眠。”或许是因为见到了尉缭的缘故，郑妃脸上的表情不再紧绷着了，她脸上飞快地闪过似哭似笑的神色，“尉缭先生可知，我心中挂念姜游……”
尉缭不自觉地朝嬴政看了一眼，随后不待郑妃说完，便打断了她，“郑妃此时提起他来，是何用意？”
徐福暗自皱眉。
瞧上去，这尉缭与郑妃并没有几分情谊啊，开口语气竟是如此生硬，半点不留情面。
徐福总觉得郑妃如今的境地有些堪忧。
而郑妃此时情绪微微激动，“尉缭先生，我心中思念……”
尉缭再度打断了她，“如今郑妃乃秦王姬妾，怎能贸然提起我这师兄？我师兄年纪已大，我离去时，便听闻他有娶妻之意，想必等回时，我那师兄已有妻儿了。”
郑妃脸上神色骤然就冷了，她收起目光，面色恢复到平静无波的状态，几乎也就是那样一瞬间的功夫，她便收拾起了所有的情绪，恢复成了从前的那个郑妃。
情绪变化之快，令徐福惊讶。
郑妃甚至连半分恍惚忧伤的表情都没有流露出来，便冷硬地回了尉缭一句，“原来如此，我知道了。”
“请尉缭先生出去。”嬴政冷声道。
尉缭也没有要多留的意思，只是走之前，他反倒还回过头来，深深地看了一眼徐福，徐福被这一眼看得有些莫名其妙。
尉缭来得快，走得也快，明显并不乐意掺合进这档事来。想来也不难理解，任何聪明人，都不会想要掺合进君王的家务事，因为一旦掺合进来，此后便可能成为毁灭自身的影子。试问，王室这些糟心的事，君王怎会乐意让别人知道呢？秦王对于任何冒犯他威严的人，都不会客气。
只是丢下了激动褪去的郑妃，这时她才不免露出了心灰意冷的表情。
“这便是你想要的结果了？”嬴政冷声问。
郑妃舔了舔干涩的唇，跪地求嬴政，“妾已活不长久了，如今王上身边已有心仪之人，求王上放妾出宫，安然死去。”
嬴政也不发怒，只单手抓着徐福的手腕，冷声问他：“如此看来，你是顾不上扶苏了。”
“扶苏原本就只有跟着王上，方能有未来。我从前护不住他，以后必然也护不好他，何况，将死之人，再无心力。”郑妃的神色冷漠，这时倒是极为理智了。
其实在徐福看来，郑妃并不会那么快就死，至少他半点征兆也没能从她的身上看见。不过，说来说去，他毕竟也并非大夫，怎么能看出人家究竟病了还是没病？徐福只是觉得有些可惜。虽然他不喜欢郑妃的性子，但郑妃是个聪明人，又是个无辜的人。如今秦始皇跟他私底下搅了一腿，回过头便要求小老婆洁身自好不能出墙，怎么瞧都怎么双标了些。
毕竟最好的处理方式，便莫过于郑妃去过她的生活，而他和秦始皇继续在一起，这样也算是不亏了郑妃，不管如何说，郑妃始终为秦始皇产下了扶苏，如果秦始皇处理此事太过双标，那岂不是就跟渣男一样儿的？
“那寡人再问你一句，扶苏是谁的儿子？”
郑妃坚定道：“自然是王上的！”
徐福心道，扶苏应当是没有错的，嬴政虽然子息微薄，但好歹总是有的。
嬴政这才从郑妃身上收回了目光，“谁让你来寻徐福的？”
“妾自己前来的，从前便听闻徐先生大名，所以才妄想能求徐先生帮助一二。”
嬴政冷笑一声，“也罢，寡人便给你一次机会，但此后你不是秦国夫人，又不是郑国王女，你要更名改姓，与那平民为伍，你也愿意吗？”嬴政自己都觉得有些惊奇，他更生气的并非郑妃心头所属，更多的反而是不高兴郑妃求到了徐福跟前来，令徐福难做。
如果徐福知道嬴政心中所想，一定会朝他投去同情的目光，叹一声，秦始皇如今想法起了变化，定然是戴绿帽都戴习惯了……
郑妃的神色平静得出奇，“妾愿意。”
嬴政转头冲内侍道：“将扶苏公子引进来。”
“喏。”内侍忙出去将扶苏带了进来。
扶苏小心地打量了一眼嬴政的脸色，方才问道：“父王，母亲可是何处惹父王不快了吗？”
嬴政的脸色缓和了一些，并未回答扶苏所问，“扶苏，你母亲病了，她要离开咸阳去治病，你愿意让她走吗？”
“扶苏愿意。”扶苏一点停顿也不带，倒是与郑妃坚定的模样如出一辙，“母亲病了，自然应该去能治好她的地方。”
徐福看了一眼扶苏脸上的神情，发现了一个很有意思的细节。
听见郑妃生病，扶苏并无惊慌，他似乎早就料到会如此，或者换句话说，他似乎知道自己的母亲心中有他人放不下，他也知道需要治病的托词之下，真相应该是如何的。
扶苏实在成熟得不似这个年纪的人。
嬴政高高在上地看了一眼郑妃和扶苏，“那寡人便赐你一次机会。回去吧。”
郑妃叩地重重地磕了几次，这才拉起扶苏的手，带着他走了出去，想必郑妃还有话要同扶苏交代。
徐福眨了眨眼，秦始皇这样便放过他们了？
徐福自然不会知晓，嬴政在影响他的同时，他的存在自然也会影响到嬴政，嬴政的决定之所以有了改变，也不过是因为他而已。
“日后若再有人求到你跟前来，你不必理会便是。”嬴政转过头来，看着他道。
徐福笑道：“王上是知晓的，我取钱财，便会替人算命。”
嬴政倒也不生气，转而道：“秦宫之中，有何物，寡人都能给你，那寡人便要你这辈子只与寡人算命，如何？”
如此诱惑的筹码，徐福是很想答应。但若是只为嬴政一人算卦，他这辈子便也不要想有何精进了。算命这一行，对于经验的要求实在太高了，看千遍书，不如看上百张面孔。
于是徐福笑了笑，不动声色地将话推了回去，“我竟不知，王上还会说些好听的话。”
“寡人时时都在你跟前说好听的话，不过你未往心里去罢了。”嬴政察觉到徐福的推拒意味，也不放在心上，淡淡说完，便握着徐福的手腕将他往外带去了。
嬴政今日难得有了几分闲情，便带着徐福在王宫之中来回散步。
终于不是一抓着他，就往床上带了。
徐福心中松了一口气。
嬴政似乎还有几分不愉，这才有了这样少女情怀的举动，哦，至少在徐福的眼中挺少女情怀的。
两人一边走着，嬴政一边还时不时地与徐福说上几句话，倒也有几分闲散的味道，只可惜这天有些阴沉，若是有日光加身，必然是暖融融的。
“那尉缭便是鬼谷门下的弟子。”说到此处，嬴政脸上终于见了笑意，“寡人会为你遮掩好的。”
徐福脸色一黑，他就知道，秦始皇果然是早就知晓他并非鬼谷弟子了。
不过徐福睁着眼装淡定，道：“无事，我并无畏惧之处。”
嬴政脸上的笑意更浓了几分，其实他倒是很享受这样将徐福护在掌心的滋味，“早有人与寡人推荐过尉缭，尉缭此人颇有几分本事，还在鬼谷门下时便已小有名气，后来游历各国，更是渐渐传出了名声，他能来投秦，于寡人来说，也是一件好事了。”
“王上放心，我不会与他为难起来的。”
嬴政还是笑道：“是，寡人放心得很。”他原本以为徐福若是被揭穿，定然会面上无光，只是没想到徐福这么快便淡定下来了。思及此，嬴政心中又不免有些好奇，徐福究竟是出自何高人门下？谁才能教出他这样奇妙的人来？
二人走了一会儿，便回去用晚膳了，用过之后，当夜入睡时，徐福做好了百般的措施，将自己裹成一个丸子，嬴政原本也没打算对他动手动脚，见他往日都作一副高冷的模样，偏偏今日裹着被子裹得有些好笑，竟是将风度气质全都抛掉了，嬴政不由觉得好笑，抬手将徐福搂入怀中，很快便就同徐福一起入睡了。
这一日的不快，倒是就这样消散了。
只是嬴政并未想到，他本能地将郑妃从咸阳城中驱走，便是已经动了只留徐福一人在身边的心思。
君王哪有深情人？嬴政的教育之中从未有过相关的知识，他缺乏这项认知，自然也没往那一处想过去。

第二日徐福醒来时，还微微怔忡了一会儿。不与秦始皇缠绵一番，他反倒不习惯了，他这是什么毛病？发情后遗症吗？徐福揉了揉额角，问宫女：“郑妃呢？”
宫女一欠身，“今日一早，郑妃便坐着马车离开咸阳城去养病了。”
不愧是秦始皇，效率果然够快。
只是徐福还有些低落。
昨日尉缭说的那番话，那不是粉碎了郑妃的心头所愿吗？而他之前说郑妃必然能如愿以偿，那岂不是他算错了？
徐福什么都能接受，但惟独不能接受自己算错了。
他算命时，向来谨慎，没有把握之事，尤其是像这等事，他向来不会给人希望，不然若是未能实现，徒惹人伤心。
徐福对这个结果有些耿耿于怀。
不行，他必须得时时关注一下郑妃的消息，一定要证实他的批语才行！
徐福皱了皱眉，起身洗漱更衣。此时嬴政已经离去。徐福用过补汤和早膳，慢悠悠地坐着马车朝奉常寺去了。
从徐福同李斯一起走了，奉常寺上下便有眼红的，也有嘲笑的。有人认为他能与李斯同行，做秦国使臣，那是代表了秦王的青睐，如何不惹人眼红？但也有人认为他有病，如今已是典事，安安分分留在奉常寺中，日日舒适享受，为何还要去吃这个苦？跑到那么远的地方去，一旦任务完不成，还可能会招致王上厌恶！
听闻李斯归来后，众人见到了王柳，却独独不见徐福，于从前变化甚大的王柳口中又问不出什么来了，这些人便只有用自己的思维暗暗猜测徐福发生了什么，他们却不知徐福在王宫之中的待遇甚好，并无操心之事，他们心中所想，全都成了自我意淫罢了。
徐福回到奉常寺，先与苏邑见了一面。
苏邑也不知刚发生了什么事，脸上神色难看，只是一见了他，面色大喜，当即便迎了上来。
“徐典事是何时回来的？”
“当然是与我一道的。”王柳的声音在不远处响起，徐福转头一看，就见王柳脸色也不大好看地走了过来。
他同苏邑之间的气氛甚为僵硬。
王柳的口气实在有些不耐烦，苏邑自然也没了好脸色。
“这样吧，若是有空，便随我过去，闲谈一二。”徐福这话是对着苏邑说的。
苏邑也不客气，当即点了点头，跟着徐福过去了。
“此行如何？”进了门，苏邑便当即问道，“李斯乃是个体贴的友人，徐典事与他可还处得来？”
苏邑在徐福的眼中顿时成了个拉皮条的模样。
说得像是他们二人在相亲一样。
徐福无奈道：“李长史的确体贴不已，与他同行，十分愉快。”
苏邑这才放了心，“未曾想到世间竟有如此巧合，本欲将李长史引见给徐典事认识，徐典事却先一步认识了。”
的确奇妙！
徐福也不知道，他来到秦国，是不是也是冥冥中注定的事。
又与苏邑聊了几句，二人聊得心情畅快不已，随后徐福才将苏邑送走了。
不过奉常寺中平常的确难有什么大事，徐福无所事事，又看了一天的古籍，之后便收拾收拾出了奉常寺。只是今日他出来得早了一些，那小内侍还未到，徐福正琢磨着是否要转身回去的时候，却见一个身影慢慢映入了眼帘之中。
……是尉缭！
尉缭脸上的冷漠之色褪去了不少，他直直地朝着徐福走来，“随我过来。”尉缭说罢，便又自顾自地转身往另一边走了。
徐福一头雾水，只觉得尉缭的口气实在不大礼貌。
不过心中的疑惑占了上风，于是徐福犹豫没一会儿，便跟了上去。
尉缭走得并不远，只是远离了奉常寺的大门而已。二人就这样立在路旁，尉缭终于转过身与徐福面对面了。
“你与秦王是怎么回事？”尉缭眉头紧锁，冷声问道。
徐福心中更加不快了，尉缭不仅是语气很不礼貌，他开口说的话也实在不礼貌。徐福眼神中带上了疏离和抗拒，他往后退了退，冷声反问：“阁下有何权利问我？”
尉缭脸色瞬间变得怪异起来，“你又忘了？”
“什么？”徐福眉头也跟着皱了起来，这尉缭究竟在说什么？稀里糊涂也不说个明白话！
“你果然又忘了，我还道，那日在王宫中，好端端的，你为何问我叫什么名字，之前在魏国时，你见了我如见陌生人般，我还当你是不便认出我。”尉缭叹了一口气。
徐福心中发毛。
难道他的原身，跟这位还有什么关系？
总不会是旧情人吧？
徐福心中暗自打了个哆嗦，他可实在不好尉缭这一款啊。
秦始皇他倒是能接受，但尉缭……
徐福又往后退了退，看着尉缭的目光更为警惕了，尉缭不由得咬牙，“你这脑袋，究竟何时才能记得住事儿！”
“你认错人了？”徐福终于忍不住出声打断了尉缭。
尉缭脸上怒气涌动，一脸恨铁不成钢的表情，“我认错人？我何时能将你认错？”
完了……徐福心中不好的预感更甚，他总觉得尉缭这语气，就像是旧情人找上门来了一样，瞧一瞧说的话也暧昧得很。可如今什么旧情人都与他无关了啊。打死不认，就假装对方认错人，或者自己失忆好了。
“此次失忆，你又要多久才能想起来？”尉缭的声音几乎是从牙齿中挤出来的，他一身沉稳的形象，顿时破坏了个干净。
哦！连借口都已经替他想好了！徐福暗暗愉悦，面不改色地扯道：“或许几个月吧……”
他就不信尉缭还能盯上他几个月不成？
尉缭抬手揉了揉额角，“希望如此吧。”说罢，他放下手来，脸色突地肃穆了起来，“你还未曾告诉我，你与秦王究竟是怎么回事？”
徐福看着他，不说话。他觉得就算他不说话，尉缭也能把对话继续进行下去。
果不其然，尉缭不等他开口，便又道：“好，你不用说了，我已经猜到几分了。”尉缭脸色一沉，“你要投秦，我本是没有意见的，我也跟着朝秦国而来，但我近几日观了那秦王的面相……”
徐福的耳朵瞬间就竖了起来。
这人果然会看相！
他看秦始皇的面相，又会得出如何的一番结论呢？是否与自己相同呢？徐福微微有些激动，同时也很想知道，秦始皇在别人眼中，又是什么模样的。
“秦王此人，蜂准、长目、挚鸟膺、豺声，面相刚烈。足见其刻薄少恩，虎狼心肠，他谦虚时便不惮屈身于人，得意时，若被冒犯必然是吃人不吐骨头，极为残暴的！我为一介布衣，然他见我常常自降身份尊敬于我。假如有一日秦王实现了吞并天下的野心，他定然是将天下人都看成为他的奴隶，他欠缺仁德之心，这样的人不可长期与之交游。”尉缭冷声道，极不留情面。
徐福愣了愣，心头骂了句我操。
你他妈才细长眼睛，鸡胸，豺一样的声音！
秦始皇长那么英俊神武，你眼睛瞎了吗？
徐福心中气不打一处来，憋得难受，于是他冷冷地盯着尉缭，忍不住脱口道：“你眼瞎。”
尉缭皱眉，冷声道：“我知你对秦王极为尊崇，但赵政实在比不上其祖父！历任秦王皆是好战之人，赵政尤甚！他脾气暴烈，不是个很好相与的人！他极能隐忍，心机深沉！日后你若是在他手中吃了苦头，都还不知怎么一回事。这样的君王，哪里值得你去辅佐效忠？还是速与我离秦，往别国去。我瞧那魏国便不错……”
不错个屁！
魏王生得猥琐，还好色！
他都把人男宠给拐走了，还跑魏国去？上赶着让魏王吃了他吗？
徐福心中火气更甚，但他多次在心中默念，我是文明人，不骂人。
但如此一番过后，他还是有些忍不住胸中翻腾的怒火。徐福一直认为自己的修养极好了，任是谁上前挑拨，他都能维持淡然的姿态，偏偏……偏偏今日，他怎么就听着这些话那么刺耳，那么难以忍受呢？
“我看不可与之交游的人，是你。”
尉缭闻言，脸色大变，“你怎么如此说话？”
“我说得不对吗？”徐福冷笑道：“我实在难以理解阁下的脑子。我问你七国之中信陵君，春申君名声如何？”
尉缭不明所以，但还是答道：“这二人礼贤下士，广招宾客，又皆为贤士……”
徐福当即就打断了他，“怎么？依你一家之言，他们二人广招宾客，礼遇于有能之人，便是礼贤下士了？而秦王自降身份，礼遇于你，便是财狼之心，颇有心计，擅长隐忍，必须提防了是吗？”
他就没见过双标这么严重的人！
尉缭说这话的时候，亏心不亏心？
尉缭却并不认同徐福之言，“我观秦王面相便是如此，此人心胸狭隘，日后谁得罪了他，他必然千般报复回去……”
徐福再度打断了他，“小人欺负了你，你是圣母还是圣父？不报复回去？难道你还要感谢他吗？”
“若是谁惹了你，便要报复回去，乃小人所为！”尉缭厉声道。
“你不要混淆概念，他是堂堂秦王，他哪有那个功夫跟人计较些小事？谁若真的冒犯了他，冒犯秦王的大事，难道不应该还回去吗？你说他心胸狭隘，便是狭隘了吗？可我瞧他面相，便觉他心胸宽大，有容人之量，又有极大的魄力，能接纳贤士，他是个好君主！”徐福顿了顿，喘口气，又道：“且不说这个，做小人有何不好？做小人才畅快！”
君子都是伪君子了！徐福心中吐槽。
尉缭惊了惊，忍不住道：“如今你到了秦国，竟是……竟是被影响得如此之严重！那秦王与你说了什么？竟让你如此相信他？”
徐福又不高兴了。
尉缭坚持自己所言，他坚持他所言，有何不对？他有自己的坚持，难道就是被秦王蒙蔽了吗？
依他看，尉缭才是被蒙蔽了！非要将脏水往秦王身上泼，凭什么啊？
“别扯开话题，你说你观他面相得出这番言论来，我观他面相，却又得出另一番言论来，我的结论与你全然不同。”徐福厉声道，竟是气势更强地将尉缭镇住了。
尉缭也气得不轻，他怒极反笑，“那你便与我说说，你观得的秦王面相又是如何？”
徐福闭了闭眼，脑中浮现了第一次见到秦王时的画面。
那些话还仿佛在耳边回响。
徐福目光灼灼地看向尉缭，朗声道：“秦王面相贵不可言！”
尉缭嗤笑一声。
徐福接着将当初埋在心中却未能说出的那番话，如今原原本本地说了出来，“观秦王仪表。神气生威！观秦王头额。额高头方，贵不可言！观秦王双眸。眼眸深邃，眸光清铄，不怒自威！观五岳三亭、五官六府，蛟欲化龙，有一日必将一飞冲天！他身材英武，气势威严！哪里有你所言的细长眼睛，鸡胸，豺一样的声音？”
徐福又冷笑一声，“莫不是你嫉妒于他？这才故意抹黑他？秦王政生有如此相貌，将来他吞并天下的野心，必能实现！他或许不是仁德的君王，但他能让平民百姓吃好穿好过得好，那他就是英明的君王！”
“胡言乱语！”尉缭气极，只能干巴巴地否认。
徐福笑道：“你且看着吧！”
你且看着吧，终有一日，秦始皇会成为千古一帝！

chapters.translated_text:
The sound of the carriage drew closer. Xu Fu couldn't be bothered to deal with Wei Liao anymore; he cast a cold, disdainful glance at him, making no effort to hide his aversion, and turned to leave.

Wei Liao frowned tightly, his tone sounding helpless, as if he were dealing with a mischievous child. "You’re always so stubborn with me. Well, this time, I’ll see if you learn your lesson!"

"Your skill in physiognomy is so poor, yet you dare to spout such nonsense in front of me. I, too, would like to see if you learn your lesson." Xu Fu threw these cold words over his shoulder and walked toward the small attendant who had arrived in the carriage.

The small attendant jumped off the carriage with a beaming smile and hurried over to Xu Fu. "Have you been waiting long, Director Xu?"

Wei Liao stared intently at the attendant. Without waiting for Xu Fu to speak, he asked, "Are you entering the palace again?"

Xu Fu ignored him and said only to the attendant, "You arrived a moment late, and some strange, inexplicable person came looking for me."

Although the small attendant didn't fully understand, he still cast a wary glance at Wei Liao.

Wei Liao felt a surge of anger at that look, feeling that everyone around the King of Qin was as suspicious as the King himself.

"Xu Fu, leave the State of Qin with me," Wei Liao said sternly.

Upon hearing this, the small attendant became even more guarded, looking at Wei Liao as if he were a human trafficker.

"Drive him away." Xu Fu quickly boarded the carriage and lowered the curtain, blocking Wei Liao’s face from view.

The small attendant had been hesitant at first. He had seen Wei Liao in the palace and knew the King treated him with great courtesy; naturally, he didn't want to offend him if he didn't have to. But Wei Liao had clashed with Xu Fu, and now he was trying to abduct him... that was simply unacceptable!

The small attendant’s expression darkened immediately. Looking fierce, he stood coldly in front of Wei Liao. "Master Wei Liao, why invite trouble for yourself? Please, just leave." The attendant didn't just stop at words; he began rolling up his sleeves as he spoke.

Wei Liao’s expression was ugly. He said in a low voice, "Xu Fu, do not be willful. You have lost your memory, so you believe anyone who offers you a little sweetness. If you are deceived, how will you ever recover your losses? Come away from Xianyang with me!"

"Go." Xu Fu spat out the single word, directed at the attendant, and naturally, at Wei Liao as well.

Since arriving in this world, the first face Xu Fu had seen was Ying Zheng’s, the first person he had read was Ying Zheng, and the person he was most familiar with was Ying Zheng. So what if he was the historical First Emperor of Qin? To him, this man had become a more real, tangible person. Would he abandon the First Emperor to trust someone who had lectured him after only a few meetings? He wasn't out of his mind.

Xu Fu trusted his own judgment more.

He was not wrong; the First Emperor of Qin was not the cruel and inhumane tyrant described in historical records!

He would prove that Wei Liao was wrong!

The carriage wheels turned, heading toward Xianyang Palace. Wei Liao could only watch the carriage disappear, gritting his teeth in frustration. Perhaps out of sheer anger, he muttered bitterly, "My teacher should never have let him leave so easily!" But after venting, Wei Liao let out a breath. "Fine. He speaks so well now, but who knows when his memory might return? When that happens, will he even remember who the King of Qin is?"

Wei Liao flicked his sleeve, turned, and strode away.

That same day, Ying Zheng received word that Wei Liao had left the residence he had arranged for him.

Because of the Lady Zheng incident, Ying Zheng inevitably held some reservations about Wei Liao. However, he was even more aware of Wei Liao’s value. This man understood military strategy, human nature, and politics, having lobbied various states. Had the State of Wei not already had Lord Xinling and Lord Longyang, Wei Liao would have stayed to assist the King of Wei. He had come to Qin to lobby and was recommended to Ying Zheng by Cai Ze. After conversing with him, Ying Zheng confirmed that Wei Liao possessed genuine talent, which was why he wanted to keep him.

To show his esteem, Ying Zheng had even arranged quarters for him within the palace to facilitate more discussions. Wei Liao used the excuse of feeling uncomfortable and out of place to move out, so Ying Zheng arranged a residence for him outside the palace. Yet, Wei Liao remained picky and repeatedly expressed his dissatisfaction.

Now, Ying Zheng finally saw through Wei Liao’s intentions.

He had no desire to stay in the Great Qin!

Ying Zheng couldn't help but feel a surge of anger.

*I have treated him with such courtesy, yet is there something that displeases him? He refuses to give me even a shred of face.*

Now that Wei Liao had vanished completely, Ying Zheng felt as though his good intentions had been fed to the dogs.

When Ying Zheng returned to his sleeping quarters, his expression remained gloomy. He stepped into the hall only to see that Xu Fu also looked displeased, holding a stylus and writing something on a bamboo slip. Seeing Xu Fu, the displeasure in Ying Zheng’s heart subsided slightly. His attention quickly shifted to why Xu Fu might be unhappy.

Ying Zheng summoned an attendant and asked, "When you went to fetch Director Xu today, did something happen?"

Xu Fu was not the type to wear his emotions on his sleeve; he was usually detached and composed, far beyond his years. Seeing him drop his cold facade and show such an expression was rare, and Ying Zheng couldn't help but wonder what major event had occurred.

The attendant played the role of a tattletale well. He bowed slightly and said, "Reporting to the King, when this servant went to fetch Director Xu today, he seemed to have just had a dispute with Master Wei Liao."

Wei Liao again?

Ying Zheng’s expression darkened instantly.

"Why did they get into a dispute?" Ying Zheng asked coldly, a flicker of murderous intent toward Wei Liao rising in his heart. A man like that, who knew no gratitude and was overly arrogant—if Qin could not tame him, then he should not be allowed to serve other states either.

While Wei Liao thought of Ying Zheng as a wolf, he did not realize that in Ying Zheng’s eyes, he was also a wolf without character.

...

The small attendant stammered awkwardly for a moment. Seeing his expression, Ying Zheng became even more convinced there was a hidden story.

"What did Wei Liao say?" Ying Zheng asked in a low voice.

"He... he said... he told Director Xu to leave Xianyang City with him, and said that Director Xu is easily deceived..." The attendant glanced at Ying Zheng’s face as he spoke, terrified that the King’s temper would flare and he would be caught in the crossfire.

Ying Zheng, who had "deceived" Xu Fu, felt a deep sense of irritation. When he pondered the words further, he realized Wei Liao was trying to poach his own person!

Ying Zheng’s expression was ghastly, his murderous intent deepening.

"He has a lot of nerve." Ying Zheng’s voice became increasingly low and cold.

The attendant didn't dare say another word.

Across the room, Xu Fu looked up and finally noticed Ying Zheng had returned. He set down his stylus and looked toward Ying Zheng, seeing his tall figure standing before the window frame, blocking most of the light and casting a long shadow.

Xu Fu looked at him earnestly for a moment, thinking to himself with annoyance: *Look at him! So tall, handsome, and imposing! How the hell is he 'deformed'? Where is he deformed? Wei Liao must be jealous that the First Emperor is taller, more handsome, and more powerful and wealthy than him!*

And how did that Wei Liao even see that the First Emperor had a pigeon chest?

Bah!

*I’m the only one who has touched the First Emperor’s chest, okay? Only me! Wei Liao can’t even touch it, so he can shut his mouth!*

Xu Fu’s emotions churned excitedly, and in a moment of carelessness, he drove his stylus into the wooden table.

The palace servants were startled, staring at him in bewilderment, their lips trembling. "D-Director Xu..."

Xu Fu snapped back to reality, calmly pulled out the stylus, and touched the hole he had poked. He hadn't realized he possessed such divine strength. He placed the stylus over the hole, perfectly covering it.

By then, Ying Zheng had finished speaking with the attendant and walked over to Xu Fu.

Pretending to know nothing, Ying Zheng sat beside Xu Fu and asked, "What are you carving?"

Xu Fu lied, "A curse. I’m writing it down so that if anyone offends me in the future, I can cast a curse on them." Even saying such things, Xu Fu didn't lose his cold, otherworldly aura—at least, not in Ying Zheng’s eyes.

Ying Zheng picked up the bamboo slip and flipped through it. Xu Fu had actually recorded names of herbs and some alchemy formulas—all compiled by himself. Ying Zheng couldn't help but raise an eyebrow; Xu Fu’s reply just now showed he was still unhappy.

Ying Zheng’s mood improved significantly.

The fact that Xu Fu showed such extreme displeasure at Wei Liao’s words meant that Xu Fu did not want to leave Xianyang, nor did he want to leave him. It was clear that Xu Fu was not without feelings for him. Ying Zheng felt comforted, and a faint smile slowly appeared on his face.

"How is the alchemy coming along?"

Xu Fu shook his head. "Nothing has been refined yet."

Just then, an attendant entered on tiptoe and bowed. "Your Majesty, General Meng requests an audience."

Ying Zheng frowned slightly. "It’s so late, why is he coming to my palace?" Although he said this, he ordered the General to be invited to the side hall. This showed the high favor he held for this General Meng.

Ying Zheng stood up and, not avoiding Xu Fu, asked, "Would you like to come with me? This man is my trusted general. He must have just finished his lessons with Fusu. I’ll introduce you to him."

Xu Fu suddenly felt like he was in his past life, where ordinary people would bring their partners into their social circles.

He nodded in a daze, and was then pulled up by Ying Zheng, who held his wrist.

The two headed toward the side hall.

Upon entering, Xu Fu saw a sturdy young man standing in the hall, dressed in casual clothes. His expression was taut, unsmiling, and he radiated an aura of iron and blood—clearly the product of a military family.

Hearing footsteps, the man turned around immediately and bowed respectfully to Ying Zheng. He failed to notice Xu Fu behind the King, so Xu Fu’s presence went unacknowledged.

"Your Majesty, Meng Tian heard that Master Wei Liao has left Xianyang City..." The man began as soon as he straightened up.

But before he could finish, he froze, his gaze lingering on Xu Fu.

Xu Fu looked back at him, and Meng Tian quickly looked away, turning to ask Ying Zheng, "Your Majesty, this... this is..."

"This is Director Xu from the Fengchang Temple."

Meng Tian nodded, still confused. Why would someone from the Fengchang Temple be with the King at this hour? Pushing aside his doubts, he said, "Your Majesty, why did Master Wei Liao leave so hastily? I heard about it today and have been restless. Such a great talent—if he is not kept in Qin, it is truly a loss for the state!"

"Pay him no mind. Wei Liao is used to wandering; it is normal for him not to stay in Qin." Ying Zheng paused and changed the subject. "How did Fusu do today?"

Meng Tian was led astray by Ying Zheng’s change of topic. He answered seriously, "Young Master Fusu is still young, so I dare not teach him too much. However, I have taught him the basics of physical training, and the Young Master practices diligently. I believe he will make rapid progress."

Ying Zheng chatted with Meng Tian about Fusu for a while, then concluded with a single sentence, "You have worked hard recently. Go home early to have your meal; it is late, and I will have someone see you out."

Meng Tian declined the offer of an escort and turned to leave on his own.

By the time Meng Tian reached the palace gates, his mind was a blur of Xu Fu’s stunning face and thoughts on how to teach Fusu. It took a long time for him to clear his head. He frowned: *Why did the King not want me to mention Wei Liao? Well, it makes sense. Wei Liao’s actions touched upon the King’s dignity; it is only natural the King is displeased.*

Meng Tian sighed and arrived at the Meng residence. Instead of going inside to eat with his family, he called for his servants, boarded a carriage, and headed quickly out of the city.

"G-General, what are we... going to do?" a servant couldn't help but ask.

"We are going to find Master Wei Liao."

Meanwhile, Wei Liao had not yet managed to leave Xianyang City. He had just stepped out of a tavern after a meal when his path was blocked by a carriage. Wei Liao was in a foul mood today, so he naturally had no pleasant expression.

"Who are you?" Wei Liao asked coldly.

Meng Tian jumped down. "Master Wei Liao, please stay!"

Thinking of Xu Fu’s refusal to listen, Wei Liao felt irritated. Now, looking at anyone in Qin felt like looking at an enemy, so his tone was sharp. "Who are you? My comings and goings are not for you to decide!"

Meng Tian’s face was resolute; when he became serious, he looked as if he were about to slaughter someone.

Seeing Meng Tian’s grim expression, Wei Liao turned to leave immediately.

How could Meng Tian watch him slip away right under his nose? In that moment, Meng Tian felt as if he were on the battlefield, unable to tolerate any enemy soldier escaping. He stepped forward, grabbed Wei Liao’s shoulder, and performed a shoulder... throw... throw... throw...

Wei Liao was a bit dazed from the throw.

But Meng Tian thought that since the King’s courtesy hadn't been enough to keep Wei Liao, he would have to try a different approach.

Meng Tian said sternly, "My apologies, Master." With that, he hoisted Wei Liao up, put him into the carriage, and took the driver’s seat himself. He cracked the whip, and the horses galloped away.

If they were any later, the city would be under curfew.

Once they reached the Meng residence, Wei Liao wouldn't be able to leave even if he wanted to.

Wei Liao was tossed about violently inside the carriage. When they arrived at the Meng residence, Meng Tian helped him down, but as soon as Wei Liao’s feet touched the ground, his legs went weak, and he nearly prostrated himself in front of the gate. Fortunately, Meng Tian caught him, though he nearly knocked the wind out of Wei Liao.

Xu Fu was in the palace and naturally didn't know that Meng Tian had already taken revenge on his behalf.

·

After Meng Tian left, Xu Fu ate with Ying Zheng. Afterward, he suddenly remembered he should check on Huhai, so he left Ying Zheng and was led by a palace maid to the side hall.

Huhai had just finished his meal. It was less like Xu Fu coming to play with Huhai, and more like the oblivious Huhai playing with Xu Fu. In any case, Huhai didn't cry easily anymore; he let Xu Fu fuss over him and even let out giggles.

Seeing how cute he was at this young age, Xu Fu became determined that he must not let Huhai be raised into a "second-generation ancestor."

*Keeping him this adorably stupid is just fine.*

Xu Fu rubbed his cheeks and, on a whim, decided he wanted to sleep in the same bed as Huhai. Ignoring the protests of the palace maids, he forcibly bundled Huhai up and took him away.

Ying Zheng had just sat down at his desk and picked up his stylus when he noticed the hole in the table.

Ying Zheng looked at the stylus with a complex expression as he put it back. *I didn't know Xu Fu possessed such sharp knife (?) skills.*

Just then, Xu Fu stepped into the hall. Ying Zheng looked up, wondering if Xu Fu was still unhappy and how he should comfort him. Who would have thought that the first thing he saw was Huhai in Xu Fu’s arms? Ying Zheng’s mood plummeted. But thinking that Huhai might soothe Xu Fu’s displeasure, he relaxed. At this point, he didn't know he had relaxed too soon.

Xu Fu entered with Huhai, and suddenly remembering Ying Zheng’s attitude toward the child, he paused and asked, "If Your Majesty does not wish to see Huhai, I will take him to the side hall."

"No need," Ying Zheng shook his head. "Since when would I hold a grudge against a child?"

If it was for Xu Fu’s sake, Huhai didn't matter.

However, while Ying Zheng was being magnanimous, Huhai was still holding a grudge. Leaning in Xu Fu’s arms, he spotted the taller Ying Zheng and wanted to blow bubbles at him. Xu Fu saw the expression and knew something was wrong, immediately reaching out to plug Huhai’s mouth.

Huhai smiled at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu did not smile back.

*He spits at everyone. If I don't stop this, it will only get worse.*

*Besides, Huhai is so stupid, he’d even spit at the First Emperor. If he gets himself executed by the First Emperor one day, his tombstone will just have the words: 'Died of too much spit.'*

"Swallow your saliva, don't spit it out, understand?" Xu Fu pinched Huhai’s cheek, his expression stern.

Seeing Xu Fu’s cold look, Huhai blinked and pursed his little lips, a line of drool sliding down the corner of his mouth.

The palace maid nearby couldn't help but laugh. "Director Xu, children are just like that. They’re teething, the drool is unstoppable."

"Can’t he swallow it?" Xu Fu frowned.

"Sometimes it’s too late to swallow, and sometimes the child is just being mischievous and wants to spit it out."

"Well, he can drool, but he cannot spit." Xu Fu pinched his little mouth. "Do you understand? You’re my son now. If you don't behave, people will say I didn't teach you well."

Xu Fu spoke without reservation, and Ying Zheng, with a faint smile on his face, watched Xu Fu’s movements with deep eyes, seemingly tacitly agreeing with what Xu Fu had said.

The palace servants noticed this and exchanged glances, feeling both shocked and panicked.

Who would dare claim the King of Qin’s son as their own?

Yet Xu Fu had said exactly that, and the King of Qin had shown no sign of refuting it.

The servants hurriedly buried their thoughts and lowered their heads even further.

After pinching Huhai, Xu Fu finished his "education." He pointed at Huhai in his arms and asked the maid, "Can I sleep with him?"

The maid looked up, noticed the icy gaze Ying Zheng was casting at her, and froze. "This... this..." *Whether he can sleep with him or not isn't for me to decide, it should be the King...*

Ying Zheng asked patiently, "Why did you suddenly decide to sleep with Huhai today?"

Xu Fu poked Huhai’s cheek. "Didn't Your Majesty say Huhai belongs to me now? Naturally, I should cultivate some affection with him."

*What affection are you cultivating with him? You should be cultivating it with me!* Though Ying Zheng could only roar this in his heart. He said calmly, "I see." He truly didn't want Huhai in the middle. If he turned over to pull Xu Fu into his arms, he would have to worry about crushing Huhai’s small body.

"If Your Majesty thinks it’s not good, then I will take Huhai to the side hall..."

Before Xu Fu could finish, Ying Zheng cut him off. "Why would I think it’s not good?"

It was then that Ying Zheng realized he had relaxed too soon.

That night, Huhai accompanied the two of them to bed.

With Huhai in the middle, there was naturally no room for flirting or intimacy. Besides, Huhai was young and fell asleep quickly, unaware of how much trouble he was causing the adults. After tossing and turning several times, Ying Zheng turned, pulled Xu Fu closer, took his wrist, and kissed his fingers.

Xu Fu was also dazed. He opened his sleepy eyes, saw Ying Zheng’s actions, and mumbled, "Mm... Your Majesty, you kissed Huhai’s drool..."

Ying Zheng’s body stiffened. He suddenly remembered... Huhai had indeed been sucking on Xu Fu’s fingers...

Ying Zheng looked down at Huhai’s stupidly sleeping face and felt a pang of regret for giving Huhai to Xu Fu.

Beside him, Xu Fu seemed to sense something and suddenly leaned in.

Ying Zheng met his gaze, falling into Xu Fu’s eyes, which were hazy as if covered in mist. Ying Zheng’s heart stirred, and he suddenly wanted to order the servants to take Huhai away. He moved his throat involuntarily, and the next moment, Xu Fu took the initiative to kiss his lips.

"Sleep..." Xu Fu forced himself to say, as if coaxing a child, then "plop," he lay back down, pulled the quilt up, and fell into a deep sleep.

Ying Zheng, who had just been set ablaze by that dragonfly-light kiss: ...

·

The next day, Ying Zheng made the decision to send Huhai back to the side hall. Although Xu Fu was a bit disappointed, thinking of the baby urine Huhai had soaked him with the night before, he let go of his obsession with cultivating "father-son affection."

Xu Fu strolled into the Fengchang Temple and found Su Yi.

Although he had tried his best to find ancient texts to make up for his lack of knowledge since arriving in Qin, it was a pity that, not being a native, there were many things he still didn't know.

Seeking help from Su Yi was the best choice.

"Yi, have you ever heard of a man named Wei Liao?"

"Wei Liao?" Su Yi looked surprised. "Of course I have. Wei Liao is from Daliang in the State of Wei. Legend has it he comes from Guigu, is skilled in military strategy, and is a wise man with many methods. His intelligence has made the rulers of the Seven States bow to him. Has he come to Qin?"

"From the State of Wei? He certainly has a sense of patriotism," Xu Fu remarked casually. But in his view, Wei Liao didn't necessarily have that much patriotism; otherwise, why would he have come to Qin? Why would he have met the King of Qin? It was just that after meeting the King, he decided it didn't fit his expectations, so he didn't want to stay.

*Saying he favors the King of Wei is probably just talk.*

*But looking at it this way, the First Emperor originally intended to keep him in Qin to assist in his great cause?*

Xu Fu hesitated. *If I drove Wei Liao away with my words... would that ruin the First Emperor’s plans?*

*Should I go and find him?* Although Xu Fu was reluctant, thinking that Wei Liao might indeed be helpful to the First Emperor, he felt he couldn't just let him go so easily. Talented people were often arrogant—didn't he have his own pride? No... Wei Liao wasn't just arrogant, he was brain-damaged! Xu Fu realized he still couldn't calm that feeling.

So, he could only try to look at it from another angle.

Keeping Wei Liao was not for Wei Liao’s own good, but for Qin Shi Huang’s. Xu Fu was well aware that while he had some skill in the arts of divination and fortune-telling, he was completely ignorant in other areas; Qin Shi Huang could not rely on him to conquer the world. A large part of the credit for Qin Shi Huang’s ability to sweep across the six states lay with the talented individuals under his command.

Just like those famous generals, or people like Li Si and Zhao Gao—perhaps Wei Liao was also a very famous figure in history. If he were to simply make the man disappear, would Qin Shi Huang’s life still be as smooth sailing?

He should keep Wei Liao, squeeze out every ounce of his strengths, and deceive him if necessary. Regardless, once the man had been used, it wouldn't matter if Wei Liao cursed them as scumbags or jackals later. A villain is a villain; the winner takes all. By then, would there even be any room left for Wei Liao to speak?

Thinking back on what Wei Liao had said at the time, Xu Fu still felt a sense of injustice in his heart.

If one day Qin Shi Huang reached the supreme position, and Wei Liao realized that he had played a part in it, wouldn't that make him even more furious?

Xu Fu thought this plan was excellent; he was almost ready to bow down to his own cleverness.

He asked Su Yi a few more questions about Wei Liao. Later on, Xu Fu suddenly remembered Consort Zheng, so he couldn't help but ask, "Do you know who Wei Liao’s senior fellow apprentice is?"

Su Yi shook his head. "How could I know that? Guiguzi has three thousand disciples; who knows who Wei Liao’s senior fellow apprentice is?"

Xu Fu felt a bit disappointed.

But then, he immediately thought of someone.

After taking his leave, Xu Fu went straight out of the Fengchang Temple. He went to look for Jianjia’s residence.

Jianjia’s family was not poor; the only reason he worked in the royal palace was to climb the social ladder. Being so young and having already achieved such a position, he was quite impressive. His family lived far away in other commanderies, so Jianjia’s residence was usually occupied only by him, with Bo Zhou and others occasionally crashing there for a night.

When Xu Fu arrived at the residence, the servant was still dozing off at the gate. The sound of Xu Fu’s footsteps startled him; the servant jumped up and shouted, "Who’s there?"

"I’m looking for your master. Tell him my surname is Xu."

The servant gave him a wary look, but thinking that someone so good-looking couldn't possibly be a liar, he quickly went inside. After a short while, someone came out, but it wasn't Jianjia—it was Lord Longyang, still dressed as a woman.

Xu Fu was startled. Why was he still dressed like this?

When Lord Longyang saw Xu Fu, he immediately smiled. "How about it? Is the gentleman here to draw my eyebrows?" Now that they were within the borders of Qin, Lord Longyang naturally could no longer call Xu Fu "the envoy."

Hearing this, the servant whispered, "How can you speak like that, Madam? While my master is away..."

A flood of information instantly surfaced in Xu Fu’s mind based on that sentence.

What kind of game were Lord Longyang and Jianjia playing?

Lord Longyang turned around and walked in front. "Please come in, sir."

Xu Fu followed him in. The servant had a look of wanting to say something but holding back; he turned around, muttering repeatedly, "It’s over, it’s all over..."

"Jianjia isn't here?" Xu Fu looked around, not seeing Jianjia’s figure anywhere in the house.

Lord Longyang nodded. "Jianjia went out for something. As it happens, I have something for you, sir."

"What is it?"

Lord Longyang clapped his hands, and a beautiful maidservant came out holding an object covered by a cloth; it was impossible to see what it was. The maid stopped in front of Xu Fu. Xu Fu reached out and lifted the cloth, revealing an exquisite tripod underneath. The patterns were incredibly beautiful!

"Are you satisfied, sir?" Lord Longyang asked.

"Many thanks, Lord Longyang." Xu Fu held the tripod in his hands and examined it closely. Indeed! It was extremely similar to his own tripod, with only minor differences in the details, but it was clear enough that they must have come from the same hand.

Lord Longyang waved his hand, signaling the maid to take the tripod, wrap it up, and bring it back to Xu Fu. Only then did he ask, "Is there something you needed to find Jianjia for, sir?"

Xu Fu always felt that Lord Longyang’s tone sounded like that of the lady of the house, but he didn't ask further. He said, "I do have a matter, but it is not to find Jianjia; rather, it is something I wish to entrust to Lord Longyang."

"Entrust to me?" The icy look on Lord Longyang’s face faded, replaced by a faint smile. "You actually have something to entrust to me, sir? Have you thought about what reward you will give Longyang?"

"What do you want?"

"Then give me a Qin identity." Lord Longyang smiled. "I find that Qin is truly very comfortable; it suits me very well."

"Alright." Xu Fu agreed without a second thought. He had long heard Qin Shi Huang mention that he would give Lord Longyang a Qin identity to avoid future trouble. Agreeing now was just taking advantage of something he already knew.

Lord Longyang assumed Xu Fu was just being straightforward and immediately said, "Then tell me what the matter is, sir. If Longyang can help, I certainly won't refuse."

"Lord Longyang, keep an eye on someone for me..." Xu Fu told Lord Longyang the general information about Consort Zheng.

Lord Longyang couldn't help but ask, "You are so concerned about this person, sir; is she related to you?"

Xu Fu immediately interrupted him. "I have no friendship with her. It is just that I once performed a divination for her, and out of responsibility for the hexagram, I want Lord Longyang to keep an eye on her for me. If what I said comes true, then I can rest easy." Otherwise, he would always feel like he owed Consort Zheng a debt. After all, he was the one who told her there was hope.

Lord Longyang nodded. "That is no great matter. But since you are here today, sir, why not perform another divination for me?"

Xu Fu didn't even pause. "Lord Longyang will have a 'chrysanthemum fortune' soon." Having said that, he turned to leave. "Jianjia is not here today, and you are dressed as a woman, Lord Longyang; it is not appropriate for me to stay long. I shall take my leave."

With that, Xu Fu walked out quickly.

Only then did Lord Longyang realize something was wrong.

He muttered, "Last time it was a 'peach blossom fortune,' what is this 'chrysanthemum fortune'?"

Could it be that he was just bluffing me?

If Xu Fu had heard his inner thoughts, he would definitely have told him: Yes, I was just bluffing you.

·

Xu Fu did not tell Ying Zheng about asking Lord Longyang to keep an eye on Consort Zheng. While his reasons for doing so were understandable, if he mentioned it to Qin Shi Huang, the Emperor would surely feel a prick of discomfort. So, for once, Xu Fu kept it a secret.

However, when Xu Fu left, he completely forgot about the tripod.

Later, when Lord Longyang saw that the tripod had been left behind, he wanted to send it to Xu Fu, but he didn't know where Xu Fu lived. After Jianjia returned, Lord Longyang asked him, and Jianjia pointed in a direction without even turning his head.

Lord Longyang raised an eyebrow, and still wearing his women’s clothing, he went out quite openly.

When he reached the end of that direction, Lord Longyang stopped in his tracks.

This... this was clearly the royal palace!

Although he had never seen the Qin royal palace, he imagined it would be similar to the Wei royal palace, and he recognized it at a glance. Could that envoy... actually live in the royal palace?

Lord Longyang was about to turn and leave, but the guards at the gate saw him carrying an object, and having never seen such a tall woman, they couldn't help but step forward and grab him. "Who are you? Acting so suspiciously in front of the royal palace?"

Lord Longyang pretended he had come to the wrong place. "I am looking for a gentleman surnamed Xu; I took a wrong turn by accident."

The guard frowned and asked, "You are looking for Mr. Xu?"

Lord Longyang was secretly shocked. Could it be that the envoy really lived inside the royal palace?

The guard hurriedly called another person over and whispered something to him, and that person immediately ran into the palace.

The guard said coldly, "Then you will have to wait for a while."

Lord Longyang felt increasingly suspicious. Besides his status in the Fengchang Temple, did that envoy have some other great status?

He did not know that the message the guard sent up never reached Xu Fu, but was instead passed on to Ying Zheng.

"A woman wants to see Xu Fu?" Ying Zheng frowned, suspicion rising in his heart.

"Indeed." The attendant who replied bowed his head and responded loudly.

Ying Zheng put down his brush. "What does this woman look like?"

The attendant paused. "Um... ah... she looks... very beautiful..."

Hearing this, Ying Zheng was furious. A beautiful woman coming to see Xu Fu? What could it be for? Thinking back to Lady Feng from the Shu region, the woman in the small town, and now this woman who had suddenly appeared... jealousy churned in Ying Zheng’s heart, and he was convinced that this must be yet another person infatuated with Xu Fu.

He is too good at attracting women... Ying Zheng thought to himself, then ordered the guard to bring the person in.

As long as he could stop them from entering the door and claiming they were pregnant with Xu Fu’s child, he could nip the problem in the bud and block all the women who admired Xu Fu.

Lord Longyang, standing outside the palace gate, was confusedly brought into the Qin royal palace. He thought he was going to see Xu Fu, but he saw these people leading him straight to a great hall. An attendant said to him coldly, "When you see the King later, do not lose your manners."

Lord Longyang was shocked, his emotions churning and complex, his mind filled with all sorts of guesses.

It was rare for Lord Longyang to be so bewildered and surprised.

He wanted to see Mr. Xu, but these people brought him to see the King of Qin? Could it be that the envoy was not from the Fengchang Temple, but was... was... the King of Qin? This guess was truly terrifying. The King of Qin wouldn't dare to go as an envoy to the State of Wei, would he? Then, thinking of how the King of Wei had been blind enough to tease the man, Lord Longyang found it more and more terrifying. But then he kept overturning his own guess. The rumors about the King of Qin didn't sound like that at all...

While thinking, Lord Longyang had already walked into the hall.

"Greetings, Your Majesty." Lord Longyang bowed from a distance.

Ying Zheng’s scorching gaze swept over him, examining him from head to toe.

...The person was too sturdy, the chest was too small; he only had a face.

But Xu Fu himself had a good face!

Ying Zheng felt relieved. Xu Fu would not take a fancy to him.

Lord Longyang felt a sense of strangeness and couldn't help but look up, only to see a completely unfamiliar face.

He had guessed wrong after all!

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s temperaments were completely different. Now that Lord Longyang saw Ying Zheng, he had to admit that only this man matched the image of the King of Qin in the rumors.

Ying Zheng looked down at him from on high, his gaze cold yet sharp. Even Lord Longyang couldn't help but shrink back, instinctively avoiding Ying Zheng’s gaze. "Your Majesty, I am but a commoner. I did not intend to see Your Majesty; I was only looking for a gentleman surnamed Xu and accidentally walked outside the royal palace." Lord Longyang felt quite wronged; he had just taken a wrong turn and was confusedly caught by the guards.

This was a forced audience with the King of Qin!

Just as Ying Zheng was about to speak, footsteps suddenly came from outside the hall.

"...Wait a moment, I forgot one thing."

"What did Official Xu forget? I will send someone to fetch it for you."

"...Never mind, I will handle it myself tomorrow."

With that, the two walked in. Lord Longyang turned around and froze. "Sir?" Lord Longyang quickly adjusted his expression and said, "So you really were here, sir."

At this moment, Ying Zheng also noticed something slightly off. For instance, it was one thing for this woman to have a sturdy build, but why was her voice so deep?

When Xu Fu saw Lord Longyang, he was also slightly stunned. He looked at Ying Zheng and said, "Please dismiss the attendants, Your Majesty; I will introduce this person to you."

Ying Zheng, being a clever man, immediately dispelled his doubts and vaguely guessed the person’s identity.

After the palace attendants had all withdrawn, Lord Longyang said helplessly, "You walked so fast, sir, you didn't even take the tripod."

"Thank you." Xu Fu took the tripod from his hands. Lord Longyang didn't need Xu Fu to introduce him anymore and immediately knelt before Ying Zheng. "Longyang greets Your Majesty." This time, he didn't deliberately pitch his voice, so it sounded much clearer.

"So it is Lord Longyang." Ying Zheng revealed a faint smile. "Why is Lord Longyang dressed in this manner?"

Lord Longyang did not hide anything and said frankly, "Since I have come to the State of Qin, I naturally have to change my appearance."

And so he just went straight from being a man to a woman?

Both Xu Fu and Ying Zheng were speechless.

However, seeing his natural demeanor, they felt a bit of admiration. Anyone who could put gender and appearance aside must be a person of broad mind and great forbearance.

"What are Lord Longyang’s plans for the future?"

Xu Fu was uncovering the cloth and touching the tripod on the side. Ying Zheng’s gaze involuntarily swept over him, and his tone became a bit more casual.

"Naturally, I will stay in Qin from now on."

Ying Zheng was a bit surprised. "Not returning to Wei?"

"Not returning."

Ying Zheng’s mood improved significantly. The State of Wei was currently dominated by the factions of Lord Longyang and Lord Xinling. If they lost Lord Longyang, the King of Wei would not just be losing a male favorite; once Lord Xinling and the King of Wei had a falling out, the State of Wei would collapse from within.

"The tripod has been delivered, and Longyang has had the honor of seeing the King of Qin, so I shall take my leave." With that, Lord Longyang straightened up. Ying Zheng did not intend to keep him and immediately ordered someone to escort him out.

Xu Fu covered the tripod with the cloth again.

"You returned late today? Was it because you went to find the tripod?"

Xu Fu nodded. "I went there, and then I forgot to take it with me."

"Lord Longyang’s character and methods are not simple. If you associate with him in the future, you need to be cautious." Previously, when Ying Zheng heard Bo Zhou’s report, he had felt a bit jealous that Xu Fu had brought Lord Longyang back to Qin. However, now that he had seen Lord Longyang, Ying Zheng didn't think so anymore. Looking at Lord Longyang, he could tell that there was only a common friendship between him and Xu Fu, and their gazes were very open. Since that was the case, it was beneficial for Xu Fu to be on good terms with Lord Longyang.

Although from his heart, Ying Zheng hoped that Xu Fu would rely only on him, from a rational perspective, Xu Fu should make many talented friends.

"Mm."

Ying Zheng glanced at the tripod in his arms. "Have you used up all the medicinal herbs I found for you? I heard that alchemy requires cooking gold and stones, so I ordered people to find some..."

Xu Fu shuddered instantly.

Gold and stones?

Is it because you think you won't die, so you want to add some gold and stones?

Anyone with a little knowledge knew that many emperors in history who sought immortality consumed too many gold and stones, which eventually led to their health deteriorating and even their early deaths.

Xu Fu wasn't stupid; of course, he wouldn't use this stuff. He immediately refused sternly. "Gold and stones are harmful to the body; they cannot be added."

Ying Zheng was a bit surprised to hear this. "Ancient records say so. So, people in the past were all wrong?" He didn't doubt what Xu Fu said; he probably believed Xu Fu’s words by instinct.

Xu Fu nodded. "In the future, Your Majesty must not believe such claims. Any elixir made by cooking gold and stones must never be consumed!" Xu Fu didn't remember exactly how Qin Shi Huang died in history, only vaguely remembering that when he was old, he seemed to have sought immortality, and he didn't know if he had died from eating elixirs. Anyway, this stuff was definitely harmful.

A gentle expression appeared on Ying Zheng’s face, and his voice was low. "Naturally, I will only consume the elixirs you refine."

No, I’m also worried that my dark cuisine will kill you...

Xu Fu swallowed the words that had reached his throat; saying them now felt like it would ruin the mood.

Ying Zheng still had some government affairs to handle, so Xu Fu sat with him in the hall. Ying Zheng was always worried that he might be hungry, so he ordered people to bring some food for Xu Fu in advance. Xu Fu flipped through bamboo slips, reading ancient anecdotes while eating; it was quite comfortable!

A few days later, Meng Tian took the initiative to come to Ying Zheng again. "Your Majesty, I have kept Mr. Wei Liao."

Ying Zheng: "..." He didn't want to keep Wei Liao anymore.

Meng Tian didn't know what Ying Zheng was thinking and said earnestly, "Mr. Wei Liao has stated that he will not leave Qin, and I expect he will come to see Your Majesty in a couple of days."

Ying Zheng: "..."

"Your Majesty?" "Your Majesty? Have you been working too hard these past few days?" Meng Tian frowned and asked with concern.

"It’s nothing. That’s what Wei Liao said to you?"

"Exactly!" Meng Tian said solemnly. "I had long talks with Mr. Wei Liao for several nights, and he became determined to stay in Qin. A talent like Mr. Wei Liao, if he can contribute to Your Majesty’s hegemony, then his trip to Qin will not have been in vain."

"He’s not returning to Wei?"

"No."

Ying Zheng didn't know why Wei Liao had suddenly changed his mind, or if he was plotting something, but regardless, as long as Wei Liao stayed in Qin, he was under his control. It was just that Ying Zheng suddenly felt a bit of sympathy for the King of Wei. Wei Liao had changed his mind so easily and abandoned the State of Wei; if the King of Wei knew he had missed out on such a person, he would surely be heartbroken.

On the other side, Xu Fu also soon learned the news of Wei Liao’s return to Xianyang Palace, and this time, Wei Liao had entered the palace very high-profile. By the time Xu Fu returned to the palace, he heard that Wei Liao had been appointed as the National Lieutenant.

Is this a case of "speak of the devil"?

Xu Fu had previously thought about finding Wei Liao and at least squeezing out all his value.

Seeing Xu Fu’s darkened expression, Ying Zheng couldn't help but explain, "This person does have some ability. Since he is willing to stay in Qin, I will let him show his value."

Xu Fu nodded. "That’s what I thought too." Xu Fu looked back at Ying Zheng. "Does Your Majesty think I am angry about this?" Xu Fu shook his head. "I am not angry. Why should I dwell on that bit of unpleasantness? Wouldn't that just make me unhappy?"

Xu Fu still didn't tell Ying Zheng what Wei Liao had said.

Even he felt furious hearing such words; if he told Qin Shi Huang, wouldn't it make him even more unhappy? Why poke at Qin Shi Huang’s heart with such words?

Xu Fu didn't notice that he had now habitually protected Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng suddenly said again, "Tomorrow, Wei Liao will come to the palace to offer his advice to me. You will accompany me then."

"Alright." Xu Fu also wanted to see what Wei Liao could say. If Wei Liao was just using an excuse to enter the palace and actually said nothing good, he would definitely not give him any face and would slap him in the face!

·

That day, Xu Fu did not go to the Fengchang Temple. After waking up, washing, and changing his robes, he ate and then sat alone reading bamboo slips. Estimating that it wouldn't be too early when Wei Liao entered the palace, he just read his books.

But Xu Fu hadn't been reading for long when he saw Fusu enter.

Fusu bowed to him and then politely knelt down opposite him.

"Thank you, Teacher." Fusu said this as soon as he opened his mouth.

Xu Fu knew he was referring to the Consort Zheng matter, and not wanting to talk about it, he brushed it off. "It’s nothing. Finished your studies for the day?"

Fusu nodded and suddenly asked, "Did you take Huhai with you a few days ago, Teacher?"

"Yes, why?"

"I couldn't find Huhai in the side hall that day." Fusu paused and suddenly said, "Can I sleep on the same couch as you, Teacher?" Fusu looked at Xu Fu with anticipation, while also projecting the look of "Huhai can, so I want to sleep with you too."

"You’re not that young anymore..." Xu Fu advised him tactfully.

Fusu shook his head, acting childish for the first time. "I am young; I’m not even ten yet."

Xu Fu examined his expression carefully. Perhaps because his mother had left, he felt lost? After thinking about it, Xu Fu agreed, but he made a deal with Fusu in the end: "Hold Huhai well at night; you have to take care of your younger brother."

"Alright." Fusu nodded hurriedly.

Xu Fu thought uncharitably: Ah, now I don't have to worry about Huhai peeing on me.

Fusu’s studies were indeed very tight, and he had to leave quickly after not talking for long. Thinking about it, if this were his previous life, at this age, he should be out playing, let alone learning such profound things; even learning basic addition and subtraction would be good enough.

It really is different fates for different people. Although Fusu had a good background, with a father who would become the Emperor through the ages, and he himself would become the crown prince, he had also lost many things that his peers could have.

After seeing Fusu off, it wasn't long before an attendant came to invite Xu Fu.

"His Majesty is already waiting for Official Xu in the hall." The attendant smiled and led Xu Fu out.

By now, Xu Fu was clearly labeled with the word "privilege." With the Hu woman, Consort Zheng, and Empress Dowager Zhao gone, the palace staff all respected Xu Fu. Although they were blind in the past, they weren't blind in their hearts; the relationship between this Official Xu and the King was something everyone tacitly understood.

Xu Fu was already used to such treatment and walked into the hall with a calm face. He sat to one side, and someone brought him small snacks and water.

Before Xu Fu could start eating, people entered.

Besides Wei Liao, there were also Meng Tian and Li Si.

Wei Liao only gave them a faint glance before looking at Ying Zheng on the throne, and then his gaze fell on Xu Fu. He looked for a bit longer, which made Ying Zheng frown.

After everyone exchanged greetings, Ying Zheng granted them seats.

Li Si sat opposite Xu Fu and smiled at him. Meng Tian, perhaps because the effect of Xu Fu’s face was too strong, didn't dare to look at him and sat stiffly in his seat with a straight face. Only Wei Liao looked at Xu Fu with a very complex gaze, with no smile on his face, and was slow to move his eyes away.

Ying Zheng’s face darkened, and he asked, "Mr. Wei Liao, what do you have to say to me? Let’s begin now."

In the past, Ying Zheng would have said, "Please enlighten me, sir."

Now...
