韩国的这位客人，在路上行了近一个月，才到了秦国，之后又是拖拖拉拉一段时日，方才进了咸阳城中。
此时天气已经入冬了。
徐福裹着厚厚的袍子，出入奉常寺，他倒是突然间想起尉缭了。
尉缭远在他国，应当……不会过得太过艰难吧。
想一想总归是原身的师兄，瞧上去对自己也没有什么恶意。徐福想起他来，心情便复杂了几分。
苏邑邀徐福过府与李斯，三人一同吃些小菜，聊些闲话。
还不等徐福答应呢，那李斯便在奉常寺外微微一笑，将苏邑拉走了。
苏邑皱眉，面带怒色，“你为何拽我？难不成如今目的达成，你便怠慢于徐典事了吗？”
李斯叹道：“你将我想成什么人了？今日大雪，徐典事定然是要急着赶回咸阳宫中的，你将人请过府去，晚一些，恐怕就是宫中来人亲至你府上请人了。”少请徐典事一顿饭事小，得罪了王上事大！
如今徐福日日宿于宫中，那李斯又不是眼拙愚蠢之人，自然看了出来徐福与嬴政之间的不对劲之处。苏邑虽然比他更早知晓，但若说起聪明行事，就远不如李斯了。
苏邑听罢，心中叹了口气。
被王上禁锢在身边的徐典事啊……何时才能获得真正的自由啊……
操碎了心的苏邑这才同李斯回了府。
全程一句话也没能插得进去嘴的徐福看着他们远去，无奈转身上马车，他正要放下车帘，却见奉常寺中突然奔出一人影来，那人渐渐近了，徐福这才看清是王柳。
王柳气喘吁吁地在马车前停下。
小内侍警惕地打量他了一眼。
徐福也有些疑惑。
却见王柳展开衣袖，露出掌心一只小手炉。
王柳将那手炉递到徐福脚边搁下，道：“今日大雪，徐典事勿要受凉。”说罢，他便转身快步离去了。
徐福顿了顿，突然想起去年时，他与王柳打赌，王柳输了，不得不与他做仆人，端茶倒水，还要给他烧好火盆子。
王柳的身影被风雪阻隔，渐渐在徐福的视线中变得模糊了。
徐福放下车帘，微微挑眉。
还真的……转性了？
如今想来，似乎还有那么两分感慨。
徐福抓起那手炉放在掌心，在马车中摇摇晃晃，不多时便入了咸阳宫中。
天寒，近来事务多，不过殿中冰寒浸骨，嬴政便将处理政务的地点改在了寝宫之中。寝宫中燃着火盆，并未燃熏香，但嗅起来，却觉得清爽许多，至少不会沉闷。
徐福由宫人拥着走进寝宫中来。
恍惚间，徐福觉得自己这派头挺像那什么……
挺像那宫斗剧里边儿的皇后娘娘。
想到这里，徐福自己又忍不住恶寒了一阵。
嬴政放下手中笔刀，命人准备饭食，随后便起身迎向了徐福，只是他目光略一扫，便扫到了徐福掌心中的手炉。那手炉瞧上去还挺精巧，但是一看便知不是宫中的物事。
嬴政笑问：“奉常寺中也有手炉了？”
小内侍嘴快，道：“是旁人给徐典事的。”
嬴政虽然不悦那小内侍插话，冷冷地瞥了他一眼，但实际上对他看眼色打小报告的行为十分满意。
那小内侍也傻傻地笑笑，便退到一边去了。
“谁人给你的？”
徐福觉得这口气似乎有点儿酸？他倒也没多想，当即便道：“就是去年同我打赌，输了便给我做仆人那个王柳王太卜。”
“是他啊。”嬴政当即便笑了。心中彻底放心。
就那王太卜，论英俊不及寡人，论美貌不及徐福自身，又兼之曾与徐福有过节，徐福又怎么可能会看得上眼呢？
徐福将手炉放到一边去。
嬴政便命人将手炉收走了。
虽然对那王太卜瞧不上眼，但嬴政也不喜欢旁人献殷勤献到徐福跟前去了。徐福用什么，穿什么，吃什么，自然是同寡人一道的。
嬴政的霸道与日俱深，只是并未显露得太过明显，而徐福对寻常事又不怎么上心，于是二人都没能发现。
用过饭食之后，徐福突然想起一件事来，“胡亥是不是周岁了？”
嬴政点头。
这二人带孩子都没有经验，平日里嬴政忙来忙去，哪里会记得胡亥的生辰？徐福连自己生辰都不知道，也更不会关注这些。
“那如何办？”徐福问完，又自己补了一句，“便在宫中摆一家宴？”
“好。”
“韩国派的官员入咸阳了，阿福可知？”嬴政突然提起了这话茬。
“知道，咸阳城中已经传遍了。”
“阿福之前所说的吉兆，难道是他？”
“我也不确定，不过王上与我想到一块儿去了。”徐福顿了顿，放下筷子，吃得有些饱了，“明日便知了。”
明日便是那人亲至朝中，拜见嬴政的日子。
嬴政点了点头，很快便将那人抛在了脑后。
一个还不知深浅的人，哪里比得上他跟前的徐福来得重要呢？
而这头徐福却压根没注意到嬴政的目光，他脑子里净想着胡亥去了。如今胡亥瞧上去也不像是以后的那个败家孩子秦二世，现在模样乖巧伶俐的，徐福当然也就拿他当普通孩子看待了。
可徐福也不知道普通孩子是如何过生辰的啊。
这个话题也暂时被搁置了。
二人用饭，洗漱，一同上床榻。徐福不知不觉就习惯了这样的生活，偏生他自己还没意识到。
一夜过去，第二日嬴政穿上黑色冕服，头戴旒冠，腰间悬挂配件，气势不怒自威，徐福穿着一身宽松的袍子站在不远处，与嬴政的模样形成了鲜明的对比。
一个过分刚强，一个过分漫不经心。
嬴政走到徐福跟前去，见徐福懒得起床如此早，还有几分睡眼朦胧的模样，忍不住道：“阿福不给寡人几分祝福吗？”
徐福知道他什么意思，“哦”了一声，然后抬手掀起他额前垂下的旒珠，敷衍地亲了一口嬴政，然后就转身留给了嬴政的一个背影。
嬴政也不生气，反倒觉得那轻描淡写的一吻，也足以令他心神愉悦起来。
嬴政大步跨出宫殿，身后跟着一行宫人。
不久之后，那韩国的来使便站在了秦国的大殿之上。
那人步入中年，长了副老实面孔。
其余人多少心中有些不屑。
若不是在韩国多受排挤，又怎会被送到秦国来？那韩王口言送一良才前来辅助秦王，哪能就真的是良才？不是废材，那都是韩王脑子被驴踢了。
那人遥遥一拜，冲着嬴政的方向道：“小人郑国，曾为韩国负责水利事务的水工！如今小人到了秦王跟前，此后便听秦王差遣了。”
水工？
秦国满朝官员都心生嘲讽。
原来只是个水工……
也难怪了，被送到秦国来。
嬴政微微抬头，目光从旒珠的缝隙间穿过，投在了郑国的脸上。
嬴政的目光有如何威慑的力量？旁人都难以与他对视。
那郑国也有些紧张，身子甚至都往里缩了缩，还隐隐有些发抖，看上去像是畏惧嬴政的威严，但就在嬴政兴趣缺缺时，那郑国突然直起了身板，上前一步，高声道：“郑国虽为水工，但却也心怀大志！”
“哦，说来与寡人听听。”嬴政淡淡道。若是随便说句雄心壮志的话，便能打动秦王，那也太可笑了。
那郑国咽了咽口水，不卑不亢道：“郑国前来，是为助秦王兴修水利……水利之益，将会成为利国利民的一件大事……”初时郑国还有些结巴，不过到了后面，或许是谈到了自己所擅长的东西，郑国便越发口舌伶俐了。
而此时徐福也到了奉常寺中，他坐在桌案前，旁边有人送了水和火盆来。
徐福伸手沾了沾水，在桌案上涂抹一番。
他闲来无事便又回忆了一番，那日观到的天象。
可惜没望远镜，他要看得更清楚一些是不行了，只隐隐能瞧见，那二十八宿之中……似乎是……
徐福绞尽脑汁地回忆。
似乎是井木犴当值？
chapters.title: 第86章
chapters.translated_text:
The autumn wind was biting. Wei Liao stood straight as a ramrod in his thin robes at the entrance of the Fengchang Temple. He assumed Xu Fu was secretly annoyed with him, which was why he had been left standing outside for so long on purpose.

In reality, Xu Fu had been speaking with Wang Liu, helping him resolve a few issues, which had delayed his departure from work.

When he and Wang Liu walked out of the Fengchang Temple together, Wang Liu ran into Su Yi and was called away. Xu Fu was left alone to walk out. After only a few steps, he caught sight of Wei Liao, whose complexion was slightly pale.

"Why is the State Lieutenant here?" Xu Fu walked up slowly. At first, seeing Wei Liao’s thin robes, he felt a bit of schadenfreude, but then, remembering that the man might be his senior fellow apprentice, his mood instantly dissipated, leaving him in a conflicted state where he didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

As soon as Wei Liao saw him, his tense expression immediately softened.

"I have something to tell you." With that, Wei Liao turned to lead Xu Fu elsewhere.

But Xu Fu stopped in his tracks, unmoving. "If the State Lieutenant has something to say, just say it here."

Wei Liao frowned, knowing that the things he had said to Xu Fu that day had made him wary. He felt deep hatred in his heart—hatred for the King of Qin, who was so good at bewitching people that once Xu Fu fell for him, he could never escape. He truly didn't know what was so good about the King of Qin. Wei Liao forgot that when he first arrived in Qin, he too had been captivated by Ying Zheng; if he hadn't later seen Ying Zheng's physiognomy, his attitude wouldn't have changed so abruptly.

"If it weren't for you, I certainly wouldn't have stayed in Qin," Wei Liao said in a deep voice. After saying this, perhaps feeling his tone was too harsh, he abruptly changed the subject: "I am always uneasy leaving you alone in Qin. I want you to come with me, but you refuse. If you suffer in the future... then leave Qin and come find me. I have already accepted the King of Qin's command; there is no possibility of going back on it now. Although I look down on the King of Qin's character, but..." Wei Liao paused, gritting his teeth with great reluctance, "but with so many people assisting him, that King of Qin will likely succeed in unifying the six states. If by then you no longer wish to stay in Qin, I will take you back."

This speech of Wei Liao's sounded decent, at least not as biased as it had sounded before.

Xu Fu was actually quite surprised that he could say such things.

This didn't seem like Wei Liao's usual style...

Xu Fu put aside his surprise and couldn't help but become even more curious about what kind of relationship he and this man actually had.

"You said I lost my memory..." This was the first time Xu Fu had taken the initiative to bring this up in front of Wei Liao.

Seeing that Xu Fu was not as resistant, Wei Liao immediately replied, "That is correct." Wei Liao paused and sighed: "Your memory was not very good when you were young. The Master said you were gifted and intelligent, yet you could never remember things. You would memorize a book one day and forget it entirely the next. That was one thing, but when you were seven, you left Guigu and forgot how to go home. When Jiang You and I found you, you were sitting on a ridge, covered in mud, having mistaken a farm woman for your mother. When you were ten, you woke up one morning and didn't recognize anyone, calling the Master 'Grandfather' and calling Jiang You and me 'Uncle.' When you were twelve, you told someone's fortune and forgot everything afterward; when we found you, you were covered in wounds, and no one knew what you had said to the person you read for. When you were thirteen..."

"Wait..." The more Xu Fu heard, the more ashamed he felt.

Did these things really happen to the original owner? This forgetfulness was beyond ordinary.

To prevent Wei Liao from counting through all his dark history, Xu Fu hurriedly cut him off.

"...So you really are my senior fellow apprentice?" Xu Fu asked.

"Naturally." Wei Liao seemed accustomed to Xu Fu asking him this, his expression very calm.

Xu Fu felt a bit dazed, and it took a long time for a sense of indignation to well up in his heart.

Guigu!

I really am a disciple of Guigu!

If I had known I was a "second-generation official" with a background, why would I have worked so hard? When people like Wang Liu came to question me, I should have just boldly thrown my background in their faces to crush them!

But it's too late for everything now...

I'm already a Dian-shi! Even Prefect Liu doesn't give me trouble anymore!

Seeing Xu Fu's strange expression, Wei Liao hurriedly said, "You don't need to be so sad. I know you have a proud temper and are determined to carve out a world for yourself. Although I don't like the King of Qin's character, you are in Qin... and you truly have great potential. You just had a poor memory in the past, and the Master was unwilling to let you leave Guigu easily, which is why you aren't as famous as your senior brothers... but in the long run, you will surely be famous throughout the six states..."

"What did I study when I was in Guigu?"

Wei Liao stopped his speech and replied, "You originally studied with Jiang You and me. Physiognomy, military strategy, political maneuvering, medicine... among the many subjects, you only favored physiognomy, astronomy, and medicine. And because your memory was poor, you could never remember the chants. The Master didn't want you to study them at first, never expecting that you would actually master them later. You were very rebellious; after you finished your studies, you said you wanted to go out and explore, and you secretly left Guigu..."

Xu Fu felt conflicted.

Setting aside the subjective adjectives Wei Liao added, such as "rebellious" and "only favored"...

Xu Fu felt that his description was actually quite like himself.

If it were him, he would probably have done the same thing.

It really is... well, an indescribable fate.

Xu Fu even had a strange thought.

Perhaps this was his past life?

Wei Liao wanted to say something more, but was interrupted by the sound of rapid hoofbeats.

Xu Fu looked over and saw Meng Tian riding a large horse toward them, his brows tightly locked.

He pulled the horse to a stop and jumped down. As soon as he saw Wei Liao, he said, "I searched everywhere for the State Lieutenant, so you were here!" Meng Tian's gaze swept from Wei Liao to Xu Fu. After seeing who was standing next to Wei Liao, Meng Tian became quite awkward, unconsciously taking a step back and saying, "...So it is Official Xu."

"General Meng is here looking for the State Lieutenant?" Xu Fu was curious, unable to figure out how these two had come together.

Wei Liao's expression immediately looked as if he had eaten dog feces. If Xu Fu hadn't been standing right there, he would have jumped three zhang away.

"Exactly! I have matters to discuss with the State Lieutenant," Meng Tian said openly.

Wei Liao kept a cold face and said, "I have nothing to say to General Meng."

"I have matters," Meng Tian emphasized, glancing at Wei Liao with a look that said, "Why can't you understand what I'm saying?"

Xu Fu felt the atmosphere between the two was strange. He looked from one to the other and said, "Since General Meng and the State Lieutenant have matters to discuss, I shall take my leave." Xu Fu turned his head and saw that the little attendant had already arrived, staring at Wei Liao and Meng Tian as if they were hiding a terrorist among them.

"Xu Fu..." Wei Liao called out, but could only watch helplessly as Xu Fu walked away heartlessly.

Wei Liao's expression instantly fell, and he looked coldly at Meng Tian. "What else does General Meng want?"

Meng Tian was no longer as simple-minded as he appeared, smiling: "There are always things to advise the State Lieutenant on, to prevent the King of Qin's great cause from going awry."

Wei Liao cursed under his breath and walked away leading his horse alongside Meng Tian.

Meanwhile, Xu Fu had also boarded his carriage, his heart still slightly unsettled.

There was a Xu Fu in Guigu, his original self, who happened to be so compatible with him, and apart from that strange amnesia, his personality was also very similar. Could it really be that there is an arrangement in the dark?

Xu Fu raised an eyebrow slightly, leaning back in the carriage.

This arrangement in the dark is actually quite good. Who else could be arranged to be by the side of the First Emperor of Qin?

Upon returning to the Xianyang Palace, Xu Fu curiously asked about Wei Liao, "How did General Meng manage to keep him?"

Ying Zheng shook his head: "I do not know either. Meng Tian said he intercepted Wei Liao outside an inn."

Xu Fu's mind immediately conjured up Meng Tian's figure.

Although Wei Liao was older, he wasn't that tall...

Xu Fu always felt he had accidentally glimpsed something. He gathered his thoughts and ordered the palace attendants to bring Fusu and Huhai. Soon, Huhai was brought, but Fusu followed behind him.

Fusu asked with a smile: "Teacher, has your cold recovered?"

Xu Fu didn't know the situation, so he replied: "Thank you for your concern, Prince Fusu, my cold has recovered."

"That is truly wonderful." The smile on Fusu's face grew brighter.

Knowing what Fusu was up to, Ying Zheng glanced at him but didn't say anything more.

Xu Fu now wanted to treat Huhai like his own son, so he naturally couldn't appear too biased against Fusu. Father and son sharing a bed to improve their relationship wasn't bad either.

Usually, Fusu followed his teacher to read books on cultivating character and thinking skills, but in the King of Qin's bedchamber, he instead openly read Xu Fu's miscellaneous books in front of Ying Zheng.

Witchcraft, incantations, physiognomy, medicine, alchemy... However, Fusu had no talent in this area. After reading for a while, he would pull Xu Fu to ask questions, and even after Xu Fu explained, Fusu would still have trouble understanding. For the gifted Fusu, this was a clear indication that he wasn't suited to learn this.

After observing this, Xu Fu felt somewhat disappointed.

But then, there was still Huhai.

Fusu wasn't supposed to learn these things anyway. As for why Fusu wanted to take him as a teacher, he hadn't figured it out yet. Perhaps it was just a child being naive, seeing that he looked impressive and choosing him. When Ying Zheng agreed at the time, he probably just did it to give him a title and make him happy.

Xu Fu put away the bamboo slips and patted Fusu's head. "Sleep."

Xu Fu, who had retracted his hand after the pat, didn't notice that this action didn't really conform to the rules.

But since he dared to "ride" the King of Qin, what was the big deal about patting his son's head?

Fusu sighed helplessly, pulled up the quilt, and lay down beside Xu Fu. Between Fusu and Xu Fu was Huhai.

How could the wise Ying Zheng let Fusu and Huhai block him and Xu Fu? Naturally, they were relegated to the other side of the bed, letting the brothers "love each other."

Xu Fu also pulled up the quilt and was about to sleep, but he suddenly remembered something.

"My King." He opened his eyes. In the dark night, only the candlelight reflected in his eyes, shining brightly.

"Hmm?" Ying Zheng also opened his eyes, turned to look at him, and waited patiently for Xu Fu to continue.

"Did you see the stars in the sky last night, my King?"

Ying Zheng thought to himself, I didn't look at the stars, I only looked at you. But he asked cooperatively: "Was there any strange phenomenon in the stars?"

"A comet slid across the sky." Xu Fu paused and added: "Do you remember at the end of last year, when I told you that disaster for the state meant disaster for the people, and then winter came with a great cold, and many people really froze to death? That was when a comet fell on Qin. After observing the celestial phenomena, I concluded it was an ominous sign."

Ying Zheng frowned and immediately asked: "Then is there some disaster this time?"

If that were the case, he would have to prepare early. And this time, it would definitely not be like before.

Ying Zheng braced himself, but saw Xu Fu shake his head and say lightly: "Not so. Comets have been recorded; a star appearing in the Big Dipper is a comet. While both are comets, there is a distinction between disaster and fortune. This comet came from the west and fell in the north, passing over Xianyang City."

"What does that mean?"

"In ancient times, there was a saying that whenever a great person is born, a star palace will light up in the sky, like the Big Dipper. A person's destiny moves with the star palace. This comet passing by allowed me to see the changes in the twenty-eight mansions; the twenty-eight mansions moved with the comet, and the sky was filled with rosy clouds. It should be a sign that a powerful person is coming to Qin." Xu Fu paused, then said: "But this comet headed toward the cities of Yuan and Puyang in Wei. The good omen brought by the comet belongs to us, while the final ominous sign of the comet belongs to Wei."

A flash of gloom passed through Ying Zheng's eyes, and he smiled: "Then Wei deserves an ominous sign."

The corners of Xu Fu's mouth curled up involuntarily. "Yes." He found the King of Wei extremely unpleasant; he was happy to see him get an ominous sign. As for Qin's good omen, he wondered what kind of powerful person it would bring to Qin.

Wei Liao and Li Si were already not simple people; who else could there be?

Xu Fu couldn't think of anyone, and he leaned against Ying Zheng's shoulder involuntarily. The warm and comfortable touch made him fall asleep before he could figure it out.

Seeing that Xu Fu had been talking eloquently just a moment ago, but now had his eyes closed and was asleep, Ying Zheng couldn't help but laugh. Watching Xu Fu's face, he drifted off to sleep as well.

Perhaps Xu Fu's face had the same effect as counting sheep.

·

While the Xianyang Palace was harmonious, Wei Liao had set off on his journey to other states, with only Meng Tian watching him go.

Riding alone on his horse, Wei Liao suddenly felt a pang of heartache.

I raised my junior fellow apprentice in vain...

I raised my junior fellow apprentice in vain!

He didn't even come to see me off!

He only follows that King of Qin! Can the King of Qin be better than me?

Wei Liao felt a lump of blood in his throat and rode off furiously toward another state. Since the indignation in his heart could not be vented, he would find a place to vent it.

Xu Fu did not know that he would be the culprit behind Wei Liao’s ruthless schemes against the powerful officials of various states in the future.

Meanwhile, in Wei, the King of Wei finally realized, under the guidance of others, that the King of Qin had sent an envoy to form an alliance with him, only to leave in a muddled state and even blame Wei for poor hospitality. What was the King of Qin's purpose?

He wanted to use me to scare Han!

The King of Wei had to be cautious.

The King of Qin had always been a warmongering madman. Apart from the incompetent ones, the rest were exceptionally brave. Who knew what dreams he was harboring to attack my Wei!

No, not to attack Wei.

The King of Wei still thought highly of himself. He believed the King of Qin wouldn't dare to touch Wei, but Han was another story...

Unable to figure it out, the King of Wei said to the attendant beside him: "Bring Lord Longyang to me..." Halfway through, the King of Wei stopped abruptly. Longyang, Longyang... where was Longyang now?!

Lord Longyang had disappeared without a trace, and his subordinates couldn't explain anything. Could he have been abducted by the Qin envoy?

The King of Wei became increasingly angry.

I don't know what kind of bad luck I've had; two beauties flew away, and now even Longyang is lost! I granted him a title, and this is how he treats me?

The King of Wei sneered and called the attendant: "Go and bring Lord Longyang's father..."

The attendant bowed and said: "My King, you are busy and must have forgotten; Lord Longyang's father passed away two months ago."

The King of Wei was stunned. "I... why did I not know at all! His father died, did Longyang not handle the funeral? He never mentioned this to me!"

The attendant added: "I heard that Lord Longyang said at the time that he came clean and would go clean, so he had the body cremated and buried in a grave."

"Is he crazy?" the King of Wei shouted in disbelief.

In ancient times, people respected the dead and their corpses.

The King of Wei knew how much Lord Longyang respected his parents...

But for Lord Longyang to do such a thing, where did his character and etiquette go? How did he learn to act like a barbarian?!

The King of Wei was filled with rage, sensing that Longyang had changed, but he didn't think deeply about it, only venting his anger and ordering people to continue searching for him.

Then the attendant, suppressing his fear, stepped forward and asked: "Otherwise... otherwise, please ask Lord Xinling..."

The King of Wei's face changed immediately, and he sneered: "Lord Xinling... Lord Xinling... what? My people only care about Lord Xinling? Since you are so loyal to Lord Xinling! Then go be a dog for Lord Xinling!" The King of Wei kicked him, and the attendant was quickly dragged away, his fate unknown.

Without the gentle and thoughtful Lord Longyang to relieve his worries and offer advice, and thinking of his half-brother Lord Xinling, whose influence in Wei was growing, the King of Wei felt increasingly restless. After his outburst, he called several beauties to the hall to amuse himself.

In the harem, now that Lord Longyang was gone, the beauties naturally dressed up and used all their skills to keep the King of Wei in their beds.

The King of Wei was arrogant and didn't take these signs of crisis to heart. While he was enjoying himself, the King of Han was trembling with fear, worried that Qin and Wei would conspire to crush Han, which was sandwiched between them.

Some ministers couldn't stand it and suggested that the King of Han also send an envoy to Wei to ask.

Qin had never been liked by the other six states; how could Wei so easily form an alliance with it?

The ministers had such clear heads, but the aging King of Han did not think so. At the end of his life, he had no ambition left, only wanting to guard Han well, at least not to be swallowed by the tiger and wolf that was Qin.

The more he thought about it, the more terrified he became, urgently wanting to find someone to discuss it with. But in Han, there was no one useful. The King of Han looked around, and his gaze fell on Han Fei.

Han Fei was a student of Xunzi and had long been famous, but in the Han royal family, he had no reputation, and some even laughed when he was mentioned as a prince of Han. This was because the King of Han had a son with extraordinary talent, but this son happened to be a stutterer.

The King of Han didn't even want to look at him, feeling that such a son was a disgrace to his face as the King of Han. But as a student of Xunzi, he should... have some ability...

So the King of Han ordered the attendant to call Han Fei and asked him how to resist if Qin had designs on Han.

Han Fei raised his head, suppressed his excitement, and spoke eloquently.

...

A few days later, Han sent a person to Qin.

·

When Xu Fu heard the news, he was slowly drinking his special tonic.

Fusu was kneeling before him, speaking.

Xu Fu almost spilled his soup. "...Why would Han send someone to Qin for no reason?"

They haven't even started fighting yet, have they?

Can Han not even take a little scare? They really are... spineless.

This is the type who gets slapped on the left cheek and offers the right!

Fusu smiled: "Perhaps they heard some rumors." Fusu spoke in an adult tone.

"What rumors could there be?" Qin hadn't even started mobilizing troops yet, and they were already panicking? It was a baseless rumor; the wind hadn't even started blowing yet. Xu Fu shook his head secretly, then looked at Fusu: "Prince Fusu, you knew?"

Fusu nodded: "Father did not hide it from me."

"Then what does Prince Fusu think of the King's decision?" Xu Fu asked.

Fusu smiled: "Father's decision is naturally good!"

"Really?"

"Really."

Although Xu Fu didn't know much history, he knew that in history, Ying Zheng didn't seem to get along well with this son—probably a warlike father and a benevolent son, two completely different opposites. If it weren't for that, Huhai wouldn't have been able to take advantage, right?

Could Fusu's personality change?

But thinking about it, Huhai could be his son now, even if only in name. But history had gone quite crooked here...

A flash of wisdom suddenly crossed Xu Fu's mind.

Could the person sent by Han be the so-called good omen left by the comet?

Who could this person be? Thinking about Qin history, who did he remember... Xu Fu pondered for a while. He couldn't remember anyone. Never mind, if the King of Han personally sent a capable person, then the King of Han could only blame his own bad luck, handing over a talent to Qin! It was simply adding bricks and tiles to his own path to destruction!

·

This guest from Han traveled for nearly a month before arriving in Qin, and then, after dragging his feet for a while, finally entered Xianyang City.

By this time, winter had arrived.

Wrapped in thick robes, Xu Fu went in and out of the Fengchang Temple, and he suddenly remembered Wei Liao.

Wei Liao was far away in another state; he should... not be having too hard a time, right?

Thinking about it, he was his senior fellow apprentice, and he didn't seem to have any malice toward him. Xu Fu felt a bit conflicted when he thought of him.

Su Yi invited Xu Fu to his residence to have some small dishes and chat with Li Si.

Before Xu Fu could agree, Li Si smiled outside the Fengchang Temple and pulled Su Yi away.

Su Yi frowned, his face showing anger: "Why are you pulling me? Could it be that now that your goal is achieved, you are neglecting Official Xu?"

Li Si sighed: "What do you take me for? It's snowing today; Official Xu will surely be in a hurry to get back to the Xianyang Palace. If you invite him to your residence, later on, the palace might send someone to your residence to invite him personally." Neglecting to invite Official Xu for a meal is a small matter, but offending the King is a big one!

Now that Xu Fu slept in the palace every day, Li Si was not a blind or foolish person; he naturally saw the unusual relationship between Xu Fu and Ying Zheng. Although Su Yi knew about it earlier than him, he was far less clever in acting than Li Si.

After hearing this, Su Yi sighed in his heart.

Official Xu, imprisoned by the King's side... when will he ever gain true freedom...

The worried Su Yi then returned to the residence with Li Si.

Xu Fu, who hadn't been able to get a word in, watched them leave and helplessly turned to board his carriage. Just as he was about to lower the curtain, he saw a figure dash out of the Fengchang Temple. As the person got closer, Xu Fu realized it was Wang Liu.

Wang Liu stopped in front of the carriage, panting.

The little attendant looked at him vigilantly.

Xu Fu was also a bit puzzled.

He saw Wang Liu open his sleeve, revealing a small hand warmer in his palm.

Wang Liu placed the hand warmer at Xu Fu's feet and said: "It's snowing today, Official Xu, don't catch a cold." With that, he turned and walked away quickly.

Xu Fu paused, suddenly remembering that last year, he had made a bet with Wang Liu. Wang Liu lost and had to be his servant, pouring tea and water, and burning the fire basin for him.

Wang Liu's figure was obscured by the wind and snow, gradually becoming blurred in Xu Fu's sight.

Xu Fu lowered the curtain and raised an eyebrow slightly.

He really... changed his nature?

Thinking about it now, he felt a bit of emotion.

Xu Fu grabbed the hand warmer and held it in his palm, swaying in the carriage, and before long, he arrived at the Xianyang Palace.

It was cold, and there had been much work lately, but the hall was bone-chilling, so Ying Zheng had moved his office to the bedchamber. The bedchamber had a fire basin burning, and no incense was lit, but it smelled quite fresh, at least not stuffy.

Xu Fu walked into the bedchamber, escorted by palace attendants.

In a daze, Xu Fu felt that his demeanor was quite like...

Quite like the Empress in those palace drama shows.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu couldn't help but feel a chill.

Ying Zheng put down his brush and knife, ordered food to be prepared, and then stood up to welcome Xu Fu. However, with a glance, he saw the hand warmer in Xu Fu's palm. The hand warmer looked quite exquisite, but it was obvious at a glance that it wasn't from the palace.

Ying Zheng asked with a smile: "Do they have hand warmers in the Fengchang Temple now?"

The little attendant was quick-mouthed: "Someone gave it to Official Xu."

Although Ying Zheng was displeased that the little attendant interrupted, he gave him a cold glance, but in reality, he was very satisfied with his behavior of reporting back.

The little attendant smiled foolishly and stepped aside.

"Who gave it to you?"

Xu Fu felt that the tone seemed a bit sour? He didn't think much of it and immediately said: "It was that Diviner Wang Liu, the one who lost a bet with me last year and had to be my servant."

"It's him." Ying Zheng smiled immediately. He was completely relieved in his heart.

As for that Diviner Wang, he wasn't as handsome as me, not as beautiful as Xu Fu himself, and he had a grudge with Xu Fu. How could Xu Fu possibly take a fancy to him?

Xu Fu put the hand warmer aside.

Ying Zheng ordered someone to take it away.

Although he didn't look down on that Diviner Wang, Ying Zheng didn't like others offering favors to Xu Fu. Whatever Xu Fu used, wore, or ate, it should naturally be the same as his.

Ying Zheng's possessiveness grew day by day, but it wasn't too obvious, and Xu Fu didn't pay much attention to ordinary things, so neither of them noticed.

After the meal, Xu Fu suddenly remembered something: "Is Huhai a year old?"

Ying Zheng nodded.

Neither of them had experience with children. Usually, Ying Zheng was busy, so how would he remember Huhai's birthday? Xu Fu didn't even know his own birthday, so he wouldn't pay attention to these things.

"Then what should we do?" Xu Fu asked, then added: "Should we hold a family banquet in the palace?"

"Good."

"The official sent by Han has entered Xianyang, does Ah Fu know?" Ying Zheng suddenly brought up this topic.

"I know, it has spread throughout Xianyang City."

"Could he be the good omen you mentioned before?"

"I'm not sure, but you and I thought of the same thing." Xu Fu paused, putting down his chopsticks, feeling quite full. "We'll know tomorrow."

Tomorrow was the day that person would personally appear at court to meet Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng nodded and quickly threw the person to the back of his mind.

Someone whose depth was still unknown, how could he be more important than Xu Fu by his side?

Xu Fu didn't notice Ying Zheng's gaze; his mind was full of Huhai. Huhai didn't look like the future spendthrift Second Emperor of Qin; he was cute and clever now, so Xu Fu naturally treated him like an ordinary child.

But Xu Fu didn't know how ordinary children celebrated their birthdays.

This topic was temporarily shelved.

The two ate, washed, and went to bed together. Xu Fu had gotten used to this life without realizing it, and he hadn't even noticed it himself.

Another night passed. The next day, Ying Zheng wore his black ceremonial robes, a crown with hanging beads on his head, and accessories hanging from his waist. His momentum was awe-inspiring without anger. Xu Fu stood not far away in loose robes, forming a sharp contrast with Ying Zheng.

One was overly strong, the other overly nonchalant.

Ying Zheng walked up to Xu Fu. Seeing that Xu Fu was too lazy to get up so early and still looked sleepy, he couldn't help but say: "Won't you give me some blessings, Ah Fu?"

Xu Fu knew what he meant. He said "Oh," then raised his hand to lift the beads hanging in front of his forehead, gave Ying Zheng a perfunctory kiss, and then turned away, leaving Ying Zheng with his back.

Ying Zheng wasn't angry; instead, he felt that the light kiss was enough to make him happy.

Ying Zheng strode out of the palace, followed by a line of attendants.

Not long after, the envoy from Han stood in the great hall of Qin.

The man was middle-aged and had an honest face.

The others felt a bit of disdain in their hearts.

If he wasn't squeezed out in Han, why would he be sent to Qin? The King of Han claimed to send a talent to assist the King of Qin, but how could it really be a talent? If he wasn't a waste, the King of Han must have been kicked in the head by a donkey.

The man bowed from afar and said toward Ying Zheng: "I am Zheng Guo, a water engineer who was responsible for water conservancy in Han! Now that I am before the King of Qin, I will listen to your commands from now on."

A water engineer?

The officials of Qin were all mocking.

So he was just a water engineer...

No wonder he was sent to Qin.

Ying Zheng raised his head slightly, his gaze passing through the gaps in the beads and landing on Zheng Guo's face.

What kind of deterrent power did Ying Zheng's gaze have? Others could hardly look him in the eye.

Zheng Guo was also a bit nervous, his body even shrinking inward, and he was trembling slightly, looking like he was afraid of Ying Zheng's majesty. But just as Ying Zheng was losing interest, Zheng Guo suddenly straightened his back, took a step forward, and said loudly: "Although Zheng Guo is a water engineer, I have great ambitions!"

"Oh, tell me about it." Ying Zheng said lightly. If a casual remark about ambition could move the King of Qin, that would be too ridiculous.

Zheng Guo swallowed and said neither humbly nor arrogantly: "I have come to help the King of Qin build water conservancy... The benefits of water conservancy will be a major event that benefits the country and the people..." At first, Zheng Guo stuttered a bit, but later, perhaps because he was talking about what he was good at, he became more eloquent.

At this time, Xu Fu had also arrived at the Fengchang Temple. He sat at the table, and someone brought water and a fire basin.

Xu Fu reached out to dip his finger in the water and drew on the table.

Having nothing to do, he recalled the celestial phenomena he had observed that day.

Unfortunately, without a telescope, he couldn't see it more clearly. He could only faintly see that among the twenty-eight mansions... it seemed to be...

Xu Fu racked his brains to remember.

It seemed to be Jing Mu Han on duty?
