他眼花了？
还是他背错了？
徐福眉头微皱，捻着手指顿在了那里，他突地一转身，差点将手旁的竹简扫到火盆里去。旁边伸来一只手将那竹简险险捞住。徐福思绪回笼，转头一看，就见王柳立在身侧。
徐福的目光从手旁的水和桌案旁的火盆扫过。
都是王柳送来的？
“多谢。”
王柳也不说话，转头就出去了，瞧上去还情绪不高的样子。
谁招惹他了吗？徐福一头雾水。不过随即他就将这点疑惑压下去了。
“井木犴，朱雀七宿之一……井宿值日，凶多吉少，所求不利，钱财耗散……”
徐福越往下道脸色越不好。
他这是把嬴政给坑了？
总不会凶兆归了秦国，那吉兆归了魏国吧？
徐福心头顿时一阵不快，就算秦国没有吉兆，那也不能归魏国。他倒要瞧一瞧，这个打韩国来的人，究竟是个什么人物！担得起二十八星宿变动，担得起彗星送霞光来！
徐福起身便要往外走，等走到一半他又顿住了。
如今朝还未散吧？
他回宫也见不着嬴政吧？
徐福又只有坐了下来。
眼瞎误事啊！徐福揉了揉眼眶。心中也不太确定，那天漫天星星，自己到底瞅清楚了什么。果然不擅长的东西，是不能装逼的。徐福翻了翻奉常寺中的关于星象记载的古籍，找到了关于彗星和二十八星宿的记载，但是可没有一个记载是关于这二者同时变动的。也就是说古时，可能没有这种异象，或者有异象，却没被记载下来。
徐福一会儿又想到了尉缭说的话，说他幼时想要学天文、看相、卜卦，但总是记不住口诀，那记忆力简直比金鱼都要不如。难道现在他也被影响着，记忆力退化了吗？不太可能吧……徐福拍了拍额头，应当只是那日自己眼花，没能看个真切。如今还不知那从韩国来的人究竟是谁，他何苦这样杞人忧天？
待到散值之后，徐福便早早回了咸阳宫，不一会儿，嬴政也大步走了进来。
嬴政笑道：“你所言无错，韩国派来的那郑国，的确有几分本事。”
嗯？
徐福顿了顿，难道真是他记错了？根本不是井木犴当值？
嬴政与徐福同坐下来，“郑国此人善水利之事，寡人本欲将他派往都江堰。”嬴政顿了顿，又道：“不过李冰也是极有本事的人，将他们二人放置在一起，不仅是浪费，恐还引起麻烦。”
有本事才能的人，或许嘴上不说，但心中都有几分傲气的。
两个有本事的人放在一起，反而会互相生出阻碍来。
“郑国向寡人进言，主张修水渠，以改变关中粮荒的境况。”嬴政皱了皱眉，“但这不是一朝一夕便能完成的事，寡人心中还有些迟疑。嘴上说得那般好，但寡人却不能贸然相信他。”
“郑国以前在韩国是做什么的？”徐福有些好奇。能被嬴政称赞，想来的确是有几分本事的。
“以前任水工，参与过荥泽水患的治理……”
虽然徐福并不知道荥泽是哪里，但他知晓能治水患的一般都是能人。他记忆中最深的就是秦始皇当政时，凿灵渠，修长城，成就了千古功业，不知道为后世带来了多少福利。
徐福不知关中在何处，灵渠建在哪里他也不知，难道那灵渠就是这个人修的？所以天象才会如此？不然的话，一个小小水工，如何称得上是厉害的人物？
“我不通此事，王上谨慎拿定便是。”徐福对这个是当真一窍不通，所以他也就不拿出自己的意见去干扰嬴政了，免得帮了倒忙。
嬴政“嗯”了一声，随即笑道：“若是真如郑国所说，那韩王便是亲手送了个宝贝到寡人跟前来。”
那韩国怕是后悔也来不及了。
“韩王胆小，送了郑国来秦，那王上可还攻打韩国？”
嬴政的面色冷了冷，“寡人欲攻魏。从前献公时，魏国强大，夺我秦国河西之地，将我大秦逼至关中，后又妄图率军直取关中，大秦几欲亡国。此一时彼一时，昔日秦国弱小，今日魏国国弱。当还的，魏国今日就应还回来了。”
嬴政暗暗补了一句，如今魏安釐王还当他魏国是曾经强大的魏国，不将寡人放在眼中，更意图染指寡人的心头好！若不是那龙阳君有几分本事，又与魏王不合，他就先拿龙阳君开刀了。他现在虽放过龙阳君，但那魏王却总是要承受他的怒火的。
“那韩国就此放过？”
嬴政见徐福面露不解，随后笑道：“韩国不打，却不能放过。郑国不算什么，阿福可知，韩王有一子，曾与李斯是同门，同出荀子门下，尚未出师时，寡人已听闻韩非之名，韩非之才，诸国皆有耳闻。李斯也曾向寡人提起，他有一师兄，集法家之大成，颇有才能，可惜身为韩王之子，却无处施展抱负。韩国无强将，也无能臣，唯一韩非，若是被寡人要来，那韩国不出几年便自行衰弱了。不消耗费寡人多少力气。”
“韩王之子？韩王会给？”
“到他国做质子并不是什么罕见的事，韩王不待见这个儿子，寡人要来，便保他一时平安，他如何会不给？”
徐福神色有些复杂，“……若是如此，那这韩王，也当真短视。”
嬴政笑了笑，不再提他。
“若是攻打魏国，那龙阳君……”他是会帮魏王还是不帮魏王呢？他虽随着自己到了秦国来，但那是秦国没有要对魏国动手的意味。龙阳君总归是魏国人……
“寡人会问他，是否愿为秦国出力。若是不愿，要么他便速速离开咸阳，要么，在打魏国之日，便是寡人杀他之时。”
龙阳君是惊才绝艳，但若是不仅不能成为秦国助力，反倒成为秦国大患，站在嬴政的角度，的确是宰了他更方便。
想到这里，徐福发现自己自从跟嬴政搅上以后，便什么都只想着对秦有利无利了。这算好事还是坏事？似乎有些违背他心中坚持客观的想法。
但是……忽然间就想打破一下那些规矩桎梏，任性一回……这是什么毛病？
徐福忽地有些心虚。
那日他道尉缭双标，今天他却好似也双标了。
……
嬴政说要问韩国讨要韩非，果真不出几日，他便令人传消息到韩国去了。
韩王担忧秦国攻打自己，便能马不停蹄地献出郑国，韩非又算得了什么？接到消息后的韩王，欣喜于韩国之危可解，当即便命人将韩非请到了宫中来。
韩非心中欣喜，只当韩王终于重视起自己，这才收拾一番入了宫。
他怎么也没能想到，为韩王献上计策的他，没过多久就被韩王转手卖给秦国了。
嬴政早就抓准了韩非的心思。
韩非一身才华，在韩国得不到施展，却始终不肯到他国去，就足见他对韩国的坚守。他忠于他的国家，为了韩国的安危，哪怕他认为韩王此举荒唐至极，他也会配合韩王，甘愿离韩赴秦。
韩非如何厌恶憎恨秦王，这些嬴政都不知晓，他和徐福也都不会去关心。
韩非启程离韩时，转眼秦国蜡祭又要到了。
徐福到奉常寺去的时候，便接受了周围无数目光的洗礼。
王柳来送火盆的时候，徐福便正好叫住了他，“今日是怎么了？奉常寺中的人倒像是从未见过我似的。”
王柳脸上露了点儿笑容出来，道：“蜡祭在即，想来主持之人，应当有徐典事的一份了。”
徐福却未放在心上，漫不经心道：“奉常寺中自有位太祝，宫中还有位老太卜，应当是轮不到我的。”
王柳心中呵呵一笑。徐典事如今什么地位，谁还瞧不清楚？奉常寺中人多的是同他想法一样的。时日久了，众人也知晓徐福常出入王宫了。蜡祭若是由徐福来主持，他们连半点惊奇都不觉得。
或许是徐典事带给人的“惊喜”实在太多了，如今就算他做出再惊骇的事来，也引不起半分惊涛了。
等到蜡祭开始准备，奉常寺中那位曾参加了秦王加冠礼的太祝，已经先言明，身体不适，恐届时身体还未痊愈，在蜡祭上出了差错。唯有宫中那位老太卜，一直未有声音传出。
按照往年惯例，若不是那位太祝主持，那便是宫中的老太卜。只是这两年老太卜年纪确实大了，这才不太露于人前。此次太祝称病，老太卜不言不语，有人笑道，这不是在为徐福让道吗？
蜡祭是秦国上下普天同庆的大事，秦国朝中自然便有好奇蜡祭主持人选的。一些世族家中也有人身在奉常寺，他们自然更看重此事。
而这日小朝，嬴政便不容反驳地宣布了徐福的名字。
蜡祭主持落在了他的头上。
这时朝中上下已经听过这个名字了，那个固执前往蜀地，后又随李斯出使他国的徐典事，徐福。
骤然听到王上口中再说出这个名字，众人都愣了愣，突地意识到此人身在奉常寺中，升迁也未免太快了些。现在如此年轻的一位太卜，便要接手蜡祭的事宜，他能担当得起吗？若论资历，奉常寺中不知有多少人比他更老的。
“王上，此事不可啊……”
“任命谁来主持蜡祭，寡人只是与你们说个名字，而不是让你们来替寡人做主。”大权在握的嬴政，如果连这点都搞不定，那还何谈出兵魏国？届时反对的人恐怕也不会少。迟早这些人都要习惯他说一不二的性子。
那昌平君才刚从蜀地回来不久，便又病倒在床榻上了，众人心中还有些发憷呢，此时听见嬴政口气威严，他们自然也不会为这样的事，与嬴政争议起来，平白得罪了王上。心中再不服气，那也得憋着啊。只是思及殿中另一位同徐福打过交道的人……
李斯立在殿中，只微微笑着，接受着那些人投到自己身上来的目光。
待到小朝散去后，李斯才刚走到殿外，便被人叫住了。
“李长史，敢问那徐福究竟是何来头？”
“李长史可曾知晓，那徐福常出入王宫之中，这莫非是……莫非是又一个魏国龙阳吧？”
这些人平日里可是不会如此八卦的，真正触动到他们那根神经的是，第二个龙阳君。
想一想如今龙阳君在魏国是个什么地位，他们就担忧这徐福会不会成为第二人。权力总是握在少数人的手中，这一任秦王对权力的把控之高，已经令世族大臣心中不满了。那样少的权力，若是再被他人瓜分，这样触及到自身利益的事，谁能容忍？
一个男宠，是没有谁愿意去理会的，但一个升迁过快，有着官职，又极为得宠的男宠那可就不一样了。
李斯知晓这些人心中所想，但李斯心中惦记着徐福引荐之恩，若无徐福，又哪来他李斯的今日？这些人想要从他口中套话，未免也想得太容易了些。
“徐典事啊……”李斯拉长语调，顿了顿，将面前几人好奇又紧张的表情收入眼中，然后笑道：“我只知徐典事师承极为厉害。”
说罢李斯便绕过几人往外大步走去了。
几人愣了愣。
这如何厉害？究竟师承于谁？你怎么不说个清楚啊……
且不说这些人是何等抓心挠肺。
此时在王宫中歇息着并未到奉常寺去的徐福，正翻动着手边的竹简，突地有内侍进门来，躬身道：“徐典事，宫中老太卜想要见您。”
徐福翻动竹简的动作顿了顿，老太卜？就是那位与尉缭都争执起来，颇受上两任秦王看重的老太卜？
从尉缭和嬴政处得到的信息综合起来，徐福的脑子里已经勾勒出了一个，古板、厉害、孤傲的老头子形象，他常年独居宫中，说不定还会有些孤僻的怪脾气。
他怎么会找到自己这里来？总不至于是为了蜡祭之事吧？
徐福脑补了许多可能性，然后一边推开竹简，直起身子往外走。
他理了理袖袍，跨到殿外去，由内侍引着他往那老太卜的住处走去。
宫中修建有一小塔，据说是方便老太卜登上观天象的，而老太卜也就住在那小塔之中。实在是待遇高得令徐福眼红。不过想一想，老太卜独居小塔，而他却是睡秦王的床，吃秦王的饭食，玩秦王的儿子……如此一想，还是他的待遇更高。咳。
徐福恢复了一脸正色。
这老太卜虽然并非国师，但他的位置也等同于国师了吧。说起来，这老太卜应当就是他国师路上最大的对手了。
算命这行，除了天分与记忆力，更多的是经验，这老太卜也不知比他多了多少的经验，肯定不是尉缭、侯生等人能与之相比的。否则，这老太卜也不可能被留在宫中，留为王室御用了。
思量间，徐福就已经走到那小塔下了。
小塔修得算不得高，塔门口守着两个小内侍，见徐福来了，忙笑道：“徐典事吗？徐典事请。”
徐福跟着走进去，就见一须发皆白的老头子穿着一身灰色袍子，跽坐在桌案前，因为年纪大了，又有些干瘦，脸上的皱纹难免多了一些，加上那不言不语，连半点笑容都没有的模样，看上去就有些震慑人了。看到他，倒是不容易让人想到太卜，反而容易显到古老的巫师。
徐福走近了，出于礼貌，还是朝人躬了躬身。
老太卜眼皮动了动，这才指着对面的位置示意徐福坐下。
同嬴政一起久了，徐福的礼仪也好了不少，他跽坐而下，与老太卜顿时形成了两个格外鲜明的对立面。从桌案分界，就好似一面黑暗，一面光明。
那老太卜身边的童子，都忍不住悄悄打量徐福，或许是从没在宫中见过这样模样出众的人。
“太卜唤我前来，可是有事？”
老太卜开口了，还带着些微的口音，声音像是粗沙砾磨过的一般，沙哑粗糙，带着陈年暮气，“蜡祭主持，交予你了。”
嗯？
徐福自己都不知道呢。蜡祭主持真的落到他头上了？
老太卜应当不会是认为自己抢了他的风头吧？
见徐福没有要回话的意思，那老太卜也并不介意，接着道：“从前蜡祭，都是由我主持，之后便换了奉常寺中的太祝。太祝现今也要给你让位了。”
让位一词说得可就有些严重啊。
老太卜又道：“蜡祭乃秦国上下同庆的大事，若是蜡祭出了差错，来年秦国有了灾祸，那主持蜡祭的人便要受到谴责。”
徐福心里骂了句卧槽。
天灾人祸，哪里是太卜或太祝能控制的？这个锅能给主持蜡祭的人背吗？
老太卜不知徐福心中所想，又慢吞吞地掀了掀眼皮，道：“你比那尉缭好，知礼节，不狂傲，想来应当是能担此重任的……”
知礼节，不狂傲……
这说的真的是他吗？徐福心中忍不住吐槽。
“个中事宜，想来你是有许多不懂之处的，届时前来问我便是。蜡祭不可出错，你可记住了？”
“……记住了。”徐福弄不清老太卜是何用意，但对方如此提醒他，总归也算是好心，徐福当然不会生出什么抵触来。
只是他觉得这差事……
够坑爹的啊！
他能撂挑子不干吗？
chapters.title: 第87章
chapters.translated_text:
Was his vision blurring?

Or had he misremembered the sequence?

Xu Fu frowned slightly, his fingers twitching as he paused. He turned abruptly, nearly sweeping the bamboo slips beside him into the brazier. A hand reached out from the side, narrowly catching the slips. Xu Fu’s thoughts returned to the present, and as he turned his head, he saw Wang Liu standing by his side.

Xu Fu’s gaze swept from the water beside his hand to the brazier by the table.

Was all of this sent by Wang Liu?

"Many thanks."

Wang Liu didn't say a word; he turned and walked out, looking rather sullen.

Had someone offended him? Xu Fu was completely bewildered. But he immediately pushed this doubt aside.

"Jing Mu Han, one of the seven mansions of the Vermilion Bird... When the Jing mansion is on duty, there is more misfortune than luck; what is sought will be unfavorable, and wealth will be dissipated..."

The further Xu Fu read, the worse his complexion became.

Had he actually sabotaged Ying Zheng?

Surely the ill omens wouldn't fall upon the Qin State, while the auspicious ones went to the Wei State?

A wave of displeasure washed over Xu Fu. Even if the Qin State had no auspicious omens, they certainly couldn't belong to the Wei State. He had to see for himself what kind of person this man from the Han State really was! Was he truly worthy of causing the twenty-eight constellations to shift and summoning a comet to bring forth a rosy glow?

Xu Fu rose, intending to head out, but stopped halfway.

The morning court session wasn't over yet, was it?

He wouldn't be able to see Ying Zheng if he returned to the palace now, would he?

Xu Fu had no choice but to sit back down.

Poor eyesight ruins everything! Xu Fu rubbed his eyes. He wasn't even sure what he had actually seen in the starry sky that day. As expected, one shouldn't try to show off in areas where they lack expertise. Xu Fu flipped through the ancient records on astrology in the Fengchang Temple. He found entries regarding comets and the twenty-eight constellations, but none mentioned both changing simultaneously. In other words, such a phenomenon might not have existed in ancient times, or if it did, it hadn't been recorded.

A moment later, Xu Fu thought of what Wei Liao had said—that in his youth, he wanted to study astronomy, physiognomy, and divination, but could never remember the formulas; his memory was worse than a goldfish's. Could he be suffering from the same thing, a decline in memory? That didn't seem likely... Xu Fu patted his forehead. It must have been that his eyes were playing tricks on him that day, and he hadn't seen clearly. Since he didn't even know who this person from the Han State was yet, why was he worrying so much?

After his shift ended, Xu Fu returned to Xianyang Palace early. Before long, Ying Zheng also strode in.

Ying Zheng smiled and said, "You were right. That Zheng Guo sent by the Han State does indeed have some ability."

Hm?

Xu Fu paused. Could it be that he had remembered incorrectly? That it wasn't the Jing Mu Han mansion on duty at all?

Ying Zheng sat down with Xu Fu. "Zheng Guo is skilled in water conservancy. I originally intended to send him to Dujiangyan." Ying Zheng paused, then added, "However, Li Bing is also a man of great talent. Putting the two of them together would not only be a waste but might also cause trouble."

Talented and capable people, even if they don't say it aloud, often have a bit of pride in their hearts.

Putting two capable people together would likely lead to mutual obstruction.

"Zheng Guo advised me to build water canals to change the grain shortage in Guanzhong." Ying Zheng frowned. "But this is not something that can be accomplished in a day. I am still somewhat hesitant. He speaks well, but I cannot blindly trust him."

"What did Zheng Guo do in the Han State before?" Xu Fu asked, feeling curious. To be praised by Ying Zheng, he must truly have some talent.

"He served as a water engineer and participated in the management of the Xingze floods..."

Although Xu Fu didn't know where Xingze was, he knew that those who could manage floods were generally capable people. The deepest memory he had was that during the reign of Qin Shi Huang, the Lingqu Canal was dug and the Great Wall was built, achieving eternal merit and bringing countless benefits to future generations.

Xu Fu didn't know where Guanzhong was, nor did he know where the Lingqu Canal was built. Could it be that this man was the one who built it? Was that why the celestial phenomena appeared as they did? Otherwise, how could a mere water engineer be considered such a formidable figure?

"I am not well-versed in these matters; you should make your own cautious decision, Your Majesty." Xu Fu was truly ignorant of this, so he wouldn't offer his own opinion to interfere with Ying Zheng, lest he do more harm than good.

Ying Zheng gave an "hmm" and then smiled. "If it is truly as Zheng Guo says, then the King of Han has personally delivered a treasure to my doorstep."

The Han State would likely regret it too late.

"The King of Han is timid and sent Zheng Guo to Qin. Will you still attack the Han State, Your Majesty?"

Ying Zheng’s expression turned cold. "I intend to attack Wei. Back in the time of Duke Xian, the State of Wei was powerful; they seized our Hexi territory and forced the Great Qin into Guanzhong. Later, they even attempted to lead an army to seize Guanzhong directly, nearly causing the destruction of the Great Qin. Times have changed; the Qin was weak then, but today the Wei is weak. What should be returned, the Wei must return today."

Ying Zheng added to himself that King Anxi of Wei still thought his state was the powerful Wei of the past, not taking him seriously and even intending to lay hands on his favorite! If it weren't for the fact that Lord Longyang had some ability and was at odds with the King of Wei, he would have targeted Lord Longyang first. Although he was sparing Lord Longyang for now, the King of Wei would always have to bear his wrath.

"So, the Han State will be spared for now?"

Seeing Xu Fu’s confused expression, Ying Zheng smiled. "I won't attack the Han, but I won't let them off either. Zheng Guo is nothing. Ah Fu, did you know that the King of Han has a son who was a fellow student of Li Si, both studying under Xunzi? Before he had even finished his studies, I had already heard of Han Fei. His talent is known throughout all the states. Li Si also mentioned to me that he has a senior fellow student who has mastered the Legalist school and is quite talented, but unfortunately, as a son of the King of Han, he has nowhere to display his ambitions. The Han State has no strong generals and no capable ministers. The only one is Han Fei. If I can get him, the Han State will weaken on its own within a few years. It won't cost me much effort."

"A son of the King of Han? Will the King of Han give him up?"

"Being a hostage in another state is not an uncommon thing. The King of Han does not favor this son. If I ask for him, I will ensure his temporary safety; why would he not give him up?"

Xu Fu’s expression was complex. "...If that is the case, then this King of Han is truly shortsighted."

Ying Zheng smiled and stopped mentioning him.

"If you attack the Wei State, then Lord Longyang..." Would he help the King of Wei or not? Although he followed him to the Qin State, that was when there was no sign of Qin moving against Wei. Lord Longyang was, after all, a man of Wei...

"I will ask him if he is willing to contribute to the Qin State. If he is unwilling, he must either leave Xianyang immediately, or the day I attack the Wei State will be the day I kill him."

Lord Longyang was brilliant and talented, but if he could not become an asset to the Qin State and instead became a major threat, from Ying Zheng’s perspective, it was indeed more convenient to kill him.

Thinking of this, Xu Fu realized that ever since he got involved with Ying Zheng, he only thought about what was beneficial or detrimental to Qin. Was this a good thing or a bad thing? It seemed to go against his desire to remain objective.

But... suddenly, he wanted to break those rules and constraints, to be willful just once... What kind of problem was this?

Xu Fu suddenly felt a bit guilty.

That day he said Wei Liao was a hypocrite, but today he seemed to be a hypocrite himself.

...

Ying Zheng said he would ask the Han State for Han Fei, and sure enough, within a few days, he sent word to the Han State.

The King of Han, fearing that the Qin State would attack him, had already handed over Zheng Guo without hesitation; what was Han Fei in comparison? Upon receiving the message, the King of Han, delighted that the crisis of the Han State could be resolved, immediately ordered someone to invite Han Fei to the palace.

Han Fei was overjoyed, thinking the King of Han finally valued him, so he packed his things and entered the palace.

He never imagined that the man who had offered strategies to the King of Han would be sold to the Qin State by the King of Han shortly after.

Ying Zheng had long since grasped Han Fei’s mindset.

Han Fei was full of talent but could not display it in the Han State, yet he refused to go to other states, which showed his persistence toward the Han State. He was loyal to his country, and for the sake of the Han State’s safety, even if he thought the King of Han’s actions were absurd, he would cooperate with the King of Han and willingly leave Han for Qin.

How much Han Fei loathed and hated the King of Qin, Ying Zheng did not know, and neither he nor Xu Fu cared.

As Han Fei set off from Han, the time for the Qin State’s Wax Festival was approaching again.

When Xu Fu went to the Fengchang Temple, he was baptized by countless gazes from those around him.

When Wang Liu came to deliver the brazier, Xu Fu stopped him. "What’s going on today? The people in the Fengchang Temple look at me as if they’ve never seen me before."

A smile appeared on Wang Liu’s face. "The Wax Festival is imminent. I suppose there should be a role for Official Xu to preside over it."

Xu Fu didn't take it to heart, saying carelessly, "The Fengchang Temple has its own Grand Invoker, and there is an old Grand Diviner in the palace. It shouldn't be my turn."

Wang Liu chuckled inwardly. Who didn't clearly see the status Official Xu held now? Many in the Fengchang Temple shared the same thought. As time passed, everyone knew that Xu Fu frequently entered and exited the royal palace. If Xu Fu were to preside over the Wax Festival, they wouldn't feel the slightest bit of surprise.

Perhaps the "surprises" Official Xu brought were simply too many; now, even if he did something shocking, it wouldn't cause a ripple.

By the time preparations for the Wax Festival began, the Grand Invoker in the Fengchang Temple who had attended the Qin King’s capping ceremony had already stated he was unwell, fearing he wouldn't recover in time and might make mistakes during the festival. Only the old Grand Diviner in the palace remained silent.

According to past customs, if it wasn't the Grand Invoker presiding, it would be the old Grand Diviner. It was just that the old Grand Diviner was truly old these past two years, which was why he didn't appear in public much. With the Grand Invoker claiming illness and the old Grand Diviner silent, some laughed, saying this was paving the way for Xu Fu.

The Wax Festival was a grand event celebrated by all of Qin, so naturally, there were those in the Qin court curious about who would preside over it. Some noble families had members in the Fengchang Temple, and they naturally cared more about this matter.

And on this day at the small court session, Ying Zheng announced Xu Fu’s name in an irrefutable tone.

The responsibility of presiding over the Wax Festival fell upon him.

By this time, the court had already heard this name—the Official Xu who had stubbornly insisted on going to the Shu region and later followed Li Si on a diplomatic mission to other states, Xu Fu.

Hearing this name from the King’s mouth again, everyone was stunned. They suddenly realized that this person was in the Fengchang Temple, and his promotion had been far too rapid. Now, such a young Grand Diviner was to take charge of the Wax Festival—could he handle it? In terms of seniority, there were countless people in the Fengchang Temple older than him.

"Your Majesty, this cannot be..."

"I am merely telling you the name of the person who will preside over the Wax Festival, not asking you to make the decision for me." If Ying Zheng, who held supreme power, couldn't even handle this, how could he talk about sending troops to the Wei State? There would likely be no shortage of opponents then. Sooner or later, these people would have to get used to his way of doing things.

Lord Changping had only recently returned from the Shu region before falling ill in bed, and people were already feeling uneasy. Hearing Ying Zheng’s majestic tone, they naturally wouldn't argue with him over such a matter and offend the King for nothing. Even if they were dissatisfied, they had to swallow it. But thinking of another person in the hall who had dealt with Xu Fu...

Li Si stood in the hall, smiling slightly, accepting the gazes cast upon him.

After the small court session dispersed, Li Si had just walked outside the hall when he was called out.

"Chief Clerk Li, may I ask what the background of that Xu Fu is?"

"Chief Clerk Li, are you aware that Xu Fu frequently enters and exits the royal palace? Could this be... could this be another Lord Longyang of Wei?"

These people wouldn't usually be so gossipy, but what truly touched their nerve was the idea of a second Lord Longyang.

Thinking of the status Lord Longyang held in the Wei State, they worried that Xu Fu might become the second. Power was always in the hands of the few, and the current King of Qin’s tight grip on power had already made the noble ministers dissatisfied. If that little bit of power were to be divided by others, who could tolerate such a thing that touched their own interests?

No one cared about a male favorite, but a male favorite who was promoted too quickly, held an official position, and was highly favored—that was a different story.

Li Si knew what they were thinking, but he remembered Xu Fu’s favor in recommending him. If not for Xu Fu, where would Li Si be today? These people wanted to fish for information from him—they were thinking too simply.

"Official Xu..." Li Si drew out his tone, paused, took in the curious and nervous expressions of the men before him, and then smiled. "I only know that Official Xu’s master is extremely formidable."

Having said that, Li Si bypassed them and strode away.

The men were stunned.

How formidable? Who exactly is his master? Why won't you say it clearly...

Not to mention how these people were feeling.

At this moment, Xu Fu, who was resting in the palace and hadn't gone to the Fengchang Temple, was flipping through the bamboo slips at his side when an attendant entered the room, bowed, and said, "Official Xu, the old Grand Diviner in the palace wishes to see you."

Xu Fu’s movement of flipping the slips paused. The old Grand Diviner? The one who had argued with Wei Liao and was highly regarded by the previous two Kings of Qin?

Combining the information from Wei Liao and Ying Zheng, Xu Fu had already sketched an image of a pedantic, formidable, and aloof old man in his mind. He lived alone in the palace for years and might even have some eccentric, reclusive temper.

Why would he come looking for him? It couldn't be for the Wax Festival, could it?

Xu Fu imagined many possibilities, then pushed aside the bamboo slips, straightened his body, and walked out.

He smoothed his robes, stepped out of the hall, and was led by the attendant toward the old Grand Diviner’s residence.

There was a small tower built in the palace, said to be for the old Grand Diviner to observe the celestial phenomena, and that was where he lived. The treatment was so high it made Xu Fu jealous. But thinking about it, the old Grand Diviner lived alone in a small tower, while he slept in the King of Qin’s bed, ate the King of Qin’s food, and played with the King of Qin’s son... Thinking of it this way, his treatment was even higher. *Cough.*

Xu Fu resumed a serious expression.

Although this old Grand Diviner wasn't the State Preceptor, his position was equivalent to one. Come to think of it, this old Grand Diviner should be his greatest rival on the path to becoming State Preceptor.

In the fortune-telling business, besides talent and memory, experience was more important. This old Grand Diviner must have far more experience than him, and certainly couldn't be compared to Wei Liao or Hou Sheng. Otherwise, he wouldn't have been kept in the palace as the royal specialist.

While pondering, Xu Fu reached the base of the small tower.

The tower wasn't built very high. Two young attendants guarded the entrance, and seeing Xu Fu arrive, they hurriedly smiled. "Are you Official Xu? Please, Official Xu."

Xu Fu followed them inside and saw an old man with white hair and beard wearing a gray robe, kneeling before a table. Because of his age, he was somewhat thin, and his face was inevitably lined with many wrinkles. Coupled with his silent, smileless appearance, he looked quite intimidating. Seeing him, it was hard to think of him as a Grand Diviner; instead, he looked more like an ancient shaman.

Xu Fu approached and, out of politeness, bowed to him.

The old Grand Diviner’s eyelids moved, and he pointed to the seat opposite him, signaling Xu Fu to sit.

Having been with Ying Zheng for a long time, Xu Fu’s etiquette had improved significantly. He knelt down, and he and the old Grand Diviner immediately formed two distinct opposites. Divided by the table, it was as if one side was darkness and the other was light.

The young attendant beside the old Grand Diviner couldn't help but peek at Xu Fu, perhaps because he had never seen someone so outstanding in the palace.

"Did you summon me here for something, Grand Diviner?"

The old Grand Diviner spoke, with a slight accent. His voice sounded like coarse gravel grinding, hoarse and rough, carrying the twilight of years. "The presiding role for the Wax Festival has been handed to you."

Hm?

Xu Fu didn't even know that himself. Had the role of presiding over the Wax Festival really fallen to him?

The old Grand Diviner shouldn't think that he had stolen his limelight, right?

Seeing that Xu Fu had no intention of replying, the old Grand Diviner didn't mind and continued, "In the past, the Wax Festival was always presided over by me, and later it was changed to the Grand Invoker in the Fengchang Temple. Now, the Grand Invoker has to make way for you."

The term "make way" sounded a bit serious.

The old Grand Diviner added, "The Wax Festival is a grand event celebrated by all of Qin. If something goes wrong during the festival and a disaster befalls the Qin State in the coming year, the person presiding over the festival will be held accountable."

Xu Fu cursed "damn it" in his heart.

Natural disasters and human calamities—how could a Grand Diviner or Grand Invoker control them? Could this burden be placed on the person presiding over the festival?

The old Grand Diviner didn't know what Xu Fu was thinking, and he slowly lifted his eyelids again. "You are better than that Wei Liao; you know etiquette and are not arrogant. I suppose you should be able to shoulder this heavy responsibility..."

Knows etiquette, not arrogant...

Was he really talking about him? Xu Fu couldn't help but complain in his heart.

"There are many things you don't understand about the process; come and ask me when the time comes. The Wax Festival must not go wrong. Do you remember?"

"...I remember." Xu Fu couldn't figure out the old Grand Diviner’s intentions, but since the other party was reminding him, it was at least well-intentioned. Xu Fu naturally wouldn't feel any resistance.

It was just that he felt this task...

...was a total trap!

Could he just quit and not do it?

Xu Fu didn't know what kind of stimulation Wei Liao had given the Old Grand Diviner previously, but now the Old Grand Diviner was treating him with such patience and kindness—it completely defied his expectations. That aside, the Old Grand Diviner even seemed to think he was a gentle, studious, motivated, and low-key person.

Heaven knows that some of those words would never be associated with him in his entire life.

Unable to bear the weight of the Old Grand Diviner’s expectant gaze, Xu Fu nodded, drawing a conclusion to this conversation.

"Thank you, Old Grand Diviner, for your heartfelt words today. I will keep them in mind." Xu Fu was not some hot-headed youth; he wouldn't impulsively promise not to let the Old Grand Diviner down. Promises shouldn't be given lightly; if given incorrectly, it was like setting up a flag for oneself, only to be slapped in the face later.

The Old Grand Diviner didn't get the answer he wanted, and a flash of disappointment crossed his face. However, since Xu Fu had already spoken, he could only order someone to escort Xu Fu out of the tower.

After Xu Fu left, the Old Grand Diviner looked at his retreating figure and sighed, "Still a bit too young. He speaks so honestly; though he looks like such a spirited child on the outside, he doesn't know how to be the least bit ingratiating..."

If Xu Fu had heard what the Old Grand Diviner said, he would have felt incredibly wronged.

Him, honest?

Then there would be few people left in this world who weren't honest.

The Old Grand Diviner’s residence wasn't a place just anyone could enter. As soon as Xu Fu stepped out, the palace attendants from the Qin King’s sleeping quarters immediately rushed up to him, looking at him with anxious eyes and asking, "Are you alright, Director Xu?"

"I'm fine." Seeing their worried expressions, he guessed they were still traumatized by the time Wei Liao clashed with the Old Grand Diviner.

Not long after Xu Fu returned, Ying Zheng also arrived back at the sleeping quarters.

"Did the King choose me to preside over the La Sacrifice?" Xu Fu immediately asked the question in his heart.

Ying Zheng nodded, flicked his sleeves, and knelt at the desk. He looked up at Xu Fu, his tone calm, and said, "One day, when you were drowsy in your sleep, you told me you wanted to be the State Preceptor."

Xu Fu recalled it for a moment; it seemed... it seemed he had said that.

At the time, he had seemed to wake suddenly from a dream, and in that instant, he had been exceptionally clear-headed.

Xu Fu suddenly felt his mouth go dry. He swallowed involuntarily. Did Ying Zheng really take those words to heart? Was he preparing to... pave the way for him?

The importance of the La Sacrifice in the Qin State, whether from his experience attending it last year or the Old Grand Diviner’s repeated exhortations this year, could be seen clearly. The people of Qin might not know what the Fengchang Temple or the Divination Bureau were, but they certainly knew who presided over the La Sacrifice. If one showed their face at the La Sacrifice, the people would naturally remember them, gain their support, and win their hearts. With such a foundation, wouldn't becoming the State Preceptor later be a natural progression?

Such a path to the heavens had been simply laid at his feet.

It seems he made the right choice by choosing to go through Ying Zheng’s back door, right?

Xu Fu also flicked his sleeves and sat down beside Ying Zheng, saying, "King, the Old Grand Diviner called me over today."

Ying Zheng frowned imperceptibly, expressing a small amount of dissatisfaction with the title "King." "The Old Grand Diviner summoned you? Did he give you a hard time?" Ying Zheng paused and said, "The Old Grand Diviner is capable himself and a bit arrogant. If he said anything to make you unhappy, don't take it to heart. He is old and will eventually step down from that position."

It seems everyone thought the Old Grand Diviner would bully him?

But he wasn't someone who was easy to bully!

Xu Fu shook his head helplessly, "The Old Grand Diviner didn't say anything to make me unhappy; on the contrary..."

"On the contrary, what?"

"He seemed happy to see me take over the position of presiding over the La Sacrifice, gave me a lot of encouraging words, and incidentally told me that if I messed up the La Sacrifice, it would be a big problem." Xu Fu’s tone was light and airy, not taking the Old Grand Diviner’s words to heart at all. It wasn't that he wasn't serious, but that there was no need to worry needlessly. If he were constantly thinking about not messing up, that was exactly when he would be likely to mess up.

Ying Zheng frowned, somewhat dissatisfied with the pressure the Old Grand Diviner had applied. However, he still answered the doubt in Xu Fu’s heart, "The La Sacrifice was once solely the responsibility of the Old Grand Diviner. Later, Lu Buwei chose Tian Tai-zhu of the Fengchang Temple to replace him, and the Old Grand Diviner grew resentful of Tian Tai-zhu. If not for Tian Tai-zhu, he wouldn't have had to step down from his position so early, and he wouldn't have lost the power he held. Now you are going to replace Tian Tai-zhu..."

Before Ying Zheng finished, Xu Fu understood.

It was roughly the idea that "the enemy of my enemy is my friend."

Xu Fu suddenly felt that these people’s minds were so twisted that he sometimes really couldn't see through them.

Ying Zheng smiled, "That is also good; then no one will be able to block your path later."

It could be considered a kind of luck. Xu Fu sighed to himself.

After the La Sacrifice, he would be one step closer to the path of the State Preceptor. Xu Fu suddenly felt relaxed. Presiding over the La Sacrifice—if it’s a pain, so be it; as long as it’s worth it.

Ying Zheng’s gaze fell involuntarily onto Xu Fu’s face again.

Those who are kings have always been solitary, and even with a harem full of children, they remain alone.

Ying Zheng used to think so too; perhaps he would only pursue his great cause in this life, with no other thoughts to spare. Only now did Ying Zheng feel that was not the case. He was willing to spare some attention for Xu Fu, hoping only that on the day his great cause was achieved, Xu Fu would stand hand-in-hand with him.

Xu Fu turned his head a beat late, meeting Ying Zheng’s gaze, and said, "That would be very good."

...

No one in the Fengchang Temple had expected the choice for the La Sacrifice officiant to be decided so quickly, and that it would actually be Xu Fu! It gave people a feeling of being both expected and unexpected. Some people couldn't help but feel a bit sour, feeling that Xu Fu’s journey had been too smooth. In this Fengchang Temple, which valued family background and seniority, he was going to preside over the La Sacrifice in less than a year—it was truly infuriating to compare people!

Su Yi was on good terms with Xu Fu, so naturally, some people went to vent their sourness to Su Yi.

"Brother Su, you have a deep friendship with Director Xu; why don't you ask him for an important position too?"

"That's right, come to think of it, Brother Su is already a Tai-zhu; you should be the good candidate to preside over the La Sacrifice..."

"Yes, if we talk about qualifications, Brother Su should come first..."

Su Yi looked impatient, but those two didn't notice his displeasure. Just then, Wang Liu happened to pass by, and the two became even more energized, calling out to Wang Liu, "Even if we don't mention Brother Su, Grand Diviner Wang has more seniority and background, yet none of us were chosen. Tsk tsk..."

Wang Liu stopped in his tracks, turned his head, and gave the two a cold, sharp look.

The two shut their mouths involuntarily, only then remembering that Wang Liu used to be the little bully of the Fengchang Temple. Ever since his competition with Xu Fu last year, he had kept a low profile, and everyone had almost forgotten his true nature. Now, seeing his unpleasant expression, the two realized that Wang Liu’s temper wasn't good and he was not someone to be offended.

They weren't a second Xu Fu, who could guarantee they would be unscathed after offending Wang Liu.

"You don't even know what kind of background Director Xu has, yet you are here gossiping and showing off your tongues—does talking big get you this opportunity? You’re just spewing sourness!" Wang Liu didn't hold back at all.

The two felt a wave of shame wash over them.

Even Su Yi couldn't help but take another look at Wang Liu.

If it were before, Wang Liu wouldn't have been any better than them, but back then, Wang Liu wouldn't have lowered himself to gossip behind people's backs. Wang Liu seemed to have truly changed completely.

The two felt more and more humiliated, and thinking back to how Wang Liu wasn't a good person before, they wondered what he was pretending to be now by lecturing them!

Naturally, they weren't willing to swallow this, so they asked defiantly, "Does Grand Diviner Wang know what kind of background Director Xu has?"

Not to mention those two, even Su Yi couldn't help but look at Wang Liu, his eyes full of surprise and curiosity.

Su Yi was quite close to Xu Fu, but even he didn't know Xu Fu’s background; how could Wang Liu know?

The three heard Wang Liu sneer, "Do you know of Guigu? Do you know of Master Wei Liao, who was just appointed as the State Lieutenant? Director Xu is a fellow disciple of the State Lieutenant, both from Guigu! Now tell me, what kind of background do you think he has?"

How many powerful figures had come from Guigu? All seven states had heard of it.

Not to mention Guigu, just the reputation of Wei Liao alone was quite resounding.

The two looked at each other and left sheepishly. They had always assumed Xu Fu had no background; who knew he wasn't without one, but had just kept it hidden for fear of scaring others. Now, they could only feel envious, jealous, and hateful in their hearts. Such good fortune—that was his own!

Wang Liu was about to leave as well, but Su Yi grabbed him.

"How do you know Director Xu’s background?" Su Yi asked, frowning slightly at Wang Liu.

Wang Liu rolled his eyes at him, "If you paid more attention to Director Xu, you would know that the State Lieutenant has come to the Fengchang Temple to find Director Xu several times."

After saying this, Wang Liu shook off his arm and strode away.

Su Yi was stunned for a long time before sighing, "...Director Xu is truly no ordinary person." A disciple of Guigu—how could an ordinary person compare to him? No wonder Director Xu could reach this point today! As for those who wanted to see him make a fool of himself, they were likely to be disappointed...

·

While Zheng Guo was still struggling to secure the construction of the water canal, Xu Fu had already begun preparing for the La Sacrifice.

The conversation between Wang Liu and the two men had spread throughout the Fengchang Temple before they knew it. Although they hadn't seen with their own eyes how Wei Liao came to find Xu Fu, a sense of awe and respect had quietly risen in their hearts. Some even privately flattered him, saying they had long seen that Xu Fu was extraordinary, and seeing it today, it was true! He was a disciple from Guigu! Naturally, he was a bit more capable than others!

Xu Fu pretended to be unaware of all this private gossip.

He didn't have the extra time to pay attention to it anyway.

It was completely different from just watching the La Sacrifice; as the person presiding over it, the first thing he had to do was memorize the chants for the ceremony.

Xu Fu vaguely remembered that day last year, when the officiant chanted the lyrics with a strange accent, but it sounded indescribably comfortable, mysterious, and distant.

Xu Fu felt... it was quite difficult for someone as tone-deaf as himself.

However, he couldn't sing it, but Ying Zheng could. Ying Zheng taught him hand-in-hand. The hardships involved need not be detailed, but it did add a bit of "bedroom fun." If he still couldn't remember it after a backache, then he deserved the backache! After tossing and turning for a few days, Xu Fu finally learned to recite it.

Besides that, he had to understand various repetitive rituals. The thing Xu Fu found most unbearable was that on that day, he wouldn't be able to eat; he had to wait until the La Sacrifice was over and the grand banquet was held in the evening before he could eat.

Xu Fu stared at the record of this on the bamboo slips, sitting bolt upright with a look of utter hopelessness on his face.

Ying Zheng, glancing at this from the side, couldn't help but frown. Last time, Xu Fu had fainted after the La Sacrifice; how could he go without food or water for almost an entire day this time? Whatever rules or taboos there were, Ying Zheng threw them to the back of his mind in an instant.

"On that day, I will have someone prepare food for you. You will eat in the morning before you deal with the La Sacrifice."

Since Ying Zheng was being so proactive and reasonable, Xu Fu wasn't one to be pretentious, so he immediately climbed up the pole, a smile appearing on his face, "Thank you, King... A-Zheng." He forcibly changed his words mid-sentence.

Since Ying Zheng was so considerate and thorough toward him, he always had to give Ying Zheng a little sweetness in return.

Hearing this, the expression on Ying Zheng’s face indeed softened significantly.

Xu Fu caught the subtle change in his expression and couldn't help but feel a bit smug. So even the First Emperor of Qin wasn't that hard to deal with. Oh no, perhaps it was just because he was too smart.

Xu Fu closed the bamboo slips; he could basically recite the contents by heart now. As long as there were no natural or man-made disasters during the La Sacrifice, he wouldn't have any problems.

Ying Zheng felt a sense of pleasure in his heart. He was just about to embrace Xu Fu to spend their private time together when he suddenly saw Fusu walk in from outside the hall. "Teacher!" As soon as Fusu walked in and saw Ying Zheng embracing Xu Fu, he froze.

Ying Zheng’s face darkened, and he silently recited three times: Father-son affection cannot be destroyed! Father-son affection cannot be destroyed! Father-son affection cannot be destroyed!

Fusu remained standing there, stunned.

In fact, he was secretly pondering how to slip out quietly, so as not to be noticed by his father for being an insensitive intruder.

Ying Zheng looked at Fusu’s stunned expression, thinking he was shocked by the relationship between him and Xu Fu.

"Fusu, come here." Ying Zheng said.

Xu Fu pushed the bamboo slips aside, looking calm and composed, without any panic or shame at being caught in an affair... or any such emotions.

Fusu moved with small, hesitant steps, stopping in front of Ying Zheng.

It’s over...

Fusu thought to himself.

Xu Fu glanced left and right, feeling that the brain circuits of this father and son weren't on the same page.

Ying Zheng reached out and patted Fusu on the head, asking gently, "Since your mother left, has there been anything troubling you?"

Fusu shook his head blankly, "No." If he said yes, he felt he would be slaughtered.

Ying Zheng sighed softly and said, "You are not young anymore; you should understand things. Your teacher and I..."

"Wait, can he understand?" Xu Fu couldn't help but interrupt Ying Zheng.

Although Fusu looked clever and exceptionally sharp, could he understand the affairs between men? There shouldn't be such a precocious child...

Just as Xu Fu was thinking this, he saw Fusu nod and say, "Fusu knows that Father likes Teacher, and the relationship between Teacher and Father is like... like the relationship between husband and wife." Fusu even had an "I am very serious" expression on his face.

Xu Fu: "..." So there really was such a precocious child!

Ying Zheng and Xu Fu were both silent, both wondering if they had set a bad example and corrupted young Fusu.

"Father, did Fusu say something wrong?" Seeing their expressions, Fusu asked in a low voice.

He hadn't said anything wrong...

Ying Zheng immediately and openly laid it out, "You didn't say anything wrong; the relationship between your teacher and me is exactly that."

Fusu nodded indifferently, "Then Fusu will not disturb Father and Teacher..." Saying this, he turned and walked out on his short legs. His nonchalant attitude made Xu Fu and Ying Zheng feel somewhat at a loss.

Ying Zheng sighed softly, feeling a bit sorry for his eldest son, "Perhaps it’s because his personality is like Lady Zheng’s; he has never needed me to worry about anything."

"Young Master Fusu has a maturity and steadiness that his peers don't have."

Ying Zheng smiled, "He’s only a few years old; how is that mature and steady?" Ying Zheng suddenly paused and said, "But there are exceptions, like you. You look steady on the outside, but isn't your heart like a child’s? Fusu is likely the opposite of you."

Xu Fu’s face darkened, and he instantly put on a cold, aloof act, ignoring Ying Zheng.

He was like a child?

Where on his body did he look like one?

Ying Zheng had already slept with him, so was Ying Zheng a pedophile!

Seeing his cold expression, as if he "disdained to speak with commoners," Ying Zheng couldn't help but smile again, "Haha, I won't say that anymore..."

The two chatted about this and that for a while before going to eat.

·

In the blink of an eye, it was the day of the La Sacrifice.

With last year’s experience and the knowledge he had crammed in at the last minute, Xu Fu was not the least bit panicked.

For some reason, Ying Zheng seemed even more nervous than him. He woke up early, and as soon as he bathed and dressed, Xu Fu was inevitably woken up. Xu Fu propped himself up from the bed and saw Ying Zheng emerge with a mist of water, while attendants stepped forward to dress him.

A palace maid saw Xu Fu wake up and immediately led him to bathe as well.

To preside over the La Sacrifice, Xu Fu had to burn incense and bathe.

After bathing, as soon as Xu Fu came out, he saw the palace maid holding a large black ceremonial robe, smiling at him.

Unlike the ceremonial robe Ying Zheng had specially prepared for him before, this one was heavier, with more intricate patterns. It was entirely black, giving a sense of solemnity and mystery. When the palace maid helped him put on the inner robes layer by layer, Xu Fu could already feel an invisible pressure on his shoulders and back, causing him to straighten his spine involuntarily.

Then Ying Zheng walked up and personally draped the outer robe over him.

The attendants could only watch this unconventional scene, not daring to make a sound.

"Serve the meal," Ying Zheng said indifferently.

The palace attendants hurriedly brought the food forward.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng sat on opposite sides of the table, eating their meal in haste.

If one were to say it was disrespectful to the gods, could a single meal really be considered disrespectful? If the gods were truly that petty, they would hardly be worth respecting anyway.

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s thoughts happened to coincide perfectly.

After finishing the meal, Xu Fu followed the eunuch out of the palace first.

A group of ministers was already waiting outside the palace. Last year, Xu Fu had been one of them, but this year, the ministers watched him approach with complex expressions.

Dressed in heavy ceremonial robes, Xu Fu walked over from a distance, looking even more dignified than the old Grand Diviner or the Grand Invoker of Tian. One look at him, and one would instinctively feel that he was the only one fit to preside over the Wax Festival.

Perhaps this was the magic of charisma.

When Xu Fu wore white, he gave off an ethereal, immortal air; when he wore black, he exuded a profound and solemn presence. Once in his presence, it seemed as if no one dared to be presumptuous. Such a strange feeling was mysterious, yet undeniably real. Those who originally disliked Xu Fu and had opposed him presiding over the Wax Festival now instinctively closed their mouths, unable to utter a word of blame.

Xu Fu stopped once he drew near, then turned his back to the crowd, gazing toward the towering palace within the royal city; that was where Ying Zheng would be coming from.

Ying Zheng did not keep them waiting for long.

Whether he truly cared for his ministers was uncertain, but he certainly cared for Xu Fu.

How could he bear to let Xu Fu stand there waiting for long? Thus, he had set out early.

Once the monarch arrived, the ministers shouted in unison, then followed him in a grand procession out of Xianyang Palace, first to offer sacrifices to the ancestors, and then toward the outskirts of Xianyang City.

As they passed through the streets, countless commoners knelt on the ground on both sides, kowtowing to the King of Qin and shouting his name.

As the carriage passed, these commoners would follow behind.

This year, they traveled a bit further, choosing a different plot of farmland.

Upon arrival, Xu Fu had to temporarily hand over the presiding duties to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng was dressed even more majestically and heroically than he was. Holding a hazelwood staff, Ying Zheng stood on a mound between the ridges of the field. He was tall, and no one could obscure the radiance he emanated.

Xu Fu looked up at his figure with an admiring gaze, a part of his heart stirring slightly. If only such an outstanding person could be cherished for a lifetime.

It must be said that in some respects, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng’s temperaments were quite similar.

After Ying Zheng finished speaking, Xu Fu chanted in a high voice: "Earth, return to your dwelling! Water, return to your gullies! Insects, do not stir! Grass and trees, return to your marshes! Earth, return to your dwelling! Water, return to your gullies! Insects, do not stir! May the harvest be bountiful, yielding a thousandfold!" His voice was cold and pleasant; even if it was slightly off-key, the flaw did not obscure the beauty. The expressions of the surrounding commoners rose and fell with his tone, their hearts led by him.

Before his voice had completely faded, Ying Zheng had already begun to chant in response.

The two voices connected seamlessly, and Xu Fu suddenly felt a bit strange, as if they were reciting wedding vows...

However, when the commoners began to sing along, Xu Fu’s strange thought vanished.

The Wax Festival ended quickly.

When the food was being distributed, Xu Fu noticed Ying Zheng’s gaze sweeping over him—it was an undisguised, lingering look.

Xu Fu’s heartbeat quickened slightly. This public display of affection actually gave him a secret thrill. Moreover, compared to last year, Ying Zheng’s attitude was much gentler. The stronger the contrast, the more difficult it was to keep his heart calm, and he even felt a faint sense of secret joy.

The crowd soon dispersed, and Ying Zheng boarded the royal carriage to return to the palace.

Su Yi had originally wanted to call out to Xu Fu as he had last year, but he suddenly remembered what Li Si had said, so he forced himself to stop, watching helplessly as Xu Fu followed the royal carriage away.

Su Yi felt a pang of heartache, thinking to himself, if things continue like this, who knows what it will develop into... whether it will be good or bad... he could not foresee it!

Xu Fu walked slowly behind the carriage, completely unaware that Su Yi was still worrying about him. Ying Zheng had wanted to stop the carriage to walk with Xu Fu, but such an act would be too improper at this moment. Furthermore, for the sake of safety, he could not easily step down from the carriage. Thus, it became a scene where Xu Fu walked behind the carriage, while Ying Zheng lifted the curtain, watching Xu Fu walk slowly ahead.

Seeing this, Zhao Gao felt a shiver of awkwardness and could only sigh, pitying himself for being all alone!

Upon returning to the palace, an exhausted Xu Fu removed his robes, knelt on the mat, and said, "Should I now pray that there will be absolutely no disasters in the State of Qin next year? Just to avoid being blamed for presiding over the Wax Festival improperly."

"No need to worry. The old Grand Diviner only said that to you because he thought you were young and wanted to find a way to scare you into being cautious," Ying Zheng immediately comforted him.

Xu Fu had only been joking, and hearing Ying Zheng say this, he felt it made sense and immediately put it out of his mind.

The grand banquet after last year’s Wax Festival had been completely ruined because of Zhao Ji. This year, however, Ying Zheng did not summon the concubines to the hall. He ordered tables to be set up, laden with wine and meat. There were only four tables.

Xu Fu was quite surprised when he entered the hall.

Four tables?

One for him and one for Ying Zheng, but who else could sit at the other two?

Before long, Xu Fu saw Fusu enter with Huhai.

Huhai was over a year old; he could mumble some sounds, but he couldn't walk at all, at most crawling around. Although Fusu was young, he had to use all his strength to support the chubby little Huhai. The palace maid watched with trepidation, but dared not disturb the eldest prince’s affection for his younger brother.

It was Xu Fu who saw this and said, "Fusu, give Huhai to me."

How could the maid dare to let Xu Fu hold him? The King’s gaze was already cold and sharp! The maid smiled and took Huhai from Fusu, sitting down at another table, which counted as occupying a spot.

Xu Fu: ...

Although such an arrangement seemed a bit strange, upon closer reflection, it felt exactly as it should be.

It was as if they were truly a family sitting together... how was it any different from the New Year’s Eve dinner in his past life?

At the banquet, Huhai was busy licking his fingers, while Fusu’s gaze kept drifting toward Huhai, eventually looking away, unable to bear the sight. As for the two adults, Xu Fu and Ying Zheng, they appeared much more serious, solemnly raising their cups to toast.

Xu Fu said in a clear voice, "May the King’s great cause be accomplished soon."

Ying Zheng smiled and drank it all in one gulp.

He naturally had a toast of his own in his heart, but he did not say it.

...Beyond the great cause of the empire, I also wish for you to remain by my side forever.

Such mushy words were not in Ying Zheng’s nature to speak, so he chose not to say them at all. Actions were more effective than words.

Xu Fu was also deep in thought. He hoped to ascend to the position of State Preceptor soon, so that he could stand side-by-side with Ying Zheng. Just thinking about the feeling of standing beside the First Emperor of Qin was wonderful! Even just imagining it made Xu Fu’s heart race.

The two exchanged a glance, then tacitly looked away.

The hall was filled with the aroma of wine and meat, and the warmth made them feel intoxicated before they knew it.

Ying Zheng ordered someone to take Fusu and Huhai back, then personally supported Xu Fu as they walked into the inner hall.

Ying Zheng was extremely mindful of Xu Fu’s reputation; if not for his consideration for Xu Fu, he would have done whatever he pleased and picked him up directly.

Back in the bedchamber, on such a day of national celebration, it was naturally another night of spring warmth.

Meanwhile, Han Fei was still on his way to Qin. Seeing the celebrations along the way, he felt increasingly uncomfortable. As the son of the King of Han, he possessed great talent but was forced to travel far to Qin. He could only witness the joy of other nations, while he could no longer see how his own country celebrated.

Han Fei sat alone in the carriage, feeling lonely and desolate.

The coachman sighed, shook his head, and whipped the horses to go faster.

·

Once the Wax Festival passed, Han Fei entered Qin.

After Han Fei arrived in Xianyang, someone escorted him to the guesthouse to rest. The person was extremely respectful, not at all like the attitude one should have toward a "hostage prince." Han Fei was suspicious, convinced that the King of Qin must have a deeper meaning behind this.

Could it be to give him a show of force? Or to demonstrate the magnanimity of Qin?

Han Fei could not fathom it and could only stay in the guesthouse for the time being.

But before he could wait for an opportunity to see the King of Qin, he encountered an old acquaintance.

"An old acquaintance has come to see you, Master Han. Will you see him?" the servant at the guesthouse asked.

This was Qin territory; if he threw a tantrum and refused to see them, it would be like slapping Qin in the face the moment he arrived. Could the King of Qin forgive him? Thinking of this, Han Fei nodded.

Han Fei sat in the room, and before long, footsteps approached.

The maid pushed open the door and whispered, "Official Xu, Chief Scribe Li, they are inside."

Han Fei was full of confusion. Official Xu? Chief Scribe Li? They didn't sound like his acquaintances.

He looked up and saw two people enter, one after the other. The one in front wore light-colored robes, his skin as delicate as white porcelain, his expression indifferent, not like a person of the mortal world. At the very first glance, one could not easily look away. Han Fei was slightly stunned but quickly recovered. Having an overly outstanding appearance had its drawbacks.

Han Fei’s gaze slid quickly over the other’s face, confirming that he did not know him.

Then he looked at the person behind.

The gentle face, the graceful demeanor, even the three parts of a smile on his face were familiar—too familiar.

"...Junior... brother?" Han Fei said.

Xu Fu had just stepped into the room and was sizing Han Fei up, seeing him dressed like a frail scholar, and was just about to speak when the other man spoke first. Xu Fu was startled. Junior brother? Who was he calling that? Could he be related to everyone?

However, Xu Fu calmed down and realized that Han Fei’s gaze was directed at Li Si.

Han Fei and Li Si were fellow disciples? This was interesting. No wonder Li Si had urged him to come to the guesthouse together; it turned out the fellow disciples wanted to meet.

The three sat down in the room. The coldness on Han Fei’s face faded as he asked Li Si, "Are... are you... an official... in Qin?"

Having long learned from Ying Zheng that although Han Fei was talented, he was not favored by the King of Han due to a natural speech impediment, Xu Fu felt it was actually fine. Observing Han Fei’s face, he saw a calm expression; his features were not tense, indicating he was very relaxed and did not feel inferior or timid because of his stutter.

It made sense; how could a person with talent and a vast mind be obsessed with such a minor flaw?

For him, the greatest trouble caused by his speech impediment was merely not being valued by the King of Han.

However, for a patriotic man like Han Fei, coming to Qin might even fulfill his patriotic heart.

Xu Fu had complex feelings about such a person. He admired him, but also lamented that such a figure was born under the King of Han. There were many talents in the world, but none were as fortunate as finding a patron like Ying Zheng.

Li Si and Zhao Gao—weren't they able to rise to fame and become world-renowned precisely because they were in Ying Zheng’s hands?

He wondered if Han Fei would be able to recognize the situation...

Li Si and Han Fei shared old ties, and within a few words, they were chatting away.

Xu Fu had not spoken, and Han Fei did not take the initiative to talk to him either. He was not willing to talk to anyone from Qin; if Li Si hadn't been his fellow disciple, he might not have even bothered with him.

After a long time, Li Si finally stopped chatting about old times with Han Fei.

He spoke directly, touching on Han Fei’s sore spot: "Have your books been promoted in Han? Does the King of Han rely on you now?"

Han Fei had written "Solitary Indignation" and "Five Vermin." He had once set aside his pride and brought the bamboo slips to the King of Han, but the King had laughed at him, saying that if he couldn't even speak clearly, what brilliant strategies could he have? Did Han need a stutterer to govern it? The King of Han’s blunt words had crushed Han Fei’s patriotism to pieces.

Now that Li Si brought it up, how could Han Fei have a good expression? His face suddenly turned cold. "Si... what... what is the meaning of this?" As he got agitated, his stutter worsened, which undoubtedly reminded him once again of the insults and neglect he had suffered before the King of Han.

In just a short time, Han Fei’s face had turned as black as charcoal.

To be able to make Han Fei change color with anger, Li Si certainly had some skill.

Only then did Xu Fu speak slowly: "Master Han, do not be agitated. Chief Scribe Li, as a former fellow disciple, is only concerned about you." Xu Fu paused, and seeing Han Fei’s displeased expression as if he were about to retort, he immediately added, "I am Xu Fu. May I invite Master Han to the palace with me? The King has seen your books, 'Solitary Indignation' and 'Five Vermin,' and is very fond of your talent."

No one disliked being praised. Even if he was Han Fei, after suffering such poor treatment from the King of Han, he could not help but soften his expression at Xu Fu’s words.

Xu Fu did not give Han Fei a chance to hesitate, raising his hand and saying, "Please, Master Han."

As it happened, Han Fei also wanted to see the King of Qin, to see what the man who wanted to attack their State of Han looked like!

Han Fei waved his sleeves with a cold face and strode out of the door.

Xu Fu stood up leisurely and followed him. Li Si smiled and said, "My senior fellow disciple’s temper hasn't changed. It’s probably impossible to get him to work for Qin."

Xu Fu did not speak.

Li Si added with a smile, "I’m not jealous of my senior brother’s talent and trying to smear him. He is just stubborn and upright; he values Han more than his own talent."

"If we can't keep the person, keeping the books is not bad either," Xu Fu said, then quickened his pace.

Li Si paused, then smiled, "So Official Xu is also a clear-headed person."

In fact, Xu Fu’s words were a bit cold-blooded, but he had long stood with Ying Zheng, so he naturally put Ying Zheng’s interests first. Han Fei was rare, but if he really insisted on fighting Qin to the end, then keeping his books would be enough.

Xu Fu would not say that two days ago, after Ying Zheng read Han Fei’s works, he had exclaimed excitedly, "If I could meet this man and travel with him, I would have no regrets in death!"

Heh...

Xu Fu felt a faint sense of unhappiness in his heart.

...

Ying Zheng did not know what Xu Fu had gone to do, but that afternoon, he heard reports that Han Fei had requested an audience.

Although Ying Zheng cherished Han Fei’s talent, he knew exactly what Han Fei’s status was. So when Han Fei arrived in Qin, he gave him full courtesy—it was no exaggeration to say it was many times better than the treatment Han Fei received in Han. But he had delayed seeing Han Fei, wanting to grind down some of his arrogance. At the very least, he didn't want him to be resistant or even harbor anger the moment he saw the King of Qin.

It had only been a few days, and Han Fei couldn't wait?

Ying Zheng ordered someone to bring Han Fei in.

After a while, seeing that it was not Han Fei who entered first, but Xu Fu and Li Si, Ying Zheng understood why Han Fei had come so early.

"Grant him a seat," Ying Zheng said coldly and indifferently.

Han Fei looked directly at Ying Zheng, but was eventually suppressed by his majesty and had to look away. Han Fei was secretly alarmed. Every King of Qin had been warlike, and this one was so heroic! If he were even slightly careless, Han might truly be destroyed in his hands.

The three sat down.

Han Fei still did not know who Xu Fu was, so he looked toward him.

Xu Fu returned a cold gaze, and Han Fei felt the pressure of his presence, forcing him to look away again. His guesses about Xu Fu’s identity became varied and chaotic.

Seeing Han Fei staring in Xu Fu’s direction for a long time without looking away, Ying Zheng’s expression darkened. He said, "I admire Master Han’s great talent. Now that you have arrived in Qin, I have a question: are you willing to stay in Qin and realize your ambitions here?"

Ying Zheng was very generous. To those who came to him with real ability and could contribute significantly to the cause of unification, he would never be stingy.

Like Li Si, who was promoted to Chief Scribe upon arrival—what was the status of a Chief Scribe? It was at the center of Qin’s political hub.

And Wei Liao—although he didn't like Wei Liao, Wei Liao had ability, so he appointed him as the State Minister of War. What was the status of the State Minister of War? The highest administrative official in the military.

Now, a bright path lay before Han Fei, depending on whether he chose it or not.

Ying Zheng’s mind was very clear: if Han Fei did not choose it, he would have no choice but to keep him in Qin by force.

Li Si shook his head secretly.

Just as Han Fei was about to open his mouth, Xu Fu suddenly interrupted him, "Master Han, may I borrow something of yours to observe?"

"What?" Han Fei was stunned.

Xu Fu waited patiently.

"What thing?" Han Fei asked.

A rare, faint smile appeared on Xu Fu’s face, "I wish to borrow Master Han’s face and hands for a look."

徐福不知道之前尉缭到底给了老太卜多大的刺激，如今老太卜竟然待他如此耐心和气，完全不符合他脑子里的构想，这也就罢了，老太卜竟然还觉得他是个温和好学上进低调的人。
天知道有些词一辈子也跟他扯不上关系。
实在扛不住老太卜寄予厚望的目光，徐福点头，为这番交谈画上了总结的句号。
“今日多谢老太卜一番肺腑之言，徐福铭记于心。”徐福不是年轻气盛的小子，他可不会在冲动之下，说什么一定不辜负老太卜的期望。承诺是不能乱给的，要是胡乱给错了，那就是活生生给自己立一个flag，之后总要被打脸的。
老太卜没能听到想要的话，面上一闪而过失望之色，不过徐福话都说到这里了，他也只能命人将徐福送出塔去。
待到徐福出去之后，老太卜望着他的背影，叹了声，“还是年轻了些，说话竟是这样老实，外表瞧上去那样灵气一个孩子，却不知半分讨巧……”
徐福若是听见那老太卜所言，一定觉得冤死了。
他老实？
那这世上也难寻几个不老实的人了。
老太卜的住处不是谁都能进去的，徐福一出来，秦王寝宫中的宫人便立即迎了上来，个个目光焦灼地看着他，问道：“徐典事无事吧？”
“无事。”看他们担心的模样，估计是对上次尉缭与老太卜杠起来，心有余悸了。
徐福回去之后不久，嬴政便也回到寝宫中了。
“王上选了我做主持蜡祭的人？”徐福当即便问出了心中的疑问。
嬴政点了点头，挥开衣角，在桌案前跽坐下来，他抬起头看着徐福，口气淡然，道：“有一日，你睡得迷糊时，对寡人道，你想做国师。”
徐福回想了一下，好像……好像是说过这话。
当时他好像乍然从梦中醒来，那瞬间还格外的清醒。
徐福突然觉得口舌有些发干，他不自觉地咽了咽口水，嬴政真的将他那一刻的话放在心上了？这是准备……为他铺路？
蜡祭在秦国的重要性之大，不管是去年他参加时的感受也好，还是今年老太卜对他千万嘱咐也好，都能看出一二来。秦国百姓们或许不知奉常寺为何物，太卜署为何物，但他们定然知晓主持蜡祭的人是谁。若是在蜡祭上露了脸，自然就会让百姓们记住，得了民心，受了百姓的拥戴，有了这样的基础，日后要做国师，那还不是水到渠成的事吗？
这样一条通天之路，就简简单单被铺在了他的脚边。
当初他选择走嬴政这道后门，似乎是选对了？
徐福也挥开衣角，在嬴政身边坐下，道：“王上，今日老太卜叫我过去了一趟。”
嬴政不着痕迹地皱了皱眉，小小地表达了一番，对“王上”这个称呼的不满。“老太卜唤你去了？他可有为难你？”嬴政顿了顿，道：“老太卜本身厉害，也有几分气傲，若是说话令你不快了，你也勿要放在心上。他年纪大了，总会退下这个位置的。”
看来所有人都以为那老太卜会欺负他？
但他又不是什么好欺负的人！
徐福无奈摇头，“老太卜并未说令我不快的话，反倒是……”
“反倒是什么？”
“他似乎乐于见到我去接替蜡祭主持的位置，对我好生说了一番鼓励的话，顺便再告诉我，若是搞砸了蜡祭，那可就是大麻烦了。”徐福口气又轻又淡，全然没将老太卜的话放在心上。不是他不认真，而是他没必要杞人忧天。若是时时刻刻惦念着不要搞砸，那才容易搞砸呢。
嬴政皱了皱眉，对于老太卜这番带有压力的话有些不满。不过他还是为徐福解答了心中的疑惑，“蜡祭曾是老太卜一力负责，后来吕不韦选了奉常寺的田太祝接替老太卜的位置，老太卜便对那田太祝心生不满了。若没有田太祝，他便不至于早早从位置上退下来，手中一干权力也跟着丢失了。此时你又要接替田太祝……”
嬴政说到一半，徐福便悟了。
大约就是那么个意思，“敌人的敌人，就是我的朋友”。
徐福顿觉，这些人心思弯弯绕，自己有时还真看不透。
嬴政笑道：“如此也好，之后便无人能阻你的脚步了。”
也算是一种幸运了。徐福暗自感叹了一声。
蜡祭过后，他离国师之路又更近一步了。徐福骤然轻松了起来，主持蜡祭，坑爹就坑爹吧，只要能值得就好。
嬴政的目光又不自觉地落在了徐福的脸庞上。
为君王者，向来称孤道寡，纵使后宫子女成群，也依旧是孤身一人。
曾经嬴政也是这样以为的，他这一生或许便只奔着大业去了，再没有旁的心思分割出来。直到这时，嬴政才觉得并非如此。他甘愿分出几分心思放在徐福的身上，只愿他大业得成那一日，徐福也同他的携手并立。
徐福慢半拍地转过头来，迎上嬴政的目光，道：“这样是很好。”
……
奉常寺上下都未曾想到，蜡祭的主持人选这么快便定下来了，竟然真的是徐福！顿时令人有种意料之中，又意料之外的感觉。有的人心中难免有些酸气，只觉徐福这一路走得未免也太过顺风顺水了，在这讲究家世背景和资历的奉常寺中，才前后不到一年，便要主持蜡祭了，实在是人比人，气死人！
苏邑与徐福交好，难免有的人就酸到苏邑跟前去了。
“苏兄与徐典事交情颇深，何不从徐典事那里也讨个重要的职务来呢？”
“对啊，说起来，苏兄才为太祝，苏兄才当是主持蜡祭的好人选呢……”
“是啊，要论资格，应当苏兄为先才是……”
苏邑面带不耐之色，偏偏那两人没看出苏邑的不快来。此时正好王柳又从旁边路过，那两人更来劲儿了，叫住王柳，道：“就算不说苏兄，那王太卜也更有资历和背景啊，偏偏我们谁也选不上，啧啧……”
王柳顿住脚步，回过头来，冷冷地瞥了那两人一眼。
两人不自觉地住了嘴，这才想起这王柳还是昔日奉常寺中的小霸王呢。自从去年王柳与徐福比试后，便低调了不少，众人都快忘记他的本性了，现在见他面色不虞，两人才反应过来，王柳的脾气并不好，也根本不好得罪。
他们可不是第二个徐福，能保证得罪了王柳，还能安然无恙。
“你们连徐典事是何来头也不知晓，就在这里随意搬弄，口上逞能可让你们得到这个机会了？不过嘴里冒些酸气！”王柳开口可丝毫不客气。
那二人被他说得脸上一阵臊。
就连苏邑都不由得多看了王柳一眼。
若说从前，王柳比起他们也好不到哪里去，只是那时王柳不会自降身份，同人在背后酸来酸去。王柳现在好像真的彻底变了一样。
那二人越想越觉得下不来台，再想到从前王柳也不是个什么好货色，现在来教训他们，也不知道装的什么！
他们自然不甘咽下这口气，于是便不服气地反问道：“难道王太卜知晓徐典事是什么来头不成？”
莫说这二人了，就是苏邑都不由得看向了王柳，满眼都是惊讶好奇之色。
苏邑与徐福算是走得极为近了，但他都不知徐福究竟什么来头，王柳如何能知道？
三人却见王柳冷笑一声，道：“鬼谷你们可知？刚被封为国尉的尉缭先生你们可知？徐典事便与国尉为同出鬼谷的师兄弟！你们说他是什么来头？”
鬼谷门下出了多少厉害人物，七国都是有所耳闻的。
且不说鬼谷，就单说那尉缭，名声也是颇为响亮的。
二人对视一眼，讪讪离去。从前都当徐福没有来头，谁知道人家不是没有来头，只是捂住了，怕吓着别人。现在想来，也只能心中各自羡慕嫉妒恨了。这样好命，那也是人家的！
王柳也正要离去，却被苏邑一把拽住了。
“你如何知道徐典事的来历？”苏邑微微皱眉，看着王柳问道。
王柳翻了个白眼给他，“若是你多关注徐典事几分，便会知道，国尉来奉常寺中寻过徐典事好几次。”
王柳说完便挣脱他的手臂，大步离去了。
苏邑怔了怔，半晌才叹道：“……徐典事，果真非常人也。”鬼谷的弟子，哪里是常人能与之比较的？也怪不得徐典事能走到今天这一步了！倒是那些想要看笑话的人，恐怕要教他们失望了……

郑国还在竭力争取修建水渠的时候，徐福已经开始准备蜡祭了。
那一日王柳与二人的对话不知不觉便飞遍了整个奉常寺，虽然他们没有亲眼见到尉缭是如何来找徐福的，但他们心中已经隐隐升起了畏惧与敬意。甚至还有人私下拍着马屁，道，早就看出徐福非同凡响了，今日一看，果然！乃是鬼谷出来的弟子！自然是比旁人要厉害几分的！
对于这些私底下的议论，徐福都是一律装作不知晓。
他也没有多余的时间去理会。
与单单去瞧蜡祭是全然不同的，他作为主持蜡祭的人，头一件事便是要将蜡祭上的唱词给背下来。
徐福还隐约记得去年那一日，主持的人口中吟唱歌词，口音还有些奇怪，但听起来却觉得说不出的舒服和神秘悠远。
徐福觉得……挺难为五音不全的自己。
不过这个他不会唱，嬴政却会，嬴政便手把手地教他，个中艰难就不赘述，不过也算是添了几分“房中之趣”。如果腰酸背疼一番过后，还记不住的话，那就活该腰酸背疼了！如此折腾几日后，徐福终于会背了。
除此之外，他还要了解各种反复的礼仪，其中最令徐福觉得难以忍受的，就是到了那一日，他是没饭吃的，必须等到蜡祭结束之后，晚上举行大宴了，他方才有机会进食。
徐福盯着竹简上关于这一点的记载，整个人都坐得直挺挺的，一脸生无可恋的冷漠表情。
嬴政从旁瞥到这一点，也不由得皱了皱眉。上回徐福便是在蜡祭之后晕了过去，这次几乎是整整一天都要不进水米，那如何能行？什么规矩，什么禁忌，瞬间都被嬴政抛到了脑后去。
“这一日寡人会命人为你准备好饭食，早起之后便先用饭食，用了之后再处理蜡祭之事。”
嬴政都如此主动地通情达理了，徐福又不是矫情的人，当然马上顺着杆子往上爬，脸上展露了点儿笑意，“多谢王……阿政。”说到那里，他硬生生地改了口。
嬴政对他这样体贴周全，他总是要给嬴政一点甜头吃的嘛。
嬴政闻言，脸上的神色果然骤然温和了不少。
徐福瞥见他脸上细微的表情变化，不由得有些沾沾自喜。原来哪怕是秦始皇，也并非那样难对付的啊。哦不，或许只是因为自己太聪明了而已。
徐福合上竹简，那些内容他基本已经能倒背如流了，待到蜡祭时，只要没有什么天灾人祸，那他就不可能出问题。
嬴政心中顿觉愉悦，他正要拥着徐福度过接下来的二人时间，却突然见扶苏从殿外走了进来，“老师！”扶苏一走进来，见着嬴政拥住徐福的模样，呆住了。
嬴政脸色微黑，心中默念三声，父子感情不能破坏！父子感情不能破坏！父子感情不能破坏！
扶苏依旧呆立在那里。
其实他是在暗自琢磨，怎么悄无声息地溜出去，免得让父王盯上不识时务跑来瞎搅合的自己。
而嬴政瞧了瞧扶苏呆住的模样，却以为他是被自己和徐福的关系给吓住了。
“扶苏，过来。”嬴政出声道。
徐福将手边的竹简推到一边去，倒是一副临危不乱的模样，丝毫没有被抓住奸情的慌乱或者羞耻等等……情绪。
扶苏忐忑不已地挪动着小碎步，顿在嬴政的跟前。
完了……
扶苏心中叫糟。
徐福左瞥一眼，右瞥一眼，总觉得这父子俩的脑回路没对上。
嬴政抬手摸了摸扶苏的头顶，语气温和地问道：“自你母亲离去后，可有不顺心之处？”
扶苏愣愣地摇头，“没有。”如果说有，他总觉得自己会被宰了。
嬴政轻叹一声，道：“你如今年纪也不算小了，应当明事理了。我与你老师……”
“等等，他能听明白吗？”徐福不由得打断了嬴政。
扶苏虽然看上去机灵又格外的精，但男男之事，他也能懂？没这么早熟的孩子吧……
徐福正想着呢，就见扶苏点头，道：“扶苏知道父王喜欢老师，老师与父王的关系，就如同……如同夫妻的关系。”扶苏脸上还露出了“我很认真”的表情。
徐福：“……”还真有这么早熟的孩子啊！
嬴政和徐福都沉默了，他们都不由得怀疑起，是不是他们做了坏的表率，把年幼的扶苏给带坏了？
“父王，扶苏说错什么了吗？”见他们二人面色都不太对，扶苏不由得低声道。
他说的也没错……
嬴政当即便大大方方摊开来，道：“你并未说错，父王与你老师的关系正是如此。”
扶苏面色平淡地点点头，“那扶苏就不打扰父王与老师了……”说着他便转身迈着短腿往外走了。他如此漫不经心的态度，反倒让徐福和嬴政有些无所适从。
嬴政轻叹一声，反倒有些心疼自己的长子了，“或许是性子向着郑妃，他向来不需要寡人操心什么。”
“扶苏公子是有着同龄人都没有的成熟稳重。”
嬴政笑道：“才几岁？就成熟稳重？”嬴政突然顿住，道：“不过也是有特例，比如你，外表稳重，内心不也像个孩子么？扶苏想来便是与你相反的。”
徐福脸色一黑，瞬间装起了高冷，不搭理嬴政了。
他像孩子？
他浑身上下哪里像了？
嬴政都把他给上了，那嬴政是恋童癖吗！
嬴政见他面色冷然，一副“不屑与凡夫俗子说话”的模样，面上忍不住又露出了笑意，“哈哈，寡人不说此话便是……”
二人又乱七八糟地扯了几句，这才去用饭食了。
