"Take him away!" he shouted.

Someone stepped forward to grab Liu Fengchang.

Perhaps it was a case of "breaking the jar because it's already cracked," but he tore off the last bit of dignity he had left and threw it on the ground himself.

He actually sat down on the ground, refusing to budge, and shouted, "Wang Liu! You are truly heartless! How have I treated you? Yet now you watch as I am bullied by Xu Fu! You won't even offer the slightest bit of help!"

Wang Liu’s expression turned cold, and he felt extremely displeased. He had already repaid the favor for Liu Fengchang’s recommendation. If not for him, how could the matter involving Liu Fengchang’s wife’s younger brother have been resolved so easily? Wang Liu was also angered by Liu Fengchang’s shameless behavior and blurted out, "Grand Diviner Liu, I have already repaid the favor for your recommendation. Why must you still deliberately drag me into this in front of others? You are truly shameless!"

Xu Fu noticed what Wang Liu said and instinctively felt something was wrong, so he immediately asked, "What recommendation?"

By now, Wang Liu had calmed down and said in a low voice, "The recommendation for the position of Assistant Grand Diviner."

Upon hearing this, Xu Fu’s face darkened, and he frowned, "When did Grand Diviner Liu ever recommend you for the position of Assistant Grand Diviner?"

Wang Liu was stunned, "...He, I went to ask Grand Diviner Liu, and he said it was he who recommended me. Could it be... not?"

Meanwhile, Liu Fengchang was already curled up on the ground, wishing he could bury his face in the dirt. His heart was pounding like a drum, thumping against his chest. He tightened his breathing involuntarily, his mind spinning with dizziness, leaving only a few words: He was about to be exposed!

"Of course not." Xu Fu really wanted to sneer. He hadn't expected Liu Fengchang to be so bold as to claim credit for this, especially when he was standing right there. Liu Fengchang dared to use this to threaten Wang Liu; he didn't know whether to call him bold or just incredibly stupid.

The attendant also said in surprise, "Grand Diviner Wang must have misunderstood. When the bamboo slips were submitted back then, the person Grand Diviner Liu recommended was his nephew. He did not recommend Grand Diviner Wang." The attendant paused and said, "The one who recommended Grand Diviner Wang was Minister Xu. His Majesty values Minister Xu’s opinion highly, which is why he chose Grand Diviner Wang from among the candidates and promoted him to Assistant Grand Diviner." The attendant even thought to himself that Minister Xu was truly kind-hearted. Judging by what was said just now, Wang Liu and Minister Xu had a history, yet Minister Xu was still magnanimous enough to recommend him, allowing him to become an Assistant Grand Diviner...

Such breadth of mind!

It is truly beyond the reach of ordinary people!

In fact, it wasn't just the attendant; everyone in the Fengchang Temple, including Wang Liu and Su Yi, were stunned after hearing this, thinking exactly the same thing as the attendant.

They had to admit that the reason he could reach the position of Minister at such a young age was because he was inherently excellent and broad-minded, capable of tolerating others. Such a person... was the most suitable for divination.

After Wang Liu processed this, his heart was filled with a complex mix of shock, anger, and embarrassment.

He hadn't expected that Xu Fu really didn't hold a grudge against him. Seeing Xu Fu’s cold attitude toward him on weekdays, he had assumed Xu Fu still remembered his past mistakes. Every time this happened, Wang Liu would secretly think that this was what he deserved; if he hadn't insisted on making things difficult for Xu Fu, how would he have invited Xu Fu’s dislike? But he really hadn't expected that Xu Fu had long since let it go... and had even recommended him for the position of Assistant Grand Diviner! He knew the relationship between Xu Fu and His Majesty; if Xu Fu spoke up... his position as Assistant Grand Diviner was indeed secure.

But looking at Liu Fengchang again.

He clearly hadn't recommended him, yet he shamelessly took credit for it. He had helped Liu Fengchang, and now Liu Fengchang was using this non-existent favor to threaten him!

His baseness is such that even if you used all the bamboo in Jing and Yue, you couldn't write it all down!

"Grand Diviner Liu, to claim credit for someone else’s work and be this shameless, you have truly opened my eyes!" Wang Liu sneered, his gaze icy as he looked at Liu Fengchang.

Liu Fengchang shivered and could no longer say a word.

It’s over... it’s over... everything is over now...

Liu Fengchang felt no shame, nor did he think he had done anything wrong. His first thought was that he would likely lose his position and face punishment...

The attendant sneered, "I have never seen such a person. I fear even His Majesty will find it astonishing when he hears of this. I think Grand Diviner Liu should feel happy, after all, he gets to show his face before His Majesty..."

To be reported to His Majesty?

Liu Fengchang could still remember how His Majesty had raged at the Fengchang Temple when someone fainted during the Great Exorcism. Thinking of it today, his legs still felt weak, and his heart was shrouded in fear.

The more he thought about it, the more terrified Liu Fengchang became, even associating it with the way the Marquis of Changxin died...

Thinking of this, Liu Fengchang actually fainted dead away.

The person holding him gave a disdainful snort and dragged him out.

Xu Fu had no desire to stay any longer. Liu Fengchang’s ability to disgust people was truly top-tier! To secure a position as a Minister, he had exposed his own ugly nature! His original assessment of him had truly not wronged Liu Fengchang at all!

Seeing the grand drama conclude, the crowd dispersed with their own thoughts.

They couldn't help but think that if someone like Wang Liu, who had offended Xu Fu, could still benefit from him, wouldn't it be even easier for them?

Unfortunately, Xu Fu was already walking away, and they didn't dare to stop him. They now realized that Xu Fu was not someone to be trifled with; he feared no one. If they went up to offend him at an inappropriate time, it would be bad. Liu Fengchang’s behavior just now must have made Xu Fu unhappy, so they decided it was better to wait a while before trying to befriend him.

Once the crowd dispersed, only Wang Liu and Su Yi remained.

Wang Liu gritted his teeth secretly, hesitated for a moment, and then followed Xu Fu.

"Many thanks, Minister Xu." Wang Liu bowed respectfully.

Su Yi said calmly, "I never imagined that it was Minister Xu who recommended Assistant Grand Diviner Wang."

Upon hearing this, Wang Liu turned his head and glared at him, quite unhappily, "Do you think I am not worthy of being this Assistant Grand Diviner?"

Su Yi shook his head, "That is not what I meant..."

"That Grand Diviner Liu is a nuisance. I am going to check his list of crimes; you two can chat amongst yourselves." Xu Fu’s mind was no longer here, and after saying this, he stepped out of the Fengchang Temple.

Wang Liu, who had been waiting to properly thank Xu Fu, was stunned, feeling a bit bitter in his heart. Only someone like Liu Fengchang would hold such a favor in his hands to threaten others, while someone like Xu Fu didn't even consider this favor worth mentioning.

Liu Fengchang had used a favor to demand repayment, which made him unhappy, but now that Xu Fu didn't want his repayment, he felt uncomfortable instead.

Su Yi glanced at his expression and frowned, "Don't stare blankly."

Wang Liu came back to his senses and said unhappily, "When did I stare blankly? It was clearly you who was staring blankly!"

Su Yi frowned, thinking to himself not to argue with Wang Liu, and turned to leave.

Wang Liu glared at his back, feeling unhappy. It was clearly Su Yi who didn't know his place, coveting Minister Xu! Why was Su Yi blaming him instead? What a weird temper! He’s sick!

Su Yi also thought Wang Liu was sick. He used to be at odds with Minister Xu, and now he admired him—if that’s not sick, what is?

·

Xu Fu didn't know where Liu Fengchang had been taken, and there was no young attendant waiting for him outside. Xu Fu didn't delay and set off on foot toward the royal palace. In any case, the palace guards already knew him, so it didn't matter if he didn't take the carriage.

Meanwhile, the attendant who announced the royal decree ran fast and had already arrived at the palace to report to Ying Zheng.

Ying Zheng had known long ago that Xu Fu had encountered trouble at the Fengchang Temple, but at that time, he had no interest in Xu Fu at all. They were strangers, and Xu Fu only had a utilitarian value to him. Why would he care about such a person? But now, hearing the attendant mention it again, Ying Zheng’s memories returned, and he felt furious!

Now that he had changed his identity and become Xu Fu’s lover, he naturally found it hard to tolerate anyone bullying Xu Fu. Thinking back on the past, Ying Zheng felt that Liu Fengchang was truly detestable!

Dismissing him from office was letting him off too easily.

The attendant then recounted how Liu Fengchang had caused a scene at the Fengchang Temple. Ying Zheng’s face turned as cold as water, and he didn't say a word for a long time.

The attendant lowered his head, trembling, knowing that Ying Zheng was truly enraged.

"Your Majesty... that Grand Diviner Liu... how should he be dealt with..."

The bamboo knife in Ying Zheng’s hand carved a long, deep mark into the bamboo slip, showing how much force he had just used.

"Why did I choose this person to be a Fengchang in the first place?"

Zhao Gao, standing by, bowed and said, "Your Majesty, the position of Fengchang was originally chosen by Lu Buwei, and later replaced by a person of the traitor Lao Ai."

No wonder... that Lao Ai was just a thug from the streets; what kind of eye for talent could he have? Choosing this person was just to annoy Lu Buwei! Ying Zheng hadn't paid attention to this before, and since the Fengchang Temple wasn't that important, he hadn't removed him. But now, counting them up, Ying Zheng realized this person had so many intolerable crimes!

"Bring him before me," Ying Zheng said coldly.

The attendant was stunned and looked up, "Your Majesty?" How was Grand Diviner Liu worthy of seeing His Majesty? Wouldn't it be better to just kill him?

But no matter how confused the attendant was, he didn't dare to question Ying Zheng’s decision, so he stood up and said, "This servant will go at once."

Grand Diviner Liu...

What a Grand Diviner Liu!

The stylus in Ying Zheng’s hand was stabbed into the bamboo slip.

Zhao Gao glanced at the stylus from the side and secretly lit a candle for Grand Diviner Liu in his heart.

Not long after, Grand Diviner Liu was brought into the hall. Seeing the limp lump on the ground, Ying Zheng asked, "What is wrong with him?"

The attendant said, "Replying to Your Majesty, he was scared unconscious."

"Scared unconscious?" Ying Zheng’s lips curled into a cold smile, "Splash him awake." This person was truly useless. When he was arguing with Xu Fu, why didn't he look this cowardly? He must have thought of Xu Fu as a soft persimmon to be squeezed! But he had to see if I would let you squeeze him!

Not to mention he was now a Grand Diviner, even if he were a Fengchang, a mere small Fengchang! What is he?

He isn't even worthy of carrying Xu Fu’s shoes!

Palace servants brought water and splashed it on his face. It was midsummer, so the water wasn't bone-chilling, but rather refreshing. Even so, Grand Diviner Liu shivered violently and woke up from his faint, scrambling up from the ground, "Where is this? Where is this?" He was too flustered and shouted without looking. When he calmed down, he saw Ying Zheng sitting above. This one look almost made the terrified Grand Diviner faint again.

"Your, Your Majesty..." Grand Diviner Liu prostrated himself on the ground, not daring to lift his head.

This was his first time meeting His Majesty alone, but he never expected it to be in such a situation.

Just then, a palace maid entered and said, "Your Majesty, Young Master Fusu and Minister Xu have arrived."

Grand Diviner Liu heard "Minister Xu" and shivered again. He had chased after him to kill him...

Grand Diviner Liu finally knew how to fear Xu Fu, but it was too late.

Ying Zheng raised an eyebrow at the maid, "Fusu and Minister Xu came together?"

The maid nodded.

"Invite them in." Ying Zheng’s tone softened involuntarily.

Before long, Xu Fu walked in holding Fusu’s hand. The palace servants didn't find it strange to see them in such a posture. Even if one day Young Master Fusu were to call Minister Xu his foster father, they wouldn't find it strange.

Xu Fu had met Fusu on the way; Fusu was coming to ask Ying Zheng for advice, and Xu Fu was coming to find Ying Zheng to watch the fun, so they came in together.

Seeing Xu Fu, Ying Zheng felt even more heartbroken. Thinking about how he hadn't cared about Xu Fu’s plight before, and that this Grand Diviner Liu had dared to make Xu Fu clean the latrines, Ying Zheng felt an irrepressible rage surging in his chest.

As soon as Fusu entered, he paid his respects with Xu Fu, then looked curiously at the soaked Grand Diviner Liu and asked, "Father, who is this?"

Ying Zheng said with a cold face, "This is the villain who once bullied your teacher." Liu Fengchang heard the chilling tone and shivered again.

"Bullied teacher?" Hearing this, Fusu raised his eyebrows, stepped forward quickly, and ordered the palace servants nearby, "Lift this villain’s face up. Let me see what kind of formidable person he is to dare bully my teacher!"

Grand Diviner Liu felt his head spinning.

What... what teacher?

Xu Fu is the teacher of the eldest son, Fusu?

Grand Diviner Liu’s breathing became cautious; he wished he could faint right then and there. How... how could he have made such a huge mistake!

"I thought he had two noses and two mouths... turns out he looks so ordinary..."

Xu Fu said faintly behind him, "Who said he looks ordinary? Compared to others, he is more than a little ugly..."

Fusu laughed, "Teacher is right, exactly! Teacher once told me that the appearance is born from the heart. This villain, with such an ugly face and a wretched demeanor, shows how base his heart is!"

Fusu turned to Ying Zheng and asked, "Father, how did he bully Teacher? Let me get it back for Teacher now."

Xu Fu and Ying Zheng looked at Fusu with some surprise.

Fusu looked like a normal person of his age now.

As the eldest son of the King of Qin, he was so young, yet he had no arrogance? He didn't bully others? He was usually calm beyond his years. But now, seeing him demand justice for Xu Fu, his cold and angry face made him look more like a young child of noble birth.

"It wasn't a big deal. He once ordered me to clean the latrines. But I didn't do it."

Fusu widened his eyes upon hearing this.

Let Teacher clean the latrines?

Let someone with such an ethereal temperament as Teacher...

"How dare he!" Fusu kicked Grand Diviner Liu in the waist, "Beat him!"

The palace servants looked at Ying Zheng, and seeing him smiling, what else was there to say? Of course, they stepped forward to beat him! Young Master Fusu was right! This person was truly detestable! How dare he give such an order to Minister Xu! Minister Xu...

That is Minister Xu, who is like a god descended to earth...

At this moment, Fusu didn't know what kind of idea he had, but suddenly said, "Father, why not bring Huhai here..."

"What for?" Ying Zheng frowned. Why bring Huhai to such a scene?

Fusu said, "Naturally, to let Huhai urinate on him..."

Xu Fu: "..."

It’s over...

Young Master Fusu has truly been led astray by him!

chapters.source_text:
苏邑凉凉地看了他一眼，直接代替徐福出了声，“有何处不服？徐典事……徐奉常本事卓绝，屡立大功。做个奉常，有何不对？”苏邑这话就是在往刘奉常心上扎。
那刘奉常脸色臊红一片，不由得想到，打自己做了奉常后，的确是没办过什么令人称道的事儿，半点出风头的时候都没有。甚至有人都不记得他这个奉常的存在。反观徐福，虽为新人，但却从来了奉常寺后，就屡屡出风头。
刘奉常心中憋着一股火气，他怎么能容忍自己被指为没本事呢？或许刘奉常心中多少是有点感觉的，大约知晓自己是个什么货色，但越是知晓，才越不愿意承认，尤其是在这样的时刻，哪怕硬撑，他也要梗着脖子发泄出胸中的不服气。不然的话，他的颜面……从何挽留？
“他屡立大功？”刘奉常冷笑一声，道：“不过是机会全到了他跟前去罢了！他一介新人，乃是后辈，难道功劳还能越过我们去吗？”刘奉常无非能抓住的也就是徐福是新人这一点了。
若是平日刘奉常哪敢这样说话？也不过是因为奉常之位，就是他心头捂着的命根子罢了。怎么样都好，平日里他可以卑躬屈膝，处处巴结，可以忍受熊义之流的呼来喝去，但触碰到他这个位置的时候，他憋着的那股劲儿就全爆发出来了。
他死死地盯着徐福，模样实在有些可怖。
众人都是一怔，没想到刘奉常也会有这样的一面。
……他莫不是受刺激大发了？疯了吧？
这内侍还没走呢，他就要与徐福争执起来，这是要连面子里子都不要吗？
刘奉常或许平日自己不知，但他在奉常寺中得罪的人可着实不少了，这些人多数都是看着他的笑话，他和徐福搁一块儿，大家还更乐意留着徐福呢。好歹徐福他恩怨分明，不会踩低捧高，行事公正啊！他那气运旁人是羡慕不来了，但端看他做了典事之后，主持月末卜筮是个什么模样，众人心里便有个数了，知晓他会放纵手底下的人去露脸，而不是自己一味强占。
刘奉常并不知自己连人心都失了，他想到平日里奉常寺上下对徐福的议论，心中便觉得有了底气。这些人总不会甘心眼看着徐福上位吧？
徐福的目光轻飘飘地落在了他的身上，徐福神色冷淡，瞧不出喜怒，只慢悠悠道：“原来刘奉常是这般看我的……”
刘奉常根本不敢对上徐福的目光，他避开了徐福的视线，暗暗咬牙，既然已经得罪他了，那今天势必要将徐福得罪个死了！为了奉常之危……他决不能就此放弃！刘奉常甚至连后果都不敢去想。
他本能地拒绝去思考徐福在王上跟前是个什么地位，若是这些细细一思考，他就什么勇气也没了，等他灰溜溜地离开这里，第二日，他便会成为奉常寺的笑柄！
对于爱颜面的刘奉常来说，这如何能忍？
那内侍已经有些不耐了，原本是个喜事，不知道从哪里出来一根搅屎棍，偏偏要将这喜事搅坏，那徐奉常还如何能高兴得起来？此事办砸了，那还了得？
“既然刘太卜如此说，那便与我干脆去仔细争辩一番！哦，刘太卜可还要腆着脸皮去问一问，王上为何撤了你的职？”内侍冷着脸走到他的跟前，那内侍却是比刘奉常高上一些，瞬间便令刘奉常感觉到了压迫。
刘……太卜？
被当众如此一叫，刘奉常登时觉得丢脸至极，旁人投来的目光都像是带着嘲讽一般，如同根根锋利的针扎在他的身上，令他无地自容。
刘奉常的战力实在不怎么样，连内侍都说不过，还妄图挑衅自己？夺回奉常之位？
徐福瞧着刘奉常窘迫臊红的模样，都替他尴尬。不过哪怕他如今的模样看上去再可怜，徐福也不会容忍他来抹黑质疑自己。你弱又不是理由，你自己本事不成，难道便能成为你肆意抹黑质疑他人的借口吗？
“还请刘太卜说一说，我可曾抢了刘太卜表现的机会？听刘太卜的口气，身为新人，不管做了何等有功于秦的事，那都不能算作功劳是吗？”徐福顿了顿，回头问那内侍，“那日我在小朝上卜筮时，曾听王上说起，我大秦，皆是论功劳封赏，可是如此？”
内侍笑道：“正是如此。”
若非这个命令，又怎么能吸引得他国有才之人，统统奔往秦国来呢？
“看来刘太卜对王令有所不满啊……”徐福才不管那么多，这刘奉常非要找事，他便不客气，他做这奉常，光明正大，堂堂正正，他丝毫不心虚，他全凭本事而得，凭什么还要来看刘奉常的脸色？于是当即便扣了个大帽子在刘奉常的头上。他少在奉常寺中出现，也久久不与人进行口头上的交锋，这些人想必是忘记他的言辞能如何刺人了。
“你……你胡说……我……我并无此意……”刘奉常一下子就慌了，甚至还往后退了退，他强自定了定心神，怒道：“徐典事何必如此污蔑我？”
徐福打断了他，“哦？刘太卜没有证据指责我，那不是污蔑？而我用刘太卜自己说的话，来反驳刘太卜，反倒成了污蔑了？”
一声声刘太卜响在耳边，点燃了刘奉常胸中的怒火。
“徐典事不过是报复我罢了！”刘奉常气喘吁吁地高喝一声，“你初入奉常寺时，我不过是命你去洒扫茅厕，那时你便用言语威胁我……徐典事真是好宽厚的心胸！”
众人都不由得竖起了耳朵。
用言语威胁？
命徐福去洒扫茅厕？
原来当初还有这么一出戏啊！有趣有趣！瞧上去今日之事不能轻易了了！
哪怕这么多双眼睛都瞧过来了，徐福也是不慌不忙的，着重念了刘奉常话中的两个词，“不过？威胁？”徐福突然轻笑了一声，奉常寺上下都惊了惊，他们可还没见过徐福轻笑的时候，乍见徐福消去一脸冰霜，轻笑起来，除了被那抹笑容晕眩了一下以外，他们首先想到的便是，不常笑的人突然笑了，要么是极开心了，要么是心头极为不痛快了。
“刘太卜口中的话，也未免太过偏向自己了。”徐福面色骤然一冷，再不给刘奉常留面子，冷声道：“我初入奉常寺时，规规矩矩，不曾得罪于谁，刘奉常却恶意令身为太史的我，去做茅厕的洒扫，这叫‘不过’？看来在刘奉常眼中，利用手中特权，恶意欺压他人，也不过是常态了！我若记在心中，便是心胸狭隘了？”
“这……你……”刘太卜被说得说不出话来。
这的确是常态，可站在这里，当着这么多人，他不能如此说！何况旁边还站着一位内侍！他若是这样说了，会不会传进王上耳中去呢？
徐福哪会给他喘息的机会，当即便又道：“我初入奉常寺时，刘太卜恶意欺压我，我可曾责骂过刘太卜？后来我升为典事，可曾故意与刘太卜不对付过？如今奉常寺上下，哦不，如今想来秦国朝中官员，也都知晓我喜好为人相面。我不过是出于习惯，为刘太卜瞧了面相，便将刘太卜的面相据实相告。怎的反倒成了我威胁刘太卜了？那时我不过是个太史令！半点权力也没有！更尚未得到王上赏识，我如何能威胁堂堂奉常？”
苏邑听罢，冷笑道：“怕是刘太卜搞颠倒了吧！我瞧那时是刘太卜想要威胁徐奉常才是。只是刘太卜未曾想到有一日，徐奉常会接替了他的位置。”苏邑可不惧刘奉常，从前就不见得将他放在眼中，如今便更是如此。
被人赤裸裸地揭开心中所想，刘奉常当即便更觉羞窘，一脸怒色，指着苏邑，“……你……你！”
徐福这才慢慢道：“刘太卜可还有话说？不如我将当初为刘太卜下的批语，也说出来，同大家分享一番。”
其他人当然是求之不得的，他们如今都已知晓徐福那神通的本事，徐福那时究竟说了什么，能让刘奉常心中记到现在，他们可都好奇得很啊！
“你……”刘奉常被气得喘不上气来，竟是无法出口堵住徐福的声音，或者说，刘奉常已经被这一串问责的话给弄昏头了，不知道该如何反驳徐福了。
他又羞又窘，最可怕的是，他发现，徐福说的话，似乎……没有错……
内侍忙道：“不如便请徐奉常说出来吧。”
有人笑道：“正是，我们也想学习一番，徐奉常的大本事。”
此时那王柳站在一旁，听完了全程，心中也如同一把火在灼烧般，羞窘至极。当初将刘奉常叫来的人，可是他啊！若非他与徐福不对付，那刘奉常也不会不由分说，就罚了徐福。如此说来，他也逃不过这个罪责。如今再想一想，便觉得自己当初的作为多么可笑！再听刘奉常的辩解，也觉得十分可笑！
当初他和刘奉常是什么心思，他们各自都清楚得很，绝不是刘奉常如今装的那样无辜。
“当初我对刘太卜说了一句，裤子还没套稳，步子可别迈大了。可是如此？”
这话一出，没有听过这话的人，当即便笑出了声。暗道一句，这徐福的嘴其实也够损的啊！只是平日里冷漠示人，看上去不声不响的，谁在知道这人内里根本不是能受欺负的呢？
这话在众人面前被抖开，刘奉常如今哪还有半点面子可言？他有些退缩了，不想要遭受更多的嘲笑和讽刺。但是他已经骑虎难下了，从他开口表达心中不满开始，他就已经无法后退了。
苏邑问徐福：“此话何解？”
徐福道：“那时刘太卜刚做了奉常不久，又是意外得来了这个位置。我从他的脸上瞧得一清二楚。偏偏他刚当了奉常，便行事肆意，半分稳重也无，那时我便想，被褫夺官位也是迟早的事了，这才出声提醒刘太卜，不要太过得意忘形，失了奉常应有的气度。可惜……如今看来，刘太卜是半分也没将我的话听进去，反倒如今还倒过来指责我，实在威胁他。”
苏邑怒道：“这如何能算得威胁？这话依我瞧，分明是徐奉常不与他计较，还好心提醒他，谁知道刘太卜自个儿心是黑的，看别人，倒觉得别人心也是黑的！”
众人闻言，纷纷议论不已。他们既为徐福的断言如此之准感觉到惊奇，又为刘奉常那不知死活的模样感觉到可笑。
原来从那时起，刘奉常便已自己埋下祸根了，可笑他不知悔改，还倒打一耙。
内侍冷冷地看着刘奉常，不带半点笑意，问道：“如今，刘太卜可服气了？”
刘奉常被旁人不屑的目光瞧得满头大汗，仿佛自己整个人都摊开来被人瞧了一般，他张了张嘴，急于辩解，但那内侍根本不想听他说话，于是直接打断了他，“服气不服气，也都是如此了，如今恐怕还要请刘太卜随我走一趟。刘太卜罪名簿上可又要多一项了。”说罢，那内侍才凉凉地笑了。
“罪名簿？什么罪名簿？”刘奉常愣住了，忙结结巴巴地问道。
众人也都愣了愣，心思敏锐的，自然知道这绝对不是什么小事。这刘奉常恐怕……是要完了啊……
莫说他们，就连徐福都怔了怔，还有什么罪名簿？不过徐福心中可无半点同情。落得什么下场，全都是有因才有果，当初刘奉常是如何作死的，如今可不是全都偿还在自己身上了吗？
刘奉常懵了懵，脚下都有些站不稳了。
“怎会……怎会如此……”他恍惚了一阵，突然间骤然回过神来，大喊一声，“我要见王上！我要见王上！”可话说完，刘奉常自己心中的害怕却更甚了。是了，他找王上又有何用呢？他连见王上一面都难，而徐福却能自由出入王宫。孰轻孰重？王上能不知晓吗？届时，说不定等着他却是更重的惩罚。
“见王上？”徐福微微挑眉。
刘奉常顿觉徐福身上气势逼人，平白又矮了他许多，连声音都不自觉地讷讷了起来，“我……不……我、我不见王上……”
旁人见状，不由得嗤笑出声来，瞧这模样，可不是心虚吗？若不是心虚，怎么先说要见，后又不敢见了呢？
苏邑冷冷地看着刘奉常，“刘太卜以后可不要将脏水往徐奉常身上泼了……”他顿了顿，突然道：“当然，以后刘太卜也没这个机会了。”
刘奉常心中恐慌更甚，目光胡乱一扫，便扫到了一旁的王柳。
“王太卜……”刘奉常出声道，他的声音有些低，但随即他便更大声地叫道：“王太卜！”仿佛抓紧了什么救命稻草。
众人朝王柳身上看去，暗暗咋舌，这刘奉常是要死也拉着王柳一块儿啊？王柳这可才刚升了太卜丞呢，这刘奉常可真是够缺德的啊！
王柳此时也羞窘不已，尤其是再看苏邑那样维护徐福，他便更觉得胸中焦灼，直想骂苏邑有病！刘奉常也有病！
“王太卜救我！王太卜，当初为难徐福之人，可也有你在其中啊！”刘奉常大叫道。
这话当即又引起了一片窃窃私语。
这刘奉常的脑子当真是被驴踢了？幸好他不再做奉常了。不然这样的人，指不准什么时候便寻着你来挡矛头了。见谁咬谁，如恶狼一般，谁敢与之相交？
王柳站在中间，也感受到了方才刘奉常那样被无数目光打量的滋味。
当真是……自己种下的苦果，便要自己尝了！
王柳是真想出口骂刘奉常的，但是想到前些日子刘奉常才推举了自己，他如何能这么快就翻脸不认人？若是这样的话，他与那刘奉常又有何区别？他在徐福眼中，是不是依旧是过去那个王柳？
他憋着气，咬了咬牙，良久才道：“曾经莽撞之下，是与徐奉常起了龃龉，但之后，我与徐奉常已经和解。刘太卜此时何必将此牵扯出来？”
刘奉常却不信，如今徐福会对他冷眼相待，难道对王柳就能毫不计较了吗？不可能！
他惨笑道：“是，如今徐奉常便只记恨我一人了……”
“记恨？我何时记恨你了？说话要有证据，若是嘴皮子一碰便要污蔑我，刘太卜可别过了分。”徐福冷声道，随即对王柳道：“我与王太卜之间恩怨已销，王太卜还是到一旁去吧。”
王柳悬在胸口的那口气陡然松了。
而刘奉常没想到徐福真的会放过王柳，当即瞪大了眼，“不可能！徐奉常如今可是刻意要为难我一人？”
徐福实在懒得与他胡搅蛮缠下去，明明半分证据也没有，反倒是他自己罪行都可清晰数来，偏偏刘奉常就要装傻，非要往他刻意报复上扯。面对一个装睡的人，你能如何？那就是干脆给他一个永生难忘的疼痛教训！
“烦请内侍将他请走吧，这等人，不配站在我跟前，与我说话。”徐福一甩袖子，也不看他了，“真相如何，在场众人心中已有评判，到时候王上必然也另有评判。既然刘太卜不服，非要陷害我，那就让刘太卜去好好服一服气吧。”你不是说我记恨你吗？不是说我威胁你吗？我现在不记恨你，也不威胁你，我当场就把仇给报了，让你感受一下，真正被我记恨，那是什么滋味儿。
那内侍也被闹得有些烦，只是碍于徐福不发话，他也不敢随意胡来，免得反倒污了徐福的名声，令他人胡乱往徐福身上抹黑，如今听徐福下了令，他哪里还能等？
“把人带走！”他高声道。
有人上前来要去抓那刘奉常。
或许是破罐子破摔，他剩下的最后那点儿脸面，他自己也给撕了扔地上了。
他竟然直接一屁股坐在了地上，赖在了那里，口中还喊道：“王柳！你实在不厚道！我如何对你的？你如今却见着我被徐福欺侮！也不肯施半点援手！”
王柳面色冷了冷，心头十分不快。刘奉常举荐他的事，他可是已经还了人情了。若不是他，刘奉常夫人的胞弟之事，哪会这样轻易解决？王柳也是被刘奉常这副不要脸不要皮的模样，给气着了，脱口而出道：“刘太卜，你举荐我之事，我可是已经将情分还了，何必如今还故意在他人面前攀扯我？实在太不要脸！”
徐福注意到王柳口中所说的话，本能地觉得有些不对劲，当即便出声道：“什么举荐？”
此时王柳也冷静了下来，低声道：“太卜丞之位的举荐。”
听完，徐福脸色一黑，皱眉道：“太卜丞之位，刘太卜何曾举荐过你？”
王柳愣了愣，“……他，我去问刘太卜，他便说是他举荐的。难道……不是？”
而刘奉常此时已经蜷缩在了地上，恨不得将脸皮都藏到地里去才好，他心跳如擂鼓，咚咚咚，敲在胸膛里，他不自觉地紧了紧呼吸，脑子里眩晕一片，只剩下几个大字：他要被揭穿了！
“当然不是。”徐福是真的很想冷笑，他没想到刘奉常这样大的胆子，这也能往自己身上揽，何况自己还站在这跟前呢，刘奉常就敢以此来要挟王柳了，实在不知是说他胆子大好，还是说他实在蠢的没边儿了好。
内侍也惊讶道：“王太卜恐是误会了吧，当时竹简呈上来，刘太卜推举的却是他一个侄儿。并未推举王太卜。”内侍顿了顿，道：“推举王太卜的乃是徐奉常啊，王上极为重视徐奉常的意见，这才从众人中择选了王太卜，升为太卜丞。”那内侍都还暗自道，徐奉常实在善心呢。听方才所言，王柳与徐奉常也是有过节的，但徐奉常却能大义举荐，让人家做了太卜丞……
这份心胸！
实非常人能所及！
其实不止这内侍，就是包括王柳、苏邑在内的奉常寺上下人等，听过之后，也都愣了愣，与那内侍想到了一块儿去。
他们不得不承认，人家年纪轻轻，为何能这样快便坐上奉常的位置，盖因他本就优秀，又心胸广阔，能容纳他人，这样的人……才是最适合卜筮的。
而王柳回味过来之后，心中五味杂陈，又是震惊，又是愤怒，又是羞窘。
他没想到，徐福真的不与他计较了，他见平日里徐福对自己冷言冷语的，还当徐福依旧记着当初自己的错处呢，每当这时王柳都是暗道，这本该是自己承受的，若不是自己非要去为难徐福，又如何会惹得徐福不喜？但他真的没想到，徐福早就不记在心上了……竟然还推举了他做太卜丞！他知道徐福与王上是什么关系，徐福开口……他那太卜丞的位置的确是坐稳了。
可再看刘奉常。
明明并未推举他，却厚着脸皮认了，他出手帮了刘奉常，如今刘奉常还拿着这份根本不存在的恩情，来要挟他！
其卑劣，尽荆越之竹，犹不能书也！
“刘太卜冒认他人之功，脸皮如此之厚，实在令我开了眼界！”王柳冷笑一声，看着刘奉常的目光冰寒至极。
刘奉常打了个哆嗦，再难说出一句话来。
完了……完了……如今什么都完了……
刘奉常并未觉得羞愧，并未觉得自己有何处错了，他先想到的却是自己恐怕要丢了官位，还要遭责难了……
内侍冷笑道：“我也未见过这样的人，恐怕王上听了都会觉得惊奇呢，我瞧刘太卜也应当觉得欢喜了，毕竟也能在王上面前露个脸了……”
要告知被王上？
刘奉常如今还能忆得起，当初大傩时，因为有人晕死过去，王上对着奉常寺发起怒来，是何般模样，今日想起来，他都仍旧觉得双腿发软，内心蒙着一层恐惧。
越往下想，刘奉常便越觉得惊惧，甚至还联想到了那长信侯的死法……
这么一想，刘奉常竟是生生厥过去了。
押住他的人，鄙夷地轻嗤一声，押着人便出去了。
而徐福也没了继续留下来的心思，那刘奉常恶心人的本事，实在是一等一的！为了个奉常的位置，也是丑态毕露！当初他的批语，可真心没冤枉刘奉常！
众人见一场大戏落幕，这才心思各异地散去。
他们都不由得想，王柳这样得罪过徐福的人，尚且都能在徐福跟前讨到好处，那他们岂不是更容易了吗？
只可惜徐福拔腿要走，他们也不敢上前拦，如今他们也算看出来了，徐福是个不好惹的人，他不惧任何人，若是在不合时宜的时候，上去得罪了人，那可就不好了。方才刘奉常的做派，肯定让徐福心中不快，他们还是且等一等，再去与徐福结交也不迟。
众人一散，便只剩下了王柳与苏邑。
王柳暗暗咬牙，迟疑一会儿还是跟上了徐福。
“多谢徐奉常。”王柳恭恭敬敬地一拱手道。
苏邑淡淡道：“我都未能想到，竟是徐奉常举荐了王太卜。”
王柳听完，当即便转头横了他一眼，颇不高兴地道：“难不成你觉得不配做这太卜丞吗？”
苏邑摇头，“我可并非此意……”
“那刘太卜是个麻烦，我去瞧一瞧他的罪名簿，你们且自己聊去吧。”徐福心思已经不在这边了，说完之后，便跨出了奉常寺的门。
原本还等着好好感谢一番徐福的王柳愣了愣，心中有些不是滋味。也就只有刘奉常这样的人，才会将这种恩情捏在手中来要挟他人了，而徐福这样的人，却是压根未将这份恩情看在眼中。
刘奉常挟恩求报，他心中不快，而如今徐福不要他报答，他反倒心中觉得难受起来了。
苏邑扫了一眼他的模样，皱眉道：“别看呆了。”
王柳回过神来，不悦道：“我何曾看呆了？分明是你看呆了！”
苏邑皱了皱眉，暗道一声不与王柳计较！这边转身离去了。
王柳瞪了瞪他的背影，心中不快道，分明是苏邑不知死活，觊觎徐奉常！怎么苏邑还反倒指责他？果然是个怪脾气！有毛病！
苏邑也心道王柳有病，以前与徐奉常不对付，如今又倾慕徐奉常，这不是有病是什么？
·
徐福并不知那刘奉常被带往何处了，而此也没有小内侍在外等他。徐福也不耽搁，拔腿步行往王宫的方向而去。左右王宫的守卫都已经认识他了，哪怕不坐那马车，也没有什么所谓。
而此时那宣布王令的内侍，跑得飞快，已经到宫中先寻嬴政禀报去了。
嬴政很早之前便知晓徐福在奉常寺中，曾经遭遇过责难了，只是那时他对徐福半点心思也无，二人之间陌生得很，徐福对他也只有一个可利用的作用。对于这样的人，他怎么会上心呢？只是如今再听内侍提起，嬴政的记忆回笼，这才觉得愤怒不已！
如今换了个身份，他成了徐福的情人，他自然难以容忍有谁欺侮了徐福。那些过去，如今一想起来，嬴政便觉得刘奉常当真可恶！
撤职便都是便宜了他。
那内侍又将刘奉常在奉常寺中大闹的事托出，嬴政听了之后，面沉如水，半晌连句话也不说。
那内侍却战战兢兢低下头，知道嬴政这是真的怒了。
“王上……那刘太卜……如何处置……”
嬴政手中的竹刀在竹简上划出长长的痕迹来，印痕深刻，可见他方才使了多么大的劲儿。
“当初寡人为何会选此人做了奉常？”
赵高在旁闻言，躬身道：“王上，当初奉常之位，乃是吕不韦所选的人担任，后来便换成了逆犯嫪毐的人。”
怪不得了……那嫪毐也不过是个出身市井的混混，他能有什么选人的目光？选了此人上来，也不过是为了膈应吕不韦罢了！当初嬴政还未注意到这一茬，原本奉常寺也不是多么重要，他便也未撤去此人职务，但如今细数起来，嬴政才发现这人身上，竟有这么多令人难以忍受的罪过！
“将人带到寡人跟前来。”嬴政冷声道。
内侍愣了愣，扬起头来，“王上？”那刘太卜如何配见王上？杀了不是便好了！
但内侍心中再疑惑，却也不敢出声质疑嬴政的决定，于是站起身来，道：“奴婢这便去。”
刘太卜……
好一个刘太卜！
嬴政手中的笔刀插在了竹简之上。
赵高在旁边斜睨了一眼那笔刀，暗暗在心中为那刘太卜点了根蜡。
不久之后，刘太卜便被带到了殿中。嬴政见地上蜷着一团软趴趴的玩意儿，不由问道：“他这是怎么了？”
内侍道：“回王上，这是吓晕了。”
“吓晕了？”嬴政嘴角翘起，露出个冷漠的笑容来，“将人泼醒。”这人可实在太没用了些。与徐福争执时，怎么不见他如此胆小？想来是将徐福当做软柿子捏了！可那也得看寡人让不让你捏！
莫说如今成了太卜，就算是奉常，一个小小奉常！算什么东西！
给徐福提鞋都不配！
有宫人拎了水来泼在他脸上，只是可惜，这时是盛夏时节，那水泼上去，可不是冰寒刺骨的，反倒是凉爽的。不过就算如此，那刘太卜还是生生打了个寒颤，从昏迷中惊醒过来，一咕噜从地上爬了起来，“这是哪里？这是哪里？”他实在太过慌乱了，看也没看便喊出了声。等到他平复下来，这才看清了坐在上位的嬴政。这一眼，差点让心中恐惧的刘太卜又生生晕过去。
“王、王上……”刘太卜匍匐在地，头也不敢抬。
这还是他头一次单独面见王上，但他怎么也没想到，会是在这样的境地之下。
就在此时，有宫女进门道：“王上，扶苏公子同徐奉常到了。”
刘太卜就听见了个“徐奉常”，当即又打了个哆嗦。他这是追上来，要弄死自己啊……
刘太卜总算知道畏惧徐福了，不过此时也晚了。
嬴政挑眉看向那宫女，“扶苏同徐奉常一起来的？”
宫女点头。
“将人请进来。”嬴政的语气不自觉地柔和了些。
不多时，徐福便牵着扶苏进来了，宫人们见他们如此姿态，也不觉得奇怪。就算哪一日，扶苏公子都认徐奉常做仲父了，他们也不会觉得奇怪。
徐福也是在路上遇见扶苏的，扶苏要来请教嬴政，而徐福是要来寻嬴政瞧个热闹，二人便一同进来了。
见到徐福的面，嬴政顿时更为心疼了，想一想从前自己竟然对徐福的遭遇不放在心上，而那刘太卜竟然敢让徐福去洒扫茅厕？嬴政便觉得胸中涌动着压抑不住的怒气。
扶苏一进来，先同徐福一起见了礼，随后便好奇地看向浑身湿了个透的刘太卜，问道：“父王，此人是谁？”
嬴政冷着脸道：“此人乃是曾经欺侮过你老师的恶人。”个中森寒意味，刘太卜皆听进了耳中，他不自觉地便又打了个哆嗦。
“欺侮过老师？”扶苏闻言，当即眉毛一扬，快步上前，命旁边的宫人道：“将此恶人的脸抬起来，且让我瞧一瞧，是何等利害的人物，才敢欺侮我扶苏的老师！”
那刘太卜闻言，只觉得脑子一片晕眩。
什么……什么老师？
徐福是长公子扶苏的老师？
刘太卜已经连呼吸都变得小心翼翼起来了，他恨不得就此昏死过去。他怎么……怎么就犯了这样的大错啊！
“我还当他有两个鼻子，两张嘴呢……原来也长得如此普通……”
徐福在他身后淡淡道：“谁说他长得普通了？比起常人来，他可是丑了不止半点……”
扶苏闻言，笑道：“老师说得不错，正是如此！老师曾对我说起过，相由心生。此恶人，面相如此丑陋，气质猥琐，可见其内心也何等卑劣！”
扶苏转头看向嬴政，问道：“父王，他是如何欺侮老师的？如今便让扶苏为老师讨回来。”
徐福和嬴政都有些惊奇地看了一眼扶苏。
如今这个模样的扶苏才像是个正常同龄人的模样啊。
扶苏身为秦王的长子，年纪小小，竟然没有半分得意？竟然都不仗势欺负一下人？平日里总是年幼却沉稳的模样。而他如今叫着要为徐福讨回来，那冷厉和溢着怒气的脸，才更像是个出身高贵的小孩子啊。
“也不是多么大的事，他曾令我去洒扫茅厕。不过我却没做。”
扶苏闻言，瞪大了眼。
让老师去洒扫茅厕？
让老师这样气质出尘的人……
“好大的胆子！”扶苏抬脚便踹在了刘太卜的腰上，“揍他！”
宫人闻言，抬头看嬴政，却见嬴政面带笑意，这还有何说的？当然是上前开揍！扶苏公子说得没错！此人实在可恶！竟然敢对徐奉常下如此命令！徐奉常啊……
那可是如神仙下凡般的徐奉常啊……
此时扶苏也不知是想到了什么鬼主意，突然道：“父王，不如将胡亥抱来……”
“做什么？”嬴政皱眉。这样的场面，将胡亥带来做什么？
扶苏道：“自然是让胡亥尿在他的身上……”
徐福：“……”
完了……
扶苏公子，当真被他带歪了！

Fusu's words dealt such a shock to everyone present that no one in the palace had ever seen him act this way. Ying Zheng looked down at Fusu, only to see him with wide eyes, looking completely innocent—a far cry from his usual demeanor. Ying Zheng simply assumed his son had finally cast aside his constraints and caution to indulge in a bit of childlike whimsy. Since Fusu was still so young, Ying Zheng naturally wouldn't scold him for being crude.

Seeing that neither Ying Zheng nor Xu Fu spoke, Fusu smiled and ordered the palace attendant beside him, "Go and bring Huhai here."

The attendant left, sweating profusely.

Grand Diviner Liu was already trembling on the ground like a sieve.

How could Young Master Fusu... how could he do this?! Yet, because this was a "gift" from the royal family, he dared not refute it in the slightest.

Before long, the attendant brought Huhai over. Huhai was still groggy with sleep, but upon catching sight of Xu Fu, he immediately reached out to be held. However, the attendant carried him straight to Fusu. Huhai pouted unhappily, and before he could even start to cry, he peed all over Grand Diviner Liu.

Xu Fu: ...

That was... truly perfect timing!

Grand Diviner Liu, sprawled on the ground, looked absolutely wretched!

Fusu laughed, "Since Grand Diviner Liu is so fond of things from the latrine, I shall grant your wish. Are you feeling happy now, Grand Diviner Liu?"

To be able to say such things at such a young age—Grand Diviner Liu looked up and met Fusu’s gaze, involuntarily shivering. Despite his youth, the boy felt strangely eerie. Under immense psychological pressure, with Fusu standing before him, the King of Qin nearby, and Xu Fu’s cold, piercing gaze fixed on him from behind, Grand Diviner Liu finally understood the taste of regret.

"Grand Diviner Liu." Fusu’s expression turned cold, and his youthful voice rang out through the hall with a hint of Ying Zheng’s own authority, "Why do you not answer me? Is it because you are still not satisfied?"

Hearing Fusu’s sharp, cold voice, Huhai suddenly stiffened. He raised his hands to cover his mouth, looking around in confusion, and didn't dare to cry anymore.

Grand Diviner Liu’s body shook again, and he could only whisper, "...S-satisfied."

The palace attendants couldn't help but chuckle.

Fusu smiled and said to Ying Zheng, "Father, how can someone who loves to associate with things from the latrine serve as our Great Qin’s Grand Diviner? Since he is so preoccupied with the latrine, why not let him go clean them? It would fulfill his heart’s desire."

Grand Diviner Liu’s face turned deathly pale. He didn't dare to utter a word of defense; only he knew how his heart was churning and how excruciatingly miserable he felt at that moment.

Watching Grand Diviner Liu, Xu Fu found it hard not to laugh. He hadn't expected Fusu to have such a sharp tongue at his age. No matter if Liu said he was satisfied or not, Fusu had dug a pit for him, and he had no choice but to jump in. Compared to the petty, smear-campaign tactics Liu had used in the Office of the Fengchang, this was on a completely different level—Liu couldn't even catch up to Fusu if he rode the fastest horse.

Ying Zheng, however, did not intend to let Grand Diviner Liu off so easily.

Fusu punishing him was Fusu venting on behalf of his teacher, but he himself hadn't taken action yet.

"Bring the register of crimes."

Hearing Ying Zheng’s command, the attendant immediately went to fetch the register. Grand Diviner Liu, already soaked, broke out in a cold sweat. Crimes... what crimes did he have? He couldn't even remember them all himself, but the fact that he couldn't remember made him all the more anxious. Not remembering meant the mistakes he had made were likely far more numerous than just one or two.

Grand Diviner Liu lay there stiffly; if his eyes weren't still open, he would have looked like a dead man.

The register was spread out before him. Fusu stepped forward, took a look, and exclaimed in shock, "Father, this man is incredibly bold! He takes the grain of Qin yet commits such evil deeds! He indulges those who are close to him while oppressing those he has no ties with, dismissing and commanding others at will. He secretly suppressed bamboo slips; to avoid punishment, he would bury any ominous signs divined by the Divination Bureau. He attempted to turn the Office of the Fengchang into his own private domain! He truly has no regard for you, Father!"

With every word Fusu spoke, Grand Diviner Liu trembled.

In truth, even he found these accusations unfamiliar. Perhaps he had done these things so often that they had become as natural as eating or drinking, so he naturally didn't feel anything was wrong. Hearing Fusu recount his sins, for a moment, Grand Diviner Liu still didn't feel he had done anything wrong.

Xu Fu cast a cold glance at Grand Diviner Liu; he hadn't expected the man to be so lawless.

It seemed he wasn't the first person to be "punished" by Liu in this manner. If his own temper had been a bit softer, he might have just accepted it.

He truly couldn't understand this man. Born of humble origins, having finally attained the position of Fengchang, shouldn't he have been cautious and guarded his position to ensure a bright future? Yet, Liu had used his meager power to obstruct others, forcing himself onto this dead-end path. Was he like Lao Ai—losing his balance the moment he climbed to a high position and then imploding?

"Grand Diviner Liu, do you confess your crimes?" Ying Zheng asked coldly.

Grand Diviner Liu looked up at Ying Zheng on the throne. The King’s lofty demeanor made him feel like an ant at the royal feet, one that could be crushed to death with a single step.

"...I confess," Grand Diviner Liu said with a hoarse voice. Having reached this point, he had no defense. He could have bickered in front of Xu Fu, but in front of the King, unless he wanted to die faster, he couldn't just stiffen his neck and refuse to submit.

"Then, as Fusu suggested, starting tomorrow, have him clean the latrines in the Office of the Fengchang. After one hundred days, strip him of his rank and throw him into prison."

Clean the latrines... strip of rank... throw into prison...

Grand Diviner Liu’s face wore an expression that was half-laugh, half-cry, as if he had gone mad.

Any one of these three punishments was enough to make him die of shame and indignation.

If he hadn't spoken up to protest earlier, could he have remained a secure Grand Diviner? But it was too late for regrets... If he were to truly regret anything, he shouldn't have become so arrogant and reckless in the first place... He should have listened to Xu Fu’s words... But who could have foreseen it? When Wang Liu was oppressing Xu Fu, hadn't he also failed to imagine that Xu Fu possessed such divine skills in divination and the fortune to be appreciated by the King?

Soon, someone came forward and dragged the wretched Grand Diviner Liu away with an expression of disgust.

Influenced by the stern atmosphere, Huhai kept his hands over his mouth, not daring to make a sound.

Once Liu was dragged away, he whispered, "Ah Hu... Ah Hu..."

Although his speech was slurred with baby talk, Xu Fu could roughly tell he was calling him. Just as Xu Fu hesitated whether to go over and hug Huhai to reward this "little hero," Fusu had already reached out and picked him up. Huhai struggled unhappily twice but couldn't break free.

When Huhai was younger, Fusu had struggled to lift him, but after training with Wang Ben and Ying Zheng for a while, Fusu had grown much stronger and could finally hold Huhai without showing any strain.

Fusu held Huhai, bid farewell to Ying Zheng, and wobbled out with him. The palace attendants were on edge, following closely behind.

As for what happened to Grand Diviner Liu after being dragged away, no one cared.

Such a person wasn't worth anyone's attention; the show was over.

Xu Fu’s displeasure had long since dissipated, and he naturally put Liu out of his mind. Watching Huhai struggling in Fusu’s arms, one hand reaching toward him while the other covered his pouting mouth—looking both ridiculous and adorable—Xu Fu’s mood improved instantly.

The hall still needed to be cleaned of the mess, and Ying Zheng naturally wouldn't stay there with Xu Fu, so the two left the hall together, leaving the attendants to clean up.

Walking side by side, Xu Fu expected Ying Zheng to say something to comfort him. Instead, with a group of attendants following behind, Ying Zheng leaned down slightly and whispered in his ear, "That ointment is finished. When will you prepare more? Hmm?"

Xu Fu, who thought Ying Zheng would discuss important matters: ...

However, Ying Zheng did remind him. He hadn't touched those two tripods in a while and hadn't continued researching what exactly they were for.

"I'll take a look when I go back today," Xu Fu said, his expression unchanged.

Ying Zheng couldn't help but look down at Xu Fu again, failing to find even a hint of a blush on his face. To be as calm as Xu Fu made it truly difficult to tease him... What a pity...

The attendants behind them only saw them talking intimately, unaware that with such serious faces and cold gazes, they were discussing such a shameful matter.

After returning to his sleeping quarters, Xu Fu dug out the small tripod, while Ying Zheng went off to handle other affairs.

Before long, Fusu came to the quarters. Seeing the tripod in Xu Fu’s hand, he was curious and reached out to touch it, "Teacher, what is this used for?"

"Refining medicine."

"Can such a small tripod refine medicine?"

"Naturally." Xu Fu said, tossing herbs inside without changing his expression.

Yes, such an exquisite and grand tripod had been reduced to his mortar.

"This tripod... it looks so... familiar..." Fusu whispered.

Xu Fu didn't pay much mind to it, saying casually, "You must have seen it before..."

"But I haven't seen it here with you before."

"Hmm?" Xu Fu paused his hand, "Then where did you see it?" Could this tripod have other "siblings"?

"My mother once showed me a sheepskin scroll. It had... no, not the tripod..." Fusu pointed to the body of the tripod, "It had patterns like this."

Xu Fu’s interest was piqued, and he asked, "Where is that sheepskin scroll now? Can you bring it for me to see?"

"I will have someone look for it," Fusu said, adding, "The scroll records some strange things; I don't know if they are true."

Fusu was young and naturally found it hard to judge, but he was different—once he had it in his hands and read through it, he would know.

The attendants received the order and went to search for the scroll.

Xu Fu picked up the small tripod again, his fingers tracing the textures. Just then, he felt something flash before his eyes; the patterns seemed to move along with his fingers. He looked closer, but there was nothing. He blinked, and as he closed his eyes, a scene suddenly appeared in his mind.

Vultures swooped down, snatching flesh from corpses.

A sky of red clouds served as the backdrop, with death and killing intent intertwined on the battlefield.

The sounds of battle suddenly erupted.

The entire scene began to move in his mind as if a switch had been flipped. Armored warriors appeared like shadow puppets, and a great banner fluttered in the gale.

Vaguely, Xu Fu could glimpse the character "Qin."

Could he see movies when he closed his eyes?

Xu Fu found it truly marvelous. While he was distracted, a powerful, sharp arrow suddenly flew toward him—or rather, he felt as if the arrow were flying directly toward his perspective, catching him off guard, aiming straight for his eyes.

Xu Fu opened his eyes reflexively.

"Teacher?" Fusu tilted his head in confusion, seeing him suddenly open his eyes.

Fusu’s face was right there, and he was holding the tripod, which was stained pitch-black by the herbs and looked a bit ugly. The images in his mind had vanished instantly, as if he had just had a dream.

How strange.

Xu Fu touched the patterns again and closed his eyes, but his mind remained dark; there were no more images.

Xu Fu put the tripod back, his desire to understand it becoming even stronger.

Just then, an attendant entered, holding a sheepskin scroll, and knelt to present it to Xu Fu.

"Teacher, please look." Fusu took the scroll and handed it to Xu Fu. Xu Fu didn't stand on ceremony and immediately unfolded it.

Fusu leaned in and pointed to a spot, "Look, it's right here."

Xu Fu looked; it indeed depicted the same patterns, with a note beside it: "Sun, moon, and stars, taking their brightness."

Xu Fu was puzzled. He picked up the tripod and examined it again, finally vaguely seeing that the patterns were drawings of the Golden Crow, the Jade Toad, and constellations. The places he had traced were the connected stars, forming the pattern of the sun, moon, and stars.

What about the other one? Xu Fu hurriedly found the second one and examined it carefully.

But the artistic style of this era was too abstract, and combined with the craftsmanship, it was hard to identify the exact figures.

"Is there a diagram for this pattern?" Xu Fu asked, pointing to it.

Fusu looked carefully for a while but shook his head, "No."

A palace maid bowed to the side, "Master Xu, Young Master Huhai is looking for his brother."

Xu Fu said casually, "Then bring Huhai in."

The maid nodded and ordered someone to bring Huhai in.

Once brought in, Huhai struggled to get down. The attendant couldn't refuse him and set him down. Huhai ran two steps toward Fusu and then "thwack," fell flat on his face.

Everyone was startled.

They rushed over, and Xu Fu dropped the tripod.

Unexpectedly, Huhai didn't get up; he just kicked his legs and crawled toward Fusu.

Xu Fu: ...

Fusu: ...

After crawling over, Huhai grabbed Fusu’s robes and wouldn't let go. Fusu had to lift him up from the floor. Huhai glared at the tripod on the ground and pointed at it, "Bird! Bird!"

Bird?

Huhai knew what a bird looked like? Xu Fu followed his gaze; the last stroke on the tripod did look a bit like... bird feathers, no, even more lush than bird feathers.

Xu Fu grabbed the tripod and examined it closely again.

Huhai seemed interested too, leaning in Fusu’s arms and reaching out to grab the tripod, but his arms were too short and he was too small—how could he reach it?

Xu Fu indulged him and brought the tripod right to Huhai. Huhai touched it and seemed to want to bite it, but suddenly his little face wrinkled, he pushed the tripod away, turned, buried his face in Fusu’s chest, and burst into a loud cry.

Xu Fu was stunned, but a guess formed in his mind.

Could it be that Huhai had also seen some images in his mind just now?

Huhai was already crying until he was out of breath. Fusu was incredibly embarrassed and wanted Xu Fu to see that he was indeed good to Huhai. "Teacher, I'll go comfort him." With that, he carried Huhai out, the two of them wobbling away.

Xu Fu picked up the tripod. With Huhai’s unintentional remark, the door to inspiration suddenly opened for Xu Fu, and he began to connect the patterns on the tripod.

Its neck feathers and tail resembled a snake.

It looked like a golden pheasant.

Xu Fu had a vague guess, but with only two tripods, it was hard to say if it was just a coincidence.

If that were true, the tripod wouldn't be of much value. By comparison, he was now more curious about how the images in his mind had appeared and who the arrow had finally struck. Was it the Qin army? He remembered the "Qin" character fluttering on the great banner. Surely the Qin army wouldn't be in trouble? A flurry of thoughts crowded Xu Fu’s mind.

The maid whispered, "Master Xu, are you still refining medicine?"

"Yes." Xu Fu collected his thoughts and said in a low voice. If the tripod was as worthless as he suspected, its only value was to be used as a mortar.

The maid hurried to find other medicinal ingredients.

Xu Fu spent the afternoon leisurely working, adding some oils, and waiting for it to boil into a paste before adding a bit of flower juice. Fortunately, he wasn't allergic to flowers.

Adding flower juice wasn't because Xu Fu was being flamboyant; if he didn't add it to dye the color, the ointment would be so ugly that no one would want to use it. Jiang You had mentioned in the recipe that one could add ingredients according to personal preference.

Anyway, he was just experimenting, so he’d make it and see.

When Ying Zheng returned, the four of them had a slow dinner together. Fusu took Huhai away, and Ying Zheng turned to chat with Xu Fu about the war at the front, eventually chatting their way into bed.

Coincidentally, the new ointment had set, and the attendants carefully brought it to the bedside.

Xu Fu held back Ying Zheng’s arm and asked seriously, "Are you allergic to flowers?" If he were, one session of intimacy would come at a heavy price!

Ying Zheng was confused, "Allergic?"

"I mean, if you smell flowers or touch pollen, do you have any uncomfortable reactions?"

"No."

Only then did Xu Fu relax and lay back on the bed, "Your Majesty, please."

Ying Zheng’s heart was burning with fire, and he felt that Xu Fu’s frankness only stirred his desires even more.

Xu Fu naturally slept much more soundly that night, though his face inevitably showed a hint of fatigue. Ying Zheng, however, put on his robes and got up to handle the affairs he hadn't finished during the day.

Before long, Ying Zheng heard Xu Fu making sounds on the bed as if he were sleeping restlessly.

This wasn't like Xu Fu’s usual habits... Was he sick? Ying Zheng couldn't help but go to the bedside. He reached out to check Xu Fu’s forehead; it wasn't hot. Xu Fu’s complexion didn't look like he was sick either. Was he sleeping restlessly because he was alone? Ying Zheng ordered the desk removed, immediately took off his robes, and lay down with Xu Fu.

At this moment, Xu Fu was completely unaware of the outside world; his consciousness had drifted far away, dragged into the depths of his mind.

The images that had appeared during the day surfaced again, and this time, they were more complete.

Xu Fu forced himself to keep his eyes wide open, watching the arrow fly toward him.

"Pfft!"

Xu Fu could clearly hear the sound ringing in his ears, and his body trembled involuntarily.

His focus wavered, and the images blurred. Xu Fu hurriedly tightened his concentration. Looking again, the scene became clearer. He heard someone shout "General," and Xu Fu’s perspective shifted to see an armored veteran falling from his horse.

Xu Fu didn't recognize the man’s face, but he could guess.

In the Qin army, there was only one such elderly general.

Wang Jian!

Xu Fu tried desperately to shift his perspective, wanting to see whose hand had fired the arrow, but his perspective failed him. He could only stare as Wang Jian was helped up, while the other side suddenly gained momentum, their battle cries shaking the heavens as they charged toward the Qin army.

Xu Fu couldn't see the faces of the others, but a voice echoed faintly in his ears, "...What Great Qin, what Wang Jian, nothing more than this." It was an extremely young voice.

Hearing this, a fire of anger ignited in Xu Fu’s heart.

Perhaps having been in Qin for so long, he had come to view it as his own country, just as he would have felt unbearable anger in his previous life if he heard another country offending China. At this moment, Xu Fu could finally understand Han Fei’s state of mind.

As a person of Qin, he could not tolerate others looking down on the state like this.

In his anger, Xu Fu woke up. He couldn't see what happened next, nor could he see what the person who spoke looked like.

He stared at the canopy of the bed, the anger in his heart unable to fade for a long time.

Ying Zheng seemed to sense something and opened his eyes. He hadn't rested enough, and there were faint bloodshot lines in his eyes, "You slept restlessly last night; did you dream of something?"

Xu Fu looked toward the hall; the sky outside was brightening. A whole night had passed just like that.

Xu Fu steadied his mind and decided not to hide it from Ying Zheng. Whether the dream was absurd or not, he had to tell him. What if... what if it was a premonition... Thinking of the dream he had before going to Shu, Xu Fu felt he couldn't easily dismiss this one.

"Where is General Wang Jian now?"

Hearing Xu Fu mention Wang Jian first thing in the morning, Ying Zheng would have been jealous if he didn't know that Xu Fu cared about Wang Jian because he cared about his own great cause.

"He should have reached Eyu by now."

"I had a bad dream."

Seeing Xu Fu’s solemn expression, Ying Zheng asked quickly, "How bad?"

"General Wang Jian was struck by an arrow."

Since Xu Fu was speaking so seriously, Ying Zheng knew he couldn't underestimate the dream. He immediately asked for the details. Xu Fu told him everything he had seen, only briefly mentioning the young voice at the end.

"You suspect the dream will come true?" Ying Zheng frowned. He waved away the maids who came forward with his robes.

"I deal with these mysterious matters, so I would rather believe it exists than dismiss it as absurd," Xu Fu said calmly.

Hearing him say this, Ying Zheng couldn't help but take it to heart.

Xu Fu wouldn't lie to him, and his abilities were proven. Although the dream sounded mysterious, Xu Fu was right—better to believe it! General Wang Jian’s status was too important; he was the pillar of the Qin army. If something happened to him, the attack on Zhao would inevitably suffer. The great cause would be hindered, morale affected, and it would lead to a series of subsequent troubles...

For example, the court might question the divination signs from that day, question his abilities, or even worse, question his own decisions.

Although these things hadn't happened yet and might not all happen, Ying Zheng had to take them into account.

"I will have someone handle this. Rest assured, as soon as there is news, I will inform you." Ying Zheng knew that without a result, Xu Fu would never be able to rest easy.

Xu Fu shook his head, sat up from the bed, and said, "Wang... A-Zheng, I want to go to the State of Zhao."

Ying Zheng’s expression changed instantly; his brows knitted tightly together, and his gaze turned several degrees sharper. "Why? The two armies are currently at war; why would you go to Zhao? Weapons have no eyes—what will you do if you get hurt?"

Xu Fu, however, showed no signs of wavering. He looked steadily at Ying Zheng, meeting his gaze, and asked earnestly in return: "If I don't go, who can persuade General Wang Jian to be careful of arrows? Would General Wang Jian be convinced by anyone else?"

"Then why are you so certain that Wang Jian will believe you?" Ying Zheng was suppressing his displeasure, and the words that slipped out naturally carried a sharp tone.

But Xu Fu didn't take it to heart; he wouldn't get upset with Ying Zheng over such trivial matters. In any case, every time he wanted to leave Xianyang, Ying Zheng was like this. Ying Zheng was simply unhappy about him leaving.

"I have my own ways to make him believe me." Xu Fu paused, his gaze cooling slightly as he added deliberately, "Unless A-Zheng doesn't trust me..." The two words "A-Zheng," rarely spoken with such intimacy by Xu Fu, sounded suddenly gentle and low, giving off a sense of deep affection.

Called like this, Ying Zheng felt his heart soften instantly.

But...

Thinking of that trip to Wei and Han, thinking of that trip to Shu... Ying Zheng felt extremely uneasy in his heart.

If others were to know of his care for Xu Fu, it would be even worse. He was currently sending troops to attack other nations; who was to say those countries wouldn't strike first, kidnap Xu Fu, and use him as leverage? The various dangers involved—Ying Zheng found it unbearable just thinking of one of them.

But Xu Fu really knew how to manipulate his psychology.

How could he ever say words of distrust toward Xu Fu?

"I naturally trust you, but the journey to Zhao is treacherous. It is not as simple as going to Shu, nor as smooth as going to Wei and Han. You are no longer an envoy, but an enemy of their state; you could be captured at any moment." Ying Zheng tried his best not to mix his own emotions into it, objectively describing the dangers that might be encountered on the way.

Yet, Xu Fu possessed a heart that yearned for freedom.

After staying in Xianyang for too long, he would want to go out for a walk; after being away for too long, he would miss life in the Xianyang Palace.

Now that he had a reason to go, Xu Fu was confident that, besides him, no one else could handle General Wang Jian.

What was General Wang Jian’s status in Qin? Ordinary people dared not easily argue with him. If General Wang Jian didn't listen, what then? No one dared to offend their superior; perhaps one glance from Wang Jian would strip them of all their courage.

Xu Fu was different. He was an outsider; he didn't have a deep sense of hierarchy. Moreover, he had spent years feigning indifference and could turn a blind eye to others' gazes. Even if General Wang Jian pierced him with a sharp, icy stare, he could remain unfazed. With him accompanying the army, the campaign against Zhao would surely be even more successful.

Xu Fu looked steadily at Ying Zheng, not backing down at all. "I want to go." Although the expression on his face didn't change much as he said this, it gave Ying Zheng a sense of coquettishness.

Ying Zheng was stunned, somewhat unable to resist this side of Xu Fu.

There was another reason Xu Fu wanted to go to Zhao.

He wondered if there might also be a cauldron in Zhao. This was just a guess, but if he could find another one, he would be able to judge the value of the cauldrons. That would avoid the possibility of wasting effort blindly.

Thinking this way, Xu Fu felt that he had an incredibly legitimate reason to go out and get some air!

"I really want to go." Xu Fu emphasized the words "really want," his gaze tightly entwined with Ying Zheng’s.

Ying Zheng felt even less able to resist.

He gritted his teeth hard, knowing that after Xu Fu returned from Wei and Han, he wouldn't stay settled for long. Or rather, few disciples of the Ghost Valley were not wanderers. Even Wei Liao had traveled to various states to lobby before, hadn't he? Xu Fu was truly pouring out the restlessness in his bones for him to see without reservation.

Ying Zheng had long been mentally prepared, but being prepared and the event actually happening were two different things. Seeing Xu Fu wanting to go to Zhao now, he still felt unhappy in his heart.

"A-Zheng should make a decision soon; General Wang Jian’s life is still in A-Zheng’s hands." Xu Fu said with a deadpan face, his tone intimate.

It made Ying Zheng both love and hate him, wishing he could simply tie him to the bed.

"Do you still want those same attendants from before?" Ying Zheng asked with a sour face.

Hearing Ying Zheng say this, Xu Fu knew he had acquiesced and immediately smiled: "Yes, just them; we are more familiar with each other."

"After dealing with this matter, you must return to Xianyang immediately." Since he couldn't stop Xu Fu’s footsteps, Ying Zheng had to set conditions first.

"Okay."

Seeing that Xu Fu’s brows and eyes were already filled with joy, Ying Zheng felt even more annoyed.

Leaving me makes you this happy? That won't do!

Ying Zheng’s expression grew even sourer. "What if I miss you?"

Xu Fu calmly grabbed Ying Zheng’s palm.

Ying Zheng narrowed his eyes slightly; how would Xu Fu appease him this time to get to Zhao?

Who knew that Xu Fu would open his palm and stuff something into it.

Ying Zheng looked down... ointment!

"Self-reliance," Xu Fu said to him very seriously.

Ying Zheng: ...

For the first time, Ying Zheng felt that sending troops to attack other nations was like digging a hole to bury himself in. War was war, but even his wife was running away... However, Ying Zheng immediately thought that even if he didn't attack other nations, Xu Fu might find some other excuse to go out and wander.

"That should be fine." After saying this, Xu Fu patted the back of Ying Zheng’s hand and got off the bed first.

The palace maid had been listening from the side; she breathed a sigh of relief and hurried over to drape a robe over Xu Fu. Just moments ago, she had been worried the King would lose his temper, yet the King had suppressed his anger completely in front of the Fengchang. The Fengchang was truly capable!

Ying Zheng suddenly remembered something. "Once you leave, how will the Fengchang Temple be handled? Don't forget, you are now the Fengchang."

"Then I must trouble A-Zheng to issue an order for Wang Liu and Su Yi to handle the affairs together."

Hearing the words "A-Zheng," Ying Zheng’s gaze couldn't help but flicker. "Come here."

"Hmm?" Xu Fu pulled his robe and walked over, not understanding. Ying Zheng pulled at his robe, exposing half his body again. The palace maid hurriedly lowered her head. When she looked up again, the curtains had already fallen, and she could only vaguely see the silhouette of Ying Zheng pressing Xu Fu down.

"Call me 'A-Zheng' a few more times." Ying Zheng’s voice sounded in Xu Fu’s ear.

At times like this, Xu Fu was always very compliant.

"A-Zheng."

"A-Zheng..."

"A... Zheng..."

Toward the end, his voice changed pitch involuntarily. The maid didn't dare to listen any longer and hurried away on tiptoe, clutching the robes. She sighed; it seemed breakfast would be delayed today.

...

Because Xu Fu’s dream was too mysterious, Ying Zheng didn't mention it at court, only stating that he was ordering Xu Fu to represent him and accompany the grain-transporting army to reward the fighting Qin troops. Now the entire court knew what status Xu Fu held in the King’s heart. That the King would even send Xu Fu out showed the King’s compassion for the Qin army. The King was truly benevolent!

After the small court session ended, Wei Liao’s face darkened, and he immediately demanded an audience with Ying Zheng.

He cursed inwardly, the King of Qin was truly no good!

Who couldn't he have sent? Even sending him would have been fine! Why did he have to choose his junior brother? His junior brother was young and weak, with no strength in his hands! Sending him as an envoy was one thing, but this was a war zone! Wasn't he worried that Xu Fu might have an accident? The King of Qin truly had a cold and hard heart!

Wei Liao didn't know that this opportunity to go to Zhao was something Xu Fu had earned through his own "physical efforts."

Ying Zheng was once again unjustly blamed.

As Wei Liao stepped out of the main hall, people came forward: "Congratulations, Guowei! Your junior brother has been promoted to Fengchang and appointed as Hujun Duwei! His future will surely be limitless!"

Wei Liao kept a cold face, snorted, brushed past them, and left immediately.

The crowd was left puzzled by his snort. Had they offended him? He hadn't given them a single good look! Was it wrong to congratulate them on Xu Fu’s promotion?

Just then, Li Si happened to pass by, and someone grabbed him to ask: "Is it possible that the Guowei and the Fengchang are at odds?"

Li Si’s expression was calm as he smiled: "Not at odds; it is precisely because they are too much in agreement."

What did that mean? The others were confused, but when they looked up, Li Si had already walked away.

Wei Liao went to see Ying Zheng, while Li Si went straight to find Xu Fu. At this moment, Xu Fu was still in his bedchamber, counting his belongings and deciding what to pack. He wondered how Lord Longyang would react when Jianjia left with him.

Just as he was thinking, a palace maid walked up to him: "Fengchang Xu, Keqing Li requests an audience."

Keqing?

Xu Fu paused for a moment before remembering that Li Si was now a Keqing.

"Does the King know?"

"I believe so; it was the King’s own attendant who brought the Keqing here."

Xu Fu put down his things and went out to lead Li Si to the side hall. As he walked in, he felt a bit strange—why did he feel increasingly accustomed to being the master of this palace? Xu Fu shook his head, banishing these thoughts.

He turned and invited Li Si to sit.

Li Si and Xu Fu were already very familiar, so naturally, he didn't stand on ceremony.

After they were seated, Xu Fu asked: "Does the Keqing have any business with me?"

"I heard that Fengchang Xu is going to the Zhao battlefield. I am truly curious why you suddenly had such an idea? Going to the battlefield is quite different from going to Wei and Han; the danger is too great. I am worried for your safety."

Xu Fu certainly wouldn't tell him it was because of a dream, so he said: "It is still for the cauldron."

"There is a cauldron in Zhao as well?" Li Si asked in surprise.

"I don't know, so I am going to take a look, and by the way, bring the King’s order to General Wang Jian to put the troops at ease."

Li Si was a smart man; seeing Xu Fu like this, he knew there were things left unsaid, but he didn't intend to press. Xu Fu’s mind was made up; he was definitely going.

So Li Si changed the subject: "The attendant named Jianjia who was with you before is now living with Lord Longyang, is that correct?"

"That is correct, why?"

Li Si whispered: "Since that is the case, when you go, you should take Lord Longyang with you."

"Why do you say that?"

Li Si smiled: "Lord Longyang is a renowned sword master across the states. With him by your side, your safety will be better guaranteed."

Xu Fu thought about it; that seemed true.

Although he wanted to go to Zhao, he didn't want to gamble with his life.

Perhaps it was a coincidence; just after Li Si finished speaking, Zhao Gao arrived with Jianjia and Sangzhong. Bozhou and Gantang were still handling other matters and hadn't come, so they wouldn't be able to accompany them this time.

Jianjia had a sour face, which only softened slightly when he saw Xu Fu.

Zhao Gao smiled: "I am only ordered to deliver these people to Fengchang Xu; the rest is not my concern." After saying this, Zhao Gao took a deep look at Li Si before leaving.

Jianjia had become familiar with Li Si during the trip to Wei and Han, so he didn't hold back: "Sir, Lord Longyang is also coming with us." Jianjia’s expression wasn't good when he said this. Xu Fu finally understood why Jianjia was sour—he didn't want Lord Longyang to come along.

However, he was quite happy to have Lord Longyang accompany them.

"Then let Lord Longyang come along," Xu Fu said.

Jianjia’s eyes widened, looking aggrieved, and he walked to the side with a cold face.

Li Si smiled: "Speak of the devil." Li Si was very good at social graces; if he had come today specifically to say these things to Xu Fu, it was just to show a bit of closeness.

Xu Fu didn't have many friends, so he appreciated Li Si’s well-intentioned suggestion.

As he saw Li Si out, Li Si smiled: "I cannot accompany you now, so please take care on your journey."

Sangzhong gave Li Si a strange look, feeling that Li Si’s words sounded very prone to misunderstanding.

On his way back, Li Si thought silently that he would also be leaving Qin soon. He would also be carrying heavy gold to other states to continue lobbying their ministers. He wondered if the attendants sent to him then would be like Jianjia or Sangzhong...

Seeing that he was about to leave, Xu Fu went to see Su Yi. Su Yi had already heard the news from the small court session and found it hard to understand Xu Fu’s actions.

"Forgive my bluntness, but you really shouldn't go to Eyu!" Su Yi had always been outspoken with Xu Fu and didn't hide his feelings now.

Xu Fu knew Su Yi would say the same thing as Ying Zheng, so he blocked him with one sentence: "I know, but I have a reason that I must go." He knew Su Yi had one trait: he always thought of Xu Fu’s best interests. As long as Xu Fu was going for a reason, Su Yi would definitely not stop him and would support him silently.

But Xu Fu didn't know that Su Yi had another trait: he was very good at overthinking.

Hearing Xu Fu say this, Su Yi’s heart sank immediately.

A reason he must go...

Could it be that the King of Qin did something to hurt Fengchang Xu? Making him sad and angry, forcing him to go to the battlefield to heal his heartache? Or perhaps the King of Qin deliberately drove him away?

Su Yi became anxious; if something went wrong between the King and his minister, what would happen?

Concerned for Xu Fu’s dignity, Su Yi didn't dare to point it out and could only worry in secret.

Later, observing Xu Fu’s cold and calm demeanor, Su Yi thought to himself: Fengchang Xu is truly extraordinary; even at such a time, he remains as steady as a mountain, showing no trace of sorrow. But then he thought, this is truly heartbreaking. To be so bitter and indignant inside, yet forced to put on such a front... enduring such pain...

Su Yi felt extremely uncomfortable.

Xu Fu knew nothing of this. After seeing Su Yi, he returned to the palace. Jianjia had left the palace and didn't return with him, going straight to his residence; he didn't know how he would discuss things with Lord Longyang.

Afterward, Xu Fu specifically instructed Fusu and checked on Huhai.

Seeing him leave, Fusu was reluctant and said: "Teacher, since you are going to Zhao, please leave a bamboo slip for me. Looking at it will be like seeing you."

Xu Fu immediately had someone bring the bamboo slips he usually read and gave them to Fusu.

Listening to Fusu, he would surely be a master of flirting when he grew up.

In the blink of an eye, the day of departure arrived.

Xu Fu had made all preparations, and his anticipation for the journey outweighed his reluctance. He looked more like the "scum gong" in those novels.

He set off with the grain army, still riding in a carriage.

He was now a Hujun Duwei, which was equivalent to a military supervisor in the army. This was no small position! Only he could receive such promotion from Ying Zheng!

Ying Zheng trusted Xu Fu, knowing he wouldn't act recklessly or interfere with the war. To prevent him from being bullied in the army, Ying Zheng gave him an transcendent status. This way, he could be a bit more at ease.

The grain-transporting army also knew of Xu Fu’s status. When he presided over the Wax Festival, it had spread throughout Xianyang.

It was rare for such a god-like figure to preside over the festival; who wouldn't talk about it? Compared to the previous Grand Invoker and the old Grand Diviner, the people of Xianyang preferred Xu Fu.

It had to be said that having a good face was indeed twice as effective. Or rather, having a good temperament made it easier to win people over.

Xu Fu sat in the carriage as it rattled out of Xianyang, with Sangzhong sitting inside with him.

Sangzhong shook his head: "I haven't seen Jianjia for a long time. Although he is unreliable, he wouldn't be this late. I wonder if something happened..."

As soon as he finished speaking, they heard the sound of galloping hooves coming from behind the carriage.

The army immediately stopped, and soldiers blocked the two horses: "Who goes there? Leave quickly! Do you dare to offend the grain-transporting army?"

"I am Jianjia, the attendant to the Duwei!"

"And the person behind you?"

Before Jianjia could answer, Xu Fu lifted the curtain and called out: "They are both my attendants; bring them over."

With Xu Fu’s order, the soldiers dared not stop them.

Jianjia and the other person entered the perimeter; who was following Jianjia if not Lord Longyang?

They abandoned their horses to the soldiers and followed them into the carriage.

"Why are you so slow?" Sangzhong asked with a frown.

Jianjia entered the carriage, his face darkening immediately.

Lord Longyang said immediately: "It is my fault."

Xu Fu’s gaze swept over them involuntarily. Lord Longyang had changed out of his skirts into men’s clothing today. He didn't know if it was because they hadn't seen each other for a long time, but at first glance, he felt something was strange.

Xu Fu withdrew his gaze and said: "I have wronged Lord Longyang by making you an attendant."

Lord Longyang smiled, the coldness on his face fading: "Not wronged at all. To be an attendant to you is my good fortune." He said this so sincerely that Jianjia glared at him several times with an expression of disgust.

...

The grain-transporting army headed toward Eyu.

Standing on the city gate, Ying Zheng watched the army turn into tiny ant-like dots and disappear before turning away with a cold face. Zhao Gao stood by his side, not daring to speak. After Ying Zheng returned to the palace, an attendant reported that the Guowei had come again.

Ying Zheng was already filled with pent-up frustration, so he immediately ordered Wei Liao to be brought in.

Wei Liao also had a dark face. They looked at each other, and Wei Liao said: "If the King treats my junior brother like this, what will happen if something goes wrong?"

Ying Zheng exerted force, and his stylus accidentally pierced the table. The attendant standing nearby shivered, thinking, this Guowei is truly bold! He has tweaked the King’s whiskers twice now, much like Han Fei’s foul temper.

"Then I will flatten the State of Zhao!" Ying Zheng’s voice was as cold as an ice arrow.

But Wei Liao didn't buy it, saying calmly: "King, if my junior brother has an accident, what use is flattening Zhao? Let alone Zhao, even if you flatten all six states, what use is it?"

Ying Zheng felt an internal injury from suppressed anger.

I think the same thing! I want to tie Xu Fu to my side every day for safety! But Xu Fu is not someone I can manipulate at will; he has his own ideas. How can I stop him? If I do, I might make him dislike me—what then? Are you, an old bachelor, going to compensate me with a Xu Fu? Are you going to repair my broken relationship!

Ying Zheng looked at Wei Liao with a sharp gaze.

Wei Liao also looked at Ying Zheng with dissatisfaction.

These two looked at each other and felt nothing but frustration and mutual dislike!

Now that Xu Fu was gone, Wei Liao had only come to annoy Ying Zheng so he could feel better. Wei Liao flicked his sleeves and took his leave.

After he left, Ying Zheng’s anger hadn't subsided. His mind was full of Xu Fu, and as he got angrier, his little brother actually stood up! Thinking of the ointment Xu Fu left behind, he felt as if a fire was burning inside him—desire rising on one side, anger on the other. He must be the most frustrated King of Qin in history!
