chapters.translated_text:
Suddenly, someone lifted the tent flap and strode in with a bold, imposing air. He broke the silence by asking, "How is it?" Everyone, including Xu Fu, looked up at him in unison.

A tall, lean figure flashed into Xu Fu's eyes.

It was the leader who had received them earlier.

Once the man drew closer, Xu Fu saw that the blood and grime had been washed from his face. That face... it was so very familiar. Xu Fu sifted through his memories and found the name he was looking for.

"Li Xin?" Xu Fu asked aloud.

The more he looked at that face, the more certain he became. Before, time had been too tight for him to look closely, but if one paid a little more attention, it was easy to ignore the blood and see the face underneath. After all, the bone structure of a face is fixed; no one else could have the same bone structure and destiny as Li Xin.

Li Xin remained silent, his expression complex as he stood before Xu Fu.

Just as Wang Jian was about to speak, Li Xin suddenly interjected, "So, you haven't forgotten me yet."

Xu Fu tilted his head to make it easier for the physician to apply medicine, saying naturally, "How could I forget that face of yours?"

If a hundred people heard these words, they would naturally have a hundred different guesses.

The people around them looked at them with strange expressions, glancing back and forth. Sang Zhong’s face darkened instantly, and he stared at Li Xin with a hostile, tiger-like gaze.

Wang Jian didn't know what was going on, so he gave a light cough to break the awkward atmosphere. "This time, I truly must thank the Duwei."

Just then, others entered the tent, and Xu Fu pointed into the distance. "General Wang Jian should thank those two instead."

Everyone followed the direction of Xu Fu's finger and saw two dashing figures, one tall and one short—what fine appearances! Wang Jian felt that strange sense of familiarity rise again. Where had he seen that tall one before? With such a striking appearance, he shouldn't have forgotten if he had seen him.

It was Lord Longyang and Jianjia walking in from outside the tent. Lord Longyang noticed Wang Jian's gaze and calmly softened his expression. Once his brows and eyes softened, he looked vastly different from the male favorite who followed the King of Wei.

Wang Jian looked away uncomfortably, thinking to himself that it was perhaps just an illusion.

At the time, some had witnessed the agile skills of Lord Longyang and Jianjia. As military men, they naturally admired those with true ability. Seeing them arrive, someone couldn't help but stand up and say to Lord Longyang, "Your swordsmanship is excellent. Might I ask for a few pointers?"

Those who possess some martial skill often have a competitive streak; when they see a master, they always want to compare notes.

Not to mention them—perhaps one day, if Xu Fu met someone better than himself, he might also want to spar with them.

Yet, Lord Longyang suddenly pointed at Jianjia beside him and said, "You'll have to ask him."

The man was stunned, not understanding what he meant.

Jianjia’s face turned dark; he sullenly kept his head down and walked toward Xu Fu.

Wang Jian finally realized what was happening and hurriedly asked Xu Fu, "Are these few all your attendants, Duwei?"

"Indeed... hiss—" Xu Fu forcibly choked back the sound of his sharp intake of breath. If he cried out in pain, it would be too damaging to his image.

Seeing that his handsome face had turned pale, everyone felt a pang of concern. Wang Jian felt slightly awkward; if not for him, Xu Fu wouldn't have followed the army to the battlefield. He had no combat ability, yet he possessed such a noble air. Standing in a crowd, it was as if he were afraid no one would recognize his status—he radiated a natural brilliance that made it impossible for the enemy to overlook him.

However, this awkwardness was only for a moment. Wang Jian quickly regained his composure and solemnly thanked Xu Fu, Lord Longyang, and Jianjia.

At this moment, a general couldn't help but ask, "Duwei, could you take another look to see if there are any more disasters ahead?"

Others chimed in, "Yes, the General must not meet with any misfortune..."

By now, the wound on Xu Fu's neck had been treated, the physician stood up, and Xu Fu could straighten his neck. The way everyone looked at Xu Fu now held a hint of awe. Someone who could remain calm regardless of what they encountered was truly impressive! They didn't know that this was merely a skill Xu Fu had honed over many years, now so deeply ingrained that it had become a habit.

"General Wang Jian should be very clear that the art of divination is not so simple," Xu Fu said with a calm expression. Upon hearing this, the others blushed and hurriedly apologized to Xu Fu, "Duwei, we are ignorant of these matters and have been presumptuous. Please forgive us!"

"Yes, yes, we didn't think of that. We imagine the art of divination must be very taxing. Hehe, then we dare not trouble you further..."

Although they said this, Xu Fu guessed that most of them didn't take it to heart.

What Duwei? Naturally, he couldn't compare to Wang Jian, who lived and fought alongside them every day! They were probably thinking right now, what if it is tiring? If it could help General Wang Jian avoid danger, wouldn't that be a great bargain? Why be so coy?

Xu Fu swept his gaze over their faces and roughly understood their personalities and what they were thinking.

Wang Jian, however, did not push it. To avoid danger once was already a great blessing! How could one ask for more? Don't many greedy people lose their lives because of their own insatiability?

Wang Jian ordered his men to look into the background of the Zhao army's leader, then chatted with Xu Fu for a few more moments. Hindered by the large number of people present and the fact that Wang Jian still needed to adjust tactics with his generals, Xu Fu consciously led his people out of the tent. As he left, Li Xin turned back to look at him, a gaze that felt quite heavy and somber.

Xu Fu felt that Li Xin was different from the person he had met in the alley; on second thought, perhaps it was the tempering of the army that had made him more mature.

Now that Li Si was a guest minister, perhaps it wouldn't be long before Li Xin became a general.

Both his and Hou Sheng's predictions had come true; he wondered who would be the winner in the end.

The tent flap fell behind them, and Xu Fu had walked far away with his companions.

The soldiers in the camp carefully observed Xu Fu and his group.

As the saying goes, there are no women in the army; after a long time, even a sow looks attractive. Let alone seeing a few people who were better looking than any girl—how could they not stare with all their might? However, their gazes were not malicious, mostly filled with curiosity and amazement. It seemed hard to imagine how, as humans, some could look like this.

Xu Fu and his group entered their tent under such gazes.

Sang Zhong, not knowing what had gotten into him, set up the bed for Xu Fu, brought him food and hot water, and then left without looking back.

Xu Fu was stunned and asked Jianjia, "What's wrong with him?"

Jianjia, whose nerves were as thick as chopsticks, shook his head. "I don't know."

Lord Longyang’s thoughts had never drifted toward Sang Zhong, so he was even less aware.

Xu Fu was confused, but since he couldn't figure it out, he let it go.

In the blink of an eye, it was sunset. There were no entertainment options in this era, and only then did Xu Fu realize he had been overactive during the day; his limbs were aching. After a simple wash, he went to bed to rest. However, Sang Zhong did not return to the tent for a long time. With Sang Zhong absent, Jianjia and Lord Longyang seemed to suddenly feel an awkwardness and were unwilling to stay in the tent either.

Soon, only Xu Fu remained in the tent.

He could hear the shouts of the soldiers outside, perhaps training or changing guard, shouting slogans. He could also hear the wind flapping against the tent... Finally, silence fell around his ears. All sounds seemed to have drifted away from him.

...Will I enter a dream tonight?

Xu Fu closed his eyes in a daze, his consciousness quickly falling into a dark abyss.

But strangely, he didn't have any more dreams about war. There was a subconscious expectation in his mind to dream, and as he waited and waited, he seemed to have truly entered a dream.

He saw himself wearing a white robe, just an ordinary white robe like those in the Xianyang Palace, but despite it being a tightly wrapped garment, he wore it with a "new style."

The white robe was lightly cinched at the waist with a leather belt, and the sleeves on both sides hung down, wide enough to almost touch the ground, revealing his fair shoulders. In the dream, he seemed much thinner; his shoulders were white, but devoid of color. The scene that should have been ambiguous and erotic was ruined by Xu Fu's own thoughts.

His perspective shifted again.

He looked up and seemed to see Ying Zheng sitting at a desk. That position was very far away, as if he could never reach it no matter how he stretched out his hand.

And Ying Zheng didn't spare him a single glance.

It was as if Xu Fu had been isolated from his world. Xu Fu looked up at him until his neck grew sore, yet Ying Zheng remained cold and stern, a chill seemingly radiating from his body. Looking at him, four words immediately popped into Xu Fu's mind: difficult to approach.

A sudden surge of anger rose in Xu Fu's chest.

How could Ying Zheng treat him like this? Even if it was a dream, he shouldn't be like this!

But his perspective and thoughts could not influence the Xu Fu in the dream. He watched as the Xu Fu in the dream walked toward Ying Zheng with a cold expression. Did Ying Zheng finally put down the bamboo slip in his hand? He looked up at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu's perspective swept across the entire hall.

He discovered that he and Ying Zheng were not the only ones in the hall. There were many palace attendants standing on both sides, their heads bowed and their expressions equally indifferent. None dared to look up at Xu Fu.

A strange feeling suddenly rose in the depths of Xu Fu's heart.

"Come here," the Ying Zheng in the dream said to him, his voice low and cold.

Xu Fu moved forward uncontrollably, and the next moment he was pressed onto the desk by Ying Zheng. Xu Fu widened his eyes in surprise—the strength was familiar! But Ying Zheng's expression and the reaction of his dream-self were both filled with something eerie.

As the white robe was pulled off his body, he suddenly remembered that there was a circle of palace attendants standing around. A jolt went through Xu Fu's mind, and he woke up with a start.

He opened his eyes, his back already covered in cold sweat.

It was at this instant that Xu Fu realized something was wrong.

There was a shadow outside the tent.

Oh no... not outside the tent... Xu Fu shuddered involuntarily. The person was clearly... inside the tent... He didn't know if that person was staring at him. Who was he? Why did he come in at this time? Was he armed? In that instant, a thousand thoughts raced through Xu Fu's mind.

He secretly gripped the dagger at his waist.

His turtle shells and other belongings were also in his bedding.

That dagger was given to him by Ying Zheng when he left Xianyang. Out of habit, he kept it in his bed along with his belongings; it was perfect to grab now.

The cold touch of the dagger calmed Xu Fu down significantly.

If it were an intruder...

How much courage would the other party need to dare enter the Qin army's encampment? It was surrounded by Qin soldiers; wasn't he afraid of being torn to pieces?

Just then, Xu Fu heard the sound of footsteps moving—inch by inch, as if coming toward him. Xu Fu held his breath slightly, waiting quietly. As long as he saw that the person's face was a stranger's, he wouldn't give them any chance.

He tightened his grip on the dagger and squinted his eyes.

The shadow drew near, and Xu Fu clearly felt the space above his eyelids darken. He could roughly see the outline of the other person—a stranger!

He didn't hesitate, springing up with the dagger in hand. He used the turtle shell in his other hand to smash it into the intruder's face, stunning him and blocking his vision. Xu Fu then took the opportunity to press the drawn dagger against the intruder's neck, pinning him firmly against the bedpost. If the dagger tilted even slightly, it would slit his throat.

"Someone! There's an assassin!" Xu Fu suddenly raised his voice.

Upon hearing Xu Fu's voice, the intruder began to struggle violently.

"Don't move!" Xu Fu pressed the blade closer to the intruder's neck. The cold, sharp sensation made the intruder pause. The intruder was too strong; he could only force him like this for now.

By now, the encampment was in an uproar. Everyone had been awakened by Xu Fu's shout. The night watchmen were the first to rush in, holding torches.

The Qin soldiers were panicked, fearing that something had happened to the Duwei. But when they rushed in with swords drawn, they saw Xu Fu holding a dagger, pinning a man against the bedpost. Seeing people arrive, the assassin struggled even harder. Xu Fu’s hand slipped, and he nicked the man's neck. Blood spurted out immediately. The man shivered in pain, let out a miserable cry, and dared not move again.

Everyone stared in disbelief—Xu Fu, with his slight build, had actually subdued an assassin?

Xu Fu’s hair was disheveled, and he was only loosely wearing his deep robe. He turned his head, his eyes cold enough to make people shiver. "What are you still standing there for? Take him down!" These words, however, did not come from Xu Fu.

Xu Fu had intended to say it, but he was beaten to it by a young general who had walked into the tent.

That young general was Li Xin.

Li Xin’s face was as dark as water, his gaze as sharp and cold as a wolf on the plains. He was holding a long halberd; if he poked it at the assassin, it would surely gut him. The assassin met Li Xin's eyes and couldn't help but tremble all over.

So gutless, yet he dared to be an assassin?

By now, Qin soldiers had stepped forward to seize the assassin. Xu Fu let go and stepped back twice. A soldier kicked the assassin, and the assassin’s knees went weak, causing him to collapse to the ground. Li Xin stepped forward and used the halberd to lift the assassin's chin. The moonlight outside, combined with the torchlight, illuminated the assassin's face clearly.

Xu Fu’s expression turned cold; old grudges and new hatreds welled up in his heart.

Wasn't this the young man who had drawn his bow and shot at them? He had some nerve, coming to raid the camp while still injured!

Because the halberd was pressed against his throat, the young man didn't even dare to move.

Li Xin said coldly, "Take him away and lock him up first."

The Qin soldiers didn't hesitate, grabbing the man fiercely and dragging him out.

Their behavior left the other party stunned.

No interrogation, no angry shouting, and no yelling about cutting off his head—he was just dragged out. Outside, the moonlight was like water, and the torches in the camp illuminated the dark faces of the soldiers, all of whom looked cold and ruthless. At first glance, it felt like arriving at the gates of hell.

The man barely steadied his nerves before being taken to another shed, where his hands and feet were bound so tightly he couldn't struggle at all.

Meanwhile, Li Xin looked at Xu Fu, his throat moving as he struggled to squeeze out a sentence: "You... you weren't frightened, were you?"

"I'm fine." Xu Fu’s emotions had calmed down quite a bit, and he had even pushed that dream to the back of his mind. However, as the wind blew in from outside the tent, Xu Fu couldn't help but want to shiver.

Li Xin hesitated for a moment, then walked to the bedside and straightened the bedding for Xu Fu. Then he noticed something was wrong, hurriedly threw aside the halberd he was holding, and sat down on the floor by the bed with a bold, imposing air. "Rest, Duwei. I will stand guard here."

Xu Fu had gone to sleep quite early, and after being woken up by a nightmare and experiencing such an ordeal, all his sleepiness was gone. How could he sleep? Still, he slowly walked to the bed and sat down.

Seeing that Xu Fu had no intention of lying down, Li Xin tightened his face and said, "When I first asked for your name, Duwei, you said I would know one day. Will you tell me today?" In fact, even if Xu Fu didn't say it, Li Xin could find out; he only needed to ask Wang Jian. But Wang Jian didn't like him, which would only add trouble.

Xu Fu didn't intend to hide it. Meeting Li Xin in the Qin army was fate, and looking at Li Xin now, he seemed to still remember how he had recklessly broken into that alley, read his fortune, and then nonchalantly walked away.

Xu Fu didn't want to be remembered like that.

"Surname Xu, given name Fu," Xu Fu said generously.

After hearing this, a look of bewilderment flashed across Li Xin's face for a moment. The answer he had been waiting for didn't seem so special. He was just stunned for a moment when he realized the Protector Duwei was Xu Fu.

At this moment, a burst of rapid footsteps sounded outside the tent, and a shadow moved quickly from far to near.

Li Xin’s expression suddenly turned cold, his hand only a short distance from the halberd he had thrown aside—within easy reach.

The tent flap was suddenly lifted. "Sir?!"

A familiar voice.

"Sang Zhong?" Xu Fu stood up and looked over.

Sang Zhong stood at the entrance of the tent, his face slightly flushed, looking as if he had run very fast. Not long after he arrived, Jianjia and Lord Longyang also came over. Seeing that Xu Fu was still standing there safe and sound, everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

Only Li Xin remained sitting on the ground, head tilted, looking at them with a cold expression, appearing like an outsider who had appeared in the tent.

"Are you alright, sir?" Sang Zhong had just called out before falling silent like a mute. Jianjia took the initiative to speak, walking inside with Lord Longyang as he did so.

"I'm fine, the assassin has been caught," Xu Fu said calmly.

Sang Zhong felt a stifled anger in his chest and gritted his teeth. "It is our fault. If we had been in the tent at the time, how could we have let you be ambushed? If something had happened, how could we have the face to see you?"

Jianjia hadn't felt much at first, but hearing Sang Zhong say this, he nodded heavily, a look of guilt appearing on his face, which was flushed red with shame.

Sang Zhong had many more things to say, but upon seeing Li Xin still sitting there, he couldn't say a word.

Li Xin was an outsider!

Sang Zhong’s gaze was as sharp as a knife, but Li Xin seemed completely unaware. After they had finished saying what they wanted to say, he slowly interjected, "You all go out. I'll guard the Duwei here."

Sang Zhong and Jianjia tensed up almost simultaneously, their cold, sharp gazes fixed on Li Xin, as if he had snatched away something precious.

He had snatched it, hadn't he...

He had snatched their position of protecting Xu Fu, as if silently accusing them of incompetence. How could they not be frustrated?

But Li Xin clearly had a thicker skin and a gaze that could pierce through people. Both sides stared at each other, neither willing to budge.

Finally, Lord Longyang sighed softly and said to Xu Fu, "Sir has been frightened and needs a good rest. We will come to see you at dawn." Lord Longyang met Xu Fu's eyes, and Xu Fu thought to himself, *how clever.* Lord Longyang’s words were clearly not meant for him, but for Sang Zhong and Jianjia. Sang Zhong and his companion already felt guilty, and now, thinking that Xu Fu must have been frightened and hadn't slept well, they couldn't stay and disturb his rest. Since they couldn't beat this man, they had to take a step back for Xu Fu's sake; they could always see him at dawn.

Sang Zhong moved first, saying, "Then let's go."

Once they withdrew, the tent became quiet again.

Distracted by them, Li Xin also became silent. Xu Fu turned around and glanced at him, seeing only his clear, resilient eyes, which were exceptionally bright in the dark night.

Xu Fu sat back on the bed and, after thinking for a moment, lay down. Before he knew it, he fell asleep, but this time he didn't have any more dreams.

Xu Fu guessed that either the Qin army would have no more trouble, or he had pried into the secrets of heaven too frequently and no longer had the opportunity to know the future. Xu Fu didn't really care. Such things were meant to be left to fate; if one cared too much, it would only disturb one's inner peace.

When he woke up, he saw that Li Xin had also fallen asleep leaning against the bed.

He could sleep like that? He really had a big heart.

Xu Fu got up, his eyes dazzled by a flash of light. He turned his head and saw that the dagger was still stuck in the bedpost. Xu Fu raised his hand to pull it out...

...It didn't move.

He pulled again.

...Still didn't move.

Xu Fu suppressed the urge to curse.

How much strength had he used at the time? No wonder he couldn't pull it out now.

Just as he was about to give up, a warm breath enveloped him from behind. Then, an arm reached out, easily pulled the dagger out, and handed it to him.

Xu Fu felt like he had been reduced to a "pretty boy" by comparison: ...

He grabbed the dagger, put it into the sheath, and turned around to see Li Xin standing behind him, though his expression wasn't as tense as it had been yesterday.

He originally wanted to say "thank you," but looking at that face, Xu Fu swallowed the words back involuntarily.

Li Xin turned and strode out. Standing at the entrance of the tent, he ordered the Qin soldiers outside, "Bring the assassin from last night here!"

And the Qin soldiers really brought him over, carrying him in their hands without giving him any dignity. It was early summer, so the assassin hadn't frozen, but having spent the night next to the warhorses, he couldn't help but tremble, fearing that the horses would step on him and leave him disemboweled. His face was pale, with dark circles under his eyes and bloodshot eyes. His already overly feminine features looked even more somber now, inexplicably making people feel a sense of repulsion toward him.

Li Xin didn't bring the man into Xu Fu's tent, but found another one—a tent large enough that one could smell the scent of blood from afar.

Xu Fu felt a sudden jolt of energy. After a simple wash, he followed along.

Before long, Sang Zhong and the others arrived as well.

However, Wang Jian had gone out and only sent someone to comfort Xu Fu first.

Li Xin turned his face and said to Xu Fu, "The General has handed this matter over to me."

When did that happen? Xu Fu was confused.

When he looked at the assassin again, the man had already been tied to a torture rack.

Yes, a torture rack.

When on campaign, they always carried such things, making it convenient to grab an assassin or spy and interrogate them at any time.

Xu Fu remembered that Wang Jian seemed to have warned him about this the day before.

"After winning a battle, the other side will inevitably resort to underhanded tricks, sending assassins to raid—this is too common in the camp. Duwei, you must be careful."

还是有人突地掀起帐子，大马金刀地阔步走进来，问了句“如何了”，这才打破了沉寂的气氛，众人都不约而同仰头向他看去，其中也包括了徐福。
徐福眼眸里乍地闪过那道挺拔精瘦的身影。
是之前接他们的那个领头人。
待到那人走近了，徐福才看清他脸上已经洗清了血污和泥灰，那张脸，可是好生熟悉得很啊……徐福细细将回忆一捋，便找到了记忆中的那个名字。
“李信？”徐福出声问。
越瞧那张脸，徐福便越肯定了，之前时间匆忙，他没来得及仔细打量，其实只要稍微多注意一些，便能忽略掉那些血污，直接看到底下的脸是个什么模样。毕竟脸上的骨头是固定摆在那里的，没有谁能和李信拥有一样的骨头和命格。
李信也一声不吭，神色复杂地到了徐福的跟前。
王翦正要开口呢，偏偏李信又突然开口说话了，“原来你还没忘了我。”
徐福歪了歪头，好让那大夫更方便为他上药，无比自然地道：“你那张脸，如何能忘？”
这话，由一百个人来听，自然就有一百种不同的猜测。
周围的人听见这话，便神色怪异地在他们身上来回打量，桑中的脸登时就拉了下来，虎视眈眈地盯着李信。
王翦也不知道这是哪一出，轻咳一声，打破了尴尬的气氛，“此次，实要多谢都尉。”
正巧此时又有人进来了，徐福便遥遥一指，“王翦将军还是谢他们二人吧。”
众人顺着徐福指的方向看过去，只见一高一矮两个风流人物，端的好相貌！而王翦心中再度升起了那怪异的熟悉感。那个高个子的，他究竟是在何处见过的？这样的好相貌，他若是见过应当不会忘记啊。
打帐外走来的正是龙阳君和蒹葭，龙阳君注意到了王翦的目光，不动声色地让神色变得温柔了一些。他的眉眼一旦温柔起来，便与那个跟在魏王身侧的男宠龙阳君有了天差地别。
王翦不自在地收回了目光，暗道，或许只是错觉罢……
当时有人是看见龙阳君和蒹葭那敏捷身手的，大家都是军中武人，对于有本事的人，自然再佩服不过，此时见他们来了，自然有人忍不住站起身来，冲着龙阳君便道：“阁下一手好剑法，能否请教一二？”
身上带点功夫本事的，多少有点好斗的脾气，看见厉害人物，总想要一较高下。
莫说是他们，或许哪一日徐福碰见了比自己更厉害的人物，他说不准也想上前跟人比试一通。
偏偏龙阳君突然一指身旁的蒹葭，道：“那得问他了？”
那人愣了愣，没明白什么意思。
蒹葭却是脸色一黑，冷着脸闷头也往徐福跟前去了。
王翦这才回味过来，忙问徐福：“这几位都是都尉的随从？”
“正是……嘶——”徐福硬生生地将倒吸气的声音掐没在嗓子里了。若是呼痛，实在太有损形象。
众人见他那张俊美的脸都透着白了，顿觉心都跟着揪了一下。王翦微微有些尴尬，若非为了他，徐福倒也不至于随军上战场，他本就毫无战力，偏偏又生得一副尊贵模样，往人群中一站，就好像生怕谁认不出他的地位一样，他的身上便不自觉地放出光华来了，敌军怎么可能忽略过他呢？
不过这尴尬也只是一瞬的，王翦很快便恢复了平静的心态，他郑重地向徐福、龙阳君、蒹葭三人道了谢。
此时有将领忍不住问道：“都尉可否再瞧一瞧，接下来可还有什么祸事？”
其他人也连忙附和，“是啊，将军可是不能出事的啊……”
此时徐福脖子上的伤口也已经处理结束了，大夫从地上站了起来，徐福也能直起脖子了。众人看着徐福的目光登时便升起了几分敬畏。不管遭遇什么，都能面不改色的人物，实在厉害啊！他们却不知，这只是徐福多年练就出来的本事罢了，如今已深入骨髓成了习惯，自然不会改变。
“王建将军应当十分清楚，卜筮之术并非那样容易。”徐福神色淡淡地说出这句话来，众人闻言，脸顿时就红了，忙向徐福道歉，“都尉，我们不通此事，多有冒犯，还请都尉原谅！”
“是啊是啊，我们也没想到这一茬，想来那卜筮之术应当是十分麻烦的，嘿嘿，那就不敢再劳烦都尉了……”
虽然他们口中这样说，不过徐福猜大部分人是没放在心上的。
什么都尉？自然不能同与他们朝夕相处，同上战场的王翦相比！他们说不定此时正在想，若是劳累一些又怎么了？若是能让王翦将军避开危险，那不是十分划算吗？何必再扭扭捏捏？
徐福的目光从他们脸上扫过，大致就知道了这些人的性格，和脑中所想。
倒是王翦并未强求，能躲过一次危险，已是大善！怎能奢求更多？许多贪心的人，不都是因为自己的贪得无厌而丢了性命吗？
王翦命人去留意那赵军领头人的来头，之后又与徐福闲聊几句，碍于跟前人实在太多，而王翦还要与诸位将领调整战术。徐福便很自觉地带着自己的人出了帐子，只是他走时，李信回过头来瞧了他一眼，那目光怪不是滋味的，带着几分沉闷的味道。
徐福只觉得李信这模样，与之前巷子里的模样不大相同了，转念一想，或许是军中历练，越发成熟了。
如今李斯已是客卿，说不定过不了多久，李信便也是将军了。
他和侯生的批语都应验了，也不知到时候算是谁胜谁负。
身后的帷帐落下，徐福已经和他们走远了。
军中士兵小心地打量着徐福一行人的模样。
俗话说军中无女人，久了见着母猪都觉得是香的呢。更莫说是瞧见几个长得比姑娘还好看的人，那还不得憋足了劲儿瞧？不过他们的目光也并无恶意，多是带着好奇和惊叹，似乎很难想象，同是人，怎么就有人能长成这副模样呢？
徐福一行人就顶着这样的目光进了帐子。
桑中也不知突然抽了什么风，为徐福布置好床榻，为他端来食物和热水，随后便头也不回地出去了。
徐福一怔，问蒹葭：“他怎么了？”
蒹葭那神经粗得都快赶上筷子了，他摇了摇头，“我不知道。”
龙阳君的心思从来没往桑中那边遛过，自然更不清楚了。
徐福一头雾水，实在想不明白也就丢开不想了。
转眼便到了落日时分，这个时代也没有什么娱乐项目，徐福这时才觉得白日里活动过度了，四肢都有些酸疼，他简单洗漱一番，便上床榻歇息去了。只是帐中久久没有等到桑中回来。而桑中不归来一同休息，蒹葭和龙阳君也就跟慢半拍地觉醒了尴尬症一样，也不愿留在帐中了。
很快，帐中便只剩下了徐福一人。
他能听见外面军士的呼号声，大约是在训练，也或许是在交换警戒，口中没事儿喊一喊口号，他还能听见外面的风将帷帐吹得呼啦作响的声音……最后他的耳边却是一片寂静了。什么声音都好似离他远去了。
……今夜，会入梦去吗？
徐福迷迷糊糊地闭上了眼，思维很快坠入了黑暗的深渊之中。
但奇异的是，他并未再做任何和战争有关的梦，他的思维之中有个潜意识在期待着做梦，期待着期待着，他好像就真的入梦了。
他看见自己穿着一身白袍，就在咸阳宫中那样普普通通的白袍，但是明明是件捂得严实的袍子，却生生被他穿出了个“新样式”来。
那白袍被革带在腰间轻轻一束，两边的袖子坠了下来，宽大的袖袍几乎能挨到地面了，露出他那白皙的肩膀来，在梦中的自己似乎瘦弱了许多，那肩膀白是白，但就跟没血色一样。原本应该是暧昧情色的画面，就生生被徐福的思维给搅没了。
他的视角又变了。
他仰头看去，似乎能瞧见嬴政的身影，坐在桌案之前，那个位置距离他特别的远，好像伸手怎么也够不到似的。
而嬴政连半点眼神也不分给他。
仿佛徐福被隔离在了他的世界之外。徐福就这样仰望着他，脖子都看得有些酸了，嬴政却还是一脸冷峻的模样，那股寒气似乎从他身体里往外在冒。徐福看着他，脑子里登时冒出了四个字来：难以接近。
徐福胸中陡然升起了一股怒气。
嬴政居然对他这样？虽然那是梦，但也不能这样啊！
但是他的视角、思维根本影响不了梦中的徐福。他看着徐福神色漠然地朝桌案前的嬴政走了过去，嬴政终于放下了手中的竹简吗，他抬头看了看徐福。
徐福的视角在整个大殿里扫视了一圈。
他发现大殿里并非只有他和嬴政二人。还有不少的宫人分立在两侧，他们低着头，脸色同样是漠然的，谁也不敢抬头去打量徐福的模样。
徐福心底陡然升起了一股怪异的感觉。
“过来。”梦中的嬴政对着他开口了，声音低沉冷漠。
徐福不受控制地往前挪了一步，下一刻就被嬴政摁倒在了桌案上，徐福猝不及防地瞪大了眼，还是熟悉的劲道！但是嬴政的脸色，梦中自己的反应，却都透着一股诡异。
身上白袍被褪下的时候，他骤然想到周围还站着一圈儿宫人呢，徐福脑子里陡然打了个激灵，猛地惊醒过来了。
他睁开双眼，背后已经出了一身的冷汗。
也就是这一瞬间，徐福发觉到了不对劲的地方。
帐子外面有个人影。
哦不……不是在帐子外……徐福不自觉地打了个冷战。那人分明是在……帐子里……他不知道那个人是不是正在盯着自己，他是谁？为什么会在这个时候进来？他手中拿兵器了吗？那瞬间，徐福脑子里已经百转千回了。
他暗暗握住了腰间的匕首。
他的被子里还有龟甲等家当。
那匕首是他从咸阳城离开时，嬴政交给他的，出于习惯，他便和自己的家当一同搁在被窝里了，这个时候抓起来倒是刚刚好。
匕首入手冰凉，倒是让徐福瞬间镇静了不少。
若是歹人……
那对方得有多大的胆子才敢进秦兵的驻扎地来？周围全是秦兵，他就不怕死无全尸吗？
就在此时，徐福听见了对方挪动步子的声音，一点一点，似乎朝着他过来了，徐福微微屏息，安静地等待着对方过来的时候，只要他看清对方的面孔是陌生的，那他就不会给对方一点机会。
他捏紧了手中的匕首，微微眯上了眼。
人影近了，徐福明显感觉到眼皮上方陡然一暗，他也大致看清了对方的轮廓，一个陌生人！
他不再犹豫，捏着匕首弹跳而起，另一只手的龟甲先朝着对方的脸糊了上去，将对方砸懵了，龟甲还挡住了对方的视线，随后徐福趁机将抽出来的匕首，插在了对方的脖颈旁，那人被他牢牢抵在了床柱上，匕首只要稍微歪一歪，就能将他的脖颈划破。
“来人！有刺客！”徐福陡然拔高了嗓门。
对方听见徐福的声音，立刻剧烈地挣扎了起来。
“别动！”徐福把刀子往对方的脖颈上贴了贴，冰凉锋利的触感，倒是让对方的动作滞了滞。对方的劲儿太大了，他只能先这样逼着对方。
此时驻扎地上已经闹哄哄一片了，所有人都被徐福这一嗓子惊醒了，当先就有守夜的人进来，手中举着火把。
秦兵可谓是惊慌不已，深怕都尉出了什么事，但是等他们慌慌张张地举着刀剑近了，才见徐福手握匕首，将一个人压在了床柱上呢，那个人见有人来了，登时挣扎得更厉害了，徐福一个手滑，你就将他的脖颈刺了一下，顿时鲜血就飚了出来，那人疼得打了个哆嗦，惨叫一声，倒是不敢再乱动了。
众人就这样目瞪口呆地看着，徐福那小身板，竟然也制服了一个刺客？
徐福头发散乱，他身上只松垮穿着深衣，他回转过头来，眼睛一横，冷得教人不自觉地直打哆嗦，“还愣着做什么？将人拿下！”这话却并非徐福之口。
徐福原本也是要说的，但却被走进帐内来的青年将领给抢了先。
那青年将领正是李信。
李信面沉如水，目光锐利冰寒如苍原上的狼，他手中还提着一柄长戟，若是戳在那刺客的身上，肯定能直接将他的肚子都给剖开。那刺客与李信对了一眼，控制不住地浑身抖了起来。
这么没胆儿还来做刺客？
此时已经有秦兵上前，将那刺客钳住，徐福松开手，退后两步，有秦兵伸腿踹了那刺客一脚，刺客绷不住，双膝一软，就跪倒在了地上，李信上前，用长戟挑起了那刺客的下巴，外面的月光并着火把的光亮，将那刺客的面容映得一清二楚。
徐福面色一冷，新仇旧怨齐上心头。
这不就是那个搭弓射他们的弱冠男子吗？胆子真够肥的，带着伤就来闯营地了？
因为有长戟就卡在脖子那儿呢，弱冠男子连动也不敢动。
李信冷声道：“先把人提走关起来。”
秦兵们也不愣着，凶神恶煞地直接将人拎起来往外走了。
他们这副做派，反倒叫对方傻眼了。
不拷问，不怒骂，更不嚷着要割下他的头，他就这样被拎出去了，外面月光如水，营地里点着火把，照亮了士兵们黝黑的脸膛，一个个神色冷酷。乍一看就好似到了阎王殿一般。
那人勉强稳住了心绪，然后被人带到了另外的棚子里，双手双脚这么一捆，就怎么样也挣扎不开了。
而这厢，李信看了看徐福的模样，喉头动了动，半天才挤出来一句话，“你……你没受惊吧？”
“没事。”此时徐福的情绪已经平复不少了，连那个梦都被他扔到了脑后去了，只是帐外的风刮进来，徐福不自觉地有点想要打哆嗦。
李信踌躇了一会儿，然后拔腿走到了床榻边，替徐福理了理床榻上的被子，随后他又注意到不对，忙将手中的长戟抛开，大马金刀地就在床边席地而坐，道：“都尉歇息吧，我便守在此处。”
徐福原本就睡得有些早，此时做了梦惊醒过来，又经历这么一出，什么瞌睡都没了，哪里还睡得早？不过他还是缓缓走到了床榻边坐下。
李信见他没有要躺下去的意思，这才绷着脸道：“当初我问都尉姓名，都尉道我终有一日会知晓，那今日都尉可肯说了？”其实就算徐福不说，李信也能打听到的，只要问一问王翦便知晓了。只是王翦不太喜欢他，会徒添麻烦。
徐福也不打算藏着掖着，能与李信在秦军中遇见，也算是缘分，何况瞧李信如今这模样，好像还记着当初他没头没脑地闯进那巷子，为他看了相，却又潇洒抛开他的事。
徐福可不想被人这么记着。
“姓徐，名福。”徐福大方地说道。
李信听完之后，脸上一瞬间闪过了茫然之色，期待许久的答案，似乎也没有什么稀奇。只是他见到护军都尉是徐福的时候，愣了一阵罢了。
此时帐外突然响起了一阵迅疾的脚步声，有人影飞快地在帐外，由远而近。
李信脸色骤然变冷，手距离那甩在一旁的长戟，也就一小段的距离，对于他来说，触手可及。
帷帐被猛地掀起，“先生？！”
熟悉的声音。
“桑中？”徐福站了起来，抬眼看去。
桑中站在帐子口，脸色微微泛着红，看来刚才跑得很急，他刚到没多久，蒹葭和龙阳君也就过来了，见徐福还好端端地站在那里，众人这才或深或浅地松了一口气。
唯有李信还坐在地面上，他仰着头，神色冷漠地望着他们，看上去像是帐子里多出来的一个异类。
“先生无事吧？”桑中刚叫了那一声，就跟锯嘴葫芦一样不开口了，倒是蒹葭主动开口说了话，一边说着他还一边带着龙阳君往里走了。
“我无事，刺客被抓住了。”徐福淡淡道。
桑中胸中憋着一股闷气，咬牙道：“是我们之过，若我们当时也在帐中，如何会让先生遭此偷袭？若是出了事，我们如何敢见先生？”
原本蒹葭还不觉得有什么，听桑中这么一说，也马上重重点头，脸上露出了愧疚的神色，脸还泛着红，那是羞的。
桑中心中本还有许多话要说，但是一瞧还坐在那儿的李信，他顿时就什么话也说不出来了。
李信是个外人！
桑中的目光锐利似刀，偏偏李信像是毫无所觉一般，等他们把想说的话都说完了，这才慢悠悠地插了句嘴，“你们出去吧，都尉这里有我守着。”
桑中和蒹葭几乎是同时都绷紧了身子，目光冷厉地盯着李信，就好像李信抢走了什么宝贵的东西一样。
是抢了啊……
抢了他们保护徐福的位置，就好像是在无声地指责他们的无能，心里多憋火啊！
但是李信明显脸皮更厚，而且目光更能戳死人，双方就这么你看我，我看你，谁也不肯挪步子。
还是龙阳君轻叹了一口气，对徐福道：“先生受了惊吓还需好生歇息，待到天亮我们再来见先生。”龙阳君与徐福对视了一眼，徐福暗道一声，真够聪明的。龙阳君这话明摆着不是说给他听的，而是说给桑中和蒹葭听的。桑中二人心中本就有愧，如今再一想到徐福肯定受了惊吓，没睡好，他们也不能继续留在这里扰了徐福的休息，既然拗不过这个男人，那就只有先为了徐福退一步了，待到天亮总能来见徐福的。
桑中率先挪了挪步子，道：“那我们先走吧。”
待到他们撤了出去，帐子里顿时又安静了下来。
被他们那么一打岔，李信也就变得一言不发了，徐福转过身来，瞥了他一眼，只能瞥见他清亮坚韧的双眸，在黑夜里格外晃人。
徐福坐回了床榻上，想了想还是躺了下去，不知不觉倒也睡着了，只是这次倒没再做什么梦了。
徐福猜测，要么是秦军不会再有任何麻烦了，要么就是他窥探天机太过频繁，如今已经没有机会可以获知未来的祸福了。徐福倒也不太在意。这种事本就是随缘的，若是太过在意，反而乱了本心。
他醒来之后，就见李信也倚着床边睡着了。
这样也能睡？心真大。
徐福起身，眼睛被一道亮光晃了下，他转头一看，才发现那把匕首还插在床柱上呢，徐福抬手去拔……
……不动。
再拔。
……还是不动。
徐福忍住了骂脏话的冲动。
当时他是使了多大的劲儿啊？现在才会拔不出来。
就在他准备收手的时候，身后突然笼过来了温热的气息，紧接着一只手臂伸来，轻轻松松就将匕首拔了下来，递到了他的眼前。
徐福顿时觉得自己被衬托成了一只小白脸：……
他抓住那把匕首放进刀鞘里，回过身来，就见李信正站在他身后，不过脸色已经不像昨天那样紧紧绷着了。
原本想要说个谢字，但是对上他那张脸，徐福又不自觉地咽回去了。
李信转身大步走出去，站在帐子口，就吩咐外面的秦兵，“把昨晚的刺客拎过来！”
然后那些秦兵就真的将人拎过来了，提在手里，丝毫不给对方留半点尊严地拎过来了，此时入夏，那刺客倒也没冻着，只是跟战马挨了一夜，免不了有些哆嗦，生怕那些战马一脚踩下来，让他肠穿肚烂。他的脸色发着白，眼下青黑，眼底更是布满了血丝。原本就过分阴柔的面孔，此时看上去更让人觉得沉郁了，莫名的就让人对他忍不住生出几分抵触来。
李信倒是没把人带到徐福的帐子里去，而是另外寻了个营帐，那个营帐足够大，远远的就能嗅见一股血腥气。
徐福不自觉地精神一震，简单洗漱过后，便跟着过去了。
不多时，桑中等人也到了。
只是王翦出去了，只派了人先过来慰问徐福。
李信转过脸来，对徐福道：“将军将此事交给我了。”
什么时候的事？徐福一头雾水。
等他再看向那刺客的时候，刺客已经被绑在了刑架上。
对，刑架。
出征在外，他们也是会随身带着这玩意儿的，方便抓个刺客、间谍随时拷问。
徐福记起前一日王翦似乎就是这样提醒他的。
“打了胜仗，对方难免动些歪邪的脑筋，派个刺客来偷袭，这在营地里已经是太过常见的事儿了，都尉可要小心。”

chapters.title: 第99章
chapters.translated_text:
How could someone who is merely a leader be so easily sent out as an assassin? Xu Fu felt a bit suspicious and looked up at the man on the rack. The assassin’s mouth was gagged, so he could only struggle in vain. He wanted to roar, but even though the veins on his neck were bulging, he couldn't make a single sound; only the rack creaked with a teeth-gritting noise as he shook it.

At this moment, the assassin glared viciously at Xu Fu, showing no awareness of his status as a prisoner.

That aside, Xu Fu also discovered a look of jealousy and resentment in the man's eyes.

Jealous of what? Resentful of what? Did he kill his whole family? Or could it be that this person... knew the original owner of this body?

Just then, Xu Fu noticed Li Xin pull a dagger from his waist. It had no sheath, and the blade emitted a sharp, cold glint. Li Xin’s face was dark, his eyes filled with a grim aura. Without asking, Xu Fu could vaguely guess what he intended to do.

The assassin’s gaze grew increasingly vicious, but it eventually turned into fear.

Xu Fu suddenly stepped forward and tore the gag from the assassin’s mouth. Li Xin was startled and paused, taking it as a sign to obey Xu Fu’s wishes.

The next second, the assassin roared angrily, "Let me go! You running dogs of Qin! Scum!"

Li Xin was neither angry nor amused; he simply stepped forward indifferently and stared at him. The assassin shivered, but unwilling to stop and lose face, he sneered at Xu Fu, "With so many men protecting you, are you someone important, or just a homosexual?"

The assassin intended to mock him for not being a "real man" and only relying on others for protection.

Xu Fu didn't get angry at all. The assassin had probably forgotten who it was that captured him in the tent. Therefore, Xu Fu didn't care about that remark; instead, he was interested in the latter half of the assassin’s sentence.

Calling him a homosexual?

This term... it had never appeared during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods. Even in later eras, ancient people usually referred to male homosexuality as the "habit of the cut sleeve" or the "fondness for Longyang." So, how could this word pop out of the assassin’s mouth? And he was clearly using it as an insult.

Just as Xu Fu was observing him unhurriedly, Li Xin had already turned hostile.

He didn't understand what "homosexual" meant, but he could tell the first half wasn't a compliment, and the second half certainly wasn't either. A prisoner, trapped in the Qin army camp, yet still daring to be this arrogant?

Li Xin stepped forward and slapped him across the face.

Since the commander didn't want him to bleed so quickly, he would let him feel pain first. He looked like a coward; a good beating should do the trick.

Li Xin’s strength was immense. With that slap, the assassin couldn't help but cry out in pain, kicking his legs wildly. His entire face was forced to one side, blood seeped from the corner of his mouth, and his face swelled up almost instantly, turning a purplish-red where one could almost see the suddenly engorged blood vessels beneath—it was horrifying!

He had turned into a pig-faced mess. Jianjia, seeing his appearance, couldn't hold back a snort of laughter.

That laugh was like a fuse lighting a stick of dynamite. The assassin lost his temper and began cursing at Jianjia, his mouth full of profanities. Because he spoke so quickly, ordinary people couldn't even make out what he was saying.

Xu Fu sneered inwardly.

A coward!

He was almost certain that the person in front of him had the same origins as himself; otherwise, how could his cursing be identical to the street aunties of his past life?

This person only dared to act this way. If he really had any backbone, he wouldn't hide behind words others couldn't understand.

Xu Fu turned to glance at Jianjia and saw her looking unhappy, her brows slightly furrowed. But because she couldn't understand what the assassin was saying, she didn't get angry enough to step up and strike him herself. If Jianjia had actually struck him, he might have lost half his life.

Li Xin was the most composed of them all. He didn't understand anything either and maintained his calm expression. However, after receiving a look from Xu Fu, he didn't hesitate. He grabbed the dagger and pressed it against the assassin’s chest, then said in the same calm tone, "Let's open a hole here first."

Lord Longyang suddenly chimed in, "And then you'll be able to hear your chest being torn open, the sound of the wind blowing through it... You'll feel how cold your chest really is, and your heart and lungs will ache with a chilling sensation..."

Lord Longyang and Li Xin played off each other, their tones so eerie that the assassin shivered uncontrollably. His lips turned white instantly, and his eyes went blank.

Someone like this could be an assassin?

Both Lord Longyang and Li Xin realized something was wrong.

Sang Zhong shook his head and said, "He’s not a professional."

Li Xin didn't hold back. With a push of the dagger and a "shhh" sound, the fabric was pierced. The assassin couldn't help but scream, "No, no, no! What do you want to do? Let's talk this over!"

Li Xin stopped and looked at Xu Fu.

Xu Fu shook his head with a cold face.

Seeing this, the assassin’s heart turned cold, and he wondered how else he could curse Xu Fu in his mind.

Xu Fu watched him coldly the entire time. He never considered himself a saint. An assassin who wanted his life, and who continued to insult him and Jianjia after being captured—he certainly wouldn't tolerate it. Besides, with Li Xin doing the dirty work, why shouldn't he let him?

Lord Longyang turned his head and looked at Xu Fu with slight surprise. Perhaps because of how Xu Fu had taken him away from the Wei palace, he couldn't help but guess that Xu Fu was cold on the outside but soft on the inside. But now it seemed... he was cold on the outside and cold on the inside too... He had misjudged him.

Li Xin thrust the dagger in, and the assassin wailed, "Let, let go!"

Li Xin, of course, didn't let go; he simply stopped the blade.

The assassin could clearly feel the cold, sharp dagger slicing through his skin and penetrating deep inside. The tearing pain instantly occupied all his thoughts. He was in pain, so much pain he wanted to curse his ancestors. He glared viciously at Xu Fu. Why? Why, as fellow transmigrators, was this person able to attain such status, while he had to struggle so hard only to end up in this state?

As fellow transmigrators, shouldn't the other party treat him with some favor?

The assassin had clearly forgotten how he had attacked Xu Fu in the first place.

Only then did Xu Fu speak slowly, "You guys interrogate him." This was directed at Li Xin.

Li Xin asked the assassin in a low voice, "Are you willing to confess?"

The assassin’s features were twisted in pain. He hadn't expected to fall into the hands of the Qin army, and even less did he expect the Qin soldiers to be so ruthless! He couldn't stop shivering, "...W-what do you want to ask..."

Damn it, if you want me to confess, tell me what you want to know first!

"What is your name?" Li Xin asked coldly, his demeanor strictly professional and so rigid that there was no room for negotiation.

The assassin knew that once in his hands, there was no chance for mercy.

"Zheng... You'an..."

Xu Fu frowned. It was a name he had never heard before, not even vaguely familiar. Was he a person not recorded in history?

Li Xin said bluntly, "A person I've never even heard of. I suppose he's just a discarded pawn of the Zhao army."

This remark seemed to infuriate Zheng You'an. His chest heaved violently, and he stared fixedly at Li Xin, but he didn't dare to curse again, fearing the dagger would truly carve a hole in his chest.

Jianjia laughed contemptuously, "Is he still unconvinced? He's just a nobody, yet he thinks he's some big shot?"

Zheng You'an couldn't bear such mockery and suddenly raised his voice to retort, "The Zhao army... should have, should have been under my command to scatter you, and then I would have taken Wang Jian’s head! Without Wang Jian, what is the Qin army?"

Lord Longyang said faintly, "He’s not entirely stupid; he knows to target General Wang Jian."

Hearing Lord Longyang’s remark, which sounded like both a compliment and an insult, Zheng You'an became agitated again. He wanted to struggle, but the dagger embedded in his skin reminded him not to move. He could only look at Lord Longyang with his effeminate face, unconvinced, and cursed in a low voice, "Pretty boy."

Xu Fu was immediately displeased.

You call Lord Longyang a pretty boy? How could he be a pretty boy?!

Xu Fu didn't necessarily like Lord Longyang that much, but Lord Longyang was now within his circle. As a prisoner, you should be grateful you weren't subjected to torture, and yet you're still acting like a spoiled brat?

Xu Fu just gave a look to Li Xin, who immediately understood and pulled out the dagger.

Zheng You'an let out a sudden sigh of relief and leaned against the rack, gasping heavily. But before he could catch his breath, Li Xin suddenly turned and stabbed his shoulder with the dagger, mercilessly. Blood splattered onto Li Xin’s armor, his expression unchanged, while Zheng You'an screamed in agony.

"Ahhhhh, what are you doing!" If not for the rack, Zheng You'an would have been rolling on the ground in pain.

Li Xin watched him coldly, "Keep your mouth shut and don't say things you shouldn't."

Sweat dripped from Zheng You'an’s forehead. He looked at Xu Fu with a tremble. Right... how could he have forgotten him? This person could understand him...

Zheng You'an carefully hid the hatred in his eyes.

"What is your status in the Zhao army?" Li Xin asked again.

Zheng You'an gritted his teeth, and it took a long time before he squeezed a sentence from his throat, "...I... I am a retainer under a merchant in the city..."

Xu Fu thought to himself, this merchant is taking in retainers for no reason—is he trying to be another Lü Buwei?

"How did you get into the Zhao army?"

"I was... I was recommended."

"Was it your idea to discard the armor for a surprise attack and to have archers target General Wang Jian?"

At this moment, Xu Fu noticed a hint of pride in Zheng You'an’s eyes, "Yes... it was me..."

This transmigrator is truly interesting.
chapters.source_text:
只是一个领头人，怎么会这样轻易派出来当了刺客呢？徐福心中有些疑惑，抬头朝那刑架上的人看了过去。刺客被堵住了口舌，只能徒劳地挣扎着，他想要嘶吼，但是脖颈上都青筋绷起了，却还是一声也发不出来，只有刑架被他摇动发出“咯吱咯吱”令人牙酸的声音。
而此时这个刺客，恶狠狠地瞪着徐福，丝毫没有身为阶下囚的觉悟。
这也就罢了，徐福还从对方的眸子里发现了，嫉妒和愤恨的色彩。
嫉妒什么？愤恨什么？难道自己还宰他全家了？或者说这个人……跟原身认识？
就在此时徐福注意到李信从腰间拔出了一把匕首，没有刀鞘，只能看见匕首散发着锋利的寒光。李信沉着脸，眼神透着森然的味道，不用问徐福也能隐约猜到他要做什么。
那刺客的目光越发狠戾起来，最后却转为了畏惧。
徐福突然上前一步扯掉了刺客嘴里堵着的玩意儿，李信一怔，顿住了脚步，算是表现自己服从徐福的意思。
刺客下一秒便愤怒地吼叫了起来，“松开我！秦国的走狗！杂碎！”
李信不怒也不笑，只是漠然地上前一步，盯着他，刺客打了个哆嗦，但是又不甘心就这样住了嘴，实在长他人志气，于是冲着徐福冷笑道：“这么多男人护着你，你是个人物，还是个同性恋？”
刺客是想嘲笑他不是个男人，只被他人保护。
徐福压根不动怒，这刺客大概是忘记了，是谁在帐篷里把他擒住的。所以徐福根本没在乎这句话，他在乎的反倒是刺客的后半句话。
骂他同性恋？
这个词……在春秋战国时期可都是从未出现过的吧，哪怕是到了后期，古时的人也常是以断袖之癖、龙阳之好来称呼男同性恋。那这个刺客嘴里怎么会冒出这个词来呢？而且他明显是将这个词当做脏话了。
就在徐福不紧不慢打量他的时候，李信已经翻脸了。
他听不出那个同性恋是什么意思，但他听得出前半句不是什么后话，后半句自然也不是。一个俘虏，被困在秦军大营里，还敢这么嚣张？
李信上前就先给了他一耳光。
既然都尉不想让他这么快见血，就先让他知道疼吧，看上去也是个怂货，先揍一顿就能起效了。
李信的手劲儿极大，那一巴掌扇上去，“啊！”刺客忍不住痛呼了一声，脚下乱踢，他整张脸都被迫偏到了一边去，血丝从他的嘴角渗了下来，脸上几乎是立刻就肿了起来，紫红一片，几乎能看见下面骤然撑大的血管，好不骇然！
他变成了一张猪头脸，蒹葭瞧着他的模样，憋不住噗嗤笑出了声。
这一声笑，就如同点燃炸药的引线，那刺客又收不住火，冲着蒹葭就大骂了起来，满嘴脏话，因为他语速极快，常人还真听不清他骂的是什么。
徐福心中冷笑一声。
怂货！
他几乎已经确定面前这人，跟他是一样的来历了，不然怎么连骂脏话都跟上辈子街头大妈如出一辙呢？
这人也就只敢这样了，若是真有点血性，倒是别藏着掖着骂别人听不懂的话啊。
徐福转头扫了一眼蒹葭，见蒹葭一脸不快，微微皱着眉，但是因为听不懂这刺客究竟说的什么，倒是没有气得上前直接招呼他。这刺客要是真被蒹葭招呼一下，那他的命也说不定就得去半条了。
其中李信最为沉稳，他也什么都没明白，看上去还是那副平平静静的模样，但他接到徐福的目光之后，便不再犹豫，抓着匕首就先顶在了刺客的胸膛上，随后用同样平静的语气道：“先在这里开个洞。”
龙阳君突然接了句话，“然后你就能听见自己的胸膛破开，被风吹过的声音……你会觉得自己的胸膛真冷啊，心肺都被吹着冷丝丝的疼……”
龙阳君与李信一唱一和的，那语气透着阴森森的味道，教那刺客硬生生地打了个寒颤，嘴唇瞬间就白了，两眼还有些发直。
就这模样还能当刺客？
龙阳君和李信都瞧出不对来了。
桑中摇头道：“不是个干这一道的。”
李信也不客气，匕首一用力，嗤啦一声，布料被捅开了，刺客忍不住叫出了声，“别别别！你们想干什么？有话好好说！”
李信停住动作，看向了徐福。
徐福冷着脸摇了摇头。
见他这副模样，刺客心都凉了半截，心中也不知又在如何咒骂徐福。
徐福始终冷冷地看着他。他本来就不觉得自己是什么圣母，一个想要他命的刺客，被抓起来之后，还辱骂他和蒹葭。他自然不会忍。而且又有李信代劳，他何乐不为呢？
龙阳君偏转过头来，略略诧异地看了一眼徐福，大概是因为以前徐福将他从魏王宫带走的举动，让他总是忍不住去猜测，徐福是个外冷内里心软的人，但现在看起来……好像是外冷里也冷的啊……他看走眼了。
李信抓着匕首就刺了进去，刺客惨叫不已，“松、松开！”
李信当然不会松，他只是顿住了手中的匕首。
那刺客能清晰地感受到，冰凉又锋利的匕首划开自己的皮肤，穿透进去，撕裂的疼痛顷刻间占领了他的所有思绪，他疼啊，疼得想要骂娘。他恶狠狠地瞪着徐福，凭什么呢？凭什么同为穿越过来的人，这个人就能获得如今的地位？而他却要费力打拼，还落到如此下场。
同为穿越者，对方难道不应该对自己优待一下吗？
那刺客显然是忘记了，当初他是如何对徐福下手的。
徐福这时才慢悠悠地开口，“你们审吧。”这话是对李信说的。
李信低声问刺客：“愿意交代吗？”
刺客脸上的五官已经痛得皱成一团了，他没想到自己会落入秦军手中，更没想到秦军中人下手这么狠！他忍不住直打哆嗦，“……你、你们想问什么……”
妈的让他交代，你倒是先说你们想知道什么啊！
“叫什么？”李信冷声问，一副公事公办的模样，冷硬得让人无从下手。
那刺客知道，落在他手里，连个求情的机会都没有。
“郑……有安……”
徐福皱了皱眉，压根没听过的名字，连耳熟都不觉得了，是历史上没有记载的人物吗？
李信直截了当地道：“听都未听说过的人物，想来也不过是赵军的弃子了。”
这话似乎还激怒了郑有安，他的胸口剧烈起伏着，他死死地盯着李信，但他又不敢开口再骂，生怕那匕首真的把他胸膛剖个窟窿出来。
蒹葭轻蔑地笑了一声，“他还不服气吗？本就是个没听过的人物，还当自己是个厉害角色吗？”
郑有安忍受不了这样的奚落，陡然拔高声音反驳道：“赵军……本该、本该在我的指挥下，打散你们，我再端了王翦人头的！没了王翦，秦军算什么？”
龙阳君淡淡道：“他还不算蠢，知道盯着王翦将军。”
郑有安听见龙阳君这句似夸似损的话，顿时又激动了起来，他原本想挣扎的，但是那把刺入皮肤的匕首提醒了他，让他不敢乱动，只能顶着那张阴柔的脸，不服气地看着龙阳君，低声骂了句，“小白脸。”
徐福顿时就不高兴了。
你说龙阳君是小白脸？他能是小白脸？！
徐福算不得多么喜欢龙阳君，但是龙阳君现在被划进了他那个圈子范围，你一个俘虏，直接宰了你都得感恩戴德没给你施展酷刑了，现在还耍什么大爷脾气？
徐福只是递了个眼神给李信，李信就立刻会意了，他抽出匕首来。
郑有安陡然松了口气，靠着刑架剧烈地喘息了起来，但是他还没能喘够呢，李信突然转手就一刀插在了他的肩膀上，毫不留情的，血溅了起来，落在李信的盔甲上，他脸色半点也没有改变，而郑有安已经痛得大叫起来了。
“啊啊啊啊你干什么啊！”如果不是有刑架，郑有安已经痛得在地上打滚了。
李信冷眼看着他，“管住你的嘴，别说不该说的话。”
郑有安额上滴下了汗水，他颤抖着看了一眼徐福，对了……他怎么忘记他了呢？这个人能听懂的啊……
郑有安小心藏起眼底的憎意。
“你在赵军中是什么身份？”李信又问。
郑有安咬了咬牙，半天才从喉咙里挤出一句话，“……我、我是城中一商贾门下的，的门客……”
徐福暗道，这个商贾好端端的收门客，是想做又一个吕不韦吗？
“如何进了赵军？”
“被……被推举去的。”
“脱去盔甲奇袭，和搭弓射王翦将军的主意，是你出的？”
这时徐福注意到，那郑有安的眼眸里，带着几分得色，“是……是我……”
这个穿越者，可真有意思。
