Chronicle of Rebirth in the Apocalypse

Author: Xiao Xia Mi Ai Chi Yu

Synopsis:

In his past life, he was lazy and gluttonous, growing fat and flabby. When the apocalypse arrived, he was treated as "two-legged mutton" and died in agony as his flesh was carved away. In this life, he is reborn and determined to be proactive, but unexpectedly gains a golden finger space. Not only does he shed all his excess weight, but he also attracts a wolf. Could this be the rhythm of marrying a tall, rich, and handsome man to reach the pinnacle of life?

Keywords for Chronicle of Rebirth in the Apocalypse: Chronicle of Rebirth in the Apocalypse, Xiao Xia Mi Ai Chi Yu, Apocalypse, Rebirth

The summer heat was intense. Surrounded by mountains on all sides, Zhou Family Village, with its population of only a hundred households, was enveloped in sweltering heat. Every house had electric fans and air conditioners running at full blast, hoping to lower the soaring temperature just a little. Outside the window, the ceaseless chirping of cicadas made people feel restless and irritable. Many of the grown men simply went shirtless, wearing only their boxers, and sprawled out on the floor covered with straw mats. The little brats under seven or eight years old ran around completely naked, swinging their little "sparrows" as they hid under the ceiling fans to cool off.

Suddenly, with a loud "bang" like an earthquake, a building at the west end of the village shook.

"Damn it! What the hell! Fatty Zhou, did you fall off your bed again? God damn it! Even a three-meter-long, extra-wide bed can't contain your fat pig body. You do this every few days; won't you let anyone sleep?" A burly man in the house next door, who was struggling to nap on the floor due to the heat, was woken up by the noise and started cursing angrily at his neighbor.

"Uh! I'm sorry, Brother Dayong. I don't know how this happened either. Don't worry, from today on, I'll sleep on the floor. I promise I won't disturb you again." A large head poked out of the window next door. His fat face was so fleshy that his small eyes were almost invisible, looking like nothing more than a giant pancake from a distance. He was making his promise with a sincere expression.

Hearing this, Zhou Dayong was taken aback. When he started cursing, he had been prepared for Fatty Zhou to snap back with a sarcastic retort. He never expected that instead of hearing a venomous comeback, he would hear a polite apology. Had the sun risen from the west today?

Speaking of Fatty Zhou, or Zhou Pan, he was the "rotten mud" of Zhou Family Village—disgusting to anyone who touched him. His father, Zhou Fugui, had originally been a construction contractor in the surrounding area, doing construction and renovation work. He had been quite successful, and the family was well-off for a time. Unfortunately, good times didn't last. While climbing a building at a construction site to inspect it, he accidentally slipped, fell from the twentieth floor, and died, leaving behind a widow and an orphan. His mother, who was only in her thirties, was unwilling to spend the rest of her life as a widow. As soon as the funeral was over, she took the family's money and the property deed for a house they had just bought in the city and ran off with an outsider, leaving behind thirteen-year-old Zhou Pan and an old house.

Overnight, he lost his parents and his money. Not knowing how to work, after going hungry for a few meals, Zhou Pan began a life of petty theft and thievery. When caught, he would righteously curse the villagers, calling them heartless for not caring that an orphan was starving. When his father was alive, he had helped many villagers, so what was wrong with him taking a little food? The villagers were quite helpless. They couldn't beat him because he was still a child, and they couldn't drive him away because they were all from the same village, all surnamed Zhou, and had some distant kinship—he was essentially a nephew to them. They had no choice but to feed him bit by bit, from one house to the next, until he reached the age of sixteen. Yet, he was lazy and gluttonous; he would complain that the food they gave him didn't have meat, being picky and causing scenes. He made everyone hate him, yet he managed to eat himself fat and round.

Fortunately, in another month, he would turn sixteen and be able to get his ID card, making him an adult. If he continued to act unreasonably after that, the villagers wouldn't be so polite.

Thinking of this, Zhou Dayong didn't care why his attitude had changed. He glared with his tiger-like eyes, "It better be that way. If you cause trouble for me again, watch out for my iron fist."

"No, no, I promise I won't cause trouble." Scared back by his imposing manner, Zhou Pan looked around. It was indeed his cramped, dilapidated old house. Although it was called a "building," its history could be traced back to the Daoguang era. Two or three hundred years of time had caused this wood-and-stone structure to age, with cracks here and holes there. When it rained, the house flooded, and when it was sunny, the starlight shone through the roof tiles. The most valuable thing in the entire house was that three-meter-long bed he had pestered the village carpenter, Zhou Dafa, to build for him.

"Heavens! Am I reborn?" Zhou Pan, feeling weak and limp, sprawled on the three-meter bed, staring blankly at the tiles on the ceiling, his mind in a state of chaotic confusion.

A moment ago, he had died. In a warehouse facing the siege of thousands of zombies, he had been cut piece by piece by a starving, red-eyed crowd, dying in agony.

The next moment, he had fallen off his three-meter bed and woken up.

Everything felt like a dream, but he was certain he had truly experienced the cruel apocalypse. In another month, the world would change drastically; morality would collapse, humanity would be extinguished, and food would be scarce. Cannibalism would no longer be a legend.

Zhou Pan remembered the feeling of being sliced piece by piece; he didn't want to experience that pain again. He lifted his thick, fleshy arm—he had to lose weight! He must lose weight! He never wanted to be caught as "two-legged mutton" again because he was too slow due to his layers of fat.

Thinking of this, Zhou Pan rolled over and struggled to stand up. He had one month left. He had to shed some of this fat, otherwise, when the apocalypse came and the villagers packed up to flee, no one would want to let a burden who took up three seats onto their vehicle.

The hot weather was practically a death sentence for a big, heat-intolerant man like him.

Zhou Pan climbed down the stairs, panting. In the courtyard downstairs, he found a rock the size of a watermelon. He struggled to carry it upstairs, then carried it back downstairs, and then back up again. Repeating this, his gray T-shirt was soaked with sweat as if it had just been washed, clinging stickily to his skin, clearly revealing the layers of fat shaking on his body.

"I can't do it, I'm so tired!" After only ten trips, Zhou Pan's legs were so weak he couldn't move. He sprawled on the stairs, his vision darkening, gasping like thunder. This was the consequence of being lazy; he never exercised, so now he was exhausted after just a little movement.

Zhou Pan was a lazy person. He knew his reputation in others' eyes was terrible, but what could he do? When he lost his parents in his previous life, he was thirteen—a half-grown boy with no family property. Who would want to adopt him? When his father was alive, he was the apple of his eye, pampered and spoiled; he hadn't even picked a scallion. When his father died and his mother ran off, his family was destroyed, and he was stunned. He didn't know how to do any work, and since he hadn't even finished middle school, no one wanted to hire a child laborer who couldn't work and was semi-illiterate. Was he supposed to go out and beg or scavenge for trash? He couldn't bring himself to do that. Pestering the villagers was just him betting that they wouldn't watch him die. Back then, his thinking was simple: his father had done so much for the village, and there were so many favors owed. He didn't want anything else; it wasn't too much to ask for a bite to eat! Once the villagers were willing to feed him, he was actually happy to be a good kid. But some people, seeing him being good, dared to feed him spoiled food and rotten buns. If the tiger didn't show its claws, they treated him like a sick cat. He would rather be hated by everyone than be bullied, so he made everyone's life miserable, which was why they had obediently supported him until he was an adult.

It wasn't that Zhou Pan had absolutely nothing; he actually had a few acres of land. But he didn't know how to farm, so he just rented it out to others for a thousand yuan a year, with a three-year lease that would end when he came of age.

One might say that a thousand yuan a year was too cheap, but this was the countryside! Everything was scarce except for farmland. The younger generation had all gone to the cities to work, and only the older generation knew how to farm. There was plenty of abandoned land; if his family's land hadn't been right by the village, no one would have wanted to rent it.

In his previous life, he hadn't dared to spend a single cent of those three thousand yuan. He knew that once he came of age, the villagers wouldn't care about him anymore, so this money was his entire fortune, and he hid it very well. But after the apocalypse, paper money became worthless. The three thousand yuan he had painstakingly hidden couldn't even buy a single bun, leaving him to starve for a long time. In this life, he had to hurry and buy some food as a reserve.

Sigh! If only he had a "golden finger," like those in the web novels on his neighbor Zhou Qi's computer—something like a portable space—he could store more food. When the disaster arrived in his previous life, most families first packed their valuables, then their food. As a result, when they left, they couldn't carry all the food and left it behind, along with him, the burden everyone hated.

It was that food that helped him survive the first three months of the apocalypse, until a team arrived. While they took the food, they also took him out of the nearly isolated little mountain village. At first, he thought the people in the team were good, but later he realized they just treated him as emergency rations. When there was no food left to eat, all that awaited him was the sharpening of knives.

If he had a golden finger from a book, he could have collected all that abandoned food after the villagers left. Zhou Family Village had been farmers for generations; no one would ever be short of a bite to eat. Otherwise, they wouldn't have supported Zhou Pan for three or four years. The total amount of abandoned grain was tens of thousands of catties. It was a pity that in the end, all that rice and grain went to waste, benefiting that group of beasts in human clothing.

Come to think of it, eight out of ten protagonists in apocalypse novels who are reborn have a portable space. He was also reborn; could he also have a chance to get a golden finger?

Thinking of this, Zhou Pan's heart pounded with excitement. He struggled to his feet, deciding to search his dilapidated house thoroughly. Maybe his golden finger was lying in some corner!

"Clatter, clatter," "crash, bang," "clunk, clunk"—various sounds were endless. Zhou Pan worked hard, burying his head in every corner of his home, hoping to find the golden finger he longed for.

One hour, two hours, three hours passed. When his neighbor, Auntie Yan, brought dinner to Zhou Pan's house, his dilapidated home had been turned into something no different from a garbage dump. Zhou Pan himself was covered in dust and grime, mixed with his own foul sweat—he looked no better than a homeless person.

"Oh! Pan, what are you doing? Look at how dirty you are." Auntie Yan's family was one of the few in the village who didn't give him a hard time. Uncle Zhou Jianguo had been good friends with his late father and had even wanted to adopt him once, but they already had five children, and the fines for exceeding the birth quota had wiped out their savings, so they had no strength left to raise another. They would only occasionally bring him some meat or eggs to satisfy his cravings.

"Auntie, you're here. I'm looking for something! You can just put the bowl on the stone step by the gate, and I'll return it to you after I finish." Zhou Pan took off his T-shirt to wipe the sweat from his face. The dust on the shirt left his face streaked with black, looking quite comical.

"Hahaha! Oh my god! You kid, you'd better wash up quickly; you're filthy." Auntie Yan laughed heartily, laughing for a long time before stopping. "I won't hold you up. Finish washing and come over to eat. The cold noodles I made are nice and refreshing right now."

After saying this, Auntie Yan placed the bowl on the stone step and left with a smile.

Having searched hard for half a day without finding anything suspicious, Zhou Pan walked dejectedly to the well. He used the wooden bucket to draw water and, without a second thought, splashed it over his dirty body. The ice-cold well water was piercingly chilly. He shivered violently. Damn, that was too refreshing!

The summer heat vanished instantly. Except for the food delivery, no one ever came to his dilapidated place, so Zhou Pan simply stripped naked. Using his T-shirt as a towel, he enjoyed a refreshing wash with the cold well water. Since the T-shirt wasn't absorbent, he also washed his hair, which caused water to get into his eyes, making it impossible to open them. He wiped his face with the T-shirt, but it didn't dry his eyes, leaving them sticky and uncomfortable. With no other choice, he squinted with blurry eyes and walked toward the kitchen at the corner of the stairs. As he reached the kitchen, he wasn't paying attention and tripped over a rock. Losing his balance, he crashed into the kitchen threshold with a loud "clunk" and passed out, his head covered in blood. The first thought he had before losing consciousness was: Oh no! Tomorrow, will there be another rumor in the village about me, Fatty Zhou, loving to run around naked?
chapters.source_text:
夏日炎炎，四面环山，人口只有百多户的周家村正被暑热笼罩，家家户户电风扇、空调死命运转着，巴望能将飙升的高温稍稍降下来一点。窗外蝉鸣声不绝于耳，吵的人心浮气躁。不少大老爷们，干脆光膀子就穿着一条裤衩，摊在铺着凉席的地上。那些七八岁以下的毛孩子，直接光着腚，晃悠着小雀儿，躲在吊扇底下乘凉。
突然“嘭”的一声巨响，犹如地震般，村西头的一栋楼房晃了晃。
“靠！尼玛的！周胖子你他妈又掉下床了？TNND，加长加宽的三米大床，都拦不住你一身肥猪肉，你这隔几天就来一出，还让不让人睡觉了？”旁边房子中正暑热难耐趴在地板上午睡的大汉，被响动吵醒，对着隔壁火冒三丈的破口大骂。
“呃！对不起啊大勇哥，我也不知道怎么会这样？你放心从今个儿起，我睡地板，保准不吵着你了。”隔壁窗户探出一颗大头，肥胖的脸肉挤得一对小眼睛几乎都看不见了，远远望去只剩一张大饼脸，此刻正一脸诚恳的保证道。
闻言周大勇吓了一跳，他破口大骂时，就做好周胖子反唇相讥的准备，没想到不但没听到他的毒舌反击，居然还听到他礼貌的道歉声，这太阳今天不会是从西边升起的吧？
说起周胖子周磐，那可是他们周家村的一块烂泥，谁碰谁恶心。他爸周富贵原本是十里八乡的包工头，搞建筑，搞装修，搞的风生水起，家里很是富裕了一阵。可惜好景不长，某次爬上工地大楼检查时不小心脚一滑，从二十多楼摔下来，一命呜呼，留下孤儿寡母。他三十来岁还很年轻的妈，不甘心后半辈子守活寡，刚办完丧事就卷起家里的钱和城里的刚买房子的房产证，跟个外乡人跑了，丢下十三岁的周磐和一栋老房子。
一夜之间父母没了，钱也没有了，又不会干活，饿了几顿后，周磐就开始偷鸡摸狗，小偷小摸的生活。被人抓着了还理直气壮的大骂村里人，狼心狗肺，看他一个孤儿孤零零的饿肚子也不管。他爸爸活着时，拉巴帮助了不少村民，他拿点吃喝怎么了？大家伙颇为无奈，即不能打他，他终究还是个孩子；也不能赶他走，好歹都是同一个村的，都姓周，多少有点亲戚关系，也算是子侄辈的。只好东家一口饭，西家一口粮的拉扯他到十六岁成年。偏偏他好吃懒做，吃人家饭还嫌人家没给肉吃，挑三拣四，大吵大闹，弄的神憎鬼厌，他自己倒吃的肥头大耳，膀大腰圆。
索性再过一个月，他就满十六岁，可以办理身份证，也算成年了，他再胡搅蛮缠村里人可不会客气了。
想到此，周大勇也不管他态度怎么变了，虎目一瞪，“最好这样，再给老子搞事，小心老子的铁拳头。”
“不会不会，我保证不乱搞事。”被他气势吓得缩回脑袋的周磐，环顾四周，果然还是他那个逼仄老旧的老房子，虽然也叫楼房，可惜历史太长久，可以追述到道光年间，两三百年的时光，将这木石搭建的老房子老化的这里一道裂缝，那里一个窟窿，下雨屋内发大水，晴天屋瓦透星光，整栋屋子最值钱的就是那张他死皮赖脸求村内木匠周大发打造的三米大床。
“老天爷！我这是重生了吗？”周磐腿脚发软四肢无力的摊在三米大床上，两眼无神的盯着头顶上的瓦片，脑中思绪万千，混乱不已。
前一刻他死了。在一个面临着数千丧尸围攻的仓库中，被饿的两眼发红的人群，一片一片割下身上的肉，活活痛死了。
下一刻他又从他的三米大床上摔下地，摔醒了。
这一切仿佛如梦般，可是他确定他确实曾经经历过残酷的末世时光，再过一个月，天地大变，道德沦丧，人性泯灭，缺衣少食，人吃人再也不是传说中的事。
周磐被人一刀一刀割下身上的肉，那种千刀万剐的痛苦，他不想再次经历了。抬起粗壮肥嫩的胳膊，他要减肥！他必须减肥！他再也不想因为拖着一身肥膘跑太慢，而被人捉住当两脚羊了。
想到此，周磐一轱辘，艰难的爬起身，还有一个月时间，好歹把这身肥肉减减膘，否则当末世来临时，村里人收拾东西逃跑时，没有一辆车愿意搭载他这白白占去三个座位的累赘。
炎热的天气，对他这样不耐热的大胖子来说，简直要了卿卿命了。
周磐气喘吁吁的爬下楼，在楼下院子里找到一块西瓜大的石头，费力的将它抱二上楼，又继续将它抱到楼下，再抱到楼上，如此往返，穿着灰色T恤衫的身上，汗如雨下，将T恤衫浸湿如刚洗过一样，湿哒哒的黏在他皮肉上，可以清晰看到他身上不断抖动的赘肉。
“不行了，好累！”才跑了十趟，周磐就腿软的迈不动步，两眼发黑的摊在楼梯上，气喘如雷。这就是好吃懒做的下场，平时不运动，如今稍稍动一下就疲惫不堪。
周磐是个懒人，他知道自己在别人的眼中评价很糟糕，可又能怎么办呢？上辈子他失去父母时十三岁，半大小子，又没家产，谁家愿意收养？他爸在时，他就是爸爸的心头宝，娇生惯养着长大，连根葱都没摘过。他爸一走，他妈就撇下他跑了，一下子家破人亡，他懵了。他啥活也不会干，况且年龄小连初中都没读完，没人乐意招个干不了活又半文盲的童工，难道要让他去外面乞讨捡垃圾？他也拉不下那个脸。跟村里人胡搅蛮缠，也只不过算定他们不能眼睁睁的看他去死。那时候他想法简单，他爸在时，为村里做了那么多事，人情债一大把，他别的不要，赏他口饭吃不过分啊！等村里人愿意管他吃喝了，其实他也乐意当个乖孩子。可偏偏有人见他乖了，就敢给他吃馊饭，臭掉的馒头，老虎不发威，当他是病猫了。他宁愿人人厌恶，也不愿被人所欺，搞的人鸡犬不宁，才会在后面老实的供养他到成年。
要说周磐家里一无所有，倒也不是，他其实还有几亩田地，只是他又不会种地，干脆租给别人，每年一千块钱的租金，租三年，到他成年就可以回收。
也许会说，一年一千块钱的租金也太便宜了，可这里是农村啊！什么都缺但是田地不会缺，年轻一辈都跑到外面城市里打工去了，会种田的也只有老一辈，多的是田地荒芜，他家的田要不是就在村边，还没人愿意租呢！
上辈子这三千块钱，他一分都舍不得花，他知道等他成年村里人就不管他了，这些钱就是他全部家当，他藏的很严实。可是末世后钞票都成了废纸，他辛苦藏的三千块钱连一个馒头都买不起，白白让他忍饥挨饿了好一段时间，这辈子他还是赶快购买一些粮食做储备。
哎！要是他有金手指就好了，像隔壁邻居周琦哥的电脑里，那些网文写的什么随身空间之类的，也能多收取一些食物。上辈子灾难来临，各家各户大多首先先收拾的是些值钱东西，然后才是粮食，结果走的时候，好多食物装不下，都被撇下，一同撇下的还有他这个神憎鬼厌的累赘。
也就是这些粮食才让他熬过了末世后的三个月，直到一支队伍到来，收走粮食的同时，也将他带出了这个几乎封闭的小山村。他开始还以为这队伍的人是好人，后来才知道人家只不过把他当做储备粮，到了无粮可食的时候，等待他的就是磨刀霍霍。
假如他有书中的金手指，他就可以在村里人离开后，收起这些拉下的粮食，周家村世代务农，每家缺啥也不会缺口饭吃，要不然也不会供养周磐三四年，拉下的粮食零零总总也有几万斤，可惜最后那么多的米粮，白白便宜了那群衣冠禽兽。
说来末世小说十个重生的人物，有八个都有随身空间，他也是重生的，莫非也有机会得到金手指？
想到这，周磐兴奋的心脏呯呯跳，他费力的爬起身，决定将这破屋烂瓦好好搜索一番，说不定哪一个嘎达正躺着他的金手指呢！
“淅沥哗啦”“噼里啪啦”“哐当哐当”各种声音不绝于耳，周磐卖力的在家中的各个角落埋头苦翻，巴望着能找到他心心念念的金手指。
一个小时，两个小时，三个小时过去，当邻居严大婶端着晚饭走到周磐家时，他家破屋被翻的跟垃圾场没啥区别，而周磐更是灰头土脸，混着一身的臭汗，简直与流浪汉有的一拼。
“呦！磐小子，你这是干啥呢？瞧你一身脏的，”严大婶一家是村里难得不对他摆脸色的人，周建国周大伯跟他死鬼老爸交情不错，曾经还想收养他来着，可惜家中已有五个子女，光超生费就将家底收刮光了，哪还有余力多养他一个，也就是偶尔给他送点肉蛋解解馋。
“大婶子，您来了，我这是找东西呢！您把饭碗放大门旁的石阶上就行，等会我吃完给您送回去。”周磐脱下T恤衫抹把脸上的汗，衣服上沾的灰，把他的脸擦的左黑一块，右黑一块，搞笑极了。
“哈哈哈！哎呦我的天！你小子还是赶快洗洗吧，都脏的不成样了。”严大婶乐的哈哈大笑，笑了半天才止。“我也不耽误你了，你赶紧洗完过来吃，我做的凉面现在冰冰凉凉正好吃呢。”
严大婶说完将饭碗放石阶上，带着一脸笑离开了。
卖力找了半天啥可疑物体都没找到的周磐，垂头丧气的走到水井旁，用木轱辘将水打上来，不管三七二十一，就将水泼在脏兮兮的身体上，冰寒刺骨的井水，刺溜溜透心凉，他激灵灵的打个寒颤，ND，太TM销魂了。
暑热一下子全消，除了送饭，其他时候也没人来他这破屋烂瓦的地方，周磐索性全身赤裸，用T恤衫当毛巾，就着寒凉的井水，爽快的清洗了一番，就是T恤衫不吸水，顺便把头也清洗的他，弄的眼睛被水冲的睁不开，用T恤衫擦了把脸，还是没擦干眼睛上的水，黏黏糊糊的难受，没法子只好勉强睁着模模糊糊的眼睛，朝楼梯拐角处的厨房走去，当快走到厨房时，一个没注意一脚绊在一块石头上，脚下失衡哐当一声响，他一头扎在厨房的门槛上，满头是血的晕了过去，晕过去的第一个念头是，妈呀！明天村里该不会又多一条他周胖子爱光腚遛鸟的谣言吧？
chapters.title: 第1章 他重生了

chapters.translated_text:
After finishing his meal, Wang Chao hummed a tune as he ran back to the dormitory and took out the fruit to enjoy it. He had worked hard to snatch this from the boss, and perhaps because it was obtained through such great effort, he felt this fruit tasted better than any he had ever eaten before.

"Crunch, crunch," he ate half an apple in two bites. It was crisp, sweet, and juicy, with a rich fruity aroma; one bite was enough to tell it was purely natural and free of additives.

"Hey! Da Chao, what are you eating?" A heavy slap landed on Wang Chao's back. "Cough, cough, cough..." Caught off guard while immersed in the delicious fruit, Wang Chao fell right into the trap. A piece of apple he hadn't chewed yet got stuck in his throat. His face turned beet red, and he had to cough violently several times before he finally dislodged the fruit.

"Damn it! Jiang Ye, you..." Wang Chao was just about to aggressively settle the score with the culprit when he caught sight of another big guy nearby and immediately lost his nerve.

"What about me? Go on, say it!" Jiang Ye raised his eyebrows triumphantly, using his backer to bully others and showing disdain for Wang Chao, who looked like a volcano about to erupt but had to extinguish himself.

"Damn it! If you've got guts, let's go outside and fight one-on-one. What kind of hero relies on their lover to back them up?" Wang Chao muttered under his breath.

"What did you say? Speak up." Jiang Ye heard him mumbling and knew it couldn't be anything good. He narrowed his eyes, raised his brows, and glared with murderous intent. The stoic man beside him also glared in solidarity.

"Oh, ancestors, I didn't say anything, you heard wrong." Wang Chao hung his head in defeat.

"I'm telling you, Da Chao, we're good brothers and comrades-in-arms, you're being too stingy with the 'brotherly love.' How can you hog all the good stuff?" Jiang Ye's sharp eyes spotted the fruit Wang Chao had hidden. Without another word, he shifted his gaze, and the man beside him swiftly snatched the plastic bag.

"Hey, that's mine!" Wang Chao rushed to grab it back, but unfortunately, the stoic man held the bag high above his head. Although Wang Chao was also a tall guy with long limbs, there was a significant difference between 180cm and 190cm. He tried to grab it for a long time but still couldn't reach the bag.

"Well done, Lao Cheng." Jiang Ye beamed with joy on the side.

A smile also appeared on the stoic face of Cheng Ang. In an instant, his previously dull and wooden face became vivid and bright because of the smile.

"Damn it! Don't go too far, you two!" Wang Chao panted as he glared back at them after his failed attempt to retrieve the bag.

"How are we going too far? Isn't this fruit sent by the 'sister-in-law'? As the boss's brothers, we should have a share of this fruit, right?" Jiang Ye calmly told Cheng Ang to bring over the fruit. He reached out and picked one; they were all full of juice and looked excellent. No wonder Wang Chao was so desperate to snatch them back.

"Get lost. If you want to eat, why don't you go get some from the boss? Why are you snatching my share!" Wang Chao watched with a pained heart as Jiang Ye pulled out a large red apple, wiped it on his clothes, and took a crunchy bite.

"Mmm! This fruit is indeed delicious. Lao Cheng, hurry and try some!" Jiang Ye satisfiedly handed the apple to Cheng Ang, who took a bite right where Jiang Ye had bitten, then nodded in approval.

Jiang Ye blushed, pulled out another piece of fruit to hand to him, and took the apple back to continue eating, his face turning redder with every bite.

Damn! Is there any justice left? Wang Chao angrily pulled out a piece of fruit to eat. Since it looked like he wouldn't be able to keep the fruit anyway, he might as well eat as much as he could.

As he ate, he stole glances at the pair of "dog men" beside him. Damn it, they weren't giving single guys any way to live. They should be careful—those who flaunt their affection die quickly!

"Da Chao, what's the deal with that 'sister-in-law'? Since when did our boss have a wife?" After enjoying the delicious fruit for a while, Jiang Ye finally had the mental energy to focus on the question he cared about.

"Sister-in-law? What sister-in-law? I don't know!" Wang Chao played dumb, looking completely blank.

"Damn it! Stop pretending. We heard everything you and the boss said in the parking lot!" Jiang Ye rolled his eyes at him. Stop acting, the secret was already out!

Oh no! How could he have forgotten that the small grove by the parking lot was the favorite dating spot for these two? Wang Chao looked miserable. He had just been caught and lectured by the boss for having no filter, saying that since nothing was set in stone yet, he shouldn't be shouting about it—what if it got back to Zhou Pan and scared him away? The boss had strictly ordered him to keep his mouth shut!

But now that both of them had heard it, they clearly weren't people he could brush off. Wang Chao's eyes darted around guiltily, trying to find an excuse to deflect the topic.

"Don't even think about lying to us! The worst that happens is we promise that what goes into our ears stays there; we guarantee to keep it a secret! If you don't tell us, I'll start shouting about it. When things blow up, let's see what you do!" Seeing his eyes darting around, Jiang Ye knew what he was planning and immediately threatened him.

"Alright, alright." Wang Chao surrendered to the evil forces. "I'll tell you, but don't you dare spread it, or the boss will come after me!"

"OK! OK!" Jiang Ye and Cheng Ang nodded.

Wang Chao carefully looked left and right, and seeing that no one was around, he leaned in mysteriously toward the two, and the three formed a tight circle.

Wang Chao gestured wildly and spoke with great animation about the first time he met Zhou Pan, how he had accurately hit a thief with a banana, and then described how his boss had acted so strangely when he met the other party. He rambled on for five or six minutes.

"Finally, the boss invited the little guy to come over and hang out tomorrow, so you'll be able to see him then." After talking until his mouth was dry, Wang Chao pulled out a banana, peeled it, and started eating.

"Ah, that's it?" So nothing was set in stone yet! What a letdown; he thought there would be something more scandalous! But then again, the other protagonist was still a minor, and the boss was just a wolf who had just spotted his prey and hadn't decided whether to strike yet!

"Let's go, let's go. Nothing else to see, let's head back!" Jiang Ye pulled Cheng Ang and prepared to retreat.

"Hey! Wait a second, leave the fruit if you're going. Hey, at least leave two for me, damn it!" Wang Chao watched angrily as the two ignored him, pretending not to hear as they walked further and further away, leaving him standing there staring in frustration.

After dinner, Zhou Pan followed Zhou Qi and several comrades, walking under the glow of the sunset,

strolling around the area to help digest their food.

"Thump, thump, thump!" As they passed a basketball court, several shirtless soldiers were already sweating on the court, each moving with agility that was not inferior to professionals.

Zhou Pan watched with envy as they moved freely and passionately on the court. Since he was a child, he simply didn't have an "athletic bone" in his body. He could only watch such intense sports from afar, never participating. Although he envied others for being able to enjoy the feeling of being drenched in sweat, he politely declined the idea of going down to experience that fiery passion himself.

"Pan-zi, want to go down and play a bit?" Zhang Dajun, seeing him staring at the court, suggested.

"Hmm?! I don't know how." Zhou Pan shook his head immediately upon hearing this. He had never played ball before; he didn't know how to play!

"Come on! It's super simple!" Zhang Dajun pulled him onto the court without giving him a choice.

The soldiers on the court saw Zhang Dajun dragging in a fair-skinned, delicate youth and stopped their movements with laughter.

"Lao Bao, throw your ball over here!" Zhang Dajun shouted to the comrade holding the ball.

"You got it!" A dark-skinned, rugged man threw the ball in his hand over.

"Come, stand here and throw the ball into that frame. It's very simple." Zhang Dajun handed the ball to Zhou Pan.

Zhou Pan clutched the ball, nervous and not knowing what to do.

"Come, move the ball back a little, then throw it forward with force." Zhang Dajun demonstrated the posture.

Zhou Pan followed along, moving back and throwing forward. The basketball flew with a "whoosh" and hit the rim. His face turned red with embarrassment.

"It's okay, it's okay. Hitting the rim on your first try is actually pretty good." Zhang Dajun comforted him, and the others smiled kindly.

The ball fell under the rim, and someone specifically helped him pick it up.

"Thank you!" Zhou Pan said shyly.

He held the basketball again, set his posture, and took a deep breath. Thinking of his senses that had become much sharper recently, he decided to make good use of his advantage.

Whoosh—the ball was thrown again, landing right on the rim, spinning around it continuously. He didn't blink, staring fixedly at the rim.

By now, quite a few people had gathered outside the basketball court to watch Zhou Pan play. Seeing the ball land on the rim, dozens of people couldn't help but hold their breath, staring at the basketball without blinking.

Clang—the basketball fell through the hoop, and a thunderous cheer erupted on the court.

"Not bad, kid. You made it on your second try. You've got a future." Zhang Dajun happily patted Zhou Pan's shoulder hard.

"Hehe!" Zhou Pan winced with a silly grin. It wasn't that he was complaining, but Zhang Dajun's slap wasn't light; his shoulder was burning.

With the technique for shooting down, Zhou Pan made several shots in a row, drawing cheers from all around. Having rarely received praise since he was a child, Zhou Pan was stimulated by the constant compliments, his vanity soaring. Excited, his face turned bright red, and he let go of his timidity to play with the soldiers. Though he was a bit clumsy at first, he later relied on his powerful senses to move left and right, steal the ball, and shoot, continuously achieving great results.

The crowd watching grew larger and larger. Everyone knew that a "divine shooter" had arrived at this court, and every time the ball went in, there was a round of applause.

"This kid is good, I haven't seen him before! Where's this new recruit from?" A company commander was attracted by the shouting and came over to take a look, unable to help but praise him.

"Report to the commander, he's not a new recruit. He's the neighbor's younger brother of the Second Company's Eighth Squad leader, here to visit the base," a soldier replied.

"Oh, I see. He doesn't look old enough to meet the standards for new recruits. That's a pity, he's too young," the company commander said with a look of regret.

Zhou Pan played for a while until 7:00 PM, when it was time to watch the news. Everyone stopped playing, and many people enthusiastically came up to pat him on the shoulder and offer a few words of praise.

Zhou Pan was drenched in sweat, but after all the running and jumping, it felt as if his entire body's meridians had been cleared. He felt refreshed and full of strength.

Bidding farewell to the soldiers he had just played with, Zhou Pan walked toward Zhou Qi and the others, who were watching from the sidelines, his face flushed red and his spirit high.

"Not bad, good kid." Zhou Qi patted him with a face full of joy. It seemed coming to the base was the right choice; finally, this kid's lazy bones were moving.

The others also smiled and praised him.

Zhou Pan blushed with embarrassment and went with them to watch the news broadcast.
chapters.translated_title: Chapter 10: Playing Ball at the Base "Seeking Recommendations, Seeking Collections"
chapters.title: 第10章 在部队打球「求推荐，求收藏」
chapters.source_text:
王超吃完饭，哼着歌跑回宿舍，掏出水果美美的吃起来，这可是他从老大那好不容易抢来的，不知道是不是千辛万苦得来的东西更珍贵的原因，他总觉得这水果比任何一次吃到的水果都更好吃。
“咔嚓咔嚓”两口就吃了半个苹果，脆甜多汁，果香浓郁，一吃就知道纯天然无公害。
“嗨！大超，你在吃啥呢？”一巴掌重重拍在王超背后，“咳咳咳咳……”正沉浸在品尝美味水果之中的王超毫无防备之下，一下子就中招了，还没咬碎的一块苹果，不小心卡在喉咙口，他脸憋的通红，死命咳嗽了几下，才将水果咳出来。
“卧槽！江烨你……”王超气势汹汹的正想找罪魁祸首算账，眼睛瞄到一旁的另一个大块头，立马怂了。
“我怎么啦？说呀！”江烨得意洋洋的扬着眉毛，仗着背后的靠山狐假虎威蔑视火山眼看要爆发，却不得不泯灭的王超。
“卧槽！有种出去单挑，仗着相好算什么英雄好汉！”王超嘴里小声嘀咕。
“你说什么？大声点。”江烨听他小声咕哝，肯定没好话，眼一眯，眉毛竖起来，杀气腾腾的瞪过去。一旁的木纳汉子也同仇敌忾的虎视他。
“哎呦，祖宗，我哪有说什么，你听错了。”王超垂头丧气认栽。
“我说大超，咱们好歹是好兄弟，好战友，你也太没有同袍之爱了，有好东西怎么可以独享？”江烨眼尖的看到王超藏起来的水果，二话不说，眼神一转，旁边的汉子立刻迅捷的抢过塑料袋。
“哎，那是我的！”王超赶紧去抢，可惜木纳汉子直接将袋子举的高高的，王超虽然也是个长手长腿的高大汉子，可180和190一比，还是差距很大的，抢了半天，依然没抢到袋子。
“老成，干的不错。”江烨在一旁乐的眉开眼笑。
木纳汉子成昂木呆呆的脸上也跟着挂上笑容，刹时间，原本呆木的脸因为笑容而变得生动爽朗起来。
“卧槽！你们不要太过份了！”王超抢了半天气喘吁吁的回瞪两人。
“我们哪里过份了？这不是‘大嫂’送的水果吗？身为老大的兄弟，这水果应该也有我们一份吧？”江烨气定神闲的叫成昂拿过来手上的水果，他伸手挑了挑，个个汁水饱满，卖相绝佳，果然都很不错，难怪王超急三火四的想抢回去。
“滚犊子，你们要吃不会去老大那拿吗？干嘛抢我这份！”王超心疼的看着江烨掏出一个大红苹果，随手在衣服上擦擦，就咔嚓咬了一口。
“嗯！这水果果然好吃，老成快尝尝！”江烨满意的将手上的苹果递给旁边的成昂，成昂直接在他咬过的痕迹上咬了一口，吃了点点头。
江烨脸红红的，另外掏了个水果递给他，自己拿过苹果继续吃，越吃脸越红。
靠！还有没有没天理了！王超愤愤的掏出一个水果来吃，反正瞧这架势，这水果也保不住了，还不如能吃一个是一个。
他一边吃一边偷瞥一旁的一对狗男男，他喵的，都不给单身狗活路了，小心秀恩爱，死的快！
“大超，那大嫂是怎么回事，咱们老大啥时候冒出一个媳妇了？”品尝了一会儿美味水果，江烨才有心神关注关心的问题。
“大嫂？什么大嫂？我不知道！”王超装傻充愣，一脸茫然。
“卧槽！别装了，你跟老大在停车场那里讲的话，我们都听到了！”江烨白他一眼，装个屁啊装，底儿早就漏了！
惨了！他怎么忘了停车场旁边的小树林可是这两家伙最爱去的约会圣地了？王超愁眉苦脸，他先前刚被老大逮到，教训了一顿，说他口无遮拦，八字没一撇呢？就大声嚷嚷，要是传的到处被周磐听到吓跑了怎么办？严令他闭紧嘴巴呢！
可是现在这两人都听到了，显然也不是他能敷衍过去的对象，王超心虚的眼珠乱转，想找个理由推诿过去。
“别想骗我们啊！大不了我们答应你出的你口，入的我们耳朵，我们保证保守秘密！如果不说，那我就要大声嚷嚷了，倒时候，事情闹大，看你怎么办？！”江烨见他眼珠乱转，就知道要打什么注意，立马威胁道。
“好了，好了。”王超屈服在恶势力之下，“我说了，你们可别往外说，不然老大要找我算账了！”
“OK！OK！”江烨两人点头。
王超小心翼翼的左顾右盼了一下，见四下无人，才神秘兮兮的凑到两人身前，三人围成一团。
只见王超眉飞色舞，口沫横飞的讲了一番初见周磐时，他如何神准的一香蕉打倒小偷，又讲他家老大遇到对方时如何的失常表现，滔滔不绝了有五六分钟。
“最后老大邀请那小家伙明天上来玩，到时候你们就可以见见了。”讲的口水都干了，王超拔出一根香蕉，剥开香蕉皮吃起来。
“啊，就这样？”这八字都没一撇嘛！搞什么，还以为有啥香艳的事情呢！不过也是，另一个主角还是未成年呢，老大现在也只不过是刚盯上猎物的狼，还没决定要不要下手呢！
“走走走，没啥事了，咱们回吧！”江烨拉着成昂准备撤退。
“喂！等一下，要走把水果留下。哎，好歹，留两个给我，卧槽！”王超气呼呼的看着两人充耳不闻，装作没听见的越行越远，站在原地干瞪眼。
吃完饭，周磐跟着周琦和几个战友踏着落日余晖，
在四周散步消食。
“咚咚咚！”路过一个篮球场，场上早有几个打赤膊的兵哥哥在场上挥洒汗水，一个个身手矫健，与专业人士相比也不宜多让。
周磐艳羡的看着众人在场上纵横自如，热情洋溢。他从小到大，压根就没有那根运动神筋，从来对这些剧烈运动，只能远观，不能近玩。虽然他很羡慕别人能够享受大汗淋漓的滋味，但是要他自己下场去感受一番这种热情似火的感觉，他又敬谢不敏。
“磐子，要不要下场玩玩？”张大军见他一直盯着场上，不由提议道。
“嗯？！我不会。”周磐一听赶紧摇头，他从来没打过球，不会玩啊！
“来吧！特别简单！”张大军不由分说的将他扯入场内。
场上的兵哥哥见张大军扯了个白嫩嫩的少年进来，都嬉笑的停下动作。
“老包，把你的球，扔过来一下！”张大军对拿着球的战友喊。
“好嘞！”一个黑黝黝的糙汉子，将手中的球扔过来。
“来，站这里，将球往那个框架里投，很简单的。”张大军将球递给周磐。
周磐抓着球紧张的不知道怎么办。
“来，将球往后面移一点，然后用力向前抛出。”张大军摆了个姿势。
周磐跟着学习，向后移，往前抛，蓝球咻的飞过去，砸到了蓝球框架，他脸都羞红了。
“没事，没事，第一次能打到框架，算是很不错了。”张大军安慰他，旁人都善意的笑了笑。
球掉到蓝框架下，有人特意帮他把球拣回来。
“谢谢！”周磐不好意思的道谢。
他再次抱着篮球，摆好姿势，深吸口气，想到最近变强了好多的感官，他决定好好发挥自己的优势。
咻～球再次被投过去，一下子投到蓝框架上，围绕着框架在不停转动，他眼眨也不眨的死盯着蓝框架。
蓝球场外此时围了不少人，一个个都来围观周磐打球，见到球投到蓝框架上，几十号人，都忍不住屏住呼吸，盯着蓝球目不转睛。
哐当——蓝球从蓝框内坠落，场上顿时响起如雷的欢呼。
“不错小子，第二次就顺利投入了，有前途。”张大军高兴的猛拍周磐的肩膀。
“呵呵！”周磐呲牙咧嘴的傻笑两声，不是他说，张大军这巴掌可不轻，拍的他肩膀那个火辣。
有了投球的技巧，周磐一连投进好几个球，引来四周一片叫好声，从小到大，很少受到表扬的周磐，被周周夸奖声，刺激的虚荣声不断往上飙升，兴奋的他满脸通红，还放下胆怯与场上的兵哥哥们玩了起来，开头有点手忙脚乱，后来凭着他强大的感观，灵活的在场上左右奔走，抢球，投篮，不断创出佳绩。
围观的人群越来越多，大家伙都知道这边场地，来了个神投手，每个球投入都是一阵拍手声。
“这小子不错，没见过啊！哪来的新兵？”某连长被叫喊声吸引走过来一看，不由夸奖道。
“报告连长，不是新兵，是二连八班班长的邻居弟弟，来部队探亲的。”一个战士回答。
“哦，我说呢，看着年纪也达不到招新兵的标准，倒是可惜了，年纪太小。”连长一脸惋惜。
周磐打了好一会儿球，直到七点要看新闻的时间，大家伙才不打了，不少人都热情的上前拍拍他，夸了两句。
周磐全身大汗淋漓，但是跑跑跳跳，仿佛全身筋骨都被打通了，浑身舒畅，充满了力量。
告别刚刚一起打球的兵哥们，周磐火红着脸，精神奕奕的朝在场外围观的周琦等人走去。
“不错，好小子。”周琦满脸高兴的拍拍他。看来来部队是正确的，这不这小子的那根懒骨头终于动起来了。
其他几个也笑着夸他。
周磐不好意思的红着脸，跟他们一起去看新闻联播。

chapters.translated_text:
Jing Chengsu led Zhou Pan and the others through several streets to reach the F City Provincial Hospital. The mission they accepted today was to clear out the zombies in the hospital area and collect medical equipment from inside. After clearing the zombies near the hospital, they had just turned toward the Provincial Hospital.

There were too many zombies gathered on the first floor of the hospital, so Jing Chengsu's team members were clearing it from the top down. They had just finished clearing the intensive care unit on the top floor; since these were all critically ill patients, the probability of them turning into zombies was one hundred percent. Fortunately, there weren't many of them, so Jing Chengsu and his team didn't spend much time clearing that floor.

Just after finishing the cleanup, Jiang Ye noticed the situation on Zhou Pan's side and left in a hurry. He didn't know how the other team members' missions were progressing now.

As one of the second-tier cities in the southern region, F City had a permanent population of nearly ten million. Less than half of the survivors remained after the apocalypse, and there were several million zombies wandering within F City. Because it was so close to the F City base, missions to clear various streets in F City were carried out almost daily to avoid triggering a zombie tide.

After the apocalypse, not only were zombies the great enemy of humanity, but various mutated plants and animals also dominated everywhere, eyeing humans covetously.

Jing Chengsu and his team intended to go up through the hospital's back entrance, but they discovered a massive Boston ivy that had occupied the area behind the hospital with its vines. To enter from there, they had to pass through the area covered by this ivy. The mutated Boston ivy climbed along the back wall and perimeter wall of the hospital. Its roots secreted acidic substances that corroded the concrete walls, and thick, rugged root fibers burrowed into the wall along the cracks. The cracks were widened significantly by the root fibers; a single misstep could potentially cause the wall it had burrowed into to crumble and collapse.

The originally docile vines had become aggressive and much more dangerous after mutation. As soon as they sensed any object moving near the vine body, they would immediately sweep over, dragging the prey into the vine mass to become fertilizer for the roots. As Jing Chengsu and his team looked up, they saw the base of the wall covered in white skulls; even zombies had become one of the fertilizers for the Boston ivy.

This Boston ivy had dominated this place for over two months, constantly sweeping up various prey as fertilizer to absorb and level up. It was now a Level 5 mutated plant, far more threatening than the zombies in the hospital. Jing Chengsu and the others had indescribable feelings; they just wanted to take a shortcut, so how could they be so unlucky as to run into a big boss?

Zhou Pan's expression was a bit bewildered. Since when did F City have such a big boss? Why had he never heard anyone mention it in his past life?

However, it wasn't strange that he hadn't heard of it. In his past life, the scope of the F City base was definitely not as vast as it was in this life. Coupled with the various chaotic situations among the base's upper echelons, the base had merely hunkered down in one area. Besides searching for supplies, what manpower did they have to clear out other areas?

Even if they had discovered this big boss, the base's upper echelons likely wouldn't have dared to speak out for fear of causing panic. They would have suppressed the news regardless, and it would have been even more impossible for Zhou Pan, who was lingering at the bottom of the apocalypse in his past life, to know about it.

With such a big boss present, everyone hesitated and lingered.

"Sss—" The vine leaves rustled, and an invisible sound wave pierced their minds. Still hesitating whether to turn around and leave or continue forward, they fell into a trance, their footsteps involuntarily moving toward the massive vine body of the Boston ivy.

Dense vines, like snakes and pythons, reached out aggressively. The leaves rustled wildly, as if something were laughing arrogantly. Just as the group was about to fall into danger and be wrapped by the vines to become fertilizer for the roots, Zhou Pan's mind jolted, and he snapped back to reality.

As soon as his eyes cleared, he saw the crisis before him. Hiss! He gasped, quickly stopping his footsteps. He wanted to retreat, but he noticed Jing Chengsu and the others walking toward the Boston ivy in a trance.

They didn't have his powerful spiritual sense to break free from the mental control of the Boston ivy.

"Brother Su, wake up!" Zhou Pan grabbed Jing Chengsu, who was closest to him, and shouted. The dazed Jing Chengsu woke up.

"Huh? What's going on?" Jing Chengsu saw that they had unknowingly walked almost into the attack range of the vines, and his face darkened.

"This Boston ivy seems to have a very strong mental presence; everyone was being controlled." Zhou Pan stated his hypothesis and quickly went to intercept Zhou Yuanyuan and the others.

A mental presence? Jing Chengsu's heart tightened. It seemed he needed to strengthen his training in spiritual sense; he didn't want to experience this feeling of being unable to control his own body ever again.
chapters.source_text:
荆成夙带着周磐等人穿过几条街道，到达F市省立医院，今天他们接的任务是清理医院一带的丧尸和收集内部的医学设备。将医院附近的丧尸都清理了，刚转到省立医院。
医院一楼聚集的丧尸太多，荆成夙的队员们是从上往下清剿的。才刚清理了顶楼的加护病房，这里住的都是重症病患，成丧尸的几率百分百。不过幸好数量不多，荆成夙带着一队人没花多长时间就清理完这层楼。
刚清理完江烨就发现了周磐那边的情况，他急匆匆离开，也不知现在其他队员任务进行的怎么样？
F市作为南方区域的二线城市之一，常住人口达到近千万，末世后活下来的生存者不到二分之一，在F市内游荡的丧尸就有好几百万，距离F市基地那么近，为了不引起丧尸潮，几乎天天都有清理F市各个街道的任务。
末世后不但丧尸是人类的大敌，还有各种变异的动植物，也雄踞在各处，对人类虎视眈眈。
荆成夙他们打算从医院后门上去，却发现有一颗超大的爬山虎，将藤蔓占据了医院后方区域，想要从此进入，必须先经过这棵爬山虎笼罩的范围。变异的爬山虎攀缘在医院后墙以及围墙上，它的根分泌酸性物质腐蚀了水泥墙，一根根粗犷的根须沿着墙的缝隙钻入墙面，缝隙被根须撑的很大，一着不甚，有可能导致被它钻入的墙面碎裂倒塌。
原本随和的藤条变异后变得张牙舞爪，危险了很多，一感觉到有什么物体在藤体附近移动，便立刻席卷而去，将猎物卷近藤体，成了藤根的肥料，荆成夙他们抬眼望去，墙体底部爬满了白色的骷髅头，就连丧尸也成了爬山虎肥料之一。
这爬山虎雄踞此处两个多月，不断席卷各种猎物做为肥料吸收晋级，如今已是五级异植，比医院里的丧尸威胁大多了，荆成夙几个心情有点难以言喻，他们只不过是想操个近路而已，怎么这么倒霉就碰到个大BOSS。
周磐表情有点懵逼，什么时候F市居然有这么号大BOSS的。上辈子怎么从来没听人说过？
不过也不怪他没听过，上辈子F市基地范围绝对没有这辈子的宽广，加上基地上层各种乱相，基地只不过龟缩在一下片区域，除了寻找物资，哪有什么人手清剿别的区域？
就算发现了这个大BOSS，为了不引起恐慌，基地上层怕是也不敢伸张，怎么也会压下这个消息，更不可能让上辈子在末世底层徘徊的周磐知道。
有这么个大BOSS，大家有点犹豫的踌躇不前。
“吡——”藤叶沙沙作响，一声无形的音波刺入他们脑海，还在犹豫是转头离开，还是继续前进的他们，一阵精神恍惚，脚步不由自主的就朝爬山虎巨大的藤体而去。
密密麻麻如一条条蛇蟒的藤蔓，张牙舞爪的直向前卷去，叶片沙沙沙狂响，仿佛有什么东西在嚣张的狂笑，眼看着几人要落入险境，被藤蔓卷住化为树根肥料之一时，周磐脑中猛然一震，清醒过来。
眼睛刚刚清明，就看到印入眼帘的危机，嗬！他倒抽口凉气，赶紧停住脚步，想要退后，却发现荆成夙几个精神恍惚的朝爬山虎走去。
他们可没有他那么强的神识，可以摆脱爬山虎精神体的控制。
“夙哥，你快醒醒。”周磐抓住离他最近的荆成夙，一阵叫喊，恍惚的荆成夙清醒过来。
“嗯？怎么回事？”荆成夙看到他们居然不知不觉快走到藤蔓攻击范围之内了，不由脸色一沉。
“这爬山虎好像有很强的精神体，大家都被控制了。”周磐说了他的猜想，就赶紧去拦截周媛媛几个。
精神体？荆成夙心头一凛，看来他要加强神识这方面的锻炼，这种身不由己的感觉他可不想再经历一次。
