这个穿衣镜能照一个人的全身上下。周磐将它靠在厨房旁边的一面墙上，他站在镜子前面，从镜子里照出一个一米七左右微胖的少年，白嫩肉肉的脸蛋上，一对杏仁眼睛璨璨生光配上挺翘的鼻型，粉嘟嘟的小嘴巴，说不出的可爱迷人。美中不足的是一头头发杂乱无章，有的长有的短，挂在头上给他的颜值降了好几个百分点。
周磐捧着一张脸左看右看，自从他胖了几后，五官完全变了形状，他都有好几年了没见过自己这张脸了，他爸爸当初老爱捏他的脸，说他的脸型长的有福气，将来肯定享福不尽。可惜上辈子他啥福都没有享到，不过如果换了这辈子说不定真能享到福。
他看了一下镜子里的全身上下，照出来的体型还有一点胖。不过他也尽力了，能在半个月就从二百斤减到一百四十斤，整整少了六十斤，已经是神速了，如果没有功法，没有灵泉水，光是靠他运动节食减肥能减个五六斤就不错了。
只见他上半身一件超大号的黑色短袖T恤，下半身米白色的短裤，穿在微胖白嫩的身体上，倒也不显的突兀。但是脚下那双凉鞋显然大了太多，后面脚后跟有一大截没踩到，他只能勉强当做拖鞋穿着。
这衣服裤子鞋子都是他爸爸的旧衣服，上衣还好再大也可以当做嘻哈服穿，裤子原本是长裤，被他减成短裤，拿去严大婶那里改了改，就是鞋子太麻烦了，根本没法改，周磐很无奈，只好等他去了城里再从新买点衣服。
距离周琦上次回来已经过了一个星期，今天又是星期天，周磐早早的就起来了。打理好个人卫生，他才在这里打量自己。
经过周磐不懈努力，大前天终于修成了缥缈炼神录第一层，因为灵气的灌溉，他的身体再一次洗髓炼体，排出不少的垃圾，才会一下子又瘦了很多。这两天他还学习了招式，只是他从来没练过武，对上面描述的招式一知半解，只能依样画葫芦，打的不伦不类。
练成第一层心法，周磐掌控了空间，嘴馋的他一口气吃了好几斤水果，不知道是不是心里作用，空间里的水果，格外好吃，他完全停不下口。
周磐身上总共才三千块钱，他就算再孤陋寡闻，也知道这么点钱根本买不了什么东西。他也没有什么生财之道，就盯上了空间里的那些水果，那么多的果子，拿一小部分出来卖一下，应该没问题吧？他也不要卖多少钱，只要够他买些衣服鞋袜，生活用品，御寒的被褥之类的就足够了。反正他空间里的食物这么多，足够他一个人吃几辈了，况且也不是不能再生，吃完还可以洒上种子继续种嘛！
早上七点从周家村到县城有一辆面包车载客。时间也差不多了，周磐兜里揣上钱，就匆匆的赶到村口等车，在那里已经有不少人在等待。都是些大叔大妈，有些比较熟，有些见过但不知道是谁。他礼貌的向他们问好。经过半个月的酝酿，大家伙已经对他的改变淡定了很多，不像当初那样惊讶的仿佛天荒夜谈一样了。
都是抬头不见低头见的同村人，没有那么多恩恩怨怨，当初他的那些不良行为，大家伙就当体谅他失去父母
而提前进入叛逆期，如今再改也不晚。
几个大妈见他瘦了那么多，形象一下子变的可爱了好多，想起家中的孩子，也怜惜他小小年纪没了长辈，对他也温和起来。还亲切的问他去哪里，要不要人陪他去？他已经好几年没出外过，大妈们怕他不识路，走丢了。
周磐觉得不管去哪里，只要认识公车站牌，去哪里应该都没问题。他摇摇头，拒绝了大妈的好意，再说他还有私人的事，根本不敢让人在旁边跟着。
一会儿面包车来了，前座两个座位，后面还有加装的三排座椅。等待的人有十几个，将一辆车子挤得满满的。周磐坐在最后一排角落里，旁边坐了三个大叔，一个两人坐的座椅，坐了四个体型都很大的人，简直难受极了，周磐完全被挤的贴到了车壁上，整个空间狭小逼仄，连空气都稀薄了，车内飘着汽油味，体臭味，汗水味，各种味道混杂，让修炼后嗅觉灵敏了很多倍的周磐折磨惨了。
再加上从周家村到县城有半个小时的路程，这一条路坑坑洼洼，凹凸不平，坐在车里左右摇晃，上下颠簸，那种难受劲别提了，一到县城下车，周磐就憋不住大吐特吐，吐完脸都青了。
“磐娃子，你没事吧？”早就习惯这条路况的，大叔大妈都没有什么不良反应，见他脸色不好，关心的问道。
“我……呕……我没事，休息一会就没事了。”周磐边吐边摆手。等同村人离开了，他找了个平静的角落，弄出一点灵泉水漱漱口呸掉，又重新喝了点灵泉水，才整个人轻松了。
人舒服了，就有心情打量四周。其实这县城他挺熟的，毕竟曾经在这里读了两三年的初中，各个大路小路巷道拐角都能如数家珍，这几年来也不过旧楼换新楼，老店改新店，大体上是没有什么变化的。
县城比较小，路上没装多少摄像头，倒是适合从空间中拿东西出来卖，就是县城购买力小，卖不出多少东西。
周磐干脆找了一个无人的角落，取出装着各种水果的筐子，放成一堆，在旁边的租车行叫了辆小货车，包车去F市，这样就不怕去市里的时候去空间取东西会被摄像头拍到，他对自己的英明决定佩服了下。
小货车被人开来，将货物装上车，周磐爬到副驾驶座上坐着，很快车子就开始开了，上的是国道，柏油马路，路面很平坦，他开了点窗户，有风吹进来，比先前的车子坐的舒服多了。
小货车司机是个矮小精悍的三十多岁的男人，长相平凡，看起来一脸忠厚老实的面相，却是个话唠，从周磐坐上车开时就一直说个不停，周磐觉得自己不是个能藏住话的人，为了不让自己的老底都被人挖出来，他只是“嗯”“哦”“啊”“咦”的发出单调音节算做回答，好在这司机大叔也不在意他有没有回答，只要有人听他将话，他一个人都能讲一天。
车子开了三个小时，终于到了F市，司机大叔问他水果运到哪个地方，他傻眼了。F市他压根没来过，根本不知道要去哪里卖啊？
“要不运到菜市场口，那里人流量多，你看怎么样？”司机大叔见他一脸茫然，就知道他是个刚进城的小白，还好司机大叔也是个热心人，给了他一个见意。
有了去处，周磐立马点头，小货车顺势转过弯道，开了一段路程，在F是最大的菜市场口停下，此时已经有十一点多，上班族刚好下班，菜市场人来人往，人流量非常多。找了处平坦干净的地方，司机大叔帮他将一一水果搬下车，周磐给司机大叔算了钱，想装点水果感谢他，却发现自己除了水果和筐子，他其他什么东西都没有准备，没有装水果用的塑料袋，也没有秤，叫他怎么卖？
无奈之下，他只好叫司机大叔帮他看一下水果，他去菜市场里面买点塑料袋，他记得一般菜市场都有批发这东西卖。很快买了塑料袋出来，装了一些水果给司机大叔，被推辞了好一会儿，司机大叔才接过水果开车走了。
留下周磐一个人面对拥挤的人流，他不由得胆怯起来。他要卖的水果有苹果，香蕉，小西瓜，梨等常见水果，个个卖相都很不错，即使他手足无措的呆在水果筐子后面，还是有人过来询问。
“老板你这水果怎么卖？”几个白领上班族从菜市场里面买菜出来，经过他这里，看他的水果水头好，就忍不住停下来问道。
周磐没秤，最主要的是他不会看秤，没法子，不能论斤卖，只能论个了。
他看着水果回忆了一下，周媛媛买的水果的价格，就说“苹果一个两块钱，香蕉一根五角钱，小西瓜一个五块钱，梨两个三块钱。”
听周媛媛说苹果一斤三个六块多，他这些苹果的个头都很大，两个都快一斤了，一个卖两块钱算是亏了，不过他也没想着赚多少钱，能把这些水果卖掉就行。
这么大的水果才两块钱，几个白领眼睛都亮了，拿起苹果闻闻，浓郁的果香扑鼻而来，一闻就知道是上品水果，要是拿到店里卖，这么好的水果没有三五块拿不下来，这可占大便宜了，这种好事可不长有，也不管这小哥为什么卖的这么便宜，大家赶紧拿袋子装了起来。
一个两块钱，算钱也简单，只要数数个数，很快就结账完毕，生意开了张，紧张的周磐也在忙碌中慢慢的淡定起来，卖了一个多小时终于将水果快卖完，过了人流高峰期，人渐渐少了。还剩下一些水果，周磐用塑料袋装了，准备去部队的时候，送给周琦吃。
他将几个筐子叠起来，拿着筐子走到一条窄小的无人小巷子里，左右观望了一下，看四周没有摄像头，迅速的就将竹筐扔进空间里。
他也不知道自己到底赚了多少钱，就找了个公用厕所，上完厕所，就躲到隔间里数了数钱。没想到城市里的钱果然好赚，一个小时他十几筐的水果就卖了七千两百块钱，从来没见过这么多钱的，周磐乐的合不拢嘴。
chapters.translated_text:
Zhou Pan took out a dressing mirror. This was his mother’s old mirror. Ever since she had abandoned him to run off with someone else, he had hated her for being so ruthless and completely disregarding whether he lived or died. She hadn't even waited for his father's seven-day mourning period to pass before impatiently putting a green hat on his father. His hatred drove him to throw all her belongings into a room and lock them away.

Years had passed, and in his heart, Zhou Pan had already cut her out. She was an irrelevant person he simply didn't need to care about. Why torture himself? Good things shouldn't just sit there gathering dust and going to waste.

This dressing mirror could reflect a person's entire body. Zhou Pan leaned it against the wall next to the kitchen and stood in front of it. The mirror reflected a chubby youth around 1.7 meters tall. His fair, fleshy face featured a pair of sparkling, brilliant almond eyes paired with a delicate, upturned nose and a pouty little mouth, making him indescribably cute and charming. The only flaw was his chaotic, disheveled hair, with some parts long and others short, which dragged down his attractiveness by several percentage points.

Zhou Pan cupped his face and looked left and right. Ever since he had gained weight, his facial features had completely changed shape, and he hadn't seen his own face in years. His father used to love pinching his cheeks, saying his face had a blessed shape and he would certainly enjoy endless fortune in the future. It was a pity that in his past life, he hadn't enjoyed any fortune at all, but if it was this lifetime, maybe he really would.

He took a look at his whole body in the mirror, and his reflected figure still looked a little fat. However, he had done his best. Being able to drop from 200 catties to 140 catties in half a month—a full 60 catties lost—was already a miraculous speed. Without cultivation techniques and spiritual spring water, relying solely on exercise and dieting to lose weight would have been considered good if he managed to lose five or six catties.

He wore an oversized black short-sleeved T-shirt on his upper body and off-white shorts on his lower body. Worn on his slightly chubby, fair body, it didn't look abrupt. But the sandals on his feet were obviously much too large, with a big section of his heels missing the sole; he could only barely manage to wear them like slippers.

These clothes, pants, and shoes were all his father's old clothes. The top was fine; even if it was big, it could be worn like hip-hop style clothing. The pants were originally long trousers, which he had cut into shorts and taken to Auntie Yan's place to alter. The shoes were just too troublesome and impossible to alter, leaving Zhou Pan quite helpless. He had no choice but to wait until he went to the city to buy some new clothes.

A week had passed since Zhou Qi last returned, and today was Sunday again. Zhou Pan woke up early. After taking care of his personal hygiene, he began to examine himself here.

Through Zhou Pan's unremitting efforts, the day before yesterday he had finally completed the first level of the Etchless Spirit Cultivation Record (Piaomiao Lianshen Lu). Because of the infusion of spiritual energy, his body underwent another marrow-cleansing and body-refining session, expelling a lot of impurities, which was why he had suddenly thinned down a lot more. Over the past two days, he had also studied the combat moves, but since he had never practiced martial arts before, he only had a half-understanding of the moves described and could only copy them mechanically, executing them in a bizarre and awkward way.

Having mastered the first level of the mental technique, Zhou Pan gained control of the space. Being a foodie, he ate several catties of fruit in one breath. Whether it was psychological or not, the fruit in the space was exceptionally delicious, and he completely couldn't stop eating.

Zhou Pan had a total of 3,000 yuan on him. No matter how ignorant of the world he was, he knew that such a small amount of money couldn't buy him much. Having no way to generate wealth, he set his sights on the fruits in the space. With so many fruits, taking out a small portion to sell should be fine, right? He didn't even need to make that much; as long as it was enough for him to buy some clothes, shoes, socks, daily necessities, and warm bedding for the winter, that would be enough. Anyway, there was so much food in his space that it was enough for him to eat for several lifetimes, and besides, it wasn't like they couldn't regenerate. Once he finished eating them, he could just scatter seeds and continue growing them!

At seven in the morning, there was a van carrying passengers from Zhoujiacun to the county town. The time was almost up. Zhou Pan tucked the money into his pocket and hurried to the village entrance to wait for the ride. Quite a few people were already waiting there. They were all uncles and aunties; some were quite familiar, while others he had seen but didn't know who they were. He politely greeted them. After half a month of brewing, everyone had grown much calmer about his changes, no longer as astonished as if it were an Arabian Nights tale like they were at first.

They were fellow villagers who bumped into each other constantly, without that many deep-seated grudges. Everyone simply chalked up his previous bad behavior to him entering a rebellious phase prematurely after losing his parents,

and changing now wasn't too late.

Seeing that he had lost so much weight and his appearance had suddenly become much cuter, several aunties thought of the children in their homes and felt pity for him losing his elders at such a young age, causing them to grow gentle toward him as well. They even affectionately asked where he was going and if he needed someone to accompany him. Having not been out for several years, the aunties were afraid he wouldn't know the way and would get lost.

Zhou Pan felt that no matter where he went, as long as he recognized the bus station sign, going anywhere shouldn't be a problem. He shook his head and declined the aunties' kind offer. Besides, he had private matters and simply couldn't dare let anyone follow him around.

Soon the van arrived, featuring two seats in the front and three rows of added seats in the back. There were over a dozen people waiting, packing the single vehicle to the brim. Zhou Pan sat in the corner of the very back row next to three uncles. A two-seater bench was crammed with four very large people, making it extremely uncomfortable. Zhou Pan was completely squeezed flat against the car wall. The entire space was cramped and narrow, making even the air thin. The van drifted with the smell of gasoline, body odor, and sweat—a mixture of various smells that tortured Zhou Pan, whose sense of smell had become many times more sensitive after cultivation.

Coupled with the half-hour journey from Zhoujiacun to the county town along a bumpy, rugged road, sitting in the car swaying left and right and bouncing up and down was indescribably miserable. As soon as he got off the van in the county town, Zhou Pan couldn't hold it in anymore and vomited violently, his face turning pale green afterward.

"Pan-wa-zi, are you alright?" The uncles and aunties, long accustomed to this road condition, had no adverse reactions. Seeing his poor complexion, they asked with concern.

"I... *blech*... I'm fine, I'll be fine after resting for a while." Zhou Pan waved his hand while vomiting. Once his fellow villagers left, he found a quiet corner, conjured a bit of spiritual spring water to rinse his mouth and spit it out, and then drank some more spiritual spring water anew, only then did his whole body feel relieved.

Once he felt comfortable, he was in the mood to look around. Actually, he was quite familiar with this county town since he had studied junior high here for two or three years. He knew every major road, minor road, alley, and corner like the back of his hand. Over the past few years, old buildings had just been replaced with new ones, and old shops remodeled into new ones; overall, not much had changed.

The county town was relatively small with few security cameras installed on the streets, making it somewhat suitable for taking things out of the space to sell. However, the county town's purchasing power was low, so he wouldn't be able to sell much.

Zhou Pan simply found a deserted corner, took out the baskets filled with various fruits, and piled them together. He called a small freight truck from a nearby car rental agency and chartered it to drive to City F. That way, he wouldn't have to worry about being caught on camera taking things from the space when he arrived in the city. He admired himself for this brilliant decision.

The small freight truck was driven over, and the goods were loaded onto it. Zhou Pan climbed into the passenger seat and sat down. Soon, the vehicle started moving. They got on the national highway, an asphalt road with a very flat surface. He rolled the window down a bit, and the breeze blowing in made it much more comfortable to ride in than the previous van.

The small truck driver was a short, sharp, and capable man in his thirties with an ordinary appearance and an honest, dutiful look on his face, but he was a chatterbox. He talked incessantly from the moment Zhou Pan got into the truck. Feeling that he wasn't someone who could keep secrets, and in order to prevent all his bottom lines from being dug up by someone else, Zhou Pan only emitted monotonous syllables like "Yeah," "Oh," "Ah," and "Huh" as answers. Fortunately, this driver uncle didn't care whether he replied or not; as long as someone listened to him talk, he could ramble on all by himself for a whole day.

After driving for three hours, they finally arrived in City F. When the driver uncle asked him where to deliver the fruit, Zhou Pan was dumbfounded. He had never been to City F in his life and had no idea where to go to sell it!

"How about we deliver it to the vegetable market entrance? There's a lot of foot traffic there, what do you think?" Seeing his blank expression, the driver uncle knew he was a newbie who had just entered the city. Fortunately, the driver uncle was also a warm-hearted person and offered him a suggestion.

Having a destination, Zhou Pan immediately nodded. The small truck smoothly turned a corner, drove for a distance, and stopped at the entrance of City F's largest vegetable market. By this time, it was past eleven o'clock. Office workers were just getting off work, and people were coming and going at the vegetable market, creating a massive flow of foot traffic. Finding a flat and clean spot, the driver uncle helped him unload the fruits one by one from the truck. Zhou Pan calculated the fare for the driver uncle and wanted to pack some fruit to thank him, only to discover that besides the fruit and baskets, he hadn't prepared anything else. There were no plastic bags to hold the fruit, nor a scale—how was he supposed to sell them?

Left with no choice, he had to ask the driver uncle to watch the fruit for him while he went into the vegetable market to buy some plastic bags. He remembered that vegetable markets usually had wholesale places selling these items. He quickly bought the plastic bags and came out, packing some fruit for the driver uncle. After being refused for quite a while, the driver uncle finally accepted the fruit, got in his truck, and drove away.

Left alone to face the crowded stream of people, Zhou Pan couldn't help but feel timid. The fruits he wanted to sell included apples, bananas, small watermelons, pears, and other common fruits, all of which looked very appealing. Even though he stood flustered behind the fruit baskets, people still came over to inquire.

"Boss, how do you sell this fruit?" Several white-collar office workers came out of the vegetable market carrying groceries. Passing by him and seeing how fresh his fruit looked, they couldn't help but stop and ask.

Zhou Pan didn't have a scale, and most importantly, he didn't know how to read a scale. With no other choice, he couldn't sell by weight and could only sell by individual pieces.

Looking at the fruit and recalling the prices of the fruit Zhou Yuanyuan bought, he said, "Apples are two yuan each, bananas are fifty cents each, small watermelons are five yuan each, and pears are three yuan for two."

Hearing Zhou Yuanyuan say that apples cost a little over six yuan for three per catty, these apples of his were all very large—two of them were almost a catty, so selling one for two yuan could be considered a loss. However, he wasn't looking to make a huge profit; as long as he could sell these fruits off, it would be fine.

Such big fruit for only two yuan made the white-collar workers' eyes light up. They picked up an apple and sniffed it; a rich fruity fragrance hit their noses. One sniff and they knew it was top-grade fruit. If sold in a store, such good fruit couldn't be bought for less than three to five yuan. This was a huge bargain! Such a good thing didn't happen often. Regardless of why this young brother was selling them so cheaply, everyone hurriedly grabbed bags and started packing them up.

At two yuan each, calculating the money was also simple; he just had to count the quantity, and the transaction was finished quickly. With the business officially opened, the nervous Zhou Pan gradually calmed down amidst the hustle and bustle. After selling for over an hour, he finally almost sold out the fruit, and as the peak foot traffic period passed, the crowd gradually thinned out. With some fruit remaining, Zhou Pan packed them into plastic bags, planning to give them to Zhou Qi to eat when he went to the military camp.

He stacked the several baskets together, carried them into a narrow, deserted alley, looked left and right, and seeing no security cameras around, quickly tossed the bamboo baskets into his space.

Not knowing how much money he had actually made, he found a public restroom. After using it, he hid in a stall to count the money. He hadn't expected urban money to be so easy to make after all; in just one hour, his dozen or so baskets of fruit had sold for 7,200 yuan. Having never seen so much money before, Zhou Pan grinned from ear to ear with joy.

chapters.translated_text:
"Ouch, what is this?" Zhou Pan cried out in pain. Something had pricked his hand, and a significant amount of blood began to flow.

After returning from the street and eating at the cafeteria, he went back to the dormitory. Jing Chengsu went to cultivate, and Zhou Pan, seeing that they had bought a lot of things today that were now piled up in his space like a messy heap of trash, found it an eyesore and went into the space to organize it.

The items bought today would have been worth a fortune in peaceful times, but unfortunately, when life is threatened, no treasure is worth as much as a mouthful of water or food.

Zhou Pan felt it was a pity not to buy them since he had plenty of space and didn't lack the spirit cores to pay for them.

He and Jing Chengsu had bought things as they strolled along; he hadn't realized it at the time, but while organizing, he found there were so many items that they couldn't even fit into one room.

Fortunately, this mansion was large and had plenty of rooms, so clearing out two of them wasn't a problem.

The items he bought were quite varied. Besides gold, silver, jewelry, jade, and porcelain, there were also elegant items like musical instruments, chess sets, calligraphy, and paintings. These things couldn't be eaten or worn, and he originally had no intention of buying them, but Jing Chengsu, fearing that these national treasures would end up in a landfill if no one bought them, had purchased them all.

In addition to these once-valuable items, Zhou Pan also bought many other things, such as novels, game consoles to pass the time, clothes, shoes, socks, and the swords he bought later.

He first packed up the non-fragile items and placed them in one room, leaving the jade and porcelain for last.

However, he didn't expect that when he picked up a jade-white pendant carved in the shape of a dragon, it would prick his hand. It had clearly felt smooth and rounded, without any sharp edges, when he picked it up.

He held the pendant up and looked at it from all angles. It was indeed smooth and lustrous, without any abrupt edges or burrs, so why was his hand injured? And hadn't a lot of blood from his finger flowed onto the pendant? Why couldn't he see a single trace of it? If it weren't for the wound on his finger still oozing a bit of blood, he would have thought his eyes were playing tricks on him.

This scene felt a bit familiar. Why was it so similar to a plot in a novel? His eyes darted around as he thought of a possibility. He couldn't help but calm his mind and probe a sliver of his divine sense into the pendant. Ever since reaching the Foundation Establishment stage, he had discovered he could project his divine sense to scout any terrain within a ten-mile radius, and his telekinetic control had also strengthened; harvesting and planting crops in the space was no longer a difficult task.

As soon as his divine sense entered, he discovered that this was actually a jade slip containing a legacy. It required a specific person to fully unlock it. Although he could probe into the jade slip, he only received a small amount of information. It turned out to be a martial cultivation technique, a method of achieving immortality through martial arts. Even though it was an incomplete version, it was enough to surprise Zhou Pan.

He himself didn't have to worry about lacking cultivation techniques, and his talent was decent. Even if he didn't achieve immortality, as long as he didn't die prematurely and kept advancing, he could live for a very long time. However, Jing Chengsu was different. Although he had lightning abilities, he was ultimately just a mortal. Even if he became stronger in the future, he would likely only live a few hundred years at most.

Zhou Pan had originally wanted to pass his own cultivation method to him, but unfortunately, Jing Chengsu was unable to receive it, so he had to give up helplessly. He hadn't expected that buying a pile of things today would lead to such an unexpected surprise.

He didn't care why this jade slip had ended up in this world, nor why it had been mixed in with these jade items like an ordinary pendant. He only knew that, barring any accidents, his path to immortality might not be lonely after all.

With a face full of joy, he continued to pack the items on the ground into boxes and cabinets. After finishing, he went to the stream to bathe, then flashed out of the space, feeling refreshed with his hair still wet.

Upon exiting the space, he saw that Jing Chengsu had finished cultivating his abilities and was sitting at the table reading some documents.

Zhou Pan excitedly ran to his side, "Brother Su, I have something good to show you."

"What is it?" Jing Chengsu put down the documents and turned to see that his hair was still dripping wet. He quickly stood up, grabbed a dry towel, and began drying it for him, saying with displeasure, "Why are you all wet? You didn't even dry yourself off. It's so cold outside, what will you do if you get sick?"

Zhou Pan stuck out his tongue. He wanted to show Jing Chengsu the surprise as soon as possible, so he hadn't bothered to dry his hair. As for getting sick, he wasn't worried at all; he had already reached the Foundation Establishment stage in cultivation! Things like colds and fevers would never happen to him again.

Once Jing Chengsu finished drying his hair, he couldn't wait to take out the pendant and wave it in front of Jing Chengsu, "Ta-da! Brother Su, look what this is."

"A jade pendant?" Jing Chengsu took the jade-white pendant. It looked a bit like mutton-fat jade, but the quality seemed even better.

"This isn't an ordinary jade pendant; it's a jade slip for cultivation," Zhou Pan said directly, without keeping him in suspense.

"Cultivation? The same as your technique?" Jing Chengsu looked up.

"Yes, but the path is different. This jade slip contains a martial cultivation technique, a way to achieve immortality through martial arts," Zhou Pan explained.

Jing Chengsu felt a surge of joy and looked at the pendant earnestly. He knew Zhou Pan's technique was unique and had guessed as much, but he hadn't expected it to actually be a cultivation method. Cultivation and immortality were almost things of legend, yet he had the fortune to learn of them. There was no need to mention why Zhou Pan had brought out this jade slip; he could guess it, and his eyes softened.

"Brother Su, press the jade slip against your forehead and focus all your attention on wanting to see what's inside," Zhou Pan instructed seriously.

Upon hearing this, Jing Chengsu pressed the jade slip to his forehead and calmed his mind.
chapters.source_text:
“哎呦，这是什么？”周磐痛叫一声，手上不知道被什么刺了一下，流出不少鲜血。
从街上回来，去食堂吃了饭回宿舍，荆成夙就去修炼了，周磐见今个儿买了不少东西，丢在空间里乱成一团，向垃圾堆在一样，看着碍眼，就跑到空间里整理起来。
今个儿买的东西在和平年代都是价值不菲的东西，可惜在生命受到威胁的时候，再宝贵的东西，也抵不了一口水一口饭。
周磐看着可惜买了不少，反正他也不缺那点晶核，又有地方储存，买下来也没什么。
他和荆成夙两人边逛边买，买的时候不觉得，没想到整理的时候居然多的一个房间都装不下了。
幸亏这宅子够大，房间也多的很，收拾两间出来，也不是问题。
他买的东西还挺杂的，除了金银珠宝玉器瓷器，还有琴棋书画等风雅之物，这些玩意不当吃不当穿，他原本是无意购买的，不过荆成夙见这些过去的国粹无人买下来的话，怕是要落到垃圾场的下场，就把他们都买了下来。
除了这些过去价值不菲的东西，周磐还买了不少其它东西，比如小说，游戏机之类的打发时间的东西，还有衣服鞋袜之类的，以及后面买的刀剑。
他先将不易碎的东西收拾好，放在一个房间，最后再来整理那些玉器瓷器等物。
不过他没想到拿一块玉白色雕着龙形玉佩的时候，会扎到手，明明拿起的时，还是圆润光滑，无菱无角的啊？
他将玉佩举起左看右看，没错一样的光滑润泽，没有任何突兀的菱角毛刺，怎么他手就受伤了呢？而且他手指上的血流了不少在这玉佩上吧？怎么没看见一丝一毫？要不是看到手指上还溢出一点血丝的伤口，他都要当自己眼花记错了。
这场景有点眼熟啊？怎么这么像小说的情节？他眼睛一转，想到一个可能，不由凝神静气，将神识探了一丝进玉佩，自从筑基以来，他发现自己可以神识外放，探查周周十里地范围内的任何地形，神识控物也更强了，收割空间内的作物和种植都已经不是什么难题了。
神识一探入就发现原来这是个传承玉简，这要特定的人才能完全打开，他虽然能探进玉简中，却只收到了一点讯息，原来是一个武修法诀，是以武入道的修仙法门，虽然是残缺版但足够周磐惊喜了。
他自己不愁没有修炼法诀，天分也还行，以后不说长生得道，只要不是意外夭折，不断晋级，他的生命可以活很久，可是荆成夙不同，他虽然有雷异能，但终究只是凡人，即使以后再强，最多多活几百年也只怕到头了。
周磐原本想把自己的功法交给他，可惜荆成夙根本无法接收到法诀，他只好无奈死心了，没想到今个儿买了一堆东西，居然有意外惊喜。
他不管这块玉简为何会沦落到这个世界，也不管它为何会像一块普通玉佩一样，和这些玉器混在一起，他只知道不出意外他的长生路，也许不会孤单了。
带着满脸的开心，他继续将地上那些东西都装箱的装箱，装柜的装柜，都一一收拾好了，又去溪边洗过澡了，才带着满身的清爽，顶着一头湿发闪出空间。
他出空间看见荆成夙已经修炼好异能，正坐在桌前看什么文件。
周磐兴奋的跑到他身边，“夙哥，我有好东西给你看。”
“什么？”荆成夙放下文件，转头见他头上发丝还是湿哒哒的，连忙起身取出一条干毛巾，边给他擦干，边不悦道，“怎么湿漉漉的，也不弄干一下，天气这么冷，生病了怎么办？”
周磐吐吐舌，他想早点拿惊喜给荆成夙看嘛，哪顾得上擦什么头发，生病之类的他压根不担心，他都已经修真筑基了好嘛！感冒发烧这种事已经不会再发生了。
等荆成夙帮他擦完，他就迫不及待的掏出玉佩，在荆成夙眼前晃着，“当当当，夙哥，你看这是什么？”
“玉佩？”荆成夙拿过这块玉白色的玉佩，有点像羊脂玉但玉质好像更好一点。
“这可不是普通的玉佩，这是玉简，修真用的。”周磐也不卖关子，直接说道。
“修真？跟你的功法一样？”荆成夙抬起头。
“对，只是道不同，这玉简里的是武修功法，以武入道的。”周磐解释道。
荆成夙心头一喜，认真的看这块玉佩。他知道周磐的功法有点独特，也有过猜想，可没想到居然是修真功法，修真长生几乎是传说中的事，他竟然有缘得知。周磐拿出这块玉简的用意不用说他也猜的到，他眼睛不由柔和下来。
“夙哥，你将玉简抵在额头上，全神贯注想着要看玉简里的东西。”周磐认真教导。
荆成夙闻言将玉简按在额头上，凝神静气。

chapters.title: 第61章 武修功法「求推荐，求收藏」
chapters.translated_text:
As soon as Jing Chengsu’s consciousness probed into the space, a massive stream of profound text slammed into his mind, filling it to the point of bursting. If he hadn’t guessed that this was a method of transmitting techniques, he would have almost dropped the jade slip.

People of cultivation are truly extraordinary; the transmission method is like a fax machine, almost directly "faxing" the information into his mind. Moreover, it was like printing, carved into his brain so deeply that he couldn't forget it even if he wanted to.

The characters in the technique looked like ancient pictographs. If he had tried to read them himself, he would have barely recognized a third of them, stumbling through. Yet, for some reason, he easily understood everything in the transmitted technique.

This was a martial cultivation technique, and it only contained the first half. Generally, cultivation requires spiritual roots; without them, one cannot cultivate. But things in the world are not absolute; heaven never cuts off all paths. It leaves another grand path for mortals who have a strong desire for the Dao and refuse to give up. Although it is ten thousand times harder than for those born with spiritual roots, as long as one is willing to work hard, it is not impossible to step onto the path of longevity.

However, while martial cultivation is more arduous than Dharma or sword cultivation, the strength gained is higher. At the same level, a martial cultivator is much stronger than those orthodox cultivators.

Jing Chengsu himself was a martial artist and naturally had a great passion for martial arts. He didn't know if he had spiritual roots, but regardless, he was extremely interested in this technique and wanted to cultivate it.

This technique is called the "Nine-Turn Hunyuan Manual," an incredibly powerful martial cultivation technique. Although it only contains the first half, the content is very rich. Beyond the cultivation moves for each stage, it also includes methods for tempering tendons, marrow, and the body, ensuring that every inch of skin can be refined.

The only trouble is that when practicing this martial technique, each stage requires a large amount of medicinal herbs to assist. Although the herbs needed for the initial stages aren't particularly rare, the sheer quantity required is the problem. In this world where everything is scarce during the apocalypse, where is he supposed to gather all these herbs?

Jing Chengsu opened his eyes to see Zhou Pan squatting in front of him, staring at him without blinking.

Seeing him open his eyes, Zhou Pan immediately leaned in, "Brother Su, how is it? Did you receive the technique? Is everything okay?"

Zhou Pan had once quietly checked Jing Chengsu’s spiritual roots; they were so weak they were negligible. Even if there were other cultivation techniques, he wouldn't be able to practice them. Fortunately, he had luckily stumbled upon this jade slip. Martial cultivation doesn't consider spiritual root talent; as long as one has martial talent and is willing to work hard, the future is not a dream.

Zhou Pan couldn't say much else, but he was certain Jing Chengsu’s martial talent was very strong. He felt this technique was practically tailor-made for him.

"I've received it," Jing Chengsu said with a smile in his eyes. "It's just that the medicinal herbs are a bit troublesome. This technique requires a lot of herbs to prepare medicinal baths at each stage of cultivation and leveling up. It won't be easy to find these things in the apocalypse."

"Medicinal herbs? What kind of herbs does Brother Su need?" Zhou Pan asked.

It just so happened that he had a small plot of land in his space currently growing some herbs.

Jing Chengsu fluently rattled off a list of herbs. He didn't notice that as he recited them, Zhou Pan was comparing them to the herbs in his space.

He already had more than half of the eighty-some herbs in his space. The others didn't sound like particularly precious herbs either; he would just have to go dig up some seeds and cultivate them later.

Zhou Pan didn't tell Jing Chengsu, planning to give him a surprise once the herbs were all gathered.

Having just obtained the technique, Jing Chengsu was full of interest. After chatting with Zhou Pan for a while, he couldn't wait to immerse himself in the technique.

Zhou Pan didn't disturb him and went into his space to cultivate instead.

Zhou Pan’s wind ability had reached level three and hadn't moved since. Although he rarely used this wind ability, as a trump card, it was best to keep it at a high level.

Zhou Pan sat in meditation directly beside the spiritual spring, going through the "Ethereal Refining Spirit Record" first before practicing his wind ability.

The ability cultivation methods he heard about in his past life were actually quite crude. Zhou Pan felt that the cultivation methods of the immortal technique had merits for his abilities as well. He had always used the method of breathing and channeling energy when practicing his abilities, and he hadn't expected it to be so effective; his ability cultivation was always a little faster than others.

He had also taught this method to Jing Chengsu, and Jing Chengsu’s progress using it was quite good.

The military had recruited the grandfather and grandson of the Zhou family. They were barely considered cultivators and knew some basic cultivation skills. They had taught the military the method of breathing and channeling energy. Although it was relatively shallow, it was still stronger than the ability cultivation methods from his past life, and now the two were being well-provided for by the military.

After cultivating for an unknown amount of time, when Zhou Pan opened his eyes again, his ability had improved slightly.

Cultivating at home was too comfortable, and progress was ultimately too slow. Techniques and abilities needed to be used more in combat for breakthroughs to be smoother.

It seemed that the next time Jing Chengsu went on a mission, he would have to follow along.

Calming his breath, Zhou Pan stood up after finishing his meditation and ran to the kitchen to tinker. Since he wanted to go out on missions, it would be inconvenient regarding food. He needed to prepare more supplies to prevent situations where they couldn't cook on the road.
chapters.source_text:
荆成夙精神一探入空间中，就有一大串深奥文字砸入他的脑海，塞的他满脑海都是涨涨的，要不是猜到这是传送功法的方式，他差点就失手弄掉玉简。
修真之人果然不简单，传送之法跟传真机似的，几乎是直接串真到他脑海，而且像打印一样，刻在他脑海中，他想忘都忘不了。
功法上的文字像是古体象形文字，原本他自己认的话，磕磕绊绊大概只能认识三分之一，不过传送过来的功法，也不知怎么，他居然全部轻易看明白了。
这是一套武修功法，只有上部分。一般修真都要有灵根，没有灵根的话是无法修真的。但世事也不是完全绝对，天无绝人之路，也给那些求道之心强烈，不肯放弃的凡人另一条大道，虽然比那些天生的修真者要辛苦万倍，但只要肯努力，也不是没机会踏上长生之路。
然则武修比那些法修剑修等辛苦，可是实力跟上，同一等级，却会比那些正经修真者强很多。
荆成夙本身就是练武之人，天生就对武术有着极大热情，他不知道自己有没有灵根，不过不管有没有灵根，他都对这功法十分感兴趣，想要修炼。
这本功法叫九转混元功，是一本极为强大的武修功法，虽然只有上半段，内容却很丰富，除了每个阶段的修炼招式，还有炼筋炼髓炼体功法，保准把身上的每一分肌肤都能修炼到。
就是有点麻烦，这武修功法修炼的时候，每个阶段都需要大量药材配合修炼。虽然上面的需要的药材初期几个阶段，并不是多稀奇的材料，可谁让他用的多，在这末世啥都缺的世界，要去哪凑起这些药材啊？
荆成夙睁开眼，印入眼帘的是周磐蹲在他身前，一眨不眨盯着他的模样。
一见他睁开眼，连忙凑到他身前，“夙哥，怎么样？功法接收了吗？没问题吧？”
周磐曾经悄悄看了荆成夙的灵根，弱的可以忽略了，就算有其他修真功法，他也练不了，不过还好，他幸运的淘到这个玉简，武修是不考虑灵根天份的，只要有武术天赋肯努力，未来不是梦。
荆成夙别的不敢说，武术天赋肯定很强，他觉得这功夫简直就像是为荆成夙量身打造的。
“已经接收了。”荆成夙眼角带笑，“就是药材方面有点麻烦。这功法修炼升级每个阶段需要很多药材配置汤剂泡澡，现在末世找这些东西可不太容易。”
“药材？夙哥需要什么药材？”周磐问道。
刚好他空间还有一小块地正种着一些药材呢。
荆成夙随口流利的报出一串药材名单，他没注意到他这边念，周磐在那边对比空间中的药材。
八十几种药材他空间中就有大半，其他的一听药材名，好像也不是多么珍贵的药材，什么时候去挖些种子过来培养一下。
周磐没跟荆成夙说，打算等药材凑齐了在给他惊喜。
刚得到功法，荆成夙兴趣正浓，与周磐聊了一会儿，就迫不及待的沉浸到功法里。
周磐也不去打扰他，自己跑去空间里修炼。
周磐的风异能上了三级，就一直没在动弹，虽然他很少使用这个风异能，但是作为杀手锏一样的存在，还是要一直保持高阶比较好。
周磐直接在灵泉水旁打坐，先把缥缈炼神录过一遍，才修炼起风异能。
上辈子听来的修炼异能的法诀，其实有点粗糙，周磐觉得修真功法的修炼方法，对异能也是有可取之处的，一直以来修异能的时候，使用的也是吐气纳气之法，没想到果然也是有用的，他的异能修炼的总比旁人快那么一点。
他也将这法子交给荆成夙，荆成夙用了这法子，进展也不错。
军队里招收了周五爷孙，他们勉强算修真之人，修真基本功也会一点，传授了军队吐气纳气之法，虽然比较粗浅，但还是比上辈子的那个所修异能的法子强，如今两人正被军队供着呢。
修炼了不知多久，当周磐再次睁开眼睛时，他的异能进步了一点。
在家里修炼太过安逸了，进展终究太慢，功法、异能还是要战斗中多多使用，晋级才更顺畅。
看来等下次荆成夙出任务的时候，他还得跟上。
平息静气，周磐打坐完爬起身，就跑到厨房里鼓捣，想要出外做任务，饮食方面总是不方便，他要多准备一些食物备着，以防在半路上有无法开火的时候。
chapters.translated_title: Chapter 61: Martial Cultivation Technique "Seeking recommendations, seeking collections"

chapters.source_text:
周磐想着出任务，第二天就有一个机会了。
F市基地是F省最大的生存基地，每天都有幸存者不断赶来，原先建造的基地有点太小了，能够容纳的空间越来越小，基地上层决定在基地原有的基础上朝外扩张在建立一个更大的外城。
人来的多了，物资消耗巨大，准备建设无菌种植农场又还没开始，就算开始少说也要一年半载才能见成效，现在粮食短缺成了个极大问题，只能尽力出外搜索物资。
而周磐作为空间异能者，自然也被征召。同样征召的还有基地内的其他空间异能者。
这次他们要去F市几十公里外的亢城，那里有个巨大粮食批发市场，储存了许多粮食，他们的任务是尽量将粮食批发市场中的粮食都帮运回来。
荆成夙是这次任务的负责人，由于这次任务奖励的贡献点积分巨大，除了军队派出的一支百人的队伍之外，接了这个任务的还有基地内那些自己成立的异能队伍。一共七支队伍，人数达到三百多人。
八点整基地大门前就聚集完毕，总共十七辆大卡车，荆成夙见人齐了就出发了。
大卡车开出基地，行驶在高速公路上。
从窗外望出去时常看到有不少变异的树木，有的高耸入云，果实颗颗能当弹药使用。有的张牙舞爪，树枝犀利如箭如鞭，缠绕刺穿了不少尸骸挂在树身下，看的人毛骨悚然。
常出外做任务的人此景已经见多了，周磐上辈子虽然末世呆的不久，但也算“见多识广”了，虽然觉得有点恶心，但习惯久了就好了。倒是有不少初次出任务的人见了趴在后车门上吐了。
距离亢城有几十公里路，还要走上数个小时，这还要交通顺畅的情况下，要是半路有个什么意外，可能耽误的更久。
这一路上还有好几个小村庄，多少都有点粮食什么的留下，他们倒是有心进去搜索一番又怕耽误时间，决定回来的时候再去。
连续走了三个小时，离亢城越来越近，已经将近午时，赶了一路，大伙都饥肠辘辘，半道上在一起片空地上停下来休息做饭。
七支队伍围成团，各自将准备的食材拿出来准备午餐。其他队伍的队长，在准备午饭期间，跑过来与荆成夙一起商量事情。
周磐跟着几个军队队友一起准备午餐，虽然他们只要准备军队的午饭就行，可好歹也有百多人，弄起来也很费劲，他们倒也没有那么麻烦的煮饭炒菜什么的，就是弄了好几锅面食，里面加了火腿蛋菜肉酱，也是很香的，绝对管饱管够。
如今新鲜的肉食可不好弄，据说变异兽兽肉可以食用，可是变异兽可不好抓，实力又强，不是随便什么人都杀的了的。
已经有很久没尝过肉味的人，闻着周磐这边几口锅传来的喷香味道，都馋的口水直流，本来吃着泡面啥的感觉自己的活食也不错，如今看看人家，顿时卖相差了一大截。
尤其感受最深的就是跑来商量事情的几个队长，咽咽口水，原本要离开的脚，霎时拔不动道了。
荆成夙见状就张口留下几人一同用餐，这次任务还需要几人一起配合，不过是一口饭的事，能拉进彼此之间的关系，也算物有所值。
周磐见荆成夙和几个异能队队长一起过来，立刻机灵的多取了几个碗出来。
果然吃了一顿满意的午餐，几个队长与荆成夙之间的关系好了不少，原本他们早就听过荆成夙的大名，对他恭敬有加，亲近不足，如今见他也不是多难相处的人，顿时关系拉进不少。
chapters.translated_title: Chapter 62: Going on a Mission "Seeking recommendations, seeking collections"
chapters.title: 第62章 出任务「求推荐，求收藏」
chapters.translated_text:
Zhou Pan was thinking about going on a mission, and the very next day, an opportunity arose.

The F City Base was the largest survival base in F Province. With survivors arriving in a constant stream every day, the original base had become too small, and the available space was shrinking. The base leadership decided to expand outward from the existing base to build a larger outer city.

As more people arrived, the consumption of supplies became massive. The planned sterile planting farms had not yet begun, and even if they did, it would take at least a year or so to see results. Now, food shortages had become a major problem, and they had no choice but to try their best to search for supplies outside.

As a space ability user, Zhou Pan was naturally conscripted. Other space ability users within the base were also conscripted.

This time, they were heading to Kang City, a few dozen kilometers away from F City. There was a huge wholesale food market there that stored a large amount of grain. Their mission was to help transport as much of that grain back as possible.

Jing Chengsu was the person in charge of this mission. Because the contribution points offered as a reward for this mission were massive, in addition to the hundred-man team sent by the military, several privately formed ability teams from the base also took on the mission. There were seven teams in total, with over three hundred people.

At eight o'clock sharp, everyone gathered in front of the base gate. There were seventeen large trucks in total, and once Jing Chengsu saw that everyone had arrived, they set off.

The trucks drove out of the base and onto the highway.

Looking out the window, one could often see many mutated trees. Some towered into the clouds, their fruits each capable of being used as ammunition. Others were clawing and brandishing their branches, which were as sharp as arrows and whips, entangling and piercing many corpses hanging under their trunks, a sight that made one's hair stand on end.

Those who often went out on missions had seen this scene many times. Although Zhou Pan hadn't stayed in the apocalypse for long in his previous life, he could be considered "well-informed." While he found it a bit disgusting, he got used to it after a while. However, quite a few people on their first mission ended up leaning over the back doors of the trucks and vomiting.

It was several dozen kilometers to Kang City, a journey that would take several hours, and that was assuming traffic was smooth. If there were any accidents along the way, it might take even longer.

Along the way, there were several small villages, all of which had some food left behind. They had the intention of going in to search, but fearing delays, they decided to check them on the way back.

After driving for three hours, they were getting closer to Kang City. It was nearly noon, and having traveled all this way, everyone was famished. They stopped in an open space halfway to rest and cook.

The seven teams gathered in groups, each taking out their prepared ingredients to make lunch. During the preparation, the captains of the other teams came over to discuss matters with Jing Chengsu.

Zhou Pan helped his military teammates prepare lunch. Although they only had to prepare food for the military personnel, there were over a hundred of them, so it was quite a chore. They didn't go through the trouble of cooking rice or stir-frying dishes; instead, they made several large pots of noodles with ham, eggs, vegetables, and meat sauce added in. It was very fragrant and definitely filling.

Nowadays, fresh meat was hard to come by. It was said that the meat of mutated beasts was edible, but mutated beasts were hard to catch and possessed great strength; not just anyone could kill them.

Those who hadn't tasted meat for a long time smelled the savory aroma wafting from Zhou Pan's pots and drooled. Originally, they felt their own instant noodles and such were decent, but looking at what the others had, their own meals suddenly seemed much less appetizing.

This was especially true for the captains who had come over to discuss business. They swallowed their saliva, their feet, which were originally about to leave, suddenly unable to move.

Seeing this, Jing Chengsu invited them to stay and dine together. The mission required cooperation between the teams, and it was just a meal; being able to build rapport was well worth it.

Seeing Jing Chengsu and the captains of the ability teams coming over, Zhou Pan cleverly took out a few extra bowls.

Sure enough, after a satisfying lunch, the relationship between the captains and Jing Chengsu improved significantly. They had long heard of Jing Chengsu's reputation and had been respectful but distant. Now, seeing that he wasn't difficult to get along with, the distance between them closed quite a bit.

The grain wholesale market in F Province was originally located at 819 Road, Cheng'an District, F City. Built in the 1990s, it underwent a second phase of construction in 2000, reaching an operating area of over 100 mu. The market housed six rice processing plants and one feed processing plant, with dozens of grain business entities and individuals from both within and outside the province operating there. Its annual transaction volume reached nearly one million tons, and it was listed by the state as one of the fifteen key monitoring units for national grain price trends.

Since F City is a grain-deficient area, about two-thirds of its grain had to be brought in from places like Jiangxi and the Northeast. At the same time, F City was also the main distribution center for grain in F Province, with an annual grain distribution volume of nearly two million tons. To solve traffic problems and because the existing market area could no longer meet the growing demand for grain transactions, the municipal government rebuilt a new grain wholesale market in Kangcheng.

The new market was set up with six functional areas, such as the processing area, storage area, railway spur line area, trade area, information and logistics area, and comprehensive supporting area. The processing area could handle over 1,300 tons of rice per day, the storage area added over 20,000 square meters compared to the old market, the railway spur line could receive and unload 1,200 tons of grain at once, and the operating scale of the trade area doubled that of the old market, reaching nearly two million tons. Every day, more grain came in than went out, and since no one went to the wholesale market to buy grain in the current apocalypse, there were still at least tens of millions of tons of grain stored in the wholesale market.

If they could obtain this batch of grain, it would be enough for the survivors in F City to eat for a year or a year and a half. By then, things like sterile cultivation should have yielded results, right?!

Although Jing Chengsu and the others were determined to get this batch of grain, they weren't the only ones eyeing it; the F City base wasn't alone. There were also people from other small bases, such as the Dalong Base, formed by several small factions in Linqing County, a dozen kilometers away from Kangcheng, and a small mountain city base on the nearby Qingping Mountain. Even if Jing Chengsu and his team were confident they were stronger than the others, they still had to prevent any accidents and make sufficient preparations.

After eating, drinking, and resting enough, they set off again for Kangcheng. With about an hour's journey left to Kangcheng, the closer they got, the more zombies they encountered. It took quite some effort to get near Kangcheng.

For some reason, the rate of mutated zombies in Kangcheng was exceptionally high. The total population of Kangcheng was only a few hundred thousand, but at least over two hundred thousand had mutated into zombies, and this number was still increasing. It was no wonder that the several bases nearby, which had been coveting this grain market for a long time, were still at a loss.

In fact, Jing Chengsu also had a headache when he heard this number. They only had a little over three hundred people in total. Compared to hundreds of thousands of zombies, it was like the difference between a river and a light drizzle; they wouldn't even make a splash if they threw themselves in.

The only fortunate thing was that most of these zombies were around level one, with fewer at level two or three, so there was still a glimmer of hope. Moreover, they didn't have to fight the zombies head-on; their main goal was to retrieve the grain, and killing zombies could take a backseat.

The mental ability users and those with ear and eye mutations in the team used their strengths to scout where the zombies were fewest and find the road closest to the grain market.

Jiang Ye was a mental ability user who had just stepped into the late stage of level one and was about to reach level two. His scouting range was about five or six hundred meters. After scouting for a long time, he chose a path.

The truck followed this small, sparsely populated path, crushing its way through.

Zhou Pan's divine sense had a much wider search range, but he didn't interfere with this scouting task. He already had enough "abilities"; it would be strange if people didn't find it odd if he added a mental ability on top of that. Anyway, he saw that the path chosen by Jiang Ye and the others didn't have any major errors, so he didn't say anything, though he still released his divine sense to observe whether any sudden situations would occur in the surroundings.
chapters.title: 第63章 亢城粮食批发市场「求枝枝」
chapters.source_text:
F省的粮食批发市场原本设在F市成安区819路，建于90年代，2000年的时候进行了二期建设，经营面积达到一百多亩，市场内有六家大米加工厂和一家饲料加工厂，并几十多家来自省内外粮食经营单位和个人在场内经营，年交量达近百万吨，还被国家列为全国十五个粮食价格行情重点监控单位。
由于F市是缺粮区，约2/3的粮食要从江西、东北等地调入。同时F市也是F省粮食主要集散地，年粮食集散粮将近两百万吨左右，为解决交通问题，且现有市场面积不适应粮食交易量增长的要求，市政府在亢城重新建设了新粮食批发市场。
新市场设立有六个功能区域，如加工区，仓储区，铁路专用线区，贸易区，信息物流区，综合配套区，其中加工稻谷能日达一千三百多吨，仓储区较旧市场新增面积两万多平方米，铁路专用线一次可接卸粮一千两百多吨，贸易区的经营规模比旧市场翻一番，达到近两百万吨。每天粮食进的多，出的少，又由于末世如今根本就没人再去批发市场购买，因此批发市场内储存的粮食至少还有数千万吨。
如果能够得到这批粮食，足够F市里的幸存者食用一年半载，到时候无菌种植之类的应该已经有成果了吧？！
虽然荆成夙等人对这批粮食势在必得，但是盯上这些粮食的不只有他们F市基地，还有一些其他小基地的人，比如隔亢城十几公里远的临清县城几个小势力组成的大龙基地和附近青平山上一个小山城基地，即使荆成夙他们自信自己比别人强，也要防止某些意外发生，做好足够的准备。
吃饱喝足休息够了，他们又再次出发开往亢城，距离亢城还有一个小时左右的路程，离的亢城越近遇到丧尸越多，费了一番功夫，才靠近亢城。
也不知什么原因，亢城这里变异丧尸的几率特别多，亢城总人口也不过几十万人，但变异成丧尸的起码超过二十万，并且这数字还在增加当中，也难怪附近垂涎了这片粮食市场许久的几个基地，到现在还一筹莫展。
其实荆成夙听到这个数字的时候也很头痛，他们总共人手才三百多人，与几十万丧尸相比，简直是江河与毛毛雨的区别，砸进去连个水花都飘不起来。
唯一庆幸的是，这些丧尸大多都在一级左右，二级，三级的比较少，还是有一丝胜算的。而且他们也没必要非得跟丧尸硬碰硬，他们的主要目的是取粮，杀丧尸什么的可以先靠后。
队伍中的精神异能者和耳、目变异者都发挥所长，探查附近哪里的丧尸最少，离粮食市场最近的路。
江烨是个精神异能者，如今刚跨入一级后期，将要二级了，他探查范围差不多能有五六百米距离右右，探索了半天，选择了一条路。
卡车就顺着这条丧尸稀少的小路，一路碾压过去。
周磐的神识搜索的范围更广，但他没有指手画脚的结果这个探查任务，他的“异能”够多了，要是再加一个精神异能，大家不奇怪才怪。反正他见江烨他们选择的路也没出什么大差错，就没有多言了，只不过还是有放出神识观察一下周围会不会出现什么突发情况。
chapters.translated_title: Chapter 63: Kangcheng Grain Wholesale Market "Seeking Branches"
Chapter 64: Zombie Siege "Please leave a comment"
chapters.translated_text:
Even with the utmost caution along the way, the vibrations from the dozen large trucks still attracted quite a few zombies.

Left with no other choice, everyone had to disembark and have the space-ability users store the vehicles away. They prepared to head to the grain wholesale market on foot, but they needed to deal with these zombies first.

There were an estimated two thousand zombies surrounding them. Being swarmed by so many was a terrifying sight, especially for those participating in a mission for the first time; their faces had turned pale. In fact, even those with plenty of experience couldn't help but feel a shiver down their spines at the sight of so many zombies rushing toward them.

Jing Chengrui saw that this wouldn't do. He stepped directly to the front, faced the zombies, and channeled his ability. Countless currents of electricity, as thin as willow branches, struck the zombies like a rain of arrows, piercing straight into their skulls. The sound of "hissing" was incessant, and in the blink of an eye, a large swath of zombies fell.

"So strong!" Several ability team leaders had heard of Jing Chengrui's formidable strength but had never seen it with their own eyes. Now that they had, he truly lived up to his reputation; that single massive strike had taken down at least seventy or eighty zombies.

Seeing the power of his own ultimate move, Jing Chengrui was a bit surprised himself. In fact, this move was a sudden inspiration he had after practicing martial arts techniques last night. He had noticed that the techniques—whether spells or stances—emphasized a solid foundation, with each level requiring constant compression and solidification. He wondered if this concept could be applied to his abilities. As the saying goes, "concentration is the essence." He had continuously compressed his ability energy, solidifying it into these willow-thin bolts of lightning, and he hadn't expected the power to be so immense.

His previous techniques were also powerful, but he hadn't known how to condense the energy, making his abilities too scattered. No wonder that when he used a lightning orb, some zombies would be obliterated while others would only be temporarily stunned.

The military elites led by Jing Chengrui, seeing him strike, also began to attack the zombies.

The leaders of the other ability squads, seeing that Jing Chengrui's people had started killing zombies, hurriedly led their own subordinates to join the fray.

For a time, the battle raged fiercely.

Zhou Pan took out two swords, threw one to Jing Chengrui, kept one for himself, and lunged at the zombies.

This Longquan sword was over seventy centimeters long, much longer than the short sword Jing Chengrui had given him, making it much more convenient for killing zombies. At the very least, he didn't have to worry about accidentally getting dirty things on himself.

His movements were light and agile, allowing him to move freely through the zombie horde. With every thrust of his long sword, he achieved results. Although it didn't have the wide-area lethality of using abilities, the number of zombies that fell by his hand in a short time was quite impressive.

Evolved zombies were much more nimble and not as easy to deal with as the initial ones; they could not only deflect abilities but also dodge attacks. Weaker ability users and mutants found them very difficult to fight.

The zombies surrounding them in the front were still level one, while the level twos were further back. Jing Chengrui carved a path straight through to face those level two zombies. It wouldn't be easy to leave this place without taking out the high-level zombies first.

Zombies became much more troublesome after evolving; not only could they unleash various abilities, but mutated zombies like crawlers and giants had thick skin and flesh that couldn't be harmed by those without sufficiently powerful abilities, making them quite tricky.

However, no matter how strong the zombies were, it didn't matter to Jing Chengrui and Zhou Pan. While others dealt with the level one zombies, the two of them took on the level two ones. Jing Chengrui's ability had reached level three several days ago, making him significantly stronger, and having acquired martial arts techniques yesterday, he hadn't actually used them in combat yet—this was the perfect opportunity to practice.

Zhou Pan's ability and cultivation were both stuck at level three, and he needed a bit of stimulation to break through the bottleneck. He channeled his spiritual energy into the precious sword, making the already sharp blade cut through iron like mud, and he killed zombies without any effort.

After fighting for over half an hour, they finally cleared out all the zombies. With so many zombies attacking, it was almost impossible to come out unscathed. A few greenhorns who had panicked in the face of the zombies were inevitably scratched. Since no anti-toxin serum had been invented yet, the survival rate after being scratched by a zombie was extremely low. Originally, over three hundred people taking down two thousand zombies was something to be proud of, but now, faced with such a tragedy, the atmosphere turned quite somber.
chapters.source_text:
十几辆大卡车，即使一路再谨慎，卡车经过的震动声还是引来了不少丧尸。
无奈之下，大家只好下车，让空间异能者将车先收起来。准备步行去找粮食批发市场，不过再走之前需要先把这些丧尸先解决了。
围攻的丧尸目测有两千多只左右，一起围过来，那场面还是很惊悚的，尤其是那些初次参加任务的人员，面色都青了。其实不说这些菜鸟，就是那些有过多次经验的人，见到这么多丧尸扑来，心里也不免打悚。
荆成夙一看，这不行。他直接站到前方，面对丧尸，异能一催，无数细如柳枝的电流攻向那些丧尸，道道犹如箭雨，直射丧尸头颅，“嗤嗤嗤”声音不绝，一眨眼功夫，就倒下一大片丧尸。
“好强！”几个异能队队长早听说荆成夙实力高强，一直没亲眼见过，如今一见果然名不虚传，这一大招下去，少说也倒下了七八十只丧尸。
见到自己大招的威力，荆成夙自己也有点意外，其实这招是他昨个晚上修炼过武修功法之后，才突发奇想的，他见那功法上无论是法诀还是招式，讲究的都是凝实的根基，每个阶层都需要不断压缩凝实基础，他就想这个观点能不能用在异能上呢？俗话说得好，浓缩就是精华，他将异能能量不断压缩，凝实成这些细如柳枝的雷电，没想到威力果然强大。
他以前使得招术也很厉害，但是不懂得凝实能量，使出的异能太过分散了，难怪一个雷光球下去，有的丧尸直接消亡，有的只不过暂时昏迷。
荆成夙带的军队精英，见他出手，也跟着攻向丧尸。
其他异能小队的队长，见荆成夙这边的人都开始杀丧尸了，连忙也带领自己的手下杀向丧尸。
一时间战斗如火如荼。
周磐取出两把刀剑，扔了一把给荆成夙，自己也拿了一把，刺向丧尸。
这龙泉宝剑长有七十多厘米，比荆成夙送的短剑长了许多，杀丧尸方便很多。至少不用担心不小心脏东西弄到身上。
他身法轻盈迅捷，在丧尸群中来去自如，长剑直刺，每每必有所得，虽然不向使用异能那样有大范围的杀伤力，但来来回回，一会儿功夫在他手上倒下的丧尸数目也很可观。
晋级过的丧尸手脚麻利很多，不在像初期丧尸那样好打，不但会打落异能，还会躲避攻击，实力差的异能者和变异者，打的也是很费劲的。
前面围着的还是一级丧尸，二级的还在后面，荆成夙直接杀出一条道，迎向那些二级丧尸。不把高级丧尸解决了，想离开这里可不太容易。
丧尸晋级之后麻烦了很多，不但会发出各种异能，连那些变异丧尸爬尸和巨尸皮糙肉厚的，异能不够强大的根本伤害不了它的肉体，相当棘手。
不过丧尸再强，对荆成夙和周磐两个不算什么，旁人去解决那些一级丧尸，他们两个就迎战二级丧尸，荆成夙异能早已晋级三级异能数天，实力强了一是一点半点，而且昨日又得了武修功法，虽然修炼了招式，但实际使用还没用过，刚好现在拿来练练招。
周磐异能、功法都卡在三级，正需要一点刺激来打破关卡阻碍，他将灵力注入宝剑，原本就很锋利的剑刃，更是削铁如泥，杀起丧尸毫不费力。
杀了大半个小时，才将丧尸全部解决掉，这么多丧尸围攻，毫发无伤的几乎不可能，有几个面对丧尸手忙脚乱的菜鸟，不可避免的有人被丧尸抓伤，现在没有发明出抗毒血清，被丧尸抓伤存活率极低，原本三百多人就将两千多丧尸解决掉，是个很振奋人心的事情，可现在遇到这种不幸的事，气氛顿时低迷了不少。
chapters.title: 第64章 丧尸围攻「求枝枝」

chapters.translated_text:
Those bitten by zombies could not withstand the virus's invasion and soon mutated into zombies themselves. Everyone felt heavy-hearted; although they knew such things were inevitable in the apocalypse, seeing a comrade who had been fighting alongside them just a moment ago turn into a hideous zombie the next was still heartbreaking, even for those whose hearts had hardened in these end times.

Watching their former teammate, now a zombie with protruding fangs and drooling mouth, lunging toward them, the team leaders had no choice but to order an attack.

After cleaning up the aftermath, they continued their journey. The dead could not be brought back, and they had to fight for the living. However, for the sake of safety, they became more cautious, trying their best to avoid conflicts with zombies.

Stopping and going along the way, they inevitably encountered wandering zombies. When there were few, they would rush up and eliminate them with a burst of firepower. When they encountered large groups, they tried to avoid them; if they couldn't, they attacked from a distance to keep the zombies at bay. After much delay, they finally reached the entrance of the grain wholesale market, only to find that there seemed to be even more zombies here, with many being of the second or third level.

Jiang Ye used his mental ability to probe the surroundings and discovered that not only were there zombies wandering about, but he also carefully noted that their movements were not aimless. What appeared to be chaotic wandering was actually a pattern that seemed to be protecting the grain wholesale market.

Shocked, he immediately reported this discovery to Jing Chengsu.

Jing Chengsu’s heart sank as a suspicion rose in his mind.

Although Zhou Pan’s spiritual detection range was wider than Jiang Ye’s, he wasn't as observant. While he had noticed there were more high-level zombies here, he hadn't picked up on the other details. Upon hearing this, he hurriedly covered the grain wholesale market with his spiritual sense again. His sense could detect everything within ten miles, so he wasn't as careless as before. He observed carefully and found that these zombies were indeed different and followed a specific pattern. He searched meticulously and finally discovered a unique zombie in the logistics area.

Its complexion was pale, but its facial features were intact, unlike other zombies covered in rotting flesh. While other zombies were dressed in rags or stained with filth and blood, this one was neatly dressed and looked quite refined. If not for the two fangs protruding from its purple-red lips, its blood-red eyes, and its sharp, long black fingernails—which were the only signs of it being a zombie—one might have thought it was just someone cosplaying if they saw it on the street in peaceful times.

He didn't know what its ability was, but the aura it exuded was very strong—at least level three, if not higher. It sat lazily on an office chair in the logistics area. When Zhou Pan’s spiritual sense swept over it, several level-three zombies were standing before it, making "gurgling" zombie noises. Zhou Pan couldn't understand them, but seeing this zombie, he knew the reason why so many zombies had gathered here.

He quickly withdrew his spiritual sense to report his major discovery to Jing Chengsu.

He didn't notice that when his spiritual sense pulled away, the zombie’s narrow eyes narrowed dangerously.

Zhou Pan secretly told Jing Chengsu about his discovery. After hearing what he had to say, Jing Chengsu’s suspicion was confirmed. Indeed, a high-level zombie had appeared here, possibly even a Zombie King. Their mission was likely to become even more difficult.

Jing Chengsu immediately summoned the others to discuss countermeasures.

"Damn it! These zombies are evolving too fast. How did a Zombie King appear so quickly?"

"Damn it, having hundreds of thousands of zombies here is terrifying enough, but if there's a commander, aren't we in danger?"

"This mission is going to be troublesome; we don't have enough manpower."

"The only thing to be thankful for right now is that we haven't provoked these zombies yet!"

"Should we just retreat? We can't handle a mission of this level!"

Upon hearing that there was a Zombie King and many high-level zombies, several squad leaders turned pale and began to lose their nerve.

Jing Chengsu frowned. He felt heavy-hearted about the predicament they were facing. He wanted to retreat, but if they didn't retrieve this batch of grain, the situation at the base would become much worse, and he couldn't make up his mind for a moment.
chapters.source_text:
被丧尸所伤的人，终究抵不住病毒的侵袭，很快就变异成丧尸，大家心情沉重，虽然明知末世里这种事不可避免，但是前一刻还是并肩作战的同伴，下一刻却成了面目可憎的丧尸，即使末世人心硬了很多，也忍不住恻然。
看着张着满口暴突獠牙，垂涎欲滴的向他们扑来的前队友丧尸，无奈之下各位队长最终下令攻击。
收拾起一地的疮痍，大家继续前行，死去的人已不可挽回，他们还要为活着的人奋斗，只是为了安全他们的行动更加谨慎，尽量避开与丧尸的冲突。
一路走走停停，路途中也难免会遇到一些四处徘徊的丧尸，丧尸少的他们一忽而冲上去，一阵轰炸将他们消灭，遇到大股丧尸，就尽量避开，避不开的也尽力远处攻击，不让丧尸靠近，这样一路耽搁好不容易到了粮食批发市场入口，才发现此处丧尸似乎更多，而且等级有不少二三级的。
江烨用他的精神异能窥探了一下四周，发现这里不但有丧尸徘徊，而且还细心的发现丧尸的行为也不是毫无规律的在乱窜，看似乱走一气，实则似乎是将这个粮食批发市场给保护了起来。
他心头一惊，连忙将这个发现禀报给荆成夙。
荆成夙心头一沉，一个猜测浮上心头。
周磐虽然神识探测的范围比江烨广，但他可没江烨细心，虽然也发现这里的高级丧尸多些，却没注意到其他情况，闻言赶忙再次用神识覆盖这粮食批发市场，他的神识能探测十里内的所有景致，不像先前那么马虎，他仔细的观察了一下，发现果然这些丧尸有点不同，特别有规律，他细心的找了找，终于在物流区发现了一只与众不同的丧尸。
它面色青白，但脸上五官完好，不像其他丧尸一样满脸腐肉，别的丧尸身上哪只不是衣裳褴褛，就是血迹斑驳肮脏不堪，这丧尸居然穿戴整洁，一副文质彬彬的样子，要不是他紫红的嘴角露出的两颗獠牙和血红的眼珠，以及尖锐的黑色长指甲，还能代表一点丧尸的特征，若换了和平年代，它这样的走在大街上，最多让人以为在cosplay什么人物。
不知道它的异能是什么，但是显露的气势好强，至少不在三级以下，甚至更高。只见它慵懒的坐在物流区一个办公室的座椅上，当周磐神识扫到它时，面前正站着好几个三级的丧尸，嘴里发出的“叽里咕噜”的丧尸语，周磐根本听不懂，但是看到这丧尸周磐就知道这里有这么多丧尸聚集的原因了。
他连忙收回神识向荆成夙汇报自己的大发现。
他没注意到当他神识抽离的时候，那丧尸狭长的眼睛危险的眯了一下。
周磐偷偷的将自己的大发现告诉荆成夙，荆成夙听他所言，心中的猜测更加确定，果然这里出现了高级丧尸，甚至有可能就是丧尸王，他们这次的行动怕是更加不顺利了。
荆成夙连忙招人过来商议对策。
“卧槽！这丧尸晋级的也太快了，怎么快丧尸王都出来了。”
“NND，这里有几十万丧尸就够恐怖了，还有了指挥者那我们岂不危险了？”
“这次任务麻烦了，我们人手根本不够。”
“现在最庆幸的是我们还没激怒这些丧尸！”
“要不我们撤吧？这种级别的任务我们接不了啊！”
一听说这里有丧尸王，更有许多高级丧尸，几个异能小队队长，面无人色，不由打起退堂鼓。
荆成夙眉头紧皱，对于即将面临的窘境，也是心情沉重，有心撤走，可是不取回这批粮食，基地内的处境将会恶劣许多，一时打定不了主意。
chapters.title: 第65章 出现一只丧尸王「求推荐，求收藏」
chapters.translated_title: Chapter 65: A Zombie King Appears [Seeking recommendations, seeking collections]

chapters.source_text:
想要从这么多的丧尸中夺取粮食几乎是不可能的任务，但是这批粮食对他们基地非常重要，即使再艰难也要去完成。荆成夙沉思良久，对其他几个异能小队说，“大家也知事态严重，如果你们不愿继续参加任务，可以自由退出。只是退出之后，是好是歹就不关你们的事了。”
几个异能队队长面面相觑，他们末世前也不过是普通人，末世后幸运得到能力，成为强者之列，这不代表他们也有颗强者之心，面临此等险境，他们终究退缩了，带着自己的小队，悄然离开这里。
原地只留下军队的一百号人。
“队长，我们该怎么办？”江烨担忧的问道，他们这么点人，还不够给丧尸送菜呢！即使都是部队精英，但是就算他们个个以一敌百，也最多杀的了一万只丧尸，可这何止一万只丧尸？
荆成夙环视这些弟兄，这些很多都是他自己带的队员，他心情沉重的道，“兄弟们，这次的任务有多艰难我也不多言，怕是生还的几率非常渺茫，如果有谁想要退出的请举手表决，我不会怪你们。”
大伙左右互相观望了一会儿，面色虽然有点苍白，但是个个表情坚定。
“队长，自从参加军队，我们早已将生死置之度外，我们不走。”
“对，我们可不是那些胆小鬼，一点困难就被吓退！”
“队长下命令吧！”
荆成夙看着一张张坚毅的面孔，明知将九死一生，却一个个视死如归的表情，心里如大石般沉重，嗓子如被什么东西堵住般，好半天发不出声来，他深邃的眼底带着隐痛，好一会儿才深吸口气，“好，既然大家都已决定好，就来好好商议一下，该怎么行动。”
周磐敬重的看着这些将生死置之度外的战友们，要他像他们一样随时做好牺牲的准备他可做不到，不过这不妨碍他对他们的好感。
他探出神识想要在这一片充满丧尸的市场内找出一条安全的路线出来。
观察了好一会儿，他只觉得每个方向的丧尸都很多，他也不知哪条路才是最安全的，索性拿出纸笔将所见的地形都一一记录下来，还把每个方向的大约丧尸数量都一一做了标示。
他拿给荆成夙，现在这里都是自己人，他也不怕泄露他的另一个能力了。
正在商量事情的众人，看到这张笔画粗糙，但基本地形都显示的一清二楚的简易地图，内心惊讶不已，这里面概括的范围，可比江烨这个精神异能者看到的详尽多了，也广阔多了。
对于周磐的能力，大家更多了一番惊叹。
“行啊，小磐子，深藏不漏啊！”江烨拍拍他的肩膀。
周磐腼腆的笑笑。
有了地图，一切都好办了，他们拿着地图好好研究一番，终于找到一条丧尸稀少的方向。
那就是仓储区背面，哪里只有一人宽的一条通道，丧尸很少会晃到这边。这条通道一面是仓储仓库，一边是九米高的水泥大墙，平时即使是再厉害的贼，想从此处爬入，简直难比登天，不过好在现在强者辈出，各种异能者，变异者层出不穷，对付这一层硬邦邦的墙壁，可比对付丧尸容易多了。
荆成夙手下就有不少土异能，沙异能和手脚变异的人，想在那个九米大墙掏个大洞易如反掌。
而且他们从外围背面墙后进入，还可避免跟丧尸冲突，只要小心点，装了粮食就走，保命的几率还是很高的。
虽然大家都做好了奉献生命的准备，但能够避免无谓的牺牲，谁也不想找死啊！
对于能够找来这么一张完整地图的周磐，大家好感大增。
大家好好商量了一会，终于开始行动。
chapters.translated_text:
Seizing the food supplies from such a massive horde of zombies was an almost impossible task, but this batch of grain was vital to their base, so they had to complete it no matter how difficult. Jing Chengsu pondered for a long time before saying to the other ability teams, "Everyone knows the gravity of the situation. If you are unwilling to continue with the mission, you are free to withdraw. However, once you leave, your fate will no longer be any of our concern."

The captains of the other ability teams looked at each other. They had been ordinary people before the apocalypse and were only lucky enough to gain powers and join the ranks of the strong afterward. This did not mean they possessed the hearts of the strong. Facing such a perilous situation, they ultimately retreated, quietly leaving the area with their respective teams.

Only the one hundred men from the military remained.

"Captain, what should we do?" Jiang Ye asked worriedly. With so few of them, they wouldn't even be enough to serve as appetizers for the zombies! Even if they were all military elites, even if each of them could take on a hundred, they could kill at most ten thousand zombies—but there were far more than ten thousand out there.

Jing Chengsu looked around at his brothers, many of whom he had led himself. With a heavy heart, he said, "Brothers, I won't say much about how difficult this mission is. I fear the chances of survival are extremely slim. If anyone wants to withdraw, please raise your hand to vote. I won't blame you."

The group looked around at each other for a while. Although their faces were a bit pale, every expression was firm.

"Captain, ever since we joined the military, we have long since put life and death aside. We aren't leaving."

"That's right! We aren't those cowards who get scared off by a little difficulty!"

"Captain, give the order!"

Jing Chengsu looked at each determined face, seeing their readiness to face death despite knowing the odds were nine to one against them. His heart felt as heavy as a boulder, and his throat felt as if it were blocked by something, leaving him unable to speak for a long time. With hidden pain in his deep eyes, he finally took a deep breath. "Alright. Since everyone has decided, let's discuss how we should proceed."

Zhou Pan looked at these comrades who had cast aside thoughts of life and death with respect. He couldn't bring himself to be ready to sacrifice his life at any moment like them, but that didn't stop him from feeling a sense of admiration for them.

He extended his divine sense, hoping to find a safe route through the zombie-infested market.

After observing for a while, he felt that there were many zombies in every direction. Not knowing which path was the safest, he simply took out paper and pen to record the terrain he saw, marking the approximate number of zombies in each direction.

He handed it to Jing Chengsu. Now that they were all his own people, he wasn't afraid of revealing his other ability.

The group, who were in the middle of discussing their plans, were astonished when they saw the rough sketch, which nevertheless clearly displayed the basic terrain. The area covered was far more detailed and extensive than what Jiang Ye, a mental ability user, had been able to see.

Everyone felt a new wave of admiration for Zhou Pan's abilities.

"Not bad, Little Pan, you've been hiding your true strength!" Jiang Ye patted him on the shoulder.

Zhou Pan smiled shyly.

With the map, everything became much easier. They studied it carefully and finally found a direction where the zombies were sparse.

It was at the back of the storage area, where there was a passage only one person wide that zombies rarely wandered into. On one side of this passage was the storage warehouse, and on the other was a nine-meter-high concrete wall. Usually, even the most skilled thief would find it harder than ascending to heaven to climb over, but fortunately, the strong were emerging in droves now, and various ability users and mutants were appearing one after another. Dealing with this hard wall was much easier than dealing with zombies.

Jing Chengsu had many earth-ability users, sand-ability users, and people with physical mutations under his command; digging a large hole in that nine-meter wall would be a piece of cake.

Furthermore, by entering from the back wall on the perimeter, they could avoid conflict with the zombies. As long as they were careful, they could load the grain and leave, keeping their chances of survival quite high.

Although everyone was prepared to sacrifice their lives, no one wanted to seek death if they could avoid unnecessary sacrifice!

Everyone's favorability toward Zhou Pan, who had managed to produce such a complete map, increased significantly.

After discussing for a while, they finally began to take action.
chapters.title: 第66章 一张地图「求枝枝」

chapters.translated_text:
Taking advantage of the early hour, everyone hurried to take action to avoid any inconvenience once night fell.

With the map and Zhou Pan keeping his divine sense fully active, constantly monitoring their route, they soon safely reached the outer perimeter of the storage area.

Looking at the nine-meter-high wall, climbing it wasn't impossible, but doing so would create a lot of noise, so everyone dismissed the idea.

Jing Chengsu made a comparison and looked at Zhou Pan. Zhou Pan scanned the inner side of the wall with his divine sense, confirming it was indeed the back of the storage area, and nodded.

Jing Chengsu instructed the earth-ability users Wang Chao, Da Long, and Huang Fei, along with the mutated individuals Jiang Cheng and Wang Wu, to create an entrance in this section of the wall.

The earth-ability users worked together to soften the wall, while the mutants used their sharp claws to dig vigorously into the surface.

With a "swish-swish" sound, large amounts of sand and dirt fell, and an entrance two meters high and three meters wide was dug at the base of the nine-meter wall.

After Zhou Pan scanned the passage with his divine sense and found no signs of zombies, Jing Chengsu had the same ability users and mutants continue to dig a hole into the back of the storage warehouse.

The warehouse did have a main gate, but unfortunately, it was at the front, where quite a few zombies were wandering about.

Using the same method, another large entrance was created.

The warehouse was massive, shaped like a giant semi-circle, and the amount of grain stored inside was so vast that those seeing such a large warehouse for the first time were stunned. In particular, the layers upon layers of grain bags were so numerous that they would give anyone with trypophobia goosebumps.

Zhou Pan and the other space-ability users continuously collected the grain, while the others had the space-ability users bring out large trucks and park them outside the wall, and the team members entered the warehouse to move the grain.

There was simply too much grain; even with Zhou Pan and the other space-ability users working hard, they had only collected the tip of the iceberg.

Once the large trucks were completely filled and the other space-ability users' spaces were full, only Zhou Pan was left still collecting grain.

Grain kept disappearing from the ground, leaving only the imprints of the burlap sacks behind.

Zhou Pan loaded the grain with all his might, and soon more than half of the grain in the warehouse had vanished. Many space-ability users stared at Zhou Pan with glowing eyes, wondering when they would be as powerful as him, able to take away vast amounts of grain with a wave of their hands.

It was unclear where things went wrong, but just as Zhou Pan was about to finish collecting the grain, the warehouse gate collapsed with a loud crash, and a swarm of zombies surged in. Most were level two or three, and as soon as they saw a group of fresh, blood-filled humans, they started drooling and howling as they lunged forward.

At the gate, a zombie with pale, cyan skin, purplish-red bloody lips, and glowing red eyes walked into the warehouse, surrounded by a group of other zombies.

"Oh no, a Zombie King?!" Seeing that the situation had turned dire, Jing Chengsu and Zhou Pan blocked the hole, telling the other members to leave immediately.

When the other team members saw their captains preparing to cover their retreat, they wanted to stay and help, but were scolded away.

Upon reaching the trucks outside, they were surprised to find many zombies attacking. They quickly climbed into the vehicles, and regardless of how loud the engines were, they drove off, crashing through obstacles as they retraced their path. Along the way, zombies kept appearing to block and attack them.

Their mission was complete, and they wouldn't let anyone stop their return; the team members drove the trucks directly, crushing anything in their way.

That Zombie King saw several of its "blood meals" escaping and decided that these last two must not be allowed to get away.

The zombie, who was dressed in a suit and tie and looked incredibly fastidious, had blood-red eyes.

It stared at Jing Chengsu and the others, let out a few "howls," and many zombies rushed toward them.

Seeing so many zombies, Zhou Pan and Jing Chengsu realized that if they tried to fight them all off, they didn't know how long it would take, so they simply prepared to retreat.
chapters.source_text:
趁着时辰还早，大家赶紧行动，免得到了晚上行动不便。
有了地图，以及周磐神识全开，不时注意路线，他们很快安全的摸到了仓储区外围。
看着九米高的墙面，想要攀爬的话，也不是不可能，但是这样上墙声音会很大，大家都打消了这个念头。
荆成夙对比了一下，看向周磐，周磐神识扫了一下这面墙的内端，的确是仓储区背面，就点点头。
荆成夙让土系异能的王超，大龙，黄飞等人和手脚变异的姜成，王武等人出手，在面墙的这片大墙挖出一道门来。
只见土异能的几个人合力将面前的一片墙面弄软，变异者则是将化成尖爪对着墙面使劲掏挖。
“沙沙沙”大片的沙泥落下，九米大墙的底部被挖出一道两米高，三米宽的入口。
由周磐神识扫过之后，没在这条通道上发现有任何丧尸的踪影，荆成夙让刚才的异能者、变异者继续在仓储仓库背面挖出洞来。
这仓储仓库倒是有大门，可惜在前方，那边可有不少丧尸在徘徊呢！
用同样的方法，又有一个大门被开发出来。
仓储仓库很大，像个巨大的半圆体，里面储备的粮食非常多，让初次见到这么大仓库的人都目瞪口呆，尤其是那一袋袋层层叠叠的粮袋，多的让有密集恐惧症的人，看的都起鸡皮疙瘩。
周磐和其他空间异能者，不断收取粮食，其他的人让空间异能者拿出大卡车，停在墙外，队员们纷纷进入仓库，搬运着这些粮食。
这粮食实在太多了，即使周磐和其他空间异能者卖力收取，也只不过收了冰山一角。
将大卡车全部填满，其他空间异能者的空间也装不下了，在场只有周磐还在收取粮食。
地面上不断有粮食消失，只留下一个个麻袋印子。
周磐死命的装取粮食，很快仓库内的粮食就消泯了一大半，不少空间异能者眼睛发亮的直盯着周磐，什么时候他们才能跟他一样这么的厉害，挥挥手就带走大片粮食。
也不知哪个地方出错，周磐将要全部收完粮食的时候，仓库大门轰然倒塌，不少丧尸涌入，大多都是二三级的，一见一群血气腾腾的血肉，立马哈喇子都流下了，嗷嗷嚎叫的要扑过来。
大门处一个肤色青白，紫红血唇，两眼闪红光的丧尸在一群丧尸拥护下，走进仓库。
不好丧尸王？！看来事态不妙，荆成夙和周磐拦在洞口让其他成员赶紧离开。
其他队员见队长要断后，想要留下来帮忙，被他给斥走。
到了外面的大卡车处，居然见有不少丧尸围攻过来，赶紧爬上车，也不管卡车行走的声音多么大，他们开着车，横冲直撞的原路返回。这一路上不断有丧尸出没，阻拦围攻他们。
他们任务都完成了，谁也别想阻拦他们的归途，队员们直接开着车，直接碾压过去。
那只丧尸王，见跑走了好几个血食，最后这两个人绝不能让他们再逃了
穿西装打领带，讲究到不行的那个丧尸，血红的眼
盯着荆成夙他们，“嗷嗷”叫了几声，就有许多丧尸朝这边攻来。
周磐和荆成夙见这么多的丧尸，他们若以武力解决掉，也不知要到什么时候，干脆准备直接撤退。
